title: ITT - Swindon Archive Decarbonisation Design Team (UID 320)
description:
Historic England is seeking to appoint a multidisciplinary design team to develop the Archive Decarbonisation Project at its national archive facility in Swindon through RIBA Stage 3. Under the terms of this contract, we reserve the right to award RIBA stage 4 following the satisfactory completion of stage 3 and the receipt of an acceptable return for Stage 4 methodology and pricing schedule (in line with rates provided at stage 3). 
The Historic England Archive is one of the nation's most significant collections of records relating to England's historic environment. The purpose-built archive store was constructed in 1993 to BS5454 standards and provides specialist environmental conditions for the long-term preservation of nationally important photographic, film and documentary collections. However, the building and its associated mechanical and electrical systems were not designed with energy efficiency or net-zero objectives in mind.
The project forms a key part of Historic England's commitment to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040 and responds to the urgent requirement to replace ageing building services plant that has reached, and in some cases exceeded, its operational life. Recent equipment failures have highlighted the increasing risk to collection preservation, building resilience and operational continuity.
A RIBA Stage 2 feasibility study has recently been completed. The study explored a range of options to reduce operational carbon, improve energy performance and secure the long-term sustainability of the archive while maintaining stringent environmental conditions required for collection care.
Based on the information provided, Historic England's preferred option currently involves:
•	Replacement of existing end-of-life environmental control systems with significantly more energy-efficient solutions.
•	Rationalisation of archive environmental zones to improve operational efficiency.
•	Fabric improvements to enhance thermal performance and airtightness.
•	Fire safety upgrades and associated building works.
•	Creation of additional archive storage capacity through the repurposing of existing plant room space, reducing reliance on external storage facilities and supporting future collection growth.
Scope of Services
The appointed design team will be required to lead the project through:
RIBA Stage 3 – Spatial Coordination
Including but not limited to:
•	Review and validation of the completed RIBA Stage 2 outputs.
•	Development of the preferred design solution.
•	Coordination of architectural, structural and building services design, ensuring full integration of archive operational, conservation and storage requirements, and compliance with relevant standards and guidance, including BS EN 16893:2018 Evaluation and mitigation of collection care risks associated with proposed mechanical solutions.
•	Interpretation and integration of thermographic surveys, air-tightness testing and other specialist investigations.
•	Use and develop the client-provided Revit BIM model as the principal tool for multidisciplinary spatial coordination, ensuring that all proposed building-services systems, plant, access requirements and interfaces are accurately modelled and coordinated with the architectural and structural design.
•	Review, validate and develop the existing building physics model to a level appropriate for RIBA Stage 3, reflecting the spatially coordinated design and demonstrating performance against the agreed environmental requirements, energy and carbon targets, plant loads and future climate scenarios.
•	Planning application preparation and submission.
•	Cost planning and value management exercises.
•	Development of a robust whole-life cost and carbon assessment.
•	Stakeholder engagement and workshop facilitation.
•	Support Historic England’s fundraising activities for the project by providing reasonable information, evidence, and documentation to assist fundraising and grant applications where requested.

description:
The council is seeking flexible nightly paid temporary accommodation within Buckinghamshire County, both self-contained (kitchen, bathroom facilities within the property) and shared accommodation. The requirement is for a range of accommodation from a hotel room, through to units that can house families of up to 8 people. The service will operate on a spot-purchase basis, enabling the Council to secure accommodation flexibly and at short notice. 
The Council has a duty under Part 7 of the Housing Act 1996 to provide homelessness advice and assistance. This includes a statutory duty to secure Temporary Accommodation (TA) for persons who are homeless and are deemed to be priority need (based on the priority need categories set down in the Act and associated Code of Guidance). It meets this duty through a combination of designated substantive TA (directly owned by the Council or a Registered Provider) or accommodation secured from a third party provider at a nightly rate as and when required (often referred to a B&B accommodation).
Evidence of Health and Safety Compliance would be required for each property, and inspections would be carried out with Environmental Health Officers prior to any accommodation being used with an agreed inspection schedule moving forwards.

title: Asset Management and Property Management
description:
Here's a clearer and more polished version suitable for a UK04 notice, tender advert or procurement introduction:
You are invited to submit a response to this Request to Participate (RtP) for the provision of Asset Management and Property Management Services.
This procurement is being conducted using the Competitive Flexible Procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. The procurement process will comprise three stages, as set out in the tender documents.
Blackpool Council is seeking to appoint an experienced Asset Manager and Property Manager to maximise performance and undertake the day-to-day management of the Council's retail assets within Blackpool Town Centre. The assets within the scope of this appointment include:
Houndshill Shopping Centre: an enclosed shopping centre extending to approximately 298,000 sq ft, with 750 car parking spaces, located opposite Blackpool Tower. The centre opened in 1980, underwent refurbishment and a significant extension in 2008, and was acquired by Blackpool Council in November 2019. A further expansion was completed in 2024, incorporating a nine-screen cinema complex, including an IMAX auditorium, a ground-floor retail unit and a diner/restaurant unit.
Victoria Buildings (Corporation Street / Victoria Street Portfolio): comprising a block of seven retail units located opposite Houndshill Shopping Centre.
Marks & Spencer Premises, Church Street, Blackpool Town Centre.
The successful supplier(s) will be expected to:
Maintain and enhance income generated from the assets through proactive asset management activities.
Support and implement the Council's plans for the future development of the assets within the wider context of Blackpool Town Centre.
Report on asset performance and progress against agreed objectives to the Council's Houndshill Steering Group.
Provide the full range of health and safety, financial administration and facilities management services required for the effective operation of commercial premises of this nature.
Provide timely financial information, including expenditure data, forecasts and budget projections, to support the Council's reporting requirements.
Liaise and collaborate with other town centre stakeholders to support initiatives that enhance the visitor experience and promote business activity within Blackpool Town Centre.
The contract is anticipated to commence on 1 July 2027. The initial contract term will be five (5) years, with an option for the Council, at its sole discretion, to extend the contract annually for up to a further five (5) years, subject to satisfactory performance, contract review and budget availability. The indicative contract budget is £150,000 per annum.
Tenders are invited either from a single organisation capable of delivering both the Asset Management and Property Management functions or from multiple organisations submitting a joint bid under a single contract arrangement. Where a joint bid is submitted, the Council will expect bidders to demonstrate previous successful collaboration on comparable projects or assignments.
The appointment will be made through a three-stage procurement process. Following evaluation of the RtP stage, a maximum of five suppliers will be invited to participate in the Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage. Following evaluation of ITT submissions, a maximum of two suppliers will be invited to attend a presentation and interview stage before a final contract award decision is made.

title: ITT - Mapping Training and Qualifications for Heritage Construction Trades in England - UID 370
description:
Heritage construction skills are essential for the repair, maintenance, conservation and retrofit of England’s 5.5 million traditional buildings (built pre-1919), but the industry faces significant skills shortages. Complex and patchy provision of relevant training is a major barrier to closing these skills gaps. At present, we have only limited visibility of provision and uptake for construction qualifications which contain heritage content.
This project would fill this gap in our knowledge and evidence by establishing a baseline dataset of current provision, funding, participation in, and completion rates of relevant training and qualifications. This will provide a detailed picture of where training is taking place, who is offering the training, and how many people are undertaking it as well as a repeatable methodology enabling this project to be repeated in future. 
This project will also analyse the data alongside other research to identify where heritage content is included, and where there are gaps in available provision (both geographically and in terms of construction roles), trends over time, and identify qualifications which might be at risk.
With this information we will be able to better target our advocacy and interventions to improve education and training provision in this area and maximise our impact at both a national and regional level. This will directly support our work supporting the supply of heritage construction skills and enabling a greater volume of relevant training.

title: Primary Care Support Services: GP Patient Medical Records
description:
The GP Patient Medical Records Service covers the end-to-end management of high-volume GP Patient medical records. The Service supports GP practices and authorised parties that require records for continuity of care, patient registration, operational processing or legally mandated access. 
The Supplier will be responsible for: 
Providing secure transportation and exchanging of GP Patient medical records between GP practices, storage facilities and authorised recipients. 
Receiving registration transactions generated through patient registration activity and authorised manual requests. 
Creating GP Patient medical record movement requests from those registration transactions. 
Managing GP Patient medical record movements associated with patient registration and authorised manual requests. 
Providing transparent end-to-end status, location, chain-of-custody and audit information. 
Identifying, retrieving, reconciling and maintaining the integrity of the complete GP Patient medical record across paper and digital formats. 
Digitising, quality assuring, indexing and uploading records to the National Document Repository when required. 
Providing secure digital exchange where the National Document Repository is unavailable in exceptional circumstances or inaccessible to the intended recipient. The supplier is not required to build a separate repository. 
Maintaining archive storage and undertaking secure destruction in accordance with approved retention and destruction arrangements. 
Operating the supporting technology, customer contact, tracking, reporting and service-management capabilities. 
Supporting authorised disclosure processes by retrieving and making complete GP Patient medical records available to the Authority’s authorised service. 
Managing non-routine requests, including missing, incomplete, misdirected and urgent GP Patient medical records. 
Providing customer contact, service support, management information and a supporting technology platform. 
Supporting transition from the incumbent supplier and maintaining continuity of service throughout Implementation. 
Mobilising the service and transfer relevant records, inventory data and operational responsibility within the agreed arrangements.
The estimated contract value is £193,000,000 inclusive of the extension options (plus optional services of up to £50,000,000) excluding VAT.

title: WCC Housing Needs Integrated Singles and Outreach Services
description:
WCC Housing Needs Integrated Singles and Outreach Services
The Authority is procuring Integrated Singles and Outreach Services in three (3) Lots. The Services are a pivotal and strategically aligned provision at the heart of the Council’s Homelessness and Rough Sleeping Strategy 2024. These Services are a cornerstone of our ambition to prevent homelessness, enhance recovery, and transform lives through a dynamic, tailored, and outcomes-driven approach. 
The Integrated Singles and Outreach Services will be procured in three (3) Lots:
Lot 1 Assertive Outreach Services: To build strong, ongoing relationships and offer consistent support to people who face long-term homelessness and multiple challenges. The Provider will provide support for complex cases, engagement strategies, and long-term recovery planning. 
Lot 2 First Contact Team: The Provider will act as the first point of contact for the dynamic movement of individuals into and out of rough sleeping (FLOW) and those at risk of rough sleeping. The Provider will deliver rapid and trauma informed support and early interventions to prevent and move Service Users away from Rough Sleeping at the earliest opportunity. 
Lot 3 Hub Support Team: the Provider will deliver a central coordination point for statutory services and housing, providing a single front door for all accommodation options. The Provider will triage Service User needs and co-ordinate support and multi-agency planning. The Provider will actively collaborate with the Authority’s services through a hybrid delivery model, helping to coordinate joined-up planning and support. The Provider will need to provide a building with working space for 20 Council staff and those commissioned to provide support functions for this Lot, as well as having the capacity for Service Users walk-in’s and confidential meetings
The estimated commencement date of this contract is 01/03/2026. The estimated service commencement date is 01/04/2026. The initial term of the contract is 3 years. The Contract may, at the Authority’s discretion, be extended for a further period of up to an aggregate of four (4) years, with a total contract period of seven years (calculated from the Service Commencement Date), expiring no later than 31 March 2033.
During the Contract Period the Authority may, at its sole discretion, require additional Services to be delivered by the Provider for up 25% of the total contract value for each Lot. This will be subject to service needs, funding and will be at the Authorities discretion in line with the Contract.

title: Tender for Sensory Impairment Rehabilitation Service in Herefordshire
description:
Herefordshire Council is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced provider to deliver a countywide Sensory Impairment Service for adults aged 18 and over who are living with visual impairment, hearing impairment or dual sensory loss. The service forms part of the Council's prevention and wellbeing offer and supports residents to maintain independence, improve wellbeing and remain connected to their communities.
The provider will deliver specialist assessments, rehabilitation and enablement support, information, advice and guidance, equipment and assistive technology provision, and administration of sensory impairment registration functions on behalf of the Council. The Service will be accessible across the County of Herefordshire, including rural communities, and will support approximately 55,000 residents living with hearing loss and 6,000 residents living with sight loss. Referrals may be received from service users, health professionals, social care practitioners, carers, families and relevant partner organisations.
The contract is expected to commence on 1 February 2027, with an initial mobilisation and implementation period prior to service commencement on 1 April 2027. The initial contract term will be 5 years, with an option to extend for up to a further 2 years. The procurement is being conducted under the Procurement Act 2023 using the Open Procedure and is subject to the Light Touch Regime.
The maximum available Contract Value for the Sensory Impairment Service is £833,000 (excluding VAT) over the full potential 7-year term. The Contract also includes the ability for the Council to purchase up to £259,000 (excluding VAT) over the full potential 7-year term of Assistive Technology, Equipment and Aids where required. This additional budget does not form part of the £833,000 Contract Value and is available only where the Council approves additional purchases. These additional purchases are not guaranteed. The maximum potential Contract Value is therefore up to £1,092,000 (excluding VAT). 
TUPE information:
TUPE is expected to apply to this contract, and bidders should ensure that the implications of TUPE, including the associated employment and cost implications, are fully considered and reflected in their tender.
Bidders must request access to the TUPE information well in advance of the tender closing date. To access the Employee's information, bidders are required to complete and sign the Completion Document 5 (TUPE Confidentiality Letter Agreement) included within the tender pack, and return it via ProContact messaging system at www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk. The TUPE information will be provided following receipt of the completed agreement.

title: Well-Led Review of Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust
description:
Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust (AWP) provides mental health services across Bath and North East Somerset, Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire, Swindon and Wiltshire, from more than 90 community and inpatient sites and through partnerships with external organisations. Services include acute mental health, recovery, liaison and dementia services, forensic services, Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services and a range of highly specialist mental health services.
AWP is currently in segment 3 of the NHS Oversight Framework and rated Amber-Green under the Provider Capability assessment. Following a Care Quality Commission inspection in 2024, reported in May 2025, the Trust’s well-led rating was ‘requires improvement’. AWP operates across two financially challenged Integrated Care Systems and works with the South West Provider Collaborative for mental health services. 
The Board has invested in strengthening external stakeholder relationships and reviewing partnership working models. It has also experienced material membership changes since the previous well-led inspection, including a new Chair in autumn 2024 and three new Non-Executive Directors commencing in 2026. 
AWP now requires an independent, developmental review of leadership and governance against the Care Quality Commission well-led framework. The review will provide objective and constructive challenge, identify prioritised developmental actions and inform targeted improvement work to secure and sustain future performance.

title: Extra Care Housing Schemes for Care and Support Services for Emma Haas, Watling Gardens and The Willows, Honeypot Lane
description:
This tender for the Extra Care services is strategically positioned to significantly contribute to Brent Council's Borough Plan outcomes. 
This setting, dedicated to serving vulnerable adults over the age of 50 and over, is crucial in enhancing resident health and well-being through providing an alternative to care homes, through a core service and assessed support to keep people as independent as possible. Furthermore, the setting not only supports employment in the local community but also enhances the resilience across our community and supports Brent’s strategy of working in neighbourhoods. This tender will ensure the continued alignment with and contribution to the Council's aspirations, promoting a healthier, more equitable, and unified community. 
The service includes the delivery of extra care housing support services at two extra care housing schemes in Lot 1 and Lot 2:
Lot 1 - Extra care schemes at Emma Haas Watling Gardens 
Lot 2 - Extra care schemes at The Willows Honeypot Lane 
The services are designed to meet the varying needs of residents, to promote health and wellbeing and to enable borough residents to live independently in their home and reduce the potential of moving to residential care. The support is for older adults with care and support needs at substantial or critical level and an identified social housing need. Needs may include physical disabilities, mental health issues (including dementia, learning disabilities) and a range of other needs.
Brent Council is the landlord of both buildings at Emma Haas, Watling Gardens and The Willows, Honeypot Lane.
There are 45 units at Emma Haas and 61 units at The Willows, of which 5 are used as step-down properties. The term step-down is used to describe accommodation units used to house residents who are medically fit to be discharged from hospital but continue to require care and support preventing a return to their own homes or may need a different type of accommodation.
Contract Term: Four years plus a single two-year extension. Extensions will be dependent on future funding settlements for the Council.
The estimated budget total of the contract will be £10,570,056.

title: Conductive Energy Devices (CED)
description:
The Home Office, working with the National Police Chiefs’ Council Less Lethal Weapons function, is undertaking market engagement regarding the potential future procurement of Conducted Energy Devices (CEDs) and associated equipment, consumables and support services for UK policing.
The potential requirement covers overt and covert CED capability and may include complete CED systems and/or individual component parts. Goods may include CED devices, holders and carriage systems, operational and training cartridges, batteries and other power components, associated software and secure data-management capability, training equipment and other ancillary equipment required to provide an operational CED capability.
Associated services may include maintenance and through-life support, software and firmware support and updates, provision of technical and safety documentation, warranty and replacement support, and assistance with the development of operational procedures, training manuals and user manuals. The potential requirement may also include inert training devices and training cartridges suitable for scenario-based training.
Solutions would be required to be suitable for use within UK policing and capable of delivery to the UK. The Authority is interested in existing, emerging and alternative CED technologies, including solutions suitable for routine overt operational policing and solutions or adaptations supporting discreet carriage and deployment.
Indicative quantity: Historic overt CED demand across forces was 23,322 devices in 2024/25 and 31,628 devices in 2025/26. These figures are provided as an indication of historic demand only and should not be interpreted as a commitment or guaranteed future volume. The RFI does not currently provide a confirmed quantity for any future procurement or for covert CED demand.

title: Care Support Services for Children with a Disability (2026)
description:
Hampshire County Council Children’s Services commissions care support for children and young people with disabilities. The children and young people requiring care support services will include those with severe disabilities such as learning disabilities, physical disabilities, autistic spectrum conditions, behaviour that challenges and complex physical or mental health needs. The Services are part of a holistic support package for the child / young person that meets identified outcomes as part of a Care Plan as agreed by the Council’s County Allocation Panel.
This Service is part of Hampshire County Council’s Children’s Services Department’s continuum of services which support children and young people with disabilities. Care support is a Tier 4 specialist service, which can be offered to a family following a social care assessment where the Disabled Children’s Team criteria has been met and/or an unmet social care need has been identified.
The Services will have the following features:
• provides a time limited or ongoing intervention for families, dependent on need
• provides a range of different types of support to be available (e.g. domiciliary care, personal care, support in the community, overnight care etc.)
• provides flexible levels of support to meet individual needs (some families may only need light touch, and some will need intensive)
• provides support at both the times that is assessed as a need by the Social Worker and requested by families, for the time period required (e.g., one hour at the beginning and / or end of the day)
• provides suitably trained, reliable, consistent workers; known to the child or young person, all of whom will have an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Services (DBS) check, to ensure continuity and stability for families
• delivers Excellent / Good care in accordance with Care Quality Commission guidance for providers of health and social care services for children and young people
• identifies opportunities for the use of assistive care technologies and equipment to enable families to support their child independently in their own home or for the young person to access the community independently
• can support a child or young person in their own homes whilst the parent or carer is not present
• can support a child or young person in a residential home, foster home or their own home
• can support the child or young person in their local communities
The current Care Support for Children with a Disability Framework was developed by Hampshire County Council to address growing and evolving needs in social care, for children who require support in their home environment and to safeguard these children. The service is coming to the end of it's life span and is required to be retendered to ensure Hampshire may meet the needs of its eligible residents.
The new framework will be an evolution from the current Framework and the Authority is looking is looking for contracts for services under the Framework to commence from 01/09/2026.
This is a light touch contract as set out in section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023. As such the Council is establishing a Framework which will be open for new entrants across it's entire term. However, the Council reserves the right to temporarily pause the Framework for new entrants at any point. Any pause will be communicated through the Councils electronic tendering system. 
The Timetable in section 4.1 relates to the initial application window. Once the Framework commences it will be reopened for new applications and suppliers will be able to apply at any point up until 3 months before the Framework expires.

title: European Traffic Management System (ERTMS) Early Works - Stage 2 (Develop) Support Services
description: LSPH’s current TVM430 signalling system is reaching obsolescence, creating increasing operational, safety and resilience risks. Without intervention, system reliability and lifecycle issues are expected to significantly impact network performance from the 2030s. Stage 1 of the upgrade programme—delivered with SYSTRA—produced an Operational Context Document, a Technical Strategy with long- and short-list options, and a Strategic Outline Business Case (SOBC) in WebTAG format. This completed the Rail Network Enhancements Pipeline (RNEP) Stage 1: Determine. LSPH and its stakeholders are now progressing to RNEP Stage 2: Develop, requiring specialist external consultancy support throughout 2026. Stage 2 will resolve key strategic questions, including the preferred technology solution for replacing TVM430, the funding approach within the HS1 regulatory and concession framework, the suitability of innovative commercial models, strategic opportunities, and the project delivery and scope choices that minimise whole-life cost. Additional strategic issues may be identified collaboratively during the process. Summary of requirement: Stage 2 has an estimated duration of six months, extending if an option to complete on-site surveys is executed, and aims to evaluate a range of delivery options for introducing ERTMS on High Speed 1. The assessment will include but not be limited to benefits, costs, deliverability, and operational impacts. The objective is to secure full stakeholder agreement on a single, coherent project delivery strategy for ERTMS implementation. To complete Stage 2, the appointed consultant will deliver: • Confirmation of the preferred technical option, commercial delivery model, funding route, and integrated project delivery model. • Long-list and short-list optioneering across technical, commercial, and funding dimensions to determine the integrated delivery model. • A whole-life cost estimate for the integrated delivery model. • A delivery schedule through to entry into service and handover to maintenance. • A comprehensive RAID (Risks, Assumptions, Issues and Dependencies) register in the authority’s format. • All Deliverables from the Deliverables Register (to be provided). • Satisfy paragraphs A.6 to A.11 of the latest Rail Network Enhancements Pipeline guidance to enable progression to the next phase. Required Outcome: All relevant stakeholders support and agree to the implementation of a single, coherent project delivery strategy for ERTMS on High Speed 1.
buyer: HS1 Ltd (t/a London St. Pancras Highspeed)

title: Wirral Restorative Justice & Mediation Service
description:
Wirral Borough Council's Community Safety Service seeks to commission a suitably qualified and experienced provider to deliver a Restorative Justice (RJ) and Mediation Service across the Borough of Wirral.
The Council require a high-quality, victim-focused Restorative Justice and Mediation Service that supports the resolution of conflict, repairs harm, improves community relationships and contributes to the reduction of anti-social behaviour and community tensions.
The successful provider will be expected to deliver services in accordance with current Restorative Justice Council (RJC) standards and guidance and adopt a trauma-informed, restorative and person-centred approach throughout service delivery.  RJC Practice Guidance 2020
As a minimum, the successful provider must be able to:
•	Manage referrals from multiple referral pathways.
•	Deliver a safe, impartial and effective restorative justice and mediation service.
•	Demonstrate adherence to Restorative Justice Council Best Practice Guidance.
•	Deliver interventions that are tailored to the needs and circumstances of participants.
•	Undertake robust assessments, safeguarding procedures and risk management processes.
•	Facilitate a range of restorative interventions, including direct and indirect restorative processes.
•	Support the resolution of anti-social behaviour, neighbour disputes and community conflict.
•	Deliver community-based restorative approaches and community problem-solving interventions.
•	Work collaboratively with Wirral Borough Council, Merseyside Police and partner agencies.
•	Monitor service performance and demonstrate positive outcomes for participants and communities.
The successful provider must ensure the service is fully operational and prepared to receive referrals from the commencement date of the contract.

title: ITT 43/2026 - PEACEPLUS Collaborative Interaction Programme - Sustaining Cross Community Relationships
description:
As part of the PEACEPLUS Action Plan, NMDDC will deliver a series of Collaborative Interaction Programmes under Strand 2 – Thriving and Peaceful Communities. Strand 2 comprises eight priority projects that collectively aim to build capacity, develop leadership, strengthen cross community relationships, provide social and emotional support, and deliver inclusive events, festivals, and community justice initiatives.
Within this strand, the Sustaining Cross Community Relations Programme seeks to build on the relationships, trust, and learning developed through previous PEACE and Council programmes. The programme will consist of seven standalone projects, one in each District Electoral Area (DEA), and will focus on engaging individuals and communities who have been less involved in peacebuilding to date—particularly those living in or affected by contested spaces.
To deliver seven standalone cross community projects—one in each DEA—engaging individuals and communities who are not typically involved in peacebuilding. Through structured contact, facilitated dialogue, and capacity building, the programme will strengthen relationships, empower communities, and support the development of shared visions for local areas. This work will contribute to the gradual removal of psychological and physical barriers and promote long term reconciliation.
The programme will also help communities identify key issues affecting them, create safe opportunities for dialogue, and address behaviours or tensions that may exclude or intimidate individuals based on religion, race, or other identity factors.

description:
West Midlands Combined Authority is undertaking a Pre-Market Engagement (PME) to gather insight and feedback from the creative industries sector on the proposed Catalyst Fund and how best to support the development of creative hubs, infrastructure and growth ecosystems across the region. 
The Creative Industries are a priority growth sector within both the UK’s Industrial Strategy and the West Midlands Growth Plan. The region has significant strengths in areas such as screen industries, gaming, CreaTech, design and fashion, with the potential to drive further economic growth, investment and job creation in these key growth sectors. The West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) is developing the Catalyst Fund as part of the Creative Places Growth Fund, with the goal of supporting and strengthening  a limited number of specialist creative hubs and which support the diverse diaspora of creatives across the region. 
WMCA is undertaking this pre-market engagement exercise to better understand current challenges, test the proposed approach, identify effective delivery models, and gather feedback that will inform the design of any future programme and associated procurement activity. title: P2326 - Micellaneous Drainage Works Framework
description:
A framework for the provision of miscellaneous drainage works.
The framework will commence in October 2026 and will be in place for a period of 4 years. Contracts called-off from the framework may extend beyond the expiry date of the framework.
Calling-off from the Framework
- There are two routes which the Council can utilise to award Call-Off Contracts for the works required, either calling-off without competition or by conducting a further competition.
- Call-off without competition - The provider ranked first will be approached to confirm if they are able to meet the Council's timescales and confirm their costs to deliver the works.  If they are able to do so, they will be awarded the Call-Off Contract. If they cannot fulfil the requirement the provider ranked second may then be approached and so on. The costs given must be based on the prices submitted as part of the provider's Tender when they joined the framework.
- Further competition - All the providers of the framework will be invited to tender for the works. During a further competition, providers may submit more competitive pricing than the pricing submitted as part of the provider’s Tender when they joined the framework.
Overview of the Opportunity
The Council has adopted the Infrastructure Conditions of Contract Measurement Version 2011 based on the ICE Conditions of Contract 7th Edition together with amendments included (004 attached) within that document by the Council for the purposes of this Framework Agreement. All future call offs under this framework agreement will be done so under the terms and conditions within this document.
The scope is related to rivers, brooks, reservoirs, pools and drainage to benefit the local residents and the wider community by improving the environment. The works are to include:
•	Routine and reactive maintenance work to existing grill structures in watercourses 
•	24 Hour Emergency clearance work to grill structures and highway culverts.   
•	Construction of new and maintenance of existing flood defense structures.
•	Repair and reconstruction of brick and other lining to watercourses.
•	Repair, improvements and rehabilitation to natural watercourses, small pools and large reservoirs.
•	Small Flood defense schemes
•	Sustainable drainage schemes and maintenance works 
•	Earthworks, dredging and general environmental works, including in environmentally sensitive areas.  
•	Construction and maintenance of lengths of drains, gullies and manholes. 
•	Resilience work to protect properties.
•	Other general measures as necessary; e.g. repairs to existing access/egress points into watercourses, tree/vegetation management on embankments to watercourses and dealing with local flooding.
•	Excavation of existing watercourse channels, embankments, open land, footways and carriageways, including deep excavations.
•	Flexible pavement and footway construction.
•	Traffic and pedestrian management.
•	Installation of new drainage systems and associated manhole constructions. 
•	Bank stabilization works and construction of new retaining structures
•	Working outside normal office hours, including the provision and placing of sandbags in flood events.
•	De-watering and flow diversion work.
•	Protection to existing underground statutory utility and other services and mains.
•	Safety fencing and associated landscape works.
•	Work in confined spaces.
•	Other miscellaneous civil and water engineering works
•	Drainage maintenance and landscape management

HIOW ICB is inviting current and prospective providers to participate in a hybrid provider market engagement event concerning the emerging future model for all-age Autism and ADHD diagnostic assessment and the ADHD medication pathway across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.
The event will cover services for children, young people and adults, including locally commissioned and Right to Choose provision. The ICB is seeking informed market insight before finalising its future service requirements, refreshed local accreditation documentation and associated commissioning arrangements. The market engagement event will share the ICB's emerging approach to local accreditation and seek provider feedback on its feasibility, requirements and implementation. We particularly want to understand provider capability, practical considerations and  potential risks,  before the accreditation model is finalised.
The event is open to current and prospective Autism and ADHD providers interested in local accreditation. Organisations do not need to currently hold a contract with NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight to participate.

title: Westminster Complex Needs Assessment Centre
description:
Westminster City Council (WCC) is undertaking market engagement and invites interested parties to complete a Market Sounding Questionnaire. The purpose of this exercise is to gather feedback from the market regarding the potential commissioning of a Complex Needs Assessment Centre for individuals experiencing homelessness and multiple disadvantage.
This Market Sounding Questionnaire is not a call for tenders or a pre-qualification exercise. The purpose of the questionnaire is to gain insight into the market and understand the level of interest, expertise, and capacity to deliver an assessment-focused service for people with complex needs. The Authority is seeking feedback from organisations that may be able to provide accommodation alongside assessment and support services, or deliver assessment and support services in partnership with a suitable accommodation provider.
The proposed Complex Needs Assessment Centre would provide a safe and structured environment for individuals experiencing rough sleeping and homelessness who present with multiple and intersecting support needs, including mental health issues, substance misuse, physical health conditions, offending histories, and other forms of social exclusion. Operating through a trauma-informed and person-centred approach, the service would provide comprehensive assessment, stabilisation, triage and short-term intervention to identify the most appropriate pathway for each individual.
A key function of the Centre would be to undertake holistic assessments and coordinate multi-agency input to determine an individual's housing, support, health and social care needs. The service would work to reconnect service users with existing support networks, local authority areas where appropriate, specialist services, and sustainable accommodation options. Through effective triage and intensive case coordination, the Centre would support individuals to move swiftly into the most suitable accommodation and support pathway, reducing rough sleeping, repeat homelessness, and unsuccessful placements.
The Centre would act as a key gateway within Westminster's homelessness system, supporting informed decision-making, improving access to services, and ensuring that individuals with complex needs receive the right intervention at the right time. The service would work closely with statutory and voluntary sector partners to facilitate onward moves, strengthen partnership working, and improve outcomes for people experiencing multiple disadvantage.
To inform its commissioning strategy, Westminster City Council is seeking market feedback through this questionnaire. The information gathered will help the Authority understand the market's capability and capacity to deliver a Complex Needs Assessment Centre, including accommodation provision where applicable, assessment and triage functions, reconnection activity, partnership models, workforce requirements, and approaches to supporting individuals with multiple disadvantage.
 The Council would be seeking a contract of a minimum of three years with an option to extend for up to two years.
 Value — Annual value £897,139, initial period £2,691,416 and for full contract period £4,485,693

description:

The work has a specific focus on three linked problems: women not being listened to, the under recognition and normalisation of procedural pain, and the disproportionate impact of both on women from the Global Majority.
Aims and objectives:
1. To improve how the women’s health workforce listens and responds to women, recognises and acts on pain, and delivers culturally competent care.
2. To build lasting training capacity in every NHS England region rather than deliver a one off national course.
3. To give integrated care boards practical guidance so they can sustain local delivery and commission further work in this area themselves.
4. To ensure the programme is shaped by the experience of the workforce and by what women have told NHS England, including women from Global Majority communities and women from the Core20 population.
5. To leave NHS England owning a complete and refreshable set of materials that can be updated as the capability framework develops.

title: Procurement of an HR and Payroll System
description:
The scope of the tender is to identify a suitable supplier for the implementation and ongoing support of a replacement HR system and managed UK payroll service for Look Ahead Care, Support & Housing. The required solution must support the full employee lifecycle, workforce administration, managed payroll and pensions administration, recruitment, onboarding, compliance, employee relations, reporting, integrations, data migration, implementation and transition to business as usual. Unless expressly identified as a separately priced option or Phase 2 requirement, Tenderers should assume that all items listed in this section form part of the core day-one scope and must be included within the tendered solution and commercial response.
•	Core HR and workforce administration: employee records, organisational structure, position and employee references, contracts and terms, multiple concurrent engagements per individual, establishment management and post control, including budgeted posts, position management, organisational hierarchy, approval workflows and reporting-line management.
•	Payroll and pensions: fully managed UK payroll service, including statutory filing, year-end activity, managed pensions administration, auto-enrolment, opt-outs, contribution submissions, provider returns, pension query support, statutory payments, salary sacrifice, attachment of earnings, off-cycle or emergency payments, payroll queries, Average Holiday Pay and NMW/NLW compliance calculations.
•	Absence management: sickness, annual leave, family leave, sabbaticals, AWOL, authorised absence, return-to-work processes and associated workflow, reporting and audit requirements. Fully customisable T&Cs in line with either Organisation policy or TUPE-in policy
•	Recruitment, onboarding, compliance and learning: recruitment and applicant tracking, candidate portal, document upload, job board integration or linking to the Look Ahead website, regulatory and safer-recruitment compliance records, dedicated DBS integration and tracking, expiry alerting, evidence capture, employee document management, retention and deletion rules, onboarding, pre-employment compliance, offboarding and leaver workflows. DBS functionality should support integration with a third-party DBS checking provider where required, including application status tracking, outcome recording, renewal monitoring, expiry reporting and audit history.
•	Employee, manager and workforce development: employee and manager self-service, performance and supervision recording, talent, succession and workforce development management, including talent profiles, succession planning, career development, skills and competency tracking, performance and appraisal linkage, succession risk reporting, development plans and management reporting.
•	Learning Pool: Learning Pool will remain in use during Phase 1. Integration with Learning Pool is core scope at HRIS go-live, while replacement of Learning Pool or the Learning Management System is a Phase 2 priced option and is not part of the day-one core replacement.
•	Employee relations and HR case management: case creation, categorisation, allocation, workflow, task management, document storage, confidentiality controls, restricted access, audit trail, key date tracking, outcome recording, reporting and the ability to manage multiple case types such as disciplinary, grievance, sickness absence, capability, probation and flexible working.
•	Reporting, governance and security: reporting, analytics, statutory reporting including Gender Pay Gap reporting, audit trails, data retention, GDPR reporting, information governance reporting, Subject Access Request and IG request support, workflow and authorisation, role-based access control, user security administration, permission management and auditable security access reporting.
•	Integrations and interfaces: key systems and data flows required to support HR, payroll, recruitment, compliance, learning, finance and reporting, including Unit4, Neuven bank and agency portal, identity provider, Active Directory and single sign-on, pension providers, Learning Pool, Access Group compliance portal, Cardinus, DBS checking providers or other third-party pre-employment compliance services, the Look Ahead website and reporting, data warehouse or Power BI feeds.
•	Data migration, implementation and transition: data migration from the incumbent iTrent system, cleansing, reconciliation, testing, training, cutover, hypercare, knowledge transfer and transition to business as usual, including system administration handover, support model definition and retained configuration documentation.
•	Separately priced options: Tenderers must provide separately priced options where requested in the Cost Schedule, including integrated or natively supported rostering and any Phase 2 replacement of Learning Pool or the Learning Management System. Such options are not part of the core day-one HR system and managed payroll replacement unless expressly confirmed by Look Ahead following evaluation and contract award.
The list above is not exhaustive and is intended to summarise the principal areas included within the scope of the tender.

title: Food Waste Receipt and Treatment
description:
Suffolk County Council is looking to appoint up to three Contractors to receive and process Suffolk’s Food Waste.
The contract(s) will be directly between the successful Contractor(s) and Suffolk County Council, who are acting on behalf of Suffolk’s District and Borough Councils. (Babergh District Council, East Suffolk Council, Ipswich Borough Council, Mid Suffolk District Council and West Suffolk Council)
We anticipate that the Contract will be let in 3 geographical lots, these being based in the East (Ipswich), North (Lowestoft), and West (Bury St Edmunds) of the county. Based on actual collections since June 2026, we expect approximately 25,000-28,000 tonnes of food waste in total to be collected each year across the County. Whilst this tonnage is not guaranteed, the successful contractor(s) will be offered exclusivity of the tonnage within each lot. We are issuing this notice to inform the market of our intentions and invite all prospective service providers to participate in the pre-market engagement exercise to enable us to shape a suitable contract and procurement process.
The waste is expected to be delivered directly to the processing sites.  The Authority is interested in solutions which minimise the overall cost and environmental impact of the service. Consequently, the future procurement will consider the transport distance between collection areas and treatment facilities, together with associated haulage impacts and treatment costs, as part of the evaluation methodology.
Processing should create Biogas and Digestate to PAS110 standards.
Average monthly tonnages expected (but not guaranteed) are as follows:
Lot 1 East - Ipswich 933 tonnes
Lot 2 North – Lowestoft 367 tonnes.
Lot 3 West - Bury St Edmunds 994 tonnes
Estimated total value (Ex. VAT):
Lot 1 East – Ipswich £1,791,360
Lot 2 North – Lowestoft £704,640
Lot 3 West – Bury St Edmunds £1,908,480
Total: £4,404,480
We intend to publish the tender notice for this opportunity in Qtr. 4 of 2026/27.

title: The Supply of Electricity to MOD sites in Northern Ireland
description:
PROCUREMENT SUMMARY
Procedure: Open Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023.
Contract Length: 24 Months + 12 Month Extension + 12 Month Extension.
Maximum Contract Duration: 48 Months.
Annual Consumption: Approximately 30.1 GWh.
Meter Portfolio: 23 Half-Hourly, 110 Non-Half-Hourly.
Portfolio Coverage: Commercial and Domestic Electricity Supplies.
Geographic Scope: MOD Sites throughout Northern Ireland.
Pricing model: Variable price, cost-plus.
Award Basis: Most Advantageous Tender (MAT).
Evaluation Split: Technical 50%, Commercial 40%, Social Value 10%.
Estimated Total Contract Value: £25,886,000 excluding VAT.
1. CONTRACTING AUTHORITY
The Contracting Authority is the Ministry of Defence (MOD), acting through the Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO).
The DIO is responsible for supporting defence outputs through the management, maintenance, development and operation of the defence estate.
The Contracting Authority is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced electricity supplier to deliver commercial and domestic electricity supply services to MOD establishments throughout Northern Ireland.
The Ministry of Defence seeks a supplier capable of delivering secure, reliable, value-for-money electricity services across the Northern Ireland defence estate whilst supporting defence outputs, operational resilience, sustainability objectives and effective stewardship of public funds.
2. PROCUREMENT REFERENCE
Procurement Reference: 715787474.
3.  BACKGROUND
The Ministry of Defence occupies a diverse estate across Northern Ireland comprising military establishments, training areas, operational facilities, administrative buildings, technical infrastructure, residential accommodation and associated support facilities.
Electricity is a critical service supporting defence capability, operational readiness, training outputs, estate resilience and the wellbeing of personnel and their families.
The Authority requires a supplier capable of delivering a secure, reliable and efficient electricity supply service across the full meter portfolio while supporting statutory compliance, financial transparency, sustainability objectives and operational resilience.
The successful supplier will become a key strategic utility provider to the Authority and shall work collaboratively with DIO and its service delivery partners during the contract term.
4. OBJECTIVE OF THE PROCUREMENT
The objective of this procurement is to establish a single contract for the provision of electricity supply services covering both commercial and domestic consumption.
The Authority seeks a supplier capable of delivering:
•	Secure electricity supplies
•	Accurate and timely billing
•	High-quality customer service
•	Consumption data management
•	Sustainability reporting
•	Carbon reduction support
•	Strong contract management
•	Continuous service improvement.
The Authority wishes to create a contract that enables value for money whilst ensuring continuity of supply and supporting Government sustainability objectives.
5. CONTRACT SCOPE
The scope includes all activities necessary to provide a complete electricity supply service across the MOD portfolio in Northern Ireland.
The successful supplier will provide all services required from meter registration through to final invoicing.
The supplier shall assume full responsibility for management of all electricity supply accounts included within the contract.
6. COMMERCIAL ELECTRICITY SUPPLY REQUIREMENT
Commercial supply points include:
•	Military establishments
•	Single living accommodation
•	Storage sites
•	Headquarters buildings
•	Offices
•	Training facilities
•	Workshops
•	Warehouses
•	Security facilities
•	Communication facilities.
7. DOMESTIC ELECTRICITY SUPPLY REQUIREMENT
Domestic supplies include:
•	Service Family Accommodation
•	Other authorised MOD residential properties.
8. METERING
The estate uses the following types of meters:
•	Half-hourly meters
•	Non-half-hourly meters
•	Domestic meters
•	Commercial meters.
Actual portfolio data is included within the tender documentation.
9. CONTRACT TERM
The proposed contract term is: 24 months initially with two option years (2+1+1).
The Authority reserves the right to exercise extension periods at its sole discretion.
10. PRICING MECHANISM
The pricing model selected for this procurement is a variable price, cost-plus model.
11. EVALUATION METHODOLOGY
Tenders will be assessed using a Quality:Price ratio as below:
60 Quality / 40 Price
Minimum standards of legal, financial capacity and technical ability and the evidence required from suppliers to prove that they satisfy quality standards are contained in the ITT document.
A Weighted Value for Money (WVFM) Index will be used to calculate the Total Scores.
Full details of the evaluation methodology are included in the tender documentation.
12. PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
Supplier performance will be measured by the following KPI’s:
1.	Timely Billing.
2.	Query and Complaint Resolution.
3.	Metering and Registration Performance.
4.	Data Quality and Reporting.
5.	Unbilled sites.
6.	Social Value – Fair Work.
Detailed KPIs are included within the contract documents
13. SOCIAL VALUE
The Authority will evaluate social value as part of the award process using Model Award Criteria (MAC) 1a - Create and/or retain high-quality jobs.
14. DEFENCE SOURCING PORTAL GUIDANCE ON RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE:
Suppliers must be registered on the Defence Sourcing Portal (DSP) before they can participate in this opportunity. Go to the DSP homepage (link below): 
https://contracts.mod.uk
Then select 'Register now' and follow steps to complete registration. 
Current Defence Opportunities can be viewed by anyone using the DSP opportunity search facility. Please search using the procurement reference: 715787474. 
Once the opportunity listing is located:
Select the Project Title.
Review the project and opportunity details.
Locate the linked ITT within the Published Lots section.
Select"Go To Project Details".
Select the ITT name to view the ITT documentation and details.
To participate in the procurement please review the ITT requirements and supporting documents. Select"Express Interest" or"Intend to Respond". After expressing interest, the ITT will move into the supplier's My ITTs area where the tender response can be completed and submitted. 
Please contact DIOComrcl-Facilities-ESus@mod.gov.uk for any queries on the above process.

title: Barbican Renewal Programme - Luminaires
description:
The Barbican Centre, on behalf of the City of London Corporation (the City) invites Bidders to complete and submit a request to participate in the Procurement for the provision of a Heritage Luminaire Manufacturer for the Barbican Renewal Programme (BRP).
The Heritage Luminaire Manufacturer will produce bespoke light fittings for the BRP. The supplier will be appointed directly by the Barbican Centre on behalf of the City and will be responsible for manufacturing the bespoke light fittings. Installation will be undertaken by a trade contractor under the Construction Manager (CM).
The appointment will commence in November 2027 and extend through to November 2030, with an estimated value of £1,100,000 excluding VAT. The delivery of the heritage luminaires on site is targeted for the end of 2028. 
The scope of the Heritage Luminaire Manufacturer is to produce a custom lighting fixture for the public spaces within the Barbican Centre, namely:
-	Main Foyers Level B1, 0 and 1
-	Lakeside/ Main Foyer canopy (external)
-	Art Gallery Foyer, Conservatory Terrace and Garden Room
-	Art Gallery/ Sculpture Court canopy (external)
The luminaires shall incorporate a modular and adaptable design suitable for installation within single-, double-, and triple-height spaces. See the Scope of Requirements document and Appendices for full information.
The appointment will be procured through a two-stage tender process, with the overall tendering and prototype development programme anticipated to be completed over a period of approximately one year.
The appointed manufacturer shall be required to collaborate closely with the existing project team, including Allies and Morrison, Asif Khan Studio, Buro Happold, Gardiner & Theobald, Blue Sky Building, les éclaireurs, Alan Baxter, and others to ensure the successful coordination, development, and delivery of the bespoke lighting fixture.
During the installation phase, the CM will assume responsibility for the coordination and management of all trade contractors on site, overall site logistics, and the integration of individual package programmes into a coherent and deliverable whole.
The Heritage Luminaire Manufacturer shall ensure that the bespoke lighting fixtures are manufactured, coordinated, and delivered in accordance with the project programme, and shall be fully prepared to meet all required delivery dates as instructed by the Client and Project Team.

Tenders were evaluated to identify the Supplier offering the Most Advantageous Tender (MAT), representing the best value for money in accordance with the published evaluation methodology. The assessment methodology used to determine the MAT was Price Per Quality Point (PPQP).

title: Provision of Treated Residual Waste Recovery Services - Thornton Waste Recovery Park
description:
Lancashire County Council is seeking tenders for the provision of services for the Collection, transportation, acceptance, and Recovery of Treated Residual Waste from Thornton Waste Recovery Park. 
In summary, the services will comprise the collection, direct transportation, weighing and recovery of up to 75,000 Tonnes per annum of Treated Residual Waste from Thornton Waste Recovery Park.
The Services are being procured on the basis of two (2) lots comprising of up to 37,500  Tonnes per annum of Treated Residual Waste.  The Authority is seeking to appoint a single Provider for each Lot.
The Authority will pay the Provider for a guaranteed minimum tonnage of Treated  Residual Waste each Contract Year as detailed in Annex B of the Specification and  the Contract. At least three months prior to the commencement of each Contract Year the Authority will notify the successful Tenderer(s) of a Reserve Tonnage for that  Contract Year; and the Tenderer will be obliged to make capacity at the relevant Provider Facilities available to accept the Reserve Tonnage of Treated Residual  Waste Collected and transported to the Provider Facility.  The Reserve Tonnage will be a tonnage falling between the Guaranteed Tonnage and the Capacity Tonnage.  
It is expected that the majority of Treated Residual Waste will be Collected in  articulated vehicles with target payloads of between 21 (twenty one) and 23 (twenty three) Tonnes. 
Collections will typically be required to take place on a Monday to Friday basis,  excluding Bank Holidays. However, there may be occasion when Collections are  required on a Saturday (for example due to Bank Holidays, scheduled site  maintenance, or higher than expected Treated Residual Waste stocks due to  increased processing) so Providers must be able to accommodate Collections on a Saturday morning up to 12noon.  
Please see tender documents for more information about the scope and requirements.

The University of Oxford (UoO) will provide NHS England with access to the ORCHID-E dataset, hosted by the Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences at the UoO. ORCHID is a unique national dataset, routinely collecting and securely storing pseudonymised patient-level data from over 2,000 GP practices across England. title: Inter-Agency Debris Co-ordination Committee (IADC) Research Studies - 2026/27
description:
The Office of the Chief Engineer within the UK Space Agency (UKSA) is intending to identify delivery partners to support a set of studies that will support ongoing research being performed as part of its role in the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC).
The IADC has 13 member states that conduct technical research to inform their publications on how to measure, model, protect from and mitigate space debris. The primary purpose is to exchange information on space debris research activities between members, to facilitate opportunities for cooperation in space debris research, to review the progress of ongoing cooperative activities and to identify debris mitigation options. The UK has been a member for nearly 30 years and has been helping to guide the international policy over this time. The IADC consists of a steering group and four working groups - Measurements, Environment and Database, Protection and Mitigation. The studies that have been identified will seek to support on-going research being performed in each of these working groups.
UKSA is seeking suppliers to perform technical studies of relevance to three of the four IADC working groups. We will require the supplier to fulfil the specification, including defining framework/model where needed and putting theoretical metrics into practice. We are splitting this competition into multiple lots linked to three of the four IADC working groups. Prospective bidders should note this requirement is not seeking any studies this year in support of IADC Working Group 1.
Bidders may bid for and be awarded one or more studies within each lot. For the avoidance of doubt, it is not necessary to bid for multiple studies to be eligible to participate. UKSA reserves the right to award multiple contracts in the event of budget availability and sufficient high-quality proposals. Equally, UKSA reserves the right to not award individual lots where insufficient high quality proposals are received.

title: CORSIA Capacity Building Project
description:
For emissions reduction credits to be eligible under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), the countries hosting the projects that generate them must provide authorisation to confirm the associated reductions will not also be counted against domestic targets, and make the adjustments to their national emissions reporting required by Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement. To increase the global supply of credits to meet the level of offsetting obligations expected from CORSIA’s First Phase, which must be fulfilled by January 2028, there is a need for capacity building support to assist and train host country governments in the authorisation and reporting process.  
This procurement aims to appoint a supplier with suitable specialist expertise to act in a delivery partner capacity, designing and overseeing multiple work packages aimed at supporting governments in emerging markets and developing economies to release CORSIA credits. The supplier would assist DfT in identifying impactful opportunities for UK-funded support, and then utilise its international networks to engage suitable experts around the world to deliver targeted support to governments. Support to specific countries would cover issuing the Letters of Authorisation required to confirm their intention to release credits, and/or completing the reporting of corresponding adjustments in accordance with Article 6.2.

The contract will operate on a guaranteed performance basis, with the successful Supplier providing a fixed annual contract price. There will be an option to extend the contract for a further period of up to three years by mutual agreement.
St Catherine's CofE (VC) Primary School is located in Kidderminster, Worcestershire. It is a Church of England voluntary controlled primary school for pupils aged 4–11, with approximately 414 pupils currently on roll, a capacity of 420 pupils, and is supported by a dedicated team of teaching and support staff. 
St. Catherine’s is truly a special school.  They nurture every aspect of child development, promoting high academic standards while fostering social and emotional skills—truly embodying their commitment as a ‘Heartsmart’ school.  Strong relationships are vital for their success, and they pride themselves on the positive connections they build within they school community. 
The existing structure comprises all six cleaners working in the evening with cleaning completed 15.15pm - 18.30pm. The current service operates for 39 weeks of standard cleaning per annum, supplemented by 51 hours of periodic cleaning spread across the year. There is currently no daytime cleaning provision.
Whilst the monthly contract payment will represent one-twelfth of the annual contract value, a monthly reconciliation process will be undertaken to verify actual hours worked against those budgeted within the contract. Where actual hours delivered are lower than those budgeted, the Supplier will be required to provide a credit to the school. This credit will be calculated by dividing the annual contract value by the annual contracted hours to establish a contractual hourly rate, which will then be multiplied by the shortfall in hours delivered.
The school is seeking a suitably experienced Supplier with a proven track record of delivering cleaning services within the primary school sector. Preference will be given to Suppliers with a strong operational presence within the West Midlands, enabling the provision of responsive contract support, operational resilience and service flexibility throughout the contract term.
Please see PSQ Document for more information.

title: Netherlands – Research and development consultancy services – DAS Innovatie- en adviesdiensten
description: De gemeente Den Haag staat voor steeds complexere maatschappelijke opgaven, die vragen om nieuwe oplossingen, innovatieve werkwijzen en aanvullende expertise. Om hier adequaat op in te kunnen spelen, investeren verschillende domeinen en diensten binnen de Gemeente in innovatie en in het versterken van het eigen innovatievermogen. Bij de ontwikkeling en uitvoering van innovatieprocessen bestaat regelmatig behoefte aan aanvullende, specialistische expertise en ondersteuning van externe partijen. Deze behoefte kan per vraagstuk, fase van het innovatieproces en organisatieonderdeel verschillen. Om deze expertise op een flexibele, efficiënte en transparante wijze te kunnen inzetten, kiest de Gemeente voor het inrichten van een Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem (DAS). Binnen dit DAS kunnen marktpartijen die voldoen aan de gestelde toelatings- en geschiktheidseisen worden toegelaten en meedingen naar Nadere opdrachten. Het Schuldenlab070 neemt het initiatief tot het inrichten van een Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem (DAS), gericht op de begeleiding en ondersteuning van innovatieprocessen binnen de gehele gemeentelijke organisatie (gemeente Den Haag). Binnen dit DAS kunnen de verschillende domeinen en diensten op afroep en naar behoefte gespecialiseerde innovatiepartijen inschakelen. Doel hiervan is om expertise flexibel in te zetten ter versterking van het eigen innovatievermogen, en om werkzaamheden efficiënter, effectiever en duurzamer uit te voeren. Het uitgangspunt voor de opdrachten die binnen dit DAS worden uitgevraagd, is het innovatieproces zoals gebruikt bij onder andere het Schuldenlab070 en van EC-DISC (expertise Centrum Digitale innovatie en Smart City). Binnen deze processen worden concepten, experimenten en pilots ingericht en gevalideerd volgens een vaste en gefaseerde aanpak. Onder het innovatieproces vallen diverse standaarddiensten ter begeleiding en ondersteuning van innovatie(processen), waaronder bijvoorbeeld: -Probleemanalyse, trendanalyse en Strategische verkenning; -Het faciliteren en begeleiden van processen, werksessies en co-creatietrajecten; -Het begeleiden van de ontwikkeling en uitwerking van innovatieve concepten; -Projectsturing en programmabegeleiding; -Monitoring en evaluatie, waaronder maatschappelijke kosten-batenanalyses (MKBA) en impact- en effectmetingen. Daarnaast worden er regelmatig evenementen georganiseerd en trainingen gegeven die los staan van het innovatieproces. Het DAS is onderverdeeld in verschillende fasen van het innovatieproces. Ten behoeve van de inrichting en uitvoering van het DAS worden deze categorieën in Mercell/TenderNed als percelen weergegeven. Gegadigden dienen bij hun verzoek tot toelating aan te geven voor welke fase(n) zij in aanmerking wensen te komen. Het is toegestaan om zich voor één, meerdere of alle fasen aan te melden, mits wordt voldaan aan de voor die fase geldende eisen. Hoewel de gemeente binnen dit DAS primair opdrachten op het gebied van procesbegeleiding van sociale en fysieke innovatie zal uitzetten, kunnen ook opdracht worden uitgevraagd op het snijvlak van sociale en digitale innovatie. Hierbij kan gedacht worden aan de inzet van Artificial intelligence (AI) en andere digitale technologieën ter ondersteuning van innovatie, dienstverlening en besluitvorming, gericht op het effectiever aanpakken van sociaal-maatschappelijke opgaven. Onder deze DAS vallen dan de procesbegeleiding, maar niet de daadwerkelijke productontwikkeling van de digitale tools of systemen. Vraagstukken waarvan het primaire doel bestaat uit onderzoek, klantreisonderzoek, servicedesign of UX-design vallen niet onder de reikwijdte van dit DAS. Deze vallen namelijk onder de gemeentebrede raamovereenkomst voor de inhuur van Onderzoeks-, Service Design- en User Experience Design (UX)-medewerkers.

title: France – Benefit services – Accompagnement à la modélisation avec MAELIA du territoire du &quot;Grand Reims&quot; et du territoire du &quot;Pays Terres de Lorraine&quot; sur une problématique méthanisation et conseil juridique sur la propriété de données et d'outils
description: Chaque lot fera l'objet d'une attribution séparée. Le détail des missions confiées au titulaire figure au cahier des charges. Les prestations sont réglées par des prix forfaitaires. ACCOMPAGNEMENT A LA MODÉLISATION AVEC MAELIA : L'objet est d'accompagner la CRAGE dans la modélisation de 2 territoires, la Communauté Urbaine du « Grand Reims » et le Pays « Terres de Lorraine », avec la plateforme de modélisation MAELIA. L'outil à utiliser est obligatoirement la plateforme MAELIA. Aucun autre outil ou modèle ne sera retenu. Le territoire sera compris comme les terres agricoles de la collectivité territoriale. La modélisation sera réalisée pour les systèmes agricoles actuels et des scénarios alternatifs de gestion des biomasses, dont les narratifs seront fournis au prestataire. L'effet du changement climatique à venir devra être pris en compte. L'accompagnement comprendra les simulations, les évaluations de la durabilité technique, socio-économique et environnementale à l'aide d'indicateurs pertinents pour le public ciblé et la fourniture des résultats sous un format exploitable facilement ; une formation est également prévue. - Le 1er objectif des simulations avec MAELIA est de fournir à l'Assemblée des acteurs des connaissances sur l'état des lieux de la situation actuelle en termes de production de biomasses agricoles sur son territoire, de transformation des biomasses par méthanisation, de la circularité entre production et retour au sol et des impacts techniques, socio-économiques et environnementaux de la gestion actuelle des biomasses. - Le 2ème objectif des simulations est de fournir à l'Assemblée des acteurs des connaissances sur les effets de scénarios alternatifs de gestion de la biomasse conçus par l'Assemblée elle-même (sous la forme de narratifs). Le nombre de scénarios n'est pas connu à l'avance, il est estimé à 3 à 6 par territoire et un maximum de 15 scénarios est fixé (15 étant le résultat de l'addition du nombre de scénarios su les 2 territoires). - Le dernier objectif des simulations est de fournir à l'Assemblée des acteurs des connaissances sur l'effet du changement climatique à venir sur la production de biomasses agricoles, la transformation des biomasses par méthanisation, la circularité entre production et retour au sol et les impacts techniques, socio-économiques et environnementaux de la gestion actuelle des biomasses et des scénarios alternatifs de gestion. CONSEIL JURIDIQUE : Apporter à la CRAGE et aux partenaires du consortium Cyclorganic un conseil juridique sur la propriété des outils et des jeux de données d'entrée et de sortie des outils, notamment accompagner la CRAGE pour rédiger des règles d'usage ultérieur des trois outils par différents types d'organismes (partenaires de l'action 5 : CRAGE, Chambres d'agriculture de la Marne et de la Meurthe-et-Moselle, ENSAIA, MAELAB, Terrasolis ; autres partenaires Cyclorganic ; prestataire opérant MAELIA dans l'action 5 ; autres organismes), dans la perspective de la réplication du dispositif de concertation territoriale sur la gestion durable des biomasses dans d'autres territoires une fois le démonstrateur Cyclorganic arrivé à son terme (5 ans de la convention). Le point de vue de l'ensemble des partenaires de l'action 5 sera à prendre en compte. Référence pourra être faite à ce conseil juridique dans le livrable de l'action 5. Ce livrable concerne les conditions de réussite d'un dispositif de concertation territoriale sur la gestion durable des biomasses (réplicabilité). La CRAGE souhaite d'une part s'entourer d'un conseil juridique spécialisé pour l'éclairer sur les enjeux liés à la propriété des données. Elle veut clarifier les conditions d'utilisation des jeux de données d'entrée et de sortie des outils produits pendant le projet sur les 2 territoires, pour poursuivre le dispositif mis en place au-delà du projet et/ou pour utiliser les données à d'autres fins sur ces 2 territoires

description: Die Kölner Verkehrs-Betriebe AG (im Folgenden KVB) planen die Erweiterung eines Elektrobusbe-triebshofes (KVB Porz) auf einem ca. 63.000 m2 großen ehemaligen Industriegrundstück an der Kai-serstraße 127 in Köln-Porz. Aufgrund der Erweiterung der Ladestellplätze ist eine erhöhte Anschlussleistung auf der 10-kV-Ebene erforderlich. Diese wird von der RheinNetz bereitgestellt. Eine vorhandene metallgekapselte Mittelspannungsschaltanlage (Fabrikat ABB ZS8.4) ist für die Erschließung des Erweiterungsgeländes mit weite-ren Schaltfeldern auszubauen. Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme von neuen Mittelspannungsschaltfeldern sowie der Austausch von Strom- und Spannungswandlern in den bestehenden Messfeldern. Zusätzlich ist am Netzanschlusspunkt eine Einspeiseüberwachung und Schutzfunktionen für den Betrieb von Erzeugungsanlagen zu installieren. Auf dem Erweiterungsgelände entstehen 3 Trafogebäudeeinheiten.
