title: Finland – Architectural, engineering and planning services – Akaan Toijalan asemanseudun hankekehittäjäkumppani
description: HANKINNAN TAUSTA JA TARKOITUS Akaan kaupunki (jäljempänä myös ”hankintayksikkö”) kilpailuttaa hankekehittäjäkumppanin Toijalan asemanseudun kokonaisvaltaista kehittämistä varten. Hankinta toteutetaan neuvottelumenettelynä siten kuin jäljempänä on tarkemmin kuvattu. Tarjouskilpailun perusteella valitaan yksi (1) hankekehittäjäkumppani, joka vastaa hankekokonaisuuden kehittämisestä ja yhteensovittamisesta kaupungin tavoitteiden mukaisesti. Hankekehittäjäkumppanin tehtävänä on muodostaa Toijalan asemanseudun maankäytöstä, liikennejärjestelyistä, kaupungin tilatarpeista, kaupallisista palveluista sekä mahdollisista asumisen ja palveluasumisen toiminnoista vaiheittain toteutettava, toiminnallisesti perusteltu ja taloudellisesti toteuttamiskelpoinen kokonaisuus. Tehtävään sisältyy myös Toijalan ratapihan alikulkuun liittyvän alikulkusillan yleissuunnittelu sekä sen yhteensovittaminen osaksi asemanseudun muuta suunnittelua ja kehittämistä. Hankintaan ei sisälly alikulkusillan eikä muiden hankekokonaisuuteen kuuluvien kohteiden rakentamista. Hankekehittäjäkumppanilla on kuitenkin oikeus hankkia hallintaansa kunnan toimintoihin kuulumattomille kolmansille osapuolille tarkoitettu tontti tai muu alue, mikäli hankekehittäjäkumppani on osana hankekehitystehtävää valmistellut kohteen toteuttamiskelpoiseksi ja hankkinut kohteelle kunnan hyväksymän kolmannen osapuolen toteuttajaksi, käyttäjäksi tai muuksi toimijaksi. Hankekehittäjäkumppani voi tällöin edistää kohteelle sijoittuvien tilojen, rakennusten ja toimintojen toteuttamista siten kuin lopullisessa tarjouspyynnössä ja hankekehittäjäkumppanin kanssa tehtävässä sopimuksessa tarkemmin määritellään. HANKINNAN KOHDE Hankinnan kohteena on Akaan Toijalan asemanseudun hankekehittäjäkumppanuus. Hankekehittäjäkumppani vastaa asemanseudun hankekokonaisuuden kehittämisestä, yhteensovittamisesta ja valmistelun koordinoinnista Akaan kaupungin tavoitteiden mukaisesti. Hankekokonaisuus muodostuu erityisesti asemaseudun maankäytön, kaupungin omien tilatarpeiden, kaupallisten palvelujen ja muiden kunnan toimintoihin kuulumattomien toimintojen, mahdollisen asumisen ja palveluasumisen, pysäköinti- ja liityntäliikennejärjestelyjen sekä Toijalan ratapihan alikulkuratkaisun yhteensovittamisesta. Kaupungin alustaviin tilatarpeisiin sisältyvät muun muassa hallinnon, kirjaston, lukion sekä kokous- ja palvelutilojen muodostama tilakokonaisuus. Asemanseudulle on tavoitteena toteuttaa kaupallisia palveluja ja muita kunnan ulkopuolisten toimijoiden tilatarpeita palvelevia toimintoja. Kaupungin ja Keskon välisen yhteistyösopimuksen mukaisesti asemaseudulle on tarkoitus sijoittaa Keskon päivittäistavarakaupan hankekokonaisuus, jonka alustava laajuus on noin 3 000–8 000 k-m². Hankekehittäjäkumppanin tehtävänä on yhteensovittaa Keskon hankekokonaisuus osaksi asemaseudun muuta kehittämistä, maankäyttöä, liikenne- ja pysäköintijärjestelyjä sekä kaupungin ja muiden alueelle mahdollisesti sijoittuvien toimijoiden tarpeita. Hankekehittäjäkumppanin tehtäväkokonaisuuteen sisältyvät hankekehityksen asiantuntija- ja koordinointitehtävät, asemaseudun kaavoitustyö, hankkeen muiden suunnittelu- ja selvitystehtävien yhteensovittaminen, Toijalan ratapihan alikulkusillan yleissuunnittelu sekä hankekokonaisuuden toteuttamiskelpoisuuden, vaiheistuksen, taloudellisten ja sopimuksellisten ratkaisujen valmistelu. Hankintaan ei sisälly asemaseudun rakennusten, yleisten alueiden, liikennejärjestelyjen eikä alikulkusillan rakentamista. Hankekehittäjäkumppanilla voi kuitenkin olla oikeus hankkia kaupungilta tontteja tai alueita hankekehitysvaiheessa itse hankkimiensa ja sitouttamiensa uusien kunnan toimintoihin kuulumattomien kolmansien osapuolten tarpeisiin. Tonttien tai alueiden luovutuksen, hankekehittäjäkumppanin mahdollisen toteutusvastuun sekä kohteiden toteuttamisen tarkemmat periaatteet ja ehdot määritellään lopullisessa tarjouspyynnössä ja hankekehittäjäkumppanin kanssa tehtävässä sopimuksessa. Hankinta toteutetaan neuvottelumenettelynä siten kuin jäljempänä on tarkemmin kuvattu. Hankinnan kohdetta koskevat vähimmäisvaatimukset, joista ei voida poiketa neuvottelumenettelyn aikana eikä lopullisessa tarjouspyynnössä, on kuvattu kohdassa ”Kokonaismäärä tai laajuus”. title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – Projektträgerschaft „Gesundheitsforschung“
description: Das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) beauftragt bei der Förderung von Vorhaben ausgewählte Auftragnehmer (AN) mit der Wahrnehmung von Projektträgeraufgaben (sog. Projektträger – PT), um mit ihrer Unterstützung die Anforderungen eines effizienten Einsatzes der Fördermittel durch sorgfältige fachliche und administrative Planung, Durchführung und Kontrolle zu erfüllen. Der AN unterstützt das BMFTR fachlich und administrativ in allen Phasen der Projektförderung (von der Beratung der Interessenten und Antragsteller über die Prüfung der Anträge einschließlich der Begutachtung durch Gutachtergremien, Betreuung während der Laufzeit bis hin zur Verwendungsnachweisprüfung), bei der strategischen Weiterentwicklung der Förderschwerpunkte und bei der Verbreitung der Ergebnisse im Rahmen von Fachkommunikation. Dies erfordert vom AN fachwissenschaftliche, administrative, betriebswirtschaftliche und forschungspolitische Kompetenz; er bildet eine wichtige Schnittstelle zwischen Antragstellern und Zuwendungsgeber auf nationaler, europäischer und globaler Ebene und erfüllt eine Servicefunktion für das BMFTR. Mit dem Rahmenprogramm „Gesundheitsforschung“ und seinen drei programmatischen Handlungsfeldern “Krankheiten vorbeugen und heilen“, „Medizinischen Fortschritt vorantreiben“ und den „Forschungsstandort stärken“, stärkt die Bundesregierung die Gesundheitsforschung, damit diese den großen gesundheitlichen Herausforderungen unserer Zeit erfolgreich begegnen und den Innovationsstandort Deutschland voranbringen kann. Die Leitlinien „Der Mensch im Mittelpunkt“ (u. a. mit den Aspekten „Translation/Transfer“ und „Partizipation“) und „Personalisierung und Digitalisierung als Schlüssel“ durchdringen alle Handlungsfelder des Rahmenprogramms. Das Programm gibt den strategischen Rahmen vor, innerhalb dessen die Bundesregierung die Gesundheitsforschung an Hochschulen, Universitätskliniken, außeruniversitären Forschungseinrichtungen und in der Wirtschaft fördert. Leitgedanke des aktuellen Rahmenprogramms ist es, den Menschen noch stärker in den Mittelpunkt der Gesundheitsforschung zu stellen; Patientinnen und Patienten sollen rascher von Innovationen und medizinischem Fortschritt profitieren. Indem Innovationen schneller bei Patientinnen und Patienten ankommen, soll der Gesundheitszustand und damit die Lebensqualität der Bevölkerung kontinuierlich verbessert werden. Für den AN bedeutet dies Zuarbeit zur Gestaltung der Fördermaßnahmen und Organisation und Durchführung von Workshops und Veranstaltungen. Nach der Veröffentlichung von entsprechenden Förderbekanntmachungen obliegen dem AN die Organisation des Auswahlverfahrens und die gesamte Projektadministration. Eine Übersicht über die laufenden Förderschwerpunkte und Vorhaben aus der Projektförderung des BMFTR im Bereich der Gesundheitsforschung findet sich unter www.gesundheitsforschung-bmftr.de.

title: Norway – Research services – Openness and inclusion - police interaction with the entire population
description: The aim of the research assignment is to obtain knowledge about how different groups of the population experience the police, what conditions affect the interaction between police and inhabitants, and how the police can ensure that different perspectives and experiences are heard and safeguarded. There is a need for knowledge about whether there are groups that find that they are not heard, how the police reach out to groups that to a small degree contact the police on their own initiative and how different forms of communication and dialogue are experienced by different groups. The research shall provide a better knowledge basis for how the police can strengthen the dialogue with the population, adapt communication and work forms to different target groups and develop services that safeguard legal security, equal treatment and high quality. The research shall also contribute with knowledge on the connection between transparency, inclusion, trust and the police's legitimacy, as well as the impact this can have on society's resilience. See further information in the tender documentation.

title: Germany – Transformers – DLR Standort Köln: Kompakt-Trafostation - Rahmenvertrag Trafostation (26-0272_S)
description: Geliefert werden vier betriebsfertige 630-kVA-Kompakt-Trafostationen, ausgelegt für eine Höchstleistung von 800 kVA. Die Stationen bestehen aus einem 6/10-kV-Drehstrom-Öl-Transformator in Hermetikausführung nach EN 50588, Öko-Design-Verordnung (EU) Stufe 2, Verlustklasse AkAAo. Auf der OS-Seite sind Elastimold-Steckdurchführungen, auf der NS-Seite umschrumpfte DIN-Durchführungen vorzusehen. Jede Station ist mit einer Fernwirktechnik auszustatten, die die Betriebszustände an die zentrale Leitwarte meldet und von dort Fernschaltbefehle annimmt. Ferner ist eine mechanische rückwärtige Verriegelung vorzusehen, die das Schalten des Lasttrennschalters im Ringkabelfeld verhindert, solange in der zugehörigen Gegenzelle der Erdungsschalter eingelegt ist. Es dürfen ausschließlich bauaufsichtlich zugelassene Materialien verbaut werden. Die Stationen sind einschließlich Zubehör und vollständiger technischer Dokumentation (u.a. Schaltpläne, Prüfberichte, Bedien- und Wartungshandbuch, Konformitätserklärungen) zu liefern. Vor der Auslieferung ist für jede Station eine Werkabnahme mit Funktionsprüfung der Schaltorgane, der Verriegelung und der Fernwirktechnik durchzuführen. Der Abruf erfolgt innerhalb von vier Jahren, geplant je eine Station pro Kalenderjahr. Der AG behält sich vor, die Abrufrhythmen an seinen Bedarf anzupassen, einschließlich mehrfacher Abrufe innerhalb eines Jahres.

title: Germany – Artificial and natural lighting engineering services for buildings – Dienstleistungen für Lichttechnik und Tageslichttechnik – Dynamisches Beschaffungssystem "Planungsleistungen Beleuchtungsumrüstung" hier: Vergebene Aufträge im 2. Quartal 2026
description: Die AG verwaltet bundesweit Liegenschaften diverser Bundesbehörden im Rahmen des einheitlichen Liegenschaftsmanagements. Im Zuge des gesetzlich festgeschriebenen Auslaufs der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen T5 und T8 zum 25.08.2023, bedarf es zur Aufrechterhaltung der Ausleuchtung eines vollständigen Austausches der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen durch eine LED-Beleuchtung. Diese Umstellung soll sukzessiv in einzelnen Sprints im Rahmen eines dynamischen Beschaffungssystems (DBS) erfolgen. Die Planungsleistungen werden in einer agilen Vorgehensweise in unterschiedlichen Umfängen der zu sanierenden Liegenschaften benötigt. Die AG wird die Planungsleistungen für die jeweiligen Liegenschaften in einzelnen Sprints, im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens, vergeben. Dadurch soll es auch KMU ermöglicht werden die Leistungen zu erbringen. Die Leistungserbringung umfasst Planungsleistungen, die zur Planung, Beratung, Ausschreibung, Bauleitung sowie für die spätere Umsetzung in Anlehnung an die LPH 1 bis 8 des § 55 HOAI erforderlich sind. Der Leistungsschwerpunkt liegt auf Planungsleistungen in den KG 440 (445), der Auftrag umfasst dabei alle weiteren Planungsleistungen, die zur Erreichung des Auftragsziels erforderlich sind. Im Wesentlichen sind folgende Leistungen angelehnt an § 55 HOAI für die Beleuchtungsumrüstung zu erbringen: - Bestandsaufnahme aller Leuchten einer Liegenschaft durch tabellarische Dokumentation folgender Merkmale: Leuchte, Leuchtmittel, Nutzungsart des Raumes, Deckenhöhe, Reflexionsgrad der Wände, Schaltung der Beleuchtung, Anzahl der Leuchten pro Stromkreis, Anzahl der Adern zu Leuchten/Schalter - Erstellen von Grundrisszeichnungen, falls diese nicht vorliegen - Fachplanungsleistungen KG 440 und 445 - Ausführungsplanung - Beleuchtungsberechnung mit Berechnungssoftware Dialux oder Relux - Planung der Beleuchtungsanlagen nach der AMEV-Empfehlung „Beleuchtung 2019“, der DIN EN 12464 sowie der ASR 3.4 in der jeweils gültigen Fassung - Erstellung von Wartungsplänen nach DIN EN 12464-1 - Erstellung von Termin- und Ablaufplänen für die Umsetzung der Baumaßnahmen - Vorbereitung und Mitwirkung bei der Vergabe - Objekt- und Bauüberwachung Im Zusammenhang damit sind z.B. auch folgende Planungsleistungen von Randbereichen / Nebenleistungen insbesondere in folgenden Bereichen – soweit im Einzelfall erforderlich – zu erbringen: Einfache Schlitz- und Durchbruchsarbeiten, Verputzarbeiten, Trockenbauarbeiten, Malerarbeiten, Gerüstbau/Gerüststellung. Die Leistungen sind grds. im Dokument „Leistungsverzeichnis“ dargestellt, im weiteren Stadium behält sich die AG vor, den Leistungsumfang zu spezifizieren. Die AG weist darauf hin, dass die gesamten Vergabeunterlagen – insb. der Prozessablaufplan - der Fortschreibung unterliegen und im Laufe des DBS jederzeit angepasst werden können. Hierüber werden alle Bewerber/Bieter umgehend informiert. Die AG sucht Unternehmen, die diese Planungsleistungen erbringen. Dabei wird die Planung in einzelne Planungsphasen strukturiert (siehe Leistungsverzeichnis, dort a.E. Übersicht differenzierter Planungsleistungen). Einige Leistungen müssen stets erbracht werden, die Erbringung bzw. der jeweilige Umfang der Bedarfs- und Alternativpositionen wird durch die AG auf Grundlage von Entscheidungsvorlagen getroffen. Abhängig von den getroffenen Entscheidungen ist für bestimmte Flächen alternativ der Leuchtmitteltausch oder ein Leuchtentausch zu planen. Für den Fall des Leuchtentausches ist eine weitere Entscheidung hinsichtlich der Planung einer Beleuchtungssteuerung der AG vorgesehen. Sollte eine Beleuchtungssteuerung gefordert sein, sind auch die entsprechenden Bedarfspositionen zu erbringen. Die AG wird ihren Leistungsbedarf im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens mit jeweils einer Aufforderung zur Angebotsabgabe an die zu diesem Zeitpunkt in dieser Region geeigneten Unternehmen (Bewerberpool) kommunizieren. Dabei sind die Sprints nach den Komplexitätsgraden „Basisprojekte“ und „Komplexe Projekte“ aufgeteilt.

title: Crisis and Resilience Fund - Financial Resilience and Community Coordination Service
description:
The Council has received funding from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) to support households experiencing financial crisis and to invest in longer-term preventative activities that strengthen financial resilience and reduce future reliance on crisis support. In Leicestershire, the wider Crisis and Resilience Fund (CRF) includes Crisis Payments administered by Leicestershire County Council and Housing Payments administered by the District and Borough Councils. This procurement relates specifically to the Financial Resilience Service and Community Coordination function that support residents to move beyond immediate crisis and improve long-term financial stability.
The service is focused on improving financial resilience, increasing access to advice and support, reducing debt and repeat crisis demand, and enhancing collaboration across organisations to provide a more joined-up and person-centred system of support.
This service will be divided into 8 lots. Lots 1 - 7 is split into the different locality (boroughs and districts) of Leicestershire:
- Lot 1: Blaby - Blaby District has a population of 103,271 residents and is located in the south-west of Leicestershire. The area combines suburban communities close to Leicester, including Braunstone Town and Glen Parva, with larger villages and rural settlements. The service will need to respond to both urban and rural needs, ensuring that residents can access support through a range of local community settings and delivery channels
- Lot 2: Charnwood - Charnwood is the largest lot by population, with 182,906 residents. The borough includes the large urban centre of Loughborough alongside a wide range of towns, villages and rural communities. Charnwood contains some of the most deprived neighbourhoods in Leicestershire, alongside areas of relative affluence, creating varied levels of financial need and demand across the area. The service will need to provide accessible support across both urban and rural settings.
- Lot 3: Harborough - Harborough District has a population of 98,254 residents and is predominantly rural in nature. The district includes the market town of Market Harborough together with a large number of villages and dispersed rural communities.
- Lot 4: Hinckley and Bosworth - Hinckley & Bosworth has a population of 113,653 residents and contains a mixture of urban and rural communities. The borough includes the town of Hinckley, together with a number of market towns, villages and rural areas.
- Lot 5: Melton - Melton Borough has a population of 51,756 residents, making it the smallest geographical lot by population. Centred on the market town of Melton Mowbray, the borough is predominantly rural, with many smaller villages and dispersed communities.
- Lot 6: North West Leicestershire - North West Leicestershire has a population of 105,004 residents and includes the urban centres of Coalville and Ashby-de-la-Zouch alongside rural villages and communities. The district contains some of the most deprived neighbourhoods in the county.
- Lot 7: Oadby and Wigston - Oadby & Wigston Borough has a population of 57,788 residents and is the most urbanised district within Leicestershire. Located adjacent to Leicester City, it comprises the towns of Oadby, Wigston and South Wigston and has a diverse population
Lot 8 is Community Coordination. This lot requires the delivery of a countywide Community Coordination function across Leicestershire, supporting a population of approximately 712,000 residents. The service will work strategically across all seven district and borough areas to strengthen collaboration between Financial Resilience Service providers, local authorities, VCSE organisations and wider stakeholders, improving referral pathways, supporting partnership development, increasing the visibility of support services, identifying gaps and opportunities within the system, and promoting a coordinated, accessible and effective countywide financial resilience support network.
This contract is for 2 years and 5 months and shall take effect from 02 November 2026 - 31 March 2029. The total allocated budget for this contract is £3,411,573. Full breakdown of each lot's value is given within the Doc 01 - Invitation to Tender (ITT).
Standstill has been observed for all 8 lots, which commences on 08/10/2026 and will end on 20/10/2026

description:

These services will be provided by high-quality Providers who can demonstrate their experience of delivering supported living services. These 7 Lots will be awarded as separate Contracts. 
Providers will be required to work with the Council to implement sustainable and flexible models of support that enable Individuals to become active members of their local communities. Delivering a ‘locality’ model will continue to enable Providers to flexibly respond to the needs of the individuals they support as and where they arise, utilise resources efficiently, and support collaborative working with the broader community. The service must be available 24 hours a day, 365 days per year in line with the assessed needs of Individuals.
The procurement process will be conducted in a single stage.
Prospective providers will be able to bid for as many of the lots as they wish, however the Council will be looking to secure a mixed market where each provider will be limited to being awarded a maximum of two Lot areas. Each Lot’s requirements will be different and so suits a range of Providers.
Benchmark data indicates that the service in current schemes totals 8979 hours of support per week delivered to 89 Individuals living in 34 housing units. Please note this is for information purposes only and further Local Area Service details will be provided to the successful providers following the conclusion and award of the Lot contracts. 
The contract agreement duration will be for an initial 4 years with additional, discretional contract extension periods for an addition up to a further 4 years. It will remain the council’s decision as to if and how any contract extension is implemented.

title: Tender for Community Family Help Service for Children and Families in Herefordshire
description:
Herefordshire Council is seeking to appoint a single provider to deliver a countywide Community Family Help Service for children, young people and families with multiple and/or complex needs who require Family Help support. The Service will provide targeted, relationship-based, whole-family interventions that promote resilience, improve outcomes for children and help prevent escalation into statutory services.
The successful Provider will act as a key delivery partner within Herefordshire's Family Help model, providing Family Help Lead Practitioners, coordinating multi-agency support, undertaking Family Help assessments and plans, and working closely with statutory, community and voluntary sector organisations. The Service will support a minimum of 150 Family Help referrals and 30 Reducing Parental Conflict cases per annum and will include the delivery of partnership training to strengthen local practice.
The contract is expected to commence on 1 February 2027, with an initial mobilisation and implementation period prior to service commencement on 1 April 2027. The initial contract term will be three years, with an option to extend for up to a further two years. The procurement is being conducted under the Procurement Act 2023 using the Open Procedure and is subject to the Light Touch Regime.
The maximum available Contract Value for the core Community Family Help Service is £1,550,000 (excluding VAT) over the full potential 5-year term. Subject to demand, additional funding and internal governance, the Council may also purchase additional referrals and/or training up to a maximum value of further £1,650,000 (excluding VAT). These additional purchases are not guaranteed. The maximum potential Contract Value is therefore up to £3,200,000 (excluding VAT). Note the service is being partially funded by Department for Education Grants.
TUPE information:
TUPE is expected to apply to this contract, and bidders should ensure that the implications of TUPE, including the associated employment and cost implications, are fully considered and reflected in their tender.
Bidders must request access to the TUPE information well in advance of the tender closing date. To access the Employee's information, bidders are required to complete and sign the Completion Document 5 (TUPE Confidentiality Letter Agreement) included within the tender pack, and return it via ProContact messaging system at www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk. The TUPE information will be provided following receipt of the completed agreement. 
Bidders are responsible for ensuring that they request the TUPE information sufficiently early to enable them to take it into account when preparing their Tender. Failure to request or review the TUPE information will not relieve the successful Bidder of its obligations in relation to TUPE.

title: School Presenter Services Tender
description:
Historic Royal Palaces (HRP) is a registered charity, responsible for the care, conservation and presentation of HM Tower of London (TOL), Hampton Court Palace (HCP), Kensington Palace State Apartments, (KP) the Banqueting House at Whitehall (BH), Kew Palace (KEW) and Hillsborough Castle and Gardens, (HCG) the official residence of HM The King in Northern Ireland and residence of the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland.  
We love and look after six of the most wonderful palaces in the world. The palaces are the setting for the stories that shape us all, and we’re bringing them to people in ways that mean more to them. We want everyone to find themselves in the spaces and stories we share.
HRP is a charity for everyone. We are committed to preserving and sharing the stories of our six magnificent palaces and making them accessible to all. Through partnerships, innovation, and storytelling, we strive to break down barriers, inspire curiosity and stir the spirit in people of all ages and backgrounds. Our curriculum-linked schools programmes bring palace stories to life through costumed, presenter-led sessions, alongside digital learning, teacher training events and activities for local community groups and families.
HRP is an independent charity, receiving no government funding and derives its income principally from admissions, retail, licensing, commercial events, sponsorship and support from donors and members.  
We will be running a tender process with the intention of awarding a contract for the provision of School Presenter Services and are seeking expressions of interest from suitably experienced / qualified organisations.
We are seeking a skilled and collaborative partner to deliver one of the UK's largest and most established heritage learning programmes. Each year, Historic Royal Palaces welcomes over 200,000 school visitors across our sites, with approximately half participating in a curriculum-linked learning session delivered by our presenter team. The contract includes the delivery of around 3,000 educational sessions annually across the Tower of London, Hampton Court Palace and Kensington Palace, together with Home Educator Days, occasional community activity and opportunities to contribute to new programme and content development.
This is an opportunity to join a highly regarded and well-established programme that combines rigorous historical scholarship with immersive, participatory and site-based learning. Working in partnership with HRP, the successful supplier will recruit, train and manage a team of presenters capable of delivering engaging learning experiences for diverse audiences, including primary and secondary schools, specialist settings, SEND learners and home-educating families. 
We are looking for an organisation that shares our commitment to educational excellence, inclusion, safeguarding and collaboration, and that can maintain consistently high standards whilst operating across multiple sites and busy heritage environments. The successful supplier will play an important role in helping young people connect with the stories, people and places that have shaped our past.
HRP’s requirements: 
The successful supplier will be expected to:
•Deliver approximately 3,000 curriculum-linked school sessions per year across our London sites 
•Recruit, train, schedule, line manage and support a team of presenters, ensuring sufficient staffing capacity and contingency arrangements to ensure reliable delivery of the programme.
•Deliver learning sessions for a diverse range of audiences, including primary and secondary schools, specialist and SEND settings, international groups and home-educating families.
•Deliver all activity in accordance with HRP's educational approach, Core Principles and commitment to high-quality, site-based learning.
•Maintain consistently high standards of delivery, quality assurance and presenter performance 
•Demonstrate a strong commitment to inclusion, accessibility and representative historical interpretation, adapting delivery to meet a wide range of learning and access needs.
•Provide day-to-day management, coordination and operational oversight of the programme, working collaboratively with HRP teams across all sites.
•Maintain appropriate safeguarding policies, training and workforce checks, and comply with HRP safeguarding requirements and procedures.
•Deliver activities safely within busy public-facing heritage environments and ensure compliance with relevant health and safety, conservation and security requirements.
•Contribute to the development of new content, learning resources, events and bespoke projects where commissioned by HRP.
•Support the delivery of Home Educator Days, community activity and other learning programmes as required.
Exclusion criteria: 
Suppliers who are unable to demonstrate the following will not be considered eligible for award of this contract
•Suppliers must have appropriate safeguarding policies, procedures and reporting arrangements for working with children, young people and vulnerable adults, including arrangements for safer recruitment, workforce training and the management of safeguarding concerns.
•Suppliers must have relevant experience and organisational capacity to deliver learning, engagement or interpretation programmes for children and young people within museum, heritage, arts or cultural settings at a scale and complexity broadly comparable to this contract.
Tender documents: 
The tender process will be run through HRP’s e tendering system, Delta e-Sourcing. Tender documents will be made available on Delta to those suppliers who expressed an interest. 
Suppliers will need to register on Delta in order to participate in the tender process. Suppliers can register here https://www.delta-esourcing.com/register/

Contract period: 3 + 2 years 
HRP reserves the right not to award a contract. 
In addition, HRP reserves the right to negotiate with short-listed tenderers or the preferred supplier.

title: Media Consumption Pathways and Trust
description:
DCMS is seeking to commission a two-phase research project to investigate UK media consumption habits and public trust in media. Phase 1 would consist of a behavioural cohort study (or another appropriate methodology) to map the specific "user pathways" audiences take to find, consume, and value information across different media sources, such as traditional news broadcasts and social media, across different demographics. Building on these findings, Phase 2 would explore how individuals perceive trust in different media sources due to their own perception of mis/disinformation, assess the broader effects of these consumption pathways on factors such as viewer retention and wider social cohesion, as well as overall integrity of the UK's information ecosystem.
This project will be commissioned either through a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, or through the RM6126 Research and Insights framework.
This is part of the DCMS Science and Analysis R&D Programme, which supports R&D capability within the department. This project will run concurrently alongside three other large projects across 2027-2030; these include 'what works' research into AI adoption in DCMS sectors; a continuation of previous research to develop data-intensive approaches for capturing engagement at unticketed cultural, heritage, and sporting events/activities/locations, e.g. using mobile app data to model how people participate in our events; and a continuation of previous research to design and improve methods for holistically tracking the long-term impact of major events, tested on a major event.
buyer: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

title: Clwyd Pension Fund Independent Person / Unigolyn Annibynnol Cronfa Bensiynau Clwyd
description:
Clwyd Pension Fund (the “Fund”) is seeking to appoint an Independent Person to provide scrutiny, constructive challenge to advice given, and to support the Pension Fund Committee and Head of Fund (LGPS Senior Officer). The role forms part of the strengthened governance framework for LGPS administering authorities as a result of MHCLG's implementation of the LGPS Good Governance reforms. 
Flintshire County Council, as Administering Authority for the Clwyd Pension Fund, provides pension benefits on behalf of over 50 participating employers and over 50 thousand scheme members. The Fund is proud to be widely acknowledged in the LGPS community as a leading example for best practice governance and management.  The Independent Person will become a key person in the Fund’s commitment to delivering high-quality pension services,  robust governance and management arrangements that support members, employers and other stakeholders.
The Independent Person will bring an external perspective and enhance the Fund's governance framework, supporting the Pension Fund Committee, the Pension Board, LGPS Senior Officer and other Fund officers in maintaining the highest standards of governance, transparency and accountability. 
The role will be critical in strengthening governance practices, providing objective and expert insight, constructive challenge where appropriate, identifying opportunities for improvement and supporting compliance with LGPS legislation, statutory guidance and regulatory expectations across all areas of Fund activity. The successful candidate will be independent of Clwyd Pension Fund and Flintshire County Council, with no conflicts of interest that could compromise their impartiality.  To ensure independence, both actual and perceived, in accordance with the Statutory Guidance, they cannot work for any advisor, fund manager or service provider that does business with the Fund (or has provided any such services within the last two valuation cycles).  They will work collaboratively with elected members, pension board representatives and officers while maintaining an independent viewpoint.

title: OO Services - ArcGIS ESRI ELA TRANS (SAAS)- Multi Site 1029
description:
The ESRI Enterprise Licence Agreement provides the ArcGIS geographic information system (GIS) platform used across SSE Networks to capture, manage, analyse and visualise geospatial and asset location data. The service supports critical operational, engineering, planning and asset management activities, enabling users to manage network infrastructure, undertake spatial analysis, maintain asset location records and support regulatory and operational reporting requirements across Transmission and other SSE Networks functions.
The ArcGIS platform is materially embedded within SSE's operational and technology landscape and forms a core component of business processes relating to infrastructure planning, network design, asset management and geospatial data governance. ArcGIS is integrated with other enterprise systems, including Maximo, where it provides the authoritative source of location and mapping data for network assets. Significant volumes of business data, mapping configurations, applications, workflows, user content and integrations have been developed and maintained within the ESRI environment over a number of years.
A review of alternative GIS platforms confirmed that while other suppliers provide mapping or geospatial capabilities, any replacement would require substantial migration of existing datasets, redevelopment of integrations, reconfiguration of business processes, extensive user retraining and the validation of critical asset and network data. Such an exercise would introduce significant cost, operational disruption and implementation risk. Furthermore, the proprietary nature of the ArcGIS platform, together with its deep integration into existing operational systems and workflows, means that a like-for-like replacement cannot be implemented without significant technical redevelopment and business change activity.
This procurement therefore relates to the continued provision of the ESRI ArcGIS platform and associated enterprise licensing required to maintain business continuity, support operational activities and preserve the integrity of existing geospatial data, integrations and associated business processes.

title: Provision of Single Homelessness Prevention Service (Rochdale)
description:
The Single Homelessness Prevention Service (Rochdale) Contract will commence on 1st January 2027 and end on 31st March 2029.
The Service will be delivered by an organisation with a proven track record of successful engagement with people experiencing multiple disadvantage or marginalised groups in the Borough of Rochdale and will operate across the Rochdale, Heywood and Pennine Townships on a neighbourhood hub and outreach-based model. 
Local data highlights both the scale of the demand and the complexity of need, with a significant proportion of individuals experiencing challenges related to financial resilience, substance use, offending histories, and previous rough sleeping. These overlapping needs increase the likelihood of housing instability and repeat homelessness, placing ongoing pressure on statutory and support services.
This evidence reinforces the requirement for a commissioned response that moves beyond a crisis and accommodation-focused response, towards one that delivers integrated interventions. The Prevention Service must be designed to respond holistically, addressing not only immediate housing risk but also the underlying factors that impact an individual's ability to sustain accommodation and achieve longer-term stability.
The primary purpose of this service is to prevent first-time homelessness, repeat homelessness and rough sleeping through early identification, proactive engagement and tenancy sustainment. The service will be responsive, but prevention focused and should aim to intervene at the earliest possible stage before an individual becomes threatened with homelessness. The Provider will develop sustainable plans to prevent homelessness or rough sleeping by providing structured engagement plans, immediate crisis intervention, specialist prevention support and outreach engagement to individuals who are harder to reach to prevent escalation into statutory homelessness.

title: Learning Management System
description:
BACKGROUND 
Wrexham County Borough Council (WCBC) are looking to engage the market with the potential of procuring a Learning Management System (LMS) to support e-learning training modules, webinars, manager reporting, and course booking requirements for both council employees and external organisations requiring our training services. 
SCOPE 
The expectation for any potential supplier would be to provide: 
•	A cloud-based Learning Management System 
•	System implementation and configuration 
•	Integration with our HR system Zellis 
•	User training 
•	Ongoing support and maintenance 
REQUIREMENTS 
The following list is not exhaustive and should be used as a guide to the technical requirements WCBC would be looking for in a successful Learning Management System solution: 
•	Dashboard Management - Ability to create, edit, assign to audiences and utilise multiple dashboards for end users. 
•	My Team - Manager - Allow managers to view information relating to team members assigned to their structure. 
•	Graphical Reports - Produce visual reports and graphs for dashboards and management information. 
•	KPI Dashlets - Create KPI-based dashboard widgets from predefined metrics. [CR1.1][EA1.2]
•	Programme Progress Block - Customisable graphical display of learner programme progress. [CR2.1][EA2.2]
•	Zellis Integration - Compatibility with the Council's Zellis HR system to maintain accurate employee information. 
•	Position Hierarchies - Support one or multiple organisational and position structures. [CR3.1][EA3.2]
•	Seminars and Events - Create, manage and report on classroom-based and blended learning events. 
•	One Click Compliance - Provide a simple visual view of mandatory training compliance requirements. 
•	Programmes - Group courses and competencies into structured learning programmes. 
•	Certifications - Manage certification validity periods and automated recertification reminders. [CR4.1][EA4.2]
•	Record of Prior Learning - Allow users to access, edit and add prior learning records. 
•	On the Job Assessments - Enable managers to assess and report on workplace observations and assessments. 
SUBMISSION AND TIMESCALES 
Please email an overview of your solution to Clare Roberts, Category Manager, at Clare.roberts@wrexham.gov.uk by midday in 22nd October 2026. Please ensure you submit information that is relevant to the requirements outlined above.

title: SE1286 Transgender Inclusion in Domestic Sports Guidance Review
description:
The Sports Councils commissioned and published the Transgender Inclusion in Domestic Sport Guidance in September 2021. The Guidance is supported by several background documents, including the Transgender International Research Literature Review 2021. In April 2025, the Supreme Court Ruling (For Women Scotland Ltd V The Scottish Ministers) ruled that, under the 2010 Equality Act, the protected characteristic of ‘sex’ means a person’s biological sex. The updated Equalities and Human Rights Commission Statutory Code of Practice for services, public functions and associations became legally binding on 5 August 2026 and provides guidance as to how the Equality Act 2010 should be applied.  
Following advice from legal counsel, and a literature review on the topic, the Sports Councils CEOs agreed that a full review is required.

title: Collections Store Refurbishments - Logistics Hub - Principal Contractor
description:
The Collection Store Refurbishment (CSR) Project forms part of both the wider NHM Unlocked Programme and NHM 150th Anniversary Campaign Programme, which supports: 
-The internal moves of 11 million specimens 
-The moves of 28 million specimens to our new facility at Thames Valley Science Park
-The 150th Anniversary Campaign to open previously closed galleries to the public
-The sale of our South London Collections facility
The NHM Unlocked Programme represents the largest ever move of natural history specimens worldwide. The wider CSR project has been tasked with refurbishing collections stores and rehousing five collections across five locations across the South Kensington Estate in suitable collections conditions.
The business case for the NHM Unlocked Programme is predicated on limited space and historic, ageing buildings; meaning that globally important specimens are being kept in conditions that hamper access and sometimes fail to meet minimum environmental standards. Moreover, the insights locked up in the collection remain largely untapped. From tackling climate change and meeting the mineral needs of a net zero world, to restoring biodiversity and achieving food security, the collection offers insights into the planetary emergency and how we might realise a brighter future where both people and planet thrive. The CSR Project supports this endeavour. 
Initially we will be tendering for works on the Osteology Store, this will convert a collections store in the basement of the Grade I Listed Waterhouse Building into a temporary “Logistics Hub” and future end state store for heavy and large specimens coming from our South London Store. 
As a separate tender there will be a further opportunity to express an interest in tendering for the Main Works package which covers refurbishment works to the other four areas around the South Kensington Estate, including subsequent areas of the Waterhouse Basement (two locations), Darwin Centre Phase 1 and in the Palaeontology Building. 
This tender relates to the initial works package located in the Osteology Store. The works comprise:
-refurbishment and alteration of Rooms B.03, B.07, B.07B-H, B.07J and BC05, 
-demolition of non-original partitions and raised floors, offices and removal of associated finishes and furnishings (excluding items retained on the eastern wall). 
-Internal works include the construction of a new security lobby with dry-lined partitions and a powered door, 
-repairs to damaged fabric and flooring, and measures to prevent pest ingress.
-Window and door works including repairs and redecoration to historic partitions and doors, installation of secondary glazing to three north-facing windows, adaptations for building services, and a new powered external door,
-Building services works include the removal and rebalancing of existing ventilation systems, strip-out of redundant electrical and data services, and the Stage 4 design and installation of new HVAC, electrical, fire alarm, security, BMS and controls systems. 
-All works will be undertaken in accordance with the fire strategy, maintaining the integrity of existing 120-minute compartment walls, and will include temporary protection of historic features, cleaning and making good on completion.
This phase of the project will initially prioritise the early conversion of the existing basement Osteology Store to a 'Logistics Hub', supporting the sequencing of moves and works in other areas and to reduce programme risk. It is critical that the Logistics Hub is made available early to enable the decant of the Old General Herbarium, the former Origins Gallery, the moves to Thames Valley Science Park (TVSP) and the sale of the South London Collections Facility. 
Following completion of the decant activities, the Logistics Hub will transition to its permanent configuration and use as a collections store accommodating the Heavy and Large Objects of the Mineralogy and Palaeontology Material Collection. Wherever possible, a 'light-touch' approach has been adopted to support the programme, minimise cost and impact to the significant historic fabric.

title: Barriers to Accessible Transport Training
description:
The Department for Transport (DfT) is a ministerial department within the UK Government. It works with its agencies and partners to support the transport network that enables people and goods to travel around the country. It plans and invests in transport infrastructure to keep the UK on the move.   
DfT has always been keen to increase staff members’ understanding of disability equality and has procured previous iterations of this training in the past. This latest round of training will coincide with a wider initiative, across the whole Department, to encourage all staff to learn more about how the transport network impacts on all those who use it by visiting areas of the network and interacting with stakeholders. Having a greater understanding of how users experience transport will help the Department to make better decisions that benefit more people.  
DfT requires a supplier to deliver Barriers to Accessible Transport training to staff across the Department, including its agencies and arm’s-length bodies. The requirement supports DfT’s wider commitment to increasing staff understanding of disability equality and how disabled people experience the transport network. It also responds to the significant gap between accessibility rights and obligations, and the day-to-day experiences of disabled passengers highlighted by the Transport Select Committee’s March 2025 report, Access Denied: rights versus reality in disabled people’s access to transport. 
The training will combine a guided tour of the transport network, supported by disabled guides with lived experience, with classroom-based disability equality learning. It is intended to help staff identify barriers, understand the Social Model of Disability, build accessibility and inclusive design into their work, and make better decisions that improve the experience of disabled transport users. DfT initially requires 12 full-day sessions for up to 20 participants per session over a 12-month period. Delivery will begin from DfT’s London office, with the ability to provide similar training from offices in Birmingham, Leeds, York and potentially other UK locations.

description: Stage 1 – Review of Existing Evidence • Review existing waste planning evidence, national guidance and relevant legislation. • Review current Cornwall waste policies and any relevant neighbouring Waste Planning Authority evidence. • Agree methodology, assumptions, datasets and forecasting approach with Cornwall Council. Stage 2 – Assessment of Existing Waste Management Capacity Prepare an assessment of existing waste management capacity across Cornwall including: • Current operational waste management facilities. • Existing Waste Planning Permissions. • Environmental Permits/Waste Management Licences. • Annual throughput using the Environment Agency Waste Data Interrogator. • Survey and verification of operational waste sites. • Existing treatment capacity by waste stream and facility type. • Analysis of operational constraints where relevant. Stage 3 – Assessment of Future Waste Arisings Prepare forecasts of future waste arisings throughout the Local Plan period including: • Local Authority Collected Waste. • Commercial and Industrial Waste. • Construction, Demolition and Excavation Waste. • Hazardous Waste (where appropriate). • Other relevant waste streams such as wastewater, agricultural waste, low level radioactive waste, clinical waste Forecasts should consider: • Population growth. • Housing and employment growth. • Economic forecasts. • Historic waste trends. • Recycling and composting targets. • National policy objectives. • Waste reduction initiatives and changes in waste composition. Stage 4 – Assessment of Additional Waste Management Capacity Requirements Using the findings of the previous assessments, identify: • Existing capacity available throughout the plan period. • Forecast demand for each waste stream. • Capacity surpluses and deficits. • The quantity and type of additional waste management capacity required. • The broad timing of additional provision. • Any implications for future waste site allocations or safeguarding policies. The assessment should clearly identify where sufficient capacity exists and where additional facilities may be required to meet future needs. A Cross Boundary Waste Movements paper A separate technical paper should assess: • Current waste imports and exports between Cornwall and neighbouring Waste Planning Authorities. • Waste arisings within neighbouring authority areas where relevant. • Nationally significant waste management requirements. • Existing and future cross-boundary waste movements. • Whether existing or planned facilities are capable of continuing to accommodate these movements.

The procurement is expected to establish an end-to-end managed service, with the appointed provider responsible for the delivery of services including, but not limited to:
•	Clinical and diagnostic services, including the provision of appropriately qualified workforce and equipped mobile units.
•	IT systems and data management services.
•	Programme management services, including logistics, stakeholder communications, and continuous service development.
Whilst the final service model remains subject to further development, the anticipated pathway is expected to include:
1.	Identification of the eligible population cohort.
2.	Appointment booking and scheduling.
3.	Lung Health Check assessment.
4.	Face-to-face clinical review and Low-Dose CT (LDCT) scanning.
5.	Reporting and clinical assessment of results.
6.	Multidisciplinary screening review meetings.
7.	Communication of results, including rebooking where applicable; and
8.	Follow-up, surveillance and recall activities.
BFT is currently evaluating potential procurement routes under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR), including:
•	A Competitive Process conducted through the open market; or

title: Gamma Irradiation of NHSBT Tissue Allografts and Consumables
description:
Gamma Irradiation of NHSBT Tissue Allografts and Consumables
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is looking to appoint a suitable supplier to provide gamma irradiation services for tissue allografts and consumables used by NHSBT Tissue and Eye Services (TES).
NHSBT wishes to engage with suppliers before commencing a formal procurement process. The purpose of this engagement is to improve NHSBT’s understanding of current market capability, capacity, service delivery options and supplier interest in this requirement.
The successful Supplier will be required to provide gamma irradiation of tissue products to an absorbed dose specification of 25kGy minimum and 40kGy maximum, and consumables to an absorbed dose specification of 25kGy minimum and 45kGy maximum.
The Supplier must be able to process a range of tissue products and consumables, provide suitable frozen storage at approximately -20°C where required, maintain appropriate temperature records and return irradiated products within a maximum turnaround time of 72 hours. 
The Supplier must provide an irradiation certificate before products are released back to NHSBT. The certificate must include the minimum and maximum absorbed dose, routine dose, irradiation batch number and the relevant NHSBT product batch number.
The Supplier will also be required to support dose mapping and performance qualification activities, undertake compatibility trials for new materials where required, operate an appropriate quality management system and maintain suitable validation, calibration, recall and business continuity arrangements.
NHSBT intends to hold preliminary market engagement meetings. Meetings are expected to be held remotely, with final dates and times to be confirmed.
To enable NHSBT to finalise the arrangements, interested organisations should send an expression of interest by email to Sahithi Bandi sahithi.bandi@nhsbt.nhs.uk no later than November 13th 2026.The response should include the organization’s name, proposed attendees and a brief overview, or website link, describing the relevant services available.
Participation in this market engagement does not guarantee any future business. NHSBT is not committed to undertaking a procurement exercise or awarding a contract as a result of this notice. NHSBT will not reimburse suppliers for any costs incurred in participating in this engagement.

Located on Shipbourne Road, close to Tonbridge town centre, Tonbridge Cemetery was established in 1858 and has served the local community for more than 160 years. The cemetery includes historic chapel buildings dating from the 1860s, mature, landscaped grounds, and a memorial garden that provides a peaceful setting for the interment and remembrance of cremated remains.
Covering approximately 14 hectares (34.6 acres), Tonbridge Cemetery is one of the borough's largest and most historic public open spaces. With around 14,000 grave spaces, the cemetery reflects generations of local history and continues to provide an important place of remembrance for residents and visitors alike.

A key requirement of any future system will be the ability to securely migrate all existing records, ensuring the continued preservation and accessibility of both historic and current cemetery data.

title: CSP26751 - Delegates for International Energy Agency Technology Collaboration Programme
description:
Introduction and Summary of Requirements
DESNZ is looking for experts in their field with a strong network of contacts across their industry to act as an Alternate Delegate for the following International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs):
Lot 1	Energy Storage (ES)
Lot 2	Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT)
Lot 3	Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS)
Lot 4	Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS)
Summary
UK Shared Business Services Ltd (UK SBS), acting on behalf of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), invites proposals for the role of Alternate Delegate for provision of support to the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programme (TCP).
UK SBS is managing this procurement process in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 (PA 2023) and the Procurement Regulations 2024 applicable to this procurement procedure (as may be amended from time to time) (the “Regulations”). This is a Services Contract being procured under the Open Procedure. 
This procurement shall be split into 4 Lots as follows and for each Lot one Contract shall be awarded to the successful supplier(s).
LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES)
LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT)
LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS)
LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS)
Please state clearly which lot you are applying for in your submission in the bid title. The application must be submitted by an organisation for a specific individual within the organisation. This can be a company, university, NGO or sole trader. An organisation may submit bids for several lots, no single individual may be proposed for more than one Lot. For example, a Supplier may bid for all four Lots; however, a different academic or employee must be nominated as the lead representative for each Lot.
 Each lot will be assessed individually so please provide a separate application for each lot applied for (including declarations). Each lot will only be awarded to one bidder.
Background
The IEA works to ensure reliable, affordable and clean energy for its 32 member countries and beyond. Founded in 1974, the IEA was initially designed to help countries co-ordinate a collective response to major disruptions in the supply of oil, such as the crisis of 1973/4. While this remains a key aspect of its work, the IEA has evolved and expanded. It is at the heart of global dialogue on energy innovations.
Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs) are independent, international groups of experts that enable governments and industries from around the world to lead programmes and projects on a wide range of energy technologies and related issues. TCPs currently cover topics related to:
•	Efficient end-use (buildings, electricity, industry, transport).
•	Cleaner fossil fuels (greenhouse-gas mitigation, extraction, supply, transformation).
•	Renewable energy and hydrogen (technologies and policies for deployment).
•	Cross-cutting issues (modelling, technology transfer, project financing).
•	Fusion power (safety, physics, materials, technologies).
The 6,000 experts in the TCPs work to advance the research, development and commercialisation of energy technologies. The scope and strategy of each TCP is in keeping with the IEA Shared Goals of energy security, environmental protection and economic growth, as well as engagement worldwide. Depending on the TCP, activities may include:
•	Basic and applied research, technology development and pilot plants
•	Technology assessment, feasibility studies, environmental impact studies, market analysis, policy implications
•	Information exchange of research results and programmes
•	Scientist exchanges
•	Databases, modelling and systems analysis
•	Experts’ networks.
More information on the IEA and the TCPs is available here: Technology collaboration - About - IEA.
Each TCP typically has two Delegates who represent each country at the Executive Committee: a primary Delegate and an Alternate Delegate.
Each TCP is its own entity and therefore have different methods for organising activities. The types of activities are, however, broadly consistent across the TCPs. 
The UK is currently participating in 28 TCPs. The Science and Innovation for Climate and Energy (SICE) directorate in DESNZ funds 12 of these. At this time, DESNZ is looking to appoint Alternate Delegates for 4 of these TCPs to represent the UK industry alongside the primary DESNZ Delegate:
•	Energy Storage - https://iea-es.org/
•	Heat Pump Technologies (HPT) - http://www.heatpumpingtechnologies.org
•	Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) - https://iea-pvps.org/ 
•	Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) - https://iea-industry.org/ 
The UK also participates in Mission Innovation, which is the leading international collaboration platform on innovation hosted by the IEA. SICE currently coordinates input into the seven Missions of Mission Innovation. Where relevant to the programme of work of the IEA Technology Collaboration Programmes, alternate delegates should seek to join up activities and stakeholder engagement. 
Acronyms and terminology:
IEA TCP	International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs): multilateral working groups established by the IEA across 8 themes (Buildings, Electricity, Industry, Transport, Renewable Energy, Fossil Energy, Fusion Power, cross-cutting) 
IEA TCP Secretariat	Organises the general TCP administration (requesting invoices, organising annual activities), liaises with the IEA and stakeholders
DESNZ (Primary) Delegate	Government representative in the IEA TCPs. Drawn from across technical and policy teams. Primarily responsible for administration and knowledge transfer within DESNZ, quality assessment of UK outputs to IEA, but can get more involved depending on expertise and resource.
Alternate Delegate (AD)	Experts in their field appointed through open competition. In charge of running the UK’s TCP activities and producing main outputs. 
DESNZ TCP Co-ordinator	Oversees all the TCPs at a working level within DESNZ and is responsible for the procurement of DESNZ and Alternate Delegates, reporting of TCP activities for DESNZ governing procedures and any general admin tasks not specific to individual TCPs. 
National TCP Coordinator	Oversees all UK TCP Activity across 28 TCP Programmes with UK representation. Facilitates engagement across TCP representatives and provides support on alignment between TCPs and policy.
Tasks / Annexes	Sub-tasks produced by TCPs, where members create working groups to produce reports, gather international data on technologies/policies/ business models, etc. Known variously as tasks, sub-tasks, working groups, and annexes in different TCPs, but referred to as ‘annexes’ for clarity in this specification.
Operating agent	Project manager or technical lead of an annex. In charge of defining the programme of work of the annexes, and ensuring delivery of outputs. Known under different terminology across TCPs, but used here for clarity.
National Team	A team of UK experts from industry, third sector and academia convened by the Alternate Delegate.
ExCo	Executive committee meeting which typically occurs twice a year (generally at least once in person).
The role of Alternate Delegate has general tasks common to all TCPs. Additional opportunities such as active participation in annex work or chairing the TCP can vary and be shaped by the AD and DESNZ Delegate. All ADs are expected to be able to complete all tasks, and the general tasks below are considered a minimum requirement. The Programme of Work will vary by TCP and will be jointly agreed with the DESNZ Delegate. The minimum requirement is expected to correspond to 12 days per financial year, amounting to a total minimum time requirement over the maximum potential duration of the contract of 29 days.
buyer: Department for Energy Security & Net Zero

title: Burial Ground Maintenance Contract
description:
Main Job Specifications:
WEEKLY - Pick up any litter in the cemetery & car park and empty all bins.				
Remove any discarded or dead floral tributes from plots and remove from site			
Remove any other debris from site
Clear debris, rake & level uneven shingle in the car park, cemetery entrance and pathways				 
APRIL - SEPTEMBER: Weekly mowing of the cemetery & strimming around the headstones.
Weekly mowing & strimming of the grass in the extension area next to the cemetery			
AUTUMN - clear and remove the leaves
MONTLY TASKS:		
Clear all weeds and remove all debris from the hornbeam hedge between the established and new areas of the cemetery.			
Clear underneath the trees along the Western boundary removing all weeds, leaves & debris.			
Clear all weeds and remove all debris from the hedge along the western, eastern & southern boundaries 			
OCTOBER - MARCH: Maintain a tidy appearance of all the grass areas, cutting & strimming as per the maintenance contract.
The levelling of graves as needed and to include the supplying of top soil and seed.				
YEARLY TASKS -
Once a year between March - April: Cut path edges in line with natural boundaries & pathways.			
Twice a year - in Spring & Autumn - keep the car park, cemetery entrance and pathways clear of weeds with a compliant weed killer.			
Once a year between July & August: Cut back all holly hedges - top and side - on the northern & eastern boundaries.  Hedges to be cut & kept at 6ft and all clippings removed.			
Once a year between July & August: Trim the top & sides of the Queens hedge.  Hedge to be cut & kept at 6ft. All clippings to be removed.		
Once a year between July & August: Trim the top & sides of the hedge along the western, eastern & southern boundaries.  Hedge to be cut & kept at 6ft. All clippings to be removed.				
Twice a year - in Spring & Autumn - build up and/or level surfaces.  Repair or replace turf as necessary.			
Once a year in Spring (or when required) - clean and apply teak oil to the benches.

title: CO2330_CYP Emotional Wellbeing_Market Engagement
description:
Wiltshire Council is seeking to engage with organisations operating within the children and young people emotional wellbeing sector to help inform the future design and commissioning of emotional wellbeing support across Wiltshire.
The Council is undertaking a period of pre-procurement market engagement to better understand current market capability, emerging best practice, innovative delivery models and potential approaches to service delivery for children and young people. This engagement will explore how emotional wellbeing services can support prevention, early intervention and access to appropriate support, whilst integrating effectively with wider systems including education, health, community and voluntary sector services.
At this stage, no final service model, contract structure, procurement route or contract value has been determined. Wiltshire Council is keen to hear from a broad range of providers, including voluntary, community and social enterprise organisations, charities, NHS organisations, independent providers and collaborative partnerships or consortiums.
Engagement activity is expected to include market discussions and a follow-up questionnaire seeking provider insight on service design, outcomes, delivery models, affordability, innovation, collaboration opportunities and potential barriers to market participation. Feedback received will be used to help shape the Council's future commissioning intentions and any subsequent procurement activity.
The Council welcomes views on what an effective emotional wellbeing service should look like for Wiltshire's children and young people, including approaches to self-referral, navigation and advice, counselling and therapeutic support, digital provision, community-based interventions, support for priority cohorts, and integration with wider emotional wellbeing and mental health pathways
Participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage in any future procurement process, nor does it commit the Council to commence any procurement or award any contract.

title: Nicotine Replacement Therapy and Smoking Cessation Medication Postal Supply within Suffolk
description:
Suffolk County Council (Public Health, Communities and Public Safety) are currently out to tender for the postal supply of Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) and smoking cessation prescription medication.
Smoking prevalence in Suffolk is currently estimated at 10.5%. The Council's ambition is to reduce this to 5% or below by 2030. NRT and prescribed smoking cessation medications are recognised as effective interventions to support people to quit smoking and remain an important element of the local stop smoking offer. The Council currently provides access to these products through a pharmacy-based pathway. However, not all clients are able to access participating pharmacies due to factors such as working hours, limited transport options or mobility issues. The Council is therefore exploring alternative delivery models to improve accessibility.
The procurement is split into two lots. Suppliers may bid for either lot individually or for both lots.
Lot 1 - Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT)
Supply a range of NRT products following referral from the Council's commissioned stop smoking service (FGS) and deliver products directly to clients using a reliable and secure postal service.
Lot 2 - Smoking cessation prescription medication
Undertake remote clinical consultations with clients referred by the stop smoking service to assess suitability for Varenicline or Cytisine and, where clinically appropriate, supply medication directly to clients using a reliable and secure postal service.
This opportunity is available in the 'Current Tenders' area of the portal. Interested parties are invited to express their interest to gain full access to the tender documentation.
The contract period is two years with an option to extend for up to a further two years.
The anticipated contract value (including the extension period) is approximately £400,000 (approximately £100,000 per annum) excluding VAT.
The deadline date for submissions of the tender is 3rd November 2026 at 11am. Please note late returns will NOT be permitted. 
The deadline for clarification questions is 20th October 2026 which must be generated via the correspondence option on the website.

title: Communication advice and strategic consultancy services
description: This notice is to inform of the intent to direct award a contract for continuation of services to Velindre University NHS Trust incumbent PR supplier. It is proposed that Scruffy Dog PR continues to support the Trust on the basis that the services required are a direct extension of the specialist communications and reputational management support already being provided. The Trust is currently managing a number of ongoing and highly sensitive reputational issues, some of which involve confidential information, complex stakeholder considerations and an evolving public, political and media context. Scruffy Dog PR has developed a detailed understanding of these matters, the associated risks, the Trust’s risk appetite, and the careful handling required to ensure that communications remain accurate, proportionate and appropriately aligned with the Trust’s position.Changing supplier at this stage would create a material risk of loss of continuity, duplication of effort and delay. A new supplier would need to be fully briefed on the background to the current reputational issues, including highly sensitive contextual information, stakeholder history, live risks and previous communications advice. This would be disproportionate given the pace and sensitivity of the work required and could compromise the Trust’s ability to respond quickly, consistently and effectively to emerging issues.In addition, Scruffy Dog PR has an established understanding of the Trust’s priorities over the coming months, particularly the communications brief relating to the transition into the new Velindre Cancer Centre in spring 2027. This is a significant strategic programme for the Trust and will require careful, consistent and well-informed communications support across a range of audiences. The supplier’s existing knowledge of the Trust, its operating context, stakeholder landscape and current reputational challenges will enable the communications approach to be delivered with the necessary pace, sensitivity and consistency.For these reasons, appointing an alternative supplier at this point would be likely to result in services that are materially different from, and potentially incompatible with, the existing work already undertaken. It would also create disproportionate operational and technical difficulties in maintaining continuity of advice, protecting confidentiality, ensuring consistent messaging and supporting the Trust’s ability to manage its communications workload effectively and efficiently. Please note NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust) will manage this procurement on behalf of the contracting authority. Due to having the same identifiers, we're unable to reflect this in the notice options.

title: DHSC: Health Survey for England 2028-31
description:
The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) is undertaking preliminary market engagement in relation to the future delivery of the Health Survey for England (HSE) 2028-2031. HSE is the principal national survey used to measure and monitor the health of people living in private households in England and provides nationally representative information on health status, health-related behaviours, long-term conditions, disease prevalence and health inequalities.
DHSC is seeking feedback from potential suppliers on the proposed procurement approach and draft specification for the end-to-end delivery of HSE from the 2028 survey year onwards. The requirement covers the design and delivery of the survey, including survey development, sampling, participant recruitment, mixed-mode data collection, physical and biological measurements, laboratory services, data processing, statistical analysis, reporting, publication support and data archiving.
The successful supplier will be expected to support the continued delivery and modernisation of HSE, including a phased transition towards an online-first mixed-mode approach, whilst maintaining data quality, representativeness, inclusivity and continuity with the established HSE time series.
The contract is expected to commence on 1 July 2027 and will support delivery of the 2028, 2029, 2030 and 2031 survey years. Noting that the contract will have an end date of 31 July 2033 to complete all associated processing, analysis, reporting, publication support, data deposit, archiving, transition and exit activities.
The proposed contract may include options for DHSC to extend the contract for delivery of an additional survey year (2032) and to commission additional services or activities related to the core requirement. Any option may be exercised at DHSC’s discretion, subject to need, funding and the terms of the contract.

title: Time and Motion Study
description:
This is a Preliminary Market Engagement Exercise - this is not a tendering opportunity or a call for competition.
This is to inform the market of the requirement and gather information and feedback from the market via a Supplier Questionnaire in advance of publishing a future tender.
The Office of the Traffic Commissioner (OTC) requires an independent time and motion study to establish a robust evidence base for the time, effort and resources required to deliver its principal casework, licensing, tribunal, compliance, finance, correspondence and support processes.
The study will identify the end-to-end elapsed time, active handling time, waiting time, rework, hand-offs and variation associated with agreed process families. It will distinguish productive activity from unavoidable delay and system or process constraints, analyse why variation occurs, and interpret the findings against actual and forecast workload. The resulting evidence must enable OTC to calculate the capacity and full-time equivalent resource required to deliver each process and the overall workload at agreed service levels.
The study is not an assessment of individual employee performance. Results must be reported at process, role or team level and interpreted in the context of case complexity, statutory requirements, quality controls, reasonable adjustments, system performance and dependencies on other organisations.
Please note this is a draft outline of the requirement and will be subject to amendment prior to any potential procurement exercise.
The responses to the market engagment will help determine the value and length of the contract.

Strong momentum across the project, with site preparation works completed, funding secured and public sector partners committed to bringing forward the vision. 
The Authority is seeking an experienced and financially robust partner capable of working collaboratively to unlock the full potential of Shrub Hill and deliver a high-quality, sustainable and commercially viable regeneration programme over the long term.
