title: Hazardous Waste Collection & Disposal Services at Household Hazardous Waste Events and Incidental Hazardous Waste
description:
Norfolk County Council, as a Waste Disposal Authority, is required by the Environmental Protection Act 1990, section 51, to provide reasonably accessible sites for the free disposal of household waste by its residents.
The seven District, Borough and City councils in Norfolk as Waste Collection Authorities have a statutory duty to provide a collection service for household hazardous waste. In terms of hazardous waste disposal, Norfolk County Council has met this obligation by holding 'Hazardous Waste Events' on set weekends, at specific Recycling Centres (RC). Such events have been held annually since 2003. This is an opportunity for householders to deposit hazardous waste such as domestic paint and thinners, pesticides, fertilisers, fire extinguishers and household cleaning products.
Visitor numbers across the network of RCs for 2025 was over 910,000. Many households therefore visit the Household Hazardous Waste Days (HHWD) to dispose of such material. There were over 12, 495 visitors to the 14 HHWD in 2025 (two events).
The HHWD take place during dedicated weekends where an area of the participating RC is designated to receive household hazardous waste. Whilst the RC is normally only open 9am - 4pm, for the purposes of the HHWD, RC will have extended opening hours of 8am to 4pm. All visits to the RCs are made via a booking system. Without a valid booking, members of the public will be refused entry.
These events are primarily designed for the receiving of hazardous waste, and therefore normal waste is restricted. The site Contractor will still be making bin collections and exchanges, but these are kept to a minimum. Any HGV movements at Hempton RC ONLY will require it to be closed for safety reasons. Norfolk's service standard is that these exchanges must not exceed 30 minutes. Any closures will be kept to a minimum.
In addition to the hazardous waste events, the Council has a responsibility to respond to unplanned incidents where hazardous waste arises due to, for example, small or larger scale fly tipping or coastal pollution incidents, ensuring that appropriate arrangements are made for the treatment or disposal of the waste.

title: WIRELESS CONFERENCE AND HYBRID MEETING SYSTEM
description:
Ryde Town Council invites you to quote for a wireless conference system for its Council Chamber. You will supply, install, commission and support it.
The Council has no preference over brand but the system will need to be compatible with our existing IT equipment. This specification details what the system must do. The Council is open to any solution that works in the way it needs. The Council welcomes quotes from all relevant manufacturers and suppliers.
The system must be simple and intuitive to operate from start-up, with no technical knowledge required. Council staff must be able to set up and run meetings confidently using clear, straightforward controls. The system must be quick and easy to set up and must not need continual adjustment. Council staff cannot adjust or operate the system once a meeting has started. It must be compatible with live streaming, as the Council streams its meetings on YouTube.
Please note that Councillors do not generally attend meetings with laptops or tablets therefore, a laptop or tablet based microphone system would not be suitable.  Staff do have laptops available for system operation.
The system requirements in brief
•	A wireless conference system to accommodate 18 people taking part in a meeting. Councillors have shared microphones in the past (one between two) and are happy to continue doing so if it is more cost effective.
•	Wireless casting of the meeting to a loudspeaker the public can hear.
•	Compatibility with hybrid meetings, with remote participants or observers on Zoom, YouTube and Microsoft Teams.
•	Room to add additional units later.
•	Compatibility with hearing loops.
Full details of the specification can be found in the tender documentation.

title: Surface Tunnel Maintenance
description:
Transport for London (TfL) is the integrated transport authority for London, responsible for delivering the Mayor's Transport Strategy and managing transport services across the Capital. TfL oversees one of the world's largest integrated urban transport networks, including London's road network and associated infrastructure. This Market Sounding Questionnaire (MSQ) seeks to obtain market feedback in relation to the maintenance of Transport for London's surface road tunnels. Currently, these services are delivered as part of the Tunnels and Pumping Stations Contract, which was established in 2021. This MSQ relates to the proposed opportunity WS2986809626 - Surface Tunnel Maintenance and is being issued in line with TfL's public notice requirements and to support early market engagement.
Transport for London is responsible for the operation and maintenance of 10 road tunnels (plus an additional 2 tunnels on the A13 from 2030) and associated infrastructure, this includes Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) assets on the 90KM London Road Tunnel Network Traffic Control System (LTRACS) and circa 107 pump stations. The tunnel estate comprises safety-critical and operationally important assets that enable the safe and efficient movement of people and goods throughout London. Maintenance activities may encompass a broad range of tunnel infrastructure and supporting systems, including mechanical and electrical (M&E) equipment, Intelligent Transportation Systems, communications networks, and other operational and safety-related assets.
Activities currently undertaken across the tunnel estate include a combination of planned, preventative and reactive maintenance, inspection, testing, condition monitoring, fault & incident response, asset performance reporting, cleaning, lifecycle replacement of consumables and components, inventory management, and physical and cyber security considerations associated with operational systems.
This MSQ forms part of TfL's preliminary market engagement activities. It does not constitute a call for competition, invitation to tender, commitment to procure, or commitment to any particular procurement strategy, delivery model or contract structure.

title: Demolition of Former Beales Store (Mansfield Connect)
description:
Mansfield District Council (the Council) require a single supplier to undertake demolition of the former Beales department store located on Stockwell Gate, Mansfield, prior to construction of the new Mansfield Connect building.
The project comprises the demolition, deconstruction, asbestos removal, site clearance and associated making good to the former Beales department store and associated former Co-op structures, including all temporary works, retained-asset protection, environmental controls and completion security works to provide the Council with a secured and cleared building site for future development.
The successful provider will be required to provide all design, surveys, notices, licences, temporary works, management, labour, plant and materials necessary to safely demolish and clear the former Beales department store and associated former Co-op structures in accordance with the Scope.
The Works include soft strip; removal of known and discovered asbestos and hazardous materials; isolation, diversion and termination of services; demolition/deconstruction of superstructures, slabs, foundations and basements to the specified levels; protection of adjoining structures and public areas; removal and lawful disposal/recovery of arisings; backfilling, compaction, grading and drainage; all permanent and temporary making good; and leaving a secure, stable and safely drained site.
The demolition shall take place under a sole contract with a single provider.
This requirement is not suitable for division into Lots and the requirement is for a single contractor to undertake the work under contract.  The successful contractor will enter into a NEC4 Engineering & Construction Contract, Opt A: Priced contract with Activity Schedule with Mansfield District Council.
The project is subject to planning approval and the successful bidder will become the preferred supplier to undertake the work subject to planning permission being received.
Subject to planning approval, it is anticipated that works will start on site in January 2027.
This procurement is reserved in accordance with PPN Action Note 005 (February 2025) and The Local Government (Exclusion of Non-commercial Considerations) (England) Order 2026. Participation is restricted to suppliers that are based or have established substantive business operations within the designated local area, comprising Nottinghamshire and the adjoining counties of Derbys, Lincs, Leics and South Yorks. title: Telephone Survey Services for Health and Wellbeing Strategy Index and Scorecard
description:
Continuation of delivery of survey (Health and Well-being related questions) previously asked in the SCC/Police Joint Neighbourhood Survey, in order to maintain trend data in the Surrey Health and Wellbeing (HWB) Strategy Index and Scorecard.
In the past 3 years the SCC/Surrey Police Joint Neighbourhood Survey (JNS) has been influenced by our SCC Public Health agenda; it has been gathering data related to Health Inequalities / Empowered and Thriving Communities. The responses to 13 of JNS questions have been included in the Health and Wellbeing (HWB) Strategy Index and Scorecard (used to track the Surrey system's progress regarding the delivery of the HWB Strategy), using rolling 12-month totals. These indicators relate to perceptions of residents' local area related to their health and well-being and the impact on them of the cost of living. These indicators have proved extremely useful where other data is not available/reliable.
The survey had previously been contracted out by Surrey Police to Opinion Research Services Ltd as part of JNS. As SCC still requires this data to feed into the HWB strategy index and scorecard, a direct award was made.
The provider has been delivering the Joint Neighbourhood Survey for a number of years; the methodology of the survey needs to be maintained in order to retain veracity of trend data in the HWB Strategy Index and Scorecard. The annual Index and quarterly Scorecards are utilised by the Surrey HWB Board to measure the Surrey's system's progress against the Surrey HWB Strategy in reducing health inequalities. This contract therefore enables maintenance of momentum of monitoring through Local Government Reform.

title: FW Supply & Deliver – LV & MV Cables – Multi Site 1232
description:
Scottish and Southern Electricity Networks, comprising Scottish Hydro Electric Power Distribution plc and Southern Electric Power Distribution plc, intends to establish a multi-supplier Framework Agreement for the supply and delivery of low voltage (LV) and medium voltage (MV) cable products. The Framework Agreement may also be called off by SSEN Transmission, SSE Renewables, SSE utility Solution Ltd, TESGL Ltd and SSE Heat Networks Ltd where technically appropriate.
The scope will include LV concentric cables, LV waveform cables, LV auxiliary “fast runner” cables, and 11kV and 33kV cable products. By combining these requirements into a single procurement exercise, SSEN aims to improve security of supply, maximise competition, support supplier participation, provide greater demand visibility, and deliver value for customers. The arrangement is also intended to support SSEN Distribution’s ED3 and ED4 investment programme and future network requirements.
The proposed scope of the new framework is intended to be, but not limited to:
•	LV Concentric Cables
•	LV Waveform Cables
•	Selected LV Auxiliary ("fast runner") Cables
•	11kV Cables
•	33kV Cables
The current proposed lotting strategy is:
Lot	Description
Lot 1	LV Concentric & Auxiliary Cables North
Lot 2	LV Concentric & Auxiliary Cables South
Lot 3	LV Waveform Cables North
Lot 4	LV Waveform Cables South
Lot 5	MV Cables North
Lot 6	MV Cables South
SSEN intends to establish a multi-supplier framework and currently anticipates appointing up to the three highest ranked suppliers per lot, subject to receipt of sufficient compliant, suitable and competitive tenders. Suppliers will be ranked following evaluation; however, SSE would retain flexibility to allocate requirements between awarded suppliers based on operational requirements, service performance, lead times, product availability, manufacturing capacity, quality performance and overall value delivered.
As part of the tender process, suppliers may be required to submit pricing against a range of indicative award and allocation scenarios, which may include sole supplier, dual-source and multi-supplier models. This will allow SSEN to assess the relationship between volume allocation, pricing efficiency, supply chain resilience and value for money before finalising the award strategy.
Suppliers may also be invited to identify any additional commercial benefits, capacity commitments, service improvements or efficiencies that could be achieved through the award of multiple lots. SSEN will consider these alongside the need to maintain appropriate supply chain resilience and continuity of supply.
Suppliers will not be required to hold full SSEN technical approval prior to framework award. This approach is intended to support participation from a wider range of technically credible manufacturers. All suppliers will remain subject to SSEN’s technical assessment and approval requirements, and no supplier will be permitted to supply cable under the framework until the relevant approvals have been successfully completed.

title: Provision of Motor Control Centres, Systems Integration and ICA Services
description:
Scottish Water is seeking to establish a multi-supplier Framework Agreement for the provision of Motor Control Centres (MCCs), Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICA), Systems Integration (SI) and ICA maintenance and support services. The Framework will provide a flexible, scalable and resilient route to market for electrical, control, automation and Operational Technology (OT) requirements across Scottish Water's water and wastewater assets, supporting capital delivery, asset renewal and operational requirements.

The Framework will be divided into three Lots, with multiple suppliers appointed to each Lot: Lot 1 – Integrated MCC, ICA and Systems Integration; Lot 2 – Systems Integration and Automation Services; and Lot 3 – ICA Maintenance, Minor Works and Support. Suppliers may apply for one, several or all Lots. Depending on the nature, value, complexity and risk of each requirement, call-offs may be for fully integrated end-to-end solutions, standalone equipment supply or discrete specialist services. The Framework will be available for use by Scottish Water and its appointed Delivery Vehicles.

Call-off contracts may be awarded by direct award or by mini-competition between the suppliers appointed to the relevant Lot(s), in accordance with the Framework Agreement. Scottish Water gives no guarantee of the volume or value of work to be called off under the Framework or any Lot. The estimated value stated in the Contract Notice is the maximum anticipated value over the full Framework term and is indicative only.

The Framework will be based on NEC4 terms. Call-off contracts may be placed under the NEC4 Professional Service Short Contract, the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Short Contract or Scottish Water Purchase Order Conditions, as appropriate to the requirement and Lot being engaged.

Suppliers must maintain all relevant certifications, standards and regulatory compliance throughout the Framework term. MCC assemblies must comply with the current edition of the BS EN IEC 61439 series, including Parts 1 and 2. As a designated Operator of Essential Services, Scottish Water will require suppliers to support its obligations under the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations, including secure-by-design engineering, OT cyber security controls, vulnerability management, personnel assurance and cyber assurance activities. Suppliers must be able to work safely within live operational environments forming part of Critical National Infrastructure, and bidders will be assessed on their capability to undertake the relevant CDM duty holder role(s) for each Lot.

Scottish Water is seeking suppliers who will work collaboratively as long-term delivery partners, including early engagement in project development, design and buildability reviews, accurate lead time and pipeline information, and support for standardisation, innovation, whole-life value and carbon reduction. Performance will be managed through key performance indicators, regular reporting and continuous improvement.

It is estimated the Framework Agreement will start in April 2027 and run for an initial term of 6 years. Scottish Water may extend it by up to 3 further periods of 2 years each. The maximum duration, including all extensions, is 12 years, ending March 2039. Scottish Water may use each extension at its discretion, depending on supplier performance, continued value for money and business needs.

title: Spain – Research and experimental development services – Pre-commercial Procurement of an innovative Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations (suHCO)
description: suHCO (Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations) is a European project funded under the Horizon Europe programme (Grant Agreement No. 101226802) and implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) scheme. The project aims to support health and care organisations in their transition towards more sustainable and environmentally responsible models by fostering the development of innovative digital solutions. Through the PCP process, suHCO will procure research and development services for the creation of an AI-enabled digital platform capable of helping healthcare organisations assess their sustainability performance, identify improvement opportunities, plan and implement actions, monitor progress, and support evidence-based decision-making. The future solution is expected to integrate sustainability knowledge, regulatory requirements, standards, best practices and relevant data sources, providing users with practical guidance tailored to their organisational context. It should also support sustainable procurement processes, impact assessment, reporting activities and organisational change management. The project is driven by a Buyers Group composed of healthcare organisations from Spain, Italy and Wales. The solutions developed during the PCP will be progressively designed, prototyped and validated in real healthcare environments to ensure their relevance, usability and scalability. By bringing together healthcare providers, technology developers and sustainability experts, suHCO seeks to stimulate innovation and contribute to the sustainability objectives of European health systems.

title: Germany – Engineering services – VG Bad Breisig - Errichtung eines Feuerwehrgerätehauses in der Ortsgemeinde Waldorf, Los 2: Planungs- und Überwachungsleistungen der Fachplanung Technische Ausrüstung HLS und Elektro
description: Die Verbandsgemeinde Bad Breisig plant die Errichtung eines neuen Feuerwehrgerätehauses in der Ortsgemeinde Waldorf. Die derzeit aktive Feuerwehrwache im Zentrum der Ortsgemeinde wird aufgegeben. Vorgesehen als zukünftiger Standort ist das am Ortsausgang Waldorf in Richtung Niederzissen gelegene Grundstück "Kühhohl", das unmittelbar an die Landstraße L82 angrenzt. Für das Baugrundstück steht eine Fläche von ca. 2.500 m² zur Verfügung. Das Vorhaben wurde mit dem bereits beschlossenen Bebauungsplan "Feuerwehrgerätehaus Waldorf" überplant. Das Feuerwehrgerätehaus ist als kombinierte Anlage aus Fahrzeughalle, Betriebshof, Sozial- und Funktionsbereichen sowie der erforderlichen Freianlage geplant. Die Fahrzeughalle ist mit drei Stellplätzen für Einsätzfahrzeuge gemäß Stellplatzgröße 2 nach DIN 14092 vorgesehen. Hinsichtlich des Raum- und Flächenbedarfes ist die aktuelle DIN 14092 zwingend zu beachten. Ergänzend sind ein Stellplatz für den Katastrophenschutz sowie eine Waschhalle vorgesehen. Aufgrund des Geländeverlaufs ist das Gebäude voraussichtlich zweigeschossig auszuführen. Die Errichtung kann in Massivbauweise, Holzbauweise, Elementbauweise oder Hybrid-Elementbauweise erfolgen. Die Anlage ist für eine Personalstärke von rund 55-75 aktiven Mitgliedern auszulegen, die auf etwa 40 Einsatzkräfte auf Männer und rund 10 auf Frauen entfallen zzgl. einer Jugendfeuerwehr mit etwa 20 Mitgliedern. Die Dimensionierung der Umkleiden, Sanitärbereiche, Schulungsräume sowie der Stellplätze für Einsatzkräfte hat auf Grundlage dieser Personalzahlen zu erfolgen. Das neue Feuerwehrgerätehaus wird nicht dauernd besetzt sein. Die Gefahrenmeldeanlage des bestehenden Feuerwehrgerätehauses wird in das neue Gebäude eingebaut und ggf. erweitert. Ziel des Vorhabens ist die Errichtung eines zeitgemäßen, funktionsgerechten und zukunftsfähigen Feuerwehrgerätehauses, das den geltenden rechtlichen, technischen und organisatorischen Anforderungen entspricht und einen sicheren sowie effizienten Feuerwehrbetrieb ermöglicht. Eine Standortanalyse aus dem Jahr 2022 liegt vor und wird zur Verfügung gestellt. Die Inhalte sind nicht verbindlich, sondern dienen nur als Orientierung für die weitere Planung.

title: Ireland – Civil engineering consultancy services – Dublin City Council Single Party Framework Agreement for an Integrated Design Team for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project
description: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 8969388 – Input when notice created . Please note that this project is subject to funding.

description: Institutionen för lärande, informatik, management och etik (LIME) bedriver forskning och utbildning som främjar praktisk implementering av forskningsrön och ny kunskap i folkhälsoarbete, vård och omsorg. Institutionen har två universitetsövergripande verksamhetsområden – pedagogisk utveckling och stödverksamhet samt forskning, utbildning och rådgivning på området hälso- och sjukvård- samt forskningsetik. Det är en spännande arbetsmiljö där forskning och utbildning står i fokus. BCI-tjänsten är en del av ett forskningsprojekt som bedrivs av Nationellt centrum för suicidforskning och prevention av psykisk ohälsa (NASP). NASP bistår regeringen och Region Stockholms beslutsfattare och invånare med kunskapsunderlag, kunskapsutveckling och kunskapsspridning. Vårt uppdrag är att genom forskning, strategiskt folkhälsoarbete, utbildning och informationsspridning bidra till att minska antalet självmord och självmordsförsök regionalt och nationellt. NASP bidrar även till att utveckla och stimulera kunskapsområdet självmord och självmordsprevention där utvärdering av olika interventioner utgör en viktig del. NASP söker en Leverantör, med erfarenhet av att kommunicera med suicidnära personer, för att utföra en Brief Contact Intervention (BCI) – en beprövad modell som i internationella studier visats sig kunna minska suicidala beteenden hos suicidnära personer. Med BCI avses här stödjande telefonsamtal till en person som har suicidtankar. Brief Contact Interventions (BCIs) är insatser där man på ett regelbundet och systematiskt sätt följer upp personer med förhöjd självmordsrisk via telefon, brev, sms eller liknande. BCI-insatser används främst som ett sätt att förmedla medmänskligt stöd och omtanke, samt till att uppmuntra till att söka hjälp vid behov eller behandlingsföljsamhet om sådan pågår. BCI-insatser är således inte någon terapeutisk behandling, och en fördel är att insatsen därmed inte behöver utföras av medicinsk personal. Ytterligare en fördel är att de regelbundna kontakterna med personerna är korta vilket möjliggör uppföljningar av en bred population. Detta gör BCIs till en kostnadseffektiv insats som kan erbjudas många personer och riskgrupper. I flera vetenskapliga studier som utvärderat BCI-insatser har man funnit positiva effekter i form av färre självmordsförsök och självmord (för systematiska översikter se: Zalsman et al., 2016; Mann et al 2022). Den upphandlade leverantören ska utveckla ett system som kan ta emot deltagare med förhöjd självmordsrisk. Systemet ska möjliggöra processer för att regelbundet följa upp dessa personer genom strukturerade telefonkontakter enligt våra riktlinjer som har syfte att förmedla medmänskligt stöd. Vid varje kontakttillfälle ska uppringaren kunna föra anteckningar som ska användas som underlag till nästa samtal. Samtliga delar av systemet ska vara utvecklade med de säkerhetsegenskaper som krävs för att kunna hantera känsliga personuppgifter enligt dataskyddsförordningen. För detta ändamål, se bifogat PUB-avtal som ska kunna signeras för att KI ska kunna ingå avtal med en leverantör angående detta projekt. Tjänsten kommer att vända sig till individer över 18 år. Den upphandlade leverantören ska kunna leverera tjänsten till så många personer som möjligt fram till år 2029, där varje person följs upp cirka åtta (8) gånger per år och varje kontakttillfälle tar ungefär 20 minuter. Vid utebliven kontakt ska den upphandlade leverantören följa studieprotokollets rutiner för upprepade kontaktförsök vid missat kontakttillfälle. Leverantören ska även kunna erbjuda personer möjligheten att specificera när på dagen de önskar bli kontaktade. Uppringare behöver inte ha formell klinisk utbildning men de ska ha relevant utbildning eller erfarenhet av att erbjuda socialt stöd (se krav nedan). NASP kommer i samband med projektet att bistå med utbildning omfattande cirka en heldag.

title: Domestic Abuse Needs Assessment
description:
Birmingham City Council is seeking to commission external consultancy to conduct a thorough domestic abuse needs assessment for the city.
The needs assessment will form a key part of Birmingham’s evidence-led approach to tackling domestic abuse, providing robust evidence of local need. The needs assessment should take the form of a well-evidenced written report, supported by a thorough compilation of both qualitative and quantitative data. It should provide a comprehensive and honest picture of the prevalence and response to domestic abuse across agencies within Birmingham, looking at changes over the past three years, expected changes in the next three years and any gaps or needs around new communities in the city.
It must go beyond the duty set out by the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, which only represents the needs of those who require support in domestic abuse safe accommodation. The assessment we require will span across the continuum of domestic abuse, capturing need at prevention, support and crisis stages.
This will include mapping the current domestic abuse pathways, across Criminal Justice services, Children Services, Health, Housing/Homelessness, Education, Adult Social Care etc. (this is a non-exhaustive list), to support Birmingham’s whole systems approach to supporting survivors of domestic abuse. The mapping will include commissioned and non-commissioned domestic abuse services, the exempt accommodation sector across the city and the associated pathways across this provision.
The contract for the services will commence on 7th December 2026 and will be in place for a period of 6 months.

title: Danes Educational Trust
description:
Catering Services Opportunity
Invitation to Tender – Catering Services Across 13 Schools within Danes Educational Trust
Danes Educational Trust is seeking to appoint an exceptional, innovative and collaborative catering partner to deliver high-quality catering services across its family of 13 schools, comprising 6 Primary Schools and 7 Secondary Schools.
As a dynamic and ambitious Multi Academy Trust, Danes Educational Trust is committed to providing outstanding educational environments where pupils and students can flourish. The Trust recognises the vital role that food, nutrition and the dining experience play in supporting wellbeing, educational outcomes and the development of healthy lifelong habits. Consequently, the Trust is seeking a catering provider that shares its vision, values and commitment to excellence.
The successful catering partner will be responsible for delivering fresh, nutritious and appealing food offers that meet the diverse needs of pupils, students and staff across both primary and secondary settings. The Trust is looking for a provider that will move beyond traditional school catering models, bringing innovation, creativity and commercial expertise to create vibrant and engaging dining experiences that increase participation and enhance customer satisfaction.
Menus should offer a range of contemporary, nutritious and appealing choices that reflect current food trends whilst remaining fully compliant with School Food Standards. The successful provider will be expected to continually evolve and develop its offer, ensuring that food provision remains relevant, exciting and responsive to the feedback of students, pupils and staff.
Food safety and allergen management are of paramount importance to the Trust. Bidders must clearly demonstrate that allergen awareness, risk management and food safety are embedded throughout their organisation and form part of the company's culture and operational DNA. The Trust expects robust allergen controls, comprehensive staff training, effective communication processes and industry-leading systems to protect those with dietary requirements and food allergies.
Danes Educational Trust is seeking more than a contractor; it is looking for a genuine strategic partner that will work collaboratively with school leaders and stakeholders to support wider educational objectives, engage with pupils and students, promote healthy eating, support sustainability initiatives and contribute positively to each school's culture and community.
Bidder Requirements
Prospective bidders must be able to demonstrate:
•	Significant experience delivering catering services within a Multi Academy Trust environment.
•	A successful track record of operating across multiple school locations under a single contract structure.
•	Proven experience catering for both Primary and Secondary Schools, with a clear understanding of the differing requirements, dining patterns and expectations of each phase.
•	The capability and resources to successfully manage catering services across 13 schools comprising 6 Primary Schools and 7 Secondary Schools.
•	Strong evidence of increasing meal uptake, enhancing customer satisfaction and delivering excellent value for money.
•	Full compliance with all relevant legislation relating to food safety, nutrition, employment, safeguarding, health and safety, and allergen management.
•	Robust allergen management systems, procedures and training programmes embedded throughout the organisation.
•	A commitment to innovation through menu development, themed events, promotional activities and customer engagement initiatives.
•	Proven mobilisation and change management expertise to ensure a seamless transition from any incumbent provider.
•	Financial stability and the ability to invest in continuous service improvement, training, technology and innovation throughout the contract term.
•	Demonstrable commitment to sustainability, food provenance, waste reduction and supporting environmental objectives.
Partnership Expectations
The appointed provider will be expected to:
•	Deliver consistently high standards of food quality and customer service.
•	Work in partnership with school leaders, Trust representatives and key stakeholders.
•	Engage regularly with pupils, students and staff to shape and improve the catering offer.
•	Support food education, health and wellbeing initiatives across the Trust.
•	Maintain outstanding standards of food safety, allergen management and compliance.
•	Drive continuous improvement and innovation throughout the contract term.
•	Create welcoming dining environments that encourage healthy eating habits and increase participation.
Contract Opportunity
The contract will be awarded for an initial term of three years, with the option, at the Trust's discretion, to extend for a further two years based on successful performance, service quality and continued alignment with the Trust's strategic objectives.
This represents an exciting opportunity for an experienced and forward-thinking catering organisation to partner with Danes Educational Trust and play a central role in enhancing the daily experience of pupils, students and staff across its schools. The Trust welcomes interest from dynamic, ambitious and education-focused catering providers capable of delivering a service that reflects the values, aspirations and excellence expected throughout the Trust.

title: Transit Payment Service Providers (TPSP),  Closed Loop cEMV Token Providers, and Handheld Revenue Inspection Devices, for public transport services
description:
Smart Applications Management Limited (SAM) is the trading name of South West Smart Applications Limited, a Membership based central purchasing body, which owns and runs the National Mobilities Procurement Hub for its Members.
This Framework is for the procurement of Suppliers providing Transit Payment Services,  Closed Loop cEMV Token Services, and Revenue Inspection Devices for public transport services. The Framework has 3 Lots:
Lot 1: Transit Payment Service Providers (TPSP)
This Framework Lot is to provide Transit Payment Service Provider (TPSP) services for integration with an existing Account Based Ticketing (ABT) ticketing solution to enable the acceptance of Contactless EMV for travel.
The Transit Payment Service provides the necessary capabilities to interface with Contactless EMV enabled validation devices to accept validation transactions (otherwise known as "Taps") including:
•	The protection of sensitive cardholder data in transit and rest (specifically via encryption and tokenisation)
•	Processing of Taps in accordance with the card scheme transit guidance (enabling aggregation, debt recovery and liability sharing)
•	Interfaces with ABT Fares engines to facilitate the calculation of fares and charges
•	Interfaces with Acquirers to perform authorisation and settlement of travel and inspection charges
Lot 2:  Closed Loop cEMV Token Providers
This Framework Lot is to provide secure closed-loop cEMV Account Based Token media capabilities, enabling the issuance, management, and acceptance of physical travel media based on cEMV technology, and digital equivalents loaded into mobile wallets that can be integrated with transport authority cEMV PAYG solutions.
The closed-loop cEMV Transit Token capability provides the necessary features to manage cEMV token media issuance and lifecycle operations, including:
•	Secure generation, cryptographic key injection, and personalization scripting for physical cards, and provisioning and management of digital cards provisioned to mobile wallets
•	Integration with administrative web tools and back-office APIs to support batch ordering, inventory management, and postal fulfilment
•	Support for physical card personalization, verification and quality assurance prior to dispatch
•	Comprehensive lifecycle management capabilities supporting activation, suspension, replacement, and secure blocking of compromised or lost credentials
•	Native interoperability with the ABT Back Offices to maintain mapping of physical or digital cEMV cards with ABT Token accounts to enable Tap processing, charging and balance management.
Lot 3:  Handheld Revenue Inspection Devices
This framework lot provides handheld Revenue Inspection Devices (RIDs) for passenger transport services.
RIDs are vital tools used by Revenue Protection officers to enable them to determine if passengers have paid for their travel (when inspecting pre-purchased ticket products or smartcards) or have validated their PAYG travel media correctly, indicating that they intend to pay for their travel.
The Framework Lot RIDs support the following:
•	Inspection of a range of travel media including multi-format 2D Barcodes, Contactless EMV and ITSO Smart Cards.
•	Multiple models of Contactless EMV inspection, including Immediate, Deferred and Hybrid
•	Integration with back-office services including eTVD, ITSO HOPS, ABT Back offices and Transit Payment Service Providers (TPSPs) as required for the travel media and inspection models in operation

title: ONR1155 - Provision of Media Training to the  Office for Nuclear Regulation  Senior Leadership Team
description:
The Office for Nuclear Regulation (ONR) is the independent UK regulator of the nuclear industry, including existing, decommissioned and new reactors. It employs more than 700 professional staff, with specialist regulatory roles (e.g. nuclear safety/security/safeguards); corporate professions including Policy and Communications, Finance, Information Technology (IT), and Human Resources, and other core functions. ONR's Head Office, housing its main functions, is in Bootle, Liverpool, with two smaller offices in London and Cheltenham.
ONR independently regulates nuclear safety and security at 37 nuclear licensed sites in the UK. We also regulate transport and ensure that safeguards obligations for the UK are met. Our duty is to ensure that the nuclear industry controls its hazards effectively, has a culture of continuous improvement and maintains high standards.
ONR requires media training for selected members of its Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and the ONR Chair to support effective, confident and consistent engagement with the media, parliamentary committees and other public-facing communication channels including social media. The training will help senior representatives respond to challenging questions, communicate complex regulatory issues clearly and develop concise, confident on-camera skills for digital and social media channels.
ONR is seeking to award a contract to a suitably qualified media training supplier to design and deliver tailored media and social media training for members of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and ONR Chair. The training must reflect the different specialisms, public-facing responsibilities and leadership roles within ONR.
ONR also requires the ability to arrange refresher training and additional ad hoc training for further personnel, as required, at fixed rates for the duration of the contract.
The successful contractor will supply broadcast media training to enable ONR personnel to talk confidently to a camera, virtually, down-the-line (radio) but also to other media including print media and social media messaging. Training should support ONR personnel to adapt their style and message delivery, depending on audience, channel and line of questioning, and be confident in conveying key messages, even when under pressure. 
Training will also encompass developing ONR personnel to deliver competent video messaging for social media and longer form in-house videos, requiring  subjects to be confident in front of a camera, able to deliver strong messaging and narratives without prompts or uncertainty.
Training may be provided virtually where practical, and also in ONR's offices (Bootle, Cheltenham and/or London) depending on the nature of the training required and the availability of ONR personnel. The contractor should make use of equipment as necessary to create a realistic environment for a range of different media scenarios, with an ability to play back interviews to review and improve performance. 
Training should be made up of a blended approach of face-to-face sessions, duration of approximately 3 hours or 0.5 day per individual, and shorter refresher sessions delivered virtually (e.g. via Zoom or MS Teams) of between 1-2 hours. 
More than one media trainer should be made available to deliver sessions so that training participants experience different interview styles during the course of their training.    
The contractor will be required to liaise with the ONR Communications team to work up realistic scenarios for training and will carry out independent research to produce a "key messages" briefing tailored for each session. The contractor will advise on the level of advanced preparation that will be required by SLT participants. Knowledge of the nuclear industry, ONR's role and regulatory parlance is highly desirable and the contractor must be able to present projected costs for such preparatory work. 
The contractor will also train ONR personnel to be able to perform competently in the parliamentary committee arena when the dynamic is different to a media environment, but no less pressured.

title: Understanding the environmental impacts of displacing UK agricultural/commodity production
description:
There is increasing pressure on land use in the UK due to demands from housing development and commitments to Net Zero and nature. This, combined with a changing climate, mean there may be less land available for agricultural commodity production within the UK. This may result in a displacement of production overseas.
While there is good evidence on the carbon, biodiversity and other environmental impacts that any given land use change will bring in situ, there is currently no established method of identifying 1) where crops are likely to be grown instead and 2) what impacts this displaced crop growth may have. A way to estimate these could provide evidence that would help guide land use decisions and policy by providing a holistic understanding of both the domestic and international implications of these decisions.
Project Aims
1.    To produce an initial interim model that estimates where production would be displaced if a given area of land in the UK, producing a set quantity of a commodity, was no longer used for commodity production. The model will be based on clear and transparent assumptions.
2.    To estimate the environmental impacts of production in these new locations. The calculated environmental impacts will ideally map onto those included in the Global Environmental Impacts of Consumption (GEIC) indicator.

title: Heating, Electrical, Mechanical and Decarbonisation Framework
description:
The procurement will establish a single combined, multi-supplier Heating, Electrical, Mechanical and Decarbonisation Framework, not divided into lots, for the provision of works and associated services to domestic and non-domestic properties and buildings, including occupied and void properties. The scope will include, but is not limited to, the provision, supply, installation, replacement, upgrading, servicing, statutory and safety inspection, testing, planned and responsive maintenance and repair of heating, electrical, mechanical, renewable, low-carbon and associated energy systems. Heating works and services will include domestic and commercial/communal systems and equipment using gas, oil, solid fuel, electricity and renewable or low-carbon technologies, including gas and oil boilers, electric storage and panel heaters, electric low-pressure hot water boilers, air source heat pumps, solar-assisted heat pumps, ground source heat pumps, biomass boilers, combined heat and power and micro-CHP systems, heat networks, solar thermal systems, microgeneration installations, wind turbines and other emerging renewable heating and energy technologies. Associated heating and hot-water systems may include hot and cold water services, vented and unvented hot-water cylinders, oil storage tanks, flues, pumps, filling loops, pipework, radiators, low-surface-temperature radiators, fan convectors, controls, smart thermostats and associated electrical controls, together with pipework system cleaning, flushing, de-sludging, de-scaling, sterilisation, water treatment and pipe insulation. The framework will include annual heating safety checks and servicing, Landlord safety and compliance requirements, servicing and maintenance of thermostatic mixing valves and unvented cylinders, planned and responsive repairs, breakdown services, replacement of defective components and systems, void and mutual-exchange checks and emergency and out-of-hours attendance, including 24-hour, 365/366-day services where required. Electrical works and services will include complete and partial rewiring, upgrading, alteration, inspection, testing, certification, Electrical Installation Condition Reports and associated remedial works; consumer units and distribution equipment; RCBOs, RCDs/RCCBs, AFDDs and surge protection devices; main service intake works and associated DNO requirements; earthing and bonding; power, lighting and final circuits; sockets, switches and appliance supplies; immersion heaters; electric showers; connections to heating and boiler systems; external and communal/landlord lighting; supplies to outbuildings and external stores; extract fans and ventilation-related electrical works; doorbells; TV aerial cabling and outlets; photocells, time switches and lighting controls; and associated electrical equipment and systems. The electrical scope will also include domestic fire detection and smoke, heat and carbon-monoxide alarm systems and associated equipment, including interconnection and radio-frequency equipment, together with servicing, maintenance and responsive repair of electric heating installations and 24-hour breakdown provision. Electric vehicle charging infrastructure may be supplied and installed, including associated equipment and services required to provide fully operational charging installations. Mechanical works and services will include mechanical ventilation with heat recovery systems and associated equipment, thermostatic mixing valves, boosted cold-water pump installations and other mechanical equipment associated with heating, hot water, ventilation and energy systems, including servicing and maintenance where required. The decarbonisation and energy scope will include solar photovoltaic systems and associated services, including inverters, controls, metering, monitoring and battery storage systems, together with solar thermal, air source heat pumps, ground source heat pumps, solar-assisted heat pumps, biomass, CHP/micro-CHP, heat networks, wind turbines, mechanical ventilation with heat recovery, smart heating controls, sensors and monitoring equipment and other emerging renewable, low-carbon and energy-efficiency technologies associated with the heating, electrical, mechanical and decarbonisation scope that may be required during the life of the framework. The framework may support retrofit, decarbonisation, ventilation, overheating, indoor-air-quality, EPC improvement, net-zero and future energy-performance requirements, including requirements arising from grant-funded programmes. Retrofit assessment, energy and technical support services may include pre- and post-works Energy Performance Certificates, energy assessments, SAP10 assessments, retrofit assessments, retrofit coordination, retrofit design, PAS 2035 site visits, air-pressure testing, technical monitoring and cavity-wall borescope services, together with associated services. Legionella risk assessments may also be instructed where required in connection with the works and systems covered by the framework. Project management services may be provided for heating, electrical, mechanical, retrofit and decarbonisation programmes, including grant-funded programmes, and may include management and coordination of the appointed supplier's own works and/or coordination of works delivered in collaboration with other framework suppliers. Requirements may be delivered as individual property works, grouped schemes, planned programmes, servicing and compliance programmes, responsive repairs, emergency works, grant-funded projects and larger retrofit or decarbonisation programmes, together with associated services. The framework is intended to remain sufficiently flexible to respond to changes in legislation, technical standards, funding requirements and technology during its term, including the introduction of emerging renewable and energy-efficiency measures falling within the heating, electrical, mechanical and decarbonisation scope. Suppliers appointed to the framework, either directly or through their declared supply chain, will be required to have the capability to deliver the overall range of works and services included within the scope.

title: Langley Wood National Nature Reserve - tree felling contract
description:
Background to the job:
Natural England is managing ash dieback and hazardous trees along roads and footpaths. It is important that work is carried out sensitively and as specified, ensuring unnecessary damage to the woodland is avoided.
Timing:
Work must be completed by 28th February 2027, to avoid disturbance to nesting birds.
Nature of the job:
• Climbing ash trees is not permitted.
• The supplier will have the responsibility for carrying out checks of PRFs (Potential Roost Features). The supplier must have a trained person on site who is qualified to inspect PRFs for bat roosts. Supporting documentation of relevant training to be submitted with quote.
• With reference to the attached spreadsheet (Tree safety works 2026_27):
- Trees with PRFs will require inspection by a qualified person immediately prior to felling. If the PRF is identified as an active roost, work must stop on that tree immediately. If no active roost is present, the tree can be felled.
- Trees with no PRFs can be felled without further inspection.
• Any trees with PRFs that cannot be checked due to access issues should not be felled. A record of these trees must be kept and submitted to your contacts at Natural England.
• Trees to be felled have been sprayed clearly with the correlating number
• Trees to be reduced or dead-wooded will have a small yellow dot sprayed at the base
• Secondary identification tags are present in some cases.
• No felling over the NNR boundary is permitted unless agreed in advance.
• Trees must be felled to minimise damage to adjacent trees. The following is acceptable:
o Coppicing hazel or felling birch to clear the direction of fell
o Damage to oak branches below 10cm in diameter - providing no potential bat roosts are disturbed and no branches are left hanging from the canopy.
• For trees being felled with approximate diameters of 15cm or more, the main bole should be left whole if not on a path or boundary. Everything else can go into brash piles. In no access areas, the crowns do not need to be broken down, unless it's obviously unsafe.
• All other timber (below 15cm diameter) to be stacked in 2m lengths where convenient.
Site considerations:
Access by vehicle is only permitted as per the attached access map, vehicles must not be driven off the hard standing. Tracks are suitable for ATV/quad bikes only. 4 x 4 pick-ups/Land Rovers should only be used on the purple tracks (see site map). Any track or ground damage must be made good at the expense of the contractor..

title: Conditional Purchase Agreement for Linear Blocks
description:
This notice relates to an arrangement which includes a series of agreements, with the main object being a land transaction which the Council considers is exempted under paragraph 8, Schedule 2 of the Procurement Act 2023, (an agreement for the acquisition of land and buildings).  
Full details of the Council's intentions for the delivery of the housing scheme are set out in the Transparency Notice, notice identifier: 2026/s 000-043335 published 12 May 2026.
The Council considers that the land transaction pursuant to the Land Swap Agreement (as further detailed below) will not meet the definition of public "works contract" as Berkeley/St William (Berkeley) will not be obligated to complete any works pursuant to it.   The arrangements do include a series of ancillary agreements, as further set out below.  This includes an agreement for the conditional purchase and development of Linear Blocks, to which this notice specifically relates.  
The Council's Contract Award Notice with respect to this contract was published on 5 August 2026, with notice identifier: 2026/S 000-074289
The total "land swap" transaction will be contracted for in phases as follows:
Primary Agreement:
1.	Land Swap Agreement - Subject to achieving a satisfactory planning permission and  Berkeley (at its own volition) building to a "golden brick" level on the part of the Site known as "Block G"  (currently owned by Berkeley), Berkeley will transfer the freehold interest in Block G to the Council in return for the Council transferring its part of the Site to Berkeley. There will be additional balancing payments paid by each party to ensure the agreed price is received for each party's land.  
2.	Block G - Following completion of the land swap, Berkeley will obtain a permissive licence from the Council to continue to occupy Block G for the purposes of completing the construction of Block G (at its own volition) in accordance with the relevant planning permission, being the planning permission with reference 22/03224/EFUL as varied under reference 25/02547/VAR  for the construction of 92 dwellings.  Note that the Council do not consider that this arrangement meets the definition of a public works contract.
3.	Fit out works - Within the Land Swap Agreement, the Council will also have an option (but not an obligation) to call for Berkeley to enter a contract to upgrade the finish for Block G at an additional cost. The Council considers that if it chooses to enter into such an agreement in the future, the value of this contract will be below the threshold for a public works contract under the Procurement Act 2023.
Ancillary Agreement/s - to which this notice specifically relates
4.	Conditional Purchase Agreement for Linear Blocks - subject to completing the Land Swap Agreement, the site for the Linear Blocks will then be owned by Berkeley. Subject to funding and therefore at its option, the Council may purchase c120 dwellings known as the "Linear Blocks" from Berkeley at golden brick. The transfer will be conditional on the Council obtaining the relevant funding and Berkeley reaching golden brick
5.	Conditional Development Agreement for Linear Blocks - the parties will also be entering into a conditional development agreement to deal with the development of the Linear Blocks from golden brick level to practical completion. Due to ownership and access limitations only Berkeley could complete these development works.
Should any of the arrangements ultimately be considered caught within the definition of a public works contract, the Council considers it has reasonable grounds for a direct award under Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 in the circumstances (as explained below).
By way of background, Bath Western Riverside is a major component of the Council's SHLAA and housing delivery trajectory. The project was committed in 2010 and has successfully delivered 854 new homes with 25% affordable housing within phase 1.  
Bath Western Riverside Phase 2 (the Site) is the former Bath gas works site. The Site is part owned by the Council (which owns 31.5%), and part owned by St William Homes LLP (part of the Berkeley Group) (Berkeley) (which owns 68.5%). The Council intervened to acquire its part of the Site in 2019 for regeneration purposes with the objective to maximise the provision of affordable housing delivered given the viability challenges faced from the former land uses and site conditions. 
In order to comply with both planning and strategic housing aims, the Council must obtain a minimum number of affordable housing units across the Site as a whole and therefore has the option to either: procure the construction of such units itself, being restricted to its own part of the Site; or to increase provision by acquiring units from Berkeley (additionality) which will be constructed on Berkeley's land.  The Council has opted for the later arrangement.

title: Seasonal Observation Wheel Opportunity at Bedgebury National Pinetum
description:
Seasonal Observation Wheel Operator Opportunity
Bedgebury National Pinetum & Forest
Forestry England is seeking early market engagement from suitably experienced observation wheel operators regarding a potential seasonal concession opportunity at Bedgebury National Pinetum & Forest, one of the South East's premier outdoor visitor destinations.
Our aim is to explore the feasibility of introducing a temporary observation wheel during the Easter visitor peak period, enhancing the visitor experience while supporting engagement with the wider site. We invite operators to provide feedback on operational requirements, commercial arrangements, site suitability and delivery considerations.
This opportunity would initially be delivered as a seasonal trial within the 28-day permitted development allowance, with the potential to inform future opportunities should the trial prove successful.
About Bedgebury National Pinetum & Forest
Bedgebury National Pinetum & Forest is one of the South East's premier outdoor visitor destinations, welcoming over 500,000 visits annually. The site attracts a broad visitor audience including families, members, cyclists, runners, dog walkers and wellbeing users, and hosts a range of established commercial and recreational activities, including:
- A well-established café
- Go Ape high ropes adventure
- Bike hire provision
- Educational and learning activities
- Active Forests programmes, including running, cycling, yoga and wellbeing activities
- A year-round programme of events and seasonal experiences
Any temporary attraction must be sympathetic to the unique landscape setting of the National Pinetum and contribute positively to the overall visitor experience.
Opportunity Scope
Forestry England is seeking feedback regarding the feasibility and commercial potential of hosting a temporary mid-sized observation wheel (approximately 30 metres in height) during the Easter holiday period.
We are particularly interested in hearing from operators able to provide:
- Supply, installation, operation and removal of an observation wheel
- ADIPS-certified equipment and compliance with all relevant safety standards
- Compliance with Forestry England Health & Safety Standards including Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (CDM)
- Experienced operational staff throughout the operating period
- Details of technical, logistical and infrastructure requirements
- Power, servicing and site access requirements
- Evidence of successful delivery at parks, gardens, heritage venues, visitor attractions or environmentally sensitive locations
Proposed Operating Period
Initial Trial Indicative dates:
18 March 2027 - 17 April 2027
Possible future contract start date will be March 2028
These dates are subject to final confirmation but are intended to cover the main Easter holiday period, including Easter Monday, traditionally one of Bedgebury's busiest visitor days.
Commercial Approach
Forestry England is open to exploring a range of delivery and commercial models and welcomes feedback from operators regarding:
- Operational responsibilities
- Ticketing arrangements
- Customer management
- Marketing and promotional approaches
- Revenue share and commission-based models
- Fixed fee, minimum guarantee or alternative commercial structures
The expectation is that the selected operator would provide, install, operate and remove the attraction, however Forestry England welcomes proposals on the most effective operating model.
Information Requested
As part of this engagement exercise, Forestry England would welcome feedback on:
- Suitability of the proposed operating period
- Typical commercial arrangements for similar installations
- Infrastructure and site requirements
- Installation and removal timescales
- Operator experience and relevant case studies
- Any challenges, risks or considerations associated with delivering an observation wheel within a forest or arboretum setting

title: Tender for UV-Enhanced Tuneable Light Source
description:
Supply of a high-power UV-optimised tuneable light source (TLS) for use in spectroscopic applications such as photo deflection spectroscopy and external quantum efficiency. This equipment will be housed in the Centre for Integrative Semiconductor Materials (CISM) and will be used across the electrical engineering and physics departments.
To maximise the dynamic range available for in these spectroscopic experiments the output of the TLS should be maximised in the UV range (200-400 nm) with an average output power of at least 1 mW and a spectral bandwidth of less than 5 nm.
The current spectroscopic capabilities in CISM include near-infrared and visible photo thermal deflection and external quantum efficiency spectrometers. The expansion of these techniques to include UV wavelengths will enable CISM to perform spectroscopic and electro-optical analysis on wide bandgap semiconductors.

title: Continuous Testing (PTaaS) Service Agreement
description:
IMPORTANT: Please read this section before deciding whether you wish to register for this event. This section provides you with information regarding the scope of this procurement and details some of the key requirements that a successful applicant MUST be able to deliver.
This tender is for a new direct contract for a Continuous Testing supplier to implement and provide a fully governed continuous testing framework for IT covering penetration testing, red/purple team exercises, cyber stress testing, vulnerability discovery and remediation re-testing.  The preferred supplier must support red and purple team testing that will include a multi phase continuous testing model (e.g. tag and release), where red team activity transitions into purple teaming upon detection, and findings are shared in cycle while testing continues across subsequent phases. 
The service must include active collaboration with Thames Water teams during purple team activities, including validation of controls, detection capability, and response processes. 
The solution must demonstrate clear human oversight across testing, validation, and remediation activities, with automation used to support workflows (e.g. tracking, reporting, prioritisation) but not to replace core testing, validation, or assurance activities.
The supplier must support collaborative remediation and retesting, ensuring findings are handed over, validated, and retested with Thames Water teams, with end to end traceability through to closure. 
The following conditions would be considered as some of key requirements for a supplier to meet to be considered for this opportunity:
•	Availability of a yearly penetration test as a minimum
•	A fully functional PTaaS service that can deliver service in line with applicable cadences
•	A qualified, accredited and suitably vetted PTaaS support team

title: Rhydymwyn Wildlife Management Contract
description:
Defra intends to run an open tender to procure a new contract for the ecological management of the Defra-owned Rhydymwyn Valley site near Mold, Flintshire, and is seeking Expressions of Interest from suppliers capable of meeting the contract requirements.
Rhydymwyn Valley is a 35.5-hectare site of significant ecological, historic and community interest. It contains semi-natural broadleaf woodland, wetland, grassland, grassland-scrub mosaic, a traditional orchard, the River Alyn and historic structures, including listed buildings and two Scheduled Monuments.
The successful supplier will manage and maintain the site’s habitats and wildlife on Defra’s behalf, deliver species monitoring and ecological surveys, maintain specified visitor routes and wildlife-related infrastructure, and provide professional advice on matters affecting the site. Delivery must reflect the site’s ecological management plan, legal protections, the sites two protected species licences, health and safety requirements and restrictions arising from its historic use and ground conditions.
Key activities will include habitat management across wetlands, grassland, scrub, woodland, riverine habitat and the traditional orchard; management and monitoring of bats, birds, reptiles, amphibians (including Greater Crested Newts), butterflies, mammals and plants; control of invasive and noxious species; maintenance of the woodland trail, bird hide, bat and bird boxes, reptile refuges and other specified ecological features; and protection of listed buildings and Scheduled Monument areas through agreed vegetation management.
The supplier will be expected to work collaboratively with Defra, the site’s facilities management provider, relevant statutory bodies, local stakeholder groups, specialist societies and volunteers. The coordination and appropriate expansion of volunteer involvement will form an important part of maintaining the site, supporting monitoring activity, engaging the local community and delivering value for money.
The contract is expected to be let for an initial three-year term, with options to extend for up to two further one-year periods at the Authority’s discretion, subject to supplier performance, compliance with the specification and the continued requirements of the site.
The contractor will be required to deliver planned habitat and species management, undertake monitoring and surveys, maintain appropriate records, and provide four written reports each year: two habitat management reports and two species monitoring reports. The contractor will also maintain and update relevant risk information, notify Defra promptly of significant incidents, ecological changes or departures from agreed practice, and provide recommendations and mitigations where appropriate.
The successful supplier will be expected to provide effective contract and programme management, attend monthly meetings with the Defra Site Responsible Officer, manage staff, volunteers and any subcontractors safely, and maintain effective communication with Defra and site stakeholders. Performance will be managed through Key Performance Indicators covering conservation standards, species monitoring, habitat management, and health and safety risk management.
Any estimated value stated in this notice is indicative only and does not represent a guaranteed level of expenditure or a commitment by the Authority. The final contract value will depend on the outcome of the procurement and the services required.

title: Managed ICT Services for Stepney All Saints School
description:
Stepney All Saints Church of England Secondary School intends to award a contract for the provision of comprehensive managed ICT services to support the School's ICT infrastructure and day-to-day technology requirements.
The services include managed network and infrastructure support, wired and wireless networking, internet connectivity and filtering, cybersecurity support, backup and disaster recovery, Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace support, device and mobile device management, telephony, service desk provision, onsite technical support, asset management, systems monitoring and reporting, and associated ICT consultancy and project support.
The service will support approximately 1,450 student devices and 220 staff devices, together with the School's wider ICT infrastructure and associated onsite technical support arrangements.
The proposed contract with Classroom365 has an annual core managed service value of £149,734.80 excluding VAT, giving a total core contract value of £449,204.40 excluding VAT over the three-year contract term.
The procurement exercise was initially commenced with the support of Everything ICT, which had been engaged to assist the School with the procurement process. During the course of that process, the School decided to withdraw from the externally managed arrangement due to operational and decision-making issues concerning the management of the procurement.
Following that withdrawal, the School continued the procurement process internally. The substantive service specification and requirements remained materially unchanged, and the School continued to seek a provider for the same managed ICT services requirement.
Three suppliers submitted tenders, which were evaluated against the stated quality and price criteria. Following evaluation, Eduthing Ltd was initially identified as the highest-ranked supplier and the School's preferred supplier.
Following that decision, the School became aware in the due diligence process that Eduthing Ltd had entered administration. In light of this material change in circumstances, the School determined that it was not appropriate to proceed with the proposed contract award to Eduthing Ltd as they did not disclose this information to school at any stage.
The School therefore reviewed the outcome of the completed competitive evaluation and identified Classroom365 as the next highest-ranked suitable supplier. Classroom365 is accordingly the School's intended supplier for the managed ICT services contract.
During a subsequent review of the procurement documentation and publication requirements, the School was unable to locate the required UK4 Tender Notice on the Central Digital Platform in relation to the procurement which should have been issued by Everything ICT. The School had understood that the relevant procurement publication requirements were being managed during the earlier externally supported stage of the process.
As part of its review, the School has contacted Everything ICT to seek clarification regarding the original procurement notice and any publication information associated with the initial externally supported process. At the time of publication of this Transparency Notice, the School has not yet received a response or information confirming that the required UK4 Tender Notice was published.
In the absence of that clarification, and in order to ensure that the School's intended award is placed transparently on the public record, the School is publishing this Transparency Notice before proceeding further with the proposed contract award to Classroom365.
The School intends to publish a Contract Award Notice before entering into the contract and to observe the applicable standstill period before contract signature.

title: Senedd Business Management System
description:
The Commission is seeking to procure a fully bilingual (Welsh and English) Senedd business management system. The required solution will support functions including, but not limited to, Meeting Management, Senedd Member Management, Issue Management and the Management of Cross-Party Groups. The contract will include the supply, implementation and ongoing support of the solution. 
The Commission seeks a sustainable, adaptable and supportable solution that can meet its current and future business requirements while providing long-term value, service continuity and the benefits of ongoing product investment.
Suppliers must demonstrate:
•	successful delivery and operation of solutions with relevant or comparable capabilities; 
•	experience supporting parliamentary, legislative, democratic services, governance or similarly complex and regulated environments; 
•	an established, supportable and adaptable solution with demonstrable capability relevant to the Commission's requirements; 
•	a credible implementation and migration approach; and 
•	a clear, realistic and supportable route to meeting the Commission's functional and non-functional requirements
Suppliers must clearly distinguish between capabilities that are available within the proposed solution, those that will be delivered through configuration, and those that will require product development, customisation or other enhancement. Any such activity must form part of a credible, deliverable and supportable approach to meeting the Commission's requirements.
The Commission's strategic direction is to adopt Software as a Service (SaaS) solutions wherever appropriate. However, recognising the specialist nature of this market, suppliers may propose alternative delivery models where they can demonstrate that the proposed solution is an established, supportable and adaptable solution with demonstrable capability relevant to the Commission's requirements.
The Commission does not intend to commission the development of a wholly new solution. It is seeking approaches that maximise the reuse of existing and demonstrable capabilities, minimise bespoke development, and support long-term maintainability, interoperability, data portability, supplier competition and whole-life value.
The contract will be for an initial period of five years from the Go Live date, with the option for the Commission to extend the contract for up to a further five years.

title: GP IT and Corporate IT Support for NHS Thames Valley Integrated Care Board
description:
Thames Valley Integrated Care Board are seeking to directly award GP IT and Corporate IT services under Regulation 41 direct award justifications, s13/s14 set down within Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023.
In June 2025 it was announced that NHS Commissioning Support Units would be disbanded and additionally in September 2025 NHS England formally approved the merger of Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and West Berkshire Integrated Board ("BOB") and parts of Frimley Integrated Care Board to create Thames Valley Integrated Care Board.
In line with these changes to the NHS landscape, the incumbent supplier of GP IT and Corporate IT services for Thames Valley ICB will cease exist and therefore provide the service from December 2026.
Thames Valley ICB has been working in collaboration with Kent & Medway ICB and Surrey & Sussex ICB to develop a model for delivering GP IT and Corporate IT services on a regional basis and this continues to be the long-term ambition once the services are stabilised. 
However, it has become clear that, in the timescale required, establishing a Regional Operating Model was not feasible and therefore in June 2026 Thames Valley took the view that it needed to put mitigations in place to ensure that the service can remain stable between the cessation of the CSU provision and the eventual transfer into the regional model.
The infrastructure provision on which this service is based covers a wide number of NHS organisations and is being moved is being moved to a third party NHS host to ensure transitional stability.
The decision to directly award is due to:
•	The need to put mitigations in place to manage the risks arising from the timescale to join the Regional Operating Model at its inception.
•	Insufficient time to conduct a robust procurement process as the merged Thames Valley ICB needs to work at pace to mitigate the service gap or material operational disruption from the CSU service cessation.
•	Some of the services being delivered are subject to NHS Regulation Operators of Essential Services (OES) as such ICB's are required to ensure that there is continuity of these critical health services.
•	Due to the merger arrangements a single solution is sought for technical reasons which will provide parity of provision across the new geographic structure, this will also lead to shared resources across the GP IT and Corporate IT service structure.
•	Trusted Technology Partnership has a contract and presence within the cluster currently and is experienced at delivering GP IT services.
The merged Thames Valley ICB has considered the risks associated with not being able to do this direct award which include but not limited to:
•	GP IT infrastructure and support service lines fail due to the complex nature and timescales required to move these to new arrangements
•	Impact on patient care should GP IT support services be adversely impacted and fail
•	Management of the Corporate IT services for merged Thames Valley ICB would impact wider health service delivery.
•	Cyber risks
The contract duration is deemed to be the minimum necessary to address the urgent requirement with a contract period of 24 months (2 years) to stabilise services.
During this contract term a compliant procurement process will be undertaken. Thames Valley ICB anticipate seeking market engagement during Spring 2027[SN1.1]. Estimated core contract value for 24 months is circa £9.35m excluding VAT.
The publication of this notice marks the start of a voluntary standstill period which will run from 07/10/2026 ending midnight on 16/10/2026.
No declared conflicts or potential conflicts of interest were identified during the decision-making process
buyer: NHS THAMES VALLEY INTEGRATED CARE BOARD
