title: Teleradiology Reporting Services
description:
County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust (CDDFT) are seeking to appoint a single supplier to provide Teleradiology Reporting Services.  The Trust operates across two large acute sites and several non-acute sites, serving the population of County Durham and Darlington. 
At County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust, our vision is to deliver care which is right first time, every time. We are guided by our core values of respect and dignity, compassion, quality care, improving lives, everyone counts and working together for patients. 
By placing people and communities at the heart of all that we do, we strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment for both patients and our workforce, ensuring that every individual receives safe, compassionate and joined-up care. 
Reporting requirements will include but are not limited to: MRI, CT, Plain Film, Nuclear Medicine, with limited reporting requiring Specialist Radiologists. 
The Trust are seeking a supplier who is able to provide reporting services twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week for Urgent and Emergency Radiology Reporting, as well as provide Elective Reporting. There is no volume commitment as part of this contract and the demand from the Trust may vary overtime dependent on in house reporting capacity. However, the supplier would hold an exclusive contract for the out of hours provision to maintain continuity on the basis that the supplier can meet the turnaround time outlined by the Trust. However, for all other reporting, the Trust will be able to use alternative suppliers if desired. As demand fluctuates, the supplier must be able to adapt to high and low demands for reporting services. 
Bidding suppliers will be evaluated in line with the below Provider Selection Regime (PSR) Key Criteria regulated scoring:
 1:   Quality and Innovation: 20%
 2:   Improving Access, Reducing Health Inequalities and Facilitating Choice: 15%
 3:   Integration, Collaboration and Service Sustainability: 15%
 4:   Value - Price: 40%
 5:   Social Value: 10%
buyer: COUNTY DURHAM AND DARLINGTON NHS FOUNDATION TRUST

title: Haigh High Ropes: Expression of Interest
description:
Background:
The Haigh High ropes course sits within the regional destination Haigh Woodland Park. The destination is set within Wigan, a 330,000 resident base town within Greater Manchester. The Park is managed by Wigan Council with Be Well (Wigan Council’s in house Leisure & Wellbeing service) operating the High ropes course.
The High ropes course was funded by Wigan Council through a phase one transformation of the park in 2016. The phase one investment also featured investment within adventure play, adventure golf, visitor centre and café , a kitchen courtyard within the Stables complex alongside major improvements to the Parking facilities.
The ropes course is comprised of a low course with 9 obstacles and high ropes course with 11 obstacles including a 40 m zip line. The tower can also accommodate a range of team building activities. More recently Be Well has invested in a jump bag from the tower to add more variety and depth to the product offer. Details of the offer is available via the web link - https://www.bewelloutdoors.co.uk/locations/haigh-woodland-park.htm
The High ropes course at Haigh forms part of a broader Be Well Outdoor adventure offer that combines forest school activities at Haigh, water sports activities at Scotman’s Flash and residential and day activities at Low Bank Ground (on the shore of Lake Coniston).
Haigh Woodland Park is undergoing a major transformation with the benefit of secured Heritage Lottery Funding and secured Government grants through the Levelling up Funding programme. Combined the investment exceeds £50 million. The ambition is to transform Haigh Woodland Park into a cultural destination of national significance whilst retaining the significant local significance and appeal.
Visitor numbers currently exceed 500,000 per year and are expected to grow significantly with the introduction of the cultural and commercial offers within the restored Hall, the restoration of key heritage assets and infrastructure, the realisation of the Woodland management plan and the implementation of audience development plans to expand the reach into current and new audience profiles.
The Opportunity:
Be Well are exploring partnership options to support the evolution of the High ropes product within Haigh Woodland Park.
One of the options we are keen to understand is the market appetite to enter into a long-term partnership arrangement on the principle of an invest, maintain and operate model where risk and opportunity is transferred to a trusted operator whilst maintaining a principle of partnership working within the continued transformation of the destination.
At this stage we are open to a range of options and welcome comment and insight from the market on the scale and type of investment alongside the form and duration of operational partnership.
The future development of the High ropes product within Haigh Woodland Park would require co-ordination with the wider masterplan for the site alongside close co-ordination with the Woodland management strategy to arrive at a suitable phase two product capable of meeting the expected demand whilst being sensitive to the historic landscape.
How to Express Your Interest:
At this stage we are inviting interested parties to enter informal dialogue so that we can gauge the level of interest and shape the next stage of the options appraisal with the benefit of market insight.
To express your interest and to arrange the discussion (on site meeting and virtual meetings can be facilitated) please respond by email to Stuart Holden (Service Lead -  Strategic Development and Innovation) at Stuart.Holden@wigan.gov.uk. Within the response, please outline the following information:
•	Company name, registration number & official address
•	Main contact person and their contact details

title: Suffolk Alternative Provision Tier One (Outreach) Service
description:
Suffolk County Council (SCC) have awarded a contract for an Alternative Provision Tier One (Outreach) Service for an initial two-year period.
Whilst the contract was signed on 29 September 2026, the contract commenced on 01 September 2026.
The service involves delivering targeted early support within mainstream schools, supporting children across all Key Stages 1 - 4, to address emerging needs promptly. The goal is to provide assistance before challenges escalate for children, reducing the likelihood of exclusion, maximising engagement and participation in learning and promoting inclusion with the mainstream educational environment.
Timely outreach support and robust intervention with Children and Young People (CYP) to ensure they can succeed and remain in mainstream education will raise education attainment and skill levels.
This is important as these CYP are often our most vulnerable in our communities and failure to secure a good quality educational offer can often lead to a reliance upon other services such as social care or mental health providers.
The CYP who will be referred, and who will access the Tier 1 Outreach support, will have complex needs that will require the provider to tailor their approach to the individual needs of the young person. This will involve working in partnership with other agencies, schools and stakeholders as well as parents/carers and the young people themselves to ensure best outcomes.
The primary objective of Tier 1 AP is to provide specific support around barriers to learning and enable pupils to remain in their referring school.
The Special Educational Needs/Alternative Provision Service Development Team has a core focus on commissioning high quality educational provision for vulnerable and disadvantaged learners as well as ensuring that this cohort of pupils can make progress based on age, ability and prior achievement through easy access to a robust 'Local Offer' as set out in the SEND reforms (Special Education Needs and Disability Code of Practice: 0 to 25 years).
Historically there has been a significant increase in the number of young people permanently excluded across all Key Stages. Suffolk County Council has a continued commitment to provide the right intervention at the right time. As such, this Tier 1 AP Outreach programme can have a key impact to avoid exclusion.
The contract value in this notice includes the optional 24-month extension period.

title: ID624 - Major Works and Repairs Framework
description:
The Major Works & Repairs Framework has been developed to provide STAR Housing with a compliant, flexible and efficient route to procuring a wide range of property maintenance, repair, refurbishment and capital improvement works across its housing stock. Rather than undertaking individual procurement exercises for each requirement, the framework establishes a panel of pre-qualified suppliers who have demonstrated the technical capability, financial standing and operational capacity required to deliver works safely, efficiently and to a consistently high standard.
The framework has been designed to improve outcomes for residents by providing timely access to competent contractors, strengthening contract management, improving quality and consistency, and delivering value for money throughout the life of the framework. It also provides STAR Housing with the flexibility to respond to changing operational priorities while maintaining compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 and ensuring a transparent and auditable procurement process.
The framework comprises eight Lots covering Electrical, Mechanical, Major Works & Major Voids, Healthy Homes, Drainage, Pest Control, Tree Works, Scaffolding and Waste Management. The specialist Lots have been structured to reflect the scale, complexity and risk associated with each service, with proportionate financial and technical requirements designed to encourage competition and maximise participation from competent local and regional suppliers, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
Lot 2 - Major Works and Voids provides a comprehensive end-to-end solution for larger and more complex programmes of work, including planned maintenance, capital investment, major void refurbishment, external works, estate improvements and planned and reactive highways maintenance. By appointing one Principal Contractor, STAR Housing aims to achieve clear accountability, streamlined contract management, effective programme coordination and a consistent approach to quality, resident engagement and health and safety.
Under Healthy Homes, Lot 3, this provides a dedicated service for internal and external adaptations, specialist equipment, damp, mould and condensation remediation, and additional specialist surveys and investigations where instructed by STAR Housing.
The framework also recognises the important contribution local businesses make to the regional economy. Suppliers will be encouraged to maximise the use of local labour, apprenticeships, specialist subcontractors and regional supply chains wherever appropriate. This approach supports economic growth within Shropshire, reduces travel and associated carbon emissions, strengthens supply chain resilience and helps develop long-term partnerships with organisations that understand the local communities and housing stock.
Overall, the framework balances robust governance and statutory compliance with commercial efficiency, providing STAR Housing with a procurement solution that delivers value for money, supports excellent resident outcomes and creates sustainable opportunities for competent suppliers to work collaboratively in maintaining and improving the quality of its homes.
Stage 1: The Major Works & Repairs Framework has been developed to provide STAR Housing (based in Shropshire) with a compliant, flexible and efficient route to procuring a wide range of property maintenance, repair, refurbishment and capital improvement works across its housing stock. Rather than undertaking individual procurement exercises for each requirement, the framework establishes a panel of pre-qualified suppliers who have demonstrated the technical capability, financial standing and operational capacity required to deliver works safely, efficiently and to a consistently high standard.
The framework has 8 Lots and has been designed to improve outcomes for residents by providing timely access to competent contractors, strengthening contract management, improving quality and consistency, and delivering value for money throughout the life of the framework. It also provides STAR Housing with the flexibility to respond to changing operational priorities while maintaining compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 and ensuring a transparent and auditable procurement process. The Lots include:
Lot 1a - Electrical

Lot 2- Major Works and Major  Voids

The 4 year framework will be established using a Competitive Flexible Procedure comprising of the following:

title: Belgium – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Studie N33 Oostende Torhoutsesteenweg
description: Deze opdracht betreft een opdracht in 1 vast en 1 voorwaardelijk gedeelte. Het vast gedeelte betreft “Deel 1: Ontwerpstudie N33 Torhoutsesteenweg Oostende” Het voorwaardelijk gedeelte betreft “Deel 2: Haalbaarheidsstudie fietstunnels R31”. Deel 1: Ontwerpstudie N33 Torhoutsesteenweg Oostende (vast gedeelte) De Torhoutsesteenweg (N33) is één van de belangrijkste invalswegen van Oostende en verbindt de stad met het hinterland richting Torhout. Ze kruist onder meer de Elisabethlaan (R31), een belangrijke ringweg rond Oostende, en loopt verder richting Leffinge en Gistel. Dit specifieke traject: ligt in een sterk verstedelijkte zone met baanwinkels en bedrijven vormt een overgang tussen stadsverkeer en uitgaand regionaal verkeer wordt gebruikt door alle vervoersmodi tegelijk (auto’s, vrachtwagens, bus, fietsers en voetgangers) De belangrijkste kernproblemen van de Torhoutsesteenweg zijn een hoge verkeersonveiligheid, een structurele verkeerscongestie, een overmaat aan in- en uitritten naar en van parkings, een gebrek aan scheiding tussen verkeersfuncties, De projectstuurgroep van de ontsluitingsstudie Oostende concludeerde voor de N33 dat “de onderzochte maatregelen niet zorgen voor een betere doorstroming. De kleine voordelen naar verkeersveiligheid wegen niet op tegen de nadelen. Verder onderzoek is noodzakelijk.” Dit verder onderzoek maakt onderwerp uit van de voorliggende opdracht. Deze ontwerpstudie heeft tot doel om een volledig concept met startnota en voorontwerp met projectnota op te maken voor de N33 Torhoutsesteenweg tussen de R31 Elisabethlaan en de gemeentegrens met Middelkerke (“De Kromme Elleboog”). Verder dient een deel van de projectzone, nl. tussen de Steensedijk en de Rolbaanstraat (inclusief de kruispunten), d.i. tussen kmpt. 2,55 en 4,4) uitgewerkt te worden tot aanbestedingsbundel, inclusief de opmaak en ingave van het dossier voor de omgevingsvergunning. De diensten voor deel 1 omvatten: het uitvoeren van een topografische opmeting het opmaken van microsimulaties (voor bestaande toestand en ontwerpscenario’s) de opmaak van een concept en bijhorende goedgekeurde startnota de opmaak van een voorontwerp en bijhorende goedgekeurde projectnota de opmaak van een technisch ontwerp bovenbouw de opmaak en ingave van het dossier aanvraag omgevingsvergunning ondersteuning in communicatie (profiel communicatiedeskundige) opmaak van 3D-visualisaties in het kader van communicatie geraamde som voor drukwerk in het kader van communicatie en participatie Deel 2: Haalbaarheidsstudie fietstunnels R31 (voorwaardelijk gedeelte) De R31 vormt de ringweg rond Oostende en fungeert als een essentiële verkeersas voor zowel lokaal als doorgaand verkeer. Langs het traject bevinden zich verschillende woonzones, zijstraten met lokale ontsluitingsfunctie, verspreide handels- en dienstenactiviteiten, scholen en kruisende fietsverbindingen. Er is een duidelijke nood aan conflictvrije dwarsverbindingen voor fietsers en voetgangers. De belangrijkste problemen zijn: sterke verkeersdruk, complexe kruispunten, barrièrewerking voor fietsers en voetgangers. De haalbaarheidsstudie focust zich op de kruisingen voor fietsers in het deel van de R31 tussen de Zandvoordestraat en de Stuiversstraat (beide kruispunten inbegrepen). De diensten voor deel 2 omvatten: het opzoeken van de grenzen van het openbaar domein het uitvoeren van doorsnedetellingen (indien nodig) het opmaken van microsimulaties (voor bestaande toestand en ontwerpscenario’s) het opmaken van een haalbaarheidsstudie Voor beide delen van de studieopdracht geldt: Om tijdens het volledige ontwerpproces de nodige aandacht aan verkeersveiligheid, verkeerstechniek, human factor en wegontwerp te verzekeren, moet er binnen ieder ontwerpteam minstens één lid over een getuigschrift van een erkende opleiding tot verkeersveiligheidsauditor beschikken (https://www.vlaanderen.be/mobiliteit-en-openbare-werken/verkeer/verkeersveiligheidsaudit). Het is de taak van dit lid om knelpunten met betrekking tot de verkeersveiligheid voor de verschillende categorieën weggebruikers op te sporen, de ernst daarvan te benoemen en het ontwerpproces daarop te (laten) bijsturen. Voor goedkeuring van projectnota en aanbestedingsfase uitvoering zal de opdrachtnemer een overleg voorzien waarbij de ontwerpplannen met opdrachtgever en het teamlid doorgenomen worden. Aandachtspunten en genomen afwegingen worden met de nodige achtergrondinformatie opgelijst in een naslagwerk zodat deze in de vervolgstappen (tot en met overdracht aan het bevoegde wegendistrict) niet telkens opnieuw in vraag gesteld worden. Voor een uitgebreide omschrijving van het voorwerp van de opdracht wordt verwezen naar de technische bepalingen.

title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – Projektträgerschaft für das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) im Bereich Technologische Souveränität und Innovationen – Schlüsseltechnologie Batterie
description: In der Batterieforschung priorisiert das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) zukünftig Maßnahmen, die auf das Ziel „Aufbau einer wettbewerbsfähigen Batterieproduktion und -kreislaufführung in Deutschland, eingebettet in ein europäisches Produktionsnetzwerk bis 2035“ der Hightech-Agenda Deutschland (HTAD) einzahlen. Die Erreichung technologischer Souveränität und Schaffung neuer Wertschöpfung in Deutschland sind die zentralen Ziele der zugehörigen BMFTR-Fördermaßnahmen. Die Kernaufgaben bei der Projektförderung betreffen die fachliche Begleitung und Unterstützung der Forschungs- und Innovationspolitik des Auftraggebers (AG). Hierzu zählt die Unterstützung des AG bei der Erstellung von Strategie- und Planungsunterlagen sowie Konzepten im Zusammenhang mit der Umsetzung, Fortschreibung und Evaluation der Förderprogrammatik. Ferner beinhalten sie – auch umfassende – Unterstützungsaufgaben des Auftragnehmers (AN) für den AG im unmittelbaren Zusammenhang mit dem Fördergeschäft, u. a. bei der Fachinformation, der Durchführung von Terminen, bei weitergehenden innovationsunterstützenden Maßnahmen wie Technology Monitoring/Foresight und der Strategieentwicklung. Die begleitenden Aufgaben stehen in weiterem Zusammenhang mit dem Fördergeschäft und umfassen insbesondere die Unterstützung des AG bei weiteren Aufgaben, etwa bei der Titelbewirtschaftung, der Fachinformation oder Vergaben. Im Sinne der effizienten Programmbetreuung sind durch den AN auch Methoden und Tools unter Einbeziehung künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) im Rahmen dieser Aufgaben einzusetzen. Dabei muss die fachlich-technisch-wissenschaftliche sowie administrative Betreuung der Fördervorhaben durch entsprechend ausgebildete und geschulte Mitarbeitende des AN in ausreichendem Maße sichergestellt bleiben, die genutzten KI-Anwendungen sind regelmäßig auf Plausibilität zu prüfen

description: 1. Die BOSS umfasst eine Fläche von ca. 10 ha mit ca. 20 Gebäuden unterschiedlicher Nutzung (Verwaltungs-, Unterkunfts-, Dienstgebäude, Werkstätten sowie Lagergebäude). Die „Dahme-Spree-Kaserne (DSK)“ liegt in Berlin-Grünau. Die DSK beherbergt das Karrierecenter der Bundeswehr in Berlin sowie das Bildungszentrum der Bundeswehr und wurde größtenteils in den Jahren 1932 – 1934 errichtet. Ergänzende bauliche Anlagen entstanden bis in das Jahr 2009. Die DSK umfasst eine Fläche von ca. 13 ha mit ca. 17 zum Teil teilsanierten Gebäuden mit unterschiedlicher Nutzung (Verwaltungs-, Unterkunftsgebäude, Garagen/ Lagergebäude, Wachgebäude, Wirtschaftsgebäude mit Vollküche und Speisesaal sowie eine Sporthalle). Der Flughafen Tegel-Nord (FTN) ist der militärische genutzte Teil des ehemaligen Flughafens Tegel. Hier ist die Flugbereitschaft des Bundesministeriums für Verteidigung untergebracht. Ein Teil der in den 1950er-Jahren errichteten Gebäude steht unter Denkmalschutz. Der FTN umfasst eine Fläche von ca. 10 ha mit Gebäuden unterschiedlicher Nutzung (Verwaltungs-, Unterkunfts-, Kantinengebäude, Werkstätten, Hallen sowie einem Wachgebäude). Die „Standorthallenschießanlage (STOSCH)“ wurde größtenteils in den Jahren 1968 bis 1971 in Berlin-Tegel errichtet. Die STOSCH umfasst eine Fläche von ca. 2,5 ha mit ca. 8 Gebäuden unterschiedlicher Nutzung (Schießhalle, Wohnhaus, Garage, Werkstattgebäude, Trafostation). Das „Wohnheim Waldstraße (WALD)“ wurde in den 1970er Jahren in Berlin-Köpenick errichtet. Die Unterkunftsgebäude wurden in den Jahren 2015 bis 2017 saniert. Das WALD umfasst eine Fläche von ca. 2,5 ha und besteht neben den Unterkunftsgebäuden aus einem Kantinengebäude, einer Heizzentrale und einer Sporthalle. Das „Wohnheim Walchenseestraße (WALCH)“ in Berlin-Köpenick wurde ebenfalls in den 1970er Jahren errichtet und im Jahr 2013 saniert. Das WALCH umfasst eine Fläche von ca. 1,2 ha und besteht aus einem Unterkunftsgebäude und einer Sporthalle. Das „Wohnheim Nordpromenade (WNP)“ wurde 1955 gebaut und liegt in Berlin-Biesdorf. title: Germany – Construction work for pipelines, communication and power lines – Sanierung Hallenbad Weikersheim_2.BA_Elektro-, Starkstrom-, Fernmeldeanlage 2.BA
description: Gewerk: Elektro-, Starkstrom-, Fernmeldeanlage - 2. BA Die Stadt Weikersheim beabsichtigt die weitere Sanierung des bestehenden Hallenbades in 97990 Weikersheim, Humboldtstraße 1. Das Hallenbad ist baulich in den Schulkomplex des Gymnasiums integriert und besteht aus drei Geschossen. Im Untergeschoss befinden sich die technischen Anlagen für den Badbetrieb. Das Erdgeschoss umfasst die Schwimmhalle, Umkleidebereiche mit Dusch- und WC-Anlagen, den Schwimmmeisterraum, die Eingangshalle sowie den Personal- und Kassenbereich. Im Obergeschoss befindet sich ein Technikraum für die Lüftungsanlage. Die Gesamtsanierung des Hallenbades erfolgt in zwei Bauabschnitten. Der 1. Bauabschnitt befindet sich bereits in Ausführung und umfasst im Wesentlichen die Erneuerung der Schwimmhalle, des Schwimmmeisterraums, der Eingangshalle sowie des Personal- und Kassenbereichs und einen Teil der technischen Anlagen und Technikräume. Gegenstand der vorliegenden Ausschreibung ist die Ausführung der Elektro-, Starkstrom- und Fernmeldeanlagen im 2. Bauabschnitt. Der 2. Bauabschnitt umfasst im Wesentlichen die Sanierung und Modernisierung der Umkleidebereiche einschließlich der Dusch- und WC-Anlagen im Erdgeschoss sowie die Erneuerung bzw. Anpassung der Badewassertechnik im Untergeschoss. Im Zuge der Baumaßnahme sind die hierfür erforderlichen elektrotechnischen Anlagen entsprechend den planerischen Vorgaben neu herzustellen, zu ergänzen, anzupassen bzw. zurückzubauen. Der ausgeschriebene Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere die erforderlichen Starkstromanlagen, Beleuchtungsanlagen, Installationsanlagen, Stromversorgungen, Verteilungen und Unterverteilungen sowie die zugehörigen Kabel- und Leitungsanlagen. Darüber hinaus sind die im Rahmen des 2. Bauabschnitts erforderlichen Fernmelde-, Kommunikations-, Sicherheits- und sonstigen elektrotechnischen Anlagen entsprechend den Vergabe- und Planungsunterlagen auszuführen. Die Leistungen sind im bestehenden Hallenbad und unter Berücksichtigung der vorhandenen baulichen und technischen Gegebenheiten auszuführen. Bestehende Anlagen und Installationen sind, soweit erforderlich, fachgerecht zurückzubauen, anzupassen, zu ergänzen oder in die neu herzustellenden Anlagen einzubinden. Die Schnittstellen zu den übrigen Gewerken, insbesondere zur Badewassertechnik, Sanitär-, Heizungs-, Lüftungs- und Gebäudeautomationstechnik, sind entsprechend den Planungsunterlagen zu berücksichtigen und abzustimmen. Zum Leistungsumfang gehören sämtliche für die vollständige, funktionsgerechte und fachgerechte Herstellung der ausgeschriebenen elektrotechnischen Anlagen erforderlichen Liefer-, Montage-, Anschluss-, Prüf- und Inbetriebnahmeleistungen einschließlich der erforderlichen Neben- und Anpassungsarbeiten, soweit diese in den Vergabeunterlagen beschrieben sind. Die Ausführung erfolgt im Bestand und unter laufender Berücksichtigung der Bauabläufe des 2. Bauabschnitts. Sämtliche Leistungen sind entsprechend den anerkannten Regeln der Technik, den einschlägigen gesetzlichen und technischen Vorschriften sowie den Vorgaben der Planungs- und Vergabeunterlagen auszuführen. Die Ausführung des 2. Bauabschnitts ist im Rahmen der Gesamtmaßnahme für den Zeitraum von Januar 2027 bis September 2027 vorgesehen.

description: Väyläviraston ja elinvoimakeskusten hankkeissa käytettäville uusiomateriaaleille on tehtävä teknisen soveltuvuuden arviointi. title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – Dienstleistungsauftrag für eine Geschäftsstelle zur Evaluation der Ausgestaltung der Gemeinschaftsaufgabe Forschungsbauten und Großgeräte an Hochschulen nach AV-FGH durch eine unabhängige Evaluationskommission
description: Bund und Länder wirken seit 2007 bei der Förderung von Forschungsbauten an Hochschulen einschließlich Großgeräten zusammen. Ziel dieser Gemeinschaftsaufgabe ist es, die investiven Voraussetzungen der deutschen Hochschulen für eine erfolgreiche Teilnahme am nationalen und internationalen Wettbewerb in der Forschung zu verbessern. Zu den förderfähigen Investitionsvorhaben zählen Forschungsbauten sowie Großgeräte. Die gemeinsame Förderung von Forschungsbauten und Großgeräten durch Bund und Länder soll durch eine unabhängige Evaluationskommission evaluiert werden, deren Vorsitz mit Frau Prof. Dr. Felser (Berufung erfolgte mit Schreiben der Vorsitzenden der GWK) bereits feststeht. Die bis zu neun weiteren Mitglieder der Kommission werden der GWK zur Beschlussfassung in der kommenden Sitzung am 10.07.2026 vorgelegt werden. Aufgabe der Evaluationskommission wird es sein, eine übergreifende, vorrangig qualitative Bewertung der Gemeinschaftsaufgabe zu erarbeiten. Zur Koordinierung, Administration sowie Unterstützung der Evaluationskommission soll ein Dienstleistungsauftrag für eine Geschäftsstelle europaweit ausgeschrieben werden. Zu den Aufgaben der Geschäftsstelle gehören insbesondere die Aufbereitung der von den an der Gemeinschaftsaufgabe beteiligten Akteuren zur Verfügung gestellten Daten, das Verfassen von Textentwürfen, die Abschlussredaktion des Evaluierungsberichts sowie die Organisation und Durchführung der Kommissionssitzungen und etwaiger Vor-Ort-Begehungen der Evaluationskommission. Auch soll eine Befragung von Antragstellern für Großgeräte auf der Grundlage der Antragstellungen mit dem Schwerpunkt auf den Zeitraum der AV-FGH durchgeführt werden (rd. 2.700 Anträge seit 2019).

description: Der Auftraggeber, die NEW Smart City GmbH, ist ein Unternehmen der NEW-Gruppe und entwickelt sowie betreibt innovative und nachhaltige Infrastruktur- und Energielösungen. Zu den Tätigkeitsfeldern gehören insbesondere Projekte in den Bereichen Wärmeversorgung, Energieeffizienz und kommunale Infrastruktur. Mit ihren Projekten leistet die NEW Smart City GmbH einen Beitrag zur nachhaltigen und zukunftsorientierten Entwicklung der Region. Die Gesellschaft setzt dabei auf wirtschaftliche, ökologische und technisch innovative Lösungen. Die NEW Smart City GmbH beabsichtigt die Vergabe von Planungsleistungen zur Transformation eines bestehenden Wärmenetzsystems auf der Voltastraße in Mönchengladbach in Anlehnung an die Leistungsphasen 2 bis 4 der HOAI. Grundlage der Planung ist ein bereits vorliegender Transformationsplan gemäß BEW (Bundesförderung für effiziente Wärmenetze), deren Ergebnisse und Vorzugsvariante durch den Auftragnehmer zu berücksichtigen, zu prüfen und in eine genehmigungsfähige Planung zu überführen sind. Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Beauftragung eines geeigneten Planungsbüros mit Planungsleistungen zur Fortschreibung, Vertiefung und Überführung der in der Transformationsstudie entwickelten Vorzugsvariante in eine umsetzungsorientierte und genehmigungsfähige Planung. Die Leistungen um-fassen insbesondere die Vorplanung, Entwurfsplanung und Genehmigungsplanung in Anlehnung an die Leistungsphasen 2 bis 4 der HOAI. Ein wesentlicher Bestandteil der Leistung ist die Prüfung, Konkretisierung und technische Ausarbeitung der im Rahmen der Transformationsstudie entwickelten Lösungsansätze und der Vorzugsvariante. Die Planung hat die technischen, wirtschaftlichen, ökologischen sowie genehmigungsrechtlichen Anforderungen zu berücksichtigen. Darüber hinaus sind die Anforderungen der Bundesförderung für effiziente Wärmenetze (BEW) einzuhalten.

title: The Essex Carers Hub
description:
The Essex Carers Hub (formerly the Essex Carers Core Offer of Support (ECCOS)). 
Essex County Council ("the Council") is committed to delivering high-quality, sustainable and preventative services that improve outcomes for residents and reduce inequalities. The Essex Carers Hub ("the Service") will support these ambitions by ensuring unpaid carers are identified early, recognised, valued and able to access timely support that promotes their wellbeing, resilience and independence. Through partnership working and a strengths-based approach, the Service will help carers improve or maintain their quality of life and prevent the escalation of need wherever possible. 
The Council is seeking a Provider, or lead provider working with delivery partners, to deliver the Essex Carers Hub, a countywide carers specialist support service that improves the wellbeing, resilience and quality of life of unpaid carers aged 18 and over. The Service also includes a counselling offer for Young Carers and Young Adult Carers under the age of 18 who are referred by Essex Youth Service. 
For the purposes of this tender a Carer is defined as follows;
"A person who provides unpaid care and support to a family member, partner, friend or neighbour who could not manage without that support due to illness, frailty, disability, mental health need, substance misuse or other support needs. All the care they give is unpaid. A carer can be a young carer (under the age of 18) or an adult carer (over the age of 18). That is ordinarily resident in the Council's administrative area" 
The following services are in scope of this procurement;
 - Specialist Information Advice and Guidance
 - Coaching and Counselling
 - Peer Support Groups
 - Wellbeing grants (ordinarily up to £300)
 - Training and Learning Offer
 - Single Point of Contact
 - Employment support (2 year pilot)
Please note that authority for carers assessments and personal budgets will still remain with the Council.
The services shall be available to Carers resident within the administrative area of Essex County Council, but will have the scope to be expanded to the administrative areas of Southend-on-Sea City Council and Thurrock Council.
Following feedback from Carers and the market, the contract is being tendered as a single contract rather than being divided into lots. Carers have expressed a preference for a consistent and co-ordinated service, with clear accountability and minimal disruption. This approach would support continuity of service as it is expected that carers will access more than one of the service elements at any one time, as well as clearer communication and a consistent approach to meeting Carer needs.
Please note the contract value includes circa £500k per year available for the provision of the Wellbeing Grants that will be administered by the Provider.

title: Mentoring in Education
description:
for the delivery of Mentoring in Education within Nottingham City and Nottinghamshire County.
The programme is an initiative aimed at providing tailored support to children within schools and extended to the local community. It is a preventative programme to engage children who are showing first signs of disengagement from education, through to those considered at risk of exclusion and those children have been exposed to serious violence predominantly as a witness or victim.
The service will be based across 8 primary school settings that have been identified as having a high level of need, as well as working with children across community spaces as necessary. This project seeks to address the diverse needs of these students through a 1-2-1, trauma-aware, complex needs approach package. Mentors will equip children with the tools and resources necessary to develop positive behaviours, effective communication skills, resilience and improve educational outcomes and objectives.
This is a programme designed to work directly within the school setting extending to the community as required, mentors will be expected to work closely alongside the safeguarding and pastoral teams within each of the identified education establishments. The Nottingham and Nottinghamshire Violence Reduction Partnership (NNVRP) will provide support identifying schools and the initial engagement stages. There may also be a need to work beyond the remit of the school if appropriate, providing wider support to families.
buyer: The Police and Crime Commissioner for Nottinghamshire

title: Mentoring in Hospital & Police
description:
For the delivery of mentoring (hospitals and police pathway) within Nottingham City and Nottinghamshire.
These services are being commissioned by the Nottingham and Nottinghamshire Violence Reduction Partnership (NNVRP) - part of the Nottinghamshire Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner (OPCC). The objective is to support children and young people (CYP) who may be at risk of involvement in serious violence with improved mental health and wellbeing and improved behaviours, thus reducing the risk factors associated with violent crime and helping to build community resilience.
This approach draws on the Accident and Emergency (A&E) and Police Custody Navigator model which has been rated by the Youth Endowment Fund (YEF) as having a potentially high impact on serious violence.
The service will be based in the community but will pro-actively reach and engage with children in several settings including custody suites (Nottingham City and Mansfield) and Hospital (Nottingham Queens Medical Centre ) as well as take referrals from these sites and from other partners as agreed with the commissioner.
Through engaging and working with children most vulnerable to violence, the service will make a tangible contribution to preventing and reducing serious violence affecting those under 18-years-old in our area.

title: Lightning Protection Systems And Person Safety Systems
description:
Anchor Hanover Group is England’s largest not-for-profit provider of specialist housing and care for those later in life. We manage 54,000 homes for both rent and sale to those aged 55 and over.
Lightning Protection Systems (LPS) and Person Safety Systems represent safety-critical assets across Anchor's portfolio. These systems help protect our buildings, residents, employees, contractors and visitors from risks associated with lightning strikes, the resulting fire risk, and working at height activities with fixed assets. Ensuring that these assets are appropriately identified, maintained, repaired and replaced forms an important part of Anchor's compliance and asset management responsibilities. 
Based on current records, LPS are understood to be present at approximately 262 locations, while Person Safety Systems are identified at approximately 44 locations. Bidders shall note that asset information continues to be reviewed and validated, and should therefore be considered indicative.
The future scope of service is expected cover, but is not limited to, the following activities across LPS and Person Safety System assets:
- Inspection, testing and PPM (Planned Preventative Maintenance)
- Repair (emergency and responsive)
- Replacement
- Installation
- Baseline survey, assessment and inclusion within service activities of undocumented assets
- Maintenance of an asset register
Anchor defines that an LPS includes the external lightning protection system and associated internal protection or interfaces:
- Air termination networks
- Conductors
- Down conductors
- Test joints
- Earth electrodes
- Bonding
- Separation distance arrangements
- Surge protection measures where applicable
- Warning labels
- Inspection pits
Person Safety Systems which are expected to fall under the contract's scope are:
- Single-point anchors, eyebolts, anchor posts and safety hooks
- Horizontal flexible lifelines, rigid rails and travelling anchor systems

title: HWTWRP Continued ME4
description:
The Hampshire Water Transfer and Water Recycling Project (The Project) is a Strategic Resource Option (SRO) and a major part of Southern Water’s long-term strategy to address the significant water supply shortfall in Hampshire. By using advanced water treatment technologies, the Project will transform treated wastewater, normally pumped far out to sea, into purified recycled water. This new resource will supplement natural spring water from Portsmouth Water’s Bedhampton Springs, with both sources being stored in the new Havant Thicket Reservoir. This integrated approach will maximise the reservoir’s capacity, ensuring greater water availability, especially during periods of drought. Water from the reservoir will be transferred to our existing Otterbourne Water Supply Works, where it will undergo further treatment to strict drinking water standards prior to going into supply. By establishing a sustainable and resilient water source, the Project will help safeguard essential water supplies for our customers while reducing reliance on environmentally sensitive water sources.
The Project consists of a Water Recycling Plant, tunnel and pipeline connections, a High Lift Pumping Station, and a circa 42 km transfer to Otterbourne Water Supply Works inclusive of intermediate pumping stations and break pressure tanks. The Project scope includes Design, Build, Finance, Maintain and Operate (DBFOM) of new water infrastructure, including water recycling, water transfer, and substantial tunnelling works. The Project will be procured using Ofwat’s Direct Procurement for Customers (DPC) model, with a Competitively Appointed Provider (CAP) to deliver the DBFOM project. Under the DPC model, Southern Water plan to openly tender for a CAP. Southern Water has carried out several market engagement exercises to support this procurement. Southern Water does not guarantee that all activities referenced by the CPV codes will form part of any future tender notice(s), nor is the list exhaustive of all activities which may be included in any procurement process under this Project.

title: WBS-FTS-64245 Haematology Testing System
description:
The Welsh Blood Service (WBS) requires an advanced automated haematology analysis system to support blood donor assessment, blood component quality monitoring, research and innovation activities. The proposed solution will be required to provide automated full blood count (FBC) analysis, 5-part white cell differential capability and integrated reticulocyte analysis on the primary analyser. Of particular interest are systems capable of generating the data required to support emerging donor health assessment methodologies, including FlowScore calculation and reticulated haemoglobin analysis for the early detection of iron deficiency in blood donors.
The requirement is includes advanced analytical capabilities that support the unique operational needs of a blood establishment. These include fluorescence platelet counting with high accuracy at low platelet concentrations, reticulated platelet measurement, low-level white cell enumeration suitable for blood component quality monitoring, and the ability to perform blood component testing without the need for separate instrumentation. Suppliers should be able to demonstrate how their platforms support routine blood component quality control programmes through dedicated blood bank functionality and provide evidence of successful implementation within blood services, blood centres or comparable blood establishments. WBS is particularly interested in solutions that are supported by robust External Quality Assessment (EQA/EQAS) programmes and can demonstrate meaningful peer group benchmarking through sufficient participant numbers using the same analyser platform and methodology. Suppliers should be able to demonstrate compliance with applicable medical device regulations, support quality and regulatory requirements through a mature quality management system and provide resilient service and maintenance arrangements that minimise downtime and ensure continuity of critical testing services.

title: Intent to direct award to CIPFA for training on leadership in public sector finance roles
description:
CIPFA LEAD occupies a genuinely distinct position in the leadership development marketplace, and one that cannot be readily replicated by a generic leadership or management training provider. It is the only programme, in our view,  that combines CIPFA's standing as the recognised professional body for public finance with a leadership curriculum built specifically around the statutory realities of the Section 151 and other senior roles that support it in UK local government.  The programme explores political accountability, governance failure, guardianship of the public purse, and the technical currency that S151 officers and their teams are required to hold. A general leadership provider could offer coaching, stakeholder management or resilience training in isolation; only CIPFA can embed that development within the actual regulatory, governance and technical context in which Welsh finance leaders operate.
The programme's structure is itself evidence of a deliberately flexible, rather than an off-the-shelf leadership course. Delivery is mixed between virtual and in-person modules, sequenced to minimise time away from the authority, and deliberately avoids formal examination or heavy homework, recognising that participants are serving finance leaders, not full-time students. Each module is built to be applied directly against participants' own live challenges, from the CFO Competency Model's individual development discussion in Module 2 through to the practical stakeholder and political-environment content in Modules 3 and 4. This is a programme designed to flex around the demands of the role, not one participants must reshape their working lives to fit.
The 2025-26 Wales cohort (the first of its kind) provides direct, current evidence that this approach delivers. The programme achieved a mean satisfaction score of 4.8 out of 5, with 100% of participants agreeing or strongly agreeing with the programme's core outcome statements and 100% saying they would recommend it to a peer. Participant testimonials specifically credit the programme with building confidence as a finance leader and creating a genuine peer network across the sector: a benefit that is only available by continuing with CIPFA, since it depends on the existing Wales-wide finance leadership cohort and relationships CIPFA has already established, not something a new provider could offer from a standing start.
Continuity with CIPFA for 2026-27 also directly addresses the workforce capacity and succession planning risk that the programme was created to respond to. Welsh local authorities face a well-documented pipeline challenge in developing future S151 officers and other senior finance leaders and running the same LEAD framework for a second year sustains a common leadership language and competency framework across the Welsh finance community, builds on the alumni network already established, and avoids the cost, delay and lost momentum of re-procuring and re-designing an equivalent programme with an unproven alternative provider. Given the demonstrated outcomes, the sector-specific depth CIPFA alone can offer, and the direct continuity benefit to succession planning across Welsh local government, CIPFA represents the only supplier capable of delivering this programme to the required (high) standard, and a single tender award is justified on grounds of both quality and value for money

title: Digital Primary Care Open Framework
description:
PLEASE NOTE - This is not a 'call to action' notice and requires no response to the Authority.
This notice is published in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 as a Planned Procurement Notice (UK3). It provides advance notice that NHS England intends to establish an open framework using the competitive flexible procedure for the future procurement of Digital Primary Care General Practice Information Technology (GPIT) solutions, ahead of the publication of a tender notice.
Digital systems are fundamental to the delivery of modern general practice services. NHS England's Digital Services for Integrated Care (DSIC) programme is improving digital products across care settings to support and enable an integrated care system, working with technology suppliers to deliver a choice of commonly assured, intuitive and innovative products and services. This framework will be key to this, as well as supporting commitments in the NHS 10 Year Health Plan (10YHP), national digital strategy, and the GP Contract’s digital requirements.
For the purposes of this procurement, GPIT encompasses the digital solutions (products and services) that support the commissioning, delivery, administration and continuous improvement of general practice. This includes technologies used by clinicians, administrative staff, patients and commissioners to facilitate access to care, care delivery, clinical decision-making, service integration, population health management and operational efficiency.
The technology used in general practice falls into two groups: core digital capabilities needed to deliver care, including the recording, management and access of patient health information (‘Foundation’ Electronic Patient Record solutions); and broader digital capabilities which provide clinical and operational support solutions to complement, extend or enhance the core digital capabilities (sometimes referred to as ‘Non-Foundation’ solutions). 
The Authority intends to establish a lotted open framework in accordance with section 49 of the Procurement Act 2023. It is anticipated that the framework will provide a simplified route to market for General Practice Information Technology (GPIT), enabling access to innovative digital solutions whilst securing value for money for the NHS. 
The indicative lotting structure is as follows:
• Lot 1: Foundation Electronic Patient Record (EPR) Solutions
• Lot 2: Clinical and Operational Support Solutions
• Lot 3: Research and Development 
The above Lots are characterised by the digital capabilities they consist of. For further description of the capabilities listed below, please see the supporting document attached titled ‘Description of Framework Capabilities’.  
Further details of the requirements for appointment to the framework will be available in the tender documentation. 
Lot 1 (Foundation Solutions) will consist of the following capabilities:
• Appointments Management - GP
• Consultation Management - GP 
• Patient Information Maintenance - GP
• Prescribing - GP
• Referral Management - GP
• Resource Management 
Lot 2 (Clinical and Operational Support Solutions) will consist of the following capabilities:
• Advice and Guidance (Professional to Professional)
• Care Plans
• Caseload Management
• Clinical Decision Support
• Communication Management
• Cross Organisation Appointment Booking
• Cross Organisation Workforce Management
• Custom Workflows
• Digital Diagnostics
• Digital Dictation
• Dispensing
• Document Management
• Domiciliary Care
• Emergency Alerts
• GP Extracts Verification
• Medical Reports
• Medicines Optimisation 
• Population Health Management
• Remote Patient Monitoring
• Reporting
• Risk Stratification
• Scanning
• Self-Service Appointment Check In
• Social Prescribing
• Task Management
• Telecare
• Video Consultation
Lot 3: Research and Development
This lot will offer successful suppliers on Lots 1 and 2 the opportunity to be involved in research and development to aid the authority with developing and proving out new capabilities and standards through discovery to public beta activities, covering key areas required to evolve solutions and support national strategy.
The framework will:
• Permit the appointment of multiple suppliers to each lot;
• Permit the appointment of same suppliers across different lots;
• The framework is expected to reopen at planned intervals during its term; and
• Allow for auto enrolment (unless opted out of) onto Lot 3 for successful suppliers awarded a place on Lot 1 or Lot 2.
Call-off contracts will be run and awarded primarily by (but not limited to) Integrated Care Boards and general practices through mechanisms that may include direct award and competitive flexible procedures in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. Detailed service models, delivery requirements, and performance expectations will be set out in future tender documentation which will be made available through Find a Tender when the UK4 Tender Notice is published.
Indicative Timeline:
The framework procurement will follow a multi-stage competitive flexible procedure and is intended to be issued in November 2026, subject to final governance approvals that are currently in progress. Framework go-live is expected in Q3 2027. A full procurement timetable will be available in the published tender notice and tender documentation. 
Please note: this timetable is indicative and subject to change.  The dates set out in the UK4 Tender Notice will take precedence.
Prior Notices
Formal market engagement for this Procurement took place between May and June 2025. Full details of this and materials released in the market engagement will be shared alongside the future tender documentation. 
Notice Status and Disclaimer
This Planned Procurement Notice is issued to provide advance market visibility only. It is not a call for competition, an invitation to tender, a request for information, or request for commitment to proceed with a procurement. The information and dates contained in this notice are indicative and subject to change. The Authority reserves the right to amend, revise, or withdraw any aspect of a future procurement in line with service requirements, the Procurement Act 2023, and applicable government policy.
Market participation
The Authority anticipates that the framework will be accessible to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs);
Consortia and subcontracting arrangements are expected to be permitted, subject to conditions of participation.
Suppliers must be registered on the Central Digital Platform.

title: Portsmouth City Council - Term Service Contract for the Servicing, Maintenance and Compliance of Gas for Council Managed Assets - 2025
description:
This notice replaces the previous contract detail notice - 2026/S 000-012705- as the redacted contract is available.
Following the receipt of tenders on 3rd October 2025, the Council has completed the assessment and award process, including the mandatory standstill period.
Portsmouth City Council (the Council) is appointing a contractor to deliver Gas Servicing and Repair services across its housing stock. 
The scope of services will include statutory gas safety inspections, responsive repairs, and planned maintenance works, ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations and maintaining the safety and functionality of the Council's gas installations.
Based on anticipated inflationary uplifts and potential growth in housing stock, the total individual contract spends over the potential 10-year term (5-year base with options to extend) is expected to range between £45M to £55M.
Housing Stock Information 
The Council has a housing stock of approximately 17,500 properties of which approximately 15,500 are socially rented and then there are approximately 2000 leasehold properties.  Within the stock there is a mix of housing types including houses and bungalows; however the majority of the dwellings are within purpose-built blocks of flats constructed in the 1950s and 1960s.
Traditionally the estate has been spread across the two geographical areas of Portsea Island (on-island, PO1 to PO5) and Paulsgrove and Havant (off-island, PO6 to PO9).  
A recent acquisition of approximately 800 properties has however subsequently increased the 'off-island' area to sites in Gosport, Fareham and Winchester.
Current & Future Demand
Over the last 5 years there have been approximately 13,000 gas safety checks annually and 14000 annual gas and general boiler repairs, which is likely to remain consistent over the course of any new contract.
The Council is currently working on a number of development options, and it is anticipated that within the next 5-10 years there is potential for up to 1000 additional dwellings to be created that will require some level of maintenance and consequently will need to be absorbed into any new contract.
However, with the impending changes to gas installations post 2025 it is unlikely that there will be an increase in demand for annual gas servicing as a result of any development and as the stock decarbonises the current level of demand may reduce.
Changing Context and Objectives
Over the next 5-10 years the Council is expecting to experience a number of challenges with regards to the maintenance of its housing and general fund properties with any incumbent provider to work in partnership with the Council to ease pressures where they can.
There will be significant pressure to decarbonise the stock to align with local political objectives and comply with national Government energy legislation.
Significant changes in legislation such as the Building Safety Act and Fire Safety Act will require greater scrutiny from suppliers to ensure they are working in a compliant way and may require them to adopt new skills such as undertaking works as a result of Building Safety Cases for buildings of 6+ storeys.
There will be more focus on the accuracy and timely manner of up-load of compliance information and ensuring repairs, particularly around damp and mould are well managed and resolved and will be monitored by the Social Housing Regulator.
New Gas Servicing & Repairs Contract 
A single term service provider will still have the responsibility in managing all gas servicing across the residential housing stock only. However, the Council will be looking to award on the basis of a M3NHF 3* contract, with an initial base term of 5 years and the option to extend the contract for a further 5 years, in increments to be agreed. The Council are estimating the contract value will be in the region of £4M to £5M per annum.  
The core scope of works, which the successful supplier will be required to deliver are -
•	Landlord Gas Safety Check
•	Annual Gas Servicing 
•	CO Detector Checks 
•	Gas Boiler Installations
•	Gas Boiler and Heating Repairs
•	Voids Gas Safety Works
•	Out of hours cover 
The supplier will be required to resource an out of hours service which is available 365 days a year.
Ancillary Scope of Works
The ancillary scope of works, which the successful supplier may be required to deliver,
namely:
•	Commercial and Communal Landlord annual gas safety check;
•	Commercial gas boiler and heating repairs; and
•	Commercial gas boiler installations including heating systems, controls and all pipework.
•	Commercial and Commercial gas boiler servicing
•	Servicing and maintenance to air source heat pumps
•	Supplementary repairs to other water systems, valves, pumps, etc
Partnership Working
In addition to working in close partnership with the council, the supplier will also be required to work in partnership with the council's other existing term service contractor partners.
Social Value
The Council are committed to continuously reviewing and improving the approach to social value delivery, and suppliers can find further information using the following link - 
https://www.portsmouth.gov.uk/services/council-and-democracy/social-value/ 
Local Government Review 
As part of the wider Local Government Review (LGR), the Council is required to actively engage in discussions with neighbouring authorities to explore potential opportunities for collaboration, shared service delivery, and governance alignment. While this engagement is ongoing, no formal decisions or agreements have been reached at this stage.
Under current LGR proposals, it is likely to require Portsmouth City Council to form a new Authority by merging with other neighbouring Authorities. For Portsmouth, this will result in a new Council being created to provide the same services to everyone in the city, whilst covering a larger area and have a different name. Effectively all the current council services in the area of the new council boundary would be merged to create a new Council.
At this stage, the Council can only confirm its current demand and scope of requirements; however, this may be subject to change should additional needs arise from other local authorities as part of wider structural reforms.
Any tender opportunities and contracts will be structured to allow adjustments in the scope of services and the value of contracts to the Council to respond to changes in demand and budgetary constraints, whilst ensuring that services remain efficient and continue to provide value for money. Additionally, provisions will be included to adapt to changes in geographical boundaries resulting from any reorganisation. This will ensure that services can be extended or retracted to align with new administrative areas.
The impacts of Local Government Review cannot be fully understood at this stage. However, when considering the potential surrounding local authorities and their current property portfolios, the Council anticipate the annual value of the Gas Servicing and Repairs could increase in the region of £1M to £2M per year, in the event these services needed to be subsumed into this opportunity. Therefore, taking account the potential value stated in the total value of the opportunity over the 10-year period could be up to £65M.
In the event of reorganisation, contracts will include clauses that allow for the assignment of the contract to successor authorities. Any assignment clause is likely to state any contract may be assigned to any new authority that succeeds the original contracting authority.
For further details in respect of LGR see the following link - 
https://www.portsmouth.gov.uk/services/council-and-democracy/devolution-and-plans-for-local-government-reorganisation/

title: DCWW2115 Service Reservoir Cleaning, Maintenance and Refurbishment CoP
description:
Overview And Objectives 
DCC intends to award a Framework Agreement for Service Reservoir Cleaning, Maintenance and Refurbishment services. It is a business-critical service required to:
•	maintain the cleanliness, integrity and operational condition of DCC’s potable water storage assets;
•	support the safe and timely return of service reservoirs to operation following planned cleaning, inspection and minor remedial works; and
•	support compliance with Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) requirements, DCC’s internal standards and applicable water quality legislation.
The Framework will be used to provide cleaning and maintenance for potable water tanks across DCC’s operational area. There are approximately 828 tanks within DCC’s estate that require routine cleaning and inspection in accordance with PNL 810 (DCC’s internal standard for drain downs and cleaning of service reservoirs) to meet Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) regulations. 
Tanks include below ground and above ground steel or concrete tanks as well as a small number of water towers however most tanks are square, underground concrete structures. 
Ensuring a clean and consistent water supply is core to DCC services and is linked directly to corporate key performance indicators.
The proposed contract term is 3 years, with the option to extend for a further 5 years (2 + 2 + 1 years). The estimated value of the framework for the initial three-year term is £25.5 million based on estimated annual expenditure of approximately £8.5 million. The value across the maximum term of 8 years is £68m.
Scope
The scope includes the following elements:  
Cleaning
This includes the cleaning and disinfecting of the tanks normally with the use of high-pressure water or soft brush as appropriate and DWI Approved disinfectant. In some instances, it may be a requirement to carry out chemical cleaning with the use of a DWI approved chemical.
The tasks to be carried out will include:
•	Cleaning and disinfection of potable water storage tanks using appropriate methods and DWI-approved products
•	Inspection of service reservoirs as part of cleaning activities
Maintenance
Maintenance activities are usually identified at the time of cleaning by the Supplier and instructed by DCC to enable the tanks to be safely returned to service. These tend to be internal and external works for concrete repairs and coatings, internal and external steel repairs, membrane fitting and repairs, replacement of ladders and pipework, joint repairs, external earthworks repairs and joint repairs. Emergency reactive repairs to concrete/ pipework / liner etc. may also be required on occasion. These works will exclude any work that involves significant engineering difficulties such as:
•	Any structural modifications to the tank(s);
•	Any works on the embankments surrounding the tank(s);
•	Any modifications to the pipework that can influence the hydraulic performance of the tank(s);
•	Any works that alters the operating capacity of the tanks;
•	Any works that constitutes the appointment of a Panel Engineer under the Reservoirs Act. 
The tasks to be carried out will include:
•	Minor planned and reactive remedial works, including concrete and steel repairs, coatings, membranes, ladders, pipework, joints and external earthworks. 
•	Emergency reactive repairs where required. 
•	Activities necessary to support the safe return of reservoirs to service. 
The Framework Agreement will be procured as a single Lot, with two Suppliers appointed to the Framework.

title: Care and Support Services, Carlton Dene Extra Care Housing
description:
Westminster City Council requires a high-quality personalised Care and Support Service at Carlton Dene Extra Care Housing; Carlton Dene is a new development, which will be ready for handover in March 2026 so that the new service can be delivered from April 2026.
The Carlton Dene building supports a variety of care and wellbeing services, including:
•	65 Extra Care Housing Units
•	Resident Lounge 
•	Staff Areas
•	Cafe Space (on-site but not part of the Contract)
•	Hairdressers and Therapy Space (on-site but not part of the Contract)
The Authority owns the building, and the Residents will be tenants of Westminster City Council.
Extra Care Housing offers self-contained, fully accessible properties with private front doors, bathrooms, kitchens, living areas, and storage space. Residents have legal rights to occupy underpinned by housing law, and the freedom to personalise their homes to suit their preferences. At Carlton Dene it is anticipated in the region of 985 personalised care hours with additional universal core hours for engagement, management, night support and oversight.  
A dedicated CQC Registered Manager is required to assist with care matters and co-ordinate support services. Staff will be available on-site 24/7. 
Carlton Dene will support the delivery of key Adult Social Care (ASC) principles: Personalisation; Prevention; Innovation; Integration and Local, by offering personalised care, giving residents choice and control over their support. The Service prevents isolation and promotes well-being by helping people stay independent in their community. Through innovation, the Service enhances digital inclusion and uses technology to support health and social needs. Integration with housing, the NHS, and social care ensures joined-up services, while a local approach allows residents to remain in the borough, creating employment and volunteering opportunities.

title: Care & Repair Open Framework
description:
Open Framework procured for Peterborough City Council in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023, for the provision of adaptations including extensions, internal alterations, level access showering facilities and associated works in domestic properties; The installation of minor aids and adaptations in domestic properties.
The overall aim of the works specified within the Care and Repair Open Framework Agreement is to assist and support elderly, vulnerable and disabled local residents (adults and children) to live independently and be warm and safe. The work will be undertaken in conjunction with the Home Service Delivery Care and Repair Team within Peterborough City Council. The work will predominantly be in the Peterborough City Council Unitary Authority area. Most will be in the city, but some will be in the surrounding areas of Peterborough.
The specific aim for each contractor of the Open Framework Agreement and Schedule of Rates is to:
- Use responsive, suitably qualified, and experienced, competent and knowledgeable contractors
- Use locally based contractors to aid in the responsiveness of the service
- Produce high quality work with minimum disruption for clients
- Obtain value for money
- Commence work promptly following the receipt of an order
- To complete the work promptly
- Work in occupied properties with the minimum disruption to the client who will be included in one or more of the following categories: elderly, disabled (mentally and/or physically), vulnerable, on a low income. This list is not conclusive.
The expected benefits of procuring work this way are a reduction in delays and poor experiences with contractors, and a consistent and shortened timescale from date of first enquiry to completion or work.
The work is in Peterborough City Council (PCC) Unitary Authority area through the Peterborough Home Services Delivery Care and Repair Team (C&R). The adaptations will often be funded by Disabled Facility Grants approved by Peterborough City Council. However, the Level Access Shower schedule of works may be used for work that the Care & Repair Team manages which is funded privately, by charities, benevolent funds, by Adult Social Care or Children's Services. It may also form the basis for work which Peterborough Care & Repair may arrange on behalf of other local Councils.
The minor aids and adaptations, which is predominantly of low value (under £1,000), is funded from Adult Social Care Budgets
The Authority intends for the Open Framework to last for the maximum possible term of 8 years, conforming to the provisions concerning reopening as set out in Section 49 of the Procurement Act 2023.

The Disabled People’s Rights Plan sets out a 10-year cross-government framework to advance the rights and opportunities of disabled people in Wales, removing societal barriers, and challenging the prejudice and discrimination they face. In line with the Public Sector Equality Duty to address the inequalities experienced by those with protected characteristics, the Disabled People’s Rights Plan directly targets the 670,000 disabled people in Wales who continue to experience inequalities and barriers across a range of areas, including in employment, education, healthcare, access to services, transport, housing, community participation and justice.
The Plan was published alongside a supporting document that outlined the short-term actions to be delivered within the first two years up to the end of 2027. The Welsh Government has committed to delivering 67 short-term actions, which are aligned to achieving the outcomes that are set out in the Plan. These actions uphold the principles of the articles outlined in the UNCRPD and Welsh Government’s National Equality Objectives. 
The Client wishes to commission an evaluation of the Disabled People’s Rights Plan, comprised broadly of the following:
- A Process Evaluation to understand the Plan’s implementation and suggest improvements for future work in this area
- Baselining work towards an Impact Evaluation to begin to understand whether the Plan has had an impact on the lives of disabled people in Wales

title: Parents As First Teachers
description: Cornwall Council is commissioning a Parents as First Teachers (PAFT) service, an evidence-based, trauma-responsive home learning programme that supports families to improve children’s early development, strengthen parent-child attachment, and enhance the home learning environment. As part of Cornwall’s Early Help and Family Hubs offer, the service will provide targeted home-based support to families most at risk of poorer outcomes, with a focus on improving school readiness and reducing inequalities. Delivery will prioritise families in Camborne & Redruth and St Austell, Newquay & Clay Country, particularly those with children aged 3–4 years, emerging or confirmed SEND, limited access to funded childcare, or experiencing trauma and adversity. Support will be delivered through structured home visits using the accredited PAFT curriculum and in partnership with Family Hubs, Health Visiting, Speech and Language Therapy, Early Years Inclusion, and other Early Help services.

title: 2026 ATS & HRIS
description:
Oak National Academy is exploring the replacement of BeApplied, its current Applicant Tracking System (ATS), which is expected to become unavailable at the end of March 2027. Oak is also considering whether to procure a linked HR information system (HRIS) at the same time, procure the systems as separate lots, or address its HRIS needs through a later procurement.
The immediate priority is an ATS that can be implemented in time to maintain recruitment services. Oak is undertaking this engagement to understand the market, test its developing requirements, assess realistic implementation times and decide how best to package the ATS and HRIS requirements. No decision has yet been made to include an HRIS in the resulting tender.
Oak invites input from suppliers of ATS products, HRIS products, integrated ATS and HRIS platforms, and suppliers able to deliver either system with a reliable integration to the other. Suppliers do not need to offer both systems to participate.
Oak’s current ATS needs are described in the accompanying working requirements guide. They include structured and blind sifting, independent reviewer scoring, separation of diversity monitoring data from hiring decisions, accessible candidate and staff journeys, recruitment administration, reporting and export of records. Oak also wishes to explore HRIS needs and the transfer of new-starter information between systems. These are working needs, not final tender requirements or evaluation criteria. Oak welcomes different ways of achieving the outcomes.
Suppliers are invited to respond by 20th October 2026 by email to procurement@thenational.academy. Please state:
Whether you offer an ATS, an HRIS, or both, and whether each is an established product or requires development.
Indicative three-year costs for the ATS and HRIS separately, including implementation, migration, integrations, licences, support and optional modules. These figures are for planning and will not be scored.
Availability for demonstrations to our team
Oak expects to hold live demonstrations or discussions during October 2026 with potential suppliers. It may use separate ATS and HRIS scenarios so suppliers offering only one system can participate meaningfully. All interested suppliers may submit written input regardless of whether they receive a live session.
The engagement will not be scored or used to select a preferred supplier. Participation is not required to bid for any subsequent contract and gives no supplier an advantage in that competition. Oak will record the engagement and make information relevant to preparing a bid available to the wider market, while protecting genuinely confidential supplier information.
Oak currently expects to publish an ATS tender in late October/mid November 2026, but the timing, scope, procurement route and contract value will be reviewed following this engagement.
This notice is not an invitation to tender and does not commit Oak to any particular procurement or award.

title: BHCC - RS - Royal Pavilion Gardens Landscape and Amenities works
description:
The Royal Pavilion Estate is the city of Brighton & Hove's cultural heart and the Royal
Pavilion is an internationally recognised emblem. Uniquely combining an historic Royal
Palace and Regency Garden, a museum & art gallery, and three performing arts spaces,
the two custodians of the Estate Brighton & Hove Museums (B&HM) and Brighton Dome
& Brighton Festival (BD&BF) are coming together with BHCC in a cross-cultural
partnership to reinvigorate and reconnect this historic Estate through the implementation
of an estate-wide masterplan. This project relates to Phase Two of the masterplan for the
Royal Pavilion Estate (Phase One was the refurbishment of the Corn Exchange).
The Royal Pavilion Garden comprises 3.3ha of paths, lawns, shrubberies, garden beds
and ancient trees. Importantly it comprises the setting and is the access point, for the
Royal Pavilion and Brighton Museum & Art Gallery.
Presently, the garden is a partially restored John Nash designed Regency Garden (listed
Grade II). It has recently been placed on Historic England's Heritage at Risk Register
(HARR) due to its deteriorating condition which is a result of overuse, antisocial behaviour
and lack of investment.
The Royal Pavilion Estate contains many historic listed buildings and features:
- Royal Pavilion Garden (Grade II)
- Royal Pavilion (Grade I)
- Brighton Museum & Art Gallery (Grade II*)
- Brighton Dome Theatre (Grade I)
- Corn Exchange (Grade II)
- Northgate House (Grade II*)
- India Gate (Grade II)
- William IV Gate (Grade II*)
- 19 William IV Lamp posts (Grade II)
Following successful completion of the development phase funded by the National Lottery
Heritage Fund, the project partners BHCC & B&HM have jointly secured £6.2M from the
National Lottery Heritage Fund with roughly 60% allocated to the capital works project to
re redevelop the estate. This notice relates to the Capital works only.
The approved designs focus on the conservation and improvement of the garden to
enhance environmental sustainability and to attract a wider range of people and ensuring
there are more opportunities for use and community involvement.
The planned capital works consist of:
- New visitor and community facilities including a new public toilet facility with changing
places, outdoor learning space, benches and bins.
- Extensive landscaping improvements including path widening and entrance
improvements.
- Restoration of historic planting designs.
- Restoration of historic fixtures such as perimeter railings and lamp columns.
- New physical interpretation and wayfinding
Our key priorities are to:
- Deliver high quality and visually engaging spaces in this highly public and well loved
public space in the centre of Brighton
- Connect the Royal Estate, creating a sense of arrival
- Minimise disruption to the site whilst delivering the works, to enable the Trust relies on
visitors to maintain the viability of the site.
The tender process is a competitive flexible procedure consisting of at least two stages; a
shortlisting stage and a full tender stage.
The shortlisting stage is released with this notice with full tender release in February 2026.
The planned site handover should then go-ahead late summer, early autumn 2026.

title: Trafford Waters - Architect
description:
L&Q are undertaking this preliminary market engagement (PME) to inform the design of a future procurement exercise for an Architect for our Trafford Water site.  
About L&Q
L&Q is one of the UK's largest charitable housing associations, owning and managing over 105,000 homes across Greater London and Greater Manchester. Alongside its core role as a housing provider, L&Q is an active developer and regeneration partner, delivering new homes across a range of tenures, including affordable housing and market. L&Q's development programme focuses on creating high-quality, sustainable places that support thriving communities and respond to local housing needs.
London and Quadrant Housing Trust (L&Q) is seeking to procure an architect for RIBA stages 2 and 3 in relation to plots 3.4 and 5.3 at Trafford Waters, Manchester, M41 7JE. L&Q may seek to expand the remit of this appointment to cover other stages, and sites in the Trafford Waters Development.  
The Project
Trafford Waters is a 53-acre regeneration site being master developed by Peel Group, with outline consent for up to 3,000 homes alongside significant public open space, commercial uses, and a new school. L&Q have already delivered an initial phase of the site, the Pearson Place scheme, comprising 83 apartments, and are now progressing the acquisition of further plots 3.4 and 5.3 within the masterplan.
Initial feasibility studies highlight the requirement for a high quality, high density family housing scheme that aligns with the requirements of the Trafford Design Code reflects the high density aspirations of the Outline Planning Consent (Reference: 85282/OUT/15). 
An initial high level programme is as follows, please note all dates are indicative and subject to change.  
Pre Market Engagement: October 2026
Tender / Framework call off: October 2026 – January 2026 (subject to decision on route to market)
Start of Services: January 2027
Planning Submission: May 2027
Start on Site: January 2028 
L&Q wish to understand the capacity and capability of potential suppliers in the market to deliver our aims for high quality high density family housing schemes to inform our route to market.  L&Q are eager to explore services beyond traditional architectural services – including how you can help us: 
1.	Ensure viability of the site
2.	Assist with sales development / promotion of the dwellings
3.	Manage risks of the development
