title: Kings Langley Cleaning Tender
description:
Kings Langley School is a co-educational Secondary School in Kings Langley, Hertfordshire WD4 9HN. It has 1,126 students between the ages of 11 and 18 on roll and there are 125 teaching and support staff. The administrative offices, currently delivered as part of a standalone cleaning contract.
The School is undertaking this procurement to appoint an experienced cleaning partner to deliver a consistently high standard of cleaning from 1st April 2027. The Contract will be for an initial three-year term, with the option to extend for a further two years (1+1), subject to satisfactory performance and the terms of the Contract.
The procurement process follows a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure. It begins with a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) followed by an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage after shortlisting. Further details of the procurement process, timetable and evaluation methodology are set out later in this pack.
The School is looking for a proactive cleaning partner with the ideas, experience and operational capability to make a positive and visible difference. The successful Contractor will have the opportunity to review the current cleaning operation and make recommendations on staffing levels, cleaning methods, equipment, materials and working practices. The School particularly welcomes ideas that will raise standards, improve reliability, embed sustainable working methods and create a cleaning service that pupils, staff and visitors can rely on every day.
A key requirement is a TUPE-compliant and operationally deliverable solution, supported by a credible and guaranteed cost of operation. Bidders are encouraged to identify appropriate opportunities for service improvement and investment in modern equipment and technology, and to demonstrate clearly how their proposals will benefit the School.
Whilst value for money is very important, this procurement is not simply about achieving the lowest price. The School is looking for the right balance of consistently high cleaning standards, reliability, responsiveness and financial sustainability.
Above all, the School wants a trusted cleaning partner that will deliver what it promises — meeting agreed input hours in full, achieving audit and KPI targets, and delivering any proposed investment and service improvements in full.
The School is committed to finding the right cleaning solution. If the tenders received do not demonstrate an acceptable and deliverable solution, the School reserves the right, subject to the Procurement Act 2023 and the procurement documents, to make no award and consider alternative arrangements, including an in-house solution.

Within the contract period, further cohorts may be added, and we would anticipate that any contract would be extended until participants have completed their studies though the EA give no guarantees of numbers of participants. As part of this procurement exercise the Education Authority is seeking to understand the market capacity to provide a range of education opportunities to support the development of a suitably qualified and highly skilled workforce. The EA Pathways to Employment Programme will require the supplier to address and provide their approach to the below requirements.
•	Education Authority requirements in relation to our Pathways Scheme 
•	Capacity to offer university places for an initial cohort of between 20-30 undergraduate places over the next 4 years.
•	Availability to provide up to 15 Postgraduate study places
•	Capacity to facilitate 5-10 Masters places
•	Cohort-based provision with greater flexibility and value for money than individual enrolment
•	Flexibility to offer a block period of teaching to support part-time study towards the successful completion of modules 
•	Course tuition to be facilitated at EA premises for a minimum of 50% of programme delivery
•	Residential teaching as an option to support academic progress

description:
The Inner West London Coroner’s Court provides coronial services for the City of Westminster, Kensington and Chelsea, Wandsworth and Merton.  The Senior Coroner for Inner West London is procuring toxicology services to support the investigation of deaths within the Jurisdiction.  
Results of toxicological testing can be vital for pathologists to ascertain the medical cause of death.  
The required toxicology services will include, but are not limited to: 
-	Comprehensive toxicological analysis of biological samples (e.g., blood, urine, tissue).
-	Detection and quantification of drugs (over the counter and illicit), alcohol, poisons, and other toxic substances.
-	In house hair analysis for drugs of abuse. 
-	Provision of detailed toxicology reports to assist in determining the cause of death.
-	Expert witness services for court proceedings, if necessary.
-	Consultation and advisory services related to toxicology findings.
All services are required to be carried out following the guidelines agreed by the United Kingdom & Ireland Association of Forensic Toxicologists.  These guidelines are recognised by the Forensic Science Regulator and Chief Coroner.  Analysis is required to be tailored to each case individually to ensure all necessary analysis is carried out but only those drug concentrations which can be interpreted are measured. At present, hair analysis is routinely offered for all the Inner West London Coroner’s cases.

title: Studying and Assessing the Benthic Response to Electrical Stimuli (SABRES)
description: High voltage submarine cables produce electromagnetic fields (EMF) external to the cable due to current flowing within their metallic components, primarily the main conductor. While the magnitude of these fields decays rapidly with separation from the cables, reducing to background levels within 10's of meters, cable circuits extend continuously across the seabed for 100's of km. Accurately quantifying and understanding the impact of anthropogenic EMF on seafloor organisms is therefore vital. Given the significant volume of new interconnector systems being installed/planned (e.g. For the Eastern Green Link projects (1-4) represent ~1800km of cable circuit), it is important to ensure that this transition to net zero does not result in ecological harm.

title: Subsea Cable Health/security Utilising Backscatter and Established Repeater Technologies (SCHUBERT)Subsea Cable Health/security Utilising Backscatter and Established Repeater Technologies (SCHUBERT)
description: With the transition away from fossil fuels and towards greater electrification of transport and heating (net zero 2050) a significant increase in electrical demand is expected over the coming decades. As a result, growth in offshore renewable power generation, "bootstrap" cables to reinforce national power grids, and international interconnects to support energy trading, are all now driving considerable investment in submarine power cable infrastructure. As cable technology and installation techniques develop, it becomes feasible to deploy ever longer subsea cables, creating new opportunities for cable construction projects. When cable spans exceed 50-100km the cost of building HVDC converter stations can be outweighed by savings due to lower transmission losses, the current trend is therefore towards construction of very long subsea HVDC cables.

The National Lottery Community Fund (the ‘Fund’) is seeking to procure a suitable contractor (an individual organisation or a consortium with a lead supplier) to scope two separate contracts to support the organisations and grantholders we fund through our Solidarity Fund programme and develop a monitoring framework. The Solidary Fund is a £250m multi-year fund for charitable organisations tackling the root causes of inequality. The Fund’s Solidarity Fund will offer grants of between £1m and £5m, to be spent over 5 to 10 years to support this aim. The programme aims to change the way organisations or sectors work together (Solidarity), and bring people together to deal with the root causes of these problems, by supporting people to work on this across different issues and communities (Build Power/Organise). Organisations must be led by, and accountable to, people with lived experience of the issues they are tackling (Lived Experience) and create, share and use learning from people that experience inequality (Learning). This may be to help people have a say, and be heard or to support people to take action and make things better by: influencing decision making and changes to systems, helping people that are trying to reduce inequality, understand what has worked elsewhere, or change public understanding of inequality by sharing people’s experiences. title: Council Services Platform
description:
The Council require a single, modular enterprise cloud platform to support all Salisbury City Council service areas and functions, not limited to any one department. The solution has to  be capable of being configured and rolled out across the organisation in phases, while maintaining a consistent data model, user management, reporting and governance.
The platform has to be capable of supporting end-to-end processes across all Council service areas, including but not limited to Customer Services and Contact Centre functions (such as enquiries, requests, complaints and communications), Parks, Open Spaces, Play Areas, Trees and Grounds Maintenance, Inspections, Compliance and Health & Safety activities (including vehicle and equipment checks where applicable), Asset Management, Task Management, Works Orders and Maintenance, Crematorium and Bereavement Services (including bookings, tasks, payments and record management), Allotments, Grants and Funding administration (covering applications, assessments, scoring, approvals, agreements, payments, monitoring and reporting), Markets, Street Trading and Events, Facilities and Venue Bookings (including halls, rooms, pitches and other council assets available for hire), Licensing and permission-based workflows, FOI, SAR, EIR and Complaints processes where required, Payments and Income Collection through integrated payment solutions, and Internal Service Requests where the Council chooses to operate the platform as a service desk.
The platform must also provide a comprehensive audit trail across all modules and service workflows, recording as a minimum the user identity, timestamp, action or event undertaken, and the associated record or context. The audit trail must capture the full lifecycle of records, including creation, amendments, status changes, assignments, approvals, closures and controlled deletions. It must also record inspection evidence, including completed forms, photographs and attachments, outcomes, findings and any actions taken, as well as task and works order lifecycle activity, including findings recorded for monitoring purposes only. The system must maintain a complete history of enquiry and case communications, covering both inbound and outbound correspondence, and where payment functionality is utilised, record payment events and their linkage to the relevant case, service or transaction. In addition, the platform must log integration and web service events, including successful and failed transactions. All audit information must be readily reportable and exportable to support operational assurance, compliance monitoring, evidential requirements, and both internal and external audit activities.

title: Dry dilution refrigerator with anti-vibration system for mK scanning probe microscopy
description:
NPL is seeking a solution for a new dry dilution refrigerator (“the system”) in which scanning probe microscopy experiments will be carried out at mK temperatures on live superconducting quantum circuits. NPL wishes to use the system for atomic scale scanning tunnelling microscopy and atomic force microscopy. As such, the system must provide a low vibration and high coherence environment (light tight mixing chamber volume). Significant emphasis will be placed on the lowest possible vibration levels that can be achieved. It is anticipated that a solution provides both a mK vibration isolation system and various vibration mitigation measures at room temperature.
The scope includes the dilution refrigerator having a low-vibration experimental platform at mK temperature, the experimental wiring tree to the mK experimental platform, and any room-temperature or low-temperature vibration reducing measures, any gas handling system, vacuum pumps or electronics required to operate the system. The system does not include the scanning probe microscopy unit itself, this will be provided and integrated by NPL.
In the below we denote “the mixing chamber plate” as the standard plate of the dilution refrigerator that reaches the specified temperature and cryogenic performance. We further specify an “experimental plate” which may be the same as the “mixing chamber plate” in some implementations, but it may for some vibration isolating solutions be a separate plate on which the experimental scanning probe system and apparatus is mounted. It is in that case assumed that the experimental plate is thermally anchored to the mixing chamber plate and reaches the same base temperature, and sits within the enclosed mixing chamber shielded volume.
Description
•	A “dry” pulse tube cooled dilution refrigerator that does not use liquid nitrogen or liquid helium to achieve cooling to 4 Kelvin.
•	The dilution refrigerator shall reach a base temperature of 20 mK or less at the vibration-isolated experimental platform, and the dilution refrigerator shall have a cooling power at 100 mK of 400 microWatts or more.
•	The experimental space below the experimental plate (if not the same as the mixing chamber plate, if e.g. a mK vibration isolation solution is used) shall be at least of diameter 360 mm, with a vertical height available for custom experiments of at least 300 mm.
•	The experimental plate shall be able to hold an experimental load of up to at least 1.5 kg, for custom experimental apparatus NPL wishes to install. Higher load will score higher.
•	Of particular importance is the achieved vibration levels at the experimental plate at 20mK or less, which shall have a demonstrated vibration level both horizontally and vertically during continuous operation of the dilution refrigerator as follows:
o	Any individual peaks in the vibration spectrum (horizontal and vertical) measured from 10 Hz up to at least 1000 Hz not exceeding a peak-to-peak displacement of 0.5 nm/rtHz.
o	An integrated noise power spectral density in the frequency range 1-10 Hz shall not exceed a root mean square amplitude of 10 nmrms.
o	The scoring in the evaluation of supplier bids will be heavily weighted against rewarding bids that significantly exceed the above minimum requirement specifications for vibrations.
o	NPL recognises that laboratory vibration levels may differ and as such will set the requirement that the above vibration levels shall be achieved in factory testing, with NPL staff present during final testing to witness compliance.
o	Any cold vibration isolation solution must remain well-thermalised and reach a base temperature of 50 mK or less and capable of conducting the active heat loads from piezoelectric nanopositioners.
In order to achieve these specifications the supplier may chose to include a range of different solutions, and may work with other suppliers to provide external (room temperature) or internal (mK) vibration isolation solutions. No such solution shall be regarded as optional and must be part of the total quoted price of the base system and the above vibration specifications are to be measured and evidenced with all the solution(s) in place. Furthermore, all these vibration reducing measures must be achievable and demonstrated with all the subsequent requirements listed below in place.
•	There shall be at least 12 coaxial input lines (high attenuation) for microwave signals up to 18 GHz down to the experimental plate.
•	There shall be at least 2 coaxial output lines (low attenuation) for microwave signals up to 18 GHz down to the experimental plate.
•	The system should be upgradeable in the future to at least a total of 24 coaxial lines.
•	There shall be at least 6 different DC wiring twisted-pair looms down to the experimental plate, each of 24 twisted pair wires going from room temperature to the mixing chamber plate operational up to +-220V for use with piezo positioners, cryogenic slip stick positioner motion, nanopositioner capacitive position readouts and experimental current and voltage biasing of experiments. Each loom shall have an interruptable connection at the 4K stage where custom filters can be installed.
•	Have an entirely sealed mixing chamber volume with a mixing chamber plate shield that is anchored to the mixing chamber plate in a sealed manner. The mixing chamber plate and wiring through it shall also be entirely shielded such as to prevent light from passing through.
•	Operation of the dilution refrigerator, shall be fully automatable and the automated scripts user configurable.
•	The total space taken up by the entire system shall not exceed 4.0m (w) x 4.0m (l) x 3.5m (h), excluding compressors for the pulse tube cooler(s). It will be expected that the entire system can fit in a single laboratory with this dimension (but any PT compressors can be located elsewhere).
•	The total weight of the system shall not exceed 2000 kg.
•	The system shall be delivered and installed before March 2028.
This is not an evaluation exercise and nothing in this activity will limit the opportunity to engage in any follow-on ITT

title: Short Breaks
description:
Over the past 3 years we have used a third sector organisation to facilitate grants, whilst
this has been successful in reaching many groups and unpaid carers, the governance and
links to statutory services has been limited and caused a number of challenges.
Therefore, a new model for the next 3 years is suggested:
Utilise a third sector organisation with established links to unpaid carers to fund:
1. This element should be viewed as a single component with 2 parts:
a) A Short Breaks Community facilitator (approx. £40k) to understand the range of
services and groups available, including UK, Wales wide and local schemes. They will
provide a ‘what matters’ type conversation and be able to link the unpaid carer to
existing short break opportunities as well as facilitate small grants/short breaks directly for
unpaid carers where appropriate through the conversation. The process for this will need to be developed in collaboration with the unpaid carer Information Advice and Assistance
services (in both Cardiff and Vale of Glamorgan).
b) To enable the Short Breaks Community facilitator to meet those with the most
significant need there will be funding for direct short breaks for unpaid carers through the
Short Breaks facilitator (approx. £20k)– this may be to pay for a hotel break, activities,
experiences, a hobby or an item which would be deemed a ‘break’ (not household). This
may also be to fill an identified gap or need in a local community, for example 10 people in
an area need a peer support group so the facilitator will work with other local groups to
establish one and may cover associated revenue costs.
2. Funding for 3rd sector grants (approx. £80k) to support the third sector to deliver a
variety of offers for unpaid carer in relation to Short Breaks, including but not limited to
regular peer-support groups. The funded organisations should work in coordination with
the Short Breaks facilitator so there is a variety of offers and so the facilitator can identify
where there are gaps in the funded 3rd sector provision and provided offers to fill those
gaps.

title: Continuation of Support for cyber assessment framework in Welsh Local Government - Contract details notice
description: Notice to Direct award contract for the continuation of works to support the implementation of the Cyber assessment framework (CAF) in Welsh local government, provided by Bridewell Consulting Ltd. Direct award justification - Continuation of Existing SupplyChange of supplier would cause incompatibility or disproportionate technical difficulty.WLGA proposes to directly award the next phase of the Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) support contract to Bridewell Consulting Ltd on the basis that changing supplier at this stage would create significant technical, operational and cyber security risks that outweigh any potential benefits of a competitive procurement exercise.The supplier has developed substantial programme-specific knowledge, methodologies, tooling, templates, dashboards and sector intelligence throughout delivery of the CAF programme across Welsh local authorities and Fire and Rescue Services. The supplier has supported organisations through assessment, quality review, critical system mapping, independent feedback and improvement planning activities. As a result, they now possesses a unique understanding of the sector baseline, organisational maturity positions, critical system dependencies and programme governance arrangements.Replacing the current supplier with an alternative supplier would create incompatibility with the existing programme infrastructure, methodologies and assessment approaches already embedded across participating organisations. Significant effort would be required to transfer knowledge, validate prior outputs and align a new supplier to established ways of working, creating a risk of inconsistency in assessment outcomes and reducing comparability with work already completed. This would undermine the continuity and integrity of the national programme.A change of supplier would also introduce material cyber risk. The current programme supports the cyber resilience of critical public services across Wales and provides visibility of sector-wide risks, vulnerabilities and areas requiring intervention. Any interruption to delivery, loss of organisational context or reduction in oversight during transition could weaken security visibility across the sector and delay the identification and mitigation of emerging risks. A prolonged mobilisation period would leave organisations without the level of support and assurance currently available through the programme.In addition, a transition to a new supplier would cause significant service disruption. A full procurement exercise, mobilisation period and knowledge transfer programme would delay delivery of planned activities and divert resources away from improvement work. Participating organisations would experience disruption at a critical stage in their CAF journey, potentially delaying assurance activities, improvement planning and the implementation of risk reduction measures

title: Strategic Resident Safety, Call Bell and Connected Care Solution
description:
Anchor Hanover Group is England's largest not-for-profit provider of housing and care for older people, operating 120 care homes across England. These services support over 6000 older people with a range of residential care needs where safety, dignity, independence, accessibility and regulatory assurance are central to day-to-day operations.
Resident safety and connected care technology is therefore a safety-critical capability, enabling residents to request assistance, supporting colleagues to respond effectively, and providing data to inform oversight, quality assurance and service improvement.
Purpose of this market engagement
Anchor is undertaking preliminary market engagement to understand current and emerging market capabilities and to help define a strategic resident safety and connected care solution. Anchor wishes to explore a safe, resilient and supportable common platform, or a small number of controlled solution patterns, across its care home portfolio.
The preliminary market engagement will help Anchor understand the art of the possible, inform its defined specifications, target architecture, business case and roadmap, and explore the most appropriate delivery models for supply, installation, service and maintenance.
Problem and opportunity
Keeping residents safe, supporting independence and enabling colleagues to provide responsive, person-centered care are priorities for Anchor. A recent portfolio audit found issues with reliability, reporting, sensor performance, replacement equipment, ageing technology and fragmented support, across a varied portfolio of legacy technologies, suppliers and configurations.
Indicative scope and areas of interest
The future solution must support Anchor in meeting all applicable regulatory and statutory obligations relevant to care home operations. Suppliers should demonstrate how their solution enables providers to evidence compliance during day-to-day operation, internal assurance activity and regulatory inspection.
The future solution should establish a consistent minimum standard for resident safety across all homes. It should also enable proportionate differentiation in resident and colleague experience to support Anchor's future Standard, Premium and Luxury care home service tiers. The solution should support person-centered care by allowing the system to be configured around each resident's individual needs, rather than being determined solely by the commercial tier of the home.
The solution should also support the potential future expansion into specialist care models, including nursing, step-down and short-stay recovery, through configurable workflows, optional devices and integration with care or clinical records, without requiring replacement of the core platform.
Anchor expects its digital care planning capability is likely to remain with the incumbent supplier in the immediate future, therefore future resident safety and connected care solutions should be capable of integrating with this and equivalent applications where appropriate.
Anchor's Connected Properties programme is nearing completion. This project removes any corporate network and replaces it with a managed public Wi-Fi service across all care homes. The future solution may make effective use of this connectivity to support mobile working, integration, reporting and remote monitoring, while ensuring that safety-critical resident safety functionality remains operational if Wi-Fi or wider network services are unavailable.

description:

Waste engine oil is currently deposited by the public at HWRCs and stored in designated containers pending collection. 
The Provider shall deliver a fully managed service for the collection, handling, transportation, treatment, recovery and recycling of waste engine oil and associated hydrocarbon liquids generated at Household Waste Recycling Centres. 
This service will include the compliant collection and transport of materials in accordance with all relevant legislation, and their treatment in line with the waste hierarchy. The scope also covers the de-sludging, cleaning, inspection and maintenance of oil storage infrastructure, as well as the removal of oil containers and receptacles left by residents. 
Waste streams to be managed include, but are not limited to, used engine oils from petrol and diesel vehicles, lubricating, gear, and hydraulic oils where deposited, contaminated oil mixtures from household sources, and oil residues such as sludges and tank bottoms arising from storage containers.
Based on historic data, the Authority estimates annual wate engine oil arisings in the region of 220,000 litres or circa. 200 tonnes per annum across all HWRCs.

title: Qualitative Research in Land-Based Premises
description:
Introduction and Background:
The Gambling Commission is an executive non-departmental public body sponsored by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.
The Commission is responsible for issuing personal gambling licences for individuals and gambling operating licences for businesses operating in Great Britain and we are responsible for ensuring all licensed gambling is conducted subject to the following licensing objectives:
•	preventing gambling from being a source of crime or disorder, being associated with crime or disorder or being used to support crime
•	ensuring that gambling is conducted in a fair and open way
•	protecting children and other vulnerable people from being harmed or exploited by gambling.
In January 2025, we published a consultation which proposed changes to our requirements on licensees, through the Gaming Machine Technical Standards (GMTS), Gaming Machine Testing Strategy (testing strategy) and the Licence Conditions and Codes of Practice (LCCP).
This was in connection with the commitment in the April 2023 Gambling Act Review White Paper (*1) that set out that:
“The Gambling Commission will conduct a review of its gaming machine technical standards. The review will include an assessment of the role of session limits across category B and C machines and the role of safer gambling tools. The review will consider the effects of any legislative change following the Gambling Act Review and, where appropriate, will consolidate the progress made so far by the industry on a voluntary basis.”
In January 2026, we set out our position in relation to our proposal to introduce a licence condition to more effectively address non-compliant gaming machines (*2). The new licence condition came into effect on 29 July 2026. Our September response (*3) sets out our position in relation to all other proposals within the consultation published in January 2025.
In line with fulfilling our 2024-2027 corporate strategy which includes evaluating the GAR White Paper commitments we are responsible for, the Commission will be conducting an evaluation of the changes arising from the consultation. As part of this evaluation, we are looking to procure qualitative research in land-based premises to be carried out between April 2027 and January 2029.
We envisage this will be delivered across 2 or 3 waves of fieldwork. The first wave of fieldwork will be a pilot study to collect baseline data after the session definition is introduced, and to test the feasibility of the methodology; this data collection must be carried out after 30 March 2027 and be completed by 29 June 2027.  The pilot study will also be an opportunity to trial approaches for the full fieldwork, to be carried out post-implementation from 30 June 2027 and should be used to inform the wider project’s design.
Land-based fieldwork in gambling premises presents an exciting opportunity for the Commission to explore an often-underutilised methodology within gambling research; capturing the experiences and behaviours of consumers, and staff, of the policy changes in real-time and in live environments. This kind of data collection is especially powerful as it partly mitigates limitations of other qualitative approaches, such as surveys or remote interviews, which rely on consumer recall and accurate self-report. Ethnographic, fieldwork-based approaches can utilise in-person interviews or questionnaires and also incorporate methods such as observation in order to gain a more rounded view of participant experiences. We also welcome innovative or new approaches within relevant disciplines.
Please note: This project will collect data to be triangulated within the Gaming Machine evaluation, it will not be carrying out evaluation itself or producing evaluation-related outputs.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose of the Engagement:
•	Understand market capability to provide expertise and specialist research in land-based gambling across Great Britain; with a focus on qualitative and ethnographic methods within live, public environments that engage members of the public.
•	Explore indicative cost models for the pilot study and full fieldwork
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Description of Requirements:
Expertise and experience -
Suppliers should have demonstratable experience with relevant methodologies, and past experience of delivering successful public-facing fieldwork in Great Britain in gambling, retail or hospitality premises. Especially strong bids would have experience conducting fieldwork in different contexts across multiple locations.
Research requirements -
Methodologies should be drawn from qualitative and ethnographic approaches and aim to capture consumer experiences and behaviour, in addition to staff experiences, relating to the policy changes; this could include interviews, questionnaires, and observational data, as examples. More innovative and original methodologies in the field are welcome; especially surrounding ethnographies, play-based research, place-based approaches, and research that has explored experiences of gaming machines. For example, methods could explore the experience of, and feelings about, limit setting functionality (Proposal 4) (*4) and its potential impact on consumer play.
Depending on the chosen methodological approaches, relevant ethical approval(s) will need to be in place that follow the Commission’s Research Governance Framework (*5); including any relevant guidelines for conducting gambling research with human participants.
Locations of premises included in the fieldwork should span city and rural areas; with geographical diversity in mind across England, Wales and Scotland; for example, covering city centre to costal locations. Researchers should also anticipate some fieldwork occurring outside of regular working hours, in order to capture different times of day and levels of business in relevant venues.
There are four types of premises affected by the policy changes, and these should all be included in the research approach:
Types of premises included in the fieldwork should include:
-	Casino
-	Adult Gaming Centre (AGC)
-	Bingo; this would include more traditional Bingo Clubs as well as high street Bingo premises
-	Betting
Exact numbers of venues will vary depending on the methodological approach. We expect the pilot to cover less venues than the full fieldwork. The full fieldwork would ideally include 2 separate waves of data collection.
In more detail, the approximate number of venues the pilot & full fieldwork would include:
Please note this is anticipating an even split between Casino, AGC, Bingo and Betting premises.
•	Minimum: 16 venues
•	Expected: 24 venues
•	Ideal: 32 + venues
These figures should be used to inform estimated minimum, expected and ideal costings.
In addition to venue coverage, ideal, expected and minimum participant sampling numbers would be established in project set up and explored via the Pilot Study to ensure a diversity of perspectives are captured; including identities that are often under-represented in gambling research.
Deliverables -
Data will be shared in clear, appropriately anonymised formats. A short report accounting the methodological approach, ethics, and any lessons learned for the Commission, would also be produced for internal use and to inform the wider Gaming Machine evaluation. The vendor must comply with all relevant legislation, including data protection (GDPR) legislation.
Timescale -
The project will have natural periods of intensity and pause due to implementation timelines. Vendors would need to be able to deliver fieldwork in windows across 2027 to early 2029.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Links to sources:
(*1) Gambling Act Review White Paper - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/high-stakes-gambling-reform-for-the-digital-age
(*2) January 2026 Response - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/consultation-response/january-2025-gaming-machine-consultation-part-1-response
(*3) September 2026 Response - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/consultation-response/january-2025-consultation-on-proposed-changes-to-the-gmts-testing-strategy-and-lccp-consultation-response/related-documents-january-2025-gaming-machine-consultation-part-2-response
(*4) Proposal 4 / September 2026 Response - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/consultation-response/january-2025-consultation-on-proposed-changes-to-the-gmts-testing-strategy-and-lccp-consultation-response/proposal-4-gaming-machine-consultation-part-2-response
(*5) The Commission's Research Governance Framework - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/standards/research-governance-framework/data-accessibility-and-data-sharing-information-and-data-research-governance

title: CP2821-26 Study of Carbon Sequestration and Soil Health Impacts within Highway Earthworks
description:
Devon County Council (DCC), is delivering the A382 Link Road Development near Newton Abbot, Devon.  In addition to the main scheme, additional funding has been made available through the ADEPT Live Labs 2: Decarbonising Local Roads programme to fund carbon reduction measures on the project. The scheme seeks not only to improve highway safety, network resilience and traffic flow, but also to demonstrate innovative approaches to reducing and removing carbon emissions from highway construction activities.
As part of the project's carbon-negative aspirations, DCC wishes to investigate the impact of construction activities on soil carbon levels and the potential benefits of incorporating biochar, enhanced mineral weathering and mycorrhizal fungi into traditional highway earthworks operations. Emerging research suggests that these products may increase carbon sequestration rates, improve soil health and increase long-term carbon storage within highway verges and associated landscape areas.
The budget available is between £150,000 and £170,000 further details on the cost strategy are given in the documentation.

title: CPH137 - Provision of Domestic Abuse Support Services
description:
Derbyshire County Council is seeking to appoint a provider (or providers) to deliver high-quality, effective domestic abuse support services for victims and survivors of all ages and genders across assessed levels of risk. Services must be accessible, trauma-informed and focus on improving the safety, wellbeing and long-term of individuals affected by domestic abuse.
The service will include a single point of access available to victims, professionals and families, delivered through a dedicated domestic abuse helpline and supporting online presence.
Provision will cover the eight district and boroughs of Derbyshire County, which excludes Derby City.
The Derbyshire Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner (OPCC) works in partnership with the Council to commission support services will provide a financial contribution to this contract. The Council and the OPCC require a cohesive service capable of delivering both emotional and practical support, in community settings and within accommodation based services, including refuge provision.
Support for children and families experiencing or impacted by domestic abuse must be an integral component of the service delivery model. A minimum of 20% of the total contract value is required to be allocated to service supporting children and young people (defined as individuals up to their 18th birthday).
The Council welcomes bids from consortia (with a lead provider) or sole providers who can demonstrate the capability to deliver a coordinated, countywide service model across the full geographic area (excluding Derby City).
The contract is expected to commence on 1 April 2027 for an initial period of three (3) years to 31 March 2030, with the option to extend for a further three periods of 12 months (3 + 1 + 1 + 1). A mobilisation period will apply prior to service commencement.
The minimum contract value is £3,545,086 per annum, giving an estimated total value of £21,270,516 over the full term including extensions.
Prospective tenderers should note that this contract may be affected by Local Government Reorganisation (LGR), anticipated to take place in April 2028. In accordance with Schedule 8 of the Procurement Act 2023, this contract may be novated to a successor Council or otherwise modified to reflect the requirements of any new Council arrangements arising from LGR. The exact nature of any modification or novation cannot be determined at this time, but such changes will be managed under both the Procurement Act 2023 and the contractual provisions.
Ahead of these changes, discussions with Derby City and District and Borough representatives are ongoing and there is a shared commitment to work together to align future domestic abuse provision as much as practicable.
The Authority reserves the right to modify the Contract during its term where:
• additional funding becomes available to the Authority from any source;
• demand for the Services exceeds forecast, anticipated or historic service levels;
• the Authority requires additional resources, capacity or service provision to improve outcomes for service users;
• the Authority identifies emerging needs, opportunities for service improvement, or wishes to develop, test, pilot, evaluate or implement alternative approaches to the delivery of the Services;
• exceptional, unforeseeable and evidenced cost pressures materially affect service delivery and are demonstrated through open-book accounting; or
• underspend, unspent grant funding, over-recovery of costs or other surplus funding is identified.
Modifications may include increases or decreases in service volumes, capacity, staffing, service delivery models, interventions, activities, locations, reporting requirements or other aspects of service delivery necessary to support the continued provision and improvement of the Services.
The financial value of any such modification cannot be determined at the commencement of the procurement because it is dependent upon future funding allocations, service demand, operational requirements, service development opportunities and other circumstances which are not known to the Authority at the time of publication.
Any such modification shall be limited to services that are within the scope of, directly related to, ancillary to, or of the same nature as the Services described in the Specification, shall be supported by appropriate evidence, and shall not alter the overall nature of the Contract.
The Authority also reserves the right to undertake annual reviews of contract rates linked to changes in the All-Items Consumer Prices Index (CPI), subject to the Authority's approval and the terms of the Contract.

title: Care and Wellbeing in Supported Living Services in Hillingdon
description:
The London Borough of Hillingdon is pleased to invite current and prospective providers to attend a Provider Engagement Event as part of the recommissioning of its Care and Wellbeing in Supported Living Services.
The Council intends to recommission these services to ensure future provision reflects current and projected demand, promotes independence and choice, and delivers positive outcomes for people requiring supported living services. The future model will support individuals to develop and maintain their skills, maximise their independence, and live fulfilling lives within their communities.
As part of the pre-procurement phase, the Council is reviewing how supported living services can evolve to meet changing needs and aspirations. The recommissioning programme aims to establish a flexible, innovative, and sustainable service model that:
•	Promotes person-centred and strengths-based support.
•	Encourages independence, choice, and community inclusion.
•	Responds effectively to changing levels and types of demand.
•	Makes effective use of technology and innovative approaches to service delivery.
•	Aligns with current and emerging regulatory requirements.
•	Supports continuous improvement and collaboration across the sector.
•	Delivers good-quality services and value for money.
The procurement is expected to establish long-term contractual arrangements for the delivery of care and wellbeing in supported living services. The scope and structure of the future service model are currently being developed and may include changes to service specifications, operating arrangements, and delivery models arising from the recommissioning review.
This event will provide an opportunity for providers to:
•	Learn about the Council's vision and objectives for the future service model.
•	Understand the recommissioning programme and anticipated procurement approach.
•	Share feedback and insights to help shape future service delivery.
•	Discuss innovation, partnership working, and opportunities for continuous service development.
•	Engage directly with Council officers.

title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – 81322998-Development of a project pipeline for the CAFI Cameroon Partnership and related activities
description: As part of its ongoing efforts to pursue its sustainable development goals and achieve the ambitions set out by the Government in its vision for 2035, Cameroon adopted in 2020, to implement the second phase of its vision covering the period 2020-2030, a policy document entitled the National Development Strategy 2020-2030 (SND30). During this phase, the Government intends to bring about the structural transformation of the economy through industrialisation. However, achieving these objectives will require well-structured measures designed to minimise the impact on the environment, particularly in light of the growing momentum of environmental protection initiatives promoted within the framework of the various Conferences of the Parties on climate change (COP), the most recent of which (COP 31) was held in Recife, Brazil, from 10. - 21. November 2025. With a view to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, Cameroon has joined the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI), which aims to recognise and preserve the value of the region"s forests in order to mitigate climate change and reduce poverty. More specifically, the long-term objective of the Cameroon-CAFI partnership is to facilitate the acceleration of economic development by promoting the application of the principle of a "green economy" through which Cameroonian value chains are made competitive and meet the demands of international, national and sub-regional markets, whilst Cameroon ensures food security and reduces the impact of the development of these sectors on deforestation and forest degradation. This is in line with the principles set out in the SND30 and defined in the Letter of Intent (LOI) signed between Cameroon and CAFI in October 2024 with a view to realising the ambitions outlined in the sectoral strategies and will underpin the success of the future partnership. In order to facilitate the consolidation and implementation of the Letter of Intent signed for a long-term partnership between Cameroon and CAFI, the partners have decided to envisage a three-year pilot phase. Furthermore, it was decided to implement a sectoral and multi-level coordination project, which will also oversee the portfolio management and coordination of three technical projects funded by CAFI. Its aim will be to strengthen the capacities of national technical bodies for enhanced and inclusive cross-sectoral coordination, and for strategic and spatial planning, in order to move towards a green economy. This coordination aims to build consensus on the planning tools to be developed, the reforms to be implemented and the innovative financing mechanisms for the development of the green economy, which will help to increase the mobilisation and alignment of interventions and funding from the public and private sectors, both national and international.

title: Germany – Transport systems consultancy services – Erstellung einer verkehrsplanerischen Untersuchung / eines Verkehrsgutachtens zur Neugestaltung der Innenstadt Brake einschließlich verkehrsplanerischer Beratung.
description: Erstellung einer verkehrsplanerischen Untersuchung / eines Verkehrsgutachtens im Zusammenhang mit der Neugestaltung der Innenstadt Brake (Unterweser) Offenes Verfahren gem. § 15 VgV Die Stadt Brake (Unterweser) beabsichtigt, ihre Innenstadt umfassend aufzuwerten und neu zu ordnen. Hintergrund der angestrebten Innenstadtumgestaltung ist ein im Rahmen der Erstellung eines Integrierten Stadtentwicklungskonzepts (ISEK) festgestellter Handlungs- und Steuerungsbedarf. In der Folge erstellte die Stadt Brake (Unterweser) ein Integriertes Handlungskonzept, den sogenannten "Masterplan Innenstadt Brake (Unterweser)", und bewarb sich mit diesem Konzept zur Neuordnung der Innenstadt um die Aufnahme in das Städtebauförderprogramm "Lebendige Zentren". Der Aufnahmebescheid ging im Dezember 2023 ein. Vor diesem Hintergrund soll der Stadterneuerungsprozess durch einen freiraumplanerischen Wettbewerb mit verkehrsplanerischen Ansätzen und Konzeptteil vorangetrieben werden. Ziel ist es, die freiraumplanerische Qualität sowie die funktionale Leistungsfähigkeit der Innenstadt durch vergleichende Entwurfsansätze abzusichern. Hierzu werden Planungsteams aus dem Bereich der Landschaftsarchitektur und Verkehrsplanung eingeladen, für das Plangebiet sowie angrenzende innenstadtnahe Teilbereiche einen Entwurfsvorschlag und einen Rahmenplan für die Entwicklung der Innenstadt zu erarbeiten. Zur Vorbereitung des Wettbewerbsverfahrens und zur Einordnung der verkehrlichen Situation in der Innenstadt soll ein Verkehrsgutachten erstellt werden. Das zu erstellende Gutachten bildet eine verbindliche Grundlage für das anschließende Wettbewerbsverfahren und wird den teilnehmenden Planungsteams zur Verfügung gestellt. Nach Zuschlagserteilung ist die Erbringung der vorgenannten Leistungen umgehend aufzunehmen, damit die erforderlichen Grundlagen rechtzeitig für die Durchführung des Wettbewerbsverfahrens zur Verfügung stehen. Das Verkehrsgutachten muss demnach spätestens Mitte Februar 2027 abschließend abgestimmt vorliegen. Neben der Erstellung des Verkehrsgutachtens ist für den bezuschlagten Bieter die Teilnahme am Wettbewerb als Sachverständige*r, einschließlich der quantitativen Prüfung der fünf Wettbewerbsarbeiten sowie die Teilnahme an den Verfahrensterminen, vorgesehen. Eine Teilnahme des bezuschlagten Bieters an dem Wettbewerbsverfahren auf Teilnehmer-Seite ist nicht möglich. description: International Media Support (IMS) seeks to establish a pool of qualified research providers through framework agreements to deliver recurring audience segmentation studies and related audience intelligence services across Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. Across the region, disinformation, information manipulation, and declining trust in information sources continue to affect public discourse and democratic resilience. title: Germany – Site preparation work – Brückenschlag für Hamburg - Planungsleistungen und Bauleistungen für Erdbau und Straße
description: Die Freihafenelbbrücke (FHEB) wurde durch einen Schiffsanprall am 28.10.2025 beschädigt. Nachfolgende Untersuchungen und Überprüfungen der HPA haben ergeben, dass die Brücke nicht vor Ort reparabel ist, nicht mehr verkehrssicher genutzt werden kann und das Mittelteil schnellstmöglich ausgebaut werden muss. Die Straße inkl. Fuß- und Radweg und die mittlere Schiffsdurchfahrt sind gesperrt. Im selben Zeitraum wurde bei Untersuchungen an verschiedenen Bauwerken in der Trasse Neue Elbbrücken (B4/B75) festgestellt, dass diese Bauwerke in einem schlechteren Zustand sind, als bisherige Prüfungen erwarten ließen. Dies führt dazu, dass in den kommenden Jah-ren immer wieder mit unterschiedlichen, erheblichen Einschränkungen an den Bauwerken dieser Trasse für Reparatur- und Ertüchtigungsarbeiten zu rechnen ist. Die zeitliche Überlagerung mit den Folgen der Schiffshavarie und die zu beobachtenden verkehrlichen Auswirkungen erzeugen eine besondere zeitliche Dringlichkeit für eine Abhilfe. Sperrungen im Bereich der Neuen Elbbrücken führen zu deutlich eingeschränkten Verkehrskapazitäten, die über einen mehrjährigen Zeitraum zu den relevanten Tageszeiten zu Ver-kehrsverhältnissen führen, die weder für den Pendler- noch für die Verkehre des Hamburger Hafens hinnehmbar sind. Um Abhilfe zu schaffen ist geplant, einen Brückenzug unmittelbar westlich der Neuen Elbbrücken errichten. Die Brücke soll Ende 2027 fertiggestellt werden. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist der Bau und die integrierte Planung eines Brückenzuges über die Norderelbe in Hamburg. Für eine schnelle Herstellung des Brückenzuges werden Brückengeräte für die militärische Infrastruktur und Zivile Verteidigung genutzt. Der Brückenzug wird als Einfeldträger-Kette aus D-Brücken und S-Brücken in Abhängigkeit von der erforderlichen Stützweite ausgebildet. Diese Brückenelemente werden von der Auftraggeberin voraussichtlich vom Bund gemietet. Es wird ein Vertragspartner gesucht, der die laufenden Planungen in der Entwurfsplanung übernimmt und fortsetzt (Stufe 1 der Beauftragung) sowie nach Entscheidung der Hamburger Bürgerschaft zur Realisierung einer Behelfsbrücke voraussichtlich Ende November 2026 mit den Bauarbeiten beginnt (Stufe 2 der Beauftragung) und diese bis Ende 2027 abschließt. Der Auftragnehmer hat auf Basis der vorhandenen Unterlagen eine ausführungsreife Planung zu entwickeln und parallel die erforderlichen Leistungen zur Kampfmittelfreimachung zu erbringen. Dies umfasst die Prüfung und Fortschreibung von Räumkonzepten, Sondierungsmaßnahmen zur Befreiung von Kampfmittelverdacht sowie ggf. die technische Unterstützung der fachgerechten Räumung und Entsorgung vorhandener Kampfmittel unter Abstimmung mit den zuständigen Behörden. Die Planung für die Ausführung beinhaltet insbesondere die Freimachung von Bewuchs, Bodenbelägen und sonstiger Bausubstanz, Erdbaumaßnahmen zur Herstellung der Rampenkörper einschließlich Geländeaufhöhungen, die Planung von Baugrundverbesserungen nach erweiterten Baugrunderkundungen sowie die Dimensionierung erforderlicher Verbaukonstruktionen, insbesondere in Form von rückverankerten Spundwänden oder vergleichbaren Systemen sowie die Planung für den Straßenbau, unterBerücksichtigung der Belastungsklasse 100, einschließlich der Anschlussbereiche. Darüber hinaus sind die Rampenbereiche im Bereich der Widerlager unter Einsatz von Stabilisierungssäulen auszubilden und ein schlüssiges Bauablaufkonzept unter Berücksichtigung der verkehrlichen Anforderungen zu entwickeln. Sollten im Laufe der Planung provisorische Flächenbefestigungen oder Baustraßen benötigt werden, sind diese ebenfalls Gegenstand dieser Beauftragung.

description: Dans le cadre de l'organisation des Jeux olympiques et paralympiques d'hiver Alpes 2030, la Solideo Alpes 2030 recherche un prestataire pour l'accompagner dans la mise en oeuvre de sa stratégie d'accessibilité universelle. Cette stratégie vise à garantir à tous les usagers une qualité d'usage optimale. Elle doit aussi laisser un héritage durable aux territoires de montagne après les Jeux. Le périmètre porte sur des ouvrages situés en Haute-Savoie, en Savoie, dans le Briançonnais et dans la métropole de Lyon. Le détail des missions est précisé dans le CCTP. L'accord-cadre est mono-attributaire. Il est exécuté par bons de commande et marchés subséquents (articles R. 2162-2 à R. 2162-14 du Code de la commande publique), sans montant minimum et avec un montant maximum de 200 000 euro(s) HT par an, soit 800 000 euro(s) HT sur la durée totale de l'accord-cadre, reconductions comprises. Il est conclu pour une période initiale de 12 mois, reconductible tacitement trois fois par période de 12 mois, soit 48 mois au maximum. Il est précisé que la valeur estimée indiquée dans le présent avis couvre la durée totale de l'accord-cadre, reconductions comprises, ainsi que la possibilité de conclure des marchés similaires en application de l'article R. 2122-7 du Code de la commande publique

title: France – Rolling stock – Conception et acquisition de Matériel roulant ferroviaire et autres prestations associées
description: Conception et acquisition de Matériel roulant ferroviaire et autres prestations associées. La présente consultation a pour objet l’acquisition d’une gamme de Matériels Roulants, la réalisation de prestations de maintenance associées, ainsi que la mise en place de dispositifs de recharge d’énergie. Ce projet est conduit par la SPL SPIIT, agissant en qualité de Maître d’Ouvrage. Les Régions Occitanie et Nouvelle-Aquitaine ont créé une société dédiée au développement du système ferroviaire sur leur territoire, prenant la forme d’une Société Publique Locale dénommée SOCIÉTÉ PUBLIQUE INTERRÉGIONALE DES INVESTISSEMENTS EN FAVEUR DES TRANSPORTS (SPL SPIIT). A la date de publication de la présente consultation, la SPL SPIIT a pour actionnaires la Région Nouvelle-Aquitaine, la Région Occitanie et la Région Centre-Val de Loire qui a intégré le capital de la SPL SPIIT en novembre 2025. Au jour de la publication du présent document, il est prévu que la Région Bretagne intègre le capital de la SPL SPIIT dans les prochains mois. La SPL SPIIT a signé avec ses Régions actionnaires un contrat de concession de quarante-deux (42) ans. Dans ce cadre, la SPL SPIIT est chargée du financement, de la gestion, de l’acquisition du matériel roulant TER des Régions, et de sa mise à disposition auprès des exploitants désignés par les Régions, au fur et à mesure de l’attribution des contrats de service public d’exploitation. La SPL SPIIT pourrait, à l’avenir, au cours de l’exécution du présent Accord-Cadre, se voir confier l’acquisition de matériels roulants ferroviaires pour le compte d’autres Régions ou entités publiques, le cas échéant, pour les mêmes objectifs que ceux faisant l’objet de la présente consultation. Dans l’objectif de décarboner les services de transports ferroviaires sur le territoire, les Régions actionnaires ont confié à la SPL SPIIT la mission d’acquisition de Matériels Roulants (MR) ferroviaires avec un objectif d’amélioration environnemental. Ces Matériels Roulants doivent réduire leur impact sur l’environnement tout au long de leur cycle de vie.

title: Norway – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Kunnskap om arbeidsinkludering i et arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv i endring og omstilling. Invitasjon til markedsdialog.
description: Globalisering og megatrender har innvirkning på arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv, og medfører behov for endring og omstilling. Raske teknologiske framskritt, demografiske endringer, klimaendringer og kriser som Covid-19 er eksempler på sentrale drivere for endring i samfunnet, og som både enkeltvis og samlet har konsekvenser for arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv. Hvordan arbeidsmarkedet vil utvikle seg framover, og hvordan arbeidstakere og arbeidsgivere vil tilpasse seg disse endringene, er usikkert. Det er grunn til å tro at endringene vil ha innvirkning på forvaltningens organisering og gjennomføringsevne, og det er usikkert hvilke tiltak og virkemidler som framover vil være de mest effektive for å bidra til arbeidsinkludering og høy arbeidsdeltakelse. Alle som kan jobbe skal få mulighet til å jobbe. Arbeids- og inkluderingsdepartementet (AID) ønsker kunnskap om hvordan store samfunnsendringer, utviklingstrekk og omstillinger i det norske arbeidsmarkedet og arbeidslivet har innvirkning på arbeidsdeltakelse og arbeidsinkludering. Det er behov for kunnskap om hvordan tiltak og virkemidler fungerer i en slik kontekst. Det er videre behov for kunnskap om grupper som i dag er vurdert til å være utsatt på arbeidsmarkedet, og hvordan situasjonen for disse vil kunne bli framover. Omstillinger kan ramme ulikt. For noen kan omstilling bidra til inkludering i arbeid, mens for andre kan omstilling føre til ekskludering fra arbeid. Det er også usikkert om grupper som vi i dag vurderer som utsatt på arbeidsmarkedet vil være det framover, eller om dette vil endre seg og om det er andre grupper som kommer til. Det finnes mye kunnskap, og det er over mange år iverksatt en rekke tiltak og virkemidler for å få flere og særlig utsatte grupper i arbeid. Det er imidlertid behov for helhetlig og mer systematisk kunnskap om hvordan endringer og omstilling treffer disse, og hvordan tiltak og virkemidler enkeltvis og samlet fungerer nå og framover. I denne veiledende kunngjøringen inviterer vi forskningsmiljøer til å komme med innspill til rammer for et FoU-prosjekt som kan gi oss relevant og helhetlig kunnskap om hvordan endringer og omstillinger i arbeidsmarked og arbeidsliv på kort og lang sikt treffer utsatte grupper, virksomheter, forvaltning og tjenester, og hvordan flest mulig kan inkluderes i arbeid.

title: Norway – Administrative educational services – 16-UDE-2026 Development and analysis of municipal natural science samples in osloskolen - New publication
description: PURPOSE AND SCOPE The Agency for Education is responsible for the design, execution and return of municipal tests, Oslo tests, in different disciplines/skills at a selection stage in primary and secondary schools. As a part of the work on design, quality assurance, implementation and return of results from the Oslo tests, the Agency for Education wants to enter into an agreement with a professional environment that will be responsible for science from the school year 2026/2027 until the end of the school year 2028/2029 with an option for up to two years. Background The Agency for Education (UDE) has a trial and follow-up plan that is included in a comprehensive work for on-the-go assessment and follow-up of the Students in Oslo. The plan is a part of UDE's system for following up requirements in the law and regulations, including the national quality assessments. The aim of the system is to contribute to quality development in primary and secondary education and increased learning outcomes for the pupils. In addition to regular underway evaluations in the class room, tests and mappings provide useful information on the pupils ́ competence and areas of development. This information shall be actively used by pupils, teachers and school managers to promote learning and ensure early efforts. The trial and follow-up plan includes both governmental tests (government mapping samples and national tests) and municipal tests (Oslo samples). Oslo tests apply for pupils in the 4th and 7th years. These are implemented electronically and re-developed each year. Only one test will be carried out for years 2-5, but the contracting authority has an option for a sample no. 2. The assignment UDE would like a professional environment that shall be responsible for the municipal tests in the discipline of rnaturfag. The Consultant shall develop, analyse and follow up the tests in accordance with the requirements in this annex. The contracting authority draws attention to the fact that the estimated value is based on historical data and the expected future need, and includes options. The estimate is only a guideline and is without obligation for the Contracting Authority. See the Norwegian Public Procurement Regulations (SSA-O), annex 1 for further information on the assignment.

title: Investigator Training Programme
description:
The Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is seeking a bespoke training programme that will equip its people with the core skills required to effectively conduct SFO investigations, based around the powers available to the SFO to exercise (including the Criminal Justice Act 1987/Section 2 and Proceeds of Crime Act 2002). The programme will cover the following areas:
•	The theory and process behind conducting an investigation
•	Interviewing witnesses and victims
•	Interviewing suspects
The primary participants of the programme will be investigators involved in criminal financial investigations, as well as civil recovery and confiscation investigations. In turn, this will range from new entrant, trainee investigators, to experienced investigators/senior investigators, investigative lawyers and financial investigators.
By completing the Investigator Training Programme, learners will gain an increased confidence in:
•	The theory and process that constitutes an investigation conducted by the SFO
•	Adopting a strategic, methodical and investigative mindset throughout all stages of an investigation
•	Their role and responsibility within an SFO investigation
•	Investigative decision making and risk management
•	Exercising the powers available to the SFO throughout an investigation
•	Interviewing, taking and structuring statements from witnesses, victims and suspects.
To support learners in digesting and applying the programme content, whilst recognising the commitments from their day-to-day roles, we intend to split the course content into modules, comprising of up to three days per module. The modules will combine theory, along with interactive engagement and regular opportunities to practice the skills taught.

title: SEND Mediation and Disagreement Resolution Service
description:
Rotherham Borough Council (RBC) are running a single procurement process that will result in the commissioning of an impartial SEND Mediation and Disagreement Resolution Service.
1The Children and Families Act 2014 (the "Act"), Chapter 6 sets out requirements regarding appeals, mediation and disagreement resolution for children and young people in England with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND).
The Act was followed by the Special Educational Needs and Disability Code of Practice 2015: 0 to 25 years.  This Statutory Code of Practice sets out the guidance for organisations who work with and support children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities explaining their duties and responsibilities under Part 3 of the Act, details of the legal requirements that must be followed without exception and statutory guidance that must be followed by law (unless there is a legitimate reason not to).  
Both the Act and Code of Practice outline: 
•	Early resolution of disagreements at a local level, 
•	Independent disagreement resolution arrangements which local authorities must make available for disagreements across special educational provision, 
•	Independent mediation arrangements which parents/carers and young people can use before deciding whether to appeal to the SEND First Tier Tribunal and for health and social care complaints in relation to Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs), 
•	Conditions for appealing to the Tribunal or making disability discrimination claims.
In addition, The Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014 set out in detail what is required by Local Authorities (LAs) for assessing the Education, Health and Care (EHC) needs of children and young people and, where necessary, drawing up EHC plans including the requirements regarding mediation and appeal.
In order to ensure strong quality standards the Service Provider must be a Registered Provider with the Civil Mediation Council and ensure that all Mediators are trained, qualified and experienced and must be included on the SEND Mediator Register.
The Service Provider must also provide a commitment to comply with any additional professional standards developed as a result of the SEND reforms.
The Service Provider will provide confidential, independent and impartial mediation advice and Mediation and Disagreement Resolution Service to Service Users within the Rotherham borough in order to assist the discharge of statutory obligations under the Act and the Code of Practice.
The Service Provider will ensure that the Service is:
•	Independent, confidential and impartial to Service Users,
•	Flexible yet cost effective, enabling Service Users to access the Service they need, when they need it. This Service should be a hybrid model with online mediation as the default.
In providing the Service the Service Provider must ensure that it, and its staff:
•	Adhere to the agreed timetable throughout the process,
•	Demonstrate trauma-informed, parent-centered practice,
•	Seek feedback from Service Users to inform and influence service development as well as providing evidence of user satisfaction improvements,
•	Tailor the Service to individual Service User needs and especially in reference to groups with protected characteristics as defined in the Equality Act 2010,
•	Is a Civil Mediation Council (CMC) registered Provider and
•	Use only Mediators registered with the CMC.
The current SEND reform programme and associated DfE policy development present a known risk which may necessitate future modifications of the contract. Whilst the final legislative and operational requirements are not yet fully defined, the reforms may result in changes to statutory mediation requirements, dispute resolution pathways, Individual Support Plan (ISP) arrangements, referral volumes, eligibility criteria, performance measures, reporting requirements, multi-agency working arrangements, and the respective responsibilities of Local Authorities, schools and health partners.
Consequently, the Council may need to modify the contract during its term to reflect changes in legislation, statutory guidance, service delivery models, demand levels or commissioning requirements arising from the national SEND reform programme. Any modifications would be limited to those necessary to maintain statutory compliance, service continuity and effective delivery of the SEND Mediation and Disagreement Resolution Service.

title: Statutory and non-statutory Advocacy: future service planning
description:
Manchester City Council is inviting organisations to participate in a Preliminary Market Engagement exercise regarding a review of statutory and non-statutory Advocacy service delivery.
Please note the following explanation of the Council’s approach to preliminary market engagement; the core principle for underpinning our approach is to ensure probity be maintained throughout the process by strict adherence to the following guidelines:
All potential suppliers are informed that they are invited to participate in soft market testing
Any information provided by the authority to a supplier participating in preliminary market engagement will be shared with all suppliers participating in the exercise.
Any information provided by a supplier participating in preliminary market engagement will be deemed as commercially sensitive and handled by the authority in such a manner as to ensure commercial confidentiality is not violated.
Any information provided by a supplier participating in preliminary market engagement will not be shared with any third party without the express permission and written consent of the participating supplier.
The preliminary market engagement exercise is to be undertaken to ascertain if the Council wishes to proceed to a competitive tender process and if so will help inform the design of any future procurement process and will assist the Council to shape their requirements to ensure that they obtain the best solution to meet their needs and that will be most attractive to the market to ensure as much competition as possible.
If the outcome of the preliminary market engagement is such that the authority decides to go out for a competitive tender (N.B: the Council reserves the right not to do so if it so decides or to utilise other procurements routes open to it such as pre-tendered national/regional/other frameworks), then all suppliers who have participated in the preliminary market engagement will be notified of the tendering opportunity.
Participation in the preliminary market engagement does not mean that you will automatically qualify for the tender opportunity and all prospective tenders, irrespective of previous participation, will be required to register and meet the conditions of participation of the tender at that time.
Overview
Manchester City Council / Manchester Local Care Organisation is undertaking a review of its Advocacy Services arrangements in advance of the current contract ending on 30th September 2027.
Advocacy providers are invited to attend a Preliminary Market Engagement workshop via Teams (to be held at 3pm on Tuesday 20th October 2026) to discuss the matters outlined below.
To help shape and inform the structure of the workshop, attendees are asked to complete a supplementary survey via The Chest e-procurement portal, which should take approximately 10-15 minutes to complete.
This preliminary market engagement exercise will help us gain insight on current challenges, opportunities, future demand pressures, and considerations for the development of a future Advocacy services model. This engagement exercise is open to organisations that currently provide statutory and/or non-statutory Advocacy services - Providers do not need to currently deliver services within Manchester to participate.
No decisions have been made regarding the future service delivery model at this stage, and feedback gathered through this engagement process will be considered alongside current Advocacy service performance, demand analysis, financial information, benchmarking activity, and statutory requirements before any future commissioning decisions are taken. The Council's key priority going forward is to ensure a sustainable, effective and responsive Advocacy provision, which enables positive outcomes for citizens.

title: The appointment of Internal Auditors
description:
First Garden Cities Homes (FGCH), a Registered Provider of Social Housing based in Letchworth Garden City and Welwyn Garden City, Hertfordshire, intends to appoint a firm to act as its outsourced internal audit function from 1 April 2027. The current contract reaches its natural end on 31/03/2027.
The appointed firm will report to FGCH's Audit & Risk Committee and provide independent, objective assurance over governance, risk management and internal control. The services include a risk-based strategic and annual internal audit plan, delivery of the agreed programme of reviews, follow-up of agreed actions through a recommendation tracker, attendance at Audit & Risk Committee meetings as required, support to counter-fraud arrangements, and an annual internal audit opinion timed to inform the Board's annual assurance to the Regulator of Social Housing.
The contract will run for three years, with an option to extend once by a further two years. It will be a rate-based engagement: FGCH will appoint a team at a single composite day rate, with the volume of work commissioned annually by the Audit & Risk Committee. Following the regulatory judgement issued to FGCH in 2025, the Committee has set an elevated assurance requirement. The programme will therefore be broader in the next three years than is typical for a Registered Provider of FGCH's size, but it is expected to reduce in years 4 and 5 if an extension is agreed.
The Procurement Act 2023 requires that consideration be given to dividing all contracts into lots. This contract will not be divided into lots. Internal audit must produce a single, integrated opinion on FGCH's framework of governance, risk management and control, from one audit provider.
FGCH intends to use the Competitive Flexible Procedure as defined in s.20 of the Act comprising a written tender stage open to all suppliers, followed by a scored presentation to the selection panel, made up of Audit & Risk Committee members, for the highest-ranked tenderers. There will be no negotiation.

title: ITT - Storage Design and Environmental Requirements Framework for Archaeological Archives in England - UID 369
description:
This a visionary project to define the ideal physical infrastructure for a National Collection of Archaeological Archives (NCAA) in England. It addresses the growing crisis in archaeological archive storage due to museum capacity limits and aims to establish a state-of-the-art national store that ensures preservation, accessibility, and sustainability for whole archaeological archives of England where regional deposition is not possible. 
The aim of this project is to define a best evidence-based storage system for a national store of archaeological archives. The baseline model for such a store has already been outlined in the Options for Sustainable Archaeological Archives Report and is described below. The Operating Model has also been explored.
In addition to establishing a vision for a national archaeological archive repository, this project will provide an evidence base for future infrastructure planning, including storage environments, spatial organisation, sustainability, and repository design requirements. The findings will support complementary work on business case development, cost modelling, building design, and site selection.
