title: OLE Monitoring for Class 730
description:
General Information & Purpose of Engagement
WM Trains Ltd is undertaking this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 to engage the market regarding the supply and deployment of Overhead Line Equipment (OLE) Remote Condition Monitoring (RCM) systems across its Class 730/0 fleet.
WM Trains currently operates eight OLE monitoring systems fitted to its Class 350 fleet, delivered via Transmission Dynamics and funded through an asset owner initiative with Angel. This legacy deployment relies on an established, proprietary front-end user interface and database accessed collaboratively by WM Trains, Network Rail, and fleet maintainers to safeguard infrastructure and maintain operational continuity.
To enhance the coverage of its electrified routes, WM Trains requires an additional six monitoring systems for the Class 730/0 fleet. WM Trains considers that procuring an alternative, non-integrated solution would create fragmented operational dashboards, split data streams, and cause disproportionate technical difficulties in maintenance and real-time operations. Consequently, the core purpose of this PME is to directly test the market to establish whether any economic operator can realistically deliver the required functionality and integrate seamlessly with the existing proprietary setup without introducing disproportionate technical and operational difficulties. If the market engagement confirms that no compatible alternative can achieve this integration, WM Trains intends to formalise a direct award pursuant to Schedule 5, Paragraph 7 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Section 41 - Direct award in special cases: Additional or repeat goods, services or works).
Key Scope Overview & Technical Constraints
The planned requirement is strictly for the supply of OLE remote camera monitoring (RCM) and wireless accelerometer hardware, alongside the ongoing SaaS analytics subscription and the necessary engineering/design documentation. The physical installation and fitment to the Class 730/0 fleet will be undertaken separately by the fleet maintainer/OEM acting as the asset design authority.
To satisfy operational, safety, and regulatory requirements, any proposed system must meet the following mandatory criteria:
1.	Database & System Integration: All data generated by the Class 730 OLE systems must integrate fully and directly into the existing Class 350 OLE monitoring database.
2.	Unified Front-End User Interface: The solution must provide a single, common front-end interface that aligns RCM imagery and sensor analytics to deliver real-time combined analytics throughout train operation, avoiding fragmented software suites.
3.	Autonomous Defect Detection: The RCM system must autonomously identify and report dynamic OLE conditions, degradation, and infrastructure defects to designated stakeholders, with specific capability to identify and report on faulty dropper wires.
4.	5G Data Transmission: The solution must enable remote collection, processing, high-speed transfer, and review of dynamic OLE monitoring data utilising 5G capability.
5.	Camera & Environmental Resilience: The camera system must be self-cleaning to prevent data and evidence loss, include a proven method for low-light conditions, and require no regular roof access for maintenance.
6.	Physical & Systems Vehicle Integration: Roof-mounted equipment must be designed specifically for the Class 730 profile while strictly minimising physical and electrical integration into the host train network.
7.	Rolling Stock Safety & Standards: The installation must fully comply with all relevant rolling stock standards and legislation, and must not adversely affect vehicle safety, reliability, maintainability, gauging, fire performance, EMC compatibility, or passenger service operations.
8.	Engineering Deliverables & Approvals: The supplier must deliver all design, installation, commissioning, acceptance, and handover documentation required by the Infrastructure Manager (Network Rail), the TOC (WM Trains), the Fleet Maintainer (e.g. Siemens), and the ROSCO.
9.	Maintenance & Calibration: The supplier must provide clear, documented maintenance, calibration, and ongoing technical support requirements for the installed system.
10.	Data Ownership & Governance: All operational, diagnostic, and raw condition data generated across the fleet must be jointly and unreservedly owned by WM Trains Ltd and Network Rail, with unrestricted sharing rights for designated maintainers.
Scope Clarification: For the avoidance of doubt, this procurement relates strictly to OLE condition monitoring interoperability and ingestion into the established OLE analytics database. WM Trains is not seeking multi-system train integration and will not review proposals detailing the ingestion of unrelated rolling stock subsystems (such as onboard CCTV, PIS, or general telematics) into an OLE platform.

title: Who pays? Understanding cost misalignment between the NHS and Local Government
description:
The Local Government Association (LGA) is seeking a supplier to undertake a focused policy research project exploring the interaction between NHS Continuing Healthcare (CHC) and local authority adult social care.
Recent evidence has highlighted growing concerns about the relationship between CHC decision-making, adult social care expenditure and the incentives created by current funding arrangements. ADASS's Spring Survey 2026 found that 75% of Directors of Adult Social Services reported an increase in the number of people presenting to adult social care who were, or previously would have been, eligible for CHC, while 84% reported that Integrated Care Board (ICB) disinvestment in CHC was contributing to adult social care overspending pressures.
Research published by The King's Fund found that CHC eligibility rates have fallen significantly despite no change to the national eligibility framework, alongside substantial variation between different ICB areas.
While CHC provides the primary lens for this project, the LGA is also interested in the wider question of whether current funding and accountability arrangements across health and social care create incentives that transfer costs and risks between organisations rather than supporting whole-system decision making.
The LGA wishes to better understand:
•	How these issues are playing out locally
•	Whether current arrangements create misaligned incentives between organisations
•	The impact on local government, the NHS, people drawing on care and support, and unpaid carers
•	What reforms could improve alignment between health and social care funding and accountability.
This work will inform future LGA policy development and engagement with government, national partners and stakeholders.

title: Metabarcoding validation framework 2026/2027
description:
DNA-based methods have the potential to significantly change how we monitor and assess ecosystems. Natural England has been exploring the use of these methods for environmental monitoring for several years, delivering a series of reports which focus on the development of DNA-based methods with potential in a particular area. These methods are now being used more widely within Natural England, particularly the detection of ecological communities using environmental DNA (eDNA). This is often conducted by employing metabarcoding assays which target specific species assemblages (e.g. fish, mammals) or broader taxonomic groups (e.g. vertebrates, invertebrates, bacteria).
The DNA Team aims to operationalise DNA-based methods and produces guidance for using them in monitoring projects. In order to provide sound recommendations, it is important that we understand the limitations of, and uncertainties with, DNA-based methods. Natural England staff need to be able to understand how DNA-derived data can be used, and the confidence they can have in data derived using different DNA-based methods which have been validated to different stages.
Natural England previously commissioned the development of a framework to enable end users to assess confidence in metabarcoding assays and results (Pagaling and others, under review; a copy of the framework can be provided by Natural England upon request by emailing monitoring.innovation@naturalengland.org.uk). By using the checklist and levelled scale, end users can appropriately interpret results. It also provides validation and reporting standards for the development of new metabarcoding assays. The framework will enable end-users to determine the recommended scenarios for application of a given assay and improve assay performance with further validation.
This project will advance the metabarcoding assay validation framework by expanding upon previous work to conduct a further literature review and meta-analysis, covering more assays being used for different purposes and in different contexts. In addition beta testing of the framework and user guide will be required, as well as the creation and delivery of training materials and course .

title: Automated Distribution and Manufacturing Centre (ADMC)
description:
Automated Distribution and Manufacturing Centre (ADMC)
Procurement Early Engagement Notice
Purpose
This notice is to make potential contractors aware that, via the Nottinghamshire County Council (NCC) procurement team, Ashfield District Council (ADC) will commence a process to appoint a commercial operator for their Automated Distribution and Manufacturing Centre (ADMC).
The publication of this notice commences the preliminary market engagement stage of the procurement process. The procurement is expected to follow a Competitive Flexible Procedure, based on the Procurement Act 2023.
Background
The ADMC is a flagship project for Ashfield District Council. The ADMC will work with businesses to create and implement bespoke automation strategies and solutions that improve productivity and enable prosperity and growth.
The ADMC will be a 3,000m2 purpose built, multifunctional, automation centre. Its vision is based on four "pillars" of activity:
•	Research and Development
•	Prototyping and Proof of Principle
•	Showcasing and Demonstration
•	Skills and Training
The ADMC will be at the centre of a cluster of automation businesses, some of which will be located on the adjacent Ashfield Innovation and Technology Park that is also in development.
The ADMC building is expected to be completed by December 2027. More details can be found on the ADMC website at www.theadmc.co.uk.
Proposed Governance and Operation
ADC confirmed its positioning regarding governance and operation of the ADMC in January 2025. It has resolved to carry out a public procurement procedure to appoint an external organisation to run the ADMC.
ADC believe that this contracted approach will allow the ADMC to be operated effectively and efficiently such that it achieves its twin goals of supporting the greater adoption of automation within local and regional businesses and achieving financial sustainability.
A previous procurement process to appoint an operator for the ADMC took place in late 2025. This process was ultimately unsuccessful in appointing an operator due to a combination of factors including feedback from potential bidders about the scope of the contract as well as subsidy and compliance issues.
ADC aims to have a commercial operator appointed in 2027.
Preliminary Market Engagement stage of the Procurement Process
The procurement is expected to follow a Competitive Flexible Procedure, following the Procurement Act 2023. This notice commences the procurement process via a preliminary market engagement stage.
The preliminary market engagement stage is intended to allow potential contractors to gain a more detailed understanding of the ADMC, its progress, and the procurement process being undertaken. It will also support NCC and ADC to develop the first stage tender by helping to:
•	Develop the requirements and approach to the procurement.
•	Design the conditions of participation and award criteria.
•	Inform the scope of works being contracted and whether these works should be split into separate lots.
•	Prepare the tender notice and associated tender documents.
•	Identify likely contractual terms.
•	Building capacity in relation to the contract being awarded.
NCC/ADC proposes to run initial group engagement events via Teams on two dates:
•	Tuesday 10th November 10:00 - 11:00
•	Thursday 12th November 10:00 - 11:00
Further events may be run before the end of November 2026 as demand requires.
NCC/ADC will be having individual discussions with potential contractors. Contractors will be invited to express an interest in being part of those discussions following the group engagement events.
All information and material collected from these pre-market engagement activities will be documented and form part of the subsequent tender pack, respecting commercial confidentiality.
Contact
To express interest in being part of the Preliminary Market Engagement stage of this
procurement process and to be sent the ADMC - Intent to Go to Market - Power Point
Information Pack, please contact Jamie Burton - jamie.burton2@nottscc.gov.uk
Please feel free to submit any clarification questions to Jamie Burton -
jamie.burton2@nottscc.gov.uk NCC/ADC will respond to these promptly.

title: Supply and Repair of Intercar Barriers for Victoria Line Rolling Stock Fleet, London Underground
description:
This Contract Award Notice is issued in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 to notify the market of the intention to award a contract and to formally commence the standstill period for the Supply of Intercar Barriers for Victoria Line to support London Underground's Maintenance requirements.
In line with the Procurement Act 2023, this Contract Award Notice triggers an 8 working day stand still period, as applied automatically by the Find a Tender system.
The Authority will not enter into the contract before the end of this standstill period.
Intercar barriers prevent the risk of passengers on platforms falling into gaps between cars at stations, making them safety critical items. Due to the bespoke nature of the Intercar barriers and the technical dependency, only ICON Aerospace Technology can ensure full compatibility and continuity of supply. It is due to their purpose that all materials are critical for train operation.
The justification for awarding the supply and repair agreement to ICON Aerospace Technology Ltd without competition is in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.Clause 41.6, Schedule 5, paragraphs 6, which states; 
(6) The following conditions are met in relation to the public contract
(a) due to an absence of competition for technical reasons, only a particular supplier can supply the goods, services or works required, and
(b) there are no reasonable alternatives to those goods, services or works.
The Intercar Barriers are currently supplied by ICON Aerospace Technology Limited UK. Due to the bespoke nature of the Intercar Barriers and the technical dependency, only ICON Aerospace Technology  Limited UK can ensure full compatibility and continuity of service.

•	Seek feedback on performance management arrangements, including KPIs and Service Level Agreements.
•	Identify opportunities for innovation, sustainability improvements and value for money.
•	Ensure the procurement approach reflects current market conditions and encourages effective competition.
This stage does not formally commence a procurement process. Participation in this Pre market engagement is voluntary and will not provide any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent tender process.

description:
Norfolk County Council (NCC) has been procuring contracts for social investor provider partnerships over the last few years as part of a wider programme of social inclusion, and is now putting in place a framework agreement to better enable departments within the council to bring on board social investors for its social inclusion projects.
This strategic framework seeks to support long-term partnerships between funders, investors, outcome payers and Norfolk delivery partners in developing and implementing a wide range of investment projects aligned to UK government policy, NCC strategic objectives and the Norfolk Local Growth Plan. NCC are keen to see partnerships that deliver higher impact for beneficiaries, delivery partners and NCC commissioners.
In respect of Local Government Reorganisation (“LGR”), on 7 September 2026 the government withdrew an earlier decision that it was minded to establish three unitary councils for Norfolk and announced a ‘rapid review’ of its LGR programme in respect of Norfolk and some other areas.
On 4 December 2025, the then Secretary of State for Local Government made a written statement [UIN HCWS1128] stating that the government intended to establish a Mayoral Strategic Authority for Norfolk and Suffolk as soon as possible, and that it was minded to hold inaugural mayoral elections in May 2028.
On 7 September 2026, the current Secretary of State said: “The Prime Minister is really clear that the Government’s ambition is to ensure that every area in England has, or is in the process of establishing, a strategic authority by the end of 2027, with strategic authorities in place everywhere by the end of 2028”.
Should LGR and/or devolution processes lead to unitary local government in Norfolk and/or to the establishment of a strategic authority covering Norfolk (i) the Framework Agreement] may be transferred, assigned or novated to any successor authority(ies) to the county council, or to any joint body incorporating or formed by any such successor and/or to any strategic authority; and/or (ii) the council or a successor authority or joint body may order services on behalf of other local authorities serving any area within Norfolk's current geographical boundaries.
The Framework Agreement may be used by any contracting authority that succeeds wholly or in part to the functions of Norfolk County Council.
The value in this notice is an estimate as it will depend on the call-offs the Council decides to make.  The estimate value of £75m is over all framework lots and can be shared between framework lots.  
Contracts awarded under the framework may have a maximum total duration of 10 years. 
No contract awarded from the framework will be permitted to extend beyond April 2040.
The values in this notice are estimates and depend on usage by the Council.

title: CEFAS26-83 Contract for Acquisition of a Controllable Plant Growth Chamber
description:
Cefas requires a plant growth chamber for the growth of microalgal cultures under controlled conditions. The chamber needs to provide consistent lighting and temperature throughout with several shelves to allow for high efficiency growth of cultures held in tissue culture flasks. The cultures need to be maintained for prolonged periods of time with growth conditions optimised towards maximum achievable cell growth rates and densities. A large internal capacity is required in order to maintain a high number of culture flasks of either the same or multiple species of marine microalgae and freshwater cyanobacteria. Options for gas or electrical lines into the unit are desirable but not essential. The unit will be expected to operate in a laboratory environment with external temperatures between 15-25 °C. As the primary use will be for the growth of marine microalgal cultures in seawater growth media, the unit will need to be able to operate with potentially high internal relative humidity.
Scope of Requirements:
1. Technical Requirement
1.1. The unit must have the ability to maintain internal temperatures between 10°C and 40°C both with and without lights across all shelves at any point. The ability to reach lower temperatures is desirable but not essential. The working internal temperature must be able to be set by the user and then maintained at the specified temperature. Temperature will be consistent throughout the unit. Temperature will be controllable in increments of 0.5°C with control in increments of 0.1°C preferable. Temperature will be monitored in increments of ±0.5°C with ±0.1°C accuracy preferable.
1.2. The unit must offer controllable lighting (preferably LED)
• The unit must offer variable light time periods (day/night cycling essential),
• The unit must offer controllable lighting intensity (able to achieve between 100 and 500 μmol photons/m²·s is essential, the ability to reach levels above or below this range is desirable)
• The unit will offer variable light spectrum (adjustable far red and/or the ability to simulate geographic light profiles is desirable).
1.3. The unit must provide a minimum of 0.5m2 of usable illuminated growth space. A total usable growth area of ≥1m2 is desirable. It is anticipated that this will be achieved with a number of internal shelves. A working height of ≥30cm between shelves is desired.
1.4. The unit must offer a thermal cutoff, deactivating the unit in the case of a set temperature threshold being exceeded, this threshold will be user modifiable. The unit must also offer a user programmable audio/visual alarm to alert users to performance outside of specified criteria.
2. Environmental Considerations
2.1. Unit will have a low power consumption.
2.2. Unit will be designed for reuse/remanufacture and of regenerative nature to eliminate waste where possible.
2.3. Consideration of how packaging will be managed. Ideally at the time of installation the supplier will remove packaging and dispose of by ethical and environmentally friendly methods. Where possible packaging is to be re-used or recycled.
2.4. Consideration of life cycle assessment for the equipment.
3. Hardware, Software, PC, Licenses, operating systems
3.1. Whilst remote connection may be a feature it is essential that all required control elements can be conducted on the unit itself.
3.2. It must be possible to transfer any collected data logs without the need for networking (USB port or similar for data transfer preferable).
4. Compatibility with existing hardware/software/equipment
4.1. Where applicable, any software must be compatible with Windows 11.
4.2. The unit must offer an interface with all the required control elements programmable on the unit itself, without the need for external connections.
5. Installation
5.1. Free standing unit will not need more than connection to power and a brief period of user tuning to the correct temperature and light cycle. Provided manual must be sufficient for all setup needs and available in accessible English, preferably the manual will be available in PDF format.
5.2. Supplier will confirm delivery requirements, including access dimensions and site preparation.
6. Ease of maintenance
6.1. It will be easy to sterilise the internal surfaces and these must be resistant to high humidity and corrosion. Stainless steel or equivalent is anticipated. Routine cleaning will be undertaken with a dilute virucide or 70% ethanol solution. It is anticipated that routine repairs and servicing may be carried out by a third-party maintenance provider. Replacement parts must therefore be available for 3rd party contractors to purchase.
7. Parts, Consumables and Updates
7.1. The unit will be serviceable by a qualified electrician/cooling unit engineer. Replacement parts must be available for purchase by a 3rd party when the unit is out of warranty period, for a minimum period of five years.
8. Warranties, Guarantees, Servicing
8.1. Warranties will start from the point of acceptance of delivery and once the goods have been tested to ensure they are in working order. Cefas expects a minimum warranty period of 12 months to be included in the purchase price. The level of technical support available during the warranty period (remote and/or on-site) must be detailed in the supplier's response. Suppliers are also invited to provide pricing for extended warranty options in the Pricing Schedule in RFQ Part II. Any pricing provided for extended warranty options will not be included as part of the tender evaluation. The information gathered will assist the Client in refining its procurement strategy, contract requirements and tender documentation before the formal procurement process commences.
Participation in this engagement process is entirely voluntary. Information obtained will be used solely to support the development of the proposed procurement and will not form part of any future evaluation process. 
The Client intends to procure a single-supplier contract for the provision of RSM services to the mechanical systems it manages across the property portfolio on behalf of it's Customers (including Nottinghamshire County Council) and projects.  The proposed contract will support the ongoing operation, compliance and maintenance of mechanical infrastructure across a range of public sector premises located primarily within Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire, Leicestershire and South Yorkshire.
The contract is expected to commence in April 2027 and will be based upon the NEC4 Term Service Short Contract. The proposed contract term is an initial two-year period with options to extend for up to two further periods of two years, giving a maximum potential term of six years (2 + 2 + 2 = maximum 6 years).
The proposed contract is expected to include, but may not be limited to:
• Mechanical works
• Plumbing works
• Drainage
• General repairs, servicing and maintenance associated with the above.
The Client may utilise the contract for both maintenance activities and construction or refurbishment projects requiring mechanical installation or replacement works.
The Client currently anticipates conducting the procurement under the Competitive Flexible Procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.  It is anticipated that the procurement will comprise a selection stage followed by an invitation to tender stage, although the final structure may be amended following market engagement and internal approvals.
Participation in any preliminary market engagement activity will not provide any supplier with an advantage in any future procurement process. The Client will take appropriate measures to ensure compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 and the principles of transparency, equal treatment and fairness.
The Client particularly welcomes engagement from SMEs, suppliers within the East Midlands Combined County Authority (EMCAA) region and specialist mechanical contractors who have experience of working within public sector environments. Feedback is sought to ensure the proposed procurement structure is proportionate, accessible and capable of delivering best value throughout the contract term.

title: UK nature-based carbon removal credits
description:
The Met Office undertook an initial Preliminary Market Engagement exercise in May 2026 to understand market capability and potential approaches to the supply of verified UK nature-based carbon credits.

Please note: The requirement has changed to verified UK nature-based carbon removal credits only; therefore, some previous PME responses may no longer apply.
Since that engagement, the proposed procurement approach and requirement have developed. The Met Office is now considering the purchase of approximately £500,000 of verified UK nature-based carbon credits during FY 2026/27, with the credits intended to be retired in FY 2030/31. A small proportion of the credits may be retired earlier to offset business travel incurred in customer funded programmes.
As the tender documentation has developed, a number of additional questions have been identified where further market insight would be beneficial. The Met Office therefore intends to undertake a further period of Preliminary Market Engagement to inform the market of the revised approach, provide an update on anticipated procurement timelines, seek feedback on the additional questions arising from the development of the tender documentation, confirm our understanding of the terminology, and assess current market interest and capability to participate in the opportunity.
The engagement will be used to support the continued development and assessment of the Met Office’s proposed approach, including the potential procurement strategy and associated documentation. Feedback received through the engagement will help inform the Met Office’s consideration of the available options and whether and how to proceed with any future procurement opportunity. Participation in this engagement does not represent a commitment by the Met Office to undertake a subsequent procurement exercise, nor provide any process exemptions or preferential treatment to any parties expressing an interest. The Met Office will not be liable for costs incurred by any interested party in participating in this exercise. This exercise does not commit the Met Office to a procurement and does not guarantee that a future procurement will take place.

title: Wilson's School - Catering Tender
description:
Parents choose Wilson's not just because of its outstanding academic reputation but also because they understand and share the school's values. These are encapsulated by our motto: Non Sibi Sed Omnibus (Not For Oneself, But For All). We strive to create a safe and kind environment where every pupil can become more confident and reach the highest levels of academic enjoyment and achievement. Consequently, pupils flourish at Wilson's.
Further information regarding Wilson’s School can be obtained here:  Https://www.wilsons.school/
Tender Information
The successful tenderer will be required to provide high-quality catering services to Wilson’s School, which has approximately 1,328 pupils, of whom approximately 4.59% are eligible for free school meals, together with approximately 120 teaching and operations staff. 
The contract term being tendered is three years, commencing on 1 September 2027 and ending on 31 August 2030, with an option to extend the contract for a further period of up to two years, to 31 August 2032, subject to satisfactory performance and the agreement of the Client.
The contract presents an excellent opportunity for the successful contractor to review, develop and enhance the existing catering provision. The services will include, but are not limited to, breakfast, morning break, lunchtime and after-school catering throughout the academic year, together with hospitality and catering services for school events and meetings as required.
Service times are as follows:
Breakfast: 07:45 – 08:15 (Main Dining Room)
Break: 10:35 – 10:55 (Main Dining Room, Bowden Room, McAlister Room and The Cuboid)
Lunch: 13:00 – 13:55 (Main Dining Room, Bowden Room, McAlister Room and The Cuboid) 
The Client is seeking a high-quality catering service that provides fresh, nutritious and, wherever possible, locally sourced ingredients prepared on site. Menu design should be flexible and responsive to the needs and preferences of the School’s students and staff, while offering a varied and appealing range of choices.
The Client is proud of its high standards and strong family ethos and expects the successful contractor to reflect and support these values. The service should be professionally and tightly managed, with a management approach that supports, encourages and develops the catering team, promotes high standards and fosters positive relationships with students, staff and the School.
The Client is not obliged to accept the lowest-priced tender. The primary objective is to secure best value, both for the School and its students, taking into account quality, service, innovation, financial value and the overall student experience.
Tenderers are encouraged to put forward innovative and creative proposals for developing the service, improving the dining experience and delivering additional value. The Client is seeking a contractor who will work collaboratively and in partnership with the School, demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement and consistently deliver the highest standards of service.
Basic Objectives of the Tender
The successful contractor will be expected to:
•Work in partnership with the School to provide high-quality, healthy and appealing meals that offer students good value for money. All food should be fresh, well-balanced, nutritious and prepared and served to a consistently high standard.
•Manage a service which is slick and efficient, maximising efficiency and minimising pupil and staff wait times. This should include operating an appropriate number of tills during busy service periods, with sufficient trained staff deployed to ensure all available tills are utilised where required and queues are kept to a minimum.
•The Catering Contractor must provide a wide range of suitable options to meet the dietary, religious, cultural, allergy and food intolerance requirements of students and staff. The Contractor must have robust procedures in place for the identification, preparation, communication and management of allergens and dietary requirements, including full compliance with all applicable food safety and allergen legislation and guidance, including Natasha’s Law.
•The catering offer should promote healthy eating and provide an appropriate choice of meals, including vegetarian and plant-based options, while taking account of current and future statutory school food standards and Government guidance. 
•Provide a diverse and inclusive food offer, including both Halal and non-Halal options, a wide range of vegetarian and international dishes, and appropriate provision for vegan, gluten-free and other dietary requirements.
•Provide a high-quality sandwich, soup, salad and drink offer so that there is sufficient range to attract staff and students.
•Have the capability to provide high-quality and competitively priced catering for school events (e.g. sit down meals; buffets etc), including for staff, trustees, Old Wilsonians and the wider community. Promote healthy eating and positive food choices, including a continued focus on reducing excessive sugar consumption and supporting the School's wider health and wellbeing initiatives. The catering service should help educate and encourage students to make healthy and informed choices.
•Demonstrate a strong commitment to sustainable and responsible sourcing, including the use of locally sourced and seasonal produce where practical, Fairtrade products where appropriate, and environmentally responsible procurement and catering practices.
•Maintain and continually improve the quality, variety, presentation and merchandising of food, ensuring that the catering offer remains attractive, relevant and responsive to changing student and staff preferences.
•Support, develop and retain the existing catering team, providing effective leadership, training, development and performance management, while fostering a positive and collaborative working environment.
•Maintain and enhance the overall dining experience within the School. This should encourage students to eat a varied range of foods, try new dishes, make healthy and informed choices and view mealtimes as a positive social experience. The successful contractor should work with the School to create an environment that supports these objectives.
•Demonstrate continuous improvement in financial and operational performance, working with the School to identify opportunities for efficiencies, innovation and service development.
•Provide a transparent and collaborative commercial arrangement that appropriately rewards the Contractor for delivering sustained improvements in financial and operational performance, while ensuring that any financial benefits generated above agreed guarantees are shared appropriately with the School.
•Work proactively with the School to monitor performance, gather and respond to student and staff feedback, and identify opportunities to improve the catering service throughout the contract period.
Competitive Flexible Procedure 
This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two-stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here a minimum of 5 candidates (or less, in the event less than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates, will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. 
Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 35% price and 65% quality.
Value of contract:
The annual value of the current contract is £535,377
Therefore the value of this contract is £2,676,855 
The contract shall be a guaranteed performance contract with hospitality requirements billed separately and at cost.
Additional requirements and information:
•The Client has a minimum requirement for a contractor’s employers' liability and public liability insurances of £5 million 
•The minimum annual turnover that your company must have achieved to be considered for this opportunity is £1 million
•There are incumbent catering staff currently within the Local Government Pension Scheme. 
•The catering services are currently contracted to Cucina.
•The client reserves the right not to appoint in conclusion of this project.

title: Provision of 24/7 Chairs and Associated Services
description:
Framework for the supply, delivery, installation, maintenance, repair and associated support services relating to 24/7 Chairs. Full Specification available as at Document 2 (Scope and Specification).
This Framework will supply 24/7 Chairs, to primarily Signallers, Electrical and Route Controllers (the ‘Users’), who have roles where a large proportion of their working day (12-hour shifts) is interacting with Visual Display Units (VDU) equipment from a seated posture. It is important to ensure that the correct seating is provided to Users from a health and safety, durability and comfort perspective to prevent user injury or discomfort.  
Network Rail intends to appoint a single national supplier to provide an end-to-end solution for: 
- Supply of 24/7 rated ergonomic chairs via a managed core catalogue 
- National delivery across England, Wales and Scotland 
- Installation and assembly (free of charge on larger orders) 
- Asset management including: Annual Maintenance, Repair under supplier warranty and beyond. 
- Removal and responsible reuse or recycling of redundant chairs 
- Catalogue access via Network Rail Oracle iProcurement 
- Ongoing account management, reporting and continuous improvement. Shape 
Chair Range:
- Suppliers will be expected to offer a limited core (max 4) and standardised range, including: 
- Core 24/7 chair (s) meeting all mandatory requirements 
- An enhanced chair exceeding mandatory requirements 
- A chair suitable for users with musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) 
- Where appropriate, a single chair model may satisfy more than one category and if appropriate two chairs or variants may be offered for the core 24/7 chair. 
- A bariatric chair where all elements accommodate weight and size (anticipated to be non-core and low volume) will need to be offered. 
Technical & Ergonomic Requirements:
- Chairs must be suitable for continuous 24h our use and comply with relevant standards, including BS 54592 (or ISO equivalent) and have FIRA FS 055 certification or demonstrated equivalence. 
Key requirements include: 
- Accommodate users from 5th percentile female to 95th percentile male for stature, weight, shoulder width and seated leg length and height. Bariatric users where possible should be accommodated in the Core selection. 
- High durability, intuitive controls and ease of adjustment 
- Minimum 5 year 24/7 manufacturer or supplier warranty 
- Samples to be made available for product trials as part of evaluation 
- Sustainability & Ethical Sourcing 
Suppliers will be expected to demonstrate: 
- Ethical sourcing and Modern Slavery Act compliance 
- Traceability and auditability of manufacturing sources 
- Environmental management systems (e.g. ISO 14001 or equivalent) 
- Strong circular economy practices (reuse, refurbishment, recycling, zero landfill) 
Contract Model :
- Anticipated start: June 2027 
- Initial term: 5 years, with optional extensions 
- Form: NR1 (MT) Goods and Non Construction Services Framework 
- Calloffs via NR01(S) Purchase Orders 
- Fixed pricing for an initial period, with controlled indexation thereafter 
- The core catalogue is expected to meet approximately 95% of demand, with limited non-catalogue provision by exception.

title: Uncrewed Ocean Surface Vehicle (USV)
description:
The School of Physical, Chemical and Environmental Sciences (PACES) seeks to procure a modern uncrewed surface vehicle (USV) to support teaching, research and innovation in marine science, hydrographic surveying and marine robotics. 
The platform will significantly enhance practical field teaching by providing students with access to contemporary autonomous survey technology that reflects current industry practice. The acquisition aligns with the strategic direction of UK marine science, where autonomous systems are increasingly central to national marine research infrastructure and offshore operations. It will provide students with experience of the technologies and operational workflows that are now expected across the marine sector, improving graduate employability and strengthening links with industry. 
The proposed system will expand the University's field teaching capability by increasing the number and diversity of environments in which practical survey exercises can be undertaken. In addition to coastal waters, the platform should be suitable for deployment in ports, harbours, estuaries, inland waters and sheltered bays, creating greater flexibility for undergraduate teaching and postgraduate research. 
Its portability will also enable deployment during residential field courses and support independent student projects and dissertations, providing more authentic, hands-on learning opportunities throughout the academic year while improving accessibility and inclusivity by allowing students to participate in advanced survey operations without requiring access to crewed survey vessels. To maximise operational flexibility, the USV should be readily transportable by a small team and capable of deployment without specialist lifting equipment.
The platform must therefore be person-portable and of modular construction, enabling it to fit within the rear of a standard SUV or pickup vehicle for transportation between field sites. 
The system should be designed for low maintenance and provide a minimum operational endurance of seven hours on a single battery charge, allowing uninterrupted operation throughout a full teaching or survey day. Hot-swappable battery carriages would be highly desired. 
The School requires a platform capable of both remote operation from shore and teleconnected operation, providing safe and effective survey capability without personnel entering the water. The system should support the creation and execution of pre-programmed navigation tracks and permit real-time editing of survey parameters and data acquisition whilst underway. Compatibility with the University's existing NORBIT multibeam sonar system is considered very highly desirable/near-essential, allowing integration with existing survey equipment and reducing additional capital expenditure. Safety, environmental sustainability and regulatory compliance are fundamental requirements. 
The platform should incorporate situational awareness and collision avoidance capabilities to support safe autonomous operations. It must produce zero direct emissions during operation, generate minimal underwater and airborne noise, and avoid pollution of the operating environment. To facilitate straightforward regulatory compliance and minimise operational burden, the vessel should have an overall length of less than 2.5 metres, enabling operation within the scope of the exemptions outlined in MGN 702(M) Amendment 1. 
Lastly, we would consider an autocast sound-velocity profiler winch highly desirable, and the ability to add/remove other sensors ad hoc, cheaply, and with ease of compatibility as a strong basis for choosing the final vessel.

title: Mongo Database
description:
At Aula, MongoDB is a core part of the platform's underlying infrastructure and acts as the centralised database used to store and manage records generated across the platform. Every interaction and action carried outby users within Aula is recorded within MongoDB. This includes user authentication, posts, submissions, resources, discussions, collaborative activity and other interactions carried out by students and educators across institution instances.
Aula's experience relies on seamless interaction between students, educators and content, and MongoDB supports this by storing the structured yet flexible data that enables these interactions to take place. Every action within the platform generates data, whether it is a student posting a submission, an educator sharing resources, or users collaborating through discussions. MongoDB's document-based model allows this information to be captured and stored in real time without being restricted by rigid table structures.
This flexibility is important for Aula because different institutions and courses can have different requirements and structures. MongoDB's schema-less design allows Aula to adapt and evolve its data model without requiring complex migrations or significant downtime. This enables the platform to continue developing and introducing changes without unnecessarily disrupting teaching and learning.

The contract is for calibration and ad-hoc repair of the current in-service Epoch 600 Ultrasonic Flaw Detector equipment. The Contract has a proposed Value of £0.134M (Inclusive of VAT)
The authority considers that the direct award of this non-competitive contract falls within the circumstances set out in the Procurement Act 2023 Sch. 5, Para. 7:
7. The public contract concerns the supply of goods, services or works by the existing supplier which are intended as an extension to, or partial replacement of, existing goods, services or works in circumstances where— 
a)	a change in supplier would result in the contracting authority receiving goods, services or works that are different from, or incompatible with, the existing goods, services or works; and 
b)	the difference or incompatibility would result in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation or maintenance.
This is because Evident Europe GMBH is the OEM of and design authority and have supported and the equipment for approximately 11 years and have the specialist skills, experience, knowledge and test equipment to continue with the support. No other contractor has access to the technical knowledge, documents, spares, skills and test equipment necessary to fulfil this requirement, and so by changing supplier there would be different/incompatible services with the existing goods and services resulting in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation and/or maintenance for the equipment in question. Therefore, only Evident Europe GMBH can provide the services required.
Epoch 600 Ultrasonic Flaw Detector (UFD) equipment is used to carry out NDT inspections on various aircraft structures and components. There is an enduring requirement to provide support for UFD equipment. The Council considers that introducing a new provider during this period would create disproportionate operational difficulties and increase the risk of disruption to established safeguarding arrangements and continuity of support for service users. A strictly time-limited direct award of 24 months is therefore considered necessary to maintain continuity of service And to allow the relevant time for future commissioning arrangements to be designed and procured in collaboration with the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner (or equivalent body), Leicestershire County Council and Rutland District and County Council.

title: T2689 - Framework Agreement for the Delivery of Various Employability and Skills Requirements
description:
Belfast City Council requires agile and flexible Employability and Skills solutions to be able to respond to challenges and opportunities within the labour market.  
Sufficient flexibility within the delivery of Employability & Skills interventions is required to take account of:
a) Emerging needs.
b) New initiatives and areas of development e.g. skills interventions within the Local Economic Partnership, Labour Market Partnership etc.
c) Specialist employability and skills delivery.
d) To test new areas of work as agreed.
e) Sectors that are not covered within the current Employment Academy Framework (T2474)
f) To pick up overflow of delivery if the current Contractors on T2474 are working to full capacity
On this basis, the Council is setting up an "Open Framework", which would allow an open, fair, and transparent way of procuring the above services in the most efficient way possible.  
There will be no guarantee of any work for those Contractors on the new Open Framework, and any future call-offs will not be initiated until the following happens sequentially (which is designed to provide budgetary control):
1.  Workplan and budget approval.
2. When agreed, a direct award or mini-competitions will then undertaken.
3. Delegated authority approval prior to awarding the call-off contract. 
An Open Framework will provide an opportunity for SMEs and Social Enterprises/Not-for-Profits to secure a place on the Framework, with the opportunity re-opening at various stages for new entrants to apply/re-apply.
The Framework will be split into 5 Lots:
1. Lot 1 – Care Sectors (Health/Social Care/Education/Playwork/Childminding)
2. Lot 2 – Customer Services (Leisure/Hospitality/Retail/Tourism/Beauty)
3. Lot 3 – Practical Sectors (Transport/Green Economy/Construction/Manufacturing)
4. Lot 4 – Professional and Business Services Sectors (Business/Technology)
5. Lot 5 – Employability Support (language/Soft Skills/Capacity Building)
The Council intends that this Framework Agreement will form part of a scheme of successive framework agreements on substantially the same terms (the “Open Framework Scheme”). The total duration of the Open Framework Scheme shall not exceed 8 years from the commencement date of the first framework awarded under the scheme.

Lot 3 (Lot 3a, 3b, 3c, 3d, 3e, 3f) – PfP New Build Developments - Scotland - The current Scottish Kitchen Framework for New Build Developments in Scotland is due to end August 2027 and so will also be included in this new framework on a supply and installation basis. Previously, the Scottish Framework included the following lots: (1) Highland – Affordable, (2) Highland – Market Sale, (3) North East - Affordable, (4) North East – Market Sale, (5) Central – Affordable, (6) Central – Market Sale.  The new framework will include these 6 sub-lots, as categorised previously. The specification will also include a high-end/quality Sales option. title: Ireland – Construction work for electricity power lines – The MaresConnect 750MW HVDC Interconnector System
description: The MaresConnect Project is a proposed 750 MW, 320 kV High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) electricity interconnector linking Denbighshire, Wales and North County Dublin, Ireland. Developed by MaresConnect Limited, a joint venture between Foresight Group Holdings Ltd and Etchea Energy Nominees Ltd, the project will transmit electricity via approximately 240 km of subsea and underground cables between new converter stations on each side. It aims to enhance security of supply, market integration, and renewable energy utilisation between the Irish and GB grids. MaresConnect shall utilise Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology and the configuration shall be a Symmetrical Monopole. The rated DC voltage shall be +/-320 kV. The link shall be bi-directional and shall have a rated power (receiving end) of 750 MW. The project is being procured as separate EPC (Turnkey) contracts, divided into four lots: LOT 1A: EPC for two HVDC Converter Stations; LOT 1B: EPC for one Irish 400kV AC Tail Substation; LOT 2A: EPC for the HVDC subsea and underground cable system, and for the HVAC underground cable system in Wales (Bodelwyddan); LOT 2B: EPC for the supply and installation of HVAC cable system in Ireland (Dublin). The contract model for the lots will be amended FIDIC Conditions of Contract for EPC/Turnkey Projects (Silver Book). MaresConnect has conducted Preliminary Market Engagement prior to publication of this Contract Notice and encourages further collaboration between OEMs and Construction Contractors to establish bidding arrangements in time for the next step of the Procurement Process (notably the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire).

title: Germany – Engineering design services – Schöpfwerk Niendorf - Ersatzneubau
description: Der NLWKN möchte die Planungsleistungen für den Ersatzneubau des Schöpfwerks Niendorf (Amt Neuhaus) mit den Losen 1 "Umweltplanung" und 2 "Ingenieurbauwerk" vergeben. Nähere Informationen entnehmen sie bitte den beiliegenden Bewerbungsbedingungen mit Anlagen sowie der Leistungsbeschreibung. Das Vergabeverfahren wird als "Verhandlungsverfahren mit Teilnahmewettbewerb" nach § 17 Vergabeverordnung (VgV) durchgeführt. Über das Vergabeportal des Landes Niedersachsen können Sie sich nun im Rahmen des Teilnahmewettbewerbs um die Teilnahme am Verhandlungsverfahren bewerben. Füllen Sie hierfür bitte die unter dem Reiter "Teilnehmerunterlagen" hochgeladenen Unterlagen zum Teilnahmewettbewerb aus und laden Sie die geforderten Unterlagen im Vergabeportal hoch. Eine Auflistung der vorzulegenden Bewerbungsunterlagen finden sie in Anlage 2 Bewerbungsbogen unter der Nummer 1.3. Das Schöpfwerk Niendorf wurde in den 1960ern in der DDR errichtet und entwässert das Einzugsgebiet der Krainke mit etwa 12.240 ha. Es schützt dadurch Siedlungsgebiete und landwirtschaftliche Flächen bei Elbehochwasser und Rückstau in die Sude oder bei Eigenhochwasser der Sude. Der am Schöpfwerk angeschlossene rechte Krainkedeich wurde im Jahr 2014 auf die Höhe des neuen Bemessungshochwassers angepasst. Die Sanierung und höhenmäßige Anpassung des linken Krainkedeiches erfolgte im Jahr 2016. Eine Anpassung an die neuen Bemessungswasserstände ist im Bereich des Schöpfwerkes noch nicht erfolgt, so dass Minderhöhen von 30 cm vorhanden sind. Sechs installierte Propellerpumpen verfügen über eine Gesamtleistung von etwa 11,7 m³/s, die Pumpen stammen aus der Zeit des Baues von 1963 und befinden sich Teils in schlechtem Zustand, zwei Pumpen wurden 2005 und 2006 erneuert. Eine Rechenreinigungsanlage ist nicht vorhanden. Daneben verfügt das Schöpfwerk über 4 Freiflutkanäle, die der regulären Entwässerung außerhalb der Hochwasserzeiten dienen, wobei diese nicht den Anforderungen an die Durchgängigkeit nach WRRL genügen. Im Jahre 2016 wurde eine Bedarfsplanung erstellt, mit dem Ergebnis eine Grundinstandsetzung vorzunehmen. Für die Planung der Grundinstandsetzung wurden seit 2021 Ingenieurplanungen der Leistungsphasen 1 bis 3 und Teilen von 4 erbracht. Im Rahmen der Planungen wurden verschiedene Bauteile des Schöpfwerkes näher untersucht: Beton, Putz, Druckrohrleitungen, Schmutzwasserkanal, etc.. Das Ergebnis der Planungen zeigte, dass annähernd sämtliche Anlagenteile des Schöpfwerkes saniert, ausgetauscht oder neu gebaut werden müssten. Aufgrund des absehbaren umfangreichen Instandsetzungsaufwands wurde 2025 im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie untersucht, ob ein Ersatzneubau des Schöpfwerks eine technisch und wirtschaftlich bessere Lösung darstellen kann als eine Sanierung des Bestandes. Der NLWKN beabsichtigt auf Grundlage der bisherigen Planungen und der Ergebnisse der Machbarkeitsstudie aus 2025 das bestehende Schöpfwerk durch einen zeitgemäßen Neubau, am Standort des bestehenden Schöpfwerks zu ersetzen. Der Schöpfwerksneubau soll die aktuellen Anforderungen beim Bemessungswasserstand, der Durchgängigkeit und dem fischfreundlichen und wirtschaftlichen Betrieb erfüllen. Zudem soll durch eine Erhöhung der Pumpenkapazität dem Klimawandel Rechnung getragen werden. Folgende Binnenwasserstände sind durch das Schöpfwerk sicherzustellen: - höchstzulässiger Binnenpeil: +7,80 mNHN - höchster Winterpeil +7,70 mNHN - höchster Sommerpeil +7,40 mNHN - tiefster Binnenpeil +7,20 mNHN Das Bemessungshochwasser liegt derzeit bei 10,60 m+NHN und die entsprechende Ausbauhöhe des Deiches unter Berücksichtigung eines Freibordes von 70 cm bei +11,30 mNHN. Die im folgenden aufgeführten Abflüsse sind durch die Pumpen des Schöpfwerkes abzuführen, sofern der Außenwasserstand über dem Binnenwasserstand liegt: - Höchster Hochwasserabfluss HHQ: 11,142 m³/s - Bemessungshochwasserabfluss: 11,30 m³/s - Bemessungshochwasserabfluss mit Berücksichtigung Klimaanpassungsfaktor: 13,715 m³/s - Sommermittelwasserabfluss SMQ: 2,076 m³/s Die Pumpen müssen auf geodätische Förderhöhen zwischen 0,00 m und 3,20 m ausgelegt werden. Diese Randbedingungen sind auch bei der Planung der Freiflut und der damit verbunden Fischaufstiegsanlage zur Sicherstellung der Binnenpeile und der Durchgängigkeit zu berücksichtigen. Das derzeitige Schöpfwerk Niendorf liegt in diversen naturschutzrechtlich geschützten Gebieten: - Biosphärenreservat "Niedersächsische Elbtalaue" (Lage des technischen Bauwerkes innerhalb des Gebietsteiles A, unmittelbar angrenzend an den streng geschützten Gebietsteil C) - FFH-Gebiet "Elbeniederung zwischen Schnackenburg und Geesthacht" - EU-Vogelschutzgebiet "Niedersächsische Mittelelbe" (Lage des technischen Bauwerkes außerhalb des EU-Vogelschutzgebietes, jedoch unmittelbar an das EU-Vogelschutzgebiet angrenzend) - Kohärenzsicherungsmaßnahme für die Fischarten Bitterling und Steinbeißer im unmittelbaren Umfeld Die entsprechenden Schutzgebietsvorschriften sind bei der Planung zu berücksichtigen.

title: Ireland – Civil engineering consultancy services – Dublin City Council Single Party Framework Agreement for an Integrated Design Team for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project
description: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 8969388 – Input when notice created . Please note that this project is subject to funding.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Project "Blosc2"
description: The contract concerns the project Blosc2, which covers the security hardening and interoperability of the open-source Blosc2 compression library and data container, involving the systematic investigation, development, and experimental validation of the best technical solutions. The aim of this service is to strengthen the security, resilience, interoperability, and long-term maintainability of Blosc2, a widely used open-source component underpinning scientific data storage and processing.

title: Denmark – Civil engineering consultancy services – EU-udbud af rammeaftale vedrørende levering af totalrådgivning til Hundested Idrætscenter i Halsnæs Kommune
description: Udbuddet omfatter totalrådgivning i forbindelse med udviklingen af området omkring Hundested Idrætscenter. Rådgivningen skal understøtte Ordregivers arbejde med at realisere visionen for området, herunder styrke sammenhængen mellem funktionerne og skabe et attraktivt og samlet idrætsmiljø. Udviklingen af Hundested Idrætscenter kan blandt andet omfatte etablering af en ny 8-mands kunstgræsbane, klubhus, parkeringsfaciliteter og vejanlæg samt arealudvikling og byggemodning med henblik på udstykning af boliger, der understøtter kommunens bosætningsstrategi. Projektets endelige indhold og omfang er endnu ikke fastlagt. Det er derfor en central del af totalrådgiverens opgave i tæt samarbejde med Ordregiver at kvalificere, udvikle og fastlægge de endelige projektløsninger på baggrund af de overordnede visioner og målsætninger for området. Ordregiver forbeholder sig i særlige tilfælde ret til at lade enkelte projekter varetage af andre rådgivere eller samarbejdspartnere. Ordregiver er således ikke forpligtet til at rekvirere rådgivningsydelser vedrørende samtlige projekter under rammeaftalen. Ordregivers behov for rådgivningsydelser vil afhænge af de til enhver tid trufne beslutninger om projektets udvikling og gennemførelse. Ordregiver tilstræber dog, at den valgte totalrådgiver inddrages i størst muligt omfang i udviklingen og realiseringen af de projekter, der omfattes af visionen for området. Den nærmere beskrivelse af den udbudte opgave fremgår af det samlede udbudsmateriale, herunder udkast til rammeaftale med tilhørende bilag. Rammeaftalen er baseret på ABR 18 og Ydelsesbeskrivelse for Byggeri og Landskab 2018 (YBL18) og fastsætter de overordnede vilkår for totalrådgiverens levering af rådgivningsydelser til Ordregiver. På baggrund af rammeaftalen kan Ordregiver løbende rekvirere konkrete rådgivningsopgaver. For hver opgave indgås et særskilt aftaletillæg (ATR – Aftale om aktivitet, tid og ressourcer), hvori opgavens formål, ydelser, leverancer, tidsplan, bemanding, rådgiverkompetencer, forventede ressourceforbrug, honorar samt øvrige opgavespecifikke forhold fastlægges. Rammeaftalen med tilhørende bilag udgør grundlaget for aftaleindgåelsen med den vindende tilbudsgiver. De enkelte opgaver gennemføres på de vilkår, der fremgår af rammeaftalen og den til enhver tid gældende ATR.

title: Germany – Artificial and natural lighting engineering services for buildings – Dienstleistungen für Lichttechnik und Tageslichttechnik – Dynamisches Beschaffungssystem "Planungsleistungen Beleuchtungsumrüstung" hier: Vergebene Aufträge im 3. Quartal 2025
description: Die AG verwaltet bundesweit Liegenschaften diverser Bundesbehörden im Rahmen des einheitlichen Liegenschaftsmanagements. Im Zuge des gesetzlich festgeschriebenen Auslaufs der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen T5 und T8 zum 25.08.2023, bedarf es zur Aufrechterhaltung der Ausleuchtung eines vollständigen Austausches der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen durch eine LED-Beleuchtung. Diese Umstellung soll sukzessiv in einzelnen Sprints im Rahmen eines dynamischen Beschaffungssystems (DBS) erfolgen. Die Planungsleistungen werden in einer agilen Vorgehensweise in unterschiedlichen Umfängen der zu sanierenden Liegenschaften benötigt. Die AG wird die Planungsleistungen für die jeweiligen Liegenschaften in einzelnen Sprints, im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens, vergeben. Dadurch soll es auch KMU ermöglicht werden die Leistungen zu erbringen. Die Leistungserbringung umfasst Planungsleistungen, die zur Planung, Beratung, Ausschreibung, Bauleitung sowie für die spätere Umsetzung in Anlehnung an die LPH 1 bis 8 des § 55 HOAI erforderlich sind. Der Leistungsschwerpunkt liegt auf Planungsleistungen in den KG 440 (445), der Auftrag umfasst dabei alle weiteren Planungsleistungen, die zur Erreichung des Auftragsziels erforderlich sind. Im Wesentlichen sind folgende Leistungen angelehnt an § 55 HOAI für die Beleuchtungsumrüstung zu erbringen: - Bestandsaufnahme aller Leuchten einer Liegenschaft durch tabellarische Dokumentation folgender Merkmale: Leuchte, Leuchtmittel, Nutzungsart des Raumes, Deckenhöhe, Reflexionsgrad der Wände, Schaltung der Beleuchtung, Anzahl der Leuchten pro Stromkreis, Anzahl der Adern zu Leuchten/Schalter - Erstellen von Grundrisszeichnungen, falls diese nicht vorliegen - Fachplanungsleistungen KG 440 und 445 - Ausführungsplanung - Beleuchtungsberechnung mit Berechnungssoftware Dialux oder Relux - Planung der Beleuchtungsanlagen nach der AMEV-Empfehlung „Beleuchtung 2019“, der DIN EN 12464 sowie der ASR 3.4 in der jeweils gültigen Fassung - Erstellung von Wartungsplänen nach DIN EN 12464-1 - Erstellung von Termin- und Ablaufplänen für die Umsetzung der Baumaßnahmen - Vorbereitung und Mitwirkung bei der Vergabe - Objekt- und Bauüberwachung Im Zusammenhang damit sind z.B. auch folgende Planungsleistungen von Randbereichen / Nebenleistungen insbesondere in folgenden Bereichen – soweit im Einzelfall erforderlich – zu erbringen: Einfache Schlitz- und Durchbruchsarbeiten, Verputzarbeiten, Trockenbauarbeiten, Malerarbeiten, Gerüstbau/Gerüststellung. Die Leistungen sind grds. im Dokument „Leistungsverzeichnis“ dargestellt, im weiteren Stadium behält sich die AG vor, den Leistungsumfang zu spezifizieren. Die AG weist darauf hin, dass die gesamten Vergabeunterlagen – insb. der Prozessablaufplan - der Fortschreibung unterliegen und im Laufe des DBS jederzeit angepasst werden können. Hierüber werden alle Bewerber/Bieter umgehend informiert. Die AG sucht Unternehmen, die diese Planungsleistungen erbringen. Dabei wird die Planung in einzelne Planungsphasen strukturiert (siehe Leistungsverzeichnis, dort a.E. Übersicht differenzierter Planungsleistungen). Einige Leistungen müssen stets erbracht werden, die Erbringung bzw. der jeweilige Umfang der Bedarfs- und Alternativpositionen wird durch die AG auf Grundlage von Entscheidungsvorlagen getroffen. Abhängig von den getroffenen Entscheidungen ist für bestimmte Flächen alternativ der Leuchtmitteltausch oder ein Leuchtentausch zu planen. Für den Fall des Leuchtentausches ist eine weitere Entscheidung hinsichtlich der Planung einer Beleuchtungssteuerung der AG vorgesehen. Sollte eine Beleuchtungssteuerung gefordert sein, sind auch die entsprechenden Bedarfspositionen zu erbringen. Die AG wird ihren Leistungsbedarf im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens mit jeweils einer Aufforderung zur Angebotsabgabe an die zu diesem Zeitpunkt in dieser Region geeigneten Unternehmen (Bewerberpool) kommunizieren. Dabei sind die Sprints nach den Komplexitätsgraden „Basisprojekte“ und „Komplexe Projekte“ aufgeteilt.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Project "Eclipse: Open Registry Security Gateway for Open VSX"
description: This service agreement concerns the FOSS component "Eclipse Open VSX" and the associated technical specification Eclipse SCINTX, covering the work needed to complete a functional reference implementation of the specification which is intended to pave the road for an open ecosystem where heterogenously operated repositories of plug-ins for integrated development environments (IDE) that are compatible with the VS Code architecture can be scanned and verified by independent third-party security service-providers. Achieving this entails studying the functional requirements specified by the open specification SCINTX, in order to design an application programming interfaces (API) and a system architecture that realizes these requirements, relying on existing open specifications and FOSS components for the implementation details where applicable, then implementing the design into a usable software system and configuration as per the state-of-the-art in the field. The work also entails studying the public APIs of two commonly used open, free security-scanning services in order to implement a provider-specific adapter for each of them as an example, within the architectural model designed for the gateway. Finally, a software-development kit (SDK) is to be produced, in order to facilitate the creation of adapters for more third-party providers and integrations. This work is intended to increase the security of the supply chain of FOSS infrastructure, and of the software industry in general, where third-party plug-ins are often used to add productive functionality to software IDEs, but can also be abused as attack vectors due to the access they are granted to development environment resources, thus threatening much more than the systems they immediately touch.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Project "anndataR: Native R access to the standard single-cell data format"
description: This service agreement concerns the FOSS‌ library "anndataR", covering the work needed to bring this implementation in R of the bioinformatics library up to compliance with the most recent edition of the reference implementation. To achieve this, a gap analysis must be performed to identify the deviation between the current implementation and the most recent edition of the reference implementation. Research must then be conducted to arrive at the best method to implement the lacking functionality within the defining capabilities and programming paradigm of the R language and its ecosystem of libraries and modules. Moreover, research and design work is required to devise solutions to several issues and limitations that are already identified within the existing implementation, by examining the relevant issue reports submitted by users, and comparing the proposed solutions in order to select the best in each case and implement it. Additionally, optimising and improving the performance of the library, which processes huge amounts of data in each run, entail profiling the resulting implementation and measuring its performance to identify bottlenecks, then design solutions to mitigate them. Finally, the design and implementation of CI/CD tests ensures the continuous validity and compliance with future editions of the reference implementation. The overall aim of this work is to maintain FOSS infrastructure components used to utilise the large datasets that are critical building blocks in the field of bioinformatics, by keeping it updated as per the state-of-the-art in the field, in terms of capabilities and performance.

title: Germany – Artificial and natural lighting engineering services for buildings – Dienstleistungen für Lichttechnik und Tageslichttechnik – Dynamisches Beschaffungssystem "Planungsleistungen Beleuchtungsumrüstung" hier: Vergebene Aufträge im 4. Quartal 2025
description: Die AG verwaltet bundesweit Liegenschaften diverser Bundesbehörden im Rahmen des einheitlichen Liegenschaftsmanagements. Im Zuge des gesetzlich festgeschriebenen Auslaufs der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen T5 und T8 zum 25.08.2023, bedarf es zur Aufrechterhaltung der Ausleuchtung eines vollständigen Austausches der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen durch eine LED-Beleuchtung. Diese Umstellung soll sukzessiv in einzelnen Sprints im Rahmen eines dynamischen Beschaffungssystems (DBS) erfolgen. Die Planungsleistungen werden in einer agilen Vorgehensweise in unterschiedlichen Umfängen der zu sanierenden Liegenschaften benötigt. Die AG wird die Planungsleistungen für die jeweiligen Liegenschaften in einzelnen Sprints, im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens, vergeben. Dadurch soll es auch KMU ermöglicht werden die Leistungen zu erbringen. Die Leistungserbringung umfasst Planungsleistungen, die zur Planung, Beratung, Ausschreibung, Bauleitung sowie für die spätere Umsetzung in Anlehnung an die LPH 1 bis 8 des § 55 HOAI erforderlich sind. Der Leistungsschwerpunkt liegt auf Planungsleistungen in den KG 440 (445), der Auftrag umfasst dabei alle weiteren Planungsleistungen, die zur Erreichung des Auftragsziels erforderlich sind. Im Wesentlichen sind folgende Leistungen angelehnt an § 55 HOAI für die Beleuchtungsumrüstung zu erbringen: - Bestandsaufnahme aller Leuchten einer Liegenschaft durch tabellarische Dokumentation folgender Merkmale: Leuchte, Leuchtmittel, Nutzungsart des Raumes, Deckenhöhe, Reflexionsgrad der Wände, Schaltung der Beleuchtung, Anzahl der Leuchten pro Stromkreis, Anzahl der Adern zu Leuchten/Schalter - Erstellen von Grundrisszeichnungen, falls diese nicht vorliegen - Fachplanungsleistungen KG 440 und 445 - Ausführungsplanung - Beleuchtungsberechnung mit Berechnungssoftware Dialux oder Relux - Planung der Beleuchtungsanlagen nach der AMEV-Empfehlung „Beleuchtung 2019“, der DIN EN 12464 sowie der ASR 3.4 in der jeweils gültigen Fassung - Erstellung von Wartungsplänen nach DIN EN 12464-1 - Erstellung von Termin- und Ablaufplänen für die Umsetzung der Baumaßnahmen - Vorbereitung und Mitwirkung bei der Vergabe - Objekt- und Bauüberwachung Im Zusammenhang damit sind z.B. auch folgende Planungsleistungen von Randbereichen / Nebenleistungen insbesondere in folgenden Bereichen – soweit im Einzelfall erforderlich – zu erbringen: Einfache Schlitz- und Durchbruchsarbeiten, Verputzarbeiten, Trockenbauarbeiten, Malerarbeiten, Gerüstbau/Gerüststellung. Die Leistungen sind grds. im Dokument „Leistungsverzeichnis“ dargestellt, im weiteren Stadium behält sich die AG vor, den Leistungsumfang zu spezifizieren. Die AG weist darauf hin, dass die gesamten Vergabeunterlagen – insb. der Prozessablaufplan - der Fortschreibung unterliegen und im Laufe des DBS jederzeit angepasst werden können. Hierüber werden alle Bewerber/Bieter umgehend informiert. Die AG sucht Unternehmen, die diese Planungsleistungen erbringen. Dabei wird die Planung in einzelne Planungsphasen strukturiert (siehe Leistungsverzeichnis, dort a.E. Übersicht differenzierter Planungsleistungen). Einige Leistungen müssen stets erbracht werden, die Erbringung bzw. der jeweilige Umfang der Bedarfs- und Alternativpositionen wird durch die AG auf Grundlage von Entscheidungsvorlagen getroffen. Abhängig von den getroffenen Entscheidungen ist für bestimmte Flächen alternativ der Leuchtmitteltausch oder ein Leuchtentausch zu planen. Für den Fall des Leuchtentausches ist eine weitere Entscheidung hinsichtlich der Planung einer Beleuchtungssteuerung der AG vorgesehen. Sollte eine Beleuchtungssteuerung gefordert sein, sind auch die entsprechenden Bedarfspositionen zu erbringen. Die AG wird ihren Leistungsbedarf im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens mit jeweils einer Aufforderung zur Angebotsabgabe an die zu diesem Zeitpunkt in dieser Region geeigneten Unternehmen (Bewerberpool) kommunizieren. Dabei sind die Sprints nach den Komplexitätsgraden „Basisprojekte“ und „Komplexe Projekte“ aufgeteilt.
