title: Play Ground Refurbishment x 2
description:
Ingoldmells Parish Council is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to design, supply and install new play equipment and associated safety surfacing at two existing play areas within Ingoldmells, Lincolnshire.
The proposed works are intended to provide attractive, inclusive and accessible play opportunities for children ranging from toddlers through to approximately 14 years of age.
The procurement is divided into two lots:
•	Lot 1 - Glebe Park, Sea Lane, Ingoldmells, Lincolnshire PE25 1NU
Design, supply and installation of new play equipment, associated safety surfacing and all necessary ancillary works
Estimated maximum value: £60,000 excluding VAT.
•	Lot 2 - Chapel Road, Ingoldmells, Lincolnshire PE25 1NA
Design, supply and installation of new play equipment, associated safety surfacing and all necessary ancillary works
Estimated maximum value: £60,000 excluding VAT.
Tenderers may submit a tender for either one lot or both lots.
The Council reserves the right to award either or both lots, subject to the outcome of the tender process, availability of funding and the Council's formal approval to proceed.
Equipment and Design Requirements
The proposed play areas must provide a suitable range of play opportunities for the intended age groups from toddlers to 14 years old and should incorporate inclusive and accessible play opportunities wherever reasonably practicable.
All equipment, surfacing and installation works must comply with all applicable legislation, regulations and relevant British/European standards, including BS EN 1176 and BS EN 1177, as applicable to the equipment and surfacing proposed.
Tenderers must provide details of the proposed equipment, including manufacturers, product references, materials, age ranges, dimensions, fall heights, safety zones and proposed surfacing.
The Council would prefer to avoid timber/wooden play equipment and would favour durable, low-maintenance materials. Tenderers should clearly identify the principal materials proposed.
Accessibility and Inclusion
The design should provide meaningful and accessible play opportunities for children with a range of abilities.
Tenderers should explain within their submission how their proposed design will support inclusive play, including consideration of access routes, surfacing, transfer/accessibility requirements and opportunities for children with differing physical and sensory abilities.
Standards, Certification and Inspection
The successful contractor will be required to provide appropriate manufacturer's certification and documentation demonstrating compliance of the equipment and surfacing with the applicable standards.
Following completion of the works, the play areas shall be independently inspected by a suitably competent post-installation inspector.
The Council intends to obtain a RoSPA Post-Installation Inspection Report before formal handover.
The tender price shall identify whether the contractor has included the cost of the post-installation inspection and any associated attendance.
Any defects, non-compliances or remedial works identified as being the responsibility of the contractor shall be rectified by the contractor before final handover, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Council.
Construction Programme
Tenderers should provide an indicative construction programme for each lot, including anticipated lead times for equipment, surfacing and installation.
The construction programme will be agreed with the Parish Council following appointment and will be subject to the Council obtaining the necessary grant funding and issuing written authorisation to commence the works.
Tenderers should state the earliest date on which they could commence works following receipt of a formal instruction to proceed.
Site Management and Waste
The contractor shall be responsible for all site management, security, plant, labour, equipment and temporary works required to complete the contract.
All excess materials, excavated material, spoil and redundant surfacing arising from the works shall be removed from site and disposed of at an appropriately licensed waste/recycling facility at the contractor's cost.
The contractor shall provide skips where required. Skips and other waste storage areas must be appropriately secured and, when unattended, protected behind suitable Heras-type security fencing or equivalent measures to prevent unauthorised access and fly-tipping.
The contractor shall leave each site clean, safe and free from construction materials and waste on completion.
Reinstatement
Tenderers must identify within their tender price all anticipated grass, tarmac, paving, kerb, drainage or other reinstatement works required as a consequence of the installation.
Any necessary reinstatement should be included within the tender price unless specifically identified as an optional item.
Site Security and Public Safety
The contractor shall maintain appropriate separation between the construction area and members of the public throughout the works.
Particular consideration must be given to the safety of children and other members of the public who may be present close to the works.
The contractor shall provide appropriate site fencing, barriers, warning signage and other safety measures and shall comply with all applicable health and safety requirements.
The contractor shall submit appropriate risk assessments and method statements before commencing works.
Insurance and Responsibility for the Works
The successful contractor shall maintain appropriate insurance cover for the duration of the works, including public liability insurance and employers' liability insurance where legally required.
Evidence of current insurance cover shall be provided to the Council before commencement of works.
Until formal handover has taken place, the contractor shall remain responsible for the care, custody and protection of the works, equipment, materials and construction area and shall be responsible for rectifying damage caused through its activities or negligence.
Formal handover shall take place only when the works have been completed to the Council's satisfaction, the required documentation has been supplied, and the required post-installation inspection has been satisfactorily addressed.
Handover shall be confirmed in writing by the Parish Clerk or the Council's nominated representative and the contractor.
Storage
The contractor shall be responsible for the secure storage of equipment, machinery, materials and other items required for the works during the construction period.
The Parish Council does not warrant the availability of such storage facilities.
Contractor Experience and Qualifications
Tenderers must demonstrate relevant experience in the design, supply and installation of public children's play areas.
Tenderers should provide details of at least [three] relevant completed projects, including client, location, approximate contract value, date of completion and a brief description of the works.
Tenderers should provide copies of current relevant certifications, memberships and accreditations, including any relevant Association of Play Industries (API) membership, together with details of any other relevant industry accreditations.
Where API membership is not held, tenderers should provide equivalent evidence of relevant competence, experience and industry compliance for the Council's consideration.
Tender Price
Tender prices must include all labour, materials, equipment, design, delivery, installation, foundations, surfacing, excavation, waste disposal, site management, reinstatement and all other costs necessary to complete the works described in the tender.
Prices must be stated exclusive of VAT, with VAT shown separately.
Tenderers must clearly identify any assumptions, exclusions or optional items.
Tender Submission
Tenderers should submit:
1.	Completed tender pricing schedule for each lot tendered for
2.	Proposed play equipment and layout/design
3.	Details of proposed safety surfacing
4.	Evidence of relevant experience
5.	Relevant qualifications, memberships and accreditations
6.	Insurance details
7.	Proposed construction programme
8.	Details of warranties and aftercare arrangements
9.	Details of proposed accessibility and inclusive-play provision
10.	Risk assessment/method statement information or outline approach
11.	Details of any exclusions or assumptions
12.	References for comparable completed projects
The Council reserves the right to seek clarification of any tender submission but will not permit a tenderer to materially alter its tender following the submission deadline.

The service is critical to the Authority's statutory responsibilities as a radiation employer. Under IRR17, the Authority is required to assess radiation risks, monitor occupational exposure where appropriate, maintain dose records, investigate potential overexposures, and ensure that exposures remain As Low As Reasonably Practicable (ALARP) and within the applicable statutory dose limits.

title: Insourced Breast USC One-Stop Triple Assessment and Symptomatic Breast Radiology
description:
Hull University Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) on behalf of the Humber Health Partnership (HHP) plan to work in partnership with an Independent Sector (IS) Provider to facilitate provision of additional “one-stop” outpatient clinic capacity within the Breast Urgent Suspected Cancer (USC) pathway, to proactively manage capacity to maintain the delivery of the Cancer Faster Diagnostic Standard during periods where there is a demand vs capacity imbalance, and symptomatic breast radiology clinic support.

The “One-Stop Triple Assessment Clinic" is a new-patient outpatient clinic that delivers a triple diagnostic assessment in the form of:
• Clinical assessment
• Mammography and/or ultrasound imaging
• Fine needle aspiration or core biopsy

The IS provider will provide a full team of appropriately qualified and experienced workforce for each Breast USC “one-stop” triple assessment outpatient clinic (1 at Castle Hill Hospital and 1 at Diana Princess of Wales Hospital), namely for each site:
• 1 x Breast surgery clinician
• 1 x Radiology clinician
• 1 x Radiographer
• 1 x Radiology Assistant (RDA)
• 1 x Appropriate Breast Healthcare Assistant (HCA)
• 1 x Registered Nurse (RN) Support
Each clinic will be an all-day 25 patient session, utilising both AM and PM clinics. Clinics are expected to be delivered between 08:00 to 18:00 only. The sessions will be arranged initially over the weekends with options to be explored for weekday sessions in the future if required.

The "Symptomatic Breast Radiology Clinic Support" requires the provision of an appropriately qualified and experienced consultant radiologist to support weekday activity. This comprises the imaging component of triple assessment for symptomatic breast imaging and will include reporting mammograms / digital tomosynthesis, ultrasound of breast and axilla with biopsy as required and marker placement. Post marker check mammograms will also need reporting where appropriate. This will focus on patients that are referred into the breast symptomatic service on the Consultant led pathway. The requirement is initially for Wednesday & Thursday clinics at Castle Hill Hospital.

The contract is expected to run with an initial term from 2nd January to the end of March 2027, with options to extend for up to another 12 months subject to demand and internal approvals.

Please refer to the full service specifications and other ITT Documents for further details.
buyer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

title: Asbestos Survey and Analytical Works for Wrexham County Borough Council
description:
Wrexham County Borough Council (WCBC) is looking to appoint a single Contractor to undertake Asbestos Surveys and Analytical Works. The agreement will run for an initial 4 year term with the option to extend for a further period of 2 years, subject to satisfactory performance. The scope of the work will include, but not be limited to:
•	Surveys and reinspection’s of domestic properties (dependant on new regulations/guidance).
•	Reinspection’s of areas that fall under CAR2012 Reg 4 (Schools, commercial units, community centres and public buildings).
•	Demolition and refurbishment surveys.
•	Bulk sample and analysis.
•	Reassurance air testing when required.
•	Analytical work and site supervision of asbestos removal works.
•	Water absorption testing.
•	Management plan and report writing where required.
•	Consultancy advice where required.
•	Asbestos awareness training.
The work may be located anywhere across Wrexham County Borough with all WCBC owned and / or managed buildings falling within the scope of this Contract. For clarity, this may include private properties that the Council does not own, but is managing or is responsible for in some other way, such as local lettings.  
The volume of work orders issued through this Contract may fluctuate and as such each Tenderer must be able to provide a flexible and scalable service that is capable of handling increases and decreases in demand throughout the Contract term. Given the nature of the work and the continued reduction in the number of buildings containing asbestos, it is entirely possible that volumes will reduce, although the Council cannot guarantee that this will be the case.

title: PGS - Pulteney Gate Scheme: Buildability, Logistics & Surveys Commission
description:
Bath & North East Somerset Council is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced contractor led team to test, investigate, appraise and develop a range of deliverable options for the replacement of the Pulteney Radial Gate on the river Avon in the centre of Bath.
A range of options are being considered, including 1) a Hydro-Station 2a) Extend the existing Horseshoe Weir 2b) Create a Stepped Weir within the existing channel 3) Infill the existing channel to create new public realm 4a) Own & Operate the Gate, 4b) Do Minimum to the Asset.
Each option will need to be assessed against relevant access, logistics and construction constraints.
The appointment will include the review and validation of existing project information; coordination and execution of intrusive and investigative survey workstreams; assessment of site access, interfaces, constraints and stakeholder considerations; and comparative appraisal of the options and associated logistics scenarios. The appointed contractor will be expected to provide advice on buildability, temporary works, programme, cost, risk, Principal Designer/CDM matters and whole-life implications.
The commission is intended to establish a well evidenced technical, commercial and construction basis for the project, in order to support the Outline Business Case at P3M Stage 2.
This commission is separate to any future decision to progress to detailed design, statutory approvals or main works procurement.
The output will be a series of in-depth evidenced based appraisal reports with a final composite report and recommendation to support Outline Business Case decision-making and any future route-to-market strategy for the Main Works.

title: CP2821-26 Study of Carbon Sequestration and Soil Health Impacts within Highway Earthworks
description:
Devon County Council (DCC), is delivering the A382 Link Road Development near Newton Abbot, Devon.  In addition to the main scheme, additional funding has been made available through the ADEPT Live Labs 2: Decarbonising Local Roads programme to fund carbon reduction measures on the project. The scheme seeks not only to improve highway safety, network resilience and traffic flow, but also to demonstrate innovative approaches to reducing and removing carbon emissions from highway construction activities.
As part of the project's carbon-negative aspirations, DCC wishes to investigate the impact of construction activities on soil carbon levels and the potential benefits of incorporating biochar, enhanced mineral weathering and mycorrhizal fungi into traditional highway earthworks operations. Emerging research suggests that these products may increase carbon sequestration rates, improve soil health and increase long-term carbon storage within highway verges and associated landscape areas.
The budget available is between £150,000 and £170,000 further details on the cost strategy are given in the documentation.

title: District Heating Network Performance, Operational Monitoring and Planned Maintenance Services
description:
District Heating Network Performance, Operational Monitoring and Planned Maintenance Services
Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust is undertaking pre-market engagement in advance of a planned procurement for the provision of Performance, Operational Monitoring and Planned Preventative Maintenance Services for the Trust's District Heating Networks and LTHW dual fuel boilers for the Basildon and Broomfield Hospital sites; with the potential for additional services at the Southend site.
The Trust has recently invested in significant decarbonisation infrastructure across its hospital estate, including district heating networks, energy centres, plate heat exchanger installations, thermal stores, pumps, boilers and specialist control systems. The Trust is seeking to engage with suitably qualified maintenance providers to better understand market capability, innovation opportunities and contract delivery models prior to commencing a formal procurement process. 
Indicative Scope
The successful contractor may be responsible for:
• Planned preventative maintenance (PPM)
• Operational monitoring and performance management
• Remote monitoring and alarm management
• 24/7 reactive maintenance and emergency call-outs
• BMS and controls maintenance
• Water treatment monitoring and management
• Boiler and heating plant maintenance
• Pressurisation systems
• Pumps and distribution networks
• Plate heat exchangers
• Thermal stores
• Heat metering systems
• Fuel oil infrastructure
• Lifecycle planning and asset management
• Energy performance optimisation and reporting
• Coordination with specialist subcontractors and CHP maintenance providers where required. 
Estate
The contract is expected to cover:
Basildon Hospital
• District Heating Energy Centre
• Multiple remote plantrooms
• CHP-supported district heating system
• Multiple heating and domestic hot water PHE installations. 
Broomfield Hospital
• District Heating Energy Centre
• Multiple remote plantrooms
• CHP-supported district heating system
• Contingency remote boilers
• Heating and hot water PHE installations. 
Southend Hospital
• District Heating Energy Centre
• Multiple remote plantrooms
• CHP-supported district heating system
• Integrated and remote network boilers
• Heating and hot water PHE installations. 
Objectives of Engagement
The Trust wishes to understand:
• Market appetite for the opportunity.
• Appropriate contract duration.
• Options for performance-based maintenance arrangements.
• Best practice approaches to remote monitoring and asset management.
• Appropriate KPIs and performance measures.
• Digital maintenance management solutions.
• Innovations that could improve system efficiency and operational resilience.
• Approaches to lifecycle planning and asset replacement forecasting.
• Mobilisation requirements and anticipated timescales.
Supplier Requirements
Interested suppliers should ideally demonstrate experience in:
• Large district heating networks.
• Acute healthcare environments.
• CHP and energy centre infrastructure.
• Building management systems.
• Water treatment and closed heating systems.
• PPM and reactive maintenance services.
• Energy performance optimisation.
Next Steps
Suppliers interested in participating in the engagement exercise are invited to register their interest. Further details regarding engagement sessions, site visits and questionnaires will be circulated in due course.
Please note this engagement exercise is for information gathering purposes only and does not constitute a call for competition.
buyer: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust

The proposed construction works contract is for the construction of a residential development on a greenfield site on the Woodside Road, Derry/Londonderry. The works is for the provision of 57 social housing units that includes a housing mix of 45 homes including split level units, 4 wheelchair accessible homes and 8 apartments including 1 wheelchair accessible. The site also includes extensive landscaping, a children's play park, amenity space and other ancillary works. Alongside the 57 units, a programme of site wide enabling works will also be undertaken. 
The complexity of this development includes site clearance, site remodelling due to site topography, utility alterations, construction of a bus turning circle and detailed phasing requirements.
It is expected ALL social housing units built under this contract will achieve Secured by Design and Lifetime Homes accreditation. All units will also be required to achieve EPC Rating 'A'. The project will also be delivered to BIM Level 2.
A Planning Application, reference LA11/2022/0681/F, for the project was submitted to Derry City & Strabane District Council in June 2022. Full approval is expected in the coming months.
The contract will be for approximately 24-months from date of award and is scheduled to start in March 2027 with the ITT documentation being issued in December 2026.

description:
Devon County Council (DCC) intends to establish an Open Framework for commissioning the delivery of high-quality skills provision services.
The Framework will support the delivery of programmes funded through the Adult Skills Fund (ASF), Free Courses for Jobs (FCFJ), Skills Bootcamps, and other future skills initiatives aligned with local and national workforce needs. The Framework is divided into
Lots based on the different programme types. They are:
• Lot 1 - Adult Skills Fund (ASF) and Free Courses for Jobs (FCFJ)
• Lot 2 - Skills Bootcamps
• Lot 3 - Future Skills Projects
The Framework includes a single common set of sectors and geographical areas which applies across all 3 Lots.
The purpose of the Framework is to enable flexible and responsive skills provision that supports adults to develop the skills needed for sustainable employment and career progression, while also meeting employer demand and contributing to economic growth.
DCC may initiate Call-Offs from both Lot 1 - ASF and FCFJ and Lot 2 Skills Bootcamps for Wave 7 Skills Bootcamp following the appointment of Providers to the Framework.
Any contract value published within this notice are estimated total contract values provided strictly for information only and are subject to confirmation of funding. Value may be revised up or down. There is no guarantee of business or award of call-off contract.

title: Supply & Installation of Protec Replacement Fire Alarm Equipment at University Hospital of Wales
description:
NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership, on behalf of Cardiff and Vale University Health Board wish to inform the market that they intend to award a contract for the provision of a partial upgrade of the existing Protec fire alarm system equipment as a one off purchase Protec are the only supplier capable of supplying and installing the replacement equipment, re-commissioning of the equipment on the current bespoke closed protocol system.
The requirement is necessary to ensure that the site’s fire alarm infrastructure remains operational, reliable and appropriately maintained. Fire alarm systems are a critical life-safety system that requires appropriate replacement to prevent deterioration and reliability of the system. Failure to replace equipment when required could result in defects within the fire alarm system remaining unresolved and could affect the reliability of the site’s fire detection. The requirement therefore supports the continued operation and maintenance of the site’s life-safety systems in order to meet its fire safety and health and safety responsibilities.
buyer: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board

title: Individual Placement Support (Substance Misuse)
description:
The Individual Placement Support (IPS) scheme aims to provide tailored employment support for individuals receiving structured community treatment for drug and alcohol dependence through the Suffolk Integrated Drug and Alcohol Treatment Service provider, Turning Point. The scheme is designed to support service users who are unemployed, as well as those currently employed but at risk of losing their employment, to obtain and sustain meaningful work.
The target group will be users who are in structured treatment in our commissioned Integrated Drug and Alcohol treatment Service provider within Suffolk (Turning Point). The provider will need to work closely with Turning Point to ensure that people receive person-centred support, and outcomes are met. This will include co location in the three hubs across Suffolk and potential to work from satellite locations in the Suffolk area.
The contract period is 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2029 (30 months) with an option to extend for up to a further 2 years (24 months). The contract value is £1,067,445 exclusive of VAT for the duration of the contract including extension.

title: 715890474 Thermoteknix EC - UK5
description:

The Ministry of Defence (MOD) intends to award a contract to Thermoteknix Systems Ltd for the continued through-life support, maintenance and repair of the in-service Thermal Clip-On Sight (TCOS) capability, together with the provision of additional TCOS systems and associated ancillaries as required during the contract period.

The proposed direct award is limited to sustaining the existing assured in-service capability, including the procurement of additional units of the same assured capability, until it's planned Out of Service Date (OSD).

£42,000,000 (estimated) 
Contract Duration 
The contract duration aligns with the current planned Out of Service Date (OSD) of the TCOS capability and is limited to sustaining the existing assured in-service capability during its remaining service life.
The advertised contract value is the maximum estimated value of all potential orders that may be placed under the contract during its term. It does not represent a guaranteed level of expenditure. title: Staff and Student Uniforms [2026]
description:
The University of Salford ("the University") is a leading provider of health and social care education in the North West of England. Provision is delivered through the School of Health Sciences and the School of Health & Society, supporting approximately 3,500 students per annum across a range of health and social care programmes, including Nursing, Midwifery, Diagnostic Radiography, Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, Podiatry, Prosthetics & Orthotics, Clinical Exercise Physiology and Nursing Associate programmes.
The University is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified supplier, for the supply and fulfilment of student and staff uniforms.
The requirement is for approximately 1,700 new students per annum, across three annual intakes in September, January and April. The successful supplier will be responsible for the establishment and operation of an online ordering portal, enabling students to select and order uniforms in accordance with the University's approved specifications and entitlements.
The scope of the requirement includes the supply, fulfilment, delivery, returns and exchanges of uniforms. Orders will be delivered directly to students at their home addresses, with the supplier responsible for managing the associated delivery and returns arrangements. The supplier must also accommodate ad hoc student orders, including maternity garments, special measurements and replacement items, with appropriate arrangements for direct payment by students.
For full tender information and to express an interest please visit our InTend portal via https://supplier.in-tend.co.uk/salford/home.

title: Vehicle Maintenance Services
CP2821-26 Study of Carbon Sequestration and Soil Health Impacts within Highway Earthworks
description:
Devon County Council (DCC), is delivering the A382 Link Road Development near Newton Abbot, Devon.  In addition to the main scheme, additional funding has been made available through the ADEPT Live Labs 2: Decarbonising Local Roads programme to fund carbon reduction measures on the project. The scheme seeks not only to improve highway safety, network resilience and traffic flow, but also to demonstrate innovative approaches to reducing and removing carbon emissions from highway construction activities.
As part of the project's carbon-negative aspirations, DCC wishes to investigate the impact of construction activities on soil carbon levels and the potential benefits of incorporating biochar, enhanced mineral weathering and mycorrhizal fungi into traditional highway earthworks operations. Emerging research suggests that these products may increase carbon sequestration rates, improve soil health and increase long-term carbon storage within highway verges and associated landscape areas.
The budget available is between £150,000 and £170,000 further details on the cost strategy are given in the documentation.

title: HBC JB Land Stability Consultancy Services (ESPH779)
description:
Hastings Borough Council is located within an area of complex geology characterised by coastal cliffs, steep slopes and areas susceptible to ground instability and landslip.
As a result, development proposals submitted to the Local Planning Authority frequently require supporting land stability and geotechnical assessments to demonstrate that development can be undertaken safely and without increasing risks to property, infrastructure or public safety.
The Council requires access to specialist geotechnical and land stability expertise to:
A) support planning officers in reviewing such submissions and determining whether development proposals are acceptable from a land stability perspective; and
B) support planning enforcement officers during investigations into unauthorised works where land stability issues may arise.
The purpose of this contract is to provide independent professional geotechnical advice to the Council on an ad-hoc basis in support of the planning application and enforcement process.

The supplier selected will be able to provide building cleaning services (excluding external window cleaning) as detailed in Schedule 1 - Specification, for a maximum of 4 years. title: Gambling Behaviour Change Campaign
description:
Leicestershire County Council is seeking an experienced provider to undertake the research, co-production, development and design of a behaviour change campaign aimed at increasing awareness of and reducing gambling-related harms across Leicestershire. The requirement is for campaign development and design only. Implementation of the campaign is not included within the scope of this commission, but it is expected that the Provider will identify channels and methods for delivery.
Gambling-related harm is recognised as a public health issue with impacts extending beyond individuals to families, communities and wider society. Harms can include impacts on mental and physical health, finances, relationships, employment, housing stability, and engagement with support services.  Evidence also highlights the need to increase awareness, reduce stigma, encourage earlier help-seeking and improve understanding of the harms.
Partners across Leicestershire are already working together in this space and have developed the Leicestershire Gambling Harms Health Needs Assessment (HNA) highlighting that anyone exposed to gambling products is at risk of experiencing the harms. A recommendation arising from the HNA was to produce a campaign to increase understanding and awareness of the harms associated with gambling. The Commissioner requires a Provider with proven expertise in the marketing and behaviour change field to bring together some of the initial work undertaken and identify what a local campaign would look like.
The successful Provider will conduct all research and development work to produce a campaign strategy, creative concept and campaign assets that would enable the future delivery of a campaign. The campaign should be informed by local need, grounded in evidence-based behaviour change approaches and co-produced with people within the identified target audiences and those with lived experience of gambling-related harm. The impact of stigma should also be central to this commission and the use of stigma free language and a trauma informed approach implemented throughout the process. The Provider will also be required work with the Council’s corporate Communications team.
All intellectual property developed through this contract shall belong to Leicestershire County Council.

title: Stop Smoking and Falls Prevention Strength & Balance Services
description:
Lincolnshire County Council is initiating a tender opportunity for a new Stop Smoking Service and a Falls Prevention Strength and Balance Service. These two services will be procured as part of a single lotted tender process, which will result in the award of two separate contracts.
Lot 1 – Stop Smoking Service: Delivery of a countywide Stop Smoking Service across Lincolnshire, providing evidence-based smoking cessation support that aligns with national policy objectives, Department of Health and Social Care funding requirements and local public health priorities. Funded through the consolidated and ringfenced smoking cessation grant, the service will offer behavioural support, access to cessation aids, digital interventions and targeted initiatives to help residents successfully quit smoking tobacco. The service will place a strong emphasis on reducing smoking-related health inequalities, increasing access for priority and underserved populations, and working collaboratively with health and community partners to maximise referrals and engagement. The service will include the delivery of a 'Swap to Stop' programme, using designated funding as part of the overall contract value to supporting smokers to move away from tobacco use through alternative nicotine products where appropriate.
Lot 2 - Falls Prevention Strength and Balance Service: Delivery of a countywide Falls Prevention Strength and Balance Service across Lincolnshire, providing evidence-based interventions to help reduce falls risk, maintain independence and improve the health and wellbeing of older residents. The service will primarily support people aged 65 and over who have been identified as being at risk of falls, helping them to remain active, confident and independent for longer. It will deliver structured Falls Management Exercise (FaME) programmes led by appropriately qualified instructors, alongside home-based exercise support, referral management, pathway coordination and signposting to wider health, wellbeing and community services. A key focus of the service will be to improve physical strength, balance and mobility, reducing the likelihood and impact of falls and supporting individuals to maintain their quality of life.
The procurement will be undertaken using the Competitive Process pursuant to Regulation 11 of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. The tender opportunity will be published on 2 October 2026, with a tender submission deadline of 2 November 2026 at 12:00 noon.
The commencement date for the new contracts will be 1st April 2027 and an initial contract period of 3 years, with options to extend the contracts by a further period or periods of up to a maximum of 36 months.

title: Department for Communities Strategic Planning Services Framework 2026
description:
The Department for Communities is procuring a Strategic Planning Services Framework 2026. The Framework Contract is for the provision of one consultancy services team, comprising a Consultant and its supply chain, collectively referred to as an Integrated Consultant Team (ICT), to provide construction related strategic planning, financial, legal, architecture and conservation architecture advice in respect of regeneration matters within the remit of the Department for Communities. The Integrated Consultant Team will be expected to provide high level and strategic advice, when required, in relation to all aspects of urban and community regeneration, local government and housing regulation, planning and transport, master planning, urban design, community asset transfer, retail development, property and valuations, evaluation of proposals, legal and financial advice, ad hoc planning and urban design advisory services, advice on procurement strategies and strategic level architectural and conservation architecture services. 
The Framework will be delivered using an NEC4 Framework Contract. Work Orders and Time Charge Orders under the Framework Contract will be executed using NEC4 Professional Services Short Contracts (PSSC) and will be ‘called off’ on an ad hoc basis as required by the Client. The Framework is not a guarantee of future workload.
DESCRIPTION OF RISKS TO CONTRACT PERFORMANCE
Due to the strategic, advisory and project-specific nature of the services to be procured under the Framework Contract, the Contracting Authority recognises that requirements may evolve during the term of the Framework. The scope, nature and volume of commissions may be influenced by changes in Government policy, legislative requirements, funding availability, regeneration priorities and emerging project requirements.
Accordingly, the Contracting Authority reserves the right to utilise the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023 relating to contract modifications where the applicable statutory conditions are satisfied. Such circumstances may include, but are not limited to:
•	unforeseeable circumstances affecting the delivery of services;
•	urgent requirements arising from Government priorities, statutory obligations or emerging business needs; and
•	the requirement for additional services that are connected to or complementary to the original scope of the Framework Contract.
In addition, the Authority may require support in relation to new or expanded programmes, initiatives or funding streams that arise during the Framework period. Such requirements may include, but are not limited to:
a. strategic planning and regeneration studies;
b. masterplanning, urban design and place-making commissions;
c. economic, financial and viability assessments;
d. stakeholder and community engagement services;
e. specialist legal, planning, transport or property advice; and
f. other professional consultancy services falling within the scope of the Framework Contract.
Such services may be commissioned through Work Orders or Time Charge Orders issued under the Framework Contract. There is no guarantee as to the volume, value or timing of any commissions, and requirements will be dependent upon the Authority's operational priorities, project approvals and the availability of funding.
Further information regarding the scope of services, ordering mechanisms and the circumstances in which modifications may be made in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 is contained within the procurement and tender documentation.

title: Heat network techno-economic feasibility study for Didcot
description:
This project will deliver a heat network feasibility study for an area northwest of Didcot. The study will consider the potential combination and/or expansion of potential heat network zones identified by the National Zoning Model (NZM), by incorporating opportunities provided by adjacent data centre development proposals. 400,000sqm of data centres are proposed by several developers on brownfield land adjacent to the operational Didcot Power Station (Oxfordshire). The NZM has not considered these future waste heat sources.
The overarching aims of this study are:
To review heat network zone development opportunities, to help prepare for the introduction of heat network zoning policy.
To determine whether heat network scheme(s) for the specified area are viable.
To understand how heat network schemes can be delivered in alignment with the forthcoming Heat Network Zoning Regulations.
To set out for the council the range of possible delivery models based on different levels of local authority leadership and investment.
To provide decision makers with recommendations which describe the next steps required to take the project through to delivery.
Study Objectives & Work Package Summary:
The council will commission a techno-economic feasibility study, incorporating elements on heat network zoning, for the development of a low carbon heat network at Didcot. This specification is based on the Heat Networks Delivery Unit Zoning Study and Feasibility Study Specifications from February 2026, with some additions to reflect the local context and circumstances. The outputs should meet the requirements to support a Green Heat Network Fund application.
The study objectives are:
Identify the potential for heat network zones and/or heat networks in alignment with the Heat Network Zoning Policy, reviewing the currently proposed zones and potential for expansion.
Assess the technical and economic feasibility of conceptual heat network projects within the local area.
Identify the key heat demand opportunities, key heat sources, and the potential energy centre sites that may unlock delivery of heat network zones.
Identify any key timescales, opportunities and risks to the development of the heat networks identified.
Produce a report to summarise the findings of the study.
Scope of Works:
The following scope of works outlines the key activities to be undertaken as part of this study. The process involves identifying major heat demands, heat sources, and potential distribution networks, and reviewing potential heat network zones. Techno-economic modelling should be undertaken a high-level alongside a description of the assumptions used, including the counterfactuals assumed.
The study must provide the Client with a clear and justifiable basis upon which to evaluate the full potential for heat networks in the study area, for both the short and long-term and how these may best be delivered. It should also be sufficient to enable the Client to complete the Economic Case within an HM Treasury compliant Outline Business Case.
For avoidance of doubt, the consultant should check what the latest guidance is from HNDU. The study should be aligned with the latest CIBSE/ADE Heat Network Code of Practice.

description:

The scope of the concession opportunity is described in this tender notice and the associated tender documents. It is intended to include advertising space at stations operated by Network Rail and participating Department for Transport Operator (DFTO) train operating companies, recognising that these organisations are expected to transition into Great British Railways (GBR) or a successor structure. The estimated value of this concession is based on forecast advertising revenues over the contract term. Due to factors including advertising demand, occupancy levels, future asset onboarding and market conditions, actual revenues may vary. Network Rail estimates that the total concession value is likely to fall within the range of £1.9 billion to £2.2 billion over the contract term.

title: Dilution Refrigerator for Cryogenic Characterisation of RF Hardware
description:
NPL is seeking engagement from suppliers who can provide "Dry" ("cryogen-free") pulse tube cooled dilution refrigerator system to be used for characterisation of quantum hardware including RF and quantum circuits with sample volume under vacuum. The system should include thermometry and associated wiring and readout electronics with provision to integrate additional temperature sensors in future for comprehensive diagnostics. The purpose is to complement our existing measurement systems and add measurement capability, for characterisation of quantum and RF hardware with high throughput and faster cooldowns repeated typically every 2 weeks.
The dilution refrigerator needs to be suitable for RF measurements of complex quantum circuits and hardware, meaning it must be equipped with 20+ coaxial lines with provision to further increase the number of coaxial lines in the future. These lines must include high attenuation input lines suitable for use with sensitive quantum devices such as superconducting qubits and parametric amplifiers and low-loss output coaxial lines suitable for use with low-noise amplifiers, isolators and parametric amplifiers. Some of these coaxial lines must operate up to 40 GHz with provision to integrate even higher frequency RF cabling in the future. There should be sufficient number of DC lines with sufficient reconfigurability to enable biasing of at least tens of RF multi-way switches, at least four low noise amplifiers and few dedicated high resistance and low resistance DC looms for devices under test with provision to integrate more DC looms in the future.

title: Test Operations Service - Future Service Management Programme
description:
The Standards and Testing Agency (STA), an executive agency of the Department for Education (DfE), is responsible for the delivery of statutory National Curriculum Assessments (NCAs), including Key Stage 1 assessments (optional), Phonics screening check (statutory) and Key Stage 2 assessments (statutory).
The current arrangements for the delivery of assessment operations for these assessments are due to expire following the delivery of assessments in 2029. To inform future decisions, STA has established the Future Service Management Programme to consider our delivery options.
The programme is considering a range of potential options for the future delivery of assessment services. These services include, but are not limited to, print production, collation and logistics, scanning, marking, customer support services, systems provision, data processing and integration.
The purpose of this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is to advise the market of STA's intention to undertake early market engagement activities to inform the assessment of our options. This engagement is intended to improve STA's understanding of current market capability, emerging technologies, innovative delivery approaches, commercial models and potential opportunities and constraints associated with the future provision of assessment services.
STA is seeking input from organisations with relevant expertise and experience in one or more aspects of the service.
Details of the market engagement activity can be found in the engagement section of this notice.
Following the engagement activities, STA may invite interested organisations to participate in further market engagement through questionnaires, workshops, requests for information or additional discussions. Feedback gathered through these activities will help shape STA's understanding of the market and support the development of future recommendations.
Participation in this market engagement process will not form part of any future procurement evaluation and will not provide any supplier with an advantage in any subsequent procurement process.
The publication of this notice does not signify the commencement of any procurement process and does not constitute any commitment by STA to undertake any procurement exercise.
Any future procurement strategy will be determined following completion of the Delivery Model Assessment, approval of recommendations through the appropriate governance channels and consideration of government priorities.
STA wishes to ensure that potential providers have early visibility of the programme and future opportunities to engage. This supports STA's objective of promoting open, transparent and inclusive engagement with the market, including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs).
STA reserves the right to amend, suspend or discontinue any aspect of the programme or market engagement activities at any time without liability. Participation in this engagement process is entirely voluntary and participants will bear their own costs associated with involvement in any engagement activity.
Any information provided by STA during market engagement activities is indicative only and should not be relied upon as a commitment regarding future service requirements, procurement arrangements or delivery model decisions.
The Authority administers its procurement activity electronically through Jaggaer https://education.app.jaggaer.com , the Department for Education's e-sourcing system, and further details of any future opportunities will be published at the appropriate time through the relevant procurement channels.

title: Prince Henry's High School ~ Cleaning Tender
description:
The successful Supplier will be required to provide cleaning services for Prince Henry’s High School 
The annual contract value is approximately £275,000.00. The initial contract term will be three years, commencing on 13 February 2027 and concluding on 31 October 2030. The contract will operate on a guaranteed performance basis, with the successful Supplier providing a fixed annual contract price. There will be an option to extend the contract for a further period of up to one plus one years by mutual agreement.
Prince Henry’s High School is a large 13–18 secondary school and Sixth Form in Evesham, Worcestershire. The school occupies a substantial and varied estate comprising buildings of different ages, general teaching accommodation, specialist curriculum areas, sports facilities, performance spaces and facilities used by the wider community.
There are approximately 1,282 pupils on role and 180 staff. 
The school has high expectations for students and places importance on providing a safe, welcoming and well-maintained environment. Cleaning standards should reflect the professional standards expected across the school.
For the avoidance of doubt TUPE Regulations will apply to this contract.  
Whilst the monthly contract payment will represent one-twelfth of the annual contract value, a monthly reconciliation process will be undertaken to verify actual hours worked against those budgeted within the contract. Where actual hours delivered are lower than those budgeted, the Supplier will be required to provide a credit to the school. This credit will be calculated by dividing the annual contract value by the annual contracted hours to establish a contractual hourly rate, which will then be multiplied by the shortfall in hours delivered.
The school is seeking a suitably experienced Supplier with a proven track record of delivering cleaning services within the secondary school sector. Preference will be given to Suppliers with a strong operational presence within the local area, enabling the provision of responsive contract support, operational resilience and service flexibility throughout the contract term.
A robust management structure must be provided to ensure the specification is delivered consistently throughout the contract period. This will include regular engagement with key stakeholders at the school and proactive contract management.
The school is seeking a Supplier that will work collaboratively and flexibly with school leaders to maintain high standards of cleanliness. The school is also keen to explore opportunities to achieve improved value for money through service efficiencies, enhanced staff training and innovative equipment solutions.
The scope of the contract includes all cleaning services across the school site, including holiday cleaning and periodic deep cleaning requirements.
The successful Supplier will be required to provide a concise but detailed monthly management report, enabling the senior leadership team to monitor contract performance, service standards and continuous improvement initiatives.
Key Contract Objectives from February 2027
The school requires the cleaning operation to deliver the following outcomes:
•Deliver consistently high standards of cleanliness and hygiene across the School, providing a safe, welcoming and well-maintained environment for students, staff and visitors. 
•Achieve and maintain particularly high standards within toilets, washrooms and other high-footfall areas, supported by an effective daytime cleaning provision and responsive approach to reactive cleaning requirements. 
•Provide a reliable and adequately resourced cleaning service, with sufficient staffing levels and robust arrangements for covering sickness, absence and vacancies without compromising service standards. 
•Ensure effective on-site supervision and contract management, supported by clear lines of responsibility, regular management presence and responsive communication with the School. 
•Implement robust quality assurance and performance management arrangements, including regular inspections, meaningful KPIs, transparent reporting and prompt corrective action where required standards are not achieved. 
•Provide appropriate, modern and well-maintained cleaning equipment, products and working methods suitable for the School's varied estate, specialist areas, flooring and cleaning requirements. 
•Provide a flexible and responsive service capable of adapting to the operational needs of the School, including lettings, events, holiday periods and other changing requirements. 
•Deliver demonstrable value for money and continuous improvement, incorporating appropriate innovation and environmentally responsible practices where these can be achieved without compromising cleaning, hygiene or infection-control standards.
Please see PSQ Document for more information.

title: CEFAS26-107 Support services for the Coastal Health Programme
description:
Following on from the work delivered in the pilot phase of the Coastal Health programme, The Association of Inshore Fisheries and Conservation Authorities (IFCA) has been selected to support delivery of core requirements as follows:
1. Work with all IFCAs to review, update and test protocols and tools to improve our preparedness, response and intelligence gathering processes, and trial their implementation at a national scale. This will include advising Cefas in the development of a scenario testing exercise, and attending preparatory meetings to ensure IFCA processes are adequately captured and tested in this exercise
Actions:
· Continue to circulate and receive input from IFCAs on the protocols and guidance.
· Set up an external shared drive with protocols, guidance and training material.
· Run through a scenario testing exercise with the IFCA Technical Advisory Group, Chief Officers Group and the National Inshore Marine Enforcement Group.
· Run through protocols and guidance at the IFCA Training Course in Brixham in February.
· Promote the work of the Coastal Health programme at relevant national conferences attended by AIFCA (including Coastal Futures and SAGB).
2. Building on work started by the AIFCA, create stakeholder maps for each IFCA district of their key local and regional fisheries and environmental stakeholder groups, including a database of contacts.
Actions:
· Work with all IFCAs to pull together lists of stakeholders in each IFCA district, including contact details, and pull together into stakeholder maps.
· Continue to engage with the Coastal Partnerships Network to build on stakeholder mapping across England.
3. Key representation for the AIFCA in attendance at the Coastal and Marine Health programme board every two months. Provide updates into the PgB pack. Attendance at CHEPARD and other Coastal Health meetings.
Actions:
· Attendance at meetings and sending over progress updates.
· Production of reports every 2 months to be delivered to the PgB.
4. Facilitating engagement with local IFCA's and industry stakeholder groups. This will consist of at least three planned engagement sessions:
a) To present and discuss Coastal Health work on cockles and mussel mortalities in the Wash estuary, with industry representatives and EIFCA officers.
b) To present and discuss the cockle baseline study led last year to relevant industry representatives and IFCA officers, Location TBC.
c) To set up a pilot 'Changing seas' study in an IFCA district (e.g. Sussex), to understand local community perspectives on changing species distribution and abundance in key fisheries.
Actions:
· Work with Eastern IFCA to to present on Cefas cockle work to stakeholders. This will include organisation of the meeting (or facilitation of other means of engagement), producing information to circulate, and travel time.
· Similar to above for second workshop presenting cockle baseline study.
· Changing Seas study
o Work with Cefas to develop design of surveys and interviews for the study.
o To work with an IFCA (e.g. Sussex) and local partners to reach out to local fishermen and wider community members.
o Conduct an engagement session or quayside interviews.
o Support write up and reviewing of final report.
o Support Cefas with scoping national study for next financial year 2027-28.
As needed, ad hoc meetings may be set up to engage with stakeholders' groups in the event of adverse coastal health events
buyer: Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science

title: Let’s Talk Money – Debt & Housing Support Service
description:
Caerphilly County Borough Council is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified organisation to deliver the Let's Talk Money Debt and Housing Support Service.
The service is jointly funded through the Housing Support Grant (HSG) and the Children’s and Communities Grant (CCG – Families First) and is designed to support individuals and families experiencing financial instability where debt is a primary driver of housing risk, homelessness, or wider family instability.
The service is referral‑led, accessed primarily through the Housing Support Gateway, and is specifically designed for individuals and families who do not engage well with appointment‑based or advice‑only services. This includes people who are homeless, living in temporary accommodation, sofa surfing, or experiencing complex needs.
The Authority is seeking to appoint a suitable Provider to deliver a targeted, debt‑led housing support service for people aged 16 years and over living within the Caerphilly County Borough. 
The aim of the service is to prevent homelessness, sustain tenancies, and improve family resilience through hands‑on, needs‑led and practical support delivered via a single lead worker model. This includes financial capability and budgeting support, managing debt by securing viable debt solution options, and addressing housing‑related issues that may impact financial stability or tenancy sustainment.
The service will provide income maximisation support, benefit entitlement checks, welfare benefit applications, mandatory reconsiderations and appeals where these relate to individuals already receiving support through the service and where debt-related financial instability remains the primary presenting issue. 
Referrals relating solely to welfare benefit support, welfare rights issues, mandatory reconsiderations, or appeals, where debt-related financial instability is not the primary presenting issue, will be allocated through the Housing Support Gateway to the appropriate Provider.
The service is not intended to operate as an advice-only provision. Whilst advise forms part of the support offer, the primary purpose of the contract is to deliver practical housing-related support that promotes financial stability, tenancy sustainment and long-term independence. 
While the service promotes independence, the Provider must deliver supported actions where vulnerability, complexity or executive‑function barriers prevent individuals from completing tasks independently.
Client groups (the list is not exhaustive) may include:
•	Individuals aged 16 years and over requiring support to manage their finances.
•	Individuals at risk of losing their tenancy due to financial pressures, including rent arrears.
•	Single people
•	Families with support needs
•	Individuals with disabilities, including mental health conditions, physical disabilities, dementia, and acquired brain injuries.
•	Individuals with learning disabilities or developmental disorders
•	Individuals with complex needs, including substance misuse.
The Service must take a proactive and preventative approach, supporting individuals to build long-term financial resilience reduce debt, prevent homelessness, and sustain tenancies. Housing instability and financial instability are often interconnected; therefore, the service must address both areas holistically.
This specification is outcome‑based. The Provider must deliver an effective, high‑quality service that achieves positive outcomes and demonstrates value for money. As individuals become more stable and independent, support must be appropriately tapered to reflect changing need.
The service will deliver a lead-worker model incorporating:
•	Debt-focused housing support
•	FCA-regulated debt advice
•	Financial capability and budgeting support
•	Income maximisation
•	Welfare benefit support
•	Housing-related support linked to financial instability
•	Home visit and outreach-based engagement
•	Tenancy sustainment and homelessness prevention
The service is designed to support individuals and families who may struggle to engage with traditional advice-based services, including those experiencing homelessness, living in temporary accommodation, sofa surfing, poor mental health, substance misuse, neurodiversity or other complex needs.
Full details can be found in the ITT documents on the Councils e sourcing platform Proactis Plaza

title: Independent Living Skills App for Young People
description:
Background
Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council's Commissioning Team is exploring the potential development of an Independent Living Skills App for young people living in supported accommodation and those preparing to move into independent living.
The concept has evolved from previous work undertaken to develop an Independent Living Skills Workbook. Feedback gathered through engagement with stakeholders indicated a preference for a digital solution, with an app being viewed as a more engaging, accessible and interactive way of supporting young people to develop essential life skills.
The proposed app could include content relating to daily living skills, health and wellbeing and tenancy rights and responsibilities and is intended to be a mixed model of engagement through guidance, learning and self-development.
The Council is currently undertaking soft market testing to understand the opportunities, constraints and indicative costs associated with developing such a solution before determining any future procurement approach.
Purpose of Market Engagement:-
The Council wishes to engage with organisations that have experience in app design, development and implementation, particularly those with experience in:
•	Youth and children's services
•	Housing and supported accommodation services
•	Educational and skills development applications
•	Public sector and local authority projects
•	User-centred and co-produced digital solutions
Feedback gathered through these engagement sessions will help inform future decision-making and procurement considerations.
The Council has identified a potential funding opportunity to support this work and is undertaking market engagement activity to better understand the feasibility, costs, technical requirements and delivery timescales associated with developing such a solution. Supplier feedback will help inform the Council's assessment of what may be achievable within the funding and implementation timeframe available.
Areas for Discussion:-
A discussion paper containing further information and specific questions will be circulated to organisations in advance of the engagement sessions, however the Council is seeking feedback in the following areas:
•	Potential approaches to app development and delivery
•	User engagement and accessibility considerations
•	Data protection, cyber security and information governance considerations
•	Hosting and technical requirements
•	Ongoing maintenance and support arrangements
•	Indicative development and implementation timescales
•	Licensing options and commercial models
•	Indicative costs and budget considerations
•	Key risks, dependencies and lessons learned from similar projects
Market Engagement Sessions:-
Individual engagement sessions will be held virtually via Microsoft Teams.
Sessions will last up to one hour and will be allocated on a first come, first served basis.

title: UK4 - Care Leaver Covenant & Corporate Parenting Market Engagement Event Notice
description:
The Department for Education (DfE) is seeking to appoint an experienced and expert external provider to support government departments and relevant public bodies with the implementation of new Corporate Parenting duties, in addition to the continuation, expansion and strategic development of the Care Leaver Covenant (CLC). 
At the heart of the Government’s reforms is improving outcomes and life chances for looked after children (children in care) and care leavers by removing barriers to opportunity. This includes strengthening enduring relationships, support and opportunities across government, public services, employers and wider society. 
This procurement presents an opportunity for a single organisation or consortium to support government departments and relevant public bodies in embedding corporate parenting responsibilities while simultaneously advancing the Care Leaver Covenant as a national platform for improving outcomes for care leavers. 
Together these strands of activity provide a coordinated approach for mobilising organisations across the public, private and voluntary sectors to strengthen policy, practice, services, delivery, support and opportunities for looked after children and care leavers. 
Corporate Parenting
The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 extended corporate parenting responsibilities beyond local authorities to government departments and key public bodies. 
Corporate Parenting is a shared responsibility requiring government departments and relevant public bodies to promote, support and improve outcomes for children in care and care leavers. The new statutory duties require relevant bodies to consider the needs and experiences of children in care and care leavers when developing policies and delivering services. Corporate parenting is an important part of the government’s response to the recently published Care Leavers’ Deaths Review. 
DfE requires specialist external support to help relevant bodies understand and implement these duties effectively, build organisational capability and cultural awareness of children in care and care leavers and develop robust delivery plans.
Care Leaver Covenant
The Care Leaver Covenant is a national commitment by public, private and voluntary sector organisations to provide practical opportunities and support for care leavers aged 16 to 25. The Covenant provides employment opportunities, apprenticeships, mentoring, financial support, discounts and wider assistance that helps young people transition to independent adulthood.
DfE requires a provider to continue to grow the Covenant's reach and impact while aligning its work with Government ambitions relating to education, employment and training (EET), relationships, housing and health.
The provider will:
•	Support implementation of Corporate Parenting duties across government and public bodies.
•	Strengthen understanding of children’s social care and care experience across the public sector.
•	Ensure lived experience informs implementation approaches.
•	Secure a refresh of offers from existing signatories and recruit more signatories for the Covenant, particularly in relation to employment, education and training 
•	Continue to build relationships with government departments and others to embed the impact of the Covenant.
•	Help local authorities to enhance their Local Offer through links with Covenant signatories.
•	Continue to raise the profile of the Covenant among care leavers so that more sign up to take advantage of offers.
•	Support delivery of Government priorities relating to children in care and care leavers.
Contract Timescale
It is anticipated that the contract will be for 2 financial years subject to business planning conformation for Year 2.
•	1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028 covering two work strands: the Care Leaver Covenant and Corporate Parenting. 
•	1 April 2028 to 31 March 2029 covering one work strand: the Care Leaver Covenant.

description:
Cumberland Council is awarding contracts for the operation of Supported Bus Services.  
These services form a critical element of Cumberland's transport network, ensuring continued provision of bus services where the commercial operation is not viable and supporting access for people to employment, education, healthcare and essential services across both urban and rural communities.

title: Dilution Refrigerator for Cryogenic Characterisation of RF Hardware
description:
NPL is seeking engagement from suppliers who can provide "Dry" ("cryogen-free") pulse tube cooled dilution refrigerator system to be used for characterisation of quantum hardware including RF and quantum circuits with sample volume under vacuum. The system should include thermometry and associated wiring and readout electronics with provision to integrate additional temperature sensors in future for comprehensive diagnostics. The purpose is to complement our existing measurement systems and add measurement capability, for characterisation of quantum and RF hardware with high throughput and faster cooldowns repeated typically every 2 weeks.
The dilution refrigerator needs to be suitable for RF measurements of complex quantum circuits and hardware, meaning it must be equipped with 20+ coaxial lines with provision to further increase the number of coaxial lines in the future. These lines must include high attenuation input lines suitable for use with sensitive quantum devices such as superconducting qubits and parametric amplifiers and low-loss output coaxial lines suitable for use with low-noise amplifiers, isolators and parametric amplifiers. Some of these coaxial lines must operate up to 40 GHz with provision to integrate even higher frequency RF cabling in the future. There should be sufficient number of DC lines with sufficient reconfigurability to enable biasing of at least tens of RF multi-way switches, at least four low noise amplifiers and few dedicated high resistance and low resistance DC looms for devices under test with provision to integrate more DC looms in the future.
The asset must enable the characterisation of quantum and cryogenic RF hardware based on the following:
- Base temperature of less than or equal to 10 mK with access to PT2 and other intermediate stages for testing components at intermediate temperatures.
- Mixing chamber plate area of at least 0.19m2 in horizontal space and vertical experimental apparatus
- We do NOT require a magnet

title: Living with Cancer Employer Collaborative - Roundtable Events
description:
DHSC will be hosting two virtual roundtable events, led by the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Health Innovation, on the “Living with Cancer” agenda to discuss how employers and other organisations can better support people to remain in or return to work following a cancer diagnosis and treatment, with a particular focus on the challenges faced by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and spreading best practice across sectors of the economy. 
The roundtables will take place on: 
• Tuesday, 27th October 2026, 09:30-10:30 GMT 
• Tuesday, 3rd November 2026, 09:30-10:30 GMT 
To register your organisation’s interest in one of these events, please complete the following registration form by Tuesday, 20th October 2026 at 11:59 pm: 
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=MIwnYaiRMUyMH-9N6Jc6HHkA63U0d81Ht4WY0oa7NW1UNFZKVktHMU9ZWVhIT01GNDRKMU0zTE9aVS4u 
Attendance is restricted to one person per organisation. 
The National Cancer Plan for England recognises the impact that cancer can have on people’s working lives and sets out an ambition to work with employers and impact economy investors to raise awareness of effective interventions, scale good practice and make support more accessible. 
Too many people are forced to stop working due to cancer. Around 830,000 working age people are living with cancer in England. Cancer can have a significant impact on people’s finances and ability to remain in work: people hospitalised with cancer face nearly £5,000 in lost income, while patients lose an average of 75 days of work across their pathway.  
People living with cancer are not always able to access interventions that are known to be useful. Through engagement on the National Cancer Plan, we have heard charities, larger companies and practitioners already know which interventions can help people living with cancer to remain in and return to work. However, some sectors of the economy still find it difficult to proactively offer support due to a lack of awareness or easily accessible tools. These challenges are often faced by sectors of the economy which account for a large share of employment, including SMEs. 
DHSC is therefore seeking to work with purpose-driven businesses, charities and the impact economy to help raise awareness, scale effective interventions and make them more accessible. The Ministerial roundtables will provide an opportunity to hear from organisations about existing approaches, the challenges they face and where collaboration between different organisations could help scale effective support.

title: Escorting and Related Services
description:
The Home Office is seeking to engage with suppliers who are interested in becoming the commercial partners responsible for delivering the Escorting Services contract, which provides the in-country and overseas escorting of detained persons and management of Short-Term Holding Facilities (STHF), across the UK and Northern France.   
Background:  
The Home Office is responsible for detaining and enforcing the removal of people from the UK who have no legal basis to remain here.  The Escorting Services contract is fundamental to delivering this through the movement of people within the UK, which supports the functioning of the immigration detention / removal estate; the removal of people from the UK, which is predominately via air travel and a mix of escorted (to destination) and unescorted (not escorted to destination).  The contract also includes the operation, management and maintenance of Residential Short-Term Holding Facilities and the operation and management of Non-Residential Short-Term Holding Facilities at air/seaports and Immigration Enforcement reporting centres (STHFs).  STHFs support the wider immigration detention / removal estate, enforcement activity within the community and protection of the UK border.  
Requirement (please note not exhaustive and subject to change):  
Management Services – includes operational control centre, performance monitoring and reporting, audit arrangement, and  complaint procedures.  
Core Services – includes welfare, care of children, risk assessments, use of force, staffing & personnel and training.  
In-Country Escorting – 24/7 escorting between locations within the UK. Includes prisons, police stations, hospitals (inc bed watches), STHFs, Immigration Removal Centres. Also includes escort to aircraft for purpose of removal (unescorted) and provision of medical escorts.  
Overseas Escorting – 24/7 escorting from place of detention within the UK to designated overseas destination, primarily via air travel with a mix between scheduled and charter flights.  Also includes provision of medical escorts and interfacing with the authorities travel service provider.  
Non-Residential STHF  - the operation and management of designated holding rooms across all parts of the UK.  There are currently 28 of these facilities which operate up to 24/7 and can hold people up to 24 hours and beyond in certain circumstances. 
Residential STHF – the operation, management and maintenance of RSTHF across all parts of the UK.  There are currently 3 of these facilities which operate 24/7 and can hold people up to 7 days in certain circumstances.  
Juxtaposed Controls (Northern France) 24/7 escorting services with the UK control zones (Calais, Coquelles, and Dunkerque) and operation and management of 5 (currently) holding rooms at these French ports.
