title: NWSLC HR & Payroll Software and Services
description:
North Warwickshire and South Leicestershire College (‘the College’) is issuing this UK5 Transparency Notice in respect of the procurement for HR and Payroll Software and Services following completion of a competitive procurement process, conducted under internal reference CA17881.
The procurement was commenced through publication of a tender via the Open Procedure on 22nd May 2026 and was conducted in accordance with the requirements applicable to above-threshold procurements. Tender notices were issued for publication to both Find a Tender and ContractsFinder through the College’s eSender. Procurement documentation was made available without restriction through the College's eSender portal, enabling unrestricted access to procurement information and tender submission.
The College has identified that, although an FO2 notice successfully published to ContractsFinder, the required UK4 notice failed to publish to Find a Tender. Investigation undertaken with the eSender confirmed that the omission arose as a result of a technical systems error and was not the consequence of any intentional action by the College. Although the underlying issue was subsequently rectified, the UK4 notice did not publish in relation to this procurement.
The College’s procurement process has been conducted competitively, and a robust process has been undertaken, despite the above omission. The procurement was subject to a competitive evaluation process, following which Assessment Summaries were issued to unsuccessful tenderers on 18th September 2026 in accordance with the Procurement Act.
The College intends to award the contract to the supplier identified in this notice. This UK5 Transparency Notice is being published to ensure transparency regarding the procedural omission described above and to provide notice of the intended contract award.
The College will observe an 8 working day standstill period subsequent to the publication of this Transparency Notice.
buyer: North Warwickshire and South Leicestershire College

title: Dunraven Educational Trust - Social, Emotional, Metal Health Services
description:
Dunraven Educational Trust (‘the Trust’) is issuing this UK5 Transparency Notice in respect of the procurement for Social, Emotional and Mental Health Services following completion of a competitive procurement process conducted under the Competitive Flexible Procedure, internal reference CA18147. 
The tender was classified as a light-touch procurement in accordance with the applicable requirements of the Procurement Act 2023. Procurement documentation was made available to participating tenderers through the e-tendering portal MultiQuote, enabling access to the procurement information and submission of tenders.
Following completion of the competitive procurement process, the Trust identified a successful tenderer in accordance with the published evaluation methodology and award criteria. The estimated value stated in the UK4 Tender Notice was below the applicable threshold and was a genuine estimate made in good faith, based on the Trust’s assessment of the anticipated contract requirement and historic contract expenditure. However, following evaluation and selection of the successful tender, the actual value of the proposed contract is above the applicable threshold. 
The Trust subsequently attempted to publish the required UK6 Contract Award Notice. However, the UK6 was not accepted for publication by Find a Tender due to the difference between the value stated in the original UK4 Tender Notice and the value of the successful award. 
The Trust’s procurement process has been conducted competitively and a robust evaluation process has been completed. The Trust intends to award the contract to the successful tenderer identified through the competitive procurement process.
This UK5 Transparency Notice is being published to provide transparency regarding the circumstances described above and to provide notice of the Trust’s intention to enter into the proposed contract.
The Trust will observe an 8 working day standstill period following publication of this Transparency Notice.

We would like to demonstrate these technologies in a cell that is designed to read and write data during the automatic disassembly of an electric motor. title: Future Transport Modelling - Strategic Advice
description:
Transport for Wales (TfW) is undertaking preliminary market engagement to inform the development of a potential future procurement for the provision of strategic transport modelling advisory services. 
TfW currently maintains and operates a suite of multi-modal regional transport models covering South East Wales, South West and Mid Wales, and North Wales. These models are used to support the appraisal of transport interventions, investment decisions, policy development and future scenario testing across Wales. 
The proposed requirement, referred to as Future Transport Modelling – Strategic Advice, would provide independent expert advice to help shape the future direction of TfW's transport modelling capability. The successful supplier would be expected to assess the current modelling landscape, identify opportunities for innovation and improvement, advise on approaches to addressing future uncertainty, and develop a phased roadmap for the evolution of TfW's modelling capability. 
The scope is anticipated to include advice relating to: 
- The evolution of TfW's existing regional transport models; 
- Opportunities for innovation, including emerging modelling approaches, artificial intelligence, big-data analytics and open-source solutions; 
- Scenario planning and uncertainty analysis; and 
- The development of a future transport modelling roadmap. 
The requirement is intended to provide strategic advice only. TfW will retain responsibility for decision-making and implementation through its existing transport modelling arrangements.

title: Southsea Castle Catering and Events Concession Opportunity - Portsmouth 2026
description:
AWARD & STANDSTILL PERIOD
Following receipt of tenders on 21st August 2026 the Council has concluded the assessment process and issued assessment summaries to the successful and unsuccessful suppliers as required under Section 50 of the Procurement Act 23 (the 'Act').
The Council reserves the right to amend (extend)the Standstill Period if needed; if this right is exercised, the Contract Award Notice will be updated and affected suppliers will be notified accordingly.
After the Standstill Period has expired, and provided no legal challenge has been made by the end of the Standstill Period or any agreed extension, the Council intends to enter into contracts with the Successful Supplier. Following this, the Council also intends to publish a Contract Details Notice.
Procurement description
Portsmouth City Council (the Council) has awarded a concession contract for the provision of catering and events services at Southsea Castle. The contract will operate under a long-term commercial arrangement incorporating a lease together with a revenue-sharing mechanism between the operator and the Council. The contract has been awarded under Lot 1, comprising an initial term of five years with the option to extend by up to a further five years at the Council's discretion.
Southsea Castle is a historic Scheduled Ancient Monument and visitor attraction located on Portsmouth's seafront. The site operates as a visitor destination, museum, restaurant, wedding venue and events location, attracting significant visitor numbers throughout the year and playing an important role in the city's tourism, heritage and cultural offer.
The successful operator will be responsible for delivering catering services and supporting a programme of events from the site, whilst working collaboratively with the Council to maximise visitor experience, increase commercial opportunities and support community engagement. Delivery of the contract will be undertaken in a manner that recognises and protects the historic significance of the Castle while balancing commercial operation with public access and heritage requirements.
The contract includes performance measures relating to customer experience, event delivery, catering quality, commercial performance, compliance and partnership working. The Council also expects the operator to support its social value objectives and work collaboratively with stakeholder organisations and local communities.
The Council recognises that local government structures and service delivery arrangements may evolve during the life of the contract. Any future changes arising from local government reorganisation, devolution arrangements or other changes in public sector governance will be managed in accordance with the contract provisions and applicable legislation.
The Council has identified the following known risks & opportunities that may occur during the duration of the term of the contract and may positively or negatively impact the scope, scale, value, timescales, end user demand, etc. related the contract:
•	Development and changing demographics of Portsmouth area which could impact positively or negatively on operator revenues
•	Marco and micro environmental impacts on utilities and other costs which could impact operator costs
•	Changes to VAT levels and other impacts of taxation which could impact operator costs 
•	Local Government Review impacts including for assignment of contract to successor unitary authority and any new requirements / objectives of the new authority which may require alterations to the technical scope, contractual and commercial structure of the arrangements 
•	Unforeseen maintenance requirements which could increase operator costs and impact revenues if closures are required
•	Inflation and other cost of living impacts which could increase or decrease operator revenues and costs
•	Changes to National Living Wage, National Insurance and other factors which could impact operator employment costs
•	Increased or decreased competition from other public or privately run facilities or attractions which could impact operator revenues
•	Introduction of new technologies, systems and processes which could reduce operator costs and / or increase revenues as well as impacting technical scope
•	Introduction of new activities through market innovations that could open up new operator revenue opportunities and impact technical scope
•	Changes to relevant government policy / legislation which could increase or decrease operator revenues & costs, as well as potentially mandating changes to the technical scope
•	An endemic or pandemic event similar to Covid 19 which could increase costs and / or reduce demand.
The Council has identified the risks and opportunities above associated with the delivery of this contract. In accordance with Schedule 8 of the Procurement Act 2023, the Council reserves the right to modify the contract, without initiating a new procurement procedure, should any of these risks materialise during the contract term.

The estimated scope is 2,000 hours over a period of 24 months, with an option for an extension for up to 12 months. The scope is an estimate and is not binding for the contracting authority. title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – Sanierung Carl-Orff-Gymnasium Unterschleißheim - Planung der Technischen Ausrüstung, Anlagengruppen 4 und 5, Leistungsphasen 2-3 und 5-9 gemäß §§ 53 ff. HOAI
description: Der Zweckverband Staatliche weiterführende Schulen in Unterschleißheim beabsichtigt die abschnittsweise Sanierung und Umstrukturierung von Teilbereichen des Carl-Orff-Gymnasiums in Unterschleißheim. Die von der bestehenden Baugenehmigung erfassten offenen Lernlandschaften umfassen eine Fläche von insgesamt bis zu 400 m². Im Rahmen der weiteren Projektvorbereitung wurde jedoch festgestellt, dass darüber hinaus Sanierungsbedarf in angrenzenden Unterrichts-, Flur-, Erschließungs- und Nebenflächen besteht. Zusätzlich sind die erforderlichen brandschutztechnischen und gebäudetechnischen Anpassungen zu berücksichtigen. Nach derzeitigem Kenntnisstand wird daher von einer insgesamt betroffenen Sanierungsfläche von ca. 800 bis 1.000 m² ausgegangen. Die abschließende Abgrenzung und Ermittlung der Sanierungsfläche sowie die Konkretisierung des Maßnahmenumfangs sollen im Rahmen der Vor- und Entwurfsplanung erfolgen. Die bauliche Umsetzung soll abschnittsweise und im laufenden Schulbetrieb erfolgen. Nach aktuellem Stand ist folgende Gliederung vorgesehen: - BA 1: 1. Obergeschoss, - BA 2: Erdgeschoss, Teilbereich 1, - BA 3: Erdgeschoss, Teilbereich 2. Die räumliche Abgrenzung, Zusammensetzung und Reihenfolge der Bauabschnitte sind im Rahmen der weiteren Planung zu überprüfen und fortzuschreiben. Änderungen können sich insbesondere aus dem Planungsergebnis, den Anforderungen des laufenden Schulbetriebs, dem erforderlichen Bauablauf sowie aus förderrechtlichen Rahmenbedingungen ergeben. Für die Maßnahme werden Kosten (KG 300+400, Stand August 2026) in Höhe von ca. 5,50 Mio. € brutto geschätzt. Nach derzeitigem Planungsstand sind folgende Projektmeilensteine vorgesehen: - Beginn der Planungsleistungen: März 2027, - Beginn der baulichen Umsetzung: Februar 2028, - Voraussichtliche Fertigstellung: Februar 2030. Die genannten Termine stellen den derzeit vorgesehenen Rahmenterminplan dar und sind im Zuge der weiteren Planung, insbesondere unter Berücksichtigung der Bauabschnittsbildung und des laufenden Schulbetriebs, zu konkretisieren. Es ist beabsichtigt mit dieser Ausschreibung folgende Leistungen (stufen- und bauabschnittsweise) zu beauftragen: Planung der Technischen Ausrüstung, Anlagengruppen 4 und 5, Leistungsphasen 2-3 und 5-9 gemäß §§ 53 ff. HOAI. Zunächst wird in der 1. Beauftragungsstufe die Leistungsphase 2 gemäß § 55 HOAI über alle Bauabschnitte beauftragt. Die Leistungsphasen 3 und 5-9 werden stufen- und bauabschnittsweise abgerufen. Ein Rechtsspruch auf Gesamtbeauftragung besteht nicht.

title: Germany – Research and experimental development services – Beratungsdienstleistung RealBat
description: Die Universität Hamburg (im Folgenden „UHH“) ist als Exzellenzuniversität mit mehr als 43.000 Studierenden und ca. 6.000 Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeitern eine der forschungsstärksten Universitäten Deutschlands und gleichzeitig eine der größten Ausbildungseinrichtungen Norddeutschlands. Mit ihrem Konzept der „Flagship University“ in der Metropolregion Hamburg pflegt sie innovative und kooperative Verbindungen zu wissenschaftlichen und außerwissenschaftlichen Partnern. Sie produziert für den Standort – aber auch national und international – die zukunftsgerichteten gesellschaftlichen Güter Bildung, Erkenntnis und Austausch von Wissen unter dem Leitziel der Nachhaltigkeit. Die Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften Hamburg (HAW Hamburg) ist die zweitgrößte Hochschule in Hamburg und die drittgrößte Fachhochschule in Deutschland. Gegliedert ist die HAW Hamburg in die vier Fakultäten Design, Medien, Information, Life Sciences, Technik und Informatik sowie Wirtschaft und Soziales. Sie fördert angewandte Forschung und Innovation in Zusammenarbeit mit der Industrie und bietet zahlreiche internationale Austauschmöglichkeiten. Moderne Infrastruktur und engagierte Lehrende, die praktische Erfahrungen einbringen, runden das Profil der Hochschule ab. Die Universität Hamburg führt als zentrale Vergabestelle gemäß § 4 VgV für die HAW Hamburg ein Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb gem. § 15 VgV durch. Die HAW Hamburg wird mit Zuschlag Vertragspartnerin und Auftraggeberin. Gegenstand des Verfahrens sind Forschungs- und Entwicklungsleistungen im Verbundvorhaben RealBat („Effizienterer Betrieb von Windenergieanlagen durch Echtzeitschutz für Fledermäuse“). Ziel des Vorhabens ist es, die bislang zum Schutz von Fledermäusen eingesetzten, weitgehend pauschalen Abschaltungen von Windenergieanlagen zu einem adaptiven Abschaltalgorithmus weiterzuentwickeln, der die Anlagen nur bei tatsächlich bestehendem Schlagrisiko abschaltet. Anders als bei der bisherigen Abschätzung der Fledermausaktivität allein aus meteorologischen und phänologischen Parametern wird dazu die akustisch erfasste Fledermausaktivität in Echtzeit als zusätzlicher Parameter herangezogen. Auf diese Weise lässt sich der Energieertrag der Anlagen bei mindestens gleichwertigem Fledermausschutz steigern. Die zu vergebenden Leistungen umfassen schwerpunktmäßig die Konzeption für Erfassung von Fledermäusen und Auswertung der akustischen und teilweise zusammenführend mit den optischen Daten sowie die Methodenentwicklung der Echtzeitabschaltung. Kern der Leistung ist die Integration der Echtzeitabschaltung als zusätzlicher Parameter in die in der Planungspraxis etablierte Software ProBat und die ihr zugrunde liegenden, in den RENEBAT-Vorhaben entwickelten statistischen Modelle sowie die Optimierung des Gesamtmodells aus Fledermausschutz und Energieertrag.

title: Germany – Highways engineering services – Planungsleistungen Verkehrsanlagen und Medienerschließung
description: Die Gemeinde Großpösna ist eine Gebietskörperschaft im Süden von Leipzig im Freistaat Sachsen. Die Gemeinde beabsichtigt die Erschließung eines Gebietes am Störmthaler See. Die Planungen sollen im 1. bis 3. Quartal 2027 erfolgen. Die Ausschreibung für die Herstellung der Medien sowie den Straßenbau ist für das 3. Quartal 2027 vorgesehen. Im Anschluss erfolgen die Auswertung der Angebote sowie die Beschlussfassung in den zuständigen Gemeindegremien. Ziel ist es, den Bauauftrag im Oktober 2027 zu vergeben und den Baubeginn im 4. Quartal 2027 vorzusehen. Die Planung und Herstellung der Parkplätze kann nachrangig zur Erschließung der Medien und zur Durchführung des allgemeinen Straßenbaus erfolgen. Die Planung des Strandabschnittes einschließlich der Freianlagenplanung bzw. landschaftspflegerischen Planung entlang der Erschließungsstraße und Parkplätze werden gesondert ausgeschrieben und sind nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. La Région Grand Est, motrice dans la transition écologique et la protection des populations face au changement climatique, porte le programme Life Adapt'Est. Ce projet vise, d'ici 2035, à accroître la résilience du Grand Est aux risques climatiques croissants (manque d'eau, vagues de chaleur, précipitations exceptionnelles…) dans des domaines tels que l'urbanisme, l'agriculture, la forêt, les bâtiments, les transports, les infrastructures, le massif vosgien, les lycées, l'eau, la santé… Il permettra de renforcer et de poursuivre la feuille de route régionale d'accélération de l'adaptation au changement climatique adoptée en 2023. Cette mission d'assistance à maîtrise d'ouvrage spécialisée en Urbanisme Favorable à la Santé, dans le cadre du programme Life Adapt'Est, avec le soutien (financier) de l'Union Européenne et de l'Agence Régionale de Santé Grand Est, a pour but d'accompagner 10 territoires sur 2 ans, soit 5 par an. Les territoires accompagnés seront sélectionnés par la Région Grand Est et concerneront des projets d'aménagement et de planification. Il est attendu dans le cadre de l'exécution des prestations, des propositions de stratégie de concertation, de diagnostic santé-environnement des territoires et de méthode d'accompagnement de maturation du projet par territoire afin d'intégrer aux projets les enjeux identifiés dans le diagnostic santé-environnement. Une approche multithématique et globale est attendue pour permettre au projet d'avoir une dimension architecturale et paysagère, urbaine et santé-environnementale. Les prestations pourront avoir lieu sur tout le territoire régional pour des projets portés par des communes et leurs intercommunalités, par des schémas de cohérence territoriale (SCoT), des Pays et des pôles d'équilibre territorial et rural (PETR). description: In 2023, the Government invited municipalities and county authorities to apply to participate in the Government’s pilot scheme for municipalities and county authorities. These pilot projects are based on the Act relating to Experiments in Public Administration of 26 June 1992 (the Experimental Administration Act), hereinafter referred to as the Experimental Administration Act. Further information about the framework of the scheme is available on the Ministry’s webpage dedicated to the pilot scheme. Duration and Budget Framework The pilot projects will, as a general rule, run for up to four years from their commencement. The evaluation assignment will cover the entire pilot period and will also include follow-up work in connection with the preparation of the final report. title: Supply, Installation and Operation of an Occupancy Sensor and Monitoring Solution
description:
The University of Portsmouth operates from a multi-building urban campus in the centre of Portsmouth, with a diverse estate comprising teaching spaces, laboratories, offices, research facilities, student services and social spaces.
The University does not currently have a systematic, data-driven understanding of how its buildings and rooms are used. Timetabling data tells us when spaces are scheduled, but not whether anyone is in them, or how many people are present compared to room capacity, and whilst we monitor attendance in certain sessions this relies on physical registration by identity card and reader resulting in a high degree of inaccuracy. This gap has two practical consequences:
• Energy waste: spaces are being heated, lit and ventilated regardless of whether they are occu-pied. Without occupancy data, the University cannot identify which spaces are consuming energy unnecessarily or target interventions effectively.
• Space planning based on assumptions: decisions about room allocation, timetabling, and future estate investment are made without reliable utilisation evidence. The University needs accurate, granular data to make better decisions about how its estate is used.
The University seeks to address both problems by deploying an occupancy sensor and monitoring solution across an initial set of campus buildings. The solution will provide real-time and historical data on room-level occupancy and headcount, accessible through a web-based reporting portal and integrated with the University's existing data analytics environment.

title: WP4051 ICS Pathway 1 Services and a Community Reablement Service
description:
"Reablement is a strengths-based, person-centred approach that promotes and maximises independence and wellbeing. It aims to ensure positive change using user-defined goals and is designed to enable people to gain, or regain, their confidence, ability, and necessary skills to live as independently as possible, especially after an illness, deterioration in health or injury. Reablement focuses on enabling people to do things for themselves rather than having things done for them.
Reablement will be achieved by working in partnership with individuals to support them to undertake tasks themselves, promoting choice, control, and functional ability rather than providing task-based care.
Reablement in the Borough will be aided by technology to deliver positive outcomes for each Service User, ensuring their support is effective, innovative, and tailored to their individual needs.
There are two types of Reablement Pathways.
1) ICS Pathway 1 Services
All Referrals to Pathway 1 Reablement service will be made by appropriate ICS staff. Individuals may be residing in acute hospitals, both inside and outside the borough, or in their own homes. (but only for the purposes of permitting the Referral of Adults who are ordinarily resident in the Borough).
Pathway 1 Reablement provides short-term, intensive, therapy-led support following hospital discharge or admission avoidance. Delivered through an integrated multidisciplinary approach, it focuses on helping people regain skills, achieve personal goals, and undertake daily activities independently wherever possible.
Pathway 1 Social provides short-term interim support for individuals who do not require Reablement, have reached their Reablement potential, or are awaiting longer-term care arrangements or other appropriate services. It ensures continuity of care while longer-term solutions are put in place, and service users may move between the Reablement and Social pathways as their needs change.
2) Community Reablement Pathway
Referrals into the Community Reablement Service will be made via the Council's customer experience centre/operational teams in Adult Social Care.
Community Reablement provides preventative, short-term support for people living in the community who are experiencing a decline in their functional ability. Delivered through a partnership between the Council's therapy team and the Provider, it aims to restore independence, improve wellbeing, and reduce the need for ongoing care and support.

title: Framework for the Provision of Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Infrastructure and Managed Services
description:
Preliminary Market Engagement Notice for the Framework Agreement for the Provision of Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Infrastructure and Managed Services to the University of Birmingham.   
Procurement description
The University of Birmingham ("the University") is procuring a Framework for the provision, installation, ongoing operation and support of a single, integrated EV charging infrastructure and managed service at the University of Birmingham.
The scope of the Framework shall include, but not be limited to: 
1.	The provision of the following services: 
•	Design, supply, installation, commissioning and ongoing operation of EV charging infrastructure across University car parks, covering staff, student and visitor charging
•	Migration and consolidation of the University’s existing EV charging network (40 connectors) across 33 charge points, plus a further 6 connectors in development, from its current single-operator arrangement
•	Proactive, automated fault monitoring and response, delivering a material improvement in network reliability against current service levels
•	Capture and management of University fleet vehicle charging data, which is not currently captured
•	Working in partnership with the University to deliver an ongoing Feasibility Study, identifying growth opportunities, and assessing further expansion sites, electrical capacity, and income-generation opportunities across the campus.
•	Supporting the resilience and future-proofing of the University’s charging network and its underlying operating model as demand for EV charging grows
•	Inclusion of our Edgbaston Park Hotel site, who’s EV charging requirement is an additional scope line
The University of Birmingham is seeking to award to a single contractor/operator who will provide all the services required from this Framework contract.  
 The University of Birmingham is seeking Expressions of Interest in the following operating models, and is open to alternative or hybrid models where a contractor/operator considers this would better serve the University’s objectives:
Model 1 – Revenue share / concession model
Infrastructure is funded, installed, operated and maintained by the contractor at its own cost.  The contractor retains the charging revenue, with an agreed share of income paid to the University.  May suit higher-footfall, commercially facing charging use cases, such as a proposed visitor-facing fast charging hub.
Model 2 – Host-owned managed service
Reflects the University’s current arrangement; may continue to suit the core, currently lower-utilisation campus network.
The University welcomes views from respondents on which of these models, or a hybrid combination applied by use case, they consider most viable and invites proposals for alternative commercial models not described above.  Responses to this notice will directly inform which commercial model(s) the University carries forward into the formal tender specification.
The terms of awarded contract shall be fixed and firm for a period of three (3) years commencing 1 January 2027 until 31 December 2029, with an option to extend one (1) period of one (1) year up to a maximum extension period until 31 December 2030.
Engagement
The University of Birmingham is inviting expressions of interest (EOI) from contractors/operators in relation to this upcoming tender opportunity.
Interested parties are required to provide the following as part of the EOI:
a.	Three (3) case studies demonstrating experience of delivering EV Charging infrastructure and managed services, ideally within the higher education or wider public sector
b.	Views on the operating models set out above, including a stated preference (if any) and rationale, or a proposal for an alternative or hybrid commercial model
c.	A high-level outline of how the respondent would approach delivering an ongoing Feasibility Study in partnership with the University
Following the initial EOI stage, the University intends to conduct contractor engagement in the formation gathering and shortlisting, following which a select number of contractors/operators will be invited to partake in the tender.
If you are interested in engaging with the University for this project, please register to our E-Tendering Portal (https://in-tendhost.co.uk/universityofbirmingham/aspx/Home) if you are not already, and express interest as directed. 
Note: the University of Birmingham is operating as a Non Contracting Authority and any process associated with this tender opportunity will be conducted outside of the Procurement Act 2023.

title: Bus Fleet Diesel and Electric Vehicles
description: In April 2023, Liverpool City Region Combined Authority (LCRCA) published an Assessment on Bus Franchising in the Liverpool City Region, which set out a proposed bus Franchising Scheme in accordance with the Transport Act 2000. In October 2023, the Liverpool City Region Mayor made the decision to introduce a Franchising Scheme covering the Liverpool City Region. Franchising is a legal model where buses are under the control of a public sector authority (LCRCA) who set the routes, frequency, fares and overall standard of buses in the region. The existing commercially led market will be replaced and private bus operators will no longer be able to run most services independently. Instead, bus services will be operated under franchise contracts and bus operators will bid to run the services through a competitive procurement process managed by the Combined Authority. LCRCA intend to introduce the second Tranche of franchised bus services from September 2027, covering Liverpool, Sefton and Knowsley. This follows the first Tranche of franchised bus services introduced in September 2026 covering St Helens and the Wirral. For Category 1 franchise contracts, LCRCA will provide the successful operator with a fleet of vehicles which the operator will then operate, manage and maintain the fleet throughout the franchise term. In preparation for the commencement of the Tranche 2 bus franchising programme in September 2027, LCRCA wish to procure a fleet of new vehicles including diesel and electric vehicles. A number of double-decker, single-decker and midi-sized buses are required to be delivered in May 2027 ahead of the commencement date of franchised services.

title: RFI: Digital Technologies for Contact Tracing, Infection Surveillance & Response
description:
The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is seeking to understand the market's ability to deliver digital technologies that support public health intervention activities such as, but not limited to, surveillance, infection identification, the management of cases, contacts and exposures during a health emergency. 
The objective of this Request for Information (RFI) is to inform future preparedness planning and ensure the UK has access to scalable, effective and deployable digital capabilities that can help reduce transmission, improve situational awareness and support public health interventions during a pandemic or other infectious disease emergency.
The key dates for this RFI are as follows:
RFI Published: 18th September 2026
RFI Response Deadline: 2nd October 2026
Specifically, UKHSA wishes to:
I. Understand the current and emerging marketplace for digital technologies that could be deployed during a future pandemic or infectious disease incident to support the prevention, identification, monitoring and management of infection 
transmission among the population, across a range of pathogens and settings.
II. Understand the intended purpose, use cases and operational objectives of technologies currently available or under development, including solutions not specifically designed for pandemic response but which may have utility in 
supporting infection control measures, population monitoring, exposure identification or public communications during a health emergency.
III. Assess the effectiveness, maturity and performance characteristics of different intervention, surveillance and outbreak-management technologies, including evidence of impact, operational limitations and suitability for deployment across 
diverse settings such as communities, healthcare facilities, care homes, schools and other educational establishments, custodial environments, travel and transportation hubs, and workplaces.
IV. Understand the costs associated with the implementation, operation and maintenance of technologies across different deployment scenarios, including infrastructure, licensing, support, integration and user adoption requirements, to inform assessments of affordability and value for money.
V. Understand suppliers' manufacturing, delivery and operational capacity (inclusive of lead times), including their ability to rapidly scale deployment during a national emergency, and identify key dependencies, risks, constraints and mitigation approaches that may affect resilience of supply.
VI. Assess industry capability to develop, adapt or configure bespoke digital solutions that support activities such as case management, contact tracing, exposure notification, outbreak investigation, provision of personalised advice, 
and wider population engagement, including the ability to provide interoperable data flows into UKHSA systems in near real time while meeting relevant legal, data protection, security and governance requirements.
VII. Refine UKHSA's understanding of requirements by identifying innovative approaches, emerging technologies and alternative delivery models that may improve public health outcomes, operational effectiveness, user experience and scalability for Pandemic and other large scale public health incidents.
VIII. Inform UKHSA's future commercial strategy and route-to-market approach, ensuring procurement requirements are proportionate, deliver value for money, maximise competition and innovation, and support the acquisition of capabilities that are fit for purpose during health emergencies.

title: 715864481 - Preliminary Market Engagement RFI Debrief – LIOS IROC/OP&S
description:
The Authority recently carried out a Pre Market Engagement (PME) exercise in support of the Integrated Readiness Output Contract (IROC) and Other Platforms and Services (OP&S) elements of the wider Land Integrated Operating Services (LIOS) programme. The Authority can now update industry partners on common themes within the PME responses received and key updates. 
LIOS is a once in a generation opportunity to begin the transformation of Land vehicle support from 2026, with a full LIOS enterprise in place from 2030) and, in doing so, bring MOD and Industry closer to delivering Defence’s intent in accordance with the Land Industrial Strategy. The vision for LIOS is to deliver long-term, output-focussed equipment support solutions that proactively and intelligently manage in-scope capabilities through-life in accordance with capability management plans. LIOS will deliver sustainable enterprise efficiencies to optimise support and capabilities through-life, combining upkeep, update, and upgrade services.
IROC, including but not limited to provision of the services currently delivered via the extant Service Provision and Transformation Contract (SPTC), covers a wide range of in-service land equipment and is intended to be a pan Integrated Operating Service (IOS) service provider incentivised to reduce duplication of work, maximise pan-Defence Lines of Development (DLOD) non-Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) efficiencies and leverage economies of scale. OP&S including but not limited to provision of post-design services (PDS) via contracts such as PMETS and other support services for in-scope platforms not included within platform IOS contracts from April 2030 and will provide IOS support for those platforms that continue beyond 2030 but do not have a planned programme of Upgrades and Update. IROC and OP&S are initially being managed as one over-arching programme until the procurement strategy is matured however there may be two or more procurements. The role and full scope of the services will be developed and matured prior to formal procurement activity commencing.
Estimated contract dates (start and finish) – 01/04/2030 to 31/03/2045 with possible option years
Estimated value - £3-7bn inc applicable VAT

title: CEFAS26-120 Statutory shellfish E.coli monitoring service for Shetland and Orkney
description:
Purpose of this engagement:
Cefas is undertaking market engagement to inform a future procurement for delivery of statutory microbiological monitoring services on behalf of Food Standards Scotland (FSS). This notice is not a call for competition or a commitment to procure. Its purpose is to help potential suppliers understand the anticipated requirement, test the deliverability of the proposed service model and provide an opportunity to raise technical, logistical, commercial and implementation questions before any formal procurement is launched.
Background:
FSS operates an official control programme to monitor faecal contamination in live bivalve molluscs and support the classification of shellfish harvesting areas, for which Cefas coordinates aspects of programme delivery. The anticipated contract will principally cover existing classified production areas and new areas seeking classification in Shetland and Orkney. Current planning assumptions indicate approximately 52 shellfish samples per month, or 624 per year, but volumes and locations may change in response to regulatory requirements, classification decisions, incidents, seasonal activity or changes in the monitoring plan. The geographical scope of the work may be expanded to other Scottish areas.
Market feedback sought:
Cefas will hold two online market-engagement sessions for potential applicants. During each session, Cefas will provide an overview of the service, including the logistics, sample-management, analytical and reporting requirements, and will respond to comments and questions raised by suppliers. The sessions are intended to help suppliers understand the proposed requirement and identify any practical issues, risks or points requiring clarification before a formal procurement is launched. The sessions will also provide Cefas with an opportunity to review any potential changes required to the scope of the work or intended contractual details.
The sessions will take place on 15/10/26 at 15:00 and 19/10/26 at 10:00 via MS Teams. Interested organisations should register on Eventbrite at https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/cefas-market-engagement-statutory-shellfish-ecoli-monitoring-service-tickets-2002621752571 no later than 2 days prior to the events.
Organisations may submit questions in advance to procure@cefas.gov.uk
Participation in either session will not confer any advantage in a subsequent procurement, and non-participation will not prevent an organisation from taking part in any future competition. A summary of the questions and responses will be made available as part of the procurement process.
Details of service required:
The requirement is for an integrated end-to-end service including laboratory analysis, as well as coordinating the logistics needed to move samples from remote island locations to its laboratory in a condition and timeframe suitable for official control testing. Sample collection itself will be undertaken under separate arrangements, but the supplier must work closely with sampling contractors and any FSS-approved industry collectors.
• Logistics and sample management: establish reliable delivery arrangements from Shetland and Orkney; pay transport costs; provide and replenish approved packing and transport equipment; coordinate with sample collectors; monitor weekly schedules; support correct packaging and documentation; receive samples Monday to Friday, including early or late deliveries where necessary; and maintain contingency arrangements for disruption. Samples must reach the laboratory in time for analysis to begin within 48 hours of collection and sample temperature must remain within 1-10°C before start of analysis.
• Laboratory analysis: receive, identify, assess and log samples; check submission information and resolve discrepancies; reject unsuitable samples in accordance with agreed criteria; analyse all programme samples using one approved UK National Reference Laboratory method for enumeration of Escherichia coli in bivalve molluscan shellfish—either the 5-tube, 4-dilution MPN method derived from ISO 16649-3 or the colony count method based on ISO 16649-2; and meet the required turnaround times.
• Reporting and coordination: upload results, rejections and associated information to the FSS Shellfish Monitoring & Classification system (Shellfish Monitoring and Classification Scotland - Dashboard using agreed templates; support urgent follow-up and resampling; provide monthly and quarterly performance information; maintain records and audit trails; and work with Cefas, FSS and sample collectors to resolve operational issues and improve delivery.
Indicative supplier requirements:
• Designation, or the ability to obtain designation during mobilisation, as an official laboratory by FSS.
• ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for the relevant shellfish matrix and selected analytical method, maintained throughout delivery, with satisfactory method validation, quality assurance and proficiency-testing performance.

title: Centralised Civil Service Learning and Training Services
description:
On 20 January 2026, the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister announced that a new National School of Government and Public Services (the "National School") would be established.
The National School, led by the Cabinet Office, will drive a new approach to delivering skills across the Civil Service and will be responsible for training across the Civil Service, providing high quality learning and development, including in priorities such as digital and artificial intelligence, leadership and management.
The Minister for the Cabinet Office (the "Authority") has decided to accelerate the transition to the National School in order to realise the benefits that it will bring, and improve overall value for money sooner than originally anticipated.
Contracts for the provision of centralised Civil Service learning and training services are to be awarded to each of KPMG LLP and Ernst & Young LLP to cover this transition period to the National School. Both suppliers have existing contracts for the same services in place with the Authority, which are due to expire in January 2027 and the intention is that these contracts will replace those existing contracts and will enable and facilitate a faster transition to the National School.
The contract values stated in this notice are estimates of the maximum value of each contract. However; no guarantees are given by the Authority in relation to the volume or value of the services that will be instructed under the contracts.
The contracts will be awarded by the Authority, however the services can be used by any of the bodies identified below (and their successors), and the contracts will be entered into for the benefit of the Authority and for the benefit of all such bodies that use the services from time to time:
- All Ministerial Government Departments;
- Non Ministerial Government Departments;
- Executive Agencies of government and other subsidiary bodies;
- Civil service bodies;
- All non-Crown Status Government Companies wholly or partly owned by Central Government Departments and their subsidiaries;
- The non-Departmental Public Bodies, other Public Bodies, Public Corporations and their subsidiary bodies sponsored by Central Government Departments which are not covered by the above categories;
- All new bodies created which fall within the criteria set out above;
- Those listed and maintained by the Office of National Statistics (ONS) as being part of Central Government at: https://www.ons.gov.uk/methodology/classificationsandstandards/economicstatisticsclassifications/introductiontoeconomicstatisticsclassifications or any replacement or updated web-link.
Direct Award Justification (as set out in the Transparency Notice published on 14 July 2026):
The contracts that are to be awarded to each of Ernst & Young LLP and KPMG LLP fall within the grounds for a direct award under paragraph 7 (Additional or repeat goods, services or works) of Schedule 5 to the Procurement Act 2023 as they concern the supply of services by existing suppliers which are intended as an extension to, or partial replacement of, existing services in circumstances where:
(a) a change in supplier would result in the Authority receiving services that are different from, or incompatible with, the existing services; and
(b) the difference or incompatibility would result in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation or maintenance.
The Authority's view is that making a change in supplier at the current time would mean that the services were different and/or incompatible with the existing learning and training services and associated systems provided by the existing suppliers, and this would result in disproportionate technical difficulties for the Authority (and the wider Civil Service) in the operation and/or maintenance of those services and systems, including having regard to the limited duration of the transition period to the National School, as outlined above.
The specific difficulties that the Authority would encounter in changing supplier at this point are: 1) the complexity of implementing and embedding cross-government managed learning service systems would prevent new providers from being able to deliver the services required within the required timeframe; 2) the Civil Service would be subjected to significant operational disruption from changing suppliers while simultaneously trying to build and then implement the new model needed for the National School; and 3) by continuing the existing service, the Authority is able to focus resources on realising the benefits of the National School sooner, reducing reliance on external spending and thereby providing better value for the taxpayer.
In addition, and in the alternative, the contracts that are to be awarded to each of KPMG LLP and Ernst & Young LLP fall within the grounds for a direct award under paragraph 6 (Single suppliers) of Schedule 5 to the Procurement Act 2023 because:
(a) due to an absence of competition for technical reasons, only a particular supplier can supply the services required; and
(b) there are no reasonable alternatives to those services.
The Authority's view is that no alternative provider could take over the provision of the relevant learning and development services from the point that these services are required following expiry of the existing contracts, as there is insufficient time for transition to another provider to take place. This absence of competition is due to the technical reasons outlined above and is not the result of an artificial narrowing down of the parameters of the procurement.

title: Harnessing geological diversity for species recovery, ecological connectivity, and climate resilience
description:
This pilot project will improve recovery prospects for species with tightly defined geologies by identifying where they can persist or expand under climate change. It will seek to enhance Natural England's climate suitability maps with geological data to identify future strongholds and connectivity corridors. For identified species, ecological and geological knowledge will be collated; and it is anticipated that for a subset, field surveys will document fine-scale site conditions (e.g. slope, hydrology, soils, geological facies).
Species-level reports will provide practical advice to site managers and support local, and wider scale regional and national survival planning. By integrating predictive mapping with ecological insight, the project informs targeted management and landscape-scale planning. It focuses on features we can manage (habitat, land use, and connectivity), recognising that fixed geology may both constrain and guide species' climate-driven range shifts.

title: MGN288 - Review of Supply Chain & Stores
description:
Magna is seeking an experienced consultancy partner to undertake an independent review of the supply chain, stores and warehouse operations that support the organisation. Whilst the primary focus will be on the procurement, storage and distribution of materials supporting Response Repairs, the review should also consider opportunities to improve stock management, demand planning and inventory processes across all services that utilise stores and materials. 
The review is intended to provide a comprehensive understanding of current demand, product flows, stock management practices, procurement arrangements and warehouse operations. It should assess how effectively materials are planned, purchased, stored, managed and distributed, while testing a number of existing hypotheses relating to inventory accuracy, purchasing practices, stock holding levels, material availability and operational efficiency. 
The review should also examine the quality and use of data, reporting and forecasting capabilities, together with the communication and collaboration between teams involved in planning, ordering, managing and consuming stock. The objective is to identify opportunities to improve visibility, decision-making, demand forecasting, process efficiency, working capital utilisation and organisational alignment. 
The outcome should be a fact-based assessment of the current operation, together with practical recommendations to improve efficiency, reduce waste, optimise stock holding, enhance service delivery and provide greater value for money. 
Magna would prefer to engage a consultancy partner with experience of reviewing Response Repairs, Asset Management and Housing Maintenance services within a social housing environment. Suppliers should be able to demonstrate expertise in analysing repairs supply chains, stores operations, inventory management, materials planning and demand forecasting, together with an understanding of the operational challenges and opportunities within the sector.

title: SEL ICB (Bexley) Health & Wellbeing Coaching and Community Health & Wellbeing Workers (CHWWs) with Social Prescribing Service Specification
description:
The notice relates to SEL ICB (Bexley) Health & Wellbeing Coaching and Community Health & Wellbeing Workers (CHWWs) with Social Prescribing Service Specification services. The service is an existing service and will be provided by an existing provider.
The process being followed is a Most Suitable Provider Process under the Provider Selection Regime 2023 under the Most Suitable Provider (MSP) process (The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 10).
This service is for those who live in the London Borough of Bexley or are registered with a Bexley GP practice.
Following the publication of the NHS 10 Year Plan, Bexley Place is driving forward with establishing a Neighbourhood Health Service in each of its three neighbourhoods. A fundamental component of a neighbourhood health service is to support residents with the wider determinants of health which have an impact on how they are able to manage their long-term conditions.
The population in Bexley is diverse, both culturally and economically. The borough is split into 3 Neighbourhoods, these are:
• Frognal (Sidcup & Bexley)
• Clocktower (Bexleyheath & Welling)
• North Bexley (Erith, Thamesmead & Abbey Wood)
There are approximately 26,000 people living in Bexley who have 3 or more long term conditions. North Bexley is the most culturally and economically diverse part of the borough, with 15,995 residents living in the lowest 20% deprivation decile - this is 15% of the North Bexley population. In the other parts of the borough, the number of residents living in the lowest 20% deprivation decile is 2,774, which is 2% of that population. People living in the most deprived 20% of Bexley have a shorter life expectancy than those living in the least deprived 20%. For females, the gap is 2.2 years, and for males the gap is 5.2 years.
Bexley Place seeks an established provider of voluntary services based in the London Borough of Bexley, with a proven track record in currently delivering social prescribing and peer support services. The provider must be an existing key partner of the integrated neighbourhood teams' development in the London Borough of Bexley.
The provider must be able to mobilise within 3 months of the contract award.
The provider will be expected to work closely with SEL Integrated Care Board (Bexley Place) to mobilise, deliver and evaluate the service model. The Commissioner may request that the provider modifies the delivery of the service if the findings from the evaluation or resident feedback gives just reason.
The commissioner is seeking to achieve, via this procurement, a service and provider that is committed to supporting the development of neighbourhood models of healthcare.
The 10-Year Health Plan mandates neighbourhood models of healthcare and these are currently being developed across England. In Bexley, by 2026, the borough will have in place three neighbourhoods each with a new integrated neighbourhood team.
buyer: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board

title: Department for Transport Shared Research, Evaluation and Analysis
description:
Invitation to tender documnets can be accessed at the following link- https://dft.app.jaggaer.com/go/7987765301A0F7302D0B
Suppliers not already registered on the Department for Transport's e-sourcing portal Jaggaer here- dft.app.jaggaer.com
The Department for Transport (DfT) is procuring a shared research, evaluation and analysis call-off contract to provide flexible access to timely, high-quality research, monitoring, evaluation, economic analysis and related analytical support across a range of transport policy areas. The proposed contract is expected to support analytical requirements across four divisions, which cover a broad range of transport policy areas:  
Accessible and inclusive transport (particular focus on those with physical and mental health conditions and/or groups with different protected characteristics) 
Active travel (cycling, wheeling and walking) 
Buses, planning and housing 
Devolution of responsibility for transport in England, including devolution deals, place-based policy, and strategy for integrated transport 
Local highways maintenance 
Local Authority capability and capacity 
Passenger transport (light rail, taxis, private hire vehicles, community transport) 
Road Freight (including: roadworthiness and vehicle regulation; international freight; HGV driver skills, hours and working conditions; traffic commissioners and operator licencing) 
Multimodal Freight (including: modal shift; freight innovation funding; work to improve connectivity of data and insights across the freight network) 
Dangerous Goods 
Future Borders (including policies to improve traffic management in Kent) 
Borders Resilience and Response (managing disruption at borders and along the strategic road network) 
Road safety (including supporting road users, safer vehicles, post collision care, safer infrastructure, and enforcement) 
Motoring Agencies (DVSA, DVLA and VCA – including MOT and driver licensing) 
International Vehicle Standards 
Connected and Autonomous vehicles 
AI, data, and other emerging transport technologies 
Vehicle Infrastructure (e.g. charging) 
Strategic Roads (Strategic Road Network managed by National Highways) 
Traffic and Technology (including traffic management, parking, street works etc.) 
Micro-mobility, such as e-scooters, and other forms of transport innovation (e.g. pavement robots) 
Lower Thames Crossing  
These divisions are home to more than 80 analysts with expertise in social research, evaluation, behavioural science, economics, operational research, statistics, and transport modelling; any of whom could commission work through the contract during its lifetime.  
The proposed contract would replace and expand the remit of an existing call-off contract that commenced in March 2023. 
The  requirement is for a call-off contract under which up to three suppliers may be appointed and individual commissions would be agreed as requirements arise. The maximum budget is £7,500,000 excluding VAT, if three Suppliers are appointed, this will result in 3x contracts of equal £2,500,000 value. The proposed contract term is  4 years. Commissions agreed before the contract end date may continue, provided each commission is completed within seven years of its start date. 
The proposed contract will cover a broad range of research, evaluation, economic analysis and related analytical services. This may include, but is not limited to: evidence reviews and synthesis; qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods primary research; secondary analysis of existing datasets; advanced quantitative analysis, modelling and forecasting; behavioural, user-centred and accessibility-focused research; monitoring and evaluation, including process, impact, outcome and value for money evaluation; cost-benefit analysis, economic appraisal and economic evaluation; and analytical quality assurance. 
Suppliers would be expected to demonstrate broad analytical capability and be able to design, deliver, peer review, quality assure and clearly communicate high-quality, policy-relevant analysis in line with relevant government guidance, including the Magenta Book, Green Book and AQuA Book. Across all work, suppliers will be expected to apply proportionate methods, document assumptions and limitations clearly, and translate findings into practical recommendations for policy, operational or funding decisions. 
Suppliers would be expected to provide sufficient technical expertise, capacity, resilience and project management capability to deliver multiple commissions concurrently, including short-term, medium-term and longer-term projects of varying complexity. Suppliers may deliver requirements through their own organisation, consortium arrangements, named subcontractors or other approved delivery partners. Due to the broad nature of the proposed requirements, the Department encourages suppliers to consider whether consortium, subcontracting or other partnership arrangements would help them provide the necessary breadth of expertise, capacity and resilience. Any such arrangements should include clear lines of responsibility, with the lead supplier retaining appropriate oversight and accountability for quality, timeliness, confidentiality, continuity and management of all work delivered under the contract. 
Outputs from the contract would be used to inform policy and operational decisions and to build the evidence base across a range of transport policy areas. Outputs may include, depending on the individual commission, reports, slide packs, spreadsheets, datasets, analytical code, models, evidence logs, technical annexes and other supporting materials. The DfT expects outputs to be robust, proportionate, clearly communicated, appropriately documented, quality assured and suitable for policy, analytical and, where relevant, public audiences.  Individual commissions will have tailored milestones, deliverables and outputs.

title: High Intensity User (HIU) Programme - Outcomes Partnership (Market Engagement)
description:
NHS North East London Integrated Care Board (NEL ICB) is exploring the market ahead of seeking to commission an ICB-wide High Intensity User (HIU) Outcomes Partnership.
The provider must have proven experience in delivering preventative health Social Outcomes Partnerships, be willing to undertake co-design with NEL ICB at risk, and have access to at least £1.0m of approved social investment risk capital available for drawdown upon contract award.
Health and care systems face a growing, structural challenge: a small number of people experiencing the deepest deprivation and complexity account for a disproportionate share of urgent and emergency care demand. This is not a marginal issue; it is a material driver of pressure, cost and inequality across the NHS. High Intensity Use is predictable, persistent, and concentrated. It is driven by unmet social need, trauma, poor access to community-based support and fragmented systems. Left unaddressed, it results in repeated crisis presentations, poor outcomes for individuals and escalating system cost.
High Intensity Use of urgent and emergency care represents a significant and growing challenge across UK health systems. National evaluation evidence shows that fewer than one per cent of people account for approximately:
• 16% of A&E attendances.
• 29% of ambulance arrivals.
• 26% of emergency admissions.
This activity is estimated to cost the NHS at least £2.5 billion per year.
Individuals with repeated attendances are highly likely to continue using emergency care unless targeted intervention occurs. By a person's eighth emergency attendance within a year, there is a greater than 50% likelihood that they will continue to attend frequently for at least two years, rising to over 80% by the fifteenth attendance. This creates a clearly identifiable cohort for targeted preventative intervention.
There are proven delivery models addressing these challenges, with a track record of reducing secondary care usage for high intensity users. However, despite the potential to improve outcomes for these individuals and reduce demand on the system, funding for these interventions has traditionally been both small compared to the need, and short-term. An outcomes approach offers a potential solution to this.
Outcomes partnerships are services where 100% of the funding is linked to evidenced outcomes achieved by individuals on the Programme.
They add value in issue areas which require a change in policy focus (i.e., from sickness to prevention) through creating an environment to test ideas, build and develop new services, or continue to improve existing ones.
The work is proposed to consist of two phases:
1. A Co-design phase working with NEL to develop the delivery model and outcomes framework, and;
2. the delivery of the intervention.
The co-design phase will include analysis of existing services, gaps in provisions, and local priorities to identify the target cohort, geography, and total contract value for the service. This would be followed by co-design of the delivery model, facilitating input from all key stakeholders (including Hospital MDT leads and patients), and joint development of an outcomes framework.
A key feature of an outcomes partnership is the flexibility of the delivery model, which can be improved over time as the Programme learns what works. The typical duration of support is expected to be between 9 to 12 weeks, but this will vary depending on the cohort to ensure sustained improvement and positive health outcomes.
The outcomes the service would be targeting include:
• Improved wellbeing and patient activation.
• Improvement in wider social determinants of health including housing, financial situation, and loneliness.
• Reduce use of secondary care services including; A&E attendances, Emergency admissions, and Ambulance conveyances.

The role of a national clinical audit is to stimulate healthcare quality improvement through the provision of high-quality information on the organisation, delivery and outcomes of healthcare, together with tools and support to enable healthcare providers and other audiences to make best use of this information. Outcomes are benchmarked against available national guidance and standards e.g. quality standards from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), and those from other established professional and patient sources. Successful national audits are those where the individuals who are engaging with and using the audit results are also in a position to improve the system, and where there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like.
National clinical audits are expected to:
a.Develop a robust, high-quality audit designed around key quality metrics likely to best support local and national healthcare quality improvement.
b.Detect, describe and help reduce unwarranted clinical variation by systematically benchmarking performance, identifying outliers, and supporting services to understand variation in outcomes, processes and experience.
c.Achieve, articulate and maintain close alignment with relevant NICE national guidance and quality standards throughout the audit, as appropriate.
d.Enable healthcare quality improvement through the provision of timely, high-quality data that compares providers of healthcare, and comprises an integrated mixture of named Trust or Health board, Integrated Care System (ICS), commissioner, multidisciplinary team (MDT), possibly consultant or clinical team level and other levels of reporting.
e.Engage patients, carers and the public in a meaningful way, achieving a strong patient voice which informs and contributes to the design, functioning, outputs and direction of the audit.
f.Consider the value and feasibility of linking data at an individual patient level to other relevant national datasets either from the outset or in the future and plan for these linkages from the inception of the contract.
g.Ensure robust methodological and statistical input at all stages of the audit.
h.Identify from the outset the full range of audiences for the reports and other audit outputs and plan and tailor them accordingly.
i.Provide audit results in a timely, accessible and meaningful manner to support healthcare quality improvement, minimising the reporting delay and providing continual access to each unit for their own data.
j.Utilise strong and effective project and programme management to deliver audit outputs on time and within budget.
k.Develop and maintain strong engagement with local clinicians, networks, commissioners, patients and their families and carers and charity and community support groups to drive improvements in services.
l.Deliver high-quality audit outputs, benchmarking and quality improvement as a priority. 
At the time of writing the specification, requirements include (but please also refer to the potential future aspirational intent section):
1. Audit Purpose
The overall ambition of the audit is to continue to capture and report data on the performance of individual healthcare providers against the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Quality Standard QS33: Rheumatoid Arthritis in Adults, Quality standard QS214: Rare diseases, and other relevant national standards and guidance, (see Appendix 1).
2. Paediatric Inflammatory Arthritis Pathway
The supplier should work with the wider Dataset and Methodology Stakeholder Group to develop, maintain and report against a minimum viable paediatric inflammatory arthritis pathway. 
The initial focus should be on establishing a clinically meaningful dataset and reporting framework sufficient to describe the patient pathway and support audit activity.
Initial measures should focus on a limited number of priority areas agreed with funders and stakeholders, for example referral, diagnosis and treatment timelines.
The updated GIRFT Paediatric Inflammatory Arthritis Pathway guidance, anticipated for publication in January 2027, should be considered a key reference for the future development of the dataset, measures and reporting framework. The supplier should work with the wider Dataset and Methodology Stakeholder Group to review and align the dataset, metrics and reporting outputs with the recommendations and standards set out within the GIRFT guidance, ensuring ongoing relevance and consistency with national best practice.
Any expansion beyond the core pathway, including additional metrics, PROMs/PREMs, transition measures and broader pathway development, should be considered future aspirational intent subject to feasibility, resources and further funding.
3. Data Collection and Audit Design
The supplier should continue to deliver a continuous prospective clinical audit and work with the Dataset and Methodology Group to ensure the audit dataset remains clinically relevant and proportionate.
The supplier is expected to collaborate with specialist disease-specific clinical groups to support interpretation of findings and improve case ascertainment and recruitment rates.
4. Organisational Survey and Quality Improvement
The supplier should review and maintain the organisational survey to ensure it remains proportionate and aligned with audit objectives. Priority should be given to maximising analysis and utilisation of existing data rather than increasing data collection burden in collaboration with the wider Dataset and Methodology Stakeholder Group.
The organisational survey should support the audit's quality improvement objectives by enabling a deeper understanding of service delivery, workforce capacity, variation in practice and barriers to high-quality care.
5. Benchmarking and Improvement
The audit is expected to support continuous improvement across all services.
While identifying high-performing and outlier services remains important, the audit should also support improvement among services performing at or around the national average, where the greatest overall gains may be achieved.
Benchmarking should encourage year-on-year improvement within individual services and provide meaningful insights that motivate all providers to improve, regardless of their current position relative to national performance.
6. Targeted improvement support
The supplier should provide targeted quality improvement support following each annual audit cycle. Activities should build on existing professional networks, collaboratives and stakeholder infrastructure wherever possible rather than creating wholly new arrangements.
Improvement support should be designed to benefit healthcare providers across the performance spectrum, including those performing at a middle level where the greatest overall gains may be achieved, while also supporting services experiencing significant challenges or demonstrating exceptional practice.
Learning generated through quality improvement activities should be shared with all participating healthcare providers to maximise the impact of the audit programme.
The anticipated outputs are:
1.Near real-time dynamic and interactive metric results.
2.Publication of an annual state of the nation report with the inclusion of an organisational survey.
3.Incorporation of validated Patient Reported Outcome Measures.
4.Quality improvement resources. 
5.The identification and notification of outliers.
For further information on the current audit, currently delivered by the British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) please head to: https://www.rheumatology.org.uk/improving-care/audits/neiaa

title: Security Services
description:
Northern Trains Limited (NTL) and TransPennine Express (TPE) intends to go to market for the procurement of Security Services across their respective estates. 
The proposed procurement seeks to procure a single supplier to deliver an integrated rail security service across the NTL and TPE networks, combining Travel Safe Officer (TSO), Station Security and Counter Terrorism Patrol (CTP) services. The overarching objective is to enhance the safety and security of customers and colleagues, reduce crime and anti-social behaviour, support compliance with railway and government security requirements, and provide a visible, customer focused security presence across stations and onboard services. 
The successful supplier will deliver a comprehensive security solution across a portfolio of managed stations and operational locations, providing proactive patrols, incident response, enforcement of Railway Byelaws, safeguarding support, and intelligence led security activity. The service will include dedicated Travel Safe Officers undertaking both station and train patrols, alongside specialist Counter Terrorism Patrol resources focused on protective security measures, threat deterrence and compliance with rail security obligations. 
A key requirement of the contract will be the ability to provide a flexible and responsive service model that can adapt to changing operational priorities across both operators. The supplier will be expected to support emerging security concerns, targeted interventions, seasonal demand changes, major incidents, rail disruption, special events and ad hoc operational requirements. 
In addition to frontline delivery, the supplier will provide all associated management, supervision, training, vehicles, uniforms, equipment, body-worn video, reporting systems and operational support required to deliver the service. The supplier will work collaboratively with NTL, TPE, the British Transport Police and other stakeholders to develop deployment plans and ensure security activities remain aligned to evolving risks and business needs throughout the contract term. 
Performance will be managed through a suite of key performance indicators covering operational delivery, resource availability, patrol completion, incident management, compliance, customer service and reporting. A strong emphasis will be placed on partnership working, continuous improvement, data-driven decision making and the ability to proactively identify and respond to emerging risks and opportunities for service enhancement. 
The procurement aims to establish a security partnership that delivers a safe, secure and welcoming environment for customers and colleagues while supporting the wider safety, security and customer experience objectives of both NTL and TPE.

title: UKSAC26_0043 EO Data Hub Service Delivery
description:
UKSA intends to run a competitive procurement to secure a supplier/consortium  to lead on the delivery and operation of the Earth Observation Data Hub (EODH) from April 2027 – March 2030. EODH provides a national gateway and platform for Earth Observation (EO) and model datasets. It enables users to access UK and global commercial and research satellite data, processing workflows, and applications for analysing surface temperature and land-use change. Through a single point of access (https://eodatahub.org.uk), the EO Data Hub integrates commercial and open EO datasets, allowing users to search, visualise, analyse, and process data at scale. The EODH is an operational national capability, currently delivered through UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and the National Centre for Earth Observation (NCEO).
The current delivery model will continue until March 2027 and will include a technical handover phase with the new delivery supplier throughout January – March 2027.
Whilst final decisions on the exact scope are yet to be made our current primary aim of the competition will be to  outsource operational delivery of the EODH to both EO and non-EO users subject to relevent internal approvals. The competition would  invite suppliers to demonstrate capability, user reach and a vision to grow the activity. An important aspect will be to maximise the re-use of existing intellectual property and minimise any disruption to current users. The expectations will include further development of the established EODH service – broadening the user base, expanding data availability, and improving overall service functionality. The chosen supplier  will also be responsible for managing a seamless transition period and  uninterrupted service continuity.
UPDATE 01/10/2026
NEXT STEPS FOR EARTH OBSERVATION DATA HUB PROCUREMENT
Thank you to everyone who participated in our EODH market engagement and responded to the RFI. Your feedback has helped shape the next stage of this important national capability.
We are pleased to confirm that a competitive procurement for the next phase of EODH will take place. The competition will operate through UKRI-STFC Procurement and will be run by CEDA (NCEO) at RAL Space, working closely with UKSA, rather than directly by UKSA through RM6235 as previously envisaged.
In accordance with UK Government policy, elements of EODH delivery have been identified as well suited to an insourced approach within Government. Details on these elements will be elaborated in future communications, but the majority of EODH activities are still expected to be delivered by competitively procured suppliers.
This approach provides a strong foundation for EODH’s future. It supports continuity for users, builds on the operational and technical knowledge of the existing service, provides greater flexibility to develop a sustainable operating model, and retains a substantial role for industry in operating, supporting and developing the Hub through to 2030.
UKSA and CEDA (NCEO) will provide a further coordinated update shortly, setting out the procurement process, timetable and how interested organisations can participate. For planning purposes and without commitment, we anticipate an ITT being issued in autumn 2026.
