title: Evaluation of the Quality & Engagement Act
description:
The Welsh Government intends to procure a contract for an independent evaluation of the implementation and impact of the Health and Social Care (Quality and Engagement) (Wales) Act 2020. 
The evaluation will build on findings from a completed evaluability assessment  and is expected to adopt a theory-based approach, assessing both the individual duties established by the Act and their collective contribution to the Act's overarching objectives. 
https://www.gov.wales/evaluability-assessment-health-and-social-care-quality-and-engagement-wales-act-2020 
The current intention is to procure the contract in 2026/2027 to commence the contract during the 2027/28 financial year. 
Estimated total contract value: up to £275,000 GBP (excluding VAT)
Contract duration: 24 months (with up to 3 months extension for final outputs with no additional budget available). 
Structure of contract:
The Welsh Government is considering a variety of models whereby: 
•	The requirement is either tendered as one whole contract or divided into five lotted work packages (Work Packages 0-4).  
•	Work Package 0 will be responsible for providing overall programme integration, coordination and synthesis across all work packages. 
•	Work Packages 1 to 4 will be the evaluation strands. 
•	At this stage we are considering whether suppliers are interested in bidding for  one individual work package as an expert on a specific topic, multiple work packages or all work packages as a lead supplier co-ordinating the whole contract. 
•	Where multiple suppliers are appointed they will be required to operate within a shared theory-based evaluation framework. 
•	Effective collaboration and data sharing between suppliers will be a contractual requirement to support programme-wide synthesis, learning and reporting. 
•	The approaches being considered reflect the recommendations made through the evaluability assessment, which identified the benefits of a single overarching evaluation delivered through distinct but connected evaluation strands. Welsh Government reserves the right to select the most appropriate model based on the feedback received through this Pre-market Engagement Notice. 
Proposed work packages
Work package 0: Evaluation integration, coordination and synthesis
The Evaluation Integration Lead and would be responsible for:
•	Overall evaluation leadership and coordination
•	Maintaining the Act-level Theory of Change
•	Developing and maintaining a shared evaluation framework and common methodological approach
•	Leading contribution analysis across the evaluation and
•	Producing interim and final synthesis reports.
Indicative budget: GBP 45,000
Work package 1: Duty of Quality
Evaluation of the implementation and impact of the Duty of Quality.
Indicative budget: GBP 70,000
Work package 2: Duty of Candour
Evaluation of the implementation and impact of the Duty of Candour.
Indicative budget: GBP 65,000
Work package 3: Citizen Voice Body
Evaluation of the implementation and impact of Citizen Voice Body provisions.
Indicative budget: GBP 60,000
Work package 4: Statutory Vice Chairs
Evaluation of the implementation and impact of the Statutory Vice Chairs provisions.
Indicative budget: GBP35,000
Ask:
The Welsh Government is seeking an indication of market interest in this future procurement opportunity.
Suppliers are invited to confirm their interest and respond to the questions below. Responses are requested for market planning purposes only and will not form part of any future procurement evaluation.
Please respond to the questions only. Do not include tender proposals, detailed solutions or commercial information at this stage. Information provided beyond the scope of the questions may be disregarded.
1. Contract and work-package Models
Which of the following models do you consider would provide the most appropriate basis for procuring and delivering the evaluation?
•	a single contract covering all five work packages;
•	a work-package model allowing suppliers to bid for one or more work packages; or
•	another model. Please briefly describe.
Please provide brief reasons for your preference, including any implications for effective coordination and integration across the evaluation.
2. Potential bidding interest
Based on the proposed structure, which work package(s) would your organisation potentially be interested in bidding for?
•	Work Package 0: Evaluation Integration, Coordination and Synthesis
•	Work Package 1: Duty of Quality
•	Work Package 2: Duty of Candour
•	Work Package 3: Citizen Voice Body
•	Work Package 4: Statutory Vice-Chairs
Please also indicate the delivery arrangement(s) your organisation would potentially consider:
•	sole supplier delivering the overall requirement;
•	lead supplier responsible for WP0 and coordinating delivery of WPs 1 to 4;
•	supplier delivering one or more individual work packages;
•	consortium member;
•	subcontractor; or
•	another delivery arrangement. Please briefly describe.
3. Work-package structure
Does the proposed work-package structure provide a practical basis for delivering a coherent and integrated evaluation?
Please identify any changes to you would recommend in relation to:
•	the number or scope of work packages;
•	the role and responsibilities of Work Package 0; and/or
•	the arrangements for coordination, integration and synthesis across the work packages. 
Please provide brief reasons for any suggested changes. 
4. Other comments 
Are there any other matters that the Welsh Government should consider when developing the procurement that have not already been covered in your responses above? In particular, you may wish to comment on: 
•	indicative budgets; 
•	contract duration; 
•	procurement and mobilisation timetable; 
•	barriers to market participation or competition; and 
•	any other factors that could materially affect deliverability.
Please keep your response concise and relevant to market planning. 
Status of this engagement: 
Responses will be used for market-planning and procurement-development purposes only. They will not be evaluated as part of any subsequent procurement process. 
Participation in this preliminary market engagement will not provide a supplier with an advantage in any future procurement. Failure to participate will not prevent a supplier from taking part in a future procurement opportunity. 
This notice does not constitute a call for competition, an invitation to tender or a commitment by the Welsh Government to undertake a procurement exercise. 
The Welsh Government may amend the scope, structure, value, timetable, contract duration or procurement approach before publishing any subsequent procurement notice. 
Suppliers should not include commercially confidential information at this stage. The Welsh Government may use and summarise the feedback received to inform the development of the requirement, procurement strategy and tender documentation. Information will be handled appropriately, subject to the Welsh Government’s legal obligations.
The Welsh Government will not reimburse suppliers for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response to this preliminary market engagement.
The Welsh Government will ensure that any information obtained through this preliminary market engagement is shared appropriately where required, to ensure equal treatment of suppliers in any subsequent procurement. 
Responding to this notice: 
Response deadline: 2pm on 16th October 2026
Response method: You can register interest via this notice. Responses should be concise and should address the numbered questions above. Please email feedback responses to Research.HealthAndSocialServices@gov.wales. 
Clarification arrangements: If you have any clarification regarding any areas of this notice please email CPDProcurementAdvice@gov.wales.

title: Supply of One New Medium Sized Low Emission Panel Van
description:
SUPPLY OF ONE NEW MEDIUM SIZED LOW EMISSION PANEL VAN
Lot 1: Plug in Hybrid Electric Vehicle, PHEV
Lot 2: Battery Electric Vehicle, BEV
Estimated contract value: approximately £45,000 excluding VAT
Closing date: 12 noon, Friday 23rd October 2026
Hythe and Dibden Parish Council invites tenders from suitably qualified vehicle suppliers for the supply, first registration and delivery of one new medium sized low emission panel van.
The Council is seeking a vehicle broadly equivalent in size and operational capability to a Ford Transit Custom L1 H1. The reference to the Ford Transit Custom is provided solely as an indication of the approximate size and operational characteristics required. Equivalent vehicles from other manufacturers will be considered.
The procurement is divided into two Lots:
Lot 1: Plug in Hybrid Electric Vehicle, PHEV
Lot 2: Battery Electric Vehicle, BEV
Suppliers may tender for either Lot or both Lots. The Council intends to purchase one vehicle only and will award either Lot 1 or Lot 2.
Required specification
The principal requirements include:
Medium sized panel van
New and previously unregistered
Minimum three seats including driver
Overall length approximately 5,050 mm
Overall height approximately 2,000 mm
Loadspace length approximately 2,600 mm or greater
Loadspace volume approximately 5.5 m³ or greater
Minimum payload 900 kg
Side and rear loading access
White
Moulded load floor liner or equivalent durable protection
Ply lining or equivalent durable load compartment protection
Tyre repair kit, spare wheel or suitable manufacturer equivalent
PHEV vehicles must have a manufacturer's published electric only range of at least 30 miles.
BEV vehicles must be capable of AC charging and DC rapid charging.
Full mandatory and evaluation requirements are contained in the tender pack.
Operational and charging requirements
The Council's operational requirements mean that full overnight charging cannot be routinely relied upon.
The vehicle is expected to spend an average of approximately two hours per working day at the Council's workshop, where electric vehicle charging facilities are available. The Council is prepared to consider an upgrade or replacement of the existing charging facility where reasonably necessary for the vehicle offered.
Tenderers must provide details of the charging requirements for their proposed vehicle and identify and price any recommended charging equipment or upgrade.
Price and evaluation
The estimated contract value is approximately £45,000 excluding VAT.
The tendered price must include all costs associated with supply and first registration, including the first registration fee and Vehicle Excise Duty where applicable. VAT must be identified separately.
Tenders will be evaluated on the basis of:
Five Year Whole Life Cost: 45%
Operational Suitability and Specification: 30%

title: Community Wrap Around and Night Support Service CRN/2026/294
description:
Stoke-on-Trent City Council is seeking to appoint one Provider for Lot 1 and one Provider for Lot 2 to deliver two specialist short-term home-based support services for adults aged 18 and over.
The services are designed to support people to remain safely within their own homes during periods of increased need, crisis, recovery, assessment or transition, whilst avoiding unnecessary hospital admissions and long-term residential care placements.
Providers may bid for one or both Lots; however, each Lot will be awarded to a single Provider.
Lot 1 - Night Support Service
Lot 1 is a short-term overnight support service delivered through block rota arrangements. The service is intended for individuals who require short-term support, supervision, observation or reassurance during night-time hours from 11pm - 6am.
The successful Provider will deliver overnight support within an individual's home, typically during periods of crisis, hospital discharge, deterioration in health, carer breakdown, increased risk or whilst assessments are being undertaken. The service will provide a physical staff presence overnight to monitor wellbeing, manage identified risks and respond to support needs as they arise.
A key function of the service is to gather evidence about an individual's overnight needs and provide professional observations to support future care planning and decision-making by the Council.
Lot 2 - Wrap Around Support Service
Lot 2 is a flexible short-term wrap around support service delivered through block support arrangements for individuals who require a higher level of support throughout the day.
The successful Provider will deliver short-term intensive home-based support to individuals whose needs require regular monitoring, observation and intervention across extended periods of the day. The service is designed to bridge gaps in support, promote recovery and independence, and provide evidence to inform longer-term care and support planning.

Lot 1 Carer Peer Support Service:
A community-based support service that enables unpaid carers to connect with and support one another through a range of peer-led opportunities. Key Functions: • Provide information, signposting and informal support to carers. • Represent carers' views and feedback to service providers and commissioners. • Promote carer awareness within local communities and organisations. • Support the development and promotion of peer support groups and activities. • Participate in service evaluation, mystery shopping and quality assurance. • Maintain knowledge of local services, support pathways and carer issues. • Act as a specialist ambassador where appropriate (e.g. mental health, autism, learning disability).

title: Human Capital Management Platform
description:
Introduction
This notice is intended to open dialogue with the market and inform any potential future formal procurement process, to test market capability, supplier interest, delivery options and implementation feasibility. Progression to formal procurement is not guaranteed.
Bromford Flagship LiveWest (BFL) is exploring the future provision of its Human Capital Management (HCM) technology for approx 5,600 colleagues. Following organisational integration, BFL currently operates a broad range of legacy people systems and associated processes across HR, payroll, recruitment, onboarding, learning, talent, workforce management and employee relations.
This document supports early, informal engagement with potential suppliers. It is not a procurement exercise, invitation to tender or commitment to purchase any solution.
The engagement will help BFL understand available market capability, delivery models, indicative costs and implementation considerations before determining the scope and route of any future procurement.
BFL is testing whether its emerging ambition is achievable and appropriately framed. We want suppliers to help us understand:
• Whether a single platform can meet the breadth of need or whether an integrated ecosystem would provide a stronger outcome.
• Which capabilities are standard, configurable, partner-delivered or dependent on third-party integration.
• Indicative commercial models and whole-life cost considerations.
• Realistic implementation approaches, sequencing, dependencies and timescales.
• Any material gaps, risks or emerging practice that BFL should consider before formal procurement.
Strategic Vision for People Services
BFL wants to create a connected, consistent and future-focused people technology environment that offers a simple experience for colleagues, managers and administrators while strengthening payroll assurance, workforce insight and organisational control.
Our ambition is to reduce fragmentation and duplication, increase self-service, improve mobile and field-based accessibility, automate routine activity and establish trusted people data that can support operational and strategic decision-making.
We are open to a single HCM platform, modular products within one technology family, or a well-integrated ecosystem. The preferred approach must provide a coherent user journey, clear system ownership, secure data flows and sustainable administration over the long term.
Design principles
• One colleague and manager experience, with single sign-on and minimal switching between applications.
• A reliable single source of people data with effective-dated records, governance and auditability.
• Configurable self-service and workflow that reduce manual intervention without weakening controls.
• Mobile-first and accessible design for office-based, remote and field-based colleagues.
• Open integration using modern REST APIs, event-based services and standard data exchange methods.
• Actionable reporting through native analytics and integration with Microsoft Power BI.
• Secure, compliant, vendor-managed cloud services with appropriate UK or EEA data residency.
• A platform and supplier roadmap capable of supporting future organisational change, AI and skills intelligence.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
This notice is issued for information gathering purposes only. Participation in this exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any future procurement process.
The contract value provided is an estimate based on current spend for a 5 year contract.
RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS
Suppliers wishing to participate should contact Kate.Metzgier@flagship-group.co.uk to receive more details about the planned procurement. The deadline for submission of information is 14 October 2026
.

title: SCC Spirit Store Container Replacement
description:
The Horniman Museum and Gardens is a grade II* listed museum with a world class Natural History, Anthropology and Musical instrument collection. Items in the Horniman Collection when not on display are stored, managed, studied and conserved at the Study Collection Centre (SCC). The existing Spirit Store is a refrigerated container which holds generally organic and biological items which are preserved in vessels of flammable spirit such as denatured alcohol or formalin. The store requires replacement. The Horniman wishes to appoint a contractor to develop their Employer's Requirements into a design and deliver the works for a replacement Spirit Store.
The Horniman Museum and Gardens is a grade II* listed museum with a world class Natural History, Anthropology and Musical instrument collection. Set within 16 acres of stunning grounds that also house an Aquarium, Animal Walk and Butterfly House. The Horniman connects us all with global cultures and the natural environment, encouraging us to shape a positive future for the world we all share. Items in the Horniman Collection when not on display are stored, managed, studied and conserved at the Study Collection Centre (SCC), Old School Close, Greenwich, London SE10 0PG. Many items require very particular storage conditions for safety and conservation.
At SCC, the existing Spirit Store holds generally organic and biological items which are preserved in vessels of flammable spirit such as denatured alcohol or formalin. Due to the need for flashpoint temperature control and inherent fire risk, the Spirit Store is a secure refrigerated walk-in container which stands apart from the main storage building.
The Spirit Store container is aged with general conditional, operational and plant performance limitations which give risk to safety and collection conservation risks. The nature and quantity of the museum's collection is also changing over time, and working practices are updating. These are the key drivers presenting opportunity for a project to re-provide a modernised Spirit Store facility. There are further containers on site which require re-organisation by repositioning them during this project.
Project broadly includes:
• The contractor's design of a replacement Spirit Store.
• The contractor's fabrication, construction, delivery, erection and fitting out of the replacement Spirit Store.
• The contractor's associated site preparations, groundworks, utilities and services provision.
• The contractor's associated firewall construction
• The contractor's carrying out repositioning of further existing container stores on the site, with associated groundworks.
The full Scope and Objectives of the project can be found in the attached Employer's
Requirements document and drawings A101, A102 and A103.
Please see supporting documents for further details
buyer: THE HORNIMAN PUBLIC MUSEUM AND PUBLIC PARK TRUST

title: Ireland – Economic research services – Consultancy Services to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in relation to the provision of Irish-language based early-years (Naíonra) facilities in Dún Gar
description: Naíonra Garbháin was established in 1981 as an early-immersion Irish-language based educational setting for pre-school children in Dún Garbhán and the surrounding areas. Dún Garbhán is a Baile Seirbhíse Gaeltachta (Gaeltacht Service Town). Naíonra Garbháin provides education and childcare services for people from the Gaeltacht who do not have access to housing in An Rinn or An Sean Phobal and who live in the surrounding area. Naíonra Garbháin is managed by a voluntary committee known as Croí na nÓg. As it is located immediately adjacent to the Irish-language based primary school, Scoil Gharbháin, progression from the Naíonra to the primary school is seamless and therefore the Naíonra is an important foundation and integral part of life on the Scoil Gharbháin campus. As the population of the town of Dún Garbháin, and in particular the area adjacent to the Naíonra, continues to grow, Croí na nÓg wishes to ensure that the facilities provided in the town of Dún Garbháin are sufficient to cater for the demand for Irish-language based education for pre-school children in the town. It also wishes to ensure that suitable facilities are available to cater for the demand for Irish-language based pre- and post-school services in the area. The latter is particularly important as a significant number of parents of primary school travel into Dún Garbháin on a daily basis for employment and are likely to avail of such services if they were available. Croí na nÓg have recently purchased lands immediately adjoining the Department of Education and Skills lands upon which Scoil Gharbháin is constructed and wish to ensure that the lands are utilised in the most efficient manner possible to meet the Irish-language based early education and pre/post school service demands of the area. Croí na nÓg wish to appoint a consultant to undertake a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case as envisaged in the Infrastructure Guidelines and the tender documents to improve the range of early-years educational and pre/post school services in the area.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Bundesanstalt für den Digitalfunk der Behörden und Organisationen mit Sicherheitsaufgaben (BDBOS), Sanierung von zwei Technikgebäuden des Bundes (TgdB) in Thüringen, Fachplanung Technische Gebäudeausrüstung
description: Bundesanstalt für den Digitalfunk der Behörden und Organisationen mit Sicherheitsaufgaben (BDBOS), Sanierung von zwei Technikgebäuden des Bundes (TgdB) in Thüringen. Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt die technischen Anlagen von zwei rechenzentrumsähnlichen Technikgebäuden des Bundes mit redundanten technischen Anlagen bei laufendem Betrieb der Gebäude zu erneuern. Dabei handelt es sich insbesondere um Trinkwasseranlagen, Lüftungs- und Klimaanlagen, Kälteanlagen, Niederspannungsanlagen, Eigenerzeugungsanlagen, Mittelspanungsanlagen, Brandmeldeanlagen, Gebäudeautomation und Sauerstoffreduktionsanlagen. Für die Planung und Realisierung werden die Leistungen der Fachplanung für die Technische Ausrüstung im Rahmen eines Verhandlungsverfahrens mit Teilnahmewettbewerb für die Leistungsphasen 2 bis 9 (Leistungsstufen 1 bis 5) ausgeschrieben. Für die Beteiligung an dieser Ausschreibung ist in der ersten Stufe (Wettbewerb um die Teilnahme) die Einreichung eines Bewerbungsbogens (Teilnahmeantrag) mit den geforderten Angaben und Nachweisen zum gesetzten Termin erforderlich. Die am Ende der Auswertung der ersten Stufe ausgewählten am besten geeigneten Bewerber werden Teilnehmer an der zweiten Stufe des Verfahrens (Bieterverfahren). In der zweiten Stufe ist dann das Erstangebot einzureichen. Über das Erstangebot wird weiterverhandelt. Nach Abgabe der finalen nicht mehr verhandelbaren Angebote werden die Bieter zu einer Vorstellung eingeladen, um sich vor einer Jury persönlich zu präsentieren. Eine schriftliche / digitale Präsentation ist nicht gewünscht und nicht erforderlich und wird nicht gewertet. Die Kostenschätzung beträgt je Gebäude ca. 110.000 Euro für die Baukonstruktion und ca. 6.036.000 Euro für die technischen Anlagen. Die Leistungen sind an beiden Standorten mit geringem zeitlichem Versatz, parallel mit denselben Ausführungsunternehmen zu realisieren. Während der Objektüberwachung ist die Anwesenheit des Bewerbers, bei Ausführung der Bauleistungen durch die Ausführungsfirmen, ständig sicherzustellen. Das Bauvorhaben wurde als VS-NfD eingestuft. Die Bedingungen für die Planung und Ausführung sind im VS-NfD-Merkblatt_GHB-Anl4 der Vergabeunterlagen festgelegt. Der gesamte Schriftverkehr in der Vertragsphase ist über ein Verschlüsselungsprogramm zu führen, das die Zulassung des Bundesamtes für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) besitzt. Der Auftragnehmer verpflichtet sich eine entsprechende Software für die Verschlüsselung anzuschaffen, vorzuhalten und zu verwenden. Entsprechende Lizenzen für das vom TLBV empfohlene Programm GnuPG VS-Desktop sind vom Planer für die Vertragsphase und den späteren Ausführungsfirmen zu erwerben. Die Kosten für das Programm, deren Installation und Mehraufwand bei der Bearbeitung des Projektes sind im Angebot einzukalkulieren und werden nicht gesondert vergütet. Aufgrund der Geheimschutz-Anforderungen müssen sich alle mit dem Projekt befassten Personen nach dem Sicherheitsüberprüfungsgesetz (SÜG) überprüfen lassen. Es dürfen keine Personen mit dem Projekt befasst sein, die aus Ländern stammen, die auf der Staatenliste § 13 und 17 SÜG stehen.

How should a new framework to support nature restoration and conservation be designed, structured, and administered to provide genuine additionality and complementarity to the Common Agricultural Policy 2028-2034, and other relevant national funding streams, while ensuring seamless delivery for farmers and public and private landowners whilst safeguarding public and European funding accountability.

title: Spain – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast
description: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.
buyer: ['European Commission, DG JRC - Joint Research Centre']

title: Ireland – Civil engineering consultancy services – Dublin City Council Single Party Framework Agreement for an Integrated Design Team for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project
description: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 9181107. Please note that this project is subject to funding.

title: Belgium – Research and development services and related consultancy services – AI for Public Good Lot 1 (Health: Innovative AI-based cancer imaging solutions for breast and prostate diagnosis) and Lot 2 (Energy: Innovative AI-based solutions for electric grid optimization)
description: The European Commission is committed to tapping into the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to collaboratively and complementarily drive research to address global challenges. DG CONNECT is the European Commission’s Directorate General responsible for digital policies. Through its Directorate A “Artificial Intelligence Office”, it is tasked to implement the AI Act and promote the development and use of trustworthy AI. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI. The purpose of this call for tenders is to develop and test AI-powered solutions for the benefit of the EU as well as wider communities and third countries. The call has two lots, on AI for Cancer imaging (LOT1) and on AI for Electric grid optimisation (LOT2). LOT 1 will explore and demonstrate how AI-powered solutions applied to EU cancer imaging data can be further fine-tuned and applied in other locations and settings covering a large variety of populations, without transferring the underlying sensitive health data. It has two predefined use-cases, breast cancer and prostate cancer. LOT2 will support the European Commission in exploring and demonstrating the application of AI- powered solutions to effectively tackle challenges within energy systems, specifically focusing on the seamless integration of renewable energy sources (RES) capacity across diverse energy system levels.

Füllen Sie hierfür bitte die unter dem Reiter "Teilnehmerunterlagen" hochgeladenen Unterlagen zum Teilnahmewettbewerb aus und laden Sie die geforderten Unterlagen im Vergabeportal hoch. Eine Auflistung der vorzulegenden Bewerbungsunterlagen finden sie in Anlage 2 Bewerbungsbogen unter der Nummer 1.3. Das Schöpfwerk Niendorf wurde in den 1960ern in der DDR errichtet und entwässert das Einzugsgebiet der Krainke mit etwa 12.240 ha. Es schützt dadurch Siedlungsgebiete und landwirtschaftliche Flächen bei Elbehochwasser und Rückstau in die Sude oder bei Eigenhochwasser der Sude. Der am Schöpfwerk angeschlossene rechte Krainkedeich wurde im Jahr 2014 auf die Höhe des neuen Bemessungshochwassers angepasst. Die Sanierung und höhenmäßige Anpassung des linken Krainkedeiches erfolgte im Jahr 2016. Eine Anpassung an die neuen Bemessungswasserstände ist im Bereich des Schöpfwerkes noch nicht erfolgt, so dass Minderhöhen von 30 cm vorhanden sind. Sechs installierte Propellerpumpen verfügen über eine Gesamtleistung von etwa 11,7 m³/s, die Pumpen stammen aus der Zeit des Baues von 1963 und befinden sich Teils in schlechtem Zustand, zwei Pumpen wurden 2005 und 2006 erneuert. Eine Rechenreinigungsanlage ist nicht vorhanden. Daneben verfügt das Schöpfwerk über 4 Freiflutkanäle, die der regulären Entwässerung außerhalb der Hochwasserzeiten dienen, wobei diese nicht den Anforderungen an die Durchgängigkeit nach WRRL genügen. Im Jahre 2016 wurde eine Bedarfsplanung erstellt, mit dem Ergebnis eine Grundinstandsetzung vorzunehmen. Für die Planung der Grundinstandsetzung wurden seit 2021 Ingenieurplanungen der Leistungsphasen 1 bis 3 und Teilen von 4 erbracht. Im Rahmen der Planungen wurden verschiedene Bauteile des Schöpfwerkes näher untersucht: Beton, Putz, Druckrohrleitungen, Schmutzwasserkanal, etc.. Das Ergebnis der Planungen zeigte, dass annähernd sämtliche Anlagenteile des Schöpfwerkes saniert, ausgetauscht oder neu gebaut werden müssten. Aufgrund des absehbaren umfangreichen Instandsetzungsaufwands wurde 2025 im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie untersucht, ob ein Ersatzneubau des Schöpfwerks eine technisch und wirtschaftlich bessere Lösung darstellen kann als eine Sanierung des Bestandes. Der NLWKN beabsichtigt auf Grundlage der bisherigen Planungen und der Ergebnisse der Machbarkeitsstudie aus 2025 das bestehende Schöpfwerk durch einen zeitgemäßen Neubau, am Standort des bestehenden Schöpfwerks zu ersetzen. Der Schöpfwerksneubau soll die aktuellen Anforderungen beim Bemessungswasserstand, der Durchgängigkeit und dem fischfreundlichen und wirtschaftlichen Betrieb erfüllen. Zudem soll durch eine Erhöhung der Pumpenkapazität dem Klimawandel Rechnung getragen werden. Folgende Binnenwasserstände sind durch das Schöpfwerk sicherzustellen: - höchstzulässiger Binnenpeil: +7,80 mNHN - höchster Winterpeil +7,70 mNHN - höchster Sommerpeil +7,40 mNHN - tiefster Binnenpeil +7,20 mNHN Das Bemessungshochwasser liegt derzeit bei 10,60 m+NHN und die entsprechende Ausbauhöhe des Deiches unter Berücksichtigung eines Freibordes von 70 cm bei +11,30 mNHN. Die im folgenden aufgeführten Abflüsse sind durch die Pumpen des Schöpfwerkes abzuführen, sofern der Außenwasserstand über dem Binnenwasserstand liegt: - Höchster Hochwasserabfluss HHQ: 11,142 m³/s - Bemessungshochwasserabfluss: 11,30 m³/s - Bemessungshochwasserabfluss mit Berücksichtigung Klimaanpassungsfaktor: 13,715 m³/s - Sommermittelwasserabfluss SMQ: 2,076 m³/s Die Pumpen müssen auf geodätische Förderhöhen zwischen 0,00 m und 3,20 m ausgelegt werden. Diese Randbedingungen sind auch bei der Planung der Freiflut und der damit verbunden Fischaufstiegsanlage zur Sicherstellung der Binnenpeile und der Durchgängigkeit zu berücksichtigen. Das derzeitige Schöpfwerk Niendorf liegt in diversen naturschutzrechtlich geschützten Gebieten: - Biosphärenreservat "Niedersächsische Elbtalaue" (Lage des technischen Bauwerkes innerhalb des Gebietsteiles A, unmittelbar angrenzend an den streng geschützten Gebietsteil C) - FFH-Gebiet "Elbeniederung zwischen Schnackenburg und Geesthacht" - EU-Vogelschutzgebiet "Niedersächsische Mittelelbe" (Lage des technischen Bauwerkes außerhalb des EU-Vogelschutzgebietes, jedoch unmittelbar an das EU-Vogelschutzgebiet angrenzend) - Kohärenzsicherungsmaßnahme für die Fischarten Bitterling und Steinbeißer im unmittelbaren Umfeld Die entsprechenden Schutzgebietsvorschriften sind bei der Planung zu berücksichtigen.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Aufbau einer Merkmalsdatenbank zur semantischen Verknüpfung von OKSTRA und IFC
description: Die strukturelle und semantische Harmonisierung der Standards OKSTRA (Objektkatalog für das Straßen- und Verkehrswesen) und IFC (Industry Foundation Classes) gewinnt für die Digitalisierung des Straßenwesens zunehmend an Bedeutung. OKSTRA ist ein nationaler Standard mit hoher straßenfachlicher Detailtiefe, objektorientierter Modellierung und integrierter Validierungsunterstützung. Er bildet die Grundlage zahlreicher Fachprozesse wie INSPIRE-Datenbereitstellung, VEMAGS-Statik-Modul und Straßeninformationsbanken. IFC ist ein international anerkannter, herstellerneutraler BIM-Standard, der mit Version 4.3 erstmals umfassend auf Infrastrukturbauwerke ausgeweitet wurde. Allerdings sind IFC-Klassen international einheitlich und nicht auf spezifische nationale Anforderungen ausgelegt. Zwischen beiden Standards bestehen erhebliche Harmonisierungsbedarfe: OKSTRA beschreibt straßenbezogene Sachverhalte fein granular und eindeutig, während IFC auf physische Bauteile fokussiert und teilweise generischere Strukturen nutzt. Derzeit bestehen zwischen den Ländern unterschiedliche Fachbedeutungslisten, die zu inkonsistenten Bedeutungszuordnungen führen. Ohne eine eindeutige, maschinenlesbare Zuordnung von OKSTRA-Fachobjekten zu IFC-Strukturen ist weder eine automatisierte Konvertierung noch eine zuverlässige Validierung möglich. Zielsetzung Ziel dieses Forschungsvorhabens ist die Erarbeitung und Bereitstellung einer Merkmalsdatenbank, die OKSTRA-Objektklassen, BIM-Objektkatalog-Objekte und die harmonisierte Fachbedeutungsliste samt Attributen beinhaltet und diese eindeutig IFC-Entitäten, Property Sets und Klassifikationen zuordnet. Zudem soll die explorative Harmonisierung unterschiedlicher Schemata durchgeführt werden. Die Merkmalsdatenbank soll maschinenlesbares Artefakt über eine standardisierte REST-API-Schnittstelle bereitgestellt werden. Das Mapping soll vollständig über alle OKSTRA-Objektklassen sowie die harmonisierte Fachbedeutungsliste erfolgen. Der Betrieb im BIM-Portal des Bundes ist zu untersuchen. Nutzen des FE-Vorhabens Das FE-Vorhaben schafft mit der Merkmalsdatenbank eine verbindliche Grundlage für die automatisierte OKSTRA/IFC-Konvertierung und ermöglicht damit einen verlustfreien Datenaustausch zwischen OKSTRA- und BIM-basierten Prozessen im Straßenwesen. Durch die semantisch korrekten Zuordnungen wird die Planungsqualität gesteigert und die Effizienz bei der Umsetzung von BIM-Projekten im Straßenwesen erhöht. Doppelstrukturen und parallele Datenhaltungen werden vermieden. Darüber hinaus unterstützt das Vorhaben die laufende Standardisierung von OKSTRA und buildingSMART, indem es konsolidierte Mapping-Regeln bereitstellt, die in die weitere Entwicklung der Standards einfließen können.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – FE 77.0708/2024/ - "Machbarkeitsstudie Neues Mobilitätspanel – Konzeption einer neuen Erhebung"
description: FE 77.0708/2024/ - "Machbarkeitsstudie Neues Mobilitätspanel – Konzeption einer neuen Erhebung" Problem/Ausgangslage: Belastbare Daten zum Verkehrs- und Mobilitätsverhalten in Deutschland sind für die Verkehrspolitik und Forschung notwendig. Dazu dient die Basis-Befragung der Studie „Mobilität in Deutschland“ (MiD) mit großer Stichprobe, die zukünftig alle fünf Jahre durchgeführt werden soll. Um auch zwischen den Basis-Befragungen Aussagen über Auswirkungen dynamischer Entwicklungen und disruptiver Ereignisse auf das Mobilitätsgeschehen treffen zu können, sind regelmäßige und in geringeren Zeitabständen durchgeführte Erhebungen notwendig. Dazu fehlen bisher zeitlich und räumlich aufgelöste und repräsentative Daten. Diese Funktion soll zukünftig die MiD-aktuell übernehmen, die Ergebnisse der MiD-Basis fortschreibt und dynamische Entwicklungen abbilden soll. Ziel und Nutzen: Im Rahmen des Projekts soll die Methodik für die MiD-aktuell entwickelt werden. Sie muss mindestens bundesweit repräsentative und jahresrepräsentative Aussagen zur Alltagsmobilität und relevanter Mobilitätskennziffern liefern (z.B. Modal Split, Verkehrsmittel-Verfügbarkeit, übliche Verkehrsmittelnutzung). Vor diesem Hintergrund soll im Projekt der geeignete Stichprobenumfang abgeleitet, ein Vorschlag für die Erhebungsmodi erarbeitet und das Befragungskonzept erstellt werden. Die Methodik und der Befragungskatalog müssen dabei kompatibel sein mit der MiD-Basis, z.B. durch geeignete Scharnierfragen. Zudem müssen in dem Konzept auch Sondererhebungen vorgesehen werden, um disruptive Ereignisse abbilden zu können. Im Projekt muss ein Konzept erarbeitet werden, wie Panelmortalität reduziert bzw. wie mit ihr umgegangen werden kann, um auch langfristig repräsentative Ergebnisse ohne Bias zu erhalten. In diesem Zusammenhang muss auch betrachtet werden, wie mit Neuerungen und Weiterentwicklungen im Panel umgegangen werden soll. Zusätzlich muss ein Konzept erarbeitet werden, wie Adressdaten der Teilnehmenden DSGVO-konform an die Auftraggeberin und zukünftige Auftragnehmende weitergegeben werden können.

description: The European Commission is committed to tapping into the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to collaboratively and complementarily drive research to address global challenges. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI. The purpose of this call for tenders is to develop and test AI-powered solutions for the benefit of the EU as well as wider communities and third countries. The call has two lots, on AI for Cancer imaging (LOT1) and on AI for Electric grid optimisation (LOT2). LOT 1 will explore and demonstrate how AI-powered solutions applied to EU cancer imaging data can be further fine-tuned and applied in other locations and settings covering a large variety of populations, without transferring the underlying sensitive health data. It has two predefined use-cases, breast cancer and prostate cancer. LOT2 will support the European Commission in exploring and demonstrating the application of AI- powered solutions to effectively tackle challenges within energy systems, specifically focusing on the seamless integration of renewable energy sources (RES) capacity across diverse energy system levels.

title: NEPO217 - Winter Bureau, Weather Forecasting &  Outstation Maintenance
description:
The proposed procurement will establish a NEPO‑led Unranked Open Framework for the provision of Winter Bureau services, weather forecasting services, and RWIS outstation maintenance for UK local authorities.
The framework will replace the existing NEPO217 (Winter Bureau & Outstation Maintenance) and NEPO230 (Weather Forecasting Services) arrangements and will bring these services together into one solution reflecting how they are used operationally by authorities.
The scope is expected to include:
Winter Bureau services, including decision support, data management, system availability, resilience and user access to operational winter information.
Weather forecasting services, providing locally relevant and operationally defensible forecasts to support winter service decision‑making.
RWIS outstation maintenance, covering inspection, maintenance, repair, calibration and associated support for existing roadside infrastructure.
Optional or modular services, which may include enhanced data products, radar data, route‑based forecasting or analytical tools, where supported by market capability and authority demand.
The framework will be designed to support continuity of existing systems and infrastructure, recognising recent investment by authorities and avoiding mandated wholesale replacement of assets. Authorities will be able to access services through clearly defined call‑off mechanisms, including further competition where appropriate.
The Open Framework is expected to operate for up to eight years, with periodic reopening in line with the Procurement Act 2023 to allow for market refresh and potential new entrants.
NEPO is a Centralised Procurement Authority as defined in the Procurement Act 2023 (PA23), providing central purchasing activity on behalf of Contracting Authorities. All elements in this notice are subject to change at the sole discretion of NEPO. This notice is intended to inform the market of the potential scope of the procurement, not to be taken as the final  version.
The agreement will be available to NEPO Member Authorities and all current and future Associate Members.
Current Associate Members are listed in the Associate Member section of the NEPO website at:
https://www.nepo.org/associate-membership
A list of permissible users is available at:
https://www.nepo.org/associate-membership/permissible-users
Organisations wishing to access the NEPO agreement will be required to register as a NEPO Associate Member in the first instance. Further information can be found at: www.nepo.org

The successful contractor will be required to undertake a full survey and mapping of existing panel I/O and wiring configurations, supply and install a replacement PLC, provide compatible software interfaces, and ensure continued operation of the existing machine and control programmes. description:

EA requires a CMDB to provide a trusted, accurate and near-real-time view of its ICT assets, applications, services and the relationships between them. Acting as the single source of truth for the DTS estate, it will reduce manual data maintenance through automation, support Cyber Essentials accreditation and provide the foundation for EA’s ICT Service Catalogue. 
To deliver these outcomes, the CMDB must integrate with EA’s Change Management process and ITSM platform. This integration will ensure that trusted configuration and service data informs change assessment, approval and implementation. 
By mapping the relationships between services, applications and infrastructure components, the CMDB will allow proposed changes to be assessed against known dependencies and potential business impacts before implementation. This visibility will support more reliable planning, testing and communication, giving decision-makers greater confidence that changes can proceed safely.

title: Christmas Light Trail for Sir Harold Hillier Gardens
description:
Sir Harold Hillier Gardens (SHHG) is a nationally significant arboretum located near Romsey, Hampshire, comprising approximately 180 acres and housing one of the most comprehensive collections of hardy trees and shrubs in the UK. The Gardens are operated as a registered charitable trust, with Hampshire County Council acting as trustee and retaining responsibility for strategic oversight and governance.
Since 2021, SHHG has hosted an annual outdoor illuminated light trail with the aim of reaching a wider audience to support its charitable aims and sustained growth. The event has been successful over the past four years, with year-on-year growth in both visitor numbers and light trail ticket sales. The existing contract for delivery of the light trail expires on 15 January 2027.
Given the success of the light trail, SHHG is seeking a provider to continue delivering an annual high-quality outdoor illuminated light trail for public sale that shall be ticketed for the duration of 6 weeks, between the end of November and the beginning of January. The appointed provider will be expected to design and deliver an exciting and immersive visitor experience that showcases the Gardens during evening hours, supports continued growth in visitor numbers towards a target of 90,000 visitors, and aligns with the Gardens’ charitable aims.
The Council intends to enter into a concession contract for provision of the services for a total duration of 10 years.
The service must be delivered in a manner that respects the sensitivities of a Grade II listed landscape and ensures a safe, accessible, and inclusive visitor experience. The provider will be responsible for all aspects of event delivery, including light trail design, lighting installation, e-ticketing, marketing, and event management. Management of the event will include provision of all required staffing and logistics necessary to deliver the trail, sourcing additional car parking if required, stewarding, security, and health and safety compliance. The provider will also be expected to provide catering facilities at the outset of the contract.
A collaborative partnership approach will be required, with the successful provider working closely with SHHG to ensure the event aligns with the Gardens’ identity, charitable objectives and its position as part of Hampshire County Council.
The Council will charge the provider a fee of £125,000.00 per annum (excluding VAT) for use of the Council’s premises for performance of the Services, payable in instalments. In addition, there will be an additional Concession Fee payable against all income generating ticket sales above 75,000 visitors, calculated on the basis of the per-ticket rate proposed by the provider in its tender submission.

Bycatch Monitoring Programme (BMP) - 26-35
description:
Defra intends to run an open tender to procure a new long-term UK Bycatch Monitoring Programme and is seeking Expressions of Interest from suppliers capable of delivering the requirements.
The programme will monitor and assess the bycatch of sensitive marine species in UK fisheries, including (but not limited to) cetaceans, seabirds, seals, and elasmobranchs. The requirement will primarily cover England and Scotland, with potential involvement from other Devolved Administrations.
The successful supplier will build on the existing programme by increasing monitoring coverage where required, enhancing data collection and analysis, integrating monitoring approaches such as observer monitoring and electronic monitoring, and improving understanding of bycatch patterns across fisheries, gear types, locations and seasons.
Key outputs will include bycatch monitoring data, annual bycatch estimates and trends, technical reporting, and evidence to support national and international reporting obligations.
We envisage that, if a new supplier is appointed, the new contract will start on the 01 June 27 with a one (1) month handover period, from 01 June to 30 June, with full responsibility being transferred to the successful contractor on 01 July 2027.  Where applicable, these handover periods are to allow a new Contractor time to get ready to take over the full operation of the contract requirement.
The contract will be let for an initial two-year term, with options to extend for two x 3 -12-month periods thereafter. (a total maximum of eight year’s).
 We estimate the contract value to be between the range of £380,000 - £430,000 funded by Defra and the Scottish Government.
The contractor will be required to provide bycatch records and annual estimates of bycatch rates for sensitive marine species, produce information on bycatch trends using historical and newly collected data, and support reporting requirements including UK Marine Strategy assessments, OSPAR, ASCOBANS, ICES and US Marine Mammal Protection Act requirements. The contractor will also be expected to maintain accurate geo-referenced and time-referenced data on monitoring effort and bycatch incidence, produce annual reports for Defra, the Scottish Government and the project steering group, and provide information to support Parliamentary Questions and Ministerial correspondence when required.
The Authority strongly encourages a consortium approach, recognising the multi-disciplinary nature of the work and the benefits of bringing together relevant expertise and organisations. The successful contractor will be expected to provide dedicated programme management, maintain effective communication with Defra and the Scottish Government, manage any consortium members or subcontractors, and ensure delivery of the programme’s aims, objectives and reporting requirements.

title: BGWM Digital Transformation (Discovery Phase)
description:
Business Growth West Midlands (BGWM) is the current West Midlands business support service and the primary digital entry point into the wider region's business support ecosystem. Delivered by West Midlands Growth Company (WMGC), through West Midlands Growth Hub, BGWM forms a vital part of the region's commitment to providing a "no wrong door" approach to business support.
As part of the new WMGC Growth Hub operating model, a new digital service is required to provide a seamless entry journey for all businesses while supporting clear routing, referral management, business intelligence capture and outcome tracking across the wider business support ecosystem. This may or may not be under the same brand.
Following a strategic review, WMGC has adopted a Hybrid Universal Front Door model for the business support digital service, which provides a consistent and high-quality entry experience for all businesses and quickly routes businesses to the most appropriate support while managing expectations around provision through clear positioning and tailored customer journeys.
While the future digital service will provide a universal entry point, universal access does not mean that every business will receive person-led support. The primary role of the service is to identify and enable the most appropriate next step for the business.
Small, micro, pre-start and startup businesses will be supported through automated referrals to Local Enterprise Services, other local and national provision, plus curated digital content and tools. High-growth potential and strategic businesses will be identified through proportionate digital triage and transferred rapidly into person-led support through the High Growth Service and Strategic Account Management functions. The future digital service is intended not only to signpost businesses that are not yet eligible for person-led High Growth support to external provision, but also to operate as a regional digital support layer. It will help address common business needs directly through high-quality digital tools, guidance and tailored recommendations. These tailored resources would supplement evidenced gaps in provision and improve continuity rather than replicate support already available through local, regional, national or private-sector providers. The future digital service should be informed by recognised best practice from comparable business support ecosystems and digital service models. Discovery activity should assess existing market solutions and ensure any future service delivers clear additional value to businesses and stakeholders, avoiding unnecessary duplication of functionality, content, tools or services already available elsewhere.
To ensure future investment decisions are evidence-based and aligned to business needs, WMGC is seeking to appoint an experienced agency or consortium to undertake a comprehensive Discovery Phase that will validate user needs, test key assumptions underpinning the hybrid model, define service requirements, and develop a robust specification for future procurement and implementation.
This is an initial procurement associated with the first phase - Discovery - of this project.

title: Repatriation of Illegally Exported Waste Framework
description:
International waste shipments relate to the import and export of waste across international boundaries. These movements of waste are subject to the controls outlined in the retained EU Waste Shipments Regulations, which aim to ensure a high level of protection for human health and the environment. The regulations also aim to prevent the unauthorised disposal/recovery of hazardous waste shipments in countries where they are not able to handle the waste in an environmentally sound manner, without hindering the legitimate trade in waste. 
International waste shipments from England can be subject to notification controls, which applies to all imports and exports of:
• Hazardous waste moving for recovery
• Any type of waste moving for disposal
• Some imports and exports of non-hazardous wastes for recovery
Where these controls apply, organisations need a uniquely numbered notification and movement form issued by the Environment Agency (EA) before movement of the waste. Organisations could also be subject to ‘green list controls’. These are the lowest level of control and only ever apply to some imports or exports of non-hazardous waste for recovery. Where these controls apply, organisations do not require EA permission before moving the waste, but they do have to comply with Waste Shipment Regulation, Article 18 controls. 
Under the regulations the EA and other public named bodies carry out regulatory duties to meet their statutory obligations. This includes ensuring that waste, which has been illegally exported or shipments which cannot be completed, can be repatriated back to the UK, preferably within the statutory 30-day timescale. Historically, the 30-day statutory requirement has never been enforced, with the EA and overseas authorities liaising to ensure the waste is repatriated as soon as practicable. Occasionally the EA have to manage repatriations and bear the cost, hence the need for a framework

title: Training, Coaching and Development Providers Framework
description:
The Development Bank of Wales (DBW) is seeking to establish a Framework Agreement for the provision of training, coaching and development services to support the learning and development needs of its employees. The framework will provide access to suitably qualified and experienced suppliers capable of delivering a broad range of professional development services, including leadership and management development, procurement and commercial skills, finance, risk and compliance, project management, coaching and mentoring, digital and technology skills, personal effectiveness, and other specialist training requirements.
Through this procurement, DBW aims to appoint a panel of providers who can deliver high-quality, flexible and value-for-money learning solutions across a range of delivery methods, including classroom-based, virtual and blended learning. Tenderers may apply for one, some or multiple disciplines within a Lot. Tenderers are not required to demonstrate capability across all disciplines contained within a Lot. Additional questions within the eTenderWales portal will require Tenderers to identify the specific discipline(s) for which they are submitting a Tender.
The framework will support DBW's strategic objectives by enhancing workforce capability, supporting organisational development and ensuring employees have access to relevant and effective learning opportunities.
Further details of the scope, lot structure, evaluation methodology and framework arrangements are set out within the procurement documents.
The framework is expected to be divided into lots to reflect different areas of expertise. The Development Bank of Wales does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work under the framework. Contracts will be awarded in accordance with the call-off procedures set out in the procurement documents.
Services may include training programmes, workshops, masterclasses, briefings, coaching, mentoring, facilitation, training needs analysis, learner diagnostics, preparation of learning materials, post-course evaluation and associated reporting. Delivery may be in person, virtual or blended, depending on the requirement, audience and relevant lot.
The framework will be divided into lots covering leadership and management development; procurement, commercial and contract management; financial services, risk and regulatory training; digital, technology and AI skills; project and change management; HR, equality, diversity and inclusion; health, safety and wellbeing; Welsh language and communication skills; coaching and mentoring; and soft skills and business development.
The framework will not guarantee any minimum level of spend, volume of work or number of call-off contracts. Requirements will be commissioned through the framework call-off arrangements and will be subject to business need, budget availability, approval requirements and supplier performance.
The tender code for etenderwales is itt_127450
Strategic Approach to Supplier Appointment
In order to maximise competition, improve resilience of supply and provide access to a diverse range of specialist providers, DBW has structured this Framework to allow Tenderers to bid for individual disciplines within each Lot.
DBW's approach is intended to support participation from SMEs, micro-businesses, specialist providers and Welsh suppliers who may possess expertise in specific disciplines rather than across all service areas within a Lot.
To ensure continuity of service, competitive tension and sufficient market capacity throughout the term of the Framework Agreement, DBW intends to appoint a minimum of two (2) suppliers and a maximum of four (4) suppliers per discipline within each Lot, subject to a sufficient number of Tenderers meeting the Conditions of Participation and achieving the minimum required evaluation standards.
Where fewer than two compliant Tenderers are received for a particular discipline, DBW reserves the right to proceed with the available compliant Tenderer(s) or take such other action as it considers appropriate in accordance with the procurement documents.
The overall maximum number of suppliers that may be appointed across all Lots and disciplines under the Framework Agreement is 314. This figure represents the total maximum framework capacity and should not be interpreted as the number of suppliers to be appointed to any individual Lot or discipline.
This approach is intended to:
maintain value for money through ongoing competition at call-off;
reduce dependency on individual suppliers;
provide flexibility to meet varying business requirements;
encourage participation from specialist providers;
improve resilience and continuity of service provision; and
support DBW's objective of creating a broad and diverse supplier base capable of delivering high-quality training, coaching and development services.

description: UK7 Contract Details Notice for Riparian Buffer Opportunity Assessment and Delivery Review. Wrexham County Borough Council has entered into a contract with the Dee Trust. Riparian buffers are already being delivered in a number of locations across the Dee catchment as part of ongoing efforts to improve habitat and biodiversity. These existing projects demonstrate both the practicality and value of buffer creation, while also highlighting that current delivery is not yet fully comprehensive or strategically targeted. There remains significant opportunity, including utilising the Sustainable Farming Scheme (SFS) to expand riparian buffer coverage and, importantly, to improve how and where buffers are implemented so that they deliver the greatest environmental benefit. At present, delivery is influenced by a range of factors including practical farming considerations, funding availability, policy drivers and site-specific constraints. To support more effective targeting and future investment decisions, the Nutrient Management Board requires a clearer understanding of where riparian buffers are most needed, what is currently limiting more strategic delivery, and where the greatest opportunities are to build on existing progress within the catchment. The work shall focus on the reaches of the Dee where farming is more intensive and the potential benefits of riparian buffers greatest.

title: Chiltern Rail - Train Planning & Rostering System Replacement
description:
Chiltern Rail is seeking to procure supplier-hosted software solutions and associated services to replace its existing Train Planning and Rostering systems.
The procurement is divided into two Lots:
Lot 1 - Train Planning System; and
Lot 2 - Rostering System.
Lot 1 is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and maintenance of a Train Planning System. The solution is required to support train planning and diagramming activities, including the creation, import, editing, validation, management and publication of timetables, schedules, rolling stock diagrams and traincrew diagrams. The solution must support planning data management, timetable change management, scenario modelling, auditability, version control, reporting, user permissions and secure data exchange with relevant operational and business systems.
Lot 2 is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and maintenance of a Rostering System. The solution is required to support base, weekly and daily rostering for relevant staff groups, including traincrew, station staff and fleet/engineering staff. The solution must support roster creation, validation, publication and management, allocation of staff to duties, management of leave, overtime, shift swaps, fatigue and risk assessment, identification of uncovered turns and roster coverage gaps, employee self-service, reporting, auditability, user permissions and secure data exchange with relevant operational and business systems.
For each Lot, the successful supplier will be required to provide a fully managed, vendor-hosted solution. This includes the software, hosting, configuration, implementation, data migration, integration, testing, training, change management, documentation, support, maintenance, updates, service management, information security, business continuity, disaster recovery, contract management and exit assistance required to deliver and operate the relevant solution.
Bidders may participate in respect of Lot 1, Lot 2, or both Lots.
Chiltern Rail may award Lot 1 and Lot 2 to different suppliers or may award both Lots to the same supplier in accordance with the procurement documents and award methodology.
The estimated value of Lot 1 is £140,000 to £430,000 per annum and £1,000,000 to £3,000,000 over the full contract term, including any optional extension period.
The estimated value of Lot 2 is £210,000 to £500,000 per annum and £1,500,000 to £3,500,000 over the full contract term, including any optional extension period.
The estimated combined value of Lot 1 and Lot 2 is £2,500,000 to £6,500,000 excluding VAT over the full contract term, including any optional extension period.
The estimated contract start date is 26 July 2027. The indicative operational go-live date is 1 March 2028, being the date from which the system is expected to start being rolled out and used by Chiltern Rail staff.
The indicative implementation complete date is 30 June 2028, being the date by which the system is expected to be fully implemented, tested, accepted where applicable, ready for and/or used in live operational production, and to have completed dual running with the incumbent tools.
The initial contract term is expected to be 60 months, with an option for Chiltern Rail to extend for a further period or periods of up to 24 months in total.

title: Progression Towards Employment
description:

Advancing equality of opportunity in the labour market, and reducing social isolation are key drivers for this programme and participants should be given the opportunity to access person-centred, one-to-one support via a Key Worker model, to enable them to participate in activities which have a positive impact on their life, address personal challenges and needs, and improve their life chances. 
The delivery model should offer a varied menu of engaging interventions which will address the most significant or pressing barriers that a participant is facing and help them on their pathway into employment (where this is right for the individual), education/training or further ongoing support. 
Ongoing community engagement and integration is a crucial aspect of this programme, as well as collaboration and partnership working with Stockport Council and other key local stakeholders, in order to support residents needs and ambitions.

title: Sound Exposure Monitoring and Management
description: The BBC operates five full-time orchestras, the BBC Singers and two amateur choruses across the United Kingdom. Together, BBC Orchestras and Choirs undertake a wide range of rehearsals, performances, broadcasts, recordings, education projects and touring activity each year. As part of its commitment to the health, safety and wellbeing of orchestral musicians, singers and other staff, the BBC has an ongoing interest in understanding and managing exposure to elevated sound levels during rehearsals, performances, recordings, broadcasts and other music-making activity. The BBC recognises that sound exposure management within professional music environments can be complex. Exposure levels may vary considerably depending on factors such as repertoire, instrumentation, venue acoustics, amplification, stage layouts, rehearsal schedules and individual positions within an ensemble. Through this RFI, the BBC wishes to engage with the market to better understand the capabilities currently available, how comparable organisations are approaching these challenges and what future developments may be emerging in this area.

title: External Tuition - Kent County Council (KCC) and Medway Council
description:
Purchasing Framework for External Tuition for Special Education Needs (SEN), KCC and Medway Council and Virtual Schools Kent (VSK) External Tuition and Mentoring Services.
Kent County Council (KCC) and Medway Council have a statutory responsibility under The Education Act 1996 to provide education for all children and young people (CYP) until the age of 19, or 25 for those with Education Health Plan (EHCP). Associated legislation includes The Children and Families Act 2014, the SEN Code of Practice (2015), the Equality Act 2010 and The Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Regulations 2014.
Within this statutory framework, KCC is seeking to establish a purchasing framework for those children and young people (CYP) that do not meet the criteria/or capacity has been reached with our inhouse service (The Education Programme) for short-term tuition for students with EHCP.
This work is taking place as a result of the Ofsted and Care Quality Commission (CQC) joint review of SEND provision for Kent CYP and the resulting of an Accelerated Programme Plan (AAP).
Medway Council has also highlighted the need for the council to implement a purchasing framework. This will enable the council greater oversight over the quality of education, inclusive practice, outcomes, and accomplishments for all CYP in Medway.
Together, Medway and Kent working in partnership will ensure there is a robust governance and assurance process in place which provides a joint review to guarantee that Medway and Kent CYP receive quality tutoring and value for money from commissioned providers.
Virtual School Head Teachers (VSHs) are responsible for promoting the educational achievement of all the children looked after by the local authority they work for.
Kent Children in Care (CiC) aged from 3 to 18 years of age are supported by Virtual School Kent (VSK). Pupil Premium Plus funding (PP+) or Early Years Pupil Premium funding (EYPP) can be used to pay for activities that will: -
• Improve the learning targets in children's Personal Education Plans (PEPs).
• Encourage CiC to be more involved and interested in their education.

title: Sussex Heritage Coast Visitor Management Plan
description:
The ambition is the development of a strategic Management Plan, formed 
from a partnership of public and private landowners, supported by other stakeholders, in the Seven Sisters, Beachy Head, Lullington Heath and Friston Forest area, loosely known as the Sussex Heritage Coast. The management plan seeks to identify the existing issues and opportunities for economic, environmental and social enhancement, including Public Health associated with suicide prevention and intervention, in the protected landscape between Seaford and Eastbourne.
The scope of this work will be a stakeholder-agreed long term Strategic Vision document for the Sussex Heritage Coast area, along with a proposed delivery plan for the first five years. 
3.3.2	This document will provide the strategic vision for all aspects of visitor experience and supporting local communities to maximise benefits on subjects, including; 
•	Sustainable visitor management and dispersal 
•	Sustainable transport, active travel and site connectivity, research and development for improving access for people in nature.
•	Supporting visitor economy growth 
•	Identifying market challenges and opportunities for growth including technology and innovation
•	Embracing cultural heritage, artisan crafts and small enterprise
•	Coordinated marketing / comms to promote the area for nature and people
•	Shared approach to public safety e.g. suicide prevention, cliff safety, beach & river safety
•	Protecting and promoting nature recovery
There will be three out deliverables for this project in line with the phases highted in section 4. These will be: 
Phase 1 	Findings report presented at a stakeholder meeting.
Phase 2 	Draft themes report presented at a stakeholder meeting
Findings report presented at a stakeholder meeting.
Phase 3 	Final document and delivery plan presented at a stakeholder meeting.

title: Provision of Digital Autopsy Services
description:
Birmingham City Council wishes to establish a framework agreement for the provision of Digital Autopsy Services. 
Digital Autopsy Service - A Digital Autopsy is a non-invasive post-mortem, referred to 	as a CTPM short for Computed Tomography Post-Mortem.
A CTPM is a scan of the deceased, conducted by a radiographer using a CT scanner.   Following which, the resultant scans are analysed by a GMC registered radiologist to produce an interpretation in the form of a digital autopsy report.
The digital autopsy report contains or suggests the cause of death for consideration by a pathologist at Birmingham Central mortuary. Section 1 of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 places a duty on the coroner to investigate certain deaths.  Section 14 of the Coroners Act 2009 allows the coroner to order a suitable post-mortem examination to enable the coroner to decide if Section 1 applies. CTPM’s are an innovative technology that should in the future prevent invasive post-mortems, which many families and some religions would like to see avoided.
This procurement relates to a call-off under a Framework Agreement, which does not guarantee or commit any level of expenditure.
The framework agreement will commence on 01 October 2026 and will be in place for a period of 2 + 1 years subject to performance and budget availability. (Unless terminated under the terms and conditions
 of the contract)
