title: Reopening of the Over 65 Residential Care Home Framework for Swindon
description:
Swindon Borough Council invites expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced service providers for admission to the existing Over 65 Years of Age Residential Care Home Framework for Swindon.
Project Description
Swindon Borough Council is undertaking the first annual re-opening of its existing Residential Care Home Framework for adults aged 65 years and over within the Swindon locality. This Framework was originally commissioned under public contract regulations and will continue to use this until the end of the total term. This framework commenced on 1st January 2026 and is currently operating within the initial contract period. Existing Framework providers are not required to reapply as part of this process. Successful applicants will join the existing Framework from 1st January 2027.
This procurement exercise does not constitute a new procurement or re-tender of the Framework. It provides an opportunity for providers that are not currently admitted to the Framework, or that were unsuccessful in previous application rounds, to apply for admission to the Framework.
The Framework has an initial term ending on 31st December 2027, with the option for the Council to extend by up to two further periods of two years each, resulting in a maximum potential Framework duration of six years from the original commencement date. Providers admitted through this re-opening exercise may remain on the Framework for the remainder of the Framework term, subject to extension options being exercised and continued compliance with contractual requirements.
The estimated value of placements commissioned through the Framework during the period 1st January 2027 to 31st December 2027 is approximately £12 million, with a potential maximum Framework value of approximately £60 million should all extension periods be exercised.
The Framework will continue to be re-opened annually via the Supplying the South West Portal to allow additional providers to apply for admission.
The Framework will be advertised and all applicants must meet the minimum selection and award criteria to be admitted to the Framework.
This Framework is for in-borough residential care homes only.
For all over-65 residential care needs (standard, enhanced and complex), providers will be required to operate within the Council's published fee structure. Acceptance of the Council's fee structure will form part of the Framework requirements.
To participate, suppliers must register as a supplier with ProContract at www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk and register an interest in the opportunity before obtaining access to the tender documents. In the event of difficulties registering as a supplier, please contact the Proactis Support Team at ProContractSuppliers@proactis.com
Tender clarification deadline: 7th October 2026, 12:00 noon (UK Local Time). Clarification questions must be submitted via the Messaging facility within the ProContract portal. Responses will be issued periodically through the portal.
Tender submission deadline: 14th October 2026, 12:00 noon (UK Local Time), via the ProContract portal: https://www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk/
Please note that this opportunity may be advertised on Find a Tender Service, Contracts Finder and other procurement websites; however, Supplying the South West Portal is the only portal containing all documentation required to submit a response. The procurement reference is DN831353
No tender submissions will be considered without completing the tender documents in full, including all required attachments, and submitting them in accordance with the instructions contained within the tender documentation

• progress towards formal learning or employment
• improve their health and well-being, including mental health
• develop stronger communities
• help parents to strengthen their children's educational success
The aim of the programme is to widen participation in learning across our communities, especially among groups that are hardest to reach. This involves not only removing barriers to learning but also actively promoting the benefits of learning and encouraging participation. Increasing access to learning will create opportunities for success and progression for a much broader cross section of residents, positively impacting the social, financial and health circumstances of many people in Somerset. Our intentions and priorities for the programme are set out later in this document. Locally based Community Learning supports residents to develop wider outcomes for their personal lives which, in turn, positively influences their communities, local businesses and the wider local economy.

The scope of the Monitor's role is intended to be consistent with undertakings accepted by Ofwat in its enforcement decisions concerning water supply resilience and customer care during supply interruption incidents, and compliance with a licence condition requiring the company to hold two Issuer Credit Ratings that are Investment Grade Ratings.
The IM will support Ofwat's monitoring of the company's delivery of remediation actions required under the undertakings, including the development and implementation of a Performance Improvement Plan.
The IM will provide independent assessment of progress, governance, risk management and delivery confidence, identify material risks to compliance and delivery, and report findings to Ofwat. The IM will support proportionate, risk-based regulatory oversight, while maintaining clear accountability with the company for delivery of the required improvements.
The scope is expected to evolve during the contract term in response to the company's performance, risk profile and progress against the undertakings. The monitoring approach must therefore be scalable, risk-based and proportionate.
The IM will be appointed by Ofwat, act independently of the company and provide advice and recommendations to Ofwat only.
The costs of the independent monitor will be met by the Company, and will not impact on customer bills.

title: Nuclear Safeguards Programme
description:
The Nuclear Safeguards Programme (NSP) provides international nuclear safeguards technical support to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ). 
Nuclear safeguards are technical measures to verify that States comply with their international obligations not to misuse nuclear materials for the manufacture of nuclear explosives.  They are an essential part of the nuclear non-proliferation regime and underpin the international system of assurance which enables trade in civil nuclear material, equipment and technology between states – as such they have a key enabling role in the UK’s own plans for civil nuclear energy as part of the low carbon energy mix.      
The NSP is part of the UK contribution to the maintenance of the international safeguards regime with main aims as follows:    
- to assist the IAEA in ensuring the continued and improved effectiveness of its safeguards system and to influence the formulation of technical safeguards policy in the IAEA;   
- to assist the United Kingdom in meeting international obligations under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (‘the NPT’) in as cost-effective a manner as possible;  
- to provide direct safeguards and technical support to DESNZ and the wider UK Government to assist in the formulation of domestic policy on safeguards and non-proliferation issues
Market engagement

title: SEL ICB (Bexley) Primary Care Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) Hub
description:
NHS South East London Integrated Care Board intends to commission a time-limited Primary Care Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) Hub for the London Borough of Bexley for winter 2026/27. The service will provide additional same-day urgent face-to-face appointment capacity for children and adults presenting with ARI-type symptoms, supporting general practice and the wider urgent and emergency care system during the period of increased winter demand. 
The planned service period is 1 December 2026 to 28 February 2027, with an optional extension of up to one month. The service is expected to operate from a centrally located Bexley primary care location during core general practice hours, Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 18:30, and to be staffed by a GP and an Advanced Nurse Practitioner, supported by appropriate administrative capacity. The service will accept referrals from Bexley GP practices and NHS 111, with approximately 10-15% of appointment capacity ringfenced for NHS 111. 
The ICB proposes to use the Most Suitable Provider process under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. This notice communicates the intended approach. The ICB will assess relevant providers against the statutory key criteria and will retain an evidence-based audit trail of its market assessment, evaluation, value-for-money review and award decision.
Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) hubs are a recognised NHS England model used across England to support the assessment and treatment of respiratory illness and to reduce pressure on emergency departments, urgent treatment centres and general practice. The proposed Bexley model reflects an established primary care-led approach that has operated within the borough over successive winter periods and is consistent with nationally recognised ARI hub delivery models.
Key service objectives and outcomes
•	Provide additional same-day urgent primary care capacity for Bexley residents with ARI-type presentations during winter pressure.
•	Provide a clinically safe alternative pathway for people who can appropriately be managed in primary care, while maintaining clear escalation routes for patients requiring urgent or emergency treatment.
•	Support timely access for adults and children referred by Bexley general practice and NHS 111.
•	Support resilience across Bexley general practice and the wider urgent and emergency care system.
•	Deliver equitable access, with operational monitoring to identify and respond to variation in referral, utilisation and outcomes across patient groups and localities.
•	Maintain effective integration with general practice, NHS 111, urgent treatment and secondary care pathways.
The provider is expected to demonstrate a proven track record in delivering an acute respiratory infection service or a similar service for a minimum of three years in South East London, with prior experience in meeting the key objectives and service requirements as outlined.
buyer: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board

We use the Public Health Commissioning process to provide a shared understanding of local need, to develop our commissioning intentions, to inform procurement and to evaluate and review whether we are enabling victims, their families and children and those who engage in abusive behaviours to have their needs met effectively.
Provision of Domestic Abuse Community Support Services, Cornwall Council will be the lead commissioner for these services on behalf of the Safer Cornwall Partnership.
The opportunity will comprise of the following 3 lots and the maximum opportunity of this contract is a period of 10 years. Comprising of an initial 5 year contract term, which may be followed by up to two optional extension clauses, the first of which is 3 years and then a further for 2 years providing the maximum opportunity of 10 years.
Lot 1 - Community Domestic Abuse Service - helpline and advocacy
To include;
• Provision of a Domestic Abuse helpline.
• Independent Domestic Violence Advisor (IDVA) Service on a need led basis.
• Health and Primary Care IDVA Services.
• Drop-in services.
• Trauma stabilisation experienced/ witnessed and/or been impacted by domestic abuse.
• Assertive outreach for those with multiple vulnerabilities.
• Peer mentoring and volunteering opportunities.
Lot 2 - Community Domestic Abuse Service - recovery and therapeutic support
To include;
• Recovery and therapeutic support programmes delivered via both 1:1 and group support including trauma stabilisation and trauma processing for those impacted by domestic abuse adults and children.
• Behaviour change and interventions (abusive person) programme (for adults and children).
• Trauma stabilisation interventions for those who have experienced/ witnessed and/or been impacted by domestic abuse.
• Peer mentoring programme
• Psychoeducational interventions for adults and children affected by Domestic abuse.
Lot 3 - Domestic Abuse Training and education

Guildford Borough Council are seeking expression of interest from D&B Contractors for the refurbishment of 19 light industrial units constructed in the 1980’s which have now reached the end of their useful life  and require significant upgrading works.  The Council intends to follow a 2-stage Design & Build procurement route comprising a Stage 1 PCSA followed by a Stage 2 Design & Build Contract The contractor will be required to assume responsibility for completion of the design and delivery of the works under a Design & Build contract.
Arranged in three terraces, to provide individual self-contained units, the construction is steel frame with powder coated, profiled steel sheeting and incorporating glazed panels. Each unit has an up and over loading door (manually operated) along with personnel door. Internally the units are single storey and open plan except for a WC block. Electricity and gas are connected. The eaves height is approx. 3.2 m. The units were originally built with lighting but no heating, though over the years some tenants have installed heating and internal fit outs to varying degrees. Externally there is parking, circulation areas and landscaping.
Floor areas: Buildings: 1,155 sq m GIA (Combined units)
Total Site area: 4,611 sq m (1.14 acres).
The units are currently failing the Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES) regulations.
The Council is now undertaking a programme of refurbishment to upgrade the existing accommodation to a standard that meets occupier requirements, ensuring compliance with MEES regulation, whilst seeking to achieve an EPC rating of ‘A’ across the estate.
Scope of works:
Unit mix:
•	8 single bay (mid terrace) 56 sqm
•	3 single bay (end terrace) 59 sqm
•	3 twin bay 117 sqm
•	1 triple bay 172 sqm
Total number of units:15
Total gross internal area: 1,148 sqm (all ground floor as per existing).
The appointment is expected to be split into a 2 stage tender:
Stage 1: Appointment under a Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA) to develop the design, support planning, undertake surveys, develop the contractor's proposals, programme and target cost/open book pricing. This is to include but is not limited to:
•	Develop designs and submit planning application
•	Review buildability
•	Undertake surveys
•	Develop construction methodology
•	Review phasing and tenant impacts
•	Develop programme
•	Develop package procurement strategy
•	Produce open-book pricing
•	Identify risks and value engineering opportunities
Stage 2: Subject to successful completion of Stage 1, approval of the developed design, agreed contract sum and governance approvals, the Council may enter into a Design & Build Contract with the Stage 1 contractor to deliver the works.
The construction works are likely to include:
•	Recladding of the three existing terraces including associated work to mechanical and electrical services, if required, and repairs to external works.
•	New doors and windows
•	PV panels to upgrade to EPC A only as required
•	Limited landscaping works and tree works
•	No new service connections
•	No significant external works other than making good and repair
Draft Timescales:
Soft market engagement: October 2026
Executive Approval: October 2026
ITT for PCSA Stage 1: October– December 2026
PCSA Stage 1: Contract Award: January 2027
RIBA 1-3 (until planning submission): February – March 2027
Stage 2 Contract Negotiation, Governance and Award: April – September 2027
Construction: January 2028 – December 2028

title: 2025-061 Technical Auditing for Engineering
description:
This procurement is for auditors to be employed by Ofgem, to carry out asset management audits and engineering asset assurance inspections at gas and electricity sites.
Ofgem requires a supplier to assess, inspect and investigate the asset management systems and equipment of licensees with a view to providing assurance that suitable governance is in place and equipment is being maintained in accordance with the relevant standards in practice.
In order to do so, the suppliers may be required, but not limited to the following pieces of work:
Item 1
The suppliers would provide their expert view on the following:
Whether the Licensee’s asset management policies and procedures are fit for purpose and consistent with international best practice. Additionally, the supplier would provide an assessment of asset management maturity within the organisation.
Whether licensees are following these policies and procedures correctly, in terms of the monitoring, maintenance and repair/replacement of their assets and whether the staff responsible for completing these procedures are appropriately trained.
Whether licensees are accurately recording these activities, including into Network Asset Risk Metrics (NARMs)/other metrics, and making appropriate/timely interventions where issues are identified through such measures and otherwise.
Item 2
The Inspectors provided by the suppliers will be employed to carry out engineering asset assurance surveys and Inspections at onshore gas and electricity sites.
The scope of services, as further detailed in Annex A technical specification, would include (but is not limited to) the following:
To inspect key electricity assets and systems including: transformers, reactors, circuit breakers, protection & control equipment, auxiliary systems, high voltage connections, cabling, busbars and buscouplers, disconnectors, earth switches, civil structures, fire suppression equipment, batteries, overhead lines (including towers and poles) and cables (including fluid filled systems, cooling and monitoring equipment).
To inspect key gas assets and systems including: gas terminals, local distribution zone offtakes, above ground installations, pipeline safety and maintenance records, compressor stations, protection and control equipment, metering installations, odorant injection facilities, storage facilities, pressure control installations, auxiliary systems, civil structures, associated electrical and communication & instrumentation installations, gas monitoring and fire suppression equipment, pre-heating and cooling installations.
For above assets that are within scope of the audit, review of maintenance schedules and plans and historic maintenance records, defects and repairs; also audit of technical and performance data submitted to Ofgem.
The supplier’s inspectors will be asked to give a view as part of submitted reports and or presentations to Ofgem, on the adequacy of the maintenance regime, maintenance performance and forward plans for the assets based on their findings from the site visits and review of maintenance schedules and maintenance records. The supplier’s inspectors will also need to make recommendations on improvements to maintenance plans and performance where they identify gaps and shortcomings based on their findings from the audit, their knowledge of best practice and experience of working with other operators of similar equipment.
Item 3
The supplier’s inspectors may also be asked to investigate the circumstances of electricity or gas network incidents or issues and provide a technical report to Ofgem setting out the root cause with conclusions about the wider circumstances and recommendations to ensure compliance with the relevant standards and policies. This work would involve:
Inspecting the relevant plant and equipment
Researching the circumstances of the incident or issue by reviewing data and other information
Writing a report on findings and presenting it to Ofgem.
For each inspection, Ofgem will require the suppliers to:
A report on the findings from a process and procedures audit on each licensee.
Item 1.
A report detailing the findings of each site audit carried out.
Item 2.
A report detailing the facts and conclusions of a network incident.
Item 3.
A presentation to Ofgem setting out the findings from each audit / inspection / investigation.

All Works and Services to be delivered are expected to meet Yellow Book Standards where applicable.
• Lot 1 - GI Works (contract value over 100K)
• Lot 2 - GI Services (contract value over 100k)
• Lot 3 - GI Works (contract value below 100k)
• Lot 4 - GI Services (contract value below 100k)
• Lot 5 – Ground Water Investigation Works and Services (contract value below 100k)
The proposed GI Framework Specification will cover a range of GI Works and Services, which will include:
• Intrusive investigations (boreholes, trial pits, probe holes),
• In-situ testing and instrumentation,
• Groundwater monitoring and pumping tests,
• Specialist investigations (e.g. embankment dams, floodplain deposits, peat, contaminated land, mineral workings).
• Drilling - (Window Sampling, Cable percussion, Rotary, Slope Climbing)
• Field Testing
• Geophysical Testing
• Installation Monitoring and Sampling
• Reinstatement
• Daily Records
• Surveying
• Lab testing (during works supervision)
• Reporting
• Works Supervision
• Lab Testing (after works supervision or survey)
• Reporting
• Desk studies and development of Ground Models
• Geotechnical Consulting
Lot 1 and 2 Opportunities
Reservoirs
The Fens Reservoir is situated between Chatteris and March in Cambridgeshire with a target date to start construction by 2029.
The Lincolnshire Reservoir is situated south-east of Sleaford, about halfway between Grantham and Boston with a target date to start construction by 2031. 
Both reservoir projects plan to have continued large scale GI requirements over the next 2 to 5 years in the run up to submission of the Development Consent Orders (DCO). 
Desalination and Water Recycling  
GI is expected to be required to enable construction of de-salination plants in Bacton, Mablethorpe and, Holland on Sea as well as an advanced water recycling plant in Colchester.
Strategic Pipeline Alliance 
The Strategic Pipeline Alliance (SPA) is a new network of large-scale interconnecting pipelines and associated infrastructure stretching from North Lincolnshire to Essex.  The pipeline will be 580km in total; including an addition of 260km of interconnectors in AMP8. 
GI will be required on the SPA projects to inform the design of the proposed interconnector assets including pipelines, thrust blocks, valves, storage tanks, pumping stations, as well as several trenchless crossings.
Lot 3 and 4 Opportunities
The @One Alliance is a long-standing capital alliance of 8 strategic partners who deliver more than half of our capital investment programme. Projects undertaken by this workstream are typically preparation and testing work for smaller scale construction projects that fall outside of the remit of the Major Infrastructure workstream. Typically, this could be the restoration or assembly of new Water Treatment Works, Water Recycling Centres and renewing or providing essential new infrastructure pipework to support the growth of water and wastewater distribution.
Generally, these are regular small to medium sized projects, with[SW2.1] a typical estimated value of between £20k and less than £100k per GI package of works. Quick turnaround times are generally required.
Lot 5 Opportunities
The Ground Water Operations Team ensure full operability of groundwater assets to maintain the upstream security of supply. 
This team require borehole drilling to collect groundwater quality data or water level data.
Generally, these are regular small to medium sized projects, with a typical estimated value of between £20k and less than £100k per GI package of works. Quick turnaround times are generally required.

title: Contract for the Supply of Hydroacoustic River Flow Instrumentation
description:
The Authority previously undertook preliminary market engagement in relation to this requirement under notice reference (2025/S 000-084584). Following the cancellation of the previous procurement due to a publishing issue, the Authority is undertaking further market engagement to update suppliers and validate current market conditions prior to recommencing the procurement.
The Environment Agency’s Hydrometry teams monitor water quantity across rivers, streams, lakes, and groundwater aquifers. Hydroacoustic instruments are used to measure water discharge in these environments. 
A hydroacoustic contract is required to secure specialist services and equipment that utilise sound in water to achieve objectives not feasible with other technologies. Area Hydrometry and Telemetry teams purchase and operate these instruments, with technical support and procurement guidance provided by the National Hydrometry team.
The Environment Agency has selected hydroacoustic instruments as a highly accurate, long-term, and cost-effective solution for measuring water. These instruments support both routine measurements and long-term monitoring programmes, which are critical for:
Trend Analysis – Tracking changes in river flows, lake levels, and groundwater over time to understand hydrological patterns.
Flood Risk Management – Providing accurate discharge data to improve flood forecasting and early warning systems.
Climate Resilience – Assessing the impact of climate change on water resources and informing adaptation strategies.
Regulatory Compliance – Meeting statutory obligations for water quantity reporting and supporting environmental legislation.
Infrastructure Planning – Supplying data for water resource management, reservoir operations, and sustainable development.
The instruments fall into three main categories:
Mobile profiling instruments
Waded point-velocity instruments
Fixed-deployment profiling instruments
To facilitate procurement and ensure continuity of long-term monitoring, the Environment Agency intends to establish commercial agreements for a fixed two-year period with an optional 1 year extension covering the following lots:
Lot 1. Mobile acoustic profiling instrument 0-20m depth
Lot 2. Mobile acoustic multipoint velocity waded instrument 0-1m depth
Lot 3. Short range fixed velocity profiling instrument 0-5m
Lot 4. Long range fixed velocity profiling instrument 0-100m
The following UK public sector bodies are authorised and enabled to use the contract, The 
Environment Agency (EA), Natural Resource Wales (NRW) and the Scottish Environment 
Protection Agency (SEPA).

title: Visual Asset Inspector Accreditation for Flood, Coastal and Environmental Assets
description:
This contract relates to three departments who help us fulfil our responsibilities across England. The three departments are Flood & Coastal Risk Management (FCRM), Water, Land & Biodiversity (WLB) and Navigation. They each use a wide variety of operational assets, which are described in more detail below.
To be an effective and efficient asset manager we require staff working for, or on behalf of, us to have suitable skills, knowledge and experience. A key role contributing to the management of our ‘fixed’, not Mechanical, Electrical Instrumentation, Control and Automation (MEICA), assets is undertaken by externally accredited, Asset Inspectors (AIs). AIs visit our assets and visually assess their condition.
Background to existing contract
The current/existing contract (Ref: C12962) with JBA for the T98 & T98a Visual Asset Inspection (New accreditation and Reaccreditation- Area Health check) training ends 21/10/2026. 
We have used the last of the extensions (4 +1+1) so we needed to undertake a procurement. 
To ensure continuation of service, we have completed a compliant procurement exercise in time to commence the new contract on 22/10/2026. Additionally, there is the potential for further work to assist the EA in developing the course and providing technical advice. 
Objective 
The overarching objective of this procurement is to ensure that Asset Inspectors (AIs) working for, or on behalf of, the Environment Agency (EA) are able to carry out visual inspections of EA assets competently, consistently, and safely.
To achieve this, all AIs must successfully complete and pass the T98 Visual Asset Accreditation course, which serves as the recognised standard for assessing inspector capability. The appointed Contractor will be responsible for:
• Assessing competence: Evaluating whether candidates have achieved the required level of knowledge, technical understanding, and practical capability to undertake inspections to EA standards.
• Accreditation decision-making: Determining whether individuals meet the pass criteria and can be formally accredited as Asset Inspectors.
• Quality and consistency assurance: Ensuring assessments are applied consistently and in line with agreed standards, maintaining credibility and reliability across the EA estate.
Accreditation is valid for a maximum of five years, after which inspectors must undergo a reaccreditation process to confirm ongoing competence and alignment with current standards and practices.
The high-level specification therefore requires a solution that:
• Delivers robust, standardised assessment and accreditation processes
• Ensures consistency and quality across all assessments and assessors
• Supports safe inspection practices and risk awareness
• Provides a sustainable accreditation lifecycle, including refresher/reaccreditation provision
• Maintains appropriate records, auditability, and reporting to evidence compliance and performance
This defined outcome and specification form the foundation for the subsequent procurement strategy, including delivery model options, commercial approach, and evaluation criteria.

title: Ireland – Construction work for electricity power lines – The MaresConnect 750MW HVDC Interconnector System
description: The MaresConnect Project is a proposed 750 MW, 320 kV High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) electricity interconnector linking Denbighshire, Wales and North County Dublin, Ireland. Developed by MaresConnect Limited, a joint venture between Foresight Group Holdings Ltd and Etchea Energy Nominees Ltd, the project will transmit electricity via approximately 240 km of subsea and underground cables between new converter stations on each side. It aims to enhance security of supply, market integration, and renewable energy utilisation between the Irish and GB grids. MaresConnect shall utilise Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology and the configuration shall be a Symmetrical Monopole. The rated DC voltage shall be +/-320 kV. The link shall be bi-directional and shall have a rated power (receiving end) of 750 MW. The project is being procured as separate EPC (Turnkey) contracts, divided into four lots: LOT 1A: EPC for two HVDC Converter Stations; LOT 1B: EPC for one Irish 400kV AC Tail Substation; LOT 2A: EPC for the HVDC subsea and underground cable system, and for the HVAC underground cable system in Wales (Bodelwyddan); LOT 2B: EPC for the supply and installation of HVAC cable system in Ireland (Dublin). The contract model for the lots will be amended FIDIC Conditions of Contract for EPC/Turnkey Projects (Silver Book). MaresConnect has conducted Preliminary Market Engagement prior to publication of this Contract Notice and encourages further collaboration between OEMs and Construction Contractors to establish bidding arrangements in time for the next step of the Procurement Process (notably the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire).

title: Germany – Artificial and natural lighting engineering services for buildings – Dienstleistungen für Lichttechnik und Tageslichttechnik – Dynamisches Beschaffungssystem "Planungsleistungen Beleuchtungsumrüstung" hier: Vergebene Aufträge im 2. Quartal 2025
description: Die AG verwaltet bundesweit Liegenschaften diverser Bundesbehörden im Rahmen des einheitlichen Liegenschaftsmanagements. Im Zuge des gesetzlich festgeschriebenen Auslaufs der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen T5 und T8 zum 25.08.2023, bedarf es zur Aufrechterhaltung der Ausleuchtung eines vollständigen Austausches der verbauten Leuchtstofflampen durch eine LED-Beleuchtung. Diese Umstellung soll sukzessiv in einzelnen Sprints im Rahmen eines dynamischen Beschaffungssystems (DBS) erfolgen. Die Planungsleistungen werden in einer agilen Vorgehensweise in unterschiedlichen Umfängen der zu sanierenden Liegenschaften benötigt. Die AG wird die Planungsleistungen für die jeweiligen Liegenschaften in einzelnen Sprints, im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens, vergeben. Dadurch soll es auch KMU ermöglicht werden die Leistungen zu erbringen. Die Leistungserbringung umfasst Planungsleistungen, die zur Planung, Beratung, Ausschreibung, Bauleitung sowie für die spätere Umsetzung in Anlehnung an die LPH 1 bis 8 des § 55 HOAI erforderlich sind. Der Leistungsschwerpunkt liegt auf Planungsleistungen in den KG 440 (445), der Auftrag umfasst dabei alle weiteren Planungsleistungen, die zur Erreichung des Auftragsziels erforderlich sind. Im Wesentlichen sind folgende Leistungen angelehnt an § 55 HOAI für die Beleuchtungsumrüstung zu erbringen: - Bestandsaufnahme aller Leuchten einer Liegenschaft durch tabellarische Dokumentation folgender Merkmale: Leuchte, Leuchtmittel, Nutzungsart des Raumes, Deckenhöhe, Reflexionsgrad der Wände, Schaltung der Beleuchtung, Anzahl der Leuchten pro Stromkreis, Anzahl der Adern zu Leuchten/Schalter - Erstellen von Grundrisszeichnungen, falls diese nicht vorliegen - Fachplanungsleistungen KG 440 und 445 - Ausführungsplanung - Beleuchtungsberechnung mit Berechnungssoftware Dialux oder Relux - Planung der Beleuchtungsanlagen nach der AMEV-Empfehlung „Beleuchtung 2019“, der DIN EN 12464 sowie der ASR 3.4 in der jeweils gültigen Fassung - Erstellung von Wartungsplänen nach DIN EN 12464-1 - Erstellung von Termin- und Ablaufplänen für die Umsetzung der Baumaßnahmen - Vorbereitung und Mitwirkung bei der Vergabe - Objekt- und Bauüberwachung Im Zusammenhang damit sind z.B. auch folgende Planungsleistungen von Randbereichen / Nebenleistungen insbesondere in folgenden Bereichen – soweit im Einzelfall erforderlich – zu erbringen: Einfache Schlitz- und Durchbruchsarbeiten, Verputzarbeiten, Trockenbauarbeiten, Malerarbeiten, Gerüstbau/Gerüststellung. Die Leistungen sind grds. im Dokument „Leistungsverzeichnis“ dargestellt, im weiteren Stadium behält sich die AG vor, den Leistungsumfang zu spezifizieren. Die AG weist darauf hin, dass die gesamten Vergabeunterlagen – insb. der Prozessablaufplan - der Fortschreibung unterliegen und im Laufe des DBS jederzeit angepasst werden können. Hierüber werden alle Bewerber/Bieter umgehend informiert. Die AG sucht Unternehmen, die diese Planungsleistungen erbringen. Dabei wird die Planung in einzelne Planungsphasen strukturiert (siehe Leistungsverzeichnis, dort a.E. Übersicht differenzierter Planungsleistungen). Einige Leistungen müssen stets erbracht werden, die Erbringung bzw. der jeweilige Umfang der Bedarfs- und Alternativpositionen wird durch die AG auf Grundlage von Entscheidungsvorlagen getroffen. Abhängig von den getroffenen Entscheidungen ist für bestimmte Flächen alternativ der Leuchtmitteltausch oder ein Leuchtentausch zu planen. Für den Fall des Leuchtentausches ist eine weitere Entscheidung hinsichtlich der Planung einer Beleuchtungssteuerung der AG vorgesehen. Sollte eine Beleuchtungssteuerung gefordert sein, sind auch die entsprechenden Bedarfspositionen zu erbringen. Die AG wird ihren Leistungsbedarf im Rahmen eines dynamischen Verfahrens mit jeweils einer Aufforderung zur Angebotsabgabe an die zu diesem Zeitpunkt in dieser Region geeigneten Unternehmen (Bewerberpool) kommunizieren. Dabei sind die Sprints nach den Komplexitätsgraden „Basisprojekte“ und „Komplexe Projekte“ aufgeteilt.

description: Het uitvoeren, coördineren en begeleiden van praktijkgericht emissieonderzoek op twee Brabantse melkveehouderijen als onderdeel van het landelijke programma Netwerk Praktijkbedrijven. De werkzaamheden omvatten de begeleiding van de deelnemende bedrijven, uitvoering van emissiemetingen, verzameling en analyse van bedrijfs- en emissiedata, wetenschappelijke kwaliteitsborging, evaluatie van emissiereducerende maatregelen en rapportage van resultaten. De twee Brabantse bedrijven worden als onderzoeksbedrijven geïntegreerd in de bestaande onderzoeks- en kennisinfrastructuur van Netwerk Praktijkbedrijven, zodat de resultaten onderdeel worden van de landelijke monitoring en kennisontwikkeling rond de reductie van ammoniak- en methaanemissies in de melkveehouderij. De opdracht heeft een looptijd van vier jaar, waarbij in eerste instantie een overeenkomst voor twee jaar wordt aangegaan met een optie tot verlenging met nog eens twee jaar. De geraamde totale waarde van de opdracht bedraagt €800.000 tot €900.000,- (afhankelijk van de eventuele aanwezigheid van meetapparatuur) exclusief btw over de maximale looptijd van vier jaar. Deze raming is gebaseerd op de uitvoering van emissieonderzoek op twee melkveehouderijen, inclusief bedrijfsbegeleiding, metingen, dataverzameling, data-analyse, wetenschappelijke kwaliteitsborging en rapportage. De geraamde kosten bedragen circa €100.000,- per bedrijf per jaar. Voor twee bedrijven komt dit neer op een jaarlijkse opdrachtwaarde van circa €200.000,-. Er is mogelijk nog een investering van €50.000,- per bedrijf nodig voor de aanschaf van meetapparatuur indien deze niet aanwezig is. De provincie is voornemens de overeenkomst in eerste instantie aan te gaan voor een periode van twee jaar, met een geraamde waarde van €400.000,- exclusief btw. De overeenkomst bevat een eenzijdige optie voor de provincie om deze eenmaal te verlengen met een aanvullende periode van twee jaar. Indien van deze verlengingsoptie gebruik wordt gemaakt, bedraagt de totale geraamde opdrachtwaarde €800.000,- exclusief btw.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF -Ermittlung und Bewertung von Dieselmotoremissionen (DME) von Fahrzeugen der Fremdrettungskräfte in Eisenbahntunneln
description: Bei Eisenbahntunneln gemäß der EBA-Ril-Tunnel (Zwei-Röhrenprinzip) ist es im Ereignisfall (z.B. Brand) vorgesehen, dass Einsatzfahrzeuge der Fremdrettungskräfte in die andere, nicht vom Ereignis betroffene Röhre einfahren. Die Fahrzeuge verfügen nahezu ausschließlich über einen Antrieb per Dieselmotor, welcher bei Betrieb entsprechende Emissionen verursacht (Abgase). Im Gegensatz zu Straßentunneln sind in elektrifizierten Eisenbahntunneln keine Systeme zur Abgasabführung vorgesehen. Im Rahmen von Planfeststellungsvorhaben (Beteiligung als Träger öffentlicher Belange) kommt es daher seitens der Fremdrettungskräfte zu Einwänden, dass ein dauerhafter Betrieb von Diesel-Einsatzfahrzeugen im Tunnel auf Grund der Dieselmotoremissionen (DME) nicht möglich sei und die Abgase einen Aufenthalt von Einsatzkräften in der Tunnelröhre auf Dauer verhindern. Gleichwohl bestehen in Bahntunneln üblicherweise natürliche Luftströme, die entsprechende Abgase abführen könnten. Es fehlen derzeit auch Ergebnisse/Erkenntnisse im Allgemeinen zu Strömungsgeschwindigkeiten und deren Auswirkungen auf Luftschadstoffbelastungen in Tunneln in Abhängigkeiten verschiedener Geometrien von Eisenbahntunneln.

title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – 10030774-Providing Technical Assistance on Industrial Decarbonisation, CBAM Readiness, Gender Inclusion, Pilot and Upscaling
description: India's industrial sector plays a central role in the country's economic growth, while also contributing significantly to energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. As India advances its climate ambitions, including the target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070, industrial decarbonisation and energy efficiency have become key priorities for enabling a sustainable and inclusive transition. In this context, the Indo-German bilateral cooperation between the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), implemented by GIZ, supports industrial decarbonisation through energy efficiency measures. Acting as a service provider and implementing agency for German international cooperation for sustainable development, GIZ works with Indian and German partners on project implementation and delivering effective solutions that contribute to sustainable transformation. The cooperation between the German side and BEE builds on a long-standing partnership in the field of energy efficiency and industrial transformation. Over the years, the collaboration has continuously supported the implementation of the Energy Conservation Act and contributed to a range of initiatives targeting both large industries and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). While significant progress has been achieved, considerable untapped potential for industrial energy efficiency and decarbonisation remains, underlining the need for strengthened policy frameworks, innovative market instruments, and scaled implementation approaches. Against this background, the project "Energy Efficiency" supports industrial decarbonisation through four key intervention areas: (a) developing strategies for industrial decarbonisation, including in the context of the Indian Carbon Market; (b) supporting the design and implementation of incentive schemes such as ADEETIE; (c) promoting industrial energy efficiency measures through demonstration projects and awareness campaigns; and (d) advancing gender equality and social inclusion in the industrial transition. Through these interventions, the project aims to strengthen policy frameworks, market mechanisms, institutional capacities, and inclusive approaches for a sustainable industrial transformation.

title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – Nationale Kontaktstelle Schlüsseltechnologien (NKS)
description: Zur Umsetzung der Forschungsrahmenprogramme (FRP) der Europäischen Union haben sich die teilnehmenden Staaten verpflichtet, ein Informations- und Beratungssystem einzurichten. Grundlage für die Einrichtung und Tätigkeit der sog. Nationalen Kontaktstellen (NKS) sind die „Leitsätze der Europäischen Kommission für die Einrichtung Nationaler Kontaktstellen“ (für Horizont Europa). Diese Leitsätze werden durch ein "Gemeinsames Pflichtenheft" des EU-Büros und der Nationalen Kontaktstellen (gültige Version vom 01.10.2024 als Anlage zur Leistungsbeschreibung) ergänzt. Die Bundesregierung unterhält ein Netzwerk von Nationalen Kontaktstellen (NKS). Dieses informiert und berät einerseits die Teilnehmer/-innen am FRP und unterstützt andererseits die Bundesregierung bei der Gestaltung und Durchführung des FRP. Ziel der NKS ist es, eine hohe, effiziente und effektive Beteiligung deutscher Forschungseinrichtungen, Hochschulen und Unternehmen (insbesondere kleine und mittlere Unternehmen - KMU) an den Fördermaßnahmen der Europäischen Union, insb. des Rahmenprogramms für Forschung und Innovation, sicherzustellen. Die Aufgaben beziehen sich inhaltlich bis 31.12.2027 auf die bisher unter dem 9. FRP etablierten Förderthemen zu den digitalen und industriellen Schlüsseltechnologien die in den beiden Programmausschusskonfigurationen der Cluster „Digital, Industry and Space“, „Civil Security for Society“ für Cybersicherheit, sowie den Bereich Mobilität im Cluster „Climate, Energy and Mobility“ behandelt werden. Ab voraussichtlich 01.01.2028 beziehen sich die Aufgaben inhaltlich auf die Förderthemen des 10. FRP zu Schlüsseltechnologien, welche zurzeit in den Policy Windows 1 (Sauberer Übergang und Industrielle Dekarbonisierung) und 3 (Digitale Führung) des Europäischen Fonds für Wettbewerbsfähigkeit verortet sind. Im Sinne der Kontinuität, die Schlüsseltechnologien weiterhin synergetisch zu bündeln, werden die Werkstoffinnovationen mitabgedeckt. Zu den Aufgaben gehört auch die Begleitung anderer Programmteile des FRP, wie bspw. aus dem Programmteil Innovation des „European Innovation Council (EIC)“ oder des „European Institute for Technology and Knowledge and Innovation Centres (EIT-KIC)“, sofern relevante technologieorientierte Aktivitäten verankert sein können oder sich entsprechende Förderaktivitäten (z.B. Missionen oder sonstige Partnerschaften) über verschiedene Programmteile erstrecken.

title: France – Consultative engineering and construction services – Mission de maîtrise d’œuvre globale (bâtiment et process industriel thermique) pour la construction d'une centrale de production de chaleur par hydrothermie à Toulouse
description: La présente consultation s'inscrit dans le cadre de la Délégation de Service Public (DSP) relative au réseau de chaleur et de froid urbain « Plaine Campus », concédée par Toulouse Métropole à la société Toulouse Énergie Durable (TED). Afin de répondre aux enjeux de transition énergétique et de sécurisation de l'approvisionnement, l'avenant n°7 au contrat de DSP prévoit une extension majeure du réseau et une densification des moyens de production via des énergies renouvelables. L'opération consiste en la création d'un outil de production de chaleur innovant utilisant l'énergie de la Garonne. Ce projet vise à augmenter le taux d'EnRR du réseau à plus de 85%. Le projet consiste en la réhabilitation et la transformation d'un bâtiment existant emblématique situé sur l'Île du Ramier en une centrale hydrothermique de 5.5Mc. title: Germany – Overhead line construction – Netzverstärkung Güstrow - Wolmirstedt Montage-/Demontageleistungen zum Ersatzneubau der 380-kV- Leitung Perleberg-Stendal West 485/486
description: Der AG plant im Zuge der Energiewende zur Erfüllung der gesetzlichen Verpflichtung einer sicheren Energieversorgung die Umsetzung des Vorhabens „Stromtragfähigkeitserhöhung Perleberg – Stendal West“. Das Vorhaben ist ein Abschnitt der im BBPlG als Teil des Vorhabens 39 (Höchstspannungsleitung Güstrow – Parchim/Süd – Perleberg – Stendal/West – Wolmirstedt; Drehstrom Nennspannung 380 kV) geführten Einzelmaßnahme „Perleberg – Stendal West – Wolmirstedt“. Gegenstand des Vorhabens: Die vorhandene 220-kV-Leitung ist zwischen dem UW Perleberg und dem UW Stendal West durch eine leistungsfähigere 380-kV-Leitung mit 3.600 Ampere Stromtragfähigkeit zu ersetzen. Mit Erlass des Bundesbedarfsplans wird für die darin enthaltenen Vorhaben die energiewirtschaftliche Notwendigkeit und der vordringliche Bedarf festgestellt. Die Feststellungen sind für die Übertragungsnetzbetreiber verbindlich, § 12e Abs. 4 EnWG. Abgesehen von kleinräumigen Trassenoptimierungen im Abschnitt Sachsen-Anhalt bei Losenrade und südlich von Rochau bis zum UW Stendal West ist geplant, die neue 380-kV-Freileitung in der Trasse der vorhandenen 220-kV-Freileitung aus den Jahren 1953/1958 zu errichten. Das Vorhaben führt zwar von Mecklenburg-Vorpommern nach Sachsen-Anhalt, ist aber im Bundesbedarfsplan dennoch nicht als länderübergreifend gekennzeichnet. Der Baubeginn ist ab August 2027 geplant. Die Inbetriebnahme des Vorhabens ist bis spätestens August 2029 vorzusehen. Im Rahmen der Ausschreibung ist zu prüfen, ob eine Inbetriebnahme bereits in Q4 2028 durchgeführt werden kann. Die vorliegende Montageausschreibung umfasst: - die Errichtung der 380-kV-Freileitung 485/486 von Perleberg nach Stendal West von Mast 10 bis Portal UW Stendal West (STW) - die Errichtung des 4-System-Gestänges im Bereich von Mast 58 bis Mast 61, um die von der DB Energie geplante 110-kV-Bahnstromleitung Insel – Wittenberge mitzuführen - die Errichtung von 4-System-Gestängen in den Bereichen von Mast 82 bis Mast 86 und von Mast 159 bis 172, um die Mitnahme der 50Hertz-eigenen 380-kV-Leitung 515/516/596 Putlitz Süd – Stendal West umzusetzen - die Errichtung von Provisorien in den Bereichen von Mast 82 bis Mast 86 und von Mast 159 bis 172, um den dauerhaften Betrieb der 50Hertz-eigenen 380-kV-Leitung 515/516/596 Putlitz Süd – Stendal West zu gewährleisten - die Errichtung der Masten 112N, 112AN, 117AN und 185N zur Ein- und Ausschleifung der 50Hertz-eigenen 380-kV-Leitung 515/516/596 Putlitz Süd – Stendal West auf den 4-System-Gestängen - den Rückbau der 220-kV-Leitung 331/332 von Mast 347W bis Mast 108W - den Rückbau der Masten 112 bis 117 und 185 bis 195 der 380-kV-Leitung 515/516/596 Putlitz Süd – Stendal West Geplante 380-kV-Freileitung Perleberg – Stendal West (485/486): Die geplante Trasse erstreckt sich über eine Gesamtlänge von ca. 63 km und verläuft von Mast 10 südöstlich des Umspannwerkes Perleberg bis zum Portal des Umspannwerkes Stendal West. Der Ersatzneubau erfolgt weitgehend innerhalb des bestehenden Trassenraumes der vorhandenen 220-kV-Leitung. Lediglich im Abschnitt Sachsen-Anhalt wurden kleinräumige Trassenanpassungen im Bereich Losenrade sowie südlich von Rochau bis zum Umspannwerk Stendal West vorgesehen. 220-kV-Bestandsleitung Güstrow – Wolmirstedt (331/332): Die 220-kV-Bestandsleitung verlief ursprünglich von Güstrow nach Wolmirstedt. Für die Ausschreibung relevant ist der Bereich von Mast 347W bis Mast 108W mit einer Länge von ca. 71 km. Die Bestandsleitung wurde größtenteils in den Jahren 1953 und 1958 als Einebenenmast erbaut. Leistungsbeschreibung: Der Ersatzneubau der 380-kV-Leitung Perleberg – Stendal West gliedert sich in 4 Baulose, die ggf. durch unterschiedliche Baufirmen realisiert werden. Es ergeben sich gleichzeitige, größtenteils voneinander unabhängige Bautätigkeiten in mehreren Abschnitten des Vorhabens. Der Baubeginn ist nach Erhalt des Planfeststellungsbeschlusses, voraussichtlich ab August 2027, geplant. Die späteste Inbetriebnahme soll im August 2029 erfolgen. Im Rahmen der Ausschreibung ist zu prüfen, ob eine Inbetriebnahme aller Baulose bereits im Dezember 2028 möglich ist. Der Bau gliedert sich in folgende Baulose: - Baulos 1: Mast 10 bis Mast 57 (~16,4 km) - Baulos 2: Mast 57 bis Mast 86 (~11,2 km) und Mast 112N bis 117AN (~2,3 km) - Baulos 3: Mast 86 bis Mast 139 (~23,6 km) - Baulos 4: Mast 139 bis Mast 172 (~12,1 km) und Mast 185N bis 199N (~4,8 km) Der Rückbau der 220-kV-Freileitung Güstrow-Wolmirstedt wird auf die oben erwähnten Baulose für den Neubau aufgeteilt. - Baulos 1: Mast 347W bis Mast 292W (~16,4 km) - Baulos 2: Mast 292W bis Mast 253W (~11,4 km) und Mast 112 bis Mast 117 (~2 km) - Baulos 3: Mast 253W bis Mast 184W (~19,9 km) - Baulos 4: Mast 184W bis Mast 108W (~23,7 km) und Mast 185 bis Mast 195 (~4,8 km)

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF - Ausgleich volatiler Energieerzeugung im Bahnstromnetz
description: Mit dem Bundes-Klimaschutzgesetz (KSG), das die Erfüllung der nationalen Klimaschutzziele gewährleisten soll und mit dem Klimaschutzplan 20250 festgelegte Klimaschutz- und Sektorziele gesetzlich verankert hat, soll in Deutschland bis zum Jahr 2045 die Treibhausgasneutralität erreicht werden. Derzeit wird der Bahnstrom aus einem gemischten Portfolio aus eigenen konventionellen Kraftwerken, Erneuerbare-Energien-Anlagen, sowie den Bezug aus dem öffentlichen Stromnetz bereitgestellt. Die Strategie zur Erhöhung des Anteils an Erneuerbaren Energien (EE) basiert u.a. auf den Abschluss von Grünstrom-Lieferverträgen auf nationaler als auch europäischer Ebene sowie den Zubau von EE-Erzeugungsanlagen auf Bahnbetriebsanlagen. Dabei wird seit April 2023 erstmals Strom direkt in das deutsche Bahnstromnetz eingespeist. Weiterhin wird durch die aktuelle Gesetzgebung die Erhöhung des Anteils von EE-Anlagen durch das Allgemeine Eisenbahn-Gesetz (AEG) §18f bzw. dem Gesetz zum Ausbau erneuerbarer Energien (EEG) §37 vorangetrieben. Der Anteil regenerativ bereitgestelltem Strom am Bahnstrommix lag im Jahr 2025 bereits bei 71,5 %. Der zunehmende Ausbau bzw. fluktuierende EE-Einspeiseanlagen wie Photovoltaik und Windkraftanlagen mit einer inhärent schwankenden Energiebereitstellung, sowie die prognostizierte Zunahme im Schienenverkehr erhöhen die Komplexität einer sicheren und nachhaltigen Energieversorgung. Hohe Lastgradienten auf Erzeuger- als auch Verbraucherseite und der Wegfall bisheriger konventioneller Kraftwerkstechnik zur Gewährleistung der Netzstabilität im Bahnstromnetz, bringen neue technische und wirtschaftliche Fragestellungen mit sich. Insbesondere die zunehmende Erhöhung leistungselektronischer Komponenten und dessen Wechselwirkung im Gesamtsystem Schiene erhöhen die Komplexität im Bahnstromnetz. Ziel des Projektes ist es, die Auswirkungen des steigenden EE-Anteils auf das Bahnstromnetz respektive auf das öffentliche Landesnetz zu untersuchen und technische und wirtschaftliche Anforderungen bzw. Maßnahmen für Energiespeichersysteme daraus abzuleiten. Das Vorhaben soll eine sichere Energieversorgung im Bahnstromnetz und eine zukünftige bedarfsgerechte Netzplanung unterstützen und den notwendigen Ausbau von EE-Erzeugungsanlagen im Bahnstromnetz stärken, um eine Umsetzung des Klimaschutzplans 2050 für ein treibhausneutrales Verkehrssystem im Jahr 2045 zu gewährleisten.

title: Belgium – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Ondersteuning van lokaal verkeersveiligheidsbeleid in 4 percelen: - Advies - Studies - Ontwerp - Participatie
description: Met het traject Verkeersveilige Gemeente wil de provincie Antwerpen het aantal verkeersslachtoffers zo snel mogelijk terugbrengen naar nul. Die ambitieuze doelstelling willen we samen met de lokale besturen en politiezones waarmaken door verkeersveiligheid hoog op de agenda te zetten en in elk mobiliteitsproject een verkeersveiligheidsreflex te stimuleren. Bijna alle lokale besturen nemen deel aan het traject Verkeersveilige Gemeente. De partners in dit begeleidingstraject zijn: • De Federale Diensten van de Gouverneur (FDG); • De Vlaamse Stichting Verkeerskunde (VSV); • Ouders van Verongelukte Kinderen - Save vzw (OVK). Met deze overheidsopdracht wil de provincie Antwerpen haar lokale besturen ondersteunen in het uittekenen en uitvoeren van hun lokaal verkeersveiligheidsbeleid om zo de Vlaamse doelstelling van 0 verkeersdoden in 2050 na te streven. Verkeersveiligheidsbeleid vergt een geïntegreerde en multidisciplinaire aanpak. Om de mogelijke noden van de lokale besturen en de provincies af te dekken is deze overheidsopdracht opgedeeld in 4 percelen: • Advies • Studies • Ontwerp • Participatie. Deze 4 percelen overkoepelen de vijf verkeersveiligheidspijlers (Engineering, Education, Enforcement, Encouragement en Evaluation). De lokale besturen en provincies hebben voor de uitvoering van lokaal verkeersveiligheidsbeleid nood aan: • een combinatie van uiteenlopende expertises (mobiliteit, gedragsbeïnvloeding, infrastructuur, handhaving, communicatie en evaluatie); • afstemming en het hanteren van verschillende methodieken om de diverse noden van lokale besturen en politiezones te kunnen invullen; • maatgerichte ondersteuningsvormen die enkel via overleg en iteratie kunnen worden verfijnd; • beheersing van inhoudelijke en organisatorische risico’s die voortvloeien uit samenwerking met meerdere actoren en beleidsniveaus.

title: Westcountry Schools Trust - CAFM System
description: WeST operates 31 schools serving approximately 15,000 pupils and employing approximately 2,300 staff. The estate comprises 23 primary schools and 8 Secondary schools, the largest of which serves approximately 2,500 pupils. Buildings are mixed in age, construction and condition. The aim is to achieve a coherent service operating through one principal interface and authoritative asset hierarchy. Current thinking is that this may be through a single platform or demonstrably integrated solution covering the following requirements: • Compliance: records, recurring schedules, evidence, audit history, alerts and remediation across fire, water hygiene and legionella, asbestos, electrical condition, gas, radon, emergency lighting, lifts and playground equipment. • Assets and maintenance: hierarchical asset register, condition and lifecycle data, planned maintenance, reactive requests, work orders, mobile working and contractor workflows. • Financial and capital planning: budget and purchase-order attribution, expenditure reporting and forecasting, DfE condition-data import, replacement forecasting and structured export. • Reporting: Trust-, school- and asset-level dashboards, drill-down, configurable reports and governance-ready outputs. The solution should support demonstrable compliance assurance; complete evidence and audit retention; end-to-end maintenance and contractor workflows; expenditure traceability; maintenance and replacement forecasting; self-service reporting; mobile working; scalability; and secure data portability. WeST is considering at least 99.5% monthly availability, prioritised support targets, service credits for material failure and acceptance-based implementation payments. Feedback is invited on proportionality and market practice.

title: Management Information Systems for Schools in England
description:
This PME does not signify the commencement of any procurement process and does not constitute any commitment by the Department for Education (DfE). If DfE decides to commence any procurement process subject to the Procurement Act 2023 as contemplated by this notice, a separate notice(s) will be published at the relevant time. 
DfE would like to encourage all relevant organisations, including Small to Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and Voluntary, Community and Social Enterprises (VCSEs), to participate and have made the engagement process as open as possible in order to facilitate this (please see further details in the “Engagement process description” section below).  Consideration will be given to consortia and collaborative bids from all forms of organisations subject to confirmation of a competitive tender process.
The Purpose:
Preliminary Market Engagement is being undertaken to refine DfE's requirements as it looks to establish a route to market for schools under the Procurement Act 2023 for management information systems (MIS) that enables them to analyse, use and report on key data with a focus on interoperability. It is currently anticipated that this will be in the form of an open framework as defined in the Procurement Act 2023. 
As part of the preliminary market engagement, DfE is keen to work with MIS suppliers in England to explore how we can harness the potential of data to provide new and valuable insights to share with schools, academy trusts, and local authorities in England to improve outcomes for children and young people, parents and carers. This particular initiative has been branded the Data spine and was referenced in the Schools White Paper published in February 2026. It is anticipated that outcomes of this initiative will be included within the remit of aforementioned route to market. 
Further information on the link between the MIS route to market project and the Data spine will be shared as part of the engagement process, starting with the market engagement webinar (please see further details in the “Engagement process description” section below).
We will conduct further market engagement during spring 2026 with a view to using the market engagement and stakeholders views to further inform the specifics of the proposed MIS route to market.
By fully engaging in this process, including the Data spine initiative, organisations have the opportunity to feed into the design of the proposed MIS route to market and ensure it is cognizant of market capabilities.

title: Day Opportunities Quality Framework
description:
Wigan Council is seeking to establish a Day Opportunities Quality Framework to deliver high-quality, person-centred support for adults with care and support needs across the Borough. 
The Framework is intended to support a diverse range of adults with differing levels of need. Providers must deliver flexible, responsive and outcome-focused services that enable adults to access the right support, in the right place, at the right time. 
Depending on individual needs, preferences and agreed outcomes, provision may be delivered:
•	at different times of the day, including full-day, half-day and bespoke sessional arrangements;
•	within specialist settings;
•	within mainstream community settings;
•	through outreach and neighbourhood-based support;
•	through a combination of building-based and community-based provision; and
•	through the appropriate use of digital tools, virtual support, assistive technology and technology-enabled care.
The Day Opportunities Quality Framework is divided into the following Lots:
Lot 1: Confidence and Community Connections
Lot 2: Enablement Support and Living Well
Lot 3: Specialist Ongoing Care and Support
The Council intends to award all contracts under the Day Opportunities Quality Framework through a Direct Award process. Providers appointed to the Framework will be eligible to receive referrals and contract awards without the need for a further competitive procedure, subject to the requirements of the individual service user, the provisions of the  Framework Agreement, and the Provider's ability to meet the assessed needs, desired outcomes and preferences of the individual.

title: Highways and Infrastructure Professional Services Contract
description:
As described in the preliminary market engagement notice  (https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/054636-2026) dated 10 June 2026 and the planned procurement notice (https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/085054-2026) dated 8 September 2026, Norfolk County Council (the "Council") is formally launching a procurement using the Competitive Flexible Procedure under section 20(2)(b) of the Procurement Act 2023 (the "Procurement") (the "Act") for a highways and infrastructure professional services contract (the "Contract").
On the launch of this Procurement, the Council is seeking suitably qualified applicants (the "Applicants") capable of integrating with the Council's wider highways team, delivering high-quality professional services in the Norfolk geographic area, and structuring its approach to the delivery of the Contract in a manner which is pragmatic, innovative, and cost-effective.
The launch of the Procurement follows a period of sustained preliminary market engagement during which the Council engaged with prospective bidders regarding: (i) the approach to the Procurement (including the timeline, dialogue sessions, and possible award criteria); and (ii) the proposed approach to the Contract and scope of services under it.
The Council has designed a lean, dialogue-focused approach to the Procurement that leverages the full flexibility afforded to it by the Act. The Procurement is designed to ensure that the principles of delivering value for money, maximising public benefit, sharing information with Applicants, acting with integrity, and facilitating SME participation are built into every stage of the process.
Further detail regarding the stages and requirements are contained within the Procurement documents which can be accessed through the In-Tend platform. Please note that all materials prepared and shared with the market during the preliminary market engagement phase are available on the In-Tend platform via the clarifications facility.
A full breakdown of the scope of services forming part of the Contract is contained within the Procurement documents, including a draft scope made available with those documents. By way of illustration, the Council anticipates that the services required under the Contract, which will be carried out collaboratively with the Council's in-house teams, will include:
• Highway design services, project delivery (including early contractor involvement and developing works orders), stakeholder engagement and consultation, and specialist expertise required for the development of highway maintenance, asset management, and capital improvement schemes
• Major highway infrastructure and other design services (feasibility, preliminary and detailed including planning and other statutory approvals), through integrated design teams as well as wider resource provision (including necessary specialist resources) 
•Bridges and structures design and advisory services, including asset management, inspection and maintenance
•Business case development, including in support of funding applications to funders such as the Department for Transport and Homes England (e.g., cost benefit analysis, carbon analysis, etc.)
•Environmental and ecology services (including carbon assessment), archaeology and heritage advisory services
•Travel and Transport planning advisory services (including strategic planning and travel planning services)
•Intelligent transport services, future mobility services, and design and advisory services
•Spatial planning (including master planning, planning applications, statutory services, carbon assessments and environmental impact assessments)
•Maritime services (including supporting design and project delivery for coastal, harbour and river environments)
•Flood and water management design and advisory services
•Land, property and asset management advisory services
•Economic development advisory services, including feasibility studies/assessments, strategic and project specific modelling, government engagement/lobbying, and associated reporting
•Quantity surveying, costing, commercial and contract administration services
•Development of tender documentation and tender evaluation support
•Construction phase services
•Surveys and investigations
•Development research, and developer design and build agreement checks
•Heat, energy, water  and sewage advisory services
•Waste services, including advice on residual waste, household waste recycling centres, waste facilities planning  advice/application, permitting
As many prospective Applicants will be aware, the Council prepared this Procurement within the context of local government reorganisation ("LGR") and devolution ("Devolution") and had proceeded on the basis that government was minded as part of LGR to reorganise the various Norfolk councils into three new unitary authorities.
On 7 September 2026 the government withdrew that decision and announced a "rapid review" of its LGR programme in respect of Norfolk.
With regards to Devolution, on 4 December 2025, the then Secretary of State for Local Government made a written statement [UIN HCWS1128] stating that government intends to establish a Mayoral Strategic Authority for Norfolk and Suffolk as soon as possible, and that it was minded to hold inaugural mayoral elections in May 2028. The current secretary of state said, in her statement of 7 December 2026: "The Prime Minister is really clear that the Government's ambition is to ensure that every area in England has, or is in the process of establishing, a strategic authority by the end of 2027, with strategic authorities in place everywhere by the end of 2028".
The Council is keen to emphasise that, despite the announcement, prospective Applicants should be confident that, in launching this Procurement in this manner and at this time, it intends to address any future considerations which may arise as a result of LGR and/or Devolution in a collaborative, solutions-focused manner which, to the greatest extent possible, protects: (i) the delivery of the Contract in the Norfolk area; and (ii) the volume of work under, and the value of, the Contract, whilst at all times being respectful of the time and costs likely to be incurred by Applicants in competing for this Contract.
The values stated in this notice exclude indexation and mobilisation.

title: CPU7343 - Homelessness Prevention Services - Open Framework
description:
This is a procurement under the Competitive Flexible Procedure, not an Open Procedure.
Nottingham City Council is seeking Tenders from sufficiently experienced and qualified providers to establish a multi-Lot, multi-Supplier Open Framework of Homelessness Prevention Services (more commonly referred to as the Commissioned Homelessness Prevention System), consisting of two Lots:
Lot 1 - Accommodation Based Services (ABS), which provide accommodation, housing management and housing-related support.
Lot 2 - Community Based Services (CBS), which provide housing-related advice, outreach, prevention, resettlement or sustainment support outside a provider-owned accommodation setting.
Services commissioned under Lot 1 may include the following, either as distinct services or as elements of a combined accommodation pathway:
a)	Emergency and immediate access accommodation
b)	Temporary accommodation with support
c)	Supported accommodation
d)	Specialist accommodation
e)	Intermediate and move-on accommodation
f)	Housing-led accommodation
Services commissioned under Lot 2 may include the following, either as distinct services or as elements of a coordinated community-based pathway:
a)	Universal housing advice and access services
b)	Targeted early intervention
c)	Homelessness prevention and tenancy sustainment
d)	Housing options and resettlement support
e)	Outreach and in-reach
f)	Rough sleeping prevention and street outreach
g)	Specialist housing-related support and pathway coordination
A Supplier can bid for any number of Lots and be successful in any number of Lots.
This Framework may also be used by other Authority departments including but not limited to Children, Adults and Public Health.
The Authority is seeking to put in place an Open Framework to establish the initial Framework and appoint one or more Framework Members in each Lot to deliver services. This Procurement is intended to set up a list of approved Framework Members for each Lot.  There is no limit to the number of Suppliers who can be Framework Members in each Lot. Call-off Award Procedures will then be conducted, and Call-off contracts will then be awarded.
This Procurement is a replacement for services previously tendered 'CPU3880 and CPU7231 - Framework for Community Based Support and Accommodation Based Services for homeless people (and those at risk of homelessness)'. It is important for Suppliers to note that if they are on the above Frameworks and wish to participate in future contract opportunities for this service, they will need to submit a response to this Procurement.
This is a light touch special regime Framework as per Sections 8 and 9 of the Procurement Act 2023. The process to be used will be the Competitive Flexible Procedure as per Section 20 of the Procurement Act 2023. 
Where a Supplier fails the any stage as described below, their Tender will not be assessed any further:
•	Stage  One - Initial Review of Tender Submission 
•	Stage Two - Procurement Specific Questionnaire Pass/Fail 
•	Stage Three - Quality Questions 1 and 2 Pass/Fail 
•	Stage Four - Quality Questions 3 to 6 Assessment Scored Pass/Fail 
•	Stage Five - Any required Final Qualification Check.
Re-Opening
The Open Framework Mechanism allows the Authority to 're-open' the Framework to new Framework Members, while allow existing Framework members to also remain as Framework Members. The Authority reserves the right to re-open the Framework to new potential Framework Members when it deems it is required to ensure:
•	Procurement legislation is complied with.
•	Capacity requirements can be met.
•	To ensure adequate competition in the Call-off Award Procedure.
•	To meet needs that are not satisfied by current Framework Members.
•	Other reasons deemed reasonable by the Authority.
The Authority will post a Tender Notice on Find Tender Service/CDP when it re-opens the Framework for new Tender submissions.
As this Procurement is for a 'Light Touch Contract', the process and award of Call-off contracts may include some flexibilities permitted by the Special Regime of the Procurement Act (2023).
Suppliers will be required to behave lawfully and ethically in sourcing Accommodation and in a manner that does not create additional Homelessness. The Authority reserves the right not to contract or proceed with Orders with any Suppliers where it is discovered this is not the case and the Authority reserves the right to no longer work with the Supplier in the future.
Consideration of SME's
SME's have been considered in the following ways:
•	Advanced notice promoted via Pipeline Notice and PME notices.
•	Reduced number of Lots so reduced Tendering requirements.
•	Clear requirements for Conditions of Participation to make it clear the type of experience and capability required.
•	Longer than required Tender submission time provided.
•	No insurance required at Framework stage. 
•	Low liability cap amounts.
•	Framework can be re-opened for new Suppliers
Framework Term
The first framework for a term of up to three years anticipated to start from 8 January 2027 to 31 December 2029 and a second framework for a term of up to a further five years from 1 January 2030 to 31 December 2034, subject to change depending on initial tendering length and termination clauses.
The actual Framework dates and number of Frameworks are indicative only, but the total Term is of all Frameworks added together is a maximum of eight years.
In the unlikely event that only one supplier is appointed to any individual Framework in the scheme of Frameworks during the open Framework Period then the maximum term for the Framework, and the open Framework, will be 4 years from the date on which the single supplier Framework is awarded.
PME
Pre-Market was undertaken.
A PME Pack is included in the Procurement Documents.
The summary of the conclusion of the PME is:
•	The reduction of Lots to make tendering easier.
•	A framework mechanism to allow new Suppliers enter the framework.
•	Split call-offs into smaller contracts where possible.
•	Case study type tender questions
Tender Modifications
The Authority reserves the right to:
•	Refine the Conditions of Participation Criteria
•	Refine/modify the Procurement process and/or terms
•	Refine the Award Criteria
•	'Roll' the Procurement to an appropriate previous stage
Clarifications
All questions/clarifications must be submitted via the Portal (more details below). Do not expect emails/calls to be responded to.
All Suppliers should access the 'Messages' section of the Portal on a regular basis to check for any clarifications issued on this project and/or any public exchange of information between interested parties, before final submission of their bid. It is the sole responsibility of Suppliers to do so.
LGR
Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) is the process in which the structure and responsibilities of local authorities are reconfigured. The Government has set out plans to move away from the current two-tier system of county and district councils which are in place in some parts of county of Nottinghamshire and other parts of England.
The Authority has now received the Government's proposed decision regarding LGR in Nottinghamshire. However, there has been a pause in the LGR process so that Central Government can conduct a review. Due to the review there is some uncertainty over the exact timing of when (or if) any new structure will be implemented. The latest information is that the Authority will remain in their current format until at least April 2028.
It is considered the period of Agreements and Call-off Contracts under this Procurement is likely to be impacted by LGR, should this process be resumed. The current intention is that this Agreement / Call-off Contract would continue following any new structure implemented.
As a consequence of LGR, any resulting Agreement or Call Off Contract may be required to be transferred, assigned or novated (in whole or in part) to one or more successor authorities or other public bodies established as part of LGR, in accordance with applicable legislation.
Suppliers acknowledge and accept that the Authority must comply with all statutory, regulatory and other legal requirements arising in connection with LGR and, to the extent necessary to do so, reserves the right to make such amendments to the procurement arrangements and/or any resulting Contract, Framework Agreement or Call Off Contract as are required or permitted by law.
Suppliers must submit their Tender on the basis that such transfer, assignment, novation or amendment may occur and that no additional charges, price adjustments or termination rights shall arise solely as a result of LGR. Any reasonable steps taken by the Authority or a successor authority to notify Suppliers of matters arising from LGR shall be sufficient for the purposes of this procurement. 
East Midlands Procurement Portal (the Portal)
Once the Tender Notice is published, Tender documents can be obtained from the East Midlands Procurement Portal at https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ by searching for CPU7343. You will need register on this website to use it Please note if you require any assistance regarding the registration on the East Midlands Procurement Portal please contact Proactis direct via Helpdesk on Tel: 0330 005 0352 or Email: procontractsuppliers@proactis.com. This is not an Authority website, so we are unable help.
Please also see the Procurement Documents for more information about the Authority's requirements.
