title: CEFAS26-74 Laboratory Container Facilities for Blue Belt Programme
description:
The Blue Belt Programme is the UK Government’s flagship marine conservation programme, partnering with a number of the UK Overseas Territories (UKOTs). Together, we work to improve protection and sustainable use practices within the waters of the UKOTs to safeguard marine biodiversity and the practices of local communities.
Fisheries Science in the UKOTs
Fishing is an important activity in a number of the UKOTs, ranging from commercial fishing operations through to recreational fishing for subsistence and leisure.
Fisheries science, the collection and analysis of information pertaining to fish species and their fishery(ies), is fundamental to effective and responsive management of these activities and their impacts. Many countries have a nationally coordinated system of data collection from fisheries, but in small communities with limited local capacity, this is generally impractical. In such contexts, fostering collaboration with fishers is essential to ensure fair and participatory management.
This requirement for UKOTs, Montserrat and Ascension Island, is for the provision of containerised laboratory facilities that will be used to support the collection of essential samples and data from local fishers.
Aims and Objectives
To facilitate the collection of samples and data for fisheries science, the Governments of Ascension Island and Montserrat require laboratory facilities that be located at the main fish landing sites. The desired contents and layout of each of these facilities are detailed in the specifications below.
The Supplier will procure, construct, and deliver these two containerised laboratories to Ascension Island and Montserrat.
Scope of Requirements
Cefas require two containerised laboratory facilities according to the general and specific criteria outlined below, including procurement, manufacture, and delivery. General Requirements in 4.1. apply equally for both laboratories. The desired layout and any specific requirements for each UKOT are provided in 4.2 and 4.3.
Installation of facilities is not required in either case as this will be handled by the respective UKOT Governments. If installation guidance is considered useful or where the installation method may be considered as potentially voiding any warranties, the Supplier may optionally provide this together with specific details and any impact on contract value in their submission as per APPENDIX 5.
General Requirements
The basic structure of each laboratory should be based upon conversion of an ISO standard 20-foot (6.06 metres external length) new shipping container1 converted into laboratory and plant room space(s).
Since these containers will require sea freight to their final destinations, they must be supplied with in-date Container Safety Certificates (CSC), adhering to the International Maritime Organisation International Convention for Safe Containers2 with recessed doors, windows, etc. The CSC should have sufficient time (at least 6 months past the expected delivery) remaining to allow for unexpected delays that may occur during transit.
Each container requires external fixtures and connections for both electrical and plumbing service, as specified below in Sections 4.2 and 4.3.
Flooring should be of laboratory standard, anti-static, anti-slip, and resistant to staining or spills of chemicals. Flooring should have a lip of at least 100mm on all sides (excluding the doorway) fit for easy cleaning.
Each container must include the components as detailed below to be procured, installed and tested by the Supplier. Representative examples of fitted equipment are given below as footnotes for clarity (such examples should not be considered requests for, or endorsements of, the specific product linked). The Supplier is free to suggest comparable products that they consider more suitable based on the grounds of cost, availability, compatibility, and functionality.
All electrical and mechanical components should be supplied new and with a warranty applicable to the working environment and lasting for a period of at least 12 months commencing upon the date of final delivery. Systems that are straightforward to be maintained by non-specialist engineers and do not rely upon or require legacy subscription costs are preferred where possible.
One single width exterior door with both a physical key lock and electronic lock/unlock functionality3.
Access to the laboratory will ideally be facilitated through the use of a low-frequency passive radio frequency identification (RFiD)-type system or similar. This system needs to be able to work independently and will not require any legacy costs through a subscription service or continual connectivity to a third-party organisation.
Access records (Card ID(s) and time-date(s) of entry) will be viewable via (password protected) download from the device.
Along with each container, the Supplier will issue 100 pre-programmed and individually numbered access cards that can be issued to registered users of the facility.
The hardware and/or software required to programme new (or re-programme existing) cards should be included and no legacy costs required.
At least three windows and/or skylights. Each should be able to be opened, and at least one window must be of a sufficient size and accessibility to serve as a secondary fire exit, in accordance with Fire Safety Regulations of the UK4. All should be fitted with physical locks.
Temperature control systems capable of maintaining a stable internal temperature in tropical climates and to deal with heat load generated from ice machine and freezers. The Supplier will provide details of potential means, which may include, but is not limited, to the following:
Interior insulation
Passive ventilation systems.
Window unit air conditioner
Overhead lighting, non-corrosive LED light fittings with motion sensor.
Supply and fitment of appropriate distribution board. Electrical supply requirements are specified below.
Eight or more electrical sockets, distributed according to the layouts below and of at least UK Ingress Protection rating IP44 or equivalent5.
Stainless steel laboratory work benches with integrated sink and mixer tap.
The bench with the integrated sink should be recessed and graded to allow the draining of blood and viscera into the sink.
Central floor drain.
Lockable drawer units under work benches to store laboratory consumables and equipment.
Wall-mounted shelving above the work benches and/or chest freezers.
One commercial grade ice machine, suitable for seafood and capable of operating in high ambient temperatures. The Supplier will detail production capacity at an ambient temperature of 30°C and in high humidity. The requirements for the ice machine for each UKOT are detailed below in Sections 4.2 and 4.3.
Two chest freezers, each with a capacity of at least 400 Litres and capable of freezing contents to at least -20°C6.
Flammable chemicals locker (key access only)7 positioned under work bench.
Wall-mounted fFire detection (i.e. ceiling-mounted smoke alarm) safety equipment, including fire extinguishers, appropriate to contents (e.g. electrical and chemical fires).
First aid station suitable for minor injuries (cuts, burns, eye wash etc).
Wall-mounted whiteboard and dry wipe marker pens.
The Supplier will state the estimated water and power consumption of the unit during normal operations of the equipment
At least two spare keys for all physical locks should be supplied.
The Supplier will provide a spare parts list for all electrical or mechanical components included in their Technical response and in Appendix 6 – Pricing Schedule. Cefas may require provision of some or all of these parts, to be agreed in writing either prior to Contract award or during the build phase prior to shipping, which will be agreed via a formal Contract Variation.
The indicative layout of each laboratory is specified below in Sections 4.2 and 4.3.
While the key requirements are included in this Specification, the Supplier will propose the solution they believe best meets the needs, based on their expertise. Final design will be agreed following Contract award, in collaboration with Cefas and the Overseas Territories, but it will be broadly in line with the technical proposal and with the proposed costs, in the awarded bid submission.

title: Winter Access Hubs Service for Bromley
description:
NHS South East London Integrated Care Board (SEL ICB) is seeking to commission a Winter Access Hubs Service to provide additional same-day primary care capacity for Bromley residents during periods of seasonal demand and winter system pressures.
The service will deliver timely assessment and treatment for patients requiring urgent same-day primary care access through a geographically distributed network of hub locations across Bromley. The service is intended to support general practice, urgent care and acute services by managing appropriate patients within primary care settings and reducing avoidable attendances at Urgent Treatment Centres and Emergency Departments. 
Key features of the service include:
•Provision of additional same-day GP-led capacity for winter illness and other urgent primary care presentations. 
•Delivery of predominantly face-to-face consultations through convenient hub locations across the borough. 
•Direct booking and referral pathways from General Practice, NHS 111 and Urgent Treatment Centres. 
•Integration with community pharmacy, self-referral pathways and wider neighbourhood services to ensure patients receive care in the most appropriate setting.
•Flexible deployment of capacity in response to emerging winter demand and system pressures. 
•Use of shared digital solutions and GP clinical systems to support integrated patient care and continuity of information. 
•Collection and reporting of activity, utilisation, patient outcomes and service impact data to support ongoing service evaluation and improvement. 
The service forms part of Bromley's winter resilience arrangements and aims to improve access to urgent primary care, reduce pressure on urgent and emergency care services, and support delivery of the NHS objective of providing timely same-day assessment in community settings.
This is a 3 months contract (subject to change).

title: Academic Half Day (AHD) Cover Service for Bromley General Practices - PSR Most Suitable Provider Process
description:
NHS South East London Integrated Care Board  is seeking to commission the provision of an Academic Half Day (AHD) Cover Service for Bromley General Practices.
The commissioner is seeking a provider capable of delivering a safe, responsive and integrated urgent primary care service during agreed AHD and PLT events, ensuring continuity of patient access whilst supporting general practice workforce education and development.
Under the contract, the provider will be expected to:
•Deliver a GP-led service for Bromley registered patients during AHD (minimum 6) and PLT sessions (by future agreement).
•Accept and manage patient demand received through diverted practice telephony systems, online consultation platforms, NHS 111 referrals and other agreed access routes.
•Ensure all clinically urgent contacts are assessed and managed on the same day.
•Operate a clinically led triage model using consult-and-complete principles and effective risk stratification.
•Maintain capability to provide telephone, digital and face-to-face consultations, together with urgent home visits where clinically required.
•Work collaboratively with Bromley General Practices to implement agreed Standard Operating Procedures for online consultations, call handling, appointment booking and urgent prescription management.
•Support reduction of avoidable demand through effective triage, care navigation, signposting and feedback to practices.
•Provide access arrangements that promote equity, patient safety and positive patient experience.
•Maintain robust safeguarding, information governance, workforce and business continuity arrangements.
•Submit detailed sessional reporting and service intelligence to support commissioner oversight, learning and continuous improvement.
This notice is an intention to award a contract under the Most Suitable Provider (MSP) process ( The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 10).
The contract for the Service will be awarded for a period of 1 year (12 months) with an option to extend for another 1 year (12 Months) at the sole discretion of the ICB (1+1).

title: Provision of 111-2 Service
description:
This opportunity is being run under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR) regulations.
The development of a specialist all age mental health response via 111 is a key ambition of the NHS England Long Term Plan (2021-2024), and the recovery plan for urgent and emergency care priority for 2023/24.  This required all calls for support during mental health crisis to be made via 111 by the end of March 2024 and is referred to as 111-2.  Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust (AWP) currently deliver this service in partnership with a system partner. 
AWP is seeking a provider to deliver an integrated model for the NHS 111 Mental Health Crisis Response Service (111 Option 2) for individuals experiencing a mental health crisis across both adult (18 years and over) and children and young people (under 18 years) pathways. The appointed provider will be solely responsible for the delivery of the call handling element of the 111 Option 2 pathway, including access, triage and call management. AWP will retain responsibility for all clinical assessment activity and associated clinical decision-making and outcomes. The provider must be able to operate within a matrix management model, whereby all partners maintain responsibility for their own governance arrangements, professional standards and areas of specialist expertise, while working collaboratively at both strategic and operational leadership levels to deliver a seamless, integrated and high-quality service.
The service forms part of the NHS England requirement that callers contacting NHS 111 and selecting the mental health option are connected directly to a dedicated mental health response service available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. The service will work collaboratively with urgent and emergency care pathways, crisis services, community mental health teams, acute hospitals, ambulance services, primary care and voluntary sector partners.

title: Customer Care (Security) Services within Emergency Housing and Resettlement Service
description:
This contract is not a security contract; it has a much wider scope. The Service Provider must have experience in dealing with vulnerable adults, families and young people with multi disadvantage and complex needs. They must have experience, competence and abilities to manage situations that may be sensitive and challenging. The Service Provider must provide officers that are able to respond to the needs of the services below and have the skills to communicate effectively, defuse situations and manage emergency situations swiftly and confidently. The Service Provider must be able to provide additional onsite support to officers within the appropriate timescales. Officers may be required to carry out welfare checks on individuals that require additional support/oversight. Officers may also be required to address issues with individuals that are challenging.
William Lyons House is supported accommodation for 14 young people, there are 10 self-contained flats and 4 bedsit flats with a communal kitchen. There are also communal areas which can be accessed by the young people when BCH staff are on site. The building is a 2 story block with a rear car park and door entry system. The role of the customer care service is to maintain the security of the building, manage the front door, not allowing visitors within the agreed time periods, carry out building safety checks, monitor the CCTV, respond to any emergency situations and record building information within the appropriate record books. The Customer Care Officer will also be required to liaise with the young people, defuse any challenging situations and deal with the young people in a friendly and effective manner, again recording information within the required record books/incident reports.
The Emergency Housing provision provides emergency accommodation for homeless families, couples and singles, with multi disadvantages and complex needs. Two buildings provide individual sleeping/living quarters with shared bathrooms, kitchens and communal corridors and one building provides fully self-contained accommodation. The buildings are 2 and 3 story blocks with a communal front door entry system. During the evenings, entry into Gorton St will be managed by the customer care service. The Customer Care Officer will carry out building safety checks, welfare checks, carry out any out of hours booking in of new residents, review CCTV, responding to any breach of rules as required within agreed procedures, deal with emergency situations including responding to fire alarm activations, responding to safeguarding concerns and record all information within the required record books. Security will also be required to carry out emergency admissions as set within the agreed admission procedures. Within our family emergency provision one customer care officer will be required to be based in one of the family provisions, Central or Clare St, they will be expected to visit the other family provision during each shift. The Customer Care Officer will carry out building safety checks, welfare checks, carry out any out of hours booking in of new residents, review CCTV, responding to any breach of rules as required within agreed procedures, deal with emergency situations including responding to fire alarm activations, responding to safeguarding concerns and record all information within the required record books. Customer Care Officers will also be required to carry out emergency admissions as set within the agreed admission procedures.

•	To reduce the incidence of suicide and self-harm across the local population through early intervention, awareness-raising, and enhanced community and professional support 
•	To promote a whole-community approach to suicide prevention by engaging local authorities, education providers, workplaces; voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) organisations, and healthcare settings. The service should also prioritise targeting vulnerable population groups including delivery of training to organisations that work with vulnerable communities (particularly those at risk of suicides). 
.
2.1.2	Objectives
•	Increase awareness and understanding of suicide risk and prevention across the community.
•	Build capacity and confidence in professionals, peers, and community leaders to identify and support individuals at risk.
•	Provide bespoke interventions that are effective and accessible for everyone, and tailored to support priority groups, including higher risk groups (e.g. men, autistic people) and groups experiencing risk factors e.g. substance misuse, domestic violence 
•	Create safe and connected communities by improving support and signposting, and provision of messages about suicide and self-harm prevention through accessible digital resources  
•	Aim to impact and reduce suicide and self-harm across South West London through early intervention, awareness, and targeted support.
•	Strengthen local suicide prevention infrastructure through multi-agency collaboration, lived experience involvement, and whole-system approaches
•	Implement evidence-based interventions that address self-harm behaviours, focussing on early identification, harm reduction and psychosocial support 
•	Embed suicide prevention into everyday settings such as schools, workplaces, and community organisations
•	To monitor and evaluate impact and outcomes through robust data collection, feedback mechanisms, and continuously improve delivery through annual monitoring and learning.

title: Offsite Direct Wire Power Purchase Agreement (RAF Wittering)
description:
Objectives: The Ministry of Defence (MOD) is seeking Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) to reduce unit electricity costs, increase site energy resilience, limit price volatility risk from its energy portfolio, and support emissions reductions aligned with Government policy.
PPA Type: Renewable energy supply for the RAF Wittering site via off-site direct wire connection.
Target contract start date: 14/02/28.
Volume: Procure power generation to meet up to approximately 2-5GWh/year of electricity consumption for RAF Wittering (total annual consumption of approximately 7.9GWh/year). Provision of higher offtake volumes is dependent on the ability to demonstrate value for money in energy costs achieved and resilience provision. Further, the site demand is expected to grow over the next ~15yrs, potentially 4-fold in electrical demand as more capability is brought onto site and the site decarbonises. Input on ability to support increasing scaling of volume, whilst minimising customer risk is sought.
Sites: This procurement is for one site only at RAF Wittering, Peterborough through an off-site arrangement using a private wire. 
Contract duration: Seeking competitive energy prices for up to 25 years, with potential option to extend.
Technology: Open to competitive proposals for Renewable Energy Guarantee of Origin (REGO) compliant technologies. 
The details provided in this notice are early indicative estimates and may be subject to change/refinement as a result of ongoing analysis and data collection.
Previous market engagement: A virtual two‑hour supplier engagement session was held on 04/03/2025 to test early market views on high‑level PPA options and to support MOD’s understanding of market capabilities. Suppliers expressed strong appetite to engage and highlighted key considerations including avoiding over‑specification, clarifying roles and responsibilities, and addressing grid‑connection and MOD site factors that will shape the delivery approach.
Social Value (SV): SV is a mandatory consideration in UK Government procurement. Any potential future tender will be assessed against the Government’s Social Value Model themes, ensuring delivery approaches contribute meaningful economic, social, and environmental benefits. Specific Model Award Criteria (MACs) to be utilised within the tender process will be confirmed should the requirement be taken forward. 
Modern Slavery: MOD must consider the potential of modern slavery at all stages of the procurement lifecycle. Please note this information will be required as part of the procurement process but is not required at this stage.

title: TRHS0025 Euston Delivery Company (EDC) Programme Challenge and Assurance Partner
description:
The Euston Delivery Company (EDC) is responsible for leading the integrated redevelopment of the Euston campus and delivering a world-class transport gateway for the UK. EDC is to integrate into a reconstructed single and coherent national transport gateway, all mainline railway, London Underground, bus and taxi infrastructure at Euston (collectively known as the Euston campus), including the new high-speed terminus, for which a public-private partnership model is being explored.
EDC plans to engage a Programme Challenge and Assurance Partner [P-CAP] to support in the delivery of the Euston Programme. The scope of the P-CAP's responsibilities will be refined over coming months, but may include:
1.	Cost Challenge, Control and Analysis: Forecasting the Expected Cost at Completion (ECC) of the programme, identifying key drivers of spend and benchmarking to provide and challenge estimates.
2.	Schedule Control and Optimisation: Examining the programme and its pipeline of deliverables, identifying interdependencies and timings to inform strategic decision-making and optimise outcomes
3.	Value Engineering and Design/Delivery Integration: Challenging design outputs, interface risks and integration issues across delivery packages and partner organisations to reduce unnecessary cost, improve constructability and protect programme schedule.
4.	Commercial Optimisation and Advice: Advising on contract delivery by scrutinising planned deliverables, programme and resourcing to identify risks to deliverability and optimise value for money.
5.	Programme Management and Performance: Supporting the EDC to implement integrated reporting and risk management across the programme, including providing MI and executive summary to support decision-making.
EDC is likely to require services of this nature throughout the Euston Programme - however, the scope of work, route to market, estimated contract value, start date, contract duration and timings for this procurement are subject to ongoing development. EDC is particularly considering whether it would be advantageous to procure a single long term contract or to reprocure services between any particular phases of the programme.
Whether or not the DfT or EDC subsequently commences a procurement and/or thereafter awards any contract related to this potential opportunity shall be solely at its discretion. Details included in this preliminary market notice should not be regarded as final or as constituting a defined opportunity.

title: Waste composition analysis of separate flexibles collections from purpose-built flats
description:
The FlexFlats project aims to understand how local authorities can provide an efficient and effective flexibles collection service to residents who live in purpose-built flats and share bins (communal bins). 
The pilots will be carried out in partnership with three London local authorities with five pilot sites (blocks) in each. The local authorities are:
•London borough of Bexley (twin-stream dry recycling service)
•London borough of Lewisham (comingled dry recycling service)
•Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (commingled dry recycling service) 
The pilot will trial a range of methods for flexibles plastics collection in 15 blocks of flats across the three boroughs. Each block will have a minimum of 25 households and will have a residual waste and dry recycling collection service already in place. 
A range of in-home solutions will be piloted. Flexibles sorted in the home will then be collected externally in either the usual dry recycling bin or a separate flexibles bin in the communal bin area - it is anticipated that separate flexibles bins will be no larger than 240l.
Pilots are still being finalised but are likely to include the following:
	In-home options	External infrastructure options* 
1	No home separation - resident behaves as now (control)	Usual recycling bin

The pilots are scheduled to go live in late September 2026, with baseline monitoring taking place prior (including WCA).  Pilots will run for 3.5 months, running until mid-January 2027, with post-monitoring taking place upon project close.
3.	The brief
The following project deliverables will be undertaken by the succesful bidder:
•	Two phase waste composition analysis to be undertaken for waste and recycling from all properties at up to 15 pilot sites situated across 15 housing estates/blocks within three London boroughs (five within each borough), using one or more sort sites provided by the local authorities.

Phase 2: Post-pilot WCA - to be undertaken late January/early February 2027 to assess impact of interventions
•	Sorting to meet the data classification provided;
•	Confirmation of all appropriate permits to sort waste and (if required) transport waste;
•	Provision of a risk assessment in advance of any collection and sorting;
•	Attendance at an inception meeting via Teams and attendance at regular contract meetings during peak delivery periods (30 minutes/fortnightly or as required) and any other communications as required leading up to and required between project phases;
•	Delivery of the project outputs as set out in section 5;
•	Presentation of the results of the project (online via teams)
•	Final close down meeting (1 hour duration online), anticipated to be held February / March 2027.

title: Integrated Project Management Office (IPMO)
description:
National Grid manages a portfolio of major transmission infrastructure projects across onshore and offshore programmes. As the scale and complexity of delivery increases, National Grid requires a more integrated and digitally enabled approach to project controls, governance and performance management.
The initial phase of the requirement will support the Onshore GGP programme, with the potential to extend to additional delivery programmes and operating models in the future.
National Grid is seeking an Integrated Project Management Office (IPMO) capability that provides a consolidated view of project and portfolio performance information across areas such as cost, schedule, risk, commercial management, change management and baseline control. The objective is to improve visibility, assurance and decision-making while reducing reliance on manual and fragmented processes.
As part of this requirement, National Grid is seeking a digital solution that supports project controls, commercial, finance, PMO and leadership teams through the integration of data and processes across existing business systems and reporting platforms.
The solution is expected to support integrated project controls activities including baseline management, change control, forecasting, contingency management, cost management, cost-value reconciliation and payment management. It should provide auditable workflows, role-based access controls and portfolio-level reporting, while supporting alignment between cost and schedule information through standardised project control structures.
National Grid requires a scalable and flexible solution capable of supporting current requirements while providing a foundation for future enhancements in project controls, reporting and analytics capabilities.
The solution must integrate with approved National Grid systems and data sources, while ensuring National Grid retains ownership and control of its data. The solution should support appropriate governance, data quality controls, metadata management, historical data retention, multi-currency capability and role-based access management.
National Grid is seeking a solution that can evolve over time as business requirements mature and adoption increases, supporting improved portfolio transparency, consistent project controls processes and effective collaboration across multiple delivery programmes and delivery partners.

title: LEDS Person Update
GMCA 2027 Stock Condition Survey
description:
GMCA are inviting feedback from potential suppliers in relation to the delivery of a stock condition model for Greater Manchester. It is expected that the model/survey would be a desktop survey which would provide modelled outputs. The survey outputs would allow the GMCA and the 10 Greater Manchester local authorities to compare the data produced with historic stock condition data, based on type and level of hazards within the Housing Health and Safety Rating system. It would support Housing Strategies, Climate Action Plans, and Fuel Poverty actions, as well as assist the local authorities to comply with their duties under the Regulatory Reform Order 2002 and the integration of Public Health responsibilities into the Local Authority.
The objectives of the potential model/survey are to understand the following:
A. The overall stock condition of homes across Greater Manchester by house type, age and tenure of the home.
B. Levels of minimum acceptable conditions as set out in the Housing Health and Safety Rating System.
C. Estimation of the state of repair, modernity of internal living facilities and thermal comfort as set out in the Decent Homes Standard, however consideration should be paid to the status of the proposed standard.
D. Levels of fuel poverty in line with the Government's current Fuel Poverty Strategy and emerging policy.
E. How the stock condition across the 10 Greater Manchester local authorities compares with the Survey of English Housing Survey trends to establish to what extent conditions in Greater Manchester follows the national trend over the same period.
F. Estimates of retrofit opportunities utilising the Net Zero Housing Retrofit Framework Agreement.
G. Understanding levels of overcrowding.
The outputs of the model/survey will be used for the following purposes:
1. As a key input into the Greater Manchester Health and Housing model. The data from the stock condition model will be combined with health data in a secure environment. The GMCA/NHSGM and the provider building the health and housing model will work closely with the successful provider to identify how best to integrate the data and note any caveats concerning the data.
2. Support the GMCA to identify locations which would benefit from retrofit interventions to support the 2038 carbon neutrality ambitions of the city region. Greater Manchester as part of the Integrated Settlement has a devolved retrofit budget which is key to meeting these ambitions.
3. Support the development of housing and retrofit strategy and delivery across the ten Greater Manchester local authorities.
4. Visualisation of the outputs on dashboards or similar to allow access to the outputs for decision makers and members of the public. What can and cannot be shared and the format can be negotiated.
5. Support the ten Greater Manchester local authorities to meet their statutory housing duties in regard to understanding the condition of housing stock in their area.
This commission potentially contains 2 x elements which views are sought on:
- A stock condition model/survey for the whole of Greater Manchester with breakdown of condition as low as possible - ideally address level.
- Visualisation tool for the model and an ability for the social housing element to be interrogated and updated.
The outputs for the model would need to be in a sharable format which the GMCA and partners can use for visualisation and modelling e.g. a CSV output. The output would be shared with the 10 x local authorities and the University of Manchester.
The contract would be for a one off piece of work delivering the model and any associated visualisations. Two costs will be sought for the two parts of the commission and the GMCA reserves the right to commission either both parts of only one part. We are interested in thoughts on the ability to deliver either or both parts.

title: Weed Control Contract
description:
Pre-Market Engagement Weed Control Contract 
The services required under this contract involve the successful contractor to undertake application of a range of pesticides and fertilisers and hand weeding across arrange of publicly accessible spaces located the city and county of Cardiff, the area of work covers the city’s 500 parks, over 300 housing estates, 2000km highway pavements but also includes special sites such as Cardiff Bay, cemeteries, Cardiff Castle and public rights of way.  
The aim of the contract is to manage weed growth to the required standards on a variety of hard surfaces, planted areas, walls, sport surfaces (natural and artificial), and control the spread of noxious weeds (such as Japanese Knotweed). Further to this there may be additional work added to include maintenance of Sustainable Drainage features and Green Roofs. 
These services must be delivered in accordance with the Government’s National Action Plan (NAP) so the contractor will be required to utilise the latest pesticide application technology to ensure that they comply with this and minimise the quantity of pesticides used to deliver the standards of control specified. Under this contract Cardiff Council will also require the contractor to reduce the volume of pesticide being used year on year over the period of the contract. The client will work with the contractor to help achieve this by increasing use of hand weeding, sweeping and mulching over the contract period.  
The successful contractor will be required to hold several of the following independently awarded industry specific quality certificates and schemes before they can tender –  
Amenity Assured Certificate 
BASIS qualification 
BASIS Advanced Contract certification 
Amenity Assured Certification 
Either ISO 14001 or BS9002 Or European equivalent certifications. 
The contractor will be supplied with digital plans of the areas of work which will be provided as either .shp or .pdf and the contractor will be required to employ a digital system to record their work daily on either a stand-alone system or a shared system to allow the Council to monitor performance, in addition to this the contractor will undertake some self-monitoring which will also need report to the contract manager.   
The contract is valued currently at just over £1.5M for the maximum four-year period assuming the two +1 extensions are taken up. The tender will be advertised in the winter of 26/27 and will be awarded once the tenders have been assessed using the following scores matrix 45% price : 45% quality : 10% Social value and will start in April 2027. The successful tenderer if not the current contractor should note that TUPE will apply to this contract and that payments are made on a monthly basis in accordance with a payment profile which will be included in the tender documentation. 
The Council is interested in receiving feedback from suitably qualified contractors to better understand any factors that may influence participation in the tender process for this work. 
If you have any questions that would help clarify the work required or the contract conditions or specification, please send them to HighwaysWasteandParks@cardiff.gov.uk. Further information can also be found on the Proactis Portal:https://supplierlive.proactisp2p.com/Account/Login

title: Co-Design and Co-Investment Research Phase 2
description:
In 2025, the GLA commissioned research to explore effective models of co-design and co-investment in adult skills provision. The research examined examples of best practice and identified lessons to support stronger partnerships between industry, skills providers and local government. The work culminated in a report setting out key findings and recommendations.
To maximise the value and impact of this research prior to publication, the GLA identified a requirement for a second phase of work. title: C086/2026/2027- Business Events Industry Engagement & Lead Generation
description:
The Welsh Government seeks to appoint a contractor to deliver and further develop a pan-Wales programme of business events industry engagement and lead generation activity over a two-year period. 
Building on the findings and recommendations of the Mid and West Wales Regional Engagement Pilot, the programme will support the development of stronger regional networks, increased industry collaboration, improved destination readiness and enhanced lead generation activity that aligns with the National Events Strategy for Wales, Tourism strategies and wider Welsh Government priorities. The programme is intended to build long-term industry capability and resilience, enabling stakeholders to take increasing ownership of engagement, collaboration and opportunity development activity beyond the life of the contract.
The primary aims and objectives of the contract are to:
•	Strengthen engagement with business events stakeholders across Wales.
•	Increase industry awareness and understanding of business events opportunities and support available through Meet In Wales.
•	Develop stronger regional networks and improve collaboration between destinations, local authorities, venues, hotels and industry partners.
•	Support destinations and businesses to identify, develop and pursue business events opportunities.
•	Improve the quality and quantity of lead generation activity across Wales.
•	Facilitate engagement with key intermediaries including agencies, event organisers, trade organisations and relevant industry bodies.
•	Identify barriers to growth and provide recommendations to support the development of Wales' business events offer.
•	Create mechanisms for sharing market intelligence, opportunities, best practice and industry updates.
•	Support the North Wales educational project by encouraging relevant industry representatives from across Wales to attend, engage fully in the sessions, take learning from the programme and apply this throughout the lifetime of the project.
•	Ensure opportunities to engage industry are fully utilised, including encouraging businesses to meet current Visit Wales accreditation requirements, secure an appropriate product listing, and explore opportunities to be bookable online through the TXGB distribution channel where relevant.
•	Support the development of a sustainable pipeline of business events opportunities that can deliver economic and wider benefits to Wales.
•	Provide measurable outcomes, regular updates and reporting and recommendations that support future business events policy and industry development activity.
•	Build industry capability, knowledge and confidence to support a sustainable and increasingly industry-led approach to business events engagement and opportunity development across Wales.
•	Develop and implement a clear transition and exit plan that enables industry stakeholders to assume greater ownership of networks, engagement activity, intelligence sharing and opportunity development by the end of the contract period.

title: T/HR061/26 Tooling and Storage Tender for ESS (Sweden)
description: The European Spallation Source (ESS) is a European Research Infrastructure Consortium (ERIC) committed to the goal of building and operating the world leading facility for research using neutrons. Once constructed in Lund, Sweden, it will provide new opportunities for researchers in a broad range of scientific areas including life sciences, energy, environmental technology, cultural heritage, and fundamental physics. It will be an accelerator-based facility producing neutrons for a large array of advanced instruments. The UK is a partner in construction of the ESS alongside 15 other European countries and has committed significant funding for construction. The Science and Technology Facility Council (STFC) is managing the UK contribution to ESS. The Active Cell Facility is one such contribution to be delivered by Remote Applications in Challenging Environments (RACE) — a department of the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA) (the ‘Purchaser’). Inside the Active Cells exhausted, highly radioactive parts involved in the neutron generation will be size reduced using remote handling technologies and removed for confinement. UKAEA are undertaking delivery of the Tooling Storage System, comprising six storage devices designed to house remotely operated tooling within the Active Cells. The scope of this tender is to manufacture, assemble, test and deliver to Sweden the following items: Shaft Cutting Station (SCS) Support Plate Storage Device Proton Beam Window (PBW) Strongback and Deployable Camera Stand (DCS) Storage Device Modular Wall Storage (MWS) Device, including Bolting Tool Caddies Chain Storage Device Storage Containers Cable Spooling Tool Testing shall include mechanical static checks, functional testing, and structural testing in accordance with the FAT plan.

title: Tuition Services Framework
description:
Royal Borough of Greenwich is establishing an Open Framework for the provision of Tuition services. The Framework will provide access to specialist providers delivering delivering outcome focussed tuition services to support and raise attainment, attendance, aspiration and engagement of vulnerable children and young people of statutory school age in education and for young people up to the age of 25 who have an Education, Health and Care Plan. To also work towards successful transition to education, employment or training post-16 at the end of Key Stage 4. The objectives of the services are to provide a flexible response to either compliment, or provide an alternative to the teaching and learning available within mainstream and specialist provision or for children not engaged in education.
The initial term of the Framework shall be three (3) years, with the option to extend for further period (s) of up to twenty-four (24) months, at the sole discretion of the Authority. 
The Framework is divided into three Lots.
Lot 1 - Universal Tuition
Lot 1 Universal Tuition is designed for Children and young people with no or low additional needs who are experiencing academic underachievement and require curriculum catch-up, reintegration support, or temporary education. Universal Tuition is educational provision for pupils who do not have Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) as defined by the SEND Code of Practice 2015, and who are accessing tuition for reasons other than special educational or medical needs.
Sublot 1 - Face-to-Face 1:1 Tuition
Individual face-to-face tuition delivered to children and young people requiring personalised academic support.
Sublot 2 - Remote/Online 1:1 Tuition
Individual tuition delivered remotely through online learning platforms.
Sublot 3 - Face-to-Face Group Tuition
Small group tuition delivered in person to support attainment, engagement and progression.
Sublot 4 - Remote/Online Group Tuition
Small group tuition delivered through online learning platforms.
Lot value (estimated)
£5,000,000 excluding VAT
£6,000,000 including VAT
Framework lot values may be shared with other lots
Lot 2 - Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Tuition
Lot 2 Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Tuition is designed for Children and young people with identified additional needs, including those with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs), Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) challenges, Autism Spectrum Conditions, Specific Learning Difficulties (SpLDs), Speech, Language and Communication Needs (SLCN), Attention and Executive Functioning Difficulties. Pupils may present with long-term disengagement, avoiding school environments, high-risk or extremely challenging behaviours such as physical aggression or offending behaviour, and require specialist adaptations, resources, and equipment.
Sublot 1 - Face-to-Face 1:1 Tuition
Specialist one-to-one tuition delivered in person for children and young people with SEND.
Sublot 2 - Remote/Online 1:1 Tuition
Specialist one-to-one tuition delivered through online learning platforms.
Sublot 3 - Face-to-Face Group Tuition
Specialist group tuition delivered in person for pupils with additional needs.
Sublot 4 - Remote/Online Group Tuition
Specialist group tuition delivered through online learning platforms.
Lot value (estimated)
£15,000,000 excluding VAT
£18,000,000 including VAT
Framework lot values may be shared with other lots
Lot 3 - Complex and Medical Tuition
Lot 3 Complex and Medical Needs Tuition is highly specialist educational provision for Pupils with significant medical, mental health, or multi-faceted needs that substantially impact their ability to engage in learning and require coordinated medical, therapeutic, and educational support during tuition delivery. Pupils may also be medically unfit for school attendance due to chronic conditions, injury, terminal illness, or inpatient care, and may require palliative care or hospital/home-based treatment.
Sublot 1 - Face-to-Face 1:1 Tuition
Individual tuition delivered in person for pupils with complex medical, mental health or other significant needs.
Sublot 2 - Remote/Online 1:1 Tuition
Individual tuition delivered remotely where online provision is appropriate to the pupil's needs.
Sublot 3 - Face-to-Face Group Tuition
Specialist group tuition delivered in person where appropriate for the needs of the cohort.
Sublot 4 - Remote/Online Group Tuition
Specialist group tuition delivered through online learning platforms.
Lot value (estimated)
£5,000,000 excluding VAT
£6,000,000 including VAT
Framework lot values may be shared with other lots

title: Provision of Asylum Support and Accommodation Services
description:
The Future Asylum Contracts Transformation (FACT), formerly Asylum Support and Accommodation Programme (ASAP), is a long-term transformation programme in the delivery of asylum support and accommodation services. 
The objective is a transformative re-procurement of services to replace the following contracts: 
•	Asylum Accommodation Support Contracts (AASC)
•	Advice Issue Reporting and Eligibility (AIRE)
•	Bridging Accommodation and Travel Services (BATS)
•	Asylum Support Payments (ASP)
The Home Office will be going to market for supplier(s) who can:
1.	Accommodation Provision – Identify, acquire, and maintain a diverse range of safe, suitable, and legally compliant accommodation types within agreed timescales and contracted regions to meet the varied needs of asylum seekers. Ensure accommodation aligns with statutory and regulatory standards, and is approved and allocated in collaboration with Local Authorities to support lawful use, community integration, and minimal impact on local services.
2.	Accommodation Management – Maintain accommodation to defined standards throughout its lifecycle, with robust systems in place for maintenance, temporary housing, and complaint communication and resolution to ensure a safe, suitable, and responsive living environment for asylum seekers.
3.	Transport – Arrange, manage, and deliver a 24/7/365 transportation service that is safe, timely, and responsive to asylum seeker needs in line with Home Office policy, whether independently or as directed by the Home Office. This includes the use of suitable, appropriately equipped, roadworthy vehicles and professional drivers, supported by an appropriate IT booking system, and ensuring the transport of asylum seekers, their dependents, and permitted belongings with appropriate assistance and within agreed timescales.
4.	Sustenance – Ensure that asylum seekers receive appropriate interim support through food vouchers or cash, including issuing food vouchers as a temporary or emergency measure until a Section 4 payment card is provided or replaced, and providing cash where full board accommodation is not available.
5.	Safety and Security – Ensure the safety and security of all staff and asylum seekers by implementing appropriate training, incident management, cross-provider collaboration, and vetting procedures.
6.	Audit & Assurance Services – Monitor provider compliance and performance through a structured assurance framework, combining inspections, desk-based reviews, and data analysis to identify trends, risks, and areas for improvement. The assuror must also produce clear, evidence-based reports to support supplier management and meet the reporting requirements of external assurance bodies.
7.	Service User Assistance – The Provider must ensure that asylum seekers receive clear, accessible, and timely information and support throughout their asylum journey - from initial application and arrival at accommodation to integration into the community. This includes maintaining a reliable single point of contact, delivering oral and written communication in a way asylum seekers can understand, assisting with access to local services, and continuously monitoring and improving the asylum seeker experience through inclusive feedback mechanisms.
8.	Wellbeing and Safeguarding – Establish effective communication channels with relevant partners to ensure timely notification and coordination on safeguarding and wellbeing matters. Where safeguarding concerns are identified, specialist safeguarding staff must be deployed and follow the prescribed action plan.
Proactively prevent and reduce safeguarding incidents, the Provider must offer ongoing support to asylum seekers and ensure that all staff and asylum seekers have access to resources that help them recognise, respond to, and report safeguarding concerns.
Regular welfare checks must be conducted for all asylum seekers.
-------
The Home Office intends to procure a proportion of the services under the Light Touch regime in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. 
For the avoidance of doubt  following the delivery model change in relation to Service User (SU) Assistance and External Assurance.
To clarify, Service User Assistance will be procured via a separate Competitive Flexible Procedure (CFP), supported by its own Market Engagement (ME) activity, and is therefore out of scope of the current procurement.
In addition, External Assurance will be procured via an alternative route and does not form part of this CFP.
Suppliers are requested to continue monitoring the original PMEN for any updates or further clarifications relevant to the current procurement.
**The content of this Notice, including the nature of works and services including start date of contract, may be subject to change.**

title: Professional and Generic Skills Programme
description:
NHS England is seeking to award a contract for a provider to design, deliver, administer and continuously improve a Professional and Generic Skills Programme for postgraduate medical and dental learners across the South-West of England. The programme will support the development of leadership, management, communication, patient safety, ethics and quality improvement skills, and must align with the General Medical Council (GMC) Generic Professional Capabilities Framework and wider NHS workforce priorities. The anticipated requirement is for approximately 225 learner places per year.
There shall be no guaranteed income under the Contract, but a cost per learner to be charged to the Contracting Authority in respect of each learner participating in the training programme under the Contract. The cost per learner shall be an all-inclusive cost and the only charge to be recovered under the Contract in respect of services provided.
The Awarded Contract shall be payable based on the volume of activity with a maximum price per learner of £1,022.22 (Exclusive of VAT).
The maximum cost per learner has been calculated using the total contract value divided by the indicative maximum learner volume over the contract term.
£1,150,000 ÷ 1,125 = £1,022.22.
The following risks have been declared through the contract notice:
Learner numbers may vary during the contract term. The current estimate is approximately 225 learner places per year, but actual demand may increase or decrease in response to workforce requirements, funding availability and regional demand. Any material change to learner numbers, and any associated change in contract value, will be subject to budget availability, agreement between the parties, NHS England governance approval and any required business case approvals.
The curriculum may also need to change during the contract term to reflect regulatory requirements, national policy, professional standards, workforce priorities or updates to the GMC Generic Professional Capabilities Framework. The successful provider will be required to work collaboratively with NHS England to review and update programme content where necessary, ensuring the programme remains current, compliant and aligned to emerging best practice. Any significant curriculum changes will be subject to appropriate governance and approval.

title: Barbican Renewal Programme - Temporary site services
description:
Temporary Site Services — Barbican Renewal Programme. Site-wide temporary site services for the refurbishment of the existing, occupied Barbican Centre, let under a Construction Management approach with Blue Sky Building appointed as Construction Manager.
The Contractor shall design (where required), supply, install, maintain, modify and ultimately remove all temporary site services supporting the site establishment and logistics set-up. Electrical scope comprises temporary distribution systems, boards, cabling, containment and sub-mains, power to all work areas including welding supplies and battery charging stations, and vertical and horizontal distribution to the hoists, tower crane, scaffolding/Haki staircases and the temporary stairs, walkways and loading platforms associated with TP1200. Lighting comprises safe access, emergency escape route, staircase, external, public-route and hoarding/fencing security lighting, with task lighting by others. Mechanical scope comprises temporary potable and non-potable water, chlorination, trace heating and booster pumps where required, supplies to welfare and site facilities, drainage, pumped drainage and waste connections, temporary ventilation, and supplies for commissioning and flushing. Energy metering, testing and commissioning are included throughout.
The package also covers phased diversions of existing electrical, water, drainage and RWP services; temporary fire alarm and life-safety measures including interfaces, wireless systems, detectors, call points, evacuation systems and isolations and reinstatements; and temporary security and access arrangements including access control, CCTV, intruder alarms, door release systems and secure partitions.
All works are to be phased to suit the site programme within a live, occupied building and may require out-of-hours working. Continuity and protection of landlord/tenant supplies, life-safety systems, critical plant and security systems is to be maintained at all times, with no outages undertaken without approved shutdown procedures. Shutdowns, terminations, isolations and controlled security access — particularly during the Pre-Closure Period — are to be planned and agreed in advance with the Barbican Centre project teams, with applications typically submitted a minimum of 2–4 weeks ahead, supported by shutdown methodologies, outage requests, contingency plans and temporary back-up arrangements. The Contractor shall develop and maintain a phasing strategy covering area-by-area handovers, temporary service adaptations, service migration works and occupier decant phases, and shall allow for all trade contractor access requirements and for fully up-to-date records of all temporary installations.
Ongoing obligations include regular inspection, planned and reactive maintenance, fault attendance, PAT and periodic testing, temporary generator support if required, and out-of-hours and 24-hour emergency call-out capability for the full project duration. On completion, temporary installations are to be removed, redundant supplies disconnected and affected areas made good. Utility consumption charges and landlord utility costs are excluded.

title: North Close Play Area Cycle Skills
description:
St Stephen Parish Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced contractor for the design, supply and installation of a cycle skills area within North Close Play Area, Greenwood Park, Chiswell Green, St Albans, AL2 3JX.
The project aims to provide a durable, safe and engaging cycle skills facility for children and young people up to 14 years of age, supporting the development of cycling skills, balance, coordination and confidence through active outdoor recreation.
The successful contractor will be responsible for the complete design, supply, construction and installation of the facility, including all associated site preparation, foundations, materials, equipment, safety measures, reinstatement works, waste removal, inspection and certification. The contractor will also be required to provide design drawings, visualisations and details of materials and construction methods.
The cycle skills area will occupy an area of approximately 1,500 square metres and should comprise a range of separate and interconnected skills-development features. These may include balance beams, rollers, bridges, berms, ramps, narrow riding sections, slalom features, elevated elements, technical riding obstacles and similar features designed to improve cycle handling skills. The Council is seeking a collection of individual skills-development features and progression zones rather than a pump track, BMX track, mountain bike trail or continuous riding circuit.
The completed facility must be suitable for unsupervised public use, constructed from durable materials, require minimal maintenance and have an anticipated service life of at least 15 years. Contractors should demonstrate how their proposals address accessibility and inclusive design principles.
The works shall include site management, welfare facilities, temporary fencing, signage, health and safety management, protection of the public, and measures to minimise disruption to park users and neighbouring properties during construction.
The completed facility must comply with all relevant British Standards, European Standards and applicable legislation. An independent post-installation inspection and certification must be undertaken prior to handover, with any identified defects rectified before completion.
The estimated contract value is £50,000 including all design, supply, installation, inspections and associated works. The anticipated contract commencement date is November 2026, with completion preferably within one month of commencement.
Full tender documentation, specifications, submission requirements and evaluation criteria are contained within the Invitation to Tender documents.

title: Apprentice Worker Agency
description:
Northumbrian Water Group (NWL) is committed to developing future talent through a high-quality apprenticeship programme which supports workforce planning, succession management and skills development across the organisation.
We require a supplier to provide Apprenticeship Agency Services across both Northumbrian Water and Essex & Suffolk Water. The supplier will act as the employer of apprentices on behalf of NWL and provide employment, payroll, HR administration, compliance and apprentice support services throughout the duration of the apprenticeship programme.
The successful supplier will work collaboratively with NWL's Early Careers Team, hiring managers and training providers to ensure apprentices receive a positive experience and are supported to successfully complete their programmes.
Service Requirements
The supplier will be required to:
•	Employ apprentices on behalf of NWL through an apprenticeship agency model.
•	Issue and maintain employment contracts and associated employment documentation.
•	Undertake payroll administration and statutory payments.
•	Manage apprentice employment records.
•	Provide HR guidance and employee relations support relating to apprentices.
•	Ensure compliance with apprenticeship funding rules and employment legislation.
•	Support apprentice wellbeing and welfare.
•	Conduct regular reviews and progress monitoring with apprentices.
•	Liaise with apprenticeship training providers where required.
•	Provide management information and performance reporting.
•	Support mobilisation and onboarding of new apprentices.
•	Deliver services across both the Northeast and Essex & Suffolk operating areas.
The supplier must demonstrate excellent customer service, strong apprenticeship sector knowledge and the ability to support the continued growth of NWL's apprenticeship programme.
Objectives
The objectives of this contract are to:
•	Provide a compliant and effective apprenticeship employment service.
•	Deliver a positive apprentice experience.
•	Support apprentice retention and successful completion rates.
•	Ensure consistent support for apprentices and managers.
•	Provide accurate and timely payroll and administration services.
•	Deliver robust reporting and management information.
•	Support NWL's commitment to early careers and future talent development.

title: Preliminary Market Engagement for the provision of  Social Care Provider Management Software
description:
Warwickshire County Council is exploring the potential commissioning of a Social Care Provider Relationship Management Tool to strengthen how the Council engages with, understands and manages its local social care provider market.
The Council works with a wide range of social care providers across different service areas, including regulated and non-regulated provision. Effective provider relationship management is essential to supporting market sustainability, understanding provider capacity and pressures, improving communication, monitoring risks, and ensuring that commissioned services continue to meet local needs and statutory responsibilities.
At present, information about providers, quality, performance, risks, engagement activity and market intelligence may be held across different systems, teams and processes. This can make it more difficult to maintain a single, consistent view of provider relationships and to use information proactively to support commissioning, contract management, quality assurance and market shaping activity.
The Council is therefore interested in understanding whether there are digital tools available that could help provide a more coordinated, efficient and intelligence-led approach to provider relationship management. This may include functionality such as provider records, contact management, engagement logs, risk and issue tracking, quality and performance information, market intelligence, reporting, dashboards, and integration with existing Council systems where appropriate.
The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to understand the range of solutions available, how they are currently being used in social care or comparable sectors, the extent to which they could meet the Council’s requirements, likely implementation considerations, support models, interoperability, data security arrangements, and indicative costs.
This engagement will help the Council assess the maturity of the market, identify potential delivery options, understand any risks or constraints, and inform whether a future procurement exercise would be appropriate.

title: UK7 - Tender Notice Prevention of Peripheral Cold Injuries
description:
Description
The UK Armed Forces are more frequently operating in cold environments to contribute to NATO’s deterrence in the High North and on the Eastern flank; but data suggest that the number of cases of peripheral cold injuries is increasing in deployed Service Personnel (SP), even during short deployments. Given our growing presence in the Nordic-Baltic regions, Defence urgently needs to identify and protect SP susceptible to cold injuries and improve the clinical assessment of injured SP for their safe and timely return to cold environments. This work will aim to reduce the risk of peripheral cold injuries by developing a prediction tool to identify susceptible SP; and improve deployability by developing a clinical assessment tool to enable clinicians to assess injured SP safely and efficiently, year-round. This laboratory-based research will largely take place at the climate chamber in North Yorkshire.

title: Stalking Advocacy Provision
description:
1.	The Provider will provide an Independent Stalking Advocacy service dedicated to delivering specialist support across the Dyfed-Powys Police area. This should include provision of an Independent Stalking Advocacy Caseworker (ISAC). 
2.	The ISAC will provide expert stalking advocacy support to victims of stalking, supporting them through the complex criminal justice system, managing risk and improving safety.
3.	The service should prioritise non-domestic abuse related stalking victims and then assess domestic abuse stalking victims on a case-by-case risk assessed basis. 
4.	ISAC Support will be delivered face-to-face, over the phone and virtually via video calls where appropriate, to allow the provision of support across the large geographical area.
5.	The Provider will work with Dyfed-Powys Police to embed a police referral process into the ISAC service.
6.	The Provider will enable self-referrals from victims/survivors and referrals from other support services as appropriate.
7.	The ISAC will work on creating pathways with, and building the knowledge of, local victim and witness support services, and specialist domestic violence and sexual violence services. This will ensure all victims of stalking in the Dyfed-Powys Police area receive high quality stalking advocacy support to meet their need, irrespective of risk level. 
8.	To ensure the service actively promotes a person-centred approach with the method of delivery and length of support being informed by the service user's needs.
9.	To make necessary referrals where there are identified safeguarding concerns.
10.	To ensure compliance with the Independent Stalking Advocate statutory guidance regarding support for victims under 16 or the children of adult victims. 
11.	To work with partners to share key trends that may inform wider interventions and awareness raising. 
12.	To actively contribute to the stalking and prevention agenda across Wales and/or nationally. 
13.	To consider the wider support needs of service users and make arrangements for onward referrals for specialist support where appropriate. 
14.	To work with the Commissioner to evidence the effectiveness of the service and the social value delivered.

title: Out-of-Hour Emergency Service for households who are at risk of homelessness outside of standard operating times. Out of Hours emergency housing options telephone service.
description:
Oldham Council require a Provider to operate a Statutory Out of Hours Homelessness Service for our residents
The support currently provided by the Council covers 'normal working' hours however access to appropriate support and advice is required 24 hours, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. The out of hours service is a telephone-based service, where residents who need emergency help and support with regards to homelessness outside of usual office hours (Mon - Fri 9am - 5pm) can telephone the dedicated number.
The out of hours service operates from 5pm to 9am Monday - Thursday and from 5pm Friday - 9am Monday. Please note the service operates 24 hours through Saturday and Sunday and bank holidays. This totals 128 hours per week not including bank holidays, the number of bank holiday hours totals 192 per annum. The Provider is required to 'triage' the telephone calls to determine if the household(s) are homeless that evening or not.
If the household(s) is not homeless that evening, details of the household should be taken and referred back through to the Homelessness Team to make contact the next working day.
If the household(s) is homeless that night then the Provider will be expected to undertake a mini assessment to establish if the household(s) are eligible for assistance, homeless that evening and there is reason to believe they have a priority need.
If the household(s) meet the threshold prescribed by the Council, then the telephone operator must secure temporary accommodation for that household using the Council's temporary accommodation framework. It is then the Provider's responsibility to place the household into the accommodation.
The Provider must then notify the Council of the placement and the Council's Homelessness team will pick up the case for full assessment the next working day.
All calls must be handled in a professional and courteous manner ensuring all enquiries are dealt with in an efficient manner.
The Provider will be expected to keep up to date records of any customer contact using the Council's systems, training of which will be provided.
At the end of every shift the Provider will be required to complete a detailed handover document, the format of which will be agreed prior to the commencement of the contract. Staff are required to have knowledge and experience in the sphere of homelessness and in particular temporary accommodation and housing needs. Staff are also required to effectively signpost residents to relevant organisations to support in the wrap around care package. It is desirable but not essential that staff undergo and hold up to date DBS checks. The Provider will be expected to attend monthly monitoring meetings with the Council along with reports, the format of which will be agreed prior to the commencement of the contract. Any complaints would be handled by the Council using the Council's complaints procedure. The Provider is required to notify the Council of any complaint and provide customer details

description:
Milton Keynes City Council (MKCC) ('The Council')  is seeking to engage with suppliers in advance of a future procurement exercise for a cloud-based Regulatory and Operational Case Management Platform.
The Council currently utilises a legacy case management solution across a range of services and is exploring replacement options that will support future service delivery, digital transformation, mobile working, data management and reporting requirements.
The Council is seeking a modern Software as a Service (SaaS) solution capable of supporting multiple service areas through a shared platform and data model.
Services anticipated to be within scope include:
•	Environmental Health
•	Environmental Crime
•	Trading Standards
•	Licensing
•	Private Sector Housing
•	Emergency Planning
•	Other related operational and regulatory functions
The Council's preferred approach is a single corporate platform, although modular solutions from a single supplier may also be considered where they provide integrated functionality and a seamless user experience.
The platform is expected to provide functionality including:
•	Case management
•	Inspection management
•	Investigation management
•	Licensing management
•	Enforcement management
•	Document and evidence management
•	Workflow and task management
•	Mobile working capability
•	Reporting and dashboard functionality
•	Information governance and retention management
•	Officer safety alerting
•	Integration with existing corporate systems
•	Data migration from an existing legacy system
The Council is particularly interested in understanding how suppliers can support:
•	Cross-service working
•	Shared premises and entity records
•	Mobile and field-based operations
•	Cloud-first delivery models
•	Integration with GIS, LLPG and other corporate systems
•	Future use of automation and artificial intelligence
•	Flexible configuration without supplier dependency
The Council intends to hold a supplier engagement session via Microsoft Teams.
The purpose of the event will be to:
•	Share the Council's objectives
•	Present high-level requirements
•	Understand market capability
•	Explore implementation approaches
•	Gather supplier feedback on proposed procurement routes and contract structures
This market engagement exercise is intended solely to gather information and understand market capabilities. Milton Keynes City Council may, at its discretion, use or choose not to use any information received during this exercise when shaping future procurement requirements.
This engagement is not an invitation to tender, a call for competition, or a commitment by the Council to undertake any procurement or award any contract. Any future procurement opportunity will be advertised separately and conducted through an appropriate procurement process.
Interested suppliers are invited to participate in a market engagement event where the Council will present its current position, emerging requirements and procurement approach.

title: CEFAS26-117 provision of an Avigilon Network Video Recorder
description:
Contract for the supply, installation, and configuration of a new Network Video Recorder to replace its existing server, which has reached end-of-support status. The current system utilises an Avigilon server supporting approximately 18 encoders and 20 users. The camera network comprises of approximately 30 analogue cameras, although they are not all always connected at the same time. 
The Home Office prefers Cefas to have video capability to be able to view the animals without human interaction, which enables the ability to spot specific behavioural patterns within the holding tanks which cannot be attributed to a prey response or change in lighting. The users of the holding tanks are required to obtain Home Office licences to undertake experiments on animals, and in most (if not all) cases, the use of cameras is laid out within this licence approval.  
Scope of Requirements: 
Technical Requirement  
One rack-mounted server is needed to handle the number of users and cameras specified above, with enough storage capacity for future upgrades to high-definition images with IP cameras. The server must use: 
a RAID6 array to withstand up to two disk failures  
enough storage to keep high definition images for a minimum of one month before being overwritten after capacity is reached  
a modern and supported Windows Server Operating System such as Windows Server 2022 or 2025 
Avigilon Server software to ensure compatibility with the existing environment.  
Environmental Considerations 
Unit has a low power consumption. 
Consideration of how packaging will be managed. Ideally at the time of installation the supplier will remove packaging and dispose of by ethical and environmentally friendly methods. Where possible packaging is to be re-used or recycled. 
Hardware, Software, PC, Licenses, operating systems 
Avigilon Server software licensed appropriately for 18 encoders and up to 20 client users. 
Compatibility with existing hardware/software/equipment  
Compatibility with existing analogue cameras and encoders is essential. 
The operating system uses a modern, supported Windows Server Operating System to ensure compatibility with Cefas' endpoint protection software and server management tools. 
Ease of maintenance  
The supplied solution is a genuine Avigilon hardware appliance. 
Parts, Consumables and Updates 
All parts are covered under warranty in the event of failure  
Warranties and Guarantees 
Warranties will start from the point of acceptance of delivery and once the goods have been tested to ensure they are in working order. A minimum warranty period of 12 months is included in the purchase.  
Warranties will include replacements of parts in the event of failure, including disk failures and full server replacement in the event of a catastrophic failure. 
Options for on-site support and/or remote assistance will be available.
