Ireland – Construction work for electricity power lines – The MaresConnect 750MW HVDC Interconnector System
description: The MaresConnect Project is a proposed 750 MW, 320 kV High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) electricity interconnector linking Denbighshire, Wales and North County Dublin, Ireland. Developed by MaresConnect Limited, a joint venture between Foresight Group Holdings Ltd and Etchea Energy Nominees Ltd, the project will transmit electricity via approximately 240 km of subsea and underground cables between new converter stations on each side. It aims to enhance security of supply, market integration, and renewable energy utilisation between the Irish and GB grids. MaresConnect shall utilise Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology and the configuration shall be a Symmetrical Monopole. The rated DC voltage shall be +/-320 kV. The link shall be bi-directional and shall have a rated power (receiving end) of 750 MW. The project is being procured as separate EPC (Turnkey) contracts, divided into four lots: LOT 1A: EPC for two HVDC Converter Stations; LOT 1B: EPC for one Irish 400kV AC Tail Substation; LOT 2A: EPC for the HVDC subsea and underground cable system, and for the HVAC underground cable system in Wales (Bodelwyddan); LOT 2B: EPC for the supply and installation of HVAC cable system in Ireland (Dublin). The contract model for the lots will be amended FIDIC Conditions of Contract for EPC/Turnkey Projects (Silver Book). MaresConnect has conducted Preliminary Market Engagement prior to publication of this Contract Notice and encourages further collaboration between OEMs and Construction Contractors to establish bidding arrangements in time for the next step of the Procurement Process (notably the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire).

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Packaging-Entwicklung bis zu einem funktionsfähigen Prototyp eines implantierbaren, optischen Stimulators
description: Das Ziel des geplanten interdisziplinären Else Kröner Fresenius Zentrums für Optogenetische Therapien (Light2Treat EKFZ) ist es, das große Potenzial der Optogenetik - die Steuerung von Zellen mit Licht durch lichtempfindliche Proteine (Opsine) - für die klinische Medizin nutzbar zu machen. Die Optogenetik ermöglicht eine räumlich begrenzte, zelltypspezifische Steuerung von Organen und verspricht eine transformative Verbesserung der klinischen Versorgung im Vergleich zu herkömmlichen elektrischen Medizinprodukten. Optogenetische Therapien kombinieren Gentherapie und optische Medizintechnik. Sie bieten eine breitere Anwendbarkeit als herkömmliche Gentherapie und versprechen eine höhere Wirksamkeit als derzeitig verfügbare Medizinprodukte, jedoch verbunden mit erhöhten regulatorischen Herausforderungen. Das Light2Treat EKFZ zielt auf die Entwicklung und Umsetzung von vier Therapien mit einem überzeugenden Verhältnis von großem erwartetem Nutzen und beherrschbaren Risiken ab. Aufbauend auf den Werkzeugen und der Expertise von fünf Light2Treat-Plattformen und dem zentralen Support werden die Light2Treat-Teams optogenetische Cochlea Implantate, Netzhautstimulation, Magenschrittmacher und Gehirn Computer Interfaces für Patient*innen entwickeln, die an Taubheit, Blindheit, Gastroparese bzw. motorischen Defiziten leiden. Die Light2Treat-Plattformen adressieren den gemeinsamen Bedarf an optimierten Opsinen, effizientem, spezifischem und sicherem viralen Gentransfer für eine stabile Opsin-Expression, experimenteller und computergestützter Krankheitsmodellierung, effizienter Immunmodulation und tiefgreifender Phänotypisierung sowie energieeffizienten, langzeitstabilen und sicheren optischen Medizinprodukten.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – "Fahrverhalten, Flächenanspruch und Sicherheit von Radverkehr auf Gefällestrecken "
description: Ziel des Forschungsvorhabens ist die Schließung der Erkenntnislücken zu Verkehrssicherheit, Fahrverhal-ten und Flächenbedarf von Radverkehr auf Gefälle- bzw. Steigungsstrecken. Die Aussagen des gegen-wärtigen Regelwerks hierzu sind nicht geeignet, Planenden einen ausreichenden Anhaltspunkt zur ver-kehrssicheren und attraktiven Gestaltung der Führung des Radverkehrs zu bieten. Die derzeitige Ausgangslage ist dadurch gekennzeichnet, dass Gefällestrecken für den Radverkehr ein erhöhtes Unfallrisiko bergen (UDV Nr. 96/98). Das gilt an allen Straßen mit und ohne separate Radver-kehrsanlagen. Wobei sich das Risiko entsprechend der Ortslage unterschiedlich darstellt. So ist bei ca. 17% der Alleinunfälle von Radfahrenden mit Personenschaden als Charakteristik der Unfallstelle „Gefäl-le“ angegeben, außerorts betrachtet bei ca. 39% (UDV Nr.98). Im Regelwerk der FGSV und international werden deshalb für Gefällestrecken größere Wegbreiten für den Radverkehr empfohlen. Konkrete Empfehlungen werden aber nicht gegeben. Es ist aber plausibel, dass verschiedene Aspekte im engen Zusammenhang mit den Geschwindigkeiten des Radverkehrs ste-hen. Gleichzeitig ist über den Zusammenhang zwischen Geschwindigkeit des Radverkehrs und dessen Verkehrssicherheit, Trassierungsparameter, Verträglichkeit mit dem Fußverkehr, Empfindlichkeit gegen Unebenheiten, erforderliche Haltesichtweiten, Fahrstabilität und den Einfluss von Randmarkierungen wenig bekannt. Damit fehlen Planenden die Grundlagen für die Wahl der geforderten Breitenzuschläge bzw. Grundlagen für die grundsätzliche Entscheidung der Führungsform bei Gefälle und Steigung. Im Rahmen eines Forschungsprojekts sind deshalb mögliche Zusammenhänge aus Längsneigung, Länge der Längsneigung und der daraus resultierenden Geschwindigkeit zu untersuchen. Auf Grundlage der Geschwindigkeiten sind die Auswirkungen auf o.g. Aspekte zu bestimmen. Auf Basis der Forschungsergebnisse sollen belastbare Empfehlungen für das Regelwerk formuliert werden.

title: Strategic Charging Infrastructure Scheme
description:
National Highways is working in collaboration with the Office for Zero Emission Vehicles (OZEV), a joint unit between the Department for Transport and the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, to strengthen electricity network capacity to selected motorway service areas (MSA) in England through the Strategic Charging Infrastructure (SCI) Scheme.
The transition to zero-emission vehicles is expected to drive significant growth in demand for electric vehicle (EV) charging at MSAs. This will require a visible and functional charging network across the motorway network to support current and future EV drivers and provide confidence when undertaking long-distance journeys. However, at several locations, the deployment of charging infrastructure is constrained by the existing electricity network capacity. In some cases, the cost of grid upgrades to meet future demand is not commercially viable for industry and represents a key barrier to the provision of additional EV charging infrastructure.
The SCI Scheme will support the development of a strong open-access (can be used with any EV vehicle regardless of manufacturer) EV charging network across the motorway network by strengthening electricity network infrastructure to selected MSAs where investment is not commercially viable.  The resulting network capacity will then be available to firms installing EV charging at the site at a subsided and commercially viable price. An indicative allocation of £190 million has been made for the scheme. Enabling civils works, such as land preparation and substation housing, to ensure all funded sites meet a minimum standard at adoption and connection stage, may also be within scope of the packages where required.
Further details are provided within a separate scope document that can be accessed via this link: https://highways.sharepoint.com/:f:/s/NationalHighwaysProcurement-MaterialforExternalRelease/IgDtJCSl2pP2R7XoJFkawLs4AWlSqYeOoUX2WNXcMEkbYWM?e=iZisZL
Following completion of Phase 1 Pre-Market Engagement, which focused on understanding supplier capability, National Highways is undertaking Phase 2 of Pre-Market Engagement to seek supplier feedback on potential delivery, packaging, commercial, evaluation and route to market options for the SCI Scheme. The objective of this engagement is to gather market feedback that will help National Highways refine its approach to best support the effective delivery of the SCI Scheme, whilst maximising market participation, supporting private sector investment, and delivering value for money.
The questionnaire for interested suppliers to complete is available via this link: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/P3t3TXQUUN. The information provided in response to this questionnaire will be collected, processed and stored solely for the purposes of designing and progressing the SCI Scheme.
The information provided in the response to the Pre-Market Engagement questionnaire will not constitute a formal tender response and will not be used to evaluate suppliers as part of any future procurement process. Responses will be used solely to inform the development of the SCI Scheme procurement strategy, including the delivery, packaging, commercial and route-to-market approaches.
National Highways thanks you for taking the time to complete this questionnaire. 
This pre-market notice will be open for a calendar month, ending on 30 October 2026.
Should suppliers have any difficulty with the questions or accessing any of the documents, please send an email to the ADProcurement@nationalhighways.co.uk inbox.

title: Procurement Intake & orchestration Software as a Service (SaaS)
description:
National Grid intends to award a contract for the provision of Procurement Intake and Orchestration Software as a Service (SaaS).
The service being awarded is Software as a Service (SaaS)
The software is a commercial off the shelf product.
National Grid's current Source 2 Pay (S2P) landscape has fragmented systems, inconsistent intake routes, and heavy manual coordination across sourcing, purchasing, and payment processes, creating friction for end users and limiting procurement's ability to control demand, enforce policy, and deliver value at scale. Employees navigate multiple tools and approval paths depending on category, business unit, and geography, resulting in long cycle times, unmanaged or maverick spend, poor visibility of requests in flight, and downstream issues in P2P execution. As procurement volumes and complexity continue to grow, this operating model does not scale and constrains the adoption of AI.
National Grid is advancing a multi-year digital transformation of the Procurement function across both UK and US to enhance strategic sourcing, supplier engagement, and operational efficiency. Building on foundational efforts, the FY 26-27 initiative will focus on upgrading core platforms, automating processes, and preparing for future technologies and agentic AI. As part of this digital transformation, the procurement team recently ran an RFP for a procurement intake and orchestration solution and has now identified a supplier with suitable and sufficient software that has the required system capabilities.

title: Oxford Law Trove
description:
Following the publication of a Transparency Notice on 13 August 2026, and a Contract Award Notice on 14 August 2026, University of Keele is publishing this Contract Details Notice to announce, in accordance with its statutory obligations under Section 53 of the Procurement Act 2023, that it has awarded a contract to Oxford University Press for Oxford Law Trove.
1. Direct Award Justification
This contract has been awarded by direct award in accordance with Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Direct Award in Special Cases). The justification for direct award is set out under Schedule 5, Paragraph 5 (Single supplier - intellectual property or exclusive rights) of the Act.
2. Justification Narrative
Oxford Law Trove provides access to specific legal textbooks, journals and digital content essential for teaching, learning and research within the University's Law School.
The publisher, Oxford University Press, owns or exclusively controls the copyright, intellectual property rights, publishing rights and licence rights to the specific works contained within this database. No competitor can legally supply that exact content without permission from the Publisher. Competition is therefore absent by law, not by market preference.
Failure to renew this subscription would:
Disrupt access to materials needed for teaching and curriculum design 
Impact student learning outcomes 
Create significant reputational risk for the University's Law School.
3. Reasons for Direct Award
The University has determined that:
Oxford University Press holds exclusive rights to the content within Oxford Law Trove.
No reasonable alternative supplier can lawfully provide equivalent access to the same content.
Continuity of access is critical for teaching delivery.
4. Estimated Contract Value
The estimated value of the contract over the 48-month period (including potential renewals) is £228,000 (excluding VAT).
5. Known Risks
None identified. The University reserves the right to terminate or renew the subscription at its sole discretion. Any future modifications will be managed in accordance with the Act.

title: CLA - Copyright Licensing Agency
description:
Following the publication of a Transparency Notice on 13 August 2026, and a Contract Award Notice on 14 August 2026, University of Keele is publishing this Contract Details Notice to announce, in accordance with its statutory obligations under Section 53 of the Procurement Act 2023, that it has awarded a contract to the Copyright Licensing Agency (CLA) for a CLA Higher Education Licence. 
1. Direct Award Justification
This contract has been awarded by direct award in accordance with Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Direct Award in Special Cases). The justification for direct award is set out under Schedule 5, Paragraph 5 (Single supplier - intellectual property or exclusive rights) of the Act.
2. Justification Narrative
The University requires a Copyright Licensing Agency (CLA) Higher Education Licence to lawfully support the copying, digitisation, storage and distribution of copyrighted extracts from books, journals, magazines and certain digital publications for teaching, learning, administration and research purposes.
The CLA Licence is not a discretionary subscription but the legal mechanism enabling the University to comply with copyright law. CLA is the sole collective licensing organisation in the UK authorised by participating publishers and authors to grant these permissions in the higher education sector.
No alternative supplier can provide an equivalent licence covering the same copyright repertoire and permissions. The procurement therefore falls within the direct award provisions relating to exclusive copyright and intellectual property rights under Schedule 5, Paragraph 5 of the Act.
3. Reasons for Direct Award
The University has determined that:
CLA holds exclusive rights to grant the copyright permissions required.
No reasonable alternative supplier exists for this requirement.
Failure to secure the licence would place the University in breach of copyright law.
4. Estimated Contract Value
The estimated value of the contract over the 48-month period (including potential renewals) is £388,000 (excluding VAT).
5. Known Risks
None identified. The University reserves the right to terminate or renew the subscription at its sole discretion.

title: UK2 - Deployable Maritime Secure Analysis Capability – Preliminary Market Engagement
description:
The Ministry of Defence (the Authority) is exploring the market for a deployable capability that would allow users to handle information securely while operating at sea for extended periods, and to share information securely between deployed and shore-based users. Existing arrangements provide limited capacity at sea. 
The Authority is interested in solutions that are readily deployable through standardised freight transport (air, land and sea) and can be procured with an ongoing maintenance, training and in-service support solution package. The Authority is also interested in suppliers who could provide all or part of such a solution and supports collaborative working with other suppliers to jointly develop a solution, together with appetite and capability for development.  Areas of interest include secure marinised deployable or modular workspaces (e.g. containers), IT and communications integration, secure data transfer (including hardware and software), in-service support, and the design, demonstration and Secure by Design process for such a capability. 
This notice opens a staged engagement. Suppliers who register an interest and meet the access conditions below will receive a Request for Information marked OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE, followed by a clarification period and an industry day. The Authority will use responses to refine its requirement, its commercial strategy and its delivery plan before any competition.
This notice is issued for preliminary market engagement only. It is not a call for competition, an invitation to tender or a commitment to procure. Participation is voluntary and at the supplier's own cost; responses are not scored. Any competition will be conducted under a separately published tender notice and will be open to all suppliers meeting its published conditions of participation, whether or not they took part in this engagement. The Authority anticipates a competitive flexible procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, subject to approval, and is considering whether a paid development stage may form part of that procedure.

title: South Midlands Connect to Work Programme (Milton Keynes Area)
description:
Milton Keynes City Council has been awarded grant funding by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) to participate in the Connect to Work initiative, via the accountable body ‘West Northants Council (WNC)’ as part of the South Midlands region.
Connect to Work is the initial and significant element of the Get Britain Working Strategy, the aim of which is to support people with disabilities, those with health conditions and people with complex barriers, to find suitable work.
The Connect to Work Programme aims to support individuals furthest from the labour market into sustainable employment. It is a voluntary programme launched by DWP (the Department for Work and Pensions) to help tackle economic inactivity by providing a specific form of supported employment targeted at the right people at the right time, based on their individual circumstances. It is a national programme, delivered in clusters of local authorities. In the case of this region, the South Midlands cluster – namely Bedford Borough, Central Bedfordshire, Luton, Milton Keynes City, North Northamptonshire and West Northamptonshire.
For the purposes of this contract, it relates to the Milton Keynes City element of the programme.
The Contractor will be expected to deliver the five stages of the supported employment model:
- Engagement: Building relationships with local services to raise aspirations and confidence among potential Participants.  
- Vocational Profiling: A detailed discovery process to identify Participants' strengths, needs, and employment goals.  
- Employer Engagement: Building partnerships with employers to understand their needs and support Participants through the recruitment process.  
- Job Matching: Identifying job vacancies that match Participants' profiles and working with employers to create suitable roles.  
- On and Off the Job Support: Providing tailored support to Participants and employers to ensure sustained employment and career progression.  
The Council proposes to enter into a contract that will be for a term of 3 years and 7 months with the successful tenderer (Service Provider) unless terminated in accordance with the Conditions of Contract. 
This procurement was undertaken via the Open procedure under the Light Touch Regime.

title: Public Transport (Bus and Tram) Shelter Improvement Programme – Full Design and Build Further Market Engagement
description:
South Yorkshire is at a transformative point in public transport, with buses joining trams under public control in 2027. This creates a unique opportunity to reshape the passenger experience and establish a system that sets new standards for design, accessibility, and civic pride.
SYMCA are seeking an exceptional architecturally designed shelter to help create a world-class family of transport infrastructure that becomes synonymous with South Yorkshire across bus and tram.
To achieve this vision, SYMCA are looking to engage in a single Design & Build procurement approach. Welcoming bids from joint ventures and consortiums to encourage submissions for a distinct, human-centred, durable design.  This will be a staged award for concept design initially, followed by progression to detailed design and a final works/build stage.
SYMCA have also recently published the South Yorkshire Peoples Network (SYPN), showcasing some of the branding updates to transport in South Yorkshire. This scheme directly links to “Make Buses work for Everyone”, SYMCA are looking to introduce a hierarchy of transport asset design for both bus and tram:
Higher:  Higher-level architectural design of a Shelter, encompassing beauty and creativity while maintaining a distinct South Yorkshire heritage.
Standard: Standard shelter design for the Bus and Tram Shelters across South Yorkshire. Modular, maintainable and functional while still coordinating in a South Yorkshire design vision.
Stop/Pole: A re-think at what a simple bus stop should deliver, from the core service identification to updated passenger information.
SYMCA are seeking to enter a Design & Build contract by March 2027, allowing the appointed bidder(/s) to start Concept Design work. SYMCA are targeting getting shelters in the ground by January 2028, with an organised prioritisation plan for the roll-out of these shelters.
The tender is expected to be published late October 2026.
Please note, an initial market engagement was published on 23rd July 2026 (2026/S 000-069955) for the expected concept design requirements only.  Following further consideration of responses, the scope has evolved into a full design and build award, the Authority are now seeking further feedback and information on this changed approach.

title: Laings Easiform Homes Redevelopment
description: Laing Easiform homes are a form of non-traditional construction built from the 1920s to 1970s using in-situ poured concrete walls within reusable steel formwork. While not designated as defective under the Housing Defects Act 1984, some dwellings have reached the end of their economic life due to structural deterioration and corrosion of embedded reinforcement. As part of Exeter City Council's wider regeneration and housing quality improvement programmes, a number of Laing Easiform homes were earmarked for reconstruction in 2015. Several homes have since been demolished and rebuilt; however, a number of properties are incomplete following insolvency of the original contractor, resulting in yet to be commenced and part-built structures that have stood dormant for some time. Following a review of options, the current intention is to demolish these partially constructed dwellings. In some cases, this will involve the rebuilding of only one side of a semi-detached pair, where the adjoining dwelling remains occupied and under separate freehold. Exeter City Council is now preparing to re-engage the market to deliver the remainder of the homes, ensuring that the design, construction approach, and delivery model are appropriate to the complexity of the site and the various stages of progress across each of the properties.

The services will stabilise children and families who have support needs that require statutory intervention. The requirement includes the supply of five deployable monitoring stations capable of monitoring methane (CH₄), hydrogen sulphide (H₂S), total volatile organic compounds (TVOCs), PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, together with wind speed and wind direction monitoring. title: Procurement of a master developer for the redevelopment of Land at Packmoor, Stoke-on-Trent
description:
Stoke-on-Trent City Council is seeking to appoint a master developer to bring forward the redevelopment of land at Packmoor in line with the Packmoor Masterplan.
The land is owned by Stoke-on-Trent City Council, who in 2023 confirmed that the subject site is surplus to operational requirements. Work has since explored options for the future use and enhancement of the land, which has a development capacity of circa 800 new homes plus a significant care facility and other local enhancements.
The site is located to the north of Stoke-on-Trent, approximately 4 miles from Hanley which is the City Centre. The M6 motorway connects Stoke-on-Trent to major cities including Manchester and Liverpool and connects south to the outskirts of Birmingham and Coventry.
The Council has produced a detailed Masterplan which considered potential development options for the site and, at a meeting of the City Council’s Cabinet on 14th July 2026, the Council approved to progress with an option which could deliver up to 816 new homes, including around 200 affordable rented homes, together with specialist accommodation for older people
The Council now wishes to carry out a formal Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) process in order to seek views from the development industry regarding the redevelopment of the site. The feedback from the PME will be used to shape the procurement strategy for this project.

title: ED0373-25 Sidmouth & East Beach Coastal Defence Scheme, Engineering Construction Works.
description: EDDC is currently preparing to initiate an open tender procurement exercise using the New Engineering Contract NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) Option C, combined with Option X22 Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) to establish contract with suitable suppliers for seeking professional services to act as the lead Designer and Delivery Supplier for Sidmouth and East Beach Coastal Defence Scheme. This is specialist work in a complex marine environment so the prospective contractors will be required to have extensive experience and expertise working in the marine environment and of heritage structures. The supplier will be required to build upon the already appraised and approved outline option, known as option 6 by; - Undertaking the technical numerical modelling, - Developing the detailed designs, - Liaising with statutory consultees, - Managing the planning and construction of coastal defence structures, including offshore rock marine structures, sea walls, coastal groynes, and other necessary infrastructure as detailed within the outline option, - Providing additional professional services to support the delivery of the scheme. The work in scope for this tender is summarised as follows: Option 6 – Indicative Scope of Works Building upon the outline design, will incorporate a combination of the following interventions. The final configuration will be subject to detailed design, environmental considerations, stakeholder engagement, and regulatory approvals: Beach Renourishment Tasks: provisions for beach renourishment techniques to support coastal defence objectives and maintain beach levels as detailed within the outline design. Rock Structures: The proposed works may include the installation of a terminal rock groyne or at one or more offshore rock breakwaters or alternative submerged features designed to dissipate wave energy and enhance overall beach stability at the eastern extent of the frontage to manage littoral drift and mitigate ongoing erosion at East Beach. Shoreline Defence Enhancements: works may include raising, replacing, or future-proofing the existing splash wall; upgrading flood gates; improving access infrastructure; and modifying the existing river training wall elements. River Sid Interface Improvements: localised enhancements to the River Sid flood wall and associated structures to ensure continuity with the coastal defence scheme and improve flood resilience.

title: Income Tax Self-Assessment Ecosystem Data and Integration - Innovation-Led Proof of Concept
description:
HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) intends to commence a competitive procurement for the delivery of an innovation-led Proof of Concept (PoC) exploring how emerging technologies, richer transaction data and integrations across banking, payment, fintech and software ecosystems could support increased simplification and accuracy within Income Tax Self Assessment (ITSA).
The PoC will build, test and evaluate a working technical demonstrator. Its purpose is to generate evidence and learning, rather than develop a live service or commit HMRC to a specific future solution.
This work supports HMRC's Transformation Roadmap and aligns with HMRC's Strategic Approach to Third Party Software. It explores how banking, payments, fintech and software ecosystems can help customers manage their tax affairs through the products and services they already use, reducing administrative effort, improving visibility of tax obligations and helping customers get their tax right first time, while building on a thriving and innovative market.
Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax provides the digital foundations for ITSA and continues to roll out. Innovation across banking, payments, fintech and software markets presents opportunities to develop, test and better understand ecosystem approaches to support more efficient and effective tax administration that makes it simpler for customers to meet their tax responsibilities.
For many ITSA customers, software and fintech products already provide valuable automation and support, helping many customers to manage their tax affairs more efficiently. However, richer data, improved standards and greater interoperability may create opportunities to further enhance transaction categorisation and apportionment, reducing customer effort, supporting customer experience and ensuring more accurate tax outcomes.
HMRC wants to test and learn with the market how banks, payment providers, fintechs and software platforms can build on existing capabilities to deliver more integrated, accurate and customer-centred tax experiences, while supporting a thriving and innovative software ecosystem.
The central question for the PoC is: to what extent can future enhanced data, ecosystem integrations, and interventions reduce customer effort, improve customer experience and improve accuracy across more aspects of Income Tax Self Assessment?
HMRC welcomes ideas from suppliers which innovate further, building on today, and looking towards future capabilities. Suppliers are welcome to bid independently or in partnership to build, test and evaluate an end-to-end working technical demonstrator of enhanced future capabilities and integrations. Alongside SMEs, HMRC anticipates that this procurement will be suitable for participation by consortia involving banks, payment providers, fintechs and accounting software providers.

title: WECDIS & Combat System Interface Unit (WIU CSIU)
description:
The National Armaments Director Group, part of the Ministry of Defence, intends to award a contract for the design, manufacture, installation and assurance of a replacement Warship Electronic Chart Display and Information (WECDIS) Interface Unit (WIU) and Combat System Interface Unit (CSIU) (together the Interfaces) to OSI Maritime Ltd (OSI). The contract will be for a term of two years and have an estimated value of £15m (inc VAT).
It is considered that this contract can be awarded under Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 because the direct award justification specified in paragraph 6 of Schedule 5 (single supplier - technical reasons) applies.
This is because the WIU and CSIU are required to interface with an upgraded WECDIS being procured from OSI (and which was the subject of a separate transparency notice 2025/S 000-074667 published on 18 November 2025 and both Interfaces need to be integrated into the wider architecture of systems currently installed on Royal Navy platforms, all of which are supplied, supported and assured by OSI. These include the Electronic Chart Precise Integrated Navigation System (EPCIS) and Warship Automatic Identification System (WAIS). Only OSI has the necessary intellectual property rights, technical drawings and expertise to design, manufacture, install and assure replacement Interfaces which are compatible with existing Royal Navy architecture. There are no reasonable alternatives.
The current CSIU/WIU supplier has been approached to ensure continuity of supply, but the equipment support package which includes an update to the WIU/CSIU component, does not offer value for money and will therefore not be progressed.
The Authority considered alternative procurement approaches prior to selecting the proposed route to market. Following assessment of the available options, OSI Maritime Ltd was identified as the only viable supplier capable of delivering the requirement whilst maintaining compatibility with the existing ECPINS, WECDIS and WAIS architecture and meeting the Authority's technical, operational and safety requirements.

title: Food Waste (Anaerobic Digestion)
description:
Following the Simpler Recycling announcement in October 2023, the council is developing a new food waste service for implementation in line with statutory requirements from 31 March 2026.
The council anticipates that its weekly food waste collection service will service all 114,000 properties via a mix of kerbside collections requiring both an internal food waste caddy, and a communal type collection service where internal caddies will be required for all properties, along with a communal type of external container.
The City of Wolverhampton Council anticipate the requirement to dispose of between 5000 and 10000 tonnes of food waste (residents who recycle their food waste are unlikely to be able to capture it all). Further compositional analysis work will be undertaken by the council in the coming months to confirm this.
No food waste delivered and received by the Provider shall be directly for disposal other than by anaerobic digestion.
Once collected or delivered, the contracts will ensure that the waste is disposed of, or recycled, in a manner that is compliant with current waste legislation and aims to increase the Council's recycling rate.

The Welsh Government Energy Service (WGES) supports public sector organisations and community energy enterprises across Wales to deliver decarbonisation, renewable energy, climate resilience, emissions reporting and wider climate action. The current framework comprises two Lots: Lot 1 Public Sector Decarbonisation Support and Lot 2 Public Sector Net Zero Reporting. 
The current framework expires on 31 March 2027. All new call-off contracts must be awarded before that date and in accordance with the framework terms. Call-off contracts awarded before the framework expiry date may continue beyond 31 March 2027 where permitted under their contractual terms and where any necessary approvals and funding arrangements are in place. This will support continuity of service while successor arrangements are developed and implemented. 
Framework users are therefore encouraged to review their anticipated requirements at an early stage and, where there is a requirement, allow sufficient time to complete any final call-off awards before 31 March 2027. Users remain responsible for ensuring that each call-off complies with the framework terms and their own governance requirements. 
Following Ministerial approval, Welsh Government has commenced preparatory work to develop an interim successor Welsh Government Energy Service Framework. The purpose of the interim framework is to provide continuity of support for public sector climate and community energy activity while wider policy developments continue to progress, including the establishment of the Welsh Public Energy Company (WPEC) and implementation of the Climate and Nature Action Plan. 
Welsh Government’s current intention is to establish an interim framework which builds on the strengths of the current WGES model whilst providing flexibility to respond to future policy developments and Ministerial priorities. Although the scope, structure, value, duration and procurement approach remain under development , as an interim arrangement the framework is likely to have a shorter initial term of 2 years with extension options, compared to the current framework’s 4-year term. Further details will be confirmed in the subsequent procurement notices. 
To help inform development Welsh Government also plan to undertake preliminary market engagement activity with stakeholders. Details of engagement opportunities will be published through the next Preliminary Market Engagement Notice. Subject to further development and market engagement, we anticipate the tender for the interim framework will be published in the next financial year 2027/2028, with the new service commencing in early 2028. 
This updated pipeline notice is published for market transparency and advance planning purposes. It does not constitute a commitment by Welsh Government to commence a procurement, award a framework or contract, or incur expenditure. The proposed procurement remains subject to governance and Ministerial approvals, finalisation of the requirement, funding availability, budget decisions and applicable procurement requirements. 
Please register your continued interest through this Pipeline Notice.

The Authorised Professional Practice (APP) is the official source of professional practice for policing and identifies that PPST Level 2 is for individuals in roles who carry/do not PPE who come into contact Public and Personal Safety Training (PPST) is required and is accredited and is not suitable for virtual training.
This learning was approved by the Commercial Board in August 2025 and is now part of BAU training events for the appropriate ESOC staff.
ESOC operational staff are responsible for tackling serious and organised crime. This includes undertaking operational visits with partners (Police, OGDs) to residential and commercial addresses to execute warrants, arrest suspect, search premises, seize evidence, transport evidence and conduct interviews under caution in Custody. Although our staff work under the direction of the Police, there are some occasions where our staff may find that the Police are not always in the immediate vicinity during an operational visit or during an interview under caution
Public and Personal Safety Training (PPST) Level 2 training is undertaken by other similar organisations including the Home Office and provides physical training to staff conducting a public facing role, to be able to de-escalate and defend themselves and withdraw from a conflict situation. 
The Authorised Professional Practice (APP) is the official source of professional practice for policing and identifies that PPST Level 2 is for individuals in roles who carry/do not PPE who come into contact with members of the public regardless of rank or role, including those who attend premises for arrests and searches and who interview suspects.
The training consists of:
Understanding of the National Decision Model (NDM).
Use of Force Legislation. 
Edge Weapon Skills.
Communications Skills and Personal Management Skills. 
Unarmed Skills - Introduction to Personal Protection.
First Aid.

title: Board Effectiveness Review
description:
BACKGROUND
The Financial Reporting Council (FRC) regulates auditors, accountants and actuaries and sets the UK's Corporate Governance and Stewardship Codes. As the Competent Authority for audit in the UK, we set auditing and ethical standards and monitor and enforce audit quality. 
The purpose of the FRC is to serve the public interest and support UK economic growth by upholding high standards of corporate governance, corporate reporting, audit and actuarial work. 
The FRC's core objectives are to promote high-quality corporate governance and reporting, support effective audit and actuarial work, hold relevant parties to account through proportionate supervision and enforcement, and contribute to well-functioning UK capital markets in the public interest.
PROJECT REQUIREMENTS
The Board of the Financial Reporting Council (FRC) is made up of non-executive and executive directors and is collectively responsible for the long-term success of the FRC. All Board Members, including the CEO and Chair, are appointed by the Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.
The Board's role is to provide strategic leadership of the FRC within a framework of prudent and effective controls which enables risk to be assessed and managed. The Board sets the FRC's strategic aims, ensures that the necessary financial and human resources are in place for the FRC to meet its objectives and reviews management performance.
The Board also sets the FRC's values and culture and ensures that its obligations to its stakeholders and others are understood and met. All directors must act in what they consider to be the best interests of the FRC, consistent with their statutory duties. For further information see FRC Board
The UK Corporate Governance Code requires that companies which follow the Code should consider undertaking an externally facilitated Board effectiveness review every three years.
THIS TENDER
The FRC is seeking an experienced, independent external reviewer to undertake a Board Effectiveness Review covering the Board, its Committees and wider governance arrangements.
PLEASE REFER TO THE INVITATION TO TENDER (ITT) FOR FULL DETAILS INCLUDING HOW TO SUBMIT YOUR TENDER
IMPORTANT:
• Please register your interest (and raise any tender queries) by emailing the FRC's procurement team - procurement@frc.org.uk
• The FRC will share all tender queries and answers with those that have registered.
• Your tender submission must be submitted within the deadline by email to procurement@frc.org.uk

description:

This Officer Decision Report is concerned with Phase 3.1 of the plan relating to the award of 1 interim contract to the incumbent provider of housing related support services funded by the Housing Support Grant until the completion of the Phase 3 commissioning process is completed.
Both the Huggard Centre and Ty Tresillian are Emergency Bed Units which are Direct Access Hostels providing accommodation and support to people who arehomeless or potentially homeless and in need of support. The project aims to “provide accommodation to people every night of the year, giving individuals, whohave come from the streets, a sense of self-respect and a concept of future opportunity that can be nurtured through having their own room and structured support planned to meet their individual needs”.
Service users will usually present with multiple secondary needs such as people suffering from drug dependency, people suffering from alcohol dependency, people with mental health problems, women fleeing domestic violence, ex-offenders and people with chronic illness.
Huggard Intervention Centre provides a ‘low threshold’ unique and highly accessible service 365 days a year for homeless people. It offers laundry and washing /bathing facilities, a free clothing store, a free meal every day and the opportunity to buy additional cost-price food. Service users can access health services and other specialist services via the Intervention centre, as well as advice and advocacy.
In addition, the Night Centre provides emergency shelter for up to 20 people per night through the provision of 17 dedicated private pod/rooms (small rooms with bed) and up to 3 additional bed spaces. All spaces have access to a safe locker to store personal valuable items

The school was rated as Ofsted Good and was rebuilt on the same site, following a fire in September 2007. It  formed part of the city’s Swanswell Regeneration Initiative in Hillfields. After 3 years of opening the Academy, Ofsted visited and the Academy achieved an Outstanding judgement. Following this in January 2014 the Sidney Stringer Multi Academy Trust was formed. 
The Trust now provides an education for over 3500 children in five schools, soon to be six, through all stages, ages, and settings: there are currently two secondary schools, two primary schools (one a Free School), a Broad Spectrum Special school and, soon to join, a Social Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) special school:
1.Sidney Stringer Academy (SSA)
2.Sidney Stringer Primary (SSP) 
3.Radford Primary (RAD)
4.Riverbank School (RIV)
5.Ernesford Grange Community Academy (EGA)
6.Woodfield (may potentially join at a later stage)
Further information regarding the Trust can be obtained here: https://sidneystringertrust.org.uk/
Tender information:
The successful tenderer will be required to provide school uniforms to include a full ordering system at Sidney Stringer Multi Academy Trust.
The contract term being tendered for 3 years, from 16/05/2027 – 15/05/2030. There is an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 15/05/2032. These dates are applicable to SSA, RAD, EGA and RIV. Sidney Stringer Primary’s contract will start a little earlier on 26/04/2027 where the initial 3 year contract period will conclude 15/05/2030 with an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 15/05/2032.
This tender project is seeking to appoint an experienced supplier to provide high quality value for money uniforms for the Schools’ pupils coupled with delivering excellent customer service to parents and the Schools. We understand the concerns regarding costs for parents and carers and our absolute commitment is to provide uniforms that excel in both quality and affordability. The Schools welcomes providers that are able to deliver cost effective solutions. 
Uniforms are currently supplied by a combination of Clive Marks Schoolwear and Brigade Clothing Ltd. The current model is a combination of purchasing via a physical shop, online and direct from the school (in limited circumstances).
Within this tender and for the model for the new contract, the Trust is open to hear from companies that can offer online only models (on the basis that a pop-up shop is developed within each school), or a hybrid mix of online and local shops providing customer service and item availability is not compromised.
The Trust is not obliged to accept the lowest price submitted for this tender, rather it is keen to secure best value from this contract and to deliver best value to its students. The Trust seeks a contractor that is keen to work in partnership and who will deliver to its highest abilities, at all times. 
Competitive Flexible Procedure 
This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here a minimum of 5 candidates (or less, in the event less than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates, will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. 
Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 40% price and 60% quality.
Value of contract:
The annual value of the current contract is £97,412 
Therefore the value of this contract is £487,060 
The contract shall be a fixed price.
Additional requirements and information:
•The Trust has a minimum requirement for a contractor’s liability insurances of:
•Employer’s (Compulsory) Liability Insurance = £5 million
•Public Liability Insurance =  £10 million
•Product Liability Insurance = £5 million
•The minimum annual turnover that your company must have achieved to be considered for this opportunity is £400,000
•Please note this is a growing Trust and any other schools that may join the Trust during the tenure of this new contract may, at the Trust’s discretion, be added to this contract.
•The client reserves the right not to appoint in conclusion of this project.

title: Three Tower Hamlets Schools Cleaning Tender
description:
Morpeth School, together with Old Palace Primary School and Cubitt Town Primary School, all within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, is undertaking a joint procurement exercise for the provision of cleaning services across all three sites. This collaborative approach has been adopted to achieve consistency of service, economies of scale and operational efficiencies, while recognising the individual needs and identities of each school. 
Morpeth School is a large, mixed secondary school and sixth form serving a diverse pupil population aged 11-18. Old Palace Primary School, a two-form entry primary school, and Cubitt Town Primary School both provide inclusive, nurturing environments for pupils age 4-11, with a strong focus on wellbeing, achievement and high standards of education. 
The contract will be tendered as a single procurement exercise, however the Schools expressly reserve the right to award the contract either as a single combined contract across all sites, or as separate individual contracts for each school, based on what is deemed to provide the most advantageous outcome for each school. Bidders are therefore required to submit proposals that clearly demonstrate their ability to delivery both a combined and where requested an individual model. 
The contract is scheduled to commence on 1st August 2026, initially spanning three years with an option for both parties to extend the contract for a further two years, (3+1+1) beyond this date by mutual agreement. Any contract extension will be subject to the Schools’ satisfaction and agreement on budgets and service levels. Some of the cleaning staff have LGPS pension schemes and either having ABS in a London Borough, or the ability to achieve ABS status, will be essential for bidders. 
The estimated combined turnover for the three-year duration is approximately £1.7 million.
The contract is focused on consistently high levels of cleaning service and pro-active management. Regular termly and annual reviews throughout the contract duration are mandatory, and a break clause should be included to support both parties in case the relationship does not thrive. The School expects high standards of support and a strong working relationship with the selected bidder. 
The procurement process follows a two stage ‘Competitive Flexible’ approach, beginning with a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) stage followed by an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage after shortlisting. 
The Schools reserve the right not to award the contract, including the option to pursue alternative delivery models, or to award on a site-by-site basis, should submissions fail to meet the required standard.

title: Responsive Repairs and Empty Homes Maintenance Services - West Rural Region
description:

It was therefore agreed that the tender would be closed with this revised tender exercise taking its place. The tender was completed as a single stage, open procedure, in line with the requirements of the Act.
Stonewater, therefore, required third-party contractor support to deliver its annual pipeline of responsive repairs and an empty homes maintenance service, against a defined specification, within its whole West-Rural geographical locality. description:
***THIS IS AN AWARD NOTICE, NOT A CALL FOR COMPETITION***
Bath & North East Somerset Council is awarding a contract for the operation and management of Royal Victoria Park Golf and Footgolf Site under a concession contract. The successful operator will be responsible for delivering a high-quality, inclusive, financially sustainable service aligned to Council priorities for parks, heritage, and wellbeing.
The facilities include a payment kiosk (small shop) and toilets, and it is located centrally with high public footfall, but with only one car parking space on site.
The site is well located to benefit from visitors attending the nearby Royal Victoria Park. The public footpaths (Cotswold Way) and mature trees impact the ability to develop the site further.

description:
Located on the Harwell Science & Innovation Campus in Oxfordshire, Diamond Light Source (DLS) is a leading-edge facility for science, engineering and innovation. DLS allows researchers from academia and industry to investigate the structure and behaviour of the world around us at the atomic and molecular level. To continue delivering the world-changing science that Diamond enables, the facility is being upgraded to Diamond-II, a co-ordinated programme of development that combines a major machine upgrade with new instruments and complementary improvements to optics, detectors, sample environment and delivery capabilities, and computing, as well as integrated and correlative methods. This will be transformative in speed and spatial resolution and will offer users streamlined access to enhanced instruments for life and physical sciences.
The scope of this contract is to carry out the detailed design, manufacture, quality control, testing and delivery of two out-of-vacuum main DC/PM septum magnets, with integrated vacuum vessels, on support stands, as well as some spares.
The two septum magnets are physically identical but will be installed with input and output ends inverted for booster extraction bend to the left, and storage ring injection bend to the right. This means that the magnet fields are also inverted, and also that the support frame should be rotationally symmetric so that the services connections are on the outside (bending channel side of the support frame) in each case.
See specification for further details.

title: Insolvency Practitioner Services
description:
Stoke-on-Trent City Council requires the provision of specialist Insolvency Practitioner services to support the recovery of outstanding debts owed to the Council where all standard and conventional debt recovery methods have been exhausted. The appointed provider will act on behalf of the Council to manage and progress complex insolvency cases involving both individuals and corporate entities, with the aim of maximising debt recovery while ensuring full compliance with relevant legislation and professional standards.
The service will support the Council's statutory responsibility to collect public funds, including unpaid Council Tax, National Non-Domestic Rates (Business Rates), and Sundry Debts. The successful provider will be expected to deliver a comprehensive end-to-end insolvency service, offering expert advice, case assessment, legal support, administration, and recovery actions throughout the insolvency process.
The scope of services includes, but is not limited to, the following:
Personal Bankruptcy Proceedings
The provider shall assess individual debtor cases and, where appropriate, initiate and manage bankruptcy proceedings. This includes conducting financial investigations, preparing and submitting statutory documentation, liaising with legal representatives and the Insolvency Service, attending hearings where required, and providing recommendations to the Council regarding the viability and anticipated outcomes of bankruptcy action.
Corporate Winding-Up Petitions
The provider shall manage insolvency proceedings against limited companies and other corporate bodies with outstanding debts owed to the Council. Services will include reviewing case suitability, issuing statutory demands, preparing and presenting winding-up petitions, instructing legal representatives where necessary, attending court proceedings, and overseeing subsequent insolvency processes to maximise recovery opportunities.
Estate Insolvency Matters
The provider shall advise on and manage cases involving deceased debtors where insolvent estates are identified. This may include conducting asset investigations, engaging with executors, administrators, solicitors, and probate practitioners, assessing the Council's position as a creditor, and undertaking any recovery actions considered appropriate within the legal framework governing insolvent estates.
The provider shall offer specialist professional advice to the Council on the suitability of insolvency action in individual cases. This includes reviewing debtor circumstances, identifying potential risks and recovery prospects, advising on legal options, and recommending the most effective and proportionate course of action to achieve the best financial outcome for the Council.
The provider shall maintain effective case management arrangements throughout the duration of each matter. This will include maintaining accurate case records, managing all correspondence and documentation, monitoring progress against agreed milestones, and ensuring timely progression of cases through the relevant insolvency procedures.
The provider shall supply regular management information and performance reports to the Council. Reports should include details of cases received, actions undertaken, outcomes achieved, monies recovered, costs incurred, and case status updates. The provider will also be responsible for ensuring accurate financial reconciliation of all recovered funds, fees, distributions, and disbursements, supported by transparent audit trails.
All services must be delivered in accordance with applicable insolvency legislation, associated regulations, case law, professional standards, and best practice guidance. The provider must hold all necessary licences, authorisations, and professional accreditations required to undertake insolvency work in the United Kingdom. The provider shall also ensure compliance with the Council's policies, procedures, governance requirements, and information security standards.
The provider will be expected to work collaboratively with Council officers, legal services, external legal representatives, insolvency bodies, courts, and other stakeholders as required. Clear communication, responsiveness, and professional conduct will be essential throughout the contract period.
The primary objectives of the service are to:
Maximise recovery of outstanding debts owed to the Council.
Deliver cost-effective and proportionate insolvency solutions.
Provide expert professional advice in complex recovery cases.
Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements.
Maintain accurate, transparent, and auditable financial records.
Reduce financial losses arising from irrecoverable debts.
Support the Council in protecting public funds and maintaining effective debt recovery arrangements.
The Council is seeking a provider with demonstrable experience in delivering insolvency services for local authorities or other public sector organisations, with the capacity and expertise to manage a varied portfolio of personal, corporate, and estate insolvency cases efficiently and effectively.

The FoUI guideline shall strengthen research supported innovation in the region ́s businesses and the municipality ́s own activities. The effort shall strengthen capacity for innovation in business and shall also contribute to strengthening Oslo municipality ́s own capacity for research-supported innovation, in line with the approved strategy for knowledge based development, innovation and digital technology for Oslo municipality (KID). Business orientated efforts will be prioritised, among other things, in accordance with the regional plan for competitiveness and value creation in Oslo and Akershus, which is at a hearing in autumn 2026. Artificial intelligence and digitalisation are in the process of taking in all parts of business and society. Knowledge on digitalisation and artificial intelligence is therefore not limited to one priority area, and it will be advantageous to be able to use digitalisation and AI within the individual commitment areas. The R&D guides have the main assignment of mobilising businesses and Oslo ́s own entities for more research-supported R&D. The R&D guides discuss project ideas and possibilities with companies or the public sector and can connect R&D needs with relevant researchers. The FoUI guideline mobilises to regional, national and international schemes, as well as for preliminary projects and the subsidy scheme SmartOslo. New this time is that we want the FoUI guidelines to also be able to contribute to mobilising to EU support schemes for businesses, including EIC.

title: Greece – Software development services – FinStart: Χρηματοοικονομικές Δεξιότητες για τη Ζωή
description: Στο πλαίσιο της παρούσας θα χρηματοδοτηθεί η υλοποίηση Δράσης για την συστηματική ενίσχυση του χρηματοοικονομικού εγγραμματισμού των μαθητών της Πρωτοβάθμιας και της Δευτεροβάθμιας Εκπαίδευσης, καθώς και η ενεργός εμπλοκή των εκπαιδευτικών, των Συμβούλων Εκπαίδευσης και των γονέων στην ανάπτυξη υπεύθυνων χρηματοοικονοµικών γνώσεων, δεξιοτήτων και στάσεων. Ειδικότερα, το πρόγραμμα αποσκοπεί στο να καταστήσει τους μαθητές ικανούς να κατανοούν βασικές οικονομικές και χρηματοοικονομικές έννοιες, να διαχειρίζονται υπεύθυνα τους διαθέσιμους πόρους τους, να προγραμματίζουν ανάγκες και δαπάνες, να αξιολογούν εναλλακτικές επιλογές και να λαμβάνουν τεκμηριωμένες σχετικές αποφάσεις στην καθημερινή τους ζωή. Παράλληλα, επιδιώκει να ενισχύσει την ικανότητά τους να αναγνωρίζουν κινδύνους που σχετίζονται με τις ψηφιακές συναλλαγές, την παραπλανητική διαφήμιση, την υπερχρέωση, τις οικονομικές απάτες και άλλες επισφαλείς πρακτικές. Το πρόγραμμα επιδιώκει, επίσης, να ενδυναμώσει τους εκπαιδευτικούς με κατάλληλο εκπαιδευτικό υλικό, γνώσεις και μεθοδολογικά εργαλεία για την αποτελεσματική διδασκαλία του χρηματοοικονομικού εγγραμματισμού. Οι Σύμβουλοι Εκπαίδευσης θα υποστηρίξουν την επιμόρφωση/ ενημέρωση, την παιδαγωγική καθοδήγηση και τη διάχυση καλών πρακτικών, ενώ οι γονείς θα ενθαρρυνθούν να συμβάλουν στην καλλιέργεια υγιών οικονομικών συνηθειών στο οικογενειακό περιβάλλον. Μέσα από τη συνεργασία της σχολικής κοινότητας και της οικογένειας, το πρόγραμμα επιδιώκει τη διαμόρφωση υπεύθυνων, κριτικά σκεπτόμενων και χρηματοοικονομικά ενημερωμένων πολιτών, οι οποίοι θα είναι σε θέση να ανταποκρίνονται στις απαιτήσεις της καθημερινής ζωής και στις προκλήσεις ενός διαρκώς μεταβαλλόμενου οικονομικού και ψηφιακού περιβάλλοντος. Το πρόγραμμα αναπτύσσεται σε δύο αλληλένδετους άξονες: αφενός στην παραγωγή τεκμηριωμένης γνώσης μέσω στοχευμένης μελέτης και αφετέρου, με βάση τα αποτελέσματα της σχετικής μελέτης, στον σχεδιασμό και την υλοποίηση εκπαιδευτικών δράσεων για μαθητές, εκπαιδευτικούς, Συμβούλους Εκπαίδευσης και γονείς. Η εφαρμογή του προγράμματος θα έχει πιλοτικό και ανατροφοδοτικό χαρακτήρα. Τα εκπαιδευτικά εργαλεία και οι δράσεις θα αξιοποιούνται σε σχολικές μονάδες διαφορετικών βαθμίδων και τύπων, θα αξιολογούνται ως προς την αποτελεσματικότητα, τη χρηστικότητα και την παιδαγωγική καταλληλότητά τους και θα αναθεωρούνται με βάση τα δεδομένα που θα προκύπτουν. Με τον τρόπο αυτό, η μελέτη και οι εκπαιδευτικές παρεμβάσεις δεν θα λειτουργούν ως ανεξάρτητες δραστηριότητες, αλλά ως μέρη ενός ενιαίου κύκλου διερεύνησης, σχεδιασμού, εφαρμογής, αξιολόγησης και βελτίωσης. Στο πρόγραμμα συμπεριλαμβάνονται οριζόντιες δράσεις που αφορούν την ενημέρωση, τη διάχυση και τη δημοσιότητα του έργου. title: Germany – Design and execution of research and development – Entwicklung und Bau einer Industrieanlage zur Entsorgung von Munitionsaltlasten auf See
description: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland, vertreten durch das Bundesministerium für Umwelt, Klimaschutz, Naturschutz und nukleare Sicherheit (BMUKN), beabsichtigte, einen Auftrag über die Entwicklung und den Bau einer Industrieanlage zur Entsorgung von Munitionsaltlasten auf See innerhalb des Sofortprogramms „Munitionsaltlasten in Nord- und Ostsee“ zu vergeben. Zur Beräumung und Vernichtung von konventionellen Munitionsaltasten in Versenkungsgebieten ist ein Gesamtsystem (Industrieanlage) unter Einhaltung der allgemein anerkannten Regeln der Technik zu entwerfen, das aus unterschiedlichen Hauptsystemen mit ausgereifter Technik besteht und die Möglichkeit bietet, die Kapazitäten in Zukunft zu steigern. Mit dem Gesamtsystem wird somit die Erkundung, Bergung, Aufbereitung und Entsorgung der Kampfmittel unmittelbar auf See beabsichtigt. Die Ausschreibung wurde als Innovationspartnerschaft durchgeführt. Die Innovationspartnerschaft ist ein spezielles Vergabeverfahren zur Entwicklung innovativer, noch nicht auf dem Markt verfügbarer Liefer-, Bau- oder Dienstleistungen und zum anschließenden Erwerb der daraus hervorgehenden Leistungen. Gemäß § 19 Abs. 8 VgV wird die Innovationspartnerschaft entsprechend dem Forschungs- und Innovationsprozess in zwei aufeinanderfolgenden Phasen strukturiert: 1) Einer Forschungs- und Entwicklungsphase (Definitionsphase), in welcher der Liefer- und Leistungsgegenstand mit dem AN definiert und spezifiziert wird. Dadurch wird der Leistungsgegenstand klar und nachvollziehbar formuliert, und 2) einer Leistungsphase, in der die aus der Definitionsphase spezifizierte Leistung (Konstruktion und Bau) erbracht wird. Ziel ist es, zum Ende der Innovationspartnerschaft eine Industrieanlage fertiggestellt zu haben und den AG in die Lage zu versetzen, diese gemäß den Anforderungen selbst oder durch einen Dritten zu betreiben.

title: Norway – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Procurement of practical action research on facility models as new organisation models in nursing homes.
description: Oslo municipality c/o the Agency for Nursing Homes has carried out a comprehensive assignment sharing project in the period 2024-2025, testing several models for alternative organisation and assignment sharing in municipal long-term homes. Some of the models have been tested both in some departments, while some were tested in and out of all institutions. One of the models, the Tåsen model was introduced and commissioned from opening in November 2024. Experiences from the assignment sharing projects show that new assignment division is feasible and provides measurable gains, provided good manager anchoring, clear role and descriptions of responsibility, systematic training and local adaptation.    The Agency for Nursing Homes would like practical action research on facility models as a new organisation model with the aim of documenting effects, evaluating the different implementation processes against "Best practice" and interpreting the findings in conjunction with other registry data in nursing homes.  Three different facility models are today introduced at Tåsenhjemmet, Langerudhjemmet and Majorstuhjemmet. The facility on other long-term homes has not been decided. The research shall be carried out as an equal cooperation between the research environment, central administration and nursing homes, with an emphasis on knowledge based practice, learning and a high degree of applicability in the service.  The contract has a duration of two years and an estimated total value of NOK 4,000,000 excluding VAT.

title: Germany – Energy and related services – 10021886-Provision of standardised consultancy services for On- & Off-Grid Regulation and Market Development
description: GET.transform, is a technical assistance program supporting national and regional partners and institutions in advancing their energy transitions. GET.transform is a component of the GET.pro (Global Energy Transformation Programme), which is a global multi-donor platform and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The three instruments of GET.pro are: - GET.invest mobilises private investments in clean energy by building a pipeline of bankable investment projects. - GET.transform supports partner governments by developing bankable frameworks for clean energy investment. - The Secretariat for Africa-EU Energy Program promotes strategic political dialogue between Africa and Europe on energy. Thematic and geographic scope: The implementation structure of GET.transform is organised along the Thematic and Geographic Approach. GET.transform offers structured advisory services on four key transformational topics: 1) Long-Term Energy Planning 2) Renewable Energy Grid Integration 3) On-Grid Regulation and Market Development 4) Off-Grid Regulation and Market Development On-Grid Regulation and Market Development measures enable power sector market reform allowing for renewable energy participation, increased investment, and promotion of private markets. Power system transformation processes should be supported by a background of technically sound energy planning, a well-functioning governance structure, policy and regulatory framework. The goal is to ensure that electricity resources, including generation, transmission, and distribution systems, are allocated efficiently. In addition, market model mechanisms can be designed and implemented to facilitate a sustainable, secure, competitive and affordable electricity system. To meet the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 target of universal access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services by 2030, decentralised renewable energy solutions such as off-grid solutions have been proven to be efficient at providing energy access to rural communities. Off-grid solutions can power over 400 million people across Africa and LAC. Off- Grid Regulation and Market Development establishes a framework for public partners to strengthen institutional capacities to accomplish their rural development mandates, as well as market incentives that promote private sector participation and finance for scaling projects. ? In addition to its core activities, GET.transform has implemented TA services to other GIZ- programs in Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as Asia and Europe. GET.transform is therefore offering activities potentially in all countries where GIZ energy portfolio is active by efficiently offering standardised solutions and scaling activities and contributing towards the concept of Vision 100 of GIZ, which serves as a guiding principle for the realignment of the GIZ portfolio for the global energy transition.

title: CPT_25_02 Financial Audit and Assurance Services Contract
description:
The National Audit Office (NAO) is the UK's independent public spending watchdog. The NAO supports Parliament in holding government to account and helps improve public services through its high-quality audits.
The NAO reprocured the Financial Audit and Assurance Services to support the high-quality delivery our portfolio of financial audits within the public sector.
Financial Audit and Assurance Services Contract
NAO sought to continue working in partnership with supplier firms to deliver high quality audits, which support effective accountability and lead to better financial reporting and financial management by public bodies.
NAO plan to contract out a series of audit engagements through a lot based structure. The Financial Audit and Assurance Services Contract will also include provision for the opportunity to procure additional financial audit related services throughout the lifetime of the contract.
For audit engagements under the contract, the Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG) will retain overall responsibility for signing the audit opinion and the NAO will work with supplier firms to ensure audit and assurance services are carried out in line with the relevant standards and quality expectations.
Audits will need to be carried out to internationally recognised auditing standards but also adapted to the public sector reporting framework, which includes the Government Financial Reporting Manual, and checking that transactions have been applied to the purposes intended by Parliament and conform to the authorities which govern them ('regularity').
The National Audit Office (NAO) will be awarding Financial Audit and Assurance Services contracts across a number of lots. Under the Financial Audit and Assurance Services contract Partner Firms will deliver audit services for a defined portfolio of audited entities. The contracts will be awarded to experienced Partner Firms who have a proven record of delivering ISA (International Standards on Auditing) compliant audits.
The new Financial Audit and Assurance Services contract will cover the provision of audit services from the 2026-27 audit cycle (year ended 31 March 2027 (unless specified otherwise)). The Financial Audit and Assurance Services Contract will initially cover 3 audit cycles from 2026-27 to 2028-29 with the option to extend for a further 2 audit cycles up to 2030-31. All audits within the lots have a 31 March year end, unless specified otherwise.
NAO sought Partner Firms to provide audit services under the following 14 lots:
• Lot 1 Crown Estate
• Lot 2 Northern Ireland
• Lot 3 Complex Provisions
• Lot 4 National Savings & Investments
• Lot 5 Defra (Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs) Entities
• Lot 6 Health
• Lot 7 Pensions
• Lot 8 Charities 1
• Lot 9 Charities 2
• Lot 10 Charities 3
• Lot 11 Infrastructure
• Lot 12 Debt Management
• Lot 13 Ministry of Justice (MOJ) Entities
• Lot 14 United Kingdom Export Finance (UKEF)
Interested suppliers were able to submit a bid for the lots of their choice (maximum of 8 lots). This means if a single supplier bids for the maximum 8 lots and is the preferred supplier based on the award and price evaluation on all 8 lots; they would be awarded all 8 lots that they have bid for. However suppliers were not be permitted to submit bids for more than 8 lots.
The new contract will run for an initial period of 3 years from Tuesday 1st September 2026 until Friday 31st August 2029 with the option to further extend for a period of up to 2 years (by 2 periods of 12 months) until Sunday 31st August 2031 with the estimated overall value of the contract being up to £68.293m inclusive of VAT (£13.659m per annum). 
No guarantee is given as to the actual value of the contract.
This figure includes an element of contingency and assumptions over additional services that may be procured in addition to contracted-out audit engagements as set out in Appendix A - Statement of Requirement.

title: PQNV 025 - Digital Mental Health Prevention and Emotional Wellbeing Support Offer in Shropshire
description:
THIS IS NOT A CALL FOR COMPETITION. THIS IS A MARKET ENGAGEMENT. 
Shropshire Council is currently reviewing its future approach to universal mental health prevention and early-help support. As one part of this review, the Council wishes to understand the range of digital mental health prevention and emotional wellbeing models currently available, their evidence base, accessibility, affordability and potential applicability to Shropshire. 
This engagement does not indicate that the Council has decided to recommission a digital service. Findings will inform a wider options appraisal alongside local needs evidence, review of current provision, stakeholder engagement and consideration of alternative approaches. 
The overarching aim is to ensure that residents with low-level mental health or emerging wellbeing needs can access timely, appropriate support that helps prevent escalation into more complex need and reduces avoidable demand on statutory services. Digital support is being considered as part of a wider suite of accessible offers that may include social prescribing, Voluntary, Community and Social Enterprise (VCSE) provision and community-based support. Any future model will need to take account of Shropshire’s rurality and the diverse needs, preferences and circumstances of local residents, alongside local system priorities, strategies and policies. 
Strategic context 
Mental health and wellbeing are central to quality of life, resilience and the ability to participate in education, work, family life and communities. Good mental wellbeing is also protective against physical illness, social inequalities and unhealthy lifestyles. 
Demand for mental health support has increased significantly, particularly among children and young people, many of whom experience long waits for care. Nationally, around one in five people are affected by a common mental health condition, and a substantial proportion of mental health problems are established by early adulthood (age 24). 
This reinforces the importance of prevention and early intervention. Providing timely support for people with low-level mental health needs can help people manage distress earlier, maintain independence and stay connected to education, work, family life and their communities. 
The emerging national direction for mental health in England also places greater emphasis on shifting from crisis-led care towards prevention, delivering support at place and within communities, and embracing the opportunities offered by digital innovation. The future offer in Shropshire should therefore support earlier, proportionate and accessible help, while complementing wider local mental health, wellbeing and community support pathways. 
Current service context 
Shropshire Council currently commissions a digital mental health and emotional wellbeing offer for residents aged 16+, providing anonymous online access to moderated peer support, self-management resources and learning tools.  The current arrangement provides a limited number of licenses annually. 
The Council is not necessarily seeking a like-for-like replacement through this engagement and is interested in understanding alternative digital models, approaches and innovations that could achieve preventative and early-help outcomes. 
The Council is interested in understanding features that; 
Are accessible without diagnosis or clinical referral 
Supports people experiencing emerging mental ill health or reduced emotional wellbeing 
Encourages self-management and early-help 
Provides safe onward escalation where necessary 
Is accessible across a large rural geography 
Can reach groups that may not engage with traditional services 
Is capable of generating meaningful information about reach, utilisation and outcomes to support review of impact and best value discussions

description: Bradford Children and Families Trust (BCFT) is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced provider to deliver an Independent Visitor Service in accordance with Regulation 44 of the Children’s Homes (England) Regulations 2015. The provider will also be expected to work collaboratively with BCFT to support continuous improvement, effective escalation, contract monitoring and quality assurance across the Trust’s residential provision.
