title: Basildon Station Platform Replacements (1&2) GRIP 5-8 2026
description:
Contract for the multi-disciplinary detailed design for renewal of the two platforms and associated infrastructure and both passenger lifts at Basildon station, in south Essex.
Basildon station is located at 24miles 26chains on the FSS2 Fenchurch Street to Shoeburyness line. Basildon Station was constructed in the 1970s comprising 2No. platforms which were partially founded on an embankment constructed in the 1930s. The main station buildings are at street level, with each platform accessed via a lift or staircase. The platforms have short canopies, where the platform construction is built off a bridge deck, that spans over Station Way public highway and the booking hall, at street level. The remainder of the platforms are exposed and of suspended concrete construction.
The platforms were found to be subject to serious defects and movement during routine inspection work carried out during summer 2021, whereafter it was concluded that the platforms were beyond economic repair. This resulted in the platforms being subject to temporary propping, monitoring and regular inspection, all pending demolition and renewal of the platforms.
C2c are now looking to run a procurement process to enter into a JCT Design & Build contract for renewal of the 1974 sections of both platforms 1 and 2 at Basildon, along with renewal of the station lifts serving the platforms, and associated station systems.

title: 5085.SH.JN - Advanced Nano-Mechanical Characterisation System with Integrated Fluorescence
description:
The University of Sheffield, supported by the Wolfson Light Microscopy Facility (LMF), is seeking the supply, installation and commissioning of a high-throughput nanoindentation platform for the quantitative mechanical characterisation of biological samples and biomaterials.
The instrument will provide a centrally managed research resource supporting investigators from across the Faculties of Health, Science and Engineering, together with external academic and industrial collaborators. The system will enable the measurement of mechanical properties across a broad range of biological specimens including single cells, organoids, tissue sections, extracellular matrices, biomaterials and engineered tissues.
The University requires an integrated platform capable of combining high-resolution nanoindentation with optical microscopy and environmental control to permit long-term measurements of live biological samples under physiologically relevant conditions. The instrument must also support high-throughput experimentation using standard multi-well plate formats to facilitate large-scale mechanobiology studies and drug screening.
The system shall be supplied as a complete turnkey solution including the nanoindentation platform, integrated optical imaging system, environmental control module, acquisition and analysis software, computer workstation, installation, commissioning and user training. Particular emphasis will be placed on systems that provide high measurement sensitivity, broad mechanical measurement capability, compatibility with live-cell imaging workflows and the flexibility to support future research developments.

title: prj_1235 - Health Access Worker service
description:
PQQ in this case is where the City, at an early stage in the development of its proposals but prior to formulating any formal procurement opportunity, seeks input from the market.   
Participants must also note that a response to this notice does not guarantee an invitation to participate in this or any future procurement that the City may conduct, nor that the City will procure any such supply and services or accept any proposals offered. Any Procurement of the supply and services by the City will be carried out strictly in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.  
Description of Service  
The Health Access Worker service will improve access to healthcare for people sleeping rough by providing wraparound connections for rough sleeping clients into the health system. The service will provide lived experience as a core component of provision.   
The Health Access Worker will:  
Improve access to healthcare for people sleeping rough by providing wraparound connections for rough sleeping clients into the health system.  
Be headquartered at the Outreach provider’s office, but with the understanding that it is peripatetic/out in the field for a primary portion of the workday.   
Provide lived experience as core component of service provision.  
Be expected to work 3 days per week and to meet with clients outside business hours as needed.   
Improve access to healthcare for people sleeping rough.  
Increase the number of GP registrations.  
Increase attendance at health appointments.  
Reduce missed GP and secondary healthcare appointments.  
Prevent deterioration of health to reduce escalation to crisis point and minimise risk of long-term impact of rough sleeping on physical health.  
Be part of a whole-system approach that recognises the interdependence of health, housing and social inclusion.  
Improve uptake of outreach primary care offer.  
Increase individuals’ confidence, knowledge and ability to take an active role in managing their own health and wellbeing, empowering them to engage effectively with treatment, appointments and longer-term health support.  
Maximise use of Health Emergency Bedspaces when available.  
Support the implementation and evaluation of a City of London-led NHS information-sharing pilot.  
Improve early identification of long-term conditions that qualify people for support through health funded palliative care.  
Support embedding inclusion health principles within outreach services, ensuring that health is a core component of their support.  
Amplify the voice of lived experience in homelessness work.  
Play a key role in both housing stability and health outcomes for individuals identified as long-term rough sleepers, ensuring access to accommodation and services that meet their individual health and care needs.  
Work collaboratively with partner agencies and stakeholders to deliver the objectives set out in the MHCLG strategy and CoL’s Long Term Rough Sleeper partnership plan.   
Management (including direct line management) of HAW workers will be the responsibility of the provider.  
The contract will run for an initial period of one year with the option to extend by one year.  
The maximum value of the contract will be £40,000 per annum.

title: Business Support North East Framework
description:
Business North East is a new region-wide approach to business support developed by the North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) in partnership with the seven constituent local authorities. It will provide a simplified, coordinated and accessible business support system for entrepreneurs and businesses across the North East, supporting business
The model will include a regional hub, use local authority network to maintaining strong relationships with businesses.
The wider Business North East programme is expected to operate through five integrated areas of activity across the business lifecycle:
Inspire - increase entrepreneurial awareness and aspiration, particularly amongst younger people and underrepresented groups.
Explore - improve enterprise readiness and strengthen the quality of business propositions entering the support system.
Start - increase business creation and improve business survival prospects through tailored support and business development assistance.
Succeed - improve productivity, innovation, technology adoption and business resilience amongst established businesses.
Grow - support ambitious businesses to scale, create jobs, access finance and enter new markets.
The North East MSA intends to establish a framework to provide a flexible route through which a range of specialist business support, enterprise and related services may be commissioned in support of Business North East and wider regional economic priorities.
It is anticipated that the framework will encompass a broad range of services, across five separate Lots:
1. Enterprise, Entrepreneurship and Business Start-up
2. Business Growth, Productivity and Specialist Support
3. High Growth, Scale-up and Investment
4. Sector, Cluster and Supply Chain Development
5. Business Engagement, Training and Programme Support
These areas reflect the anticipated breadth of Business North East, which is intended to respond to business needs including access to finance, productivity, workforce development, innovation, digital adoption, mentoring and growth support.
The Framework is intended to enable the North East MSA and constituent local authorities to identify suitably qualified suppliers with the capability and experience to deliver services within one or more of these areas.
The approach is intended to accommodate a diverse supplier market, including organisations capable of delivering broad business support programmes alongside specialist providers with expertise in particular sectors, business needs or forms of intervention. It will also support the development of new and emerging provision as business needs, economic conditions and regional priorities evolve.

title: External Board Effectiveness Review
description:
The Legal Services Board (LSB) is looking to appoint a suitably qualified third party to undertake an external evaluation of the LSB Board. The last external evaluation was undertaken in 2022. In the intervening years internal evaluations have been undertaken.
The Legal Services Board is the independent oversight regulator for legal services in England and Wales, established under the Legal Services Act 2007. Our role is to oversee the organisations that regulate lawyers and hold them to account for ensuring regulation works in the public interest and protects consumers. We also regulate the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal and have oversight of the Office for Legal Complaints, which is responsible for administering the Legal Ombudsman scheme.
The LSB is an Executive Non-Department Public Body sponsored by the Ministry of Justice (MoJ). The Legal Services Board is accountable to Parliament through the Lord Chancellor and is sponsored by the MoJ. 
The prospective professional services provider will be expected to deliver the following outputs as part of the Board Effectiveness Review:
a.	Project Plan which outlines key milestones, methods and timelines. 
b.	Survey and Analysis: It is expected that, as a minimum, this will include a desk-based review of evidence (board papers, governance policies, minutes etc), a review of external best practice with specific reference to other regulators and ALBs, and interviews (can be undertaken virtually) of all Board Members, members of the executive, key internal and external stakeholders.
c.	Board Observation: The provider will observe at least one Board meeting and the Audit, Risk and Assurance Committee in November to assess boardroom behaviours, interactions and decision-making in practice. Observation is likely to take place at LSB's autumn Board meeting 24 November (in person). 
d.	Interim Findings: A draft report in January 2027 summarising initial observations, emerging themes and a presentation to the LSB Board should be scheduled to allow sufficient time for feedback prior to finalisation.
e.	Final Board Effectiveness Report and Presentation in February 2027 setting out findings, analysis and evidence-based recommendations aligned to the review objectives should be presented to the Board.
f.	A facilitated session in the form of a Board workshop to reflect on findings and support collective ownership and understanding of the recommendations. 
g.	A summary of the outcomes of the review is expected to be reported in the LSB's Annual Report and Accounts, and the Review will be made available to the sponsor department. 
A tender is required which should include method statements, but not be limited to:
• A description of how you would work with us, the key people that will work the LSB and their background, experiences and skills.
• A description of how you will meet the service specification requirements listed in paragraph 18 onwards above, with demonstrable experience of conducting Board Effectiveness Reviews with regulators.
• A fully costed proposal with fixed and variable costs.
• A completed supplier questionnaire form (annex A).
• A completed EDI form (annex B).
Bids are expected to be between £30,000 - £35,000 with a budget ceiling for this work of £35,000 excluding VAT. Bids above this may be disregarded with no further evaluation. Bids should clearly indicate if they include VAT or not. 
A breakdown of costs should be provided including where appropriate the different costs of different staff members. 
Failure to provide any of the above details may lead to bids being disregarded with no further evaluation. Electronic completion and signing of the forms is acceptable.
Full details of the background, scope, scoring criteria and how to apply may be found in the invitation to tender attached to this notice.
All tender submissions should be submitted by 13:00 on 16 October 2026 to tenders@legalservicesboard.org.uk . Submissions submitted to other addresses or beyond this time will not be accepted.
Please contact Heather McLoughlin, Head, Corporate Governance, tenders@legalservicesboard.org.uk, if you have any questions or require any clarification. Enquiries received after the deadline of 9 October 2026 for questions may not be answered.
A summary of the questions received and LSB's response will be published on Contracts Finder.

title: MID/26/26 - Auchendinny, Penicuik , Affordable Housing
description:
In terms of Midlothian Council’s affordable housing policy, it is noted that the Penicuik area is one of the Council’s locations with high demand. As a result the Council requires to secure land within the Penicuik area to assist with meeting that demand and policy ambition and to deliver its Affordable Housing Supply Programme. The area of land at Auchendinny Penicuik owned by BELLWAY HOMES LIMITED incorporated under the Companies Acts, (Registered Number 00670176), having its Registered Office at Woolsington House, Woolsington, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE13 8BF (“the Sellers) fits with that policy ambition. The contract for the purchase of land is an excluded contract under Regulation 11(1) of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015 (2015 Regulations).
The Sellers have included as a condition of the sale of its land that the Council is required to enter into a construction contract with the Sellers for the construction of 75 social rented units on the land being acquired. Without acquiring the land, the Council could not meet its policy in respect of affordable housing in the Penicuik area and the scheme would not be capable of progressing.
As a result the Council progressed using the negotiated procedure without prior publication on the basis the works could only be provided by the Sellers on the basis that (i) for technical reasons competition is absent and (ii) the Sellers have exclusive rights in respect of the land and has taken steps within the missives to protect its exclusive rights. There is no reasonable alternative in the Penicuik area. The negotiated procedure without publication was carried out pursuant to Regulation 33 (1) (b) of the 2015 Regulations.
Through this negotiated procedure, the Council has ensured that value for money has been achieved.
The Council has now awarded the contract to BELLWAY HOMES LIMITED.

title: County Wide Grounds Maintenance Services
description:
The contract is to supply grounds maintenance, play area inspection and maintenance and Green Space services, as described in this tender pack. The successful Tenderer will have the expertise to, and the experience of, supplying and continually improving grounds maintenance, play area inspection and maintenance and Green Space services. The results of the services it will provide will have a significant influence on the attractiveness and effectiveness of public spaces and facilities.
This Green Space Contract will take the form of a contract between Buckinghamshire Council and the appointed contractor. The contract is based predominantly on an Output Specification and contract arrangements are as set out in the tender documents. 
The contract is for the provision of Green Space Services covering grounds maintenance within the urban areas of Buckinghamshire, Play area inspection & maintenance throughout the Buckinghamshire area and other green space services for Buckinghamshire Council; including allotment and cemetery management, pitch bookings ,changing room management, and general green space enquiry and complaint handling .
Contract summary:
•	Grass Maintenance
•	Hedge Maintenance
•	Shrub/Rose Bed Maintenance
•	Woodland Management and Maintenance
•	Hardstanding Maintenance and parking
•	Winter Weather Work -gritting and snow clearance
•	Litter Collection
•	Play Area Inspection and Maintenance
•	Changing Room Facilities
•	Exterior Furniture Maintenance
•	Bye-law Enforcement
•	Allotment Services Management
•	Pitch Bookings and Income Collection
•	Cemeteries provision including burials.
•	All other Non-Routine Works
•	Maintenance of the soft landscape within Parking areas
The contract will be for an initial term of 5 years, commencing on 1st of January 2027 and ending on 31st December 2031. There will be an option for the Council to extend for a period, or series of periods, up to a maximum of 48 (forty-eight) additional months, making a potential total contract length of 9 years. The total contract spend for the full 9 years is estimated at £25,232,451. This is only an estimate, and the actual spend maybe higher or lower than this figure. 
The Council is of the opinion that TUPE will apply. 
The contract will not be divided into Lots. The reason for not having Lots is that we have previously considered fractionalizing the tender into lots, however had moved away from this direction. The reason for this is that we have a business need for a single contract, with one main contact and oversight presiding over the whole, which would reduce our management time and pick up economies of scale throughout the supply chain. We have previously found that one point of contact overall with several area managers gives us a suitable and timely service response, with resilience provided through the area managers.

title: Elizabeth Line Tunnel Ventilation and Controls System Maintenance
description:
Rail for London Infrastructure (RfLI) will issue a Tender for planned maintenance and repairs to the Tunnel Ventilation and Controls System on the Central Section of the Elizabeth Line.
RfLI are responsible for maintenance of the Elizabeth Line. A fundamental element of the RfLI maintenance obligation is maintenance of the Tunnel Ventilation and Controls Systems - critical for the operational railway. The Tunnel Ventilation & Controls System on the Elizabeth Line are a critical part of the railway's infrastructure, designed to ensure safety, comfort, and operational reliability across the 21km of twin-bore tunnels beneath central London.
These systems support both normal environmental management and emergency response, including smoke extraction and safe evacuation. They are fully integrated with fire detection systems and centrally managed through an automated SCADA control platform.
The Elizabeth Line's Tunnel Ventilation & Controls System are vital to the safe and effective functioning of one of the UK's most advanced railway lines. Their robust design, automation, and safety integration ensure continuous protection for passengers and staff, while supporting the operational demands of a modern, high-frequency railway.
Regular and rigorous maintenance is essential to ensure system reliability, safety compliance, and continuity of service in both normal and emergency scenarios
The Rail Industry Supplier Qualification Scheme (RISQS) was utilised to identify the initial supplier longlist. RISQS is a Qualifying Utility Dynamic Market. Through RISQS, 157 potential suppliers were identified within the following RISQS (RICCL) categories:
• D.E.5.1 - Fixed Ventilation Systems / Maintain
• H.L.3.1 - General Building Management / Service
A Market Sounding Questionnaire (MSQ) and Expression of Interest (EOI) were issued to these suppliers on the 12/11/2025. The suppliers who registered interest were invited to PSQ
The MSQ  obtained market feedback and supplier appetite, capability and capacity. The results from the findings were used to help shape the procurement strategy. Suppliers who engaged and expressed an interest was invited to participate in the PSQ
Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) was published on 29/07/2026, Suppliers who participated will be invited to tender stage (ITT)

title: Assisted Accommodation with Housing Related Support and Tenancy Support Services
description:
Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust recognises the significant role that suitable accommodation, housing stability and social inclusion play in supporting individuals to live independently, participate within their communities and maintain sustainable tenancies. Access to safe, affordable and appropriate accommodation is a key factor in improving wellbeing, reducing social exclusion and supporting positive life outcomes. Housing instability is frequently associated with increased reliance on statutory services, tenancy breakdown and barriers to independent living. 
The service is required for eligible adults leaving LPFT inpatient and rehabilitation services who need accommodation-transition and tenancy support. It will be used by Service Users, authorised LPFT referral teams and partner agencies involved in discharge, housing, welfare, health and social care.
The required model will maintain the core accommodation-sourcing, discharge and tenancy-sustainment service while strengthening measurable outcomes, tenancy sustainment at 3, 6 and 12 months, Service User experience, accommodation-sourcing timescales, void management, equality analysis and value-for-money assurance.
The current service is an established provision. Commissioned capacity is 15 active concurrent Service Users; recent performance information reports average occupancy of 93%, 27 referrals since April 2024, a 74% acceptance rate and positive move-on outcomes for all recorded Service Users.
The service supports broader integrated system objectives by improving access to housing options, tenancy sustainment services and coordinated support arrangements across Lincolnshire. It also supports national and local priorities to move support from hospital to community, prevent avoidable delay, improve independence, address housing as a determinant of health and enable people to live well in their communities.

title: Provision of Heathrow Expansion Banking Advisor
description:
The Department for Transport (DfT) is seeking to appoint an experienced Banking Adviser to provide independent financial and commercial advice in support of the Heathrow expansion programme.
The Government's ambition is to enable the delivery of an operational third runway at Heathrow Airport by 2035 through a privately financed, market-led delivery model. As one of the UK's largest and most complex infrastructure programmes, Heathrow expansion presents significant financing, affordability, delivery and regulatory challenges.
The successful Adviser will act as a sponsor-side adviser to DfT, providing independent advice on matters including:
• The financeability and financial deliverability of Heathrow expansion;
• Debt and equity market appetite and financing conditions;
• Affordability, risk allocation and investor confidence;
• Measures to improve financeability and reduce delivery risk;
• Government exposure to programme costs and risks;
• Delivery structures, governance arrangements and commercial models; and
• Emerging financing, commercial and regulatory issues.
The successful Adviser will also be required to deliver a strategic financeability assessment every six months throughout the contract term.

title: UPN-00417 - Residential Solar Collective Buying Scheme
description:
In order to support our Growth Strategy priorities of increasing clean, renewable energy and decarbonising homes across the region by 2035, the West of England Combined Authority (WECA) is exploring facilitation of a Collective Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Purchasing Scheme for local authorities within our region.
The aim of this early market engagement exercise is to determine whether there is a market to help residents, SME buildings, community venues and places of worship purchase "Supply and Fit" PV arrays, battery storage, and electric vehicle (EV) chargers at an affordable price from accredited installers. The contractor will handle customer service, vet installers and provide regional capacity for rollout of solar PV, plus provide relevant project data to WECA.
The contractor will deliver a collective purchasing Scheme for the supply and installation of photovoltaic panel (PV) systems for householders to enable them to take advantage of discounted panels via collective purchasing, with options for battery storage and electric vehicle charging. The Contractor will set up an online platform to facilitate the collective purchasing scheme by allowing 3rd party suppliers to bid for work for which householders have registered interest. Supply and installation contracts shall be between the Contractor and the Household/establishment. The Contractor will pay the Authorities a commission for every successful installation completed. The supplier will deliver and install at least 500 domestic solar systems across the West of England by 31 September 2027.
The supplier will be expected to work with the Combined Authority to maximise customer access to the scheme and delivers Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) outputs.
The planned contract start date is 15th January 2027. This contract is categorised as a below threshold concessions contract as the Authorities are not able to commit or guarantee any orders.
This Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is not a call for competition. Responses will inform our procurement strategy, which may or may not include a future competitive tender process. description:
The Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) for Warwickshire invites tenders for the provision of Victim Support Services across Warwickshire.
The PCC seeks to commission experienced providers to deliver high-quality, accessible and specialist support services for victims and survivors of crime including family members and friends where appropriate, enabling individuals to cope with and recover from the impact of crime, access appropriate support and exercise their rights under the Victims' Code. Services will contribute to the PCC's wider priorities of supporting victims and survivors, protecting vulnerable people, improving access to justice, reducing violence against women and girls, reducing inequalities in access to support and improving wellbeing and recovery outcomes.
The requirement is divided into four lots:
•	Lot 1 – Multi Crime Victim Service
•	Lot 2 – Sexual Violence Support Service
•	Lot 3 – Child Exploitation Support Service
•	Lot 4 – Slavery and Exploitation Support Service
Bidders may tender for a single lot or multiple lots.
Across the four lots, the PCC is seeking services that provide appropriate specialist support according to the needs and circumstances of victims and survivors. Services will be expected to provide equitable access to support across Warwickshire, manage demand, capacity and risk effectively, and work collaboratively with relevant statutory, criminal justice, health, safeguarding and voluntary and community sector partners.
The successful provider(s) will be expected to have relevant experience and expertise appropriate to the lot(s) for which they tender and to provide suitably skilled, trained and resilient workforces. Providers will be required to maintain robust safeguarding arrangements and deliver inclusive services capable of responding appropriately to vulnerability and the differing needs of individuals accessing support. 
The contracts will be awarded for an initial period of three (3) years, commencing 1 April 2027, with an option to extend for up to a further two (2) years, subject to funding availability.
Funding is allocated separately to each lot and is subject to the applicable funding terms and conditions. title: 9005587 - Supply of B22 Multiple InfraRed Mirror System
description:
Located on the Harwell Science & Innovation Campus in Oxfordshire, Diamond Light Source (DLS) is a leading-edge facility for science, engineering and innovation. DLS allows researchers from academia and industry to investigate the structure and behaviour of the world around us at the atomic and molecular level. To continue delivering the world changing science that Diamond enables, the facility is being upgraded to Diamond-II, a co ordinated programme of development that combines a major machine upgrade with new instruments and complementary improvements to optics, detectors, sample environment
and delivery capabilities, and computing, as well as integrated and correlative methods. This will be transformative in speed and spatial resolution and will offer users streamlined access to enhanced instruments for life and physical sciences.
Beamline B22 is the InfraRed (IR) beamline of Diamond that will utilize a dipole quadrupole (DQ) magnet as synchrotron source in the new Diamond-II storage ring. The beamline operates 3 end stations, which provide IR and TeraHertz (THz) synchrotron
radiation for microspectroscopy and nanospectroscopy experiments. The operational energy range of the beamline is 1 meV to 1 eV (i.e. wavelength range circa 1 ?m to 1 mm). The visible light from the Diamond-II source is also collected and used for optical alignment at B22.
The scope of the contract is to design, manufacture and deliver an opto-mechanical multiple mirror system for the InfraRed (IR) beamline B22 of DLS to the performance specifications using a shared concept.
The system will support 3 synchrotron IR mirrors (mirrors not part of this tender) designated as Mirror 2a, Mirror 2b and Mirror 2c (M2a, M2b and M2c). Each mirror will have motorised 3-point kinematic motion. The system will have an Ultra High Vacuum
(UHV) vacuum vessel, with support structures and fine adjustments for mechanical alignment.

title: WP5 Social Science - The future of food regulation
description:
Calling off from C425727 Research: Social Science Call-Off.
The Food Standards Agency (FSA)'s Future Food Regulation (FFR) programme aims to deliver a regulatory system that is effective, sustainable and trusted, ensuring food is safe and is what it says it is. The programme aims to establish a national approach to regulating large food retailers, rather than at a local level. Alongside this, the programme aims to implement improvements at the Local Regulation and Online Regulation level, as well as enhance and ensure food business Registration, Enforcement and the Food Hygiene Rating Scheme (FHRS) works alongside regulatory changes. A central Guidance hub is also being developed. A programme and workstream-level Theory of Change (ToC) has consequently been developed, which articulates the problems the programme seeks to address and the outcomes it intends to achieve. 
Following ToC development, the FSA now requires a comprehensive evidence review to establish a clear and defensible rationale for intervention across the programme. This should systematically evidence programme-level and workstream-level problem statements and identify any evidence gaps. Then identify relevant market, behavioural, regulatory and government failures, to assess whether government (FSA) intervention is justified. The outputs will directly support policy development, economic appraisal, stakeholder engagement, and future business case development.

title: 5112.SH.JN - High Yield Electrospinning System
description:
A team at the School of Clinical Dentistry have developed a novel microfiber-based mucoadhesive oral matrix that can deliver drugs and advanced therapeutics directly to the oral mucosa. This technology is highly acceptable to patients and has been evaluated for clinical use in human studies. The team at Sheffield are world leading. We have reported that such matrices can incorporate and release a range of lipophilic, low molecular mass compounds that rapidly diffuse throughout the mucosa following release and without loss of properties. Moreover, we have incorporated larger macromolecules such as peptides and proteins and achieved high loading efficiency, rapid release profiles and retention of functional activity.
The patches are prepared using electrospinning, a versatile, voltage-driven manufacturing technique that uses electrostatic forces to draw and stretch polymer solutions or melts into continuous micro- and nanofibers. Electrospinning offers the production of patches that are flexible, enabling them to conform to wet, curved and dynamic surfaces. Furthermore, their high surface-to-volume ratio facilitates efficient drug loading/release and sustained mucoadhesive interactions, leading to prolonged tissue residence time.
The team have recently secured a UKRI Engineering Biology Mission Award for the adaptation of the technology for mRNA vaccine delivery. For this award we require a high yield electrospinning system.

description:
The Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) for Warwickshire invites tenders for the provision of a Criminal Justice Related Drug and Alcohol Referral Service for Adults.
The PCC seeks to commission an experienced provider to deliver an Arrest Referral Service across police custody settings in Warwickshire, together with associated substance misuse assessment, intervention and referral services.  In addition, the provider will deliver a service within the Leamington Justice Centre courts' setting to offenders who have a history of substance use related problems, the provider will complete court requested suitability assessments for community sentences; and provide information to Court Probation Staff to inform Pre-Sentence Reports.
The service will undertake holistic criminal justice substance misuse assessments for individuals in custody who test positive following a Drug Test on Arrest and those who voluntarily engage with the service. Assessments will consider drug and/or alcohol use alongside offending behaviour, health, safeguarding, vulnerabilities and wider social needs, with the aim of identifying appropriate treatment, support and risk management interventions. The service will also undertake suitability assessments for Community Sentence Treatment Requirements, including Drug Rehabilitation Requirements and Alcohol Treatment Requirements.
The service will maximise opportunities to identify and engage individuals experiencing drug and/or alcohol misuse at a key point of intervention within the criminal justice system. It will provide early intervention, harm reduction advice, brief interventions, and effective pathways into community drug and alcohol treatment and wider support services.
The successful provider will operate as a key partner within Warwickshire's multi-agency response to substance misuse and offending, working collaboratively with Warwickshire Police Custody, Probation, the commissioned community drug and alcohol treatment provider and other relevant statutory and community partners. The service will contribute to improved treatment engagement, improved criminal justice outcomes and the reduction of reoffending in Warwickshire.
The PCC is seeking a provider with relevant experience and expertise in delivering substance misuse and/or criminal justice services, with the capability to provide an appropriately skilled and resilient workforce within police custody and criminal justice environments. The provider will be expected to demonstrate effective multi-agency working, strong safeguarding and risk management arrangements, and the ability to engage individuals with complex needs and support them into appropriate treatment and wider services. 
The requirement will be procured as a single contract and has not been divided into lots. The Authority considered whether to separate the custody and court-related elements of the service but determined that delivery through a single contract would provide continuity of service and straightforward, integrated referral pathways.
The contract will be awarded for an initial period of three (3) years, commencing 1 April 2027, with an option to extend for up to a further two (2) years, subject to funding availability.
The contract is funded through a fixed budget, subject to applicable funding terms and conditions. Funding levels may be subject to change during the contract period and any underspent funding must be returned to the Authority and/or relevant funding body.  Contract values provided are indicative and dependent on VAT status of successful bidder(s).

title: CEFAS26-106 Contract for Expert contribution for data-limited methods for category 4-6 stocks
description:
Cefas requires expert services from Laurence Kell 'SEA++' limited, for the provision of expert contribution to support the delivery of Cefas Large Collaborative Project LCP003, Task 1.1 "data-limited methods for category 4-6 stocks". The contract is based on the requirements and structure of a previous agreement with Cefas, adapted for current needs.
Task 1.1 of the relevant project will use length data from fisheries to design catch rules that lead to substantial improvement in performance (in terms of increased yield and reduced risk of resource depletion), when compared to the current International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES) catch rules for category 4-6 stocks (stocks without stock size indices; catch advice reduced every three years). It develops methods that utilise alternative data in catch rules (e.g. spatial indicators) and builds the simulation framework to test them.
Requirements:
Specialised technical requirements to be met by the supplier:
• Expert contribution for the method development for data-limited fish stocks.
• Expert, in-depth knowledge of management strategy evaluation (MSE) and associated techniques (including the Fisheries Library in R, FLR) and internationally recognised leader in these topics.
• In-depth knowledge of data-limited evaluation techniques, including methods development, and well-established experience in the ICES data-limited methods workshop WKLIFE (including life-history and length-based methods).
• World leading expert in stock assessment methods, model validation, and diagnostics.
• Expertise in high-performance computing, including methods for massive parallelisation.
• Supervision of PhD students.
The supplier will provide expert contribution to the project, including:
• Conceptualisation of framework for severely data-limited stocks
• Exploration of length-based catch rules
• Review of size-based fisheries management options
• Development and testing of spatial indicator approaches, including hindcasting.
• Contributions to international workshops, such as the ICES data-limited methods workshop ICES WKLIFE in September 2026, and attendance at monthly meetings with Cefas.
• Supervision and support of Cefas staff PhD students on spatial indicators in collaboration with Imperial College London
Meetings and Communication
• The supplier will attend monthly meetings (in-person or online) as agreed with the project team.
• Additional meetings may be scheduled as required.
• Regular updates and correspondence will be maintained throughout the contract period.
Deliverables:
Delivery, as outlined in the requirement section above, will be throughout the duration of the contract with regular meetings and agreed contributions which will be confirmed via correspondence with Cefas project LCP003 1.1 task leader. The deliverables include support for the following elements:
1. Work on data-limited catch rules (including conceptual framework for severely data-limited stocks, review of length-based catch rules, written review of size-based fisheries management options)
2. Hindcast analysis of spatial indicators
3. Regular meeting attendance and expert input
4. Support, review, and feedback on project outputs and publications
5. Supervision of Cefas PhD student , as part of the project
a. Elements 1-5 are to be delivered by 31 March 2026.
Quantity:
• 20 working days by the supplier
• Travel
o UK travel reimbursed at actual cost with receipts
o International travel reimbursed as per UK Government rates, with receipts, e.g. 6 days to cover attendance at international meeting
Location for services to be undertaken:
Hybrid: Online and in-person meetings at Cefas, Lowestoft laboratory, UK; international meeting attendance, either in person or online.

title: Remote Offsite IT Backup and Disaster Recovery Services
description:
The scope of the Contract is the provision of Off Site IT Backup and Disaster Recovery Services. The core requirements of the Contract are:
•Comprehensive Hybrid Backup Coverage – Protection for both on-premise servers (physical and virtual) and Microsoft 365 cloud workloads (Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams).
•Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Protection – Backup and recovery of directory structures, user identities, security groups, and roles to ensure continuity of identity and access management.
•Secure Off-Site Data Storage – All backup data replicated to off-site UK-based data centres or UK GDPR-approved cloud regions, encrypted at rest and in transit (AES-256 minimum).
•Immutable & Ransomware-Protected Storage – Backups stored in immutable or air-gapped form to prevent alteration, deletion, or encryption by malicious actors.
•Active Threat and Malware Scanning – Continuous integrity and antivirus scanning of all backups to prevent the reinjection of infected files during restoration.
•Automated & Scheduled Backups – Policy-driven backups with daily incremental and weekly full backups, covering approximately 15TB of data.
•Granular and Full-System Recovery – Ability to restore entire systems, virtual machines, individual files, or Microsoft 365 items with minimal downtime.
•Defined RPO and RTO Targets – Recovery Point Objective (RPO) ≤ 15 minutes; Recovery Time Objective (RTO) ≤ 4 hours for critical workloads.
•Centralised Monitoring and Reporting – Unified dashboard and regular reporting on backup status, success rates, storage capacity, and security alerts.
•Disaster Recovery and Failover Testing – Annual or quarterly DR testing for both on-prem and cloud workloads, with documented outcomes and improvement actions.
•Business Continuity Support – Assistance with recovery planning, testing, and post-incident review.
•Compliance and Assurance – Provider certified to ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials Plus, operating within UK GDPR and NCSC guidelines.
•Scalability and Futureproofing – Capacity to scale storage and add new workloads (e.g. Azure VMs, SaaS systems) without major service disruption.
•24/7 Support and Incident Response – Access to a UK-based service desk and escalation for high-severity incidents.
• AI-based anomaly detection for early ransomware or corruption warnings.
•Self-service restore portal for authorised staff.
•Carbon-neutral or energy-efficient data centres to support Pioneer’s sustainability objectives.
•Integration with your ITSM system for automated incident alerting and reporting.

title: Refurbishment of Ground Floor Toilets & Cloakroom at Cornerstone Arts Centre, Didcot
description:
South Oxfordshire District Council (SODC) is seeking to appoint a suitably competent Contractor to carry out internal refurbishment works to national building specifications and standards, at The Cornerstone Arts Centre located in Didcot, Oxfordshire.   
The Cornerstone is a municipal multi-purpose arts and community venue, owned and managed by SODC.  It is located in the heart of Didcot town centre, adjacent to the popular Orchard Shopping Centre. The premises is staffed from 10:00 to 23:00, Monday to Saturday. It is open to the public on these days, with ticketed shows taking place in the evenings and other community-based hire functions throughout the day.  It is principally closed on Sundays, though may open on an infrequent basis for shows if required.  
The premises was constructed in 2007/08 and comprises of three storeys, accommodating a ground floor café and various exhibition rooms, toilets, cloakroom, offices, auditorium and smaller multi-functional rooms. The premises is constructed on an incline so that there is a lower ground, upper ground and 1st floor areas. The floors are linked via a staircase that ascends from lower ground floor to the upper floors.  The stair is open to the lower ground floor café and exhibition spaces.  The café and exhibition spaces are popular with the local community and visitors alike, attracting busy lunchtime trade as well as during evening performances and events.  
The ground floor toilets and cloakroom require upgrading to improve general decorative order, functionality and accessibility.  The Works briefly comprises of: 
Male Toilet: to include; localised damp-proofing, installation of PVC wall cladding to all walls, minor electrical works, cleaning and pressure testing of the IPS, cosmetic improvements to sink area, general painting and decorating. 
Female Toilet: to include; localised damp-proofing, installation of PVC wall cladding to all walls, minor electrical works, cleaning of IPS, cosmetic improvements to sink area, general painting and decorating, installation of new ceiling. 
Disabled Toilet: to include the re-decoration of ground floor disabled toilet facility (woodwork and ceiling). Removal of secondary toilet and associated pipework/boxing.  Replacement flooring. Removal of tile finishes and installation of new PVC wall cladding. Minor electrical works. Cleaning and pressure testing of the IPS system. 
Ground floor Cloak Room Area:  To include; removal of existing counter in current cloakroom.  Painting of floor. Create new cloakroom in adjacent understairs alcove complete with storage, modified counter and new electric roller shutter. Minor electrical works, painting and decorating.  
Tenderers should note that the above is not an exhaustive list and should include for any additional items of work as identified in the specification, tender drawings, schedule of works and other tender supporting documents, that is not specifically mentioned or listed above but will be required in order to complete the Works as necessary.  
The successful Contractor must demonstrate their ability to provide the services required, conformation to current appropriate legislation, as well as all other relevant health and safety regulations.   
The successful Contractor must provide a suitably trained workforce that has experience and knowledge of the Works required to be undertaken.  
The successful Contractor is to provide all labour, materials, plant/equipment, and other items necessary for the proper execution of the Works, in its entirety.

title: North Northamptonshire Council Provision of Integrated Healthy Lifestyles Service
description:
North Northamptonshire Council have appointed  a lead Service Provider to deliver a comprehensive Integrated Healthy Lifestyles Service (IHLS) in North Northamptonshire, with elements of subcontracting permitted to support residents to make sustainable changes to the key modifiable risk factors across the adult life course, enabling them to live longer in better health, whilst achieving a reduction in inequalities between communities. 
The service will seek to address key modifiable risk factors that contribute to preventable ill-health. The service will have a primary focus on physical activity, diet and excess weight, strength and balance for falls prevention and earlier identification of increased risk of developing long-term conditions.
The service will introduce a central triage function to improve access and referrals into healthy lifestyle support, along with an expanded range of interventions to support behaviour change.
The service will include a range of interventions organised into three core pillars:
Pillar 1: a universal self-help pillar comprising of health promotion
campaigns and digital self-help tools
Pillar 2: a behaviour change pillar providing health coaching support to address the in-scope risk factors
Pillar 3: a structured treatment pillar targeting reducing inequalities through provision of community falls prevention, an enhanced behaviour change support, and a targeted NHS Health Checks programme in workplaces and specific communities.

title: Chesterfield Gas Cylinders
description:
CSC is the sole economic operator capable of delivering PDS activities due to its role as the approved Design Organisation (DO) and OEM, holding the design licence, technical 
drawings, product knowledge, and in-service reliability data for the equipment. Any 
alternative supplier would require licences from both CSC and the air system OEMs, incur 
significant additional costs, and need to demonstrate suitability as a DO. An option to separate spare parts procurement from the PDS function was considered and rejected by the MoD Engineering Authority due to significant airworthiness, safety, and 
interoperability risks. The air system Design Organisation specifies exact part numbers that are manufactured exclusively by CSC to approved drawings and processes, making CSC the only supplier capable of providing compliant spares. CSC also holds the specialist tooling required to manufacture these components and ensure configuration and quality control. Introducing an alternative supplier would require costly and complex aircraft design revalidation, part requalification, and approval activities, with no guarantee of acceptance by the air system DO. This would create unacceptable safety and operational risks, including potential aircraft grounding, while imposing disproportionate cost and technical burden on the Authority.

At the heart of the Trust is the focus on school improvement, staff development and ensuring that our pupils receive the absolute best educational experience. We adhere to a philosophy of continual improvement.
We are a family of schools with a plan for further growth and aim to welcome more primary academies and more primary children into our MAT over the coming years.
For more information, please visit https://www.mosaicschoolslearningtrust.org/
Procurement
The ICT Support at the Trust is currently provided by a single outsourced support provider who provides a mix of scheduled onsite visits and remote support.
As a result of a change in circumstances, the Trust is taking the opportunity to go to the market to identify the best innovative and forward-looking partner to support them in the delivery and development of their ICT provision over the next five years.
This procurement includes (but may not be limited to) the items listed below.
•	A core managed service, covering management of all ICT against an agreed SLA
•	A Service Desk, available 52 weeks a year including out of hours access
•	On-Site local staffing covering (at a minimum) term time, which suppliers deem necessary to deliver the service and meet the SLA requirements
•	Strategic advice and direction to the Trust regarding ICT
•	Responsibility for design, specification, installation, and management of all ICT infrastructure
•	Supply of goods and services based on an agreed Best 3approach
•	Management of 3rd parties where relevant to the ICT support
•	Relevant monitoring, management, patching
•	Regular performance reporting
•	CPD and training - digital skills and curriculum as necessary
•	There is an expectation that the provider will support and/or drive innovation
•	Maintain technical documentation
•	Maintain operational documentation, for example inventory management and risk registers
•	Collective partnership targets aligned to the Trust's objectives
•	In Trust support for the integration and upgrade of the connectivity, communications and security infrastructure as required
•	Suppliers may be required to deliver a range of technology and change management projects in addition to the providing the core managed service.

Belgium – Military research and technology – Framework Contract for the Provision of Services “Ensuring accessibility and availability of Civilian Transport Infrastructure for Military Platforms”_24.CAP.OP.160
description: The overarching objective of the Framework Contract (FWC) is to support EU Member States in ensuring accessibility and availability of civilian transport infrastructure for military platforms. To this end, the FWC should identify gaps and deficits in logistical capacity related to military transport needs, as well as procedural aspects related to military transport in various dimensions, mapping the current situation and providing EU Member States with information that would serve to improve their Military Mobility capabilities. Moreover, this knowledge will ultimately enable the Agency to propose relevant and concrete actions which will enhance Military Mobility related capability development activities. The overarching objective of the FWC will be achieved through specific contracts (SCs) in the various distinct areas related to logistic capacity, including but not limited to: • Landscaping of capability gaps in logistic capacity for the different forms of transportation (land, air, sea, inland water ways); • Landscaping the legislative framework applicable to movement of military assets; • Assessing the potential for improving the above mentioned capacity; • Providing recommendations for future activities on improved accessibility of civilian transport infrastructure for military purposes.

title: Austria – Substation construction work – (ProVia-ID 161711) UW Landeck; UW Landeck - Baumeisterarbeiten
description: Das gegenständliche Projekt umfasst die Errichtung einer neuen Unterwerksanlage am gleichen Standort mit drittelweiser Abschaltbarkeit und Einsatz eines fahrbaren Unterwerks. Der Neubau besteht aus einem 15-kV-Schaltanlagengebäude und Warten-/Gerüstraum, einer 15-kV-metallgekapselten Anlage, einer 110-kV-Freiluftschaltanlage mit drei 110/15-kV–Umspannern, einem 15-kV-Schaltgerüst mit Kabelkollektor einschließlich aller Nebeneinrichtungen. Das Unterwerk Landeck wird in 2 Bauphasen an Ort und Stelle erneuert. Während der 1. Umbauphase wird mit einem Drittel der Bestandsanlage einem fUW und dem bestehenden Oberleitungsschaltgerüst weiter Betrieb geführt. In dieser Zeit wird die 110-kV-Bahnstromleitung Pettneu 2 – Ötztal 2 am Ü-Leitungsmast Nr.Ld 2 durchgeschliffen. Der vordere Teil (U3) und der Mittelteil (U2) der Anlage werden außer Betrieb genommen. Nach Neubau der vorderen 2 Drittel (U3, U2) der Freiluftanlage und deren Inbetriebnahme mit der neuen 15-kV-Anlage, inklusive neuem Schaltgerüst wird das hintere Drittel (U1) neu gebaut. In dieser 2. Umbauphase wird die 110-kV-Bahnstromleitung Pettneu 1 – Ötztal 1 am Ü-Leitungsmast Nr. Ld 1 durchgeschliffen. Die neue 110-kV-Freiluftschaltanlage ist in Reihen-Längsbauweise als Doppelsammelschienenanlage mit oben liegender Sammelschiene und 2 Längsteilungen mit Kupplung konzipiert. Die Umspanner werden gleisgebunden in die Anlage geliefert. Die gesamte Erdungsanlage für alle Anlagenteile wird gemäß den gültigen Vorschriften und Normen unter Berücksichtigung der ÖBB Vorschriften sowie der technischen Festlegungen für Schaltanlagen errichtet. Das Unterwerksgebäude entspricht der Gebäudeklasse 1 gemäß den gültigen OIB Richtlinien. Die Oberflächenentwässerung der befestigten Flächen, einschließlich der Straßen, erfolgt über die Versickerung auf eigenem Grund. Die Dachwässer werden in einen neu herzustellenden Sickerschacht geleitet und am eigenen Grund zur Versickerung gebracht. In den neuen Räumlichkeiten ist kein ständiger Arbeitsplatz vorgesehen. Erneuert werden folgende bestehende Anlagenteile: 15-kV-UW Schaltgerüst. Komplette 110-kV-Freiluftschaltanlage. UW – Gleis. UW-Gebäude. Alle Arbeiten sind unter Berücksichtigung der bestehenden Infrastruktur, der geltenden Normen und der projektspezifischen Anforderungen auszuführen. Die Planungsleistungen umfassen die Erstellung von Lage- und Schnittplänen, statischen Nachweisen, Schal- und Bewehrungsplänen sowie Leistungsverzeichnissen für die spätere Ausschreibung der Bauleistungen.

Market validation, quality, and regulation reviews will be handled by third parties under separate contractual arrangements, which will be the subject to separate tender processes outside of this procurement. A framework agreement constitutes a means of establishing overall terms and conditions in accordance with which, for a specified duration, individual contracts may or not be awarded. In the context of a multi-party framework agreement, the successful framework members compete for each new contract, with potential options for follow-on work which arises and is linked to the original contract. For clarity, these follow on contracts can be awarded directly to the winner of the initial contract by direct negotiation and will not generally be subject to mini tendering. title: Netherlands – Market research services – EA Klantonderzoek - 2024
description: Voor deze opdracht is het volledige domein van Klantonderzoek van NS binnen scope (met uitzondering van een aantal specifieke gevallen zie paragraaf 3.2.1). Een opdracht kan bestaan uit een geheel Klantonderzoekstraject of een deel hiervan. NS onderscheidt hierin de volgende stappen: 1. Probleemverkenning (vaststellen onderzoeksdoel, hoofdvraag en hypotheses) 2. Methode (onderzoeksvoorstel) 3. Steekproef 4. Vragenlijst/Gespreksleidraad 5. Veldwerk 6. Analyse 7. Rapportage/data levering 8. Advisering Percelen Deze aanbesteding is ingedeeld in de volgende vijf (5) percelen: • Perceel 1: Online Kwantitatief onderzoek • Perceel 2: Merktracking • Perceel 3: Face-to-face Kwantitatief onderzoek. • Perceel 4: Kwalitatief onderzoek • Perceel 5: Neuro-onderzoek Gegadigde kan zich aanmelden voor en inschrijven op één (1) of meerdere percelen. Of een partij zich wel of niet voor meerdere percelen aanmeldt, heeft geen invloed op de beoordeling van de Aanmelding. Perceel 1: Online Kwantitatief onderzoek Dit perceel betreft het gehele domein van Kwantitatief onderzoek binnen NS (hoofdzakelijk online maar ook telefonisch en schriftelijk) met uitzondering van Merktracking (zie perceel 2) en Face-to-face Kwantitatief onderzoek (zie perceel 3). NS onderscheidt drie vormen van Klantonderzoek binnen dit perceel; • ad hoc onderzoeken – eenmalige onderzoeken over een specifiek vraagstuk. • herhaalmetingen – bijv. 0- en 1-metingen of andere terugkerende metingen zonder vaste regelmaat en met ruimte om de vragenlijst aan te passen tussen metingen. • monitoren – lang lopende onderzoeken met een vaste regelmaat die altijd exact dezelfde vorm hebben om de vergelijkbaarheid te waarborgen. Binnen dit perceel vallen deze ad hoc onderzoeken, herhaalmetingen en monitoren die een kwantitatieve aard hebben en niet face-to-face worden uitgevoerd Perceel 2: Merktracking Binnen dit perceel vallen merkpositietracking, kwantitatieve pre-testen en effectmetingen van communicatiecampagnes en Social Media tracking. In het perceel Merktracking wordt Klantonderzoek uitgevraagd dat inzicht biedt in de effectiviteit van gevoerde (Social Media) communicatiecampagnes in relatie tot doelstellingen. Daarnaast wenst NS de merkpositie te tracken door het jaar heen en de invloed van communicatiecampagnes op de merkpositie inzichtelijk te maken. Perceel 3. Face-to-face Kwantitatief onderzoek Dit perceel betreft Kwantitatief onderzoek dat face-to-face afgenomen wordt. Deze onderzoeken worden afgenomen op het moment dat de respondent de beleving ervaart, om zo de daadwerkelijke beleving van de respondenten te kunnen meten. Perceel 4. Kwalitatief onderzoek Dit perceel betreft het gehele domein van Kwalitatief onderzoek binnen NS: Klantonderzoek dat gericht is op het verzamelen en analyseren van niet-numerieke gegevens om inzichten te krijgen in attitudes, overtuigingen en motivaties van individuen of groepen. Dit type onderzoek is daarmee exploratief en beschrijvend van aard. Kwalitatief onderzoek wordt doorgaans via focusgroepen of via individuele gesprekken uitgevoerd op locatie of online. Perceel 5. Neuro-onderzoek Neuro-onderzoek is een redelijk nieuwe tak van Klantonderzoek voor NS; NS maakt hier pas sinds een paar jaar gebruik van. Het behelst onderzoek dat met behulp van medische technieken (zoals fMRI, huisgeleiding en EEG) brein- en lichamelijke reacties meet. Doel hiervan is om in kaart te brengen hoe respondenten onbewust op bepaalde stimuli reageren.

title: Switzerland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Generalplaner SIA 32 - 53 für Kompensationsanlage im UW Romanel
description: La sous-station 380/220 kV de Romanel (VD) est située dans la commune de Romanel-sur-Lausanne, dans le canton de Vaud. En 2025, un avant-projet (phase SIA 31) comprenant différentes variantes a été élaboré pour ce projet. Le choix de la variante a été arrêté en 2026. Le présent appel d’offres porte désormais sur les phases allant du projet de construction jusqu’à la fin du projet (équivalent des phases SIA 32 à SIA 53). Dans un premier temps, les prestations des phases SIA 32 à SIA 41 sont commandées. Les phases SIA 51 à SIA 53 font l'objet d'un appel d'offres en option et seront commandées, le cas échéant, dans un deuxième temps. Les travaux de planification doivent donc être réalisés dans une mesure habituelle pour un tel projet. Pour la planification et la coordination de ce projet, le présent appel d'offres vise à recruter le maître d'œuvre pour les phases SIA 32 à 53. Outre l'étendue des prestations spécifiques à son domaine de compétence, le maître d'œuvre assume également la supervision et la coordination générales de tous les domaines spécialisés impliqués, y compris les interfaces, en tant que responsable général au sens de la norme SIA 103. Les sous-domaines suivants doivent être organisés par le planificateur général: * Ingénierie et conception dans le sous-projet « Technique primaire » (y compris les câbles haute tension) * Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet « réactance de compensation » * Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet « besoins propres » (y compris les chemins de câbles) * Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet « technique du bâtiment » (CVC) y compris les chemins de câbles * Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet « génie civil » * Conception et planification dans le sous-projet Géologie * Conception et planification dans le sous-projet Environnement Les sous-domaines suivants sont mis à la disposition du planificateur général: * coordination générale des modèles BIM côté mandante; * ingénierie et planification côté mandante dans le sous-segment «SAS»; Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter les documents C100 et C101 du dossier d'appel d'offres.

title: BCU-ITT-63452 - ABERGELE CLINIC ROOF UPGRADE
description:
Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board requires a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake roof upgrade works for the Abergele Community Clinic. The works are part of BCUHB Capital Programme have been approved at BCUHB Capital Board.  
The works shall comprise the complete renewal of the existing flat roof construction to provide a fully warranted warm roof system incorporating a seamless cold-applied liquid waterproofing membrane and thermal upgrade to current Building Regulations requirements.
The contractor shall:
•	Provide all scaffolding, edge protection and access equipment.
•	Strip the existing roof construction back to the timber joist structure.
•	Inspect and verify the structural suitability of the roof deck and supporting structure.
•	Install a new 18mm plywood deck in accordance with BS EN 1995-1-1 (Eurocode 5).
•	Install a new warm roof build-up including: 
i.	Air and vapour control layer.
ii.	Tapered PIR insulation scheme.
iii.	Carrier membrane where required.
iv.	Reinforced cold-applied liquid waterproofing system.
•	Dismantle the disused chimney to below deck level and form new deck support structure.
•	Install high and low-level ventilation grilles to the retained chimney stack.
•	Complete all associated roof details, penetrations, upstands, outlets, flashings and terminations.
A sectional method of working shall be adopted to ensure the building remains weather-tight at the end of each working day. 
The contractor will be responsible for coordinating architectural, mechanical, electrical, and structural elements required to deliver the refurbishment works. 
All works will be carried out within a live hospital environment and must be carefully phased to minimise disruption to ongoing clinical services. The contractor will be expected to manage logistics, access arrangements, infection control measures, and health and safety requirements in accordance with NHS estate standards and hospital operational constraints.

title: Cryo-EM Talos Arctica Service Contract
description:
Provision of a 3-year original equipment manufacturer (OEM) service agreement for the Thermo Fisher Scientific (FEI UK Ltd.) Talos Arctica Cryogenic Electron Microscope (Serial Number 09950877, commissioned Sept/2020) and associated cryogenic electron microscopy equipment.
The agreement provides comprehensive manufacturer-backed support, including remote diagnostics and technical support as the first stage of fault assessment (same day within hours), followed where required by escalation to on-site physical inspection (48-hour response), troubleshooting, emergency repair support and corrective maintenance by manufacturer-certified service engineers.
The contract includes a targeted response time of 48 hours during normal business hours, emergency breakdown assistance, remote service capability, scheduled preventive maintenance, performance verification, software licences, software maintenance and updates, replacement parts and components (excluding consumables), and access to proprietary service tools, firmware, calibration procedures and technical documentation.
Service delivery is provided through the manufacturer's UK organisation and authorised UK-based service infrastructure, ensuring timely support and compliance with applicable UK operational requirements. The equipment and supporting systems comply with applicable UKCA and CE marking requirements. The agreement ensures continued reliability, performance, software compatibility and operational availability of a nationally significant research infrastructure asset.
Thermo Fisher Scientific (FEI UK Ltd.) is the original equipment manufacturer of the Talos Arctica Cryogenic Electron Microscope (Serial Number 09950877, commissioned 09/2020) and associated integrated cryogenic electron microscopy equipment. The manufacturer is the only supplier with access to proprietary software, firmware, service documentation, diagnostic tools, calibration procedures, certified replacement parts, software licences and manufacturer-trained service engineers required to maintain the system to the original manufacturer's specification. Support is delivered through a combination of remote diagnostics and technical assessment, followed when necessary by on-site intervention by certified field service engineers.
No alternative supplier can provide the complete package of OEM-supported maintenance, software updates, performance verification, spare parts provision and manufacturer-backed service coverage. Competition is therefore absent for technical reasons, and the contract must be awarded directly to the OEM to ensure continued operation, reliability and performance of this nationally important research infrastructure asset.

title: What works in AI Adoption within DCMS Sectors
description:
Full information is provided within the specification. 
DCMS are seeking to commission "what works" research into the impact and effectiveness of AI adoption interventions within DCMS sectors. We are interested in two broad sets of questions. The first is analysis of how businesses within DCMS sectors that are in the process of adopting AI achieve this, the challenges they face and the opportunities and benefits realised. We anticipate this will be explored through an ethnographic study that observes how individuals and teams actually use AI tools in their jobs. The second set of questions is what policy interventions work best to support businesses that wish to adopt AI, which we anticipate will be answered by testing hypothetical interventions through randomised control trials (RCTs). Bidders will be able to propose alternative methodologies if they think they suit these questions better; the core need for this project is to produce direct, robust evidence of what works, as opposed to what is self-reported (e.g. through interviews, focus groups, surveys, and similar) to work.

title: Servicing and Maintenance of Medical Gas Pipeline Systems (MGPS) at Nottingham City Hospital
description:
The Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (The Authority) requires a Supplier for the provision of Servicing and Maintenance of the Medical Gas Pipeline System (MGPS) at the Nottingham City Hospital.
The purpose of the contract is to ensure the Authority complies with Health Technical Memorandum (HTM) 02-01 as well as applicable standards and relevant legislation. A copy of HTM 02-01 can be found on the NHS England website:
- https://www.england.nhs.uk/estates/health-technical-memoranda/ 
The objective of the contract is to ensure the provision of safe and MGPS for administering of medical gases (E.g. oxygen) to patients under the care of the Authority.
An MPGS comprises a source of supply, pipeline distribution system, terminal units (to which the user connects and disconnects medical equipment) and a warning/alarm system. Systems include for, but are not limited to, provision of oxygen, nitrous oxide and medical air for respiratory and surgical applications.
To ensure the MGPS operates safely and reliably, the Authority requires a Supplier to provide regular planned preventative maintenance (PPM) to mitigate risks of faults or failures occurring. A minor issue, such as a leak in the pipeline for example, may have major consequences such as patient fatality as a result of oxygen deprivation.
The PPM must be carried out in full accordance with the requirements of HTM 02-01 Part B (Operational Management Chapter 10 maintenance 10.1 to 10.161) and the Supplier must include all consumables and manufacturer’s identifiable parts for quarterly or annual routine servicing on all of the Authority’s medical gas pipe, plant and systems and include:
- All plant equipment servicing as per manufacturer’s recommendations
- Annual AGSS LEV testing and certification.
- Dental air and vacuum. 
- Pathology Gases. 
The Services detailed in the associated procurement documents are deemed to be the minimum required to be undertaken during each quarterly and annual service visit. The Supplier shall be required, from time to time, to perform any other task required as part of the service  in order for the relevant system(s) to remain compliant with HTM 02-01.

title: Water Management - Legionella
description:
The Northern Lighthouse Board has 208 lighthouses protecting the coastline of Scotland, the Northern Isles, The Western Isles and the Isle of Man as well as an office in Edinburgh, and bases in Oban, Inverness, Lerwick and Kirkwall.  The lighthouse stations are infrequently visited, with some being annual or biennial maintenance visits of varying lengths as detailed in the requirements document. This should be taken into account in the risk assessment. 
Of these buildings 66 have a water system that is supplied from either mains, private or stored water supplied by NLB tender.  NLB has a duty to ensure those systems are assessed, compliant and maintained to ensure they pose no risk.
It should be noted on all lighthouse station sites that the water system is used for washing, showering and flushing toilets, bottled water is provided for drinking and cooking.  For mains sites bottled water is still the preferred means for drinking water.
All stations with water have UV and particulate filters within the water system, unfortunately the UV system is switched off between visits and is not optimally maintained.  NLB supplement the UV system by storing water automatically dosed with a silver stabilised hydrogen peroxide solution at 250 parts per million. 
The Northern Lighthouse Board is seeking to appoint a Contractor who will: -
Undertake Legionella Risk assessments, remedial works and advise necessary control measures and testing regimes to all buildings, structures or assets with hot and cold-water systems and services at all easily accessible road end sites. 
For remote sites the Contractor will carry out a desk top risk assessment based on information provided by NLB. 
Answer ad hoc queries and provide advice on legionella related matters at NLB sites. 
When required, approximately every three years, the Contractor will provide suitable and sufficient training or refresher training to NLB Technicians to allow them to gather the appropriate information on the remote sites.
Further information on requirements of this procurement including technical specifications can be found in Schedule 2 - Requirements Specification.

title: British Museum Round Reading Room Roof Oculus Works
description:
Project Overview
The British Museum is seeking to appoint a Principal Contractor for a programme of essential roof repair and replacement works to the Grade I listed Round Reading Room, located at the centre of the Museum.
Building Context and Heritage Significance
The Round Reading Room was designed by Sydney Smirke and completed in 1857. It is a structure of exceptional national heritage significance, combining iron primary construction with brick masonry, a copper-clad dome, and a fully glazed central lantern. The roofscape comprises three elements: a perimeter flat roof known as the Snow Gallery Roof; the copper dome in batten-roll standing seam; and a twenty-sided glazed lantern incorporating patent glazing, timber sidelights, and a decorative internal laylight.
Scope of Works
The works span four principal areas:
•	Snow Gallery Roof: Removal of an existing membrane and mineral wool flat roof build-up down to the concrete deck. Installation of a warm roof with cold-applied liquid waterproofing membrane, including upstands, penetrations, and new lightning protection.
•	Copper Dome Conservation and Repair: Close-quarters condition survey and conservation-led repair from temporary scaffold, including localised copper panel replacement, seam and flashing repairs, and full replacement of the lantern base apron. Works must be undertaken by heritage-accredited metal roofing specialists.
•	Lantern Glazing, Windows and Refurbishment: Full replacement of the existing patent-glazed lantern atop the dome with a bespoke tiered steel glazing bar system; repair and redecoration of external windows and internal sliding sashes; installation of BMS-linked actuators; and in-situ conservation of the historic internal laylight.
•	Maintenance Access and MEP: Upgrade of permanent access provisions including fall-arrest and restraint systems, internal walkway refurbishment, replacement heating, LED lighting, and BMS integration.
The project includes a number of CDP items, including, but not limited to, scaffold and temporary works, tiered patent glazing, access systems and MEP systems.
Key Project Constraints
•	Access and Logistics: The site is entirely enclosed within the Foster+Partners Great Court roof, with no direct external crane access, and the Round Reading Room is to remain open to staff and the public for the maximum time possible during the works. A Stage 4 design for a cable-restrained scaffold system and temporary roof has been developed by an access specialist and needs to be completed as a CDP item, alongside a full lifting, logistics and evacuation strategy.
•	Operational Environment: Although temporary periods of closure and exclusion will be possible in the Round Reading Room, the Museum will remain open without restriction throughout the construction period. Noise and vibration limits apply, and protection of the Reading Room interior and collections is mandatory throughout.
•	Hazardous Materials: Asbestos-Containing Materials and lead-based paints are confirmed present within the lantern and on historic ironwork. Safe methods of removal must be provided during the works.
Procurement and Programme
The project will be procured via a single-stage traditional tender under a JCT Standard Building Contract 2024 with Contractor's Design Portion. A contractor will be selected on capability, heritage experience, and commercial submission, with appointment aimed for November 2026, a start on site in January 2027 and Practical Completion targeted for Q1 2028.
Contractors will be required to demonstrate CDP and construction experience across: conservation of Grade I or II* listed structures; heritage metal roofing; liquid-applied roofing; bespoke patent glazing fabrication; heritage window joinery and ironwork; works within live occupied public buildings; and complex temporary works in constrained environments.
Due to the confidential/commercially sensitive nature of information that will be included in the associated tender documents we require that interested suppliers enter into a confidentiality agreement before they are given access to the tender pack. A copy of the confidentiality agreement is available by request via email to procurement@britishmuseum.org. The terms of the confidentiality agreement are not subject to negotiation.
