title: Suicide Prevention Works – Multi-Storey Car Parks
description:
Dear Supplier,
The Council is currently undertaking pre-market engagement in relation to potential suicide prevention works at its multi-storey car parks.
For one car park work is required to install new vehicular edge protection alongside suicide prevention works, and for all car parks the Council has a requirement to consider immediate, temporary suicide prevention remedies.
The purpose of this exercise is to gain a better understanding of the current market, available solutions, delivery models, indicative costs, timescales, technical considerations and potential procurement routes. The information gathered will help inform the Council’s requirements and future procurement strategy.
Please note that this is not a procurement exercise, invitation to tender or request for a quotation. Responses will not be evaluated, scored or used to select suppliers, and participation in this exercise will not provide any advantage or disadvantage in relation to any future procurement opportunity.
The Council is not committed to proceeding with a procurement exercise as a result of this market engagement and reserves the right to amend, defer or not proceed with any future requirement.
Any information provided should therefore be considered as market intelligence only. Suppliers should not incur any costs in responding, and the Council will not be responsible for any costs associated with participation in this exercise.
We would be grateful if you could provide a response in PDF form and return it by Thursday, 1st October 2026.
Thank you for taking the time to engage with the Council and for sharing your expertise and experience.
Kind regards,
Procurement
Guildford Borough Council
Purpose: To obtain market intelligence to inform the Council’s procurement strategy, technical requirements, delivery model and potential route to market. Responses should be treated as indicative market information and not as a request for a binding quotation.

Supporting Scotland's Response to Exotic Animal Disease Outbreaks
The Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) is seeking support from vet practices across Scotland to help respond to outbreaks of exotic notifiable and reportable animal diseases, including Avian Influenza (AI) and Bluetongue (BT).
During disease outbreaks, APHA often requires additional veterinary capacity to undertake field-based disease control activities such as farm visits, clinical inspections, examinations and sampling. We recognise the invaluable local knowledge and expertise held by veterinary practices across Scotland and would like to work with practices to strengthen Scotland's ability to respond quickly and effectively when outbreaks occur.
We intend to invite interested practices to join a framework that would allow APHA to call upon veterinary resource within your local area when additional support is needed.
Before designing this framework, we are interested to hear from vet practices in Scotland about how you think we can best work together.  We are inviting you to:
1. Submit written feedback to us by Fri 16th October. 
2. Join one of our engagement sessions (via Microsoft Teams), during which we will present our draft plans for the framework. The time has yet to be agreed, but we propose either 7pm Wed 28th Oct or 12:30 pm Fri 30th Oct allowing you to engage with us over lunch or after practice hours. If you wish to attend, please let us know which time works best for you.
Below, we provide further information regarding the services, and describe the areas on which we are keen to hear your thoughts about how we can best work together.
Training and Support
Any vets deployed through this arrangement will receive comprehensive training before undertaking outbreak work. Practices can decide which members of their team receive training and make themselves available for deployment; there is no requirement for all vets within a practice to participate.
APHA will provide disease-specific training and ongoing support. Deployed vets will be briefed before each assignment and supported by experienced APHA colleagues throughout the process. Practice principals and senior vets will not be expected to supervise these visits or provide the training themselves.
APHA will reimburse participating vets for the time spent completing the required training.
Flexible Participation
The framework will operate on a best endeavours basis, recognising that private veterinary work remains your priority and that staffing availability can vary significantly between practices.
While we hope practices will support disease control activities wherever possible, there is no obligation to release staff when operational pressures make this difficult. Participation in the framework does not guarantee deployment, nor does it commit practices to providing resource on every occasion.
When additional veterinary support is required, APHA will contact practices within the relevant geographical area to determine availability and arrange deployment.
Contract and Payment
We are open to considering a range of pricing models to provide these services.  For example: (1) practices could submit pricing to us, we would then award work to practices that represent the best value for money for a specific requirement; (2) we could use the OV19(S) hourly rates; or (3) you could propose other models for our consideration.
Travel and Expenses
Deployed vets will be required to hold a valid UK driving licence and have access to a practice or personal vehicle. We propose that travel  and subsistence expenses will be reimbursed in line with APHA's published rates.
Working Together to Protect Scottish Livestock
Scotland's geography presents unique challenges for animal health and disease control. The remote nature of many farming communities means that local veterinary practices play a vital role in protecting livestock health and supporting farmers.
By working together, APHA and private veterinary practices can strengthen Scotland's disease response capability, helping to safeguard animal health, protect rural livelihoods, and support Scottish farming communities when they need it most.
We hope you will consider joining this important initiative.
If your practice would like to learn more, please contact Tom Redfearn, tom.redfearn@defra.gov.uk, provide feedback regarding how we can best work together, and join one of our online information sessions.
NOTE ON VALUE: a £ 1mn contract value is advertised to allow for a large disease outbreak that would require significant resources to manage.  We however expect to spend in the region of £25,000 per year.

title: Pan London Substance Use Programme - London Inpatient Detoxification and Stabilisation (IPD)
description:
The City of London Corporation (the  Contracting Authority ), as the Lead Commissioner, and Accountable Body, is seeking to commission Provider organisations with demonstrable experience in delivering complex health and social care services to deliver Inpatient Detoxification and Stabilisation (IPD) beds. This model will support both London residents and individuals who are sleeping rough or at risk of sleeping rough.
Building on the existing Pan-London Substance Misuse Programme, the Provider/s will help realise the City’s ambition to:
•	Establish long-term, sustainable, and geographically dispersed IPD provision that effectively meets diverse and complex client needs; and
•	Deliver equitable, pan London access to IPD beds for all London Local Authorities.
This initiative represents a significant opportunity to collaborate with partners across London to transform the delivery model for Inpatient Detoxification and Stabilisation (IPD) service. The aim is to create accessible, inclusive and responsive IPD delivery that supports health inclusion groups and contributes meaningfully to reducing health inequalities across the capital. The IPD provision will deliver a broad range of care to meet diverse and complex client needs.
A key feature of the IPD service will be the strategic distribution of IPD bedspaces to support equitable access with a particular emphasis on increasing availability within London and surrounding region of M25
The model will encompass:
•	Specialist inpatient medically assisted withdrawal beds
•	Residential medically assisted withdrawal beds.
To provide the required stability and guaranteed access, block booking of a proportion of IPD bed capacity will be essential.[JG3.1]
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention-to-award notice under the Competitive  Process for the purposes of Regulation 11 (9) of the PSR  . The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 as amended by Regulation 28 of the Procurement Act 2023 ( Consequential and Other Amendments) Regulations 2025.   
The publication of this notice marks the start of the 8 working day mandatory standstill period. which will be introduced the day after this notice is published. Written representations by providers must be made to decision makers before midnight on the 6th October 2026 . The contract has not yet formally been awarded. This notice serves as an intention to award to the chosen provider under the Competitive Process of the PSR.
Approval has been obtained in accordance with the Contracting Authority's own internal governance to award the contract to the chosen provider via the Competitive Process of the PSR.
The decision-makers reasons for selecting the chosen provider were identified via a full competitive tender process of the PSR through assessing the bidders’ responses to the Technical/Responsible Procurement key criteria which was set out on the ITT documentation. Following moderation of bids, the chosen provider achieved the highest overall score. 
In accordance with Regulation 21 of the PSR, any potential conflicts of interest have been considered, there are no conflicts of interest to declare.  Where any conflicts of interest may arise during the contract the Contracting Authority will manage any conflicts in accordance with the Contracting Authority's own internal governance.

title: Strategic Partnership Framework for Commissioning of Children's Services
description:
The Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement in respect of a potential future procurement to establish up to three Strategic Partnership Frameworks for the commissioning of Children's Services.
These frameworks would aim to support the development and delivery of high-quality, inclusive and outcomes-focused services for children and young people.
At this stage, the proposed approach, structure and scope of the Frameworks are indicative only and subject to change following market feedback.
The Council is considering a model comprising three service clusters, with initial indicative annual values as follows:
Cluster 1: approximately £56,142,500 per annum (exclusive of VAT)
Cluster 2: approximately £18,050,000 per annum (exclusive of VAT)
Cluster 3: approximately £5,865,000 per annum (exclusive of VAT)
This equates to a combined indicative annual value of approximately £80,057,500, and a potential total value of up to £800,575,000 (exclusive of VAT) over an anticipated maximum term of up to 10 years.
This notice is issued for information and engagement purposes only and does not constitute a call for competition. The Council is seeking feedback from the market to help inform its future commissioning strategy and procurement approach.
The Cluster 3 market engagement event will be held on 7 May, 11:00-12:00 via Microsoft Teams.
The session will provide an overview of the proposed scope for Cluster 3 and will cover the following indicative Lots:
Lot 1 - Complex Health Needs
Including medical and mental health services
Lot 2 - Care and Personal Support
Day-to-day support provided in the home and community
Lot 3 - Behavioural Support
Support to manage and reduce behaviours that challenge
Lot 4 - Short Breaks
Wraparound support, day services and overnight respite
Lot 5 - Emergency / Crisis Support
Rapid response provision to support crisis situations
Lot 6 - Therapeutic Support Services
Psychological, emotional and therapeutic interventions
Lot 7 - Specialist Assessment Service
Multi-disciplinary and specialist assessment provision
Suppliers interested in attending are requested to complete and return the following form:
Strategic Partnership Framework for the Commissioning of Children's Services - Fill in form via link:

Liverpool City Council is preparing to commission a new Strategic Partnership Framework for Children's Services, which includes Children's Social Care Services (Cluster 1).
The framework will provide a continuum of care and accommodation, supporting children and young people from fostering and residential care through to independence. Its purpose is to ensure that future provision maximises independence, choice and control, best value, and long‑term sustainability within the local care market.
This procurement will be undertaken in line with the requirements of the Procurement Act 2023.
We are inviting providers to attend a Market Engagement Event, where we will outline our commissioning intentions, proposed lot structure, and anticipated procurement approach. This session will also provide an opportunity for providers to share early feedback and help shape the final specification and framework design.
The proposed indicative Lots are:

title: Feasibility assessment of bioclimate vulnerability approaches for priority marine migratory species in the Caribbean and Pacific UK Overseas Territories
description:
Project Aims
To assess the feasibility of applying bioclimate vulnerability assessment approaches to priority marine migratory species within the Caribbean UK Overseas Territories and the Pitcairn Islands. Building on previous work undertaken for JNCC, the study will evaluate the suitability of the proposed bioclimate vulnerability approach, consider relevant alternative approaches where appropriate, and determine whether sufficient evidence, data and expertise exist to support future implementation.
4.	Project Background
Climate change is increasingly affecting marine migratory species through changes in sea temperature, ocean productivity, habitat availability, ocean circulation patterns, species interactions and the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events (IPCC, 2022; Martay et al., 2023). These pressures may alter species distributions, abundance, migration routes and ecological relationships, with potentially significant consequences for biodiversity, ecosystem services and economies across the Caribbean Overseas Territories (OTs) and the Pitcairn Islands (IPCC, 2022; Martay et al., 2023). Evidence from marine vertebrates indicates that climate-driven changes in ocean conditions can alter migration timing, migratory routes, species distributions and access to suitable feeding and breeding habitats through changes in environmental conditions and prey availability (Kuletz et al., 2024). However, considerable uncertainty remains regarding how priority marine migratory species are likely to respond to future climate conditions and what these changes may mean for conservation and management (Martay et al., 2023).
Previous JNCC work has reviewed available evidence on climate impacts affecting marine migratory species and identified a suite of priority species for further investigation. This work also highlighted the potential application of bioclimate vulnerability assessment approaches, which seek to combine information on species ecology, environmental change and climate pressures to better understand species vulnerability under future climate scenarios. However, uncertainty remains regarding the suitability of these approaches for the priority species and Territories, the data required to support their application, and whether resulting outputs would be sufficiently robust to inform management and decision-making.
Previous work undertaken for St Helena, by Strathclyde University, explored ecosystem-based bioclimate vulnerability assessment approaches to project biomass declines in the marine protected area food web due to climate change (Olher et al., 2026). This study should consider the extent to which this and similar approaches may be applicable to priority species within the Caribbean Overseas Territories and Pitcairn.
While bioclimate vulnerability assessments represent a promising approach, a range of alternative methods of assessing ecological/biological impacts of climate change may also be relevant. These vary in their assumptions, data requirements, technical complexity, resource needs and intended applications. It is therefore important to understand whether the proposed bioclimate vulnerability approach represents the most appropriate option for the priority species and Territories, and whether sufficient evidence exists to support its implementation. However, the primary purpose of this study is to assess the feasibility of applying a suitable bioclimate vulnerability approach to priority marine migratory species, and new geographies, rather than to undertake a comprehensive review of assessment methodologies. Consideration of alternative approaches should therefore be targeted and proportionate, focusing on whether an alternative method would offer a materially stronger basis for future implementation.
The next phase of work is therefore to undertake a feasibility assessment that builds on previous work while critically evaluating the suitability of the proposed approach in comparison with other relevant assessment methods. This will include reviewing methodological requirements, assessing the availability and suitability of biological, ecological, environmental and climate datasets, identifying key evidence gaps and technical constraints, and determining the level of confidence that could be achieved through future assessments.
The study will provide an evidence-based assessment of the most appropriate approach or approaches for application to priority marine migratory species, what analyses could be undertaken using currently available information, and what additional data, expertise or investment would be required to support future implementation. The findings will inform future implementation decisions and provide a roadmap for any subsequent climate vulnerability or bioclimate vulnerability assessment programme, supporting climate adaptation, marine conservation and environmental decision-making across the Caribbean Overseas Territories and the Pitcairn Islands.
5.	Project Objectives
To meet the overall aims of this project (Section 2), the objectives are: 
Objective 1
Review the proposed bioclimate vulnerability assessment approach and assess its suitability for application to priority marine migratory species within the Caribbean Overseas Territories and the Pitcairn Islands.
Objective 2
Compare the proposed approach against a limited number of relevant alternative assessment approaches and identify the most appropriate option(s) for future implementation.
Objective 3
Assess the feasibility of implementing the recommended approach for a priority list of marine migratory species supplied by JNCC.
Objective 4
Identify key evidence gaps, data limitations, uncertainties and resource requirements associated with future implementation.
Objective 5
Develop recommendations and an implementation roadmap for any future climate vulnerability or bioclimate vulnerability assessment programme.

title: For the provision of a Higher Education Institution to deliver the Step Up to Social Work Programme for the East Midlands Regional Partnership	 (Cohorts 10 and 11)
description:
Derby City Council (the Council) is undertaking this procurement to establish a contract for the provision of a single Higher Education Institution to deliver the Step Up to Social Work Programme for the East Midlands Regional Partnership (EMRP) for up to two cohorts (Cohorts 10 and 11) beginning March 2027. We will be procuring this contract for all Authorities/Bodies in the EMPR, which currently consists of: 
•	Derby City Council - Lead Authority 
•	Northamptonshire Children's Trust
•	Nottinghamshire County Council 
•	Nottingham City Council
•	Leicester City Council
•	Leicestershire County Council
•	Derbyshire County Council
•	Lincolnshire County Council
•	Rutland County Council
The Step up to Social Work programme is funded by the Department for Education (DfE) with the intention of raising the standard of social workers who work in children's statutory services. 
The programme recruits high calibre candidates who have a 2:2 degree and who already have experience of working with vulnerable children, young people or adults who want to train as social workers. 
The procurement process adopted by the Council is based on the 'Open' tendering procedure as detailed in the Procurement Act 2023 (the "Act") and the Procurement Regulations 2024 (the "Regulations") but with the added flexibility offered by Light Touch Regime (Section 9 and Schedule 1 of the Procurement Regulations 2024) and any subsequent amendment or re-enactment thereof.
Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) is underway in several areas across the country, including the East Midlands, and this may result in changes to council structures, service delivery and responsibilities, and geographical coverage during the life of the contract. 
For this contract it is anticipated that the effects of LGR will not lead to an increased service demand or the need to extend provision to new areas or client groups. However, it may be necessary to novate the contract to a new entity (that may replace Derby City Council) in future.
The Council did not undertake any preliminary market engagement in advance of this procurement. This decision was taken following an internal assessment of the market, which concluded that the Council has sufficient knowledge of supplier capability, service delivery models, and pricing structures based on recent procurements of a similar nature.
The Council has procured similar services twice within the last ten years, and officers have engaged with market intelligence, benchmarking data, and lessons learned from contract management to inform the service specification and procurement strategy. Insight gained through ongoing supplier performance monitoring and user feedback has enabled the Council to refine its approach without the need for further engagement at the pre-procurement stage.
To ensure a fair and competitive process, the Council has taken care to avoid including bespoke or overly prescriptive requirements that could favour incumbents or any particular delivery model. 
All potential suppliers are encouraged to raise questions via the clarification process during the tender period should they require further detail or context regarding any aspect of the specification or commercial arrangements.
The Council is committed to ensuring a transparent and level playing field and has taken steps to ensure that no supplier is unfairly advantaged or disadvantaged by the decision not to conduct formal market engagement.

The deadline for returns is 10.00am on Friday 23rd October 2026.

title: Grounds Maintenance Contract
description:
TOTNES TOWN COUNCIL 
GROUNDS MAINTENANCE SPECIFICATION 2027/28 
The contract is for Grounds Maintenance at Totnes Cemetery and Castle Meadow. 
Maintenance shall include the removal from the site of all cuttings which are to be disposed of legally. 
Hedge and shrub cutting must comply with seasonal restrictions relating to bird nesting. 
Grass cutting will include maintaining the grass and any other growth around headstones /monuments/ 
benches / boundaries to the same height as the surrounding grass. Grass to be cut up to boundary fences 
or walls. 
The Contractor will comply with all relevant Health and Safety legislation in respect of both the 
Contractor's employees and the general public. Suitable and sufficient risk assessments on all work 
processes must be provided. Machinery and equipment used must be subject to the necessary servicing 
and safety inspections. 
The Contractor will give consideration to the area of work and noise levels when funerals are in progress 
and not start before 0800 hours given the proximity of residential properties. 
The Contractor must hold adequate and current Public Liability Insurance. 
The Contractor must comply with the Council's policy banning any use of Glyphosate on Town Council 
owned land. 
Totnes Cemetery 
The Cemetery is shown on the enclosed map A and consists of approximately 7.01 acres.  
Grass cutting - 17 cuts per annum, as close to the ground as practicably possible, on the following 
frequency - - - - - 
1 cut in January or February (prior to wild flower blooming) 
1 cut in March (before Easter or Mothering Sunday if Easter is in April)  
2 cuts per month April to September 
1 cut per month October and November 
1 cut in December by the 15th of the month 
Grass cutting to take place only on the perimeter of wild areas on the circle (plus paths through the 
middle) and on the island containing the Chapel to one mower width. 
Raised graves - growth on raised graves to be kept below 30cm as part of the monthly grass cutting 
schedule. 
Garden of Rest - area to be cut/strimmed and grass blown off the memorial stones/tablets. 
Hedge cutting - 1 cut per annum. To be cut on internal sides and tops only. 
Shrubs and bushes (see plan provided) - to be trimmed/cut back tight once a year between September
November to form rounded shapes and to remove the year's growth. 
Roadside dry stone wall bank - to be kept trimmed and tidy on top and both sides. Any shrubs or brambles 
on the bank or overhanging the wall to be kept trimmed and cleared so as not to cause an obstruction to 
the public footpath. 
Pathways - to be kept clear of any up growing and overhanging vegetation. Weeds to be strimmed. All 
debris to be blown off paths. 
Itemised quote requested for annual maintenance of the Wild Areas on the circle and the Chapel - to be 
cut back annually in late summer, cuttings left for up to two weeks for seed to drop and then cleared.  
Winter leaves and debris from trees to be cleared before Easter and before Christmas. 
Castle Meadow  
Castle Meadow is shown on the enclosed map B and the hedge runs along Collins Road and Lower Collins 
Road as highlighted in pink. 
Hedge cutting - 1 cut per annum. To be cut on both sides and on top. In the area enclosed by allotments 
only outside to be cut. 
Grass Cutting -  2 cuts per annum of Castle Meadow to be carried out in June and October, with the 
exception of the trial meadow area, to be marked by stakes and roped off prior to these cuts.  
Term of contract 
The initial contract will be for two years from 1st April 2027 to 31st March 2029.  
If both parties are satisfied with the conduct of the contract during the first two years', the contract will 
continue into subsequent years with a review after five years. 
The Contractor is expected to provide and pay for their own tools, machinery, equipment, materials, 
transport and support staff. 
Either party shall have the right at any time to terminate this contract by giving not less than 3 months' 
notice in writing to the other party. 
Contract monitoring 
The contractor will be required to co-operate in meeting with the Town Council's appointed officer to 
review progress with the contract, and to promptly address any failure in service identified at those 
meetings. Contract monitoring meetings will be held as required either on site at Totnes Cemetery or in 
the Town Council offices. 
Pricing and payment 
The agreed cost of the contract, together with VAT (if applicable), will be paid in equal monthly payments 
in arrears by the 30th day of the month immediately following the month in which the Services have been 
performed.

title: RCC-1655 DESIGN, BUILD AND INSTALLATION OF THE 'DIGGING RUTLAND GALLERY FROM STONE AGE TO ANGLO SAXON' FOR THE RUTLAND COUNTY MUSEUM
description:
Rutland County Council ("the Council") is seeking proposals from suitably qualified and experienced suppliers to design, build, and install a new permanent gallery at Rutland Museum. The gallery will interpret Rutland's history from the Stone Age to the Anglo?Saxon period, with a feature Roman section dedicated to the nationally significant Ketton Roman Mosaic.
The successful supplier must deliver an end?to?end service incorporating creative design, technical development, fabrication, installation, and commissioning, resulting in an
accessible, engaging, and durable visitor environment.
The expected timeframe for this project is 6 to 7 months from design, build and installation. The Gallery needs to open in January 2027.
This Gallery will constitute the second instalment of the "Digging Rutland" exhibition series. The first gallery, currently in development, will focus on the Mid Jurassic period and will showcase the recently discovered Rutland Ichthyosaur. 
The Stone Age to Anglo?Saxon Gallery will occupy an approximate footprint of 195 m² within which an area of approximately 10m x 6m will be allocated to a new digital
interpretation experience exploring the Roman history of Rutland. The centrepiece of this digital offer will be a high?quality digital representation of the Ketton Roman Mosaic.
Both galleries form part of the wider transformation of Rutland County Museum project. This capital development programme includes the creation of a new multi?use space, a redesigned public entrance, café and retail area, and a dedicated gallery showcasing the Rutland Ichthyosaur. The Gallery described within this tender specification will form the second permanent gallery, presenting a chronological narrative from the Stone Age
through to the Anglo?Saxon period. A list of the artefacts intended for inclusion within this Gallery is provided in Appendix A(i) & (ii) of this Specification.
Please note that this gallery is part of Rutland County Council's Levelling Up funds and is therefore subject to the associated brand guidelines of acknowledging UK Government for these funds. Brand guidelines will be provided to the successful bidder.
Further information about the service requirements can be obtained in the tender documentation within this tender pack.
Contract Value
The budget for this contract is £450,000.00 excluding VAT in total. Please note: the Council reserves the right to reject any submissions that are over budget without further evaluation.
Contract Type (Terms)
The Contract Agreement for this project shall be JCT Design & Build Contract 2024 (DB2024).

Open procedure in accordance with Procurement Act 2023.

title: VCSE Prevention and Infrastructure Development 2027/28
description:
East Riding of Yorkshire Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement in relation to a proposed one-year VCSE Prevention plus 6 month extension and Infrastructure Development Contract commencing on 1 April 2027.
The proposed arrangements will maintain continuity of essential VCSE support while enabling the Council and the sector to develop and test longer-term approaches to collaborative working, prevention and investment across the East Riding.
The Council is currently considering a coordinated service with three connected requirements:
Prevention and resilience grant administration:
Administering relevant funding under the proposed VCSE Prevention and Investment Framework. The delivery of resilience and community coordination activity for residents, alongside grant decision-making process, grant payments, due diligence checks, performance monitoring, reporting and gathering intelligence.
VCSE infrastructure and organisational development:
Support offer for VCSE organisations, organisational development, governance support, volunteering, leadership and training, funding advice, and strategic sector representation.
Independent VCSE Participatory Research:
An independent piece of work focused on listening to and understanding the sector and working with it to shape what a future East Riding VCSE model could look like from April 2028 onwards.
A separately funded Inclusion Health function is also currently delivered through the existing contract. The Council is seeking views on whether this should sit alongside the infrastructure requirement or be separately priced as an additional requirement.
The Council is seeking views on the proposed scope, deliverability, market capacity, indicative costs and procurement structure, including the appropriate separation and boundaries between the requirements.
The Council also wishes to understand how smaller, specialist and locality-based VCSE organisations could participate meaningfully in delivery and governance, and how the proposed arrangement could reflect the geographical size and diversity of the East Riding.
The one-year arrangements are intended to maintain continuity while informing the Council’s longer-term commissioning approach. Participation in the engagement process or appointment to any transitional requirement will not guarantee the award of future contracts.
The proposed scope, budget, contract value, procurement structure and timetable remain indicative and may change following preliminary market engagement and the Council’s internal financial, legal, procurement and governance approvals. This notice does not constitute a call for competition or a commitment by the Council to proceed with the procurement.

title: BCU-ITT-63595 - WREXHAM MAELOR HOSPITAL PHARMACY BOILER REPLACEMENT
description:
Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board requires a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake the replacement of the existing heating plant serving the Pharmacy Department at Wrexham Maelor Hospital. The project involves the removal of three existing Remeha Gas 210 ECO natural gas boilers and the installation of three new Remeha Gas 210 Ace 120/4 sectional boilers within the Pharmacy Plantroom located on the second floor of the hospital. 
The works comprise a turnkey mechanical and electrical installation project and will include the phased removal and replacement of the existing boilers, modification and reconnection of associated pipework and services, integration with the existing Building Management System (BMS), alterations to electrical supplies where required, testing and commissioning, production of record drawings and operation and maintenance manuals, and all associated builders' works necessary to complete the installation. The successful contractor will also be responsible for fulfilling the role of Principal Contractor under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 and for preparing and implementing the Construction Phase Plan. 
The replacement works will be undertaken within a live hospital environment and must be carefully planned to maintain continuity of service to the Pharmacy Department. The installation will be carried out on a phased basis to ensure that two of the three boilers remain operational at all times, allowing the heating system to continue functioning throughout the duration of the project. Any temporary interruptions to services must be agreed in advance with the Health Board and undertaken in accordance with site operational requirements. 
The contractor will be expected to coordinate all aspects of the works, including project management, health and safety compliance, site supervision, logistics, transportation of materials, commissioning activities, waste disposal, and stakeholder engagement. Particular consideration will be required for working within a healthcare environment, managing access restrictions, maintaining service resilience, and ensuring compliance with relevant industry standards, Health Technical Memoranda (HTMs), gas safety regulations, and all applicable statutory requirements.

title: Security Operation Centre
description:
Bournemouth University ("BU" or the "University") is exploring options for the provision of a co-managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) service to enhance and future-proof its cyber security operations capability. The University is seeking market feedback from experienced Managed Security Service Providers to better understand available service models, implementation approaches, commercial arrangements and indicative costs.
BU has invested significantly in its internal cyber security capability and Microsoft security technologies, including Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, Entra ID Protection, Security Copilot and related services. The University is now considering how external specialist support could complement its in-house team through a co-managed SOC operating model.
The key objectives of a future service are expected to include:
- Enhancing monitoring, detection and response capabilities through either 24/7 or out-of-hours SOC coverage.
- Improving threat detection, triage, false-positive reduction and incident response effectiveness.
- Providing additional specialist expertise, operational resilience and surge capacity during major incidents or periods of heightened risk.
- Maintaining and continuously improving detection rules, playbooks, automation and security monitoring capabilities.
- Leveraging threat intelligence, sector insight, automation and AI-enabled capabilities to strengthen cyber resilience and operational effectiveness.
- Establishing a robust governance, reporting and service management framework with clear responsibilities between BU and the supplier.
- Maximising the value of the University's existing Microsoft security investments while minimising the need for additional tooling wherever appropriate.
The University wishes to understand how the market can support these objectives, together with the costs, benefits, risks and implementation considerations associated with different service models. Supplier feedback received through this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise will help inform the University's future requirements, budget planning and procurement strategy.

NB - This procurement is being undertaken as a below-threshold Request for Quotation (RFQ) under the Procurement Act 2023. As the estimated contract value is below the applicable procurement threshold, it is not subject to the full regulated procurement procedures that apply to above-threshold procurements. The Act requires a proportionate approach to below-threshold procurement and provides contracting authorities with greater flexibility in determining an appropriate route to market. 
In accordance with this approach, the RFQ will be conducted on an invitation-only basis, with quotations being sought from a selected number of suppliers assessed as capable of delivering the requirement. This enables meaningful competition whilst maintaining a proportionate process aligned to the value, complexity and risk profile of the contract. Similar approaches are reflected within procurement guidance and procurement policies developed in response to the Procurement Act 2023. 
For completeness, the Procurement Act 2023 does not require contracting authorities to run an open tender process for below-threshold procurements. In particular:
•	Part 6 of the Act establishes a separate regime for below-threshold contracts, recognising that fewer obligations apply than for covered procurements. 
•	Section 85 sets out requirements where a contracting authority chooses to invite tenders for a regulated below-threshold contract but does not mandate that the opportunity must be advertised openly to all suppliers. 
•	The Act allows contracting authorities to take a proportionate approach to supplier selection and competition for below-threshold opportunities, provided that transparency requirements applicable to the procurement are met.

title: Isles of Scilly Transport - Inter-Island Commuter Passenger Boat Services
description:
The Council of the Isles of Scilly is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced and appropriately licensed passenger boat operator to provide a reliable Inter-Island Commuter Passenger Boat Service connecting St Martin's and St Agnes with St Mary's.
The service provides an essential lifeline between the islands and is required to support a range of Council-facilitated and concessionary travel requirements, particularly during the winter period when the frequency and availability of normal commercial inter-island services is reduced. The journeys supported through the service principally provide for:
•	Early Years transport;
•	Home-to-School Transport;
•	Children and Young People (C&YP) travel, principally to enable participation in clubs and organised activities;
•	Adult Social Care travel;
•	Discretionary Concessionary Fares supported by the Council; and
•	Employment-related travel, particularly for teachers and school support staff where inter-island transport is necessary to enable attendance at work.
The service also provides broader community connectivity, enabling residents to access essential services and facilities on St Mary's. Other passenger journeys outside the Council-supported service requirements may continue to be provided by operators on a commercial basis.
The Department for Transport (DfT) has provided short-term emergency funding to support the service during the 2026/27 winter period. This funding is intended to provide an interim solution for this winter only while the Council considers the longer-term requirements for sustainable inter-island connectivity.
The Contract(s) will therefore also provide an important opportunity for the Council to gather information on passenger demand, journey patterns, service reliability, operating costs and service utilisation. This evidence will help the Council understand how the revised service is being used and inform consideration of a more permanent and sustainable solution for future years.
The principal subsidised Winter Service Period is expected to run from October 2026 to 31 March 2027.
From 1 April 2027, the normal commercial summer inter-island timetable is expected to resume, and the wider winter service subsidy will cease. However, the Contract will provide for a limited Academic Year Extension Period from April to July 2027, covering only the services required to support the continuation of Early Years, Home-to-School, and associated education employment travel until the end of the academic year. The journeys and service requirements applicable during this extension period are set out in Schedule 1 - Service Specification.
The Council is therefore seeking a proportionate, flexible, reliable and dependable service which recognises the essential lifeline function of inter-island connectivity, the range of Council-supported passenger requirements and the particular commercial challenges associated with maintaining these connections during the winter period. The Contract is intended both to maintain these essential journeys in the short term and to provide the operational evidence required to inform the Council's approach to their longer-term provision.

title: UK Space Agency - Operational Support to the International Charter: Space and Major Disasters
description:
The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. 
Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/
Unlike many space faring nations in the Charter, the UK Government does not own or operate its own national EO satellite system assets. The UK Government therefore fulfils its Charter commitments through partnership with the UK EO commercial sector. This procurement seeks to maintain and strengthen that model by securing operational support from an organisation with UK licensed and operated EO satellite data assets that can be contributed to Charter activations. 
The continued participation of UK EO commercial satellite operators in the Charter delivers both public benefit and strategic value by showcasing sovereign EO capabilities, supporting international disaster response and demonstrating operational utility of UK-developed EO missions.

Lincolnshire Housing Partnership (LHP) is a greater Lincolnshire based housing association created in April 2018.  LHP is a charity regulated as a Community Benefit Society and a not for profit housing provider regulated by the Regulator for Social Housing. 
LHP’s Data and Technology Strategy 2026–2029 sets out LHP’s vision to become a digitally confident, data-driven housing association by March 2029, supported by a sequenced three-year roadmap structured around three phases: Foundations (Year 1, 2026/27), Transformation (Year 2, 2027/28), and Innovation (Year 3, 2028/29).
The strategy has one overriding objective: to give LHP the technology and data foundations it needs to achieve and sustain a C1 Consumer Standard grading, with a target of March 2027. The most important implication is that LHP needs a modern, integrated housing and repairs platform, supported by a clear integration architecture and a stronger data foundation.
	Core Systems — a modern, integrated core housing and repairs platform at the heart of operations, supplemented where necessary by specialist capability that is tightly integrated into the target architecture, replacing our Housing Management System alongside a fit-for-purpose finance system and consolidated service charge platform.
	Data Foundation — the Data Warehouse as a single source of truth, with Power BI as the reporting and analytics layer and governance embedded through the Data Stewards.
	Integration Layer — an API-first architecture with a strategic integration partner, removing manual re-keying between core systems, with the integration architecture agreed before any new system is procured.
	Customer & Colleague Experience — a fully AI-enabled CXone contact centre, an enhanced customer portal integrated with the new HMS, and mobile-first field working tools.
Within this roadmap, the HMS/Digital Repairs Options is a priority Year 1 initiative. The decisions taken through this appraisal will shape the future platform architecture, the integration approach, and the sequencing of wider change across the strategy period.
This project is associated with the procurement of a solution for a Housing Management System, Repairs Platform and Dynamic Scheduling tool.

title: London's VRU Boys, Young Men and Future Fathers Support Services
description:
Project Background:
Research commissioned by the Greater London Authority on Understanding the Manosphere (2025) found that many boys and young men are navigating increasing uncertainty around identity, masculinity, purpose and belonging. Evidence suggests that social isolation, loneliness, limited access to trusted adults, and exposure to harmful online content can increase vulnerability to misogynistic and harmful online narratives. At the same time, research highlights that boys and young men are seeking guidance on issues such as relationships, identity, wellbeing and masculinity, often in online spaces that can expose them to harmful or misleading content.
Emerging evidence indicates that strengthening critical thinking, digital literacy and opportunities for open discussion and reflection can help young people to better understand, question and challenge harmful content and online influences. Research also demonstrates the importance of trusted relationships, positive male role models, supportive peer networks and meaningful offline spaces as protective factors that support healthy identity development, resilience, wellbeing and positive relationships. These opportunities can help boys and young men explore identity, belonging, relationships and different experiences and expressions of masculinity in safe and supportive environments.
This evidence sits within a broader context of concern about the impact of online misogyny and harmful online narratives on both boys and young men and on the safety and wellbeing of girls and young women. Research highlights increasing exposure to misogynistic content online, the role of algorithms in amplifying harmful narratives, and the importance of early intervention approaches that build critical thinking, digital literacy, emotional wellbeing and healthy relationship skills. Evidence also highlights the value of creating spaces where boys and young men can explore identity, belonging, relationships and masculinity, reflect on the influences shaping their views, and develop resilience to harmful online content and messaging
In response, the Mayor has launched a programme of activity to challenge harmful online narratives and support boys and young men to develop confidence, resilience and a strong sense of identity. In June 2026, the Mayor warned of the risk of a "lost generation of young men" if the growing influence of harmful online content is left unchecked, announcing a package of interventions to strengthen support for boys and young men at home, in schools and across communities. The Mayor's polling found that only 15% of Londoners believe boys and young men have access to enough positive role models, reinforcing the need for investment in trusted adults, mentoring and positive influences.
The VRU is leading the development of this programme of interventions. Through mentoring, workforce development, support for fathers and carers, and preventative work in education settings, the programme aims to strengthen critical thinking and digital literacy, increase access to positive male role models and trusted adults, support boys and young men to explore identity, belonging, relationships and masculinity, and reduce vulnerability to exploitation, violence and harmful online influences.
Scope of delivery
The programme will be structured into three complementary lots as summarised within this notice.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – FE 08.0283/2026/BCG - Einfluss verschiedener AKR-Prüfzementchargen auf die statistische Verteilung von Dehnungen im Schnellprüfverfahren mit verschiedenen Gesteinskörnun-gen
description: FE 08.0283/2026/BGB - Einfluss verschiedener AKR-Prüfzementchargen auf die statistische Verteilung von Dehnungen im Schnellprüfverfahren mit verschiedenen Gesteinskörnungen Zur Verhinderung einer betonschädigenden Alkali-Kieselsäure-Reaktion (AKR) an Betonfahrbahndecken kommt derzeit eine straßenbauspezifische Gutachterregelung gemäß Allgemeinem Rundschreiben Straßenbau (ARS) Nr. 04/2013 zur Anwendung. Als Voruntersuchungen dienen das Schnellprüfverfahren gemäß TP-Beton-StB 1.1.11 oder der Mörtelschnelltest gemäß TP-Beton-StB 1.1.12. Diese Verfahren ermöglichen eine Überwachung der Gesteinskörnungen, hinsichtlich einer sich ggf. verändernden Alkalireaktivität mit fortschreitendem Abbau im Natursteinbruch oder Kieswerk. Für beide Prüfverfahren war bisher ein einheitlicher AKR-Prüfzement CEM I 32,5 R vorgeschrieben, der durch den Verein Deutscher Zementwerke (VDZ) verwaltet wird. Da dieser Zement seit Ende 2024 in Deutschland nicht mehr lieferbar ist, müssen alle Prüfinstitute zukünftig auf einen vorhandenen CEM I 42,5 R umstellen. Erste Vergleichsversuche am VDZ und an der TU Hamburg/Harburg haben jedoch gezeigt, dass mit dem CEM I 42,5 R im Schnellprüfverfahren andere Ergebnisse erzielt werden, als mit den früheren Lieferchargen des CEM I 32,5 R – die Vergleichbarkeit der Prüfergebnisse ist somit nicht direkt gegeben. Im Forschungsvorhaben soll der Einfluss verschiedener AKR-Prüfzementchargen auf die statistische Verteilung von Dehnungen im Schnellprüfverfahren mit verschiedenen Gesteinskörnungen (AKR-Referenzgesteinskörnung des VDZ sowie Splitte) untersucht werden. Die Erforschung des Einflusses verschiedener AKR-Prüfzementchargen ermöglicht die Identifikation spezifischer Zementeigenschaften, die die Dehnungsentwicklung im Schnellprüfverfahren sowie im Mörtelschnelltest maßgeblich bestimmen. Auf dieser Basis können verbindliche Anforderungskriterien für zukünftige Prüfzement-Chargen definiert werden, um künftig Schwankungen zwischen verschiedenen Chargen zu minimieren.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Neubau eines Pflegeheims und Sanierung/Umbau des Bestandspflegeheims zu Studenten-/ Mitarbeiterwohnen - Leistungen der Technischen Ausrüstung, ALG 4, 5, 6, Leistungsphasen 1-3, 5-9 gemäß §§ 53 ff. HOAI
description: Neubau eines Pflegeheims und Sanierung/Umbau des Bestandspflegeheims zu Studenten-/ Mitarbeiterwohnen - Leistungen der Technischen Ausrüstung, ALG 4, 5, 6, Leistungsphasen 1-3, 5-9 gemäß §§ 53 ff. HOAI Das Kreszentia-Stift ist ein traditionsreiches Wohnstift und Pflegeheim in der Münchner Innenstadt und dient seit 1859 der Betreuung und Pflege älterer Menschen in unterschiedlichen Lebens- und Pflegesituationen. Die bestehende Anlage umfasst mehrere Gebäudeteile unterschiedlichen Alters und weist sowohl vollstationäre Pflegebereiche als auch Angebote des barrierefreien Wohnens sowie ergänzende Nutzungen auf. Die baulichen Strukturen entsprechen in weiten Teilen nicht mehr den heutigen und künftig zu erwartenden Anforderungen an ein modernes Pflege-, Betreuungs- und Wohnkonzept. Insbesondere die Grundrisse, Zimmergrößen, Erschließungswege, technischen Anlagen sowie die energetische und brandschutztechnische Ausstattung erfüllen die aktuellen funktionalen, pflegerischen und rechtlichen Standards nur eingeschränkt. Zudem bestehen erhebliche Einschränkungen hinsichtlich Barrierefreiheit, Wirtschaftlichkeit des Betriebs sowie der langfristigen Anpassungsfähigkeit an sich wandelnde Pflegekonzepte. Vor diesem Hintergrund wurden in den vergangenen Jahren unterschiedliche Varianten zur Weiterentwicklung des Standorts untersucht. Im Ergebnis wurde festgelegt, dass der Neubau des Pflegeheims die zentrale Projektmaßnahme darstellt. Ziel ist die Umsetzung eines zukunftsfähigen Pflege-Betreuungs- und Wohnkonzepts mit insgesamt rund 150 vollstationären Pflegeplätzen, organisiert in überschaubaren Wohngruppen. Die Bestandsgebäude (Haus 2 und Haus 3) sollen einer neuen Nutzung zugeführt und entsprechend baulich angepasst werden. Vorgesehen ist hier insbesondere die Schaffung von Wohnraum für Mitarbeiter und Studenten sowie ggf. eine Kindertagesstätte. Die Planung umfasst neben Sanierungs-, Umbau- und Neubaumaßnahmen auch die Neuordnung der inneren und äußeren Erschließung, die funktionale Verknüpfung der Gebäudeteile sowie die Gestaltung und Nutzung der Freianlagen als Aufenthalts-, Erholungs- und Begegnungsräume für Bewohner, Mitarbeiter und Besucher. Zudem ist Öffnung des Stifts ins Quartier geplant. Es ist beabsichtigt, folgende Leistungen zu beauftragen: Technische Ausrüstung, ALG 4, 5 und 6, gem. §§ 53 ff. HOAI, LP 1-3, 5-9 Zunächst werden in der 1. Beauftragungsstufe die Leistungsphasen 1-2 gemäß HOAI beauftragt. Die weiteren Leistungsphasen werden stufenweise abgerufen. Ein Rechtsanspruch auf Gesamtbeauftragung besteht nicht.

description: Das AKK plant auf dem Gelände Bleickenallee 38 in Hamburg Altona Umbaumaßnahmen im Gebäude "Reha Aufstockung" um drei weitere Geschosse. Das Bestandsgebäude ist teilunterkellert, im Untergeschoss befinden sich Technikräume und Umkleiden, das Erdgeschoss wird weiterhin als Rehabilitationseinrichtung genutzt. Das Reha-Gebäude wird gemäß § 2 HBauO in die Gebäudeklasse 5 eingestuft. Im 1. Obergeschoss der Aufstockung wird eine teilstationäre Tagesklinik untergebracht, die als Ersatzfläche für die Baufeldfreimachung des Ersatzneubaus I-Haus dient. Die Station beinhaltet überwiegend Untersuchungsräume für diagnostische Zwecke sowie Liegeräume, in denen Patienten Infusionen erhalten. Dienende Räume wie Stützpunkt, Arbeits- und Lagerräume, Sanitärräume und Verteilküche ergänzen das Raumangebot. Die dreigeschossige Aufstockung wird in Stahlbetonbauweise errichtet, bestehend aus tragenden Außenwänden sowie tragenden Wänden und Stützen im Gebäudeinnern. Die Decken werden aus Fertigteilelementen in Verbundbauweise als Spannbeton-Hohlplattendecken mit deckengleichen Verbundträgern geplant. Die Außenwände erhalten ein WDVS-System mit Riemchenverkleidung. Die Aufstockung erhält ein extensiv begrüntes Flachdach mit Photovoltaikmodulen. Die Baumaßnahme soll unter Aufrechterhaltung des laufenden Krankenhausbetriebes erfolgen. Die Zufahrt zur Baustelle erfolgt über die Lisztstraße; sämtliche Zuwege zu Ein- und Ausgängen sowie Feuerwehr- und Rettungswagenzufahrten sind in jedem Fall freizuhalten. Die Abriss- und Anschlussarbeiten müssen mit Rücksicht darauf durchgeführt werden.

Las características técnicas de los trabajos, con la ejecución de sondeos de investigación, geofísica, así como el empleo de softwares específicos de modelación numérica, junto con la dispersión geográfica y la carga de trabajo de campo que conlleva, así como el amplio rango de disciplinas implicadas en las distintas tareas, hacen que sea inviable acometerlos únicamente con los medios humanos y materiales de la Dirección General del Agua (DGA) y organismos de cuenca, siendo por lo tanto necesario recurrir a la contratación de apoyo externo para la realización de estos servicios.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Generalsanierung Ulrich-von-Dürrmenz-Schule Mühlacker, ELT
description: Die Ulrich-von-Dürrmenz-Schule in Mühlacker bereitet sich auf eine umfassende Neuausrichtung vor, um den Anforderungen der kommenden Jahrzehnte gerecht zu werden. Als zentraler Bildungs- und Lebensraum im Stadtteil Dürrmenz muss die Schule auf den tiefgreifenden Wandel in der Bildungslandschaft und veränderte ge-sellschaftliche Rahmenbedingungen reagieren. Ursprünglich als kombinierte Grund- und Hauptschule dimensio-niert, wird der Komplex heute als reine Grundschule geführt. Um den zukünftigen Anforderungen an eine zeit-gemäße Pädagogik, Chancengleichheit und die Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf gerecht zu werden, soll der Standort planerisch vollständig neu konzipiert werden: Ziel ist die Entwicklung zu einer modernen, durchgehend vierzügigen Grundschule mit einem voll integrierten Ganztagsbetrieb. Dieser Schritt sichert langfristig eine hoch-wertige Lernumgebung und schafft die räumlichen Voraussetzungen für moderne, rhythmisierte Bildungsange-bote. Die Ulrich von Dürrmenz Schule in Mühlacker besteht aus einem heterogenen Gebäudekomplex, der zwei bau-lich völlig unterschiedliche Epochen vereint: dem historischen Altbau aus dem Jahr ca. 1885 und einem Erweite-rungsbau inklusive Zwischenbau aus dem Jahr 1968. Beide Gebäudeteile sind baulich, energetisch und technisch stark in die Jahre gekommen. Die Technische Gebäu-deausrüstung (TGA) sowie die Elektrotechnik (ELT) sind veraltet und durch punktuelle Teilsanierungen der ver-gangenen Jahrzehnte fragmentiert. Zudem weisen die Bestandsgebäude erhebliche Barrieren auf. Die starren Raumstrukturen entsprechen weder den Anforderungen an einen modernen, inklusiven Unterricht noch den logistischen Abläufen eines zeitgemä-ßen Schul- und Ganztagesbetriebs. Die bestehenden Freianlagen der Ulrich-von-Dürrmenz-Schule weisen derzeit nur eine eingeschränkte Nut-zungs- und Aufenthaltsqualität auf. Der Schulhof präsentiert sich überwiegend als große, zusammenhängende und asphaltierte Fläche mit geringem gestalterischem Differenzierungsgrad. Altersgerechte Spiel-, Bewegungs- und Aufenthaltsbereiche für die unterschiedlichen Nutzergruppen sind nur in begrenztem Umfang vorhanden. Die Ausstattung der Außenanlagen beschränkt sich im Wesentlichen auf einzelne Sitzbänke entlang der Randbe-reiche sowie die vorhandenen, überdachten Pausengänge im Bereich der Gebäudezugänge. Darüber hinaus be-stehen bauliche Mängel in den Freianlagen. Insbesondere die Außentreppe an der Nordseite ist infolge von Ge-ländesetzungen in ihrer Verkehrssicherheit beeinträchtigt und kann nicht mehr uneingeschränkt genutzt wer-den. Zur Verbesserung des Komforts sind darüber hinaus mehrere überdachte Unterstellmöglichkeiten mit inte-grierten Sitzgelegenheiten als Sonnen- und Regenschutz zu schaffen sein. Weitere Informationen entnehmen Sie der Maßnahmenbeschreibung des Verfahrensleitfadens.

title: Belgium – Military research and technology – Service Framework Contract for the provision of “Strategic Analysis of the European Defence Technology Industrial Base (EDTIB) ”
description: The objective of this framework contract is to assist EDA in implementing its Core Task 5, as defined in the EDA’s Long term review 2024. The EDA’s Core Task 5 consists in consolidating and promoting EU Member States’ Ministries of Defence (MoD) common interest towards EU wider policies, both civilian and defence related. EDA contributes to promoting a shared understanding of the legal, technological, and defence challenges to benefit all Member States, industry and EU bodies and agencies. EDA thus contributes to implement current and future strategies and policies, striving to reflect appropriately MoD’s views. This contract aims to support a continuous monitoring and awareness of wider policies affecting the EDTIB, in a fast pace evolving security, policy and economic environment. The overarching goal of this framework contract is to help EDA develop and refine tools and instruments that will support the development of the EDTIB. These are multifaceted and can address all policies that touch upon the activities of the defence industry at the national, intergovernmental and supranational levels.

title: Community Living Ethical Framework
description:
Wigan Council and NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (Wigan Locality) are committed to enabling people to live fulfilled and valued lives in their own homes and communities. Central to this ambition is the delivery of high quality, ethical, asset based support by a skilled, caring and compassionate workforce.
The Community Living Ethical Framework has been developed to establish strong, values based partnerships with high quality providers who share this commitment. The Framework will be the Council's primary mechanism for commissioning with confidence ethical providers who deliver strengths based, community focused support, while recognising and valuing the essential contribution of their workforce.
The Framework seeks to support a transformed model of care and support that focuses on people's strengths, networks and aspirations, enabling them to live independently and remain connected within their local communities.
All providers on the Community Living Ethical Framework will demonstrate:
•That people have real control over their care and support, actively engaging residents, local communities and partners in the co-design and development of support packages.
•The difference that they are making to people's lives through a strengths-based approach celebrating and facilitating people's gifts, talents and aspirations.
•That they seek solutions that actively plan to avoid or overcome crisis and focus on people within their natural communities, rather than service and organisational boundaries.
•That they enable people to develop networks of support in their local communities and increase community connections.
•That they take time to listen to a person's own voice, particularly those whose views are not easily heard.
•That they fully consider the needs of the family and carers when planning support and care.
•That they ensure that support is culturally sensitive and relevant to diverse communities.
•That they take into account a person's whole life, including their physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual needs.

description:
London Borough of Tower Hamlets is recommissioning a borough-wide, world-class adult substance misuse treatment system, aligned with the Combatting Drugs Partnership Strategy (2024–2027). Currently Tower Hamlets commission and deliver a range of substance misuse treatment and recovery services for residents aged 18 plus, collectively branded as “Reset”. These services meet the needs of Tower Hamlet’s residents facing the challenges of substance misuse by equipping individuals with the tools to move towards a life where drugs and alcohol do not negatively impact on themselves, their families, and/or the wider community.
The borough’s substance misuse treatment and recovery services have undergone significant change over the last six years. The “Reset” service model was launched in October 2019, followed by a challenging period of mobilisation during the pandemic years. More recently the borough has seen a substantial increase in investment, through time-limited grant programmes in support of the national drug strategy, From Harm to Hope. This has resulted in a series of iterative, short-term investments to improve the quality and outcomes of services, with the aim of increasing the numbers of individuals accessing and sustaining treatment.
Following a period of review the borough is seeking to re-procure these services; providing an opportunity to build on the successes of the last few years and refresh our model within the context of a more sustainable funding framework.

title: Workflow Management System
description:
WM5G Ltd is seeking to procure a configurable Digital Discharge Service (DDS) Workflow solution to support the coordination of hospital discharge-to-home pathways across NHS partner organisations. The solution will provide a single operational platform through which WM5G Ltd staff can manage referrals, patient workflows, consent, tasks, communications and service performance, replacing fragmented processes that currently rely on multiple supplier systems and manual administration.
The procurement covers the software platform, implementation, integration, hosting, training, support and maintenance required throughout the contract term. The solution will act as the operational orchestration layer for the wider DDS service, providing a unified view of patient journeys while integrating with existing Home Readiness, Remote Monitoring and Asset Management services. It is intended to improve the efficiency, scalability and governance of discharge services while maintaining clear accountability and visibility across multiple organisations and care settings.
The platform must support the complete discharge workflow, from patient identification and referral through triage, enrolment, discharge preparation, discharge, monitoring and completion. Core capability areas include referral and onward-care management, workflow and task management, consent management, reporting and analytics, administration and role-based access control, standards-based integration, and data quality management.
WM5G Ltd has defined a mandatory high-level architecture that suppliers must conform to. The solution must support API-first integration, HL7 FHIR interoperability standards, UK cloud hosting, strong identity management and secure integration with external systems. The architecture is designed to support rapid onboarding of new customers and providers while minimising operational complexity and vendor lock-in.
The authority's desired outcomes are improved patient flow, reduced discharge delays, better patient and carer experience, reduced administrative burden, improved operational oversight, higher data quality and a platform capable of scaling across multiple regions and thousands of patients. Compliance with NHS and regulatory standards, including DCB0129, DCB0160, DTAC, DSPT, Cyber Essentials Plus and UK GDPR, is mandatory. 
Contract award will be based on the Most Advantageous Tender (MAT), assessing suppliers' ability to meet both the mandatory architectural requirements and the operational outcomes defined within the Requirements Compliance Matrix.

The Police and Crime Commissioner for Cambridgeshire and Peterborough is seeking to award a Contract for the delivery of a Child Focused Courts Independent Domestic Violence Adviser (IDVA) Support Service across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough.
The service will provide specialist, trauma-informed support, advocacy, risk assessment and safety planning for adult victim-survivors of domestic abuse who are involved in private family law proceedings within the Child Focused Courts model. The service will work closely with Family Courts, Cafcass, local authorities and other relevant partners to identify and respond to risks at an early stage, support victim-survivors throughout court proceedings, and contribute to improved outcomes for children and families.
The Contract will commence on 14 January 2027 for an initial period ending 31 March 2028, with the option to extend for up to two further periods of 12 months each.

title: Better Care Fund VCSE Integrated Wellbeing Pathways SC, HI & W/2025/93
description:
Stoke-on-Trent City Council and Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent Integrated Care Board (ICB) are seeking providers within the local Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise (VCFSE) sector to deliver the Better Care Fund (BCF) funded VCFSE Integrated Wellbeing Pathways service for adults aged 18+. The new model has been developed through engagement with VCFSE organisations and health and care partners and aims to provide a more integrated and person-centred approach to supporting local residents.
The proposed contract term is 3 years, with the option to extend for a further two 1 year periods (3+1+1). The estimated annual contract value is up to £557,282.00 with a maximum potential contract value of £2,786,410.00 over the full contract term.
The service will be delivered through two lots:
Lot 1: Community Support and Development
Annual Value: Approximately £285,282.00
Through predominantly home visits, this lot provides responsive and preventative support that helps individuals maintain independence while fostering stronger community capacity and connections.
Providers will be expected to:
•	Deliver responsive short-term wellbeing support, primarily through home visits.
•	Support socially isolated, vulnerable and at-risk residents.
•	Connect individuals with voluntary, community, faith and statutory services.
•	Identify emerging unmet need within communities.
•	Strengthen communities by working with local partners to develop sustainable community-based solutions and support networks.
•	Deliver flexible and innovative approaches that respond to local needs and circumstances.
•	Operate a responsive seven-day service model.
Lot 2: Integrated Hospital Discharge and Neighbourhood Support Pathway
Annual Value: Approximately £272,000.00
This lot will support safe and timely hospital discharge, helping people recover, remain independent, and avoid unnecessary readmissions through coordinated community and VCFSE support.
Providers will be expected to:
•	Work in partnership with hospital, community, primary care and social care teams.
•	Support patient identification, discharge planning and same-day discharge where appropriate.
•	Coordinate rapid access to community, VCFSE and Personal Health Budget (PHB) support.
•	Deliver post-discharge follow-up to promote recovery and reduce readmissions.
•	Develop and coordinate neighbourhood-based VCFSE support services.
•	Identify gaps in provision and strengthen local community capacity and resilience.
•	Operate a responsive seven-day service model.
What the service will deliver
Across both lots, providers will work alongside people to help them:
•	Live independently and confidently for longer.
•	Improve their health, wellbeing and overall quality of life.
•	Stay well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital admissions or readmissions.
•	Access the right support at the right time, including safe and timely discharge from hospital.
•	Maintain independence and delay or avoid the need for long-term care and support.
•	Build meaningful connections, reduce isolation and strengthen support networks.
Providers will need strong links with local communities and referral partners, experience of collaborative working, and the ability to share outcomes and performance. Successful providers for Lots 1 and 2 will be expected to work together to create a seamless pathway for residents.
Recognising the expertise of providers, outcomes, key performance measures and indicators will be agreed collaboratively during mobilisation to ensure measures are meaningful, outcome-focused and reflect local priorities.
The procurement opportunity is expected to be published in Early October 2026. We welcome submissions from individual organisations, partnerships, consortia, or lead provider/subcontractor arrangements.

title: NSDC-1722 Property Safety and Compliance Check Service and Maintenance Contract for Newark and Sherwood District Council
description:
Newark and Sherwood District Council (NSDC) is seeking to form a contract with one Contractor suitably qualified and experienced Property Safety and Compliance Check Contractor (PSCC/C) to deliver essential health, safety, statutory and regulatory compliance checks across all domestic properties under its management to be delivered under a Three-Star Contract which is a Fully Inclusive Service, Maintenance, Repair and Compliance Contract. The Contract shall operate on a fully inclusive basis whereby the PSCC/C shall be responsible for the inspection, servicing, maintenance, repair and continued operational performance of all heating and hot water systems included within the Contract throughout the Contract Term. The contract will also require the successful PSCC/C to provide operational support to NSDC's Remedial Repairs and Void Management functions, where required and in accordance with the requirements set out within the specification.
The Contractor will be responsible for ensuring compliance with all relevant legislation, industry standards, Approved Codes of Practice (ACOPs) and manufacturer requirements, whilst maintaining accurate records, certification and audit trails. Services shall be delivered in a resident-focused manner, adhering to NSDC's access procedures and safety requirements.
The Contract places a strong emphasis on quality assurance, safety, asset longevity and evidence-based compliance, requiring robust reporting, digital documentation and performance management throughout the Contract Term. The Contractor will work collaboratively with NSDC to support tenant safety, regulatory compliance and the effective management of the Council's housing assets.
Further information about the work requirements can be obtained in the tender documentation within this tender pack.
Contract Term and Duration
The contract commencement date is: 1st April 2027.
The Council propose to enter into one Contract for an initial period of four (4) years with the preferred supplier, with an option to extend for a further period of one (1) year, subject to an annual review by the Council. Any proposed extension is subject to
satisfactory performance by the supplier and in accordance with the Council's business requirements. Please note: that extension options are not in any way guaranteed.
Contract Terms
The Contractor will operate under the conditions of the JCT Measured Term Contract 2024 including Volume 2a.
Contract Value
The total contract value for this procurement is £7.4m excluding VAT. Please note: the Council reserves the right to reject any submissions that are over budget without further evaluation.
Procurement Procedure
Open procedure in accordance with Procurement Act 2023.
Additional Information
This procurement process is being managed by Welland Procurement in partnership with the Council. Further information on Welland Procurement can be found at:
http://wellandprocurement.org.uk/
Suppliers are welcome to view the opportunity and access the tender documents on the East Mids Tenders portal using the link below: https://www.eastmidstenders.org/

title: Family Support Services (Inverclyde)
description:
Inverclyde Health and Social Care Partnership (HSCP) and the Inverclyde Alcohol and Drug
Partnership (ADP) require the delivery of a Family Support Service (FSS) for adults and young
people aged 16 years and over, who reside in Inverclyde and are affected by the alcohol
and/or drug use of a family member, partner, friend or loved one.
The Family Support service will recognise that substance use can have a significant and
lasting impact on family members in their own right and that families require support regardless
of whether their loved one is currently engaged in treatment, recovery or active substance
use.
The Family Support service will place families at the centre of all activity and will operate within
a framework of:
Trauma-Informed Practice
Family Inclusive Practice
Whole Family Approaches
Human Rights Based Practice
Recovery-Oriented Systems of Care
The Family Support service will provide; early intervention, prevention, emotional support,
education, advocacy, peer support, bereavement support, pathways for moving on to other
community-based supports when appropriate, and family recovery interventions to improve
outcomes for individuals, families and communities across Inverclyde.
