title: Accredited learning programmes across the policy profession
description:
The Civil Service Policy Profession consists of approximately 38,500 civil servants, making it the second largest profession in government. It has a presence across the regions and nations of the UK. The work of policy professionals has a significant impact on the lives of people across the country. Investing in the development of policy makers supports the creation of stronger policies and improved outcomes for the public.
The Policy Profession Unit, part of the Department for Education and operating on behalf of policy professionals across government, is responsible for overseeing the development of the Policy Profession. This includes building the skills and capability of policy professionals at different stages of their careers.
Following a competitive procurement process, the Department for Education has awarded contracts for the development and delivery of accredited postgraduate learning programmes designed to build the skills and capabilities of UK civil servants in line with the Policy Profession Standards. The programmes will be available from September 2027 and will support policy professionals across government departments.
The procurement was divided into two lots:
Lot 1 (itt_3995):
A contract for the delivery of five cohorts of an accredited 180-credit Master's programme, with one cohort delivered per academic year from Academic Year 2027/28. The programme is designed for experienced civil service policy leaders and will strengthen advanced policy capability, enabling participants to apply academic rigour and best practice to complex government policy challenges while continuing in their roles.
Lot 2 (itt_3999):
A contract for the delivery of a postgraduate accredited learning offer for civil service policy professionals, including standalone modules and qualifications at Postgraduate Award, Certificate and Diploma level for experienced practitioners. The contract also includes a separate 30-credit Postgraduate Award for Government Policy Fast Streamers, delivered annually through a structured three-year programme.
The Department for Education will hold the contracts on behalf of the Civil Service Policy Profession; however, the programmes will be accessible to participants from all UK Government departments.
The estimated values published are based on historic student volumes and expenditure. Actual contract expenditure will be determined by future learner numbers and departmental demand over the contract term. The Department for Education does not guarantee any minimum level of spend under the contracts and reserves the right to vary volumes in accordance with operational requirements.

title: Children’s Passive Online Measurement (CPOM)
description:
Ofcom is undertaking this market engagement to gather general feedback to inform and help us finalise our procurement strategy and tender documentation. A formal procurement procedure is expected to follow this market engagement exercise but please note that undertaking this market engagement exercise does not commit Ofcom to any course of action, including undertaking a subsequent procurement process. This is an information gathering exercise only.  
Prospective suppliers are not being assessed at this stage and taking part is not a necessary pre-condition to being part of the tender.
Some more information about what Ofcom needs: 
The study needs to contain information on what 8-17 year olds are doing online. This is an extension beyond our current study which only goes up to the age of 14. Ideally we’d like to be able to answer questions about children’s online usage levels and refer to fairly recent usage at any time during the year, so this may mean continuous monitoring or at least a multi-wave approach during the year. The data must be able to be used for enforcement and regulation activities. 
Our main aim is to ensure that our thinking about the objectives and structure of the study match market capability both in terms of new possibilities and also limitations.

title: TfGM Connected Vehicle Data
description:
TfGM is looking to find and contact with a specialist supplier in the area of connected vehicle data.
TfGM on behalf of Safer Roads Greater Manchester (SRGM) Partnership is seeking a connected vehicle data provider to collaborate with TfGM's internal teams and partner authorities.
SRGM is a multi-agency partnership dedicated to reducing fatalities and serious injuries on Greater Manchester's (GM ) roads by influencing attitudes and behaviours. The Safer Roads Partnership is responsible for countywide functions, as agreed with Greater Manchester partners, including casualty data and analysis, performance monitoring, and safety camera operations. 
The SRGM Partnership is committed to Vision Zero.
Vision Zero represents Greater Manchester's ambition for zero fatalities and life changing injuries (FLCI) on our roads by 2040, whilst increasing safe, healthy and equitable mobility for all. It includes a challenging interim target of 50% reduction in FLCI casualty numbers by 2030, from 2022 levels. The Vision Zero Strategy adopts the Safe System, whereby people, vehicles and the road infrastructure interact in a way that secures a high level of safety.
The objective is to deliver a comprehensive suite of analytical services aimed at deepening our understanding of road user behaviour and collision risk. In addition, several further benefits and use cases for connected vehicle data have been identified within TfGM and its partner network.
TfGM is therefore looking for a partner who can provide a multi-use source of connected vehicle data. The data will support a range of use cases enabling historic trend analysis, operational insight and real-time intervention.

title: 003625 - Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) for the Provision of Meals at Aycliffe Secure Centre
description:
Durham County Council is seeking market engagement in relation to a future contract for the provision of a fully managed catering service at Aycliffe Secure Centre, a secure children's home accommodating up to 34 young people aged 10-18 years. The service will operate seven days per week, 365 days per year and will include the planning, preparation and delivery of nutritious meals for young people and staff.
The catering service will include the provision of a daily two course lunch and evening meal service, with at least a choice of two main dishes for an agreed contract meal price, plus a management fee. In addition, the provider will also provide a weekend brunch provision (instead of lunch), special dietary and allergen management, menu development, themed and cultural food events, packed lunches, hospitality catering and ongoing engagement with young people to help shape food offerings.
The successful provider will be responsible for kitchen operations, staffing, food safety compliance, safeguarding requirements, supply chain management, sustainability initiatives, performance monitoring and contract management. The Council is seeking a proactive and flexible provider capable of delivering a high-quality catering experience that supports the health, wellbeing and diverse cultural, religious and medical needs of young people within a secure environment.
The Council is particularly interested in hearing from suppliers with experience of catering within education, healthcare, residential care, custodial or similarly regulated environments where safeguarding, nutrition, compliance and stakeholder engagement are key service requirements
The contract will commence 1st September 2027 and will be for a period of 36 months with 2 x 24 month optional extension periods. The approximate annual contract value is up to £280,000 per annum.
It is anticipated that this contract will be procured via an Open Tender procurement process, in Autumn/Winter 2026. A full tender specification will be provided for the tender process.

title: DHSC: LERO Development and Resilience Project
description:
To deliver a 3-year national Lived experience recovery organisation (LERO) development and resilience project from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2030. The project will support the development and resilience of emerging and established LEROs and local authorities looking to support and sustain LEROs and recovery communities in their locality.
Building on the previous LERO capacity-building project, the LERO development and resilience project will support LEROs to develop and sustain through peer-led mentoring, specialist bespoke learning opportunities, reusable good practice resources and local authority support. This contract builds on learning from the first 2 project years. This includes strong demand for practical peer-led support and bespoke learning opportunities for leaders; the value of mentoring from experienced LERO leaders; the need for continued support on governance, leadership, financial management, fundraising and workforce development; and the importance of supporting local authorities to create the conditions in which recovery communities, LEROs and other peer-led initiatives can develop and sustain.
The previous project has been developing an offer for local authority commissioners primarily through regular drop-ins. In this new iteration of the project, the Authority wishes to further develop this approach by providing universal and targeted support for local areas seeking to develop or sustain LEROs. This will help local authority commissioners to understand the conditions that enable independent, peer-led LEROs to develop within local recovery-oriented systems of care, and to access support that responds to local context, readiness and need.

title: Proc-26-84 Heritage and Traditional Skills Project
description:
UK 7 - Contract Details Notice
WCBC Gorwelion Newydd - Provision of a community and alternative education provision provider whose specialism lies within heritage and traditional skills, with proven experience to support the delivery of an expanded service provision across wider school community. The service to be provided. As part of the Education Department, the Council has a statutory responsibility to ensure the delivery of high quality education for all learners. The Pupil Referral Unit (PRU) Service provides specialist support for children and young people with complex educational needs who require an alternative to mainstream provision. The most recent Estyn inspection recognised both the quality of this service and the positive steps taken to broaden the curriculum for learners accessing PRU support. Despite these strengths, Wrexham County Borough Council (WCBC) acknowledges that further action is required to meet the needs of young people who are at risk of disengaging from mainstream education. Demand for places across the three PRU sites continues to exceed capacity. To address this challenge, WCBC proposes to build on the success of the UKSPF Best EET Forward project (completed April 2026) by offering an equitable programme of heritage crafts, traditional skills, and green space development across secondary schools. This programme will operate in addition to WCBC’s statutory duties and existing budgets. Early intervention remains central to improving life chances. WCBC views this project as a key mechanism for helping young people remain successfully engaged in mainstream education by providing additional, targeted provision within their own secondary schools. Through previous initiatives, including the Multiply project and the Best EET Forward project, WCBC has already piloted a range of practical, heritage based learning opportunities. These have included sessions in traditional construction skills, permaculture, and blacksmithing, delivered in partnership with specialist providers. These programmes have had a significant positive impact on learners, many of whom have expressed a strong interest in exploring employment pathways within the heritage construction and land based sectors. At a senior leadership level, WCBC will design and coordinate delivery to ensure the programme targets young people aged 11+ who are most at risk of becoming disengaged with mainstream education. WCBC will work closely with secondary schools and its procured delivery partner, who are best placed to identify suitable learners. Together, they will offer new programmes of learning designed to enhance engagement and build confidence.

title: Next Generation Technology Reseller Arrangements
description:
The Bank of England is considering its future approach to procuring technology products and associated services following the expiry of its current technology Value Added Reseller (VAR) framework.
At this stage, the Bank has not made a final decision on the structure of any future procurement and is undertaking preliminary market engagement to help inform its thinking, procurement strategy and framework design.
Whilst one option is a like-for-like replacement of the existing arrangement, the Bank's initial view is that the future model may comprise multiple frameworks rather than a single framework. In particular, the Bank is considering a dedicated framework focussed on Cyber & Emerging Technology, alongside one or more additional frameworks covering other areas of technology spend.
The categories currently being considered are:
Cyber & Emerging Technology
Software & Platforms
Hardware, End User Computing (EUC) & Connectivity
Enterprise Applications, Cloud Hosting & Infrastructure
The purpose of this engagement is to obtain market feedback on areas including:
Framework structure and lotting strategy
The advantages and disadvantages of single versus multiple framework arrangements
Supplier capability and capacity across the proposed categories
Commercial and pricing models
Routes to market for emerging technologies
Innovation and market developments
Supplier onboarding, framework governance and competition models
The Bank welcomes input from suppliers operating in one or more of the proposed categories and intends to use the feedback received to inform its future procurement strategy, framework design and any subsequent procurement activity.
This Preliminary Market Engagement exercise does not constitute a call for competition and will not result in the award of any contract. The Bank reserves the right to amend the scope, structure, lotting approach and procurement strategy of any future procurement following completion of the engagement process.

title: ICT Managed Service Partner
description:
The ICT Support at LAAT is currently provided by a single outsourced support provider who provides a mix of scheduled onsite visits and remote support.  This contract will end in March 2027, and so the Trust needs to run a procurement to ensure continuity of service.
In addition to this, the Trust is planning a major ICT related investment and commitment to pupil learning by implementing a Trust wide 'One to One' (hereafter, 1:1) mobile device scheme for its students.
The Trust has already piloted a 1:1 mobile device scheme using Apple iPads so the Trust understands its requirements clearly.
Going forward, given both the scale of the requirement and the need to sustain and develop the programme over five years the point has been reached where a significant procurement exercise is needed to both be compliant with the Procurement Act and ensure best value with a capable partner going forward.
Therefore, LAAT is taking the opportunity to go to the market to identify the best innovative and forward-looking partner to work with them in the support, delivery and development of their ICT provision over the next five years providing both the Managed Service Support and potentially 1:1 device procurement and support.
Given the significant investment in Apple devices, and based on experience from the pilot 1:1 project, the Trust will require specific training and CPD on the use of Apple devices and education specific applications in the classroom (including, but not limited to, Showbie - which is currently used in the pilot schools) from an appropriately accredited training provider, with 'real-world' experience of Apple devices being used in a 1:1/classroom context.
The Trust is open to the MSP providing this training, but the Trust has built up a strong relationship with an existing 3rd party supplier in this area, and reserves the right to continue this relationship to ensure the most effective use of the 1:1 devices and the best outcomes for the 1:1 project.
This procurement includes (but may not be limited to) the items listed below.
•	A core managed service, management of all ICT against an agreed SLA
•	A Service Desk, available 52 weeks a year including out of hours access providing a 'remote fix' to issues as they are reported where possible
•	On-site school staffing which suppliers deem necessary to deliver the service and meet the SLA requirements
•	Support for the Trust's Safeguarding/Filtering solution, Securly
•	Support for the Trust's Barracuda email security/Anti phishing solution
•	Strategic advice and direction to the Trust regarding ICT
•	Responsibility for design, specification, installation, and management of all ICT infrastructure
•	Supply of goods and services based on an agreed Best Value approach
•	Management of 3rd parties where relevant to the ICT support
•	Relevant monitoring, management, patching
•	Responsibility for ensuring appropriate backup and anti-virus is in place
•	Regular performance reporting
•	Support for cybersecurity readiness
•	CPD and training - digital skills and curriculum as necessary across Microsoft and Apple devices/software
•	There is an expectation that the provider will support and/or drive innovation
•	Maintain technical documentation
•	Maintain operational documentation, for example inventory management and risk registers
•	Collective partnership targets aligned to the Trust's objectives
•	In Trust support for the integration and upgrade of the connectivity, communications and security infrastructure as required, including liaising with relevant third parties on behalf of the Trust
•	Suppliers may be required to deliver a range of technology and change management projects in addition to the providing the core managed service.
•	Enhanced support during OFSTED visits, Exam periods, and around results days for Exams
•	The potential supply of a significant amount of Apple iPad devices - currently estimated to be c.2,500 over 5 years
o	A comprehensive managed service for repair and replacement,
	Repair and/or replacement of devices
	enrol/re-enrol hardware into the management console
•	Provision and management of VoIP phones/telephony across the trust

title: Prj_7117 - ITT - Purchase of carbon credits as part of the construction of a new HQ for the European Centre of Medium Range Weather Forecasts
description:
The final date and time for the submission of bids is Tuesday 23rdJune 2026 @ 11:00am
DO NOT apply directly to the buyer.
All tender information MUST be submitted through the Jaggaer eSourcing Portal.
Overview
The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) is an intergovernmental research institute with its headquarters in Shinfield (UK), and sites in Bonn (Germany) and Bologna (Italy), and contributes to major European programmes including Copernicus (the Earth observation component of the European Union's Space Programme) and Horizon Europe (EU's flagship research and innovation programme).
The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology are funding and constructing a new net zero headquarters for ECMWF at the University of Reading's Whiteknights campus, with construction expected to complete between December 2026 and March 2027.
As part of the project’s objectives, the building will need to meet the UK Net Zero Carbon Buildings Standard. To ensure this objective is met, DSIT are undertaking a procurement exercise to secure a supplier to support carbon offsetting objectives for the embodied carbon of the newly constructed headquarters.
Key requirements for this procurement:
• DSIT are looking to offset approximately 5165 tonnes of carbon (or equivalent green house gasses), as a one-off procurement via a broker to balance out embodied emissions as a result of the construction.
• The allocated budget for this procurement is up to £2,500,000 inc VAT where applicable.
How to Apply
UK Shared Business Services Ltd (UK SBS) will be using the Jaggaer eSourcing Portal for this procurement.

title: Older Persons Residential and Nursing Care Services
description:
Kent County Council (the Council) is seeking providers (referred to in this notice as Tenderers) of Care Quality Commission (CQC) registered residential and nursing care homes within the geographic boundary of Kent, to provide facilities, accommodation and care for individuals who require support due to age, disability, or health conditions, to join a new Older Persons Residential and Nursing (OPRN) Care Homes Services Open Framework.   
An open framework allows for the award of successive frameworks on substantially the same terms. This notice relates to the opportunity to apply to be admitted to the First Framework of the Kent OPRN Open Framework Scheme. 
Care homes should promote safety, dignity, and quality of life, while ensuring that People who draw on care and support receive tailored support to meet their individual needs.
The Service Specification has been designed to incorporate the provision of accommodation, care, support, and meaningful activities for individuals, residing in a Care Home setting as their own home, either temporarily or long-term. The Service should enhance an Individual’s quality of life by offering a safe, manageable, and comfortable living environment, and a range of care and support, from assistance with daily living tasks to comprehensive nursing care for those with complex medical needs.
The Services under the Kent OPRN Open Framework Scheme and Framework Agreement are ‘light touch’ and are governed by the rules relating to light touch contracts under the Procurement Act 2023.
The Council intends, but is in no way obliged to, re-open the Kent OPRN Open Framework Scheme on the first anniversary, the third anniversary and the fifth anniversary, where the Kent OPRN Open Framework Scheme continues for the full term of 8 years.
The estimated values set out in this Tender Notice are on the basis that the Kent OPRN Open Framework Scheme continues for 8 years, on the basis of 4+4 years. The term of the Third Framework in the Scheme will be 1+1 years, to account for the extension period. The Council does not guarantee that the framework will continue for the full term of 8 years.
The estimated value of the Kent OPRN Open Framework Scheme over the 8-year term is £2.2bn (inclusive of VAT) but this estimate is purely indicative and is subject to amendment prior to the publishing of any future Tender Notices and associated tender documentation. The estimated value of this First Framework is £275,000,000 (inclusive of VAT). 
No guarantee is given as to the actual value of any Frameworks under the Kent OPRN Open Framework Scheme, or any call-off contracts entered under any framework agreement. This estimated value is by no means a commitment to spend. 
 The organisation of local government is undergoing reform and the Council anticipates a change to the responsibilities of the delivery of adult social care in the administrative area of Kent County Council. The Framework Agreement and Open Framework Scheme can be used by the Council on its own behalf and on behalf of the Relevant NHS Body (as defined in the Framework Agreement) and or any successor body of the Council, or Contracting Authority that delivers adult social care services in the geographical area of Kent County Council during the term of the Open Framework Scheme.

description:
This notice is to advise of a proposed contract modification.
The Council has made the decision to extend the contract for a period of one (1) additional year, with an option to extend for an additional one (1) year again, up to a maximum of two (2) years.  The contract will be varied increasing the value of the contract by £74,076.28 (original contract value £369,000).
The increase to the value of the contract will rely upon:
•	Regulation 72(1) (b) for additional works, services or supplies by the original contractor that have become necessary and were not included in the initial procurement, where a change of contractor-
1.	cannot be made for economic or technical reasons such as requirements of interchangeability or interoperability with existing equipment, services or installations procured under the initial procurement, and
2.	would cause significant inconvenience or substantial duplication of costs for the contracting authority,
provided that any increase in price does not exceed 50% of the value of the original contract. 
The grounds relied upon to use Regulation 72(1)(b) are set out below:
(a) A change of contractor within the required timeframe would create material technical, operational and local government re-organisation implementation risks due to the complex and integrated nature of the contract.
(b) The technical capability to reconfigure the council's current systems and processes is another reason an extension is required to provide additional time to procure a replacement contract. The current system is fully integrated into the Council's ICT system to ensure that legal documents held within it are stored subject to robust security measures.  
(c) A change of contractor is not possible as a short-term measure and would result, in a potential failure to meet court and quasi-judicial deadlines thereby affecting the council's ability to deliver some of its statutory services, which extends beyond the statutory test of simple "inconvenience".  
(d) The proposed modification is necessary, proportionate, and compliant with Regulation 72(1)(b). It ensures continuity, avoids unnecessary cost and disruption, and maintains the integrity of the original procurement.
(e) The increase in contract value arising from the proposed modification will not exceed 50% of the value of the original contract.
(f) The modification will not alter the overall nature of the contract.

title: HCC Sept 2026 – Provision of Supported Housing at Westbury
description:
Hertfordshire County Council is procuring a delivery partner for a new Supported Housing scheme at Westbury, Letchworth. The project forms part of the Council's wider five-year programme to increase the supply and quality of supported living accommodation for disabled adults and its Extra Care Housing Programme, which aims to provide modern, accessible homes that promote independence and wellbeing for older people who require care and support.
The Council's preferred approach is to work with a Registered Provider that can bring development expertise, long-term ownership and housing management experience, supported by Homes England funding and Registered Provider investment alongside Council resources. The successful partner would develop, own and manage the accommodation on Council-owned land under a long lease arrangement.
The Council is currently undertaking preparatory work on the site and expects to progress design and enabling works during 2025/26, with construction planned from 2026 onwards and completion between 2027 and 2030. Outline planning permission is expected to be secured through North Hertfordshire District Council, with any necessary enabling works undertaken to facilitate delivery of the scheme.
Hertfordshire County Council (the “Council”) is a large shire county in the south-east of England with a population of 1.2 million. Hertfordshire is a two-tier authority with 10 district and borough councils providing complementary local services to residents.  
In February 2025, the Council launched a five-year delivery plan to increase the supply and quality of supported living accommodation in Hertfordshire and, in doing so, deliver wider health and wellbeing outcomes to meet the existing and future demand for disabled adults in Hertfordshire by 2030.  The programme responds to current and future demand, including people who currently live in unsuitable existing HCC accommodation, people living with their family who now need a home of their own, people in residential care whose needs could be met in supported living, and people living outside Hertfordshire who wish to return. The Supported Living Delivery Programme is intended to replace outdated accommodation, improve quality and accessibility, support independence, and provide modern homes.   
The Council’s Extra Care delivery programme focusses on the provision of modern, accessible homes across the county that support independent living for older people and adults with care needs. By increasing the supply of Extra Care housing, the council aims to meet growing demand, promote well-being and independence, reduce reliance on residential care and ensure residents can remain in their communities while receiving flexible support tailored to their changing needs. The programme is responding to significant demographic growth, with evidence indicating a need for around 8,000 additional Extra care units by 2042, including approximately 1,800 affordable homes.   
The Council’s preferred delivery approach is to work with Registered Providers who can bring housing development expertise, long-term ownership and housing management experience. This approach is intended to support delivery at pace while also making use of Homes England funding and Registered Provider investment alongside Council resources. The Council is exploring the best approach to work with developing Registered Providers (both Housing Associations and Local Authorities) (‘RPs’) to deliver, own and manage accommodation on Council owned land via a long lease (virtual freehold).    
The Council is currently undertaking preparatory work on the Westbury site which is Council owned with a view to progressing design and enabling works during 2026-27, construction in 2027/28 – 2028/29 and phased completion and handover in 2028–30.   
The Council anticipates obtaining outline planning approval for the site via the Local Planning Authority at North Herts District Council and undertaking enabling works where required to bring the site forward.  
The Council seeks submissions from a Registered Provider partner to deliver, own and manage supported living accommodation at the Westbury Site.

title: Supply of Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG)
description:
Hampshire County Council’s Energy Team currently manages utility services, including water, electricity, gas and liquid fuels, across a diverse property portfolio. This includes the corporate estate, schools and colleges, nursing care homes, children’s centres, libraries and museums. The Supplier will supply sites with Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) fuel to heat their buildings and for the use of catering equipment and hot water systems.

The existing supply arrangement is with Calor Gas through the ESPO Framework 92_21 (Liquefied Petroleum Gas and Other Liquid Fuels), with current annual expenditure in the region of £150,000 to £200,000.

It is anticipated that the new call-off contract will have an estimated annual value of approximately £250,000. This increase reflects rising energy costs and incorporates additional budget flexibility to accommodate market volatility resulting from geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and other external factors affecting global energy prices. The procurement will ensure continued compliance with procurement regulations while securing value for money and mitigating risks associated with energy market volatility and supply chain disruption.

title: Molecular Analysis of Water Primrose (Ludwigia)
description:
This project will undertake genetic analysis of Ludwigia populations in England to strengthen and refine the national eradication programme and provide baseline research towards a potential biological control.
Ludwigia (water primrose) is a high-priority invasive non-native species due to its capacity to spread rapidly, form dense mats, outcompete native aquatic vegetation, and significantly alter freshwater ecosystems. These impacts are already well documented across continental Europe and elsewhere, where the species has caused ecological degradation and increased management costs.
There is a legal commitment for Defra to eradicate water primrose under the EU Regulation 1143/2014, retained in UK law. Achieving this requires not only effective physical and chemical control, but also a stronger understanding of the species’ biology, origin, and pathways of spread. This will allow us to recognise pathways of spread and manage these through good biosecurity and Pathway Action Plans.

title: GL RFCA Barnet ARC Boiler Replacement
description:
Below threshold procurement - by invitation only.
Due to the urgent on-site need for these works, we are only inviting bids from suppliers who are on-boarded to both the Central Digital Platform and our own finance system, Symphony. This is intended to avoid delaying the delivery of the works, as the on-boarding process can take some time. Only those invited suppliers will be asked to attend a site open day, and only submissions from those invited will be evaluated. All others will be disregarded, not opened or evaluated.
This project consists of the replacement of the existing central heating boiler plant and equipment at Army Reserve Centre, St Albans Rd., Barnet EN5 4JX. Barnet Army Reserve Centre is a drill hall and associated amenities currently used by 118 Close Support Company and 240 Transport Squadron in St Albans Rd., Barnet. 
The building was designed and completed in 1937. The complex was used continuously by reserve and transport units since World War II. The existing boiler installation was undertaken in the early 2000’s. 
There is a main plantroom room in the basement that provides domestic hot water and heating to all the facilities in Barnet Army Reserve Centre. Cold water storage tanks on the roof provide a cold water supply to the bathrooms and to the hot water calorifiers. 
The existing plant consists of 3 No. Ideal Commercial Concord CXA 120 gas fired boilers, 2 No. hot water storage calorifiers fed from the heating system, associated pumps, expansion vessels and controls. The boiler flue routes through an existing chimney to discharge at roof level.  New communal boilers and replacement pumps are to be provided in the basement plantroom.

The assignment will help explore how the total funding apparatus can be further developed so that it more fully supports the social goal of a sustainable Norwegian film industry that creates films the public wants to see, through flexible and effective financing that strengthens companies' ability to take risks. The concepts shall contribute to highlighting how the financing system can provide: - more predictable and efficient financing processes. - better liquidity and economic robustness of the production companies. - increased ability to combine artistic ambition and public appeal - increased attractiveness for private investments. - a greater strategic scope of action for established companies. - stronger incentives for long-term value creation and utilisation of content. The ambition is to explore a broad possibility room and develop concepts that challenge the current structures, at the same time remain within overall cultural policy objectives and administrative frameworks. The assignment shall start from the knowledge already established through the preliminary project and contribute to exploring how different means can be adapted and combined to meet the challenges identified. It is vital that the concepts are developed with a general perspective on the financing process and that they see the connection between the current and future means. The assignment shall not primarily be about improving existing individual schemes, but on exploring how a future system can be designed to provide better goal achievement, greater flexibility, better liquidity and increased industry sustainability. NFI requests concepts that challenge established mindsets and practices, and at the same time are relevant and sufficiently mature to form the basis for further analyses, impact assessments and strategic decisions.

title: France – Design and execution of research and development – Prestations de layout de circuits intégrés analogiques et mixtes
description: Les prestations confiées au titulaire seront des prestations de layouts de blocs analogiques et mixtes. Ces blocs seront décrits sous forme de schémas annotés disponibles dans une base de données Cadence au démarrage de la tâche. Une base de données de circuit intégré rassemble notamment tous schémas constituant le circuit, organisés de façon hiérarchique. L’implémentation physique de ces schémas va se faire en plusieurs étapes et selon plusieurs granularités. On peut les décrire ainsi : Layout d’un schéma de bloc : - Analyse du schéma : o Identification des points sensibles, des contraintes topologiques, des précautions d’implémentation à prendre o Proposition d’un floorplan du bloc et évaluation de la surface - Réalisation du layout : o Placement et connexion des composants o Proposition de modification mineure schéma si pertinent - Réalisation des vérifications : o DRC o LVS A l’issue des étapes de layout, des vues schémas intégrant les éléments parasites induits par l’implémentation physique sont extraites et simulées par les concepteurs CEA pour valider l’adéquation du layout avec la performance attendue. En cas de performances insuffisantes, une reprise pour optimisation du layout peut être demandée. Layout d’assemblage de blocs entre eux en macro-blocs : les étapes sont sensiblement les même que pour les blocs unitaires, (analyse, layout, vérifications), mais à un niveau de hiérarchie supérieur. La complexité de ces assemblages dépend du nombre des signaux d’interface, des contraintes topologiques diverses (contraintes d’alimentations, d’isolation, de limites de surfaces…) Layout d’assemblage TOP : Il s’agit de faire l’assemblage aux plus hauts niveaux du circuit, entre les plots (souvent organisés en couronne), et les macro-blocs de plus haut niveau. Cet assemblage est très différent si le TOP du circuit est dit « numérique » ou « analogique ». Les assemblages TOP considérés pour les tâches de layout seront uniquement des TOP analogiques.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF - Grünes Gleis – Untersuchung der Auswirkungen von Vegetation auf die Gleisinfrastruktur und Sicherheit im Schienenverkehr
description: Wie grün dürfen Gleise im Schienenverkehr sein? Untersuchungen zu den Auswirkungen von Vegetation auf die Gleisinfrastruktur und die Verkehrssicherheit. Ziel Im Rahmen dieses Forschungsprojektes sollen umfangreiche Vegetationsbestandsaufnahmen und Kartierungsarbeiten auf verschiedenen Gleisanlagen des Schienenverkehrs erfolgen. Hierbei soll neben der Vegetation auch der Zustand der Gleisinfrastruktur erfasst und bewertet werden. Ziel ist es, durch systematische Untersuchungen den maximalen Bedeckungsgrad bzw. Bewuchsdichte auf Gleisanalgen bezogen auf die Gewährleistung der Verkehrssicherheit und Gleisinstandhaltung zu identifizieren bzw. mittels ergänzender Simulationen zu ermitteln. Darüber hinaus sollen die Möglichkeiten zum Einsatz von biologischen bzw. naturidentischen Substanzen zur Vegetationskontrolle im Schienenverkehr untersucht recherchiert und bewertet werden. Beschreibung Die Vegetationskontrolle ist für die Durchführung eines sicheren Eisenbahnbetriebs unerlässlich. Dabei besteht das Vegetationsmanagement aus einer Reihe von verschiedenen Maßnahmen und Verfahren. Die Auswahl der entsprechenden Methoden richtet sich hierbei nach betrieblichen Nutzungsanforderungen, Flächeneigenschaften sowie der Art und dem Ort der Vegetation. In sicherheitsrelevanten Bereichen, wie den Gleisanlagen (inkl. Randwegen), wird kein Aufwuchs toleriert und vorhandener Bewuchs systematisch bekämpft. Durch die Nutzungseinschränkung des chemischen Wirkstoffs Glyphosat und dem damit verbundenen Wechsel zu anderen Wirkstoffen oder Verfahren unterliegt das Vegetationsmanagement von Gleisanlagen derzeit einem systematischen Wandel. Neben logistischen Problemen, die aus häufigeren Anwendungen resultieren, gehören auch veränderte Betriebsabläufe in der Instandhaltung und steigende Unterhaltungskosten zu den aktuellen Herausforderungen der Vegetationskontrolle. Auch Alternativverfahren mit z. B. biologischen oder naturidentischen Substanzen stellen bisher aufgrund der heterogenen Datenlagen sowie fehlender Erfahrungen im Verkehrssektor keinen adäquaten Ersatz für gängige chemische oder mechanische Verfahren im Gleisbereich dar. Systematische Untersuchungen zu den Auswirkungen von Vegetation gegenüber der Gleisinfrastruktur, z. B. hinsichtlich der Gleisstabilität bzw. Schotterbeschaffenheit, allgemeinen Sicherheitsaspekten oder ökonomischen und betrieblichen Faktoren, liegen bislang nicht vor. Daher soll in diesem Forschungsvorhaben eine wissenschaftliche Grundlage zu diesen Fragestellungen geschaffen werden, um fundierte Informationen/Daten zur Beschleunigung von behördlichen Aufsichtstätigkeiten und Genehmigungsverfahren bereitzustellen.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF - Automatisierte Überwachung instandhaltungsrelevanter Parameter im SGV
description: Aus vielfältigen Vorgaben zu Kontroll- und Instandhaltungsmaßnahmen von Güterwagen sollen konkrete technische Anforderungen an die Zustandsüberwachung abgeleitet werden. Das Ziel ist ein Portfolio mit bewerteten Einzellösungen, das die Anforderungen und den Mehrwert der Zustandsüberwachung in einzelnen Bereichen der Instandhaltung definiert und als Grundlage zur Ableitung von Konzepten einer aufwandsreduzierten Instandhaltung dient. Mittels Zustandsüberwachung (engl. Condition Monitoring, CM) können Defekte an Schienenfahrzeugen frühzeitig erkannt werden. Deren Kenntnis bietet einen großen Mehrwert für die Planung der Instandhaltungsmaßnahmen und dient der Vermeidung größerer Betriebsstörungen. Ein weiteres Potenzial, das bisher lediglich eingeschränkt genutzt wird, ist die Reduktion der Kontroll- und Instandhaltungsaufwände durch den Einsatz von Zustandsüberwachung in Kombination mit der (Teil-)Automatisierung der Prozesse. Viele Anforderungen aus etablierten regulatorischen, technischen und anderweitigen Vorgaben für Kontroll- und Instandhaltungsmaßnahmen können grundsätzlich durch die Verwendung der Zustandsüberwachung erfüllt werden. Gleichzeitig sind diese Vorgaben nicht auf deren Einsatz ausgerichtet und enthalten deshalb keine konkreten technischen Anforderungen an die Systeme der Zustandsüberwachung. Die Konkretisierung der technischen Anforderungen an die Zustandsüberwachung zur Erfüllung bestehender Vorgaben eröffnet Spielräume für eine aufwandsreduzierte (teil-)automatisierte Instandhaltung, steigert den Mehrwert und kann zur Kosten- und Aufwandsreduktion im Schienengüterverkehr (SGV) beitragen.

title: Framework for the Provision of Housing Adaptations
description:
The City of Doncaster Council (CDC) is seeking to establish an open Framework for the Provision of Housing Adaptations under the regulations outlined in the Procurement Act 2023 (PA23). It is a requirement under the regulations to detail the process suppliers must follow and the call off process. All Framework management, post tender, will also be in accordance with PA23.
The Framework is divided into nine lots; you are invited to apply for one or more lots.
Lot One: Minor Adaptations - supply, installation, commissioning, testing, and completion of minor adaptations tailored to the needs of individuals, enabling them to regain independence or return home from hospital sooner. Trades required electrical, plumbing, joinery, handyman. Estimated lot value £6,720,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
Lot Two: Bathroom Adaptations - redesign and modification of existing bathroom facilities to enable individuals to regain independence or allow carers to provide personal care safely and effectively. Estimated lot value £960,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
Lot Three: Kitchen Adaptations - adjustments to existing kitchen or full kitchen redesigns to improve accessibility, safety, and usability.  Estimated lot value £6,720,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks
Lot Four: Housing Adaptations - minor adjustments or significant internal layout changes to improve accessibility, safety, and usability.  Estimated lot value £1,440,000  inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
Lot Five: Extensions - modular extensions; design supply and build, modular extensions; design and supply only. Groundworks for modular extensions, garage conversions, traditional brick and block extensions.  Estimated lot value £768,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
Lot Six: Accessibility Adaptations - ramps; permanent concrete, ramps; semi-permanent modular metal, handrails and grab rails, hardstanding and driveways.  Estimated lot value £5,760,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
Lot Seven: Stair Lifts, Through Floor Lifts and Hoists - supply, installation, commissioning, testing, and maintenance of stair lifts, through floor lifts, and ceiling/portable hoists.  Estimated lot value £5,760,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
Lot Eight: Safe Spaces - installation of padded wall systems, secure door and window features, half‑doors, and other protective measures designed to minimise injury and improve safety.  Estimated lot value £960,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
Lot Nine: Fencing - supply and installation of fencing systems; concrete post, gravel board, and wooden panel fencing. Wooden post and wooden feather edge boards with arris rail. Wooden ledged and braced gate. Estimated lot value £960,000 inclusive of VAT over the entire term of the frameworks.
The Council is looking to contract with multiple providers across all nine lots of the framework. The Framework(s) will be in place for a total of eight years, once Framework One is established a new Framework will open on an annual basis for new Contractors to apply. As required by PA23 each time a new Framework is opened it will replace the existing Framework and a new notice published on Find a Tender (FTS)
New Frameworks Frequency
Framework Two - Year Two / Three Open 1st February 2027
Framework Three - Year Three / Four Open 1st February 2028
Framework Four - Year Four / Five Open 1st February 2029
Framework Five - Year Five / Six Open 1st February 2030
Framework Six - Year Six / Seven Open 31st January 2031
Framework Seven - Year Seven / Eight Open 2nd February 2032
Framework Eight - Year Eight Open 1st February 2033
Reopening of the Framework
Where a Contractor has previously been awarded a place on the current Framework there will be no requirement to submit a new application when the next Framework is opened if they do not wish to update their offer. Providing that all documentation is up to date, prior to opening a new Framework all Contractors awarded a place on the current Framework will be asked to confirm how they want to be processed. The decision cannot be changed once the new Framework is open for applicants. If a Contractors documentation is not up to date, then they will not have the option to passport over, only to reapply or withdraw.
Options Available
Passport Over - Any Contractor that opts to passport over will automatically be awarded a place on the new Framework. No further action will be required by the Contractor.
Re Application - Contractors may choose to submit a new application and update their offer when the new Framework opens. Contractors must complete new documents including the QA process in full, if successful on evaluation. Any Contractor that fails to meet the required level on evaluation will not be allowed back on the framework. If this option is chosen it is the responsibility of the Contractor to submit the new tender on time and there is no guarantee that they will be successful. Should a Contactor be unsuccessful they will not be allowed to reapply until a new framework opens again.
Should a Contractor, that was successful on a previous application, choose to reapply to a new framework they can request that their previous application from an earlier appointment is re assessed. However, should a Contractor want to change/amend their offer a new application must be made.
Withdraw - Contractors have the option to withdraw from the framework. No further action is required by the Contractor at this time. The Contractor may reapply at any point when a new framework has been opened without prejudice.
Applications
The deadline for the receipt of applications for Framework One is 12:00 noon on 23rd July 2026. Providers admitted onto the Framework will be required to complete the quality assurance process before they are able to take part in any mini competitions or any direct call offs can be placed. Thereafter CDC will invite Contractors admitted to the Framework to participate in further competition or direct award as required.
Admittance onto the Framework is not a competitive process and there is no limit to the number of Contractors who can be appointed to each lot. Contractors who are successfully admitted on to the Framework are not guaranteed any minimum or maximum number of orders or value of orders placed.
Once admitted to the Framework Contractors will have to complete the Quality Assurance (QA) process to the satisfaction of the CDC before they can be awarded any works under this Framework. As part of the QA process Contractors will be required to provide evidence / copies of the documents to the appointed contact.
The option to conduct a mini competition is available to all nine lots. Assessment of mini competitions will be based on some or all of the award criteria that was used to assess tenders when the framework was awarded. CDC shall invite all compliant Contractors within the relevant lot to submit a response to the mini competition to deliver the required services. All complete responses will be evaluated in terms of ability to deliver the services to the required specification and the evaluation criteria as set out in the documents
While it is anticipated that the majority of call offs from the Framework will be via the mini competition route there is the option to direct award, this will carried out using a taxi rank system. A taxi rank system is a structured method of allocating work to Contractors on a Framework. Contractors on the Framework are arranged in a predetermined order and call off opportunities are offered sequentially. All Contractors once awarded a place on this Framework, and they have completed the QA process, hold an equal standing. Therefore, all Contractors will be placed in alphabetical order for each lot they have applied for. This mechanism provides a transparent, fair and efficient way of distributing work without the need to run a mini competition. Under a taxi rank system, all Contractors who have been appointed to the Framework have already demonstrated that they meet the required commercial, technical and quality standards. Because this due diligence has been completed at the Framework award stage, CDC can assign work to Contractors simply by moving down the list for that particular lot. When a new requirement arises, the first Contractor in the "rank" is approached to confirm whether they can deliver the requirement in line with the framework terms, specification and pricing. If they accept, the call‑off contract is awarded directly to them.

title: Regenerative Schools Pilot - Innovation Lead
description:
As part of the Regenerative Schools Programme, the Department intends to award two separate contracts for the Innovation Lead and Academic Adviser roles. These organisations will produce feasibility studies, research the building materials and techniques required to produce ultra-low-carbon school buildings and develop 6 standard designs. In March 2027, the Department plans to appoint a contractor to deliver the works, using the materials and methods specified by the Innovation Lead and Academic Adviser. This Contract Award Notice is for the Innovation Lead.
The Innovation Lead
The Innovation Lead will serve as the Department’s primary technical partner, guiding the programme from its earliest feasibility work through to the delivery of completed buildings. This work will include developing an understanding of each school site, identifying opportunities for nature-led retrofit, and delivering 6 standardised concept designs for new single and dual external classroom pods, ultra-low-carbon buildings that meet demanding embodied carbon targets. The Innovation Lead will explore and develop a range of regenerative material strategies, produce clear and accessible design material, and provide the technical direction needed to ensure that the Department’s ambitions for low embodied carbon, buildability and replicability are embedded from the outset.
As the programme moves from concept into development, the Innovation Lead will take on a client-side assurance role, overseeing the Contractor’s design under the Pre-Contract Services Agreement and ensuring alignment with carbon targets, safety standards, and the Department’s technical requirements. During the delivery phase, the Innovation Lead will provide project management and technical assurance, monitor the quality of off-site manufacture and on-site installation, support statutory compliance, and ensure that handover, commissioning, and early operation run smoothly. The Innovation Lead will also be responsible for producing technical guidance, case studies, and updated documentation so that learning from the programme can be scaled across the wider education estate.
Working with the Academic Adviser
The Innovation Lead and Academic Adviser are intended to operate in parallel, each with a distinct focus but with close coordination throughout. The Innovation Lead will ensure technical feasibility, safety, and low-carbon performance, while the Academic Adviser will ensure that the programme responds to the needs and experiences of the schools and communities involved. Together, the suppliers will provide the Department with the combined academic, social, and technical expertise required to develop a set of replicable, ultra-low-carbon solutions that are grounded in real-world school environments and capable of informing future national delivery.
The publication of this notice triggers the 8-working-day standstill period as defined in the Procurement Act 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, this standstill period ends on 1 October 2026.

title: RBBC-AL-Westvale Park Open Spaces - Public Art
description:
Following completed tender evaluations in accordance with the ITT pack, a Lead Consultant is to be appointed to work with  an artist or collective of artists, consultants and contractor to design, manufacture and install a series of permanent artworks within Westvale Park's Riverside Green Chain.
The permanent artworks may include a variety of forms, which may include, but not be limited to:
• Site-specific sculptures.
• Land art, which might include using natural materials like stone, earth or wood that integrate into the environment.
• Eco art installations, art pieces that highlight technological themes or support biodiversity, such as pollinator-friendly sculptures or habitat structures.
• Interactive or participatory works such as sound installations or kinetic sculptures.
• Ground mural or text-based installations that transform surfaces.
• Functional art including artists designed seating, playable art and wayfinding or trail markers.
The permanent artworks will be safe, durable, accessible, and appropriate to their setting.
The artworks will be designed and shaped by a process of community engagement and participation.
The artworks will need to give consideration to sustainability that carefully considers the environmental impact of both the fabrication and installation processes.
This includes considering the carbon footprint of materials, foundations, and fixings, prioritising the local sourcing of materials, equipment, and resources wherever feasible, and exploring the use of natural, recycled, recyclable, or reusable materials where appropriate. Artists will be expected to align to RBBC's commitment to the achievement of RBBC's Environmental Sustainability Strategy and net zero 2030 target.
The  original allocated budget of £225k is intended to support the creation of a minimum of six permanent distinct public artworks across the Westvale Park Riverside Green Chain. It is inclusive of all stages of the design and delivery process, from early research and concept development through to detailed design, fabrication, installation, and meaningful community engagement throughout the entirety of the project. The project budget is fully available and funded through Section 106 contributions.
It is anticipated that the contract term will be in the region of 12 - 18 months.

title: Bracknell Forest Council - Forestcare Evaluation
description: The Council is seeking to establish a Contract for conducting a detailed evaluation of Forestcare services. Bidders are invited to submit a quotation for these services as set out in the Specification, attached separately. BFC are seeking to appoint a suitably qualified provider to support as a delivery partner to work with BFC through a joint delivery approach to review and evaluate the current range of Forestcare services in order to inform future improvement opportunities. The adult social care element of the programme in Bracknell Forest has a focus on ensuring that we transform and change to give ourselves a long-term sustainable future. Forestcare is a key system partner, acting as a strategically significant service which supports over 3,200 vulnerable adults (of which over 1000 are Bracknell Forest residents) to live safely and independently. The monitoring, response and out-of-hours functions act as front-door demand management mechanisms for Adult Social Care, Urgent Care, ambulance services and hospitals. A recent Strategic Commissioning Overview has shown that from a commissioning perspective Forestcare represents high value for money prevention despite being projected to operate a net deficit of approximately £70,000 in 2026/2027 - which must be considered against the significantly higher system costs that would arise were Forestcare to be reduced or de-commissioned. The operating model for Forestcare is resource intensive and currently incorporates a significant amount of down time that is not being recovered from traded activities. This is a key driver for the overall service deficit which supports the current requirement for an urgent, detailed evaluation of the service. The evaluation needs to go beyond incremental change and focus on the fundamental design of the service. It should consider how the service can retain its strengths while addressing the structural issues that are driving inefficiency and financial pressure. This includes re-examining how the service is staffed, what services are delivered, how these are funded, and how technology can be used to enable a more effective and sustainable model. Carrying out a detailed evaluation will help to ensure the service can continue to operate effectively, meet future demand and remain sustainable over the long term.

description:
Transport for Wales (TfW) is developing a new multi-lot Framework agreement for the provision of Contingent Labour to support Transport for Wales (TfW) in fulfilling their Infrastructure Maintenance (IM) obligations on the Core Valley Lines (CVL). 
To support in fulfilling the Infrastructure Maintenance (IM) obligations, TfW require a compliant and efficient route to market to secure Contingent Labour to supplement its directly employed workforce to support the delivery of routine, planned maintenance activity for safety critical and off-track requirements across the CVL network with occasion reactive and emergency maintenance activity. 
Transport for Wales (TfW) is scheduled to assume the role of Infrastructure Manager (IM) in February 2028. This Framework will commence in September 2027 to support TfW's mobilisation activities and ensure operational readiness from Day One (February 2028) of the Infrastructure Manager (IM) transition.
The Framework is intended to provide TfW with access to approved and compliant, temporary maintenance labour providers who can provide reliable, competent and appropriately assured labour in line with the volumes and response times required to meet maintenance demands, including short-notice and out-of-hours labour requirements. 
The multi-lot Framework will be structured to reflect requirements for Contingent Labour specialisms utilising on-track (safety critical) and off-track labour requirements to reflect market specialisms, delivery capability, and the range of requirements required to support the TfW Infrastructure Maintenance (IM) programme.
The Framework is expected to comprise of a multi-lot structure, potentially including:
Lot 1 – On-Track Operatives & Protection Staff
Lot 2 – On-Track Plant (OTP) Operators & Machine / Crane Controllers
Lot 3 – Electrification (OLE/OHLE) Operatives & Isolation Staff
Lot 4 – Civils, Construction & General Trade Operatives
Lot 5 – Plant Operators (Labour only)
Lot 6 – Vegetation Management & Lineside Clearance Operatives
Lot structure is subject to change following market engagement.
The proposed framework structure, scope, and lotting structure is currently under development and will be presented to the market through a supply-chain engagement workshop to support the finalisation of the scope and procurement strategy to ensure it aligns to industry knowledge and capability, emerging trends, and customer needs.
Transport for Wales intends to undertake a formal procurement exercise following completion of its supply chain market engagement activities.

title: CASCADE evidence synthesis and research for JNCC's Areas of Research Interest
description:
2.	 Project Aims
This project will focus on further developing the six agreed JNCC Areas of Research Interest (ARI): 
1)	Integrating novel monitoring technologies for biodiversity and ecosystem health.
2)	Improving predictive and foresight modelling of land/sea use and environmental change.
3)	Optimising the sustainability and resilience of different marine food systems.
4)	Evaluating the impacts of agricultural policies and management regimes.
5)	Identifying evidence needs for funding nature conservation and recovery through market-based approaches.
6)	Strengthening knowledge on the outcomes of conservation and recovery actions.
The project will ensure that for each ARI: 
•	Priority research questions and methodologies are identified;
•	The readiness of novel technologies and data approaches are assessed;
•	Interdisciplinary and cross-sector capability needs are clarified;
•	Policy-relevant evidence gaps and uncertainties are identified; and
•	Coordinated research networks capable of rapid future delivery are established.
3.	Project Background
JNCC, Defra, and wider government require robust, forward-looking evidence to support work towards biodiversity commitments, environmental targets, food security objectives, and international obligations. 
Delays in establishing coherent evidence baselines and research priorities risk duplication of effort, inefficient allocation of future Research & Development (R&D) funding, reduced policy effectiveness, and missed opportunities to integrate emerging technologies and approaches.
The six ARIs all relate to complex challenges requiring interdisciplinary approaches that integrate ecological, socio-economic, technological, governance and policy expertise. With existing evidence bases varying significantly in maturity, methodological consistency, and accessibility to decision-makers. 
The project will support effective future R&D investment and decision-making, and demonstrate a model for rapid, coordinated, cross-institutional research to provide policy-relevant evidence foundations to support the design of targeted research on strategic biodiversity and environmental challenges. 
4.	Project Objectives
To meet the overall aims of this project (Section 2), the objectives are: 
1.	To develop six evidence synthesis reports aligned to JNCC's ARIs. 
•	Each evidence synthesis report will include: 
o	Collation of an evidence database;
o	Evidence synthesis and gaps identification; 
o	Identification of solutions and emerging issues;
o	Incorporation of technical expertise across the CASCADE consortium and JNCC through workshops and review opportunities.
2.	To develop six summary policy briefings and presentations, associated to the finalised ARI evidence synthesis reports.
3.	To develop a cross-cutting recommendations report. 
•	The report will include: 
o	Recommendations for future targeted research investment;
o	Incorporation of technical expertise across the CASCADE consortium and JNCC through workshops and review opportunities.
5.	Project Objectives: Detailed Tasks 
The project is to be delivered across two financial years due to funding allocation timelines. 
The proposed split of work allows progress on Objectives 1 and 2 before the end of the 2026/2027 financial year, with completion of these objectives and Objective 3 in 2027/2028 financial year.  
The proposed objectives will be delivered by end of March 2027 (FY 26/27): 
•	Objective 1- partial delivery
o	Evidence synthesis 1 & 2 will be fully delivered.
o	Evidence synthesis 3 & 4 will be delivered to draft full report stage. 
o	Evidence synthesis 5 & 6 will be delivered to evidence database collation stage. 
•	Objective 2- partial delivery
o	Policy summaries and presentations for evidence synthesis 1 & 2 will be fully delivered. 
The proposed objectives will be delivered by end of September 2027 (FY 27/28):
•	Objective 1- partial delivery to complete
o	Evidence synthesis 3 & 4 will be fully delivered by finalising full report. 
o	Evidence synthesis 5 & 6 will be fully delivered by completing the evidence synthesis, solutions and emerging issues review, incorporation of technical expertise and providing a full report.
•	Objective 2- partial delivery to complete
o	Policy summaries and presentations for evidence synthesis 3,4, 5 and 6 will be fully delivered. 
•	 Objective 3- full delivery 
o	Cross-cutting recommendations report completed.

title: Onasemnogene Abeparvovec Intravenous (Zolgensma®) Service & Onasemnogene Abeparvovec Intrathecal (OAV101 IT) Service
description:
Intention to award the Onasemnogene Abeparvovec Intravenous (Zolgensma®) Service & Onasemnogene Abeparvovec Intrathecal (OAV101 IT) Service.

This is a a one-time, in vivo gene replacement therapy, for use in babies aged 12 months and under, that utilises an adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector, modified to contain a functional copy of the human SMN1 gene. It is administered intravenously, allowing the vector to deliver the gene into motor neurones and peripheral tissues, enabling the sustained expression of survival motor neuron (SMN) protein, which is deficient or mutated in individuals with SMA.

Onasemnogene abeparvovec intrathecal (OAV101 IT) is a one-time in vivo gene replacement therapy for patients with SMA, proposed to treat individuals with SMA aged 2 years and over. This intrathecal injection will be used to treat a distinct cohort of SMA patients to Zolgensma. It will be assessed via NICE’s technology appraisal programme, with an expected final guidance publication date in late 2026.

Procurement was carried out in Lots for the services as detailed above. Contract values are estimated and will be dependent on number of patients actually treated at each awarded provider.

title: Western Range Planning Communications Consultant
description:
The British Museum brings together the history of humankind, all cultures of the world spanning millennia. It connects us to our past and to each other. It is a place where everyone is welcome, where many voices meet to understand, and to question what brings us together and what separates us. It is a place of exploration and a place of inspiration. The collection that the Museum holds in trust for the world is of unparalleled breadth, depth, beauty and significance. A truly global resource, free and available to everyone. The Museum's role is to enhance and make accessible the collection through research, through interpretation, through display, through lending, and to share what it learns, as well as the process of learning, with others. With this matchless position comes a responsibility to ensure that this work can continue, ensuring the collection is cared for and accessible for generations to come, and that the Museum remains a centre of excellence and is continually relevant into the 21st century.
The physical manifestation of the British Museum in Bloomsbury is iconic. It comprises almost an entire city block in one of the most intricate and established parts of central London. It is a treasured national icon within a conservation area that is, in itself, emblematic of the Capital. The Museum has an internal floor area of over 100,000m2, within a footprint that is packed with a diversity of buildings; the estate is Grade I listed, with perimeter properties that are listed Grade II.
Each part of the Museum contains, iconic, often sizeable and irreplaceable items from the collection, and each is visited by many thousands of people, every day. Space on the site is both limited and precious, especially in terms of gallery spaces. The original quadrangle was designed for 100,000 visitors per annum, a figure that was already far exceeded in the 1850s. As it stands, annual visitor numbers to the Museum now regularly exceed six million. Today, there are heightened security requirements and a fundamental need to ensure inclusivity and access, as well as enabling intuitive wayfinding, addressing dilapidations, and creating an environment where people can connect with the collection, and by doing so, with each other.
The Western Range Programme focuses on a substantial part of the estate that is in urgent need of both repair and re-imagining. This offers the Museum an opportunity to make a statement of its future intent, through reimagined galleries, new state-of-the-art storage facilities and engaging contemporary architecture, in juxtaposition to the highly significant and already celebrated listed buildings on the site. A multi-disciplinary design team led by Lina Ghotmeh Architecture has been selected to deliver the Western Range programme which is currently at the end of RIBA Stage 2 in the design process. 
Despite appearing as a single entity, the Western Range comprises a miscellany of 10 separate buildings which have been added to Robert Smirke's original Grade I listed Museum; as a result, the exact extent of the red-line boundary and phasing for this project is dependent on a number of interlocking considerations. The proposed project outline can be seen in the attached documentation. In the region of 15,000m2, it accounts for almost 15% of the floor space within the Bloomsbury site, in a warren of inflexible and static rooms. Further, recent surveys indicate that the existing building fabric and infrastructure are in a state that is below modern expectations. It comprises around 7,500m2 of gallery space and currently houses the Ancient Egypt, Ancient Greece (including the Parthenon Sculptures), Rome, and Ancient Assyria and Middle East collections, along with 4,500m2 of back-of-house collection storage.
The delivery of the Western Range redevelopment will take place within a complex and highly sensitive operational environment, requiring construction works to be carefully planned and coordinated alongside the ongoing activities of the British Museum. As a live cultural institution, the Museum must continue to provide safe and effective access for visitors and staff, while ensuring the protection, movement, and management of its collections throughout the construction period.
The project presents a number of unique challenges, including working within a heritage setting, constrained site conditions, restricted access, neighbouring property interfaces, complex logistics requirements, and the need to coordinate multiple stakeholder requirements. A Planning Communications Consultant is therefore required to provide specialist, project-specific expertise to develop and deliver  coordinated communications services in relation to Town and Country Planning matters for the Western Range programme throughout the pre-application, planning submission, determination and, if instructed, post determination processes. Full details of the scope of services required are contained in the associated tender documents.
Due to the confidential/commercially sensitive nature of information that will be included in the associated tender documents we require that interested suppliers enter into a confidentiality agreement before they are given access to the tender pack.
A copy of the confidentiality agreement is available by request via email to procurement@britishmuseum.org. The terms of the confidentiality agreement are not subject to negotiation.
As soon as practical after the receipt of completed confidentiality agreements, interested suppliers will be granted access to the tender documents.

title: UKRI-6338 R55 Roof Overlay – Supply and Installation
description:
The existing roof covering to R55 Target Station 1 has reached the end of its serviceable life and is experiencing recurring water ingress events which present a risk to scientific operations, equipment, and business continuity. A full roof refurbishment is required to provide a durable, weatherproof building envelope and ensure the facility remains operational for the long term.
The existing roof construction comprises a 1960s Flintkote Monoform roofing system installed over a reinforced wood wool deck, with a subsequent refurbishment undertaken in the 1990s. Investigations have identified widespread deterioration of the roof covering and saturated insulation within part of the southern gutter.
The proposed works comprise refurbishment of approximately 4,800m² of roof covering through installation of a new overlay roofing system, together with localised replacement of failed insulation within the southern gutter area and associated alterations to roof-mounted services and lightning protection systems as required.
A thermal upgrade has been assessed but is not considered technically feasible or economically viable due to the existing roof construction. The proposed roofing solution will therefore focus on delivering a long-life waterproofing system while incorporating a high-reflectivity finish to reduce thermal loading on the building and roof structure.
The project will be undertaken within an operational scientific facility and will require careful coordination with building users, existing plant and equipment and lightning protection systems.

Supply of MGO Fuel to the RRS Discovery - Halifax Oct 2026
description:
Supply of Marine Gas Oil (MGO) to a National Oceanography Centre research vessel.
Delivery D-01: RRS Discovery (IMO No. 9588029), Port of Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada. Estimated quantity 230 metric tonnes. Required on the estimated delivery date 04.08.206.
All quantities are estimates. The final invoiced quantity will be confirmed by the Bunker Delivery Note for the delivery and by the actual density recorded on the Certificate of Analysis at 15 degrees Celsius.
Delivery is by bunker barge or road tank wagon to the vessel at its stated berth.
Fuel must comply with ISO 8217:2024/2017 grade DMA. Sulphur content must not exceed 0.10 per cent by mass, as required within the North American Emission Control Area under MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 14. Flash point must be not less than 60 degrees Celsius, in line with SOLAS. Cold flow properties must be suitable for the vessel's operating area and season. Water content, ash, and total sediment must be within the limits set by ISO 8217 for the grade supplied.
The supplier must be registered on the local fuel oil suppliers register maintained by the relevant authority for the port of delivery, in accordance with MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18.9.
At the time of bunkering the supplier must provide the fuel specification, representative fuel samples drawn in accordance with MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18.8.1 and the sampling guidelines at MEPC.182(59), a Technical Data Sheet with Certificate of Analysis, and a Safety Data Sheet to the Chief Engineer. A Bunker Delivery Note must be provided in the MARPOL Annex VI Appendix V format, stating quantity in metric tonnes, carrying the supplier's signed declaration that the fuel meets the fuel quality requirements of MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18, together with the sulphur content statement and the flash point statement.
