title: National Parking Platform (NPP)
description:
The National Parking Platform (NPP) aggregates parking service providers and facilitates the use by consumers of a wide range of payment providers when parking at locations operated by Birmingham City Council. The platform enables motorists to pay for parking using their preferred parking application and provides a common interface between Birmingham City Council and participating parking payment providers. Under the agreement, the National Parking Platform Limited provides access to and operation of the National Parking Platform, associated integration services and ongoing platform support. The contract provides for reciprocal consideration of £1 between the parties with no other fees payable by either party under the agreement. The National Parking Platform Limited is currently the only organisation operating the National Parking Platform and is the recipient of intellectual property and associated assets developed through the Department for Transport's National Parking Platform programme. Birmingham City Council considered that a direct award was justified pursuant to section 41 and Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023.
Birmingham City Council awarded this contract by way of a direct award pursuant to Section 41 and Schedule 5, Paragraph 6 (Single Supplier) of the Procurement Act 2023. The Council determined that NATIONAL PARKING PLATFORM LIMITED was the only organisation capable of providing access to, operating and supporting the National Parking Platform, including the associated integration services required to enable interoperability between the Council's parking estate and participating parking payment providers.
The Council's assessment concluded that only NATIONAL PARKING PLATFORM LIMITED held the necessary rights, assets, intellectual property and operational control of the National Parking Platform necessary to deliver the required services. On this basis, the Council relied upon the single supplier direct award ground available under Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023.
Following award, the Council undertook a review of the procurement file and associated transparency requirements. Information relating to the award, including details of the supplier, contract value, contract term and the justification supporting the procurement approach, was published through Contracts Finder in order to promote transparency and provide visibility of the award decision.
To further enhance transparency and maintain a complete procurement record, the Council is publishing this Contract Details Notice. Publication of this notice provides additional visibility of the contract arrangement and the basis upon which the award decision was made. This notice is published in the interests of openness, transparency and good procurement governance and does not alter the underlying procurement decision.
The Council retains a documented procurement justification supporting reliance on the single supplier direct award provisions and remains satisfied that the procurement represented an appropriate and proportionate means of securing continued access to the National Parking Platform and associated services. The publication of this Contract Details Notice is intended to provide a clear and comprehensive record of the contract and to further mitigate any residual transparency risk associated with the award.

title: EU harmonised surveillance of AMR E. coli and Salmonella found in beef and pork
description:
The objective of microbiological food safety research themes is to provide robust information on the presence, growth, survival, and elimination of pathogenic microorganisms throughout the food chain; the extent, distribution, causes, risks and burden of foodborne disease will also be considered where appropriate.  The reduction of foodborne disease has been one of FSA’s key objectives in ensuring food safety. The reduction of foodborne disease is a continuing priority, ensuring that food produced and sold in the UK is safe to eat. We are taking a targeted approach to the control and reduction of individual pathogens, with the aim of reducing the overall burden of foodborne disease in the UK.
The FSA are inviting tenders to carry out a survey of antimicrobial resistant (AMR) E. coli found in fresh beef and pork meat on retail sale in the UK in 2027, in accordance with the Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/1729 and Technical specifications on a randomisation of sampling for the purpose of antimicrobial resistance monitoring from food‐producing animals and food as from 2021. The applicant(s) must be familiar with both the Commission’s Decision and technical specifications to ensure the survey is totally compliant with their specific requirements. 
The survey will be awarded in two procurements:
1. Sampling (This procurement):
Survey design, sample collection at retail and transportation to the testing laboratory
2. Testing (Tendered separately):
Microbiological testing, data analysis, reporting and archiving of recovered bacteria and their AMR profile.
By submitting an application, tenders will be bidding to complete the work required for sampling. Suppliers should note that sampling is operationally dependent upon laboratory testing. title: Frankwell Bridge: Design and Build Step-free Ramp incl. Flood Defence Works
description:
Shropshire Council, working with the Environment Agency, is undertaking preliminary market engagement for the supply and installation of permanent flood defences and a step-free access ramp at the northern approach to Frankwell pedestrian bridge, adjacent to the Guildhall, Shrewsbury. Two options are under consideration: Option 1, integrated permanent flood defences including glazed panels, with a step-free ramp landing on the dry side of the defences; and Option 2, a step-free ramp over the existing stepped ramp, landing on the wet side of the existing demountable flood defences. Associated works include foundations, drainage, surfacing, tie-ins to the existing bridge, public realm interfaces and support with statutory approvals, including planning permission in a conservation area and a Flood Risk Activity Permit.
The Council wants the market to identify which option is the best solution and whether it can be delivered ahead of the flood season commencing September 2027. Suppliers will be asked which option they recommend and why; whether they can deliver both options; whether they can deliver the proposed solution and also source and install the flood defence barriers, and which barrier solution they would recommend; an indicative cost band for their proposed solution; their delivery model (direct delivery, subcontracting or supply chain); and the key risks they foresee.
Project progression is subject to a funding application, which feedback from this engagement will directly support. This notice is not a call for competition and the Council is not committed to proceeding with a procurement. Any subsequent procurement would be advertised on the Find a Tender service.

In parallel, the aim is to deliver improved value for money for taxpayers through robust and effective contract management that drive continuous improvement in supplier performance throughout the initial contract term. The Authority therefore wishes to procure a Core IT solution which: • Meets all existing business requirements, providing continuity of service across all Authority operations; • Supports the transition from the current contractual arrangements to the new contract, ensuring minimal disruption to ongoing IT services and operational capability; • Provides flexibility and scalability to accommodate future and evolving business requirements, including changes in operational scope, technology, or user demand; • Maintains the confidentiality, availability, and integrity of all Authority systems, networks, and data in accordance with applicable legislation, security policies and standards; • Ensures the secure storage and management of Authority data, both on-premises and within any approved hosted or cloud environments; • Complies with all relevant current and future requirements relating to IT infrastructure, operational standards, and data protection legislation, including but not limited to UK GDPR and associated security frameworks; • Implements continuous quality enhancements in all areas, identified as requiring improvement, ensuring that service performance and user satisfaction are maintained and developed throughout the contract term; • Supports the adoption of automated services and modern management capabilities to streamline operational processes across both on-premises and cloud-hosted environments, delivering infrastructure services through a standardised, service-oriented model that provides a consistent and simplified user experience regardless of where the underlying data or services are hosted; and • Actively explores and adopts innovative technologies,. including artificial intelligence (AI) and Automation, where such technologies demonstrably streamline processes, enhance efficiency, resilience, and value for money, whether on-premises or cloud. 
The Core Towers are: 
1.	Infrastructure and Hosting Services;

title: Barbican Renewal Programme - Construction logistics services
description:
Barbican Renewal Programme - Construction logistics services.
•	Site-wide construction logistics service supporting the refurbishment of the existing, occupied Barbican Centre, let as a Trade Contract under a Construction Management approach with Blue Sky Building appointed as Construction Manager. The logistics strategy continues to be developed alongside the programme, design and possession strategy.
•	Logistics management and labour: Logistics Manager, supervisors, general logistics operatives, traffic marshals/banksmen, hoist/lift operators, slingers/signallers, gatemen/security, welfare/cleaning staff, fire marshals and out-of-hours/weekend cover.
•	Site accommodation and welfare: survey of the existing accommodation/welfare facilities for re-use, adaptation and ongoing operation for the project duration, assessed against condition, capacity, servicing and the anticipated workforce/programme, with any additional temporary accommodation identified.
•	Site security and access control: hoarding and temporary fencing, pedestrian/vehicle gates, turnstiles, access-control systems, CCTV/security interfaces and visitor management.
•	Traffic and delivery management: delivery booking system, traffic marshals, unloading areas, vehicle/pedestrian segregation, temporary signage, road/pavement protection and cleaning, permits and suspensions.
•	Vertical and horizontal distribution: hoists and/or gantry cranes (with operators) and associated scaffold ramps, platforms and Haki stairs; pallet trucks, trolleys, forklifts/telehandlers, stair climbers, temporary scaffold, edge protection and boarding associated with the logistics scope.
•	Cranes and lifting: coordination of tower crane use, including appointed person(s), lift supervisors, slingers/signallers and banksmen, plus associated lifting equipment.
•	Temporary works and access: temporary stairs, walkways, edge protection, handrails, loading platforms, opening protection, scaffold interfaces and temporary works associated with the logistics installations.
•	Waste management: bins and segregation, floor-by-floor collection, skips, compactors, removal/disposal, hazardous-waste arrangements, transfer documentation and environmental reporting.

title: Support for Victims of Modern Slavery (SVMS) Contract
description:
Modern Slavery is an umbrella term that encompasses human trafficking, slavery, servitude and forced or compulsory labour. It cruelly destroys the lives of victims who are exploited by criminals for profit, often in seemingly legitimate businesses. The Modern Slavery Unit, within the Home Office's Modern Slavery Directorate, is responsible for leading the Government's response to modern slavery.
Modern slavery is a barbaric crime that dehumanises people for profit. The Government is committed to tackling it in all its forms and to giving survivors the support and certainty they need to recover. The UK is committed to meeting its obligations and to providing effective support to ensure that victims are assisted in their recovery from their experiences of exploitation or trafficking. 
These obligations are currently met through the Modern Slavery Victim Care Contract (MSVCC) which provides specialist support to adult victims of exploitation and trafficking identified through the NRM in England and Wales, as well as support delivered through wider state services.
The new Support for Victims of Modern Slavery (SVMS) contract will replace the MSVCC. The SVMS service will lift modern slavery victims out of exploitation, keep them safe, and provide temporary tailored needs-based support to assist them in their recovery and reduce their risk of re-exploitation. It will be innovative, flexible, responsive to demand, and adaptive to the needs of Service Users. It will facilitate the smooth transition of Service Users out of the service when contracted support is no longer required, through alignment with other statutory services and productive partnerships with statutory and non-statutory organisations. It will harness new data and technology advancements to support Service Users and deliver contract efficiency.
The following key pillars and enablers will be required as part of SVMS service provision. 
Support worker: each Service User is assigned a Support Worker who plays a central role in their recovery. Support Workers complete the assessment process, develop Support Plans and conduct monthly support meetings with Service Users to review progress and adjust support as needed. This includes providing referrals, advocacy and access to services across social, legal, psychological and health domains. Support Workers operate to defined minimum standards to ensure a high quality and consistent level of support across all cases, receive enhanced, trauma-informed training and have access to specialist resources for complex cases. Emphasis is placed on consistency of care, ensuring that Service Users experience reliable and coordinated support across geographical areas. Suppliers shall respond to the needs of staff, ensuring their safety and supporting their overall well-being. 
Accommodation: Service Users at risk of re-exploitation or destitution can access safe accommodation that meets their needs and level of independence. A range of shared single sex, family and individual units will be available, which must meet minimum standards stipulated in the Authority's requirements and be regularly and well maintained. A transport service safely transports Service Users to the accommodation and on to alternative accommodation when they are required to exit. Most Service Users will not require accommodation from the service and will receive outreach support.
Financial support: Service Users will be paid means-tested financial support payments to meet their essential living needs and recovery needs. A deposit grant and move-in funding is available to help eligible Service Users secure suitable long-term accommodation.
Psychological assistance: Service Users are entitled to psychological assistance, including a Mental Health Assessment by a qualified healthcare professional. Should the assessor deem local NHS service wait times do not align to the urgency of the identified need, the Service User would be in scope to receive short-term therapeutic support. This support is documented in a Psychological Support Plan. Referrals are made by Support Workers, and therapy is primarily delivered remotely to increase accessibility. 
Digital tools and technology: The service includes digital solutions to enhance accessibility and engagement, including streamlined data capture and sharing across the contract, automated translation and interpretation, a victim portal for Service Users to access personal information and track progress, and a resource hub with information on rights, entitlements, and external services. The Supplier will design, maintain, and report on these systems as part of monitoring and evaluation.
Partnership working across the supply chain and a range of external support providers and stakeholders such as local authorities, job centres, GPs and asylum support services will ensure Service Users can access longer-term support pathways and transition to independence outside the service.

The City invites Quotations for the provision of its GLA London Talent Pathways project, with contract opportunities for up to 2 tenderers. The project is a Mayor of London–led funding initiative that supports vocational training for London residents aged 19+ to help them gain skills for priority jobs in key sectors. The programme addresses skills shortages, supports under‑represented groups, and links training directly to the skills businesses need. It aims to provide services that reflects the skills needs of London’s employers and key growth sectors, is responsive to economic change and opens up opportunities for all Londoners. The funding aims to create clear, supported pathways into good work, especially for those who have been historically underrepresented in London’s growth sectors. This includes Londoners facing barriers due to income, disability or health being supported to access quality training and progress into good jobs. 
London Talent Pathways combines ASF and Free Courses for Jobs (FCfJ) funding that will provide Londoners with further vocational training opportunities to upskill and progress into priority occupations within key London sectors.  The project will run until the end of March 2028 initially with an optional third year of funding until March 2029 dependent on the quality and performance of contractual delivery. The maximum funding value will be up to £80,000 for each successful bidder, with a potential additional £20,000 funding upon successful delivery, subject to agreement from all parties.   
Quality and performance monitoring will be monthly and payments will be monthly based on validation and quality assurance of evidence in line with GLA London Talent Pathways specifications; evidence of enrolment, progression and completion will be required to trigger related learner payments*.  The successful tenderer will submit their monthly return by the last day of each month.  
The tender submission will include planned learner numbers, course/s duration and related estimated costings to maximise the £80,000 funding value within the contract duration.  Learner retention targets will be agreed based on the contract delivery plan and forecasted learner numbers.  There is no specified minimum and maximum number of learners, the course duration will be a maximum of 12 months, and all learning will be completed before the end of March 2028. The project will run until the end of March 2028 initially with an optional third year of funding until March 2029 dependent on the quality and performance of contractual delivery.

description:
Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (The Authority) requires a Supplier to undertake relevant six facet surveys across the entirety of its estate (The Services).
The purpose of the Services is to update the Physical Condition, Functional Stability, Space Utilisation, Quality, Statutory Compliance and Environmental facets across its Nottingham City Hospital, Queen's Medical Centre and Ropewalk House sites (The Premises and Locations).
The objective is to establish a refreshed baseline identifying unpalatable risk across the estate to align with the objectives and targets of the Authority's relevant strategies and to inform an action plan for any remediation that may be required.
The Services shall include the six facet surveys and gathering of relevant data in accordance with applicable industry standards whilst ensuring consistency of results between the various surveys required.
The Services shall enable the Authority to determine the condition and risk for each facet element and allocate condition categories to its Premises and Locations on a “per facet” basis.
Together with a summary of remedial works required, photos of non-compliant areas and estimated costs to bring each facet to a safe and acceptable condition, the six facet survey shall assist the Authority in prioritising budget allocation to the relevant critical areas.  This information will support the Authority’s backlog maintenance reporting and Estates Return Information Collection (ERIC) information.
To enable successful provision of the Services, as a minimum, the Supplier shall:
a) lead on the production and collation of relevant asset survey reports 
b) provide the Services:
(i) in accordance with the Authority’s budgets
(ii) in line with its Programme
c) ensure successful outcomes achieving the Authority’s required level of quality
d) provide technical management of the survey including, but not limited to, survey activities, data collection and production, access and Permits [DS1] to Work under the direction of the Contract Manager
e) collate the data captured during the relevant surveys and develop of a detailed overarching technical report that will enable the Authority to develop its subsequent estates strategy

title: Manchester Piccadilly Strategic Regeneration Framework (SRF) Update
description:
The Manchester Piccadilly area (the 'study area') is of national strategic significance, serving as a major gateway to Manchester city centre and the Greater Manchester city region and beyond. Anchored by Piccadilly Station, the district is set to evolve into a world-class, highly productive, and connected destination.
Manchester Piccadilly station serves as a central transport hub for the city, and is at the centre of the planned Northern Powerhouse Rail ('NPR') network. Manchester City Council ('the Council') strongly believes that the optimal solution for the proposed NPR station at Manchester Piccadilly is for an underground through station, which would unlock the full potential of the study area, maximising transport connectivity and the long-term economic and social benefits of investment.
The Council is seeking to appoint a consultancy team to provide a SRF for the study area (building upon the previous Manchester Piccadilly SRF), based around the anticipated growth opportunity and connectivity benefits provided by the NPR and other investment proposals, aligned with the Council's ambitions and policies. This work should review, and incorporate existing, and update new regeneration areas within the study area.
While the study will concentrate on the 'Piccadilly Central' and the 'Ardwick' areas, a key aspect of this commission will be to integrate and harmonise the outputs of the Manchester Piccadilly SRF with those of the adjacent and related SRFs, to produce a coherent, comprehensive and integrated strategy, which can maximise economic and social benefits.
Further information is provided in the Specification.
This Procurement is being conducted in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and Procurement Regulations 2024, using the Open Tender Procedure. The documentation published with this opportunity describes how the procurement will be conducted, including details of the associated procurement timetable and award criteria and how to respond to this opportunity.
Suppliers are strongly encouraged to read the documentation including the appendices and all other documentation published as part of this Invitation to Tender, as failure to comply with the information in the documentation may result in exclusion from the Procurement and/or the rejection of any submission.
Manchester City Council invites tenders for the provision of the Services, from organisations with relevant experience and technical ability to demonstrate sufficient capacity for providing the Services.
It is intended for the contract to commence 18 January 2027.
The estimated total value of the opportunity is £250,000 (including Work Packages 1-4) over the total contract period although Suppliers should note that this is only an estimate to give Suppliers an idea of the potential scale of the opportunity.
Bidders should ensure that their proposed team collectively possesses all relevant skills, qualifications, experience and resources necessary to deliver an adoptable Strategic Regeneration Framework, in line with the Specification. Where all required expertise is not held within a single organisation, bidders may wish to consider forming appropriate consortium, joint venture, or subcontracting arrangements.
Where a consortium, joint venture, or subcontracting arrangement is proposed, bidders should clearly identify the proposed structure, the role and responsibilities of each organisation, and how the combined team will provide the requisite expertise and capacity to successfully deliver the contract.
It is envisaged that the contract will be awarded to one (1) lead provider or consortium.

Contracts for Innovation Cymru - Reducing Missed Appointments and Improving Access to Planned Care
description:
Challenge Overview
Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board (CTM UHB) experiences persistently high rates of missed outpatient appointments, with approximately 64,000 appointments missed over the last 12 months. These missed appointments create challenges for patients and services alike, contributing to longer waiting times, underutilised clinical capacity, financial inefficiencies and poorer patient experience. 
CTM estimates that missed appointments may account for approximately £9.6 million of avoidable lost value each year, representing a significant opportunity to improve both patient access and the use of NHS resources.
Evidence suggests that non-attendance is often linked to a range of practical, behavioural, communication and accessibility barriers rather than a simple choice not to attend. These barriers can include challenges associated with appointment communication, transport, geography, caring responsibilities, socioeconomic factors, digital exclusion, health inequalities and service design. 
Contracts for Innovation Cymru (CfIC) is seeking innovative solutions that help people overcome these barriers, reducing missed appointments whilst improving access to planned care.
The challenge is deliberately open and does not prescribe a particular technology, product or service. We welcome ideas from a wide range of sectors and disciplines and encourage applicants to think creatively about how attendance, access and patient experience can be improved.
We are seeking innovative approaches that help reduce missed appointments and improve access to planned care.
Solutions may address one or more aspects of the challenge, including but not limited to:
•	Appointment communication and engagement
•	Accessibility of information
•	Appointment planning and management
•	Behavioural approaches that encourage attendance
•	Identification of individuals at increased risk of non-attendance
•	Travel and accessibility barriers
•	Digital tools and services
•	Community-based support models
•	Service and pathway redesign
•	Data-driven approaches to improve attendance and access
Applicants are encouraged to consider how different barriers interact and how solutions may support a diverse population with differing needs and circumstances.
We are not seeking a predetermined solution and welcome a broad range of innovative approaches.
________________________________________
In Scope
We are interested in solutions that can contribute to one or more of the following:
•	Improving appointment attendance and reducing missed appointments.
•	Improving access to planned care services.
•	Appointment communication and engagement.
•	Accessibility of information and services.
•	Appointment planning, scheduling and management.
•	Behavioural approaches that support attendance.
•	Identification of people at increased risk of non-attendance.
•	Reducing practical barriers to accessing services.
•	Data-driven, digital or technology-enabled approaches.
•	Community-based or service redesign approaches.
•	Improving equity of access across different populations and geographic settings.
•	Welsh language, accessibility and inclusive service delivery.
Out of Scope
We are not seeking projects that:
•	Focus solely on increasing demand for healthcare services.
•	Are primarily academic or research studies with no credible route to implementation.
•	Require extensive fundamental research before development can commence.
•	Cannot demonstrate a realistic route to adoption within health and care services.
•	Do not consider affordability, scalability or long-term sustainability.
•	Rely solely on English-language patient-facing delivery.
•	Seek to replace appropriate clinical oversight or professional judgement where this remains necessary.
________________________________________
Desired Outcomes
Successful solutions should demonstrate potential to deliver measurable improvements in one or more of the following areas.
Patients and Citizens
•	Improved access to planned care services
•	Increased appointment attendance
•	Improved patient experience
•	Reduced travel and logistical burden
•	Better health outcomes through more timely access to care
•	Fairer access irrespective of location, income or personal circumstances
Staff
•	Improved clinic utilisation
•	Reduced administrative burden
•	More effective use of clinical time
•	Improved operational efficiency
Health and Care Systems
•	Reduced DNA rates
•	Improved productivity and service flow
•	Reduced waiting times
•	Better use of public resources
•	Reduced health inequalities
•	Improved sustainability and environmental outcomes
Potential measures of success may include attendance rates, service utilisation, waiting times, patient experience, equity measures, operational efficiency and value for money.
Funding and Support 
Phase 1 Funding 
Funding Available: £200,000 total budget to support a portfolio of projects.
The total funding available for the competition can change and the funders reserve the right to adjust the provisional funding allocations, i.e., should additional funding become available. 
Number of Projects: Current funding is available to support a portfolio of projects, dependent upon the number/quality of submissions received. 
Portfolio Approach 
Funding decisions may be made using a portfolio approach, recognising that complex challenges often require a range of complementary solutions rather than a single intervention. Consideration will be given to the overall balance of projects supported, the evidence generated and the potential for wider adoption and learning across Wales.

title: Contracts for Innovation Cymru - Transforming Multi-Agency Safeguarding for High-Risk Domestic Abuse in South Wales
description:
Domestic abuse remains one of the most significant public protection challenges facing South Wales. For people assessed as being at highest risk of serious harm or homicide, timely safeguarding interventions and effective multi-agency coordination can be critical in reducing harm and improving safety outcomes.
South Wales Police and its partners currently deliver safeguarding through the Multi-Agency Risk Assessment Conference (MARAC)  process. MARAC is a long-established mechanism that brings organisations together to share information, assess risk and coordinate actions for victims experiencing high-risk domestic abuse. It remains one of the most important safeguarding arrangements available to public services and plays a vital role in protecting some of the most vulnerable people in society. 
However, the current model is under increasing pressure. Across South Wales, more than 5,000 high-risk domestic abuse cases are managed annually through seven separate MARAC arrangements operating across Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan, Rhondda Cynon Taf, Merthyr Tydfil, Bridgend, Neath Port Talbot and Swansea. Together, these arrangements account for approximately 44% of MARAC demand across Wales. Different governance structures, processes and operating approaches have evolved over time, resulting in variation in delivery, increasing administrative burden and challenges in maintaining consistency across the region. 
Demand continues to increase whilst cases become more complex. In some areas, approximately 70 cases may be discussed during a single weekly MARAC process, and concerns have been raised regarding delays between referral, discussion and action. National reviews, safeguarding investigations and wider research have highlighted issues relating to fragmented information sharing, inconsistent processes and delays in identifying and responding to escalating risk. 
South Wales Police, working alongside regional MARAC governance groups, the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner and wider safeguarding partners, has identified an opportunity to explore whether a different approach could deliver faster, more consistent and more effective safeguarding outcomes. The challenge has been developed following significant stakeholder engagement and reflects a shared recognition that future approaches may need to move beyond the traditional meeting-based MARAC model. 
________________________________________
The Challenge
We are seeking innovative organisations to help South Wales Police and its partners explore how high-risk domestic abuse safeguarding could operate differently in the future.
This challenge is intentionally outcome-focused and does not prescribe a specific technology, product type or delivery model.
Applicants are encouraged to propose the approach they believe will best address the challenge and demonstrate how their expertise could help develop a more responsive, coordinated and sustainable safeguarding model for South Wales.
The challenge is not simply about introducing new technology or digitising existing MARAC meetings. Whilst technology, data and artificial intelligence may form part of the solution, partners have identified the need to explore wider service, governance and operating model redesign.
We are interested in organisations capable of helping answer questions such as:
•	How can risk be identified, prioritised and escalated more effectively?
•	How can organisations work together more dynamically and efficiently?
•	How can safeguarding actions be coordinated more effectively across agencies?
•	How can professionals spend less time managing administration and more time safeguarding vulnerable people?
•	How can information be shared more effectively whilst maintaining appropriate governance and accountability?
•	How can future models remain practical, affordable and sustainable?
•	How can innovation support improved safeguarding outcomes without creating additional complexity?
Applicants should not assume that technology alone is the answer. We welcome proposals that combine service design, systems thinking, operational redesign, governance innovation, behavioural approaches, digital innovation, data, analytics and artificial intelligence to explore how multi-agency safeguarding could evolve. 
________________________________________
Desired Outcomes
We are interested in approaches that can contribute towards measurable improvements in one or more of the following areas.
Safeguarding Outcomes
•	Earlier identification of escalating risk.
•	Faster safeguarding interventions.
•	Improved protection for people at highest risk of harm.
•	Reduced repeat victimisation.
•	Improved management of complex and repeat cases.
•	Better safeguarding outcomes for victims and families. 
Victim Experience
•	More consistent safeguarding support regardless of location.
•	Improved coordination between agencies.
•	Reduced delays in accessing support.
•	More responsive safeguarding interventions.
•	Improved confidence in safeguarding processes.
•	More person-centred approaches to safety planning. 
Professional Practice
•	Reduced administrative burden.
•	Better access to relevant information.
•	Improved coordination and communication between organisations.
•	Better visibility of decisions and actions.
•	Improved accountability and action tracking.
•	More professional time focused on safeguarding activity. 
Service Delivery and Equity
•	Reduced variation between different MARAC arrangements.
•	More consistent safeguarding approaches across South Wales.
•	Improved information sharing.
•	Better visibility of risk.
•	More equitable safeguarding outcomes regardless of geography.
•	Improved partnership working. 
System Outcomes
•	Better use of public resources.
•	Reduced duplication of activity.
•	Improved operational intelligence.
•	Improved governance and oversight.
•	Stronger evidence for future service transformation.
•	Improved understanding and measurement of safeguarding outcomes. 
Sustainability
•	Affordable and scalable approaches.
•	Long-term sustainability beyond the funded project period.
•	A realistic route to implementation.
•	Approaches capable of supporting future adoption in other regions where appropriate.
•	Creation of capability that can support future safeguarding transformation. 
Applicants should clearly identify which outcomes their project is expected to influence and explain how impact will be assessed.
Phase 1: Discovery and Concept Development 
This challenge is being delivered as a Phase 1 Contracts for Innovation Cymru competition. 
South Wales Police and partners recognise that this is a complex system challenge. Whilst the need for change has been identified, there is not yet a single agreed solution or future model. This competition is therefore focused on discovery, exploration, evidence generation and concept development. 
We are seeking organisations capable of helping define what a future safeguarding model might look like, which has the potential for scalability across other MARAC areas and what practical steps may be required to implement it. 
Funding Allocation and Project Details 
Competition Type: Phase 1 Discovery and Concept Development 
Funding Available: Up to £60k per project  
Number of Projects: Up to 6 projects  
The total funding available for the competition can change and the funders reserve the right to adjust the provisional funding allocations, i.e., should additional funding become available

title: Contracts for Innovation Cymru - Modernising the Bowel Screening Pathway in Wales
description:
Innovative solutions to improve participant assessment, triage support and progression following a positive FIT result
Introduction
Bowel cancer is one of the most common cancers in Wales, with over 2,200 new cases diagnosed each year , and early diagnosis remains one of the most important factors in improving patient outcomes. It is more common as people get older, with most cases diagnosed in those over 50.
Bowel Screening Wales  plays a vital role in identifying people aged 50-74 who might be at increased risk of bowel cancer, through the routine use of an at home stool sample kit, known as Faecal Immunochemical Testing (FIT) . Each year, more than 500,000 people are invited to participate in bowel screening, with around 12,000 participants receiving a positive FIT result and requiring further assessment  and investigation.
Following a positive FIT result, screening participants are informed to contact the national bowel screening administration team to make a mutually convenient appointment for a nurse-led pre-colonoscopy assessment. This assessment is predominantly undertaken by telephone and uses a standardised assessment form with questions designed to determine an individual's suitability for colonoscopy, identify clinical risks and ensure participants receive the support they need before further investigation. The assessment lasts between 30 and 60 minutes, depending on the level of complexity. Appointments are available Monday to Friday, 9am to 4pm, and this is currently the only option available to screening participants.
The current process was established when the Bowel Screening Wales programme launched in 2008 and has remained largely unchanged since that time. Whilst the pathway continues to provide a safe and effective means of assessment, the environment in which it operates has changed considerably. Bowel Screening participation has increased, eligibility has expanded, workforce pressures have intensified and public expectations around digital access, communication and convenience have evolved.
Bowel Screening Wales is therefore seeking innovative approaches that can support service modernisation, improve participant experience, improve the timeliness of pre-colonoscopy assessments and strengthen the ability of NHS Wales to meet future demand.
________________________________________
The Challenge
Current pre-colonoscopy assessment processes remain heavily reliant on manual and telephone-based activity during routine office hours (Mon-Fri. 9-4pm). This can limit access for screening participants (especially those of working age), create pressure on specialist nursing teams, contribute to variation in waiting times and participant experience, and limit opportunities to make better use of participant information resources (i.e. current inability to signpost participants to digital resources and video content).
We are seeking innovative solutions that can improve access to timely assessments, provide increased flexibility for participants to undertake an assessment, enables participants to have more control over their engagement with the service, including the possibility of them booking their own appointment slots following assessment. In addition, the innovation should have the ability to enable the screening programme to triage participants for appropriate investigations and stratify individuals for timely interventions based on clinical need following a positive FIT result.
The challenge is outcome focused and does not prescribe a specific technology, product type or delivery model.
Applicants are encouraged to propose the approach they believe will best address the challenge and demonstrate how their solution could be adapted, developed or enhanced to meet the needs of Bowel Screening Wales.
We are not seeking to specify a single solution in advance. The purpose of this challenge is to support the development and demonstration of solutions that can address the underlying service need as described above whilst creating foundations for future improvement.
Phase 2: Development and Real-World Demonstration 
This challenge is being delivered as a Phase 2 Contracts for Innovation competition. 
We are seeking organisations with existing technologies, products, platforms, or solutions that require adaptation, enhancement, or development to meet the needs of Bowel Screening Wales. 
Projects should support the development, refinement, and real-world demonstration of innovative approaches capable of improving participant assessment, triage and pathway management following a positive FIT result. 
The expectation is that solutions will be deployed and evaluated in a real-world setting where appropriate, enabling learning from practical implementation to inform ongoing refinement and future development throughout the project. 
Funding Allocation and Project Details 
Competition Type: Phase 2 Development and Real-World Demonstration 
Total Funding Available: £ 300,000 
Number of Projects Anticipated: Current funding of £300,000, excluding VAT, is available to fund 4-5 projects which may be subject to change. 
The total funding available for the competition can change and the funders reserve the right to adjust the provisional funding allocations, I.e., should additional funding become available. 
Portfolio Approach 
This challenge is open to applications that deliver a Phase 2 development and real-world demonstration project. Current funding of up to £300,000 is available to support up to 4-5 projects which may be subject to change, dependent upon the number/quality of submissions received. 
All costs must be clearly justified and value for money demonstrated with willingness for appropriate contributions from the provider to help deliver the project. We reserve the right to consider an increased budget for exceptional applications if the scale of the delivery across Wales warrants it.    
Please note any adoption and implementation of a solution from this competition would be subject of a separate, possible competitive, procurement exercise. This competition does not cover the purchase of any solution although we may choose to investigate and explore innovative procurement routes as part of this challenge.

title: Contracts for Innovation Cymru - Ending Abandonment After Stroke
description:
Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability in Wales and affects around 7,000 people each year. While survival rates continue to improve, many people experience a significant reduction in support once they leave hospital at a stage when rehabilitation remains critical to recovery and long-term independence. Around 45% of stroke survivors report feeling abandoned following discharge because they do not receive the support they need to recover well. 
The impact extends far beyond the individual. Variations in access to rehabilitation, follow-up support and community services can lead to poorer outcomes, increased carer burden, avoidable demand on health and care services, and significant societal and economic costs. Stroke currently costs NHS Wales approximately £220 million per year and the wider Welsh economy approximately £1.63 billion annually. Without intervention, these costs are expected to increase significantly. 
The challenge has been developed following extensive investigation across Wales involving clinicians, health boards, national leaders, stroke survivors, carers and the Stroke Association. This work has helped define the challenge, identify unmet needs, understand existing service variation and explore the current market landscape. The conclusion is clear: Wales requires innovative, scalable approaches that can strengthen recovery, improve experience, reduce feelings of abandonment and support more equitable outcomes beyond hospital discharge. 
The challenge aligns with the Welsh Government Quality Statement for Stroke, which places renewed emphasis on rehabilitation, recovery, person-centred care and ensuring that stroke survivors do not feel abandoned during their recovery journey.
The Challenge
We are seeking innovative solutions that can improve rehabilitation, recovery and long-term support for stroke survivors.
Access to rehabilitation and follow-up support varies across Wales. As a result, outcomes can depend too heavily on where a person lives rather than on their clinical need. This challenge seeks innovative approaches that can improve equity of access and help ensure people can receive high-quality rehabilitation and recovery support regardless of geography, including those living in rural, remote, underserved and seldom heard communities across Wales. 
The challenge is outcome-focused and does not prescribe a specific technology, product type or delivery model.
Applicants are encouraged to propose the approach they believe will best address the challenge and demonstrate how their solution could be adapted, developed or enhanced to meet the needs of NHS Wales and stroke survivors.
We are not seeking to specify a single solution in advance. The purpose of this challenge is to support the development, demonstration and evaluation of innovative approaches that can improve recovery, reduce feelings of abandonment and create foundations for sustainable improvement across Wales.
Particular consideration should be given to how solutions can improve access to rehabilitation and recovery support for people who may face barriers associated with geography, transport, service availability, digital exclusion, workforce capacity or being within a seldom-heard group.
The challenge is not simply about providing more therapy. We are interested in approaches that enable personalised, continuous and motivating rehabilitation and self-management support across home, community and outpatient settings whilst supporting better experiences and outcomes for stroke survivors.
This challenge is being delivered as a Phase 2 Contracts for Innovation competition. In contrast to a Phase 1 competition, focusing on feasibility, we are seeking organisations with existing technologies, products, platforms, services or rehabilitation approaches that require adaptation, enhancement, configuration or further development to address the identified needs of stroke survivors, carers and rehabilitation services across Wales.
This challenge follows significant investigation and engagement to understand the problem, review evidence, define requirements and explore potential market solutions. We are therefore seeking solutions with an established foundation. Early-stage concepts requiring fundamental research or proof-of-concept development are unlikely to be supported
Projects should support the development, adaptation and real-world demonstration of innovative approaches capable of improving rehabilitation, recovery and life after stroke.
Successful projects are expected to generate practical evidence relating to:
•	Patient and carer outcomes.
•	Rehabilitation outcomes.
•	User experience.
•	Service and workforce impact.
•	Affordability and sustainability.
•	Adoption readiness.
•	Future scalability.
Applicants should describe in-detail:
•	What they propose to deliver.
•	How it will be tested and evaluated.
•	How impact will be measured.
•	How the solution could evolve in future. 
•	A core delivery plan to 31 March 2027, including activities, milestones, deliverables and costs. 
Applicants should describe in outline:
•	A separate proposal for a potential further stage beyond April 2027, including the additional activities, deliverables, outcomes, milestones, timescales and costs. 
•	How the further stage would build on the evidence and learning generated during the core project. 
•	What additional value the further stage would deliver for stroke survivors, services and the wider recovery pathway. 
•	How the core project would remain viable and deliver meaningful outputs if further funding does not become available.
Funding Allocation and Project Details 
Competition Type: Phase 2 Development and Real-World Demonstration 
Funding Available: £300,000 Total budget to support a portfolio of projects
The total funding available for the competition can change and the funders reserve the right to adjust the provisional funding allocations, i.e., should additional funding become available. 
Number of Projects: Current funding is available to support a portfolio of projects, dependent upon the number/quality of submissions received. 
Portfolio Approach 
Funding decisions may be made using a portfolio approach, recognising that improving recovery and reducing abandonment after stroke is a complex challenge that may benefit from multiple complementary solutions rather than a single intervention. 
Consideration may be given to the overall balance of projects supported, the evidence generated, opportunities for collaboration between projects and the potential for wider adoption and learning across Wales. 
Solutions may address different aspects of rehabilitation, self-management, recovery, service coordination, family support, accessibility, digital capability, assistive technology, data, analytics or outcomes measurement. Collectively, these may contribute towards the wider ambition of improving life after stroke across Wales.  
Potential further funding: Additional funding may become available to support a further stage of development or demonstration beyond April 2027. This funding is not currently confirmed and should not be assumed as part of the initial project award. Any decision to provide further funding would be subject to funding availability, project performance, evidence of value and the priorities of the challenge partners.

title: Holiday Short Breaks For Children and Young People
description:
The Council is seeking providers of Group Based School Holiday Short Breaks Services for children and young people with disabilities. Informal expressions of interest in the provision of these services are sought at this stage in order to establish the level of market interest.
Short breaks are intended to have positive benefits for both disabled children and young people (0-25 years) and their parents and carers. The main aims of short break services are to provide disabled children and young people the opportunity to:
• Spend time away from their parents and carers
• Relax and have fun to develop friendships
• Develop their independence.
They also give families an opportunity to have a break from their caring responsibilities; and spend time with other members of their family. Short break provision can range from a few hours per week to an allocated number of activity days/breaks per year.
Short breaks can include day, evening, weekend activities, school holidays and after school. It can also include befriending and enabling young people to access leisure-based activities, transition support and independence skills. The services may take place in the child or young person’s own home, or an activity centre or community setting.
The provision of short breaks is considered an important part of the support provided to families of disabled children and young people.
The service is for children and young people with disabilities aged 5 – 18 with a wide range of needs including complex behavioural and medical conditions. The new contract is scheduled to commence on 24th July 2027. It is anticipated that the contract will be for a period of three years with two possible extensions of up to two years each, dependent on performance.
The council is intending to issue one tender separated into three Lots. This will be one Tender Notice made up of three Lots, one for each contract, leading to three separate evaluations, contract awards and contracts.
One service is to be provided for each contract as follows:
Service 1:
Specification: Short Breaks during school holidays for Low to Medium Level Needs. These will be focused on Physical Activity with other types of activities also available. Provider to deliver a minimum of 5 hours per day for a minimum of 23 days per annum.
Service 2:
Specification: Short Breaks during school holidays for High Medical Need and Mobility Needs. These will be mainly arts, crafts and other creative activities. Provider to deliver a minimum of 6 hours per day for a minimum of 29 days per annum.
Service 3:
Specification: Short Breaks Hub arrangements during school holidays for Low to High Level Needs. Lead provider to identify and coordinate community resources i.e. a range of providers delivering a minimum of 5 hours per day for a minimum of 24 days per annum.

title: UK2 Notice: Preliminary Market Engagement - Asylum Seeker Travel Services
description:
The Home Office (the Authority) has a statutory duty under Section 55 of the Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009 to discharge its immigration and asylum functions having regard to the need to safeguard and promote the welfare of children in the UK. 
In addition to this, under the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999, the Home Office has a statutory obligation to provide temporary support for Asylum Seekers who appear to be destitute or are likely to become destitute within a prescribed period.  
These obligations include Unaccompanied Asylum-Seeking Children (UASC) who arrive in the UK and enter the immigration system without a parent or guardian as well as an adult Asylum Seeker Cohort.
The service includes the arrangement of transport on behalf of local authorities, as well as the Home Office, for the movement of UASC when these movements are required. A number of core business units will utilise this contract. Further details will be provided through additional materials that will be made available to parties, upon completion and receipt of a signed Non-Disclosure Agreement (more information for which is set out in this document). 
This service will not be used for Home Office staff transport and is intended as a civilian travel programme only.  The Home Office is still considering all of its options with regards to aggregation and disaggregation and therefore encourages suppliers who may not be able to deliver the full scope of services to still participate in any subsequent market engagement activity.
The purpose of this engagement is to better understand market capability, capacity, delivery models, and commercial approaches available to support the future service. Information regarding service requirements, volumes and operational arrangement will be shared with interested organisations as part of this engagement activity. Please refer to “Engagement process description” below.
The content of this Notice, including the estimated contract value and indicative contract timelines, is subject to change and does not commit the Authority to commence any procurement process.

title: Adult Advocacy Service
description:
Adult Advocacy Service
Swindon Borough Council invites expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced service providers for the provision of adult advocacy service.
Project Description
The Council is seeking to award a single supplier contract for the provision of an integrated Adult Advocacy Service. This requirement will not be divided into Lots. TUPE does apply. The contract will be for an initial period of three years, with the option to extend for up to a further two years.
Swindon Borough Council is seeking to commission an independent, person-centred and out-come-focused Adult Advocacy Service that enables people to have their voices heard, under-stand and exercise their rights, and participate fully in decisions that affect their lives. The ser-vice will support adults to access appropriate care, support and services and ensure that they are able to influence decisions affecting their health, wellbeing and independence.
Advocacy plays a vital role in promoting independence, protecting individual rights and ensuring that people can express their views, wishes and feelings. The service will support individuals who may experience barriers to participation, including people with learning disabilities, autism, mental health needs, dementia, physical or sensory impairments, older people, and those experiencing disadvantage or vulnerability.
The successful provider will be required to deliver a range of statutory advocacy functions through an integrated service model, including:
•	Independent Care Act Advocacy (ICAA)
•	Independent Mental Capacity Advocacy (IMCA)
•	Independent Mental Health Advocacy (IMHA)
•	Independent Health Complaints Advocacy (IHCA)
•	Independent Social Care Complaints Advocacy
•	Court of Protection Representation and Advocacy
•	Relevant Person's Representative (RPR) type role
•	Support to the Learning Disability Partnership Board (LDPB) and associated engagement activities.
The Council is seeking a provider that can deliver a high-quality, accessible and responsive advocacy service that promotes voice, choice and control, reduces inequalities, safeguards rights and improves outcomes for people who may otherwise struggle to engage with complex health and social care systems.
The successful provider will work collaboratively with Swindon Borough Council, health partners, care providers, the voluntary and community sector and other stakeholders to ensure advocacy is embedded within wider care and support pathways. The provider will adopt a rights-based approach, actively tackle barriers to inclusion and ensure equitable access to advocacy services across the Borough.
The Council's vision is to commission a sustainable and high-quality advocacy service that supports people to live independent and fulfilling lives whilst contributing to the wider ambitions of the Swindon Plan and Adult Services Strategy, including promoting independence, reducing inequalities and ensuring people have "Lives, Not Services".

title: Hosting Capability Supplier Procurement
description:
The Home Office Enterprise Networks & Infrastructure function is preparing an award with competition to procure a Hosting Capability Supplier. The successful supplier will provide a comprehensive 24x7x365 operational support capability, alongside outcome-based engineering, transformation, and service delivery services across the Home Office technology estate. The objective is to establish a simplified and integrated operating model that delivers improved service resilience, enhanced automation, accelerated technology transformation, and a single point of accountability for hosting-related services.
The scope of the requirement is expected to include:
•	Platform services spanning on-premise, cloud and hybrid environments.
•	Hosting, cloud, network and infrastructure operational support and engineering services.
•	Legacy infrastructure and application support, including the transformation and modernisation of services to align with future-state technology strategies.
•	Technology services covering datacentre, platform, storage, backup, virtualisation, operating systems, network infrastructure, cloud services and associated management tooling.
The Hosting Capability Supplier will absorb service elements currently delivered through the Home Office's Network Capability Services (NCS) and Private IaaS contracts that are not provided by internal Networks & Infrastructure engineering teams. This includes integrating operational support capabilities into a single commercial construct, simplifying supplier engagement, reducing contractual complexity, and removing longstanding interdependencies across the hosting, platform, cloud, network, and infrastructure landscape.
The successful supplier will be expected to work collaboratively with internal engineering teams, strategic technology partners, and other service providers to support an integrated service management model and deliver continuous service improvement. The supplier will also support the transition from legacy technologies and applications, driving resilience, automation, transformation, and operational excellence whilst maintaining businesscritical services throughout the contract lifecycle.

title: Electronic Presentation of Evidence - Court Equipment and Presentation Packages PR 2025 083
description:
This Procurement will establish a Framework Agreement for the Electronic Presentation of Evidence (EPE):  Court Equipment and Presentation Packages.  
The services covered by this Framework Agreement have been divided into two lots, and each Lot shall operate for a period of two (2) years.
Lot 1 shall be utilised by both the Crown Prosecution Service and the Serious Fraud Office.  Lot 2 shall be utilised by the Crown Prosecution Service.  Additionally, both lots within this Framework are open for use by any other Contracting Authorities (as defined in the Procurement Act 2023) whose activity requires the services procured in a Court, Tribunal, or similar setting, e.g. wider member of the criminal justice system, The Ministry of Justice, Police Forces, the National Crime Agency etc.
Lot One:  Court Equipment
The Contract (Framework Agreement) will be for a two-year duration.  The estimated whole life contract value is £3,817,997.85 ex-VAT /£4,581,597.42 inc-VAT. Tenderers should note that Framework Agreements offer no guarantee of business over their term.	
The service requires the temporary installation of a range of audio, video, and tablet hardware to facilitate the electronic presentation of evidence in a court (or alternative) setting over the course of a trial.  Technician support will be required for,
a)	equipment installation and removal, 
b)	user training, 
c)	onsite support.
This lot shall be divided into three geographical zones, for full details of each zone please refer to ITT Document 2 (note: Court Equipment services at The Central Criminal Court of England and Wales, also known as The Old Bailey, are excluded from this tender). A maximum of four (4) ranked Tenderers shall be awarded a place in each zone. Services will be commissioned via Direct Award (by rank) each time a call-off is made within any given zone (for more complex requirements the Authority reserves the right to utilise a competitive selection process as detailed in the ITT suite).
For the avoidance of doubt, the first-ranked Tenderer in each zone will hold the primary role and be offered each call-off opportunity first, followed by the second-ranked Tenderer, then the third, and finally the fourth.
Bidding and Award Process:
a)	Tenderers may bid for any number of zones, however, no single Tenderer may hold the primary role (i.e., first-ranked position) in more than one geographical zone.
b)	The highest-scoring Tenderer in each zone shall be awarded the primary role for that zone, unless the situation in point (a) (above) occurs.  If point (a) occurs the following steps will be taken.
i.	The highest scoring Tenderer will be asked to choose which zone they wish to hold the primary role for.
ii.	The next highest-scoring Tenderer will then be offered the primary role in the other zone(s).
iii.	If the second Tenderer accepts the primary zone(s), point (i) will then apply should they be successful in more than one zone.
iv.	The final primary role will be awarded to the highest scoring Tenderer who does not already hold a primary role in the other two zones.
v.	Once primary roles are assigned, ranks 2, 3, and 4 will be awarded based on score within each zone.
Lot Two:  Presentation Packages
The Contract (Framework Agreement) will be for a two-year duration.  The estimated whole life contract value inclusive of all options is £1,015,463.83 ex-VAT/ £1,218,556.60 inc-VAT.
The service requires the transformation of various forms of evidence (e.g. photographs, CCTV, audio files, technical drawings etc) into a digital format that is easily understandable, and can be presented in a court (or alternative) setting, including but not limited to;
a)	creation of a chronological timelines to link related documents and other Source Materials
b)	forensic injury mapping – including interpretation of pathologist report
c)	closed circuit television and video enhancement
d)	audio enhancement 
e)	voice distortion
f)	Technician support may be required for;
g)	supplying the relevant presentation package to the court
h)	conducting a test of the presentation on the display equipment available in the court
i)	operation of the package throughout the course of the hearing
This lot shall operate on a national basis, across England and Wales.  A maximum of four (4) ranked Tenderers shall be awarded a place in this lot (ranks will be dictated by final scores). The majority of services will be commissioned via Direct Award (by rank) each time a call-off is made.  For the avoidance of doubt, the first ranked Tenderer will be offered each call-off opportunity first, followed by the second ranked Tenderer, then the third, and finally the fourth (for more complex requirements the Authority reserves the right to utilise a competitive selection process as detailed in the ITT suite).

title: Road and Rail Noise measuring tool
description:
The Department for Transport (DfT) seeks to procure specialist technical expertise to finalise new road and rail noise calculation methods. As noise policy and assessment are devolved matters, adoption of the method outside England would be a decision for the relevant Devolved Administrations. 
The current methods, Calculation of Road Traffic Noise (CRTN, 1988) and Calculation of Railway Noise (CRN, 1995), no longer reflect modern vehicle technologies, infrastructure design or the latest evidence on environmental noise. New evidence-based methods have now been developed through joint research commissioned by the DfT, the Department for Environment Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), National Highways (NH) and the Rail Safety and Standards Board (RSSB) and require completion before they can be used. 
This procurement will deliver the work needed to bring the new method to a fully usable and publishable standard. This includes consolidating the research outputs into a coherent four-part calculation method, producing an open-source reference implementation, completing outstanding integration and validation tasks, and supporting the Authority (DfT) during an initial beta testing period. The outcome will be a new single, authoritative document describing the calculation method for both road and rail noise that will supersede CRTN (1988) and CRN (1995).

title: Surface Intelligent Transport System (SITS) – Video Analytics
description:
Strategic Objective
As part of the Surface Intelligent Transport Systems (SITS) programme, the SITS Video Analytics project seeks to provide an enhanced understanding of transport demand, road-user movements and network performance through the deployment of advanced video analytics technology. The capability will support TfL’s operational, strategic and policy objectives by delivering high-quality data and insights to improve network management, transport planning, road safety analysis and performance monitoring.
High-Level Scope & Open Market Exploration
TfL is currently technology- and model-agnostic. We are approaching the market to explore the full spectrum of available solutions. Areas we wish to investigate with suppliers include:
Deployment Architecture: Assessing the feasibility and benefits of edge-based analytics, cloud-processing, or hybrid environments using existing TfL infrastructure.
Delivery Models: Exploring various commercial structures, including fully managed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), bespoke software deployment, or combined hardware/software solutions.
Data & Analytics Maturity: Understanding current market capabilities regarding multi-modal classification (e.g., separating cargo bikes, e-scooters, pedestrians, and heavy freight) and trajectory tracking.
How to Participate
Interested suppliers are invited to review the Market Brochure and complete the Market Supplier Questionnaire (MSQ).
To request copies of both the Market Brochure and the MSQ, please email videoanalytics@tfl.gov.uk.

title: Staying Close
description:
Essex County Council is procuring a specialist intensive coaching service to deliver the Staying Close programme for children in care and care leavers, primarily aged 16-25, who present with complex needs, placement instability and heightened risks.
The service will provide relationship-based, trauma-informed coaching and practical support to vulnerable young people for up to 25 hours per week over a period of up to 18 months. The programme is designed to improve stability, safety, resilience and life outcomes by working closely with young people, their families, carers, social workers, placement providers and other relevant agencies.
The appointed provider will recruit, manage and supervise skilled coaches who will deliver personalised, strengths-based interventions focused on reducing risk, improving emotional wellbeing, strengthening family and social relationships, supporting engagement in education, employment and training, and enabling successful transitions into adulthood. The service will also support young people to step down safely from higher-cost or higher-intensity care placements, return home where appropriate, or achieve greater stability within their existing placement arrangements.
The provider will operate across Essex, delivering flexible support including evenings, weekends and out-of-hours arrangements, whilst maintaining strong multi-agency partnerships and robust safeguarding, performance monitoring and outcome measurement processes.
The overall aim of the service is to achieve improved outcomes for vulnerable young people, reduce placement breakdowns, promote sustainable independence and resilience, and deliver a cost-effective alternative to more intensive care settings.

title: NHP Health Care Planning Tool SaaS Licence
description:
NHS England (NHSE) has awarded a 12-month Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) contract for an enterprise Healthcare Planning Tool to support Wave 1 schemes within the New Hospital Programme (NHP).
The platform will provide a secure, structured and centrally governed environment for the management of Schedule of Accommodation data,
Room Data Sheets, equipment planning information and industrialisation demand data across multiple hospital developments. The solution will
support the delivery of Hospital 2.0 through programme-wide standardisation, data governance, auditability, role-based access controls,
interoperability with BIM and design systems, automated validation and enhanced assurance processes.
The contract will ensure continuity of an existing digital capability currently being provided through one of NHSE’s delivery partners to NHP, and will enable the contracted platform to operate under direct control of NHP from 1 October 2026. Access by NHP to the service will support ongoing planning, design development, assurance and standardisation activities across Wave 1 hospital schemes.
The scope of the contract is limited to SaaS platform licences together with standard software support, maintenance, security updates and product
enhancements. Implementation, configuration, user adoption and training activities are not within the scope of the contract.
As set out through the Transparency Notice published 24 August 2026 (ref: UK-14009), NHS England considers that the conditions in Paragraph 6 of Schedule 5 to the Procurement Act 2023 are satisfied. Due to an absence of competition for technical reasons, only the identified single supplier can provide the healthcare planning tool services required by the New Hospital Programme (NHP). NHS England has concluded that there are no reasonable alternatives to the services being procured. While other suppliers may offer software products operating in the same market, dRofus is the only solution that can meet the programme scale requirements essential to this national programme, enforcing Hospital 2.0 across many schemes: aggregation and impact analysis across schemes, programme-wide assurance reporting, version control and audit, open API integration, and scalable multi-scheme deployment.
In addition, the supplier owns and operates the HCPT software platform, associated data model, system architecture, configuration, functionality and proprietary intellectual property upon which the capability is based. The requirement is for continued access to, and use of, that specific platform and its associated functionality rather than for a generic healthcare planning software solution. The platform contains programme-specific data structures, workflows, controlled templates, validation rules, governance controls and interoperability capabilities that have been developed and configured, by the supplier via the current contract with an NHSE delivery partner, to support the requirements of NHP and Hospital 2.0. These capabilities are proprietary to the supplier's platform and are not available from alternative suppliers.  NHS England therefore considers that, due to an absence of competition for technical reasons, only this single supplier can supply the services required and that there are no reasonable alternatives to those services.
NHS England intends to undertake further assessment over the course of the 1-year contract duration to ascertain if there are alternative technical solutions or providers becoming available.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – MLSim-DZ
description: Virtuelle Trainingsumgebungen sind Teil moderner Ausbildungssysteme und müssen daher das Trainingsgebiet möglichst realistisch abbilden. Gerade im thermalen Infrarot ist eine realistische Darstellung aufgrund zeitlicher Zusammenhänge, Wetter und Ortsabhängigkeiten erschwert. Echtzeitfähigkeit wird erst durch starke algorithmische Vereinfachungen ermöglicht, mit visuellen Abweichungen vom realen Erscheinungsbild. Gegenüber traditioneller, physikbasierter Bilderzeugung bieten KI-Verfahren hier einen alternativen, datengetriebenen potentiell beschleunigten Lösungsansatz. In den vorherigen Studien wurde ein Demonstrator erzeugt, der die entwickelten KI-erfahren mit modernsten, typischerweise in 3D-Softwareprodukten verwendeten Technologien koppelt. Digitale Zwillinge und KI haben sich in wenigen Jahren rasant zu den relevantesten Themen der modernen, anwendungsnahen Forschung entwickelt. Im militärischen Kontext ermöglichen diese Themenfelder die realistische Simulation und damit realitätsnahes Training von Einsatzszenarien oder Bildauswertung/-interpretation, effiziente Datenauswertung auch bei limitiertem Personaleinsatz, Geländebewertung, Entscheidungsunterstützung, uvm. Besondere Herausforderungen und Rahmen-bedingungen bilden dabei die notwendigen Trainingsdaten für KI, die Simulationsdaten, welche zum Aufbau digitaler Zwillinge benötigt werden (Höhenmodelle, Landnutzung, Gebäudemodelle, Materialdaten, etc.), sowie allgemein die militärisch relevanten Spektralbereiche. Letztere umfassen neben dem sichtbaren Spektralbereich auch den Nah-, kurzwelligen, mittelwelligen und langwelligen Infrarot-Bereich. Während RGB-Bilder im Allgemeinen große Aufmerksamkeit erhalten aufgrund des Interesses aus zivilen Leitbranchen (z.B. Gaming- und Unterhaltungsbranche, Automobilindustrie) und damit eine zügige Weiterentwicklung von Generierungs- und Auswertungsmethoden erfolgt, spielen Infrarotbilder meist nur in Randbranchen, im Wissenschaftssektor, und im militärischen Kontext (Aufklärung und Verteidigung) eine Rolle. Aus diesem Grund sind militärische Entwicklungen begrenzt verfügbar und zivile Errungenschaften nur erschwert auf den militärischen Sektor zu übertragen, und gezielte Forschung zu ML-Trainingsdaten und digitalen Zwillingen wird hier notwendig.
buyer: ['Bundesamt für Ausrüstung, Informationstechnik und Nutzung der Bundeswehr']
