Tavoitteena on muodostaa ja analysoida seurantatietoa, joka kertoo työttömien (ja hiipuvilla aloilla työskentelevien) osaamisen kehittämisestä ja alan vaihtamisesta. Hankinnan kohteena on kvantitatiivisia aineistoja ja menetelmiä hyödyntävä tutkimus, jossa muodostetaan: 1)Kuvaileva analyysi: Kokonaiskuva työttömien sekä hiipuvilla aloilla ja ammateissa työskentelevien osaamisen kehittämisestä, sen tavoista, palveluista, jakautumisesta eri taustatekijöiden mukaan sekä osaamisen kehittämisen kohdistumisesta työvoiman kysyntäaloille ja ammatteihin, joissa osaajista on pulaa. Huomion kohteena ovat erityisesti pitkäaikaistyöttömät. 2) Vaikutusanalyysi: Analyysi osaamisen kehittämisen vaikutuksesta työttömien työllistymiseen erityisesti hiipuvilta tai ylitarjonta aloilta tai ammateista työttömäksi jäävien tai matalan koulutustason omaavien työnhakijoiden osalta. Tarjouspyyntö kohdistuu tietopohjan vahvistamiseen työllistymistä ja kohtaantoa edistävästä osaamisen kehittämisestä etenkin työttömyyden aikana. Tutkimuksen kohderyhmänä ovat työttömät, erityisesti pitkäaikaistyöttömät, ja pienemmällä painotuksella hiipuvilla aloilla tai ammateissa työskentelevät. Tutkimuksessa muodostetaan aineisto, jonka pohjalta tarkastellaan, miten TE-palvelutarjonta, ja muu osaamisen kehittäminen, ja sen kohdentaminen parantaa kohtaantoa tukemalla työttömien työnhakijoiden ja hiipuvilla aloilla tai ammateissa työskentelevien osaamisen kehittämistä ja siirtymiä työvoimapula-aloille ja työvoimapula-ammatteihin. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tämän tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus. Hankintayksikkö valitsee yhden (1) toimittajan, jonka kanssa se tekee sopimuksen. Sopimuskausi alkaa sopimuksen allekirjoittamisen jälkeen. Tavoitteena on, että tutkimushankkeen toteutus alkaa arviolta 17.8.2026. Loppuraportin on oltava valmis ja palvelun ohjausryhmän hyväksymä viimeistään 04.12.2027. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska tutkimuksessa ei ole sellaisia selkeitä erillisiä kokonaisuuksia, joita useampi eri taho voisi toteuttaa, vaan on tärkeää, että tutkimuksen kokonaiskuvan hallinta pysyy yhdellä taholla.

title: Denmark – Construction consultancy services – Udbud af totalrådgivning for ombygning af Vildanden og Penalhuset
description: Kommunalbestyrelsen i Bornholms Regions Kommune har besluttet, at renovere Børnehuset Vildanden, samt ombygge faciliteterne til Hjemme- og Sygeplejen i Penalhuset. Der indgås en ABR 18 totalrådgiveraftale for rådgivning til brug for ombygning af Børnehuset Vildanden og Hjemme- og sygeplejen i Penalhuset. De er begge beliggende i den samme bygning i Rønne, på tidligere Østre Skole. Bygningsændringer. Rådgiveropgaven forventes at omfatte projekteringen af det samlede projekt, for at kunne planlægge renoveringen og de midlertidige rokader i huset mest hensigtsmæssigt. Bygningen er af ældre dato, og er en del af det tidligere Østre Skole, med en indretning der består af klasse-og faglokaler. Bygningen vil få renoveret tag og facade, bygningens indretningen vil blive tilpasset, med en rumfordeling egnet til børnehus og hjemmepleje. Der etables nyt ventilationsanlæg, el, vand og varme i bygningen vil blive opdateret til et tidssvarende niveau. Der etableres personalekøkken i Penalhuset, i kælder etableres omklædnings- og badefaciliteter. Der ombygges ca. 710 m2 i stueplan og 390 m2 i kælderplan. De eksisterende bygninger er oprindeligt bygget til en. De konkrete ydelser som en kommende totalrådgiver skal levere, fremgår af Hoveddokument A-Projektbeskrivelsen og Hoveddokument B-Ydelsesbeskrivelsen, samt alle tilhørende bilag til udbuds materialet. Der skal ske en række ombygninger og renovering af de eksisterende bygninger. Selve bygningsarbejdet skal udføres i flere etaper da, begge funktioner skal være i drift under bygningsarbejderne. Den samlede bevilling til projektet udgør ca. kr.32.750.000,- eksl. moms. Bevillingen udgør det samlede anlægsbudget, som omfatter alle udgifter til håndværkerudgifter, omkostninger, honorarer, interne honorarer, grundudgifter, byggepladsomkostninger, bygherreleverancer pulje til uforudseelige udgifter etc. Det påhviler den pågældende rådgiver der skal udføre den aktuelle opgave at udføre en samlet rådgivning for Bornholms Regions Kommune (BRK), hvor rådgiveren har ansvaret for rådgivningen. Rådgivningen omfatter i hovedtræk: Indledende rådgivning, forundersøgelse m.v. Byggeprogram. Dispositionsforslag. Projektforslag. Myndighedsprojekt. Udbudsprojekt. Udførelsesprojekt. Rådgivning under udførelse og aflevering, byggeledelse, fagtilsyn m.v. 1- års eftersyn. ABR 18 totalrådgiveraftalen træder i kraft den dato, hvor den underskrives og løber herefter frem til, afholdt 1-års eftersyn jf. Udbudstidsplanen. Der er ikke option på forlængelse af ABR 18 totalrådgiveraftalen. I forhold til udbudslovens § 49, stk. 2 har Ordregiver valgt ikke at udbyde særskilte delaftaler med baggrund i økonomiske- og markedsmæssige hensyn. Ordregiver har konkret vurderet, at det ikke er den kommercielt bedste løsning eller anbefalelsesværdigt at adskille og opdele opgaven i særskilte delaftaler. Ordregiver har til hensigt at udvælge 5 ansøgere til den endelige tilbudsafgivning. Udvælgelsen, såfremt der er flere end 5 egnede ansøgere, vil finde sted på grundlag af en helhedsvurdering af, hvilke ansøgere der ved referencerne har dokumenteret den mest relevante erfaring indenfor de ydelser, der efterspørges af ordregiver i Hoveddokument A-Projektbeskrivelsen og Hoveddokument B- Ydelsesbeskrivelsen. De objektive kriterier, der vil blive lagt til grund for begrænsning af antallet af ansøgere, der opfordres til at give tilbud, vil ske ved en vurdering af, hvilke ansøgere, der har dokumenteret de mest relevante referencer. Ved ”relevante referencer” menes der referencer, der i størrelse og karakter ligner den totalrådgivning der skal understøtte Bornholms Regionskommune i ombygning og renovering af henholdsvis en børneinstitution og faciliteter for syge- og hjemmeplejen. For at sikre et større tilbudsfelt vil udbyder acceptere referencer der er udført mere end 3 år tidligere at regne fra ansøgningstidspunktet, med henvisning til Udbudsloven §155 stk. 1 pkt. 2. Ansøger skal angive referencer for udført totalrådgivning i de seneste 5 år for at sikre tilstrækkelig konkurrence. Såfremt en reference delvist er udført tidligere (dvs. rådgivning er delvist udført uden for referenceperiodens 5 år) bedes det oplyst, hvor stor en andel (angivet i procent) af den samlede rådgivning, der er leveret inden for referenceperioden. 5 år er at regne fra det tidspunkt hvor rådgivningsydelsen er afsluttet og frem til ansøgningstidspunktet for denne aktuelle opgave. Såfremt 1-års eftersynet har været indeholdt i kontrakten for referenceopgaven er 5 års perioden at regne fra den måned hvor selve eftersynet har været afholdt. Ordregiver lægger positiv vægt på nedenstående ved vurderingen af referencerne: I jo højere grad referencerne kan demonstrere erfaring med rådgivningsopgaver, der i størrelse og karakter ligner den rådgivningsopgave, der skal udføres i forbindelse med nærværende projekt, beskrevet i det samlede udbudsmateriale. I jo højere grad at referencerne demonstrerer erfaring med rådgivning af en offentlig organisation eller tilsvarende (Kommune, region, stat, almen boligorganisation, selvejende institutioner). I jo højere grad at referencerne demonstrerer erfaring med at rådgivningen har omfattet brugerinddragelse. I jo højere grad at referencerne demonstrerer erfaring med at rådgivningen har omfattet totalrådgivning ifm. fag- eller hovedentreprise. I jo højere grad at referencerne demonstrerer erfaring med, at rådgivningen har omfattet byggeledelse. Dette kan være hos totalrådgiveren eller underrådgiver som indgår i ansøgning om prækvalifikation. I det omfang referencen ligner den udbudte opgave i størrelse og karakter, men kun delvist er leveret indenfor de sidste 5 år, kan der alene lægges vægt på den del af referencen, der er udført indenfor de sidste 5 år. Under tilbudsfasen vil det være muligt at besigtige de eksisterende bygninger, for ved selvsyn at danne sig et overblik over opgavens omfang og kompleksitet.

description:
Attain Academy Partnership (hereinafter referred to as 'the Trust) comprises seven primary schools located across Essex, serving approximately 1,600 pupils across its sites.
The successful supplier will be required to provide Cleaning Services for the following academies:
• Cressing Primary School
• Newlands Spring Primary & Nursery School
• Rayne Primary & Nursery School
We are seeking a suitably experienced contractor who has experience of working in the education sector. The contractor will be required to

title: Lancaster Farms - Therapeutic Community Plus Service
description:
The Authority intends to procure the provision of a Therapeutic Community Plus (TC+) service at HMP Lancaster Farms as part of the Offender Personality Disorder (OPD) Pathway. The service will provide a specialist residential therapeutic treatment programme for men with mild to moderate learning disabilities who present with complex psychological and emotional needs associated with offending behaviour. The service will operate within a 12 to 14 bed residential therapeutic community and be delivered in partnership with HMPPS and other relevant healthcare providers.
The successful provider will be required to deliver specialist clinical services in accordance with the accredited TC+ programme manuals and standards approved by the Correctional Services Advice and Accreditation Panel (CSAAP). The service will include the provision of suitably qualified clinical professionals, including a Clinical Lead Psychotherapist (or equivalent modality), Learning Disability Specialist, and access to Occupational Therapy, Speech and Language Therapy, and Creative Therapy services as required to meet participant needs.
The provider will be responsible for delivering therapeutic interventions, supporting assessment and treatment activities, contributing to service governance, collecting and reporting service performance data, maintaining appropriate clinical oversight, and working collaboratively with HMPPS, probation services, mental health providers and other relevant stakeholders to support pathway progression and rehabilitation outcomes.
The service will be delivered at HMP Lancaster Farms and operate in accordance with the OPD Pathway's strategic objectives to reduce reoffending, improve psychological wellbeing and relational outcomes, support staff capability, and deliver effective and high-quality treatment services.
*The contract start date is currently subject to a number of operational and implementation dependencies and is therefore yet to be confirmed. However, the Authority intends to progress the procurement at pace with a view to commencing the contract as soon as practicable.
Suppliers who have the capability and experience to deliver the services outlined are invited to register their interest by contacting the Offender Welfare mailbox at MoJProcurement.OffenderWelfare by 1st October 2pm.
Please note that this market engagement exercise does not commit the Authority to proceed with a procurement and no contractual commitment arises from participation in this excercise.

description:
The Wendling Estate is a council estate located in the Gospel Oak ward, with St Stephen’s Close immediately adjacent. Together they are known as the Wendling and St Stephen’s Close Estate, covering approximately 2.6 hectares and comprising 240 existing homes, including at the time of writing 191 Council-tenanted homes and 49 leasehold properties. 
The regeneration of the Wendling Estate and St Stephen’s Close is an important part of the Council’s Community Investment Programme. Residents voted in favour of full redevelopment of the Estate in July 2021 because they wanted new homes, better outdoor spaces, and a safer, more welcoming neighbourhood. The redevelopment proposals aim to deliver high-quality, energy efficient, genuinely affordable and private homes that meet residents’ needs and address long standing issues facing the existing Estate, such as overcrowding and antisocial behaviour. 
The Council intends, subject to Cabinet approval, to procure a joint venture development partner to deliver a redevelopment of the estate comprising circa 650-750 high-quality, sustainable new homes; replace the existing hostel and health centre; and improve the existing neighbourhood for current and future residents. The redevelopment will be delivered in accordance with the Landlord Offer that formed the basis of the resident ballot. The contract estimated value is £500m GDV (Gross Development Value).

description:
Leicester City Council (the Council) undertook a below threshold targeted quotation procurement process, in line with the requirements under the below-threshold contract regulations of the Procurement Act 2023. The procurement exercise was undertaken to find a suitably qualified and experienced provider for the Provision of Enablement Supported Living Services for people with Physical and /or Sensory Disabilities - Harrison Court, Supported Living Scheme.
The procurement of this service has now concluded and the contract provisionally awarded, subject to standstill. Services procured are as detailed in the tender documentation.
This is a well-established Supported Living scheme with Leicester City Council working in partnership with Platform Housing Group and the care and support provider at this site.  
This three-storey scheme is located within Leicester City and has 16 self-contained flats and provides an opportunity to provide supported living services to eight people. The remaining rooms within Harrison Court are: 3x supported living voids, 1x communal room and the remaining flats are used by Platform Housing Group for general needs tenants.  
The Provider will work closely with Care Management and health professionals to monitor individuals’ health and identify any deterioration in their ability to manage health conditions, promptly informing Commissioners and relevant professionals of any significant changes. Staff must understand the needs of people with physical and sensory disabilities to ensure timely, responsive, and compassionate support. They should also be knowledgeable about available services and support, such as aids and adaptations, assistive technology, hearing support, sign language services, and carer support, enabling effective signposting. The Provider will collaborate with housing providers, the individual, and other tenants where appropriate to ensure the living environment accommodates and supports the person’s disability, health condition, or sensory impairment.
The proposed Contract will be for an initial period of 12 months to commence on 15th November 2026 to 14th November 2027 with the option to extend for a further period of 12 months, taking the total contract duration to 24 months, up to 14th November 2028.
The publication of this contract award notice will formally commence the standstill period (8 working days), expiring on 23:59 Wednesday 30th September 2026.

title: Pre-Market Engagement: Commercial Filming Services
description:
Network Rail currently delivers an end-to-end commercial filming service across a diverse portfolio of railway assets, acting as the primary interface between the rail industry and the screen sector. With the transition to Great British Railways (GBR), Network Rail is exploring future options for delivering these services across a larger estate that will encompass both Network Rail and Train Operating Company assets.
Through this market engagement exercise, Network Rail seeks to understand market capability, supplier interest, potential delivery models, opportunities for innovation, and the extent to which external providers could deliver some or all of the service currently carried out in-house. The exercise will help inform future strategy development by assessing market maturity, operational considerations, resource requirements, and the risks and benefits associated with different delivery approaches. 
Network Rail will be holding supplier engagement sessions in London on 13 and 14 October 2026, providing an opportunity for suppliers to learn more about this forthcoming requirement. Details of how to register can be found in the RFI document, 'Pre-Market Engagement – Commercial Filming Services', which is available under "View Current Opportunities" on the Network Rail eSourcing Portal (Bravo): https://networkrail.bravosolution.co.uk/web/login.html
The engagement sessions will be conducted on a one-to-one basis, with each supplier offered a one-hour time slot.
Please note that, should it become necessary to reschedule the market engagement sessions, Network Rail will notify all interested suppliers using the email address provided within their RFI response.

title: Sustainable Procurement Technical Consultancy Framework - FRA087
description:
WRAP is seeking to establish a multi-supplier framework agreement for the provision of specialist sustainable procurement technical consultancy services. The framework will support the delivery of Welsh Government-funded programmes, Defra-funded programmes and other WRAP initiatives across Wales, England and the wider UK.
Services may include, but are not limited to, sustainable procurement strategy and policy support, circular economy and resource efficiency consultancy, low-carbon procurement and Scope 3 emissions support, supplier and market engagement, procurement document development, training and capability building, contract management and performance measurement, programme evaluation, impact reporting and specialist category expertise.
WRAP intends to appoint up to five suppliers to the framework. Call-off contracts may be awarded through direct award for requirements below £30,000 (inclusive of VAT) or through mini-competitions. The framework will operate as an Open Framework in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and is anticipated to have a total value of up to £1.5 million (inclusive of VAT) over its lifetime.

title: Determination of levels of PFAS in (+ migrating from) Food Contact Materials FCM
description: This research project aims to develop analytical capabilities for measuring PFAS and to generate risk-assessment-ready data on PFAS occurrence in food packaging and other FCMs and their migration into food, enabling a better understanding of the extent to which these materials may contribute to PFAS detected in food relative to other sources of contamination. This information will help to reduce some of the current data gaps in the evidence base. This will therefore enable a more accurate assessment of the risk to human health as well as identify any issues to take through the FSA’s risk analysis process and support future policy requirements/decision making.

title: Transaction and Balance Sheet Concilliation Software
description:
Trintech Matcher is transactional reconciliation system, matching individual sales made with a payment card/PayPal to the payment service providers processing records - this effectively is a check that each sale has a payment. Non-matching items are investigated and issues reported for corrective action. The system covers LNER Online, Travel Centres, Onboard, and TVM transactions, which cover most of LNER's card transactions and all PayPal transactions.
Due to the volume of payment transactions, it would not be possible to reconcile these without a tailor made reconciliation system .
Balancer is a tool for the recording of Balance Sheet reconciliation, providing finance with a standard format for reviewing reconciliations, with the allocation of recs, their progress through to submission being viewable, and back up documents being accessible to reviewers and is essential for LNER's governance processes.
Both systems are SAAS, with a number of licences for each application.

title: Healthy Schools and Early Years Services
description:
Liverpool City Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement to inform the development of the proposed Healthy Schools and Early Years Programme. The programme will provide a structured whole setting approach that supports the physical, emotional, and social wellbeing of students, teachers, staff and parents. The programme is intended to provide coordinated and free, comprehensive and accessible health and wellbeing offer that will be responsive to new and emerging needs. It will support both settings and providers to increase access, choice and reduce duplication and will ensure that the local offer is based on the best possible evidence.
The Council is therefore exploring a model that focuses on coordination, partnership working and system leadership, bringing together and maximising the impact of existing services rather than replacing them. The intention is to create a single, coherent offer that helps schools, early years settings and alternative provision settings access appropriate support, identify local needs and improve health and wellbeing outcomes.
The Council is seeking to engage with organisations that have experience of coordinating complex multi-agency services, facilitating partnership working and supporting whole-system approaches to health improvement, prevention and early intervention.
Feedback gathered through this engagement will help inform the future service specification, delivery model and procurement approach.

title: 33kV Substation SCADA Supply
description: The United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority are looking to engage a Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) specialist to develop a new SCADA system in J5 based on the IEC 61850 protocol, replacing the existing SCADA. The 400/33kV substation, the existing control and automation system, comprising historic CODAS system, SCADA and Programmable Logic Controllers, will be decommissioned and replaced with an advanced site-wide master SCADA system in full compliance with the IEC 61850 protocol. The work includes the design, manufacture, delivery, installation, and commissioning of the complete system, including an operator workstation in J5 control room. The SCADA will provide full control authority with intelligent interlocking to prevent failures or operational errors. The system will integrate with all numerical and auxiliary devices, transmitting all alarms, trip signals, and status indications over fibre or Ethernet to the main control room.

title: Interim Highways Services - Birmingham
description:
Kier Transportation Limited ("Kier") previously provided interim highways maintenance and associated operational services across the Birmingham highways network (the "Services") through an Interim Services Contract ("ISC") with Birmingham City Council's ("the Authority") subcontractor, Birmingham Highways Limited ("BHL"). The ISC novated from BHL to the Authority on 31 July 2026.
The ISC was originally procured in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. Following the Department for Transport's recent decision to withdraw its support for the continued funding of the Authority's highways PFI project, the Authority will procure an alternative long-term solution to replace this project. To enable the procurement of this alternative solution, the Authority requires the continued provision of the Services on an interim basis and therefore proposes to enter into a variation agreement to extend the ISC, such that it will expire on 31 July 2028 (or on 30 April 2029 if the Authority exercises an option to extend the ISC set out in the variation agreement). The variation agreement will therefore ensure the continued uninterrupted delivery of critical public services and the continued safety of the public in accordance with the Authority's statutory duties.

title: Sustainability and Climate Data Services
description:
Border to Coast wishes to procure sustainability and climate data services to support implementation of its Responsible Investment and Engagement Strategies, including portfolio risk management, investment decision-making, stewardship activities, external reporting and Partner Fund support.
The required information and analytics will support the identification, assessment and management of sustainability-related risks and opportunities relevant to long-term investment performance.
The scope of information required is expected to include sustainability metrics and assessments; controversy and conduct-related indicators; human rights and international norms data (including UN Global Compact-related information); information supporting the monitoring of exclusions; climate and net zero analytics; and data to support portfolio monitoring, stewardship activities, risk management and reporting requirements.
The tender is currently expected to be structured across three Lots.Border to Coast recognises that no single provider may be able to meet all requirements and therefore reserves the right to appoint multiple providers, both across Lots and within individual Lots, where this delivers the most effective solution. 
Border to Coast may choose not to procure data in certain areas where relevant information is already available through existing provider relationships outside the scope of this contract.
The solution should be provided under an enterprise-wide license, enabling access across multiple teams, including Responsible Investment, Research, Investment and Portfolio Risk. The required coverage spans a broad range of asset classes, including listed equities, corporate credit, sovereign credit, private markets and real estate. 
The contract is expected to support reporting and disclosure requirements across Border to Coast and its Partner Funds, including climate-related, stewardship and wider sustainability-related reporting. Certain headline sustainability and climate metrics will also need to be made available to Partner Funds through reporting processes. Partner Funds must be permitted to use relevant outputs and data for their own reporting, disclosure, stewardship and regulatory requirements. Appropriate redistribution rights within the Border to Coast partnership will therefore be required.
The provider's operating model must be capable of integrating with Border to Coast's Investment Research and Data Platform, including BlackRock Aladdin, to support efficient data management, investment analysis, risk oversight and reporting activities.
Providers should demonstrate an ability to support changing sustainability-related reporting requirements, market standards and regulatory frameworks over the life of the contract.
buyer: BORDER TO COAST PENSIONS PARTNERSHIP LIMITED

title: Electric Theatre - Preliminary Market Engagement Notice
description:
The Electric Theatre is an iconic and historic building in the heart of Guildford, originally built as an electricity works in 1913 and converted into a theatre in 1997. The venue is currently vacant, with Guildford Borough Council assuming full responsibility for the building and its associated holding costs.
The Council has undertaken a programme of technical surveys and stakeholder engagement to establish a clear evidence base to inform the future of the asset, confirming both the significant cultural value of the venue and a strong community aspiration for its continued use as an arts and performance space. The Council intends to appoint an operator or leaseholder to run the venue on a lease or concession basis pending final classification and is undertaking preliminary market engagement to understand market capacity and appetite among cultural, community and commercial operators before finalising its procurement route and minimum requirements.
This is not a call for competition and does not commit the Council to commence a procurement process.

title: Fleet Key Management System
description:
The Police and Crime Commissioner for Warwickshire, on behalf of Warwickshire Police, intends to enter into a contract for the provision of a secure Fleet Key Management System across operational police sites within Warwickshire, following the evaluation of tenders received through a competitive tendering procedure conducted under the Procurement Act 2023.
The proposed contract will provide a secure electronic fleet key management solution to manage, track and audit vehicle key access across operational police sites.
•	Applies to approximately 350 fleet vehicle key sets across 17 operational sites.
•	Covers secure storage, issue, return, audit, reporting, and support.
•	Initial scope is fleet vehicle keys, with extensibility for other controlled assets (e.g. fuel cards, equipment) as optional.
Aim/Purpose:
The solution shall:
•	Provide a secure, auditable, and standardised method for managing fleet vehicle keys across all Warwickshire Police sites.
•	Replace inconsistent local practices with a force-wide controlled system.
•	Support improved governance, accountability, and risk management for vehicle access.
•	Enable future operational efficiencies (e.g. pooling and utilisation insight); however, no system integrations are required at initial implementation.
We were seeking a provider that has currently or in the past 3 years have successfully delivered a Key Management system (equivalent to the scope of this tender) to at least one or more UK police customers or comparable organisation, and can demonstrate the required technical capability and capacity.
The contract dates stated in this notice are estimated. The software contract term will commence following successful installation and completion of User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to the satisfaction of the Authority. The contract end date and any extension expiry dates stated in this notice are therefore provisional and will be confirmed following successful completion of UAT.
At commencement of the procurement, the estimated maximum contract value, calculated in accordance with section 4 and Schedule 3 of the Procurement Act 2023 and inclusive of VAT, exceeded the applicable threshold. The procurement was therefore conducted as a covered procurement. Following competition, the successful tender price is £150,368.88 exclusive of VAT (£180,442.66 inclusive of VAT), which is below the applicable threshold. The reduction in value is a result of the competitive procurement process and does not represent an artificial reduction or subdivision of the requirement.
This Contract Award Notice gives notice of the Authority's intention to enter into the proposed contract with the successful supplier. The Authority will not enter into the contract before the end of the standstill period stated in this notice.

title: The Provision of Secure Payment Kiosks
description:
Denbighshire County Council (The Authority) are looking to engage with the market in relation to cost effective and high quality payment kiosks.  This pre-market engagement notice outlines the high level requirements for payment kiosks capable of accepting payments via cash, chip and PIN, contactless and mobile wallets.  The kiosks are to be installed in Local Authority One Stop Shops, ensuring secure, accessible, and user-friendly transactions for a diverse range of customers.
Aims of Engagement
The purpose is to:
- Understand supplier capabilities and the very latest technologies and solutions available in the market
- Identify opportunities for innovation and best practice
- Test assumptions on costs, timescales, and implementation approaches
- Understand options available to the Authority
Requirements
•	Payment Methods: The kiosk must accept major debit and credit cards (including contactless), Google and Apple Pay, as well as cash (notes and coins).
•	Receipts: The kiosk must provide printed and digital receipts for all transactions.
•	Transaction Processing: Payments must be processed in real time, with confirmation displayed to the user.
•	Change Dispensing: For cash payments, the kiosk must dispense change where necessary.
•	Multiple Services: The kiosk should support payments for various Local Authority services (e.g., council tax, parking, permits).
•	Ability to view analytics and run reports
•	The devices must be able to operate bilingually in Welsh and English
•	Data Protection: All card transactions must comply with PCI DSS standards. Sensitive customer information must be encrypted and not stored locally.
•	Physical Security: The kiosk must be robust, tamper-resistant, with lockable compartments for cash and maintenance access.
•	Alarm Systems: Integrated alarms for unauthorised access or tampering.
•	Audit Trail: The system must maintain a secure log of all transactions for audit purposes.
•	Cash Handling: Secure cash management system, including automatic counting and secure storage of notes and coins.
•	Physical Accessibility: The kiosk must comply with UK accessibility standards, including wheelchair access (height and reach requirements).
•	User Interface: Large, clear touchscreen interface with intuitive navigation. Option for audio guidance and multiple languages.
•	Assistance Features: Braille labelling, tactile buttons, and headphone jack for visually impaired users.
•	Clear Instructions: Step-by-step instructions displayed on screen and available in print.
•	Connectivity: Secure internet connection for real-time transaction processing and remote support.
•	Reliability: Minimum uptime of 99.5%. Automated alerts for faults or maintenance needs.
•	Integration: Ability to integrate with Local Authority back-office systems for reconciliation and reporting.
•	Maintenance: Easy access for authorised personnel, with modular components for quick replacement.
•	Durability: Suitable for indoor use; resistant to spills, dust, and vandalism.
•	Power Supply: Standard UK mains power; battery backup for short-term operation during outages.
•	Space: Compact footprint, suitable for installation in existing One Stop Shop locations without major modifications.
•	Promote energy efficiency, for example by using low-power processors and LED displays
•	Compliance with relevant British Standards for electrical and payment equipment.
•	Certification for accessibility and security as required by Local Authority regulations.
•	On-screen help and customer support contact information.
•	Routine maintenance schedule and rapid response for breakdowns.
•	Remote diagnostics and software updates capability.
Summary
The payment kiosk must deliver secure, accessible, and reliable payment solutions for Local Authority customers, supporting both card and cash transactions. The design should ensure compliance with all regulatory standards, protect customer data, and provide a seamless user experience for all visitors to One Stop Shops.

title: Public Health Funerals - Supplier Information Session
description:
Public Health Funerals- Supplier Information and Support Session
1.	Purpose
Ipswich Borough Council is inviting funeral directors and funeral service providers to attend a Supplier Information and Support Session relating to the forthcoming procurement of Public Health Funeral Services.
This supplier information and support session is intended to:
•	Raise awareness of the forthcoming tender opportunity,
•	Provide an overview of the Public Health Funeral Services requirements,
•	Explain the procurement process and anticipated timetable (where possible),
•	Support suppliers in understanding how to participate in the tender process,
•	Provide an opportunity for suppliers to ask questions regarding the forthcoming procurement.
Attendance at the supplier information and support session does not form part of the tender evaluation process and is not a requirement for participation in the future procurement opportunity.
2.	Background
Under the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984, Ipswich Borough Council has a statutory responsibility to arrange a dignified and respectful funeral where no other person is willing or able to make funeral arrangements.
The Council currently arranges approximately 20 to 30 Public Health Funerals each year.
Public Health Funerals are generally direct cremations unless:
•	The deceased is known to belong to a faith that prohibits cremation; or
•	The deceased has left written instructions requesting burial.
The anticipated contract period is expected to be:
•	An initial term of 24 months with an option to extend for a further 24 months
•	The estimated value of the contract is anticipated to be in the region of £80,000 over the maximum four-year term. This figure is provided for information only and does not constitute a commitment by the Council.
3.	Nature of Requirement
The successful provider must be able to collect and convey the deceased to Ipswich Cemetery and Crematorium within a maximum journey time of 30 minutes under normal circumstances.
Suppliers should carefully consider this requirement, as compliance with the requirement will form a key part of the tender evaluation process.
The service is expected to include:
•	Collection and transportation of deceased persons,
•	Appropriate storage and care of the deceased,
•	Completion of statutory documentation and liaison with relevant agencies,
•	Provision of a suitable coffin for burial or cremation,
•	Liaison with Ipswich Borough Council Bereavement Services,
•	Attendance of suitably trained staff to facilitate burials and cremations,
•	Delivery of all services with dignity, professionalism and respect.
4.	Supplier Support Open Morning
Ipswich Borough Council will be hosting a supplier information and support session for local funeral directors and interested providers.
The session is intended to:
•	Overview of Public Health Funeral Services
•	Details of the Council's requirements/specifications
•	Information about the proposed procurement process
•	Guidance on participating in public sector opportunities
•	An opportunity to ask questions regarding the service requirements and procurement process.
Date: Tuesday 27 October 2026
Time: 10:00am to 11:30am (90 minutes)
Venue: Ipswich Borough Council, Grafton House Orwell Room, 15-17 Russell Road, Ipswich, Suffolk, IP1 2DE.
Parking arrangements:  You will be able to park at the far rear of the car park behind Grafton House. Please drive through the barrier and continue straight ahead, passing the wooden fence. The Facilities Team is aware that this meeting is taking place and has approved these parking arrangements.
Suppliers wishing to attend the Supplier Information and Support Session must register their interest by 12 noon on Tuesday 20 October 2026. Registration requests should be submitted by email to procurement@ipswich.gov.uk and include the organisation name, attendee name(s), and a contact email address.
Next Steps
Following the Supplier Information and Support Session, the procurement opportunity will be formally advertised via the Suffolk Sourcing Portal. Suppliers interested in providing the service will be invited to submit a tender in accordance with the published procurement timetable and guidance.

title: Development Opportunity: Seaview Road - Site of former Liscard Municipal Buildings and Adjacent Carpark
description:
Wirral Council (the Council) is the local authority for the Metropolitan Borough of Wirral.
The Council's Economy, Regeneration, and Housing Committee adopted the Neighbourhood Framework for Liscard: An Integrated Master Plan on 22 November 2021. The Masterplan is published on Wirral Council's website, and the vision is to create a Liscard town centre loved by local people where:
	Everyone feels welcome;
	People can live, work, and play;
	There is a strong sense of local identity, and;
	People can come together.
Members of the Council's Policy and Resources Committee (the Committee) agreed on 12 July 2023 to declare the former Liscard Municipal Offices fronting onto Egerton Grove and the adjacent carpark accessed by Seaview Road and behind businesses fronting on to Seaview Road and Liscard Village (the Site) surplus to requirements (further context on the Site is set out below). The Committee also gave authorisation to progress a procurement process to secure a development partner for the sites' redevelopment on 11 December 2024.
The Site was proposed for development as a part of the Masterplan. The Masterplan notes that the Seaview Road carpark was underused relative to other carparks in Liscard area and proposes repurposing the carpark and former municipal offices into housing to attract more local residents and better link the site to Liscard Village.
The Council adopted its new Local Plan on 31 March 2025. The Local Plan requires 14,400 net additional dwellings in Wirral by 2040. These are all to be delivered on brownfield sites, including the former Liscard Municipal Offices and adjacent carpark. The 2021 Strategic Housing Market Assessment for Wirral, which was a key piece of evidence in developing the Local Plan, states a need for around 700 affordable homes each year borough-wide.
Following the introduction of the new Local Plan system in March 2026, the Council published a Notice to Commence work on a new Local Plan and Timetable at the end of June 2026. An initial Scoping Consultation and Call for Sites exercise was concluded in August 2026.  The Council is required to publish its Gateway 1 self-assessment by the 31 October 2026. This will trigger the start of the 30-month period envisaged in the new system for preparing and adopting a new Local Plan. The timetable envisages adoption of the new Local Plan in June 2029.
The new Local Plan will need to plan for the significantly higher housing numbers introduced by the new Standard Method - 1,622 dwellings per annum - compared with 800 dwellings per annum under the previous approach. It will also need to take account of the new National Planning Policy Framework issued in August 2026 and the emerging Spatial Development Strategy for the Liverpool City Region (LCR), which will be responsible for distribution of future housing growth across the LCR.  
A new Strategic Housing Market Needs Assessment for Wirral is about to be commissioned which is likely to report in the second quarter of 2027 which will determine the level of affordable housing need which the new local plan will need to plan for.
Whilst there is a high need for all types of affordable housing across the Borough, the greatest pressure for the local authority is for rented affordable housing. As of late March 2026, there were over 4,800 households on the housing waiting list, with over 800 of these having the highest priority need.
The Council is now seeking to appoint a Lead Development Partner which can bring skills, experience and expertise in delivering the affordable housing at pace and in line with local housing needs within the Borough.
Suppliers are referred to the separate, Development Prospectus document which provides more detailed information on the Site and the opportunity. This can be accessed via the Chest Portal https://procontract.due-north.com DN819286 (the Portal). 
An initial study of site constraints has been completed. Further detail regarding site constraints can be found within the Development Prospectus and highlights the non-developable aspect of the site to the south to enable ongoing delivery and servicing of neighbouring commercial units.
The capacity study has indicated the site can deliver approximately 100 new affordable homes. This project consists of the replacement of the existing central heating boiler plant and equipment at Army Reserve Centre, 1A Iverna Gardens, Kensington, London W8 6TN. Kensington Army Reserve Centre is a drill hall and associated amenities currently used by Battalion Headquarters of the 7th Battalion The Rifles, and 217 Hospital Squadron in Iverna Gardens, Kensington. 
The building was designed and completed in 1903 as the headquarters for the 4th (Kensington) Middlesex Volunteer Rifle Corps. The existing boiler installation was undertaken in the early 2000’s.  
There is a main plantroom room in the basement that provides domestic hot water and heating to all the facilities in Kensington Army Reserve Centre. Cold water storage tanks on the roof provide a cold water supply to the bathrooms and to the hot water calorifiers. 
The existing plant consists of 2 No. Ideal Commercial Concord CXA 70 gas fired boilers, 2 No gas fired hot water storage heaters, associated pumps, expansion vessels and controls. The boiler flue routes through an existing chimney to discharge at roof level. New communal boilers and replacement pumps are to be provided in the basement plantroom.

title: Preliminary Market Engagement for Education Software Suite
description:
Halton Borough Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement to understand the current software solutions available to support the delivery of its Education Services.
The Council is currently an Access Synergy customer and is seeking to test the market and review the range of alternative solutions available. The purpose of this exercise is to understand current market capability, functionality, technology, integration opportunities, implementation approaches and indicative costs for a modern Education Services software solution.
The Council is interested in solutions that can support a number of Education Service functions, ideally through an integrated platform.
The anticipated scope includes the following key functional areas:
•	Admissions – supporting the end-to-end school admissions process, including applications, preferences, eligibility, allocations, offers, waiting lists, appeals, correspondence and reporting. Creation, export and importing of statutory admission files.
•	FIS / Early Years – supporting Early Years services, including funding, eligibility, applications, provider management, claims, payments, reconciliation and reporting, EY Census production. FIS Childcare Directory, ‘OFSTED Feed’ api data import
•	Free School Meals (FSM) – supporting applications, eligibility, verification, notifications, records and reporting.
•	SAM – supports the LA’s Schools, (School Admissions Module), allows school to access their admissions round allocation and FSM entitlement for their children in Realtime.
•	SEND – supporting the end-to-end management of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities processes, including referrals, assessments, EHC needs assessments and plans, parent and professional portals, reviews, consultations, placements, provision, funding, correspondence, transport and statutory reporting (SEN2).
•	PSS – supporting Pupil Support Services requirements, including referrals, case management, interventions, actions, outcomes, professional involvement and reporting. Work of Education Welfare Team, penalty notices, Exclusions, AP, EOTAS, Elective home education, Entertainment Licences and chaperones
•	Children's Centres (Hubs) – capturing activity data across Family Hubs within the Borough and reporting.
•	EIS – Case Management – providing flexible case management functionality to support workflows, referrals, tasks, alerts, contacts, chronology, document management, correspondence, assessments, outcomes, audit trails and reporting.
The Council is particularly interested in solutions that provide a single, modern and secure platform, enabling appropriate information to be shared across services and providing a consistent approach to the management of children, young people, families, providers, cases and associated information.

title: All Age Service  Substance Misuse
description:
This is a Corrigendum to Contract Award notice issued 08/09/26, confirming the end of the standstill period and formal award.
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) confirmation of contract award notice. This contract has been awarded under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award. This contract has now been formally awarded using the competitive process.
Medway Council looking to commission an effective, accessible and equitable All-Age Drugs and Alcohol Prevention, Treatment and Recovery Service. The service will support children, young people and adults to access full range of interventions (including harm-reduction, clinical and psychosocial treatment, one to one and group support, outreach, recovery services and education). 
 A comprehensive Health Needs assessment has highlighted gaps in the local system, including challenges in transitions between young people’s and adult services, unmet need in both children and adults, the need for trauma informed approaches to engagement and treatment and co-production and lived experience informed service delivery. Whilst improvements have been made within the existing contract term, Medway wishes to commission a fully integrated all-age model that will remove barriers between services and ensure smooth transitions for service users. 
Currently, young people’s and adult substance misuse services operate as separate contracts, commissioned at different times and under different arrangements. This new commissioning arrangement is a major step towards aligning contracts, pathways, governance and workforce under single lead provider model as Medway develops its full all age service. 
The core principles for the new contract are focused on: 
•Tailored, Person-Centred and Age-Appropriate Care
•Prevention and Early Intervention
•Recovery-Focused Support
•Accessible and Flexible Services 
•Partnership and Integrated Working
•Lived Experience and Co-Production
•Safeguarding and Safety
•Evidence-Based Innovation and Accountability
•Staff Wellbeing and Development
The Provider will also be required to deliver a successful Individual Placement Support (IPS) programme, ensuring people using the service have access to evidence-based employment support to help them gain and sustain meaningful employment as part of their recovery journey.
The All-Age Treatment, Prevention and Recovery contract will run for an initial term of 36 months, with the option for two further extensions of 24 months each, subject to mutual agreement.
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award. The standstill period begins on the day after the publication of this notice. Representations by providers must be made to the relevant authority by 18/09/2026. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award a contract under the competitive process of the PSR.’
Written representation can be made to graham.thomas1@Medway.gov.uk
This is an Existing service with an existing Provider.
The contract award criteria are specified in the procurement documents.
Award Decision Makers:
Claire Hurcum, Senior Public Health Manager, claire.hurcum@medway.gov.uk
Svajune Ulinskiene, Health Improvement Programme Manager, svajune.ulinskiene@medway.gov.uk
Steve Chevis, Head of Public Health Programmes, steve.chevis@medway.gov.uk
Aeilish Geldenhuys, Public Health Principal and Strategic Head of Public Health Programmes, aeilish.geldenhuys@medway.gov.uk
No Conflicts of interest.
Key criteria summary
SECTION 1: Quality and Innovation (25%)
The provider demonstrated a comprehensive, high-quality service model that incorporates prevention, treatment, recovery and employment support within an integrated all-age framework. The submission clearly described governance arrangements, leadership responsibilities, clinical oversight, safeguarding and auditing processes, providing confidence in the safe and effective delivery of services. The model detailed clearly described the interventions delivered across all ages and stages of recovery. This included: seven-day clinical and outreach offer, flexible support pathways, self-help and digital interventions, and tailored support for individuals across different age groups and needs.
The provider evidenced a strong commitment to innovation through the use of lived experience in service design and delivery, dedicated innovation/learning approaches, and peer-led initiatives. Innovation was specific to Medway and embedded into staff performance and development. The proposal demonstrated how continuous improvement, collaboration with partner organisations, workforce development and evidence-based practice would be used to enhance outcomes and ensure services remain responsive to emerging needs.
SECTION 2: Integration, collaboration and service sustainability (25%)
The provider presented a clear and credible approach to integrating services across the local treatment and recovery system. The proposal demonstrated strong partnership working with statutory, voluntary and community sector organisations. Including arrangements to support children and young people, transitions between services, coordinated care planning, and co-located delivery models designed to improve access and referral pathways.
The provider placed lived experience at the centre of service development and recovery support, with a strengthened peer mentoring model, recovery-focused community activities and mechanisms for ongoing service improvement informed by service users. Effective approaches to continuity of care, workforce development and succession planning were evidenced, including clear pathways for individuals with lived experience to progress into training, volunteering and employment opportunities. The overall model demonstrated a sustainable approach to service delivery, informed by data, and a person-centred "team around the person" approach.
SECTION 3: Improving access, reducing health inequalities, and facilitating choice (20%)
The provider outlined a flexible service offer delivered through multiple community locations, outreach provision, digital interventions, blended face-to-face and online support, and clinical model. Particular consideration and examples were given to engage underserved populations and ensuring services are taken to where people are.
The provider evidenced a trauma-informed, person-centred approach that takes account of the wider determinants of health and the needs of priority groups. The service model included targeted outreach, women-only provision, collaborative working with partner organisations and mechanisms to reduce barriers to access. Living expertise was embedded throughout service design, delivery, research and evaluation, along with willingness to work with a LERO for independent reviews. The provider also demonstrated a strong commitment to using qualitative and quantitative data to monitor performance, address inequalities (with links to Marmot principles) and continuously improve outcomes for local communities. The provider also gave assurance of transparency through the use of live data systems and dashboards that provide up-to-date performance information. 
Social Value 5% - The provider has set out social value commitments in accordance with the Council's Social Value requirements.
Price 20% - The provider confirmed delivery of the service within the financial envelope.

description:
A direct award is being made by Nuclear Restoration Services Limited (Dounreay) to Mirion Technologies (Canberra) UK Ltd for the supply of specialised analytical equipment to upgrade laboratories on the Dounreay site.
The proposed route to market is a PA23 Direct Award Procedure under Section 41, Schedule 5, Paragraph 7 on the grounds of:
a) a change in supplier would result in the contracting authority receiving goods, services or works that are different from, or incompatible with, the existing goods, services or works, and;
b) the difference or incompatibility would result in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation or maintenance.
This requirement can only be supplied by Mirion Technologies (Canberra) UK Ltd, as the equipment is required to form part of, and integrate with, an existing bespoke analytical system in operation at the Dounreay site. 
Changing supplier would introduce compatibility and integration risks, potentially requiring modification or replacement of existing assets and resulting in additional costs for system changes, validation activities, maintenance arrangements, and staff training. Such changes would also introduce programme delays and could adversely affect NRS's ability to support future statutory, regulatory and decommissioning requirements.
Given the need to maintain compatibility with the existing analytical system and avoid disproportionate technical difficulties in operation and maintenance, the Authority considers that no reasonable alternative or substitute exists capable of delivering the required goods within acceptable levels of risk, cost, and timescale.

title: NSpOC: Sovereign Sensor - Active RF Radar Capability
description:
**This notice supercedes UK3 Planned Procurement Notice reference 2026/S 000-009745, which was issued on 3rd February 2026. Please note the timetable provided remains indicative and subject to internal approvals**
The UK Space Agency (UKSA), as part of the National Space Operations Centre (NSpOC) programme, intends to commence a competitive procurement for the deployment of a sovereign, high‑power (~1 MW class) space surveillance radar in the Southern Hemisphere (final location is still to be determined but bidders should note the requirement to deploy into the Southern Hemisphere) to enhance the UK's Space Surveillance & Tracking (SST) and Space Domain Awareness (SDA) capability.
It is expected that the radar system will operate as a key national asset, providing enhanced detection, tracking and custody of resident space objects, particularly small-size debris and operational satellites in Low Earth Orbit. It will deliver significant improvements to UK resilience, space safety, collision avoidance, re-entry monitoring, fragmentation detection, and wider civil-military situational awareness objectives.
The radar shall be capable of detecting a target with radar cross-section of -22 dBsm (approx. 5cm) at 1,000 km slant range, with probability of detection Pd ≥ 95% and probability of false alarm Pfa ≤ 10⁻⁵, using a Swerling 3 target fluctuation model with a maximum of 100ms integration time. The system shall produce Azimuth (0.01°), Elevation (0.01°), Range (10m), Range Rate (~0.1 m/s) and Radar Cross Section (supplier in m2) measurements. Values in brackets are 1 sigma uncertainties. The requirement is for 24 hour remote, autonomous operation and achieving 10,000 tracks per day at a minimum (equivalent to 417 tracks per hour). 
The budget for this hardware requirement is capped at £25,000,000 exclusive of VAT and will cover the following elements:
* Radar hardware (including, but not limited to, antenna systems, signal generation/timing/processing hardware, power systems, cooling and thermal management)
* Radar software (noting the Authority is likely to specify software covers both edge and cloud elements, with a 10 year licence including free security and basic maintenance updates)
* Software development to integrate software with wider Government systems (including capture and implementation of user stories/change requests to better exploit the equipment provided)
* Two separate training courses - one focused on tasking/sensor capabilities and one focused on hardware support and maintenance
* Obtaining spectrum rights and permissions: whilst the Authority will support the appointed contractor with this, responsibility will rest with the appointed contractor
* Software and hardware support and maintenance for the initial 3 year contract term
* Cyber assurance
* Project and contract management (including interface with the infrastructure contractor)
* Collaboration around installation and commissioning at final deployment location
The following is currently expected to be in scope of the infrastructure and enabling works contract, which is expected to be valued at £5,000,000 exclusive of VAT. Prospective bidders should note that at least some staff are likely to require SC or DV clearance for this requirement. To assist prospective bidders with planning, an indicative requirements list is provided below. Depending on final deployment location, some of these elements may not be required:
* Planning investigation and, if required, planning consents
* Site surveys and ground works (including environmental and site safety surveys)
* Enabling works to prepare the site for radar deployment (e.g. construction of concrete base)
* Site civils and foundations (design and build)
* Power and data connectivity
* Potential utilities connections as required (e.g. drainage) 
* Collaboration around installation and commissioning at final deployment location
* Temporary or permanent access to site, as required
* Site security (e.g. perimeter fencing, CCTV, gates)
* Site support
* Project and contract management (including interface with the radar hardware contractor)
The following is expected to be in scope of neither contract:
* Ongoing utilities costs
* Spare components (the radar contractor will be expected to include in the pricing schedule the cost of spare components)
A suitable location for deployment has been identified but discussions cannot progress further until the actual equipment specification and characteristics are known. The appointed contractor will therefore be required to work closely with the Contracting Authority and the appointed infrastructure contractor to ensure successful deployment. Bidders will be provided with details of the broad location and constraining assumptions at PSQ stage to assist with technical responses, but should note the final location is unlikely to be disclosed until tender stage. The Contracting Authority will only enter into discussions relating to deployment locations with bidders under NDA, noting that detailed discussions will not be possible at SQ stage.
Please note the Contracting Authority will not respond to any further queries raised on the technical specification or conditions of participation at this point: these will need to be raised as formal clarifications at PSQ stage via the e-tendering portal.

title: Market Engagement Notice: EOTIS Coordinator Services
description:
West Northamptonshire Council is undertaking a market engagement exercise to better understand the current provider market for the delivery of Education Otherwise Than in School (EOTIS) Coordinator Services. We are seeking to identify organisations with the experience and capacity to support children, young people, and families in West Northamptonshire through the provision of this service.
The purpose of this engagement is to raise awareness of the opportunity and engage with organisations that currently provide similar services, or that could develop and deliver them in the future. Through this process, the Council aims to expand the range and diversity of providers available to support children and young people accessing EOTIS provision.
The EOTIS Coordinator will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and monitoring all aspects of a child or young person's EOTIS package. This may include arranging and overseeing provision such as tuition, therapies, vocational activities, and enrichment opportunities. The role will ensure that support is appropriate, delivered consistently, and aligned with the provision and outcomes set out in the child or young person's Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).
The EOTIS Coordinator will:
•	Coordinate educational, health, therapeutic, and other support services.
•	Work collaboratively with alternative provisions, families, professionals, and other stakeholders.
•	Monitor attendance, engagement, progress, and outcomes across all elements of provision.
•	Support children and young people through key transition points.
•	Ensure provision is delivered in line with statutory requirements and agreed outcomes.
•	Maintain accurate records and provide reports and information as required by the Local Authority.
Organisations delivering EOTIS Coordination Services must be able to allocate a dedicated EOTIS Coordinator, or case manager, to each child or young person. The level of support required and the number of hours allocated will vary depending on individual needs and family circumstances.
Providers must ensure that staff:
•	Have undergone a comprehensive safer recruitment process in accordance with statutory guidance, including the appropriate pre-employment and safeguarding checks, are suitable to work with children and young people, and possess the necessary qualifications, skills, experience, and safeguarding knowledge to undertake the EOTIS Coordinator role effectively and safely.
•	Have a strong understanding of SEND, EHCP processes, and the statutory framework relating to EOTIS arrangements.
•	Have experience of multi-agency working, case management, and coordinating complex packages of support.
•	Possess the knowledge, skills, and training required to commission, arrange, and manage a range of specialist services, including (but not limited to) academic tuition, therapeutic interventions, and enrichment activities.
•	Maintain an up-to-date knowledge of safeguarding legislation, policies, procedures, and local protocols, ensuring that any concerns relating to the welfare of children and young people are promptly identified, accurately recorded, and escalated through the appropriate channels.

title: Provision of Hospital Based Domestic Abuse Advocacy (HBDAA) Services
description:
Project background: 
Since 2014, City Hall has invested in embedding youth Independent Domestic Violence Advocates (IDVAs) into London’s Major Trauma Centres (MTCs). 
Since 2023, this programme of work, referred to as hospital-based domestic abuse advocacy (HBDAA), has been overseen and managed by the VRU. Prior to the VRU, this programme and investment had been overseen and managed by MOPAC within City Hill, aligned to the Mayor’s Police & Crime Plan (PCP). 
The HBDAA programme represents a violence reduction initiative, heavily aligned to the VRU’s own violence reduction strategies, most notably: the trusted relationship between a young person, and a trusted adult, as well as the concept of place, reaching young people where they are, and, in this case, leveraging a reachable moment in the lives of young people to break patterns of violence and harm.  
Additionally, this intervention sits within a wider programme of hospital-based initiatives, specifically, operating alongside the VRU’s hospital-based youth work (HBYW) programme, which embeds highly skilled and specialised youth workers into London’s four MTCs and eight London A&E units. 
Description of the service 
The purpose of embedding these IDVAs is to support children and young people who have been impacted by domestic abuse and other gender based harm; IDVAs are there to offer a supportive and stabilising presence in crisis or distress, and help young people cope and recover from the trauma of physical or psychological injury due to domestic abuse, and help disrupt future patterns of violence and harm. 
The service engages young people aged 11–25 who present at Major Trauma Centres (MTCs) as victims of domestic abuse, or who are identified as being at risk of future harm. IDVAs provide practical support, advocacy, and help to coordinate a broader safeguarding response for the young person, working alongside clinical and community partners to help young people access appropriate services and support. Support offered typically at the point of presentation may extend beyond that of the hospital, and into the community. 
Target audience 
The VRU expects the Service to proactively identify, assess, and engage, young people, aged 11-25, who present at MTCs with injuries resulting from domestic abuse, or other gender-based harms.  
The following eligibility criteria will apply to the young people offered the Service. 
A young person: 
- will present at one of the specific MTCs within the scope of this service, AND; will be aged between 11 and 25 years of age;  
Additionally, a young person: 
- will have been, or will be suspected as having been, the victim of domestic abuse, OR; will have been, or will be suspected as having been, the victim of child sexual abuse, OR; will have been, or will be suspected as having been, the victim of rape, OR; will have been, or will be suspected as having been, the victim of sexual exploitation; and, or where a suspected safeguarding issue has arisen.  
This list is not intended to be exhaustive, and the Provider will be expected to use their professional judgment, sometimes in collaboration with hospital staff, to identify forms of vulnerability that warrant intervention.  
Scope of delivery 
Services will be delivered in London’s four MTCs, namely: 
- King’s College Hospital 
- Royal London Hospital 
- St George’s Hospital 
- St Mary’s Hospital 
Whilst the principles of delivery will remain the same across all hospitals, it is important that the successful bidder demonstrates a strong understanding of, and connection to, the local communities and systems in which their allocated hospitals are situated. 
The specific outcomes which the VRU are seeking through this provision include, but are not limited to: 
- Supporting young people to access positive opportunities and support. 
- Disrupting cycles of violence and reducing violence and harm. 
- Ensuring that children and young people feel and are safe. 
- Reducing hospital (re)admissions/attendance. 
- Reducing offending / severity of offending.

title: 9005401 - Supply of K14 SWIFT Beamline KB Mirror System
description:
Located on the Harwell Science & Innovation Campus in Oxfordshire, Diamond Light Source (DLS) is a leading-edge facility for science, engineering and innovation. DLS allows researchers from academia and industry to investigate the structure and behaviour of the world around us at the atomic and molecular level.
To continue delivering the world-changing science that Diamond enables, the facility is being upgraded to Diamond-II, a co-ordinated programme of development that combines a major machine upgrade with new instruments and complementary improvements to optics, detectors, sample environment and delivery capabilities, and computing, as well as integrated and correlative methods. This will be transformative in speed and spatial resolution and will offer users streamlined access to enhanced instruments for life and physical sciences.
The scope of the contract is for the design, supply of material, manufacture, assembly, test, delivery, installation and commissioning of a two-mirror combined system (a pair of
Kirkpatrick-Baez (KB) mirrors) and its position adjustment systems. The mirrors will focus the beam onto a sample positioned in the K14 beamline second end-station. 
• The minimum scope of the contract should include: HFM - Horizontally Focusing Mirror  Horizontally (outboard) reflecting, monochromatic beam mirror & mechanics.
• VFM - Vertically Focusing Mirror- Vertically (upward) reflecting, monochromatic beam mirror & mechanics.
• Temperature monitoring for interlocking.
• Vacuum vessel. 
• Support frame. 
• Interface to beamline services. 
• Training for Diamond personnel in the operation of the mirrors 
• Installation of the mirrors in their benders at the DLS Optics Metrology Lab (OML).

title: Provision of T Quest Forms and Bags
description:
This is the provision of T-Quest Blue and Pink Label Sheets, which are used within laboratory processes to categorise and identify patient samples. The colour-coded labels support the accurate tracking, processing, and management of specimens throughout the testing pathway, enabling rapid visual recognition by laboratory staff and reducing the risk of processing errors. T- Quest specimen bags are used for the secure and contamination- free transport of patient samples between collection points and the laboratory.
The colour-coded label system is embedded within existing laboratory processes and enables rapid visual identification of specimens, supporting efficient workflow management and reducing the risk of processing errors. The associated specimen bags provide secure and contamination-free transport of samples between collection points and laboratory facilities. Together, these products contribute directly to patient safety by maintaining sample integrity, traceability and accurate identification from collection through to analysis.
A change of supplier would require significant operational changes, including the reconfiguration of printer settings, amendment of templates and label formats, and extensive validation and testing activities across multiple sites. Such changes would introduce implementation risks, place additional resource demands on clinical and laboratory teams, and create the potential for disruption to critical pathology services.

title: Gloucestershire Dental Treatment Hub
description:
The title of this service has been renamed from 'Dental Services within a Centre of Dental Excellence' as it was titled throughout the procurement process to 'Gloucestershire Dental Treatment Hub at University of Gloucestershire (UoG) Three Counties Dental School'.
NHS Gloucestershire Integrated Care Board (GICB) sought providers who have the capability and capacity to deliver Dental Services in Gloucester.
Fundamentally this contract seeks to increase access to NHS dentistry in a part of the county where deprivation is greatest by working in partnership to commission a new bespoke primary care Dental Treatment Hub facility in a fit for purpose environment.  
•	The contract will be a Personal Dental Services (PDS) contract to deliver dental services as part of a Gloucestershire Dental Treatment Hub in Gloucester. Premises are located at 3rd floor, City Campus, Northgate Street, Gloucester, GL1 1SQ.
•	The premises are mandated and owned and leased by the University of Gloucestershire (UoG). The successful provider will need to secure a lease with UoG for the duration of the PDS contract term.
•	A draft Heads of Terms were included in the Invitation to Tender (ITT) pack which sets out the expected terms and conditions between the owner of the building and the service provider.  
•	Construction has been undertaken on behalf of UoG, and floor plans and room data sheets are included in the ITT pack to inform potential bidders about the premises and what is provided as part of the building fit out.  
•	The successful provider will need to provide any additional fit out and equipment to deliver the services.  It will also be expected to fund associated, recurrent revenue costs, for example servicing and maintenance; rent and rates; cleaning and lighting.
•	The premises will have space for up to 6 dental chairs.
•	There is an expectation that the provider is or becomes a postgraduate training practice and hosts foundation dentists. 
•	Funding for hosting foundation dentists is awarded and administered by NHS Workforce Training and Education (NHS WTE) and the successful provider will be expected to apply to NHS WTE for funding.
•	The PDS contract term is for an initial term of 10 years, with an option to extend for any period up to a further 5 years, and then for a further 5 years, at the sole discretion of the Commissioner. 
•	Rental payment and services are currently scheduled to commence on 1st March 2027.
•	Service will commence no later than 6 months after contract award (scheduled for 1st September 2026), unless there is an agreement with the Commissioner to extend the mobilisation period.
•	The contract term and service payments will start on the service commencement date. 
•	The Commissioner had a maximum financial envelope available of £1,200,000 per annum. The total maximum contract value for the duration excluding extensions is £12,000,000, and £24,000,000 including extensions.
•	Subject to the detail of Dental Contract Reform, the successful provider will need to deliver urgent care, dental access & health inequalities pathways and routine care as part of the contract. 
•	Following discussion and agreement by the commissioner, the successful provider may offer private treatment from the same premises however this must not be at the detriment of NHS patients or the provider's delivery of the PDS contract.
•	TUPE was not applicable for this procurement process. 
This exercise was carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit (SCW) on behalf of the Commissioner.
