description:
We are a family of Catholic schools in the Roman Catholic Deanery of the Lea Valley and whilst each school retains its own distinctive ethos and mission, we are united in our endeavours to deliver a Catholic education excelling in the academic, pastoral and spiritual life, and which produces fully flourishing pupils. We are currently 8 primary schools and 1 secondary school, and we have active plans for imminent growth which will result in more schools joining the Trust within the next 12-18months.
We take much inspiration from by the charism of St. Francis - To be caring towards everyone in the community; Being compassionate - standing up especially for the poor and oppressed; Acting with reverence towards all creation; Being peacemakers, reconcilers, and healers to all those in need. 
Further information regarding the Trust can be obtained here: https://www.stfrancistrust.net/
Tender information:
Our Schools:
1.Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
2.St Augustine's Catholic Primary School
3.St Cross Catholic Primary School
4.St Joseph's Catholic Primary School (Bishop's Stortford)
5.St Joseph's Catholic Primary School (Hertford)
6.St Joseph's Catholic Primary School (Waltham Cross)
7.St Thomas of Canterbury Catholic Primary School
8.St Paul's Catholic Primary School
9.St Mary's Catholic School (secondary)
All 9 schools listed above (8 primary and 1 secondary) – are participating in this tender.  Please note this is a growing trust where additional schools may join during the new contract term. Additional schools that join may, at the Trust’s discretion, be added to this contract.
The successful tenderer will be required to provide excellent catering services to the schools. 
The contract term being tendered is for three years, 1st September 2026 – 31st August 2029. There is an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 31st August 2031.
The contract offers an excellent opportunity to review and propose enhancements to the current catering services at all of the Schools within the Trust. This includes but is not limited to; breakfast, morning break, lunchtime and after school services, over the academic year, plus hospitality services upon request.
The Trust is keen to secure a high quality catering service including fresh locally sourced ingredients prepared on site, with a menu design that is flexible to suit the requirements of each of the Trust’s specific students. The Trust is proud of its ‘family ethos’ and expects both a tightly managed service and a management style delivered by the successful contractor that supports, encourages and develops the catering staff. Management must be present and engaged, actively building relationships at both school and Trust level and driving the contract forwards at all times. Monthly management information is expected to be timely, accurate and easy to interpret.
The Trust is not obliged to accept the lowest price submitted for this tender, rather each school is keen to secure ‘best value’ from this contract and to deliver ‘best value’ to its students. Innovative and creative ideas as to how the services can be developed and value added, will be welcomed. The Trust seeks a contractor that is keen to work in partnership and who will deliver to its highest abilities, at all times. 
Competitive Flexible Procedure 
This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here a minimum of 5 candidates (or less, in the event less than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates, will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. 
Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 40% price and 60% quality.
Value of contract:
The annual value of the current contract is £950,000
Therefore, the value of this contract is £4,750,000 
The contract shall be a guaranteed performance contract with any hospitality requirements billed separately.
The tender process will be run under a two stage Competitive Flexible procedure. 
Additional requirements and information:
•The Trust has a minimum requirement for a contractor’s employers' liability and public liability insurances of £5 million. 
•The minimum annual turnover that your company must have achieved to be considered for this opportunity is £2 million.
•There are incumbent catering staff currently within the Local Government Pension Scheme.  
•The catering services are currently contracted to Aspens Services and HCL.
•As above, please note this is a growing Trust and any other schools that may join the Trust during the tenure of this new catering contract may, at the Trust’s discretion, be added to this contract.
•Please note that the successful tenderer will be required to pay the RIVA tender fee for this project directly to RIVA, upon their contract award.

title: Streetlighting Services - Maintenance & Capital programme
description:
Future Street Lighting Service
What Staffordshire County Council and Stoke-on-Trent City Council are seeking from the market
Staffordshire County Council (SCC) and Stoke-on-Trent City Council (SoTCC) are working together to develop successor arrangements for their existing street lighting PFI contracts, which expire on 18 May 2028 and 31 August 2028 respectively. Our priority is to secure a safe, legal, reliable and value-for-money service, with effective mobilisation and uninterrupted service continuity from the relevant commencement date for each authority.
Our anticipated requirement
Subject to the outcome of the business case and formal approvals, the current direction is a jointly procured, single-contractor service, potentially comprising separate authority-specific arrangements under a common commercial and technical structure.
The anticipated scope includes:
•	planned, preventative and reactive maintenance;
•	emergency attendance and response;
•	electrical and structural inspections, testing and compliance;
•	investigation and repair of faults referred by the authorities;
•	access to professional, technical and street lighting design services where required;
•	delivery of flexible capital investment and asset-replacement programmes;
•	maintenance of accurate, accessible and authority-owned asset information;
•	customer, stakeholder and third-party liaison; and
•	mobilisation, transition and service-continuity support.
This integrated model is intended to provide clear end-to-end accountability while retaining flexibility for design services to be commissioned through the contractor where required, thereby managing operational interfaces and supporting effective delivery.
The present planning assumption is an initial four-year contract with an option to extend for up to a further four years. Any extension would be subject to satisfactory performance, affordability, value for money and the requirements of the successor authorities.
What we want from our future contractor
We are looking for a capable and collaborative delivery partner that can:
•	Protect public safety and statutory compliance, supported by competent people, robust systems and clearly defined emergency and routine response arrangements.
•	Deliver a reliable, customer-focused service, responding to faults referred by the authorities and completing investigations and repairs within agreed service levels, while supporting the authorities’ management of customer enquiries and complaints.
•	Assume clear operational accountability across maintenance, inspection and capital delivery, with the capability to provide design services when commissioned and to work effectively with each authority’s intelligent-client team.
•	Demonstrate whole-life value, balancing maintenance, energy consumption, capital replacement, risk, asset condition and long-term affordability rather than focusing only on the lowest initial price.
•	Mobilise successfully from the existing PFI arrangements, including the controlled transfer and validation of asset, maintenance, condition and operational information.
•	Maintain high-quality asset data, with open access for the authorities, appropriate interfaces with authority systems and no avoidable supplier dependency.
•	Provide flexibility, allowing each authority to vary investment levels, service priorities and programmes within an agreed contractual framework.
•	Drive measurable improvement, including energy efficiency, carbon reduction, productivity, digital working and appropriate use of central management, smart asset and connectivity technologies.
•	Support responsible employment and supply-chain practices, including workforce transition where applicable, health and safety, skills development, local economic benefit, social value and opportunities for SMEs.
•	Operate through open-book, evidence-led contract management, with meaningful performance measures, timely reporting, effective escalation and a constructive approach to resolving problems.
•	Identify innovation and commercial opportunities, where these offer a demonstrable benefit to the authorities and communities, with benefits, savings and risks shared on a fair and transparent basis.
These expectations reflect the authorities’ emphasis on whole-life value, flexibility, innovation, energy efficiency, clear service levels, effective KPIs and strong contract management.

title: CEFAS26-78 Contract for the provision of a marine environmental survey vessel.
description:
Cefas and Natural England (NE) have been working collaboratively to deliver a monitoring survey within the Kentish Knock East (KKNE) Marine Protected Areas (MPA) as part of the ongoing MPA monitoring programme funded by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra). Through this programme, Cefas co-ordinates some of the evidence collection for the monitoring of MPAs in English waters.
The survey aims to support NE’s monitoring objectives and provide robust evidence to inform conservation measures (Type 1 monitoring) as well as at assessing the recovery of benthic habitats after the implementation of proposed management measures within the MPA (Type 3 monitoring).
The first part of the survey at KKNE was undertaken in November 2025 and focuses on grab sampling. However, the data collection could not be completed due to equipment failure. Cefas and NE are therefore seeking to deliver the remaining objectives of the survey:
1. Monitor the extent and distribution of sediment Broadscale Habitats (BSH) through the acquisition of imagery data, using an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) as the primary system, with a Drop-Down Video (DDV) camera as a back-up.
2. Monitor the carbon content of sediment BSH features through the collection of sediment imagery, using a Sediment Profile Imaging (SPI) camera.
Objective 1 above will be conducted in collaboration with a team from the University of Southampton (UoS).
Survey design:
The KKNE survey design adopts a Before-After Control-Impact approach and a box design, to collect data from within the MPA and in control areas outside the site boundary. The boxes are labelled Case Study Areas (CSAs): two located within the MCZ (‘impact’) and two corresponding CSAs outside the MCZ (‘control’).
Each CSA has an approximate area of 8-9 km2 and were positioned to avoid existing infrastructure in the MPA such as a power cable running through the south of the site (Figure 1). A 1nm buffer was applied to all infrastructure to delineate the survey boxes following the recommendation of the Crown Estate Seabed survey licence (arranged by Natural England). Each control CSA has been selected for comparable fishing pressure, and environmental conditions (e.g. depth and sediment type).
Vessel Specification Requirement:
Cefas requires provision of a marine environmental survey vessel for a single mobilisation of up to 6 survey days, planned at neap tide in September or October 2026 (exact dates will be agreed post-award).
Cefas requires the use of an MCA (MISW) “small workboat” class Category 2 coded survey vessel to support deployment and recovery of environmental survey equipment with a maximum single lift of up to 400 kg. The vessel will act as a deployment and recovery platform for equipment operated by:
• University of Southampton (UoS) – mini Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV).
• Cefas – Sediment Profile Imaging (SPI) and Drop-Down Video (DDV) camera; and
Cefas/UoS/NE will be responsible for survey planning, deployed equipment, equipment operation and data acquisition.
The Supplier will allow for and assist in the vessel being mobilised by a team of up to 5 Cefas personnel to undertake:
• Mini AUV (~100 kg) deployment and recovery operations
The Supplier will provide safe vessel positioning and competent deck operations to support repeated AUV launch and recovery cycles throughout the survey period.
• SPI camera (up to 400kg) deployment and recovery
At each station selected by Cefas/UoS/NE (to be confirmed at start-up meeting), the SPI will be deployed (maximum of 10 stations per CSA). At each station the camera will be deployed, and five replicates (“hops”) will be collected, between each hop the camera will be raised and the vessel moved 5 m. Two images are collected at each replicate, giving a total of 10 images per station. The location of the sampling station will be provided at the start up meeting. Cefas will provide an engineer that can support/advise on deployment and recovery.
• Contingency: DDV camera deployment and recovery
In case the AUV proves unsuitable for the environmental conditions at the site, a DDV camera frame will be used to collect video and still images at all proposed stations (location to be confirmed at the start up meeting). DDV camera sampling will comprise of an extended video transect of 100-150 m, providing sufficient data coverage to detect change in BSHs across each CSA. Cefas will provide an engineer that can support/advise on deployment and recovery.
Survey planning:
Cefas/UoS/NE will undertake the planning (including access), notifications (including Notice to Mariners) - with the Supplier being expected to ensure safe execution of the vessel operations. Should licences or consents be required (e.g. a Marine Licence) these will be obtained by Cefas and provided to the Supplier prior to the survey.
Cefas/UoS/NE will be providing survey staff (up to 5 persons) for operation of the above-described environmental survey equipment. Personnel will comprise up to 2 survey staff from Cefas, up to 2 survey staff from UoS and up to one survey staff from NE.
Summary of provision:
The Supplier will provide:
• An MCA MISW “small workboat” class Category 2 coded workboat, meeting the Vessel Specifications set out in this document.
• A-frame or crane with a minimum Safe Working Load (SWL) of 400 kg, compliant with LOLER and PUWER.
• Adequate deck space for safe AUV/cameras handling operations
• Crew support for launch and recovery operations, including, at minimum, a suitably qualified vessel Master, a suitably trained and experienced Mate, and competent deck crew / ABs sufficient to ensure safe lifting operations.
• Welfare facilities for up to 5 embarked Cefas/UoS/NE personnel for the duration of the charter.
• Valid insurance, including evidence that the vessel's Protection & Indemnity (P&I) insurance covers the additional Cefas/UoS/NE personnel on board for the duration of the charter. A copy of the insurance certificate is to be provided with the bid.
• A demonstrable track record of marine environmental survey equipment deployment and data acquisition (to be summarised in the bid).
The requirements of the Vessel include:
• Use of the vessel for up to 6 days during the contract period including mobilisation and demobilisation. Final survey dates will be confirmed with the Supplier as early as possible following contract award and no later than two weeks before mobilisation to allow for adequate planning and scheduling.
• Full compliance with the Vessel Specifications listed in subsequent sections of this document.
Cefas will:
• Supply up to 5 survey personnel
• Be responsible for all environmental survey equipment provision, operation, acquisition and data quality.

Additional or repeat services - under paragraph 7, Schedule 5 of the Act
The contract concerns the supply of services by the existing supplier which are intended as an extension to, or partial replacement of existing services provided by the existing supplier whereby:
(a) A change of supplier would require the contracting authority to acquire services that are incompatible with those already in place, with which they must interoperate

The services are not operated as standalone products but form part of a wider integrated technology ecosystem supporting both public and private market investment activities. In particular:
• the contracting authority's private markets operations rely upon data and functionality provided through the existing supplier's platform, which forms an integral part of its investment analysis processes.
• the contracting authority's public markets operations utilise data which is integrated with the supplier's software systems and other connected risk-management systems.
Absence of competition for technical reasons - under paragraph 6, Schedule 5 of the Act.
a) due to an absence of competition for technical reasons, only a particular supplier can supply the services required
The contracting authority has considered the availability of alternative suppliers in the market. While alternative providers may offer certain individual capabilities, they are not technically able to provide a readily substitutable solution capable of replacing the full range of integrated services currently utilised by the contracting authority without substantial technical redevelopment and disruption.
(b) there are no reasonable alternatives to those services.

The provision of bed based nursing services commissioned by Suffolk County Council in Partnership with Morar Living to provide a swift discharge of medically optimised customers from the acute as part of the Discharge to Assess model.
Due to current provider of the service having declined to continue their services for the remaining contract period, a Direct Award has been agreed.
 The proposed approach is a 12-month direct award to a new provider with an option of a plus one year extension.
The rationale for this includes:
•	The operational complexities of providing D2A care.
•	The need to ensure continuity and avoid disruption to hospital discharge pathways.
•	The preventative role of the service under Section 2 of the Care Act 2014.
•	The need to provide stability within the local care market.
•	The importance of giving the new provider sufficient certainty to recruit, retain and mobilise staff.
•	The need to plan capacity across both winter and summer periods.
•	Alignment with the wider 12-month extension arrangements.
•	The fact that there are currently no voids within the area, demonstrating continued demand for the service.
•	The proposed provider's proven track record in delivering D2A services and ability to deliver the service successfully.
•	The proposed provider currently has capacity, including approximately 14 voids, which is significantly more than any other provider in the area and supports immediate mobilisation.
•	The provider's willingness to engage proactively with Suffolk County Council and work collaboratively to build a strong and productive partnership relationship.
A 12-month arrangement would provide sufficient time for the new provider to mobilise and establish the service, while also allowing commissioners to monitor delivery and develop a longer-term procurement approach.

title: Technology Services
description:
Sanctuary Group is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) with prospective suppliers and other interested organisations operating within the technology services market. This is a broad, multi-service opportunity across an enterprise technology estate currently estimated at approximately 265-300 applications, spanning SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft platforms and other enterprise technologies and supporting both operational and transformational technology services.
Sanctuary Group's Technology Directorate has undergone significant change across its operating model and technology estate. Sanctuary Group is therefore assessing sourcing arrangements for technology services that support the delivery, development, transformation and ongoing operation of the estate in 2027.
This engagement gives participating organisations an opportunity to contribute market insight and inform potential service groupings, sourcing approaches and procurement considerations before final decisions are made.
The purpose of this engagement is to:
•	Provide an overview of Sanctuary Group, its technology landscape and strategic objectives.
•	Obtain market feedback on potential service groupings and sourcing approaches.
•	Understand supplier capability, capacity and appetite.
•	Explore potential procurement structures, routes to market and commercial models.
•	Understand mobilisation, transition and service-delivery considerations.
•	Inform the development of Sanctuary Group's technology procurement strategy.
Organisations interested in participating should register with Group Procurement from publication. The supplier questionnaire is intended to be issued with, or shortly after, the notice. A supplier webinar is proposed for early-mid October 2026, with questionnaire responses proposed to close in October 2026. The indicative timetable is set out below.
Procurement Objectives
Sanctuary Group is considering requirements across a range of technology service areas, including:
•	Application Managed Services (AMS)
•	Application Development, Product Management, Project Delivery and Programme Delivery Services
•	Technology Consultancy & Advisory Services
•	Data Services (Data Engineering, Data Governance, Data Quality Management, Master Data Management, Data Architecture, Data Modelling, Reporting & Analytics, Data Platforms and Storage Management)
•	Data Integration & Ingestion Services
•	Cloud Services & Platform Support
•	Licensing & Software Asset Management
•	AI, Innovation & Emerging Technologies
These services may apply across a range of technology platforms and business capabilities, including SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft platforms and other enterprise applications.
The service areas above are indicative and are intended to support market engagement and feedback. The final service structure, grouping, boundaries, scope, sourcing model and procurement approach have not been determined and will be informed by market feedback, commercial assessment, legal advice and governance decisions.
Sanctuary Group is interested in approaches that:
•	Encourage innovation, continuous improvement and thought leadership.
•	Support effective competition and system integrations.
•	Enable participation by SMEs, specialist providers and larger organisations where appropriate.
•	Provide flexibility and scalability to meet changing requirements.
•	Support efficient procurement and call-off arrangements.
•	Deliver demonstrable value for money.
•	Support both business-as-usual and strategic transformational requirements.
•	Enable access to specialist skills and capabilities when required.
Areas where Market Feedback is Sought
Sanctuary Group welcomes feedback on:
•	Service groupings and lotting structures.
•	Supplier appetite for individual service areas and combinations of services.
•	Supplier capability and partnerships across individual and multiple service groupings.
•	The benefits and risks of platform-specific versus platform-agnostic service models.
•	Suitable procurement routes, commercial frameworks and contractual arrangements.
•	Commercial and pricing approaches.
•	Information required to support supplier participation and commercial engagement.
•	The most appropriate treatment of Data Services and Integration Services, including whether they are best delivered separately, together, embedded within wider services or through alternative arrangements.
•	Transition and mobilisation considerations.
•	Supplier participation barriers and opportunities.
•	Any aspects of the proposed scope or approach that suppliers believe could be improved.
•	Approaches that maximise innovation, market participation and long-term value.
Engagement Activities
Sanctuary Group currently intends to undertake the following engagement activities:
Supplier Webinar
Interested organisations may be invited to attend a market engagement webinar covering:
•	Introduction to Sanctuary Group.
•	Overview of Sanctuary Group's technology environment.
•	Strategic objectives and priorities.
•	Potential service areas, sourcing considerations and procurement approaches.
•	Indicative timelines.
•	Questions and answers.
Supplier Questionnaire
Interested organisations may be invited to complete a structured questionnaire seeking feedback on:
•	Service areas and capabilities.
•	Supplier appetite.
•	Service grouping and sourcing approaches.
•	Procurement and commercial considerations.
•	Procurement vehicle and route-to-market considerations.
•	Transition and mobilisation considerations.
•	Participation barriers.
•	Innovation opportunities.
•	Comparable market experience.
Supplier Discussions
Sanctuary Group may invite organisations to participate in follow-up discussions to further explore market feedback or clarify responses where appropriate.
Expressions of Interest
Organisations wishing to participate in this engagement should register their interest by contacting Group Procurement at:
group.procurement@sanctuary.co.uk
Using the subject line:
Technology Services PME 2026
When registering interest, organisations should provide:
•	Organisation name.
•	Primary contact name. It is the responsibility of the primary contact to forward the invitation to other attendees within their organisation. 
•	Contact email address.
•	Summary of relevant services and capabilities.
•	Areas of interest.
•	Proposed attendees (where applicable).
Following registration, Group Procurement will provide further information regarding engagement activities, webinar arrangements, questionnaires and any subsequent supplier discussions.
Indicative Timetable
PME Notice Publication: 21st September 2026
Supplier Registration From Publication to 9th October 2026
Supplier Questionnaire Issue:	Minimum 1 week prior to the 
Supplier Webinar: Early- mid October 2026
Supplier Discussions: October 2026
Questionnaire Submission Deadline: Late October 2026
Review of Market Feedback: Late October 2026
Procurement Strategy Confirmation: Following review of market feedback and internal advice
These dates are indicative only and may be amended. 
Important Information
Sanctuary Group has not reached a final decision regarding:
•	Procurement structure.
•	Service groupings.
•	Lotting arrangements.
•	Procurement vehicle.
•	Route to market.
•	Commercial model.
•	Contractual arrangements.
•	Supplier model.
•	Contract duration.
•	Estimated value.
•	Implementation approach.
The purpose of this engagement is to obtain market feedback and challenge assumptions before any final decisions are made.
Feedback may inform:
•	Procurement strategy.
•	Sourcing approach.
•	Procurement vehicle and route-to-market decisions.
•	Service structures and groupings.
•	Qualification and participation considerations.
•	Procurement and call-off mechanisms.
•	Commercial arrangements.
•	Contractual arrangements.
•	Transition considerations.
Participation in this engagement is entirely voluntary and will not form part of any subsequent procurement process.
Participation, non-participation, discussions or responses provided during this engagement will not provide any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process.
Sanctuary Group reserves the right to amend, refine, combine, separate, postpone or discontinue any aspect of the proposed approach following completion of this engagement.
Sanctuary Group is not obliged to proceed with any procurement activity and makes no commitment to award any contract as a result of this engagement.

title: Virano Managed Service Catering Framework
description: Virano Frameworks Ltd is seeking to establish a single supplier framework agreement for the provision of managed catering services, primarily for education settings and other eligible contracting authorities. The call-off process will be used to confirm customer-specific requirements, apply the approved pricing methodology, agree mobilisation and service-specific details and complete the relevant call-off contract. title: Repairs & Maintenance contract for Our Town Hall
description:
Future Repairs and Maintenance Services for Manchester Town Hall
Manchester City Council is undertaking preparatory work for the future procurement of repairs and maintenance services to support the ongoing operation of the refurbished Manchester Town Hall.
As the Town Hall returns to full operational use following the completion of refurbishment works, the Council intends to establish a short-term service arrangement to provide essential repairs and maintenance support during the initial occupancy period and whilst longer-term service requirements are reviewed and developed.
In parallel, the Council is developing its future asset management, maintenance and building support requirements with a view to undertaking a comprehensive procurement exercise for a longer-term contract. The future procurement is expected to encompass planned preventative maintenance, reactive repairs, minor capital works and associated technical building maintenance services required to support the safe, efficient and effective operation of Manchester Town Hall as a major civic and heritage asset.
This pipeline notice is being published to provide advance visibility of the Council's future procurement intentions and to support supplier awareness of a potential forthcoming opportunity. The scope, procurement strategy, contract structure, estimated value and anticipated timetable remain under development and may be subject to change.
Publication of this notice does not constitute a call for competition, invitation to tender or commitment by the Council to commence a procurement process or award a contract. Further information will be published in due course should the Council decide to proceed with a formal procurement exercise.
The future procurement is expected to include maintenance activities that reflect the operational, heritage and conservation requirements associated with one of the UK's most significant historic civic buildings.
Estimated contract dates are subject to change at the Council's discretion but it is currently anticipated that the contract length will be 8 years (4+2+2).

title: SEMD Red Button Class 1 drivers
description:
Our initial proposed specification includes:
Emergency Driver Provision: Ability to supply up to 10 qualified Class 1 drivers on a 24/7, 365-day basis. Drivers may be required to operate anywhere across Yorkshire as requirements may be as the Solo Driver from our depot in south Leeds or as a relay driver taking over operations at a location in Yorkshire such as Cities, Towns, Villages or other rural settings.
Driver Competence and Compliance: Drivers must hold a Category C+E (Class 1) licence with no more than 6 penalty points, Driver CPC, EUSR Water Hygiene Card, NRSWA qualifications for basic traffic management, Moffett licence, relevant experience operating the required vehicle types, no goods vehicle-related convictions or endorsements, and appropriate PPE.
Operational Resilience: Agencies must be able to manage driver hours and provide replacement drivers as required to maintain continuous tanker operations during prolonged incidents, ensuring uninterrupted service availability 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
Areas for Market Engagement Discussion
- Service Delivery Model
Ability to meet the proposed Specification under either a Full Red Alert or Phased Red Alert options. Examples being
Full mobilisation of up to 10 drivers within 12 hours of activation,
Phased mobilisation of 3 drivers within 6 hours, a further 3 within 9 hours, and up to 4 additional drivers within 12 hours
An alternative phased driver response structure that results in no less than 10 drivers within 12 hours of activation.
Preferred delivery approach and any alternative mobilisation models the market would recommend.
Geographic coverage and ability to support incidents anywhere across Yorkshire.
- Driver Availability and Resilience
Capacity to provide up to 10 qualified drivers at short notice.
Approach to managing driver hours, fatigue and shift rotations during extended incidents.
Availability of contingency and replacement drivers.
- Driver Competence and Training
Current availability of drivers holding the required qualifications and licences.
Timescales and costs associated with obtaining any missing qualifications.
Approach to Yorkshire Water specific training requirements, including CALM Network Training and Tanker Filling & Water Quality Sampling training.
- Commercial Model
Preferred pricing mechanisms, including standby, mobilisation and deployment charges.
Impact of maintaining a dedicated emergency response capability on pricing.
Any market considerations regarding contract length.
- Operational Requirements
Management of PPE, vehicle checks through YW system, compliance and safety requirements.
Experience supporting utilities, emergency response or similar critical services.
Requirements for depot access, inductions and onboarding.
- Contract and Risk
Appropriate performance measures and service credits.
Insurance requirements and liability considerations.
Key risks suppliers foresee in delivering the service and proposed mitigations.
A 24/7 duty management function capable of receiving activations and managing escalations throughout an incident.
Assurance of guaranteed service during periods of high national demand
- Innovation and Market Feedback
Suggestions to improve the specification or mobilisation requirements.
Opportunities for technology-enabled workforce management, tracking and reporting.
Any barriers to participation that Yorkshire Water should consider before commencing procurement.
These topics should help determine whether the proposed SLAs are achievable, whether the market has sufficient qualified resources, and what commercial structure will provide the most resilient emergency response service.

title: CPT_26_25 Market Data Software Subscription
description:
At the NAO, we have a business need to access reliable market and financial information to inform our financial audit and value for money audit work. Around 50 financial audit teams across the office accessed these services in the 2025-26 cycle. This is a business-critical need, used in providing independent evidence to support key assumptions in asset and liability valuations and historical pricing. Our value for money audit work also requires access to high-quality market, corporate, financial, geopolitical and sector intelligence that is not readily available through standard internet searches or publicly available government sources.
We require the provision of a product that provides quick and efficient access to asset and liability prices as well as economic and market data. The minimum requirements for this service are as follows:
•	A software product capable of meeting International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 500 requirements that provides quick and efficient access to asset and liability prices, such as bonds, equities and fund investments in both a real-time and historic basis, and the ability to price derivative instruments such as interest rate swaps.
•	The software must also provide economic and market data such as current and past FX rates, access to financial indexes, basic company financial and performance metrics, sovereign and corporate credit ratings, macroeconomic data and forecasts (such as GDP).
•	We require flexibility to retrieve data for a variety of dates and timepoints and in different formats for larger vs smaller volume requirements. The volume of data we require varies from day to day and the software should be able to accommodate changes in the volume of requests without compromising service or performance, as well as high-volume requests.
•	Unlimited access to a dedicated helpdesk to help resolve routine queries over functionality and performance, as well as more complex aspects of the software. In addition, access to an account manager is required, who can efficiently resolve any issues with the software.
•	Regular training, as well as the opportunity to occasionally engage in 'deep dives' i.e. more detailed questions surrounding methodology (such as valuations for particular financial instruments or datasets). Both of these benefits are required at no extra cost above the core subscription.
•	The software itself must be available for use year-round and for 24hrs a day. Any supplier IT/service outages must be resolved promptly and as a priority.
•	Ability to retain retrieved data on our audit files in accordance with statutory requirements is essential. The provider must permit the unrestricted retention and storage of market data and supporting evidence on NAO audit files, ensuring compliance with audit methodology and quality requirements.

title: Switzerland – Construction work – La Punt – Filisur – Sils im Domleschg (i.D.) – Baumeisterarbeiten Tiefbau
description: Le tronçon de ligne La Punt - Filisur - Sils im Domleschg (i.D.) fait partie du tracé 380 kV TR1360 Pradella - Sils i.D. Étant donné que ce tronçon joue un rôle central dans les échanges d'électricité avec l'Autriche et l'Italie et que la ligne a presque atteint la fin de sa durée de vie technique, une rénovation et une modernisation complètes s'imposent. Le présent projet porte sur l'ensemble du tronçon de La Punt à Sils i. D., qui compte 132 pylônes et s'étend sur environ 43,5 km. Le tronçon de ligne commence à La Punt au pylône 1360x127, puis passe par le col de l'Albula, à 2 315 m d'altitude, jusqu'à la sous-station (SS) de Filisur, où se trouve une dérivation vers Robbia et Sils i.D. Depuis la SS de Filisur, la ligne traverse le versant glissant de Brienz jusqu’à la SS de Sils i.D. Les mesures suivantes doivent être mises en œuvre sur la ligne existante : • Remplacement, rénovation et renforcement des fondations de certains pylônes • Remplacement, renforcement et rehaussement de certains pylônes de lignes aériennes • Remplacement des chaînes d'isolateurs • Remplacement des conducteurs et des câbles de terre • Utilisation de potences isolées • Renouvellement de la protection anticorrosion Le présent appel d'offres porte sur les travaux de génie civil (travaux de maçonnerie) sur les pylônes de la ligne 380 kV TR1360 Pradella - Sils i.D. - tronçon La Punt - Filisur - Sils, y compris les aires de stockage. Les emplacements des pylônes sont en partie exposés et l'accès est parfois difficile. Tous les pylônes ne sont pas accessibles par des engins de chantier. Les travaux suivants doivent être réalisés : • Travaux de démolition • Travaux d'excavation • Réalisation de fondations sur pieux • Travaux de bétonnage • Aménagement d'aires de stockage Les travaux de génie civil de l'ensemble du projet sont répartis en 6 lots. Les prestations détaillées sont présentées dans le document C100.

Le présent projet porte sur l'ensemble du tronçon de La Punt à Sils i. D., qui compte 132 pylônes et s'étend sur environ 43,5 km. Le tronçon de ligne commence à La Punt au pylône 1360x127, puis passe par le col de l'Albula, à 2 315 m d'altitude, jusqu'à la sous-station (SS) de Filisur, où se trouve une dérivation vers Robbia et Sils i.D. Depuis la SS de Filisur, la ligne traverse le versant glissant de Brienz jusqu’à la SS de Sils i.D. Les mesures suivantes doivent être mises en œuvre sur la ligne existante : • Remplacement, rénovation et renforcement des fondations de certains pylônes • Remplacement, renforcement et rehaussement de certains pylônes de lignes aériennes • Remplacement des chaînes d'isolateurs • Remplacement des conducteurs et des câbles de terre • Utilisation de potences isolées • Renouvellement de la protection anticorrosion Le présent appel d'offres porte sur les travaux de génie civil (travaux de maçonnerie) sur les pylônes de la ligne 380 kV TR1360 Pradella - Sils i.D. - tronçon La Punt - Filisur - Sils, y compris les aires de stockage. Les emplacements des pylônes sont en partie exposés et l'accès est parfois difficile. Tous les pylônes ne sont pas accessibles par des engins de chantier. Les travaux suivants doivent être réalisés : • Travaux de démolition • Travaux d'excavation • Réalisation de fondations sur pieux • Travaux de bétonnage • Aménagement d'aires de stockage Les travaux de génie civil de l'ensemble du projet sont répartis en 6 lots. Les prestations détaillées sont présentées dans le document C100.

title: Belgium – Research services – Interventiestudie naar de effectiviteit van preventieve maatregelen voor vermindering van blootstelling via binnenhuisstof
description: Deze opdracht heeft als doel een interventiestudie uit te voeren naar de effectiviteit van bestaande preventieve maatregelen, ter vermindering van de blootstelling aan PFAS en zware metalen (minimum lood en cadmium) via binnenhuisstof bij ongeveer 100 Vlaamse gezinnen met jonge kinderen (0-6 jaar). Daarbij ligt de focus op de maatregel "nat reinigen", maar ook eventuele aanvullende maatregelen of combinaties van maatregelen kunnen onderzocht worden. De studie moet inzicht verschaffen in: • de effectiviteit van preventieve maatregelen voor het reduceren van concentraties van PFAS en zware metalen in binnenhuisstof; • de omstandigheden waaronder deze maatregelen het meest effectief zijn; • de invloed van de frequentie, kwaliteit en consistentie van toepassing van de maatregelen; • de mogelijkheden voor verfijning van bestaande gezondheidskundige adviezen voor burgers. Daarnaast beoogt de opdracht een versterking van de kennisbasis inzake binnenhuisstof door: • de ontwikkeling van referentiewaarden voor concentraties van PFAS en zware metalen in binnenhuisstof; • de verdere onderbouwing van een uniforme en reproduceerbare staalnamemethodiek (neergezet stof) voor binnenhuisstof in vergelijking met buitenstof. De opdrachtnemer staat in voor de voorbereiding, uitvoering, analyse, interpretatie en rapportering van de studie. De opdracht omvat onder meer: • projectcoördinatie; • uitwerking van een onderzoeksprotocol en studieontwerp; • Opmaak van vragenlijsten en procedures voor deelnemers • ontwikkeling van een interventiestrategie; • rekrutering van deelnemers; • uitvoering van de staalnamecampagne; • laboratoriumanalyses; • statistische analyse en wetenschappelijke interpretatie; • ontwikkeling van referentiewaarden voor de meetresultaten; • de verdere onderbouwing van een uniforme en reproduceerbare staalnamemethodiek voor binnenhuisstof; • terugkoppeling van de resultaten en ondersteuning bij communicatie; • eindrapportering en overdracht van de onderzoeksgegevens. De resultaten van de studie moeten het Departement Zorg ondersteunen bij de verdere wetenschappelijke onderbouwing van gezondheidskundige adviezen, communicatie en beleidsbeslissingen rond blootstelling aan chemische stoffen via binnenhuisstof.

title: Denmark – Civil engineering consultancy services – Solvænget - Totalrådgivningsudbud
description: Nærværende udbudsbekendtgørelse gælder for udbud af totalrådgivning vedrørende Boligforeningen Lillebælts helhedsplanrenovering af afd. 01 – Solvænget i Nr. Aaby. Med baggrund i en renoveringshelhedsplan, godkendt ved skema A i Landsbyggefonden og Middelfart kommune, skal afdeling 01, Solvænget renoveres. Renoveringen omfatter 64 eksisterende almene boliger opført i 1946-1953 som et støttet byggeri iht. Lov om almene boliger m.v., LBK nr. 1023 med senere ændringer. Boligerne er opført som 40 rækkehuse i 2-3 plan (37 stk. i 2-plan, 3 stk. i 3-plan) og 24 boliger i 1-plan Renoveringsprojektet indeholder følgende hovedelementer: Renoveringen omfatter forskellige grader af ombygning/renovering og er inddelt i følgende hoveddele: - Delafsnit 301, nr. 1-37 – Renovering - Delafsnit 307, nr. 2-42 – Renovering - Delafsnit 308, nr. 44-66 – Renovering - Delafsnit 308, nr. 39-61 – Renovering og tilgængelighedsboliger Skema A og beboerproces Det kan oplyses, at projektet har opnået skema A-godkendelse i december 2025. Rådgiverydelser Totalrådgivningen indeholder projektering af dispositionsforslag/projektforslag, myndighedsprojekt, ud-budsprojekt, entrepriseudbud (hovedentreprise), udførelsesprojekt og som udført. Totalrådgiver er ansvarlig for myndighedsandragende, projekteringsledelse, byggeledelse, fagtilsyn, opfølgning, IKT-ledelse, bæredygtighedsledelse og arbejdsmiljøkoordinering (P+B). Entreprisesum Håndværkerudgifterne (entreprisesum) til renoveringssagen er kalkuleret til en samlet budgetramme på i alt kr. 106.930.318 inkl. byggeplads/vinterforanstaltninger og ekskl. moms (kr. 133.662.897 inkl. moms). Der henvises til LBF-budgetark 06.10.2025 (indeks 2025/K2) som vedlagt i udbudsmaterialet. Vær opmærksom på, at budgetark viser udgifter inkl. moms. Udbuddet Totalrådgivningsudbuddet gennemføres som et udbud med forhandling iht. Udbudslovens §§ 61-66 med en forudgående prækvalifikation. Ordregiver forbeholder sig ret ikke at gennemføre en forhandling og således tildele kontrakten på baggrund af det indledende tilbud. Tidsplanen i udbuddet er tilrettelagt efter, at der ikke gennemføres en forhandlingsrunde, men tildeles på baggrund af det indledende tilbud. Såfremt der gennemføres forhandling, vil tidsplanen blive parallelfor-skudt tilsvarende. Tildelingskriteriet er ”Det bedste forhold mellem pris og kvalitet” iht. udbudslovens § 162, stk. 1, nr. 3). Udelukkelse En økonomisk aktør udelukkes fra deltagelse, hvis den økonomiske aktør er omfattet af en af de obligatoriske udelukkelsesgrunde i udbudslovens § 135, stk. 1-3, og § 136, stk. 1, nr. 1.-4. Endvidere udelukkes en økonomisk aktør fra deltagelse, hvis den økonomiske aktør er omfattet af de frivillige udelukkelsesgrunde i udbudslovens § 137 stk. 1, nr. 1 - 2. En økonomisk aktør kan ikke udelukkes fra deltagelse, hvis den økonomiske aktør fremlægger tilstrækkelig dokumentation for, at den økonomiske aktør er pålidelig, selv om den økonomiske aktør er omfattet af en eller flere af udelukkelsesgrundene i udbudslovens §§ 135-137, jf. udbudslovens § 138, stk. 1. Der kan ikke tildeles kontrakt til følgende virksomheder, jf. Rådets forordning (EU) 2022/576 af 8. April 2022 om ændring af forordning (EU) nr. 833/2014 om restriktive foranstaltninger på baggrund af Ruslands handlinger, der destabiliserer situationen i Ukraine: A. russiske statsborgere eller fysiske eller juridiske personer, enheder eller organer, der er etableret i Rusland B. juridiske personer, enheder eller organer, hvoraf en enhed som omhandlet i nærværende stykkes litra a) direkte eller indirekte ejer over 50 %, eller C. fysiske eller juridiske personer, enheder eller organer, der handler på vegne af eller efter anvisning fra en enhed som omhandlet i nærværende stykkes litra a) eller b), Ligeledes kan der ikke anvendes underleverandører eller støttende enheder, der er omfattet af ovenstående, hvis denne aktørs bidrag udgør mere end 10 % af kontraktværdien.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Nationale Vulnerabilitätsanalyse internationaler Lieferketten
description: Ziel der Beauftragung ist die Identifikation und Bewertung von Abhängigkeiten Deutschlands/deutscher Unternehmen in globalen Lieferketten. Hierzu sollen in einem ersten Schritt Supply-Chain-Indizes für verschiedene Analysezwecke entwickelt werden (Modul A). In einem zweiten Schritt sollen nationale Abhängigkeiten gegenüber Handelspartnern hergeleitet werden (Modul B). Der Analyserahmen soll danach um indirekte Abhängigkeiten erweitert werden (Modul C) und unter Anwendung geeigneter Kriterien um die Bewertung tatsächlicher Vulnerabilitäten auf nationaler Ebene ergänzt werden (Modul D). Es soll auf Basis der Erkenntnisse eine für Analysezwecke geeignete interaktive (teil-)visuelle IT-basierte Darstellung entwickelt werden, die Nutzern Analysefunktionen über verschiedene Analyseebenen bereitstellt und visualisiert (Modul E). Abschließend sollen Abhängigkeiten und Vulnerabilitäten auf disaggregierter Ebene mit Liefer-, Wertschöpfungs- und Technologieketten verknüpft werden, um in Szenarien betroffenen Lieferketten identifizieren und Auswirkungen modellgestützt betrachten zu können (Modul F).

title: Denmark – Construction work – Transformerstation til Kalundborg Forsyning, Udvidelse af Renseanlæg (F1.EL.01)
description: Kalundborg Central Renseanlæg (herefter ”KCR”) skal udvides som en konsekvens af, at industrien i Kalundborg Kommune i de kommende år forøger sin tilledning. Udvidelsen af KCR (herefter ”Projektet”) sker både for at øge den biologiske kapacitet af anlægget, bedre styring af overløb, ny slamafvanding og fjernelse af miljøfremmede stoffer gennem tredje og fjerde renseanlæg. Projektet realiseres gennem en række udbud inden for byggeri- og anlæg, maskin- og el, systemleverandører og SRO. Kalundborg Renseanlæg A/S (”Bygherre”) har indgået en totalrådgiveraftale med Envidan A/S, som forestår teknisk rådgivning og bistand, projektering, byggeledelse og processpecialistrådgivning i forbindelse med Projektets realisering. Foruden pris på de faste ydelser, som er forbundet med at realisere kontrakten, skal tilbudsgiverne afgive pris(er) på følgende option: - Tilbudslistens post 4.8: Option: Ydelse for ny elforsyning Deudover skal tilbudsgiverne i tilbudslisten prissætte variable ydelser, herunder reguleringspriser, som kommer til anvendelse, i det omfang, der er behov herfor. title: Switzerland – Construction work – La Punt – Filisur – Sils im Domleschg (i.D.) – Baumeisterarbeiten Tiefbau
description: Le tronçon de ligne La Punt - Filisur - Sils im Domleschg (i.D.) fait partie du tracé 380 kV TR1360 Pradella - Sils i.D. Étant donné que ce tronçon joue un rôle central dans les échanges d'électricité avec l'Autriche et l'Italie et que la ligne a presque atteint la fin de sa durée de vie technique, une rénovation et une modernisation complètes s'imposent. Le présent projet porte sur l'ensemble du tronçon de La Punt à Sils i. D., qui compte 132 pylônes et s'étend sur environ 43,5 km. Le tronçon de ligne commence à La Punt au pylône 1360x127, puis passe par le col de l'Albula, à 2 315 m d'altitude, jusqu'à la sous-station (SS) de Filisur, où se trouve une dérivation vers Robbia et Sils i.D. Depuis la SS de Filisur, la ligne traverse le versant glissant de Brienz jusqu’à la SS de Sils i.D. Les mesures suivantes doivent être mises en œuvre sur la ligne existante : • Remplacement, rénovation et renforcement des fondations de certains pylônes • Remplacement, renforcement et rehaussement de certains pylônes de lignes aériennes • Remplacement des chaînes d'isolateurs • Remplacement des conducteurs et des câbles de terre • Utilisation de potences isolées • Renouvellement de la protection anticorrosion Le présent appel d'offres porte sur les travaux de génie civil (travaux de maçonnerie) sur les pylônes de la ligne 380 kV TR1360 Pradella - Sils i.D. - tronçon La Punt - Filisur - Sils, y compris les aires de stockage. Les emplacements des pylônes sont en partie exposés et l'accès est parfois difficile. Tous les pylônes ne sont pas accessibles par des engins de chantier. Les travaux suivants doivent être réalisés : • Travaux de démolition • Travaux d'excavation • Réalisation de fondations sur pieux • Travaux de bétonnage • Aménagement d'aires de stockage Les travaux de génie civil de l'ensemble du projet sont répartis en 6 lots. Les prestations détaillées sont présentées dans le document C100.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Project "FreeBSD – AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery"
description: This service agreement concerns the FOSS operating system FreeBSD and covers research into how artificial intelligence can strengthen open source maintenance, focusing on the FreeBSD Security Team's process of finding, validating, patching, and disclosing vulnerabilities and producing Security Advisories. FreeBSD is a modern, Unix-like operating system released under a permissive licence. As part of two work packages, the contract covers a code review workflow that works with both hosted commercial models and models the project runs itself, a tested method for discovering vulnerabilities that produces findings developers can act on, improved ways of validating and fixing what is found, work on existing and prototype tools that detect defects in the kernel, and an evaluation of these models in automated testing, and the publication of the methods, findings, and lessons learned so that other open source projects can reproduce and adapt them. The aim of this service is to establish a proactive workflow, compatible with free and open source software terms, that improves the speed and quality of repairing and maintaining without overwhelming maintainers.

title: Norway – Research services – The importance of Norwegian requirements and Norwegian level for the transition to work - NORKRAV
description: The aim of the project is to obtain systematic knowledge on what importance the Norwegian level has for transition to work. The project shall examine how language requirements are used in different branches, how Norwegian proficiencies are assessed in practice, and what characterises employers who are successful in including people with limited Norwegian abilities. The project shall also analyse what factors contribute to immigrants coming in and staying in work, despite limited Norwegian proficiencies. The knowledge shall provide a better basis for understanding how language can function both as a door opener and barrier to participation in working life, and should be able to be used in policy development and to strengthen IMDi's guidance work and cooperation with employers, municipalities and other relevant actors. This can, among other things, contribute to more precise and flexible language requirements, clearer distinctions between oral and written skills and better adaptations of language requirements for specific work assignments. The project will provide a better basis for understanding how language can function both as a door opener and barrier to participation in working life and how language requirements can be adapted.

title: Ireland – Surface water pollution monitoring or control services – Provision of the design of a non-native and invasive species surveillance and monitoring programme for the island of Ireland
description: Surveillance and monitoring of invasive species in both Ireland and Northern Ireland is currently fragmented and not considered sufficient to meet the requirements of legal instruments and agreements. The National Biodiversity Data Centre in the Republic of Ireland and the Centre for Environmental Data and Recording (CEDaR) in Northern Ireland, are the two national record centres for biological data on the island of Ireland. While both receive and act as a repository for biological data, there are sources of information that are not routinely and/or timely reported to either organisation. In the case of the highest risk invasive non-native species, this creates undesirable and preventable barriers to understanding the distribution of invasive species across the island of Ireland, and in certain situations, delays response action when a species might be highly localised. This situation can impact on Ireland and Northern Ireland’s ability to effectively understand the true distribution of invasive species on the island of Ireland, with real world impacts on effective management and prevention measures. However, under the new Shared Island Biosecurity and Invasive Species Initiative, there is an opportunity to review current surveillance and monitoring programmes active in both jurisdictions and make recommendations on a new system that effectively and efficiently captures relevant data for Ireland and Northern Ireland.

title: Germany – Research and experimental development services – HAW Beratungsdienstleistung RealBat
description: Gegenstand des durchgeführten Verfahrens sind Forschungs- und Entwicklungsleistungen im Verbundvorhaben RealBat („Effizienterer Betrieb von Windenergieanlagen durch Echt-zeitschutz für Fledermäuse“). Ziel des Vorhabens ist es, die bislang zum Schutz von Fleder-mäusen eingesetzten, weitgehend pauschalen Abschaltungen von Windenergieanlagen zu einem adaptiven Abschaltalgorithmus weiterzuentwickeln, der die Anlagen nur bei tat-sächlich bestehendem Schlagrisiko abschaltet. Anders als bei der bisherigen Abschätzung der Fledermausaktivität allein aus meteorologischen und phänologischen Parametern wird dazu die akustisch erfasste Fledermausaktivität in Echtzeit als zusätzlicher Parameter her-angezogen. Auf diese Weise lässt sich der Energieertrag der Anlagen bei mindestens gleichwertigem Fledermausschutz steigern. Die zu vergebenden Leistungen umfassen schwerpunktmäßig die Konzeption für die Erfassung von Fledermäusen und Auswertung der akustischen und teilweise zusammenführend mit den optischen Daten sowie die Methodenentwicklung der Echtzeitabschaltung. Kern der Leistung ist die Integration der Echtzeitabschaltung als zusätzlichen Parameter in die in der Planungspraxis etablierte Software ProBat und die ihr zugrunde liegenden, in den RE-NEBAT-Vorhaben entwickelten statistischen Modelle sowie die Optimierung des Gesamtmodells aus Fledermausschutz und Energieertrag. Der Projektbeginn war Juni 2026. Die Laufzeit des Vorhabens beträgt drei Jahre.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Planungsleistungen Technische Ausrüstung ALG 4, 5 und 6, gem. §§ 53 ff. HOAI 2021, LPH 3-9, stufenweise Beauftragung
description: Gegenstand des Auftrags sind Leistungen der Technische Ausrüstung ALG 4, 5 und 6 (ELT) gem. §§ 53 ff HOAI 2021, LPH 3-9 bei stufenweiser Beauftragung. Ggf. werden auch verschiedene besondere Leistungen beauftragt werden.------Die Klinikverbund Allgäu gGmbH plant die Errichtung des Neubaus „Bauabschnitt 1 Erweiterungsbau Nordwest“ am Standort Klinik Immenstadt.------Die Klinik Immenstadt ist ein Krankenhaus des Klinikverbunds Allgäu.------Am Standort Immenstadt besteht für den Klinikverbund Allgäu gGmbH ein zusätzlicher Raumbedarf aufgrund der im Mai 2026 vom Bayrischen Staatsministerium für Gesundheit, Prävention und Pflege beschlossenen Planbettenerhöhung auf 230 Betten und zur Schaffung aktuell fehlender Nebenräume. Das Bauvorhaben erhält die Bezeichnung „Bauabschnitt 1 Erweiterungsbau Nordwest“. ------Der Neubau mit einer Nutzfläche von ca. 3.921 m² gemäß Zielplanung umfasst vier Geschosse mit: - UG: Technik, Umkleiden - EG: Arztdiensträume, U+B-Räume, Seelsorge, Soziale Dienste, Raum der Stille - 1.OG: Highcare-Bettenstation - 2.OG: Arztdiensträume, Verwaltung, Besprechungsräume, Archiv - 3.OG: Pflegestation, Wahlleistung Auf der Dachfläche sind Flächen für eine Technikzentrale (z.B. Lüftungszentrale) und PV-Anlage vorgesehen. ------Für die Baufeldfreimachung sind zudem Rückbauarbeiten, Spartenanpassungen und Kanalverlegungen im Bereich des Baufeldes bzw. des angrenzenden Bürgersteiges erforderlich. Der Bauherr holt derzeit aktuelle Spartenpläne ein. ------Die Umsetzung zur Baufeldfreimachung, Rückbau der Kapelle, Errichtung des Neubaus, Umbau im Bestand und Herstellung der erforderlichen Anschlüsse an den Gebäudekomplex erfolgt in mehreren Bauphasen. ------Es ist eine Verlegung des Sauerstofftanks notwendig; als neuer Standort wird der nördliche Grundstücksbereich vor der Zufahrt zum GZI-Parkplatz favorisiert. ------Die Aushubsohle wird unterhalb des mittleren Grundwasserstandes liegen; somit werden nach bisherigen Erkenntnissen Spundwände für die Baugrube erforderlich, die in die Seetonschichten einbinden. ------Für die weiteren Planungsschritte der Tragwerksplanung wird zeitnah ein Baugrundgutachter beauftragt. ------Zusätzlich zum Neubau ist ein Umbau im Bestand in Form einer Erweiterung der Zentralen Notaufnahme (Schaffung Überwachungsplätze, bisher: Umkleiden) im Untergeschoss vorgesehen (s. Plananlage). Während der Bauausführung muss eine Zufahrt zur Zentralen Notaufnahme uneingeschränkt möglich sein. -----Das beiliegende Raum- und Funktionsprogramm wurde vom Bayrischen Staatsministerium für Gesundheit, Prävention und Pflege freigegeben. Bei dem Projekt werden Fördermittel gemäß Art. 11 BayKrG beantragt. Die förderrechtlichen Rahmenbedingungen (u.a. Terminschiene, vergaberechtliche Vorgaben, Anforderungen an Förderantragsunterlagen) sind bei der Projektabwicklung zwingend einzuhalten.------ Die im Juni 2026 für die Förderantragserstellung beauftragten Fachdisziplinen gelten als vorbefasste Bewerber. Die bereits erstellten Planunterlagen werden allen Teilnehmern mit den Verfahrensunterlagen (siehe 5.1.11) zur Verfügung gestellt, um alle Bieter auf denselben Informationsstand zubringen. ------Zeitschiene: Die Vergabeverhandlung findet voraussichtlich Mitte November 2026 statt. Die Auftragsvergabe und der unmittelbar darauffolgende Projektstart ist für Ende 2026 / Anfang 2027 vorgesehen. Die Bauausführung des Neubaus ist von Q3/2028 bis Q4/2030 vorgesehen.------Hinweis: Die Projektbesprechungen finden in deutscher Sprache statt.

title: Charities Hub  - Parapet Wall Replacement
description:
The Charities Hub is combination of the Arts Centre & Meeting Place, constructed circa 1971-72, and forms two thirds of the Galley Hill Local Centre. 
The Local Centre is a steel framed building consisting of shops, the Arts Centre at Ground Floor and a Small Meeting Place located at first floor above the retail units, consisting of a function room with ancillary rooms. 
The fabric of the buildings consists of external infill wall panels made up of brickwork and galvanised Steel crittal windows. The roofs at first floor are flat roofs, made of metal profile decking and a mineral felt membrane system. The first-floor slab, including the balcony roofs, is a beam and clay pot system with a concrete screed. The balcony areas, on both sides of the Meeting Place, have an asphalted surface.
Milton Keynes City Council is looking for a contractor to undertake the works to rebuild the parapet wall to the 1st floor of the Charities Hub in Galley Hill. 
The works consist of:
•	Submission of Building Control Application.
The Contractor shall prepare and submit all necessary documentation to Building Control to obtain approval prior to commencement of works.
•	Parapet Wall Reconstruction
The Contractor shall undertake a full rebuild of the first‑floor parapet wall in accordance with the DSA proposed drawings and planning approval PLN/2025/0172.
•	Abutment and Weathering Details
The Contractor shall form all necessary junction details at parapet abutments and installing flashing with a gutter at the parapet base to prevent water accumulation.
Works are to comply with BS standard and Building Control as per Pre Construction      information – Appendix D.
Works are to start in August 26 with an anticipated 10-week contract. This is to allow works to be undertaken in a safe manner.
Works will be undertaken under a JCT Minor Works with Contractors Design 2024 edition.  
This is notify of the award of the contract

title: PQ0705 - Behavioural Systems Mapping
description:
Birmingham City Council (the Council) is seeking to commission a specialist behavioural science consultancy to design and deliver a comprehensive behavioural systems model to understand the drivers of car and vehicle dependency across Birmingham and determine targets for behavioural interventions.
This work will directly support the development and implementation of the city’s Healthy Streets programme, which aims to shape neighbourhoods that are safer, easier to navigate, and more pleasant to live in by supporting greater use of walking, cycling and public transport, and decreasing dependence on private vehicles.
Vehicle dependency is a multifaceted behavioural challenge influenced by numerous interacting factors, such as habits, feelings of safety and ease, access to transport options, and broader environmental and societal influences. To address this complexity, BCC requires a robust, evidence‑informed modelling approach capable of identifying the most influential behavioural drivers and the highest‑impact opportunities 	for change.

title: Preliminary Market Engagement Round 3 for the Life in the UK (LITUK) Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service
description:
The Home Office (HO) is the government department responsible for safeguarding the nation through border control, immigration, passport issuance, policing, fire services, counter-terrorism and drugs policies. 
UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) plays an integral role in delivering this vision, managing millions of applications annually, enabling foreign nationals to visit, study, work or settle in the UK. As part of the evolution of existing services, UKVI pursues the transformation and modernisation of services in a manner that enhances customer experience and ensures accurate and efficient outcomes. One of the core services delivered by UKVI is the Life in the UK test, an essential component of the route to settlement in the UK and to UK citizenship. 
The Life in the UK Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service (LITUK) Project is procuring a new service; enabling the continued delivery of front-end services, balancing continuity with improvements and transformation. 
LITUK aims to move to a 'Digital-by-Default' approach, while upholding the rigorous standards necessary to support UKVI immigration decisions. The successful provider will deliver a service that combines technological innovation with security assurance, enabling customers to demonstrate their knowledge of life in the UK with confidence and convenience throughout their UK immigration journey. 
The purpose of this third round of Preliminary Market Engagement is to share information relating to the Authority's vision for the LitUK service and the procurement approach. At this stage, no final decisions have been made regarding the preferred solution.
Please Note: the content of this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice may be subject to change.

Thames Water intends to establish a single-lot, sole-supplier framework agreement for the provision of pump optimisation and aeration efficiency services across Thames Water operational assets.
The scope of the framework includes monitoring, testing, and analysis of pumping and aeration systems and associated equipment. The objective is to identify and deliver opportunities to reduce whole-life costs, improve efficiency, and optimise performance across operational sites.
The contract will include:

Suppliers will be expected to support a culture of continuous improvement and contribute to ongoing enhancement of processes and delivery approaches throughout the contract lifecycle.
Delivery Model
The anticipated delivery model will follow a structured approach comprising:
- Initial site identification and data collection.
- Project mobilisation and stakeholder engagement.
- Efficiency and control studies to identify optimisation opportunities.
- Approval to proceed to testing and monitoring.
- Site-based testing and performance monitoring activities.
- Review of outcomes, including business case validation.
- Handover for delivery through relevant engineering or capital delivery mechanisms.
The contract is expected to support a programme of approximately 200 tests across 60 operational sites during the AMP period.
Further detail on the scope, service requirements, and call-off mechanisms will be provided within the procurement and contract documents.
The following conditions would be considered as some of key requirements for a supplier to meet to be considered for this opportunity:
•	Must be able to cover the Thames Valley, London and Home Counties geographical area
•	Must have a proven track record in delivering measurable savings and innovation within the scope of this framework.

title: Marine Research Vessel Refit, Maintenance, Equipment and Support Services Framework
description:
The National Oceanography Centre (NOC) is looking to establish an open framework for the refit, maintenance, equipping and sustainment of its operational research vessels, including RRS James Cook and RRS Discovery, together with associated marine assets and scientific systems, across their working life. The support sought is expected to include the following broad areas, which are indicative and not exhaustive.
Refit and docking support across the classification cycle, including the intermediate and special survey work falling due within it, broadly covering hull, structural and coating work, propulsion and steering intervention, tailshaft and rudder work, and the repair and renewal identified through survey. Both wet berth and dry dock coverage will be needed over the life of the framework, and the structure will be designed to accommodate suppliers offering either or both.
General marine engineering and support capability, required both during refit periods and on an ongoing basis outside them, in the United Kingdom and overseas, broadly covering marine mechanical and electrical engineering, fabrication, pipework and hydraulics, HVAC, cabling and systems installation, interior works, running maintenance, defect rectification, modification, and commissioning and mobilisation to port.
Support for critical vessel systems, from original equipment manufacturers and their approved partners, broadly covering propulsion, engines and gearboxes, navigation and bridge systems, communications and information and operational technology, electrical distribution and generation, safety and lifesaving systems, and control, automation and energy management, together with the inspection, overhaul, upgrade and certification these systems require.
Support for marine research and survey systems, including supply, installation, integration, calibration, servicing and upgrade, broadly covering multibeam and singlebeam echo sounders, sub bottom profilers and acoustic positioning, oceanographic and environmental sensors and sensor packages, water column and seabed sampling systems, deck handling and over the side deployment equipment, and the associated data acquisition, processing and control infrastructure.
Technical and professional marine services, independent of the yards, broadly covering naval architecture, marine surveying, superintendency, class liaison, project and programme management and specialist engineering consultancy.
Supply of maritime hardware on a supply only basis, broadly covering equipment, spares, components and consumables, including original equipment manufacturer and approved equivalent parts.
Capability for decarbonisation and environmental retrofit is of interest across all of the above.
The framework is expected to be divided into lots. The lot structure, the number of suppliers appointed to each lot and the call off mechanisms will be confirmed following preliminary market engagement. Suppliers will be able to apply for one or more lots, and geographic capability, together with dry dock or wet berth capability, will be recorded at framework stage.
NOC will be the sole contracting authority. The framework is expected to be established as an open framework under the Procurement Act 2023, with a duration of up to eight years, and will be reopened to new suppliers at points set out in the framework documents. Work will be ordered by call off contract on a task by task basis, covering both programmed and unplanned requirements, at yards, ports and NOC sites in the United Kingdom and overseas. Call off routes are expected to include direct award and further competition among the suppliers appointed to the relevant lot, with the applicable route set out in the framework at the outset.
The estimated total value of the framework is estimated to be worth between £65,000,000 & £100,000,000 excluding VAT over its full duration. No guarantee of volume or value is given to any supplier appointed to the framework.

title: National Infection and Sepsis Audit – Acute NHS settings
description:
The contract for the Infection and Sepsis Audit - Acute care settings (NISA-Acute) will initially be delivered for NHS-funded care in England and Wales for a period of three years, at a maximum total budget of up to £ 1,146,300.00 excl VAT and £1,375,560.00 with VAT.  
Bids exceeding these limits will be rejected. 
All pricing submissions must be in regard to this 'core' value, and not inclusive of any extension costs or aspirational intent costs, i.e. Please only submit a cost schedule up to the maximum core value of £ 1,146,300.00 excl VAT and £1,375,560.00 with VAT.  
The maximum budget ‘core’ value excludes the potential two year extension and aspirational intent as described in section 14.3 of Annex A - Service Specification.
Please note, there is no commitment by the Authority at this stage to include any of the below aspirational intent. Taking this aspirational intent into account, including the possibility that a contract extension may be offered for an additional 24 months, the potential ceiling value is £8,988,606.00 GBP including VAT.
 This is a new national clinical audit for severe infection and sepsis in acute NHS hospital settings. The aim is to provide benchmarked infection and sepsis care data to identify variation and drive improvement over time. 
 Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. While it is an unusual complication of developing an infection, it can be triggered by any infection. When people die from an infection, it is most commonly due to sepsis. Sepsis is complex and hard to diagnose, with no single test and symptoms that overlap with other conditions (NHS England Modern Service Framework, 2026)  
 Severe infections may lead to the development of sepsis, particularly in at-risk groups, and are one of the most common reasons for emergency admission to hospital.  
 Both infection and sepsis are major causes of morbidity and mortality in the UK, and costly to the NHS and wider economy:  
In 2025 there were over 23,000 deaths involving sepsis (Office for National Statistics).  
Patients and carers who we engaged with as part of specification development told us of long-term impacts that some sepsis survivors experience, from reduced mobility and cognitive difficulties, to loss of limbs or vision impairments.  
Each year, the NHS in England spends over £1billion on sepsis care, and over £6.5billion on infection care. Wider economic costs are estimated at £10-15billion annually (York Health Economics Consortium, 2017).  
1,300 clinical negligence claims were made regarding sepsis from 2020/21 to 2024/25, costing £65.3m in litigation. Most claims relate to delays and failures in treatment and diagnosis. 
 Several major healthcare initiatives have been launched to help improve care related to sepsis and severe infection, including: 
NHS England’s sepsis Modern Service Framework (MSF), which aims to reduce death, life-threatening complications and long-term impact from sepsis and severe infection by at least 25% by 2035, as well as reducing health inequalities (published July 2026).  
NHS England’s National Improvement Programme for ‘Optimising the acute management of sepsis’ (as part of the MSF activities). 
The National Patient Safety Plan for NHS Wales 2026-2031, which includes sepsis care.  
The UK Anti-Microbial Resistance (AMR) National Action Plan, which pledges to strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC) and antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) in health and social care settings 
New NICE guidelines for recognition, diagnosis and early management of suspected sepsis, published in November 2025 (NG253-NG255) 
 Establishing the NISA-Acute audit is a key ambition of the NHS England sepsis MSF, and the audit will be expected to align closely with all the initiatives listed above. 
 The audit funders have selected ‘early stages of care’ as the initial priority for this audit because this is a critical point for effective severe infection management and the swift identification and treatment of sepsis. Prompt, effective treatment is vital to improving outcomes, and both Prevention of Future Death (PFD) reports and Health Services Safety Investigations Body (HSSIB) investigations have highlighted opportunities to improve care in this area.
