title: Wales & Western - Civils Examination Services (Earthworks)
description:
Civil examinations within Network Rail refer to the inspection, examination and reporting of structural assets to ensure the safety, reliability, and longevity of railway infrastructure. These examinations help identify defects, monitor structural integrity, and determine necessary maintenance or repair works to prevent failures and ensure continued safe operation of the rail network. An Earthwork examination shall be sufficient to identify or determine and record information to enable Network Rail to manage the safety and performance of the Earthwork in accordance with NR/L3/CIV/065.
 Asset types to be examined:
•	Earthworks (as defined by NR/L3/CIV/065): Five chain lengths of Earthwork slope: a soil cutting, rock cutting embankment, or natural slope
•	Coastal and Estuarine Defences that are formed of earthworks: A Structure that protects railway infrastructure against erosion or flooding by tidal waters.  It includes protection works, which protect land against erosion and encroachment by such waters, and which perform no flood defence role; and defences, which protect against flooding or attack by such waters.
•	Outside Party Slopes, whose failure may impact on Network Rail infrastructure, where the outside party is unable to provide a satisfactory management policy for the slope, will be, so far as is lawful, be subject to a cyclical examination.
•	A cutting, embankment or natural slope, outside of the Network Rail boundary, owned or managed by an outside party, which may impact on Network Rail infrastructure.  Where the outside party is unable to provide a satisfactory management policy for the slope or demonstrate by other means that it is being managed in a satisfactory manner, the slope will, so far as is lawful, be subject to a cyclical examination.
Examination Types:
•	Cyclical Earthwork Examination: These examinations are cyclical in accordance with the Task Schedule or as otherwise instructed by Employer's representative. The scope must adhere to SCHI, SEHI and/or RSHI in accordance with NR/L3/CIV/065
•	Rapid Response Earthwork Examination: These examinations are for Emergency Situations as required. The scope is as required by Network Rail.
•	Geotechnical Incident Report: These examinations are as required by Network Rail. The scope is in accordance with NR/L3/CIV/185. 
Each Examination of an earthwork shall:
•	Include the production of a report.
•	Include an examination to record and report the findings related to the condition of the earthworks including all necessary preparations and arrangements for access to the earthwork. 
•	Update and record data obtained during the examinations in the Network Rail Earthworks Database using Network Rail Earthworks Examination Software.   
•	Support the Employer’s Representative in the management and co-ordination of examination of earthworks.  
•	Include any vegetation clearance necessary to enable examinations of earthwork. 
•	Provide a rapid response service to attend and report on earthwork failures and Geotechnical incidents in accordance with NR/L3/CIV/065 and NR/L3/CIV/185.
In the later years of this Framework, the Geotech teams plan to move to non-traditional methods of examination. By integrating satellite data into core processes, and other observed data sets, the business can significantly reduce its reliance on traditional on-site examinations, enhancing efficiency and improving asset management decisions. Based on currently available information we are expecing the following: 
•	CP7 Y4 50% reduction in Condition A-C assets excluding rock cuttings
•	CP7 Y5 70% reduction in Condition A-C assets excluding rock cuttings

• Review and refine the question sets progressively based on the findings from each interview phase.
Interviews
• Support up to four Ofwat interviewees.
• Conduct up to five interviews per interviewee, resulting in a maximum of 20 interviews.
• Interviews will progressively explore career experience, critical experiences, tacit knowledge, patterns and indicators, case studies, decision-making and key lessons that should be transferred to others.
Interview analysis
• Analyse individual interview outputs.
• Identify lessons, experience and knowledge areas from each interview.
• Refine subsequent interview questions based on the findings from earlier interviews.
Experience library development
• Analyse the overall interview corpus.
• Develop structured experience cards and an initial Ofwat Experience Library.
• Identify cross-interview and cross-theme organisational knowledge and lessons.
Demonstration of exploitation
• Demonstrate how Ofwat staff could use the Experience Library, including through Copilot, to identify relevant previous experiences, approaches, lessons, warnings and options when considering a current problem or situation.
Deliverables are:
• Interview question sets - Five configured interview question sets within DUCHESS, refined during delivery based on interview findings.
• Interview evidence - Transcripts from up to 20 interviews, provided in an agreed format such as PDF, Word or Excel.
• Lessons list - A consolidated list of the knowledge and experience areas identified from each interview, together with the associated lessons.
• Experience cards - Structured cards capturing, as applicable: situation, problem, context, warning signs/cues, experienced approach, action, why it worked, lesson learnt, rule of thumb, conditions/limitations, source and thematic tags.
• Ofwat Experience Library - An Excel-based experience matrix containing the lessons list, individual experience cards and organisational knowledge cards covering cross-interview and cross-theme lessons.
• Exploitation Guide - A presentation, including screenshots or video as appropriate, demonstrating how Ofwat staff can interrogate and use the Experience Library, including through Copilot.
• Pilot Report - A Word report comprising an executive summary and detailed sections covering the introduction, approach, findings, conclusions and recommendations, together with supporting annexes.
• Final pilot recommendations - Recommendations arising from the pilot on the effectiveness of the approach, potential improvements and considerations for any future development or wider implementation.

description:
This will be a two stage process with conditions of participation Stage 1 and ITT Stage 2. Further stages may be an option. 
The Royal Parks have identified the facilities located in the Roehampton Gate Car Park as being a priority for redevelopment.  There is currently a small café building with adjacent catering kiosk, a cycle hire facility with a separate storage shed, and public toilets provided in two temporary modular buildings. All of these are of very poor quality and require replacing in the near future. 
This contract is for the replacement of these facilities.  
The site is iconic very popular. The site is located at the north-east edge of Richmond Park, close to Roehampton Gate which is to the north of the site, and which is the closest access point to the park. The Alton Primary School is to the north-east beyond the park boundary and the Richmond Park Golf Course to the south-east. The existing car park is separated from the wider park by Priory Lane which forms part of the network of roads within Richmond Park, giving access to the car parks and forming a circular route for cyclists. Adjacent to Priory Lane is the Tamsin Trail, a running and cycling path which goes around the whole park.  
Richmond Park is the largest of London’s Royal Parks, covering an area of 2,500 acres, and has enjoyed a long and rich history as a Royal Park since being enclosed as a deer park in 1637 by Charles I. The Park is of national and international importance for wildlife conservation and is a National Nature Reserve, a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and a Special Area of Conservation. It is also included on Historic England's Register of Historic Parks and Gardens as Grade I.

Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust has undertaken preliminary market engagement to inform the development of its requirements and procurement strategy for the provision of an electronic key management system.

The Trust currently intends to procure the requirement through a further competition under the Pagabo Small Works Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS).
Suppliers with an interest in the opportunity are encouraged to review the Pagabo Small Works DPS arrangements and ensure they are appropriately positioned to participate in any future competition. For further information please contact Lee Pontin, Pagabo Small Works DPS Manager, leon.pontin@pagabo.co.uk. Questions about the EKMS opportunity should be directed to the Trust procurement contact listed below.
The further competition is expected to launch in mid-October 2026 and will be open to suppliers admitted to the DPS at the date of invitation.
Publication of this notice is intended to promote transparency and market awareness. Any information necessary for participation in the procurement will be made available equally to all bidders as part of the procurement process.
Description
Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust provides mental health and learning disability services across Greater Manchester. The Trust operates 18 electronic key management cabinets and seven associated ward door access control pods across its inpatient sites. Manufacturer support for 16 of the cabinets ends on 31 May 2027. The Trust intends to procure a replacement system, installed and supported, with all cabinets managed in a single central environment.
This notice informs the market of the forthcoming requirement and the intended route to award. It is not an invitation to tender. The full specification, pricing schedule, evaluation criteria and contract terms will be issued through the procurement.
Requirement (high level; full detail will follow in the procurement)
• Replacement of 16 end-of-life cabinets, with the remaining two either replaced or fully managed within the same environment.
• Retention of the Trust's existing physical keys, locks and master suites. Re-keying is out of scope.
• Biometric release with a non-biometric alternative, at cabinets and at the controlled door points.
• Ward entrance and exit control at the existing airlock locations, where a person still holding relevant keys cannot leave through the normal exit until the keys are returned, including all readers, controllers, software and interfaces.
• Central web-based administration, audit, scheduled reporting, alarms and overdue-key escalation; standalone operation during outages.
• Installation, commissioning, migration, training, removal of replaced equipment and ongoing support and maintenance, in inpatient mental health settings.

The scheme comprises the milling and removal of the existing surface course and binder course with the construction of a new Hot Rolled Asphalt (HRA) surface course. Existing carriageway levels and profiles are to be maintained throughout the works. The extent of the works is generally confined to the existing carriageway footprint. The works may also include regulation of existing pavement layers and/or localised replacement of the binder course where identified within the contract documents. The objective of the project is to restore the structural and functional condition of the carriageway through the replacement of the existing deteriorated surfacing while maintaining the existing road geometry and levels.
The successful Contractor will be required to undertake all construction activities necessary to complete the resurfacing works, including traffic management, milling, pavement repairs, surfacing operations, iron work reinstatement, road markings, associated ancillary works and all testing and quality assurance requirements specified within the contract documentation. The contract will be delivered under the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) Option B.
Scope of Works includes the following: 
A. Provision and maintenance of traffic management arrangements. 
B. Milling and removal of the existing surface course and binder course layers 
C. Regulation and/or localised binder course replacement as detailed in the contract documents. 
D. Laying of new Hot Rolled Asphalt (HRA) surfacing and binder course. 
E. Reinstatement and adjustment of iron work. 
F. Reinstatement of road markings and other affected highway features. 
G. Completion of all associated testing, quality assurance and health and safety requirements.

title: DHSC: ASC: Leadership Development Programme for new and aspiring DASS
description:
DHSC is undertaking preliminary market engagement to understand supplier interest, capability and capacity to deliver a Leadership Development Programme for new and aspiring Directors of Adult Social Services (DASS). This exercise gives potential bidders an opportunity to review the requirement and provide market feedback to help DHSC develop the final Invitation to Tender (ITT) fairly and transparently.
The government recognises that its significant ambitions for adult social care reform and improvement will require strong leadership at local level. We need to ensure that new and aspiring DASSs are equipped with the confidence and capability to harness the benefits of reforms and to deliver improvements in outcomes for residents. In order to develop leadership capacity, support career progression and enable reform and improvement across adult social care, we are exploring a new leadership development programme for new and aspiring DASSs.
The proposed Leadership Development Programme for adult social care aims to help develop adult social care leadership capacity and capability, specifically amongst those new to leadership. The programme should support up to 50 participants across two streams, one for aspiring DASSs and one for those recently appointed to the role. Its aims are to:
• Rapidly equip a cohort of aspiring DASSs with the necessary capability and confidence to be exemplary leaders.
• Support a cohort of new to post DASSs to develop their capability and confidence–contributing to improving attrition rates within the sector by helping DASSs remain in post for longer periods.
• Support DASSs to drive sustainable, strategic improvement in councils. 
• Help to increase the number of councils rated as ‘Good’ and ‘Outstanding’ in the CQC’s local authority adult social care assessments.
Although this PME is being made available via the open market, DHSC currently expects to conduct the procurement through the GCA Learning and Training Services Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS), RM6219. We have identified this as our proposed route to market due to the benefits it provides for both DHSC and potential bidders. Organisations wishing to participate in any tender which may follow this market engagement, should ensure they are registered on this DPS. If the DPS is used as the procurement strategy, only suppliers listed in the DPS according to the specified filters will receive an ITT.
DHSC is also keen to maximise opportunities to participate in procurement for Small to Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and Voluntary, Community and Social Enterprises (VCSEs). Consideration will be given to collaborative bids.
Contract Value: The estimated total value of the contract is up-to £909,000 excluding VAT, £1,090,800 including VAT. The funding is expected to be divided broadly equally between the two financial years, reflecting the substantial work required to develop and mobilise the programme rapidly during the final quarter of 2026/27 and to support delivery throughout 2027/28.
Contract Term: A term of 15-months. The programme is expected to commence in January 2027, with programme evaluation to conclude in March 2028. There is not expected to be an option to extend at this stage. 
Disclaimers - this PME:
• Does not signify the commencement of a competitive procurement.
• Does not constitute any commitment by the Department of Health and Social Care to procure services.
• Does not create any obligation on the Department.
• Does not provide a competitive advantage to any suppliers engaging with DHSC at this early stage, and DHSC will ensure equal treatment of all interested parties at all times.
Any funding estimates referenced are indicative only and subject to change. The Department makes no commitment at this stage to the final scope or funding envelope of any future contractual activity.

description:
Wigan Council is seeking to appoint a provider to deliver an Emotional and Mental Health Service for Children and Young People in Care and Care Leavers.
The service will provide flexible, evidence-based, trauma-informed therapeutic and preventative support to children and young people in care, care leavers and their carers. Interventions will include a range of psychological and therapeutic approaches, individual and group work, therapeutic parenting support, psychological consultation and formulation, systemic and dyadic approaches, assessments and evidence-based parenting programmes.
The service will work closely with Wigan Council's social care teams to improve the mental health, emotional wellbeing and resilience of children and young people, support carers and foster carers, prevent escalation to more specialist services, and promote placement stability and permanence. A key focus will be ensuring that support is responsive and tailored to the individual needs and circumstances of children, young people and their carers.
The service will support Wigan children and young people in care whether placed within or outside the Wigan Borough. Delivery will be flexible and may take place across a range of appropriate venues, with some out-of-hours provision required where necessary.

title: Preliminary Market Engagement for provision of waste & recycling collection services by joint venture or single supplier
description:
Derbyshire Dales District Council (The Council) is currently considering a range of potential delivery models for the future provision of its waste and recycling collection service.
As part of its service review, the Council is assessing which delivery model is best placed to meet its strategic objectives, statutory obligations, service requirements and value for money considerations.

•	A joint venture arrangement between the Council and a private sector partner, through which a jointly owned company would operate the waste and recycling collection service.

The Council is conducting this PME in accordance with Sections 16 and 17 of the Procurement Act 2023. Information obtained through this process may be used to inform the Council's future procurement strategy and contract requirements. The Council will take appropriate steps to ensure no supplier obtains an unfair advantage through participation in this engagement and may share relevant information arising from the engagement with all prospective suppliers in any future procurement.
For the avoidance of doubt, this PME is not part of a formal procurement process, and the Council is not committing, at this stage, to carrying out such a process.
Participation in this process is entirely voluntary and non-binding and shall not prevent any supplier participating in a future procurement process.

title: ITT - Taxation and reuse - UID 350
description: We know that the structure of taxes shapes decisions about how and what to invest in.    To better understand the incentives around the reuse of historic buildings, this study will look at how tax impacts on the finances of reuse projects, how the tax impacts differ depending on the type of project or developer, what the implications are for cash flow vs total financial impacts, and where the incidence of tax may be different to where the liability falls.  The outputs of the research will include a set of project finance / tax numbers for a range of representative projects covering a range of different types of development / developer; an assessment of how the impacts of tax – and different approaches to subsidy, impact on different types of developer and project and the relative impacts of changes to tax / subsidy.

title: EM Lawshare Framework Agreement for Legal Services
description:
West Northamptonshire Council (the Authority) is acting as lead authority and running this procurement on behalf of the EM Lawshare (EMLS). This procurement is being conducted in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and is being conducted through the Competitive Flexible procedure to identify the Potential Suppliers for the requirement.  This is a Light Touch procurement.  
EMLS is a consortium of public bodies (the Consortium) that have been procuring legal services frameworks over the last 20 years.  This procurement is for a new framework agreement to replace an existing one that is expiring on 31 March 2026. Contracting authorities will be required to be members of the Consortium in order to use the new framework agreement.   
There are just over 240 contracting authorities signed up as members to use the existing framework agreement. 82% of these are local authorities and parish councils located in England and the remaining 18% is made up of wholly owned local authority subsidiary companies, blue light services, park authorities, combined authorities, NHS bodies,  police and crime commissioners,  universities and colleges. A full list of current members signed up to use the existing framework can be seen by using this link to the EMLS website:  https://emlawshare.co.uk/directory/  
The number of contracting authorities signed up to use the current framework has grown significantly from the number using the initial framework set up 20 years ago when seven local authorities in the East Midlands initially started undertaking procurements as a consortium.  The range of users has also spread geographically so it now extends country wide and includes some of the largest local authorities in the country such as:  Birmingham, Leeds, Bristol, Nottingham and Sheffield City councils and Cornwall, Kent, Somerset, Derbyshire, Oxfordshire and North Yorkshire councils.   
The EMLS has now formalised its consortium arrangements in the form of a new Consortium Agreement intended to strengthen the consortium's governance arrangements in anticipation of this tender for a new framework. The agreement is available on the publicly accessible part of the EMLS's website so that any bidder interested in understanding the EMLS's governance and operating arrangements can view it - see [Insert link to webpage]. 
All contracting authorities (as defined in the Procurement Act 2023) in England & Wales will be eligible to join the Consortium, either before or during the term of the new framework agreement, to have access to use the framework.  Contracting authorities that are not local authorities require approval of the Consortium Board to join the Consortium, whereas local authorities do not.     
The closed framework agreement will deliver legal services to members of the Consortium.  These services will sit under ten areas of work.  These include every major category of work dealt with by local authorities other than child care work. The scope of the services is further detailed in the Specification. The framework agreement will not be split into lots as the appointed firms are required to be able to respond to requirements across all of the ten areas of work. 
The framework agreement will have 10 private law firms appointed to it.  
The framework agreement will have a maximum total value of £1 billion (exclusive of VAT) for the delivery of the requirements as set out in the Specification.   The framework agreement will not bind any Consortium member to use the appointed firms nor will any guarantee be given as to the minimum levels of work which will be awarded under the framework. 
The Consortium will during the course of the framework agreement charge appointed firms  a management fee calculated as a percentage based on a sliding scale of the income they invoice to Consortium members each year (net of VAT and disbursements), as detailed in the Invitation to Tender. 
Firms appointed to the framework will be required, jointly & /or solely, to provide certain added value services as part of the contract. These are detailed in the Specification. 
Annual indexation to the pricing will apply from the third contract year of the framework agreement. Please refer to Schedule 4, paragraph 1 of the framework agreement for further details. 
A conflicts assessment has been prepared and revised in accordance with Section 83. 
If your organisation wishes to participate in this process, you need to register with In-Tend Portal. You will be unable to take part if you do not register. Please use the link below and follow the instructions on the website: https://in-tendhost.co.uk/wnc/aspx/Home   
  
Tenders must be returned via the Portal.   
The tender return date is midday on Monday 19th October 2026. Tenders received after this time and date will not be accepted.

description:
Powys County Council (‘The Council’) is seeking tenders from suitably qualified and experienced providers for the provision of a care and support service at Pont Aur Extra Care Light scheme, Ystradgynlais.
In entering a contract with the Council to provide care and support services for individuals living in the extra care housing scheme. The Service Provider will comply with the Care Inspectorate Wales (CIW) and Regulation and Inspection of Social Care (Wales) Act 2016 (and any subsequent amendments), and the values and principles stated within the service Specification. There is a requirement that the provider will be registered with Care Inspectorate Wales (CIW).
The extra care scheme will aim to provide the additional support which will enable individuals to remain living independently within their own home for longer, with the level of support they need to meet their care and support needs.
The scheme is being modernised and developed into an Extra Care Light model, providing 43 properties in total, made up of 41 apartments and 2 attached bungalows. This includes the refurbishment and the development of 12 new purpose-built extra care apartments.

title: Anglian Water Fens and Lincolnshire Reservoirs Early Works Partner (EWP)
description:
AWS is facing unprecedented challenges due to climate change, population growth and environmental constraints. These challenges include more frequent droughts, increased demand for water, and the need to reduce water abstraction from environmentally sensitive areas.
To address these challenges, the Water Resources East regional planning and the Water Resource Management Planning of Anglian Water and Cambridge Water have selected the Fens Reservoirs (FR) and Lincolnshire reservoir (LR) schemes as low-regret Strategic Resource Options (SRO) to improve water security and meet societal and environmental outcomes.
The reservoirs will provide safe, resilient supplies of drinking water, as well as environmental, socioeconomic, leisure, and wellbeing benefits for the communities they serve. FR and LR will be delivered to the benefit of both AWS and Cambridge Water (CWC) customers.
The FR and LR and associated assets (abstraction, treatment and transfers) are being progressed through the fast-tracked delivery framework overseen by the Regulators' Alliance for Progressing Infrastructure Development (RAPID), and each is proposed to be a Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project (NSIP) seeking consent through the Development Consent Order (DCO) regime.
Due to the size and complexity of the programme, Specified Infrastructure Project Regulations (SIPR) is the preferred delivery model for the reservoirs. SIPR was introduced by the UK Government in 2013 as a mechanism for an alternative approach to financing and delivering large and complex water and sewerage infrastructure projects.
Under SIPR, the Secretary of State (SoS) or Ofwat (under delegation from the SoS) may specify an infrastructure project for delivery under a "project licence" by a third party where certain conditions are met. Early Works are the preparatory activities; site investigation works and construction tasks to be completed prior to Development Consent Order (DCO) determination and commencement of Enabling Works and Main Construction Works.
The works will comprise preparatory statutory, technical, and construction activities required to support the obtaining of the necessary consents prior to DCO determination. 
Anglian Water are considering the following activities as part of the EWP Framework scope where the EWP will act as the Principal Contractor (PC), where it is reasonably practicable. 
Principal Contractor Services – Overall site coordination, health and safety management, logistics and contractor management. Duty under CDM.
Site Management & Logistics – Site operations, welfare, security, access management and logistics controls.
Site Establishment & Compounds – Establishment and operation of site compounds, welfare facilities and supporting infrastructure.
Constructability & Design Coordination – Construction planning, buildability reviews and coordination with design development activities.
Environmental Mitigation – Delivery of environmental mitigation measures required to support the programme.
Ecological Mitigation & Monitoring – Habitat creation, species protection works and ecological monitoring activities.
Archaeology, Heritage & Geophysical Investigations – Archaeological investigations, heritage works and geophysical surveys.
Water Surveys – Water level and quality monitoring
Topographical & Utility Surveys – Topographical surveys, utility detection, mapping and verification activities.
Geotechnical Investigations – Ground investigations, testing and reporting.
Environmental Surveys – Environmental baseline and compliance surveys.
Ecological Surveys – Ecological surveys supporting environmental assessment and mitigation requirements.
UXO Investigations – Unexploded ordnance surveys and investigations.
Temporary Traffic Management – Temporary traffic management, road closures and associated highway measures.
Site Discharge & Consenting Support – Delivery of drainage and discharge infrastructure and support to consent compliance activities.
Temporary Works – Design, management and assurance of temporary works.
Property Management & Dilapidation Surveys – Property-related activities, condition surveys and management of affected assets and interfaces.
Demolition Works – Demolition and clearance of existing structures where required to facilitate delivery of Early Works.
Earthworks Trials – A scaled-down embankment constructed to validate ground behaviour, design assumptions, construction methods and specifications before full-scale reservoir embankment delivery.
The duration of the Framework is proposed to be an initial 5-year term with a possible extension option. The contracting authority reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend the Framework Agreement on up to three occasions with each extension being for a period of 12 months. Accordingly, the maximum duration will be eight years (5 years + 1 year + year + 1 year).
We anticipate releasing a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) at the beginning of November 2026 with return by the end of November 2026 and launch an ITT January 2027.
Anticipated Award Date is May 2027 with Contract Completion quarter 2 of 2032.
The estimated contract value is currently anticipated to be between £60 million and £80 million. This estimate is provided for market engagement purposes only and will be confirmed in the tender notice.

title: Mobile Transformer Oil Processing Vehicles (Trailer Mounted) - Design, Manufacture, Supply, Commissioning and Support
description:
National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET) is seeking a supplier to design, manufacture, supply, commission and support two (2) fully integrated, trailer-mounted mobile transformer oil processing vehicles, with an option, at NGET's sole discretion, to purchase up to two (2) additional equivalent units under the resulting contract. Any additional purchases will be subject to business requirements, funding approval and satisfactory performance of the initial units. The solutions shall be road-legal, self-contained and suitable for deployment at operational substations and construction sites throughout UK.
The scope includes:
•  Design, manufacture, testing, supply and delivery of two (2) mobile transformer oil processing trailers, with an option for NGET to purchase up to two (2) additional equivalent units under the resulting contract.
•  Provision of transformer oil treatment plant capable of oil filtration, drying, degassing and vacuum processing operations, including a minimum oil processing capability of 7,500 litres/hour at 50°C.
•  Integrated vacuum systems capable of transformer and chamber vacuum treatment, both independently and simultaneously.
•  Supply of an onboard power generation system including generator, fuel storage, distribution equipment and changeover facilities for external power sources.
•  Installation of monitoring, control and automation systems, including PLC/SCADA functionality, process alarms, operational data recording and remote-access capabilities.
•  Provision of welfare facilities, environmental controls, storage arrangements and operational workspaces suitable for field personnel.
•  Incorporation of all required safety, fire protection, emergency lighting, access and environmental protection systems in accordance with applicable UK legislation and industry standards.
•  Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning and demonstration of operational performance.
•  Delivery of complete technical documentation, operating manuals, maintenance schedules, drawings, software licences and spare parts recommendations.
•  Provision of operator and maintainer training, warranty support, technical assistance and after-sales service arrangements for the lifecycle of the asset.
Expected Outcome:
Two (2) fully operational mobile transformer oil treatment and vacuum processing vehicles that enable safe, reliable and efficient transformer oil conditioning, moisture removal, degassing and associated maintenance activities across the NGET transmission network, while maximising operational availability and long-term asset value. The resulting contract will also provide NGET with the option to procure up to two (2) additional equivalent units, subject to business requirements, funding approval and satisfactory performance of the initial units.

title: LEGISLATION PRINT PUBLISHING CONTRACT
description:
The purpose of this Procurement Process is for The National Archives (TNA) to select a Print Publishing Supplier to deliver its Legislation Print Publishing Contract.
The intention is to award the Contract for an initial period 2 years, with options to extend for three further periods of up to twelve months each (2+1+1+1).
The attached Invitation to Tender document gives an overview of the print publishing requirements and should be read in conjunction with Annexes 1 - 4, which provide more information about what is printed and why. If you require access to them, please contact us at procurement@nationalarchives.gov.uk
We estimate the maximum contract value over the whole contract term (i.e. 5 years) to be circa £4,200,000 (inc. VAT).
The Print Publishing Supplier will operate the print publishing of legislation, associated documents, annual bound volumes of legislation and legislative effects, Chronological Tables and correction slips. The Print Publishing Supplier is responsible for all aspects of print production. 
The Print Publishing Supplier will make sure that all printed items are made available for sale and deliver all aspects of order fulfilment and customers services related to the printing and sale of legislation items, including taking payment, handling enquiries and complaints, despatch and record keeping. 
Printing legislation is a statutory requirement - the Print Publishing Supplier must provide a print publishing service that meets exacting quality standards and specifications, and that prints legislative items to prescribed and non-negotiable deadlines.
In addition, government departments pay a publishing fee for online publishing. The Print Publishing Supplier is not responsible for online publishing but is responsible for the financial administration of the publishing charges made to government departments. This involves invoicing departments for the correct publishing fees and ensuring that invoices are paid in a timely manner, including chasing where invoices have not been paid. The Print Publishing Supplier then transfers the publishing fees to The National Archives on a quarterly basis. The Print Publishing Supplier needs to inform The National Archives of any overdue outstanding departmental invoices.

title: The Broxbourne School - Catering Tender
description:
At Broxbourne School we are proud to provide an outstanding education which shapes our young people to become confident, kind, respectful and hard-working adults, able to make a full contribution to society. 
In recent years the school has been completely rebuilt and all our stakeholders now benefit from state-of-the art facilities. These facilities support the exemplary teaching and learning provided by our highly qualified and experienced staff who work tirelessly to ensure all of our students enjoy the ‘Achievement and Opportunity For All’ that is our school’s mission. In June 2024 we were inspected by Ofsted, and were delighted to be graded ‘Outstanding’ in every category. We seek a catering provider that will match our high standards.
The close partnership we form with our supportive parental body is an essential ingredient of our sustained success, as are the partnerships we form with our support service providers. 
Further information regarding the School can be obtained here: https://www.broxbourne.herts.sch.uk/
Tender information:
The successful tenderer will be required to provide excellent catering services to The Broxbourne School, which has 1415 pupils, of which approximately 11.2% are eligible for free school meals, and 200 teaching and support staff. 
The contract term being tendered is for three years, 1st January 2027 – 31st December 2029. There is an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 31st December 2031.
The contract offers an excellent opportunity to review and propose enhancements to the current catering services at the School. This includes but is not limited to: breakfast, morning break, lunchtime and after-school services, over the academic year, plus hospitality services upon request.
The school is keen to secure a high-quality catering service, including fresh, healthy, locally sourced ingredients prepared on site, with a menu design that is varied and flexible to suit the requirements of the school’s specific students. The school is proud of its ‘family ethos’ and expects both a tightly managed service and a management style delivered by the successful contractor that supports, encourages and develops the catering staff.
The school requires the contractor to maintain a model health and safety culture, demonstrating a commitment to rigorous compliance and a proven ability to address any emerging concerns with immediate, proactive responses.
The school is not obliged to accept the lowest price submitted for this tender; the school is keen to secure ‘best value’ from this contract and to deliver ‘best value’ to its students. Innovative and creative ideas as to how the services can be developed and value added will be welcomed. The school seeks a contractor that is keen to work in partnership and who will deliver to its highest abilities, at all times. 
Competitive Flexible Procedure 
This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two-stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here, a minimum of 5 candidates (or fewer, in the event fewer than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement, and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. 
Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 35% price and 65% quality.
Value of contract:
The annual value of the current contract is £457,622 (the total sales, including FSM, in the last contract year)
Therefore, the value of this contract is approximately £2,288,110 
The contract shall be a guaranteed performance contract with any hospitality requirements billed separately.
Additional requirements and information:
●The school has a minimum requirement for a contractor’s employers' liability and public liability insurance of £5 million 
●The minimum annual turnover that your company must have achieved to be considered for this opportunity is £1 million
●There are incumbent catering staff currently within the Local Government Pension Scheme 
●The catering services are currently contracted to Herts Catering Ltd.  
●The client reserves the right not to appoint in conclusion of this project.

title: NHM150 Western Galleries - Base Build Mechanical, Electrical and Public Health
description:
The Natural History Museum has announced important transformations of its internal spaces ahead of the 150th anniversary of the opening of the South Kensington site, occurring in 2031. As part of these transformations, the popular Dinosaur Gallery will be restored, and the Origins Gallery, the Old General Herbarium and the Swing Space, currently closed to the public, will be reopened and returned to public use. These galleries are identified collectively as the' Western Galleries'. The works in each gallery will be articulated in two phases: base build, which is the object of this tender, and fit out, which will be tendered separately.
The first works to commence will be the Swing Space in Autumn 2027 (base build) for an opening in 2028, followed shortly after by the Botany Library and the Old General Herbarium, due in 2029, Dinosaur Gallery, opening in 2030, and Origins Gallery that will be completed in 2031.
A Feasibility Study has just been completed both for base build and fit-out leading to the identification of a set of recommended options for the base build and a set of design principles for the fit-out.
The base build works for all the galleries in scope will encompass design and works for (high-level scope, including but not limited to):
- Conservation of the gallery spaces
- Making good of the fabric of the building
- Removal of redundant services
- New ventilation and heating / cooling system and associated Building Works in Connection (BWIC)
- Mechanical, electrical and public health systems
- Creation of new plant rooms to support the increased needs of the spaces
- Required structural works
Additional works (including but not limited to):
- Clearance of existing spaces
- Dismantling and removal of Dinosaur Gallery walkway, with relocation of connected existing service.
- Decant and recant of Botany Library contents
- Temporary relocation of Dino Shop
- Decant and relocation of offices to make room for the new circulation core
- Conservation of existing fixtures and finishes (e.g. cabinets and bookcases) in Old General Herbarium and Botany Library
- Removal of existing Dino shop and dog leg corridor in the Swing Space
- Creation of 2 new vertical circulation cores (lifts and staircase), with all the related M&E works
- Creation of new toilets and ancillary spaces, with all the related MEPH works
- Relocation and enlargement of ground floor café and MEP service provision for it
- Creation of new café on the first floor and MEP service provision for it
- Fit out of new Dino Shop and the two cafes.
The appointed consultants will be asked to act as Mechanical, Electrical and Public Health (MEPH) and Acoustics consultant, developing the MEPH design for the galleries and ancillary spaces across RIBA stages 2-7, working with the other consultants and Museum stakeholders to ensure the appropriate solutions are identified and developed.
In order to access the documents for the tender exercise, all tenderers must complete the NDA available in the SQ stage document library. The NDA must be signed by an appropriate representative of the tendering company and returned to the Museum for countersignature. Once the NDA has been completed by both parties, it will be sent to tenderers for record keeping. The tenderer will then be added to the Tenderbox stage. Once bidders have been added to the Tenderbox they will receive an automated e-mail from Delta.

title: PR Agency Services
description:
Synchronicity Care Limited on behalf of Fresh and Balance are seeking a provider of PR Agency Services.  Fresh and Balance is the North East's integrated programme for reducing tobacco and alcohol harm in the region. They are one single joint programme carrying out much of the public and partner facing work under the two separate, well recognised brands of Fresh and Balance.
Fresh and Balance remit is to reduce smoking rates and the harm caused by tobacco and alcohol amongst the local population and key audiences using a multi-strand approach based on best national and international evidence. This includes mass media campaigns, campaigning and advocacy, effective internal communications, and making voices heard on the national stage to politicians and decision makers.
A key element of their work and priority of local funders is the delivery of all year round news and social media reach/engagement to ensure issues and messages in the public eye all year round on the channels that people see, read and hear, providing a highly cost effective return on investment. This also involves working with a range of senior stakeholders for messengers and champions, building support for measures to reduce smoking and harmful drinking, motivating and triggering behaviour change, and engaging and motivating key partners to prioritise these agendas regionally and nationally.
Communications cover three main strands:
•	Behaviour change - highlighting the risks and signposting positive behaviour change around quitting smoking, reducing second hand smoke and reducing drinking - via campaigns, socials and two key websites FreshQuit.co.uk and ReduceMyRisk.tv.
•	Highlighting the harm - the cost of tobacco and alcohol across the region and nationally to motivate regional stakeholders and the public
•	Campaigning for change - a strong policy focus to call for more action nationally on tobacco and alcohol, increasing public and partner support for this. This also includes an increasing focus on building partnerships across the health system, local communities and community and voluntary sector.
Fresh and Balance are looking for a PR agency with the experience, skills and knowledge to develop communications across the increasing range of available media channels to secure content - both traditional and online.
Since we are a joint programme, this will be one contract serving both campaign brands, while still requiring the insight and experience in social marketing approaches to plan campaigns and approaches around both tobacco and alcohol.
The successful agency will be expected to provide PR support to support the programme from 1st April 2027 with the potential for contract extensions and subject to satisfactory performance and reviews and funding.
buyer: COUNTY DURHAM AND DARLINGTON NHS FOUNDATION TRUST

title: Theatre in Education
description:
The Authority has agreed to take over the ownership of the theatre in education contract from the council, a decision was made to continue with the incumbent supplier for a period of 1 year, allowing the Authority working alongside the council, to run a competitive process for a replacement contract which will go live September 2028. 
This contract is for 1 year only with no extension options and is for the delivery of the following:  Four-week tour (40 schools) with a target number for 7200 students. 
Split Second is a dynamic, multimedia theatre performance that follows three students, whose fast-paced, 
carefree lives reflect the reality of many young people today. Through their shifting friendships and 
everyday choices, the play explores how distractions, peer influence, and time pressures can impact their 
behaviour as pedestrians. A series of small decisions ultimately leads to a life-changing incident, 
highlighting the importance of road awareness and safe decision-making.
The accompanying workshop reinforces the production's key learning outcomes, with a focus on:
• The leading causes of pedestrian KSIs
• The personal and wider consequences of KSIs
• External influences on young people's behaviour
• Practical strategies for managing attitudes and making safer choices on the road
Using interactive techniques such as hot-seating, pupils have the opportunity to challenge characters 
directly and unpack their choices. The session culminates in the re-staging of a pivotal moment from the 
play, allowing pupils to intervene and guide the characters towards safer outcomes. This empowers 
students to recognise risk, resist negative peer influence and build confidence in choosing safer 
behaviours

title: Belgium – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Thema Ruimte. Dienst Omgevingsbeleid. Opmaak van een gemeentelijk beleidsplan ruimte
description: De opdracht omvat de opmaak van een gemeentelijk Beleidsplan Ruimte voor de Stad Aalst, zoals voorzien in de Vlaamse Codex Ruimtelijke Ordening (VCRO). Artikel 1.1.3 van de Codex bepaalt namelijk dat de ruimtelijke ordening van het Vlaamse Gewest, de provincies en de gemeenten beleidsmatig wordt vastgelegd in ruimtelijke structuurplannen of ruimtelijke beleidsplannen. Het Beleidsplan Ruimte zal als beleidsdocument het kader vormen voor de ruimtelijke toekomst van de stad, zowel strategisch op lange termijn als operationeel op middellange termijn. Het zal het Gemeentelijk Ruimtelijk Structuurplan (GRS, goedgekeurd in 2002) vervangen. De realisatie van een gemeentelijk Beleidsplan Ruimte doorloopt een gefaseerd proces in wisselwerking met de opmaak van een plan-MER. Dit plan-MER moet de beleidskeuzes in het Beleidsplan Ruimte aan een milieueffectenbeoordeling op strategisch niveau onderwerpen met als finaliteit de beleidskeuzes te bevestigen, te verantwoorden en/of bij te sturen. De Stad verwacht dat de opdrachtnemer de wisselwerking en afstemming tussen het beleidsplanningsproces en de milieueffectenrapportage mee bewaakt. Essentieel voor de opmaak van een gemeentelijk Beleidsplan Ruimte is het organiseren van een volwaardig en inclusief publiekstraject. Een volledige en uitgebreide omschrijving van de opdracht is terug te vinden in de hierna vermelde technische bepalingen. De dienstverleningsplaats is het grondgebied van de stad Aalst.

title: Denmark – Technical testing, analysis and consultancy services – Udbud af rammeaftale vedr. rådgivning ifm. ledningsanlæg i oplandet
description: TårnbyForsyning Spildevand A/S udbyder som offentligt udbud en rammeaftale vedr. ydelser af rådgivning ifm. ledningsanlæg i oplandet. Rammeaftalen vil primært omfatte rådgivningsydelser indenfor hydrauliske beregninger, dimensionering af ledninger, bassiner og pumpekapacitet samt løbende opdatering og analyse af det eksisterende regnvandssystem. Følgende opgaver vil bl.a. være omfattet af rammeaftalen: • Hydraulisk modellering, konsekvensberegninger og kalibrering • Dimensionering af ledninger, bassiner og pumpestationer • Udarbejdelse af notater og rapporter om forudsætninger og resultater (f.eks. overløbsberegninger, notater ifm. skybrudshændelser) • Projektledelse, fremdriftsrapportering og koordinering • Løbende opdatering af hydraulisk model med data fra projekter og SRO-system • Workshops og analyser • Deltagelse i møder og løbende dialog med TårnbyForsyning • Koordinering af flowmålings kampagner • Koordinering med Tårnby Kommune og øvrige parter Opgaverne omfatter både konkrete projekter og løbende ad hoc-bistand. Rådgiverens ydelser vil også kunne omfatte projektering af fysiske anlæg og i den forbindelse også bygherrerådgivning, udbud og byggeledelses- og tilsynsopgaver, kvalitetssikring, økonomistyring, sikkerhedsledelse, risikostyring, kommunikationshåndtering samt, afslutning af sager med afleveringsforretning, opfølgning på mangler, kontrol og aflevering af som udført data samt 1-års eftersyn. I øvrigt kan der opstå opgaver vedrørende: • Myndighedsproces og behandling ifm. miljøopgaver (udledningstilladelser mv.), • bistand ved bearbejdning af data fra droner, scanninger og lignende hjælpemidler fra f.eks. landinspektører eller fra andre digitale leverandører. • Screening og Review af opgaver/projekter udarbejdet ifm. forsyningens renseanlæg Rådgiverens ydelser skal leveres i overensstemmelse med FRI's Ydelsesbeskrivelse for Anlæg 2019 som finder anvendelse i det omfang, de er relevante for de pågældende konkrete opgaver, der tildeles på rammeaftalen, ligesom ABR 18 er gældende med de modifikationer, der fremgår af udkast til rammeaftale og af dokumentet ABR18 med tilføjelser og bemærkninger. Rammeaftalen udbydes med en varighed på 2 år, gældende fra indgåelse af aftalen. Der er option på forlængelse af rammeaftalen for yderligere 2 x 12 måneder, i alt 2 år. Rammeaftalens maksimale løbetid er således 4 år inkl. mulige forlængelser (optioner). Der indgås en ikke-eksklusiv rammeaftale med én leverandør, og det er alene Ordregiver, der kan trække på rammeaftalen. Den udbudte rammeaftale har en anslået værdi på DKK 16 mio. og en maksimal værdi på DKK 20 mio. Idet rammeaftalen er ikke-eksklusiv, er leverandøren dog ikke sikret eller berettiget til nogen omsætning på rammeaftalen udover de konkrete træk, Ordregiver foretager i rammeaftalens løbetid.

title: Ireland – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – Pre-Qualification Questionnaire for the Provision of Mystery Passenger Survey Services
description: The Authority intends to engage a service provider to deliver continuous Mystery Passenger Surveys across multiple modes of public transport. The Services shall include all, but are not limited to, the following survey types: • Bus Service Mystery Passenger Surveys; Bus Station Mystery Passenger Surveys; Light Rail Service Mystery Passenger Surveys; Rail Service Mystery Passenger Surveys; Rail Station Mystery Passenger Surveys; Dublin Bus Head Office Mystery Passenger Surveys; and Static Bus Stop Mystery Passenger Surveys. The Services shall include all necessary management and administration, survey design, data collection, data processing and analysis and reporting of performance data. At each stage it is paramount the research is carried out using a rigorous method of quality control. Surveys shall be conducted continuously and reported on a quarterly basis. Results of each survey should be available to the Authority and to the relevant Operator post quality checking from the team, to allow any queries on the data to be raised. Circa 2,500 individual Mystery Passenger Surveys are required to be completed each quarter. The central aim of the Services is to provide data that can be used to manage Operator performance and allow the Authority to assign target service levels which can then be used by contract managers and Operators to effectively monitor and improve customer experience. The survey results are subject to a high level of scrutiny and its methodology and quality is required to be robust. The mystery passenger survey is a critical piece of work for the Authority and various transport contracts that rely on its results.

description: Vandmiljø Randers udbyder nærværende kvalifikationsordning for geoteknisk rådgivning i henhold til forsyningsvirksomhedsdirektivet art. 77, direktiv 2014/25/EU af 26. februar 2014.Kvalifikationsordningens formål er at etablere en liste over kvalificerede virksomheder, der kan levere rådgivning vedr. geo- og miljøtekniske undersøgelser og jordhåndteringsopgaver til Vandmiljø Randers indenfor kvalifikationsordningens fagområder.Opgaverne vedrører blandt andet geo- og miljøtekniske boringer, geotekniske forundersøgelser, miljøundersøgelser, hydrogeologiske boringer, forklassificering af område kortlagt som forurenet, forklassificering af jord, monitering/overvågning af grundvand og vibrationer samt ad hoc rådgivning i forbindelse med projekter og driftsopgaver. De geotekniske boringer kan have en eller flere af formål, eksempelvis boringer for bygværker, byggegruber og ledninger, boringer i forbindelse med regnvandsbassiner, boringer i forbindelse med grundvandsproblematik samt screening for forurening – overfladeprøver/nedstik.Optagelse på kvalifikationsordningen er ikke ensbetydende med, at virksomheden er garanteret opgaver i Vandmiljø Randers regi.Optagelse på ordningen medfører, at virksomheden kan blive inviteret til at afgive bud på konkrete opgaver inden for fagområderne omfattet af ordningen. Udvælgelsen blandt de på ordningen optagne virksomheder, der inviteres til at afgive bud på den/de enkelte opgave(r), sker på baggrund af en konkret vurdering fra opgave til opgave i henhold til kriterierne i vejledningen til kvalifikationsordning afsnit 8.Bemærk: Vandmiljø Randers er ikke forpligtet til at anvende denne kvalifikationsordning og forbeholder sig retten til at udbyde de omfattede arbejder separat eksempelvis hvis de indgår som en del af en anden leverance.Vandmiljø Randers etablerer med kvalifikationsordningen en liste over kvalificerede ansøgere. Der vil kunne udføre geotekniske opgaver samt jordhåndtering for Vandmiljø Randers inden for følgende områder:Type A: Simpel geotekniske undersøgelser udenfor bebygget område.Type B: Geotekniske undersøgelser indenfor bebyggede områder med jordhåndtering.Type C: Komplicerede geotekniske undersøgelser indenfor bebyggede områder, med jordhåndtering og vanskelige grundvandforhold.Type D: Udførelse af landskabsanalyse.Hvor en CPV-afdeling, - gruppe eller -klasse er nævnt forbeholder Vandmiljø Randers sig ret til, at en udbudt opgave kan omfatte elementer fra alle underliggende CPV-grupper, - klasser, eller -kategorier.De faglige discipliner er omfattet af de supplerende CPV-koder, hvilket er oplyst i bekendtgørelsens del II 2.2 og udspecificeret i det omfang, det har været muligt, held ned i kategori/underkategori.Et givent udbud vil typisk ikke omfatte alle oplyst supplerende CPV-koder. Ét udbud kan omfatte nogle, mens et andet vil omfatte andre m.v.Da kvalifikationsordningen er åben for løbende optag, er der ikke en egentlig tidsfrist for indsendelse af anmodning om optagelse.Det præciseres, at første udbud under denne kvalifikationsordning forventes udsendt til udvalgte ansøgere oktober/november 2026.For at ansøgere kan komme betragtning ved dette udbud er senest frist for indsendelse af anmodning om optagelse på kvalifikationsordningen: 22. oktober 2026.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – FE 04.0369/2026/BGB - Zeitliche Entwicklung der akustischen Eigenschaften von Walzasphaltdeckschichten unter Verkehrsbelastung
description: Im Rahmen der Lärmvorsorge besteht gemäß dem 16. Bundesimmissionsschutzgesetz ein gesetzlicher Anspruch auf Lärmschutz. Mit der Absenkung der Auslösewerte der Lärmsanierung für Bundesfernstraßen unterstrich das BMDV, dass die Lärmreduzierung ein zentrales Thema unserer Gesellschaft auf dem Gebiet des Umweltschutzes ist. Die akustischen Eigenschaften von Fahrbahndeckschichten können hier einen wesentlichen Beitrag des Straßenverkehrs zum Umweltschutz liefern. Entscheidend dabei ist, dass die Reduzierung des Reifen-Fahrbahn-Geräusches nicht nur im Neuzustand erreicht wird, sondern auch nach mehreren Jahren unter Verkehrsbelastung noch vorhanden ist. Mit der Einführung der überarbeiteten Richtlinien für Lärmschutz an Straßen (RLS-19) wird erstmalig auch der akustischen Dauerhaftigkeit von Fahrbahnbelägen Rechnung getragen, denn für die Festlegung der Straßendeckschichtkorrektur nach TP KoSD-19 werden ausschließlich Streckenabschnitte berücksichtigt, die zum Zeitpunkt der Messung mindestens 6 Jahre unter Verkehr sind. Dies berücksichtigt die Erkenntnis, dass sich die akustischen Eigenschaften der Fahrbahnoberfläche (Textur) unter dem Einfluss von Verkehr und Witterung verändern. Der Mechanismus von Texturveränderungen von Fahrbahndeckschichten unter dem Einfluss von Verkehr und Witterung über einen definierten Zeitraum ist jedoch bislang kaum wissenschaftlich untersucht worden. Daher wurde 2021 das Forschungsprojekt FE 04.0333/2021/BRB „Zeitliche Entwicklung der akustischen Eigenschaften von Walzasphaltdeckschichten unter Verkehrsbelastung“ ausgeschrieben und vergeben, in dem die akustischen und bautechnischen Eigenschaften von drei Walzasphaltdeckschichten SMA 8 S und SMA 8 LA sowie DSH-V5 auf 15 Neubaumaßnahmen unterschiedlicher Verkehrsbelastung zunächst über einen Nutzungszeitraum von drei Jahren untersucht und bewertet wurden. Es liegen detaillierte Daten zu Materialprüfungen sowie Textur- und akustischen Messungen aus jährlichen Mess- und Untersuchungsprogrammen vor. Die Untersuchungen, die im Forschungsprojekt FE 04.0333/2021/BRB „Zeitliche Entwicklung der akustischen Eigenschaften von Walzasphaltdeckschichten unter Verkehrsbelastung“ begonnen wurden, sollen nun für weitere 3 Jahre fortgesetzt werden, wobei die durchzuführenden Untersuchungen auf den betrachteten Strecken in Art und Umfang den bisherigen entsprechen sollen. Ziel des Forschungsprojektes ist es, die primär verantwortlichen Einflüsse, die zum Verlust der geräuschmindernden Wirkung von Fahrbahnoberflächen führen, über einen Zeitraum von mindestens 6 Jahren aufzuzeigen sowie die Effekte im Detail an spezifischen Messstellen über einen definierten Zeitraum zu analysieren. Durch das grundlegende Verständnis der mechanischen Veränderungsprozesse, die für die Dauerhaftigkeit der akustischen Wirksamkeit verantwortlich sind, können die Erkenntnisse ggf. auch auf andere, hier nicht untersuchte Bauweisen übertragen werden.

title: Ireland – Architectural design services – Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary
description: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. Tipperary County Council is undertaking a competitive tendering process for the establishment of a Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Multi-Disciplinary Consultancy Services for Public Realm, Landscape and Building Upgrade Projects in Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. The Framework Agreement will require the successful Consultant to provide, either directly or through its proposed multi-disciplinary team, all of the following services: 1. Architectural Services – Public Realm 2. Conservation Architectural Services 3. Landscape Architectural Services 4. Civil and Structural Engineering Services 5. Quantity Surveying Services 6. Project Management Services 7. Project Supervisor Design Process (PSDP) Services 8. Employer’s Representative Services 9. Public Liaison / Stakeholder Engagement Services 10. Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Services 11. Planning Services 12. Archaeological Services 13. Fire Engineering Services Only Applicants capable of providing all of the above disciplines and associated specialist expertise, whether in-house, through subcontractors or as part of a grouping/consortium, will be considered. This competition will be conducted using a restricted procedure. At Stage 1, Applicants will be assessed against the suitability and selection criteria set out in the Suitability Assessment Questionnaire. It is intended that the five highest-scoring Applicants, subject to a sufficient number meeting all minimum requirements and rules for selection, will be invited to participate in Stage 2. At Stage 2, shortlisted Applicants will be issued with the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documentation. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the award criteria and weightings set out in the Invitation to Tender. The highest-ranked compliant Tenderer will be appointed to the Single-Party Framework Agreement and will also be awarded the Initial Contract. The Initial Contract will relate to the further development and delivery of public realm and associated projects in Clonmel. Clonmel Town Centre requires a significant streetscape and public realm upgrade. A design previously received Part VIII approval; however, the design now requires further development, amendment and coordination to reflect the current project scope and available funding and to bring the project through detailed design, tender, construction and handover stages. Tipperary County Council has also acquired a protected structure for which design development and a Part VIII planning process will be required. The Architect-Led Design Team may therefore be required to deliver a combination of public realm, landscape, civil engineering and building upgrade works, including works to protected and heritage structures. The Architect will act as Lead Consultant and will be responsible for coordinating and managing the full multi-disciplinary design team, programme, cost and delivery of the projects. During the construction stage, the Design Team will be required to provide ongoing technical support, respond to queries arising on site and advise on proposed variations and other matters affecting the delivery of the works. Projects arising under the Framework Agreement are anticipated to be funded, in whole or in part, through the Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund (TCRIF) and/or other available funding programmes. Please note that an ITT is not required for this stage of the tender process.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Planungsleistungen Technische Ausrüstung ALG 4, 5 und 6, gem. §§ 53 ff. HOAI 2021, LPH 3-9, stufenweise Beauftragung
description: Gegenstand des Auftrags sind Leistungen der Technische Ausrüstung ALG 4, 5 und 6 (ELT) gem. §§ 53 ff HOAI 2021, LPH 3-9 bei stufenweiser Beauftragung. Ggf. werden auch verschiedene besondere Leistungen beauftragt werden.------Die Klinikverbund Allgäu gGmbH plant die Errichtung des Neubaus „Bauabschnitt 1 Erweiterungsbau Nordwest“ am Standort Klinik Immenstadt.------Die Klinik Immenstadt ist ein Krankenhaus des Klinikverbunds Allgäu.------Am Standort Immenstadt besteht für den Klinikverbund Allgäu gGmbH ein zusätzlicher Raumbedarf aufgrund der im Mai 2026 vom Bayrischen Staatsministerium für Gesundheit, Prävention und Pflege beschlossenen Planbettenerhöhung auf 230 Betten und zur Schaffung aktuell fehlender Nebenräume. Das Bauvorhaben erhält die Bezeichnung „Bauabschnitt 1 Erweiterungsbau Nordwest“. ------Der Neubau mit einer Nutzfläche von ca. 3.921 m² gemäß Zielplanung umfasst vier Geschosse mit: - UG: Technik, Umkleiden - EG: Arztdiensträume, U+B-Räume, Seelsorge, Soziale Dienste, Raum der Stille - 1.OG: Highcare-Bettenstation - 2.OG: Arztdiensträume, Verwaltung, Besprechungsräume, Archiv - 3.OG: Pflegestation, Wahlleistung Auf der Dachfläche sind Flächen für eine Technikzentrale (z.B. Lüftungszentrale) und PV-Anlage vorgesehen. ------Für die Baufeldfreimachung sind zudem Rückbauarbeiten, Spartenanpassungen und Kanalverlegungen im Bereich des Baufeldes bzw. des angrenzenden Bürgersteiges erforderlich. Der Bauherr holt derzeit aktuelle Spartenpläne ein. ------Die Umsetzung zur Baufeldfreimachung, Rückbau der Kapelle, Errichtung des Neubaus, Umbau im Bestand und Herstellung der erforderlichen Anschlüsse an den Gebäudekomplex erfolgt in mehreren Bauphasen. ------Es ist eine Verlegung des Sauerstofftanks notwendig; als neuer Standort wird der nördliche Grundstücksbereich vor der Zufahrt zum GZI-Parkplatz favorisiert. ------Die Aushubsohle wird unterhalb des mittleren Grundwasserstandes liegen; somit werden nach bisherigen Erkenntnissen Spundwände für die Baugrube erforderlich, die in die Seetonschichten einbinden. ------Für die weiteren Planungsschritte der Tragwerksplanung wird zeitnah ein Baugrundgutachter beauftragt. ------Zusätzlich zum Neubau ist ein Umbau im Bestand in Form einer Erweiterung der Zentralen Notaufnahme (Schaffung Überwachungsplätze, bisher: Umkleiden) im Untergeschoss vorgesehen (s. Plananlage). Während der Bauausführung muss eine Zufahrt zur Zentralen Notaufnahme uneingeschränkt möglich sein. -----Das beiliegende Raum- und Funktionsprogramm wurde vom Bayrischen Staatsministerium für Gesundheit, Prävention und Pflege freigegeben. Bei dem Projekt werden Fördermittel gemäß Art. 11 BayKrG beantragt. Die förderrechtlichen Rahmenbedingungen (u.a. Terminschiene, vergaberechtliche Vorgaben, Anforderungen an Förderantragsunterlagen) sind bei der Projektabwicklung zwingend einzuhalten.------ Die im Juni 2026 für die Förderantragserstellung beauftragten Fachdisziplinen gelten als vorbefasste Bewerber. Die bereits erstellten Planunterlagen werden allen Teilnehmern mit den Verfahrensunterlagen (siehe 5.1.11) zur Verfügung gestellt, um alle Bieter auf denselben Informationsstand zubringen. ------Zeitschiene: Die Vergabeverhandlung findet voraussichtlich Mitte November 2026 statt. Die Auftragsvergabe und der unmittelbar darauffolgende Projektstart ist für Ende 2026 / Anfang 2027 vorgesehen. Die Bauausführung des Neubaus ist von Q3/2028 bis Q4/2030 vorgesehen.------Hinweis: Die Projektbesprechungen finden in deutscher Sprache statt.

title: Norway – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Review of the extent and development of child and youth crimes.
description: Today's official crime statistics are based solely on the police registers and have several methodic limitations. Other data sources based on survey data do not necessarily form the same picture of the extent and development of child and youth crime as the official crime statistics. There is uncertainty as to how the developments in child and youth crime are actually measured and how the statistics are understood. In order to understand the extent, development and possible explanations of the development in the child and youth crime, a solid data basis is needed. The aim of the assignment is to procure an independent, research-based and comprehensive knowledge basis for the development of child and youth crime in Norway. It includes: 1. Map existing data sources 2. Highlight how developments in child and youth crime can be collated and understood over time 3. Recommend measures for long-term high quality of the knowledge basis The knowledge will form an important basis for authorities and other actors who work with the prevention of child and youth crimes being able to implement as much effort as possible. The final delivery deadline for the contract is 30 November 2027. The assignment has a value of NOK 1.8 million excluding VAT. See annex 1 of the contract for further details on the delivery.

Sir Thomas Rich's School (and Sixth Form) is currently out to tender for the provision of a full daily catering service.
The contract is being offered for three years with the option to extend for a further two periods of 12 months.  The contract commencement date is 26 October 2026
The services at the school are  an outsourced provision.
The Contractor will be responsible for the provision of a full school food catering service for the pupils and staff at the school. This will consist of breakfast and morning breaks and full lunch service for each school day.
 The catering facilities at the school include two kitchens, one for the main school and one in the Sixth Form. There is also currently a snack pod for the main school. There is an After School Service 'Late Clubs' provision.
Across the school there are currently 1238 pupils on roll for the academic year 2025/26.  Of this figure, 66 pupils are entitled to Free School Meals. 
TUPE is expected to apply, details of which can be found in the tender documentation.
There are presently no members of the catering staff who have membership of the LGPS.
The school is keen to further increase uptake and continue the good work already in place for catering.  It wishes to do so by working closely with the successful contractor in developing and continuously improving the service and partnership during the period of the contract and by introducing innovative and creative ideas as submitted in the tender process and ongoing.
The school is aware that there are always opportunities to improve and modernise. They are interested in ensuring that the caterers provide the best possible service, introducing new menu ideas and initiatives so that pupils are all eating and utilising the service regularly.

The contract is being offered for three years with the option to extend for a further two periods of 12 months.  The contract commencement date is 26 October 2026

title: P12819 - National School of Government and Public Services
description:
This notice is not an official launch of our procurement(s), it is to alert the market to future opportunities and allow us to begin conversations that will shape plans for multiple future requirements.
The Cabinet Office (Government Skills Group) is transforming the way learning and development (L&D) is designed, procured, and delivered across the Civil Service. Following the announcement by the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, the government is establishing the new National School of Government and Public Services (hereon The National School).
The National School is tasked with delivering high-quality, targeted training to approximately 558,000 civil servants, developing executive leadership in the wider public sector, and to partner with public sector training bodies.
The strategic goal of the National School is to shift away from the historically outsourced prime-supplier managed-service model. In its place, the Cabinet Office is building an insourced, hybrid capability. Under this new Future Operating Model (FOM), the Cabinet Office will directly manage core operations, standard curricula, and stakeholder engagement. However, expert external provision will remain a critical element of the programme.
The National School transformation programme relies on three core, interdependent pillars to transition Civil Service training away from fully outsourced prime-supplier models toward an in-house, hybrid operating model by April 2028.
Together, these pillars work to build direct relationships with suppliers, provide a modern digital learning infrastructure, and establish robust in-house operational workflows.
Pillar 1: Future Supplier Partnerships (FSP)
The FSP project serves as the commercial enabler of the new operating model, building the in-house capability required to buy learning services and manage supply chains directly. We aim to establish direct, value-driven contractual relationships with UK-based SMEs, universities, business schools, and niche providers.
The project team have identified an indicative Three-Stage Roadmap to enable this delivery:
Stage 1 (Immediate - April 2027): Procuring urgent digital and specialist training needs that cannot be fulfilled through existing frameworks.
Stage 2 (April 2027-March 2028): Phased procurement for core, National School-sponsored curriculum, coaching, and talent programmes.
Stage 3 (March 2028 onwards): On-going phased procurements falling out of Stages 1 and 2, depending on the length of contracts identified.
The scope of the requirements will cover several key procurement categories, including, but not limited to, specialised coaching pools (including for neuro-diverse leaders), blended training delivery, learning design (retaining Crown Intellectual Property), access to subject matter experts including within academia, independent research and evaluation, helpdesk/admin surge, and off-the-shelf qualifications.
Pillar 2: Future Technologies (FT)
The Future Technologies project focuses on designing and implementing the digital architecture required to run a personalised training operation for approximately 558,000 civil servants. The core objective here is the setting up and integration of platforms to manage the access, booking, payments, and evaluation of learning materials. This involves transitioning away from heavy manual processes to maximise technological efficiencies.
At this stage the project team has identified the central deliverable as a unified online portal allowing learners to access the full National School offering. Key technologies in scope for procurement include, but are not limited to, a new Learning Management System (LMS)/ Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems to centralise stakeholder engagement, and design/delivery tools.
Pillar 3: Future Learning Operations (FLO)
The Learning Operations project is responsible for building the actual systems, processes, and internal capabilities required to run the day-to-day training operations in-house. Their core objective is establishing an integrated operational function by April 2028 that supports over 558,000 civil servants in completing their learning journeys. It is highly dependent on the digital and commercial pillars to develop the underlying platforms that support operations.
Market Involvement
As part of the initial phases of the programme, the project teams are keen to connect with the market and gain insight into current trends, operations and barriers. title: TfGM - Cloud Public Address System
description:
This tender relates to Transport for Greater Manchester's (TfGM) need to procure a Cloud Public Address (PA) System and associated services to provide a secure, resilient, IP-based PA capability across TfGM Transport Service Facilities (TSFs). The PA service is intended to provide real-time passenger information, site-specific passenger safety and security (PSS) messages, and event-driven announcements, operable centrally from the Operations Control Centre (OCC) and locally by designated TSF Site Co-Ordinators. 
TfGM requires a cloud-hosted PA management system (with main and failover capability) integrated with an on-net estate of PA end user devices (EUDs) such as IP speakers, audio gateways, AFILs, paging stations and user clients, including the ability to interface with legacy Long Line Public Address (LLPA) systems during transition and with existing third-party systems (e.g., Cisco Unified Call Manager) as required. 
This is an Open Tender procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. This route has been selected to ensure unrestricted market access, maximise competition, and enable engagement with the full range of capable Bidders across the services market.
