title: E Scooters Trial Phase 3
description:
This is a Contract Details notice for two contracts in relation to the third phase of the transport for London (TfL) E-scooter Rental Trial (the 'Trial'). The procurement has been conducted pursuant to the Procurement Act 2023. TfL awarded two contracts and entered into two Administration Agreements ('Agreement') with the Operators who submitted the most advantageous tenders in relation to performance of thee-scooter services required by the Trial. 
The Agreement sets out the terms that apply to an Operator in relation to the provision of e-scooter services in the Greater London Area and its obligations to a) TfL as the Administrator of the third phase of the Trial and b) the various London Boroughs and/or the City of London Corporation who wish to participate in the Trial by permitting the use of e-scooters within their respective jurisdictions (referred to as 'Participating Boroughs'). The Agreement provides that a Participating Borough may issue a notice to require the relevant Operators to enter into a contract for the provision of e-scooter rental services in the geographic area controlled by that Participating Borough. Participating Boroughs may choose to enter a Full-Service contract for the provision of an e-scooter rental service or to allow e-scooters to be ridden through only (Ride-Through-Borough).
TfL awarded two (2) contracts. Three (3) Tenders have been submitted that met the minimum requirements and met the award criteria. TfL evaluated responses from all three Tenderers. 
This is a contract details notice that the Authority has entered into legally binding contracts with the top two scoring Tenders (most advantageous tenders) after observing the required standstill period. Note: pursuant to the Agreement, which is a concessionary arrangement, Operators must pay the Charges set out in the Specification. The Charges payable to TfL as the Administrator comprise an annual Administration Charge and an annual Per Bay Charge relating to the number of parking bays available. Further detail about the Charges is given in the Specification. Operators are not entitled to request payment under the Agreement from the Administrator or any of the Participating Boroughs.
The third phase of the Trial is planned to commence in September 2026 and will run for an initial term up to 24 months, which will comprise twenty-six consecutive 28-day periods. The Trial term may at TfL's discretion be extended for up to 4 years in increments of any length up to a maximum of 4 years. The Trial term will run in line with national legislation, currently in place until May 2028.
The total value of the Agreement is defined as the maximum aggregate revenue accessible to Operators over the duration of the Trial term (assuming the maximum four-year extension period is used).
Total value (estimated)
£35,280,000 excluding VAT
£42,336,000 including VAT
Contract Dates ( estimated)
21 September 2026 to 17 September 2028
Possible extension to 12 September 2032
5 years, 11 months, 22 days
Description of possible extension:
The contract includes options to extend for
increments of any length up to four years.

title: BCU-ITT-64089 - North Wales Medical School - West (YG)
description:
Bangor University (BU) and Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) are working in partnership to deliver the North Wales Medical School (NWMS), an established Welsh Government-funded programme designed to increase medical education and training capacity across North Wales. 
The works comprise of the alterations and adaptations of the existing building to form a new medical training centre. All activities must be planned for a live hospital environment, coordinating outages and access with Estates/ICT, and must comply with site rules, CDM, and applicable NHS W /BCUHB technical standards. 
The Ysbyty Gwynedd contract comprises the development of additional teaching accommodation together with the refurbishment of the existing education facilities. 
The existing education accommodation at YG has a fragmented layout, which limits the functionality and effectiveness of the current teaching environment. A review of the available accommodation against the space requirements necessary to support the teaching and learning activity associated with the curriculum has also identified that the existing rooms and overall available space are undersized. 
In addition, the existing education facilities are located along a corridor which is also used by patients, staff and carers as a route to and from the Endoscopy Department. The Estates Department has confirmed that there is no alternative route available, which presents an additional consideration in the planning and development of the education environment. 
The proposed works include: 
•	Extension onto the existing roof area to provide additional teaching accommodation. 
•	Refurbishment and improvement of the existing education spaces. 
•	Reconfiguration and enhancement of the education environment to address the current fragmented layout and improve its suitability for teaching and learning activities. 
•	Improvements to the education accommodation to support the space requirements associated with the NWMS curriculum. 
The scheme will increase the available teaching capacity at Ysbyty Gwynedd and provide an improved and more appropriately sized education environment to support the delivery of the NWMS programme.

The session will be held virtually via Microsoft Teams. 
Places for London, Transport for London's property company (formerly Transport Trading Limited Properties (TTLP)), is seeking to appoint an experienced PBSA operator to support the mobilisation and operation of the Southwark OSD scheme. The development will comprise of 429 private studios. While the scheme is at an advanced stage of design, the appointed operator will be expected to provide targeted input into the fit-out of amenity spaces, as well as lead the mobilisation phase and oversee the ongoing operation and management of the asset. 
Although the immediate requirement relates to the Southwark scheme, Places reserves the right to utilise the contract across its wider development pipeline. Accordingly, the procurement process will seek to identify an operator with the capability and expertise to support the successful delivery of Southwark and, subject to performance and strategic alignment, potentially provide services for future PBSA developments from the inception stage onwards.

title: Private Sector Development Programme in Sierra Leone
description:
The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) is undertaking early market engagement (EME) in advance of a potential future procurement for a new private sector development programme in Sierra Leone.
This programme is expected to complement a joint FCDO-British International Investment (BII) programme, Horizon Sierra Leone, which focuses primarily on unlocking near-term investment opportunities. The proposed new programme will focus on strengthening the underlying conditions required to make investment in Sierra Leone's tradable sectors, particularly agriculture and manufacturing, more attractive, productive, and inclusive.
Indicative areas of support may include:
-	Provide targeted support to investors and businesses to identify opportunities, reduce market-entry risks and costs, test new business models, and unlock investment through market scoping, feasibility studies, pipeline development, business viability assessments, and piloting innovative financing solutions
-	Technical assistance and advisory support to businesses that strengthen market systems and create wider benefits to sector(s), including providers of inputs, logistics, infrastructure, capital goods, and other enabling services.
-	Support to anchor firms to adopt more inclusive business practices, including employing more women into better-quality jobs, promoting women into leadership positions, and strengthening sourcing from women-owned businesses within supply chains.
-	Provide targeted assistance to government ministries, departments, and agencies to deliver priority reforms that unlock sectoral growth, improve the business environment, and strengthen the financial sector.

title: C0138 - UK Fund Monitoring Evaluation & Learning
description: The UK Portfolio is seeking a single supplier or consortium of suppliers to conduct an impact evaluation of the UK Fund and provide a range of learning services to UK Fund grantholders. The UK Fund is a funding programme that cover two distinct thematic areas: - Connected Communities - CYP and Youth Voice The first awards were granted in February 2024, focusing on Connected Communities, and in 2025 the funding expanded to Children and Young People (CYP) and Youth Voice. The key themes that run across the different thematic areas include voice, relationship building, agency, community systems and lived experience. UK Fund has adopted a funding approach that spans across and between countries, rather than being geographically restricted, and focuses on supporting well-established programmes that demonstrate proven impact, enabling them to scale and expand further. The funding also prioritises equity - targeting only communities facing poverty, disadvantage, and discrimination. Another distinguishing factor about the UK Fund is its emphasis on long-term systems change, requiring projects to include a mix of service delivery and systemic transformation in their plans. The evaluation and learning contract will adopt a collaborative, co-design approach that engages all grantholders, ensuring that all activities align with their learning needs. The supplier is also encouraged to involve the communities with whom the projects work, enabling them to shape and contribute to the learning and evaluation processes. This is particularly important given the programme’s emphasis on voice, agency, and power.

title: Major Water Infrastructure Programme (MWIP) - Programmatic Delivery and Opportunity Assessment
description:
Undertake a programme-wide Value for Money (VfM) appraisal of the Major Water Infrastructure Programme (MWIP) to identify, test and prioritise credible cost reduction and VfM opportunities, with a focus on decisions that can influence cost, schedule, risk and deliverability at the early stages of the project lifecycle across identified VfM drivers.
The study will adopt a two-stage approach to delivery. Stage 1 will provide a programme-wide VfM assessment, covering VfM drivers and identifying, testing and prioritising credible opportunities. Greater emphasis will be placed on those drivers where there is currently greatest potential to influence VfM, particularly given the maturity of assets within the Reservoir Programme.
Stage 2 will comprise subsequent steps required to further develop, evidence and unlock priority opportunities identified through Stage 1. These may include targeted technical, commercial or delivery assessments, where required. Any such subsequent work will be defined and commissioned separately based on the findings and recommendations from Stage 1.
The objectives of the Services are to:
• Identify potential VfM drivers across MWIP.
• Challenge and develop the initial opportunities through structured input from relevant industry and technical experts.
• Identify and prioritise the most significant opportunities for further assessment.
• Quantify potential benefits, where sufficient evidence is available, including potential cost and schedule benefits and wider value.
• Assess each priority opportunity against cost, schedule, risk, deliverability, commercial implications and wider value.
• Identify key assumptions, evidence gaps, confidence levels, dependencies, enabling conditions and risks.
• Assess the implications for delivery approaches, governance, commercial models and wider system enablers.
• Identify opportunities that may be applicable across the wider Reservoir Programme and, where relevant, other asset types in MWIP.
• Develop practical recommendations for taking priority opportunities forward.
• Provide Ofwat and relevant stakeholders with a robust and transparent evidence base to support decision-making.
Scope of Services
The Supplier shall be responsible for determining the appropriate methodology, approach and activities required to achieve the purpose and objectives of the Services.
Outputs / Deliverables
The Supplier shall provide a VfM Appraisal Report and Prioritised VfM Opportunity Matrix setting out, where evidence permits.
Schedule
The Supplier shall deliver the Services in accordance with the following indicative programme:
• Week 1: Project mobilisation and receipt of information.
• Weeks 2-3: Baseline review and development of the VfM diagnostic framework.
• Week 4: Expert input, workshops and opportunity prioritisation.
• Week 5: Draft findings issued for review, followed by final report and presentation.
The Supplier shall maintain and update the programme throughout the Services and provide a revised schedule where required to reflect progress, dependencies and any changes to the delivery approach.
The schedule shall include key milestones, review points and stakeholder meetings, including, as appropriate, meetings/checkpoints with key stakeholders.
The Supplier shall ensure that sufficient time is allowed for stakeholder review and feedback and shall promptly identify any risks to the agreed programme, together with proposed mitigation actions.
Success criteria
The Services will be considered successful where they:
A. Identify and prioritise credible VfM opportunities across the agreed VfM drivers.
B. Provide, evidence-based assessment of potential cost, schedule, risk, deliverability and wider benefits.
C. Clearly distinguish between evidenced benefits, indicative opportunities and areas requiring further investigation, with appropriate confidence levels.
D. Provide practical and actionable recommendations, including enabling conditions, dependencies, owners and next steps.
E. Demonstrate how priority opportunities can be implemented and applied
across the MWIP, where relevant.
F. Provide Ofwat and stakeholders with a clear, transparent and decision-ready evidence base to support investment and delivery decisions.
G. Deliver the agreed report, opportunity matrix and recommendations within the agreed programme, allowing sufficient time for stakeholder review and challenge.

title: North Tyneside Council Waste Management Contract
description:
This notice is being re-published to reflect a 2 day extension to the standstill period, therefore the new end date of the standstill period will be 11:59PM on Monday 21st September 2026.
North Tyneside Council (the Authority) is seeking to appoint a contractor (Contractor) for the safe, compliant and efficient management of its Waste Management Contract (the Contract) in line with the Authority's objectives as set out in the North Tyneside Plan (the Opportunity).
Following a pre-market engagement exercise which included a market engagement event on 21 July 2025, the Authority has refined its approach to the procurement and Contract and wishes to bring the Opportunity to market and invite participation formally (the Procurement).
The Opportunity
The Authority is responsible for the management of c. 77k tonnes of waste across all treatment types (Energy from Waste, landfill, composting, recycling and reuse) per annum.
The Contract will cover all existing responsibilities under the current arrangement including the: (i) transfer and treatment/management of all residual waste; (ii) management and operation of the Authority's transfer station (the TS); (iii) management and operation of the Authority's household waste recycling centre (the HWRC), including transfer and treatment of all materials; and (iv) transfer and treatment of kerbside and collected garden waste.
The Authority is seeking a Contractor with whom it can work to integrate waste management hierarchy principles into the Contract. These principles, rank (in order): (i) waste reduction at source; (ii) reuse; (iii) recycling; (iv) energy recovery; and (v) disposal without energy recovery (the Waste Hierarchy Principles).
It is anticipated that during the term of the Contract, the Contractor will perform the following services:
1. Operate the TS to (i) receive all waste delivered by the Authority under the Contract (including from the HWRC); (ii) interface with the Authority's Food and DMR contractors regarding collection of their wastes from the TS (iii) segregate and provide haulage services for all other waste for onward transportation; (iv) integrate and apply the Waste Hierarchy Principles; and (v) ensure the TS remains compliant with all relevant environmental permitting regulations.
2. Operate the HWRC to (i) receive household waste without charge to residents; (ii) ensure that only household waste is deposited at the HWRC;
(iii) provide for clear and efficient segregation of household waste, such that the potential for re-use or recycling is maximised; and (iv) maintain safe
and efficient access to and through the HWRC, while minimising vehicle queues on the public highway.
3. Make arrangements with suitably licensed facilities to accept materials segregated at the HWRC that do not require processing at the TS.
Further details about the services and the Authority's requirements are stated in the tender documents.
In addition to the existing service requirements under the Contract, the Authority is considering a variety of options as part of this Opportunity, including:
1. gainshare arrangements for reuse and recycling income, third party waste income and electricity and/or heat income;
2. the potential development and operation of a second HWRC site; and
3. proposals for reuse of materials to generate income.
The Authority is seeking to appoint a market leading organisation with demonstrable experience across similar contracts and a market leading approach to innovative waste management. Applicants are encouraged to use this Procurement to demonstrate to the Authority how they will work pragmatically and collaboratively to develop solutions that satisfy the Authority's needs and incentivises the Contractor's performance.
The Authority encourages small and medium size enterprises to participate in this Procurement, either as Applicants, consortium members, supply-chain partners or sub-contractors.
The Contract is valued at approximately £11,000,000 yearly for an estimated total value of £220,000,000 over the maximum duration of the Contract (20 years).
Applicants should note that the top three KPIs that the Authority intends to publish performance information against are likely to be the following:
1. Rectification of Non-Compliance Failures
2. Receipt of Contract Waste
3. Recycling and Reuse
Further information regarding those KPIs and more generally on the Procurement and the Authority's requirements can be found in the tender documents.

title: Department for Education Period Products Scheme 2026
description:
The Department for Education (DfE) is looking to provide free period products to schools and post-16 education providers across England through a procurement to appoint a national provider.
The Period Products Scheme ensures that period products are available and accessible, free of charge, to girls and women who need them in schools and colleges. The scheme aims to reduce periods as a barrier to education, promote dignity and equality in learning environments and tackle stigma associated with periods. The scheme was introduced after a 2018 Omnibus Survey suggested that 14% of female college students and 6% of female school pupils has been unable to access period products in the last 12-months due to affordability and 83% of secondary school leaders made free period products available in their school.
Tackling this problem remains a key priority and is part of DfE's strategy to support the Government's mission to break down the barriers to opportunity; one of the six missions which form the centrepiece of our plan for change. This mission-led approach drives coordination between different programmes and workstreams by setting ambitious shared goals.
The Department has published a competitive flexible tendering opportunity to find a single national supplier who can from September 2026:
•	Source an appropriate range of period products including reusable and environmentally friendly products
•	Design and implement user interfaces and support services
•	Plan and execute a national delivery service
We require a ‘demand-led’ service which must be available to approximately 21,000 organisations across England, with an accessible and easy to use means of interaction and product ordering.
The Department is also seeking to maximise the value of the scheme beyond the core offer through financial benefits, added value, and/or awareness activities and materials. In return, the Department proposes to offer a package of rights to the lead supplier and/or key sub-contractors/supply chain members.

title: London Borough of Newham - Future Housing Repairs, Compliance, Building Safety and Capital Investment Programme | Strategic Market Engagement
description:
The London Borough of Newham is undertaking a comprehensive market intelligence and engagement exercise to inform the future design and delivery of its Housing Repairs, Maintenance, Compliance and Capital Investment Programme. The Authority is currently considering a long-term programme of works and services with an indicative value of between £288 million and £416 million over a potential ten-year period, covering a broad range of specialist housing services including compliance, building safety, planned investment, major repairs, adaptations, voids and asset improvement programmes. The proposals outlined within the accompanying draft specification are intended solely to support this engagement process and should be viewed as initial concepts that will be refined through consultation with the market.

The Authority is seeking views on market capacity, capability, commercial models, lot structures, delivery approaches, innovation, digital solutions, social value, sustainability and emerging legislative requirements. title: Children and Young People Pathfinder - Supported Systems
description:
The commissioned activity relates to the development of child sexual abuse (CSA) systems and pathways across the South West region, building on work already undertaken to strengthen local responses to children and young people affected by CSA.
The project responds to the recognised need for improved coordination, accessibility and consistency of services across health, justice, safeguarding and voluntary sector systems. Current arrangements vary across the region, creating challenges in service accessibility, workforce confidence, governance arrangements and multi-agency working.
The organisation undertaking this work is the Bluestar Project (a Community Interest Company, in partnership with The Green House charity). 
The project aims to improve coordination, accessibility and consistency of responses to children and young people affected by CSA across health, justice, safeguarding and voluntary sector services. The work will include needs assessments, service mapping, workforce development, governance and pathway improvement, and the promotion of trauma-informed, CPS-compliant practice. Children, young people and families will be involved through co-production activities.
Bluestar will build on existing work in Swindon & Wiltshire and Dorset and undertake further systems development activity, including sequential needs assessments in Devon & Cornwall and Gloucestershire, to identify service gaps and opportunities for improvement.
At the heart of this programme is a simple aim: to support sustainable, system-wide change so that every child who experiences sexual abuse can access a timely, compassionate, and coordinated response. Achieving this requires more than new services - it demands equipping the children's workforce across all agencies with the skills, confidence, and structures to act together, and embedding a culture of listening, believing, and responding. By laying these foundations, the programme enables to move beyond fragmented provision towards lasting, joined-up systems of care. 
The Bluestar Project also led national development of pre-trial therapy guidance, training and accreditation, working alongside the police and CPS. This has been rolled out nationally.

title: Research Services: Unlocking Barriers to Audit Technology
description:
THIS IS A CONTRACT AWARD
The Financial Reporting Council (FRC) regulates auditors, accountants and actuaries and sets the UK's Corporate Governance and Stewardship Codes. As the Competent Authority for audit in the UK, we set auditing and ethical standards and monitor and enforce audit quality.
The Financial Reporting Council (FRC) is committed to supporting a resilient audit market which delivers high-quality services and outcomes.
FRC research and stakeholder engagement highlight that the largest audit firms are making significant advances in the use of technology. Mid-tier audit firms are also experimenting and adopting new tools, with varying levels of maturity in their approaches. Smaller audit firms, however, often face greater barriers to adoption, including limited time, resource constraints, technical expertise, and perceived need. As a result, they may be less able to invest in audit technology and are more likely to rely on off-the-shelf third-party solutions.
FRC via further competition under the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) framework agreement - CCS Research & Insights - GCA have commissioned  an independent research provider to undertake qualitative research into the factors influencing the adoption and usage of audit technology across the UK audit market.

title: Pavilion Management and Exhibition Production: British Pavilion at the Venice Biennale
description:
The British Council is tendering for a supplier to provide overall management, maintenance and exhibition production of the British Pavilion. The duration of the contract is two years with the option to extend for a further two years. The contract will begin with an induction period from November 2026 to January 2027, to provide effective briefing on the role and the building and to ensure the handover of responsibilities from the existing supplier. The British Council has been responsible for the British Pavilion at the Venice Biennale since 1937 and is renowned for commissioning the highest calibre UK artists and architects to present exhibitions and installations at the Pavilion.
Acting as the main point of contact in Venice for the British Council, the Service Provider will be responsible for planning, overseeing and managing all works at the pavilion including property management and operations, exhibition production and installation, building maintenance and stewarding management and Fellowship support during the Venice Biennale. The Service Provider will ensure that relationships in Venice are managed effectively, contracts with Service Providers are in place and payments are processed efficiently.
The service will cover general building management and maintenance, stewarding management and invigilation, as well as exhibition production and installation for the International Art and Architecture exhibitions held each year at the British Pavilion for la Biennale di Venezia. The British Council requires a Service Provider with expertise in exhibition production, exhibition design, fabrication and installation, with the ability to respond to a brief with creativity, and work with the British Council and appointed Artist / Curator to deliver high-quality solutions and value for money the available resources. The Service Provider will ensure that we are meeting all EU regulations with regards to building management and health and safety and will build excellent working relationships with the Biennale di Venezia, as well as the British Council extended Venice project team to deliver outstanding exhibitions at the British Pavilion for la Biennale di Venezia.

title: National Focal Centre (NFC) to Model and Map Air Pollution Impacts on UK habitat
description:
Defra is seeking to contract with supplier(s) possessing the scientific, technical and analytical expertise required to maintain and develop the UK National Focal Centre (NFC). The successful supplier(s) will deliver annual UK-wide modelling and mapping of pollutant deposition (ammonia, oxides of nitrogen and sulphur dioxide) and assess against critical loads for acidity and nitrogen. They will also map ammonia concentrations and assess against critical levels. The assessments will be reported for the UK as a whole and broken down by country. In addition, the data will be reported for specific habitat types, Special Areas for Conservation (SACs), Special Protection Areas (SPAs) and Areas/Sites of Special Scientific Interest (A/SSSIs). The modelled outputs will support annual reporting, evidence generation, biodiversity protection, environmental policy development and the UK's domestic and international reporting obligations.
We are envisaging that the new contract will start on the 01 June 27 with a one (1) month handover, from 01 June to 30 June, with full responsibility being transferred to the successful contractor on 01 July 2027.  These handover periods are to allow the new Contractor time to get ready to take over the full operation of the contract requirement.  We estimate the contract value to be between the range of £680,000 - £720,000.

Commissioning of a training provider to deliver a minimum of 6 of each of the following: • Group B (Level 2) Safeguarding Intermediate Course & Group C (Level 3) Safeguarding Advanced Course• Emergency Paediatric First Aid & Full Paediatric First Aid.
The content of the courses should be in line with the requirements specified in the National Minimum Standards for regulated childcare 2023.The courses should be delivered to meet the varying needs of the early years and childcare workforce through a mixture of daytime, evening and weekend courses, for a minimum of 8 participants per course. The training provider will be responsible for identifying and managing room bookings, including payment for all courses through this specification. The training provider will be required to provide evaluation information from participants to Wrexham County Borough Council following each course. The training provider must be able to deliver the training through the medium of Welsh if required, in line with Welsh Language Standards. The provider must be able to ensure their courses meet the requirements set out in the National Minimum Standards for Regulated Childcare 2023. Wrexham County Borough Council wish to commission our training programme for the early years and childcare workforce under the following two Lots. 
Lot 1: Group B (Level 2) Safeguarding Intermediate Course & Group C (Level 3) Advanced Safeguarding Course.
Intermediate Safeguarding Children courses help to increase existing safeguarding knowledge and teach more about what is involved in the safeguarding process. The course shows how to identify abuse, and report concerns as well as learn more about the safeguarding structure, recognising risks and what happens after a referral to social care has been made. Course type and considerations: • Face to face course• Duration: 4-6 hours/1 day/2 x evenings Advanced Safeguarding courses teach more about what the role involves and helps to understand the safeguarding process in more detail. The course uses a variety of written activities and interactive exercises to help review and develop the safeguarding procedures within the setting and ensure that all staff members understand their responsibilities towards safeguarding children. title: Fuel Cycle Technical Specification Development
description:

United Kingdom Fusion Energy Ltd (UKFE Ltd) seeks to maximise the national and regional economic and industrial benefit of the STEP programme, in line with the strategy published in March 2026, which is featured below:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/uk-fusion-energy-ltd-ukfe-strategy
Expertise in fusion and particularly tritium handling system design, manufacture, and commissioning is concentrated within national laboratories, research facilities, and a limited specialist supply chain. There is not yet a unified set of nationally or internationally adopted codes and standards that define prescriptive tritium design and qualification requirements in a form readily accessible to new or adjacent suppliers. 
This absence of clear, standardised, and accessible design benchmarks represents a barrier to wider supply‐chain engagement and hinders opportunities to expand UK industrial participation in fusion delivery. title: St Ives Pioneering Parish Affordable Housing Project-project/consultancy support
description:
St Ives Town Council is seeking project support from suitably qualified and experienced  individual(s) to assist in the delivery of an innovative housing enabling project - the Pioneering Parish project. 
The vision for the project is to develop a range of tools and interventions to support and accelerate the delivery of affordable and local needs housing and associated community infrastructure for the St Ives Parish. The project aims to apply innovation and flexibility to find local solutions which best meet community aspiration and the homes which St Ives' needs.  
The project will utilise planning contributions collected for the St Ives Parish, by Cornwall Council, specifically to enable the delivery of affordable housing.   
The project is a partnership between the Town Council and Cornwall Council to identify, de-risk and assist in the progress and / or delivery of 250 affordable housing plots within the parish of St Ives. It is expected to run for up to 3 years and will include the following key outputs and outcomes: 
•	A deliverable supply of sites and opportunities for a minimum of 250 affordable homes 
•	A RAG assessment of the most deliverable sites with timescales and agreed action plans for each 
•	A schedule of sites and for each, a suitable set of delivery tools with the aim of accelerating delivery. Tools will vary from site to site but, in general could comprise of  
•	A completed development brief capable of being adopted/ recognised by the planning authority  
•	Completed supporting studies or documents with the aim of re-risking a planning application or delivery  
•	Planning permission (planning in principle, outline or detailed) 
•	Site purchase / Land owner / affordable housing provider heads of terms for agreement  
•	Land owner collaboration agreements 
•	Cornwall Council approval for land transfer 
•	Completed economic viability assessments with agreed affordable housing outputs aligned to housing need and adopted policy 
•	A proactive delivery board with a key objective of accelerating delivery of affordable and local needs homes  
•	The completion of a neigbhourhood priorities statement subject to community consultation. 
Required Resources 
Dedicated people resources are identified as the key success factor. Expressions of interest are, therefore, sought from suitably experienced and qualified individuals, freelancers or consultancies. The Council is adopting an open approach to resourcing solutions and welcomes proposals which could see the project scope delivered in the following ways:
•	An individual seeking a short term contract of employment
•	A fixed term contract with a freelance consultant
•	An award to an established consultancy with the relevant skills and a commitment to fund the necessary hours. 
Project Duration 
In order to progress and de-risk sites and opportunities, the project is proposed to extend over three years. However, these timescales are flexible and can be reduced, should the project outputs and outcomes be achieved over a shorter period, by being resourced differently. 
It is anticipated that the likely pace of the project will require a part time project lead, equivalent to 2.5 days a week, to be reviewed annually. However, depending upon how the people resources are procured, this may be on an annualised-hours basis of approximately 975 per year. 
Funding 
The business plan sets out an indicative allocation of funding for the project resource's hours of up to £100,000, plus a separate budget of up to £150,000 in order to commission / procure necessary advice, technical reports and support planning applications and community engagement. These estimates are indicative and may be varied by negotiation. 
Should a member of staff be recruited to the Council establishment, the role will be aligned with the Town Council's adopted pay structure.

title: Expression of Interest - Specialised Support for an Individual with Complex Needs
description:
Buckinghamshire Council is seeking expressions of interest from organisations with the capability, capacity and experience to deliver specialised support for an individual with complex needs.
The service provides specialised residential support for an individual with complex needs. The Individual has a learning disability, autism, ADHD, and behaviours that can challenge. It was established as a bespoke residential placement following a transition from long-term hospital care, with the environment carefully adapted to ensure safety, structure, and therapeutic benefit. Located near Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire, the service delivers intensive staffing and tailored interventions aimed at maintaining stability, promoting engagement, and reducing incidents.
Looking ahead, the service will remain a residential provision whilst continuing to focus on promoting independence, developing daily living skills, and maximising opportunities for meaningful community participation. The long-term vision is to support the individual to achieve the highest possible level of independence and quality of life within a safe and sustainable residential environment. As the individual’s skills, resilience, and confidence increase, support arrangements will be regularly reviewed to explore opportunities for the gradual and safe reduction of care levels where appropriate, ensuring that any changes are outcome-focused, person-centred, and responsive to assessed need.
Estimated Contract Commencement: 1st April 2027
Estimated Contract Term: 36 months with an option to extend for a further 36 months

title: Online Harms Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme
description:
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is undertaking a virtual market engagement exercise Wednesday 5th August 2026 @ 10am , via MS Teams, to inform the commissioning of the Online Harms Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme.
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is committed to understanding the factors that place children and young people at risk of violence, exploitation and harm, and to working collaboratively with partners to deliver long-term, sustainable solutions. We work across communities and sectors, including youth services, local government, education, health, policing and the voluntary and community sector, championing a public health approach that combines prevention, early intervention and effective support for those experiencing the greatest levels of risk and vulnerability. 
At the heart of our approach is the belief that violence is preventable, not inevitable. We recognise, however, that many children and young people are already navigating the impacts of trauma, exploitation, abuse and complex community dynamics. As such, our work seeks not only to prevent harm before it occurs, but also to strengthen the systems, services and trusted adults responsible for safeguarding, supporting and intervening with those most affected. Central to this approach is a commitment to partnership working, evidence-informed practice and ensuring that the voices, experiences and expertise of young people and communities shape the solutions designed to support them. 
The Mayor's Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is seeking to engage with the market in advance of a forthcoming procurement opportunity relating to the delivery of its flagship Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme. 
The programme forms part of the VRU's wider public health approach to violence reduction and sits within a London-wide model developed following extensive consultation with young people, practitioners, safeguarding professionals, academics and sector experts. 
Digital life brings clear benefits for many children. Ofcom found that 99% of 13–17-year-olds see at least one benefit to being online, including help with schoolwork, learning new skills and maintaining social connections.  93% of children in the UK play video games, and children
report that gaming helps them socialise with friends, learn new skills and have fun, with most online interactions taking place with friends they already know offline. 
At the same time, the VRU is concerned that these same digital environments expose children and young people to a wide range of harms and risks.  
Digital safety is increasingly a public safety and public health concern. Children and young people are navigating identity, relationships, influence, exploitation and conflict across interconnected online and offline environments. However, systems, services and safeguarding responses have often struggled to keep pace with the rapidly evolving nature of digital spaces. This matters for the VRU because online harms do not sit separately from wider concerns about violence, vulnerability, exploitation and safeguarding.
The VRU is seeking delivery partners to pilot innovative Digital Youth Work (DYW) approaches across London that drive new models of engagement with young people and promote safeguarding in digital spaces.  
The VRU is seeking approaches that: 
Design, deliver and test new or existing digital youth work models 
Extend trusted, relationship-based youth work into digital environments 
Strengthen early intervention, prevention and safeguarding online  
Generate learning, insight and practical outputs to strengthen future activity  
The programme aims not only to deliver effective pilot activity, but also to contribute to sector-wide innovation and the development of scalable models of digital youth work across London.  
Scope of delivery 
The programme will be structured into three complementary lots: 
Lot 1: Supporting High-Need and Digitally Dependent Young People 
Testing approaches that improve accessibility and engagement for young people who face barriers to traditional provision, including SEND.  
Lot 2: Early Intervention and Prevention of Online Harms 
Testing models that enable early identification, prevention and response to online risks, with a focus on safeguarding and preventative practice of deterring online to offline violence.  
Lot 3: Universal Digital Youth Work and Positive Opportunities 
Exploring how digital youth work can foster connection, creativity, play, participation and digital citizenship for all young people. 
Bidders may apply for one, two or all three lots. Applications may be submitted by individual organisations or as partnerships/consortia.  
Target Audience 
The programme will focus on delivering digital youth work to children and young people aged 11–25 across London, including but not limited to: 
Young people at higher risk of being impacted by online harms 
Those facing barriers to traditional youth provision, including SEND and young people who may be more digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded  
Young people experiencing vulnerability linked to violence, exploitation or disadvantage 
Young people with caring responsibilities  
Young people in the care system 
Young people affected by Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) 
The wider youth population through universal provision 
Potential delivery settings and workforces may include, but are not limited to: 
Community-based youth organisations and youth services 
Detached, outreach and neighbourhood-based provision 
Faith and community organisations 
SEND and disability-focused youth provision 
Organisations supporting young people experiencing vulnerability, exclusion or barriers to traditional youth provision 
Specialist services working with young people affected by violence, exploitation or online harms 
Informal education, mentoring and participation-based youth provision 
Indicative Outcomes 
The programme is expected to contribute to: 
Increased engagement of young people in safe, supportive digital environments 
Improved accessibility of youth work for young people who do not traditionally engage with youth work and are digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded)  
Strengthened early identification and prevention of online harms in the digital space 
Increased use of technology to foster positive opportunities  
Strengthen young people’s digital citizenship  
Increased workforce confidence and capability in incorporating digital youth work into traditional practice and safeguarding policy 
Development of scalable models, guidance and practical tools 
A stronger London-wide evidence base on digital youth work and online safety  
Timeframe and Budget 
The maximum estimated budget for this programme is up to £650,000 excl. VAT over a full contract period from November 2026 – March 2029, subject to confirmation of funding, internal governance and relevant approvals.  
This comprises: 
£390,000 core funding across the 2026/27 and 2027/28 financial years from November 2026 to March 2028 
An extension option of up to £260,000 for a further 12 months from April 2028  
The VRU welcomes bids from individual organisations as well as collaborative partnerships and consortia. We recognise that expertise may be distributed across different organisations, and we encourage applications that bring together complementary skills, knowledge and experience. Providers do not need to demonstrate strength across every area independently, provided that the partnership as a whole can evidence the required expertise and capacity to deliver the programme.  
This may include, for example, combining specialist knowledge in DYW, supporting SEND or neurodiverse children, digital safety, contextual safeguarding, fostering positive digital opportunities, and preventative violence reduction approaches. 
Market Engagement / Response 
The VRU welcomes engagement from organisations with expertise in: 
Youth work and youth engagement 
Digital youth work  
Gaming, AI, technology  
Safeguarding and contextual safeguarding 
Online harms, exploitation and violence prevention 
Working with vulnerable and hard-to-reach young people 
Youth participation and co-production 
Learning, evaluation and evidence generation 
If you are interested in the opportunity and meet the core capabilities as set out above, then please join us for our early market warming event on Wednesday 5th August 2026 at 10:00AM.  
Attending the early market warming session does not constitute a commitment to participate in any future procurement process. 
The Eventbrite link for market warming session can be found here - https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/london-vru-online-harms-digital-youth-work-pilot-market-warming-session-tickets-1994744836503?aff=oddtdtcreator  
Please note that this exercise is in no way a call for competition and will not result in the award of a contract to any respondents to this notice.

vruprocurement@london.gov.uk

title: Bromley Sexual Health Market Engagement Event
description:
The London Borough of Bromley is seeking feedback from suppliers ahead of a planned procurement for future Sexual Health Services in Bromley to provide information on the proposed service model and procurement approach.
A supplier market engagement Event has been scheduled for Tuesday 13th October 2026 between 13:00 and 14:30. The event will be delivered online via Microsoft Teams.
The proposal is for the future service to be delivered through two separate contracts, representing a change from the current integrated model:
• Lot 1: Clinical Sexual Health Service – specialist consultant-led STI, HIV
and contraception services, assessment, diagnosis and treatment.
• Lot 2: Outreach, Prevention and Community Engagement Service –
prevention, outreach, health promotion, early intervention and targeted
support to reduce inequalities and improve access.
The redesigned model aims to strengthen prevention and community-based support while ensuring specialist clinical services focus on residents requiring higher-threshold care. The procurement timetable is currently indicative, with publication of the tender anticipated in March 2027. Providers interested in shaping the future service are encouraged to attend the market engagement event.
The event will provide an opportunity to:
• Receive an update on the Council’s commissioning intentions for the
Bromley Sexual Health Service.
• Learn more about the proposed service delivery model and expectations
for future delivery of the Service.
• Explore supplier interest in the proposed procurement
• Understand the anticipated procurement process, timelines and next
steps.
Organisations wishing to attend should complete the Registration Form attached to the opportunity on the London Tenders Portal (ProContract) reference ID; DN829449, and return the completed form via the message function on the London Tenders Portal no later than 12:00 noon on Thursday 8th October 2026.
Microsoft Teams joining instructions will be issued to registered attendees in advance of the session.

title: Germany – Electrical services – Prüfung von ortsfesten elektrischen Anlagen und ortsveränderlichen elektrischen Betriebsmitteln
description: Bei den im Rahmen dieses Vergabeverfahrens angefragten Leistungen handelt es sich um die wiederkehrende Prüfung der elektrotechnischen Anlagen und um die Prüfung von ortsveränderlichen elektrischen Betriebsmitteln an den Standorten Köln, Bonn und Aachen des Westdeutschen Rundfunks. Es kommen hierbei die jeweils aktuell gültigen Vorschriften und Regeln zur Anwendung. Die Ausschreibung ist in zwei Lose unterteilt. Los 1 umfasst die wiederkehrende Prüfung der ortsfesten elektrotechnischen Anlagen an den vorgenannten Standorten. Ziel der Prüfung ist es, die Wirksamkeit und Betriebssicherheit der Anlagen festzustellen. Alle Prüfungen erfolgen entsprechend den DIN VDE Bestimmungen, maßgeblich der DIN VDE 0105. Los 2 umfasst die Prüfung von ortsveränderlichen elektrischen Betriebsmitteln. Der Auftragnehmer führt die vollständige Überprüfung von ortsveränderlichen elektrischen Betriebsmitteln nach DIN VDE 0701 / 0702 durch. Weiterhin empfiehlt der Auftragnehmer dem Betreiber anhand einer Gefährdungsbeurteilung pro Gerät eine Prüffrist gemäß Betriebssicherheitsverordnung (BetrSichV) und TRBS 1111. Der Vertragsbeginn ist jeweils für den 01.09.2026 mit einer Grundlaufzeit von zwei Jahren vorgesehen mit je einer Verlängerungsoption um weitere zwei Jahre. Die maximale Gesamtlaufzeit beträgt vier Jahre. Die im Rahmen dieses Vergabeverfahrens angefragten Leistungen sind in den beigefügten Leistungsbeschreibungen einschließlich der dazugehörigen Anlagen umfassend beschrieben. Die Höchstabnahmemenge in dieser Rahmenvereinbarung liegt im Los 1 bei ca. 6.048 Stunden. Die Mindestabnahmemenge liegt bei ca. 3.024 Stunden. Im Los 2 liegt die Höchstabnahmemenge bei ca. 264.400 einphasigen (230 V) und ca. 1.640 dreiphasigen Betriebsmittel (450V). Die Mindestabnahmemenge liegt bei ca. 132.200 einphasigen und ca. 820 dreiphasigen Betriebsmitteln.

title: Belgium – Research and experimental development services – EU Complementary Time (C-T) and Complementary Position and Navigation (C-PN) services
description: Satellite-based navigation and timing services are a cornerstone of Europe’s economy and critical infrastructure resilience. Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) functions, delivered principally by Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) such as the EU owned Galileo, underpin sectors ranging from transport and finance to energy and telecommunications. Several studies attribute roughly 10 % of EU GDP to PNT related activities, while a single day without GNSS could have a financial impact up to €1 billion. The Commission proposal for the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), includes for the 2028‑2034 Multi‑annual Financial Framework, a contribution to complementary PNT services, which shall increase the resilience in case of disruptions to the services provided by the PNT component (Article 59). The project shall assess how best can the Commission contribute to complementary PNT services in the next MFF. Leveraging existing national and pan‑European infrastructure, the Commission would like to assess: • How to best strengthen with the resilience of PNT services to radio frequency interference (RFI) affecting GNSS services throughout the EU. • How to best contribute to the deployment of a mature, interoperable C T architecture that is ready for operational use within the multi financial framework 2028 2034. • How to best support candidates for a C-PN service, that utilise the C-T infrastructure and are resilient to RFI and to assess whether the technology is ready for deployment or, if not what is required.

Por su parte, el programa de medidas del Plan de gestión de riesgos de inundación (2º ciclo) de la Demarcación Hidrográfica del Segura tiene por objetivo que no se incremente el riesgo de inundación actualmente existente, y que, en lo posible, se reduzca mediante la prevención, protección y preparación; todo ello considerando los posibles efectos del cambio Climático. En relación con los objetivos de protección de las aguas y del dominio público hidráulico y de prevención, protección y preparación ante el riesgo de inundación; a través de las labores de mejora y recuperación de capacidad de cauces se pretende conseguir la mejora del régimen de corrientes y recuperación del espacio fluvial eliminando obstáculos, posibles tapones y acumulaciones excesivas de restos vegetales , además de llevar a cabo otras actuaciones puntuales de estabilización y reparación de márgenes que estén sufriendo procesos erosivos o con riesgo de sufrirlos. También se realizarán actuaciones correctivas tras posibles episodios de crecidas e inundaciones y actividades de restauración de vegetación de ribera que contribuyan a que se restablezcan los procesos naturales en el ecosistema fluvial facilitando su auto-recuperación y contribuyendo a alcanzar también el objetivo de mejorar el estado de las masas de agua, en coordinación con la Directiva Marco del Agua, puesto que está ampliamente demostrado que un río en buen estado es capaz de adaptarse y responder con mayor eficacia ante eventos extremos.

title: Germany – Government services – Projektträgerschaft zur fachlichen und administrativen Umsetzung der Förderrichtlinie „Etablierung einer industriellen Bioökonomie durch die Weiterentwicklung und Skalierung biobasierter Verfahren sowie den Aufbau regionaler Innovationscluster“
description: Die industrielle Bioökonomie bietet enormes Potenzial für nachhaltiges Wachstum, indem sie fossile Rohstoffe durch erneuerbare biologische Ressourcen ersetzt, Klimaziele erreicht und die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit stärkt. In der Forschung und Entwicklung bioökonomischer Produkte und Verfahren ist Deutschland gut aufgestellt. Die bisherigen Fördermaßnahmen anderer Ressorts sowie der Bundesländer zeigen, dass bioökonomische Produkte und Verfahren im Labormaßstab umsetzbar sind. Es mangelt jedoch an der breiten Umsetzung bioökonomischer Produkte und Verfahren im industriellen Maßstab. Daher wurde zur Unterstützung der Transformation der Wirtschaft zu einer nachhaltigen, klimaneutralen Wirtschaftsform das Förderprogramm „Industrielle Bioökonomie“ initiiert, das mit Inkrafttreten der „Richtlinie zur Förderung der Nutzung und des Baus von Demonstrationsanlagen für die industrielle Bioökonomie“ vom 16. Dezember 2020 am 29. Dezember 2020 (BAnz AT 28.12.2020 B2) startete. Diese Förderrichtlinie wurde durch die am 27. September 2024 im Bundesgesetzblatt veröffentliche „Förderrichtlinie zur Etablierung einer industriellen Bioökonomie durch die Weiterentwicklung und Skalierung biobasierter Verfahren sowie den Aufbau regionaler Innovationscluster" (BAnz AT 27.09.2024 B1) abgelöst. Ziel des Programms ist es, das Potenzial neuer biobasierter Verfahren für die Industrie zu erschließen und nachhaltige Produkte in die breite Anwendung zu transferieren. Um die wirtschaftlichen und technischen Risiken der Entwicklung und Markteinführung zu verringern, soll durch die Förderung frühzeitig das Potenzial biobasierter Produkte und Verfahren demonstriert werden. Gefördert werden Projekte, die ein hohes Potenzial für die industrielle Anwendung, die Schaffung neuer Wertschöpfung und von neuen Arbeitsplätzen besitzen, die Marktposition der beteiligten Unternehmen stärken und einen relevanten Beitrag zur Nachhaltigkeit leisten.

title: Germany – Engineering services – 26-027 Objektplanung – Sanierung des SWR-Funkhauses Stuttgart, Bauteil A, Ebene 2 bis 5, 2. Bauabschnitt
description: Das Funkhaus Stuttgart des SWR wurde in den Jahren 1973 bis 1976 errichtet und steht seit dem Jahr 2000 unter Denkmalschutz. Aufgrund des altersbedingten Zustands der Bausubstanz und der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung sowie veränderter Anforderungen an moderne Arbeitswelten wird das Gebäudeensemble in mehreren Bauabschnitten saniert und modernisiert. Im Fokus stehen die Erneuerung der baulichen und technischen Infrastruktur, die Umsetzung aktueller Brandschutz-, Sicherheits- und Hygienestandards sowie die Anpassung der Flächen an moderne Büro- und Nutzungskonzepte mit Desksharing und hybriden Arbeitsformen. Gegenstand des 2. Bauabschnitts ist die Sanierung von Teilbereichen der Ebenen 02 bis 05 in den Bauteilen A und B mit einer Bruttogrundfläche von rund 6.000 m². Die Maßnahme umfasst insbesondere die Neustrukturierung und Modernisierung von Büroflächen, Archiv- und Lagerbereichen sowie die Umnutzung bestehender Flächen. Darüber hinaus werden umfangreiche Sanierungsmaßnahmen an den technischen Anlagen der Gewerke Sanitär, Heizung, Kälte, Lüftung, Gebäudeautomation sowie Elektrotechnik durchgeführt. Ergänzend sind Schadstoffsanierungen, brandschutztechnische Ertüchtigungen und Maßnahmen zur Verbesserung der Aufenthaltsqualität und Barrierefreiheit vorgesehen. Die Umsetzung erfolgt bei laufendem Betrieb des Funkhauses und unter Berücksichtigung der Anforderungen des Denkmalschutzes. Für die Vergabe der Technische Ausrüstung Planungleistungen nach § 55 HOAI (ELT) wird ein Verhandlungsverfahren nach § 17 Abs. 1 VgV durchgeführt. Das Verfahren befindet sich derzeit in der ersten Stufe, dem Teilnahmewettbewerb. Auf Grundlage der in der Bekanntmachung festgelegten Eignungs- und Auswahlkriterien werden die Bewerber ausgewählt, die anschließend zur Angebotsabgabe und zur Präsentation ihrer Konzepte aufgefordert werden.

description: Auch für 2026 plant die WTD 71 Unterwassersprengungen in der Ostsee. Voraussetzungen für diese Sprengungen ist eine Ausnahmegenehmigung der zuständigen Umweltbehörden. Zur Erlangung der Genehmigung sind die Auswirkungen von UW-Sprengungen auf die Meeresumwelt, sowie Schutz- und Minderungsmaßnahmen darzulegen. Es hat sich gezeigt, dass die Datenlage zu diesen speziellen Fragestellungen nicht ausreichend ist. Nach ausführlichen Diskussionen mit den zuständigen Umweltschutzbehörden hat man sich geeinigt, die für die WTD 71 dringend erforderlichen UW-Sprengungen mit großen Ladungsmassen weiterzuführen und diese Sprengungen umfangreich messtechnisch zu begleiten, um so die Auswirkungen der Sprengungen auf die Meeresumwelt bzw. die Wirksamkeit der Minderungsmaßnahmen (Blasenschleier) besser beurteilen zu können. In 2026 ist die vierte Ansprengung einer Ansprengserie von max. 6 Sprengungen der ExKarlsruhe durchzuführen, die zur Gewinnung dieser Daten genutzt wird.

title: Germany – Electrical wiring and fitting work – Videokontrollsystem
description: Die Stromnetz Berlin GmbH beabsichtigt den strukturierten Rollout eines Videokontrollsystems (VKS) über ihre technischen Standorte, Betriebs- und Verwaltungsstandorte sowie definierte Sonderstandorte. Ziel der Ausschreibung ist die Erweiterung und rollierende Umsetzung eines vorhandenen Videomanagementsystems (BVMS) der Firma Bosch Sicherheitssysteme GmbH mit dem Leistungsgegenstand Planung, Ausführung, Inbetriebnahme, Dokumentation sowie nachgelagerter Service- und Wartungsleistungen. Der Rollout dient der Stärkung der physischen Sicherheit von Anlagen und Liegenschaften der kritischen Infrastruktur. Das VKS soll nicht lediglich der passiven Beobachtung dienen, sondern als aktiver Bestandteil der Sicherheitsarchitektur Ereignisse detektieren, visualisieren, eine schnelle Lageeinschätzung unterstützen und Folgeprozesse ermöglichen. Die bestehende Systemlandschaft umfasst ein zentrales Videomanagementsystem, dezentrale Videospeicher, Kameratechnik in den Liegenschaften, Clients für berechtigte Nutzer sowie Monitoring- und Netzwerkkomponenten des Auftraggebers. Der Vergabegegenstand ist in 4 Lose untergliedert. Die Losstruktur trennt die Planung und Steuerung, die technische Ausführung, Tiefbauleistungen sowie den Servicebetrieb, stellt jedoch zugleich einen verbindlichen Gesamtkontext her. Die Leistungen sind so aufeinander abzustimmen, dass Planung, Tiefbau, Montage, Inbetriebnahme, Dokumentation und Betrieb innerhalb eines einheitlichen Rollout-Modells ineinandergreifen. Alle Auftragnehmer haben die projektbezogenen Schnittstellen, die Vorgaben des Auftraggebers, die einschlägigen technischen Regelwerke sowie die Anforderungen an Informationssicherheit, Arbeitsschutz und Dokumentation zu berücksichtigen. Der Rollout umfasst alle technischen Standorte (Umspannwerke, Netzknoten) sowie alle Betriebs- und Verwaltungsstandorte der Stromnetz Berlin. Die Anzahl der zu berücksichtigenden Standorte umfasst ca. 110 (Schätzwert) bis max. 130 Liegenschaften (Höchstwert). Unabhängig davon, ob der Zuschlag auf einzelne Lose oder ein Kombinationslosvariante erteilt wird, müssen die angebotenen Leistungen eine konsistente, sichere, interoperable und vollständig dokumentierte Gesamtlösung gewährleisten. Maßgeblich ist die vollständige Erfüllung sämtlicher in den Vergabeunterlagen festgelegten Anforderungen. Die Verträge (Los 1 bis Los 4) werden mit Zuschlagserteilung wirksam und haben hinsichtlich der Leistungserbringung eine Grundlaufzeit vom 01.08.2027 – 31.07.2033 (6 Jahre). Der Auftraggeber ist berechtigt, die Verträge um zwei Jahre, d.h. bis maximal 31.07.2035 zu verlängern.

title: Norway – Research and development services and related consultancy services – New Procurement - Strategic Foresight in regard to the exam scheme and stance assessment.
description: In 2025, the Norwegian Directorate of Education and Training (Udir) received a comprehensive assignment from the Ministry of Education and Research (KD) to examine a safer and improved exam scheme in sixth form education. The aim of the KD assignment is to develop a sustainable exam scheme that tolerates change, which reduces risk and reduces costs. In addition the desired effect for the target groups is that the assignment from KD shall ensure a good connection with curricula in the subject(s) and that the quality principles in the framework for exams are adhered to. The background for the assignment from KD is, among other things, that the exam scheme in the last 5-6 years has been marked by a number of concurrent changes and events that affect the complexity and risk of the exam, including: Implementation of new curricula, as well as the need to further develop the content and format of exam development and the introduction of a new digital systemPandemienInduction of KI in societySelv if the exam is the assignment from KD's main focus. Must also be seen in the context of the stance assessment: The exam character and the stance character have the same purpose, i.e. an expression of the pupil's competence at the end of the training in the subject. The connection between these two schemes is significant for the future final evaluation scheme in disciplines, including the role of the exam. This is detailed in 5.1.The review of the assignment from KD lasts for several years and will assess all aspects of what is currently a very complex system, but also how the exams should be in the future. The Norwegian Directorate for Education and Training has therefore appointed an internal work group that shall work on a strategic forward process in relation to the assignment from KD.  Strategic foresight is about combining analyses of long term trends and possible futures with inter-disciplinary cooperation and anchoring. The foresight methodology can function as an important tool for navigating uncertainties and identifying possibilities. Udir will use the methodology in relation to the assignment in this procurement, given the complex character of the exam system, as well as uncertainties connected to the future of the exams. The tenderer shall assist Udir's internal work group in identifying driving forces for the final assessment as well as developing future scenarios by utilising the foresight methodology. See further description in point 1-3 under point 5.2 below. The mapping of driving forces shall occur in cooperation with different groups of interested parties. The interested parties, for example, include the different interest organisations connected to the education field, as well as other interested parties such as counties, the Government Manager, professional environments, suppliers of technical systems etc. The forwarding work is limited to apply to a study preparatory education programme and joint subjects in sixth form education. The assignment shall be implemented by 1 September 2027. The cost limit for the main assignment is NOK 1.2 million excluding VAT. In addition the contracting authority would like to enter into an option for an extension and extension of the assignment for 1 year, see point 5.4. The option is for exams in vocational subjects. See points 4 and 5 in the tender documentation for a complete description of the delivery. The Norwegian Directorate of Education and Training reserves the right to make political decisions that can lead to changes in the scope of the assignment.

title: Digital Exposure Analysis
description:
The Analysis is intended to identify all accessible digital data that may pose a security risk to the Chair and Panel members. The supplier will be required to identify all available digital information that may lead to whole or partial identification of the subject’s personal address(es); their family members identities, likeness, personal or work address(es) or contact information; locations they frequent; personal or individual contact information; medical history; internet and social media history; financial or business information other than that declared publicly in the course of their duties; or any other data that may give rise to security risk. 
The supplier will be required to develop a mitigation plan, detailing steps to be taken to remove the data or otherwise digitally mitigate the risk it creates. This and the analysis will be contained together in a single report per subject to be produced by the supplier. 
The supplier may be required to complete some or all of the mitigating actions proposed in the report. The Inquiry timeline requires that public evidential hearings begin in December 2026. It is imperative that mitigating actions have been successfully concluded by the commencement of hearings to enable the Chair and Panel to proceed with their work confident in their personal security.

description:

The current Civils and Infrastructure Framework is set to expire May 2026, the current Demolition Framework is set to expire upon execution of this procurement. It is proposed that this new Framework will be for a four year term from September 2026.
The Framework intends to appoint a number of Contractors to provide a full range of Civil Engineering and Infrastructure works, Demolition works and Land Preparation works.
The resulting Framework will be UK wide and will be available to all Public Sector Bodies.
It is anticipated that, while the Framework Agreement is governed by the English Law, the Contracting Authority may, during the first 2-weeks of the tendering period introduce Scottish Law to form a part of the Framework Agreement Terms and Conditions. title: DLR TEx - Cadent Gas Feasibility and Options Study
description:
Contract for the provision of a C3 stage feasibility design and options study for potential gas diversion works required to enable the proposed DLR Thamesmead Extension.
The current alignment of the Thamesmead Extension (TEx) route intersects a highly strategic and asset-dense section of Statutory Undertaker Cadent's London Network, comprising high, intermediate and medium-pressure gas mains, alongside key installations including the Beckton Above Ground Installation and associated pressure reduction infrastructure. These assets present one of the most significant technical and programme-critical risks to the TEx programme.
This request relates solely to the Feasibility Design and Options Study (C3 Works), This phase will provide a comprehensive desktop -based assessment of all potential diversion and AGI rationalisation requirements aligned to the current TEx design. The scope includes options development, engagement of a Cadent-approved design house, initial material take-off assessments, high level cost estimates for later phases, and mobilisation of a dedicated multi-disciplinary project management team to coordinate technical interfaces and third party stakeholders.
The value for this contract is £1,594,000

title: Housing, Health & Wellbeing Hospital Discharge Support Service
description:
The service is to prevent individuals aged 18 and over from being discharged from hospital into street homelessness, and to support safe, timely, and sustainable discharges through coordinated in-hospital intervention and time-limited post-discharge support.
The service will provide proactive, responsive, and coordinated support through:
•Early identification of individuals who are homeless or at risk of homelessness; 
•In-hospital assessment, advocacy, and discharge coordination; &
•Time-limited post-discharge support to sustain accommodation and reduce the risk of readmission. 
The service will specifically support individuals who:
•Are homeless or at risk of homelessness; 
•Have support needs relating to drug and alcohol use; and 
•Are known to Adult Social Care services, including those with assessed care and support
needs, those open to Adult Social Care teams, and those requiring coordinated discharge
planning.
The service is commissioned in recognition of the significant risks associated with hospital discharge into homelessness, and the adverse impact this has on individual health and wellbeing, as well as system pressures across health, housing, and social care. The
Council is committed to ensuring that no individual aged 18 and over is discharged from hospital into street homelessness, and that all discharges are safe, timely, and supported
by appropriate accommodation and care pathways.
The service will operate within the framework of statutory duties under the Care Act 2014, including the duty to promote individual wellbeing, prevent, reduce, and delay the need for care and support, and ensure the integration of services where this contributes to improved outcomes. The service will also support the Council in meeting its responsibilities under the Homelessness Reduction Act 2017, including duties to prevent
and relieve homelessness and to work collaboratively with partner agencies through the Duty to Refer process.
The service will deliver an integrated model of support spanning in-hospital intervention and time-limited post-discharge assistance, ensuring continuity of care for individuals with
complex and multiple needs. It will form a key part of a wider system approach to discharge planning, working in close partnership with Adult Social Care, housing services,
health providers, and other relevant stakeholders to facilitate coordinated and person centred outcomes.
A core feature of this integrated approach is the requirement for the provider to work proactively and collaboratively with Transfer of Care Hubs, clinical teams, and wider hospital-based staff to identify individuals who are homeless or at risk of homelessness at
the earliest possible stage of admission. The service will accept and respond to referrals from Transfer of Care Hubs, hospital wards, Emergency Departments, and clinical teams,
ensuring timely engagement and intervention to support discharge planning processes.

title: Cheshire and Warrington Outline Water Plan
description:
The newly established Cheshire and Warrington Combined Authority (CWCA) has recently stated its intention to commission an Independent Economic Review (IER) for the subregion - setting out the evidence for the opportunities for and constraints on local growth. In support of this, it is vital to better understand where water infrastructure may require upgrades to support local ambition, and how we can better work together to ensure that flooding and drought are not impediments to growth whilst ensuring that wider ecosystem services and farming resilience are better supported.
Simultaneously, the Water White Paper published in January 2026 committed Government to act on the Independent Water Commission recommendation, setting up Regional Systems Planning in England. DEFRA have set out an intention to pilot this through Regional System Planners (RSPs), established across each region of England with the aim of influencing both PR29 and other water system investment plans. Defra are keen for partnerships to pilot RSP governance and structures during this set-up year. and have set out that they only intend to provide high level direction on form. Within this context there is a significant opportunity to influence water planning, and ensure alignment with local growth and wider environmental ambitions.
To support the IER along with engagement with the establishing North West RSP, ECW is seeking to appoint consultants to develop a strategic, place based evidence base and outline water plan that sits between national/regional water planning processes and local spatial, economic, and infrastructure planning.

title: Constructing West Midlands 3 - Construction Framework
description:
CWM3 is a publicly owned and managed framework, intended to deliver general construction and building services work. The main areas of activity will comprise of individual construction projects or programmes, including new build, extensions, remodelling, retrofit, refurbishment, renovation and repair work, mechanical and electrical services, demolition and enabling works, fit-out and interiors, civils, landscaping, specialist installations  and infrastructure works, and may also include design and other services as required to develop and construct the works.
Contractor Partners selected to join the framework are expected to demonstrate a strong collaborative working ethos - engaging openly and closely with the CWM Framework Management Team, client organisations, consultants, and other Contractor partners - and to provide clear support throughout the pre construction period. Their performance will be monitored against a comprehensive set of performance indicators.
The framework will consist of 3 Lots as follows:
Lot 1: Minor Works (works generally £250,000 to £5,000,000) with 8 Contractor Partners.
Lot 2: Medium Works (works generally £2,000,000 to £15,000,000) with 6 Contractor
Partners.
Lot 3: Major Works (works generally over £10,000,000) with 6 Contractor Partners.
The Framework sets out a number of Permitted Forms of Call-Off Contract which are available for authorities to use. Full details are set out in Schedule 2 to the Framework, but these allow the flexibility for authorities to use the CWM Model Form of Call-Off Contracts or utilise any of the NEC or JCT forms with or without their own amendments. In addition, there is scope to use alternative contract forms including, without limitation, alliancing forms of contract.
Please note that an award of a Call-Off is for the entirety of the Project covered by an authority within its Call-Off process as detailed within the Operations Manual. Authorities may enter into contracts following the expiry of the Framework if such contract is captured within the scope of a Call-Off Process awarded and entered into prior to the expiry of the Framework (e.g. PCSA is entered into with the ability to issue a notice to proceed to a Works Contract).
CWM is committed to complying with all mandatory requirements set out in the National Association of Construction Frameworks (NACF) Regional Framework Accreditation Attributes, ensuring its continued membership of the NACF.
In addition, CWM will strive to fulfil the NACF's core objectives by:
• sharing best practice with fellow members, framework users and the wider public sector;
• providing guidance and support to public sector organisations where requested;
• promoting social value through procurement and construction framework activity;
• strengthening links between local and central government on construction related matters.
Following publication of this notice, Acivico DCFM Ltd. will observe the mandatory standstill period, which will end at midnight on 25 September 2026, and Acivico will not enter into the Framework Agreement before 28 September 2026.

As part of our commitment to reducing carbon emissions, improving air quality, and preparing for the transition to a predominantly zero-emission fleet as part of the zero-emission vehicle mandate from government, we are seeking to better understand the solutions, technologies, delivery models and innovations currently available within the market.
Fleet electrification is expected to involve a programme of works including, but not limited to, electrical capacity assessments, network upgrades, EV charging infrastructure, energy management systems, load balancing solutions, renewable energy integration, battery storage opportunities, software platforms, and ongoing operation and maintenance considerations. Given the scale and complexity of the transition, Nottinghamshire Police are undertaking this engagement to ensure our future procurement approach is informed by current market capability, best practice, emerging technologies, and lessons learned from similar projects.
