STEP is the UK's flagship fusion energy programme, sponsored by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), and aims to design and construct the UK's first prototype fusion power plant capable of demonstrating net energy production, fuel self-sufficiency and a viable route to plant maintenance. UKFE, a wholly owned subsidiary of the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA), is responsible for delivering the programme.
A key challenge for future fusion power plants is the management of tritium, which serves as a fuel for the deuterium-tritium fusion reaction. Tritium is both radioactive and scarce, making accurate measurement of its retention within plasma-facing components essential to demonstrating fuel self-sufficiency, supporting tritium accountancy, and monitoring the condition of first wall materials throughout plant operation.
The successful supplier will develop a concept design for a measurement system capable of operating within the demanding environment of a fusion power plant, taking into account constraints such as neutron radiation, strong magnetic fields, thermal loading, limited installation space, and exposure to radioactive materials.
This procurement represents the initial concept design phase of a wider programme of work. Subject to future funding and programme approvals, the outputs of this contract are expected to inform subsequent detailed design activities, technology maturation, de-risking and testing, and ultimately the development of an integrated tritium measurement system for deployment within the STEP tokamak.

title: QQ26043 - Interchange Land Assembly - Land Acquisition and Agency Services
description:
The Council seeks specialist consultancy support in relation to the potential acquisition, assembly and control of strategic landholdings immediately adjacent to the Wolverhampton Interchange. The purpose of this commission is to support the City of Wolverhampton Council (CWC) in assessing and securing positions in respect of six key land parcels under the ownership and control of three principal landowners.
The appointed consultant will provide targeted early-stage feasibility, development and land assembly advice to support the delivery of the Interchange Quarter regeneration programme. The commission will focus on identifying opportunities, assessing constraints and de-risking future development proposals, with the overarching objective of residential and mix use.
Key Requirements
The consultant will be required to undertake, but not be limited to, the following activities:
1.Preparation of early-stage options appraisals and valuation assessments to inform the Council's land assembly and acquisition strategy.
2.Baseline site analysis, including review of planning, ownership, title, utilities, access, physical constraints and heritage considerations.
3.Initial development capacity testing and high-level master planning to assess development potential across the identified sites.
4.Early-stage design optioneering, including massing studies and density testing to determine viable development scenarios.
5.Targeted heritage, environmental and development risk assessments to support feasibility analysis and inform decision-making.
Required Outputs
The commission is expected to deliver the following outputs:
•Site-specific options appraisals, including indicative land valuations and acquisition considerations.
•An initial masterplan framework setting out potential development scenarios and land-use options.
•High-level housing capacity assessments and density assumptions for each site.
•Identification and assessment of key development risks, constraints and delivery challenges.
•A robust evidence base to inform future business cases, investment decisions, funding applications and regeneration delivery planning.
Objectives
The primary objective of this commission is to provide the Council with the evidence, analysis and strategic advice necessary to support land acquisition and assembly decisions, reduce development risk and establish a clear pathway for the delivery of the Interchange Quarter regeneration programme.

title: Physical and Personnel Security Assessment for UK Telecoms
description:
The UK’s public telecommunications networks are a critical national infrastructure (CNI) subsector, underpinning the functioning of every other CNI sector, the digital economy, and essential public services, for which the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) is the lead government department. Their continued availability, integrity and confidentiality are fundamental to national security, economic resilience, and the everyday lives of UK citizens and businesses.
Telecoms operators manage complex, large-scale, geographically distributed systems,  including exchanges, data centres, transmission sites and access network assets , which are increasingly attractive targets for hostile state and state-aligned actors seeking to disrupt, degrade or exploit UK infrastructure. Physical compromise and insider threat are significant attack vectors that hostile actors could seek to exploit. Strengthening physical and personnel security across the sector is therefore a priority area of work for DCMS.
DSIT is exploring options for obtaining specialist support to undertake a physical and personnel security assessment of UK public telecommunications networks and services. We are seeking engagement from accredited security consultancy firms to conduct a sector-level physical and personnel security assessment of UK public telecoms networks and services. This should include assessment of current vulnerabilities and potential threat vectors, and set out a prioritised list of recommended mitigations for operators to reduce the risk of security compromise stemming from physical and personnel security vulnerabilities. This list of prioritised mitigations should identify how existing NPSA guidance can be applied to address telecoms sector vulnerabilities.
An estimated project commencement date is October 2026 , to conclude in February 2027, subject to a tender launch and agreed contract.
Some of the core deliverables are listed below:
 A detailed report setting out:
(i) current physical and personnel security vulnerabilities within the UK’s public telecoms networks and services,
(ii) physical and personnel security threat vectors (i.e. how threat actors could exploit these vulnerabilities, not a threat assessment), and
(iii) a prioritised list of mitigations for operators to take to reduce the identified physical and personnel security risks - this should include identification of how existing NPSA guidance can applied to address telecoms sector vulnerabilities.

title: Engineering Vehicles - Strip and Spray and Bogie Overhaul for General Purpose (GP)
description:
London Underground Limited (LUL), is a wholly owned subsidiary of Transport for London (TfL), the statutory corporation responsible for the transport network in London. 
London Underground Limited (LUL) engineering and maintenance is managed by Transport for London (TfL), the public body running the Tube, with the LUL Asset Performance Directorate overseeing the actual upkeep, renewal, and modernisation of its vast, historic infrastructure (tracks, signals, stations) using in-house teams and external specialist contractors. Railway carriages, wagons and engineering vehicles ('EV') are the principal part of London Underground ('LU') services assets. These assets require periodic maintenance and overhaul. This tender notice is being posted in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 to invite bidders to express interest to participate in the following tender activity.  
London Underground Engineering Vehicles fleet requires strip and spray and bogie overhaul of 10 General Purpose (GP) Engineering Wagons to achieve a life extension of 8 years. The scope of works is to achieve a strip and spray and overhaul that meets the requirements of the TfL strip and spray and overhaul specification.
These wagons are vital for the upkeep and maintenance of the LU track infrastructure and are a key asset for the Battery Locomotive Programme.
Bidders wishing to take part in the process and submit a tender response should contact LynetteGatsi@tfl.gov.uk and ensure they are registered on the SAP Ariba e-tendering platform. 
Registration is required to receive an invitation to the procurement event and access to the ITT (Invitation to Tender) documentation. 
Bidders are required to Express Interest to participate by 23/09/2026 at 12PM GMT.
Scope
Strip, surface preparation, repair, painting and bogie overhaul of 10 engineering wagons at the Supplier's premises, returned to Transport for London for reassembly. The wagons comprise General Purpose (GP), Concrete Mixer and Match (CM and MW) and Jubilee Line Extension (JLE) types. The final quantity by type will be confirmed at contract award.
The work covers:
•	Body strip, blasting, surface preparation and painting to the specified paint system.
•	Welding and body repair to BS EN ISO 15085-2 and the associated welding standards.
•	Overhaul and repair of bogies.
•	Repair of corrosion, damage and distortion found on inspection.
•	Collection and return of wagon bodies and bogies to the nominated Transport for London site.
Overhaul materials are free issue. The Supplier provides all consumables, paint system, blast media, PPE, plant and tooling. The tender price is for labour and services only.
Delivery is at one wagon every three weeks, all 10no within the contract term, with no mobilisation period. Collection and return will be from Acton Works, 130 Bollo Lane, London W3 8BZ, or Ruislip Depot, West End Road, HA4 6NS, confirmed at contract award.
Suppliers must evidence prior delivery of both rail vehicle body strip and repaint and bogie overhaul, supported by two reference contracts.

title: CEFAS26-85 Contract for provision of Water and Sediment Sampling Analysis for HPC
description:

Through this programme, Cefas provide authoritative scientific information on the marine and transitional waters in the vicinity of potential new build nuclear power stations and require the Supplier to deliver the marine sampling, profiling, and laboratory analysis services described in Section 3 below.
Scope of Requirements
Cefas require the supplier to acquire sediment and water samples along with water column profiles of conductivity, temperature and depth (CTD) and other variables from a suitable vessel for the purpose of physical and chemical monitoring of the marine offshore environment adjacent to the Hinkley Point C new nuclear build power station.
It is anticipated that the required sampling will involve circa 3 days of vessel operations – two days for water sampling and one day for sediment sampling. The requirement includes collection of all samples and field measurements and all laboratory sample analysis, excluding hydrazine analysis which is to be conducted by Cefas laboratory.

title: Expert Networks Long Term Provision
description:
The Authority is seeking to procure Expert Network Services to provide on‑demand access to vetted and pre‑qualified subject‑matter experts across a broad range of industry sectors, to support informed decision‑making in relation to investment activity and wider financial, strategic, and operational matters.
The Services will primarily support the Authority’s Investment & Advisory function, comprising its Banking & Investment team and its Local Authority Advisory & Lending team. The Services may also be utilised by other functional teams across the Authority, including Portfolio Management, Risk, and Impact teams.
The Supplier will be required to provide access to a diverse network of subject‑matter experts, including (without limitation) founders, senior executives, high‑level officials, and academics. The Services will enable the Authority to engage directly with selected experts to obtain targeted insights on companies, assets, sectors, technologies, markets, and wider industry developments.
The Supplier shall facilitate project‑specific requests and provide shortlists of relevant experts aligned to defined project profiles. The Authority will select experts for direct one‑to‑one meetings, typically of up to 60 minutes’ duration, delivered via online meetings or, where appropriate and agreed, in‑person meetings. The Authority must have the option to withhold or anonymise its identity when engaging with experts.
Where meetings are conducted online, the Authority requires the option to record consultations and to generate audio recordings and written transcripts, using artificial intelligence and/or human transcription services. The Authority must be able to access, download, and retain such recordings and transcripts for internal use.
The Supplier must provide an intuitive and secure online platform to support delivery of the Services, enabling expert search, project request management, meeting facilitation, and access to recordings and transcripts.
Where suitable expertise is not available within the Supplier’s existing network, the Supplier must be capable of sourcing, vetting, onboarding, and contracting additional experts, including those nominated by the Authority, to equivalent standards of credibility, compliance, and relevance.
The Services are expected to cover a wide range of industry sectors, including but not limited to advanced materials, aerospace supply chains, artificial intelligence, battery manufacturing and electric vehicle supply chains, carbon capture, critical minerals, defence, energy infrastructure, hydrogen, life sciences, nuclear, offshore wind, place‑based regeneration, ports, power networks, semiconductors, solar, sustainable aviation fuels, transport infrastructure, and water. This list is non‑exhaustive and may evolve during the contract term.
Further detail is included in the procurement documents pack made available by NWF in respect of the tender notice.
It should be noted that the value of these contracts represents their maximum value, as opposed to committed spend.

title: From Local Shocks to Systemic Impacts: A Multi-hazard, Systems-based View of Physical Climate Risk
description:
Please provide a detailed description of the notice you are adding: 
The final date and time for the submission of bids is Wednesday, 14th October 2026 at 11:00 
DO NOT apply directly to the buyer. 
All tender information MUST be submitted through the Jaggaer eSourcing Portal. 
Brief Description of Requirement
It is broadly recognised that physical climate risk and related nature dependencies can pose risks to economic and financial stability. Governments and regulators in the UK and internationally have recognised this and continue to take action to address underlying vulnerabilities and support wider systemic resilience. Notwithstanding the clear need for accelerated global action, there remains significant uncertainties in appraising the future economic and financial implications of physical risk meaning market practices, government policy and regulation, may not be optimised (within the bounds of wider limitations and mandates) to align with climate-resilient pathways. 
Climate scenario analysis is a key tool to inform approaches to climate risk management. But due to the complexity and heterogeneity of climate risk, academic and industry evidence has highlighted that current mainstream scenarios – whilst highly sophisticated – may not capture all potential physical risk due to limited data availability and modelling constraints. Furthermore, whilst reference scenarios continue to be enhanced, some potential hazard exposures and highly complex systems dynamics may not be well suited to quantification through empirically calibrated, top-down damage functions, which provide estimates for economic damages in climate scenarios.  
There is, therefore, a need to investigate the potential for complementary methodologies to support more holistic approaches to physical risk appraisal and management. This is the focus of this research project.  
Specifically, research will focus on how local physical climate shocks (e.g. storms, flooding, droughts, heat stress) can - through cascading, compounding, and contagion effects - become systemic risks. There will be a particular focus on furthering understanding of UK vulnerabilities to climate shocks in other countries, with the objective of supporting improvements to industry practices and providing insights for government policy, regulation, and prudential supervision. 
This research project will be delivered in coordination with the Financial Conduct Authority’s Climate Scenarios Sandbox , with potential for insights generated through the sandbox to provide practical evidence regarding the utility of research outputs. The project will also be delivered in partnership with the recently established UK Taskforce on Climate and Nature Security  and will, where possible, be aligned with ongoing work on high-impact climate possibilities at the Climate Financial Risk Forum.

title: Disrepair Works & Case Management Managed Service (DMS)
description: The London Borough of Lewisham is seeking a consultant-led provider, or a consortium led by a professional services consultant, to manage a Disrepair Works & Case Management, Managed Service (DMS). The Council has duties as a social landlord under the Defective Premises Act 1972, section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, the Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018, the Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS) and Awaab's Law. In June 2025 the Council had just over 1,000 open housing disrepair claims, with approx. 35 new claims per month. Total HRA disrepair-related spend in 2025/26 was circa £8.5m, including legal fees, tenant compensation and works. Following an options appraisal, Mayor & Cabinet approved the procurement of a DMS as the fastest route to clearing the backlog. The ‘enhanced in-house’ option was subsequently tested and has stabilised the position (open claims in the 800–850 range since April 2026), but a sizeable backlog remains. The Council is engaging the market to gauge supplier capacity, experience and innovation ahead of formal tendering for a DMS supplier.

title: SCE0040 - Occupational Therapy Trusted Assessor Learning and Development project
description:
Leicester City Council (the Council) undertook a procurement process to find a suitably qualified and experienced provider for the Occupational Therapy Trusted Assessor Learning and Development Service for residents of Leicester.
The procurement of this service has now concluded and the contract awarded. Services procured were as detailed in the tender documentation.
The proposed Contract will be for an initial period of 6 Months to commence on 24th August 2026 to 23rd February 2027 with no option to extend. 
The awarded Provider will develop and deliver face to face Trusted Assessor training to staff working across the Adult Social Care and Safeguarding Division. The training will support staff who are not part of the Occupational Therapy Service to identify when equipment or minor adaptations can help someone to live safely and well in their own home, without requiring specialist Occupational Therapist skills. The training will focus on understanding the built environment of people’s homes in Leicester in relation to adaptations and provision of equipment, including how to arrange a prescribed list of equipment and small modifications via a contractor. 
Through the Service, the Provider will deliver 11 full days of face-to-face training for approximately 150 to 155 staff, using local venues arranged by the Council. The provider will develop training resources, ensure trainers are appropriately qualified and understand local need, and ensure the training is culturally appropriate and reflects the diverse communities in Leicester. The proposed Contract will commence on 24th August 2026 and expire on 23rd February 2027. The contract period will be for six months. There is no option to extend. The estimated contract value is £35,000 plus VAT (£42,000). Further details in respect of this tender opportunity are contained within the Invitation to Tender documentation.

title: GL1 Leisure Centre Contract 2 and Stage 3 Design
description:
See attached contract for details.
Progressing Design from RIBA Stage 3 to RIBA Stage 4
1.1. Appoint and lead the Design Team
a) Employ Design Consultants: Engage key consultants such as architects, structural engineers, MEP
engineers, and other necessary specialists to complete the Technical Design, for manufacturing
and construction stage (RIBA 4).
b) Design Coordination: Lead design workshops and meetings to ensure integrated design solutions
across disciplines.
c) Design Management: Manage the design process, ensuring all parties adhere to the design brief,
project scope, and cost parameters.
d) Review and Sign-off: Regularly review design progress with the Project Manager and ensure all
design outputs meet project requirements before sign-off at the end of RIBA Stage 4.
1.2. Technical Design Development
a) Technical Design Development: Progress the design to RIBA Stage 4, including detailed
specifications, construction details, and schedules for all building elements.
b) Value Engineering: Collaborate with the design team and Employer to refine the design, ensuring it
aligns with budget constraints while meeting quality and performance standards.
c) Building Control: Ensure designs are co-ordinated and with Building Control requirements. Ensure
that the design complies with Building Regulations and engage with Building Control as needed to
obtain all necessary approvals.
1.3. Design Input
a) Providing advice on requirements for off-site design, temporary works and manufactured
components.
b) Providing advice on all aspects of "buildability" in relation to the proposed design and on the
feasibility of construction interfaces and tolerances and suggesting any construction changes
which could be used to reduce the incidence of conflicts or difficult interfaces between different
elements of a single package of work or between different packages of work.
c) Through the design development process, developing a "Contractor's Proposals" document that
satisfies the Employer's Requirements for agreement with the Employer to be included in the Main
Contract.
2. Supply Chain Engagement and Tendering
2.1 . Pre-tender Engagement with Supply Chain
a) Market Engagement: Identify and engage potential subcontractors and suppliers early in the
process to gather feedback on design feasibility, material availability, and buildability.
b) Package Scoping: Define and scope work packages for the supply chain based on the developed
RIBA Stage 4 design.
2.2 . Open Book Tender Process
a) Prepare Supply Chain Package Tender Documentation: Compile and issue tender documents,
including drawings, specifications and schedules of work.
b) Tender Management: Facilitate an open book tender process for supply chain packages, ensuring
transparency in pricing and compliance with the project's requirements.
c) Bid Evaluation: Evaluate tenders with the Project Manager, Cost Manager, design team and
Employer, conducting thorough assessments of cost, quality, and programme implications.
d) Negotiations and Recommendations: Lead negotiations with suppliers and subcontractors,
providing recommendations for appointment based on best value.

title: Integrated Partnerships Framework
description:
Northern Ireland Water (NI Water) intends to undertake a procurement for the establishment of the IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework (IF109). The future framework is being developed to support delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme and will succeed the existing IF105 Integrated Partnerships Framework, which is due to expire in May 2028. The framework is intended to support delivery of the PC28 investment programme and future regulatory periods whilst securing the capacity, capability, flexibility, value for money and resilience required to deliver NI Water's future capital programme.
The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework is expected to support a range of works and related services including programme and project management, design, engineering, construction, commissioning, and other supporting or ancillary activities necessary to support the successful delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme.
The framework is intended to support delivery of NI Water's future investment priorities, including regulatory compliance, service improvement, resilience enhancement, environmental performance and long-term sustainability objectives.
The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework is currently expected to comprise four lots covering Minor Civil Pipelaying Works, Minor Civil Works, Minor MEICA & Process Works, and Major Civil, MEICA & Process Works. Together, these Lots are intended to support the delivery of projects ranging from small-scale network investment and rehabilitation activities through to large-scale, complex, multidisciplinary capital programmes across NI Water's water and wastewater asset base.
NI Water is currently developing the procurement strategy, commercial model, lotting structure, appointment methodology, supplier allocation arrangements and delivery arrangements for the framework. Consequently, aspects of the future framework and procurement approach remain subject to further development and ongoing market engagement activities.
Indicative Programme and Key Activities:
NI Water will engage with the market throughout the development of the framework and prior to commencement of the procurement process. The current indicative programme is outlined below for information only and may be revised. NI Water may further refine its procurement programme over the coming months. 
•	Supplier Market Briefing Event - 7th October 2026
•	Publish UK 4 Tender Notice & Issue Participation Stage Package - 14th October 2026 
•	Notify pre-qualified suppliers - Q1 2027
•	Supplier Market Briefing Event - Q1 2027
•	Issue Invitation to Negotiate  - Q1 2027
•	Framework Award - Q4 2027
•	Publish the applicable award and contract notices in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023: Q4 2027

title: Gordon Gourt: Capital Works – Main Contractor
description:
The project has been developed for jLiving (Jewish Community Housing Association) and is located on a 0.2825 hectare site in Edgware on the A5 ‘Stonegrove’ between Stonegrove Gardens and Calthorpe Gardens. The site is currently occupied by Gordon Court, a two storey residential building in an ‘L’ shaped form. 
jLiving provides the Jewish community with affordable, secure, welcoming accommodation, including associated services for those aspiring to live independently.
Gordon Court currently provides: 
• 33 flats in total arranged over two floors, including 26 studio flats for single people, 6 one-bedroom flats and 1 two-bedroomed flat for couples. 
• 7 residents car parking spaces. 
• Parking is available to the front of the property – restrictions apply Mon-Fri 7-10am, 3-6pm. 
• Parking is also available in Calthorpe Gardens – resident permit parking Mon-Sat 10-11am and 3-4pm. 
The new development proposes an additional 11 new affordable rented flats, and the reconfiguration of the existing accommodation to create one-bedroom apartments from existing bedsits and ancillary accommodation. The units will be a mix of both 1B1P and 1B2P flats. 
The new development proposes to retain the existing building on the site, adding two new storeys to the front and side wing, and retaining a two-storey element in the vicinity of mature trees on the western side of the site. In addition to the airspace development a number of small extensions have been added to allow improved accommodation in existing apartments and achieve dual aspect requirements.
The main façade is being reconfigured to create a modern frontage with balconies provided to break up the façade and add rhythm. 
We invite you to submit your lump sum, firm priced tender to execute the Main Contract works. This will be a Design & Build contract and should include for all (outstanding) design, labour, plant and materials necessary to complete the works

title: Business Rates Review
description:
Royal Berkshire Fire Authority (the Authority) requires a review of the business rates charged on its estates to ascertain if any ongoing savings could be achieved by appealing the underlying rateable value (RV) of each property owned, including investment properties and fire stations. The Authority will pay the commission rate (%) if there are demonstrable savings. If there are no rebates from these reviews, then the Authority is not liable for any payment. 
Business rates bills are generated annually by the Local Authorities across Berkshire based on the RV and issued to the Authority. The Valuation Office Agency (VOA) is responsible for setting and periodically reviewing the values. Still, property owners can appeal at any time if there is a justified reason. 
The procurement process was a 3-quote process conducted under the Contract Standing Orders. A Request for Quote email was sent to three suppliers, detailing a 3-year contract period and a commission rate based on total savings across all listed sites for the duration of the contract, based on a no-win, no-fee basis.
The Authority has made an estimate for the contract value. This is based on a previous contract. As this is an estimate, the contract value could potentially change based on the savings that the supplier can achieve.

title: Supply of HVO fuel to RRS Discovery and RRS James Cook September 2026
description:
Supply of Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO) fuel to two National Oceanography Centre research vessels by way of two bunker deliveries at two ports on consecutive days. The contract is to be awarded to Standard Fuel Oils Limited as a single contract covering both deliveries, each performed against its own delivery reference.
Delivery D-01: RRS Discovery (IMO No. 9588029). Estimated quantity 252 m³ (252,000 litres). Required delivery date 15 September 2026.
Delivery D-02: RRS James Cook (IMO No. 9338242). Estimated quantity 430 metric tonnes, approximately 551,000 litres. Required delivery date 16 September 2026.
Aggregate estimated quantity approximately 803,000 litres. All quantities are estimates. Payment will be made solely on the actual quantity delivered against each delivery reference, as evidenced by the Bunker Delivery Note for that delivery and by the actual density recorded on the Certificate of Analysis at 15 degrees Celsius. No minimum or maximum quantity is guaranteed and the contract value stated is therefore indicative.
Delivery is by road tank wagon (RTW) to each vessel at its stated berth. The exact delivery window and operational hours for each delivery will be confirmed to the supplier in writing no later than five days before delivery.
Fuel must comply with EN 15940 and must be derived from used cooking oil (UCO) feedstock only, with no palm oil, palm oil sludge, POME, or animal fats. Sulphur content must comply with MARPOL Annex VI and the applicable MCA requirements, at less than 5 mg/kg (5 ppm). Flash point must be not less than 60 degrees Celsius, in line with SOLAS. CFPP must be minus 15 degrees Celsius or lower. Greenhouse gas emissions intensity of 15.86 gCO2e/MJ with a minimum 83 per cent saving against fossil diesel, and biogenic carbon (C14) testing on all imports. Fuel is to be supplied on a non-obligated basis in line with the requirements for marine research use.
The supplier is registered on the Maritime and Coastguard Agency Local Fuel Oil Suppliers Register as compliant with MARPOL Annex VI, and is registered on the Central Digital Platform with a current Public Procurement Organisation Number.
At the time of each bunkering the supplier must provide the fuel specification, representative fuel samples, a Technical Data Sheet with Certificate of Analysis, and a Safety Data Sheet to the Chief Engineer. A Bunker Delivery Note must be provided in the MARPOL Annex VI Appendix V format, stating quantity in metric tonnes, carrying the supplier's signed declaration that the fuel meets the fuel quality requirements of MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18, together with the sulphur content statement and the flash point statement. A representative MARPOL fuel sample must be drawn, labelled and sealed in accordance with MARPOL Annex VI.
The following sustainability documentation is required for each delivery: proof of sustainability of the biofuel component, certified under either ISCC or RFAS 2 Heat-Power-Marine (RSB is not required), a biofuel delivery statement, and the greenhouse gas emissions data for the fuel supplied.
The requirement was competed through a competitive quotation exercise on a best and final basis. Suppliers were invited to price each delivery on the basis that it might be awarded alone, and separately to price both deliveries taken together, and were permitted to bid for one delivery only without disadvantage. Award is made on the basis of the Most Advantageous Tender, tested by comparing the aggregate of the individual delivery prices against the price offered for both deliveries together. Award of both deliveries to a single supplier is the most advantageous outcome available. A transparency notice was published in advance of this notice under reference 2026PRNOC-1244.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – FE 07.0325/2024/ERB - Untersuchung der Rissbildung in Asphaltdeckschichten nach kurzer Liegedauer
description: Die Auswertung der letzten Messreihen der Zustandserfassung und -bewertung (ZEB) im Netz der Bundesfernstraßen belegt in mehreren Bundesländern eine signifikante Zunahme von Risserscheinungen in Asphaltdeckschichten. Der Anteil der Streckenabschnitte, bei denen der Zustandswert für die Rissbildung den Warnwert überschreitet, hat zwischen zwei aufeinanderfolgenden Messzyklen teilweise um bis zu 10 % zugenommen. Im Rahmen eines wiederholten Austauschs zwischen Bund und Ländern sowie auf Grundlage mehrfacher Prüfungen und Auswertungen wurde festgestellt, dass diese Schadensbilder auch bei neu hergestellten bzw. grundhaft erneuerten Streckenabschnitten mit vergleichsweise geringer Liegedauer beobachtet werden. Die kausalen Zusammenhänge der beobachteten Rissbildung sind gegenwärtig nicht abschließend geklärt. Vorliegende Analysen lassen jedoch auf bautechnische Ursachen schließen. Gegenstand des Forschungsvorhabens ist die wissenschaftliche Untersuchung der wesentlichen Ursachen frühzeitiger Rissbildung in Asphaltdeckschichten neu hergestellter Asphaltbefestigungen. Auf Basis der ermittelten Erkenntnisse sollen Maßnahmen zur Prävention derartiger Schäden abgeleitet werden. Die Ergebnisse des Vorhabens sind in die Fortschreibung der einschlägigen Technischen Regelwerke einzubringen.

title: Finland – Research laboratory services – Dynamic Purchasing System for Sequencing Services for Human-Derived Biological Samples
description: The contracting authority establishes a Dynamic Purchasing System for sequencing services for human-derived biological samples. All suppliers meeting the suitability requirements will be admitted to the system. Individual procurements will be conducted through mini-competitions within the DPS. The procedure is fully electronic. This Dynamic Purchasing System covers sequencing and associated laboratory and bioinformatics services for human-derived biological samples. The DPS is platform-agnostic and includes services performed using commercially available sequencing, enrichment, and single-cell analysis technologies, such as but not limited to: Sequencing modalities Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS), Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) Targeted DNA and RNA sequencing (custom and standardized panels) RNA-seq (bulk), single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq ATAC-seq (bulk), single-cell and single-nucleus ATAC-seq ChIP-seq and chromatin-state profiling Hi-C and related genome conformation assays Sequencing platforms (non-exhaustive, non-binding examples) -Short-read sequencing platforms, including optical- and chemistry-based systems -Long-read sequencing platforms, including single-molecule real-time and nanopore-based systems -Capillary electrophoresis Sanger sequencing systems (e.g., platforms commonly represented by ABI 3730/3500 series or equivalent) -Two-color and novel chemistry short-read platforms (e.g., platforms comparable to AVITI or equivalent) Single-cell and enrichment systems (non-binding examples) -Microfluidics- and droplet-based single-cell workflows (e.g., platforms comparable to 10x Genomics Chromium or equivalent) -Hybrid capture and target enrichment kits/workflows (e.g., systems comparable to Twist Bioscience target capture or equivalent) The DPS also covers: -Sample reception, QC, and nucleic acid preparation -Library preparation and enrichment -Sequencing execution -Primary, secondary, and optional tertiary bioinformatics analysis -Secure data delivery and optional data archiving All platforms and workflows offered must be commercially validated, reproducible, and compliant with biosafety and data protection requirements for human-derived materials. Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Operating Model A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) is an entirely electronic procurement framework used to purchase goods, services, or works that are commonly available on the market. Unlike a traditional framework agreement, the DPS remains open for new suppliers to join at any time during its validity, as long as they meet the selection criteria. How the DPS Works: 1. Establishment of the DPS The contracting authority defines the procurement scope, requirements, and supplier qualification criteria. A contract notice is published, and the DPS is set up as an electronic system (e.g., in an e-procurement platform). No suppliers or prices are selected at this stage—only the system is created. 2. Supplier Admission Suppliers can apply to join the DPS at any point while the system is active. They submit evidence that they meet the predefined eligibility and capability requirements. Once verified, they are admitted to the DPS supplier pool. 3. Call-Off (Mini-Competition) Procedure When a specific need arises, the contracting authority: Defines the requirements for that individual procurement and Invites suppliers under the DPS to submit bids. A competitive bidding process follows, typically with simplified tender documentation. Minimum tendering period is 10 days in DPS and the exact object of the procurement is a case by case decision. 4. Evaluation and Contract Award Bids are evaluated based on the award criteria defined for that specific call-off. A contract is then awarded to the supplier offering the best value according to the evaluation. Evaluation criteria generally include (but not limited to): -Price 40–60% -Quality / protocols / turnaround time 40–60% 5. System Remains Open New suppliers may continue joining the DPS throughout its duration. Requirements and call-offs may be repeated as needed. There is no limit on the number of suppliers admitted.

title: Netherlands – Endangered species protection services – Opstellen Soortenmanagementplan (SMP) Gemeente Hulst
description: Het onderzoeksgebied bestaat in beginsel uit bebouwing binnen de komgrenzen van de gemeente Hulst. Naast reguliere woonbebouwing dienen bijzondere objecten binnen of direct grenzend aan deze komgrenzen expliciet te worden beschouwd, waarbij onderbouwd wordt welke objecten ecologisch relevant zijn en welke onderzoeksinspanning passend is. De opdracht omvat naar verwachting onder meer: • bureauonderzoek en gegevensinventarisatie; • gebiedsdekkende quickscan; • soortgericht ecologisch onderzoek en nulmeting; • analyse van beschermde gebouwbewonende soorten; • effectbepaling; • opstellen van een concept en definitief SMP; • mitigatie- en compensatiestrategie; • monitorings- en evaluatieplan; • proces-, administratie- en managementplan; • GIS-dataset, kaartlagen, metadata en dataoverdracht; • afstemming met overheden De opdrachtnemer is verantwoordelijk voor de samenhang tussen onderzoek, analyse, effectbepaling, planvorming, vergunningaanvraag, GIS-data, monitoring en overdracht Als voorbereiding op het veldwerk en het opstellen van het soortenmanagementplan wordt er een gebiedsbrede quickscan uitgevoerd. Op basis van de quickscan wordt vastgesteld of gebiedsuitbreiding noodzakelijk is en of er diersoorten worden toegevoegd aan het onderzoek. Uitbreiding van gebieden en soorten vindt plaats in overleg met gemeente Hulst. Onderzoeksgebied Het primaire onderzoeksgebied bestaat uit de bebouwde kommen binnen de gemeente Hulst, zoals voorlopig weergegeven op de door Gemeente Hulst aangeleverde conceptkaart “Komgrenzen gemeente Hulst”. Deze begrenzing is nog niet definitief en kan voorafgaand aan publicatie van de aanbesteding worden aangepast of nader worden gespecificeerd. Het buitengebied behoort niet tot de primaire scope, tenzij aanvullend onderzoek buiten de komgrenzen ecologisch of vergunningtechnisch noodzakelijk blijkt voor een vergunningwaardige onderbouwing van het SMP. Naast reguliere woonbebouwing dienen inschrijvers in hun onderzoeksstrategie expliciet rekening te houden met bijzondere objecten binnen of direct grenzend aan de voorlopige komgrenzen. Daarbij kan onder meer worden gedacht aan kerken, kapellen, monumenten, gemeentelijk vastgoed, maatschappelijk vastgoed, scholen, sportaccommodaties, zorgvastgoed, appartementencomplexen, hoogbouw, begraafplaatsgebouwen, molens, torens, oude nutsgebouwen en overige ecologisch relevante gebouwen. Deze bijzondere objecten worden niet op voorhand allemaal als volledig onderzoeksplichtig aangemerkt. Van de toekomstige opdrachtnemer wordt verwacht dat hij in de onderzoeksstrategie onderbouwt welke objecten ecologisch relevant zijn, welke onderzoeksinspanning daarbij passend is en hoe wordt voorkomen dat relevante verblijfplaatsen, kraamlocaties, massawinterverblijven, nestplaatsen of functionele leefgebieden buiten beeld blijven. De definitieve onderzoeksbegrenzing, objectcategorieën en eventuele objectenlijst worden vastgesteld in de aanbestedingsstukken. Gebouwbewonende beschermde soorten Minimaal worden er in het onderzoek de gebouwbewonenden vleermuizen, de gierzwaluw, de huismus, huiszwaluw en de steenmarter (mogelijk alleen als indicatiesoort) meegenomen. Op basis van de quickscan is eventuele uitbreiding mogelijk.

title: Churchgate Regeneration Zone Procurement - Hitchin Town Centre
description:
The Churchgate Regeneration Zone (CRZ) represents one of the most significant long-term regeneration opportunities within Hitchin town centre. The site occupies a prominent and strategically important location adjoining the historic core, the River Hiz corridor and the existing market area. Over the past year, the Council has undertaken an extensive programme of work including financial analysis, specialist technical work, Project Board workshops and Member briefings. This work has enabled the Council to move from high-level vision setting into a more informed, evidence-led and delivery-focused phase.
Alongside this, the Council has also undertaken a Pre-Market engagement exercise and early engagement with the development and investment sector to inform future procurement, delivery and partnership decisions. Feedback from this work has demonstrated strong market interest in Hitchin and increased confidence in both the credibility of the opportunity and the Council’s commitment to delivering a high-quality regeneration programme for the town centre.
The next stage of work is intended to ensure that future decisions regarding the regeneration of the site are informed, evidence-led and commercially robust.
The Council is now seeking to procure specialist regeneration and development expertise to work alongside the project team in refining a deliverable scheme, testing assumptions in greater detail, reducing uncertainty and supporting the transition from strategic visioning into delivery planning and implementation.
The procurement will be structured around two phases. The initial phase of the appointment would comprise of feasibility, viability, master-planning and delivery planning activities designed to refine the regeneration proposals, test commercial assumptions, assess development risk and inform the preferred delivery model. The scope of Stage 2 will be informed by the outputs of Stage 1, and determine whether the Council wishes to proceed onto Phase 2 or not. Phase 2 will include detailed development planning, delivery preparation, planning and consenting activities, development agreement support, implementation planning and other services required to support project delivery. Any progression beyond Phase 1 would remain subject to future Council approval, satisfactory performance of the appointed partner, confirmation of any necessary funding (i.e. setting a capital budget for the scheme) and compliance with the contractual gateway provisions established through the procurement.

title: South Tees All Age Carers Support Serviced
description:
Redcar & Cleveland Borough Council and Middlesbrough Council are commissioning an All Age Carers Support Service to support unpaid carers across the South Tees area.  The service will be designed to meet the needs of adult carers, young carers and carers supporting people living with dementia.
The overarching aim of the service is to ensure carers can access timely, appropriate and preventative support that promotes their health, wellbeing and resilience, enabling them to sustain their caring role where appropriate.
The future service is expected to contribute to delivery of the Councils' statutory duties under the Care Act 2014 and the Children and Families Act 2014, ensuring carers have access to high-quality information, advice, and support that is accessible and proportionate to their needs.
The contract will comprise three lots as follows:
Lot 1: Adult Carers Core Service
A single-provider service delivering information and advice, outreach within primary and secondary healthcare settings, mental health support for carers, and opportunities for peer support.
Lot 2: Young Carers Core Service
A single-provider service focused on the identification of young carers, provision of tailored support, delivery of whole-family approaches, and assistance with educational achievement and personal development.
Lot 3: Dementia Carers Support and Advisory Service
A single-provider specialist service offering advice, guidance, training, and targeted support for carers of individuals living with dementia.
Together, these services will provide a comprehensive support offer for unpaid carers across South Tees, helping to improve outcomes for carers while enabling them to maintain their caring responsibilities safely and effectively.
The contract period is for an initial duration of 4 years, plus an optional 1 x 48 month optional extension period.

title: Best Start In Life Family Hubs Services
description:
The London Borough of Croydon is seeking to appoint suitably qualified and experienced providers to deliver a range of services under its Best Start in Life Family Hubs Programme. 
The programme forms part of the Council's commitment to improving outcomes for children, young people and families through accessible, integrated, and community-based support services. 
The commissioned services will contribute to the delivery of a borough-wide Family Hubs model, providing support from conception through to age 19, and up to age 25 for young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Services will focus on improving child development, school readiness, parental wellbeing, family resilience, and early intervention outcomes. 
The procurement will be conducted as an Open Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 and is divided into multiple specialist lots to encourage participation from a diverse provider market, including SMEs, voluntary, community and social enterprises (VCSEs), and specialist organisations. The Council intends to appoint a single supplier to each lot, with suppliers permitted to bid for multiple lots but limited to a maximum award of three lots. 
The services comprise the following lots:
1.	Online Parenting Courses
2.	Expectant Fathers Service
3.	Child Development Parental Training
4.	PEER Support Service
5.	Parental Mental Health Support
6.	Mild to Moderate Singing and Breathing Group
7.	Antenatal Parental Training
8.	Trauma Informed Baby Training
9.	One-to-One Peer Maternity Support Service
10.	Interactive Infant Feeding App 
The total estimated contract value is approximately £905,522 excluding VAT, with contract durations ranging from two years to two years and three months, commencing on or around 1 January 2027. 
The Council is seeking providers who can demonstrate expertise in delivering evidence-based family support, parenting interventions, maternal wellbeing services, digital solutions, early years development programmes, and community engagement activities. Successful providers will be expected to work collaboratively with Family Hubs, health partners, children’s services, and community organisations to ensure integrated service delivery and improved outcomes for Croydon residents. 
The Council particularly welcomes innovative approaches that support inclusion, improve accessibility, strengthen local communities, and deliver measurable social value in line with the Council's priorities and Family Hubs agenda.

description:
Havant Borough Council (the council)  invited tenders from suitably qualified suppliers for the refurbishment of the play area at Gauntlet Park, Crookhorn, Havant. The supplier will be required to design and build a new play provision within the existing footprint of the current site.
Gauntlet Park is in the Purbrook Ward to the east of central Havant borough in Hampshire. The Purbrook Ward is home to approximately 9300 residents. Directly adjacent to Gauntlet Park is a primary school with a preschool nursery, within the wider ward there is one secondary school and a college offering further education for young people.
The supplier will be required to:
- Design a new play provision within the existing footprint of the current site
- Work with the council to negotiate and update the design as required
- Supply and install the new play provision
- Complete any additional refurbishment works required.
The contract is due to commence on 01 October 2026. The contract period will be determined by the selected supplier's programme, however the council anticipates that practical completion and any snagging periods will be complete by no later than 31 December 2027.
The estimated value of the Gauntlet Park contract is estimated to be £140,000 - £150,000 excluding VAT (£168,000 - £180,000 including VAT).
The value of the available opportunity is estimated to be £1million excluding VAT (£1.2million including VAT). This is because, in addition to Gauntlet Park, the council has a wider pipeline of play parks across the borough to be refurbished over the next 3 years. These include:
- Nutwick Road Play Area
- Southwood Road
- Park Parade (Leigh Park High Street)
- Havant Play Area
- Longwood Avenue
This list includes all currently known play parks for refurbishment, but the list may not be exhaustive. The council continues to seek funding to improve the play park provision in the borough and therefore this list could increase.
To facilitate delivery of these play parks, the council reserves the right to award future contracts for the design and build of new and refurbished play parks to the winning bidder of this tender. Where future contracts are awarded, this will be via the direct award provisions in Section 41 and Schedule 5 paragraph 7-9 of the Procurement Act 2023.
The council is under no obligation to award future contracts in this manner and where additional work requires skills or capacity not tested or demonstrated by the tenderer, the council may still seek an alternative competitive process.

description:

- Confirm interest
- Complete and submit capability assessment attachment

The top four suppliers, based on the evaluation of their ITT submissions, will be invited to interview with the Trust. Accordingly, all suppliers should be advised that interviews are provisionally scheduled for the afternoon of 16 November 2026. As this date has been agreed with key stakeholders, it is not expected to change.
East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust (ESNEFT) is the largest NHS organisation in its region, formed on July 1, 2018, through the merger of Colchester Hospital University NHS Foundation Trust and The Ipswich Hospital NHS Trust.
ESNEFT provides comprehensive hospital and community healthcare services across multiple locations, including Colchester, Ipswich, Clacton, Halstead, Harwich, Felixstowe, and Aldeburgh. The trust offers a wide range of medical services such as acute medicine, cardiology, dermatology, emergency assessment, gastroenterology, neurology, and many more.
ESNEFT is committed to delivering high-quality care and continuously improving its facilities and services to meet the needs of the local communities. 
Every year hundreds of individuals, community groups and businesses generously donate money to help us achieve our aims. It is our job to make sure that the money is spent carefully and for the purposes for which it was given.
The ESNEFT Charity holds designated charitable funds for many of the services in the hospital as well as appeal funds. They have a duty to maximise the value it gets from public donation, but without exposure to undue levels of risk. We do not have the skills in house therefore appoint advisors to assist us with this.
The Charity's existing portfolio is invested in Ethical investment funds, property funds and a common deposit fund. 
ESNEFT is looking to re-procure the management and advice of The Trusts Charitable Funds Investment.

title: P0486 - KNOW YOUR OWN MIND AND BODY - YOUTH HEALTH AND WELLBEING PILOT (TYWI TAF CLUSTER)
description:
Hywel Dda University Health Board’s (HDUHB) Tywi Taf Cluster (2Ts) is seeking to commission a preventative health and wellbeing pilot designed to improve the emotional, physical and social wellbeing of young people across Carmarthen. 
This pilot has been developed in response to growing evidence of poorer emotional wellbeing, confidence and health literacy among adolescent girls, young women, and gender-diverse individuals requiring services related to women's health, including those who identify as female, transgender, non-binary, or gender diverse alongside increasing concerns about body image, social media influences, anxiety, self-esteem and healthy relationships. Informed by emerging evidence, it recognises the significant pressures many adolescent girls, young women and gender-diverse young people experience in defining their self-worth and identity through appearance and peer acceptance. These pressures can be further amplified by digital media and evolving social expectations, contributing to declining wellbeing, confidence and mental health among young people.
The pilot will provide safe, welcoming and inclusive environments where young people can develop confidence, build positive relationships, improve health knowledge and access support or signposting where required.
Whilst the primary focus of the pilot is adolescent girls, young women and gender-diverse individuals requiring services related to women's health, including those who identify as female, transgender, non-binary or gender diverse, the pilot will also include planned engagement opportunities for boys and young men. These activities will promote healthy relationships, mutual respect, emotional literacy, equality, consent and positive health behaviours, recognising the important role that all young people play in creating supportive and respectful communities.
The pilot supports the principles of prevention, early intervention, prudent healthcare, co-production and reducing health inequalities. It also contributes to the wider aims of improving population health outcomes, strengthening community resilience and enabling young people to make informed choices about their health and wellbeing.

The CRF is funded through ringfenced Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) funding rather than Council resources. DWP guidance requires local welfare provision to include support for people facing immediate financial crisis and those needing assistance to establish or maintain a home. As a result, the provision of essential furniture and white goods forms a core component of the CRF and the Council must maintain arrangements for the delivery of this support.
Direct provision of goods ensures that residents receive the items they need to maintain a safe and functional home environment, whilst providing greater assurance that public funds are used for their intended purpose. This approach reduces the risk of fraud and misuse compared with cash-based awards and supports effective contract management through clear audit trails.
Leicestershire County Council is exploring options for the provision, delivery and, where appropriate, installation of essential furniture and white goods for eligible residents experiencing financial crisis.

title: Adult Primary Care Continence
description:
This contract has been awarded to Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust under Direct Award Process A of the Provider Selection Regime. The specialist urogynaecology physiotherapy service forms an integrated element of the wider Primary Care Continence Service delivered to the Cheshire West population and is clinically interdependent with the existing continence pathway operating across the West Cheshire Health Collaborative. The service requires direct integration with the established multidisciplinary continence team, shared clinical pathways, referral and triage arrangements, clinical governance processes and collaborative working arrangements that are already in place between the Provider and Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust.
The service is not a standalone physiotherapy service that can be separated from the wider continence pathway without creating fragmentation of care, duplication of processes and disruption to patient management. Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is the only provider currently embedded within, and able to deliver the specialist physiotherapy component as part of, the existing integrated continence model across the West Cheshire Health Collaborative. Continuation of the existing arrangement ensures safe and effective patient care, maintains pathway integration and avoids disruption to patients accessing specialist continence services.
The service relies upon established clinical relationships, referral pathways, governance arrangements and multidisciplinary working practices that have been developed as part of the West Cheshire Health Collaborative model and cannot reasonably be replicated by an alternative provider without fundamental redesign of the service pathway.

title: Rough Sleeping Drug and Alcohol Treatment (RSDAT) - Community Detox
description:
For 2026-27 Gloucestershire County Council are introducing dedicated specialist housing provision as an integral part of the treatment and support pathway, starting on the 1st October 2026. This new service will be based within the existing drug and alcohol service (Via Care Ltd.) with additional wraparound support in the community being provided through this opportunity, with the intention that this will be developed into housed, supported community alcohol detox for rough sleepers and those who may be at risk of homelessness for 2027-29. The providers are both established providers who have worked together in the past.
The provider of the wraparound support which complements the substance use treatment service will provide end-to end support within accommodation for people who are sleeping rough, or at risk of sleeping rough. This will include:
• Provision of two bed spaces located in Gloucester city in dedicated residential accommodation with on-site 24-hour support from practitioners experienced in supporting people with severe substance use and other complex needs.
• Contributing to a specialist outreach team whose purpose is to meet individuals where they are, reduce immediate harms, and create low-threshold pathways into the wider treatment and recovery system.
• Alongside the clinical and recovery services provided by Via Care Ltd, the provider will deliver intensive wraparound support, focusing on stabilisation, practical harm reduction, motivational engagement, and navigation of wider systems. This will include support with benefits, GP registration, access to mental health pathways, housing teams, and safeguarding processes.
• Offer practical support including ID documentation, facilitating transport and appointment accompaniment.
• Deliver trauma-informed, persistent engagement to reduce disengagement during referral stages.
• Support the creation of dedicated supported pathways into inpatient detoxification and residential rehabilitation as well as ambulatory detox and wraparound homelessness services. The provider should be highly familiar with supporting people at every stage of recovery from dependency, from emergency shelter through to independent living, recognising that not all recovery journeys are linear and predictable.
• Joint working with housing partners, criminal justice agencies, community mental health teams and voluntary sector organisations will ensure seamless transitions and shared risk management.
• Use assertive follow-up and coordinated aftercare to maintain engagement after discharge.
This notice is an intention to award a contract to Emerging Futures under the most suitable provider process with a contract value of £215,00 over the contract term which runs from 1st October 2026 to 31st March 2029.

title: National Centre for Arts and Music Education
description:
The Department for Education is contracting with a delivery partner to establish and operate a National Centre for Arts Education (previously called the National Centre for Arts and Music Education) (the "Centre"). The intention is to establish the Centre by September 2026. The Centre will play a pivotal role in delivering the government’s ambition to revitalise arts in schools in England, so every child can access a rich, high-quality arts education that nurtures creativity, confidence, cultural understanding, and personal expression. This ambition will be underpinned by close collaboration with leading arts and cultural organisations and sector bodies to ensure the Centre reflects the breadth, diversity, and excellence of England’s cultural landscape.
The Centre will act as a strategic system leader, working across national, regional, and local levels to strengthen arts provision in schools. By convening and mobilising a broad coalition of partners from across arts, culture, education and philanthropy, the Centre is intended to create the conditions for meaningful social impact. It will coordinate and align funding, investment, and activity to maximise the collective impact of all partners involved in arts education in schools. It will also generate and share data and evidence to guide decision making and target support where access to high-quality arts education is most unequal. In this way, the Centre will be an important partner in revitalising arts education, securing equitable access to high-quality teaching and enrichment opportunities, particularly for children and communities currently least able to access them.
The Centre will operate with transparency, accountability, and a commitment to sector engagement, building trust and long-term partnerships across the arts and cultural ecology.
The delivery partner will lead the Centre and therefore be responsible for the design, implementation, and oversight of the Music Hubs network to support delivery of these priorities:
•	Priority 1: Providing strategic national leadership in revitalising arts in schools, mobilising a coalition of national, regional, and local partners to generate and direct investment to support equitable access to high-quality arts in school, with a focus on under-served communities.
•	Priority 2: Supporting excellent teaching, through a new online CPD offer for primary and secondary school teachers and support to access existing high-quality teacher development provision available from others.
•	Priority 3: Promoting arts education to school leaders, teachers, parents, and young people, including promoting opportunities for children and young people to progress in the arts and pursue their interests and career aspirations.
•	Oversight of the Music Hubs network, including being fundholder for the network, monitoring hubs’ performance and delivery, and working with hubs to achieve the Centre’s three priorities.

title: GMCA 1134 North West Community Flood Resilience Engagement Support Services
description:
This is for a neutral intermediary organisation operating in the space between communities who have flooded, or who are at risk  of flooding, and flood risk management authorities (RMAs),  across the North West of England, supporting those authorities to
increase the resilience of those communities to flooding and coastal change.
The desired outcome of the service is to increase the resilience of communities to flooding and coastal change through engagement to inform, educate, and drive behaviour change.
The initiative is funded primarily by the North West Regional Flood and Coastal Committee and the RFCC are therefore a key customer.
The supplier will be required to work with and support North West flood risk management authorities as required: local authorities (of which there are 24 Lead Local Flood Authorities and 12
district councils); the Environment Agency; and United Utilities, as the primary water company.
The communities to be supported include:
• Residents including homeowners and tenants
• Businesses, including agricultural businesses and farmers.
Communities vary considerably in terms of their characteristics (size, demographics, situation e.g. urban, rural) and needs. 
Many are in areas of deprivation which are generally harder to reach and require different approaches to engagement to meet their needs.
The scope of the engagement needed is primarily in relation to flooding, flood risk and resilience and any measures or matters related to this.
A smaller but important element of the scope includes broader coastal change and erosion which may require communities to adapt over time. Some support to coastal authorities is likely to be
required, to support planning and implementation of community engagement, as well as developing online content relating to the coast.
The service provider will maintain a neutral, constructive, and professional working relationship with all flood risk management authorities (RMAs). Following flooding incidents, residents and businesses may be highly emotional and urgently seeking explanations, often directing blame towards local councils, water companies, or the Environment Agency. Communities commonly expect authorities to "fix" the issue so that flooding does not recur. These circumstances can make engagement challenging, and careful handling is required.
The supplier will:
• act in a neutral, balanced, and mutually supportive capacity;
• help communities to understand the roles and responsibilities of the RMAs;
• support and complement multi partner engagement activities;
• assist communities in accessing information, without attributing blame or making demands for action on their behalf.
The supplier will navigate the political context of flood risk and resilience with sensitivity and professionalism, maintaining neutrality at all times. They will work constructively with a wide range of stakeholders, including RMA officers, local councillors, Members of Parliament, the Regional Flood and Coastal Committee (RFCC), the five sub regional Flood and Coastal Risk Management Partnerships, and United Utilities.
The provision of a public access website is an essential element of the service which provides a continuous source of up-to-date and consistent information for communities to refer to as they progress along their resilience journey, as well as extending the reach of the engagement activity much further than will ever be possible through direct engagement alone.
The Environment Agency holds the intellectual property rights over the content of the website.
The selected supplier will take over the management and ongoing development of the website and its content, building on the existing content which has been developed over many years

title: ​​​Underwater Pipeline Crossing Surveys & Remedial Works​​
description:
Northern Gas Networks (NGN) requires the provision of specialist river crossing survey and assessment services across its gas distribution network to monitor the condition, integrity, and ongoing safety of pipeline assets located within river crossings and associated watercourses.
The scope of services includes, but is not limited to:
- Determination of pipeline cover depths and profiles within river crossings.
- Identification and assessment of changes to riverbeds, banks, and watercourses that may affect pipeline integrity or stability.
- Confirmation of pipeline locations through topographical and hydrographic survey techniques, supported by geomorphological assessments where required.
- Surveying of riverbed and bank levels to identify erosion, scour, exposure, or other changes in condition.
- Inspection and assessment of exposed pipeline sections.
- Evaluation of the condition and construction of riverbeds, banks, and associated crossing infrastructure.
- Close Interval Polarised Potential (CIPP) Surveys and other corrosion monitoring activities where specified by NGN.
The appointed supplier shall provide comprehensive survey reports detailing the methodology employed, survey findings, identified risks, and recommendations for any remedial or risk mitigation measures. Where required, the contract may also include the provision of remedial works arising from survey findings to maintain the safety, integrity, and operational performance of the pipeline network.
This procurement seeks to establish a contract for the delivery of these specialist services across NGN's geographical operating area, ensuring the continued monitoring, assessment, maintenance, and protection of pipeline river crossings. The contract will support NGN in maintaining compliance with applicable engineering, environmental, and safety requirements while ensuring the long-term resilience and integrity of its gas distribution infrastructure.

description:

Pwrpas y prosiect yw darparu eiddo addas i’r diben sy’n fodern a hygyrch ac sydd a digon o le ar gyfer darpariaeth bresennol a darpariaeth yn y dyfodol. Bydd mewn lleoliad da i ddarparu gofal yn nes at adref a diwallu anghenion iechyd a gofal pobl leol gan gynnwys anghenion heb eu diwallu, h.y. darpariaeth i henoed bregus eu meddwl, a chefnogi darpariaeth gwasanaeth yn yr adeilad ei hun ac yn y gymuned leol.
Ar hyn o bryd, mae angen rhoi sylw i’r materion canlynol yng nghartref Dolwen
- Ystafelloedd bach sy’n cyfyngu ar allu’r darparwr gwasanaeth i ddiwallu anghenion y preswylwyr, er enghraifft, mae ystafelloedd sy’n addas ar gyfer teclynnau codi, ond nid yw hyn yn wir trwy’r cyfleuster i gyd. Mae’r cyfyngiad hwn yn cyfyngu ar bwy ellir darparu llety iddynt, yn dibynnu ar eu hanghenion.
- Nid oes gan yr un ystafell en-suite, ac nid ydynt yn cynnig gofod byw digonol, na’r cyfleusterau a ddisgwylir gan safonau modern.
- Mae’r darparwr gwasanaeth yn ei chael hi’n anodd diwallu anghenion cymhleth, sy’n golygu nad oes modd darparu llety i gleifion fel yr hoffant.
Mae amrywiaeth eang o ffactorau yn dylanwadu ar y cynnig: - cynnydd disgwyliedig ym mhoblogaeth hŷn Sir Ddinbych i 30.9% erbyn 2040; gan gynnwys na fydd y cyfleusterau presennol yn addas ar gyfer anghenion y preswylwyr; gwella darpariaeth gwasanaeth; dod â gwasanaethau’n nes at y gymuned; gwella’r ddarpariaeth bresennol ar gyfer pobl hŷn a’r angen 
i oresgyn cyfyngiadau fel mynediad, lle a pharcio, a bodloni her a nod Sir Ddinbych i fod yn garbon niwtral erbyn 2030.
Mae’r prosiect hwn, a gaiff ei arwain gan Gyngor Sir Ddinbych (CSDd) yn cydweithio â Thai Cymunedol, Cyngor Gwasanaethau Gwirfoddol Sir Ddinbych a Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr ar brosiect i adolygu datblygiad posibl Cartrefi Gofal Preswyl Dolwen. Mae’r prosiect yn cynnig estyniad a gwaith moderneiddio i gartref Dolwen gan gynnwys 
- Capasiti preswyl i henoed bregus eu meddwl, h.y. datblygu adain dementia 
- Darparu model mân ofal ychwanegol yn y cyfleuster tai pobl hŷn sy’n ffinio â Dolwen, mewn partneriaeth â Thai Cymunedol. 
- Model prif ganolfan a lloerennau o gefnogaeth gymunedol ar sail allgymorth a mewngymorth ar y cyd â Thai Cymunedol a Chyngor Gwasanaethau Gwirfoddol Sir Ddinbych.
- Uwchraddio a moderneiddio’r cyfleuster preswyl presennol o 32 i 50 gwely. Bydd hyn yn cynnwys estyniad a bydd yn galluogi’r llety presennol i gael ei ailddatblygu i sicrhau ei fod yn diwallu anghenion cymhlethdod yn y dyfodol, e.e. teclyn codi ym mhob ystafell a chyfleusterau en suite.
- Gwella darpariaethau presennol cymorth dementia yng nghymuned Dinbych a’r ardal gyfagos
Dolwen is a 32 bedded residential care home that was build in the 1960s which is struggling to meet the complexity of need that is being experienced by citizens requiring residential care.  The purpose of the project is to deliver fit for purpose premises that are modern, accessible, have sufficient space for current and future provision, utilise digital and AI technology, are well located to deliver care closer to home, meet the health and care needs of local people including unmet need I.E residential EMI provision and supports service delivery both building based and within the local community
Currently Dolwen has the following issues that need to be addressed
- Small rooms which limit the service providers to meet the needs of the residents, for example there are rooms which can accommodate hoists however not throughout the facility. This restriction limits who can be accommodated depending on their needs.
- None of the rooms are en-suite and do not offer the size of living space or facilities which would be expected in modern standards.
- The service provider struggles to meet the complexity of the needs meaning patients cannot be accommodated in the way which they would like.
The proposal is influenced by a broad range of factors: - predicted increase in the older population of Denbighshire to 30.9% by 2040; including the current facilities being unsuitable for the needs of the residents; improving service delivery; bringing services closer to the community; enhancing the current provision for older people and the need to overcome limitations such as access, space and parking and meet Denbighshire's challenge and objective to be carbon neutral by 2030.
This project which is led by Denbighshire County Council (DCC) is working collaboratively with Community Housing, Denbighshire Voluntary Services Council (DVSC) and BCU on a project to review the potential development of Dolwen Residential Care Home. The project proposes both an extension and the modernisation of Dolwen to include 
- Residential EMI capacity I.E developing a dementia wing, 
- Provide an extra care lite model to the older peoples housing facility bordering Dolwen in partnership with Community Housing. 
- Hub and Spoke model of community support on an outreach and in reach basis in collaboration with Community Housing and DVSC.
- Upgrade and modernisation to the current residential facility from 32 to 50 beds. This will include an extension and will enable the current accommodation to be redeveloped to ensure that the accommodation meets future needs of complexity e.g. hoist in every room and ensuite facilities.
- Enhance the current provisions of dementia support within the community of Denbigh and t's surrounding area.

title: OneLSC Pest Control Services
description:
The Authorities require the provision of a comprehensive, resilient and integrated pest control service across a diverse healthcare estate comprising acute hospitals, community hospitals, outpatient facilities, administrative locations and specialist healthcare environments operated by East Lancashire Hospitals NHS Trust, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Foundation Trust. The service will support the delivery of safe patient care by maintaining pest-free environments that protect patients, staff, visitors and assets from the risks associated with pest activity.
The Supplier shall recognise the unique operational challenges of NHS healthcare environments, where pest incidents can have a direct impact on patient safety, infection prevention and control (IPC), service continuity, regulatory compliance and organisational reputation. The Supplier shall therefore adopt a proactive, intelligence-led and preventative approach to pest management, ensuring that emerging risks are identified and addressed before they escalate into infestations or operational disruptions.
Working in partnership with Estates, Facilities, Infection Prevention and Control teams and other key stakeholders, the Supplier shall deliver a coordinated service that combines routine monitoring, planned preventative maintenance, rapid reactive response, specialist technical support and strategic pest risk management. The service shall be underpinned by Integrated Pest Management (IPM) principles, utilising data analysis, environmental assessment, proofing recommendations and targeted interventions to achieve sustainable pest control outcomes while minimising environmental impact and reducing reliance on chemical treatments.
The Supplier shall provide consistent standards of service across all Trust locations while retaining sufficient flexibility to accommodate site-specific risks, seasonal variations, operational pressures and the differing requirements of acute, community and non-clinical settings. Through effective governance, reporting and continuous improvement, the Supplier shall support the Authorities in maintaining compliant, safe and welcoming healthcare environments aligned with NHS standards, regulatory requirements and best practice.
