title: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit
description:
The National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) will be for NHS-funded care in England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Jersey (inclusion of other devolved nations/Crown dependencies is yet to be determined and will be detailed within the tender documentation). 
The initial contract is anticipated to be for a period of 3 years, at a maximum total budget of up to £ 951,168.00 excl VAT and £1,141,401.00 with VAT. Bids exceeding this limit will be rejected. Due to the unknowns in advance of holding the premarket engagement session, it is currently expected that the extension value will be a 2-year pro rata of the core 3-year funding, estimated at £634,112.00 excluding VAT.  
There is potential to include other Devolved Nations and/or Crown Dependencies, and aspirational measures (which will be defined in the service specification).
The role of a national clinical audit is to stimulate healthcare improvement through the provision of timely and high-quality information on the organisation, delivery and outcomes of healthcare, together with tools and support to enable healthcare providers and other audiences to make best use of this information. Outcomes are benchmarked against national guidance and standards e.g. quality standards from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), and those from other established professional and patient sources. Successful national audits are those where the individuals providing the data can also improve the system, and there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like. 
The National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) was established in 2011 and has been delivered by the Royal College of Anaesthetists (RCoA) - https://www.nela.org.uk/  
 The overarching aim of this audit is to stimulate improvements in care for patients undergoing and not undergoing emergency laparotomy through the provision of high-quality comparative data from all providers of emergency laparotomy by measuring and reporting variations in quality of care and patient outcomes. During this contract period, the successful tenderer will need to build on the achievements of the audit to date and enhance the ability for the audit to be used for healthcare improvement by engaging with clinicians, patients and commissioners (both local and national) and regional networks.  
Successful national audits are those where the individuals providing the data are also in a position to improve the system, and where there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like. Data is most useful locally for healthcare improvement when its provision to clinical teams is timely, the data is refreshed regularly, and appropriate tools, support and guidance accompany the data outputs. The intent is for all of these features to be implemented and improved during the period of this future contract.
Develop a robust, high-quality audit designed around key quality metrics likely to best support local and national quality improvement 
Detect, describe and help reduce unwarranted clinical variation by systematically benchmarking performance, identifying outliers, and supporting services to understand variation in outcomes, processes and experience 
Achieve, articulate and maintain close alignment with relevant NICE national guidance and quality standards throughout the audit, as appropriate 
Enable healthcare quality improvements through the provision of timely, high-quality data that compares providers of healthcare, and comprises an integrated mixture of named Trust or Health Board, Integrated Care System (ICS), multi-disciplinary team, possibly consultant or clinical team level and other levels of reporting 
Engage patients, carers and the public in a meaningful way, achieving a strong patient voice which informs and contributes to the design, functioning, outputs and direction of the audit 
Consider the value and feasibility of linking data at an individual patient level to other relevant national datasets either from the outset or in the future, and plan for these linkages from the inception of the contract 
Ensure robust methodological and statistical input at all stages of the audit 
Identify from the outset the full range of audiences for the reports and other audit outputs, and plan and tailor them accordingly.

Shift from retrospective reporting to near real-time data and interactive dashboards 
Improved insight for regulators, commissioners and systems (ICSs) through consistent performance data

Standardised performance metrics aligned with NICE and other national guidance

Utilise strong and effective project and programme management to deliver audit outputs on time and within budget 
Develop and maintain strong engagement with local clinicians, networks, commissioners, patients and their families and carers and charity and community support groups to drive improvements in services 
Embedded healthcare improvement plans with measurable objectives and ongoing impact evaluation 
Support for coordinated improvement across the entire emergency laparotomy pathway 
Increased use of routine data and data linkage to reduce manual data collection burden 
Improved data completeness, quality and efficiency, supporting robust analysis and decision-making 
Systematic assessment of inequalities in access, care and outcomes 
Support for national and local priorities to reduce inequalities and promote parity of care 
Active involvement of patients, carers and the public in audit design, outputs and improvement priorities 
Flexibility to expand scope (e.g. non-operative pathways, wider geographies including devolved nations and Crown Dependencies)

title: Online Digital Catalogue and Archive Management Solutions (ERO Online Digital Catalogue)
description:
Description
Essex Record Office (ERO) is seeking to engage with the market to understand available solutions and supplier capabilities that can support the modernisation of its archive management, digital preservation and public access services.
ERO is undertaking this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to inform future procurement activity and ensure that any proposed solutions align with the organisation's statutory responsibilities, service requirements and long-term digital preservation ambitions.
ERO is looking to understand the market's ability to provide solutions that can deliver the following outcomes:
•	Replacement of the current in-house developed Archive Management System (SEAX), which underpins over 80% of ERO's operations and public-facing services, including income-generating online services.
•	The archive management system will need to:
o	facilitate viewing the catalogue on-site at Essex Record Office locations and online
o	provide free access to digital and digitised collections on-site at Essex Record Office locations
o	provide online access, outside of ERO locations, to digital and digitised collections via a subscription service
o	facilitate the creation of user accounts with role dependent security/access levels
o	provide a paywall to access certain collections
o	manage the personal data of users of the service, including taking payments from them
•	Support for statutory archive, records management and civil registration functions.
•	Secure, scalable and standards-compliant digital preservation capabilities to support the long-term preservation, integrity and accessibility of digital records. We require a solution for preserving digital records with retention periods of 100 years or more, as well as potentially shorter retention periods. The solution must be able to deal with a variety of file formats including proprietary software files and a range of sound and moving image files.
•	Progression towards National Digital Stewardship Alliance (NDSA) Level 4 digital preservation maturity. Specifically, we require:
o	For digital records storage: three copies in at least two geographic locations (storage will need to be in the UK or EU)
o	A means of controlling, auditing, and recording file permissions
o	A means of recording sufficient metadata about the files using an appropriate metadata standard e.g. METS (Metadata Encoding and Transmission Standard), PREMIS (PREservation Metadata: Implementation Strategies), BagIt (BagIt File Packaging Format) and/or Dublin Core
o	Periodic integrity checking and disaster simulation, and a means of regularly updating the results of these checks
o	A means of recording details of people and software that have accessed or taken preservation actions on files.
•	Improved management and discovery of digital assets through modern digital asset management capabilities.
•	Enhanced public access, search and discovery through modern online archive and catalogue services.
•	Improved customer journeys and increased public engagement.
•	Support for current income generating services and potential for enhanced income generation opportunities.
•	Integration capabilities with existing and future corporate platforms and digital services.
•	Modern, intuitive and user-friendly interfaces for both staff and public users. As a minimum, we will need:
o	The ability to allow members of the public to access suitable digital preservation files
o	A means of providing redacted access copies of the content where necessary
o	A means of recording when files have been accessed and by whom
o	A means of ensuring the content is protected from unauthorised changes and any loss
•	Scalable architecture capable of supporting current digital holdings of 88.8TB and significant future growth over the coming decades.
•	Strong governance, audit, compliance and security features to support statutory and regulatory requirements, including the Public Records Act, Freedom of Information legislation and Data Protection requirements.
Background
Archive Management System
It is estimated that over 80% of the work of the ERO is currently managed through an in-house developed tool called SEAX. SEAX was created by Essex County Council as a bespoke system. It was created over 25 years ago in a now archaic programming language. Seax Explorer was written in VB (Visual Basic) and uses forms to create the different screens of its various modules (e.g. Catalogue Manager, Accession Manager, etc.). These forms have been written in a custom language based loosely around XML and are stored within the Seax Explorer database.
The online element of the system is known internally as Seax PAM and to the public as Essex Archives Online. This includes our online catalogue and income-generating subscription service and income-generating single-image service. Seax PAM was written using .NET framework and C# and is currently using an old version of .NET framework.
We are seeking a modern, sustainable and future-proofed solution for managing our requirements for accessioning, cataloguing, storage locations, document production, reader management and user access (at the ERO and online).
The ERO has a staff of around 25 people. Up to 12 users are likely to require login access to the staff side of the AMS, including generic logins for Searchroom staff, document production staff, volunteers, etc.
Digital Preservation
As of July 2026, the ERO has 88.8TB of digital data. This figure is expected to grow at an estimated rate of 5TB per year. Within the 88.8TB of data, 3.3TB consists of born-digital records; the other 85.5TB being content the ERO has digitised from its manuscript, image, sound and video collections. This data is all currently stored on Microsoft Azure Cloud Storage.
Most of the content is listed in basic form on a spreadsheet. Detailed metadata at file level is being added as resources allow. Further documentation about rights is kept in separate filing and on our archive management system (alongside information about our paper and analogue collections). The ERO has a dedicated ingest PC through which we process digital collections as they arrive. We are able to take images of disks using ISO Buster software, transfer files as they are or transfer them to a file format with greater longevity. Transfers can be made using Teracopy software and we can interrogate the files we receive using TNA’s Droid software.
The main element of NDSA (National Digital Stewardship Alliance) Digital Preservation Level 1 we are not currently achieving is the requirement to have two complete copies of our digital content in separate locations.
Our aim is to progress through the NDSA digital preservation levels to meet NDSA Level 4.
Areas of Interest
ERO is particularly interested in understanding solutions relating to:
•	Archive Management Systems (AMS)
•	Digital Preservation Management Systems (DPMS)
•	Digital Asset Management Systems (DAMS)
•	Preservation storage and hosting solutions
•	Public catalogue and online archive access platforms
•	Migration services from legacy archive systems
•	Integration and API capabilities
Contract Considerations
At this stage, ERO is seeking supplier feedback on:
•	Appropriate contract lengths and commercial models
•	Implementation and migration timelines
•	SaaS, cloud-hosted and hybrid delivery models
•	Opportunities for phased delivery across AMS, DPMS, DAMS and public access capabilities
•	Scalability to support long-term digital preservation requirements.
The information gathered through this PME will help shape ERO's future procurement strategy, solution design and business case development.

title: Provision of Mortuary services to HM Coroner for the County of Staffordshire
description:
Service Description
The service will provide mortuary and post-mortem facilities and associated services to support coronial investigations into deaths within Staffordshire.
The service will provide appropriate mortuary facilities for the secure receipt, storage, care and release of deceased persons referred under the jurisdiction of the Senior Coroner for Staffordshire.
The service will provide facilities and appropriately qualified and competent staff to undertake post-mortem examinations as required by the Senior Coroner. This will include support for routine, complex and other post-mortem examinations where appropriate facilities and expertise are required.
The service will provide appropriate facilities to enable authorised viewing and identification of deceased persons, including facilities for bereaved relatives where required. Suitable facilities will also be available for authorised observers attending post-mortem examinations, including Coroners' Officers, Police representatives and relevant medical or nursing students.
The service will operate during normal working hours, Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 16:00, excluding public and bank holidays, with appropriate out-of-hours/on-call arrangements to support urgent coronial requirements.
The service will accommodate hospital and community deaths in Staffordshire requiring a post-mortem examination following referral by the Senior Coroner. Post-mortem examinations may be undertaken at Royal Stoke University Hospital Mortuary or another appropriate mortuary facility within the relevant pathology service network, as agreed with the Senior Coroner.
The service will also support digital post-mortem examinations where required by the Senior Coroner. This will include appropriate arrangements for the secure holding and transfer of deceased persons to a designated facility for digital imaging and any subsequent examination required.
The service may be required to accommodate additional or non-standard post-mortem examinations, including bariatric cases, prison or deaths in custody, complex cases that cannot be undertaken at the public mortuary, and deaths occurring within emergency departments where a post-mortem examination is required.
The service will support mortuary requirements arising from Bradwell Hospital, Leek Moorlands Hospital, Longton Cottage Hospital and Haywood Hospital.
The service will require effective liaison and coordination with Coroners' Officers, Staffordshire Police, funeral directors, healthcare providers and other relevant organisations involved in the coronial process. This will include communication regarding workload, urgent cases, anticipated delays, transfer arrangements and the release of deceased persons.
The service will be delivered in accordance with all applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, professional standards and relevant health and safety, infection prevention and control requirements.

title: Modern Fire Fighting Strategy - Phase 2 Urban Fire Fighting Training Provision
description:
The London Fire Commissioner is undertaking a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to inform the development of a future procurement strategy for the provision of specialist urban firefighting training facilities and associated support services.
The purpose of this engagement is to better understand current market capability, capacity, commercial models and potential delivery approaches capable of supporting London Fire Brigade's Modern Firefighting Strategy Phase 2 programme. 
The Brigade anticipates delivering advanced operational firefighting training to approximately 4,800 operational firefighters and 200 officer observations over a three-year programme commencing in Q1 2027. 
We are particularly interested in engaging with organisations capable of providing some or all of the following:
- Specialist live fire training facilities.
- Carbonaceous fire behaviour training environments.
- Advanced fire behaviour and tactical firefighting facilities.
- Basement fire training facilities.
- Tactical ventilation training facilities.
- Fire compartments capable of venting gases and smoke to atmosphere.
- Temperature monitoring and environmental monitoring systems.
- Residential accommodation.
- Catering and welfare facilities.
- Structural firefighting PPE and associated laundering and maintenance services.
- Operational support infrastructure, including equipment storage and breathing apparatus support services. 
LFB's current preference is to explore a model whereby London Fire Brigade instructors design and deliver the training, whilst the supplier provides facilities, accommodation, catering, welfare, PPE and logistical support services. However, suppliers are invited to provide feedback on alternative delivery models that may improve value for money, resilience, innovation or operational effectiveness. 
As part of this engagement, suppliers are invited to provide feedback on:
- Market capability and capacity.
- Mobilisation requirements.
- Commercial and contractual models.
- Pricing structures and key cost drivers.
- Capacity and resilience risks.
- Sustainability and social value opportunities.
- Innovation and emerging technologies.
- Any aspects of the proposed requirement that may impact competition or market participation. 
This engagement is not a Call for Competition and does not form part of any formal procurement process. Information gathered will be used solely to inform the future procurement strategy, commercial approach and specification development. 
Participation in this exercise will not provide any supplier with an advantage in any future procurement process. 
We would be grateful if your organisation could review the accompanying PME Pack and complete the associated questionnaire by 5th October 2026 deadline. The pre-market engagement pack and questionnaire can be accessed and downloaded from https://sell2.in-tend.co.uk/blpd/publictenders

description:
Background to the requirement:
The fleet is managed by Synchronicity Care Limited representatives and is a 24 hour, 365 days a year operation. 
The fleet is used to carry supplies, post, medical equipment and pathology items to various locations throughout the North-east of England.
The fleet requires 22 vehicles in total, 5 x Luton 3.5 tonne with tail lifts multi-drop vehicles transporting stores / supply cages, sterile services trolleys (capes), linen supplies and ad hoc duties to various sites. The remaining 17 are a mixture of small and medium sized EV's and ICE vehicles that are used as multi-site vehicles delivering post, supplies (non-caged), pathology samples, estates maintenance and smaller ad-hoc duties. The premises involved are wide ranging including Health Centres, Doctor Surgeries, hospitals and other institutions. The need for a flexible vehicle is a much-needed requirement. 
The successful supplier will be responsible for the provision of the courier vehicle fleet including a comprehensive service and maintenance contract covering all safety, maintenance and repair work related to operating the vehicle fleet. 
This includes responsiblity for the following items for the duration of the contract:
o	Relief vehicle delivered to Darlington Memorial Hospital or University Hospital of North Durham while servicing of vehicles or breakdowns occur (must be fit for purpose and of equal or greater specification to that of the vehicle it is replacing) and supplied at vehicle exchange time.
o	Replacement tyres - fair wear and tear.
o	Fluids, lubricants and windscreen wipers - related to the continued use of the vehicle.
o	Full maintenance and service
o	Mandatory and preventative inspections on the vehicle and its equipment including tail-lift - tail lift inspections must meet The Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations 1998
o	Windscreen / glass replacement.
o	Customised livery as directed by the Trust representatives. 
o	NHSV Class (taxation exempt disc)
o	Vehicle driver training as required to demonstrate vehicle functionality. 
o	24/7 Breakdown recovery assistance, RAC or equivalent within 1 hour of receiving breakdown call including a dedicated breakdown contact number; Failure to repair the vehicle on the road, must be recovered and a replaced with another vehicle of equal or greater size and specification within 2 hours.
o	Puncture repair service including mobile with a response time no greater than two hours.

title: Procurement for an Out of Hours (OOH) Contact Centre Service (Brunelcare)
description:
Brunelcare invites tender responses for the provision of an Out of Hours (OOH) Contact Centre Service to deliver urgent housing, property, and welfare-related support during evenings, weekends, and public holidays. 
The service will support residents living in Brunelcare's sheltered flats and bungalows, which provide an independent living environment within a supportive community. The service requirements include, but are not limited to: 
- Emergency repairs and safety-related incidents. 
- Welfare checks and safeguarding alerts. 
- Assistance with access issues, lockouts, and other urgent housing matters. 
- Escalation of incidents and handover to Brunelcare's daytime operational teams. 
The supplier will be responsible for coordinating with Brunelcare's DLO and specialist contractors in relation to any repair-related call-outs.
The procurement of an OOH Service provider is a key step in ensuring Brunelcare continues to meet its operational requirements, deliver a responsive and high-quality service to residents, and provide reassurance to residents, staff, and stakeholders. 
The successful Supplier will provide a comprehensive call handling and triage service, including the logging, monitoring, escalation, and reporting of all out of hours incidents. 
Brunelcare is a Bristol-based charity providing high-quality housing, care, and support services for older people across the South West. 
Brunelcare is conducting an Open Procedure to appoint a suitable Supplier to deliver this service, commencing on 1st April 2027.  
The contract will comprise an initial term of three (3) years, with the option to extend for up to two (2) additional years, giving a maximum contract term of five (5) years. 
Full details of the requirements and scope of services are contained within the associated tender documents available via ProContract. 
The deadline for submission of tenders is 12pm (noon) on 20th October 2026. 
Please note that Shared Services for Housing (SSfH) is acting as the managing organisation on behalf of Brunelcare for this tender opportunity.

title: Gallery 33 - Principal Contractor
description:
In September 2027, we will open a new, permanent gallery at South Kensington dedicated to building a positive connection to nature in our very youngest audiences - aged 4-7 years old - and their adults.    This brand-new gallery will be a place where visitors delight in the dazzling variety of life on Earth, from the very small to the very tall, and discover that all life – including us! – share the same needs. We all need to breathe, eat, move, communicate and grow to survive and often depend on each other to do this. Together, we are all part of this great, big, weird and wonderful natural world. It will deliver inspiring stories that celebrate diversity and welcome in the widest possible audience of children and their adults. It will combine our world-leading collections, with hands-on and multi-sensory interactives that evoke joy, empathy and care.   This project supports our Strategy and Mission to 2031 and our vision of a future where both people and the planet thrive, with a mission to create advocates for the planet. By appealing to visitors’ sense of kindness, their curiosity, and their imagination, this gallery will lay the foundations of advocacy for nature at a young age, foster a lifelong appreciation of the natural world and build a positive connection to nature in early childhood. 
Gallery 33 (working title) will replace the current Creepy Crawlies gallery on the ground floor the Grade 1 listed Waterhouse East Building and refurbishing the space for the new exhibition. It will open in September 2027 as a free, permanent gallery, and is expected to welcome millions of visitors over a 25-year lifespan. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to create a new gallery which positions children at the heart of our Museum and inspire the next generation of children to start their lifelong journey of advocacy for the planet.   
The Natural History Museum wishes to secure the services of a Principal Contractor to undertake the exhibition fit-out, including sub-contracting the services of an AV Integrator and specialist showcase manufacturer.

title: Health Cover Services
description:
The West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service (WYFRS) is inviting expressions of interest for an upcoming tender for Health cover Services. 
As the fourth-largest Fire and Rescue Service in the UK, WYFRS serves over 2.2 million people across 800 square miles, providing emergency coverage 24 hours a day, every day of the year. WYFRS employees approx. 1500 staff.
At this time, WYFRS is looking to assess the market's interest and its appetite to bid for and deliver this upcoming contract. A high-level overview of the key requirements is outlined below, although full details will be provided in the tender opportunity.
1. Cash Plan
A healthcare cash plan that enables employees to reclaim the cost of routine healthcare expenses, including but not limited to:
Prescription charges
Dental treatment costs
Optical expenses, including eye tests and corrective eyewear
Specialist consultations and diagnostic services
Diagnostic scanning services, including MRI, CT and PET scans
In addition, the cash plan should provide access to a range of wellbeing and preventative health benefits, such as:
24/7 GP services
Counselling and wellbeing support
Cancer risk assessments and screening services
Neurodiversity assessment and support services
2. Private Medical Insurance (PMI)
A private medical insurance provision that enables employees to access eligible consultations, diagnostics and surgical procedures through accredited private hospitals. This should support timely access to treatment and reduce waiting times for covered medical conditions compared to the NHS.
The tender is expected to be issued approximately November 26. The contract term will last a minimum of 3 years, with options to extend for +1 + 1 year periods, bringing the total
duration to a maximum of 5 years total.

title: Data Platform Implementation Partner
description:
Award of Data platform implementation partner. The University is seeking to design, build and implement a modern, enterprise-grade data platform to replace the existing on-premises Oracle data warehouse. The new platform will provide a scalable, secure and future-ready foundation capable of supporting the full ecosystem of data ingestion, transformation, semantic modelling, operational reporting, strategic insights, and AI-enabled analytical capabilities.
The platform will form a critical foundation for decision making across the University, supporting academic operations, student lifecycle management, finance, HR, research and other domains. It will empower approximately 4,000 internal users while indirectly supporting services that impact more than 20,000 students.
The solution will be developed using Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Fabric as the strategic technology stack. It must deliver high levels of scalability, improved data accessibility, and automation, alongside advanced analytics capabilities. The platform will also be designed to support future integration of AI agents and LLM-based natural language querying, enabling more intuitive and democratised access to insights.
As part of its broader analytical capability, the platform should provide the foundations to enable advanced learning analytics and support data modelling use cases aligned to student recruitment, retention and engagement.
There is an expectation that the delivery will include at least one agreed proof of concept to demonstrate the platform's advanced analytics capabilities. The specific use case will be defined collaboratively, but is expected to align to one or more of the following innovation areas:
• Predictive analytics (e.g. student number forecasting in collaboration with Strategic Planning)
• Advanced learning analytics capabilities
• Data modelling solutions to support student recruitment and engagement
The final scope and prioritisation of this proof of concept will be agreed during the delivery phase to ensure alignment with institutional priorities and data readiness.
A key objective is to democratise data access and capability across the University. The platform will provide governed self-service capabilities, allowing teams beyond the Information Management function to access curated data models and develop their own data modelling solutions where appropriate, while maintaining strong data governance and quality standards.
The scope of work includes the design, implementation and migration of approximately 1,200 ODI mappings, over 35 database schemas, and 3,000 tables. It also includes comprehensive documentation, training, and a structured knowledge transfer programme to ensure long-term sustainability.
The supplier will ensure that the final solution is production-ready, secure, fully documented, and successfully transitioned into business-as-usual support structures, while enabling ongoing evolution of analytical capabilities over time.
The University of Portsmouth requires an experienced supplier to deliver a complete cloud‑based data platform to modernise its existing data estate and enable future analytical growth. The contract will cover end‑to‑end delivery: architecture design, build, migration, operational readiness and early‑life support.
The University plans to retire its legacy Oracle data warehouse and build a new data platform, migrating key datasets that remain in active use. This will improve performance, ensure long-term sustainability, and open new capabilities such as AI-driven querying and predictive analytics. The platform will support both strategic and operational reporting, including self-service tools, automated data updates, and advanced modelling aligned with the University's goals.
Beyond the development of the core data platform, the University is interested in working with the successful supplier to explore innovative applications of data. This may take place alongside the implementation or once the platform is established, and could include areas such as learning analytics, forecasting, and other advanced insights.

Co-op Academies Trust, founded in 2010 is a group of schools across the North of England doing things differently. Made up of Primary, Secondary, Special and Colleges we operate under the belief that by raising aspirations, offering a leading education alongside forward thinking experiences and opportunities outside of the classroom, we can develop tomorrow’s leaders and help communities.

https://www.coopacademies.co.uk/ 
The Trust is tendering the fully managed lettings services for one of its schools, as below: 
Co-op Academy Stoke-on-Trent:
We will deliver an exceptional education to all children and commit to achieving the very best outcomes. We will do this by ensuring a laser sharp focus on standards, in all senses of the word. This is how we will demonstrate our unrelenting ambition for every young person. Our decision-making will place children at the core, making sure we do the things today that will secure their futures. In turn, we will enhance the life chances of our young people, ensure that they have the best opportunities, and can realise their ambitions. 
Further information regarding the School can be obtained here: https://www.stokeontrent.coopacademies.co.uk/
Tender information:
The successful tenderer will be required to provide an efficient and effective fully managed letting services for the Co-op Academy Stoke on Trent which has 1300 pupils and 120 teaching and support staff. 
The contract term being tendered is for three years, 1st September 2026 – 31st August 2029. There is an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 31st August 2031.
The contract offers an excellent opportunity to review and propose enhancements to the current letting services at the schools.
The school seeks to increase income streams and ensure the commercial viability of lettings by maximising all assets and actively promoting all facilities. A consistent, professional approach to lettings management is required, aiming to increase income, maintain and enhance the school’s reputation, deliver a positive social impact, strengthen community engagement and potentially to attract new pupils.  
The school is not obliged to accept the best financial offer submitted for this tender, rather the school is keen to secure best value. Creative ideas as to how the lettings activity can be developed, improved and maximised, will be welcomed. The school seeks a contractor that is keen to work in partnership with them and who will deliver to its highest abilities, at all times. 
Competitive Flexible Procedure 
This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here a minimum of 5 candidates (or less, in the event less than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates, will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. 
Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 50% price and 50% quality.
Value of contract:
The annual value of the current contract is £62,000 (the total lettings revenue from the last contract year).
Therefore the value of this contract is £310,000 (above total x 5 as this contract is for a maximum of 5 years)  
The tender process will be run under a two stage Competitive Flexible procedure.

description:

Trafford Council - Provision of Domestic Abuse Safe Accommodation - Soft Market Testing.
Please note that this is not a call for competition. This is a soft market testing exercise is undertaken on behalf of Trafford Council under the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023.
Purpose: Part IV of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 mandates a statutory duty on local authorities to provide safe accommodation for people fleeing domestic abuse. In Trafford we currently provide safe accommodation in the form of refuges for women, families and male survivors of domestic abuse. We also provide dispersed accommodation for some survivors when they move on from refuges.
Trafford Council are undertaking this soft market testing exercise to fully understand what the market can offer and the challenges in procuring and setting up this service. It is hoped that this will be an opportunity for us to obtain an insight of how participants might approach delivery of the service, and how they might address circumstances that may impact on the service. It will also help us to further understand the market.
We anticipate that should a tender exercise be undertaken, the maximum annual value for the contract might be in the region of £357,559, and the duration to be 5 years, with an initial period of 12 months with the option to extend for period(s) of up to 48 months.
We are therefore seeking expressions of interest from participants with the relevant expertise and experience to assist us in determining the feasibility of this project by answering the questions that are published on the Chest portal - Project Ref DN827443.

title: Construction, Maintenance and Minor Works Framework
description:
Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council gives notice of its intention to award a Construction and Minor Works Framework for the delivery of construction, maintenance, repair, refurbishment and associated minor works required by Council during the framework term, which is three years.
The proposed framework is intended to provide the Council with access to suitably experienced and competent contractors capable of delivering a range of planned, reactive and project-based works across the Council estate. The scope will include, but is not limited to, general building works, minor civil works, repair and maintenance activities, small-scale refurbishment, enabling works and associated construction-related services.
The proposed framework will offer access to a range of construction and minor works trades and disciplines, including painting and decorating, plastering, plumbing, Gas Safe engineering, joinery, drywall and ceilings, skilled labour, general labouring, fence erection, glazing, bricklaying and stonemasonry, tiling, welding and roofing, playpark installations.
The estimated total value of the Framework over its term is £1,500,000. This estimate is provided for transparency and planning purposes only and does not constitute a guarantee of volume of work or number of call-off contracts to be awarded under the Framework.
The framework will be used exclusively for works and contractors/individuals located within the borough area of Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council.
It is intended to support the efficient, compliant and timely delivery of Council requirements across the Borough whilst providing support to local firms through direct procurement and ensuring that works are procured and delivered in a manner that meets Council’s operational needs, statutory responsibilities and commitment to transparency in public procurement.
The framework is not intended to confer exclusivity on any single supplier, and any subsequent call-off arrangements will be managed in accordance with the terms of the Framework and the applicable requirements of the Procurement Act 2023 and the Procurement Regulations 2024.
Council considers that the framework is particularly suitable for small and medium-sized enterprises. The nature, scale and geographic focus of the works are expected to provide opportunities for local and regional contractors, including SMEs, to participate as subcontractors.
Council will seek to ensure that the procurement documentation is proportionate, accessible and clear, with requirements set at a level that encourage participation from SMEs and to reduce unnecessary barriers to competition.
In publishing this notice, the Council is providing advance transparency to the market regarding its intention to establish and award the framework. This notice is intended to inform interested suppliers of the Council’s proposed approach and to support openness, accountability and understanding of the Council’s procurement decisions.
Publication of this notice does not create any binding commitment to award the framework, nor does it prevent the Council from amending, delaying or discontinuing the proposed procurement where it considers it appropriate to do so.

The ASEAN-UK SAGE programme is a six-year Business Case  funded by the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) through the UK Mission to ASEAN. Delivered in two phases, the UK Mission to ASEAN is now seeking eligible organisation(s) to deliver a three-year Phase 2. 
Phase 2 will run for three UK financial years, from August 2026 to March 2029, with a total budget of £9,000,000. It will be delivered by a lead organisation under an agreement with the UK Mission to ASEAN, supported by downstream partners as needed. 
The focus of ASEAN-UK SAGE is to support inclusive and equitable quality education for children across Southeast Asia Region in close collaboration with ASEAN secretariat, especially for girls and the most marginalised, contributing to regional integration and narrowing of development disparities between ASEAN Member States (AMS) .  
The emphasis in Phase 2 will be on the use of evidence to improve learning outcomes and inclusion, especially for priority countries in the region.

title: Delivery of Perinatal Mental Health Support to Families
description:
Connecting Mums Programme Overview:
The Connecting Mums programme consists of six carefully designed sessions, each focusing on key themes to support mothers in enhancing their mental health, building social connections, and developing coping strategies. Each session combines group discussions, practical activities, and relaxation techniques to address specific challenges faced by new mothers while creating a supportive and safe environment. 
Mums Matter Programme Overview :
Mums Matter is an 8-week course designed to support mothers experiencing very poor mental health - postnatal depression (PND), anxiety, and related mental health challenges. It offers practical tools, peer support, and a safe environment for mothers to address their wellbeing. Each session is built on input from women with lived experiences and incorporates evidence-based practices such as cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) techniques, mindfulness, and self-care strategies.  
Mindful Mums Peer Support Group:
Mindful Mums is an informal drop in peer space to allow mums to connect with each other, build friendships and learn how to manage either wellbeing in every day life. The group runs on a fortnightly basis through out the year.   
Muslim Mums Support in Peterborough:
Co-produced, this course supports Muslim women facing challenges including anxiety, postnatal depression, and isolation. It provides a safe environment for women to connect and discuss unique issues. Facilitated by Muslim Project Workers, the course follows the structure of Connecting Mums, however in addition, also incorporates cultural and religious contexts, weekly "Asma of the week," and Quranic discussions. Topics include family dynamics, expectations, and intergenerational differences. 
Dads Support in Peterborough:
Sessions to support fathers' mental health and wellbeing including out of usual working hours such as evenings and weekends. This would be group support through our co designed 'Dads Matter' workshop and check ins.  
The service is primarily delivered through community-based group sessions and peer support activities designed to promote wellbeing, reduce isolation, and build resilience amongst parents during the perinatal period. The programme provides preventative and early intervention support, including facilitated group discussions, wellbeing activities, and peer networks, with participation not dependent on individuals being under a clinical mental health pathway. The service is intended to complement existing statutory and NHS provision through community-based support, peer connection, and wellbeing interventions, rather than replacing or replicating clinical healthcare services.

title: Play Equipment at Ladygrove Park, Didcot
description:
Ladygrove Park is a well-used public open space located within the Ladygrove area of Didcot, comprising approximately 29 acres of accessible green space. The park provides a range of recreational facilities for residents and visitors, including:
•
Extensive public open grassed areas
•
Outdoor sports facilities
The project seeks to maximise the use of currently underutilised landscaped mounds within the play area to create an engaging, adventurous and inclusive play environment for children, primarily aimed at those aged between 5 and 11 years. Tenderers are encouraged to develop innovative design proposals that incorporate these existing landforms and create a cohesive play experience by linking the mounds where appropriate.
As part of the overall design, contractors should consider the relocation of the existing multi-play unit to higher ground within the play area. The current location is susceptible to seasonal flooding during the winter months, and proposals should demonstrate how relocating this equipment could improve its long-term usability and accessibility.
The Council invites tenderers to submit their own design concepts, making imaginative use of features such as, but not limited to:
•
Tunnels
•
Bridges
•
Slides
•
Climbing elements
•
Accessible and inclusive play features
•
Natural play opportunities
The proposed design should complement the existing playground while significantly enhancing the quality, variety and accessibility of the play experience. The Council wishes to create an attractive destination that encourages active, imaginative and inclusive play, supporting the cognitive, physical, social and emotional development of children and young people.
The existing play equipment is over 25 years old and, whilst remaining serviceable, the Council is seeking to modernise the play provision to better meet the needs of the local community and to provide facilities comparable in quality to those available at Edmonds Park.
The available project budget is currently £40,000. The Council is actively seeking additional external funding and, if successful, anticipates increasing the total project value to approximately £100,000. Subject to successful funding, the anticipated allocation is:
•
Approximately £80,000 for the design, supply and installation of new play equipment.
•
Approximately £20,000 for the relocation of the existing multi-play unit and the possible installation of an accessible see-saw, utilising the existing accessible infrastructure where appropriate.
Tenderers should therefore identify which elements of their proposal could be delivered within the confirmed budget and which additional enhancements could be incorporated should further funding become available.
This project needs to ensure full compliance with all Playground Regulations - specifically EN1176, and BS7188 and EN1177 for surfacing.
Didcot Town Council prefer to work with companies who sources their equipment from the United Kingdom, so there are less issues with delays for replacement parts.
•
A dedicated children's play area
Within the existing playground are two landscaped mounds that are currently underutilised and do not accommodate any play features.
As part of its ongoing commitment to enhancing community recreation and play opportunities, Didcot Town Council's Environment & Climate Committee has identified these mounds as suitable locations for additional play equipment. The Council is therefore seeking proposals for the design, supply and installation of play equipment that makes effective use of these features, enhances the existing play provision, and provides engaging, inclusive and high-quality play opportunities for children and young people.

title: Germany – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Neubau Campus Zentralklinikum, Planungsbegleitung Zentralklinikum
description: Die aktuelle bauliche Struktur des UKMD ist gekennzeichnet von einer dislozierten Gebäudestruktur, abgängigen baulich-technischen Infrastruktur sowie weiten Wegen und nicht mehr zeitgemäßen Funktionsstrukturen. Es besteht dringender Handlungsbedarf, um die UMMD für die künftigen Herausforderungen der universitären Medizin aufzustellen und drängende bauliche Probleme zu lösen. Zur Lösungsfindung wurde im Zeitraum 2022 – 2024 eine übergreifende, bauliche Masterplanung für den Campus der UMMD an der Leipziger Straße erstellt. Ausgehend von einer prospektiven Medizinstrategie wurde eine Kapazitäts- und Flächenbedarfsbemessung durchgeführt, die anschließend über bauliche Machbarkeitsstudien in eine campusweite Masterplanung überführt wurden. Diese Bauliche Masterplanung stellt eine portfolioadjustierte und an den dringenden Bedarfen der UMMD orientierte Konzeption dar, zu der bereits umfangreiche Vorarbeiten, Untersuchungen und Abstimmungsergebnisse vorliegen. Diese müssen nun, in Vorbereitung einer konkretisierten baulichen Umsetzungsplanung für Einzelvorhaben, weiter konkretisiert werden. Die Umsetzung der vorliegenden, baulichen Masterplanung für das Universitätsklinikum Magdeburg als „Neuer Campus Zentralklinikum“ ist gegenwärtig eines der größten Bauvorhaben des Landes Sachsen-Anhalt und erfolgskritisch für die Zukunftsfähigkeit des Standorts an der Leipziger Straße. Für die Planung und bauliche Umsetzung des Projektes „Neubau Campus Zentralklinikum“ wurde an der Universitätsmedizin Magdeburg der Vorstandbereich 6 gegründet. Dieser übernimmt die Aufgaben des Nutzerprojektmanagements. V6 fungiert als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen der UMMD (Nutzer) und der IPS (Bauherr) und ist u. a. für die Koordinierung sowie Steuerung der internen und externen Informationsbeschaffung verantwortlich. Die Realisierung des Bauprojektes wird von der landeseigenen Immobilien- und Projektmanagementgesellschaft Sachsen-Anhalt mbH (IPS) übernommen. Die IPS ist in der Funktion des Bauherrn tätig und wird außerdem Eigentümer der Immobilen und baulichen Anlagen, die im Rahmen der Baumaßnahmen entstehen. Als 100%ige landeseigene Gesellschaft des Landes Sachsen-Anhalts wurde sie vom Ministerium der Finanzen (MF) mit der Planung und der Errichtung des Projektes „Neubau Campus Zentralklinikum“ beauftragt. Die IPS setzt für dieses Bauprojekt das Modell der Integrierten Projektabwicklung (IPA) ein. Dabei handelt es sich um ein Verfahren, das insbesondere für die Durchführung komplexer und anspruchsvoller Bauvorhaben geeignet ist. Bereits in der Planungsphase werden alle an Planung und Bau beteiligten Akteure frühzeitig in einer vertraglich geregelten Allianz eingebunden. Somit wird die Trennung zwischen Bauplanung und -ausführung aufgehoben. Ziel ist es, ein gemeinsames Verständnis des Bauprojektes über den gesamten Projektverlauf hinweg zu entwickeln und gemeinsame Projektziele zu definieren. Ein wesentlicher Vorteil dieses Ansatzes liegt darin, dass die Expertise der bauausführenden Partner von Beginn an einbezogen wird. Grundlage dieser Form der Projektabwicklung ist ein gemeinsames Verständnis von Zusammenarbeit sowie eine kooperative und kollaborative Projektkultur aller Beteiligten. Die in Rede stehende Leistung ist nicht Bestandteil der Integrierten Projektabwicklung, sondern wird außerhalb dieses Verfahrens eigenständig durch die UMMD als Auftraggeber und Nutzer beauftragt. Die Maßnahme besteht aus mehreren Teilleistungen: Erstellung der BO-Feinplanung einschließlich der Teilleistung Erstellung eines IT-Konzeptes zur Integration der betriebsorganisatorischen Prozesse in die bestehende oder neu zu schaffende IT- und medizintechnische Infrastruktur, Inbetriebnahme-Planungen, Second Opinion für/Bewertung von Planungsinhalte/n, Rochadenplanung für Bauzustände

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Project "OPAM"
description: The contract concerns the project "Opam", which covers the sustained maintenance, hardening, and continued stewardship of the package manager for the OCaml programming language. As part of nine work packages, the contract covers especially the diagnosis of structural limitations and identification of underlying recurring issues through the systematic triage of community reported problems and the review of contributor submissions, a refactor of the codebase, repairs to the mechanism that pins exact dependency versions, including an assessment of a more robust redesign to minimize the need for subsequent fixes, the hardening of the tool's preview and write-protection modes, checks for reproducible builds, the resolution of known security issues, expanded documentation and tutorials, a repeatable release process, and broader test coverage. The aim of this service is to sustain and secure a package manager on which the entire OCaml ecosystem depends, keeping the analysis and verification tools it builds from source rebuildable, inspectable, and independent of any single vendor.

Teemme siksi markkinakartoitusta ennen varsinaisen hankintailmoituksen julkaisua. Tavoitteena on kertoa tulevasta kilpailutuksesta, kartoittaa hankinnan kohteen markkinoita sekä saada kattavasti tietoa palvelun saatavuudesta, toteutusmahdollisuuksista sekä potentiaalisista toimittajista. Tämä on kutsu markkinavuoropuheluun, joka koskee Turun kaupungin suunnittelemaa energiankulutuksen valvontapalvelusta. Turun kaupunki valvoo energiankulutusta n. 600 rakennuksessa, joista yli 200:ssa on kaukolämpö. Mittauskeskitin, jolla saadaan tarkempaa kulutustietoa löytyy n. 70 rakennuksesta. Tavoitteena on luoda energiankulutuksen valvontaa tuottava digitaalinen palvelu, joka tekee asiantuntijan manuaaliset työvaiheet tuottaen mahdollisimman pitkälle valmiiksi jalostettua tietoa kulutusmuutoksista helpoilla näkymillä, selitteillä ja jatkotoimenpiteillä. Tavoitteena on tehdä kulutusvalvonnasta mahdollisimman automaattista vähentämällä manuaalisen työn vaiheita, kuten nousseen kulutuksen alkuajankohdan, esiintymisen ja kokonaisvaikutusten selvittämistä. Käyttäjän tulisi saada automaattisesti tärkeimmiksi priorisoidut kärkihavainnot näkyviin ja helposti havainnon analyysi näkyviin. Markkinavuoropuhelu järjestetään webinaarina Teamsissa 2.10. klo 9 -11. Tilaisuuden ohjelma: 9:00-10:00 Kilpailutuksen esittely 10:00-11:00 Kysymyksiä, vastauksia ja keskustelua Lämpimästi tervetuloa! title: Finland – Electrical services – Ratajohtoverkon sähkönlaatumittauspalvelu
description: MARKKINAVUOROPUHELU Markkinavuoropuhelun kohteena on valmistelussa oleva Ratajohtoverkon sähkönlaatumittauspalvelu Väyläviraston tarpeisiin. Mittauspalvelu alkaa 1.7.2027 ja sopimus tehdään 3 vuodeksi sisältäen myös option 2 vuodeksi. TAUSTAA JA TAVOITTEET Ratajohtoverkon sähkönlaatumittauspalvelu tarjoaa verkonhaltijalle (jatkossa Tilaaja) mahdollisuuden tutkia sähkönlaatuun liittyviä ilmiöitä sähkörataverkossa, selvittää ilmiöiden aiheuttamien vikaantumisten tai rikkoontumisten juurisyitä ja käyttää sähkönlaatumittausten tuottamaa tietoa tukena kunnossapito- ja investointipäätöksiä tehdessä. Sähkönlaatumittauspalvelusta saadun mittaustiedon sekä analyysien avulla seurataan muun muassa syöttöasemilla olevien yliaaltosuodattimien toimintaa. Ratajohtoverkkoon on liittyneenä Tilaajan sähkölaitteistojen lisäksi rautatieyritysten liikkuvaa kalustoa. Ratajohtoverkon nimellisjännite on 25 kV ja ratajohtoverkkoa syötetään 110 kV sähköverkosta syöttöasemien kautta. Osana sähkörataverkon käyttövarmuuden kehittämistä ja sähköradan kunnossapitoa Väyläviraston tulee kehittää sähkörataverkon sähkönlaatumittausten verkostoa, jotta eri puolilla sähkörataverkkoa ilmeneviä häiriöitä, vikoja ja vaurioita pystytään tutkimaan, paikantamaan ja ymmärtämään entistä paremmin. Sähkönlaatumittaustiedon pohjalta pystytään päättelemään ja analysoimaan ko. ilmiöitä entistä tehokkaammin ja tarkemmin. Sähkönlaatumittauspalvelun avulla mahdollistetaan sähkörataverkon sähkönlaatumittausten analysointi ja siirrettävien tilapäisten sähkönlaatumittausten toteuttaminen Väyläviraston tarpeiden mukaisesti. Sähkönlaatumittauspalvelun tuottamia raportteja ja tietoja hyödynnetään osana kunnossapitoa ja verkon käyttövarmuuden kehittämistä. Sähkönlaatumittauspalvelu sisältää seuraavat tehtävät: • Tilaajan kiinteästi asennettujen sähkönlaatumittalaitteiden etäluenta ja tulosten raportointi palveluun, johon Tilaajalla on pääsy ja josta pidetään varmuuskopiota • Tilaajan mittalaitteiden kanssa yhteensopivan etäluenta- ja raportointipalvelun tuottaminen • etäluenta- ja raportointipalvelun käyttäjätuki- ja opastus • vuosittain arviolta viisi (5) sähkönlaatumittausta, sisältäen mittarin asennuksen ja poiston Tilaajan ilmoittamissa mittauskohteissa Tilaajan omistamilla tai Toimittajan vuokraamilla siirrettävillä mittalaitteilla sekä näiden mittausten etäluenta ja raportointi kuten Tilaajan kiinteästi asennetuilla mittareilla. Tällä hetkellä on 10 mittaria käytössä, joissa kussakin joukko erilaisia mitattavia suureita ja arvoja • mobiilireitittimien (vähintään 4G) hankkiminen ja asentaminen myös Tilaajan kiinteästi asennettuihin sähkönlaatumittalaitteisiin • mittaustulosten analysointi ja kirjallisen raportin muodostaminen suoritetun mittausjakson ajalta • kirjallisten raporttien toimittaminen Tilaajan projektipankkiin. ALUSTAVA AIKATAULU Tilaajan tavoiteaikataulu markkinavuoropuhelun ja hankinnan toteuttamiselle on: - markkinavuoropuhelu lokakuussa 2026 - tarjouspyynnön julkaisu marraskuussa 2026 - tarjousten vertailu helmi- maaliskuussa 2027 - hankintapäätös ja jatko huhtikuussa 2027 ----- ILMOITUKSEN LISÄTIEDOT Tämä ilmoitus on ennakkoilmoitus. Tällä ilmoituksella ei pyydetä tarjouksia. Ennakkoilmoitukseen liittyy kutsu markkinavuoropuheluun, jolloin kaikilla hankinnasta kiinnostuneilla toimittajilla on mahdollisuus käydä hankintaa koskevaa teknistä vuoropuhelua Väyläviraston kanssa. Teknisen vuoropuhelun tarkoituksena on käydä yleisellä tasolla vuoropuhelua hankinnan kohteesta ja sen määrittämisestä. Tekninen vuoropuhelu ei sido Väylävirastoa toteuttamaan hankintaa. Tekninen vuoropuhelu ei myöskään sido toimittajaa mahdolliseen tarjouskilpailuun osallistumiseen. Tekninen vuoropuhelu järjestetään tarjouspyyntöaineiston luonnosversioiden kommentoinnin ja tilaajan hankinnan kohteeseen liittyviin kysymyksiin vastaamisen kautta. Alustava päivä tarjouspyyntöaineiston luonnosversioiden ja kysymysten toimittamiselle on 1.10.2026. Tilaaja varaa toimittajille noin kolmen viikon kommentointiajan (viikoilla 41-43). Ilmoittautumisohje: Toimittajan tulee ilmoittaa kiinnostuksensa osallistua markkinavuoropuheluun 30.9.2027 klo 12.00 mennessä lähettämällä osoitteeseen harri.alanko@vayla.fi viesti otsikolla: "Ratajohtoverkon sähkönlaatumittauspalvelu - markkinavuoropuhelu". Toimittajaa pyydetään ilmoittamaan viestissä seuraavat tiedot: - toimittajan yhteyshenkilön sähköpostiosoite Tilaaja varaa oikeuden kutsua toimittajia myös kahdenkeskisiin neuvotteluihin tai jatkaa teknistä vuoropuhelua muulla erikseen ilmoitettavalla tavalla, joista ilmoitetaan tarvittaessa myöhemmin. Tässä ennakkoilmoituksessa esitetyt kuvaukset ja hankintailmoituksen arvioitu julkaisupäivämäärä, kuten myös myöhemmin toimitettavat vuoropuhelun luonnosmateriaalit ovat alustavia ja suuntaa antavia hankinnan ennakkotietoja. Osallistuneille yrityksille ei makseta korvausta vastaamisesta tai osallistumisesta.

title: Germany – Engineering design services for mechanical and electrical installations for buildings – Sanierung und Erweiterung Grundschule Züttlingen
description: Sanierung und Erweiterung der Grundschule Züttlingen Grundlage Machbarkeitsstudie Pläne, Grundrisse und Angaben Büro Huber, Billigheim 1. Ausgangslage und Zielsetzung Die Grundschule im Möckmühler Ortsteil Züttlingen befindet sich in einem Bestandsgebäude in der Jahnstraße 5, direkt angrenzend an das Rathaus und die Kirche. Das Gebäude weist funktionale, räumliche und energetische Defizite auf, die eine umfassende Modernisierung notwendig machen. Ziel des Projekts ist die Sanierung des Bestandsgebäudes sowie eine bauliche Erweiterung, um den heutigen pädagogischen, funktionalen und energetischen Anforderungen gerecht zu werden. Es soll ein ganzheitlicher Ansatz verfolgt werden, der Umbau, Erweiterung und energetische Ertüchtigung in einem Projekt vereint. 2. Projektumfang Auf Basis einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurde nachfolgender Umfang ermittelt 2.1 Sanierung des Bestandsgebäudes Die bestehende Grundschule wird umfassend modernisiert: - Energetische Sanierung (Dämmung, Fenster, Haustechnik) - Barrierefreie Erschließung (bis auf das Dachgeschoss) - Optimierung der Raumstruktur - Modernisierung der Sanitärbereiche - Anpassung an Brandschutzmaßnahmen 2.2 Erweiterungs- und Ergänzungsbau (Neubau) Auf Basis der Machbarkeitsstudie erfolgt die Erweiterung in mehreren Gebäudeteilen und Geschossen, dabei sollen neue bzw. vergrößerte Bereiche entstehen: Erdgeschoss (EG) - Erweiterung Klassenraum 1 (F = 70 m²) - Erweiterung Klassenraum 2 (F = 73 m²) - Überdachte Pausenhoffläche (F = 74 m²) - Neues Lehrerzimmer (F = 49,86 m²) - Materiallager, Teeküche, neue WC-Anlagen - Flur- und Garderobenbereiche Obergeschoss (OG) - Erweiterung Klassenraum 3 (F = 84 m² - Erweiterung Klassenraum 4 (F = 73 m²) - Neuer Differenzierungsraum (F = 45 m²) - Schülerbibliothek (F = 27 m²) - Neue Treppenanlage und optimierte Verkehrsflächen Dachgeschoss (DG) - Schaffung eines neuen Präsentations- und Aufenthaltsbereichs (F = 72 m²) - Empore / Galerie (F = 13,5 m²) - Anpassung der Dachstruktur inkl. neuer Gaube Untergeschoss (UG) - Neuer Multifunktionsraum (F = 72,78 m²) - Essensausgabe und Essensvorbereitung - Personalraum, Technikräume, Kellerbereiche - Große Terrasse (F = 83 m²) 3. Funktionale und pädagogische Verbesserungen Mit der Sanierung und Erweiterung des Schulgebäudes soll eine moderne Lernumgebung entstehen mit: - größeren, flexiblen Klassenräumen - zusätzlichen Differenzierungs- und Gruppenräumen - einer Schülerbibliothek - einem multifunktionalen Raum für Veranstaltungen - verbesserten Lehrerarbeitsbereichen - optimierten Pausenflächen (innen und außen) Durch die Investition soll der Schulstandort im Ortsteil Züttlingen zukunftsfähig, nachhaltig und pädagogisch aufgewertet werden. 4. Wirtschaftlichkeit und Förderung Die Planung setzt bewusst auf Bauen im Bestand, um Kosten zu reduzieren und Fördermöglichkeiten zu nutzen. Im Rahmen der Machbarkeitsstudie erfolgte eine Kostenermittlung: Die Kostenschätzung nach DIN 276 ergibt: Baukosten brutto: 3.800.000 € Gesamtkosten ohne Grundstück, Außenanlagen, Ausstattung: ca. 3,8 Mio. € 5. Übergangslösung während der Bauzeit Für die Bauphase ist eine Auslagerung des Schulbetriebs notwendig. Geplant ist eine Interimslösung mit Container. 6. Fazit Das Projekt „Sanierung und Erweiterung der Grundschule Züttlingen“ stellt eine umfassende Modernisierung dar, die sowohl pädagogisch als auch baulich einen deutlichen Mehrwert schafft. Die Kombination aus Sanierung und Erweiterung ermöglicht eine nachhaltige, wirtschaftlich sinnvolle und förderfähige Lösung, die die Schule langfristig stärkt und den Standort Züttlingen attraktiv hält.

title: Ireland – Civil engineering consultancy services – Dublin City Council Single Party Framework Agreement for an Integrated Design Team for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project
description: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 8969388 – Input when notice created . Please note that this project is subject to funding.

title: Unaccompanied Asylum-Seeking Children (UASC) Support Services
description:
The Home Office (the Authority) has a statutory duty under Section 55 of the Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009 to discharge its immigration and asylum functions having regard to the need to safeguard and promote the welfare of children in the UK. 
This includes Unaccompanied Asylum-Seeking Children (UASC) who arrive in the UK and enter the immigration system without a parent or guardian.
The Support Services for UASC ensure that their immediate needs are met upon arrival in Kent, or elsewhere, prior to entering the care of a local authority. Additionally, there is a need to ensure UASC have access to information and support to help them navigate the asylum process.
The services will operate alongside, and in collaboration with the Authority and a range of other services and Authority suppliers, to enable the effective operation of the system to manage and support UASC. It is recognised that service users may require only one, or a combination of these services at any given time. Therefore, all services areas must be available, but would be delivered on an as-required basis, according to the needs of each individual case.
The core service areas are:
Service Area 1: Delivery of Services at Kent Intake Unit (KIU)
Service Area 2: Delivery of Orientation Sessions

title: End User Workspace and Hosting
description:
The End User Workspace & Hosting procurement event was to secure a single supplier to deliver both End User Workspace (EUW) and Hosting services under a single contract. The Services had to be ITIL-aligned and delivered using the Council's own ServiceNow ITSM platform, with contract aims of improving service delivery, reducing complexity, and enhance user experience through integrated support.
Key requirements of scope:
• Service Desk - Single point of contact for all ICT issues, with a focus on first-contact resolution and self-service enablement.
• Incident Management - Rapid restoration of normal service with clear ownership and root cause analysis.
• Problem Management - Identification and elimination of root causes to reduce incident recurrence.
• Change Enablement - Safe, timely implementation of changes with strong governance, TAB and CAB participation.
• Service Request Management - Efficient fulfilment of user requests via a structured service catalogue.
• Service Configuration & Asset Management - Accurate tracking of assets and configuration items using ServiceNow CMDB.
• Release & Deployment Management - Controlled rollout of new
software and updates, including packaging and testing.
• Availability & Capacity Management - Ensuring services meet
performance and uptime targets, with proactive planning.
• Monitoring & Event Management - Real-time monitoring and alerting to detect and respond to issues before they impact users.
• Security Management - ISO27001-compliant controls, vulnerability management, and incident response.
• Service Continuity Management - Disaster recovery planning and testing to ensure resilience.
• Knowledge Management - Centralised, structured knowledge base to support selfservice and efficient resolution.
• Supplier & Risk Management - Collaboration across multiple suppliers with shared risk registers and joint governance.
• Continual Improvement - Ongoing service enhancements tracked via a formal improvement plan and CMMI assessments.
• Project & Portfolio Management - Support for operational,
enhancement, and strategic projects with defined governance
End User Workspace (EUW):
• Service Desk (first-line support, triage, escalation, and resolution).
• Deskside Support (field engineering across 66 sites).
• Second Line Support (technical escalation, patching, anti-virus and infrastructure support
• Device lifecycle management (builds, refresh, repairs).
• Microsoft 365 and Windows 11 environment support.
• Knowledge management and training provision.
Service Management Expectations
• Operate within a SIAM model with strong collaboration across
suppliers.
• Use of ServiceNow for all ITSM functions (incident, problem, change, asset, etc.).
• Monthly and annual reporting, SLA/KPI tracking, and continual
improvement.
• Supplier must achieve CMMI Level 3 within 6 months.
The contract is over 7 years (including extensions), with published contract value of £13,800,000 (inclusive of VAT)

title: Residential and Nursing Care Homes for Adults - Framework Agreement
description:
Nottinghamshire County Council is procuring a Framework Agreement for the provision of residential and/or nursing care home services for adults. The Council intends to appoint multiple successful bidders as Providers under the Framework.
The Framework will support individuals whose primary support needs include learning disabilities, autism, mental health needs, physical disabilities, brain injuries and sensory impairments. Services may include standard placements, short breaks, emergency placements, forensic provision and exceptional and highly specialist care arrangements.
The service is primarily for adults. The Council may also use the Framework to commission provision for young people aged 16 or 17, provided that the relevant home satisfies all applicable registration, policy and regulatory requirements, including those of the Care Quality Commission and/or Ofsted.
For older adults, typically those aged 65 and over, the Council will ordinarily commission residential provision through alternative contracts that the Council has developed specifically for residential care for older adults. It is anticipated that this Framework will only be used for people aged 65 years and over in exceptional circumstances where suitable provision cannot be identified via the alternative contracts.
Most placements are expected to be within the seven districts of Nottinghamshire. However, the Council may commission placements outside of Nottinghamshire where required.
Bidders are advised that, following the UK Government's publication of the English Devolution White Paper in December 2024, a programme of Local Government Reorganisation ("LGR") is underway which may affect the governance, boundaries and/or legal status of the Council during the term of any Framework or Call-Off Contract entered pursuant to this procurement. As a consequence of LGR, any Framework or Call-Off Contract may be required to be transferred, assigned or novated (in whole or in part) to one or more successor authorities or other public bodies established as part of LGR, in accordance with applicable legislation.
The Council intends to establish this Framework for an initial term of 6 years, with the option to extend for up to two further periods of 24 months (6+2+2). The maximum potential duration of the Framework is therefore 10 years.
Appointment to the Framework does not guarantee a Provider any volume of placements or minimum level of expenditure.
The Council reserves the right, at its discretion, to advertise one or more further opportunities to admit additional Providers to the Framework. No dates have been set for any such opportunities. Any future opportunity will be separately advertised and conducted in accordance with the applicable procurement requirements. A bidder that is unsuccessful in this procurement may submit a new tender in response to any future advertised opportunity but a bidder that has been successful will not need to re-apply. For the avoidance of doubt this Framework is not an Open Framework within the meaning of the Procurement Act 2023.
Full details of the requirements are set out in the procurement documents.

title: Peatland ACTION FW02 Field Ecologists Framework
description:
NatureScot work to improve our natural environment in Scotland and inspire everyone to care more about it. We work to ensure that all nature in Scotland - our key habitats and landscapes, all our green space and our native species - are maintained, enhanced and bring us benefits. Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency.
Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions.
Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water.
Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss.
The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.

title: CPT_26_03 IT Service management (ITSM)
description:
The National Audit Office (NAO) is the UK's independent public spending watchdog. It supports Parliament in holding government to account and helps improve public services through high quality audit and assurance work.
The NAO sought to appoint an experienced supplier to provide an enterprise-grade IT Service Management (ITSM) solution and associated support services for internal users across the organisation.
The requirement included the provision, implementation, configuration, and ongoing support of an ITSM platform capable of supporting core ITSM processes, including incident management, service requests, change management, asset and configuration management, workflow automation, reporting, and governance. The solution is required to be scalable, configurable, and proportionate to the NAO's operational needs, and capable of supporting multiple internal functional areas.
The procurement sought a supplier capable of delivering a controlled transition from the incumbent system, including secure data migration, integration with the NAO's Microsoft-based digital estate, and service readiness activities, with minimal disruption to business operations. The solution is required to provide an intuitive user experience, configurable workflows, and accessible reporting, without reliance on complex development or ongoing external consultancy.
The requirement also included robust ongoing platform support, including routine updates, security maintenance and patching, and effective vulnerability management and remediation. This includes the ability to identify, assess, track, prioritise, and remediate security vulnerabilities affecting the ITSM platform and its components, supported by appropriate controls, governance, and reporting.
The successful supplier is required to provide assurance that vulnerabilities are managed in line with recognised industry good practice and the NAO's information security and risk management requirements.
In addition, the procurement sought a supplier able to demonstrate a sustainable product roadmap and ongoing service support model to ensure long-term service continuity, platform resilience, and alignment with the NAO's future operational and digital requirements.
The contract will commence on Monday 2 November 2026 and includes an initial six-month mobilisation and implementation period, with service go-live anticipated from Tuesday 1 June 2027.
The initial contract term is three (3) years until Friday 31 May 2030, with options to extend for up to two further periods of twelve (12) months, up to a maximum contract end date of Monday 31 May 2032.
The contract has been awarded with a maximum value of up to £1.8 million inclusive of VAT over the full potential five-year term.
