title: NLP Condition Survey Programme
description:
North Lanarkshire Properties (NLP) has a requirement to update its asset management register in respect of the condition of its property estate to ensure compliance with its statutory and legal obligations and to inform a multiyear investment strategy. The resulting dataset will form the foundation of NLP's future asset management, lifecycle investment, maintenance planning and portfolio optimisation activities. NLP manages a portfolio of approximately 990 assets. The current condition survey programme is anticipated to cover approximately 672 operational property assets, excluding ground lease assets and other property categories outside the scope of this procurement. Information is required on the following split:
- 4 Business Centres
- 28 Offices
- 233 Retail
- 402 Industrial
- 5 Miscellaneous
- 672 Total
The procurement is for the appointment of suitably qualified and experienced building surveyor (a “Contractor”) to carry out condition surveys across a number of properties within the NLP portfolio.
The aim of the resulting Agreement is to obtain by means of visual inspection consistent, accurate and actionable information regarding the physical condition, statutory compliance, risks, and investment needs of the defined buildings within the estate. Applying the findings to inform a data driven investment strategy to maximise portfolio value. The objectives are to:
- Establish the current physical condition of each property asset defined.
- Identify defects, risks, and compliance issues.
- Provide an assessment of each asset’s life.
- Provide prioritised maintenance actions. Year 1-5 with year 1 being the faults in most urgent need of attention.
- Provide costs as a basis for estimating and to identify the level of funding required for future capital and revenue expenditure.
- Provide sufficient information to allow a maintenance programme to be developed over a planned period that will support operational planning and asset management decision making
- Deliver the condition survey in accordance with the following mandatory professional standards:
a. RICS Building Surveying Standards & Guidance
b. RICS Surveying Safely
c. RICS New Rules of Measurement (NRM) for cost estimation
d. PFI Asset Condition Playbook (2025) – survey methodology and reporting guidance
e. General Implementation Guidance (2025) for asset condition hand back surveys
f. Centre of Best Practice (CoBP) specification (where applicable)
The purpose of the commission is to provide portfolio-wide condition intelligence to support NLP asset management and investment decisions through Level 1 visual, non-intrusive surveys.

Alongside this, the service offers in-depth specialist advice through a single open door access system, enabling coordinated and consistent support. Referral-led services are designed for clients who may struggle to access advice through standard routes and require more targeted, intensive support due to multiple and layered issues. This includes stabilising financial situations through specialist debt advice, income maximisation and budgeting support, as well as providing representation at welfare benefit appeals where required. The service works collaboratively with local authority services including social workers, support workers, Resilient Families Teams and homelessness prevention services, to plan and deliver support together, ensuring shared outcomes for clients and a seamless and joined up client journey. All advice is delivered by highly skilled advisers, with debt advice provided by FCA-registered staff and subject to robust quality assurance processes. The service holds the Advice Quality Standard (AQS) across Consumer, Debt, Welfare Benefits, Health and Community Care, Disability, Older People, and Students and Young People, as well as the IAQF quality standard, ensuring high-quality specialist advice for those requiring additional and targeted support.

title: Cleaning of Council  Vehicles and Waste Receptacles
description:
The London Borough of Barnet require a cleaning service to wash the Council’s fleet vehicles and plant, food waste bins within our town centres and ad-hoc washing of containers in different sizes within the borough.
The cleaning service will be divided into 2 LOTS 
LOT 1 Vehicle, Plant and Equipment Washing
LOT 2 Container Washing Services - Regular, scheduled washing of town centre food waste bins and Ad-hoc washing services for all container types and waste streams
Vehicle, Plant and Equipment Washing 
The London Borough of Barnet requires a supplier to deliver comprehensive vehicle washing and cleaning services for its mixed fleet of operational vehicles and plant.
The services include routine, periodic and ad hoc washing for light and heavy vehicles including, refuse collection vehicles, sweepers, winter maintenance gritters, buses and tippers, and preparation of vehicles for MOT and chassis inspections to DVSA standards. Volumes and frequencies are indicative and may vary throughout the contract to reflect operational requirements.
Services will be delivered primarily from the Council’s wash bay facilities at Oakleigh Road Depot. The supplier is responsible for providing all labour, cleaning materials, equipment and PPE, and must comply with all health and safety, environmental, and COSHH regulations. 
Container Washing 
Barnet provides a range of containers of varying types and sizes for the collection of general waste, food waste, recycling, and garden waste. This service requirement covers the washing and cleaning of waste containers used across the borough.
The bin washing service will include:
•Scheduled washing of all town centre food waste bins, and
•An ad-hoc washing service for containers of various sizes, ranging from 200 litre's to 1,100 litre's, and across all waste streams (general waste, recycling, and food waste).
There is a statutory requirement for all Local Authorities in England to implement separate collections of food waste and recycling across all residential property types. To meet this obligation, the council has installed a number of communal food waste bins across the borough, predominantly serving flatted properties within town centres. These bins require cleaning in accordance with an agreed schedule to maintain hygiene standards and operational efficiency.

Gauge current market interest, capacity, and capabilities across service delivery models

Full and seamless transition
Full management processing of monthly payrolls.

Pay scales - To be able to cope with Teaching pay scales, support staff pay scale, apprenticeships plus off-scale pay grades where needed
Pay awards and increments To be able to apply pay awards to current staff automatically
For back pay to be automatically calculated
To be able to chose to backdated pay awards to some leavers
To be able to apply increments at different dates for some staff
To be able to apply 'No Increment' for specific contracts
Integration capability with existing HR and Finance systems and simple data input
Integration with MIS - currently Arbor - to provide a 'single source of truth' from which reports and data flows
Access for Employees - To efficiently be able to download payslips, P60s etc.

Knowledge and experience working with MATs in the education sector.

title: London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme
description:
London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme
Indicative Contract Value: Up to £2900,000 excl. VAT 
Contract Duration: 1 March 2027 – 31 March 2029 with option to extend to 31 March 2030.
This market warming session will be delivered jointly with the VRU's Tertiary Service. The two programmes form complementary elements of the VRU's tertiary violence reduction offer for young people affected by violence and exploitation. While the Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme will provide specialist youth workers embedded across Mayoral youth club settings to identify risk, build trusted relationships and connect young people to support, the redesigned tertiary service will provide intensive, specialist and longer-term support for young people experiencing established, escalating, or entrenched violence and exploitation. Together, these programmes aim to strengthen London's pathway of support for vulnerable young people through earlier identification, stronger partnership working and improved access to specialist interventions.
The London Violence Reduction Unit. The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. 
The VRU invests in interventions at critical moments to keep young people safe in and out of school and at the key touchpoints that influence a young person’s journey; early years and families, education, positive opportunities, youth work, and communities and place. The Mayor of London has increased investment in London’s Youth Clubs. Across 32 London boroughs and the City of London, a £30 million programme is funding youth clubs to extend and expand their existing offer into weekday evenings, weekends, and school holidays – when young people need safe spaces the most – and provide specialist support to those facing the greatest challenges. 
This investment strengthens youth clubs as trusted community spaces – where connections are made, young people feel safe and valued, and opportunities are created, all with support from trusted adults. The programme will help community organisations reach more young people aged 14–24 years old and strengthen the quality and sustainability of their provision. It will do this by delivering an increased universal, open-access provision, and targeted specialised support for young people facing greater challenges. 
For more information on this specific Youth Clubs programme, please see The Mayor's investment in youth clubs | London City Hall.  
Safety is a core outcome of this Mayoral investment in youth clubs. Whilst it will provide universal youth provision alongside targeted support, some young people will require specialist interventions beyond the expertise and capacity of local delivery partners.  
It has been agreed that a London-wide Safety Offer sits alongside the core Youth Clubs programme.   
Drawing on its regional oversight and networks across London, alongside seven years of experience and expertise in commissioning impactful violence reduction programmes, the VRU is looking to commission a specialist organisation to provide additional capacity to connect with the Mayoral funded youth clubs across the 32 boroughs.   
This provider will deliver a pan-London service providing specialised youth workers, who will be embedded across the 33 Mayoral Youth Clubs, who will provide targeted support for young people experiencing or at risk of violence and exploitation, offer support to enhance feelings of safety and boost connections and pathways into wider specialist services.  
Description of the Service
The future service will operate as a pan-London tertiary intervention with strengthened local delivery through dedicated, specialised youth workers for each Mayoral Youth Club area, with a minimum of 2:1 borough to youth worker ratio.   
The aim of the Safety Programme will be to provide a visible, connected and meaningful presence across the 33 Mayoral Youth Clubs to support children and young people who are affected by, or vulnerable to, violence and exploitation. Its purpose is to identify those at risk (working with the youth club provider), provide direct support, make referrals into appropriate services and interventions and enhance feelings of safety. 
The VRU will commission a specialist organisation to deliver the Safety Programme. This additional resource will establish a network of specialist practitioners who will work alongside funded Youth Club partnerships, providing additional capacity and expertise to identify, engage, and support young people who face higher levels of risk. They will work with local partnerships to build trusted relationships with young people, provide targeted interventions and support, and help young people access wider opportunities and services.  
The Safety Programme will operate as a pan-London network, enabling practitioners to share learning, insight and effective practice across boroughs and communities. This will help strengthen local responses to emerging issues, support partnership working and contribute to the wider learning and development of the programme.    
The service will contribute to the Violence Reduction Unit's public health approach to preventing and reducing violence in London, by preventing harm, identifying and addressing risk factors, and improving outcomes for children and young people.
The service is expected to: 
•Provide specialised youth workers who build trusted relationships with children and young people who may be at risk of harm, supporting them to access the Mayoral youth club as a safe space.
•Provide a regular presence within the Mayoral youth clubs, working with youth club staff to identify young people with existing or potential risk and need for further support.
•Assess needs and vulnerabilities of children and young people identified as at risk, including those impacted by exploitation, extra familial harm, online and digital harms and domestic abuse.  
•Provide targeted support and engagement, including 1-1 support for children and young people at greater risk of harm, holding casework where appropriate.  Prioritise tertiary young people, with support extending to secondary young people as capacity allows.
•Facilitate access to appropriate statutory, community and specialist support services through referrals and where needed building connections and support pathways, including connecting with families /parents /guardians as appropriate to ensure a whole family approach.
•Undertake contextual safeguarding assessments, working with the youth club providers and local authority partners, to assess contextual risk of youth club and surrounding environments, and deliver peer group contextual interventions where appropriate. 
•Deliver workshops and group work aimed at increasing safety of young people attending the youth club and support awareness of risk, based on identified local concerns/need. 
•Work collaboratively with mayoral youth clubs and wider statutory agencies to strengthen the connections and pathways between the many safety programmes held both by VCS and public authorities; and do so through a place-based approach.   
•Strengthen local partnership responses to emerging safeguarding and violence-related issues through sharing understanding of emerging risks, contextual safeguarding and issues impacting children and young people in local areas.   
•Operate as a pan-London network, share intelligence and effective practice across London through a connected practitioner network. 
•Contribute to reductions in vulnerability and harm and improving outcomes for children and young people.  
•Embed trauma-informed practice, lived experience and cultural sensitivity throughout service delivery. 
Target Audience
Young people aged 14 to 24 living in London who are identified as experiencing, or are at significant risk of violence, criminal exploitation, sexual exploitation and related harms. Scope of Delivery
The provider will be expected to deliver a consistent pan-London service of support for children and young people at risk across the 33 mayoral youth club partnerships, through strong local relationships with Mayoral Youth Club Providers, Local Authorities, safeguarding partners, community organisations and specialist services.
Core elements are expected to include specialist youth engagement and support, identifying and assessing needs, facilitating targeted referrals and engagement with wider services, contextual safeguarding and where appropriate, casework.

Specialist Youth Work and Engagement 
The Safety Programme seeks to enhance the capacity of Youth Club partnerships to prevent violence and exploitation, improve safeguarding and ensure young people receive timely, appropriate support.

description:
London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) Tertiary Service , formally known as Violence & Exploitation Support Service (VESS)
Indicative Contract Value: Up to £11,493,534 excl. VAT 
Contract Duration: 1 June 2027 – 31 May 2029 with option to extend to 31 May 2030
This market warming session will be delivered jointly with the VRU's forthcoming Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme. The two programmes form complementary elements of the VRU's tertiary violence reduction offer for young people affected by violence and exploitation. While the Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme will provide specialist youth workers embedded across Mayoral youth club settings to identify risk, build trusted relationships and connect young people to support, the redesigned tertiary service will provide intensive, specialist and longer-term support for young people experiencing established, escalating, or entrenched violence and exploitation. 
Together, these programmes aim to strengthen London's pathway of support for vulnerable young people through earlier identification, stronger partnership working and improved access to specialist interventions.
The London Violence Reduction Unit
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. 
The VRU invests in interventions at critical moments to keep young people safe in and out of school and at the key touchpoints that influence a young person’s journey; early years and families, education, positive opportunities, youth work, and communities and place.
Project Background
The Violence and Exploitation Support Service (VESS), also known as The Safe Place, was launched in June 2024 to provide coordinated, holistic support for children, young people and families affected by violence and exploitation in London. The service provides specialist support for young people aged 11 to 25 affected by violence and exploitation through an alliance of organisations delivering housing support, advocacy, mentoring, mental health support and other specialist interventions. The current contract expires in June 2027. 
Young people aged 11 to 25 living in London who are experiencing, or are at significant risk of, entrenched violence, criminal exploitation, sexual exploitation and related harms. Particular consideration will be given to young adults, young people with complex safeguarding needs, and those facing barriers to engagement with mainstream services.
Following stakeholder engagement, needs analysis and review of learning from current delivery, the VRU intends to procure a redesigned tertiary service focused on young people experiencing established, escalating or entrenched violence and exploitation. The future model reflects evidence highlighting the importance of trusted relationships, trauma informed practice, specialist support, and strong local partnerships.
Key themes emerging from this work include:
•The need for a clearer focus on young people experiencing entrenched violence and exploitation.
•Greater emphasis on trusted adult relationships and long-term support.
•Stronger transitional safeguarding support for young adults aged 18 to 25.
•Improved local partnership and borough-level integration.
•Enhanced specialist provisions around housing, mental health, education, employment and family support.
•Improved referral pathways and engagement approaches for young people who are least likely to access traditional services.
•Greater recognition of sexual exploitation alongside criminal exploitation.
•Increased focus on neurodiversity, inclusion, and cultural competence. 
The redesigned service is expected to become the VRU's flagship tertiary intervention for young people at risk, and those experiencing the highest levels of vulnerability to violence and exploitation
Description of the Service
The future service will operate as a pan-London tertiary intervention with strengthened local delivery through cluster-based arrangements. It is expected to provide intensive, flexible and relationship-based support; specialist expertise in housing, mental health, education, employment and training; support for young adults aged 18 to 25; specialist responses for girls and young women; and improved pathways for criminal and sexual exploitation. A team-around-the-worker approach will support case workers with specialist advocates and navigators.
The service is expected to:
•Provide dedicated lead practitioners who build trusted relationships with young people.
•Deliver flexible, community-based support in locations that are accessible and comfortable for young people.
•Operate through a partnership model that combines core casework with specialist expertise.
•Strengthen local partnerships and referral pathways while maintaining a pan-London offer.
•Support young people through a long-term journey of engagement, stabilisation, change, and sustained outcomes.
•Embed trauma-informed practice, lived experience and cultural competence throughout service delivery. 
Target Audience
Young people aged 11 to 25 living in London who are experiencing, or are at significant risk of, or currently entrenched in violence, criminal exploitation, sexual exploitation. 
Scope of Delivery
The provider partnership will be expected to deliver a consistent pan-London service whilst maintaining strong local relationships with boroughs, safeguarding partners, community organisations and specialist services. Core elements are expected to include targeted referrals, intensive casework, housing support, family support, education and employment pathways, mental health navigation, support for neurodiverse young people, transitional safeguarding and county lines rescue capability.
Indicative Service Model
While the final specification has not yet been developed, current thinking suggests the service may include:
Core Specialist Casework
Dedicated Violence and Exploitation Practitioners providing intensive support and care for coordination for young people. 
Specialist Pathways and Expertise
Potential specialist functions may include:
•Housing and accommodation support.
•Mental health and therapeutic support.
•Education, Employment and Training (EET).
•SEND and neurodiversity expertise.
•Family support.
•Support for girls and young women.
•Transitional safeguarding for young adults aged 18-25. 
County Lines Rescue Function
The recommissioned service is expected to retain a county lines rescue and relocation capability, although the final model is currently under consideration.
Timeframe: The contract is expected to commence on 1 June 2027 following a mobilisation period from March to May 2027. The initial term will be two years with an option to extend for one additional year.

title: Provision, Installation and Operation of Christmas Attractions in Albert Square Manchester
description:
Manchester's annual festive programme is one of the most celebrated in Europe, attracting millions of visitors and creating a vibrant seasonal atmosphere across the city. As part of Manchester City Council's commitment to enhancing the city's cultural and event offering, we seek competent proposals for the delivery of Albert Square's Christmas attraction from 2027 onwards.
Historically, Manchester's Christmas activities have included the award-winning Christmas Markets, an ice rink at Cathedral Gardens, and a range of family-friendly installations. With the full reopening of Albert Square following Town Hall regeneration works, the Council aims to create a world-class festive destination that complements the existing city-wide offer and strengthens Manchester's reputation as a leading winter destination.
The requirement is for a Christmas attraction in Albert Square, operating seven days a week during the festive period (November to early January), featuring the following core elements:
An ice rink, managed and installed by the appointed operator, providing a safe and authentic skating experience for visitors. The proposal should include rink size, capacity, and associated facilities such as skate hire and changing areas.
A varied food and beverage offering, aligned with the Manchester Christmas Markets ethos, catering for diverse tastes and dietary requirements while delivering a sense of place.
Family-friendly festive attractions, which may include (but are not limited to) an ice bar, curling rink, ice sculptures, an observatory wheel, rides, funfair, or other creative installations that enhance the visitor experience and differentiate Albert Square from other UK festive destinations.
Seasonal theming and dressing, including Christmas decorations, lighting features, projections, music, and branded signage to create a cohesive and welcoming environment.
The successful operator will be responsible for full site management, including stewarding, first aid, staffing, security, emergency procedures, and compliance with all licensing and health and safety requirements. Marketing and promotion of the attraction will also form part of the operator's obligations, working in partnership with Manchester City Council to maximise visitor engagement.
It is anticipated that to deliver these elements, the winning contractor will need to source equipment and collaborate with specialist providers where necessary. All proposals should demonstrate creativity, operational competence, and a commitment to sustainability, social value, and community engagement.

title: Transportation and Processing of Dry Mixed Recycling
description:
The Council requires a contractor to provide the collection, haulage, sorting, processing and onward marketing/reprocessing of approximately 18,500 tonnes of Dry Mixed Recycling (DMR) per annum, collected from approximately 160,000 residential properties through the Council's kerbside recycling service. Annual tonnage is expected to increase towards approximately 20,000 tonnes per annum.
The DMR will be supplied by the Council at Federation Road Transfer Station, Burslem, Stoke-on-Trent, ST6 4HU, or an alternative Council-nominated location within North Staffordshire where required. The Contractor must provide sufficient haulage capacity to collect the material, currently approximately three loaded trailers per day, Monday to Thursday, with additional capacity to manage seasonal and Christmas peaks. The Contractor must provide and maintain the required empty trailer capacity at the Council's nominated delivery point.
The Contractor must transport the DMR to a suitably licensed and permitted processing facility, where it must be sorted and processed into recyclable material streams suitable for onward sale and reprocessing. The resulting Sorted Output Materials (SOM) must be transported to suitably licensed merchants, reprocessors or other approved end destinations.
Non-recyclable materials, contamination and process residues must be managed in accordance with the waste hierarchy, with the service designed to maximise diversion from landfill. Energy from Waste should be used for contaminants and process residues where practicable.
The Contractor must provide suitable licensed and permitted processing facilities, contingency arrangements, certified weighing facilities and full traceability of the DMR from collection through processing to its final destination. The service must include monthly reporting of tonnage, material composition, contamination, processing destinations and weighbridge information, together with waste composition analysis.
The service must be delivered in compliance with all applicable waste, environmental and permitting legislation, including the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, Environmental Protection Act 1990 and Environmental Permitting Regulations 2010.
Any alternative processing or contingency arrangements required to maintain service continuity must be provided at no additional cost to the Council.
Summary:
What is required: collection, haulage, sorting, processing and marketing/reprocessing of DMR.
Amount: approximately 18,500 tonnes per year, increasing towards 20,000 tonnes.
Where/how supplied by the Council: Federation Road Transfer Station, with an alternative North Staffordshire location if required.
How the contractor must supply the service: approximately 3 loaded trailers per day, Monday-Thursday, sufficient trailer capacity, processing at licensed facilities, sorting into recyclable streams and onward delivery to licensed end destinations.
How non-recyclables are dealt with: waste hierarchy, maximum landfill diversion and EfW where practicable.
Key delivery requirements: licensed facilities, contingency, weighing, traceability and reporting

description:
Swindon Borough Council invites you to contribute to Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) in relation to providing Vacant Property Repairs (Voids) works to its housing stock.
The Council intends on establishing a framework of up to three contractors to deliver Vacant Property Repairs (Voids) works over an initial framework period of 24 months with an option to extend by up to 12 months. The estimated contract commencement date is 14th January 2027.
Swindon Borough Council has a housing stock of approximately 10,500 properties across the Borough plus a number of sheltered accommodation properties (if required), of which approximately 600 properties are void each year. Vacant properties may require refurbishment, general maintenance, repair and improvements to return them for re-letting on line with Swindon’s Re-let standard. The works can range from minor repairs to major capital works requiring full property renovation, depending on the age of the property and condition upon return.
Of the approximate 600 void properties each year, approximately 250 properties per year are refurbished by the Council’s in-house team.
A further circa 175 properties are refurbished by an external contractor under a term contract.
For the remaining circa 175 properties, the Council is proposing to establish a framework consisting of up to three contractors to deliver the required works on those properties and, upon completion, handed back to the Council for allocation to prospective tenants.
Details of the proposed format for call-offs is provided in the PME Questionnaire.
Information of the work types required under this framework is provided within the PME Questionnaire.

description:
The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) seeks to commission an external consultant to undertake an independent programme level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan 2025-2030.
The evaluation will assess the design, implementation, and impact of a complex, multi-strand programme delivered between August 2025 and March 2030. This will include directly funded activities, wider activities mobilised through the programme and selected aligned activities where appropriate and supported by the available evidence. 
The commissioned evaluation is intended as a cross-cutting programme-level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan as a whole. It is recognised that individual projects, interventions and delivery activity within the wider programme will be subject to separate monitoring, evaluation and research activity commissioned by the North East MSA or undertaken by delivery partners. 
The evaluation will synthesise evidence generated through proportionate project level evaluations (including light touch monitoring and in depth project deep dives) to provide a coherent, programme wide assessment and will not be responsible for conducting primary project-level evaluations, except where explicitly agreed. This will support strategic assurance, learning and decision making, and inform future iterations of the Action Plan and wider North East MSA and regional policy and investment decisions.
The programme-level evaluation will therefore consider both the evidence relating to individual interventions and the combined contribution of the wider programme towards the intended outcomes of the Child Poverty Action Plan.
The programme‑level evaluation will also seek to determine the degree to which reducing child poverty has been embedded as a cross-cutting theme across North East MSA activity, and that of partners. This will include examining how the Child Poverty Reduction Unit and the regional Child Poverty Action Plan have influenced strategic priorities, programme and project design, funding and delivery decisions, and whether they have contributed to changes in policies, practices and activities beyond those directly funded through the programme.

title: Undercliffs NNR Humble Glades Holm Oak felling
description:
The contractor is required to carry out safe felling and removal of all spray marked trees in the project area, the Humble Glades. This is the equivalent of approximately 80 medium-size trees, approximately 40m3 of timber, although the actual number of trees may be higher. There are a small number of Turkey Oak and Pine that are included in the felling contract but 90% of the trees are Holm Oak. The trees need to be safely felled and then processed. The majority of the timber felled needs to be burnt on site following instructions from Natural England concerning location and number of firesites. The cut stumps of all felled trees need to be treated with a Glyphosate based herbicide to prevent re-growth.
The Axmouth to Lyme Regis Undercliffs NNR is a remote and wild coastal landslip. The worksite is located a 20-30 minute walk from the nearest vehicle access. The terrain across the NNR includes steep, uneven and sometimes difficult ground. The worksite is similar in terrain, on uneven, challenging and sometimes steep ground.
Contractors will be required to hold and submit relevant chainsaw, herbicide and first aid certification, including felling and processing of medium-size trees (380mm to 760mm / up to twice bar length). Contractors must wear all relevant PPE at all times. No lone working at any time. The contractor must hold and submit a copy of their public liability insurance.
It is a requirement that contractors undertake a site visit prior to submitting a tender or quote unless they are already familiar with the site. This can be arranged with Natural England please contact tom.sunderland@naturalengland.org.uk .
A thorough Risk Assessment will need to be drawn up and agreed with Natural England before any work starts.

title: Control Software
description: For this project We have 6 modules. Each module is made up of 3 stages. These stages are (1) an x-y stage, (2) a tilt goniometric stage, and (3) rotational stage. The links to these stages and the control box can be seen in the attached supporting document. The difference between our stages and the COTS stages is that each stage has a different motor to the COTS item (integrated 485 bus-type closed-loop stepper driver, IRS42E-K02, manual available). All modules are controlled via a single controller box. The controller box has power and user instructions from control software (via RS232 to USB cable) as inputs and has six output cables, each connected to one of the modules (RS232 to RS232). Each output cable is limited to 2m length. The cable from the controller connects to the bottom most stage of the module, that is the x-stage. The x-stage is then connected to the y-stage via a RS232 cable. The y-stage is connected to the goniometric stage via a RS232 cable. Finally, the goniometric stage is connected to the rotational stage via a RS232 cable. In this way, a controller with 6 outputs controls 6x4=24 motors. This setup is shown in the diagram and a picture of a single module is also provided on the attached supporting document. The control signal is sent via the control box to the desired module. If the control signal is not for the x-stage, the control signal is passed up the chain, and so on. We need the control software to interface with our existing hardware to control the 6 modules. The solution could interface with the existing control box, or alternatively provide a new controller to interface with the 6 modules. The requirements above are for the software/control of the 6 modules.

title: Supply of HLA Sequencing Systems
description:
NHS Blood & Transplant (NHSBT) Histocompatibility & Immunogenetics function intends to undertake a Procurement Act 2023 tender exercise for the supply of HLA sequencing systems.
Histocompatibility & Immunogenetics (H&I) is a strategic business function of NHSBT, providing testing and support in transplantation, specialised transfusion including the supply of selected blood products, immunogenetics, platelet and granulocyte immunology.
Services are supplied through a national network of six laboratories across England. Building on our strengths as a national provider, NHSBT’s strategic aim is for its diagnostic services to become the preferred provider and supplier of choice for these services in the NHS in England. We would like to work with future suppliers to realise this ambition and to perform HLA typing in an efficient, timely and cost-effective manner to meet the demands and expectations of our customers and the patients we serve.
Prior to commencing a formal procurement process and to help inform our strategy, NHSBT is seeking to engage with suppliers of commercially available HLA sequencing systems. Our current contract ends in August 2028 and NHSBT would like to improve our knowledge of all current and future systems available in the marketplace. This will aid identification of opportunities and gauge market interest in this field.
We require HLA typing systems to cover the following:
· Allelic Test Kits SHOULD detect and uniquely identify all alleles of the HLA-A, B, C, DRB1, DRB3/4/5, DQA1, DQB1, DPA1 and DPB1 loci at the level of resolution that additionally defines the third field according to WHO nomenclature by at least resolving all ambiguities resulting from: (1) polymorphisms located within the exons coding for HLA class I and class II proteins and (2) that encompass a null allele wherever the polymorphism is located.
· The optimal solution SHOULD define fourth field level resolution.
· We are not restricting which sequencing platform the allelic test kits are compatible with, however HLA typing should be completed within 72 hours of the start of the process.
NB: Procurement of the above systems may be managed by individual tenders.
It is NHSBT's intention to hold pre-procurement engagement meetings the week of 21OCT2026 to 23OCT2026 these will be held remotely, the date to be confirmed. To enable NHSBT to finalise arrangements (e.g. send meeting details and agree time slots) for the supplier engagement meetings, interested organisations are required to send an expression of interest via email to coco.otiotio@nhsbt.nhs.uk by no later than 17:00 hrs (GMT) on 09OCT2026. This should include a list of your potential attendees and a brief overview (or a website link) of the Goods / Services which might be offered. Please include options, if available, to offer a managed service contract.
No business whatsoever is guaranteed under any resulting framework agreement or contract, and there is no guarantee that any framework agreement or contract will be put in place in relation to this notice. No compensation etc. will be paid if a tender or resulting framework agreement is withdrawn for any reason. Bidders should take part in this process only on the basis that they fully understand and accept this position.
It should be noted that this procurement exercise may allow other Health authorities to utilise any contracts/ framework agreements awarded.

description:
University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust (UHL) is commencing a programme of Pre- Market Engagement in relation to the future operation of a new Urgent Treatment Centre (UTC) located at Leicester Royal Infirmary (LRI).
UHL is currently undertaking a significant programme of investment in its urgent and emergency care estate, including the development of a new purpose-built UTC at

The proposed UTC will provide assessment and treatment for patients presenting with minor illness and injury and will work alongside existing urgent and emergency care services across Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland.

One of the options under consideration is the engagement of an external provider to support delivery of elements of the service. Before any decisions are made, the Trust wishes to

title: High-Throughput Experimentation (HTE) Software for Drug Discovery
description: HTE is a field of chemistry that expanded exponentially in the past five years, and most pharmaceutical companies are currently using it in their workflows. This methodology allows multi-parameter optimisation of chemical reactions but also synthesis of multiple compounds (96 to 384) on a small-scale using plate chemistry. Combined with the implementation of Direct-to-Biology (D2B) approaches, which involves the direct testing of non-purified mixtures, biological data is obtained faster. The combination of these methods greatly improves the Design, Make, Test, and Analyse (DMTA) cycle.

title: National Parking Platform
description:
Guildford Borough Council intends to join the National Parking Platform (NPP), a not-for-profit, government-backed initiative designed to modernise and simplify parking payments across participating local authorities. The NPP provides an open and interoperable platform that enables multiple parking service providers to connect to a single national parking ecosystem, allowing motorists to use their preferred parking application when paying for parking rather than being restricted to a single provider.
Through integration with the NPP, the Council will offer users greater choice, improved accessibility, and a more consistent customer experience across participating locations. The platform operates through a transaction-fee funding model and provides a centralised mechanism through which multiple approved parking service providers can facilitate parking payments on behalf of the Council.
As part of the service, participating providers will collect parking charges, undertake transaction processing and monthly reconciliations, and remit all parking revenue due to the Council in accordance with the agreed operating and settlement arrangements. The solution supports improved interoperability within the parking sector while maintaining the Council's control over parking tariffs and revenue.

title: CEFAS26-11 Framework for Next Generation Sequencing Services
description:
Cefas are seeking to establish a Framework for the provision of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) services, for a variety of NGS analyses methods, to support the delivery of numerous and varied research programmes that are utilising genomics.
The framework is split into 4 Lots and Suppliers can bid for any number of Lots. Cefas intends to award up to 5 Contracts for each Lot, based on Suppliers meeting the required technical and pricing evaluation criteria. Cefas will then call-off from the framework for individual project requirements, as set out in the full Specification of Requirement document in the Bidder Pack. If a Supplier is awarded multiple Lots, one Contract will be awarded to cover the relevant Lots.
The Contract implementation is expected to start in August 2026 for a period of 3 years with the option to extend for 2 further periods of 12 months each.
Prices will be fixed for the initial 3 year period of the Contract. Prices may then be increased on an annual basis if the Contract is extended, in line with CPI.
Lot 1 - Targeted Sequencing
Suppliers will deliver targeted sequencing analyses, such as:
• Amplicon sequencing and metabarcoding, utilising mainly 16S, 18S, COI and ITS markers, but also other custom primers may be required on an ad-hoc basis.
• Library enrichment, such as bait capture/hybrid probe capture techniques.
Lot 2 - Whole Genome
Suppliers will deliver whole genome, metagenomic and transcriptomic sequencing, in applications such as:
• Whole genome/metagenomic sequencing for microbial diversity, microbiome analysis, species identification, pathogen detection, genome assembly, AMR screening, population genetics.
• Transcriptomic/single-cell/spatial transcriptomic sequencing for host-pathogen interactions, functional annotation/classification, metabolic pathways, gene expression.
Lot 3 - Long-Read Sequencing
Suppliers will provide long-read sequencing analysis, using either PacBio or Oxford Nanopore Technologies. This may be for several different applications, mainly studies of:
• Microbial diversity, microbiome analysis, species identification, pathogen detection
• Whole-genome assembly, AMR screening, population genetics
• Nanopore-specific - Methylation sequencing, epigenetics
Lot 4 - Ad-Hoc Requirements
Suppliers will ad-hoc requests, i.e. those that do not fit in the prior lot categories. This would most likely be utilised when a unique/proprietary technology or analysis is required, such as RAD-Seq, that Cefas cannot undertake in-house.
Specifics would be detailed in the individual project request via the call-off process, which will be a mini-competition process as set out in Appendix 4.

title: The Provision and Maintenance of Two Mass Spectrometry systems
description:
The MHRA has a requirement to award a contract for The Provision and Maintenance of Two Mass Spectrometry systems to one Tenderer as replacements of two Triple Quad Mass Spectrometers (s/n TQH-Q1-0526 and TQH-Q1-0525) for quantification and characterisation of biological medicine standards, including influenza, and to support counterfeit and sub-potent medicine characterisation. These systems are to be purchased with service maintenance and any bespoke consumables required to run the systems as follows:
System 1. A high-resolution mass spectrometer coupled with a low flow liquid chromatography (LC) system (hereinafter referred to as a “high resolution mass spectrometry system” or “HRMS system”). The system should include all the instrumentation and software to allow qualitative and quantitative analysis of samples in a wide range of complex biological matrices in the areas of proteomics, intact protein analysis, biopharmaceutical characterisation, e.g. multi-attribute monitoring of therapeutic antibodies, post-translational modifications and small molecules/metabolomics as well as glycoproteins and oligonucleotides (OGNs).
System 2. A triple quadrupole mass spectrometer coupled with an ultra-high performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) (hereinafter referred to as a “triple quad MS system”). The system should include all the instrumentation and software to allow for high throughput targeted quantitative analysis across biopharma, clinical and small molecule applications, supporting large SRM/MRM panels.

title: Invitation to submit a proposal for human resources information system (HRIS) and fully managed payroll service
description:
Vanguard Learning Trust invites qualified suppliers to tender for the provision of a cloud-based human resources information system (HRIS) and a fully managed payroll service to support approximately 615 employees across 6 schools and a central Trust team. The solution must deliver secure, efficient HR and payroll processes, ensure statutory compliance with UK employment, pensions and HMRC regulations, and provide high-quality support to both Trust leaders and school-based staff.
Objectives
The Trust aims to procure a combined HRIS and payroll solution that:
Provides a single source of truth for employee data across all schools and the Trust's central team.
Reduces administrative workloads and manual processing.
Ensures accurate, timely payroll with all third-party submissions completed by the provider, including HMRC, pension providers, and statutory bodies.
Supports workforce planning, reporting, and strategic oversight at Trust level.
Offers excellent employee and manager self-service.
Ensures data security, GDPR compliance, and UK-based hosting.
Scope of software and services
The software will include:
General HR system of record (SoR)
Absence and attendance management functionality, which will link to occupational sickness scheme requirements
Time and expenses (the functionality for employees to log additional hours and expenses, which would only be approved at managerial level)
Organisation structure
Employee Self Service
Manager Self Service
People Analytics
A fully managed payroll and pension service
The Trust would not be procuring the functionality below in the first instance but may consider doing at a later date. These are, therefore, 'desirable' rather than 'essential':
Integrated applicant tracking and onboarding functionality
Performance management and appraisal functionality
Case management functionality
The service provision will include:
Fully managed payroll services
Fully managed pensions services
Solution hosting
Requirements
Our requirements (functional and non-functional) have been listed and are provided in an Excel sheet along with this document.
Supplier Responses
Suppliers are requested to complete the supplier response columns within the requirements document and to provide a commercial proposal using the template in the attached sheet. Additionally, please provide a high level project plan to demonstrate the timescales that your solution could be deployed in and a copy of your customer support service-level agreement (SLA). Finally, short-listed providers will be required to complete the Trust's data protection impact assessment (DPIA).

title: Live Fire Training Unit
description:
East Sussex Fire Authority (ESFA) on behalf of East Sussex Fire and Rescue Service require to replace their Live Fire Training Building situated on our Training Centre site in Maresfield East Sussex.
This exercise is being created to replace the previous exercise called Live Fire Training Building (but with the same reference number) as we ran into portal constraints that blocked this being an open tender open to all new interested parties. To do so we had to cease the previous exercise and commence a new one.
Our intention is to replace essentially what we have now on a like for like basis but taking into account some design changes identified that will improve both flexibility in use and reduce the impact we have on the environment. We have a fairly clear idea of what we want, and that we can afford it, and believe we have a basic understanding of who might be able to supply what we require in a fairly small niche market. However, the aim of this document is to allow the market to confirm, or otherwise, our assumptions and for us to gather some information that will allow us to prepare an equitable tender that any capable supplier could bid for.  As well as establishing capable suppliers we are very keen to establish whether this can be achieved as a single supplier integrated project, or not.
Whilst we may consider alternative innovative approaches, we believe that a steel framed metal structure or container-based solution is likely to be all that we can afford and of which, we have a lot of experience being the basis of the current unit.

title: Provision of Gas Renewal Services - Midsomer Norton Schools Partnership
description: This Tender opportunity has been issued by ESOS Energy Ltd on behalf of Midsomer Norton Schools Partnership (the Trust) and Tenderers are invited to Tender for the provision of Gas Renewal Services. The Contractor’s gas renewal service will be responsible to secure and implement a new gas supply arrangement for the Trust and it’ schools ahead of existing contract end dates, ensuring continuity of supply, compliance with applicable regulations, and transparent, auditable decision-making. The service typically covers coordination of site and meter data, market engagement and quotation management (or support to the Trust’s chosen route to market), evaluation and award support, and onboarding/mobilisation with the incoming Contractor. Delivery will be planned around the contract expiry profile for each school and follows a defined sequence of activities from data validation through to contract start and live service commencement. The Contractor should provide a clear timeline, identified dependencies, and named points of contact for both operational delivery and escalation. The Contractor will operate appropriate governance and reporting throughout delivery, including regular status updates (e.g., weekly during active renewal windows), exception reporting for any at-risk sites, and confirmation that all communications and decisions are captured for audit purposes. Delivery must support the Trust’s safeguarding, data protection and compliance requirements (including secure handling of site and billing data) and ensure that any third parties involved are clearly declared and managed. Typical performance measures include on-time renewals (before contract end), zero loss of supply incidents, accuracy of meter/site data, successful first-time billing (correct sites, rates and dates), and responsiveness to queries and escalations. The contract start date will be the 1st September 2026 and is to be for a period 12, 24 or 36 months, The actual contract term with the successful supplier will be determined based on which option represents the most economically advantageous outcome / best value for money, having regard to total contract cost, pricing profile, risk, and service delivery considerations

title: Norway – Environmental services – Request for Information (RFI) - CCS as a service
description: Eidsiva Bioenergi AS is a wholly owned company in the Eidsiva group and was established in 2007. The company operates, designs and constructs fully-owned and partially owned bioenergy installations, mainly in Innlandet County. The company is currently Norway's third largest district heating producer and produces approx. 475 GWh per annum. Eidsiva has set ambitious targets for sustainability and by 2030 shall have 100% renewable district heating production, without the use of fossil oil and gas, as well as reduce their own emissions by 60%. As a part of this work, carbon capture and storage (CCS) at Eidsiva Bioenergis waste incineration plant at Trehørningen energy centre outside Hamar. Eidsiva Bioenergi wants to map the market to identify suppliers who can offer carbon capture and permanent storage of CO2 as a service (CCS as a service). The deadline for input is 30 September 2026. In this context, "CCS as a service" refers to the business model in which the supplier assumes responsibility for establishing, financing, and operating carbon capture facilities, as well as managing the transport and permanent storage of captured CO2 from the Trehørningen energy center. Eidsiva Bioenergi procures in such a model a service connected to capture and permanent storage of CO2 based on further agreed commercial and technical terms. The tenderer is required to handle the downstream value chain for storing biogeneous CO2, including the sale of CDR (carbon removal credits).

title: Denmark – Construction work – Copenhagen - New Metroline, M5 Civil Works South
description: This tender presents a substantial opportunity for prospective contractors to bid for the M5 Civil Works South (CWS) package, an important component of the Copenhagen metro system's expansion. This project is of significant strategic importance, as the M5 line is a fully automated driverless metro system that will not only enhance passenger service on existing metro corridors but also extend connectivity to emerging urban development areas, including Kløverparken, Refshaleøen, and Lynetteholm in the East Harbour. The M5 is designed to operate as an independent system, ensuring that its construction and subsequent operation do not disrupt the existing M1-M4 metro lines. MAIN COMPONENTS OF THE M5 CIVIL WORK The M5 south consists of approx 6.5 km twin bored TBM tunnels, 5 underground stations (incl. 3 transfer stations), 2 underground crossovers, 1 shaft, 5 cross passages, 1 ramp, approx 2.0 km viaduct, 1 elevated station, 1 viaduct cross-over, 1 elevated bifurcation, short embankment sections. For further details on scope ref. is made to M5-2.1-CMBS-SW and M5-2.2-CWS-SW PHASES: The current tender, Phase 1, encompasses the southern section of the line, from north-west of København H to north of v/Prags Boulevard, with an anticipated operational commencement in 2036. The broader vision includes phase 2 north of v/Prags Boulevard to Lynetteholm opening in 2045 and a potential future extension to form a ring line, signifying a long-term commitment to urban mobility. Phase 2 is not included in this tender. CONTRACT SPLIT OF M5: The M5 project as a whole consists of several contracts: • M5 Civil Works South (this contract) • M5 Transportation System South contract (tendered out as a separate contract in June 2026) • Operation and Maintenance contract (will be tendered out at a later stage) • Enabling Works contracts, e.g. relocation of utilities, relocation works at Kh etc. (enabling works will be tendered out in separate contracts) • Station and Shaft areas (will be tendered out at a later stage) • Canopy contracts (will be tendered out at a later stage). CONTRACT The contract is structured as a design & build contract under ABT18 terms, placing comprehensive responsibility for both design and execution upon the Contractor. This two-phase approach—design followed by execution—is a standard framework for complex infrastructure projects. A market dialogue has been carried out before issuing the tender. The purpose of the market dialogue was to ensure that the project is attractive to the market, and to ensure competitive and compliant final tenders to be used as basis for the award of contract. Metroselskabet I/S is grateful for the potential tenderers who took their time to participate in the dialogue and provided input. INDICATIVE TIMESCHEDULE FOR THE PROCUREMENT Publication of contract notice September 10th 2026. Publication of tender documentation September 11th 2026. Deadline for submission of application for prequalification October 13th 2026, ref. made to section 5.1.12. Dialogue phase November 2026-October 2027. Final tender November 2027. Award of contract December 2027. The time-schedule may be subject to change.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Machbarkeitsstudie: Räumliche Analysen zur Identifikation von Verbesserungspotenzialen der Landstraßensicherheit
description: Das Unfallgeschehen auf Landstraßen ist (im Vergleich zu Autobahnen und Stadtstraßen) durch eine besonders hohe Unfallschwere und viele Verkehrstote gekennzeichnet. Nach umfangreichen Forschungen liegen mittlerweile Erkenntnisse zur Sicherheitswirkung infrastruktureller Defizite, geeigneten Gegenmaßnahmen sowie Analysewerkzeuge für unfallauffällige Netzelemente vor. Es fehlt jedoch bislang eine Möglichkeit, regional ausgeprägte Spezifika der Infrastruktur aus makroskopischer Perspektive mittels einfacher Analysen zu erfassen. Insbesondere existiert keine Methode, um mit vergleichsweise einfachen Mitteln – etwa ausschließlich auf Basis polizeilicher Unfalldaten – regional ausgeprägte Spezifika der Infrastruktur oder infrastrukturelle Verbesserungspotenziale im Landstraßennetz zu erkennen. Ziel/ Nutzen Ziel des Vorhabens ist es zu klären, ob Unfalldaten als Indikatoren für Straßeninfrastruktur verwendet werden können und welche Grundgesamtheit an Unfällen in welcher strukturellen Tiefe auf welcher räumlichen Gliederungsebene erforderlich ist, um regionale Unterschiede und Verbesserungspotenziale systematisch ableiten zu können. Die angedachte Analyseebene befindet sich dabei explizit oberhalb der im Fachgebiet bereits vorhandenen und etablierten Verfahren und Methoden (insbesondere netzbezogene Verfahren zur Sicherheitsanalyse sowie örtliche Unfalluntersuchung). Aufbauend auf einer Analyse des nationalen und internationalen Kenntnisstandes sind zunächst die Unfallkonstellationen zusammenzustellen, die durch geeignete Infrastrukturmaßnahmen systematisch beeinflusst werden können. Anschließend ist eine repräsentative und plausible Basis von Unfall- und Infrastrukturdaten aufzubauen und zu verknüpfen. Zielgerichtete Auswertungen dieser Datenbasis dienen dazu, zu prüfen, ob allein aus Unfalldaten belastbare Aussagen über regionale infrastrukturelle Spezifika auf Landstraßen abgeleitet werden können. Im positiven Fall sind geeignete Analyseparameter abzuleiten und die Methode exemplarisch anzuwenden.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Zentralisierung der Abwasser- und Schlammbehandlung in der VG Ransbach-Baumbach - Anbindung Teichkläranlagen
description: Die Verbandsgemeinde Ransbach Baumbach betreibt zur Reinigung des anfallenden Abwassers aus den jeweiligen Einzugsgebieten neben der Hauptkläranlage Hundsdorf (Ausbaugröße 17.250 EW) u. a. die mechanisch-biologische Kläranlage Haiderbach (Ausbaugröße 3.000 EW) sowie die beiden Teichkläranlagen Sessenbach (Ausbaugröße 900 EW) und Wirscheid (Ausbaugröße 400 EW). Es ist vorgesehen, die Kläranlage Hundsdorf zukünftig als zentrale Anlage zur Behandlung des Klärschlamms aller von der VG betriebenen Kläranlagen zu betreiben. Die hierfür erforderlichen Ausbaumaßnahmen (u. A. Umstellung der Verfahrensführung auf Schlammfaulung) befinden sich derzeit bereits in der Planung. Die Planung der weiteren Zentralisierungsmaßnahmen (Umbauarbeiten auf der KA Haiderbach; Anschluss der Teichkläranlagen Wirscheid und Sessenbach an die KA Hundsdorf) werden in getrennten Fachlosen ausgeschrieben. Gegenstand dieses Loses ist der Anschluss der Teichkläranlagen Sessenbach und Wirscheid an die KA Hundsdorf. Die nicht mehr den heutigen Anforderungen an die Abwasserreinigung genügenden Teichkläranlagen Sessenbach und Wirscheid sollen an die Kläranlage Hundsdorf angeschlossen werden. Hierzu ist es vorgesehen, das Abwasser von Sessenbach mittels Pumpstation mit anschließender Druckrohrleitung bis zum Standort der TKA Wirscheid zu fördern. Die Druckleitung endet hier im Pumpensumpf der ebenfalls neu zu bauenden Pumpstation Wirscheid. Anschließend wird das Abwasser von Sessenbach und Wirscheid über eine gemeinsame Pumpleitung zur KA Hundsdorf gefördert. Hierzu sollen folgende wesentlichen Maßnahmen geplant werden: --- a) auf dem Altstandort Sessenbach: Zur Auflassung der TKA Sessenbach ist eine Anpassung der Mischwasserbehandlung erforderlich. Hierzu soll ein neues Regenüberlaufbecken mit einem Behandlungsvolumen von 60 m³ gebaut werden. Das anfallende Abwasser wird dann mittels Pumpstation und einer anschließenden, rd. 2.600 m langen Druckrohrleitung bis zum Altstandort der TKA Wirscheid gefördert. --- b) auf dem Altstandort KA Wirscheid: Zur Auflassung der TKA Wirscheid ist keine Anpassung der Mischwasserbehandlung erforderlich. Zur Weiterleitung des Abwassers von Sessenbach und Wirscheid wird eine gemeinsame Pumpstation mit einer anschließenden, rd. 4.600 m langen Druckrohrleitung bis zur KA Hundsdorf vorgesehen. Die Ausführung der Pumpstation erfolgt analog zur Pumpstation Sessenbach. Nach Fertigstellung werden die beiden Teichkläranlagen stillgelegt und renaturiert.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Brandschutztechnische Ertüchtigung, Amokprävention sowie statische und energ. Sanierung der Carl-Orff-Realschule Plus, Los 2 - Planungsleistungen der Technischen Ausrüstung HLS und Elektro
description: Der Landkreis Bad Dürkheim beabsichtigt die brandschutztechnische Ertüchtigung, Amokprävention sowie statische und energetische Sanierung der Fassade der Carl-Orff-Realschule Plus in Bad Dürkheim. Das gesamte Gebäude weist Mängel im Brandschutz auf und muss ertüchtigt werden. Die dafür erforderlichen Planungsleistungen sollen ausgeschrieben werden. Die Realschule (Baujahr 1974) verfügt über eine Nutzfläche von ca. 7.000 m³, verteilt auf 6 Geschosse, davon ein Untergeschoss. Für die brandschutztechnische Sanierung wurde 2008 ein Brandschutzkonzept erstellt. Dieses sieht Ertüchtigungsmaßnahmen insbesondere im Hinblick auf Wände und Decken vor. Ferner müssen Lüftung-, Sanitär-, Heizung und die Elektroinstallation überprüft und den Anforderungen entsprechend ertüchtigt werden. In dem Zug soll auch eine Brandmeldeanlage und Amokalarmierung eingebaut werden. Die Gebäudehülle weist zudem statische Mängel in der Verankerung der Fassaden- und Attikaplatten auf und muss ertüchtigt werden. Vorgesehen ist eine vorgehängte Fassade mit Faserzement- Fassadentafeln. Die Fenster und Außentüren werden ebenfalls ausgetauscht. Die Dachflächen müssen überprüft und gegebenenfalls ertüchtigt werden. Die besondere Herausforderung der Planungsaufgabe liegt in der Planung der Durchführung der Arbeiten während des laufenden Betriebs. Die Schüler können, während der Sanierungsarbeiten, in Containern untergebracht werden. Dies ist jedoch lediglich in begrenztem Umfang möglich. Weitere Einzelheiten ergeben sich aus der Leistungsbeschreibung sowie dem Brandschutzkonzept nebst Anlage. Die Unterlagen sind Bestandteil der Vergabeunterlagen. Die Baukosten (netto) für die Technische Ausrüstung werden wie folgt erwartet: KG 410 - Abwasser-, Wasser-, Gasanlagen - ca. 490.000 EUR; KG 420 - Wärmeversorgungsanlagen - ca. 200.000 EUR; KG 430 - Lufttechnische Anlagen - ca. 500.000 EUR; KG 440 - Starkstromanlagen - ca. 1.000.000 EUR; KG 450 - Fernmeldeanlagen - ca. 900.000 EUR. Gesamtsumme: ca. 3.090.000 EUR Es handelt sich um eine erste Kostenschätzung zum Erhalt vergleichbarer Angebote, die sich noch verändern kann.

title: Compassionate Birmingham Expert Support and Delivery
description:
Birmingham City Council (the Council) is seeking to appoint an organisation for the provision of Compassionate Birmingham workstream, which is a core delivery of the Birmingham Ageing Well Strategy and the continued delivery of our Compassionate Birmingham commitment.
Compassionate Birmingham is the umbrella term given to a series of organisations that work to deliver better services and support for people who are dying, bereaved, grieving, or caring.  It follows the ideas laid down by Professor Allan Kellehear in the Compassionate Cities Charter: Compassionate Cities Charter.
Examples of work carried out previously has revolved around arts and health approaches to health, supporting people dying alone in hospital, offering training to community organisations, and funding death cafés.
Pre-pandemic, NICE guidance suggested that around 30% of people that experience a close bereavement needed organised support opportunities.  Additionally, a further 10% struggled with complex or prolonged grief, needing specialist mental health interventions.  However, figures suggested at this time, 20-30% of bereaved adults were unable to access the support they needed.
Left unsupported, bereavement is associated with increased risk to health and wellbeing, including mortality, physical health problems, physical disability, medication usage, hospitalisation, and in some cases more visits to a GP.  The pre-pandemic costs of this were estimated to be £8bn annually plus an additional £23bn in lost revenue
The contract for the services will commence on 1st November 2026 and will be in place for a period of 3 years.

description:

-	Tools and Frameworks, including techniques on practical application, to recognise behaviours, and suggest improvements to build effective working relationships and better support others through these behavioural/ mindset changes.
-	Tools and Frameworks to help support individuals in measuring success, reflection techniques and a particular focus on maintaining the positive changes made

title: Preliminary Market Engagement for Bolsover Shopfront Improvements in Bolsover Town Centre
description:
Bolsover District Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to attend a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Event for the Bolsover Town Centre Shopfront Improvement Scheme.
The proposed scheme involves the repair, restoration, replacement and enhancement of shopfronts within Bolsover Town Centre, which is a designated Conservation Area. The works will include interventions to a number of Grade II Listed Buildings and will form part of the wider Bolsover Regeneration Programme, funded by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG).
The total funding allocation for the scheme is £1,000,000, with approximately £900,000 allocated to the shopfront improvement works.
The Council is keen to engage with contractors that can demonstrate experience in:
•	Conservation and heritage construction projects
•	Working on listed buildings and within conservation areas
•	Traditional building materials and construction techniques
•	Specialist joinery and shopfront restoration
•	Delivery of high-quality commercial property improvement works
•	Collaborative working with local authorities, conservation officers and other stakeholders
Purpose of the Event
The Preliminary Market Engagement Event will provide an opportunity for contractors to:
•	Have one to one allocated time with the project team
•	Receive an overview of the proposed scheme
•	Meet the appointed architects and project team
•	Take part in a guided tour of Bolsover Town Centre
•	Gain an understanding of the anticipated scope and scale of works
•	Provide feedback to help inform procurement and delivery options
•	Discuss contractor capacity, capability and market interest in delivering the scheme
The Council anticipates that the project will be delivered in phases, with all works to be completed by March 2028.
This event is being held solely for market engagement purposes and is not part of a formal procurement process. Attendance or participation will not provide any advantage or disadvantage in any future procurement exercise associated with the scheme.

title: DDAITF/013 Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services & COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning
description:
The Ministry of Defence (MOD), through the Defence AI Accelerator Task Force (TF RAID), intends to procure a secure, scalable capability to support operational planning across Defence. 
TF RAID exists to accelerate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-enabled capabilities in support of Defence outcomes, working with users, technical specialists and industry to identify, test and transition operationally relevant solutions. 
This requirement is expected to support operational planners by improving access to authorised planning information, enabling reusable machine-readable planning knowledge, orchestrating analytical services, and supporting the modelling, testing and comparison of alternative Courses of Action (COAs).

            
The procurement will be structured as a single competition with 2 Lots: 
-	Lot 1 will focus on planning data, knowledge and analytical orchestration services; and 
-	Lot 2 will focus on COA testing, evaluation and adaptation services. Suppliers are invited to bid for 1 or both lots. 
Together, the Lots are intended to improve the speed, quality, traceability and robustness of operational planning while maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency, security and interoperability within Authority-approved environments, including those handling information up to SECRET UK EYES ONLY where required.
MOD will be seeking to compete this requirement through the Government Commercial Agency Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS/RM6200). title: Governance Risk and Compliance tool
description:
DELTA Access Code :4J4GPFS79V
Description 
The Authority aims to procure a scalable, integrated Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) software solution, capable of supporting its organisational growth and any required regulatory obligations. The solution is intended to consolidate risk data from across the Authority into a single platform that strengthens oversight, enhances analysis & reporting, improves operational efficiency, and ensures accountability.  A GRC tool may also provide the opportunity to identify data synergies and move away from several systems used across the Authority. 
Strategic Objectives 
Integrated View of the Risk and Control Environment 
A unified cloud-based platform will provide a single source of truth for risks, controls, incidents, actions and metrics. Full traceability will be maintained across taxonomies, business units, policies and key processes, improving framework integration, transparency and decision-making.  
Data Driven Culture and Analytics 
The system will enable trend analysis, early warning indicators and data driven insights to support proactive management of current and emerging risks.  
Operational Efficiency and Improved Ownership 
An intuitive user experience, default ‘outofthebox’ configurability, guided workflows and automation will reduce manual effort and embed firstline ownership of risks and controls, while supporting second line oversight and challenge.  
High Quality Data and Reporting 
Automated dashboards and configurable reporting to the Microsoft Office suite will streamline internal and external stakeholder reporting, including for senior management, committees and regulators.  
Assurance and Regulatory Compliance 
The platform will facilitate compliance with the UK Corporate Governance Code (including Provision 29) and relevant FCA expectations. Evidence trails, compliance monitoring and control testing will support a robust assurance framework. 
Core Capability Requirements 
Initial core capability requirements have been identified, with activities still ongoing to define the full scope of requirements and determine the business units which a GRC tool may be implemented into. A full prioritised list of requirements and business units identified as part of ongoing activities, will be incorporated into future specifications. 
The current core GRC solution must support, but not be limited to the following key modules: 
Risk & Control Management 
- Risk and control library 
- RCSA: inherent/residual assessments, control tiering and assessments, risk acceptances and outoftolerance management 
- Heat maps, bow ties and risk scoring matrices 
- Control improvement actions 
- Endtoend traceability of risk, control and incident data by risk taxonomy, business unit, policy suite, and key processes 
Control Testing 
- Structured workflows, evidence capture and reporting to support assurance activities.  
Data, Reporting & Analytics 
- Configurable automated reporting 
- UK Corporate Governance Code Provision 29aligned reporting 
- Data ingestion from internal and external sources 
- Use of AIassisted tooling where appropriate  
Risk Appetite & Key Risk Indicators 
- Capture, monitoring and reporting of KRIs and risk appetite metrics.  
Incident Management 
- Central reporting portal 
- End to end incident lifecycle management, including automations 
- Metrics and trend analysis  
Policy Management 
- Governance and maintenance of the policy suite 
- Evidence based assessment of policy effectiveness using risk, control, testing and incident data  
Regulatory Compliance 
- Compliance monitoring plan execution 
- Horizon scanning and analysis of regulatory changes 
- Impact assessment of external developments on the control environment  
Ethics & Integrity 
- Management and reporting of gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, personal account dealing and insider lists.  
Internal Audit 
- Audit planning and delivery workflows 
- Action tracking and reporting  
Non-Core Capabilities 
While not central to the initial procurement, the system should also be capable of supporting: 
- Business continuity and resilience 
- Programme/project risk management 
- Third party risk management

title: Mental health, social inclusion and resilience building for at risk young people in Leicester.
description:
THIS IS NOT A CALL FOR COMPETITION - 
Public Health is exploring opportunities to commission preventative mental health and wellbeing support for young people who may be more susceptible to developing poor mental health due to a range of factors such as the experience or risk of involvement in the criminal justice system or having lived experience, experiencing higher levels of vulnerability and poorer mental health outcomes. 
The opportunity would be lotted, Lot 1 would explore the commissioning of a preventative mental health and wellbeing programme for young people aged 12-25 who are at risk of or involved with justice services. The delivery model is currently being developed through stakeholder engagement and participation with young people. Early scoping suggests that an effective approach to programme delivery would be through a flexible programme which comprises of group activities, workshops, and practical support. 
Lot 2 would explore the promotion of social inclusion and improve the emotional wellbeing of care-experienced young people aged 18-25 by reducing social isolation and loneliness and strengthening confidence, emotional resilience, independence, and positive relationships. Care-experienced young people can experience disadvantages in education, employment, physical and mental health, and access to supportive social networks. The commissioned service will provide practical, strengths-based support to help participants develop the skills, resilience and social connections needed for a healthy and fulfilling transition to adulthood. 
The programme will be designed and delivered in collaboration with care-experienced young people, ensuring that activities reflect their priorities, experiences, and aspirations. It will combine practical life skills, life-journey work, and emotional wellbeing support, informed by the Five Ways to Wellbeing framework. 
With this soft market test we aim to understand the markets capabilities and range of services offered in relation to both groups.
