title: C047PA Deceased Storage Service
description:
Essex County Council (ECC) is responsible for delivering the Coroner Service for the Essex Coroner Area, which includes the administrative areas of Essex County Council, Thurrock Council and Southend-on-Sea City Council.
As part of this statutory function, ECC requires suitably qualified and experienced providers to deliver Deceased  Storage Services across Essex.
The purpose of this contract is to provide secure, compliant and dignified secondary contingency storage arrangements for deceased persons on behalf of HM Coroner when additional capacity is required beyond that available through primary mortuary provision. The service forms an important component of the Essex Coroner Area's resilience arrangements and supports continuity of service during periods of increased demand, maintenance works, service disruption, major incidents or other circumstances affecting mortuary capacity.
The successful provider/s will be required to maintain suitable facilities capable of receiving and storing deceased persons safely, securely and respectfully, operating in accordance with all relevant legislation, professional standards, health and safety requirements and recognised industry best practice.
The service provider/s shall maintain:
 - Secure refrigerated deceased storage facilities.
 - Support transfers to and from NHS mortuaries within Essex, including Basildon, Broomfield, Colchester, Princess Alexandra and Southend Hospitals.
 - Robust identification, tracking and audit arrangements.
 - Appropriate temperature monitoring and alarm systems.
 - Arrangements for the receipt and release of deceased persons at short notice.
 - Suitable procedures for handling complex, traumatic and bariatric cases.
 - Business continuity and emergency response arrangements.
 - Appropriate staffing to ensure a responsive and professional service.
The service will operate on a 24-hour, 365-day basis and must be capable of responding to urgent requests from the Essex Coroner Service.
The Authority welcomes participation from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), funeral directors and specialist providers with relevant experience and suitable facilities.
This contract is intended to provide contingency deceased storage capacity and will be utilised only when operational circumstances require additional provision.
No minimum throughput, call-off volume, contract value or level of expenditure is guaranteed under the contract.
Historical utilisation and occupancy data has been provided within the procurement documentation to assist bidders in understanding the nature of the requirement. This information is provided for indicative purposes only and does not constitute a guarantee of future demand.

title: UKRI-6064 ISP-1157 Replacement of Large ISIS Power Supply System
description:
The ISIS Neutron and Muon Source Facility, part of UKRI’s Science and Technology Facilities Council, are looking to procure a replacement three-phase Alternating Current (AC) Magnet Power Supply System to make up the losses in a resonant magnet circuit. 
The requirement is for a modular 1200 kVA three-phase AC voltage source power supply that includes a control system capable of regulating the designated magnet load current to a given setpoint and to a high level of stability. It is important to emphasise that the magnet load current to be regulated is not the same as the AC power supply output current and the measurement signal for the load current will be provided by the facility in the form of a DCCT with a -10/+10 V signal representative of the load circuit current. The three-phase output shall have a variable voltage output from 0 V to 250 V line-neutral and an output voltage accuracy of ±50 mV. The system shall be fed from a nominal 400 Vrms AC, 3-phase 50 Hz sinusoidal supply, intrinsically safe by design, with high efficiency, high reliability, high maintainability and fully compliant and marked with relevant standards.

The successful Supplier will be required to provide catering services for Pontarddulais Comprehensive School, located in Swansea, Wales. 
The annual contract value is approximately £300,000 and the initial contract term will be three years, commencing 1 September 2027 and concluding 31 August 2030. The contract will operate on a guaranteed performance basis, offering a fixed annual return and/or subsidy. There will be an option to extend for a further term of three years by mutual agreement.
Pontarddulais Comprehensive School is an English medium 11-16 mixed school in the City and County of Swansea. There are currently 850 pupils on roll with approximately 17% of those entitled to a Free School Meal. The School was opened in 1982, with a Specialist Teaching Facility added in 2007 for up to 10 pupils with profound and multiple learning disabilities. It serves a large catchment area that includes Llangyfelach, Pengelli, Pontarddulais, Pontlliw and Penllergaer primary schools. Pupils are drawn from a widely dispersed catchment area including urban areas, small villages and hill farms. A significant demand for places outside the designated catchment confirms the popularity of the school.
The School has sustained a record of excellent performance in pupil outcomes over several years. The School received a hugely positive Estyn inspection in December 2023. It was noted that "Pontarddulais Comprehensive School is a dynamic and inclusive school where pupils, regardless of background or ability, thrive academically, socially, and emotionally”.
The school places great value on their partnerships with parents and carers. They believe that pupils’ success is founded on forging positive relationships through mutual respect, and excellent teaching and learning experiences.
Please see PSQ Document for more information.

title: SBRI - Agri-Food Tech Contracts for Innovation Cymru Phase 1 Challenge
description:
It is the ambition of the Welsh Government to develop a thriving and confident agriculture sector in Wales built around innovation and growth, to rise to the challenges we face and make most of the opportunities available. In July 2025 the Welsh Government published its Sustainable Farming Scheme designed to ensure Welsh Government support for agriculture in Wales delivers against the four Sustainable Land Management objectives of the Agriculture (Wales) Act:
- Produce food and other goods in a sustainable manner
- Mitigate and adapt to climate change
- Maintain and enhance the resilience of ecosystems and the benefits they provide
- Conserve and enhance the countryside and cultural resources, promote public access to and engagement with them, and to sustain the Welsh language and promote and facilitate its use.
Innovation will play a key role in delivering this scheme. In 2023, the Welsh Government published an Innovation Strategy for Wales. Innovation in food and Agri-Food Tech was seen as a key part of Wales’s future economic development. In late 2023, the Welsh Government published an Agri-tech action plan for Wales. The development and adoption of Agri-Tech and Precision Agri-Tech is a strategic area of growth for the Welsh economy and one the Welsh Government deems requiring of focussed attention and a road map for development. The action plan has four priorities:
1. Accelerate Home Grown Welsh Agri-tech Capabilities.
2. Drive on-farm adoption to achieve productivity and efficiencies (incl. Environmental) gains ‘more for less’.
3. Deliver environmental benefits and help transition to Net Zero.
4. Support educational and skills development to equip future and existing agricultural professionals to exploit Agri-tech to its fullest.
SCOPE: 
Cattle mortality data may provide valuable information on animal health, disease emergence and herd management. However, there are opportunities to make better use of mortality data alongside wider animal health surveillance information to generate timely intelligence that supports veterinary decision-making, farmer engagement and evidence-based policy.
Improving the collection, access, interpretation and communication of mortality intelligence could enable earlier identification of disease risks, encourage preventative herd health management and support the delivery of the Animal health and welfare framework | GOV.WALES for Wales, while contributing to the objectives of the Sustainable Farming Scheme.
We are therefore seeking innovative technologies, digital tools, data-driven approaches or other novel solutions that improve the collection, integration, analysis and application of cattle mortality intelligence to support proactive animal health management.

description:

The procurement process adopted by the Council is based on the 'Open' tendering procedure as detailed in the Procurement Act 2023 (the "Act") and the Procurement Regulations 2024 (the "Regulations".) 
For Lot 1 the asbestos removal and remediation services contract, the initial contract period is two years and is estimated to commence on 1st February 2027 and expire on 31st January 2029.

Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) is underway in several areas across the country and may result in changes to council structures, service delivery and responsibilities, and geographical coverage during the life of the contract. For this contract it is anticipated that the effects of LGR may lead to an increased service demand or the need to extend provision to new areas or client groups.
For Lot 1 the asbestos removal and remediation services contract, bidders should note that the total estimated contract value of £1,172,000, comprises of two components:
i)	The core contract value, estimated at £293,000, based on known current service requirements

For Lot 2 the asbestos analyst services contract, bidders should note that the total estimated contract value of £2,616,000, comprises of two components:

title: Quarrying - North District
description:
Quarrying works in the north of England (Northumberland) comprise extraction and processing of aggregate from 4 (maybe 5) hard rock quarries, including associated drilling and blasting works.
Materials are extracted in relatively small quantities and used in various Forestry England civil engineering applications, mostly for the construction and maintenance of forest roads for the purposes of facilitating timber harvesting. Quarrying operations are therefore undertaken in a number of specific locations, in close proximity to the point of use of the extracted materials. Typically, extraction of materials will take place over a period of a few weeks each year, with material then stockpiled within the quarry, or at other designated locations for use as and when needed.
This Framework will be divided in to two Lots:
1. Drilling and blasting
2 . Extraction and quarry development and crushing
Lot 1 - Drilling and blasting
The Supplier carries out all drilling and blasting operations, in accordance with the Quarries Regulations 1999 particularly Part V and the Explosives Regulations 2014 , and the quarry Health and Safety Document. Blasting activities typically take place at 2 to 5 sites per year, with tonnages between 20,000 and 35,000T per blast.
The Client (The Operator) will retain 8.1.(c) responsibilities during blasting operations.  The supplier’s named individual will be appointed as the 8.1. (d) and the client will also appoint the supplier’s named individual as the Explosives Supervisor under regulation 25 of the Quarries Regulations for the duration of the Work Order.
This requires the Supplier to have capability in the following areas:
1.	Provide suitably qualified, competent and qualified personnel to undertake the following duties.
	Explosives Supervisor
	Shotfirer
	Driller
	Blast Designer
	Face profiler
	Trainee Shotfirer (if required)
	Handing of explosives
	Transportation of explosives
      Provide all required survey work relating to the blasting operation.
Provide all plant and equipment required including fuels, oils, transportation, explosives and accessories.
Lot 2 - Extraction and quarry development and crushing
The Supplier carries out all extraction and processing, in accordance with the Quarries Regulations 1999, and the quarry Health and Safety Document.
The Client (The Operator) will retain 8.1.(c) responsibilities during operations.  The supplier’s named individual will be appointed as the 8.1. (d) deputy quarry manager to supervise the works for the duration of the Work Order.
The Client requires the Supplier to carry out the following services to facilitate the extraction and processing of aggregates at Forestry England quarries:
1.	Removal of material from processed stockpiles and blast piles.
2.	Excavation of raw materials
3.	Processing of raw materials including crushing and screening.
4.	Provision of stemming material and plant for movement and placement
5.	Maintenance and reinstatement of quarry floor and safety features
6.	Maintenance and reinstatement of egress and quarry roads, during quarrying operations
7.	Crushing of as blasted material.
8.	Loading of aggregate during quarry operations
9.	Haulage of aggregate to forest locations
10.	Daily inspections as required by the Quarries Regulations in accordance with the client’s requirements.
11.	Soil and overburden excavation, haulage within the quarry and tip creation.
12.	Restoration works.

title: Pre-Market Engagement Questionnaire: Microsoft Enterprise Licensing, CSP Services and Expertise
description:
INTRODUCTION
Mid Ulster District Council is preparing a procurement for the renewal, supply, management and optimisation of its Microsoft enterprise licensing, associated CSP services and specialist Microsoft expertise. This pre-market engagement exercise will help the Council understand available market models, risks, pricing approaches, support arrangements and proportionate requirements before any formal procurement is issued.
PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE
The objectives are to confirm market interest, test the most suitable agreement route and service model, identify risks or dependencies, understand pricing and governance options, and inform the Council's procurement strategy. This is not a procurement process and responses will not be evaluated as part of any future tender.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION
The Council's Microsoft estate includes Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, Azure, server licensing and associated Software Assurance requirements. Market input is sought on CSP, Enterprise Agreement or other Microsoft agreement routes, billing options, licence optimisation, tenant support, adoption, security and compliance support, escalation and access to qualified Microsoft expertise.
STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS
MUDC wishes to establish a contract with a suitably experienced Microsoft CSP partner to provide:
•	licensing renewal, supply and management through CSP, Enterprise Agreement or another suitable route;
•	licence optimisation, proof of licence, inventory records, renewal tracking and compliance reporting;
•	Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, security, compliance, identity, endpoint and server licensing expertise;
•	support for billing, subscription changes, incidents, Microsoft escalation, account governance and roadmap advice;
The Council also wishes to understand transparent pricing structures, including margins, discounts, billing models, separate professional services rates and how best to separate user subscriptions, device subscriptions, Azure consumption, server licensing, trial/free SKUs and advisory services.
Responses should assist the Council in considering proportionate partner status, accreditations, insurance, service capability, support model and future evaluation balance between price, quality and added value.
5.0	PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT APPROACH
INDICATIVE PROCUREMENT TIMEFRAME
7.0	Indicative milestones: PME published 10th September 2026 ; responses due via eTendersNI by 3.00 pm on 24th September 2026; procurement launch October , contract award December ; licensing renewal / contract commencement 31st January 2027.

title: Statutory Assessments Service
description:
The Statutory Assessments Service is a statutory requirement that supports Birmingham City Council in discharging its legal responsibilities for the assessment and moderation of pupil attainment across Birmingham schools. The service provides quality assurance, compliance monitoring and moderation of national assessment processes, ensuring adherence to Department for Education requirements and maintaining the integrity, consistency and accuracy of assessment outcomes across the city. 
A core element of the service involves the monitoring of Key Stage 2 SATs. This includes undertaking visits to selected schools during SATs week to ensure that assessments are administered in accordance with the statutory Assessment and Reporting Arrangements (ARA). The service is responsible for identifying and reporting any concerns, irregularities or instances of non-compliance to the Standards and Testing Agency (STA). 
The service also delivers Key Stage 1 Phonics monitoring, carrying out compliance checks to ensure that schools are administering phonics assessments in line with national guidance and statutory requirements. 
Additionally, the service coordinates and delivers Key Stage 2 Writing Moderation across Birmingham schools. This includes organising moderation visits, validating teacher assessment judgements against national standards, reviewing evidence where there are concerns regarding the accuracy of assessments, and confirming final outcomes. The service is responsible for recording and submitting moderation decisions through the appropriate national systems, ensuring that teacher assessments are robust, consistent and reliable. 
The service plays a critical role in maintaining the integrity and consistency of statutory assessments across Birmingham and ensures that the Council meets its legal obligations as a Local Authority in relation to assessment, moderation and quality assurance.

Reablement Services provide short-term support to Individuals in their homes. This can be following hospital discharge, illness, or acute episode, or for people who are new to care. Reablement Services aim to restore confidence and independence. The Council takes a “Reablement First” approach meaning that everyone new to care is considered for the service and should only be opted out where Reablement is not deemed to be the appropriate service. These services are provided for up to four weeks (six in exceptional circumstances), are non-chargeable and are delivered without a Care Act eligibility assessment, helping to prevent long-term dependency.

title: Prisoner Telephony Services – Bridging Agreement
description:
This direct award procurement is a concession contract to continue the existing prisoner telephony service for the prisons in England and Wales which are run by HM Prison and Probation Service. The Bridging Agreement is drafted as an extension/contract change notice to the current PTS contract. 
The prisoner telephony service (PTS) is currently provided by British Telecommunications Limited (company number 01800000) (BT) in the prisons in England and Wales which are run by HM Prison and Probation Service and has been for several years.  The ability for prisoners to maintain relationships with family and friends is critical as it contributes to prisoners’ wellbeing, order and discipline, rehabilitation, and a reduction in the likelihood of reoffending. The main communication channel in use currently is voice calls, provided by the PTS. PTS is a critical service which allows prisoners to make phone calls to approved contact numbers using a unique personal identification number (PIN). The PTS scope includes use of in-cell phones, wing phones, mobile PIN phones and staff to cell phones. 
This direct award, known as the Bridging Agreement, will bridge the period between 1 June 2027 (the current contract expires on 31 May 2027) up to 30 November 2031, which is the period required to enable governing, procuring, mobilising, testing and transitioning to the replacement next generation communications service called the Prisoner Integrated Communications Service (PICS). Under the Bridging Agreement, BT will continue to provide the PTS on substantially the same terms as the current PTS contract together with exit services to transition to PICS. PTS is procured as a concession contract as it is predominately funded from the income generated by prisoners who purchase phone credit from BT.     
The contracting authority (MOJ) is relying on the single supplier direct award justifications under section 41 and schedule 5 paragraphs 5 and/or 6 of the Procurement Act 2023 in the alternative:   
-paragraph 5 (a)due to a particular supplier having intellectual property rights or other exclusive rights, only that supplier can supply the goods, services or works required, and (b)there are no reasonable alternatives to those goods, services or works.   
and in the alternative:   
-paragraph 6 (a)due to an absence of competition for technical reasons, only a particular supplier can supply the goods, services or works required, and (b)there are no reasonable alternatives to those goods, services or works.   
The explanations for why the justifications apply are as follows:  
Intellectual property rights - paragraph 5.  
This justification applies because only BT has the intellectual property rights needed to be able to provide the services. This is a consequence of the intellectual property clauses in the current PTS contract and the Bridging Agreement. 
No reasonable alternatives  
In the absence of the intellectual property rights that would be needed for an alternative supplier to be able to provide the services, the only reasonable potential alternative would be for MOJ to procure another supplier/s to develop a replacement solution that meets MOJ’s requirements – whether building from scratch or configuring a commercial-off-the-shelf solution. Any replacement supplier/s would then need time for mobilising, testing and transitioning to that replacement solution after it had been appropriately governed and procured by MOJ. There is not sufficient time to do all these activities which would be necessary to transition to a replacement solution by the date the services are required, which is 1 June 2027. This is evidenced by the number of years it is taking to replace the PTS and transition to the next generation replacement service, PICS. PICS is being designed for use in the prisons in England and Wales which are run by HM Prisons and Probation Service and will be rolled out incrementally over time to eventually end use of the PTS service. MOJ is approximately two years into the PICS project. The direct award for the Bridging Agreement is for the period required to facilitate MOJ procuring, governing, testing, mobilising and transitioning from PTS to PICS.  Therefore, there are no reasonable alternatives.  
The second justification is absence of competition for technical reasons - paragraph 6  
There is an absence of competition for technical reasons which are based on the same arguments as for the intellectual property rights justification under paragraph 5, which are stated above. The PTS is bespoke and an alternative supplier would not be able to walk in and take over the services on the date from which they are required due to the intellectual property rights of BT. Instead, there would have to be an appropriately governed procurement/s and then the selected supplier/s would have to mobilise, test and then transition to that service and as stated in the justification under paragraph 5 above, this is not possible to do by the time the services are required on 1 June 2027.  
No reasonable alternatives  
The same justifications, stated above, for why there are no reasonable alternatives for paragraph 5 intellectual property rights, apply to the justification for paragraph 6. 
Therefore, there are no reasonable alternatives.  
For background information, MOJ has conducted several forms of preliminary market engagement for PICS to replace the Bridging Agreement. Following that market engagement, MOJ has been developing plans for the future. MOJ anticipates that the contracts for prisoner telephony services to support PICS will be let through relevant frameworks agreements such as RM6377 Network Services 4, RM6098 Technology Products & Associated Services (TePAS) 2 and/or TePAS 3 operated by the Government Commercial Agency (GCA); Procurements to commence after February 2027. Prospective suppliers are encouraged to engage with GCA (gca.gov.uk) and/or on-framework suppliers to participate in framework opportunities.  
To obtain information from the preliminary market engagement which has occurred already and to register for updates for PICS, please contact vvn.cmo@justice.gov.uk 
Note: With effect on 25 June 2026, BT registered a change at Companies House to reflect its re-registration from a plc.  Whilst the company’s name has changed, the legal entity remains the same with the same company number.

title: My Ends 3.0 Programme
description:
MyEnds 3.0 is an evolved version of the flagship VRU MyEnds programme which will run from April 2027 until March 2029. This new iteration will allow us to implement key learning from the MyEnds programmes and strengthen the key components of the overall programme design, optimising innovation with more targeted strategic alignment.
Background to Current Service :
The MyEnds programme utilises a hyper-local approach to address needs in neighbourhoods across the capital that are most affected by high and sustained levels of violence. The core model endorsed by the VRU for this programme is based on the empowerment of communities, recognising the critical role and collective impact community stakeholders have in local violence reduction initiatives. This is achieved through the delivery of key activity strands, including strengthening local partnerships, young people and community participation, capacity building of the grassroots sector, and the delivery of locally informed interventions.
Evidence shows that a community-led approach, by those who know their area and its challenges best, is the most effective way to prevent violence.
MyEnds provides communities with the tools and resources to deliver their own prevention measures. This includes support networks for parents and carers, after-school activities, youth work in neighbourhood youth clubs, mentoring and targeted support interventions.
Service Requirements
The VRU Area Prioritisation Tool, previously used to identify areas for the 2019 MyEnds pilot and MyEnds 2.0, has been refreshed with updated data and metrics to identify eligible locations for MyEnds 3.0. The tool identifies ward-level areas that have consistently ranked within the top 15% of London wards across a range of violence and public health indicators between 2021 and 2026. Based on this analysis, the 16 boroughs containing the highest-scoring wards have been shortlisted as eligible for the programme.
The VRU is seeking community-based organisations or consortium bids led by a lead provider to deliver the programme across these boroughs. Bidders will be invited to provide additional evidence of local need within their proposed delivery locations as part of the application process.
Eligible Boroughs:
1. Lambeth 2. Croydon 3. Southwark 4. Tower Hamlets 5. Newham 6. Enfield 7. Haringey 8. Hackney 9. Lewisham 10. Islington 11. Camden 12. Brent 13. Hillingdon 14. Greenwich 15. Wandsworth 16. Barking and Dagenham

title: ECC049 - Words and Worlds (Artist in Residence)
description:
Works & Worlds is a bespoke methodology developed and delivered by the awarded supplier. The project model, workshop structure, editorial process, anthology production approach and celebration event format has been refined through multiple successful iterations.
The project's success is directly linked to this established approach, which combines creative writing facilitation, oral storytelling, community engagement, editorial development, publishing and participant celebration in a distinctive format. Replicating this model through another provider would require significant investment, and redevelopment. Not only would this be costly, but it would risk losing the authenticity and impact that have become synonymous with the awarded supplier.
The primary aim of the project is to amplify voices that are often underrepresented in mainstream cultural activity and will seek to work with individuals who:
• Have limited confidence in creative writing
• Have complex relationships with formal education
• Have varying literacy levels
• May speak multiple languages
• Have experienced social exclusion or marginalisation.
Delivery requires skilled and experienced facilitators, who can create safe, inclusive and accessible environments. The project's ethos preserves participants' authentic voices, ensuring contributors feel ownership of their stories and represented within the final publication/showcase.

title: MEH&UCL Relocation Services
description:
This procurement was conducted by Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust ("MEH") in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. University College London ("UCL IoO") (acting through its Institute of Ophthalmology) participated in this procurement. UCL is not a contracting authority for the purposes of the Procurement Act 2023, and by its participation in this process has not submitted to the provisions of that Act.
Two separate contracts were entered into. Although this notice is published as a single notice, it relates to two distinct contracts, both entered into with Crown Workspace Limited following the same procurement process:
- a contract between MEH and Crown Workspace Limited, to the value of £385,252.00 excluding VAT; and
- a contract between UCL (acting for its Institute of Ophthalmology) and Crown Workspace Limited, to the value of £195,812.44 excluding VAT.
The total contract value stated in this notice is the combined value of both contracts and should be read as split between the two contracts as set out above. Each contract covers only the relocation requirements of the organisation that entered into it, and each organisation is responsible for its own contract, budget and commercial schedule.
The procurement was carried out to appoint a single supplier to deliver relocation services for both organisations, with each organisation entering into its own contract with the successful Tenderer at the conclusion of the process.
MEH and UCL IoO sought to appoint a suitably experienced supplier to provide relocation services in support of the planned relocation of clinical, research, laboratory and administrative services from existing sites to a new integrated centre.
The contract scope included the coordinated planning, management and delivery of relocation and decanting activities for hospital clinical services and laboratory services and associated assets. This included specialist equipment, fridges and freezers, chemicals, wet laboratory items including biological samples, information technology equipment and general administrative facilities.
The appointed supplier was required to deliver a safe, controlled and sequenced move approach that maintained service continuity and managed the constraints and risks associated with clinical service operations and laboratory environments.
Existing sites included:
- Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, 162 City Road, London EC1V 2PD (and associated satellite buildings); and
- University College London Institute of Ophthalmology, 11-43 Bath Street, London EC1V 9EL.
The new integrated centre ("Oriel") is located at:
- 4 St Pancras Way, London NW1 0QG.
The contracts were awarded following a two-stage competitive flexible procedure under the Procurement Act 2023.

These channels have been historically disconnected from the floodplain through the artificial raising of the main river and parallel Mill Race (Snobs Brook) to power the historic water mills and more recently aid recreational navigation.
The attached construction plans detail the proposed scheme that currently has live applications for both Flood Risk Assessment Plan (FRAP - Environment Agency) and Section 38 - Works on Common Land (Planning Inspectorate). We are seeking an experienced river restoration contractor to deliver the scheme on this sensitive, public site close to the historic city centre. 
Bidders are required to demonstrate significant experience in delivering similar schemes on river floodplains with public access, grazing animals, tree and protected species constraints.

title: Window Cleaning Services
description:
The University of Edinburgh will shortly be going out to tender via a Restricted Procedure to engage suitably qualified, resourced and experienced suppliers to provide window cleaning services across the estate.
The University of Edinburgh is procuring window cleaning services across a large and diverse estate, including historic listed buildings and modern facilities, spanning multiple campus locations. The requirement is for a prompt, efficient and consistently high-quality service delivered year-round (52 weeks), with capacity to flex to changing priorities and emerging needs. Suppliers are expected to work collaboratively with University representatives and operate in a way that minimises disruption, as many buildings will be occupied during service delivery.
Window cleaning requirements include both planned/programmed cleans and reactive/short-notice cleans. For planned works, cleaning will be scheduled in advance and must be delivered to agreed timescales, with early notification to the University if issues arise that may affect delivery. For reactive requests, the University requires a same working day response to enquiries, with a quotation and agreed delivery timescales within 24 hours. Predominant cleaning method is expected to be reach and wash, however some buildings will require alternative access methods such as rope access/abseiling and MEWPs, and bidders must demonstrate capability to deliver these safely and compliantly.
A key operational feature is significant peak demand during defined periods, with a requirement for sufficient staffing, vehicles and equipment to deliver high volumes within short timescales. Quality sign-off is required following completion of cleans (by the University’s nominated representative). Contractors are responsible for taking due care of University fixtures and fittings and must report any defects discovered (e.g., broken or defective windows, hinges, safety catches) and any accidental damage immediately, in line with contract reporting procedures.

title: Event Management System
description:
Background
Innovate UK Business Connect brings together businesses, researchers, investors and partners to accelerate innovation across the UK. As part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), and a strategic delivery partner to Innovate UK, we connect organisations to funding opportunities, partnerships and expertise to help ideas move from concept to scale. 
One of the key tools for making these connections is events. We deliver a diverse portfolio of in-person, virtual and hybrid events, ranging from webinars and workshops to large-scale conferences and exhibitions. 
To support the effective planning, delivery and evaluation of these events, we are seeking proposals from suppliers who can provide a modern event management system that streamlines event operations, enhances the participant experience and supports data-driven decision-making.
Description of work
Innovate UK Business Connect is seeking tenders from providers who can supply a single event management system that supports the end-to-end event lifecycle, including event creation, registration management, attendee communications, speaker and exhibitor management, networking, reporting and post-event evaluation. 
The system should integrate with existing business systems where required and provide a single source of truth for event delivery teams. This aligns with the organisation's wider objective of ensuring events are outcome-led, measurable and supported by efficient registration, communication and reporting processes.
The event management system should:
•	Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up
•	Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors
•	Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency
•	Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance
•	Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models
•	Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI
•	Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements
The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: 
•	Event Managers
o	Full end-to-end event management capabilities
o	Creation, configuration and administration of events
o	Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors 
o	Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data
•	Marketing Managers 
o	Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content
o	Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting
•	Integrated Systems
o	Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) 
o	Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes
o	Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations
•	System Administrators
o	 A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals)
o	Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration
We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually.
The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including:
•	In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees
•	Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity.
•	Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups.
The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats.
Timings
This is a two-stage evaluation process. We will do an initially score of each supplier bid with the top two or three scoring suppliers invited to provide a demonstration. 
This will be the opportunity for the selected suppliers to demonstrate the setup of an event using a given scenario. 
Anticipated timeline:
•	October: demo
•	November: final evaluation
•	November - December: Contract is awarded
•	1 April 2027: Contract starts
•	April - September: Onboarding, training, templates created and integrations built
•	September onwards: Events start to be managed from the platform
Cost
The maximum value of this requirement over the three-year period is a maximum of £600,000.00 excluding VAT.
This contract is structured as an initial two-year period with a maximum budget of £400,000.00 excluding VAT with an optional 12-month extension valued at maximum £200,000.00 excluding VAT.
Submission
In response to this tender, please provide the information listed below.
•	Short narrative describing your overall approach to working with Innovate UK Business Connect 
•	Checklist against the requirements
•	Supporting information against the essential requirements
•	A rate card of costs associated with services you provide
•	A completed copy of the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire including:
o	A copy of your audited accounts for the most recent two years (or alternative means of demonstrating financial status if trading for less than a year)
•	Legal information i.e. Your standard T&Cs
Please provide the information requested above to re.support@iukbc.org.uk by 17:00 10 October 2026 at the latest. IR35 will be assessed before the awarding of a successful contract. Submissions sent without relevant documents as listed above will be automatically rejected. 
Innovate UK Business Connect may require successful submissions to be subject to non-disclosure agreements.
Evaluation structure
Submissions will be scored against the following areas:
•	Value for money - 20% 
•	Technical specification - 70%
o	alignment to objective 10%
o	essential requirements 40%
o	desirable requirements 20%
•	Demonstration - 10%

Known-unknown risks:
1- Declining or failing end markets
Impact: Financial pressure, operational disruption, and performance risks for both the Contractor and the Authority.
Why this cannot be addressed upfront: Neither party can accurately forecast long‑term end‑market viability or values, making upfront risk pricing potentially disproportionate and poor value for money.
2- Geopolitical events / Wars / Blockades
Impact: Service delays, reduced recycling performance, financial pressure on the Contractor, or value‑for‑money risks for the Authority
Why this cannot be addressed upfront: Pricing, service volumes, and operational impacts cannot be accurately or proportionately quantified at contract inception without introducing excessive risk premiums.
3- Extreme weather events
Impact: Effects to service continuity, performance standards, and contract affordability.
Why this cannot be addressed upfront: It is not possible to price or fully mitigate all operational and financial impacts upfront without introducing disproportionate cost or risk premiums.
There is a possibility that the contract may require modification if one of the identified risks above materialise

title: Primary Care Orthodontic Services
description:
Orthodontics is the dental specialty concerned with facial growth, development of the dentition and occlusion, and the assessment, diagnosis, interception and treatment of malocclusions and facial deformity.
Orthodontic treatment should only be undertaken where it is believed to be in the patient's best interests in terms of their oral health and/ or psychosocial wellbeing. The clinical advantages and long-term benefits of Orthodontic treatment should justify and outweigh any detrimental effects.
Patient factors to consider include co-operation, motivation and their ability to maintain good oral hygiene. It is not generally in the patient's best interest to deliver orthodontic treatment in the absence of a stable oral environment or where there is evidence of active dental disease.
There are several factors used to define orthodontic treatment complexity which can be classified as level 1, 2, 3a or 3b. Factors include the type of malocclusion, technical difficulty in improving function and aesthetics, together with any patient modifying factors.

title: Appointment of an Independent Competent Person (ICP) to support undertaking Safety Verification for the Mass Transit Project (Sheffield Supertram Network)
description:
The purpose of this exercise is to support the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority (SYMCA) to identify and select an appropriate procurement route for appointing an 'Independent Competent Person' as defined in the Railways and Other Guided Systems (Safety) Regulations 2006 in relation to the Mass Transit (Supertram) Renewal Project. 
SYMCA is keen to understand market capability, preferred contractual routes, and an anticipated cost for the services required.  
This exercise consists of a short market engagement questionnaire for completion and return.
SYMCA is the owner of the South Yorkshire Supertram system, a 29km light rail network running predominately within the city of Sheffield in South Yorkshire, England, UK. The network includes two fleets of trams (32 vehicles in total), 29km of tracks, 12 substations, one depot, 29km of overhead line electrification, numerous civil engineering assets including bridges, an underpass, earthworks and drainage, and signalling and communications assets. The network originally opened in 1994 and was extended in 2018 into the neighbouring town of Rotherham using innovative tram train technology.   
The network was previously operated by South Yorkshire Supertram Limited between 1994-2024 which was a subsidiary of national transport operator Stagecoach Group. When this contract ended, SYMCA appointed South Yorkshire Future Trams Limited (SYFTL) to operate the system and undertake day to day maintenance. SYFTL, which is a subsidiary company of SYMCA, is contracted via an Operating Agreement, which allows SYMCA to act as the commissioner (specifying the service levels, maintenance and cleaning standards etc.) with SYFTL responsible for the delivery. Under the Operating Agreement, SYMCA is generally responsible for the funding and delivery of renewals and investment into the system.
The Railways and Other Guided Systems (Safety) Regulations (ROGS) place obligations on both SYFTL and SYMCA in relation to managing the network's safety. SYFTL is a Transport Undertaking as the entity which runs trams on the network. SYMCA is the Infrastructure Manager through its role in strategic management of the assets which form the tramway and its role in delivering renewals, however certain activities are undertaken by SYFTL under delegation. Therefore both SYFTL and SYMCA meet the definition of a 'Transport Operator' under ROGS.
1ROGS places certain obligations on Transport Operators where new or modified infrastructure and vehicles are introduced, including the requirement to undertake formal Safety Verification where a Duty Holder's Safety Management System identifies this requirement. As part of this process, Duty Holders must appoint an Independent Competent Person to support this process.
SYMCA is currently embarking on a significant project to renew many assets forming the network and needs to appoint the services of an Independent Competent Person as described by ROGS.

title: Market Engagement Notice for the Provision of FMS Managed Services
description:
NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. 
The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales.  These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: 
- An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. 
- A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense.
- An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System
- A Warehouse Management System
- Other BI Reporting Systems
The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment.   
The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement.  
The main objectives of this exercise are to: 
- Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS),
- Test market capability and capacity,
- Validate the proposed scope and service model, 
- Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and 
- Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. 
The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model.   
This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project.
Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk).  
When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that:
-	the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions;
-	they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the service; and
-	they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments.
Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October.  There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered.
buyer: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership-Procurement Services (hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust)

The Welsh Government (WG) and Transport for Wales (TfW) share a clear ambition to deliver a more accessible, efficient and sustainable transport network across Wales. Along the west coast of Wales, this includes improving public transport connectivity and encouraging a modal shift away from private car use, in line with the National Transport Delivery Plan and Regional Transport Plans.
A Welsh Transport Appraisal Guidance (WelTAG) Stage 3 appraisal identified the introduction of an express coach service between Bangor and Carmarthen as the preferred intervention to support these objectives. Transport for Wales intends to introduce the service in October 2026 through the appointment of one or more operating partners following completion of a competitive procurement process.
The contract will appoint one or more suitably qualified operators to deliver the express coach service on behalf of Transport for Wales. description:

It is NWF’s intention to award contracts to two (2) suitably qualified suppliers, reflecting the potential for conflicts of interest that may arise in relation to target companies or differences in service line capability and capacity. Each contract is anticipated to be for a duration of four (4) years. Whilst the contracts will be established on a no‑committed spend basis, it is anticipated that they will represent the default route for the procurement of Management Due Diligence services throughout the contract term.
The required outputs and deliverables associated with the services shall comprise draft and final Management Due Diligence reports.
Services may be undertaken in respect of any combination of the following individuals, as specified by NWF on a case‑by‑case basis:
- Founders and co‑founders
- Executive directors
- Members of the senior leadership team
- Functional leads and other key individuals identified by NWF
Specialisms sought under this contract include:
- Management Capability Assessment (Core Requirement): A comprehensive assessment of the capability, effectiveness, and overall suitability of the target company’s management team.
- Referencing and Evidence Gathering (Core Requirement): The undertaking of referencing and evidence‑gathering activities, which may include, as appropriate: referencing with previous employers or colleagues; referencing with current employees; and blinded or anonymised reference discussions.
- Integrity and Background Checks (Optional Capability): Where relevant to the target company, the completion of integrity and background checks.
- Compensation and Incentives Review (Optional Capability): Where relevant, a review of management remuneration and incentive arrangements, including benchmarking of base salary, variable cash compensation, equity participation, and option schemes.
- Enhanced Team Effectiveness and Psychometric Assessment (Optional Capability): Where relevant, enhanced assessment of team effectiveness, potentially including the administration and interpretation of recognised psychometric or behavioural assessment tools at an individual and/or team level.
- Regulatory, Government, and Stakeholder Engagement (Optional Capability): Where relevant, an assessment of management’s experience in engaging with central and local government bodies, together with experience of regulatory compliance and planning processes.
Suppliers must offer those service lines marked as Core Scope and may apply for any service lines marked Optional Capability within their bid in order to be able to offer them under the contract.

title: Population Health Management (SBS10511)
description:
This procurement covers the Population Health Management framework. The framework will cover population health management software solutions that enable analysis and management of health data from a variety of sources to improve healthcare delivery and decision-making. This will empower Approved Organisations and stakeholders to deliver proactive, personalised care while improving efficiency and supporting preventative health interventions. Also can support addressing health inequalities and the wider social determinants and support the decision-making process across the health and social care sector.
The framework is divided into three lots:
Lot 1: Population Health Management Digital Solutions
Delivery of population health management systems that will support the NHS's and other public sector organisations desire to deliver population level health and care across whole, or large-scale areas of the population - for example, an integrated care system, a city or town, a health community, a large acute Trust or a local authority - or multiples of these.
Lot 1 is suitable for solutions with the below characteristics:
•	Solutions that can address large scale populations, however defined.
•	Multiple features and functionality, covering a wide range of Population Health Management.
•	Typically draws data from a range of sources of other organisations.
•	Horizontal integration to provide large populations to manage.
•	May or may not include the features and functionality of more specialist solutions.
Lot 2:  Consultancy &Support Services
The nature of services will be to address a variety of needs through providing information, advice, direction and potential solutions to customers. Suppliers will be expected to be able to assist customers to make more informed decisions surrounding their population health programme.
• Support of the delivery of population health management to the NHS and broader public sector.
• Consultancy services are about helping the NHS or other public sector organisations that may use this framework to implement and deliver population support for some or all of the people who live in the areas they either commission or provide health and care services to.
• Consultancy could extend across the NHS, wider health, public health, local government, broader policy areas impacting on health (such as transportation policy, housing policy, employment, environmental - other areas of policy relating to population health management and social determinants of health.
• Consultancy might also be more targeted, dealing with a more limited area of healthcare, such as risk stratification, social prescribing, medicines usage, etc.
Lot 3: Combined Solutions
This Lot covers the provision of Population Health Management solutions that deliver bundle services or comprehensive workflows. Population Health Management provided under this Lot should ensure a seamless, integrated approach, delivering all the necessary components required for Approved Organisations.
Across all lots, suppliers must provide:
• Software licences or subscriptions
• Implementation, configuration, and integration services
• Training, onboarding, and change management support
• Ongoing maintenance, updates, and technical support
• Clear service level agreements and performance reporting

title: Victim & Citizen Engagement Technology Solution
description:
Further to the UK1 Pipeline Notice published on 19th November 2025 by BlueLight Commercial Limited (ref: 2025/S 000-077692) in relation to a Victim & Citizen Engagement Technology Solution which will be used by UK law enforcement agencies, this UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is issued to inform the market of a potential future opportunity.  
This Pre-Market Engagement Notice is issued solely for the purposes of information gathering and engagement with the market. It does not constitute a call for competition and create any obligation on the Authority to proceed with a procurement exercise,  or enter into any commercial arrangement. Please note the procurement route and anticipated publication date for this opportunity are yet to be determined. These elements will be confirmed following completion of the market engagement process and development of the Authority’s commercial strategy.  
Any future procurement will be subject to separate formal notice and the publication of full procurement documentation via the Find a Tender Service (FTS). 
BlueLight Commercial Limited (BLC) are conducting Preliminary Market Engagement to gain a better understanding of the market, supplier appetite, capacity, and capability, as well as perceived risks and opportunities. Any learnings will be used to formulate the associated procurement strategy. 
BLC work in collaboration with blue light organisations to maximise commercial benefit to UK emergency services. The focus of this solution will be improving Victim & Citizen Engagement, building trust and confidence, reducing demand within control rooms, and reducing the costs of serving the public by using innovative software to keep both victims and citizens more engaged. The aim is to ensure all forces have access to the most effective, reliable, and innovative solutions available in the market. 
This Solution needs to facilitate the force contact engagement from first contact with a police force to final closure of the contact, and via integration with police systems, e.g. Command and Control, Records Management Systems providing contact and updates throughout the journey without the need to call the force contact centre.  It seeks to further drive standardisation and consistency, whilst helping forces to develop capability and invest in technology which will not only improve the service at first point of contact but will improve the overall contact experience. 
This Solution must facilitate Victim & Citizen engagement to reduce failure demand whilst proactively engaging to ensure high levels of customer (internal and external) trust and confidence. The delivery of the desired solution may be considered to follow the same customer service path as an online application or ordering process. For example, acknowledgement of the initial contact, time appropriate follow up contacts at defined points within the communication journey, and a closure contact at the end of the process.  
All communication will be auditable and align with the Victims code as appropriate. We are looking for solutions that can meet individual force needs and achieve the following: 
*Improve experience of members of the public accessing the policing service 
*Provide the public with consistent updates in a timely manner,  
*Improve public trust, confidence, and satisfaction,  
*Reduce Contact Management demand,  
*Improve force's overall Contact Management performance.

title: UK6 - Step Up to Social Work Cohort 10 Contractor
description:
The Department for Education (DfE) is responsible for children’s services including children’s social care in England. 
Children’s Social Care (CSC) reform is a major priority for the government and backed by £2.5bn investment in this SR period. Government aims to transform children’s services to deliver better outcomes for children and families, as set out in the CSC National Framework. Social Work Workforce is a key enabler of reform: ensuring we have a sufficient and capable workforce to enable better outcomes and contribute to cross-government priorities on tackling Child Sexual Abuse, Domestic Abuse and Violence Against Women and Girls.
To ensure we have sufficient social workers for vulnerable children and their families, the DfE funds the Step Up to Social Work (SUSW) programme. SUSW is a specialist, fast track 14-month programme in child and family social work. The programme is a mixture of academic learning and work placements. Local Authorities form Regional Partnerships with a Higher Education Institution to deliver the academic element of the programme.
The department is awarding a contract for marketing and attraction, recruitment and supporting the application process, working with Regional Partnerships to ensure all 700 funded places are filled. 
The remit of the contractor is to:
a.	Design, manage and host a web portal enabling potential candidates[KP1.1][KP1.2][RH1.3] to register an interest, access programme information and submit applications.
b.	Work with the DfE and Regional Partnerships (RPs) to develop web content.
c.	Programme marketing with a focus on attracting candidates from diverse backgrounds and targeting male applicants.
d.	Provide a candidate helpline.
e.	Conduct eligibility check on qualifications, non-UK equivalency qualifications and eligibility to live and work in the UK.
f.	Develop an applicant tracking system.
g.	Host a timed ‘written exercise’ on the recruitment platform.
h.	Host a booking process for applicants to select a date/time for attendance at an assessment centre.
f.	Provide personnel to support RPs during assessment centres.
g.	Keep candidates engaged throughout the process.
h.	Develop and manage a National Reserve List.
i.	Manage candidate information and data analytics.
j.	Produce an End of Year report detailing RP and candidate satisfaction data and recommend areas of the recruitment process that could be improved.

title: Light Touch Framework for Care Home Provision for Older People and Mental Health Older Persons in Cardiff
description:
Cardiff Council Adult Services are re commissioning their Care Home provision for Older People and Mental Health Older Persons in Cardiff. The intention is to commission these services via a new Light Touch Services Framework, underpinned by a number of key principles. 
1.	It is proposed that the framework is underpinned by a set of principles as set out below:
•	A “Framework First” approach will be taken, whereby all placements are expected to be made through the approved framework, with off-framework placements only permitted in clearly defined exceptional circumstances. This will ensure a consistent approach to decision-making, while also supporting better control of costs, as rates will have been set through the framework arrangement. 
•	Provider Commitment – providers will be required to give the council first refusal on their vacant care home placements.
•	Quality as Standard - Quality will be a key focus of the framework. Only providers meeting established quality standards will be admitted to the framework, with ongoing performance monitored through existing governance processes.  
•	A Fixed and Transparent Pricing Structure - the proposed framework will operate on the basis of set fee levels, with all providers required to accept the Council’s pricing structure as a condition of entry. The rationale for this approach is to address the current variation and unpredictability in placement costs, where prices are often driven by individual bidding behaviour and urgent need. By establishing clear, standardised rates for each care category the new model will introduce transparency and consistency, ensuring that pricing better reflects actual care requirements rather than market pressure or negotiation dynamics. 
•	Maximising Choice and Continuity -a key principle of the framework is to maximise choice for service users, allowing them to choose from all the placements available within the framework that would meet their needs. Support will be provided to service users to assist them and their families in making this choice. The framework will also allow for continuity, allowing individuals to remain with existing providers when a placement becomes permanent or where needs change, as long as those needs can still be met by the existing provider.
•	A City Wide Model - it is proposed that the framework adopts a city-wide model, rather than a locality model as the number of care homes is limited.  Operating a city-wide model will maximise service user choice and help to ensure placement availability, reducing risks associated with limited local capacity. 
•	Supporting Providers and Market Sustainability -a further key principle is that the framework arrangement will support providers, by introducing a more personalised approach to placements and working in partnership with providers to encouraging growth and development in the areas where demand is likely to continue to increase.  
2. It is also proposed that the framework is structured around four lots based on care categories. These will be General Residential, Dementia Residential, General Nursing and Dementia Nursing within each care category there will be 4 sub categories. i) Permanent  ii) Temporary iii) Emergency iv) Respite (planned and unplanned).

title: Justice-wide Intermediary Services - Preliminary Market Engagement
description:
The MoJ is currently exploring the future of intermediary services provision and conducting preliminary market engagement, prior to any procurement process. This notice is published for transparency purposes in accordance with the Procurement Act (2023) and does not constitute the commencement of a procurement.
The MoJ is exploring how these services may be delivered across the Ministry and the wider justice sector. Services being considered include those currently provided under the HMCTS Appointed Intermediary Services Frameworks (HAIS) and the Witness Intermediary Scheme (WIS), in addition to ad hoc intermediary services provided to support His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) and the Parole Board.
You can find out more about the current HAIS arrangements at: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/hmcts-intermediary-services#about-hmcts-intermediary-services
You can find out more about the current Witness Intermediary Scheme at: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/ministry-of-justice-witness-intermediary-scheme
Intermediaries are impartial communication specialists whose primary responsibility is to enable complete, coherent and accurate communication with vulnerable witnesses, defendants and parties in the justice system, in order to improve the quality of evidence and facilitate the vulnerable person’s understanding and participation in the proceedings.
The role of an intermediary includes making an assessment and reporting, orally or in writing, about the communication needs of the vulnerable person and the steps that should be taken to meet those needs. It also includes implementing those measures, at a court hearing or interview, for example at a solicitor’s office or police station.

title: Earth Observation: Data Products and Services for the UK Public Sector 'Public Sector EO'
description:
The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services.
The procurement will comprise two Lots:
Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data
 A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. 
Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services
 A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue.
The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year.
The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate.
The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. 
Dynamic Market Participation
Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register.

The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline.

title: Ecohydrological survey and hydrological restoration plan at Roudsea Wood and Mosses NNR - 2026/2027
description:
This study is funded by and contributes toward the Species Recovery Programme - Raised Bog Lagg Restoration Boosting Species Recovery project. The four species that project addresses are:
- Carex flava - Large Yellow Sedge (a vascular plant)
- Coenophila subrosea - Rosy Marsh Moth
- Rheumaptera hastata - Argent and Sable Moth
- Hagenella clathrata - Window-winged Sedge (a caddisfly)
This contract spans two financial years 2026/27 and 2027/28 to enable background research and a full field season to take place.
The aims of this project are to
-understand and characterise the development of the peatlands at Roudsea and the likely pre-modification status of habitats and ecohydrology.
- understand how modifications from this 'reference' state have influenced the development of what we see today, and how this can be remediated.
- understand how the status of the four species is likely to have been affected by these changes.
- identify where and how these habitats are hydrologically damaged.
- to model the impacts of sea level rise on these habitats and species.
- to design a restoration plan to restore (within the project area) the hydrology of the SSSI Lowland Raised bog, the fen habitat within the wood and to maximise opportunities for the habitats and the four protected species to thrive and be resilient to the impacts of climate change and sea level rise.

title: Road Surface Preservation
description:
Trial project through a Direct award from a framework.  
The purpose of applying a "preservation treatment" to selected roads of the Stockton Council network is to extend their service life. The treatment resolution is to slow down the ageing process of the treated asphalt surface course thus significantly reducing the amount of funds Stockton Council needs to spend on maintenance works. 
The option of applying a "preservation treatment" would provide the Council with an alternative solution to resurfacing. The "preservation treatment" would be cheaper offer than resurfacing which would be beneficial if funding became restricted or was not available. This measure would also be less impactful to local businesses and residents as the process would require the affected roads to be closed for a shorter period of time than for a resurfacing scheme.

description:
Leidos Supply Ltd (LSL) intends to extend contract LSL/DC/0141 for a period of 24 months to ensure continuity of supply whilst the replacement procurement activity is completed, awarded and mobilised.
LSL has reviewed its future requirements and determined that additional time is required to complete the successor procurement and associated implementation activities. The extension is necessary to maintain uninterrupted supply and avoid operational disruption during this period.
LSL considers Cooneen Defence Ltd to be the supplier capable of delivering the specified Waterproof Garments in line with all technical requirements and within the timescale required by the Authority. The Authority considers that a change of supplier within the required timeframe would present significant operational and transition risks, creating a material risk to continuity of supply and operational support.
The proposed extension does not materially alter the overall nature or scope of the contract. At the time of publication, expenditure under the contract remains below the original advertised contract value of £15 million. The extension will enable the remaining contract value to be utilised over an extended delivery period, resulting in expenditure being spread across a total contract duration of six years rather than four years.
It is considered that this contract can be extended without prior publication of a contract notice pursuant to Article 32 of Directive 2014/24/EC of the European Parliament (Regulation 72(1)(c) and Regulation 32(5)(b) of PCR 2015). 
The extension is intended solely to maintain continuity of supply whilst the replacement procurement is concluded, and the successor contract is implemented.

title: Billingham South Community Primary School: Ceiling Replacement Phase 1

This prompted further investigations and a structural assessment of all lath and plaster ceilings throughout the school. The assessment concluded that remedial works were required to stabilise the ceilings and prevent further collapse. To further compound the issue, an asbestos survey identified contamination within the loft spaces resulting from historic mechanical and electrical installation works.
This project represents the first phase of a long-term programme of works aimed at providing a safe environment for the school's occupants and those responsible for maintaining the building in the future.

description:
Greater Norwich, comprising the local authorities of South Norfolk Council (SNC), Broadland District Council (BDC) and Norwich City Council (NCC), also working with Norfolk County Council (Norfolk CC), has an established track record of partnership working in the context of plan-making, strategic infrastructure planning and investment.   
The potential for delivery of a new settlement, or settlements, in the Greater Norwich area was considered during the preparation of the, now adopted, Greater Norwich Local Plan (GNLP).   Whilst none of the potential new settlement sites considered were allocated, the adopted GNLP identified that any review of the local plan in the future would assess the potential for a new settlement or settlements.   
In the context of a proposed GNLP Review, the Greater Norwich Development Partnership (GNDP) has recently committed to developing an evidence base and exploring the potential allocation of land for a new settlement or settlements.
