title: Access to pay check household income data - Contract Award Notice
description: The Welsh Local Government Association (WLGA), on behalf of a consortium of local authorities and other organisations in Wales, has directly awarded a contract to CACI Limited for continued access to the Paycheck household income dataset. The dataset provides modelled estimates of gross household income at individual postcode level and is used by consortium members to support work on Local Housing Market Assesments, Local Development Plans, Strategic Housing Investment Plans and Ward profiles. WLGA facilitates the procurement and management of access to this dataset on behalf of the consortium. CACI Limited is the current provider of the Paycheck household income dataset used by a consortium of local authorities and partner organisations across Wales. The Welsh Local Government Association (WLGA), acting on behalf of a consortium of local authorities and partner organisations across Wales (the “contracting authority”), considers that the conditions for direct award under Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 are met, specifically in relation to technical considerations and the avoidance of disproportionate operational disruption.The Paycheck dataset supplied by CACI Limited is currently embedded within established analytical models, evidence bases, and longitudinal datasets used across multiple Welsh authorities. A change of supplier at this stage would introduce significant incompatibility due to differences in modelling methodologies, data definitions, and dataset structure.Transitioning to an alternative provider would require substantial reworking of analytical models, re-baselining of datasets, and validation of outputs, resulting in loss of comparability over time. This would create disproportionate technical and operational difficulties and would risk delays to statutory planning processes and the robustness of evidence supporting housing and planning decisions.Alternative datasets have been considered at a high level; however, they cannot be adopted within the required timeframe without incurring unacceptable cost, delay, and analytical risk.For these reasons, the contracting authority considers that competition is not feasible at this time without disproportionate disruption.This direct award is strictly limited to a period of 12 months and is intended as a time-limited bridging arrangement only.During this period, WLGA will:Undertake a structured review of technical requirements and available datasetsEngage with the marketPrepare and conduct a compliant competitive procurement for longer-term provisionThe contract duration reflects the minimum period necessary to ensure continuity while this work is undertaken.

title: Medical Examination Gloves
description:
Supply Chain Coordination Limited (“NHS Supply Chain”) intends to procure a National Framework Agreement for the supply of Medical Examination Gloves including but not limited to:
6N Examination Gloves: 6N Nitrile Exam Gloves
Examination Gloves Specialised
Following further review of the category strategy, market landscape, and customer requirements, it has been concluded that Medical Examination Gloves and Surgical Gloves will be procured through separate frameworks.
Whilst the original PME notice (2025/S 000-052117) indicated an intention to combine the two categories into a single framework, subsequent analysis identified that they operate as distinct markets with differing customer needs, supply bases, technical specifications, and procurement considerations. In addition, the categories are subject to different commercial models, pricing mechanisms, market dynamics, and contract management requirements.
Maintaining separate frameworks will enable a more tailored procurement approach for each category, support effective category management, and better align with customer and market needs. This revised approach is expected to enhance supplier engagement, promote competition, and provide greater flexibility to respond to future market developments and evolving customer demand.
We are looking at ways to review the procurement strategy and simplify commercials in terms of agreements and pricing points, rationalise ranges for stocked product. This framework will continue to incorporate sustainability requirements for third party social audits across Medical Examination Gloves.
NHS Supply Chain is assessing the most appropriate procurement approach, and the tendering procedures that may be used for future contract awards.
The Framework Agreement will be entered into between the Authority and individual Supplier(s). The Authority may purchase goods under the Framework Agreement, which will be made available for purchase by:
• any NHS Trust;
• any other NHS entity;
• any government department, agency or other statutory body (for the avoidance of doubt including local authorities); and/or
• any private sector entity active in the UK healthcare sector.
The award of a place on the Framework Agreement does not guarantee any commitment by the Authority or its customers to place any orders under the Framework Agreement.
To participate in NHS Supply Chain procurements, Tenderers must be registered on the Central Digital Platform (CDP) and have shared their information with NHS Supply Chain via the CDP. The CDP is available at: https://www.gov.uk/findtender
Please ensure your details match your account details in Jaggaer, Companies House and CDP.
It is the Suppliers responsibility to ensure the account set up in Jaggaer is in the correct company name. For example, if the name has been set up incorrectly or the business has had changes to its organisation we recommend the following:
Incorrect Name (such as typo) - Contact Jaggaer via the help options (seen on page after logging in) and explain that the details are incorrect and provide correct details.
Company organisation Changes - 2 options:
Note: Audit trails need to be maintained in Jaggaer which makes it difficult to allow changes to business that have had significant changes such as merges of businesses or been purchased by other organisations.
Option 1: Create a new account with new name (preferred).
Option 2: Current account - Contact Jaggaer via the help options (seen on page after logging in) and provide details of the changes (such as a company name change document from companies house).
Tenderers must also be registered on Jaggaer, as all tender activity will be conducted through this system. The Tenderer is responsible for ensuring that its Jaggaer account is set up in the correct company name and that all information is kept up to date. Jaggaer can be accessed via https://nhssupplychain.app.jaggaer.com
The Authority estimates that, in the first 12 months of the Framework, the total value of purchases will be approximately £125,000,000 excluding VAT. Over the full 48-month term, the estimated total value is approximately £500,000,000 excluding VAT. These values are indicative only and do not constitute any guarantee of business with successful Tenderers.
The following requirements are anticipated to apply but are not exhaustive and may be updated in accordance with applicable legislation and/or relevant guidance (please refer to the requirements set out in the ITT):
• ISO Certification
Tenderers must hold ISO 9001: 2015, ISO 13485:2016 or Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP) certification, accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service (UKAS) or internationally recognised equivalent. The certification must cover all relevant elements of the Tenderer’s and the product(s)’ supply chain, including (but not be limited to) sales, manufacturing, storage and distribution. Acceptable UKAS alternatives are listed at: https://global-aci.org/en/full-members
• CE Certification and Declaration of Conformity
Where applicable, valid CE Certification and Declarations of Conformity must be submitted at the tender submission stage.
• Modern Slavery Statement
Tenderers with an annual turnover of £36 million or more must comply with the Modern Slavery Act 2015, publish an annually updated Modern Slavery Statement on their website, and provide a link to that statement.
• Modern Slavery Assessment Tool (MSAT)
Tenderers must have achieved an MSAT score of 41% or above within 12 months prior to the tender close date. The assessment results must be shared with NHS Supply Chain via the ‘share’ function on the Supplier Registration Service (SRS) Portal, available at: https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk
• Third-party Audit
Tenderers must provide evidence of third-party social audits for manufacturing facilities supplying products under the Framework. Audit requirements are expected to include assessment against forced labour risks, including the 11 International Labour Organisation (ILO) Forced Labour Indicators. NHS Supply Chain continues to review its responsible sourcing approach and, as such, third-party audit requirements may be developed further during the procurement process. Further details will be provided within the ITT documentation.
• Evergreen Sustainable Supplier Assessment
Tenderers must have completed the Evergreen Sustainable Supplier Assessment and achieved Level 1 or above within 12 months prior to the Tender Close Date. Guidance and access are available at: https://www.england.nhs.uk/nhs-commercial/central-commercialfunction-ccf/evergreen
• Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP)
Tenderers must provide a valid Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP) link on their website that meets the requirements of PPN 006.
• Cyber Security
Tenderers that handle patient or personal data, or provide IT systems, services, or devices, must either:
• hold a valid Cyber Essentials Plus Certificate; or
• where the Tenderer does not have a Cyber Essentials Plus Certificate, submit a completed Information Security Third Party Questionnaire (ISTPQ).
• Distribution Agreements
If tendering as a Distributor, the Tenderer must provide written evidence from the relevant Original Equipment Manufacturer(s) (OEM) confirming that they have rights to distribute goods for the Term as defined in the Framework Agreement Award Pack. If the Term is extended, Distributors must provide further written evidence from the OEM confirming that they have rights to distribute goods for the remaining Maximum Term as defined in the Framework Agreement Award Pack.

Lot 1 of this Framework is seeking the provision of On Vehicle Digital Technology (AVL, CCTV, APC, TLP, Comms, On Bus Destination, AVA, Bridge Strike Systems & Vehicle Compute Capability).
Lot 1 - has 9 parts:
Lot 1 - Part 1 - Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) Solution
Provision of an integrated Automated Vehicle Location solution capable of accurately determining and communicating vehicle location in real time. The solution shall support route, journey and stop association, estimated arrival/departure information and integration with other onboard and back-office systems. Requirements include resilient positioning, industry-standard data interfaces, remote configuration, monitoring, diagnostics, reporting, security and ongoing support throughout the solution lifecycle.
Lot 1 - Part 2 - Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Solution
Provision of a comprehensive onboard CCTV solution providing appropriate internal and external vehicle coverage for passenger safety, operational management and incident investigation. The solution shall support continuous high-quality recording, secure storage and retrieval, authorised access and evidential integrity. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, equipment health monitoring, remote diagnostics, secure communications, configurable camera arrangements and enhanced analytics where required.
Lot 1 - Part 3 - Automatic Passenger Counting (APC) Solution
Provision of an Automatic Passenger Counting solution capable of accurately recording passenger boarding and alighting and determining vehicle occupancy without driver intervention. The solution shall provide reliable passenger-count data for operational, planning and passenger-information purposes and integrate with onboard and central systems. Requirements include appropriate counting accuracy, standardised interfaces, secure data transfer, reporting, monitoring, diagnostics, remote management and resilient operation.
Lot 1 - Part 4 - Traffic Light Priority (TLP) Solution
Provision of a Traffic Light Priority solution enabling suitably equipped vehicles to request priority at traffic signals based on vehicle location, route and operational circumstances. The solution shall support configurable and conditional priority strategies and integration with vehicle, roadside and central systems. Requirements include secure, low-latency communications, monitoring and reporting, remote configuration, interoperability, performance analysis, testing, cybersecurity and ongoing technical support.
Lot 1 - Part 5 - Comms Tool (Radio) Solution
Provision of an onboard communications solution enabling reliable and secure voice and data communication between drivers, vehicles and operational control functions. The solution shall support operational messaging, service information, alerts and emergency communications through an appropriate driver interface. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, secure communications, operational logging, remote configuration, equipment monitoring, diagnostics and resilient operation across the vehicle fleet.
Lot 1 - Part 6 - On-Bus Destination Solution
Provision of integrated on-bus destination equipment capable of clearly displaying route and destination information to passengers and intending passengers. Solutions shall support appropriate front, side and rear displays, accessibility and visibility requirements and integration with onboard systems to automate displayed information. Requirements include remote configuration, operational overrides, equipment monitoring, diagnostics, secure communications, robust vehicle-grade equipment and ongoing maintenance and support.
Lot 1 - Part 7 - Audio Visual Passenger Information (AVA) Solution
Provision of an accessible onboard Audio Visual Passenger Information solution delivering automated visual and audible information concerning routes, destinations, next stops, disruptions and other relevant passenger messages. The solution shall integrate with vehicle location and onboard systems to trigger information accurately. Requirements include accessible presentation, remote and priority messaging, configurable content, secure communications, monitoring, diagnostics, resilient operation and ongoing system support.
Lot 1 - Part 8 - Bridge Strike Prevention Solution
Provision of an onboard Bridge Strike Prevention solution designed to reduce the risk of vehicles approaching or striking structures with insufficient clearance. The solution shall use vehicle dimensions together with accurate location, mapping and detection information to provide timely audible and visual driver warnings. Requirements include reliable hazard identification, minimisation of false alerts, offline resilience, secure updates, event logging, diagnostics and onboard-system integration.
Lot 1 - Part 9 - Vehicle Compute Capability (VCC) Solution
Provision of a robust onboard Vehicle Compute Capability providing a shared computing platform for hosting, integrating and managing multiple vehicle applications and data services. The solution shall provide sufficient processing capacity, storage and future scalability while supporting secure application separation and interoperability. Requirements include edge processing, secure communications, remote software management, monitoring and diagnostics, onboard-system integration and future expansion throughout its operational lifecycle.
Lot 2 is for Franchising and Wider Transport Ticketing & Payment Consultancy Services. It has 6 Parts:
Lot 2 - Part 1 - Franchised Bus Scheme Development and Implementation Support
The provision of specialist consultancy services to support the development, assessment and implementation of bus franchising schemes. Services may include business cases, network and commercial design, financial modelling, consultation, procurement, mobilisation, integrated fares and ticketing, assets and technology, contract management, service permits, independent assurance and stakeholder engagement.
Lot 2 - Part 2 - Transport Ticketing Management Policy Advice
The provision of strategic, policy and management consultancy relating to transport ticketing and payment systems. Services may encompass ITSO, Stored Value, contactless EMV, barcode and QR ticketing, Account Based and Multi-Token Ticketing, Mobility as a Service, and wider ticketing initiatives across public-sector authorities, transport operators and national organisations.
Lot 2 - Part 3 - Transport Ticketing Technical & Revenue Scheme Delivery
The provision of technical consultancy and delivery support for transport ticketing schemes, including development of technical specifications, implementation and integration of ITSO and other ticketing technologies, Electronic Ticket Machines and ticketing readers. Services may also include management of multi-platform implementations and development of technical solutions through engagement with relevant stakeholders.
Lot 2 - Part 4 - Transport Ticketing Governance, Research and Competitive Bidding Services
The provision of specialist support relating to transport ticketing governance, research, procurement and competitive funding or bidding activities. Services may include governance advice for public and commercial organisations, preparation of grant, tender and franchise submissions, support for public procurement exercises, and research activities contributing to sustainable transport policy and delivery.
Lot 2 - Part 5 - Entitlement (Concessionary) Travel Management Services
The provision of management, policy and project support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, with particular emphasis on revenue reimbursement and apportionment. Services may include multi-operator and multimodal schemes, multiple ITSO HOPS and Customer Management Systems, and schemes operating across multiple ticketing channels, technologies and participating organisations.
Lot 2 - Part 6 - Technical Entitlement (Concessionary) Support Services
The provision of specialist technical support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, including reimbursement implementation, revenue modelling and apportionment, ETM data analysis, national reimbursement guidance and alternative allocation methodologies. Services may also encompass auditable datasets, payment reporting, stakeholder-led revenue solutions and expert technical evidence supporting appeals, tribunals or legal proceedings.

title: Reablement Care Service
description:
The Reablement Care Service shall provide short-term, outcome-focused support to eligible Enfield residents who require assistance to regain, maintain or improve their independence following discharge from hospital.
The externally commissioned support will focus on hospital discharge pathways only and will be underpinned by a strong reablement approach. The service will provide time-limited, person-centred support in residents’ own homes, with the primary aim of enabling individuals to regain confidence, relearn or restore daily living skills, and continue to live as independently as possible within their own home.
Suppliers will be expected to take an enabling, outcome-focused approach, doing with rather than doing for individuals wherever appropriate. Support should help people rebuild practical skills, establish safe routines, improve mobility and confidence, manage everyday tasks, and reduce or avoid the need for ongoing domiciliary care wherever this can be achieved safely.
The Council is seeking market insight on the service delivery models, solutions and areas of emerging best practice that could support the Council’s current requirements and inform improvements to future service delivery. 
Information provided through this exercise will be used for information-gathering purposes only. It may help the Council understand solutions that are available in the market and may inform and shape any future requirements, reflecting common approaches across the marketplace where appropriate.
As outlined above, the intention of the Service is to ensure the provision of high-quality, accessible support for eligible residents requiring reablement support following hospital discharge, promoting independence, safety and wellbeing
Due to the need for a borough-wide service, the Council is currently considering dividing the future service into four (4) Lots, potentially split by four geographical areas: North West, South West, North East and South East of the borough (please refer to the Indicative Service Specification, Appendix 2 and the accompanying Introduction plus Appendix 2.A and Appendix 2.B for further information). Under this model, it is envisaged that four (4) Suppliers would deliver the Council’s next generation Reablement Care Service within a defined geographical area. The Council would welcome organisations’ views and feedback on this potential service delivery model through the SMT Questionnaire.
An indicative Service Specification, Appendix 2, and its accompanying documents (Introduction, Appendix 2.A and Appendix 2.B) are provided as part of the Preliminary Market Engagement documentation.
Additional information
Please note that organisations will not be prejudiced by any response or failure to respond to this preliminary market engagement.

title: TfL Vegetation Inspection Services
description:
Transport for London (TfL) is establishing a contract for vegetation inspection services to enable TfL to access arboricultural, ecological and environmental expertise, whether that is regular, ongoing maintenance or one-off, project-specific requests.
In addition, this contract will require the supplier to provide TfL with full access to, and ownership of, the track inspection and ecological data that is collected. The context supporting this contract is an increased legislative requirement for TfL to be aware of, and report on, ecological data.
The contract will include:
Track-side vegetation inspections - Environmental and vegetation inspections occurring on and around the track, including fencing (if required) inspections, routine off-track PM6 vegetation inspections, cyclical Tree Condition Assessments, possession tree work specifications and canopy corridor assessments in relation to leaf-fall adhesion risk. Inspections will be carried out in line with TfL track engineering safety standards to ensure the track is safe for operation, by suitably certificated personnel (including Sentinel with ICI-LUL endorsement and LANTRA tree inspection qualifications).
Built environment vegetation inspections - Environmental and vegetation inspections in and around station grounds, car parks and green roofs (if required). These inspections will be carried out to ensure TfL's built environment is safe for staff and the public using TfL services.

description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης αποτελεί η λειτουργία Μονάδας Διοίκησης Έργου (εφεξής ΜΔΕ) για την παροχή εξειδικευμένης υποστήριξης της Διακυβέρνησης του Εθνικού Συστήματος Επαγγελματικής Εκπαίδευσης και Κατάρτισης και του Στρατηγικού Σχεδίου, αλλά και η ετοιμασία Μελετών/Εμπειρογνωμοσυνών σε θέματα σχετικά με την ΕΕΚ και τη Δια Βίου μάθηση. Η Μονάδα Διοίκησης Έργου έχει σκοπό την παροχή εξειδικευμένης υποστήριξης κατά τη Διακυβέρνηση του ΣΣ έως το 2029 (και όχι πέραν της λήξης της Πράξης). (Β) Υποστήριξη στην κεντρική διαχείριση εκροών, αναφορών, εκθέσεων και λοιπών εγγράφων των εμπλεκομένων φορέων και διαχείρισή τους. (Γ) Υποστήριξη στην επικοινωνία / συνεργασία επί στρατηγικών θεμάτων. Ενότητα Εργασιών 2: Εκπόνηση Μελετών Εμπειρογνωμοσυνών, που περιλαμβάνονται στην υφιστάμενη Στρατηγική της Επαγγελματικής Κατάρτισης & Δια βίου μάθησης για την Αναβάθμιση της ΕΕΚ. Οι παρεχόμενες υπηρεσίες κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων (CPV): • 72224000-1 Υπηρεσίες παροχής συμβουλών σε θέματα διαχείρισης έργων • 79411000-8: Υπηρεσίες παροχής συμβουλών σε θέματα γενικής διαχείρισης • 79415200-8: Υπηρεσίες παροχής συμβουλών σε θέματα σχεδιασμού • 73200000: Υπηρεσίες παροχής συμβουλών σε θέματα έρευνας και ανάπτυξης Η σύμβαση δεν υποδιαιρείται σε τμήματα λόγω της σχετικότητας και της συμπληρωματικότητας των ζητούμενων υπηρεσιών. Προσφορές υποβάλλονται για το σύνολο της προκηρυσσόμενης σύμβασης. Η εκτιμώμενη αξία της σύμβασης συμπεριλαμβανομένου ανέρχεται στο ποσό των 968.750,00 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ ήτοι 1.201.250,00 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (ΦΠΑ: 232.500,00 €). Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης ορίζεται σε σαράντα τέσσερις (44) μήνες από την υπογραφή της σύμβασης και το αργότερο μέχρι 30-11-2029. Αναλυτική περιγραφή του φυσικού και οικονομικού αντικειμένου της σύμβασης δίδεται στο ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ Ι της Διακήρυξης. Η σύμβαση θα ανατεθεί με το κριτήριο της πλέον συμφέρουσας από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει της βέλτιστης σχέσης ποιότητας-τιμής

title: Germany – Environmental planning – Machbarkeitsstudie: Rahmenbedingungen für den Schutz des Welterbes vor den Folgen des Klimawandels verbessern
description: Deutschland ist verantwortlich für den Erhalt des außergewöhnlichen universellen Wertes von derzeit (2026) 55 UNESCO-Welterbestätten (52 Kulturerbestätten und 3 Naturerbestätten) sowie acht Geoparks. Die UNESCO und ihre Beratergremien werten Klimawandelfolgen als höchste Gefährdung für den langfristigen Erhalt des Kultur- und des Naturerbes. Die materiellen Schäden durch akute und schleichende Klimawandelfolgen steigern nicht nur die Kosten des Erhalts, viele Verluste und Schäden sind monetär auch nicht zu kompensieren und gefährden den außeror-dentlichen, universellen Wert des Welterbes. Das Bundesministerium für Umwelt, Klimaschutz und nukleare Sicherheit (BMUKN) koordiniert federführend die Klimaanpassungsstrategie des Bundes. Der Schutz der UNESCO Welterbestätten und der UNESCO Geoparks in Deutschland ist als ressortübergreifendes Ziel angelegt, wobei die Bundesländer und die jeweils zuständigen Stellen vor Ort die Verantwortung für die Umsetzung tragen. Das Bundeskabinett hat 2024 Ziele, Unterziele und Maßnahmen für das Handlungsfeld „Schutz des Welterbes“ in der Klimaanpassungsstrategie beschlossen. Im Rahmen der Deutschen Anpassungsstrategie an den Klimawandel (DAS 2024) gibt es für ressortübergreifende Handlungsfelder ein Cluster „Übergreifendes“, welches gemeinsame Ziele der Ressorts enthält. Das BMUKN führt die Aktivitäten des Bundesministeriums für Bauen, Wohnen und Stadtentwicklung (BMWSB), des Beauftragten für Kultur und Medien (BKM) sowie des Auswärtigen Amtes (AA) zusammen und steuert die Zielerreichung. Dabei trägt jedes Ressort im Rahmen seiner Zuständigkeiten eigenverantwortliche Maßnahmen bei, die in der Summe die Zielerreichung gewährleisten. Für den Schutz des Welterbes vor den Folgen des Klimawandels ist als Ziel Ü-4 im Cluster „Übergreifendes“ in der Klimaanpassungsstrategie des Bundes Folgendes verankert: „Der Bund zeigt einen nationalen Rahmen mit Indikatoren und Maßnahmen auf entsprechend der internationalen Grundsatzdokumente und Aktionspläne und im Einklang mit den Verpflichtungen der Welterbekonvention, damit die UNESCO-Welterbestätten in Deutschland bis 2030 Klimaschutzmaßnahmen und/oder Klimaanpassungskonzepte oder -pläne (zum Beispiel als Teil ihrer Managementpläne, Pläne für das Katastrophenrisikomanagement und Rahmenkonzepte) entwickeln können.“ Das Ziel wird durch drei Unterziele und Maßnahmen konkretisiert. Die Unterziele lauten wie folgt: (Ü-4-1) Informations- und Datenmanagement verstetigen (Ü-4.2) Unterstützung der Maßnahmen zur Klimaanpassung der Welterbestätten im Rahmen verfügbarer Ressourcen. (Ü-4.3) Förderung von Klimaanpassungsmaßnahmen Welterbestätten im Rahmen verfügbarer Ressourcen. Für das das Ziel Ü 4 und seine Unterziele (Ü-4.1, Ü 4-2 und -Ü-4.3) sind zudem weitere Unterstützungsmaßnahmen formuliert. Für ein koordiniertes Vorgehen der Ressorts sind nun im Nachgang zu dem Kabinettsbeschluss 2024 der Sachstand und die Fortschritte bei der Zielerreichung zu bestimmen. Entsprechend der Maßnahmen zu den Unterzielen sind u.a. institutionelle Vorschläge, wie der Aufbau einer Koordinierungsstelle oder die Vernetzung auf Machbarkeit und Anknüpfungsmöglichkeiten einzuschätzen. Diesbezüglich beabsichtigt das BMUKN eine Studie in Auftrag zu geben.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Studie Zukunftsprojektion und Entwicklungspotentiale der Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft 2037
description: In den vergangenen fast 20 Jahren seit Gründung der Initiative Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft (KKW) der Bundesregierung haben sich die Rahmenbedingungen, Marktstrukturen, Wertschöpfungsketten und Herausforderungen für die KKW grundlegend verändert. Kaum eine Branche ist von den Auswirkungen durch den Wandel von Transformation, Plattformökonomie, Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz so stark betroffen wie die KKW mit Auswirkungen u.a. auf kreative Produktion, Distribution und Rechteverwertung. Die kommenden Jahre werden durch weitere tiefgreifende technologische, wirtschaftliche und gesellschaftliche Umbrüche geprägt sein. Digitalisierung (insb. Künstliche Intelligenz), Nachhaltigkeit und neue Formen der Publikumseinbindung sind zu den zentralen Treibern der Veränderung geworden. Nach fast 20 Jahren ist es daher an der Zeit einerseits Bilanz zu ziehen, und andererseits den Blick nach vorne zu richten und Grundlagen für strategische Handlungsoptionen zu schaffen. Um den weiteren Strategieprozess evidenzbasiert führen zu können soll eine qualitative und quantitative Grundlagenstudie zur Zukunftsprojektion für die KKW in Auftrag gegeben werden. Die letzte Grundlagenstudie „Gesamtwirtschaftliche Perspektiven der Kultur und Kreativwirtschaft“, ebenfalls erstellt im Auftrag des BMWE, stammt aus dem Jahr 2009. Die Studie soll eine Projektion für die kommende Dekade entwickeln, um strategische Antworten auf strukturelle Veränderungen der Branche zu geben. Es geht darum, die Zukunftsfähigkeit der KKW kritisch zu beleuchten, Risiken zu identifizieren sowie eine Prognose zu Chancen und Trends zu entwickeln. Die Studie „Kultur und Kreativwirtschaft 2037“ (Arbeitstitel) soll mit Hilfe zukunftsorientierter und prognostizierter Szenario-Analysen ein Fundament für eine langfristige strategische Ausrichtung politischer und ökonomischer Steuerungsinstrumente liefern. Für eine Zukunftsprojektion bis 2037 ist daher entscheidend, nicht allein bestehende Wachstumsverläufe fortzuschreiben, sondern strukturelle Brüche, neue Wertschöpfungslogiken und disruptive technologische Entwicklungen systematisch in die Prognose einzubeziehen. Als Grundlagen sind hier die Projektionen der Bundesregierung zum gesamtwirtschaftlichen Wachstum angemessen zu berücksichtigen. Die Studie soll ein wissenschaftliches Fundament für die strategische Weiterentwicklung der Initiative Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft der Bundesregierung schaffen und dabei insbesondere eine langfristige strategische Ausrichtung politischer und ökonomischer Steuerungsinstrumente liefern. Die Strategie richtet sich perspektivisch an Entscheidungsträgerinnen und -träger aus Politik, Wirtschaft, Verwaltung sowie an die Akteure der Kultur und Kreativwirtschaft selbst, die gemeinsam die Weichen für ein nachhaltiges, innovatives und wirtschaftlich starkes Kreativökosystem der nächsten Generation stellen wollen.

title: NEL ICB Latent Tuberculosis Infection (LTBI) Screening Programme (Lots 1-6)

NHS North East London Integrated Care Board (ICB) has concluded a competitive process
under Provider Selection Regime to appoint providers of  National Latent Tuberculosis Infection (LTBI) Services - Testing Service.
The Latent Tuberculosis Infection (LTBI) Screening Programme aims to reduce the incidence of active tuberculosis (TB) through the early identification and treatment of individuals infected with Mycobacterium tuberculosis who do not have active disease.
By preventing progression to active TB, the programme contributes to the elimination of TB as a public health threat and supports national and global TB reduction strategies.
Specifically, the programme aims to:
• Prevent the development of active, transmissible TB through detection and treatment of LTBI;
• Protect public health by interrupting the chain of transmission within communities;
• Support national TB control and elimination goals;
• Promote health equity by ensuring access to screening and care for populations at increased risk.
The service aims to reduce the incidence of tuberculosis (TB) across the populations of Newham, Tower Hamlets, City & Hackney, Redbridge, Barking & Dagenham, and Waltham Forest.

title: West Yorkshire Supply Chain Programme
description: West Yorkshire has a strong manufacturing economy worth £7.7 billion and employing around 110,000 people. The region is home to nearly 6,000 manufacturing SMEs which play a crucial role within local, national and international supply chains. However, there is currently a gap in dedicated supply chain support, with many SMEs facing challenges around supply chain fragmentation, procurement readiness, diversification, access to new markets and engagement with larger organisations. These challenges can limit business growth, competitiveness and resilience. The Combined Authority is seeking to procure an experienced delivery partner to design and deliver a comprehensive supply chain support programme across West Yorkshire. The programme will support manufacturing SMEs to strengthen supply chain capability, diversify into high-growth sectors including defence and energy security, improve procurement readiness, secure relevant accreditations, adopt new technologies and access opportunities with OEMs, Primes and larger organisations. The programme will also facilitate engagement activities, networking opportunities, workshops, masterclasses and business support interventions that help businesses secure new contracts and grow within regional, national and international supply chains. title: AMCV 355 - Digital Solutions to Support Unpaid Carers
description:
Shropshire Council is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to understand the current market for digital solutions that support unpaid carers. This engagement will help inform the Council’s future commissioning approach before any decision is made about whether to tender, use an existing compliant route, develop an alternative model, or take no further procurement action.
Shropshire Council has an established Unpaid Carer Support offer.  Recently this has become an all-age offer supporting Young Carers and Parent Carers. The Unpaid Carers portal will be an online offer which will be available to Unpaid Carers 24/7 throughout the journey of their caring role. We are aware there are a large proportion of people who do not identify as an Unpaid Carer, we envisage the portal will support with that identification and will provide relevant up to date information to support families in a preventative manner.
Any proposed solution should offer the following support:
Increase the identification recognition and early interventions for unpaid Carers
Delay and reduce the need to access high-cost statutory provision
Improve accessibility to information, advice and guidance, improve links and signposting to services that are already available nationally, regionally and locally.
Support Unpaid Carers to access self-help and self-management support to reduce the need for Unpaid Carers crisis interventions.
Include access to Unpaid Carers 'self-assessment' focused on individualised outcomes
The solution should have the capacity to collect and produce relative data regarding demographics, ethnicity, age range as well as information such as when and where the portal is accessed.

description:

The London Borough of Croydon is undertaking preliminary market engagement in relation to the potential commissioning of an Erasmus+ teacher/educator training and international mobility programme for Croydon schools.
The Council is seeking expressions of interest only from organisations with demonstrable previous experience of managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects and international education mobility programmes on behalf of schools or public-sector organisations.
The appointed provider would be expected to provide end-to-end programme management, including:
•	Previous experience of successfully managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects, including details of the number and type of projects delivered
•	Management and coordination of international teacher training, CPD and school visits across European destinations, with destinations to be confirmed
•	Organisation and management of participant travel, accommodation, and associated logistics
•	Support with participant recruitment and selection, including ensuring appropriate eligibility and allocation processes
•	Management of Erasmus+ grant administration, financial monitoring, evidence, and reporting requirements
•	Support for safeguarding, risk management and participant welfare throughout the programme
•	Delivery or commissioning of high-quality teacher CPD and training aligned to the agreed programme objectives
•	Development and implementation of programme evaluation, impact measurement, and outcomes reporting
•	Monitoring and reporting on participant outcomes and the wider impact of the programme on participating schools; and
•	Effective stakeholder management and communication with the Council, schools, training providers, and international partners.
The programme is intended to support Croydon schools in developing practice in areas including inclusion and SEND, digital and AI-enabled education, wellbeing, sustainability, innovation, and oracy/communication-rich learning, aligned with relevant Erasmus+ priorities.
Providers should only register an interest where they can demonstrate the relevant specialist experience, capacity, international networks and organisational infrastructure required to manage an Erasmus+ mobility programme from participant selection through to final evaluation and grant reporting.

title: Mid Sussex District Council Hard Facilities Management Services
description:
Mid Sussex District Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement to inform the development of a potential future procurement for the provision of Hard Facilities Management services across its property estate. 
Mid Sussex District Council is a local authority in West Sussex, covering a district that includes the towns of Haywards Heath, Burgess Hill and East Grinstead, together with surrounding villages and rural areas. The Council manages a varied property estate supporting public services, operational delivery, commercial activity and community use. Approximately 118 properties are expected to be included within the scope of the contract, subject to final confirmation of the property list, service requirements and procurement strategy. 
The Council is seeking to understand market interest, capacity, delivery models and supplier feedback before finalising its procurement strategy, service specification, commercial approach and timetable. This notice is intended to encourage early interest from suitably experienced providers and to support an open, fair and proportionate future procurement process. 
The anticipated scope may include, but is not limited to, planned preventative maintenance, statutory compliance, mechanical and electrical services, building fabric maintenance, reactive repairs, emergency call-outs, specialist servicing, asset data management, lifecycle advice, compliance reporting, minor works and works projects. 
The Contract may include provision for the delivery of minor works and project works up to an agreed value threshold, where these fall within the scope of the Hard FM Services.  Any such works would be instructed in accordance with the MSDC Procurement Code, financial regulation and the Council's governance requirements.  The Council would retain the right to test the market, seek alternative quotations, or otherwise satisfy itself that value for money is beng achieved. The appointed supplier will be expected to use the Council's CAFM system as required for receiving and managing work orders, updating asset and compliance records, reporting progress, and supporting effective contract management. 
The Council's estate may include, office, operational, commercial, public-facing and community buildings including temporary residential accommodation. The final property list, service scope, contract value, procurement route, lotting structure and contract duration have not yet been confirmed and may be refined following this engagement. 
The Council is currently proposing a contract term of four years, with the option to extend by up to two further periods of one year each, subject to performance, ongoing need and the Council's governance requirements. 
The anticipated contract commencement date is Summer 2027, subject to completion of procurement, award, governance approvals and mobilisation arrangements. 
The Council currently anticipates that the contract will be based on the NEC4 form of contract and will include requirements relating to social value, local supply chain opportunities, sustainability and wider community benefit. The detailed contractual model, performance mechanisms and social value requirements will be developed as part of the procurement preparation process and may be informed by supplier feedback received through this engagement.
This preliminary market engagement exercise is not a procurement competition and does not commit the Council to commencing any procurement, awarding any contract, or accepting any proposal. The Council reserves the right to amend the scope, timetable, procedure, contract structure or any other aspect of any future opportunity following this engagement. Failure to respond to this notice will not affect your ability to participate in any future procurement exercise. 
The Council will take appropriate steps to ensure that any preliminary market engagement is conducted transparently and does not distort competition or provide any supplier with an unfair advantage.

title: Coding NDNS Consumption data into EFSA’s food classification+description -FoodEx
description:
As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to.  
To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS).  The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. 
Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food.

title: Employee Voice Pre Market Engagement
description:
Organisations are invited to take part in the pre maket engagement seek input from market participants to inform and help Ofcom inform our procurement strategy for our employee voice programme. 
Ofcom currently relies on an annual colleague survey as the primary means of gathering measurable feedback on employee experience. This model does not provide sufficiently timely or agile insight into emerging colleague experience, culture, engagement and organisational challenges. As a result, there is a risk that feedback is gathered too infrequently to support timely action and evidence-based decision making.
The opportunity is to explore how to procure a pulse survey tool that enables shorter, more frequent colleague surveys, as well as the ability to run multiple surveys in parallel across different populations and topics. This would support a more agile employee listening model, provide quicker insight into priority issues, and strengthen the link between colleague feedback and visible action.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?​
description:
With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed.
Dialysis journeys account for more than 40% of all non-emergency patient transport activity, costing 9.1 million GBP annually. Yet current arrangements can be inconsistent, creating avoidable pressures for patients, providers and NHS services.
NHS Scotland is seeking innovative, patient-centred and sustainable solutions that improve reliability, efficiency and patient outcomes, while reducing administrative burden and delivering better value for money.

title: Civtech 12 - Challenge 12.2 - How can technology enable fast-growing digital public service providers to dynamically scale their service management capabilities as demand, complexity and customer expectations increase?

description:
This is a Preliminary Market Engagement Notice (PMEN). It is not a formal invitation to tender. You will need to respond to the tender notice ( when it is issued) in order to be considered for these contracts. 
The purpose of this PMEN is to maximise transparency and competition for the upcoming tender notice and to advertise a market engagement event. All details in this PMEN are subject to being updated or changed in the tender notice. We are publishing this notice to ensure as wider audience as possible are aware and informed of Norfolk County Council's intentions. 
The PMEN fulfils the requirement for a Preliminary Market Engagement Notice to be issued under the Procurement Act 2023. There are no tender documents at this stage.
Norfolk County Council intends to procure a new framework for Educational Psychology, Occupational Therapy and Speech, Language and Communication services for children and young people. The framework will support statutory responsibilities, early intervention, inclusion and improved outcomes through evidence-based, person-centred and outcome-focused provision.
Scope of the Future Procurement
The forthcoming framework will cover the following service areas:
•	Educational Psychology: evidence-based psychological services for children and young people aged 0-25, including psychological advice for Education, Health and Care needs assessments, contributions to Education, Health and Care Plans, tribunal-related activity where required, and support to Specialist Resource Bases.
•	Occupational Therapy: evidenced based occupational therapy services within our educational settings including advice for Education, Health and Care needs assessments, contributions to Education, Health and Care Plans, tribunal-related activity including assessment, reports and attendance at court where required, support to Specialist Resource Bases and moving and handling training to staff at educational settings.
•	Speech, Language and Communication: specifically relating to tribunal activity including assessment, reports and attendance at court when required.
The detailed requirements, eligibility criteria, referral routes, delivery standards and performance expectations for each service area will be set out in the tender documents and relevant service specifications.
Market Engagement
The Council intends to hold a market engagement event for prospective providers. The date and joining arrangements will be confirmed through the Council's e-procurement system.  The expected date for the event is 30th September 2026. 
Prospective providers wishing to participate should register on In-tend, express an interest in the project and use the correspondence facility to provide the email addresses of proposed attendees when requested.
This procurement will be managed electronically via the Council`s e-procurement system. To participate in this procurement and gain access to documents when they are available, applicants must first be registered on the system at https://in-tendhost.co.uk/norfolkcc. Full instructions for registration and use of the system can be found at https://intendhost.co.uk/norfolkcc/aspx/BuyerProfiles. Once registered you will be able to see the procurement project under the `tenders` section and `express an interest` in this tender. title: NWS Independent Assurance Service
description:
The service shall provide confidence that all designs, construction activities, quality management processes and technical decisions are compliant with regulatory requirements, aligned with approved standards, and capable of delivering the required long-term environmental and operational performance of the Repository.
The proposed Independent Assurance Services may support Nuclear Waste Services (NWS) across its wider business and repository-related demand, including but not limited to focusing on the activities at the LLW Repository near Drigg and the lifecycle of the Vault Optimisation & Capping Delivery (VOCD) Framework, which scope includes repository capping, adherence to regulatory guidance on landfill design and construction, use of Best Available Techniques etc.
The Independent Assurance Services scope is not intended to be exclusive to the LLWR site and may extend to other NWS programmes, projects, assets or locations where independent construction quality assurance, technical design assurance or critical friend assurance services are required. 
The service shall support the achievement of regulatory confidence, audit readiness and effective delivery of NWS programmes through independent challenge, review, verification and certification activities.
The services shall comprise of three primary functions:
1) Independent Construction Quality Assurance (CQA):
• Review and development of Construction Quality Assurance Plans.
• Inspection, surveillance and audit activities.
• Verification of materials, workmanship and installation.
• Hold point and witness point inspections.
• Review of contractor quality records.
• Assessment of non-conformances and concessions.
• Verification of testing and validation activities.
• Compilation of assurance evidence and records.
• Preparation of Construction Quality Assurance Validation Reports.
The service shall provide confirmation that completed works have been delivered in accordance with approved design and regulatory requirements.
2) Independent Technical Design Assurance (TDA):
• Independent review of design deliverables.
• Verification of technical assumptions and methodologies.
• Independent challenge of engineering decisions.
• Design compliance assessments.
• Constructability reviews.
• Long-term performance reviews.
• Participation in design reviews and technical governance processes.
• Verification of action close-out.
• Production of design assurance recommendations and reports.
The service shall support informed technical decision-making and confidence in design maturity prior to implementation.
3) Critical Friend Assurance:
• Independent review of delivery strategies.
• Technical and programme challenge.
• Review of governance and assurance arrangements.
• Identification of emerging risks and opportunities.
• Benchmarking against industry good practice.
• Participation in workshops, assurance reviews and project boards.
• Independent assessment of key project decisions.
• Strategic technical advisory support.
The Critical Friend function shall provide objective and unbiased advice to support effective programme delivery.

title: Working Age Adults Care Home Services
description:
Carmarthenshire County Council, in collaboration with regional partners Pembrokeshire County Council and Ceredigion County Council, is developing a regional framework for Working Age Adult Care Home Services across the West Wales region. 
The proposed Framework will be structured into three service Lots, reflecting the primary client groups:
Lot 1: Learning Disabilities, including Autism
Lot 2: Mental Health
Lot 3: Physical Disabilities
Providers may apply for one or more Lots, depending on their area of expertise and service provision. The Lots are intended to support a more structured and consistent approach to commissioning across the region, ensuring that services can meet a range of needs for working age adults.
The proposed Framework will be open to:
- Providers with existing care home provision within the region; and/or
- Providers who intend to establish a care home service within the region within the next 12 months. 
(This means:
• Securing or being in the process of securing suitable premises.
• Obtaining planning permission (where required).
• Registering or preparing to register with Care Inspectorate Wales (CIW).
• Recruiting staff and developing operational arrangements.
• Having a clear business plan and timetable for opening.)
Providers joining the Framework will be required to demonstrate a commitment to supporting citizens from across the West Wales region and prioritising regional placements.
This procurement is being conducted as a Light Touch Contract under Section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023 (PA23). In accordance with Section 23(6), the Authority considers proximity between service users and providers to be important for the effective delivery of the services and therefore in order to be included on the Framework suppliers must have an existing care home provision within the region (Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion and/or Pembrokeshire); and/or intend to establish a care home service within the region within the next 12 months.
The Authority may, in accordance with the flexibility afforded under the Light Touch Regime (Section 9, PA23), undertake a refresh of this Framework at one or more intervals during the Framework Term. 
The Authority will publish a Tender Notice for each refresh event, clearly setting out the requirements, evaluation methodology and timeline. Suppliers admitted through the refresh shall be appointed on the same substantive terms as existing Framework Suppliers. The refresh may include, but shall not be limited to, varying the number, scope, extent and description of the Lots, Services and/or Pricing (as the case may be), together with the appointment of additional (new) Suppliers onto the Framework Agreement to maintain market access and continuity of service.
Business Wales Business Wales will deliver a live tender workshop to support providers interested in applying for the Working Age Adult Care Home Services Framework. The event will be held on 30/07/2026 and providers must register: https://wales.business-events.org.uk/en/events/working-age-adults-care-home-services/

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description:
Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities.
While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred.
This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources.
Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description:
This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners.  Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities.
These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families.

title: VRU - Expert Partner for Youth Digital Safety in London
description:
About the VRU
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence through prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London.
Working with partners across government, local authorities, education, health, policing and the voluntary and community sector, the VRU supports coordinated action at the key touchpoints that influence a young person’s journey: early years and families, education, positive opportunities, youth work, and communities and place. Central to the VRU’s approach is a commitment to embedding the voices of young people, practitioners and communities in policy, programme design and decision-making.
Programme Background
The VRU recognises that the rapid growth of digital platforms and technologies has created both new opportunities and new risks for children and young people. While online spaces can support connection, creativity, learning and participation, they can also expose young people to harmful content, exploitation, misogyny, harassment, coercion and technology-enabled abuse, and can contribute to the escalation of offline harm and violence.
As digital risks continue to evolve, there remains a significant gap between young people’s lived experiences of the online world and the systems, policies and services designed to support them. The VRU is therefore developing a wider digital safety programme to strengthen London’s response to online harms through a more coordinated, place-based and multi-agency approach. This programme is expected to include:
- Strengthening trusted adult capability through specialist training and practical support.
- Piloting innovative digital youth work approaches that engage young people safely in digital spaces.
- Supporting local authorities and borough partners to test and strengthen local responses to online harms through safeguarding and place-based practice.
- Building a stronger London-wide evidence base, strategic understanding and coordinated regional response. 
To support this ambition, the VRU is seeking to appoint an Expert Partner for Youth Digital Safety in London. The successful provider(s) will help the VRU keep pace with emerging trends in online harms, strengthen the evidence and practice base, embed youth-informed approaches, and support the development of a more coordinated public health response across London.
Description of the Service
The appointed provider(s) will act as an expert partner to the VRU, delivering specialist support across policy, research, evidence, programme development, learning and practice translation. The role will support the wider digital safety programme by strengthening connections between research, policy, safeguarding and frontline delivery, ensuring that insight and learning are translated into practical improvements for young people, practitioners and systems across London.
The commission is structured into two complementary lots:
Lot 1: Research, Policy and Evidence Partner
Lot 2: Programme Development and Learning Partner
Bidders may apply for one or both lots, and proposals may be led by a single organisation, partnership or consortium. The VRU particularly welcomes collaborative delivery models that bring together complementary expertise, capacity and reach.
Target Audience
The commission focuses on online harms affecting children and young people aged 11–25, with particular relevance to the VRU’s violence reduction, safeguarding and prevention agenda. Providers should demonstrate an understanding of how digital risks, behaviours and protective factors may vary across adolescence and young adulthood, and how they may be shaped by factors such as age, gender, race, sexuality, disability, neurodivergence, socio-economic disadvantage and wider vulnerability.
The work is expected to address a broad and evolving range of online harms, including peer conflict, harmful social media dynamics, exploitation, violence against women and girls (VAWG), misogyny, technology-enabled abuse and online harms that may contribute to or escalate offline violence. The scope is intentionally flexible and intended to support the VRU in identifying emerging risks and priority areas over time.
Intended Outcomes
The commission will contribute to:
- Stronger strategic understanding of digital safety and opportunity for children and young people.
- Stronger multi-agency safeguarding responses to digital risk.
- Youth-informed research, policy and delivery across the wider VRU digital safety programme.
- Stronger learning partner support and programme improvement across priority delivery strands.
- More practical and timely support across the wider VRU digital safety programme.
- A more coordinated public health response to online harms across London.
- Stronger external influence and strategic leadership on youth digital safety.
Timeframe and Budget
The intended contract period is 36 months, from October 2026, comprising an initial 24-month term with an option to extend for a further 12 months, subject to funding, performance and relevant approvals.
The budget breakdown is detailed below:
Lot 1 - Fixed Services: £110,600
Lot 2 - Fixed Services: £205,400
In addition, optional draw-down provision may be commissioned subject to programme need, funding availability and approvals:
Lot 1: up to £82,000
Lot 2: up to £152,000
The maximum potential contract value is therefore up to £550,000 excluding VAT, inclusive of core and optional provision. The VRU does not guarantee that any draw-down provision will be utilised.
Note: Market engagement was conducted on 29th June 2026, you can see the notice here https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/058240-2026

title: Co-Developing the 'Digestive Disease Centre' at University Hospital Southampton, Hybrid Procurement and Sponsorship Opportunity
description:
UHS is seeking to engage with interested parties to discuss and refine an opportunity to become a strategic endoscopy partner to the Trust. UHS provides a regional endoscopy service to a population of 3m+, offering a comprehensive range of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.
Following a fire earlier this year, UHS has reviewed its long-term endoscopy requirements and is considering a new purpose-built regional diagnostic endoscopy centre situated close to the main hospital. 
UHS has existing endoscopy equipment to the value of approximately £8-10m. This will need to be refreshed throughout this contract. UHS has an indicative budget of £20-25m for the design and construction of the new centre.
This will be designed to meet current and projected future endoscopy and motility needs, 'a one-stop-shop' and be an important centre to both trial new technology and techniques and provide training for the next generation of the endoscopy workforce.
This opportunity is to explore and discuss how a partnership approach may drive better outcomes for patients, for innovation, for UHS clinicians, and for the partner[S(1.1][L(1.2]. This opportunity may include, but not necessarily be limited to:
1: Provision of endoscopy equipment to a new offsite location, both for the use of clinicians undertaking NHS clinical activity, and for use as a test bed for innovation and new technique development, and for use within a training environment.
2: Regional Training Centre: The physical co-location of experienced UHS staff, clinicians, data, patients with an industry partner seeking to promote best practice and create future workforce.
3: Joint Innovation Deal & Test Bed: The provision of a live, data-rich NHS environment to validate new technology, and techniques, for example artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic tools and ergonomic designs and potentially the exploitation of emerging shared Intellectual Property. This would also include SME and VCSE participation for research and innovation. 
4: Commercial Sponsorship Opportunity with Associated Rights and Benefits: 
In addition to the core procurement opportunities above, there is potential to explore a complementary commercial sponsorship arrangement, which may include the provision of value-in-kind goods and/or services that support contract delivery.
This strategic partnership approach would identify and agree a range of associated rights and benefits for suppliers who also become sponsors. These may include appropriate sponsor recognition, opportunities for collaboration and innovation, shared learning, thought leadership engagement, and other mutually agreed activities that support the objectives of all parties.
UHS, with support from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), is trialling the integration of commercial sponsorship into this procurement opportunity to explore how strategic partnerships can deliver additional value while supporting the successful delivery of contract outcomes.
Whilst this notice is not intended to create a commitment to a contract, it is running alongside a live funded NHS capital project to develop designs and take forward the concept of a regional endoscopy centre. 
This hybrid procurement and sponsorship model is being piloted by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and UHS, offering potential suppliers a unique opportunity to play an active role in delivering a best-in-class new facility for patients: supporting improved care, championing innovation and delivering lasting benefits for all parties.
To ensure fair and open competition in any future procurement, the developing design and specification will remain supplier-neutral and will not be tailored to any specific manufacturer, supplier or solution.

title: Public Footpath Surface Works - Harris Park Extension
description:
1.1 The Authority
Cockermouth Town Council is inviting competitive tenders for minor civil works to improve a public footpath section. Engineering drawings and technical specifications were prepared on behalf of the Town Council by Cumberland Council.
1.2 Purpose of Work
The objective is to establish an accessible, surfaced route from Double Mills footbridge to the woodland section behind Dale View, Cockermouth. Currently, this missing link prevents access for pushchairs, wheelchairs, and less-mobile pedestrians.
1.3 Key Project Details
•	Design & Standards: Formulated via engineering drawings provided by Cumberland Council.
•	Target Start Date: February / March 2027 (Spring 2027) or before.
•	Contract Duration: Estimated 2 consecutive weeks.
2.1 Scope of Works
The contractor will provide all plant, labour, and materials to execute the following sequence:
1.	Site Establishment: Set up a secure temporary compound near the park entrance at Dale View.
2.	Safety Measures: Formally close Footpath No. 223015 to the public for the 2-week duration of works. (Cumberland Council has agreed to meet the costs of this)
3.	Excavation: Dig out a ground tray 50mm deep along the path alignment. Retain topsoil and arisings on-site for reuse.
4.	Membrane: Supply and lay a heavy-duty geotextile separation membrane along the length of construction.
5.	Sub-Base: Supply, lay, and compact a 150mm depth of Type 1 granular sub-base.
6.	Surface Course: Supply, lay, and compact a 40mm depth of 0-6mm crushed aggregate to form a smooth, accessible top finish.
7.	Alignment Note: The path alignment must run to the right-hand side of the park bench and to the left-hand side of the trees.
8.	Tie-ins: Saw cut the existing macadam path at chainage 0m near the Double Mills footbridge to ensure a flush finish. The end chainage must meet completely flush with the existing timber bridge deck.
9.	Landscaping: Smooth out and reinstate path edges using the saved arisings and topsoil, then seed with an 80/20 wildflower mix.
2.2 Critical Site Constraints
•	Narrow Access: Access to the park area is via a restrictive, narrow road at Dale View. Large commercial HGVs or oversized plant will not physically fit. Bidders must check this access profile prior to pricing.
•	Watercourse Proximity: The works run directly alongside the River Cocker.
•	Environmental Protection: All materials and plant machinery must remain at least 5 metres away from the watercourse channel on ground with no immediate flooding risk. Absolutely no refuelling, servicing, or greasing is allowed on site. Equipment must be checked for leaks before entering the site.
•	Flood Risk Management: Works must be carried out in generally dry conditions. The contractor is required to monitor local water levels and Environment Agency flood alerts prior to and during construction to reduce risk to the workforce.

title: DfT National Freight Model
description:
The Department for Transport (DfT) intends to procure a supplier to develop a new National Freight Model (NFM), an in-house, cross-modal freight modelling capability designed to support transport policy development, appraisal, forecasting and decision-making across the UK. The NFM will replace existing freight modelling approaches and provide a modern analytical framework capable of representing freight movements across road, rail and domestic maritime modes.
The contract will include the design, development, calibration, validation and implementation of a multimodal freight model capable of estimating current and future freight demand and flows by commodity, vehicle type and transport mode. The model must support the analysis of domestic freight movements and international freight movements to and from the United Kingdom, including maritime and rail freight services.
The NFM will be required to assess the impacts of changes to infrastructure, land use, economic conditions, logistics behaviours and government policy interventions. It will also enable the testing of alternative scenarios and sensitivities to support transport planning, network resilience analysis, decarbonisation initiatives, freight mode shift assessments and wider strategic policy development.
The successful supplier will be expected to develop and document the model, provide supporting methodologies, undertake any necessary data collection or acquisition activities, deliver stakeholder engagement and training, and ensure that the Department can operate, maintain and further develop the model independently following completion of the contract.
The procurement may include associated research, data acquisition, innovative analytical approaches and the development of new methodologies necessary to deliver the required modelling capabilities and outcomes.

title: Transport for Wales and Transport for Wales Rail – Public Transport Summit 2027
description:
Transport for Wales and Transport for Wales Rail is seeking expressions of interest from organisations wishing to participate in the Public Transport Summit 2027 at Swansea Arena on 16–17 June 2027. 
Opportunities include sponsorship, exhibition space, innovation participation and attendance. 
This is a market engagement exercise only and not a procurement or call for competition. 
1. Overview
Transport for Wales (TfW) is undertaking a market engagement exercise to invite expressions of interest from organisations wishing to participate in the TfW Public Transport Summit 2027
Taking place on: Date: 16–17 June 2027
Venue: Swansea Arena
This notice is issued to ensure an open, fair and transparent approach to engaging the transport market and wider stakeholders. This is not a procurement exercise and does not constitute a call for competition. It is a pre-market engagement activity only, intended to inform event planning and gauge interest in participation.
2. Background
Following the success of the inaugural Public Transport Summit held in Wrexham, Transport for Wales is pleased to confirm that the Summit will return in June 2027.
The Summit will bring together transport leaders, policymakers, industry experts, and stakeholders to engage in strategic discussions on the future of public transport across Wales and the Borders.
The event will focus on:
• Connecting ideas
• Moving people and communities
• Shaping the future of public transport
Transport for Wales is continuing to transform public transport services and infrastructure. The Summit provides a platform to build on this momentum and support future investment, integration and innovation across the network.
3. Purpose of the Summit
The Summit will provide an opportunity for the public, private and third sectors to:
• Collaborate on the future of transport in Wales and the Borders
• Share strategic visions and priorities
• Support integrated transport development
• Drive wider economic and social impact for communities
The event will include:
• Themed panel discussions
• Keynote speeches
• Workshops
• Exhibition and innovation space
• Networking opportunities
4. Summit Themes
The 2027 Summit will focus on the following key themes:
• Connectivity – Building economic and social impact through connectivity
• Integration – Bus franchising
• Future Investment
• Safety, accessibility and inclusion
• Sustainability and innovation. 
Opportunities for Participation
TfW is seeking expressions of interest across the following participation and sponsorship categories:
Sponsorship Categories

• Official Partners – 5 partners (~£20k–25k each), aligned to Summit themes

title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?
description:
Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe.
People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality.
When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions.
The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.
