title: Modular Lift, Design, Manufacture, Installation, Testing and Commissioning
description:
Description of the Requirement 
Network Rail Infrastructure Limited intends to enter into a contract with Explore 2050 (Trading as Vertiq) for the design, manufacture, installation, testing and commissioning of the Vertiq Modular Lift and associated services. The requirement comprises a fully integrated off-site manufactured modular lift solution including factory-based manufacture, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning and associated support services. 
Justification for Direct Award 
Network Rail intends to make a direct award under Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 relying upon Schedule 5 Paragraph 1 (absence of competition for technical reasons). 
Network Rail has undertaken a review of currently available market solutions and engaged with suppliers active within the lift and modular construction sectors to assess the availability of alternative solutions capable of meeting its requirements. 
Network Rail has determined that an off-site manufactured modular lift solution is necessary to minimise passenger and operational disruption, reduce on-site construction activities, reduce railway possession requirements, improve installation certainty and support the efficient delivery of accessibility and station enhancement programmes across its estate. 
Following market analysis, supplier engagement and technical assessment, Network Rail has concluded that it has not identified any reasonable alternative supplier capable of delivering a fully integrated off-site manufactured modular lift solution that satisfies its operational, safety, installation, programme delivery and standardisation requirements. Network Rail therefore considers that competition is absent for technical reasons and that a direct award is justified. 
The proposed contract term is limited to 18 months and includes a break clause exercisable by Network Rail after 12 months. The inclusion of the break clause reflects Network Rail's intention to undertake further market testing and assess whether effective competition has emerged for future requirements. 
Procurement Act 2023 Compliance Statement 
Network Rail Infrastructure Limited considers that the proposed direct award satisfies the conditions for direct award set out in Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 and relies upon the justification contained within Schedule 5 Paragraph 1 (absence of competition for technical reasons). 
This Transparency Notice is being published in accordance with Section 44 of the Procurement Act 2023 prior to the proposed award of the contract. 
Evidence supporting the direct award decision, including market analysis, supplier engagement records and technical assessments, is retained within the procurement file. 
Network Rail will continue to review market developments throughout the contract term and will utilise the contractual break clause and ongoing market testing to inform future procurement decisions. 
Break Clause 
Undertake further market analysis 
Assess emerging modular lift solutions and suppliers 
Review continued value for money 
Determine whether future requirements should be subject to a competitive procurement process 
Transparency Statement 
This notice is published pursuant to Section 44 of the Procurement Act 2023 and provides advance notification of Network Rail Infrastructure Limited's intention to award a contract to Explore 2050 (Trading as Vertiq) using a direct award ground permitted under the Procurement Act 2023. The publication of this notice is intended to provide transparency regarding the Authority's proposed procurement approach.

title: Invasive Vegetation Control (IVC) Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS)
description:
FLS has established a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the provision of Invasive Vegetation Control (IVC) services across Scotland’s national forests and land, which commenced 8th September 2026.
A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) is an electronic system established by a contracting authority to purchase commonly used goods, works or services in accordance with the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015. Admittance to a DPS gives participants the opportunity to subsequently bid for relevant future opportunities which are procured through the DPS.
The purpose of the DPS is to provide a compliant route to market for FLS to procure services which are unable to be provided through existing contracts or to replace contracts which have terminated or expired.
The scope of the DPS is primarily for establishment operations including but not limited to:
- Cutting – power or hand tools.
- Burning.
- Stump Treatment.
- Foliar application of pesticides.
- Stem injection of woody material with sprayed pesticides or eco plugs.
- Stem injection of herbaceous weeds.
- Hand pulling of seedlings.
- Steep ground/rope access work.
- Non-chemical and non-cutting treatments (manual removal).
- Chipping of cut material.
- Traffic Management.
- Manual Labour.
Parties who request to be admitted to the DPS will have their submissions evaluated by FLS within 10 working days of submission (this deadline could be extended to a maximum of 20 working days in individual cases), and if successful, will be admitted to the DPS thereafter.

title: Provision of Worldwide Conveyance Services of HM Forces Mail
description:
The Ministry of Defence, acting through the British Forces Post Office (BFPO), intends to procure a comprehensive global mail conveyance service to support the delivery and return of Forces mail and courier services worldwide.
BFPO's mission is to provide an efficient, effective and resilient postal and courier service in order to sustain the fighting power of UK Armed Forces worldwide. BFPO delivers postal services to Service Personnel, Defence Civil Servants and entitled family members located across the globe through a combination of military and commercial transportation networks.
The Authority is considering a requirement that may include some or all of the following service elements:
Scheduled Worldwide Mail Conveyance
International inbound and outbound mail conveyance services.
Freight forwarding through commercial air carriers and express courier networks.
Customs management and associated documentation.
Provision of tracking and tracing services.
Non-Scheduled (Ad Hoc) Worldwide Mail Conveyance
Urgent and operational mail movements.
Support to HM Ships and deployed military operations.
Flexible worldwide collection and delivery capability.
Airport Road Trunking
Routine movement of mail between BFPO Headquarters and designated airport cargo facilities.
Handling, storage and secure transportation of military mail consignments.
UK Road Trunking
Collection and delivery services between BFPO, Royal Mail facilities, RAF Brize Norton and other Defence locations.
Provision of suitable vehicles, drivers and associated operational support.
Witness Loading and Specialist Freight Forwarding Services
Support for secure international movement of designated consignments.
Airport handling and customs liaison activities.
Entry Summary Declaration (ENS) Filing Services
Submission and management of customs declarations and associated regulatory requirements.
Support for BFPO requirements relating to the movement of mail into EU territories.
Key Requirements
Potential suppliers should be capable of demonstrating:
Proven experience in international freight forwarding, mail conveyance or logistics services.
Access to worldwide transportation networks.
Appropriate aviation, freight forwarding and customs accreditations.
Robust track and trace capabilities.
Ability to operate within secure and sensitive government environments.
Compliance with all applicable UK transport, customs, security and health and safety legislation.
Business continuity and resilience arrangements capable of supporting operational military requirements.
Experience supporting public sector or defence customers is desirable.

title: DCWW2114 LPCB Certified Security Assets
description:
Loss Prevention Certification Board (LPCB) Certified Security Equipment are required to strengthen the physical security of DCWW’s critical clean water and wastewater infrastructure and to comply with statutory and industry security standards. These assets require enhanced physical security to prevent unauthorised access, vandalism, theft, sabotage, and contamination risks. 
The framework covers the supply, installation, and optional maintenance of LPCB certified security equipment including covers, doors, bar sets, cages, enclosures, and cylinder clamps across operational assets such as reservoirs, treatment works, pumping stations, and service reservoirs.
The scope also includes conducting site surveys and the creation of site plans to provide recommendations to DCWW to satisfy Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) standards. Suppliers are required to undertake site surveys and recommend the appropriate security measures needed for each asset to achieve the required LPCB security rating. 
Two Bidders will be awarded per Lot within the Framework Agreement on a primary/secondary basis. 
SCOPE OF GOODS AND SERVICES 
Goods 
The framework includes five product areas across: 
o Lot 1 Covers – the supply, installation and support of LPCB security-rated covers; 
o Lot 2 Double/single entry doors – certified security doors for operational assets; o Lot 3 Bar sets, cages and steel enclosures: – certified physical security products used to protect assets and equipment; 
o Lot 4 GRP enclosures – certified GRP kiosks or enclosures for relevant site requirements; and 
o Lot 5 Roller shutter doors – certified roller shutter doors where required across the estate. 
Services 
The scope of services includes: 
o conducting site surveys to verify requirements 
o creation of site plans to enable compliance to DWI standards 
Call-offs will be made by direct award to the Primary Supplier for the relevant Lot. The 
Primary Supplier will be expected to fulfil all requirements in accordance with the 
Framework Agreement terms, including the agreed service levels, delivery times and 
performance standards.

title: Design and Delivery of a Train-the-Trainer Service for the Diverse Angel Syndicates Programme
description:
Following on from 
Qualifying Planned Procurement Notice OCID: ocds-h6vhtk-0695d7  allowing BBB to reduce the timescales for this tender from 25 days to 21 days.
Pre Market Engagement Notice: OCID: ocds-h6vhtk-0695d6
The Diverse Angel Syndicate (DAS) Programme supports the development and sustainability of diversity-focused angel syndicates across the UK. The programme aims to broaden participation in angel investing, increase investment into diverse founders, and strengthen the capability of emerging angel syndicates across the UK nations and regions. DAS places a particular emphasis on engaging and supporting new and novice angels, with the aim of broadening access to angel investing as an asset class and improving confidence, capability and participation among underrepresented groups. The programme is expected to support approximately 10–15 syndicates, delivered through three cohorts of up to five syndicates each, in addition to the current cohort of five. 
Successful applicants will receive a package of financial and non-financial support, including funding for operational costs, training and capability-building, guidance on operational tooling and infrastructure, and access to peer learning and ecosystem connections through the programme. 
As part of the non-financial support offer, British Business Bank Plc (“British Business Bank” or “BBB” or “Buyer) is seeking to procure a training provider to design, deliver, and support a Train-the-Trainer education programme for angel syndicate leads across the United Kingdom. The aim of this programme is to upskill syndicate leads to deliver consistent, high-quality training to their own syndicate members.  
BBB anticipates that the contract will span a period of up to four years. During this time, supported syndicates are expected to continue recruiting new angel investors on a rolling basis. As such, the training requirement is expected to be front-loaded, with an initial focus on programme design, content development and early delivery, followed by a transition to a lighter-touch model in later years. This is likely to include ongoing support, updates to training materials, and periodic engagement to maintain quality and relevance. 
The training offer is expected to be modular in structure and designed to:  
support angel activation and portfolio understanding for new / novice angels  
enable syndicates to tailor delivery to their own membership base  
establish a minimum standard of training across supported syndicates  
ensure clarity of purpose and avoid duplication between syndicate development and angel education

title: Framework for Environmental & External Improvements
description:
The Council aims to invest in the external environment of its estates and to create safe, accessible and attractive environments for its tenants and residents.
The total estimated annual contract value is £1,590,000 (plus VAT), and the Council is seeking to appoint a single Contractor to this framework agreement. 
It should be noted that the estimated value is indicative only, and may change dependant on demand and budget.
The Contract period will be 2 years (starting 1st March 2027) with the option to extend for up to a further 2 years.
The works primarily involve: Courtyard Improvement Programmes, Boundary Improvements, Small Environmental Improvement Schemes, Fire Actions, Highways & Footway Improvements, Garage Site Improvements, Neighbourhood Regeneration Division Services (i.e., Alley Gating) and other related works / scheme
(including but not limited to; defensible space, unadopted highways, structural surveys & design and small to medium isolated schemes).
Some comprehensive estate regeneration schemes based on needs and priorities identified through consultation for individual areas. 
Schemes generally include improvements or renewal to parking provision, property curtilages, rear gullies and alley-ways, lighting, amenity areas footpaths carriageways and courtyards.
Smaller one-off improvements in response to specific issues, such as fire actions, gulley improvements, alley-gating, parking, courtyards or footways.
Alley Gating are ongoing 2-year programmes to investigate and secure rear lanes by the means of manually operated gates. 
Programmes are agreed every 2 years and include lanes identified as the highest priorities for the Council, in terms of the levels of anti-social behaviour, crime and environmental issues. 
All schemes are subject to support from the local community and consideration of any representations during the legal process. 
The programme aims to deliver approximately 11-12 gated schemes with approx. 22 gate set installations per year.
Fire actions are typically the relocation of an existing bin-store sited too close to the main building. Repositioned in a new location a set distance away to prevent fire spread to the main building. The works are usually a new brick built bin store, set on a concrete slab, steel railings and a secure steel lockable gate. Enabling works may also include, concrete paths, slabs, drainage etc.
A rolling programme of courtyard improvements has been developed specifically tackling issues around security, improved amenity space for tenants, improved bin storage, surfacing and access. The programme is based on prioritising the courtyards in worst condition first and it is anticipated undertaking around 7 courtyard improvements every year depending upon capacity.
Defensible space improvements to flats are also planned this will include Railings and gates, pathway renewal and where possible level access ramp to front communal door.

title: NHS Health Checks
description:
An NHS Health Check is a free health assessment offered to help prevent serious cardiovascular conditions by spotting risks early. For the purpose of this local service, those eligible are between 40 and 74 years old without already diagnosed long term cardiovascular health conditions, and either registered with a Somerset GP or living in Somerset. The service may be offered to staff or patients meeting this criterion.
The aim of this service is to reduce access barriers for those with severe mental illnesses by combining the NHS HC opportunity with other treatment access. This may be extended to other cohorts like those accessing bariatric services as the service develops.
The service will need to be run to the standard protocol for NHS Health Checks service including measurement of pulse rate, blood pressure and POCT blood cholesterol. It will enable detection of risk factors for hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol, kidney dysfunction, obesity and heart arrythmias which would be referred to the patient's GP to consider formal diagnosis. It will also include lifestyle support for alcohol use, smoking, healthy weight and physical exercise.

title: Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework
description:
This invitation to tender ('ITT') relates to Lake District National Park Authority's (the 'Authority') procurement for a Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework Agreement, for our Ranger Services Team and others.
Successful Tenderers will be appointed onto a multi-supplier Framework Agreement divided into Lots. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Authority and by other bodies in the Authority's network by prior agreement. The Authority is seeking a mix of contractors to bid for a place on the Framework Agreement, including companies, consultants, sole traders, and Small and Medium Sized Enterprises.
This procurement is divided into Lots (and sub-lots in the case of Lot 4). Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots/sub-lots provided that you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in the Lot Specification at Table A.
Please note that you do not need to be able to provide all of the services listed in the Lot specification, provided you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in that Lot you may submit a tender.
All Prices should be submitted as a maximum for provision of your goods/services and will be a commitment for the duration of the Framework Agreement, subject to the allowed increase in price annually.
This Framework Agreement will allow for Direct Award and Further Competition of Call-off Contracts.
Tenderers should read the instructions contained in this ITT carefully before submitting a response. Failure to comply with the requirements set out in this ITT may result in the rejection of the Tender.
Tenderers are advised to acquaint themselves fully with the extent and nature of the goods and/or services in the Statement of Requirement and with the Terms and Conditions. Participation in this procurement automatically signals that the Tenderer accepts the Terms and Conditions contained in this ITT.
If a Tenderer is awarded a place on any Lot of the Framework, a draft Framework Agreement will be provided after all awards have taken place (est. February - March 2027). Any award is not legally binding and subject-to-contract until the final Framework Agreement between the Authority and the Tenderer is signed.
The Lake District National Park Authority looks after the Lake District National Park, encouraging people to enjoy and understand its beauty and supporting those who live and work here. Further information about the LDNPA, including our statutory functions, is available on our website.
We are working towards making the Lake District an inspirational example of sustainable development in action. We want its prosperous economy, world class visitor experiences and vibrant communities to come together in sustaining the spectacular landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage here. Details of how we are doing this are outlined in our Vision: Our purpose and vision - Lake District National Park
Our Ranger Services Team at LDNPA has a focus on maintaining and improving the Rights of Way and other access in the Lake District National Park, while encouraging and educating users in responsible outdoor recreation on accessible land and navigable lakes. They support visitor management and nature recovery initiatives, and the enhancement and maintenance of our rural properties, in line with our strategic priorities. They work closely with communities to help them meet their needs in ways that contribute to our Vision. The Ranger Team's workload includes project work, such as the Coast-to-Coast and Fix the Fells.
The Historic Environment Team commissions specialist consultancy support to inform the conservation, management and enhancement of the National Park's historic environment. This may include heritage impact assessments, conservation area appraisals, historic building recording, conditions surveys, archaeological investigations, landscape and townscape character assessments, design advice, and other specialist heritage and built environment studies to support planning, conservation and place-shaping objectives.
Our needs are specific and will vary.  We are looking for Suppliers who understand the work we do and not only can provide exceptional services, but who can contribute to our wider Vision for the Lake District. Please note that the Lot Descriptions in section 2 are included to provide some background information on the work of the Authority. The following are examples of types of services which may be required by our Ranger Service. This is not exhaustive but is intended to demonstrate the breadth of the services which will be required:
Providing services on a recurring and annual basis, such as our bridge maintenance responsibilities and sourcing of materials for daily use;
Providing advice and practical work on specific public sector funded projects, such as the Coast-to-Coast project.
Providing specific advice to our internal team of individuals and organisations with whom we operate, for internal projects involving our own land and property, and also to our partner organisations such as Fix the Fells.

title: Data of Last Resort Data Collection
description:
This Market Engagement seeks to identify options to enable procurement of a dedicated backup collection tool for Operational Technology (OT) environments. The solution will ensure that the complete data state of critical OT assets is consistently captured and securely stored across multiple sites, serving as the organisation's data of last resort.
The tool must collect the full backup state of OT assets including configurations, control logic, firmware, hardware metadata, and associated files. It must support both automated, policy-driven backup collection and authorised manual backup initiation, operating through secure and non-intrusive protocols that do not interact with OT control or programming interfaces and have no impact on live operations or safety-critical systems.
The solution must be vendor-agnostic, deployable fully on-premise or within a private cloud, and capable of operating in air-gapped environments, with full audit trails and compliance reporting.

title: Equipment - The Paddocks
description:
This capital procurement project represents a strategic investment in the health, fitness, and modern infrastructure of the council's leisure portfolio. It focuses specifically on the targeted acquisition of equipment assets across two distinct work streams
1. The Paddocks (Lot 1): A completely new fitness installation requiring standard premium cardio and fixed resistance equipment (Lot 1) 
2. The Paddocks (Lot 2): Deployment of fully automated, advanced digital strength and diagnostic equipment featuring real-time data streaming and NHS reporting integration. The infrastructure demands high-durability hardware capable of supporting automated user tracking, data-driven facility management, and direct synchronisation with exercise referral clinical metrics. (Lot 2) 
3. Runnymede Leisure Centre (Lot 1): Cardiovascular replacement consisting strictly of premium cardiovascular equipment upgrades. (Lot 1) 
4. The Paddocks (Lot 3): A dedicated suite of power-assisted, continuous motion exercise machines equipped with digital cloud connectivity software. This equipment is specifically engineered for inclusive rehabilitation, active aging, community health referral pathways, and users with limited mobility or long-term health conditions. (Lot 3)
The existing assets at Runnymede Leisure Centre have reached the end of their operational lifespan, resulting in increased maintenance overheads and a decline in user experience. Simultaneously, the development at The Paddocks requires a highly sophisticated setup to attract and retain members while supporting targeted health and physical progression initiatives.
Rather than relying on legacy hardware configurations or static, unmonitored equipment, the Authority is prioritising a forward-thinking, data-driven approach to gym management. By introducing automated biometric tracking and high-precision physical diagnostics alongside premium traditional fitness lines, the council aims to drive member engagement, reduce member attrition, and optimise overall facility performance.
Options Appraisal
1. Continued Maintenance of Legacy Hardware: Rejected. Continuing to repair out-of-warranty machinery or relocating aging equipment to new sites is financially non-viable. It fails to meet modern public expectations, incurs high ad-hoc maintenance costs, and does not provide the tracking capabilities required for contemporary data-driven health strategies.
2. Unified Multi-Vendor Bulk Purchase: Rejected. Attempting to bundle specialised digital diagnostic ecosystems and standard mechanical gym equipment into a single, generic lot restricts competitive bidding. It prevents the Authority from strictly specifying the unique software integrations required for real-time strength progression tracking and cloud-based user diagnostics.
3. Split-Lot Framework Procurement (Preferred Framework): The procurement is divided into three distinct, specialised Lots. This strategy allows the Authority to independently evaluate best-in-class manufacturers for traditional cardiovascular and mechanical resistance machinery (Lot 1) while establishing exact technical criteria to secure a highly specialised, closed-loop digital strength circuit and automated onboarding ecosystem that links in with NHS (Lot 2).
4.  Acquire a state-of-the-art power-assisted, digitally connected physical therapy and active health circuit designed for inclusive access, rehabilitation, and active aging (Lot 3)

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – FE 03.0615/2021/IRB - „Untersuchungen der Wirkungen von VBA mit reduziertem Anlagenumfang und Entwicklung eines darauf aufbauenden Anwendungskriterienkatalogs“
description: Die Bewältigung steigender Verkehrsnachfrage erfordert verstärkt den strategischen Einsatz intelligenter Telematiklösungen. Während Verkehrsbeeinflussungsanlagen (VBA) bisher vorrangig auf Strecken mit besonderen Rahmenbedingungen (z. B. Verkehrsspitzen, Unfallhäufungspunkte, spezielle Wetterbedingungen) zum Einsatz kommen, besteht zunehmend die Notwendigkeit, auch Autobahnabschnitte mit hohem Standard durch fokussierte Optimierung ausgewählter Verkehrsparameter zu betrachten. Das Forschungsvorhaben untersucht wie VBA mit reduziertem technischen Aufwand wirksam eingesetzt werden können. Im Projektschwerpunkt wird die aktuell laufende Erprobung einer reduzierten Streckenbeeinflussungsanlage (SBA) auf der Bundesautobahn (BAB) A8 empirisch ausgewertet. Hierbei werden Effekte auf Verkehrssicherheit und Verkehrsablauf einer zeitgesteuerten sowie einer zu erarbeitenden verkehrsabhängigen Steuerung gegenübergestellt. Basierend auf der Bewertung von technischer Funktionalität, Wirkung und Wirtschaftlichkeit der Pilotanlage erfolgt eine Abschätzung der Übertragbarkeit auf weitere BAB-Abschnitte und Bundesstraßen. Die Ergebnisse ermöglichen die Ableitung von Kriterien und Einsatzfeldern für VBA mit reduziertem Funktionsumfang, insbesondere ob diese eine sinnvolle Ergänzung für Strecken mit bisher unwirtschaftlichem Nutzen-Kosten-Verhältnis sein kann.

title: Germany – Electrical services – Erstverkabelung des neuen RZ Nürnberg
description: Gegenstand der Vergabe ist der Abschluss eines EVB-IT Systemlieferungsvertrag für die vollständige Lieferung, Montage, Beschriftung, Abnahmeunterstützung und Dokumentation einer passiven Verkabelungsinfrastruktur im Rechenzentrum, sowie erweiterte Planung und Messung nach bestehenden Verkabelungs- und Besiedelungsplänen. Projektierung und technische Detailplanung der passiven Verkabelung. Fristgerechte Lieferung von LWL und Twisted Pair-Patchkabeln lt. Mengengerüst inkl. Belabung nach Vorgabe des AG. Durchführung von Messungen, Prüfungen und Zertifizierungsmessungen gemäß vereinbarter Prüfkriterien. Erstellung vollständiger, elektronisch weiter verarbeitbarer Dokumentation einschließlich Port-, Faser-, Kabellisten nach Vorgabe des AG. Online abrufbare Bereitstellung von Messprotokollen einzubauender LWL-Verkabelung Unterstützung der Abnahme und Mängelbeseitigung bis zur betriebsbereiten Übergabe. Sicherstellung redundanter A-/B-Verbindungswege zur Unterstützung hochverfügbarer Betriebsmodelle. Minimierung betrieblicher Risiken durch standardisierte Komponenten, Qualitätssicherung und nachvollziehbare Abnahmeprozesse. Schaffung von Reservekapazitäten für Wachstum, Technologiezyklen und spätere Erweiterungen im laufenden Betrieb. Der AN hat sicherzustellen, dass die angebotenen und verbauten Komponenten der passiven Verkabelungsinfrastruktur für einen Zeitraum von mindestens fünf Jahren ab Abnahme der Leistung verfügbar bleiben. Dies umfasst insbesondere ODF-Systeme, Patchfelder, Chassis, Kassetten, Module, Trunkkabel, Patchkabel, Keystone-Module, Kabelmanagementkomponenten, Befestigungsmaterialien sowie sonstiges systemrelevantes Zubehör. Innerhalb dieses Zeitraums müssen Erweiterungen, Nachbestellungen, Ersatzbeschaffungen und Austauschmaßnahmen mit identischen oder vollständig kompatiblen Komponenten möglich sein. Sofern einzelne Komponenten innerhalb des genannten Zeitraums durch den Hersteller abgekündigt, ersetzt oder technisch weiterentwickelt werden, hat der AN rechtzeitig gleichwertige und vollständig kompatible Nachfolgekomponenten anzubieten und deren Kompatibilität zum bestehenden Gesamtsystem nachzuweisen. Änderungen dürfen die bestehende Systemgarantie, Dokumentationslogik, Beschriftungssystematik, Port- und Kassettenzuordnung sowie die Betriebs- und Wartungsfähigkeit der installierten Infrastruktur nicht beeinträchtigen. Der AN hat mit Angebotsabgabe eine entsprechende Hersteller- oder Lieferantenerklärung vorzulegen, aus der die Verfügbarkeit, Nachlieferbarkeit oder Kompatibilität der angebotenen Systemkomponenten für mindestens fünf Jahre hervorgeht.

title: Norway – Substation construction work – Prior information notice - Market dialogue building and ground contract for the new Tjøtta transformer station.
description: Invitation to Market Dialogue Civil Works and Building Contract for the New Tjøtta Substation Project KE Nett is the contracting entity for this procurement. KE Nett AS is the electricity distribution system operator in the Municipality of Klepp on the Jæren region in Rogaland County, Norway. The company builds, operates and maintains the electricity distribution network and ensures a safe and reliable power supply for households, businesses, agriculture and public institutions. KE Nett is headquartered in Kleppe and is part of Klepp Energi Holding. KE Nett AS is planning to establish a new substation at Tjøtta in the Municipality of Klepp. The purpose of this prior information notice is to obtain input from the market regarding the optimal procurement strategy for the new substation project, including the civil works and building contract. In particular, KE Nett seeks the market's views on the most appropriate contract model, level of design maturity, allocation of detailed design responsibilities, interfaces with the electromechanical deliveries, and how project schedule risks and ground condition risks should be allocated. A new substation will be established at Tjøtta in the Municipality of Klepp as part of the upgrade of the Jæren regional grid to 132 kV. The new Tjøtta Substation will replace the existing Tu Substation, primarily due to the age of the existing facilities. The station will be constructed as a Class 2 substation and will primarily consist of the following components: Substation building with two transformer bays and provision for a future third bay. A construction licence has been granted, and the current plan is for the substation to be completed during 2030. Electromechanical Installations Two (2) 50 MVA transformers, 132/22-15 kV 132 kV GIS switchgear 22 (15) kV GIS switchgear, up to 26 bays Two (2) 22 (15) kV capacitor banks Two (2) neutral grounding reactors Connection of the transformer neutral point on the 132 kV side to reduce earth fault currents in the 132 kV network Civil Works and Building Contract The civil works and building contract is expected to include the establishment of a complete substation site, including permanent access roads, site preparation, earthworks, excavation and material handling, foundations, and construction of a substation building with two transformer cells and provisions for a potential third cell. The contract may also include: Foundations and structures for technical installations Cable basement and cable ducts Trenches and cable routes Drainage and stormwater management systems Water and wastewater infrastructure Outdoor grounding systems HVAC installations Building-related technical installations Fencing and site security measures Landscaping and external works Site reinstatement works Extensive coordination and interface management with separate transformer and electromechanical equipment contracts should be anticipated. The final scope of work, contract model, design responsibilities and interface arrangements have not yet been determined and will be further developed based, among other things, on the outcome of this market dialogue. Further information regarding the anticipated scope of the contract, as well as the questions for the market dialogue, is provided in Appendix 1 – Prior Information Notice – Civil Works and Building Contract. Market Dialogue Meeting The market dialogue will be conducted on 17 September 2026. Available time slots are: 08:30 – 09:15 09:30 – 10:15 10:30 – 11:15 12:00 – 12:45 13:00 – 13:45 14:00 – 14:45 To register, please send an email to anders.rostbakken@inventura.no indicating: Preferred time slot Number of participants Email addresses of all participants This information is required in order to invite all participants to the Microsoft Teams meeting. Registrations will be handled on a first-come, first-served basis. Market dialogue meetings will be held with a suitable number of suppliers based on the contracting entity's needs and capacity.

title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – Dynamisches Beschaffungssystem_BNB- und Nachhaltigkeitskoordination
description: Als öffentlicher Auftraggeber verwaltet die Berliner Immobilienmanagement GmbH über 5.000 Liegenschaften des Landes Berlin. Hierzu zählen Liegenschaften zugehörig u.a. zum Allgemeinen Bestand (z.B. Verwaltungsbauten), zu Flüchtlingsunterbringungen, Kulturgebäuden, Polizei und Feuerwehreinrichtungen sowie Schulen und Justizgebäuden. Im Zuge dieser Verwaltungseigenschaft besteht regelmäßig der Beschaffungsbedarf hinsichtlich vielfältiger Leistungen aus dem Bereich der BNB- und / oder Nachhaltigkeitskoordination. Im Rahmen des dynamischen Beschaffungssystems sollen regelmäßig Ausschreibungen für BNB- und / oder Nachhaltigkeitskoordination durchführt werden. Ziel ist es über einen Teilnahmewettbewerb einen Bieterpool aufzubauen, der für zukünftige Ausschreibungen zur Verfügung steht. Die Aufnahme in den Bieterpool ermöglicht die Teilnahme an zukünftigen Ausschreibungen für BNB- und / oder Nachhaltigkeitskoordination. Unter anderem sollen Leistungen über die dynamische Beschaffung bzgl. folgender Bereiche abgedeckt werden: Zu Kategorie I: BNB-Koordination - Leistungsbild: Der Auftragnehmer übernimmt die Koordination und fachliche Begleitung der angestrebten BNB-Zertifizierung über alle Projektphasen hinweg. Ziel ist die Sicherstellung der Einhaltung der Anforderungen des Bewertungssystems Nachhaltiges Bauen (BNB) sowie die erfolgreiche Durchführung der Konformitätsprüfung bis zur Zertifikatserlangung. Hierzu gehören die Definition und Abstimmung der Nachhaltigkeitsziele, die Steuerung der Nachweisführung, die Durchführung der BNB-Bewertung sowie die fachliche Begleitung von Planung, Ausschreibung und Bauausführung. Zu Kategorie II: Nachhaltigkeitskoordination - Leistungsbild: • Nachhaltige Projektbegleitung – Fachliche Steuerung von Bau und Sanierungsprojekten unter Berücksichtigung von Kreislaufwirtschaft, Ressourcenschonung und ökologischer Optimierung über den gesamten Lebenszyklus. • Re Use und Materialstrategien – Analyse des Bestands, Bewertung von Wiederverwendungspotenzialen, Entwicklung zirkulärer Bauweisen, Erstellung von Materialkatalogen und Gebäuderessourcenpässen. • Ökobilanzierung und Lebenszyklusbewertung – Vergleich von Varianten, Berechnung von CO2- Einsparungen, Lebenszykluskosten und Umweltwirkungen sowie Dokumentation für nachhaltige Entscheidungsgrundlagen. Zu Kategorie III: BNB-Koordination und Nachhaltigkeitskoordination - Leistungsbild: Die Kategorie III bildet ein kombiniertes Leistungsbild der Kategorien I bis II ab. Bei bestimmten Aufträgen (insbesondere bzgl. Portfolio Polizei oder Justizgebäuden) kann eine Sicherheits- und /oder Zuverlässigkeitsüberprüfung des eingesetzten Personals erforderlich sein. Weitere Einzelheiten siehe Vergabeunterlagen (insbesondere Verfahrensbrief und Kurzerläuterung).

title: SIA 968 - Lone Worker Application for Mobile Devices - 2026
description:
The SIA are seeking providers of Lone Worker Applications for mobile devices to support the health, safety and wellbeing of staff who may be required to work alone, and in potentially vulnerable situations, as part of their job. This requirement is for an SIA user community of initially 150 colleagues, anticipated to increase to 200 over the course of the contract
- The Mobile Device Application must;
• Be available on iOS, Android or Windows,
• Have an alert function which notifies users emergency contacts and 24/7 monitoring company once triggered,
• Have a journey and meeting planner, which allows users to register journeys, pre-planned meetings/events and their estimated timings,
• Have a welfare / check in feature prompting users to confirm safety at the conclusion of registered journeys, scheduled meetings, etc,
• Have a live / real time GPS tracking facility to confirm user location to monitoring company if alert triggered
• If an alert is activated the user's phone will live stream audio and video from the mobile device's microphone and camera to the monitoring company to enable staff to ascertain the user's situation and the appropriate support required.
• The app should have a panic button feature, whether this be a button, or 'shake' for duress alarm activation
• The system should be compatible with Bluetooth Smart buttons (including V.ALRT) - this can be used for raising an alarm and updating the handset's current location.
• The application should have a solution for use on low data modes, or compatible for use in on GPRS or areas which don't have 3G/4G/5G signal.
• Low battery life warnings
- The Monitoring Solution must;
• Be manned monitoring and response centre operating 24/7,
• The 24/7 monitoring company will attempt to call user upon activation of an alert.
• The 24/7 monitoring company will call Emergency services if required.
• Individuals working at the monitoring centre must be vetted to a minimum standard of BPSS
• An immediate emergency response solution should be offered upon, which must offer complete coverage of the UK
- Service Desk
The service desk acts as the primary user interface between the Buyer's IT users and the information system support function. The role of the service desk is to:
• Take ownership of all calls made to it;
• Ensure that the Buyers are provided with incident resolutions.
The service desk may include, but will not be limited to, the provision of the following services:
• A logical 'single point of contact' for all user issues
• Telephone and email support
• Accurate recording of all issues
• Categorisation including issue type and severity levels
• Issue prioritisation
• Instigation of escalation procedures as appropriate
• Direct and prompt resolution of issues
• Providing timely and accurate information to users
• Active ownership, tracking and management of all issues within scope - to ensure issues are resolved
• To keep the caller updated of the status of any issue where they are unlikely to be resolved or completed within the agreed time
• To update appropriate IT and user management of the status of all high priority and service affecting issues

title: Turbine Hall Fire Detection and Suppression System
description:
The contractor shall provide a complete engineered fire detection and suppression system, including all labour, materials, plant, access equipment, design services, testing equipment, certification and documentation necessary to deliver a fully operational system.
The protected scope comprises four individual turbine areas within the Turbine Hall. For tendering purposes, each turbine shall be assumed to have an approximate protected area of 15 m², giving an indicative total protected turbine area of approximately 60 m². Tenderers shall verify all dimensions, access constraints, hazard locations and coverage requirements during the site survey and shall base the final design on confirmed site measurements and risk assessment.
• Site surveys and risk assessment of the Turbine Hall and protected turbine assets.
• Design of the fire detection, alarm interface and suppression system.
• Selection and supply of detectors, control panels, suppression equipment, pipework, nozzles, cylinders, pumps, valves, cabling, containment, signage and ancillary equipment.
• Installation of all system components, including interfaces with existing fire alarm, plant control, shutdown, ventilation or building management systems where required.
• Factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning and functional performance testing.
• Provision of certification, operation and maintenance manuals, as-built drawings, cause-and-effect documentation and training.
• Provision of warranty, defects support and proposals for ongoing inspection, testing and maintenance.
4. Regulatory and Standards Compliance
The system and all works shall comply with all applicable UK legislation, regulations, approved guidance and recognised standards current at the date of tender and installation. The contractor shall identify and declare all applicable standards within their tender submission and shall state any proposed deviations.
• Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 and the duties of the Responsible Person.
• BS 5839-1 for fire detection and fire alarm systems in non-domestic premises, including design, installation, commissioning and maintenance requirements.
• Applicable BS EN 54 standards for fire detection and alarm components.
• Applicable standards for the selected suppression technology, which may include BS EN 15004 for gaseous extinguishing systems, BS 8489 for industrial and commercial watermist systems, BS EN 12845 for sprinkler systems, or other relevant recognised standards appropriate to the proposed solution.
• Where water mist is proposed, the system shall comply with BS 8489 or another applicable recognised standard for industrial and commercial water mist systems, together with manufacturer approvals, fire test evidence and any insurer requirements relevant to turbine or machinery-space oil-fire protection.
• BS 7273 requirements for interfaces between fire detection systems and ancillary fire protection measures, where applicable.
• Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, CDM Regulations 2015, Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and all applicable site safety requirements.
• Manufacturer installation instructions, insurer requirements and industry best practice.
5. Technical Requirements
5.1 Fire Risk Basis
The principal fire risk within the protected turbine areas arises from steam pipework operating at conditions and temperatures above the flash point of the oil used within the turbine systems. Oil pipework and steam pipework run adjacent to one another, increasing the likelihood that an oil leak, spray, mist or release could come into contact with hot steam pipework or other high-temperature surfaces and ignite.
The fire detection and suppression design shall therefore be based on credible oil-release scenarios, including pressurised leakage, dripping, pooling, spray impingement, atomised mist and contact with hot pipework or adjacent hot surfaces. Tenderers shall explain how their proposed solution detects and suppresses fires originating from these scenarios at an early stage and how the design reduces the risk of fire escalation to adjacent turbine equipment, cable routes, insulation, lagging and structural elements.
5.2 Fire Detection
• The detection system shall provide reliable early warning appropriate to the turbine risk profile and environmental conditions within the Turbine Hall, with particular consideration of oil leakage onto high-temperature steam pipework and associated hot-surface ignition scenarios.
• The preferred detection technology is infrared flame detection. Tenderers shall propose IR flame detectors, or an equivalent or superior flame detection solution, and shall justify the suitability of the proposed technology for the turbine environment.
• The detection system shall be capable of reliable operation in dark conditions and in areas containing numerous hot surfaces, including turbine casings, pipework, lagging, exhaust surfaces and other high-temperature equipment.
• The system shall be capable of detecting fires fuelled by different substances and materials reasonably foreseeable within the Turbine Hall environment, including but not limited to hydrocarbon fuels, lubricating oils, electrical equipment, insulation materials, plastics, cable materials and other combustible or flammable materials associated with turbine operation and maintenance.
• The design shall address potential false alarm sources, including hot surfaces, reflected radiation, welding or maintenance activities, sunlight or artificial light, airflow, temperature variation, dust, vibration, access constraints and maintenance requirements.
• The system shall include appropriate zoning, device identification, alarm indication and integration with the existing fire alarm infrastructure.
• The tenderer shall provide a proposed cause-and-effect matrix showing alarms, alerts, shutdowns, suppression release logic, delays, interlocks, manual release and abort functions where applicable.
5.3 Fire Suppression
The suppression design shall provide suitable protection for all four turbine areas. Tenderers shall state whether their proposed suppression approach is based on individual turbine local application, grouped zone protection, total flooding or another engineered arrangement, and shall justify how the design achieves effective coverage for each approximate 15 m² turbine area.
• The suppression system shall be suitable for the turbine fire risks, including oil leakage or spray onto steam pipework operating above the oil flash point, electrical, mechanical and hot-surface ignition scenarios where relevant.
• Any water mist design shall be suitable for oil leakage, spray or pool-fire scenarios involving ignition on or near high-temperature steam pipework and other hot surfaces, and shall demonstrate effective suppression or control without relying on excessive water application.
• The preferred suppression technology is a water mist system, selected to minimise water usage, reduce collateral damage and improve suppression effectiveness for credible oil-fire scenarios within the turbine areas. Tenderers shall propose a water mist solution, or an equivalent or superior suppression technology, and shall justify the selected suppression medium and method, including design basis, discharge performance, droplet characteristics, protected volume or local application approach, compatibility with turbine equipment and impact on personnel safety.
• The solution shall minimise collateral damage, avoid unacceptable operational impact and be suitable for the environmental conditions of the Turbine Hall.
• The system shall include all required detection-release controls, manual release points, lock-off or isolation arrangements, warning devices, signage, monitoring, status indication and fault reporting.
• The contractor shall identify any requirements for ventilation shutdown, plant trip, fuel or oil isolation, electrical isolation, dampers, access control, evacuation warnings or post-discharge recovery.
5.4 Integration and Interfaces
The contractor shall identify all required interfaces with existing site systems and shall include the design, testing and commissioning of those interfaces within their tender price unless explicitly excluded. Interfaces may include the existing fire alarm system, turbine controls, emergency shutdown systems, ventilation controls, building management systems, security systems, local alarms and remote monitoring arrangements.
6. Contractor Competence and Quality Requirements
• Tenderers shall demonstrate proven experience in designing and installing fire detection and suppression systems in industrial, power generation, energy-from-waste, turbine, machinery space or comparable high-value asset environments.
• Tenderers shall provide evidence of relevant third-party certification, competent-person arrangements, manufacturer accreditation and quality management systems.
• All works shall be undertaken by trained and competent personnel using approved materials and methods.
• The contractor shall provide project-specific risk assessments, method statements, lifting plans, access plans, isolation requirements and commissioning procedures before commencing work.

title: Living Well and Early Help Service for Adults on the Isle of Wight
Ground Lease in respect of land at Royal Bolton Hospital
description:
On 7th August 2026, Bolton NHS Foundation Trust ("BFT") entered into an Option Agreement with Noviniti Dev Co 14 Ltd ("Noviniti") giving Noviniti the right to call for a Ground Lease in respect of land at Royal Bolton Hospital ("the Hospital") being the site of a proposed new building/extension of the Hospital entrance incorporating improved and extended retail space with the provision of three retail units plus circulation space within the extended building plus additional retail space and internal refurbishment works within the existing Hospital building ("the Potential Development"). 
The Option Agreement is for an initial period of 39 weeks (subject to extension).  HFT has had valuation advice and will grant the Ground Lease (which will be for a term of 40 years subject to earlier break rights) ("the Ground Lease") at a premium which reflects market value as advised by independent valuation advice. IFM (the Trust's wholly owned subsidiary company) is a party to the Option Agreement and will grant rights to Noviniti in the Ground Lease.
The Ground Lease does not contain any development obligations upon Noviniti and does not in itself permit Noviniti to undertake the Potential Development unless BFT elects to grant a Licence for Alterations to Noviniti authorising it to undertake the Potential Development.
The contractual arrangements are structured as a land contract within Schedule 2 paragraph 8 of the Procurement Act 2023 ("the Act") and underlying case law, and as such an "exempted contract" for the purposes of the Act and the Procurement Regulations 2024.
Whilst the Option Agreement and Ground Lease contain no provisions authorising the Potential Development, BFT contemplates the possibility that it may choose to enter into further contractual arrangements with Noviniti at a point in the future (subject to separate BFT authorisations) subject to terms being agreed between Noviniti and BFT. If terms are agreed, then BFT and IFM may authorise Noviniti to undertake the Potential Development via a Licence for Alterations.  At that stage, Noviniti and BFT and IFM (together with other relevant third parties) would enter into an Agreement for Underleases leading to (inter alia) the construction of the Potential Development and the grant of underleases to relevant third parties and BFT of parts of the completed Potential Development.
In the event that BFT chooses not to enter into further documentation with Noviniti, then BFT will have a right to terminate the Ground Lease on the second anniversary of the date of the grant of the Ground Lease, provided that works to construct the Potential Development have not commenced. The Ground Lease is subject to a further break clause in favour of BFT on the 35th anniversary of the date of completion by Noviniti of the construction works constituting the Potential Development.  Noviniti will also have the right to break the Ground Lease at the expiry of the first anniversary of the Ground Lease.  
The arrangements between Noviniti and BFT include a cost underwrite by BFT of Noviniti's costs incurred in pursuing consents and design development capped in accordance with an agreed schedule.  Those costs are not payable in circumstances where Noviniti and BFT enter into further documentation and Noviniti undertakes the Potential Development.  In circumstances where Noviniti does not undertake the Potential Development, then the costs become payable by BFT and in return Noviniti is obliged to assign the benefit of all reports and surveys undertaken and reliance rights from the professionals engaged by Noviniti. 
The contractual arrangements referenced in this Notice were previously the subject of a Contract Award Notice dated 26th June 2026 and prior to that the subject of a Transparency Notice dated 16th June 2026.

description:
Currently, the contractor is tasked to visit any of the locations listed below, as directed by the Defence Recycling & Disposals Team (DRDT). From there, equipment is evaluated and sold by the contractor, usually from site using the most cost-effective method. Under current arrangements, equipment is sold through this contract, and proceeds are split between the contractor and the MOD on a gainshare basis. The division of proceeds from the sale is decided at the outset and forms part of the tender evaluation process.
All taskings are made through DRDT’s Disposition Management System for which all contractors receive training in its use.
Characteristics of Demand
There is also a significant amount of waste to be removed and disposed of in an environmentally friendly manner, and it must be in accordance with local environmental regulations. The disposal of waste from the Falkland Islands also makes up a large portion of this contract with all waste matter having to be removed from the islands.
Where equipment or waste products are disposed of, an estimate of cost is presented by the contractor and on completion an invoice is placed through and paid by the MOD using the Contract Procurement & Finance (CP&F) system. Contractors are registered through Exostar to enable usage of CP&F.     
There is a requirement for the occasional, disposal of waste oil under this contract from various overseas locations. Such disposal requirements can be at short notice due to the unpredictable nature of overseas operations.  
Preferred Future Approach
The above describes the current operating arrangement and should not be interpreted as the Authority’s preferred future solution. Respondents are encouraged to identify alternative approaches where these could improve competition, compliance, resilience, commercial performance or value for money.
Scope
Equipment Included 
•	Accommodation Stores 
•	Portable Infrastructure 
•	Vehicles & Vehicle Spares 
•	Tooling 
•	Communications Equipment 
•	Gifts & Memorabilia 
•	Hazardous Waste 
•	Waste Fuel 
Excluded Categories 
•	Real Estate 
•	Explosives

Global Operating Environment
Activity arises across a mixture of established overseas locations, remote islands, temporary deployments and potentially fragile or operational environments. Demand is not evenly distributed and may be intermittent in some locations. title: Repairs and Maintenance for Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service
description:
Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service (HIWFRS) is seeking to engage the market and provide interested suppliers with early sight of its proposed approach to the procurement of a Repairs and Maintenance Framework for Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service.
HIWFRS maintains a diverse operational estate that is essential to the delivery of frontline emergency response, prevention, protection and support services across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. The estate includes fire stations, headquarters and administrative buildings, training facilities, workshops, stores and other operational assets that require ongoing maintenance and repairs to ensure they remain safe, compliant, efficient and fit for purpose.
To support the effective management and development of its estate, HIWFRS is seeking to establish a new four-year Repairs and Maintenance Framework Agreement. This will be a multi-lotted, multi-supplier framework designed to provide a compliant, flexible and efficient route for procuring a wide range of minor construction, maintenance, refurbishment and improvement works across the Service’s property portfolio.
The scope of this procurement will focus on establishing a framework that enables the delivery of estate management and construction-related projects ranging from routine repairs and planned maintenance through to refurbishment schemes, building improvements and capital investment projects. The framework will support both planned and reactive requirements, ensuring the Service can respond effectively to operational needs, statutory compliance obligations, changing service demands and emerging estate priorities.
The framework has been structured into specialist lots to reflect the varied nature of works undertaken across the estate. This approach will allow HIWFRS to engage suppliers with the appropriate technical expertise and capabilities for each area of work, whilst maintaining value for money and ensuring high standards of project delivery.
The proposed lots are:
• Lot 1 – General Building Project Works (£250,000 to £2,000,000 per project)
• Lot 2 – Minor Mechanical & Electrical Works (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 3 – HVAC (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 4 – General Building Project Works (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 5 – Groundworks and Drainage (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 6 – Fabrication and Manufacturing (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 7 – Renewables (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 8 – Final Finishes (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 9 – Isle of Wight General Build (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 10 – Isle of Wight HVAC (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 11 – Isle of Wight Minor Mechanical & Electrical Works (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 12 – Isle of Wight Fabrication and Manufacturing (up to £250,000 per project)
• Lot 13 – Isle of Wight Renewables (up to £250,000 per project)
Each lot will comprise a defined number of pre-appointed suppliers, creating a resilient and competitive supply chain with sufficient capacity to support programme delivery throughout the lifetime of the framework. Establishing specific lots for Isle of Wight-based projects will help to ensure that projects can be delivered efficiently by contractors with local knowledge and established supply chains.
This framework will be particularly suitable for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) and local providers. The lotting structure has therefore been designed to reflect the scale and value of typical works packages.

title: Transport Infrastructure Planned & Reactive Maintenance
description:
This contract is for the provision of transport infrastructure planned and reactive maintenance across TFWM's asset portfolio (bus stations and park and ride sites), including proactive and reactive maintenance tasks, PAT testing and provision of a helpdesk service to manage tasks.
There are 5 key requirements set out in this specification, these are:
Planned Maintenance
Reactive Maintenance
Portable Appliance Testing
Helpdesk
Semi-Skilled Operative
These services will be delivered in line with the following objectives:
- The provision of Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) services to the Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) plant & equipment included within the contract
- The provision of reactive and emergency maintenance services to the Building Fabric and all M&E plant and equipment included within the contract
- The provision of "ad-hoc" escort / access assistance to all specialist Service Providers, engaged in the delivery of these services
- The carrying out of regular condition inspections across the facilities, at agreed intervals
- Ensuring that all Statutory and Legislative compliance maintenance works are carried out to all M&E plant & equipment covered in this specification
- The provision of specialist maintenance where required
- The provision of a comprehensive Planned and Reactive maintenance service across the facilities that complies with the standards and provisions as outlined within this specification
TfWM has made a commitment to and is working to develop good practice in infrastructure sustainability, including green and sustainable technologies in the design, refurbishment and maintenance of transport infrastructure facilities. The Service Provider will be required to demonstrate a commitment to sustainability by integrating sustainable development into their operating practices and culture throughout the Contract. This can be achieved by using low fuel consumption and emissions vehicles, optimising visits to each site, recycling of waste materials, disposing of any controlled waste in an approved manner, working with reusable components, using innovative designs and green technology or ethically sourced materials.

title: Yorkshire & Humber - Digital and Technology Skills Programme
description:
DSIT is seeking a Regional Delivery Partner who will be responsible for ensuring successful on-the-ground delivery of the TechFirst youth programme in the Yorkshire and Humber. TechFirst is the Government’s flagship digital and technology skills programme, created to remove skills as a barrier to growth in the sector. The sector relies on specialist digital and STEM skills, but there is a clear gap between demand and supply. This programme aims to build the sustainability and diversity of the tech talent pipeline, creating the foundations for long-term growth in one of the Government's 8 growth-driving sectors.
The youth strand of TechFirst, TechYouth, aims to reach 1 million students in schools and colleges across the UK with opportunities to develop their digital skills, gain confidence with AI and insight into a range of potential tech careers. Regional delivery partners will support the programme at a local level, delivering skills building activities and career inspiration days for schools and colleges in the area. They will work in partnership with local industry and academia to achieve this. 
With the support of Regional Delivery Partners, the TechYouth programme should spark young people's interest in technology and encourage more to pursue digital and computing qualifications at age 14 and 16, both academic and vocational. It will particularly encourage uptake from currently underrepresented groups, including girls and those from socioeconomic disadvantage. These students will form the pipeline of future technology researchers and professionals needed for the sector to achieve its potential growth.

title: Appointment of Archaeological Geophysical Surveyor
description:
Tavistock Town Council as Client and Accountable Body invites tenders from consultants with the relevant skills and capability to carry out an archaeological geophysical survey (CIfA standards) of the area shown on drawing J26.014. The method suggested and to be priced for, due to the site conditions and project aims, is Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR). Alternative methods, with associated rationale as an addition to the price schedule will be accepted as part of the tender submission. 
Due to the time sensitivities relating to the overall wider project deliverables, on appointment, contractors are required to apply for the necessary consents to enable the survey work to take place, which includes the Section 42 licence and production of the accompanying method statement. When considering pricing the works and the drafting of the method statement, the locations and associated activities need to be considered. e.g. The site plan include a churchyard which has funerals and ceremonies, a highway/public footpaths and a busy public realm (Bedford Square which has regular markets). Allowance should be made when surveying the highway for unsociable hrs/traffic management arrangements. 
As part of the National Lottery Heritage Fund grant conditions, the project has complimentary initiatives relating to community engagement. The appointed consultant should allow when surveying the churchyard/or Bedford Square for two half days working with community groups. (Note: this will include small groups, no more than 5 in No., either from the Youth Café or Heritage community partners). 
The contractor should allow for contacting sector specialists and statutory bodies as part of a desk top exercise to ascertain what previous equivalent survey work exists which will inform the works programme. 
On completion of the survey work, the contractor will produce a written report which is suitable to inform next steps with work commissioned to an appointed archaeologist, regarding possible excavation works as well and being in a appropriate format for public perusal as the results will feed into a wider interpretation programme, both digital and physical. As a minimum the report should include: tile page, summary of results, introduction, methods (techniques and methodologies), results, conclusions, acknowledgements, statement of indemnity, references, appendices and associated plots and plans, including interpretative plans/diagrams. These plans should be cross referenced to Blaylock's plan of the Abbey.
The contractor must allow for the costs of data archiving, within 6 months of completion of the report, including completing the online OASIS entry and depositing the digital archive with the Archaeological Data Service.  
The estimated budget allowance for this project for the Geophysical Surveyor's fees is between £13,000 to £20,000 plus VAT.
The start date for contract and applying for consents is early October 2026 with survey work and completion of the report targeted for the end of December 2026.

title: Small Venues Fund - Fund Administrator
description:
Following the North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) Cabinet meeting in March 2026, North East Mayor Kim McGuiness announced a package of £104million to turbocharge the region's creative industries driving new jobs and opportunities for local people. As part of that package, a commitment was made to back small venues across North East England.
Working alongside the sector, the North East MSA's Small Venues Fund (SVF) has been developed to support creative grassroots venues, providing them with the resources and capacity to host events and provide space and a platform for creatives to thrive. It has been shaped to ensure that this fund is fit for purpose and supports an array of artists from across the creative industries. The fund will support an increase in opportunities for both artists and venue operators supporting the exposure of such facilities both within the region and further afield. The fund will open more opportunities to touring artists, providing an increase in the visitor economy and a wider economic impact.
The North East MSA is looking to appoint an external Fund Administrator with experience of public sector grant administration and knowledge of the creative and cultural sector to manage the programme from initial enquiry through to project closure. The fund will be delivered on a phased basis.
The successful bidder will provide a fully managed grant administration service for the Small Venues Fund. Services will include:
o Programme mobilisation.
o Applicant support and enquiry management.
o Expression of Interest management.
o Full application management.
o Application appraisal and due diligence.
o Independent assessment panel administration.
o Grant contracting and subsidy control compliance.
o Grant monitoring and compliance activity.
o Financial management and payment administration.
o Reporting and management information.
o Support for programme evaluation.
The overall project value is £2.45m million, of which £2.2 million is set aside for grant awards.
The value of the contract for the Fund Administrator is up to £250,000 excluding VAT, for the duration of the contract.

title: Alternative Provision, Education Outreach and Inclusion Support Framework
description:
Royal Greenwich Council is establishing an open framework for the provision of Alternative Provision, Education Outreach and Inclusion Services.
The initial term of the Framework is three (3) years, with the option to extend for further period (s) up to twenty-four (24) months, at the sole discretion of the Authority.
The Framework will provide access to specialist providers delivering outcome focused education services to support vulnerable children and young people who are unable to access, engage with, or thrive within mainstream educational settings. To also work towards successful transition to education, employment or training post-16 at the end of Key Stage 4. The objectives of the services are to provide a flexible response to either compliment, or provide an alternative to the teaching and learning available within mainstream and specialist provision or for children not engaged in education.
The Framework will support children and young people of statutory school age, and young people up to the age of 25 with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), where appropriate.
The objectives of the services are to provide a flexible response to either compliment, or provide an alternative to the teaching and learning available within mainstream and specialist provision or for children not engaged in education.
The Framework is divided into three Lots.
Lot 1 - Alternative Provision
Lot 1 Alternative Provision will deliver a minimum of 25 hours (full-time) per week of education placements within a Department of Education (DfE) registered school on-site for secondary-aged pupils (Key Stages 3 and 4) who are permanently excluded, at risk of exclusion, or unable to engage with mainstream education.

title: GOV Voice
description:
The Gov Voice programme, led by the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, is focused on establishing a cross-government, AI-enabled voice capability to modernise how citizens interact with public sector contact services. It centres on deploying generative AI voice technology as a core component of a more integrated and consistent approach to service delivery across organisations.
A key aim of the programme is to enhance the overall citizen experience by enabling automated handling of routine enquiries. This approach is designed to reduce wait times, improve accessibility, and provide quicker resolutions for common queries, supporting a more responsive interface with government services.
Alongside these user benefits, the programme introduces a reusable and scalable platform that can be adopted across multiple organisations. By providing a centrally assured solution, it reduces duplication of effort and enables a more efficient, coordinated model for delivering voice-based services at scale.
Crucially, while led centrally, Gov Voice is intended to be applicable across the whole public sector landscape, enabling adoption by central government departments, local government organisations, and Arm’s Length Bodies (ALBs) to provide a consistent, interoperable voice capability that can operate securely within government environments and scale across multiple services.

title: Complex Move On Contract
description:
This UK6 contract award notice informs the market of the Authority's contract award to Langley Trust for the provision of the Complex Move On service. 
The Complex Move On service provides specialist risk management services, rehabilitation and resettlement support for people on probation with complex needs who are accommodated within pre-existing specialist accommodation settings. 
The service supports His Majesty Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) in managing individuals who require enhanced levels of care and risk management, by providing access to supported housing and other relevant support to individuals with complex needs with the aim of reducing the risk of reoffending. The funding from the Authority enables HMPPS to make referrals into these services by covering the additional costs associated with managing increased forensic risk and delivering appropriate criminogenic interventions. Funding for the accommodation and other support services will be obtained and managed by the supplier separately. Accordingly, the Authority does not have exclusive rights to the bed spaces used to deliver the service.
The support service is to be delivered within a portfolio of accommodation operated or accessed by the supplier, including: 
•	24/7 registered care home provision (Care);
•	24/7 staffed provision (Extra Care); and 
•	step-down supported accommodation in the community which is not staffed (Supported Housing).
The service is expected to be provided in at least 8 out of the 11 Probation Service regions in England - listed below:
- North East
- North West
- Yorkshire and the Humber
- West Midlands
- East Midlands
- South West
- South Central
- East of England
- London
- Kent, Surrey and Sussex
- Greater Manchester
The Authority expects to refer, as a maximum, 350 people at any one time within the service.
The cohort will include individuals subject to Multi Agency Public Protection Arrangements (MAPPA) Level 2 and Level 3 management, including those convicted of offences such as arson and sex offences.
Individuals referred to the service may present with a wide range of complex needs/risk levels, vulnerabilities and health conditions including autism spectrum conditions, dementia, hearing impairment, visual impairment, learning disability, mental ill health, personality disorder, physical disability, and poor physical health.
Referrals into the service will be made by Probation Practitioners and subject to capacity and suitability assessments, the provider will be expected to accept referrals where an appropriate placement is available.  
There is no maximum duration for an individual’s eligibility for the service. Where living independently is part of the individual’s sentence plan, the supplier will assist the individual to support that transition through appropriate accommodation, rehabilitation and support interventions. The Supplier does not claim VAT as part of their payment for the performance of this contract.

description:
Provider Selection Regime (PSR) Direct Award Process C for Provision of Outsourcing Neurology Services for Barking, Havering & Redbridge University Hospital NHS Trust (BHRUT). The contract is for general neurology services to treat 100x patients and support the reduction of waiting lists, improve patient access to care by providing an end-to-end pathway from outpatient appointment through to treatment, follow-up (where clinically required) and discharge back to the referring clinician or GP. This award is being made under Provider Selection Regime Direct Award C to Health Now Ltd. The appropriate lifetime value of the contract is £66,000 will be provisioned from 18/09/2026 till 31/03/2027.
The provider will treat or discharge General Neurological patients that have been triaged as suitable for outsourced clinics by BHRUT. If follow-ups are required and part of general neurology pathways, the provider will continue to provide treatment for these patients. Any patients requiring long-term follow-up (e.g. diagnosis of Epilepsy, Multiple Sclerosis, or Parkinson’s) will be discharged to the patients GP with advice to re-refer to BHRUT, which will be expedited. The expectation is that they will provide the full pathway, including all diagnostics with the exception of DaT scans which should be returned directly BHRUT.
The provider ensures that all patient information, clinical records and correspondence are managed securely and that discharge summaries are sent promptly to the referring clinician, detailing diagnosis, investigations undertaken, treatment provided, ongoing management recommendations and any further actions required. Justification for Direct Award under Procedure C: 
• The provider is the current incumbent and has delivered the service to a high standard.

title: SF6 Leak Repair Framework
description:
National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET) intends to establish a framework for the provision of Sulphur Hexafluoride (SF6) leak repair, leak reduction and preventative treatment services across its portfolio of Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) and Gas Insulated Busbar (GIB) assets located at transmission substations throughout Great Britain. The framework is intended to increase the delivery of SF6 emissions reduction activities through the use of standardised contracting arrangements and approved repair methodologies. Appointed contractors will be responsible for the design, installation, testing, inspection and quality assurance of external, non-intrusive repair solutions that maintain asset integrity and operational performance while reducing or preventing SF6 leakage. Solutions may include permanent repairs, leak-rate reduction treatments, and preventative interventions, and will typically be required to be installed without taking equipment out of service where reasonably practicable. Contractors will be expected to provide technically robust, evidence-based solutions, operate under ISO 9001-compliant quality management systems, and fulfil the roles of Principal Contractor and Principal Designer under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015. The framework will enable NGET to respond efficiently to emerging SF6 emission reduction requirements across its transmission network.
The anticipated term of the framework will be a 3-year initial term with 2 year extension options upon mutual agreement.
