title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – " Ausbildung und Gestaltung von seitlichen Baustellenzuwegungen im Längsverkehr auf BAB "
description: Im Zuge der Durchführung von Bauarbeiten müssen regelmäßig Baustellenfahrzeuge, Transportfahrzeuge und Baumaschinen in den Arbeitsbereich ein- und ausfahren. Hierfür kommen insbesondere bei langen Baustellenabschnitten Baustellenzuwegungen innerhalb der Arbeitsstelle, d. h. im Längsverkehr der Autobahn, zum Einsatz. Solche Zuwegungen führen zu zusätzlichen Konfliktpunkten mit dem fließenden Verkehr, die die Verkehrssicherheit mindern bzw. zu Störungen im Verkehrsablauf führen können. Aktuell gibt es keine Standards für die Ausbildung und Gestaltung von solchen Baustellenzuwegungen. Während Baustellenzuwegungen in Regelwerken und Arbeitsschutzvorschriften grundsätzlich berücksichtigt werden, liegen bislang nur wenige wissenschaftlich fundierte Erkenntnisse zu deren sicherer und leistungsfähiger Gestaltung vor. Ziel dieses Forschungsvorhabens ist die systematische Untersuchung von Baustellenzuwegungen innerhalb von Arbeitsstellen längerer Dauer auf BAB sowie die Erarbeitung wissenschaftlich fundierter Empfehlungen für deren Planung, Gestaltung und Betrieb. Weiterhin sollen geeignete Bewertungsmaßstäbe entwickelt werden, mit denen die Eignung unterschiedlicher Lösungen hinsichtlich Verkehrssicherheit, Verkehrsablauf und Praktikabilität beurteilt werden kann. Als Ergebnis des Forschungsvorhabens sind Handlungsempfehlungen für die Planung, Ausschreibung, Genehmigung und den Betrieb von Baustellenzuwegungen im Längsverkehr zu erarbeiten. Es sind unter anderem Vorgaben zur geeigneten Lage, Entwicklungslänge, Beschilderung und Markierung sowie zu verkehrstechnischen Maßnahmen abgeleitet werden. Zudem sollen Vorschläge für die Fortschreibung bestehender Regelwerke, Leitfäden, Verordnungen und technischer Vorschriften abgeleitet werden (z. B. RSA, VwV StVO, ZTV SA). Das Vorhaben soll einen Beitrag zur sicheren, effizienten und regelwerkskonformen Abwicklung von Arbeitsstellen längerer Dauer auf hochbelasteten Bundesautobahnen leisten.

description: Um die Primärversorgung in Österreich weiter zu stärken und zu attraktivieren, ist die Durchführung von relevanten und qualitativ hochwertigen Forschungsprojekten notwendig. Aus diesem Grund sollte die Durchführung von praxisnahen Anwendungsforschungsprojekten in der Primärversorgung inklusive der Etablierung von Forschungsnetzwerken mit Einrichtungen der Primärversorgung über Mittel aus dem Projekt „Attraktivierung und Förderung der Primärversorgung in Österreich", das durch die EU Aufbau- und Resilienzfazilität (RRF) finanziert wird, unterstützt werden. Zielgruppe der vorliegenden Ausschreibung waren Universitäten oder Fachhochschulen mit medizinischem oder gesundheitswissenschaftlichem Fokus. Außerdem waren wissenschaftliche Einrichtungen gemäß § 2b Z. 12 FOG (oder gleichwertiger Status gemäß den anwendbaren gesetzlichen Bestimmungen im Sitzstaat) mit medizinischem oder gesundheitswissenschaftlichem Fokus zur Teilnahme berechtigt. Die einzureichenden Forschungsprojekte sollten sich thematisch an die Ziele des Projekts „Attraktivierung und Förderung der Primärversorgung in Österreich" und zwar (1) Verbesserung der sozialen Inklusion, (2) Verbesserung von ökologischer Nachhaltigkeit, (3) Verbesserung der Digitalisierung und (4) Verbesserung der Multiprofessionalität halten. Darüber hinaus bestand die Möglichkeit zum Thema "Prozesse" einzureichen, im Sinne von Behandlungs- und Versorgungsprozessen bzw. innerorganisatorischen Abläufen. title: Germany – Engineering services – Zweckverband der 12 Gemeinden des ehemaligen Amtes Thronecken - Energetische Sanierung der Kindertagesstätte Regenbogen, Los 2: Planungsleistungen der Technischen Ausrüstung HLS und Elektro
description: Der Zweckverband der 12 Gemeinden des ehemaligen Amtes Thronecken plant die energetische Sanierung der Kindertagesstätte Regenbogen in Thalfang. Im Zuge der geplanten Sanierung soll die Kindertagesstätte auf den Effizienzhausstandard 70 ausgerichtet werden. Dies soll einerseits durch die Verbesserung der Gebäudehülle mittels Dammmaßnahmen und andererseits durch die Erneuerung der Wärmeerzeugung/-verteilung/ -übergabe erreicht werden. Es ist vorgesehen, die Gebäudehülle in ihrer Gesamtheit durch geeignete Dämmmaßnahmen auf das energetische Niveau eines Neubaus zu bringen. Dies erfordert, dass sämtliche an die Außenluft angrenzenden Bauteile hinsichtlich ihrer Wärmedurchgangskoeffizienten über die Anforderungen des Gebäudeenergiegesetzes (GEG) hinaus ertüchtigt werden. Hierfür sind folgende Maßnahmen vorgesehen: - Dämmung der Fassade mit 18cm Dämmstoff in der Wärmeleitgruppe 035, - Austausch aller Fenster auf dreifachverglaste Fenster, - Dämmung des Daches mit einer Kombination aus Zwischen- und Aufsparrendämmung, - Dämmung des Flachdaches, - Raumseitige Dämmung der Bodenplatten. Die an das Erdreich angrenzenden Außenwände sollen nach Möglichkeit ebenfalls deutlich verbessert werden, sofern der Kosten-Nutzen-Faktor in einem rentablen Maße steht. Im Rahmen der energetischen Sanierung soll zudem die Anlagentechnik modernisiert werden. Dazu soll das bestehende Heizungssystem vollständig auf Wärmeerzeugung über eine Wärmepumpe umgestellt werden, die die erzeugte Wärme an das Fußbodenheizungssystem abgibt. Mittels Erdsonden, welche die Wärmepumpe versorgen, soll zukünftig erneuerbare Energie zum Heizen eingesetzt werden. Dieses System soll in der Perspektive auch zum Kühlen genutzt werden. Weiterhin ist vorgesehen, auch die Wärmeverteilung und -übergabe vollständig zu erneuen. So soll ein modernes und intelligent gesteuertes Fußbodenheizungssystem für einen geringen Wärmeverbrauch sorgen. Ebenso soll in dem Zuge auch der untere Gebäudeabschluss, die Bodenplatte, energetisch verbessert werden. Durch den Einbau der Fußbodenheizung muss der Estrich entfernt werden, was vorliegend die Gelegenheit bietet, moderne, gut gedämmte Fußbodenaufbauten zu verwenden. Zudem soll der Strombedarf des Gebäudes zukünftig zu einem großen Teil über Photovoltaikanlage gedeckt werden. Die Maßnahme wird aus öffentlichen Mitteln gefördert. Es wurde ein Fördermittelantrag (EFRE) gestellt, welcher bereits bewilligt wurde mit der Folge, dass die Vorgaben des Konzepts zur Energetischen Berechnung der geplanten Sanierung, der EFRE-Fördercall sowie die Vorgaben des Zuwendungsbescheides planerisch und baulich verbindlich sind und umgesetzt werden müssen. Der Kostenschwerpunkt der Sanierungen liegt entsprechend der Vorgaben des Fördermittelbescheides mit mindestens 70% auf den gebäudeseitigen energetischen Sanierungsmaßnahmen, d.h. auf Fassadendämmung, Dämmung Dach / oberste Geschossdecke, Dämmung Bodenplatte / Kellerdecke / Kellerwände, Austausch Fenster / Außentüren / Pfosten-Riegel-Fassaden (zuzüglich Ausgaben für den sommerlichen Wärmeschutz etwaig in Form einer kombinierten Lösung über die Fenster), für notwendige Gebäudeautomatisation, Steuerung und Regelung sowie Raumlufttechnische Anlagen. Die Vorgaben des EFRE-Zuwendungsbescheids sind verbindlich und zwingend einzuhalten. Hinsichtlich der weiteren Einzelheiten wird auf die beigefügte Leistungsbeschreibung Bezug genommen, welche Bestandteil der Vergabeunterlagen/Vertragsunterlagen ist.
buyer: ['Zweckverband der 12 Gemeinden des ehemaligen Amtes Tronecken']

description: Es handelt sich um die nur geringfügig angepasste Neuausschreibung des erfolglos verlaufenen Vergabeverfahrens VOEK 173-26. Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Leistung ist die Erstellung eines ausschreibungsreifen Bau-Leistungsverzeichnisses („Bau-LV“) für die Errichtung und den Betrieb von Photovoltaikanlagen („PV-Anlagen“) auf Dächern von ca. 500 bis 650 Bundeswehrgebäuden bis zum Jahr 2030. Hierzu hat der Auf-tragnehmer auf Grundlage von Bestandsaufnahmen und Untersuchungen an fünf repräsentativen Liegen-schaften ein umfassendes, alle potenziell erforderlichen Leistungen abdeckendes Bau-LV gemäß § 7b VS VOB/A zu erstellen. Das Bau-LV soll als Grundlage für die Beauftragung von Unternehmen zur Realisierung der PV-Anlagen in einem nachgelagerten Vergabeverfahren dienen. Die Leistungserbringung erfolgt in enger Abstimmung mit parallel beauftragten Planungsbüros, die die technische und wirtschaftliche Eignung der Gebäude prü-fen und die jeweiligen Ausführungsplanungen erstellen. Ziel ist es, durch die frühzeitige Erstellung des Bau-LV und die vorgezogene Beauftragung der Bauunternehmen eine unmittelbar anschließende Bauaus-führung nach Abschluss von Analyse und Planung zu ermöglichen.

description:
This procurement is for a works contract valued at £1.6m in line with the Procurement Act 2023 Regulated Below Threshold procedure for works to modernise and refurbish the Horley Community Centre. 
As a works contract exceeding the statutory minimum values outlined in Section 85(3) of the Procurement Act 2023, a separate suitability assessment stage (Stage 1) is being utilized before the invitation to tender (Stage 2).
The Council has a requirement to appoint  an experienced contractor will be responsible for completing the design development of the proposals post RIBA Stage 4 and to deliver the physical works required to revitalise this important and valued community asset.
The proposed project will see the existing building fully refurbished with some internal remodelling. 
This will involve (but is not limited to) minor demolition works of removing walls and creating new spaces to create partition wall/openings, replacement and upgrading of windows and doors, full replacement of toilets, creation of a new Changing Places Toilet and new wall, floor and ceiling finishes throughout. 
Externally works will involve relandscaping the existing forecourt to include resurfacing, planting, installation of fencing, planting and cycle stands, removal and replacement of a new entrance canopy with feature signage and roof installation of photovoltaic panels.

title: The provision of NRT, E-Cigarettes and Stop Smoking Medication Solution
description:
Leicester City Council's Public Health team is seeking a provider to support the delivery of its integrated lifestyle service, Live Well, by managing the storage, dispensing, and distribution of Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT), e-cigarettes, and stop smoking medications. The project aims to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and clinical governance of stop smoking support offered to Leicester residents by replacing the current in-house stock management and postal distribution process with a comprehensive outsourced solution.
The appointed provider will be responsible for managing stock levels, dispatching NRT and e-cigarette products directly to clients within agreed timescales, and facilitating pharmacist-led prescribing and dispensing of stop smoking medications, including Varenicline, Cytisine, and Bupropion. The service must operate in line with relevant clinical, regulatory, and governance requirements, including NICE guidance, Patient Group Directions (PGDs), GDPR, GPhC standards, and Leicester City Council's Public Health Clinical Governance Framework.
The project also requires the provision of a secure, user-friendly digital system to manage orders, appointments, inventory, prescription activity, reporting, and delivery tracking, alongside staff training and ongoing support. The overall objective is to enhance the client experience, reduce delays in accessing treatment, and contribute to Leicester's smokefree ambitions through a safe, efficient, and clinically robust service.

title: NW2964 - Microsoft 365, AI and Intelligent Automation Partner Framework Agreement
description:
NW2964 - Microsoft 365, AI and Intelligent Automation Partner Framework Agreement
Northumbrian Water Group (NWG) provides essential water and wastewater services to 2.7 million customers across the North East of England and drinking water services to over 2 million customers in Essex and Suffolk. 
Northumbrian Water Group (NWG) has a strategic ambition to become the world's most digitally enabled water company and continues to invest significantly in Microsoft 365, Microsoft Azure, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Intelligent Automation, Data & Analytics and associated cloud technologies to support this ambition. Our digital strategy is focused on maximising business value from these technologies through improved productivity, collaboration, operational efficiency, automation and data-driven decision-making.
As the Microsoft technology landscape continues to evolve rapidly, NWG requires access to a broad range of specialist expertise to support advisory services, architecture, design, implementation, optimisation, governance, adoption, change management and ongoing innovation across its Microsoft estate. This demand is expected to vary over time and will require the ability to access both strategic advisory capability and specialist technical resources across multiple disciplines.
To support these requirements, NWG intends to establish a multi-supplier (up to 10 suppliers ultimately appointed in total, reserving the right to appoint a different amount subject to suppliers meeting relevant quality thresholds) Microsoft 365, AI and Intelligent Automation Framework Agreement (or framework). The Framework terms shall be 3 years with options to extend for 3+1+1 years (up to 8 years in total). The total forecasted spend under the Framework is estimated at up to £900,000 pa, equating to an estimated total potential spend of up to £7,200,000 over the full 8-year framework lifecycle. The framework will create a panel of pre-qualified partners with proven expertise across Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Copilot, AI, Intelligent Automation, Azure, Data & Analytics and related technologies. This will provide NWG with a flexible and compliant mechanism to engage specialist partners through future call-off engagements and mini-competitions as business needs arise.
The framework is intended to establish long-term strategic partnerships rather than transactional supplier relationships. By appointing multiple partners, NWG will have access to a diverse range of skills, capacity and innovation capabilities, enabling the organisation to quickly respond to changing business priorities while maintaining consistency in governance, delivery standards and value for money.
 Implementation is expected to take approximately six weeks following contract award, with a planned go-live date of February 2027. Future capability areas may be introduced during the lifetime of the framework in response to emerging technologies and evolving business priorities.

title: Supported Accommodation Framework
description:
Hampshire County Council’s Children’s Services Directorate intends to establish a flexible and future‑ready Framework for Supported Accommodation, designed to attract high‑quality providers capable of delivering a diverse and evolving range of supported accommodation services for young people across the Hampshire region.
A Framework is a flexible procurement mechanism built around a set of pre‑agreed terms. The Authority evaluates potential providers against clearly defined criteria, and those who meet the requirements are appointed to the Framework. Once onboarded, these approved providers can then compete for service delivery opportunities through individual call‑off contracts.
The Supported Accommodation services will be for the support of 16-21-year-old young people across Hampshire, including:
• Looked After Children
• Care Leavers
• Separated Children
• Children in Need (in accordance with Section 17 of the Children's Act)
The Framework will enable the purchasing, delivery and management of services designed to meet the needs of young people within Hampshire. It will cover a wide range of Supported Accommodation services, including providing Ofsted regulated accommodation-based support for 16-21 year olds, with varying levels of support and intensity required across the service.
The Framework term is for an initial term of 4 years, with the potential to extend for a further 4 years, in 2 year increments, to a maximum term of 8 years.
All providers will require Ofsted Registration in order to be eligible for this Framework. This is part of the Ofsted Inspection Framework for services for children in need of help and protection, Looked After Children (LAC) and Care Leavers. All providers delivering supported accommodation must be registered with Ofsted in one or more of the four approved categories:
• Self‑contained accommodation
• Ring‑fenced shared accommodation exclusively for LAC and 16/17 care leavers
• Non‑ring‑fenced shared accommodation, which may include 18+ care leavers
• Supported accommodation provided in a private residence (e.g., supported lodgings)
Providers must only operate within the categories for which they are registered. Registration requires meeting all Supported Accommodation (England) Regulations 2023 and associated Quality Standards, including leadership, protection, accommodation and support. If a provider awarded a contract under this framework becomes subject to an Ofsted restriction on accepting placements, the Council reserves the right to suspend or remove the provider from the framework with immediate effect. It is the sole responsibility of the provider to ensure that they are operating in full compliance with all applicable Ofsted inspection framework requirements and that they remain eligible and suitably authorised to accept placements at all times.
This is a light touch contract as set out in section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023. As such the Council is establishing a Framework which will be open for new entrants across it's entire term. However, the Council reserves the right to temporarily pause the Framework for new entrants at any point. Any pause will be communicated through the Councils electronic tendering system. 
The Timetable in section 4.1 relates to the initial application window for the Framework. Once the Framework commences it will be reopened for new applications and suppliers will be able to apply at any point up until 3 months before the Framework expires.
Providers wishing to enrol on the Framework will need to apply for the Supported Accommodation Framework via In-Tend. There is no work (i.e. no placements) awarded at Framework level, all future placements will be awarded at call-off level. Any subsequent call offs from this Framework will be advertised to all providers onboarded onto the Framework, and each individual call off will include more in-depth information regarding the services being called off from the Framework. In order to apply for any call-off opportunities from this Framework in the future, a Framework Agreement must first be awarded.
Devolution/Local Government Reform 
The government wants all remaining two-tier areas in England to be eventually restructured into single-tier unitary authorities and is termed Local Government Reform (LGR). This reorganisation is part of a broader devolution strategy to simplify local government structures, save public funds, and improve local accountability. It is anticipated, that during the life of this contract, the LGR process will commence and/or progress potentially impacting this contract. Impacts most likely will include, novations of the legal entities you may contract with. There are assignment clauses within the Contract Terms and Conditions that allow us to assign, novate etc. the agreements to another body. 
Regional Care Cooperatives
As part of reforms to the children’s social care system, there is a drive from central government to move towards regional commissioning arrangements under Regional Care Cooperatives (RCCs) which may affect the Council’s commissioning activities in the future.

title: Class 331 Heavy Maintenance infrastructure upgrade Allerton TCC
description:
Scope of Works:
The supplier shall provide facilities capable of supporting the Heavy Maintenance re-quirements of the Class 331 fleet. The Class 331 Heavy Maintenance programme needs to start no later than 1st March 2028 to ensure that the Heavy Maintenance activities can be undertaken within the required maintenance schedule of the fleet and ensure it does not have a detrimental impact on customer rail services.
- All design, construction, EIS, handover and training is required to have been completed in advance of the 1st March 2028. A high level programme is to be generated by the contractor as part of the tender process
A key part of this programme is the replacement of bogies across the fleet, which needs to happen in an efficient way to maintain programme. 4-road at Allerton has been iden-tified as the location where this work will take place. To undertake bogie change re-placement on 4-road, the following items will need to be installed/addressed:
· Installation of a vehicle jacking system capable of lifting 3 x class 331 vehicles in a synchronized manner without the need for splitting/decoupling the units. The system shall also be capable of jacking single and two car units.
· To facilitate the vehicle jacking system, there will be a need for the supplier to ensure that the floor is capable to safely withstand the expected loads when jacking a Class 331, and that the floor is suitably level and flat for the jacks. Sur-veys will be required in order to validate this.
· The supplier shall ensure that the jacks are interlocked with the Depot Protec-tion system so that no rail vehicle movements can take place unless jacks are in the stowed/birthed position.
· The design shall ensure that there is adequate clearance for personnel to safely walk around the jacks in both operational and stowed positions. The preference is for the jacks to be mounted on rails and be compact to maximise clearance around the jacks.
· Road 4 pits and floorings shall painted.
· Circa 30m x 1.5m along road 4 has a side pitted area. As part of this work there would be a need to bring the height of these side pits to be level with the adja-cent flooring in order to accommodate the jacks and facilitate easy removal of jacks if required. This area should be reinforced throughout to enable jacking of any class of vehicle. As per design development a barrier should be considered between road 4 and 5 along this section to prevent the risk of falling from height from road 4 into the side pit of road 5, this cannot be of detriment to operations on adjacent road.
· There is currently roof access equipment and a crane situated along road 4. NTL would like to retain this equipment. The expected positions of the jacks on road 4 have been marked out and it is not expected that the jacks would foul with these items of equipment. However, there will be a need for the supplier to vali-date that during lifting operations that the train is adequately clear of the roof ac-cess equipment. The supplier should make provision for modifications to the roof access equipment to ensure adequate clearance is achieved.
· Once vehicles are lifted, the bogies would be rolled by hand along the rail to ei-ther end of the shed where a forklift will be used to lift the bogies and transfer to a storage location. There will be a need for the supplier to design and build a level concrete hardstanding to be extended on both ends of the shed in order to support the safe lifting of bogies by a forklift and the transfer of components from the hardstanding on road 4 to an identified storage location.
· Storage for a minimum of 12 bogies in total, to be segregated into “clean” and “dirty” bogie storage. The ability to store 16 bogies in total should be explored within the designated area, to provide potential future capability. The identified location for storing the bogies is shown in the image below.
· A battery forklift truck is proposed to be used. The supplier is required to work with NTL to identify a suitable fork lift truck. The supplier shall design and build a covered storage area for the Fork Lift Truck, with battery charging facilities.
· A swept path analysis shall be undertaken for Fork Lift truck operations from the pick up position at the rail, to the storage location of bogies. The supplier shall check that there is adequate clearance and that floor loadings are acceptable throughout, inclusive of any RRAPs, manhole covers, general road surfacing.
· The supplier shall undertake a Hazid review of the Fork Lift truck movement around site with the movement of components to ensure that any hazards are identified and mitigated where required.

title: Advocacy & Independent Visitor Service
description:
Advocacy Service.
The Council has a duty to offer an independent advocacy service to care experienced young people, children subject to a child protection plan and children in need. The main purpose is to empower and enable young people to have a voice by providing independent information, advice, support and advocacy. It provides a confidential opportunity to share information and concerns about their care or treatment, to be informed of their rights and be able to access independent representation. Advocacy should be led by the views, wishes of children and young people, and champion the rights and needs of children and young people. These measures must be implemented alongside relevant guidance including Effective Advocacy for Looked-After Children, Children in Need and Care Leavers 2023 and adapt to new guidance released.
The Council also has a duty to provide independent advocacy to 16 and 17 year-old people who may be homeless and/or require accommodation. The service needs to provide independent advocacy to this cohort of young people so that they can make an informed decision about their accommodation.
The Independent Visitor Service .
Independent Visitors can play an important role in safeguarding children in care, helping to identify problems early and to secure for them the help and support they need to flourish. An Independent Visitor is an adult who has been trained to befriend a child in care, take an interest in their welfare, spend time with them, offer advice, support and guidance, and encourage them to take part in challenging and stimulating personal development activities. Independent Visitors provide positive influences in the lives of children in care, encourage them to express their concerns about issues or query where they are unhappy about any aspects of their care. By maintaining productive relationships with children in care, Independent Visitors help to raise their self-esteem, confidence and ability to nurture trusting and healthy relationships while safeguarding these children.

title: Strategic Consultancy and Technology Services Framework
description:
INTRODUCTION
Energia Group is a leading energy provider operating across both the Republic of Ireland (ROI) and Northern Ireland (NI), supplying electricity and gas to a broad and diverse customer base. In ROI, Energia serves over 300,000 residential and small business electricity and gas customers. In NI, its subsidiary Power NI is the largest electricity supplier, with approximately 550,000 domestic and business electricity customers. The Group also serves large industrial and commercial customers across the island, providing tailored energy solutions, including renewable energy offerings and energy efficiency services. Energia plays a central role in the island's energy transition, underpinned by a strong focus on sustainability, innovation, and customer-centric services.
This procurement forms a key component of Energia's broader technology transformation strategy. As the energy sector undergoes rapid change driven by evolving customer expectations, increasing regulatory complexity, and the transition to net zero, Energia is committed to modernising its technology platforms to ensure agility, resilience, and longterm value delivery.
Energia Group requires strategic partners to support us through this transformation, partnering with us to deliver both enterprise scale transformation and scalable, resilient, adaptable technology services that can support unified, efficient service across our operating markets.
Please click on the below link for further information on Energia Group ("Energia").
https://www.energiagroup.com/
Energia wish to appoint a multi supplier framework agreement to provide support in the enhancement and development of new systems and business processes. This framework is intended to establish a pool of trusted, high-quality partners capable of providing both strategic and delivery focused support. Suppliers appointed to the framework will be expected to bring deep subject matter expertise, strong delivery capability, and the ability to work collaboratively with internal teams to deliver outcomes at pace. This includes supporting enterprise scale transformation initiatives as well as providing flexible, scalable resources to augment internal capability where required. 
The framework will enable Energia to:
• Access highly skilled specialist resources to supplement internal teams and address skills gaps as they arise.
• Scale delivery capacity efficiently to support both business-as-usual activity and project-based change.
• Deliver end to end initiatives, from discovery and design through to implementation and transition into operation.
• Maintain agility and resilience by drawing on a diverse supplier ecosystem, rather than relying on single supplier arrangements.
Overall, the procurement will provide a structured, compliant mechanism through which Energia can engage strategic partners who are able to support the Group's technology transformation, enhance delivery capability, and contribute meaningfully to the successful execution of its energy transition objectives.

title: Environmental Surveillance: OSMA and OSD
description:
The FSA has awarded a contract for delivery of a research and evidence project to strengthen the FSA’s environmental surveillance capability for foodborne disease (FBD) and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The project will generate robust, transferable evidence to support a One Health approach to environmental surveillance, demonstrating the feasibility, operational value and cost effectiveness of combining a One Sample Many Analyses (OSMA) approach with targeted On Site Diagnostic (OSD) technologies, using environmental samples that are already collected across government.
The requirement is to deliver a structured, phased programme of work that enables the FSA to determine where and how OSMA and OSD approaches provide added value relative to existing laboratory based, single organisation surveillance models, and where they do not. The emphasis is on evidence generation, evaluation and decision support, rather than deployment at scale.

title: British Gurkas Nepal White Fleet Vehicle Replacement
description:
British Gurkha’s Nepal (BGN) current vehicle fleet requires replacing.
The north of Nepal is dominated by the Himalayan Mountain Range; this region is sparsely populated and requires reliable vehicles with off road capabilities. The middle band of the country is hilly and more densely populated, including the two largest cites, Kathmandu and Pokhara where two of BGN’s camps are situated.  The southern strip of the country, bordering India, is comparatively flat but again, densely populated.  Both regions also require transport capable of traversing in off road conditions, particularly in the monsoon season.  Roads throughout Nepal often lack tarmac, including in population centres.  The road quality varies drastically from tarmac to potholed dirt tracks. There is a requirement for 4 x 4 vehicles to ensure BGN can meet its outputs across all geographic regions. 
The new fleet should comprise of the following: 
1.	8 x Passenger conveying 4x4. 
2.	10 x Closed cab goods conveying 4x4. 
3.	2 x Open dual cab goods conveying 4x4. 
4.	3 x Ambulatory 4x4. 
5.	1 x Combination Van. 
6.	2 x Delivery Van. 
7.	1 x Baggage Truck.

title: EXTRA CARE HOUSING PETERSFIELD
description:
The vision for Extra Care is to enable people to continue to live independently for longer through the development of
vibrant and balanced communities with onsite care that adapts to changing needs, through effective partnership
working between registered landlords, service providers and wider stakeholders.
To support balanced communities within Extra Care housing, each scheme aims to balance the following split in care
needs: 40% high need (10 hours +); 40% medium need (5-10 hours); and 20% low need (less than 5 hours).
The aims and objectives of Extra Care services are:
To provide personalised care and support to people living in Extra Care Housing who have assessed eligible
care needs under the Care Act 2014.
To maximise the independence of people living in Extra Care Housing, including those with Dementia,
enabling them to live well and independently, carry out the functions of daily living, and to achieve positive
outcomes in respect of addressing their identified needs and their overall experience of the service.
To promote and maintain residents' health and wellbeing, enabling them to overcome any anxieties, build
resilience and increase their confidence to live independently.
To support recovery from illness, through supporting timely discharge from hospital and preventing
unnecessary acute hospital admissions and re-admissions.
To reduce residents' social isolation, improve the maintenance and development of their social support
networks, facilitate community access and enable them to feel confident living in their community.
To meet the fluctuating and developing needs of residents.
To reduce to need for onward moves to residential and nursing care.

title: Community Wellbeing Workers Service (CWWS)
description:
In response to growing demand on Adults’ Health and Care services, it has been identified that additional capacity is required to support individuals who would benefit from preventative or lower-level interventions. 
This new service will take account of learning from the previous service and aims to build on its successes. It retains several of the key features of the previous service such as community-based workers delivering short- term, holistic interventions to individuals and supporting them to reduce debt and maximise income and to navigate and access services across the community as well as the health and care system to build greater financial resilience.
The new service will retain these core principles while introducing several developments designed to strengthen outcomes, improve sustainability, and respond to emerging local and national priorities. A key change is the move to a county-wide delivery model operating through four geographical clusters. This approach will provide greater consistency of service across Hampshire, create larger and more sustainable contract opportunities for providers, and support improved outcomes through a more coordinated service structure. The service will continue to adopt a strengths-based approach, working alongside individuals to build on their existing skills, networks, and community assets to improve independence and resilience.
A further enhancement of the service is its emphasis on supporting individuals to navigate and access coordinated support across a broad range of local services. This recognises that financial hardship is often linked to wider social, health, and wellbeing challenges. The service will support individuals experiencing financial difficulties to access specialist financial advice where required, alongside services that promote employment, volunteering, and pathways towards work. It will also provide support for individuals living with dementia, those awaiting assessment, and their carers, helping them to access preventative support and improve long-term financial resilience.
As with the previous service, support will also be available for individuals already known to Adults’ Health and Care whose circumstances are particularly complex and who would benefit from additional non-statutory support alongside statutory provision. Building on the previous model, the new service will broaden the scope of interventions available to include activities that support population health objectives. This may include facilitating access to smoking cessation services, substance misuse support, domestic abuse services, and other specialist interventions that can improve health, wellbeing, and financial resilience.

title: HELP TO LIVE AT HOME SERVICE FOR ZONE 1
description:
South Tyneside is a vibrant coastal borough in the North East of England, with a strong commitment to supporting residents to live healthy, independent and fulfilling lives. The Council works in close partnership with health, voluntary and community sector organisations to deliver person-centred care that reflects the diverse needs of local people, particularly older residents and those with complex needs. There is a well-established focus on strengths-based practice, early intervention and reducing inequalities, underpinned by integrated working with NHS partners and a shared ambition to improve outcomes across the system.
Service Providers play a key role in shaping future provision, contributing to a sustainable local care market that supports people to remain in their own homes and communities wherever possible. 
The Council currently operates three HTLAH Zones in the borough, at contract inception there were four Providers, offering marketplace flexibility, whilst ensuring the needs of residents could be met.
The aim of the HTLAH service is to supports adults aged 18 and over to maximise their independence, wellbeing, and quality of life by providing flexible, outcome-focused support that enables them to remain living safely in their own homes and communities, while preventing, reducing, or delaying the need for more intensive health and social care services. Often these are older people with for example dementia or frailty needs but may include people of all ages with physical disabilities and mental health needs.
In the initial contracts, this approach included Extra Care provision, it has now been agreed that this activity will be funded separately. Therefore, this leaves two types of support to be provided via future HTLAH provision within the borough, these include:
Home Independence Support Service (HISS)
This is the long-term home care element of the contract for people who need ongoing support to remain living independently at home. Typical services include Personal care (washing, dressing, toileting, Medication support, assistance with meals and nutrition), Support with mobility and transfer and social inclusion and community access. Support is also available for people with dementia, physical disabilities, and long-term conditions. Night-time support is provided where required. 
Home Independence and Crisis Support Service (HICSS)
This is the short-term, reablement and hospital discharge element of the contract. Services include, Hospital-to-home support, Admission avoidance, Intermediate care, Short-term reablement, Active recovery following illness or injury, Crisis response, Community alarm response, and support to regain daily living skills and reduce long-term care needs.
Please note the Council has determined that suppliers currently delivering the Help to Live at Home contracts for Help to Live at Home Zones 2 and 3 are not eligible to participate in this procurement.

title: RIIO-GT3 Control System Replacement MWC Framework Expression of Interest
description:
This opportunity is published to advertise a preliminary market engagement exercise being conducted by National Gas Transmission PLC ("NGT"). NGT is seeking feedback from the market to support and refine its approach to a forthcoming procurement process in respect of the RIIO-GT3 Control System Replacement Main Works Contractor (MWC) Framework.
Who are NGT
NGT play a vital role in delivering gas to millions of people across Great Britain. NGT owns, manages, and operates the National Transmission System ("NTS") in Great Britain, making gas available when and where it's needed. NGT ensure that the network is safe, reliable and available, and that it delivers value for our customers and stakeholders, while minimising impact on the environment. 
What is the Control System Replacement Programme
The overarching scope of each project in the programme is the complete replacement and upgrading of the compressor station's control systems to enhance cyber resilience. This involves modernising legacy infrastructure, implementing robust cybersecurity measures, and ensuring that the control systems are capable of withstanding evolving digital threats. The upgrades are intended to safeguard operational integrity, protect critical assets, and align with national and international standards for cyber-secure infrastructure.
RIIO-GT3 Control System Replacement MWC Framework
NGT has now transitioned from the RIIO-GT2 regulatory period into RIIO-GT3, which runs from April 2026 to March 2031. As part of this new regulatory period, NGT is implementing a new delivery model for the remaining projects within the Control System Replacement Programme. Under this model, a FEED Partner will be appointed to undertake the FEED study for each project. Upon completion of the FEED phase, NGT will appoint a Main Works Contractor (MWC) to deliver the detailed design, manufacture, installation, testing, and commissioning of the relevant station control system works. To support the efficient delivery of the programme, NGT intends to establish a framework agreement through which a number of Main Works Contractors will be appointed and subsequently engaged to deliver projects across the programme.
How to express an interest
Interested parties are to express an interest by completing and returning the response template. Please request the response template by emailing Thomas.Jones@nationalgas.com and Syed.Kully@nationalgas.com.

title: High 5 4 Heritage - Professional Services in Respect of Repair and Restoration Works to the Mechanics Theatre, Burnley
description:
Working in partnership with the National Lottery Heritage Fund (NLHF), the Council is seeking the services of a suitable consultant/s to assist in the delivery of repair and restoration works to the Mechanics Theatre, as part of a five-year heritage led programme, High 5 4 Heritage, focused within Burnley's Civic Core.
Through this programme, we are setting out to connect the people of Burnley with our civic history by focusing on the built and social heritage within Burnley's Civic Core. This is an area of central Burnley which encompasses some remarkable buildings and spaces which are used every day by local people. However, this is an area under threat, as some of the buildings are in decline and it is felt the heritage is not well known about or understood, which we want to change.
To achieve this, we have identified our 'high-five' objectives - 1) make physical improvements to the area by addressing the threats to heritage through building repair and restoration works, while; 2) making our heritage assets sustainable and manageable; 3) engage the community with the intriguing historic events, people and stories that have shaped our town; 4) public realm works to improve visitor experience, and the setting of listed buildings, and; 5) enhancement of public squares.
Ultimately, we want to protect our heritage, make it sustainable for the future, connect with our community and make Burnley a more attractive and vibrant place to live, work and visit.
Burnley Borough Council seeks to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced architect, building surveyor or multi-disciplinary consultancy to act as Lead Consultant for the delivery of a major repair and restoration project at the Mechanics Theatre, Burnley. The appointment will build upon design and development work already undertaken and take the project through the remaining RIBA Plan of Work stages, from Stage 3 onwards, through to completion and close-out.
The appointed Consultant shall: Act as Lead Consultant, responsible for overall coordination and delivery of the design team; Undertake the role of Principal Designer in accordance with CDM Regulations; Provide all professional services required to deliver the project from RIBA Stage 3-7.
The full details of the Council's requirements and further instructions for the tender response can be found in the Tender Brief. Tenders are invited from organisations that have the necessary resources, ability, and experience to meet the Council's requirements.
It is anticipated that the contract will start on 21st September 2026.

Environmental and Site Monitoring

title: Standards Development
description:
WRAP is conducting preliminary market engagement to understand market capability and capacity for the provision of Standards Development services, ahead of an anticipated Invitation to Tender in October 2026. The intended contract is a single, non-lotted award covering the full scope described below (Phase 1 and Phase 2 are phases of delivery under one contract, not separate lots).
This engagement was conducted in two stages. An initial RFI (V1) was issued; a revised RFI (V2) was subsequently issued to refine the questions asked and obtain more detailed market insight. Both stages form part of this single preliminary market engagement exercise.
The engagement covers the following anticipated scope of services:
-Drafting, editing, reviewing, and refining standards, specifications, and technical guidance documentation.
-Conducting product screening Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs), including updating an existing eligibility screening tool and associated calculations, and producing LCAs for single-use comparator products.
-Translating technical subject matter into clear, user-accessible written content.
-Managing stakeholder engagement and consultation processes, including incorporating feedback into draft standards.
-Managing review cycles, including engagement with a Standards Development Committee, ballots, public comment periods, and periodic reviews.
-Advising on governance, version control, and document management for standards outputs.
-Producing publication-ready documentation.
The anticipated work is phased under a single contract:
-Phase 1 — expansion of an existing Refillable Product Standard (launching September 2026) to additional product categories, comprising screening LCAs, comparator LCAs, updates to the eligibility screening tool and formulas, standard and guidance document updates, and management of the Standards Development Committee and public comment process.
-Phase 2 — development of new standards within WRAP's product standards suite, in collaboration with WRAP and strategic partners, to create Circular Living standards.
The engagement sought insight into supplier experience, delivery models, relevant expertise and accreditations (e.g. UKAS, ANSI), risks and success factors, quality assurance approaches, and indicative delivery timelines and budget ranges, to inform the scope and structure of the future procurement.

title: Barton’s Point Coastal Park Catering and Educational Opportunities
description:
Barton’s Point Coastal Park
Marine Parade, Sheerness, Kent, ME12 2BX
Expressions of Interest for Catering and Educational Opportunities
Swale Borough Council is keen to build upon and widen the offer at Bartons Point Coastal Park (Google map link below)
https://maps.app.goo.gl/uLnjK882kYLDbHSc7
The site measures 31ha and is located on the Northern Coast of the Isle of Sheppey, nestled between Minster-on-Sea and Sheerness; accessible via Marine Parade, the main coastal road link between the two. Currently the site consists of the Boat House Café, toilets, car park, lake, play and picnic areas, an events field along with large areas of open space. There are two tenanted areas used for flying model aircraft and miniature gauge railway. A shared access road provides both for the coastal park and also the adjacent Sea Cadet Corps. As well as being an active leisure site, the coastal park also has extensive wildlife and biodiversity habitats and these remain important to both protect and potentially utilise as a resource.
The Council provided a new toilet block, including showers and ancillary facilities, in 2023.  These are available for the benefit of visitors to Bartons Point.  The existing drainage provision is via a cesspool. 
The Council is seeking expressions of interest (EOI) for two opportunities at Barton’s Point Coastal Park.  The Council is open to EOI’s for each of Lots 1 and 2, individually or consolidated proposals which seek to meet both requirements.  
For both opportunities, the Council is seeking experienced operators that can demonstrate not only the financial viability of any proposals but also how social value will be delivered.  Proposals also need to be sympathetic to the ecology of the site, with consideration for the environment and wildlife and the adjacent Queenborough Lines waterway, which is a scheduled ancient monument.  
Whilst acknowledging there is a seasonality to the types and level of activity on the site, the Council is keen to encourage activity throughout the year and this will be reflected in how proposals are considered.  As the site has multiple users, with other leased areas, it is also important that proposals can work alongside or with these. 
It is anticipated that the Council will continue to provide basic grounds maintenance services to the whole site. The playground and bridge also remain the council’s responsibility.   Operators on site will be responsible for general site maintenance relating to their activity, such as litter generated from their operations, signage for activities etc. 
Lot 1:  The Old Boathouse Café
The old boathouse is a block frame, timber clad building with corrugated roof of the shore of the lake with a self-contained patio area (please see map 1 below).  The property provides a good opportunity for a provider to deliver a food & beverage provision for the coastal park and a lease will be offered to the preferred bidder, when identified.  
The Council is keen that bidders should demonstrate strong community values in how the Café offer operates.  We ask that EOI’s show how the proposed operation contributes positively to how the site delivers social value; for instance by facilitating programmes, events, and activities that strengthen local connections and promote inclusive use of the Coastal Park.
The building has benefited from some refurbishment in recent years but is of basic construction.  It is the intention that the terms of occupation will require the successful bidder to maintain the building and undertake improvements required, subject to the Councils consent.
The internal part of the building will be cleared of all existing equipment and fittings ahead of occupation. Bidders are therefore advised to inspect the building and carefully consider the cost of providing catering equipment and any necessary works before submitting in their EOI.
Lot 2:  Outdoor Learning 
The Council invites proposals which bring structured inclusive outdoor learning opportunities to Bartons Point.  This may involve collaboration with local organisations, schools and community partners to create meaningful learning opportunities that support wellbeing, environmental awareness, and lifelong learning. These could be operated from the Lot 1 café building if agreement is reached or from temporary structures within the park supplied by the chosen provider, to be agreed with the Council.
The Council is open-minded as to the nature of proposed activity and any provider will be able to work with the Council’s Greenspaces Ranger, to facilitate activity.  
There is an area of grass alongside the lake which is suitable for camping during the summer season and use and management of the lake which may be of interest to Bidders, but individual operators would need to satisfy themselves that proposals would be compliant with all regulatory requirements, including planning and any H&S regulations. 
Please submit your EOI by 12pm on Monday 5th October 2026 to jayjenkins@swale.gov.uk.
Please include the following information:
•Terms of occupation being sought (the Council will be seeking a minimum of 3 years)
•Annual rent being offered to SBC
•A basic Business Plan that demonstrates that the proposal is viable and sustainable for the duration of operation. Your proposal should include details of the operation including the following:
Evidence of previous experience/operations of a similar nature
Detail of the activity and/or food and beverage offer to be provided
Proposed operating dates and times
If intention to make use of the lake then an operation management plan
Any marketing proposals
Details of any other events or activities proposed to increase community engagement and visitor numbers
Some detail as to how social value will be secured from the operation and what benefits you expect to be delivered.
Financial projections demonstrating a strong viability, showing profit & loss forecasts and any surplus in addition to a cash-flow for at least 3 years,
Details of how any planned repairs and improvements will be funded (e.g., grant funding, personal savings, temporary rent concession, etc).
Two business references
Supporting Documents
Plan 1: A historic site plan, showing the extent of the site.  This reflects both current and historic uses, with the pitch and putt and camping area.
Plan 2:  Plan showing the location of the Old Boat House Café and enclosed patio.
A copy of the Environmental Report produced for Bartons Point is available on request
Please email graemetuff@swale.gov.uk or jayjenkins@swale.gov.uk for any further information or to arrange to view the premises.

description:
Millenium Lodge is a pathfinder 28 bedded Local Authority Secure Children’s Home, it is designed around the learning taken from visits to all secure children’s homes in the UK as well as the secure estate in Norway. The home will provide care for the most traumatised, vulnerable children in our society whilst catering for children placed through the Youth Justice System and children placed on Welfare Grounds.
LCC is considering the instalment of an in-room environmental sensing system across 28 children’s rooms within the secure unit.  Any requirement would be for the provision of the system hardware, guidance and support of installation (which will be carried out by the LCC contractor responsible for the build) system configuration, guidance, training and support for staff in the use of the system, operational support and maintenance of and updates of the system.
The Council needs to establish how to balance the imperative to keep children safe with the equally important duty to preserve dignity, privacy, and relational care.  Children placed in secure settings are among the most vulnerable in the care system, and as such, any intervention, particularly one involving human monitoring, must be held to a higher ethical and practice threshold than would apply in other contexts.
The rapid uptake in the adoption of new technologies has generated a growing concern around privacy, transparency, inclusion, and confidentiality. Within inpatient and custodial settings, there has been intense scrutinization around the use of restrictive and intrusive practices, for example, camera-based monitoring systems

title: Grounds Maintenance and Gardening Servces
description:
First Garden Cities Homes Limited is an English Registered Provider of Social Housing. We were formed on 1 March 2020 through the amalgamation of Howard Cottage Housing Association and Welwyn Garden City Housing Association, two organisations with a combined history of over 170 years of providing affordable homes.
Howard Cottage HA was established in 1911 to provide affordable housing in Letchworth, the world's first Garden City, whilst the eponymous Welwyn Garden City HA was founded fifty years later for the same purpose.
Today, First Garden Cities Homes is a modern, dynamic 2400 homes housing association with an active development programme and deep roots in its communities.
Our current contract for the Grounds Maintenance and Gardening Services services expires on 31/12/2026 and there is no option to extend or renew in a manner compliant with the Procurement Act 2023. We are now starting the process of procuring a new contract to provide the services.
A GIS mapping project has already been commissioned to ensure that we have the most accurate information available about the scope and volume of the works at approximately 65 locations across North Herts and Beds. This will be completed prior to tender publication and form part of the tender pack.
We are now accepting expressions of interest for participation in a market engagement exercise ahead of publishing a tender.
The Grounds Maintenance requirement will be divided into two lots of broadly similar volume, organised by geography, to create a manageable scale of delivery for providers of different sizes.
On 3rd September the decision was taken to add a 3rd lot for the provision of planned and responsive tree maintenance services across all of our properties. The relevant CPV codes have been added to this notice.
Our homes sit within a Garden Cities context, and the appearance and condition of the grounds are central to the identity of these places and to the pride residents take in them. A consistently high quality, well presented standard of finish is therefore essential, and we do not believe this can be achieved through solely unskilled labour. We will expect at least some of the operatives attending site on every occasion to hold relevant horticultural qualifications or demonstrable equivalent experience, and we are interested in how providers structure and deploy their workforce to meet this standard reliably.
Environmental responsibility and social value matter to us. We welcome approaches that advance environmental initiatives across our sites, and we are keen to understand how SMEs can be supported to compete to further our social value aims.
We also invite innovation. We want to hear how providers would bring new methods, technology and ideas to improve quality, efficiency and sustainability.
We have recently concluded a consultation exercise with our residents to understand the levels of quality and detail they expect from the service, and the outcome of that work will inform our final specification.
Once this is complete we will contact interested parties to arrange meetings to give potential suppliers the opportunity to shape this procurement.
****************************************
NOTE: This notice has been amended in order to include the 3rd Lot for Tree Services. If you have previously registered your interest and received an acknowledgement, you do not need to do so again.

title: UK4 Notice - DDAITF/008 Computer Vision Capability - Model Arena Comp
description:
The Defence AI Model Arena is opening a new competition for suppliers developing computer vision (CV) capability relevant to UK Defence; this use case is sponsored by the Rapid AI Delivery Taskforce (Taskforce RAID). 
We are looking for suppliers who can demonstrate strong model performance against a military object detection use case and who are interested in working collaboratively with Defence to improve that capability using representative data and feedback from live exercise activity. 
The competition will use the Model Arena’s “demonstration by doing” approach: suppliers will be assessed on how their models actually perform against the use case, rather than on written proposals alone.
The use case is to develop and deploy the CV – based components for autonomous drones in the land domain, operating within an AI enabled drone swarming system.
This phase is focused on establishing an effective baseline for experimentation and iterative deployment. The intention is to evolve this capability and implement other sensing-specific AI domains and multiple layers of decision-making behaviour; any potential successful supplier would be a core component of an industry co-creation ecosystem. 
Why take part: 
-	The Model Arena gives suppliers an opportunity to demonstrate capability directly against a real Defence requirement and receive evidence-based feedback on model performance.

title: Royal Navy Museums Broadband Services
description:
All existing broadband connections to Museum sites are provided by a single supplier. The individual Museum sites are currently interlinked via an MPLS network provided by the current supplier. Each site has a Juniper SRX300 router installed which is managed by the current ISP. The Portsmouth HQ site has a Juniper SRX340. Backup connections are also present at each site for redundancy, with a separate router installed and managed by the current ISP. The backup connection at the Portsmouth HQ site terminates into a separate building. As part of the MPLS network provided by the current ISP, all sites route through a cloud firewall and have a centralised internet breakout. We are provided visibility over the cloud firewall through an online portal which allows us to view and download firewall logs and add/edit/remove inbound firewall rules for our sites as required.
Museum IT infrastructure and services are centralised at the HQ site in Portsmouth. Other sites communicate with this infrastructure to access resources over the MPLS network. Multiple VLANs are in use across all Museums sites to support differing requirements. The Museum also has a presence in Microsoft Azure and an offsite datacentre, which is hosting a full Disaster Recovery infrastructure, but these do not form part of the existing MPLS network.
The broadband connection at the Portsmouth HQ site is currently shared between 6 separate businesses onsite, each with their own public IP address(es). The Museum also has requirements to route certain services using individual public IP addresses.
The current site connections are outlined in the document.
Royal Navy Museums is evaluating different broadband options available and as part of this procurement, would like to consider two technologies that we believe can deliver the requirements of the business; MPLS and SD-WAN.
As the Museum has been operating on an MPLS network for several years, we know that this technology can deliver the requirements. SD-WAN has previously been considered but never implemented for the Museum. The Museum is now in a position to evaluate its suitability to deliver the requirements, whilst assessing potential benefits and cost savings.
This procurement has been split into two lots, representing the separate considerations for MPLS and SD-WAN. To help the Museum make an informed decision, we would like to invite suppliers to respond to both lots and pitch solutions for both MPLS and SD-WAN. This will allow the Museum to assess the benefits, operating costs and overall suitability of the two solutions to help identify which is best able to deliver the requirements over the next 3-5 years. Whilst we would encourage suppliers to respond to both lots to help inform our decision, Royal Navy Museums recognise that this may not be possible for all suppliers. Therefore, if a supplier is only able to offer a solution for one of the lots, we would still welcome their response.
It should be noted that, following evaluation, only one of the two lots will be awarded depending on the suitability of each solution for the Museum. Where possible, we would like all sites to be managed under a single contract.
The internal networking of our sites is out of scope of this procurement. Suppliers also do not need to include connectivity for the offsite datacentre in their proposal.
Pricing 
The maximum budget available for the individual lots are detailed within the individual lot requirements. Cost proposals should include any installation and equipment costs, if appropriate. As part of your submission, please indicate when billing for services would be expected to start.

title: Germany – Engineering design services – Schöpfwerk Niendorf - Ersatzneubau
description: Der NLWKN möchte die Planungsleistungen für den Ersatzneubau des Schöpfwerks Niendorf (Amt Neuhaus) mit den Losen 1 "Umweltplanung" und 2 "Ingenieurbauwerk" vergeben. Nähere Informationen entnehmen sie bitte den beiliegenden Bewerbungsbedingungen mit Anlagen sowie der Leistungsbeschreibung. Das Vergabeverfahren wird als "Verhandlungsverfahren mit Teilnahmewettbewerb" nach § 17 Vergabeverordnung (VgV) durchgeführt. Über das Vergabeportal des Landes Niedersachsen können Sie sich nun im Rahmen des Teilnahmewettbewerbs um die Teilnahme am Verhandlungsverfahren bewerben. Füllen Sie hierfür bitte die unter dem Reiter "Teilnehmerunterlagen" hochgeladenen Unterlagen zum Teilnahmewettbewerb aus und laden Sie die geforderten Unterlagen im Vergabeportal hoch. Eine Auflistung der vorzulegenden Bewerbungsunterlagen finden sie in Anlage 2 Bewerbungsbogen unter der Nummer 1.3. Das Schöpfwerk Niendorf wurde in den 1960ern in der DDR errichtet und entwässert das Einzugsgebiet der Krainke mit etwa 12.240 ha. Es schützt dadurch Siedlungsgebiete und landwirtschaftliche Flächen bei Elbehochwasser und Rückstau in die Sude oder bei Eigenhochwasser der Sude. Der am Schöpfwerk angeschlossene rechte Krainkedeich wurde im Jahr 2014 auf die Höhe des neuen Bemessungshochwassers angepasst. Die Sanierung und höhenmäßige Anpassung des linken Krainkedeiches erfolgte im Jahr 2016. Eine Anpassung an die neuen Bemessungswasserstände ist im Bereich des Schöpfwerkes noch nicht erfolgt, so dass Minderhöhen von 30 cm vorhanden sind. Sechs installierte Propellerpumpen verfügen über eine Gesamtleistung von etwa 11,7 m³/s, die Pumpen stammen aus der Zeit des Baues von 1963 und befinden sich Teils in schlechtem Zustand, zwei Pumpen wurden 2005 und 2006 erneuert. Eine Rechenreinigungsanlage ist nicht vorhanden. Daneben verfügt das Schöpfwerk über 4 Freiflutkanäle, die der regulären Entwässerung außerhalb der Hochwasserzeiten dienen, wobei diese nicht den Anforderungen an die Durchgängigkeit nach WRRL genügen. Im Jahre 2016 wurde eine Bedarfsplanung erstellt, mit dem Ergebnis eine Grundinstandsetzung vorzunehmen. Für die Planung der Grundinstandsetzung wurden seit 2021 Ingenieurplanungen der Leistungsphasen 1 bis 3 und Teilen von 4 erbracht. Im Rahmen der Planungen wurden verschiedene Bauteile des Schöpfwerkes näher untersucht: Beton, Putz, Druckrohrleitungen, Schmutzwasserkanal, etc.. Das Ergebnis der Planungen zeigte, dass annähernd sämtliche Anlagenteile des Schöpfwerkes saniert, ausgetauscht oder neu gebaut werden müssten. Aufgrund des absehbaren umfangreichen Instandsetzungsaufwands wurde 2025 im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie untersucht, ob ein Ersatzneubau des Schöpfwerks eine technisch und wirtschaftlich bessere Lösung darstellen kann als eine Sanierung des Bestandes. Der NLWKN beabsichtigt auf Grundlage der bisherigen Planungen und der Ergebnisse der Machbarkeitsstudie aus 2025 das bestehende Schöpfwerk durch einen zeitgemäßen Neubau, am Standort des bestehenden Schöpfwerks zu ersetzen. Der Schöpfwerksneubau soll die aktuellen Anforderungen beim Bemessungswasserstand, der Durchgängigkeit und dem fischfreundlichen und wirtschaftlichen Betrieb erfüllen. Zudem soll durch eine Erhöhung der Pumpenkapazität dem Klimawandel Rechnung getragen werden. Folgende Binnenwasserstände sind durch das Schöpfwerk sicherzustellen: - höchstzulässiger Binnenpeil: +7,80 mNHN - höchster Winterpeil +7,70 mNHN - höchster Sommerpeil +7,40 mNHN - tiefster Binnenpeil +7,20 mNHN Das Bemessungshochwasser liegt derzeit bei 10,60 m+NHN und die entsprechende Ausbauhöhe des Deiches unter Berücksichtigung eines Freibordes von 70 cm bei +11,30 mNHN. Die im folgenden aufgeführten Abflüsse sind durch die Pumpen des Schöpfwerkes abzuführen, sofern der Außenwasserstand über dem Binnenwasserstand liegt: - Höchster Hochwasserabfluss HHQ: 11,142 m³/s - Bemessungshochwasserabfluss: 11,30 m³/s - Bemessungshochwasserabfluss mit Berücksichtigung Klimaanpassungsfaktor: 13,715 m³/s - Sommermittelwasserabfluss SMQ: 2,076 m³/s Die Pumpen müssen auf geodätische Förderhöhen zwischen 0,00 m und 3,20 m ausgelegt werden. Diese Randbedingungen sind auch bei der Planung der Freiflut und der damit verbunden Fischaufstiegsanlage zur Sicherstellung der Binnenpeile und der Durchgängigkeit zu berücksichtigen. Das derzeitige Schöpfwerk Niendorf liegt in diversen naturschutzrechtlich geschützten Gebieten: - Biosphärenreservat "Niedersächsische Elbtalaue" (Lage des technischen Bauwerkes innerhalb des Gebietsteiles A, unmittelbar angrenzend an den streng geschützten Gebietsteil C) - FFH-Gebiet "Elbeniederung zwischen Schnackenburg und Geesthacht" - EU-Vogelschutzgebiet "Niedersächsische Mittelelbe" (Lage des technischen Bauwerkes außerhalb des EU-Vogelschutzgebietes, jedoch unmittelbar an das EU-Vogelschutzgebiet angrenzend) - Kohärenzsicherungsmaßnahme für die Fischarten Bitterling und Steinbeißer im unmittelbaren Umfeld Die entsprechenden Schutzgebietsvorschriften sind bei der Planung zu berücksichtigen.

title: Germany – Government services – Projektträgerschaft zur fachlichen und administrativen Umsetzung der Förderrichtlinie „Etablierung einer industriellen Bioökonomie durch die Weiterentwicklung und Skalierung biobasierter Verfahren sowie den Aufbau regionaler Innovationscluster“
description: Die industrielle Bioökonomie bietet enormes Potenzial für nachhaltiges Wachstum, indem sie fossile Rohstoffe durch erneuerbare biologische Ressourcen ersetzt, Klimaziele erreicht und die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit stärkt. In der Forschung und Entwicklung bioökonomischer Produkte und Verfahren ist Deutschland gut aufgestellt. Die bisherigen Fördermaßnahmen anderer Ressorts sowie der Bundesländer zeigen, dass bioökonomische Produkte und Verfahren im Labormaßstab umsetzbar sind. Es mangelt jedoch an der breiten Umsetzung bioökonomischer Produkte und Verfahren im industriellen Maßstab. Daher wurde zur Unterstützung der Transformation der Wirtschaft zu einer nachhaltigen, klimaneutralen Wirtschaftsform das Förderprogramm „Industrielle Bioökonomie“ initiiert, das mit Inkrafttreten der „Richtlinie zur Förderung der Nutzung und des Baus von Demonstrationsanlagen für die industrielle Bioökonomie“ vom 16. Dezember 2020 am 29. Dezember 2020 (BAnz AT 28.12.2020 B2) startete. Diese Förderrichtlinie wurde durch die am 27. September 2024 im Bundesgesetzblatt veröffentliche „Förderrichtlinie zur Etablierung einer industriellen Bioökonomie durch die Weiterentwicklung und Skalierung biobasierter Verfahren sowie den Aufbau regionaler Innovationscluster" (BAnz AT 27.09.2024 B1) abgelöst. Ziel des Programms ist es, das Potenzial neuer biobasierter Verfahren für die Industrie zu erschließen und nachhaltige Produkte in die breite Anwendung zu transferieren. Um die wirtschaftlichen und technischen Risiken der Entwicklung und Markteinführung zu verringern, soll durch die Förderung frühzeitig das Potenzial biobasierter Produkte und Verfahren demonstriert werden. Gefördert werden Projekte, die ein hohes Potenzial für die industrielle Anwendung, die Schaffung neuer Wertschöpfung und von neuen Arbeitsplätzen besitzen, die Marktposition der beteiligten Unternehmen stärken und einen relevanten Beitrag zur Nachhaltigkeit leisten.

title: Spain – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast
description: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.

title: Pre Market Engagement: Community Accommodation Service Tier 3 (CAS3)
description:
Community Accommodation Service Tier 3 (CAS3) is a provision funded by the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) and overseen in Manchester by the Greater Manchester Probation Service and Manchester City Council, to provide short-term accommodation and support for people who are threatened with homelessness upon their release from prison or approved premises, for up to 84 days. The CAS3 provision emphasises the prevention of homelessness and the reduction in reoffending. 
Manchester City Council is seeking to engage with existing and potential providers of support and accommodation services to understand the market's capabilities in providing short-term support and accommodation for people who have recently left custody.
It is anticipated that any future service model would adopt a trauma-informed approach, recognising the diverse experiences and support needs of people leaving custody. The proposed model is intended to provide access to accommodation alongside person-centred support to address homelessness, improve wellbeing, increase independence and support positive move-on outcomes.
The proposed service is expected to operate collaboratively with statutory and voluntary sector partners, including Probation, local authorities, Greater Manchester Police and other relevant agencies, to support effective risk assessment, risk management and information sharing.
At this stage, the Council is considering a model that may include separate accommodation and support elements. To inform this approach, the Council is seeking feedback from the market regarding capacity, deliverability and potential service design considerations.
The accommodation element could include a minimum of 66 lettable self-contained single-sex units and/or compliant single-sex shared accommodation, available for occupation by CAS3 residents for up to 84 nights per placement. The support element could involve the provision of a floating support service delivered by a dedicated team of support workers. Such support may focus on helping individuals to secure and sustain accommodation, improve stability and resilience, access appropriate services and support successful resettlement outcomes.
The information contained within this notice is for market engagement purposes only and does not constitute a commitment by Manchester City Council to undertake a procurement process or award any contract.

title: Data Management Solution for Train Service Specification Data
description:
Network Rail is developing an Access and Use Policy that will set out how Great British Railways (GBR) will make decisions regarding access to GBR infrastructure for train operations. GBR will record these decisions in a new document called the ‘Infrastructure Capacity Plan.’
Network Rail is seeking a data management solution that could enable GBR to manage the train service specification data that will inform, feed into and support the Infrastructure Capacity Plan.
GBR will require a data management solution to store and manage train service specification data, supporting the objective of establishing and maintaining a published Infrastructure Capacity Plan.
The solution will also need to hold data about proposals to amend the Infrastructure Capacity Plan, and to manage change controls and auditing of the data.
The solution should also support a clear relationship between service specification data and detailed train schedule data, enabling users to understand how proposed and approved specification changes relate to individual train schedules in the timetable and data held in other operational systems. 
For clarity, GBR will be responsible for developing and maintaining the Infrastructure Capacity Plan, including populating, editing and governing the data held within the solution. The supplier would be expected to provide the data management capability, not to own or determine the underlying train service specification decisions.
Network Rail is developing this capability to support future GBR readiness and requires suppliers to consider both immediate implementation needs and long-term operational requirements.
Please see the Request for Information document attached to the opportunity listing in Bravo for further information.
