title: Research Services for Pensions illustrations: presenting uncertainty and variability
description:
BACKGROUND
The FRC is the UK's independent regulator responsible for issuing and maintaining technical actuarial standards. It is responsible for Actuarial Standard Technical Memorandum 1 (AS TM1), which specifies the assumptions and methods used to calculate statutory illustrations of money purchase, or defined contribution, pensions.
Pension illustrations are based on assumptions about future investment returns, inflation and retirement choices. The uncertainty and variability inherent in future retirement outcomes can be challenging for defined contribution (DC) savers to understand. The FRC is interested in how this uncertainty and variability can be communicated clearly and effectively to support savers in understanding and assessing the adequacy of their pension arrangements.
PURPOSE
This research will gather evidence on how information can be presented to help DC savers understand the uncertainty and variability of their estimated pension income. It will inform the development of pension illustrations and related communications and support savers in understanding and assessing the adequacy of their pension arrangements.
The FRC is considering the information provided in the following contexts:
•	For pensions illustrations given to DC savers in early- and mid-career, there are uncertainties in the estimates of projected pension income; the further away from retirement, the greater the uncertainty. 
•	For pensions illustrations given to DC savers approaching retirement, there is uncertainty and variability in both the amount and pattern of income beyond the first point of accessing DC savings. 
The primary focus of the research will be on the presentation of pensions illustrations information. The successful contractor(s) will therefore need strong knowledge and experience of savers' behavioural responses to such information; they will also need sufficient technical knowledge of the investment, inflation, longevity and retirement timing risks inherent to pensions planning.
SCOPE
The research project will comprise three phases: 
1.	Literature review of the relevant academic and professional expert research in this area. 
2.	Solution development - drawing on phase 1, the successful contractor(s) will work closely with the FRC policy team to develop a range of potentially viable solutions for communicating DC pensions uncertainty and variability. 
Activities will include: 
•	developing alternative wording and narrative approaches; 
•	developing presentation formats and visualisations; 
•	considering how savers may interpret and respond to communications; 
•	assessing the extent to which communications may support informed decision-making. 
Outputs will include: 
•	behavioural design principles; 
•	prototype communications; 
•	visual mock-ups;  
•	supporting rationale for proposed approaches. 
3.	Empirical testing - drawing on phase 2, the FRC will select the approaches to be taken forward for empirical testing, taking account of the objectives of the research and the evidence gathered during phase 1. The successful contractor(s) will then carry out empirical testing of these approaches, allowing for a segmentation of DC savers, for example by stage of career, and any other relevant categorisation.
FEEDBACK SOUGHT
We are looking for feedback on a range of delivery approaches, including but not limited to:
SCOPE
•	Are there any additional or alternative phases or activities that are required to meet the Purpose of the project?
•	Are there relevant insights from other sectors or jurisdictions that could be adapted to improve how uncertainty and variability are communicated to DC savers?
RESEARCH METHODS
•	What approaches and methods could be used, and what issues might we encounter, in each of the following:
- Defining suitable bodies of academic and professional literature to review, and upon which to draw.
- Developing the potential solutions for communicating DC pensions uncertainty and variability; working closely with the FRC team in doing so.
- Selecting among the above potential solutions for field based empirical testing with users.
- Conducting that testing with rigour and inclusiveness, using suitable techniques and population samples.
STRUCTURE
•	What key milestones and dependencies would you envisage? What would be the best way(s) of involving the FRC team in review phases, and key decision-making?
•	How could responsibilities and interfaces between different parts of the project be managed, especially if delivered by different contractors?
TIMETABLE
•	The realistic overall duration of the project and indicative time needed for each of the three phases.
•	The lead time required for participant recruitment, research approvals, data collection, analysis and reporting, and any seasonal or market factors that could affect delivery.
ADDITIONAL COMMENTS
•	Are there any other insights that you could provide?
PRELIMINARY MARKET ENGAGEMENT PROCESS
The process comprises two parts (a)  questionnaire for your completion and (b) A virtual market engagement session.
IMPORTANT :- You must register your interest to procurement@frc.org.uk (no later than 5.00pm 14/09/2026) to receive the questionnaire / further details. 
CONDITIONS OF PARTICIPATION 
The FRC welcomes participation from potential contractors with demonstrable experience, capacity and capability relevant to the proposed services. Contractors will be required to confirm their independence (in relation to the scope of this research) and declare any actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest. Such matters may be taken into account as part of the procurement process, particularly where an entity tendering for this work is subject to direct or delegated regulation by the FRC.

title: Analysis of VECTO data for HGVs
Biological control of invasive plants 2026/27
description:
Invasive non-native plant species like Himalayan balsam (HB) and Australian swamp stonecrop (ASS) significantly reduce biodiversity by crowding out native vegetation and limiting plant and animal species diversity. ASS deoxygenates water and reduces numbers of small invertebrates, amphibians and fish. Traditional methods for the control of HB and ASS are generally ineffective. Chemical control with herbicides is the most effective but often inappropriate next to or in waterbodies or protected nature conservation sites. 
The contract includes field and lab based experiments and release of relevant biological control agents (mites and rust fungus) to manage these two plant species. Pilots and testing projects are an important part of understanding the benefits and effectiveness of biological controls and the problems these species cause.  This investment now in biological control methods and their effective implementation have the potential to provide considerable benefits in terms of reduced costs and impacts as described above in future years.

description: This service applies to a 40-unit floating support service to be delivered for families with support needs clients. 5 units are dedicated to service users living in 5 designated RSL properties in Barry and Penarth. title: Warwickshire Care Home Pathway 2 Residential Short Stay Bed Block Contracts
description:
This was a retender of WCC Care Home Pathway 2 Residential Short Stay Bed Block Contracts (OCID ocds-h6vhtk-05496e/ Ref' WAR-0053) which has been terminated.
Warwickshire County Council is seeking bids for care home block contracts for Pathway 2 Residential Short Stay Bed block contracts, commissioned for patients whose discharge from hospital is being led by Adult Social Care (currently short stay social care assessments beds and moving on beds).
Pathway 2 Residential Short Stay Beds provide short-term residential care for people who are medically optimised for discharge from hospital but are unable to return home, therefore requiring a short stay in a care home setting to support their recovery and time for assessment for future needs. People will stay in the service until their assessment and ongoing arrangements have been determined.
Moving On Beds: are for people that are medically fit for discharge and can return home but require further support and time before this can take place. People that use a MOB typically return home once environmental or social issues are resolved and have an average length of stay of 6 weeks.
D2A Short Stay Beds: are for people that are medically fit for discharge whose needs have increased since their admission to hospital meaning they are unable to return to their normal place of residence. They require assessment and time to recover to understand their future requirements, whether this is to return home or to go into long term care.
People that use a D2A Short Stay Bed have an average length of stay of 4 weeks. The Council is seeking to award approximately 52 D2A short stay beds and 8 Moving on beds across three Place areas in Warwickshire, these being North Warwickshire, Rugby and South Warwickshire.

title: SafetyNet II
description:
Provision of SafetyNET II service to support the dissemination of Maritime Safety Information (MSI) through a Recognized Mobile Satellite Service (RMSS).
In accordance with Chapters IV and V of the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) 1974, as amended, and the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS), the UK is required to promulgate MSI, including navigational and meteorological warnings and forecasts, through all approved RMSS providers. As the NAVAREA I and METAREA I Coordinator, the UK is responsible for the ensuring the provision of internationally coordinated MSI services to vessels operating within its area of responsibility. As an RMSS, the SafetyNET II service, provided by INMARSAT, forms an essential component of this capability and is required to enable the dissemination of MSI via the International Enhanced Group Call (EGC) service to vessels operating within GMDSS Sea Area A3.
This service supports the Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) to implement the UKs obligations under SOLAS.

title: Future Catering and Canteen Provision at Gwent Police Headquarters
description:
Gwent Police is undertaking a Preliminary Market Engagement exercise to inform the future provision of catering and canteen services at Gwent Police Headquarters, Cwmbran.
Prior to commencing any formal procurement process, Gwent Police wishes to engage with the market to gain an understanding of the options available for the operation, management and development of the existing canteen facilities. This engagement will help shape any future procurement strategy and service requirements.
Scope of Engagement
Gwent Police is seeking input from suppliers with experience in the provision of catering, café, restaurant, hospitality and workplace food service operations.
Suppliers are invited to review the existing facilities and provide feedback on:
- Potential operating models.
- Service delivery options.
- Opportunities for improving utilisation of the facility.
- Commercial viability considerations.
- Innovation and best practice within the sector.
- Potential investment requirements.
- Sustainability and social value opportunities.
Site Visits
Interested suppliers are invited to attend an individual site visit at Gwent Police Headquarters.
To ensure commercial confidentiality and to accommodate operational requirements, site visits will be arranged on an individual basis. Suppliers will not attend site visits jointly and no group engagement sessions will be held.
Suppliers wishing to participate should register their interest during the engagement period by contacting:
Anna Rogala
Senior Procurement Specialist
Email: anna.rogala@gwent.police.uk
and
Rachel McLaren as well as Jamie Jones
Estates Department
Email: Rachel.McLaren@gwent.police.uk / Jamie.Jones2@gwent.police.uk
Following registration, a mutually convenient date and time for the site visit will be arranged.
Suppliers should provide:
- Organisation name.
- Contact name and details.
- Names of proposed attendees.
- Any specific areas of interest they wish to discuss during the visit.
Important Information
This notice is issued solely for the purpose of preliminary market engagement and information gathering.
Participation in this exercise:
- Does not constitute a formal procurement process.
- Does not commit Gwent Police to undertake any future procurement.
- Will not provide any supplier with an advantage in any future tender process.
- Will not result in the award of any contract.
Should Gwent Police decide to proceed with a procurement exercise, this will be advertised separately in accordance with the applicable procurement regulations.
Engagement Period: 12/08/2026 to  - 10/09/2026 to be agreed
Gwent Police welcomes responses from all interested suppliers and looks forward to engaging with the market.

Through this Prior Information Notice (PIN) and accompanying Request for Information (RFI), the Council wishes to engage with contractors, to gain a better understanding of current market capacity, supply chain capability, contract structures, mobilisation requirements, and innovation opportunities associated with the delivery of large-scale housing kitchen replacement programmes.
The Council is aware of a number of national framework arrangements currently operating within the marketplace and of the various procurement routes available under the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015. At this stage, no decision has been made regarding the preferred procurement strategy or route to market. The Council may consider a range of options including existing frameworks  or a future open market procurement.
The purpose of this exercise is to gather information that will help inform the Council's future procurement strategy and delivery approach. The Council is particularly interested in obtaining feedback on market capacity.
This PIN is issued solely as a market engagement and information gathering exercise.
It does not constitute a call for competition, a commitment to procure, or a commitment to award any contract.

title: Finland – Survey services – Kyselytutkimuspalveluiden hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena oli kyselytutkimuspalveluiden hankinta. Vantaan kaupunki toteuttaa vuosittain useita eri kokoisia ja eri kohderyhmille suunnattuja asukas- ja asiakaskyselyitä. Tähän tarpeeseen kilpailutetaan palveluntarjoaja kyselyiden kehittämiseen yhteistyössä tilaajan kanssa, tilaajan sisäisiä ohjeita soveltavien kyselytutkimusten suunnitteluun ja toteuttamiseen sekä tulosten analysointiin ja raportointiin. Palveluiden kehittämisen ja kohdentamisen näkökulmasta on tärkeää saada säännöllisesti tietoa asukkaiden ja asiakkaiden palveluihin liittyvistä tarpeista ja kokemuksista. Tavoitteena on saada tietoa myös siitä, millainen heidän kokemuksensa palveluiden vaikuttavuudesta on, eli onko palvelu tuottanut heille lisäarvoa. On huomioitava, että asiakas saattaa asioida saman palvelun osalta eri kanavissa (esim. verkkopalvelu, puhelinpalvelu ja toimipiste) – tietoa tarvitaan sekä palvelujen eri kosketuspisteiltä, että koko palvelua koskien. Vantaan kaupungin eri toimialojen toteuttamat kyselytutkimukset voivat olla keskenään erityyppisiä. Tarpeet voivat vaihdella laajoilla otannoilla toteutettavasta asiakastyytyväisyyden mittaamisesta satunnaisotannalla toteutettaviin kaupunkitasoisiin kyselyihin sekä kyselyihin, joilla pyritään tavoittamaan kohdennetummin erityisesti haastavia kohderyhmiä (esim. vieraskieliset, nuoret). Hankinnan kohteena oli palvelu, joka sisältää kyselytutkimusten ja/tai mittaamisen suunnittelun, toteutuksen, tulosten analysoinnin ja raportoinnin. Hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelu voi tapauskohtaisesti kohdistua yhteen tai useampaan päätyövaiheiseen. Toisin sanoen Tilaaja voi hankkia palveluna esimerkiksi vain tiedonkeruun tai kaikki päätyövaiheet sisältävän palvelukokonaisuuden. Toimeksiannot perustuvat asiakkaan tekemään kirjalliseen tilaukseen. Tilauksessa määritellään kyselytutkimuksen- ja analyysipalveluiden mittaamisen tarve, kohderyhmä, sekä yhteyshenkilöt tilaajan puolelta. Tähän tarpeeseen kilpailutetaan kyselyn kehittämiseen, toteuttamiseen ja tulosten analysointiin ja raportointiin palvelutarjoaja. Hankinnan kohteen tarkempi kuvaus tilattavasta palvelusta oli kuvattu liitteessä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Vantaan kaupungin sopimusta voivat käyttää kaikki Vantaan kaupungin toimialat. Sopimus tehdään määräaikaiseksi kahdelle vuodelle. Tilaaja varaa oikeuden jatkaa sopimusta kahdella (2) yhden (1) vuoden optiolla.

title: Finland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Digital exhibition design, software development and production for the reopening exhibition for the National Museum of Finland.
description: The Finnish Heritage Agency, the Exhibitions and Events department of the National Museum of Finland (hereinafter the “Procurement unit”) invites suppliers to submit tenders for media design and production (hereinafter the “Service”) in this call for tenders and its attached annexes. The Service consists of programming, project management and technical delivery of an artificial iIntelligence System in the form of an interactive media software which will be used according to attached plans. The entire deliverable procurement is referred to in hereinafter as the "System". The National Museum of Finland will conduct the procurement through an open tendering procedure. The aim is for production to begin immediately after the selection of the supplier in approximately September 2026, and for delivery to the Procurement Unit to be completed no later than January 2027. The procurement documents are available in English. The Procurement unit requests a tender for: 1. Exhibition Media, AV and Interactive Elements including: - Lobby Screen - Intro to the Universe (projection) - Chatty objects - 9 interactive conversational artificial intelligence stations: - Chatty Objects Birds - Chatty Object Scarab - Chatty Object Meteorite - Chatty Object Shiva - Chatty Object Canoe - Chatty Object Turtle Seats - Chatty Object Raven Mask - Chatty Object Chilkat Blanket - Chatty Object Bad Luck Bird - Chatty Object Scarab - Projection (Hybrid element) - Agnicayana film projection solution -Exhibition wide - soundscapes including: - Anvil & hammer - Chatty Objects Birds - Audio - Egg - Chatty Object Meteorite - (hybrid element) - Chatty Object Canoe - (hybrid element) - Chatty Object Raven Mask - (hybrid element) - World tree - Conch - Universe - Overhead Screen - Universe - Chatty Universe The following items are not included within this tender: - Film content for the Agnicayana film projection - Recording of poem for the Egg Soundscape 2. Software, Services and Project Management including: - Software development and testing - Software installation and configuration - Technical and user documentation - Support and on-call services during the exhibtion run - Training for the client's staff in the operation of the delivered systems - Project management covering the entire Procurement 3. Documentation set: - Technical documentation (architecture, APIs, content formats, deployment instructions). - Operational documentation for daily use by exhibition staff. - Maintenance instructions, including restart procedures and troubleshooting steps. - Documentation required under the attached Annex 3 "03_Data and privacy requirements annex". - The tenderer shall provide sufficient documentation to enable re-installation and re-use of the System by the Procurement unit without dependency on the tenderer if the Procurement unit wants to use the System in the future after the exhibition. 4. Installation & on site deployment The tenderer shall: - Install all required system software components on site in coordination with the AV integrator contractor (procured separately) and the Procurement unit's team. - Integrate "The Universe" content into existing overhead LED screen and newly purchased hardware. - Conduct full system testing. 5. Training for museum staff The tenderer shall: - Provide training sessions for Procurement unit's staff on System operation, daily use and safety as applicable and needed for the procurement. - Provide training materials (slides, troubleshooting guides, quickstart sheets). 6. Final handover package The tenderer shall provide: - Final approved versions of all media assets. - Backup copies of the System and its configurations. - A complete inventory of all delivered software. - End of project report summarizing methods, design decisions, and technical notes. The procurements requirements are explained in more detail further on in this call for tenders and its attached annexes. The estimated value of the procurement is according to the Procurement unit 400 000 - 550 000 EUR (VAT 0%). Some of the attached annexes in the call for tenders contains confidential information. The documents are available upon request via email to hankinnat@museovirasto.fi. The tenderer shall in its request to receive the documents ensure, that it keeps the information received from the Procurement unit only to itself and uses that information for its tender according to this procurement process. The information is considered confidential even after the procurement process has ended.

title: Netherlands – Research services – Onderzoek Draadslachtoffers en Effectiviteit Hawk Eye-draadmarkeringen Verbinding Vierverlaten Ens 380 kV
description: Voor het project Verbinding Vierverlaten-Ens 380 kV (VVL-ENS380) moet er onderzoek worden uitgevoerd naar de effectiviteit van Hawk Eye (nieuwe vorm van draadmarkering, zie deze link naar artikel op TenneT website ) en actualisatie van kengetallen naar draadslachtoffers per soort. Beide zijn nodig voor de vergunningverlening voor het project, maar moeten ook TenneT-breed kunnen worden toegepast voor andere lijnenprojecten. Voor de bepaling van het aantal draadslachtoffers onder hoogspanningsverbindingen wordt momenteel gebruikgemaakt van onderzoeksgegevens uit 1987. Deze gegevens sluiten niet langer aan bij de huidige situatie en bieden onvoldoende basis om de ecologische impact van hoogspanningsinfrastructuur zorgvuldig te onderbouwen. Hierdoor ontstaat onzekerheid over de omvang van de effecten op vogelpopulaties en over de effectiviteit van eventuele mitigerende maatregelen. Het beoogde onderzoek kent daarom twee samenhangende doelstellingen. Allereerst wordt een actuele nulmeting uitgevoerd om inzicht te verkrijgen in het aantal draadslachtoffers onder en in de directe omgeving van de bestaande 220 kV-hoogspanningsverbinding tussen Vierverlaten en Ens. Vervolgens wordt de effectiviteit van mitigerende maatregelen onderzocht door deze op geselecteerde masten en geleiders toe te passen en de resultaten te monitoren. Een belangrijk onderdeel van het onderzoek betreft de beoordeling van de effectiviteit van verschillende typen vogelmarkeringen. Binnen de organisatie bestaat een voorkeur voor toepassing van de Hawk Eye-draadmarkering als mitigerende maatregel. Voor een bredere implementatie ontbreekt momenteel echter nog de wetenschappelijke onderbouwing van de effectiviteit ervan onder Nederlandse omstandigheden. Het onderzoek dient daarom de kennisbasis te leveren die nodig is om onderbouwde keuzes te maken over de inzet van deze maatregel en om de bijdrage ervan aan het verminderen van draadslachtoffers aantoonbaar te maken.

description: GET.transform, is a technical assistance program supporting national and regional partners and institutions in advancing their energy transitions. GET.transform is a component of the GET.pro (Global Energy Transformation Programme), which is a global multi-donor platform and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The three instruments of GET.pro are: - GET.invest mobilises private investments in clean energy by building a pipeline of bankable investment projects. - GET.transform supports partner governments by developing bankable frameworks for clean energy investment. - The Secretariat for Africa-EU Energy Program promotes strategic political dialogue between Africa and Europe on energy. Thematic and geographic scope: The implementation structure of GET.transform is organised along the Thematic and Geographic Approach. GET.transform offers structured advisory services on four key transformational topics: 1) Long-Term Energy Planning 2) Renewable Energy Grid Integration 3) On-Grid Regulation and Market Development 4) Off-Grid Regulation and Market Development On-Grid Regulation and Market Development measures enable power sector market reform allowing for renewable energy participation, increased investment, and promotion of private markets. Power system transformation processes should be supported by a background of technically sound energy planning, a well-functioning governance structure, policy and regulatory framework. The goal is to ensure that electricity resources, including generation, transmission, and distribution systems, are allocated efficiently. In addition, market model mechanisms can be designed and implemented to facilitate a sustainable, secure, competitive and affordable electricity system. To meet the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 target of universal access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services by 2030, decentralised renewable energy solutions such as off-grid solutions have been proven to be efficient at providing energy access to rural communities. Off-grid solutions can power over 400 million people across Africa and LAC. Off- Grid Regulation and Market Development establishes a framework for public partners to strengthen institutional capacities to accomplish their rural development mandates, as well as market incentives that promote private sector participation and finance for scaling projects. ? In addition to its core activities, GET.transform has implemented TA services to other GIZ- programs in Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as Asia and Europe. GET.transform is therefore offering activities potentially in all countries where GIZ energy portfolio is active by efficiently offering standardised solutions and scaling activities and contributing towards the concept of Vision 100 of GIZ, which serves as a guiding principle for the realignment of the GIZ portfolio for the global energy transition.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Erweiterung und Sanierung der Astrid-Lindgren-Grundschule in Waldalgesheim, Los 2 - Planungsleistungen der Technischen Ausrüstung HLS und Elektro
description: Die Verbandsgemeinde Rhein-Nahe plant die Erweiterung und Sanierung der Astrid-Lindgren-Grundschule in Waldalgesheim, um den schulischen Bedarf gemäß dem Schulentwicklungsplan Rheinland-Pfalz sicherzustellen. Die Schule besteht aus mehreren Gebäudeteilen aus den späten 1950er-Jahren. Die Gesamtnutzfläche beträgt ca. 1.930 m², der umbaute Raum beträgt ca. 8.300 m³. Ziel der Maßnahme ist es, zusätzliche Räume für den Schulbetrieb zu schaffen und bestehende Gebäudebereiche funktional und technisch zu modernisieren. Zudem soll die barrierefreie Erschließung der wesentlichen Nutzungsbereiche gewährleistet werden. Mit Abschluss der Maßnahme soll ein funktional, technisch und energetisch zeitgemäßer Grundschulstandort entstehen, der die pädagogischen Anforderungen erfüllt, zusätzliche Raumkapazitäten bereitstellt und langfristig den Vorgaben des Schulentwicklungsplans entspricht. Eine Machbarkeitsstudie (Stand: 20.11.2025) liegt vor und wird zur Verfügung gestellt. Die Inhalte sind nicht verbindlich, sondern dienen als Orientierung für die weitere Planung. Die konkrete Ausarbeitung erfolgt im Rahmen der zu beauftragenden Planungsleistungen. Erweiterung - zusätzliche Räume für Verwaltung, Betreuung, Bibliothek und Differenzierung - pädagogische Ergänzungsflächen (insbesondere MINT-Bereich) - barrierefreie Erschließung der neuen und bestehenden Bereiche - Anbindung an den Klassentrakt und die Turnhalle Umbau und Sanierung der Bestandsgebäude - Sanierung und Neuordnung der WC-Anlagen - Anpassungen an Erschließung und Fluren (Übergänge Alt-Neu) - teilweise Erneuerung der technischen Anlagen, insbesondere im Hausanschlussraum (HLS, Elektro, IT) - mögliche Umnutzung einzelner Räume (ehem. Lehrmittelraum, Hausmeisterraum etc.) Gebäudehülle / Energie - Austausch eines Teils der Fensteranlagen in Klassenräumen und Fluren - energetische Maßnahmen gemäß GEG, u. a.: o punktuelle Verbesserungen an Gebäudehülle und Bauteilanschlüssen o energetische Optimierung in Verbindung mit der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung Außenanlagen - Anpassung der Außen- und Freianlagen im unmittelbaren Baufeld - barrierefreie Wegeführung und Anbindung an die Bestandsflächen Allgemein: Die Bauausführung erfolgt im laufenden Schulbetrieb. Dabei sind insbesondere folgende Aspekte zu berücksichtigen: - Sicherheit von Schülern und Lehrkräften - Lärm- und Staubschutz - abschnittsweise Bauabläufe - temporäre Wegeführungen - Abstimmung der Arbeiten mit der Schulleitung Für die Maßnahme wird eine Förderung im Rahmen der Schulbauförderung des Landes Rheinland-Pfalz angestrebt. Energetische Einzelmaßnahmen, insbesondere der Fensteraustausch, können zusätzlich über Bundesprogramme (z. B. BAFA) gefördert werden. Die Fördervoraussetzungen werden im Zuge der weiteren Planung fortgeschrieben und mit den zuständigen Stellen abgestimmt. Die anrechenbaren Kosten werden auf Grundlage der in der Machbarkeitsstudie dargestellten Variante 3 in Höhe von 3.159.115 EUR netto angesetzt. Diese Kosten dienen ebenfalls ausschließlich als Orientierungswert für die Ausschreibung der Planungsleistungen. Die Variantenuntersuchung ist nicht bindend; die konkrete Planung wird in den weiteren Leistungsphasen gemeinsam mit den Planungsbeteiligten entwickelt und fortgeschrieben.

title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – Projektträgerschaft für das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) „Quantentechnologien und Photonik“
description: Die Hightech-Agenda Deutschland (HTAD) steht für mehr Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Wertschöpfung und Souveränität Die Quantentechnologie gehört zu den sechs Schlüsseltechnologien der HTAD. In diesem Rahmen und im Rahmen des Programms „Forschungsprogramm Quantensysteme“ fördert das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) Forschungs- und Entwicklungsaktivitäten (F&E), die gemeinsam mit Wissenschaft und Wirtschaft durchgeführt werden. Das Forschungsprogramm steht unter dem Motto „Spitzentechnologie entwickeln. Zukunft gestalten.” Es beschreibt den innovationspolitischen Rahmen für die Forschungsförderung in diesem Bereich bis 2032. Mit dem Programm fördert das BMFTR die Zukunftsthemen Photonik und Quantentechnologien erstmals unter einem gemeinsamen Dach. Denn Photonik und Quantentechnologien sind nicht nur wesentliche Innovations- und Wachstumsmotoren für den Wirtschafts- und Wissenschaftsstandort Deutschland, sondern auch für die moderne Gesellschaft. Als Schlüsseltechnologien sind sie außerdem inhaltlich eng miteinander verknüpft. Daraus ergeben sich Synergien, die das BMFTR gezielt nutzt, um beide Technologien voranzubringen. Das BMFTR finanziert im Rahmen des hier ausgeschriebenen Förderbereichs F&E-Vorhaben. Die Förderung erfolgt i.d.R. im Rahmen von Projekten sowie anhand anderer Förderinstrumente (z.B. Forschungskäufe). Grundlage dafür sind Förderbekanntmachungen, in denen zu Projektvorschlägen aufgerufen wird. in der Projektförderung anzuwendenden Bestimmungen und Verfahren sind im Einzelnen im Handbuch der Projektförderung dargestellt. Aufgabe des Auftragnehmers ist die Unterstützung des BMFTR bei der Umsetzung der genannten Programme bzw. ihrer Weiterentwicklungen. Hierzu gehört die Unterstützung bei der Weiterentwicklung bestehender Förderlinien und -maßnahmen sowie die Unterstützung bei der Entwicklung neuer Förderansätze, insbesondere solcher mit einem starken Fokus auf Transfer und Wertschöpfung. Dies ist ein fortlaufender Prozess. Der AN berät das BMFTR in der Weise, dass Anregungen und neue Rahmenbedingungen aus dem Forschungsumfeld aufgegriffen und ggf. in Vorschläge für die Weiterentwicklung der Programme umgesetzt werden. Das BMFTR und der AN stützen sich dabei auf die Ergebnisse der Beobachtung, Analysen und Bewertungen. Aus diesem Prozess resultierende Konzepte und Entwürfe für Förderbekanntmachungen werden durch das BMFTR mit Hilfe des AN erstellt. Zudem werden Unterstützungsleistungen erbracht, die das Programm-Management sowie den Komplex Bürgerbeteiligung und Kommunikation betreffen.

title: Enterprise Geospatial Licensed Maps &  Data
description:
National Grid currently procures geospatial (GIS) data independently across Business Units, driven by project specific needs. This decentralized approach has led to duplication of datasets, inconsistent coverage, variable quality, and limited reuse. A single view is required of what geospatial data is owned, licensed, open, and stored. The project supports National Grid's ambition to move to enterprise wide data reuse, stronger governance, and improved commercial outcomes; a single tool that provides a variety of datasets such as ordnance survey, natural resources, environmental etc. 
•	Objectives:
•	Establish a single, enterprise-wide procurement and governance model for all geospatial (GIS) data across NG Group, UK.
•	Replace fragmented, project-led data purchasing with standardized, centrally managed access.
•	Eliminate duplication, inconsistent coverage, and limited reuse caused by historic Business Unit-led procurement.
•	Improve visibility, control, and availability of both licensed/premium and open geospatial datasets.
•	Enable cost reduction and greater value through enterprise-wide reuse and optimized licensing.
•	Successful supplier will  supply, license, and support core geospatial datasets and 
•	Enable access to both premium and open datasets.
The maps and data should be provided through electronic means, via a suitable software platform.

title: Wormwood Scrubs Masterplan Biodiversity & Improvement Works
description:
London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham Council (the "Council") invited tenders seeking a supplier who is suitably qualified and experienced in landscaping and the creation and management of ecologically sensitive habitats.
Wormwood Scrubs is an open space located at the northern end of the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham. It is the largest open space in the Borough, at around 80 ha (200 acres), and is one of the largest areas of common land in London.
The work is to implement the proposals in the AEM (Alternative Ecological Mitigation) Masterplan for Wormwood Scrubs open space. The overall objective of the AEM Masterplan is to improve and enhance biodiversity on the Scrubs and at the same time improve drainage across the site to better manage surface water and improve access.
The work is split into two phases:
Capital works - this phase of work should be completed in 6-8 months and will include the creation of a SUDs (Sustainable Urban Drainage scheme) made up of a series of scrapes and swales to the south of the site and the northwest corner of the site. Retention ponds will be created in the existing wet woodlands in the southeast of the site. Tree planting will take place at various locations and existing vegetation will be improved along with the creation of meadows and grasslands. Hibernacula's will be created and bird and bat boxes installed.
Maintenance and Management Plan (MMP) - Phase 2 of the work will be a 10 year Management and Maintenance Plan (MMP) which will include the management of the features implemented as part of the Phase 1 Capital Works including the SUDs scheme and meadows and will also involve the management of the existing woodland, scrubland and meadows that have not previously been regularly managed and are in need of ongoing management to improve conditions for wildlife and increase biodiversity. For example, selective thinning in woodland areas will allow more light in to allow a greater variety of woodland plants to grow in the understorey.
buyer: London Borough of Hammersmith and Fuham (LBHF)

title: Regenerative Schools Pilot - Academic Assurance Partner
description:
The Department for Education and the Education Estates Strategy
The Department for Education (DfE) is the UK government’s Department responsible for the schools in England. As part of this role, we oversee the safety, condition, and long‑term sustainability of the education estate. This includes ensuring that current and future school buildings are provided with safe, high‑quality environments where children can learn and thrive.
On 11th February 2026 the Department published its 10-year plan for the Education Estate, the Education Estates Strategy, A decade of national renewal. The Regenerative Schools Pilot was outlined within the strategy:
“Testing new solutions, technologies and construction methods – we will continue to look at how we can go further for our future design specifications as part of a research and development programme supported by £33 million to 2029-30. This will prioritise regenerative approaches looking at a wide range of outcomes from energy storage to bio-based construction materials, such as timber and working closely with Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) on the Timber in Construction Road Map.”
The Regenerative Schools Pilot, Introduction:
The Department for Education intends to research, develop, and deliver a series of single and dual classroom, ultra‑low‑carbon school buildings under the Regenerative Schools Programme. This will be accompanied by a package of landscaping and retrofit interventions which will support biodiversity, passive heat‑reduction (such as tree shading), fabric upgrades to existing buildings (cladding and windows), sustainable drainage systems and the creation of outdoor learning spaces. This programme will also produce case studies, guidance and resources for schools.
This notice outlines the Department's intent to award a contract to the successful supplier for the Academic Assurance Partner role. As communicated in prior notices, we intend to publish a separate notice for the Innovation Lead role shortly. These organisations will produce feasibility studies, research the building materials and techniques required to produce ultra‑low‑carbon school buildings and develop 6 standard designs. Then, in 2027, the Department plans to appoint a contractor to deliver the works, using the materials and methods specified by the Innovation Lead and Academic Assurance Partner. Separate market engagement and tender events will be held for the construction contractor’s appointment.
The Academic Assurance Partner
The Academic Assurance Partner will complement the Innovation Lead’s technical work by focusing on the social, educational, and behavioural dimensions of the programme. You will use your research capabilities and academic expertise related to ultra-low-carbon materials to advise the Department and Innovation Lead. Your role will begin with the creation of a school‑ready engagement toolkit and the delivery of inclusive engagement across the participating regions. This will involve working directly with pupils, staff, governors, parents, and other stakeholders to build a picture of community needs, aspirations, and challenges, ensuring these insights inform both retrofit strategies and the design of the new learning spaces. You will translate these findings into clear design inputs so that lived experience directly shapes feasibility work and guidance documents. 
As projects move into delivery and buildings begin to be used, the Academic Assurance Partner will lead a structured programme of post‑occupancy evaluation, bringing together qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand how the new and refurbished environments perform in practice. Your work will consider internal and external environmental factors (such as air quality, temperature, and acoustics), wellbeing, nature‑connectedness, and educational impact, helping the Department understand what works and where further development may be required. The insights you produce will be shared through publications, reports, and case studies, contributing to future policy and guidance for the wider education estate. 
Working with the Innovation Lead
The Innovation Lead and Academic Assurance Partner are intended to operate in parallel, each with a distinct focus but with close coordination throughout. The Innovation Lead will ensure technical feasibility, safety, and low‑carbon performance, while the Academic Assurance Partner will ensure that the programme responds to the needs and experiences of the schools and communities involved. Together you will provide the Department with the combined academic, social, and technical expertise required to develop a set of replicable, ultra‑low‑carbon solutions that are grounded in real‑world school environments and capable of informing future national delivery.
For the avoidance of doubt, the publication of this notice triggers the mandatory 8 day standstill period and this period will end at 17:00 on 08/09/2026.

title: All Age Carers Hub
description:
Cheshire East Council is recommissioning its support offer for carers across the borough. The service will support adult age carers who provide unpaid care and support to family members, friends and neighbours living within Cheshire East.
The Council is currently reviewing its future operating model for supporting unpaid carers and the role of commissioned provision within the wider carers support system. This review has involved extensive engagement and co-production with carers, Adult Social Care, health services, voluntary and community sector organisations, and other key stakeholders. The final scope of the procurement, including the respective roles of commissioned provision, Council-delivered functions and partnership arrangements, will be confirmed following market engagement and completion of the service design process.
Under the Care Act 2014, the Local Authority has a statutory responsibility to identify, assess need and support carers. The Council recognises the vital contribution unpaid carers make to sustaining families, communities, health services and social care and is committed to ensuring carers are recognised, valued and supported as equal partners in care.
The recommissioned service will move beyond a traditional advice and support model, delivering a strengths-based, preventative and outcomes-focused approach that enables carers to maintain their health, wellbeing, independence and quality of life. The service will play a key role in identifying carers, promoting wellbeing and reducing the risk of deterioration in carer wellbeing, reducing loneliness and social isolation, and ensuring carers can access the right support at the right time.

•	Early identification, outreach and engagement with carers.
•	Wellbeing, resilience and preventative interventions, including training, skills development and support to access local community-based provision.
•	Interventions that enable carers to maintain interests, relationships and opportunities beyond their caring role. 
•	Training opportunities to upskill carers
•	Borough-wide opportunities for peer support, mutual aid and community connection, delivered through a range of accessible channels. 
•	Digital and innovative approaches to engaging and supporting carers.
•	Co-production activity and mechanisms that enable carers to shape and influence local service design and delivery.  
•	Developing a strong partnership across VCSE, social care and health services.
•	Targeted support for carers experiencing inequalities or additional barriers to accessing support.
The contract is anticipated to commence in July 2027 and is expected to run for an initial period of five years, with options to extend

title: Supply & Maintenance of Platelet Agitator and Incubator equipment
description:
Background 
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is responsible for collecting, processing, testing and supplying blood components to hospitals across England. As part of this role, NHSBT operates a network of blood centres, manufacturing facilities and hospitals services departments that require the safe and compliant storage of platelet components.
Platelets must be stored under controlled conditions and maintained under continuous agitation to ensure product quality, safety and compliance with applicable regulatory and quality requirements (JPAC/BSQR). NHSBT currently utilises Helmer platelet agitators and incubators across its sites to support these activities. Helmer models in operation include: PC4200, PC1200, PC900, PC2200 
NHSBT is undertaking a Preliminary Market Engagement exercise to gain a better understanding of the current market, available technologies, product developments and service models relating to platelet agitators and incubators. The information gathered will help inform the development of the technical specification, procurement strategy and future requirements.
Requirements
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is seeking to engage with the market in advance of a potential future procurement for the supply, installation and maintenance of platelet agitator and incubator equipment used for the storage of platelet components within NHSBT facilities.
The engagement process seeks to better understand the following (but is not limited to):
• Current products and technologies available within the market.
• Equipment platelet storage capacity
• Configuration options (connectivity to environmental monitoring systems).
• Regulatory compliance
• Validation support.
• Maintenance and servicing arrangements.
• Sustainability and energy efficiency considerations
• Supply chain resilience and lead times.
NHSBT anticipates that the future requirement may include a range of platelet storage solutions across multiple locations and operational settings. These include:
• Large floor-standing platelet incubator and agitator systems.
• Smaller benchtop platelet agitators and incubators.
• Solutions capable of accommodating both agitating and non-agitating platelet storage within the same unit or integrated system.
NHSBT requires platelet storage solutions capable of maintaining platelet components in accordance with applicable regulatory and quality requirements, including controlled storage at 20°C to 24°C and continuous agitation where required.
NHSBT is seeking feedback from suppliers regarding the availability of such solutions, associated configurations, capacity ranges and any alternative approaches that may offer operational, technical or commercial benefits.
Proposed Lot Structure
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is considering a procurement comprising three separate lots. The final lot structure and scope will be informed by the outcome of this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise.
Lot 1: Supply and Maintenance of Platelet Incubators and Agitators
This lot will include the supply, installation, commissioning, validation support, maintenance and repair of:
• Large floor-standing platelet incubator and agitator systems.
• Smaller benchtop platelet agitators and incubators.
• Associated accessories, spare parts and consumables where applicable.
• User training and technical support services.
Lot 2: Supply and Maintenance of Dual-Function Platelet Storage Solutions
NHSBT are considering a separate lot for this requirement due to limited understanding of the availability of this technology in the market. This lot will include the supply, installation, commissioning, validation support, maintenance and repair of solutions capable of accommodating both agitating and non-agitating platelet storage within the same unit or integrated system.
NHSBT is interested in understanding the range of solutions available within the market, including capacity options, operational benefits, monitoring capabilities and maintenance requirements.
Lot 3: Maintenance of Existing Platelet Incubators and Agitators
This lot will include maintenance and support services for around 170 platelet incubators and agitators currently operated by NHSBT, including:
• Preventative maintenance
• Calibration to two points as a minimum
• Equipment servicing and inspection.
• Breakdown and emergency repair services.
• Supply of replacement parts.
• Technical support

title: RFQ - Investigating the hygrothermal and dynamic thermal properties of English traditional solid wall construction for resilience in a changing climate  - literature review and gap analysis (UID 332)
description:
This project forms part of Historic England’s Technical Guidance Review, which has the overarching aim to ensure our guidance is up to date, reflective of current understanding and best practice for historic building climate change mitigation and adaptation. To this end, Historic England has identified that robust, evidence-based solutions for climate change mitigation in English buildings of traditional construction are needed that demonstrably balance savings in energy and carbon (operational and embodied) across heating and cooling seasons, whilst supporting the climate resilience of fabric and their occupants through the anticipated changes to our climate.
As a first step, a literature review and gap analysis is required to determine the current level of understanding of the topic and help steer the development of further research. It will focus on the following research questions: 
1.	How do the hygrothermal and dynamic thermal properties of English traditional solid wall construction affect whole-building overheating risk and passive cooling performance, and how are these affected by insulation retrofit and future climate scenarios? 
2.	How do these wall-related effects interact with other whole-building factors, including orientation, solar gain, ventilation, occupancy/use, moisture condition, heating/cooling patterns and other mitigation and adaptation measures?
The findings will be presented as an article for publication in a peer-reviewed journal (journal to be agreed) and for publication in Historic England’s Research Report Series format. They will be disseminated through Historic England’s Technical Tuesday webinar series.

title: Young People’s Supported and Semi-Independent Accommodation and Support Services
description:
The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham has a statutory duty to ensure that there is sufficient, good quality and safe provision for the young people in its care in accordance with Section 22G of the Children Act 1989. The Council is advertising to seek tenders from suitably experienced and qualified organisations to join our new open framework of providers for the provision of Young People’s Supported and Semi-Independent Accommodation and Support Services, for our looked-after young people aged 16 and older (up to a maximum age of 25).  
The aim of the Open Framework is to establish a range of placement provisions that best meet the individual needs of our looked-after young people, acknowledging that these needs are often ongoing. The Open Framework will be composed of four (4) lots and will seek providers as follows:    
Providers of supported accommodation for those aged 16-17 years, under the new supported accommodation regulations (OFSTED), that do not provide semi-independent accommodation;    
Providers of semi-independent accommodation for those over 18 who have not, or cannot, move into independent accommodation, that do not provide supported accommodation;   
Providers of both supported accommodation and semi-independent accommodation types in order to ensure consistency and continuity of care and relationships for a Young Person; and    
Providers of both supported accommodation (OFSTED regulations) and semi-independent accommodation types in order to ensure consistency and continuity of care and relationships for Young People that are parents.    
The new framework is expected to run for a period of eight (8) years commencing on Monday 20th April 2026. Entry on to the framework will be based on providers meeting the necessary quality standards. Contracts will be awarded based on the individual needs of our young people. This will be an Open Framework, as defined under the new Procurement Act 2023, which provides for the award of successive frameworks on substantially the same terms at regular periods.  
The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Commissioning team is planning on reopening the Framework within two years of the original day of award and then in two-yearly cycles, up to the eighth year of the original day of award, in line with the new regulations.  
To achieve our vision, we will need to work with contractors who can demonstrate specific experience for this specialist area of work. Organisations who wish to express an interest must:  
Have within the Organisation (or anyone within the proposed staffing), at least two years’ experience in providing support to vulnerable children and young people accommodated by children’s social care 
Be registered with Ofsted to deliver under: The Supported Accommodation (England) Regulations 2023 (the Regulations) and Quality Standards, if they are planning to deliver supported accommodation for those aged 16-17 years 
Employ staff (keyworkers) who have a minimum of a QCF/NVQ Level 3 in Health and Social Care (Children & Young People) or equivalent 
Employ a Contract Manager/Manager (who will supervise all keyworkers) with a minimum QCF/NVQ Level 4 in Health and Social Care or equivalent  
The Framework Contracts will have no minimum value, nor will any commitment to expenditure by the Council be stipulated within the contract itself. Expenditure will only be incurred when placements are made. The estimated value of the eight-year framework will be approximately £50 million based on the Council’s current spend; however, the Council has no obligation to spend through the framework.
buyer: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham

title: Impact of HPV self-testing- insights & good practice in FGM, sexual abuse&trauma
description:
With the planned roll-out of HPV self-testing, we may see improvements in uptake rates, however there will still be a need for cervical screening for those where self-testing indicates high risk HPV, meaning that there will be an ongoing need to provide culturally competent and trauma informed interventions in cervical screening services.
Previous insights suggest that although there are a small number of specialist services concentrated in major cities in England which provide a range of women’s health services for women who have experienced FGM, including cervical screening, many women are unaware of these or are unable to access them.
This project aims to ensure that there is sufficient access to culturally sensitive trauma informed staff able to respond to this need. This will support the objectives of the NHS England » Cervical cancer elimination by 2040 – plan for England.
The project will consist of 5 phases:
1. Explore accessibility to HPV self-testing and cervical screening for victims of sexual abuse/trauma/FGM (working with stakeholders).
2. Scope interventions deployed in other countries to ensure self-testing and screening is accessible for these groups.
Comprehensive review of published material detailing effective pathways into and subsequent to HPV self-testing, including how those with positive high risk HPV tests are supported in cervical screening.
3. Scope existing educational and informational resources and training in England for healthcare practitioners.
Scope what existing educational and informational resources and training has been developed/evaluated to equip healthcare practitioners in supporting women and people with a cervix who have experienced FGM and other types of trauma to engage in HPV self-testing and cervical screening
4. Engage with practitioners to assess current competence and confidence.
Engage with practitioners including CS sample takers to assess extent to which they are trained in TIC and how confident they are in their skills and competence in providing TIC, including those in GP and specialist settings. Identify knowledge and training gaps and co-produce any assets required to address identified gaps, e.g. development of content/e-learning /video to include in the NHS Cervical Screening Sample Taker Update Training - (working with relevant sexual abuse/trauma charities).
5. Trial assets and training and evaluate impact with a small group of practitioners
Trial a selected set of assets and training with a small group of practitioners supported by training and evaluate the impact on their reported competence and confidence.

title: UEFA EURO 2028 Tournament Impact Evaluation​
description:
In October 2023, the UK and Ireland successfully secured the rights to host UEFA EURO 2028. The tournament will take place in England, Scotland, Wales and Republic of Ireland over 31 days in June and July, and will attract the attention of the sporting and major event communities, the media, and the public at large across the UK & Ireland, Europe and the World. A projected 1 million international visitors will visit the UK & Ireland during the tournament. Delivery Partners are committed to evaluating the impacts of the tournament to evidence the value of their investment and the benefits which will accrue throughout the tournament hosting period.
​Delivery Partners are now seeking to appoint a supplier who will be responsible for evaluating the benefits and impacts of the tournament from 2026-2030. The Successful Tenderer will have the capability to effectively deliver on a diverse range of multi-disciplinary analysis requirements across both the UK and Ireland as part of a single, cross-nation, multi-jurisdictional evaluation of the benefits and impacts of the tournament. There will be 6 key outputs from the work:
​1) An Evaluation Plan
​2) An assessment of the viability of extending the Evaluation Programme to 2033
​3) A pre-tournament report
​4) A post-tournament flash report
​5) A post-tournament full report
​6) A post-tournament legacy report​

title: The Provision of a Design, De-modification & Installation Service for Communication Equipment in Police Rotary and Fixed Wing Aircraft
description:
This tender is being published by BlueLight Commercial on behalf of the National Police Air Service (NPAS) who are seeking to award contracts for 'the Provision of a Design, De-modification and Installation Service for Communication Equipment in Police Rotary and Fixed Wing Aircraft.' 
Scope:
The Authority requires a UK Part 21 approved modification that provisions the installation of Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) namely a new Aircraft Communication System (ACS) as part of the Emergency Services Mobile Communication Programme (ESMCP). Thereafter, the Authority requires the execution of an approved installation and associated testing of the ACS along with a Certificate of Release to Service (CRS).
For the Authority to successfully transition onto the new Emergency Services Network (ESN), the Authority requires the de-modification (removal) of existing TETRA radio equipment and the installation of compatible replacement new hardware that initially supports a new TETRA solution and pre-positions for the future ESN LTE capability via dual wiring looms and antennae. This will provide the Initial Operating Capability (IOC) to ensure continued operational capability during the ESMCP transitional period and compliance with the future ESN requirements.
The scope includes the removal of the existing TETRA, and where applicable, marine band VHF radio suite, the design for the installation of the replacement solution; and the subsequent installation of IOC and marine band VHF hardware across the Authority’s aircraft fleet. 
Total aircraft to be modified:
Rotary Wing =11
Fixed Wing = 4
This contract is being tendered on behalf of the West Yorkshire Combined Authority (WYCA) who are the contracting authority for NPAS. NPAS is not a separate, incorporated entity and therefore WYCA currently enters into contractual arrangements on behalf of NPAS.
The Chief Constable of West Yorkshire is responsible for the operational delivery of NPAS. BlueLight Commercial provides commercial support services to police forces and blue light organisations across England and Wales and has been appointed by WYCA to administer the Procurement.
The requirement will be tendered as two separate lots as follows;
• Lot 1: Rotary Wing  
• Lot 2: Fixed Wing
Bidders may bid for either one or both lots.
BlueLight Commercial reserves the right to refine the award criteria at Stage 3 of this procurement process, in accordance with Section 24 of the Procurement Act 2023. The final award criteria and associated weightings will be published prior to the invitation of final tenders at Stage 3 of the procurement. d. changing weightings within the pre-existing range as indicated in the table above.

title: Coaching Training
description:
The successful service provider will be required to provide the Council with coaching services that include, but are not limited to, the following requirements:
Potential suppliers should provide a programme of coaching qualifications, with the intention of training staff to become practicing and certified workplace coaches within the council. These qualifications should be tiered to represent beginner, intermediate, and advanced candidates.
Identified staff are expected to be trained in two groups, across two years. The first group is expected to start training early 2026 and the second will begin training in January 2027. The councils reserve the right to adjust the number of candidates within the second group or to cancel this group, should the need arise. Each group is expected to need the beginner, intermediate, and advanced coaching offers and may not include the same number of staff for each level of the course.
Identified staff will be expected to attend one course each only and the councils have undertaken an initial evaluation process to assess suitability.
The courses are not expected to specifically cover mentoring; the focus is coaching.
Suppliers are expected to assess and support staff throughout their training, including identifying potential issues and learning needs support, and resolving these.
In the event that the programme requires coachees for the purpose of the programme, the councils will identify and source coachees.
Where course specifications are listed with a recognised qualification, bidders should demonstrate that their qualification is of a similar quality and level.
Potential innovative aspects of course implementation and delivery will be welcomed where there is a genuine benefit to students.

title: BF1085 Fuel Monitoring System
description:
Bedfordshire Fire and Rescue Authority is inviting suitable qualified organisations to bid for a modern, fit for purpose self-managed cloud-based Fuel Monitoring System. 
Bedfordshire Fire and Rescue Authority operate six (6) sites with bunkered diesel vehicle fuel stations, three of which contain dual tanks. The sites are located within the county of Bedfordshire: Fire Headquarters Kempston (2 tanks / 1 dispenser), Bedford Fire Station (2 tanks / 2 dispensers), Stopsley Fire Station (1 tank / 1 dispenser), Luton Fire Station (2 tanks / 2 dispensers), Leighton Buzzard Fire Station (1 tank / 1 dispenser) and Dunstable Fire Station (1 tank / 1 dispenser). 
The objectives are to:
•	Provide real-time monitoring of six bunkered fuel site and eight fuel dispensers 
•	Enable full auditability of fuel usage
•	Reduce human error in recording and reporting as a result of manual processes 
•	Provide accessible management information across the organisation
•	Support automated fuel reordering and monitoring
•	Enable all BFRS vehicles to access bunkered fuel with appropriate recording mechanisms 
•	Improve overall fleet fuel management, including non-bunkered fuel users
The high level requirements include but are not limited to:- 
•	Installation of Electronic Fuel Capacity Gauges and an Electronic Fuel Monitoring System at each fuelling station.
•	The information gathered at each fuelling station will be cloud based and be accessed from PCs at BFRA Headquarters Workshops for analysis.
•	The Fuel Monitoring System must provide relevant monitoring information.
•	The Fuel Monitoring should, where technically possible, be compatible with the existing High/Low level alarms.
•	The system must record the mileage of the vehicle as well as the vehicle registration, time of refuelling, and quantity of fuel dispensed into the vehicle.

title: Hounslow Community Services
description:
This is the core NHS contract for Hounslow Community Services, underpinning the delivery of integrated community-based care across the London Borough of Hounslow. Hounslow Community Services comprise a large-scale integrated community
services model incorporating;
• Adult community health services;
• Children's community health services;
• Multidisciplinary neighbourhood teams;
• Long-term condition and specialist pathways;
• Community nursing and therapy services;
• Musculoskeletal (MSK) services;
• Wheelchair services;
• Diabetes services;
• Urgent community response services;
• Rehabilitation services;
• Care home support services;
• Integration with primary care;
• Integration with local authority services;
• Interfaces with acute and mental health services; and
• Neighbourhood-based models of care.

These services are delivered through multidisciplinary neighbourhood teams and specialist pathways operating across community settings, primary care, schools, care homes and patients' homes.

Collectively, these services support the delivery of neighbourhood health, prevention, early intervention, proactive management of long-term conditions and coordinated multidisciplinary care, enabling residents to receive care closer to home and reducing reliance on hospital-based services.

The contract operates through established clinical pathways, workforce infrastructure, digital systems, governance arrangements and partnerships across the Hounslow health and care system. It is a key enabler of integration across community, primary care, local authority, acute and mental health services, supporting seamless patient pathways, population health
management and the strategic objectives of the Hounslow Borough Based Partnership and the wider Integrated Care System.

The ICB's strategic intentions remain focused on strengthening
neighbourhood-based delivery models, supporting integrated care and continuing the shift of care from hospital settings into community settings. The continuing requirement is therefore not simply for the delivery of individual community services, but for the operation of a fully integrated borough-wide
community services model that brings together multiple service lines, workforce groups, delivery settings and system partners.

title: Architect / Engineers and Cost Consultant Team - Lymington Sea Water Baths
description:
Lymington and Pennington Town Council is seeking to appoint one integrated Architect, Engineering and Cost Consultant Team to deliver Phase 1 of the Lymington Sea Water Baths Restoration Project.
The project is supported by the National Lottery Heritage Fund and will develop the technical, design and cost evidence needed to inform the future restoration and sustainable operation of the Baths.
The Lymington Sea Water Baths are a nationally significant historic coastal leisure facility. The site is affected by substantial structural deterioration, marine saltwater exposure, historic settlement, potentially unstable tidal deposits, ageing infrastructure, accessibility limitations and outdated facilities.
The appointed team will be responsible for delivering and coordinating the architectural, structural engineering, geotechnical engineering, mechanical and electrical engineering, marine and environmental consultancy, quantity surveying and technical survey services required to complete the Phase 1 feasibility work and develop coordinated proposals to RIBA Stage 2.
The Council requires a single integrated consultant team with clear lead responsibility for the coordination, management and quality assurance of all design, engineering, survey and cost information produced through the commission.
The Phase 1 services will include:
Mobilisation and project coordination
• Participate in an inception workshop with the Council, Project Manager and other appointed consultants.
• Confirm the design and technical programme, survey schedule, responsibilities, communication arrangements and information requirements.
• Review and refine the scope of services, project risks, site constraints, dependencies and opportunities.
• Coordinate the architectural, engineering, cost and technical survey workstreams.
• Attend project meetings and provide progress information to the Council and Project Manager.
Technical surveys and investigations
The appointed team will lead, commission, manage or directly undertake the technical surveys and investigations required to support RIBA Stage 2.
These are expected to include:
• Structural condition surveys.
• Concrete sampling, testing and condition mapping.
• Structural integrity assessment.
• Geotechnical investigations, including boreholes, trial pits or other appropriate investigations.
• Assessment of settlement, groundwater and hydrogeological conditions.
• Review of existing pumping, circulation and water-management systems.
• Mechanical and electrical services assessment.
• Drainage, outfall and marine water-management assessment.
• Electrical infrastructure and lighting assessment.
• Environmental, climate resilience and sustainability assessments.
• Assessment of opportunities for low-energy systems and sustainable materials.
The team will be responsible for determining the precise investigations required, coordinating access and sequencing, managing survey information and ensuring that the results are incorporated into the design proposals.
The required outputs will include technical survey reports, drawings, testing results, data summaries, risk information and recommendations informing the RIBA Stage 0 to 2 process.
RIBA Stage 0 and Stage 1
The appointed team will undertake the appraisal, briefing and initial design work required to establish a clear and deliverable basis for the project.
This will include:
• Site appraisal and constraints mapping.
• Review of existing infrastructure, buildings, structures, heritage features and the marine setting.
• Identification of technical, operational, access, environmental and conservation constraints.
• Development of the project brief in collaboration with the Council and other consultants.
• Initial accessibility and inclusion strategy.
• Sustainability and climate resilience principles.
• Feasibility layouts and concept proposals.
• Integration of relevant findings from heritage research, business analysis and community engagement.
RIBA Stage 2 design development
The team will prepare coordinated RIBA Stage 2 proposals for the full Baths site.
The work will include:
• Developed architectural layouts.
• General arrangement drawings, sections and elevations.
• Structural design strategy.
• Geotechnical design advice.
• Mechanical and electrical outline strategies.
• Pumping, circulation, drainage and water-management proposals.
• Accessibility and inclusive design proposals.
• Landscape and public realm strategy.
• Conservation-led proposals informed by the Heritage Consultant's work.
• Visualisations and illustrative materials.
• Sustainability and climate resilience proposals.
• Programme and construction phasing strategy.
• Recommendations for materials suitable for a marine and heritage environment.
The design must respond to the site's heritage significance, ground conditions, structural deterioration, marine exposure, operational requirements, accessibility objectives and long-term maintenance needs.
Cost consultancy
The Quantity Surveyor will prepare and maintain cost information throughout the Phase 1 design process.
The services will include:
• Preparation of the RIBA Stage 2 cost plan.
• Advice on affordability and value for money.
• Construction phasing cost analysis.
• Design risk and cost risk assessment.
• Preparation and maintenance of a cost risk register.
• Lifecycle and maintenance cost projections.
• Cost advice to support the Business Options Appraisal.
• Identification of assumptions, exclusions, inflation allowances and contingencies.
The Quantity Surveyor will work closely with the design team, Project Manager and business planning specialists to ensure that capital and lifecycle costs are properly reflected in the wider feasibility evidence.
Consultation and engagement support
The team will support the appointed Consultation and Engagement Consultant by:
• Preparing accessible drawings, visualisations and explanatory materials.
• Attending relevant public exhibitions, workshops or design feedback sessions.
• Explaining the technical and design proposals to non-specialist audiences.
• Reviewing and responding to consultation findings.
• Demonstrating how relevant engagement feedback has informed the final RIBA Stage 2 proposals.
Collaboration with the wider consultant team
The appointed team will be expected to collaborate with the Council, Project Manager, Heritage Consultant, Consultation and Engagement Consultant, business planning specialists and other project advisers.
The team must ensure that design decisions are informed by:
• Heritage significance and conservation principles.
• Technical survey findings.
• Community and stakeholder engagement.
• Operational and business planning requirements.
• Capital and lifecycle costs.
• Accessibility and inclusion.
• Climate resilience and environmental sustainability.
Final Phase 1 outputs
The required final outputs will include:
Coordinated RIBA Stage 2 Design Report.
General arrangement drawings, sections and elevations.
Architectural, structural, geotechnical, mechanical and electrical design narratives.
Full technical survey and investigation reports.
Developed accessibility and inclusive design narrative.
Sustainability and climate resilience statement.
Landscape and public realm proposals.
RIBA Stage 2 cost plan.
Capital cost, lifecycle cost and construction phasing information.
Design, technical and cost risk registers.
Visualisations and materials for consultation and funding purposes.
Programme and recommendations for subsequent project stages.
Contributions required for National Lottery Heritage Fund reporting, evaluation and future funding evidence.
All documents must be coordinated, clearly presented, accessible and suitable for use by the Council, the National Lottery Heritage Fund and other project stakeholders.
The Phase 1 contract value is up to £120,000 excluding VAT. The fee must include the professional services of the architect, structural engineer, geotechnical engineer, mechanical and electrical engineer, marine or environmental specialists, Quantity Surveyor, all required technical surveys and testing, and preparation of the required drawings, reports and RIBA Stage 2 deliverables.
