Brasil

Programa Progestão Alagoas

Empréstimo nº 9435-BR 

Número de Referência: ED3 BR-SEDUC/AL-555632-CS-INDV

O Estado de Alagoas recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear parcialmente o Programa Progestão Alagoas, e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos para serviços de consultoria.

Os recursos têm por objetivo a execução do Programa Progestão, o qual visa promover a melhoria contínua da gestão fiscal, orçamentária e patrimonial da administração pública estadual por meio de ações que findem na redução e na racionalização do gasto público com resultados perenes, de modo a contribuir para a sustentabilidade fiscal de Alagoas.

Nesse sentido, a Secretaria de Estado da Educação se propõe a utilizar parte dos recursos do programa para a seleção de Consultor Individual para apoiar o Governo do Estado de Alagoas na avaliação de impacto da operacionalização dos programas de alimentação escolar da Secretaria de Estado da Educação – SEDUC no âmbito do Programa Progestão Alagoas

Com o objetivo de contratar esse serviço, a  SEDUC convida profissionais a manifestarem seu interesse na prestação dos serviços como consultor individual.

Os profissionais interessados deverão proporcionar informações que indiquem que estão qualificados para prestar os serviços, mediante a apresentação de currículo, devendo constar nome completo, CPF, endereço completo, telefone, e-mail, histórico acadêmico, experiências comprovadas nas competências abaixo.

Obs.: A presente Manifestação de Interesse deverá conter todos os documentos comprobatórios anexados juntos ao documento de Manifestação de Interesse (Currículos, Certificados, Atestados, Publicações, Relatórios, Diplomas...), em um único arquivo com tamanho máximo de 7mb.

É necessário que o perfil do(a) profissional atendas às seguintes exigências, que são indispensáveis à presente contratação:

a) Pós-graduação (Mestrado ou superior) em educação, economia, políticas públicas ou áreas afins;

b) Experiência mínima de 10 anos em avaliação de impacto, preferencialmente no setor educacional;

c) Experiência comprovada na avaliação de programas de alimentação escolar ou proteção social será considerada um diferencial;

d) Domínio de métodos quantitativos e qualitativos de pesquisa;

e) Capacidade analítica sólida, incluindo análise estatística e financeira;

f) Excelentes competências de redação, comunicação e apresentação;

g) Experiência prévia com instituições governamentais, organismos multilaterais ou projetos financiados por doadores.

h) Será considerado um diferencial: artigo, tese de mestrado ou doutorado publicado em journal nacional ou internacional com a avaliação de política pública de alimentação escolar ou área relacionada à gestão escolar pública no Brasil.

 

O profissional será selecionado de acordo com os procedimentos indicados no Regulamento de aquisições para mutuários de operações de financiamento de projetos de investimento do Banco Mundial, quarta edição de novembro de 2020.

É parte integrante desta Manifestação de Interesse o e Termo de Referência (TdR) no qual consta a descrição detalhada das atividades a serem desempenhadas e dos produtos a serem elaborados, e que está disponível no website: www.sefaz.al.gov.br/licitacao.

Os profissionais interessados deverão encaminhar as manifestações até o dia 23 de agosto de 2026, às 18 horas, devidamente identificadas como ED3 BR-SEDUC/AL-555632-CS-INDV, no seguinte endereço eletrônico celp@sefaz.al.gov.br.

IDA-E6230

Assignment Title

Engagement of a Road Safety Expert (Road Safety Auditor) under the Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP)

Procurement Plan Ref Number

GH-MRH-DFR-563246-CS-INDV

Country of Delivery

Ghana

  1. The Government of the Republic of Ghana has received a Grant from the World Bank toward the cost of the Project Preparation for the Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the Engagement of an Individual Consultant as a Road Safety Expert (Road Safety Auditor).

 

The primary objective of this assignment is to undertake Road Safety Audits (RSAs) on all roads under Clusters 1, 2, 3, and 4 under the preparatory phase of the GMACP to ensure that all safety considerations are embedded in the feasibility and design stage reports for the road works.

 

The consulting services ("the Services") will ensure that road safety considerations are fully integrated into the feasibility and detailed design process in accordance with the Ghana Road Design Manual, the MRH Low Volume Roads Manual, the World Bank Road Safety Screening and Appraisal Tool (RSSAT), and recognised international best practices. The Individual Consultant is expected to undertake the following activities among others:

  1. Review existing road conditions, crash history, community safety concerns and assess preliminary alignments for safety implications.
  2. Identify systemic road safety risks and recommend practical mitigation measures for incorporation into feasibility studies and preliminary designs.
  3. Undertake Road Safety Audits of detailed engineering designs, including geometric layouts, cross-sections, junctions, sight distances, road signs, road markings, pedestrian and cyclist facilities.
  4. Review contractor Traffic Management Plans (TMPs) and bidding documents to ensure that appropriate road safety provisions are incorporated before procurement.
  5. Provide technical advice to the Agency Implementation Team (AIT) and prepare stage-specific Road Safety Audit Reports and compliance matrices to facilitate review and approval by MRH and DFR.

The estimated level of effort (professional person-months) is 3.35 person-months.

The implementation period for the assignment is expected to be 4 months from the commencement of the Assignment. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained by sending an official request to the email addresses given below.

elormnyoagbe@icloud.com, cynthia.anane@mrh.gov.gh, patienceonny@gmail.com  

 

The Ministry of Roads and Highways (MRH), acting through the Department of Feeder Roads, now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultants are expected to submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV) with a description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc. Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

 

2. Eligibility Requirement for the Assignment

The best qualified Individual Consultant to carry out the services will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, the Seventh (7th) Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”). The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:  

(a) Minimum Mandatory Requirements (pass/fail):

  1. Certified copy of an Academic Degree (Master's Degree in Transportation Engineering, Civil Engineering, Transport Planning or related field with a bias to Road Safety Engineering).
  2. Copy of Professional Qualification Certificate demonstrating membership of a recognised Professional Body.
  3. Copy of Certificate of Competence from recognised bodies (IRF, PIARC, or equivalent).
  4. Evidence of experience in road safety engineering, road safety audits (at least 3 Road safety audit of designs as team lead), road user behavior and related areas (audits) under donor-funded projects in the Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) within the last 10 years.

2. PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT DE L’AGRICULTURE COMMERCIALE EN GUINEE PHASE 2 (PDACG2)

Financement  Banque Mondiale : Crédit N° 6771– GN / Don N° D713 – GN

 

 

 

 

TERMES DE REFERENCE

 

 

 

Recrutement du Responsable des aménagements et des infrastructures (RAI) pour le Projet de Développement de l’Agriculture Commerciale en Guinée Phase 2 (PDACG2)

 

 

 

 

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DU RESPONSABLE DES AMENAGEMENTS ET DES INFRASTRUCTURES (RAI) DU Projet de Développement de l’Agriculture Commerciale en Guinée Phase 2 (PDACG2)

NUMERO DE L’ACTIVITE GN-PDACG 2 -AGRICULTURE-560239-CS-INDV

AMI N°001-MA/PDACG2/2026

Date de début : 12 août 2026

Date de fin : 28 août 2026

  1. Contexte et justification

Le Projet de Développement de l’Agriculture Commerciale en Guinée Phase 2 (PDACG2) s’inscrit dans l’exécution de la Politique Nationale de Développement Agricole (PNDA) arrimé au Plan de Développement Economique et Social responsable de la Guinée dénommé ‘’Programme SIMANDOU 2040’’ en son Pilier 1 : Agriculture – Industries alimentaires & Commerce, en vue de faire de l’agriculture le moteur de croissance socio-économique inclusive et durable de la Guinée. Le projet s’inscrit dans la logique d’intervention de l’Initiative AgriConnect Guinée et vise également à contribuer à l’accélération de la mise en œuvre du Plan National d’Investissement Agricole, de Sécurité Alimentaire et Nutritionnelle (PNIASAN-2018-2025) soutenu par l’Union Africaine (UA) et la Communauté Économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO).

 

L’approche du projet est fondée sur la transformation du secteur agroalimentaire en un secteur agricole commercial compétitif susceptible d’attirer des investissements privés en Guinée en vue de développer des chaînes de valeur agricole en vue d’approvisionner les marchés à croissance rapide et créer des emplois et des opportunités économiques. Les principes d’intervention du projet sont essentiellement de : (i) tirer parti des infrastructures de transport existantes le long des corridors Kankan – Mamou - Kindia et Kindia-Conakry, (ii) concentrer le soutien initial dans les agropoles retenus pour le Programme Simandou 2040 et (iii) répondre, grâce à une flexibilité, aux opportunités d’affaires pouvant contribuer à l’atteinte de l’objectif de développement du projet.

Les interventions du programme axées sur trois chaînes de valeur (riz, fonio et volaille) centrées autour des pôles de croissance du programme Simandou 2040 : Kankan, Mamou et Kindia. Ces sites ont été sélectionnés pour leur capacité à favoriser la transformation des chaînes de valeur ciblées. Dans la région de Boké, les activités essentielles de la phase1 seront consolidées.

 

Le PDACG2 sera financé par l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour un montant de cent (100) millions de dollars US et pour une durée d’exécution de cinq (5) ans.

Le projet comporte les cinq (5) principales composantes résumées ci-après :

 

Composante 1 : Investissements structurants pour l’agriculture commerciale -Cette composante renforce les fondements du marché, les infrastructures physiques et numériques, ainsi que les connaissances nécessaires au développement d’une agriculture commercialement viable et adaptée au climat. Il s’agit de i) établir des modèles d’agrégation axés sur le marché qui relient les petits exploitants aux marchés commerciaux en déployant des solutions AgTech pour cartographier les acteurs de la chaîne de valeur, les parcelles de production et les points de blocage ; ii) développer des infrastructures écoénergétiques et résilientes au climat en développant la production de riz et de maïs irrigués, en réhabilitant et en construisant des systèmes d’irrigation, en renforçant les systèmes de stockage, d’agro-logistique et de chaîne du froid, et en établissant des plateformes publiques numériques interopérables telles que des registres agricoles unifiés, des systèmes d’information sur les marchés et des services de données sur les sols, alignés sur des investissements complémentaires dans les routes rurales, l’électricité et les transports afin de positionner les agropoles comme des pôles compétitifs et intégrés ; iii) améliorer la productivité, la résilience et la qualité des produits par la consolidation du continuum recherche-vulgarisation-innovation grâce à la modernisation des stations de recherche agricole et des centres de formation à la vulgarisation, notamment par l’acquisition de laboratoires modernes, d’équipements et d’outils numériques.

 

Composante 2 : Développement des services financiers et réduction des risques liés aux investissements privés – A travers cette composante, il est prévu de déployer un ensemble d’instruments complémentaires de financement du GBM, notamment les subventions de contrepartie du les guichets de garantie partielle de portefeuille déjà expérimentés pal le GBM dans le cadre de la Phase 1 du PDACG et autres interventions de la SFI. Deux institutions publiques seront accompagnées à cet effet : le Fonds de Garantie Partielle aux Entreprises (FGPE) et le Fonds de Développement Agricole (FODA).

 

Composante n°3 : Établissement d’un environnement favorable à l’agriculture commerciale - Cette composante vise à améliorer les politiques, les systèmes réglementaires et les capacités institutionnelles afin d’attirer les investissements privés. Il est prévu de : i) soutenir les réformes clés (telles que l’adoption d’une politique nationale des semences, la mise en place d’un registre foncier numérique pour renforcer la sécurité foncière, l’élaboration d’une stratégie de commercialisation du fonio et d’une loi sur les organisations agricoles interprofessionnelles, ainsi que la création d’un Bureau national de développement du riz … ) ; ii) soutenir les systèmes sanitaires et phytosanitaires (SPS) à travers l’actualisation de la réglementation, la mise en place des systèmes de surveillance et d'alerte précoce pour les ravageurs et les maladies, la modernisation des laboratoires et la promotion des normes de qualité, la traçabilité et la marque « Origine Guinée » ; iii) renforcer les capacités opérationnelles des institutions publiques et des organisations de la chaîne de valeur grâce à des formations, de l’assistance technique et des investissements dans les domaines de l'agriculture numérique, de la certification, de la coordination et de l'engagement du secteur privé de manière  – afin de garantir des s services de qualité et une meilleure gouvernance du secteur.

 

Composante 4 : Gestion et coordination du projet - Cette composante financera : a) les coûts de fonctionnement de l’Unité de coordination du projet (UCP) et la coordination multisectorielle aux niveaux central et décentralisé, y compris les fonctions techniques, fiduciaires (approvisionnement et gestion financière) et environnementales et sociales ; b) le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles et techniques pour appuyer la mise en œuvre efficace du projet ; c) le suivi et l’évaluation (S&E) et les systèmes d’information de gestion ; d) le développement et la maintenance du site Web du projet ; e) les évaluations initiales, à mi-parcours et finales, y compris les évaluations d’impact ; f) communications et mobilisation des parties prenantes; (g) mécanismes de règlement des griefs, éthique et activités d’échange de connaissances; (h) diffusion des résultats du projet; et (i) coûts de réinstallation pour indemniser les personnes touchées par les activités du projet, principalement le développement de zones de gestion hydro-agricoles.

 

Composante n°5 : Intervention d’urgence -   Cette composante constitue un fonds d’urgence qui peut être débloqué en cas de catastrophes naturelles donnant lieu à une situation d’état d’urgence officiel, ou à une demande du Gouvernement. La composante financera les dépenses d’intervention rapide afin de répondre aux besoins d’urgence.

La mise en œuvre du Projet sera effectuée sous la responsabilité et la coordination du ministère de l’Agriculture (MA) qui s’appuiera sur une unité autonome de coordination de projet (UCP) implantée au sein de l’Unité de suivi de la mise en œuvre du Pilier I du Programme national Simandou 2040. L’UCP sera responsable de la coordination générale du projet, de la gestion fiduciaire, de la supervision technique et de l’assurance qualité, des garanties environnementales et sociales, de l’inclusion des femmes, de la gestion des sous-projets et des protocoles d’accord (PA), du suivi et de l’évaluation, ainsi que de l’exécution du plan de travail et du budget annuels approuvés. L’UCP sera dirigée par un coordonnateur de projet à temps plein, sélectionné au sein de la fonction publique et rémunéré par des indemnités financées par le projet.

 

Le présent document représente les termes de référence pour le recrutement du Responsable des aménagements et des infrastructures de l’UCP du projet.  Il précise les missions, les tâches, les qualifications et les modalités de sélection

  1.  Descriptif du poste

Sous l’autorité du Coordonnateur, le (la) Responsable des aménagements et des infrastructures est chargé (e) des tâches suivantes :

  • Coordonner et harmoniser toutes les activités du projet liées au développement des aménagements hydroagricoles et des infrastructures (ingénierie civile/rurale et sociale) ;
  • Contribuer à l’élaboration des plans de travail et budget annuels (PTBA) pour les activités liées aux aménagements hydroagricoles et autres infrastructures ;
  • Elaborer des termes de référence relatifs aux interventions des prestataires de services et autres partenaires ;
  • Participer au processus de validation des DAO ;
  • Participer aux processus de sélection des prestataires des services ;
  • Assister l’Unité de Coordination du projet et participer à l’élaboration, le suivi (technico-administratif et financier) et l’évaluation des contrats avec les prestataires et des conventions/protocoles avec les autres partenaires du projet ;
  • Examiner et approuver des rapports (études, exécution des travaux, missions, etc.) et tous autres livrables fournis par les prestataires et partenaires ;
  • Valider les attachements et décomptes ;
  • Participer aux processus de réception des réalisations et travaux ;
  • Participer aux missions de supervisions des activités mises en œuvre par le projet ;
  • Assurer et coordonner la mise en place des dispositifs de gestion durable des investissements autour des bénéficiaires ;
  • Rédiger les sections des rapports périodiques (mensuels, trimestriels, et annuels) du projet relatives aux volets aménagements hydroagricoles et infrastructures ;
  • Réceptionner, évaluer et valider les rapports de progrès d’activités des partenaires :
  • Participer à la préparation et à l’organisation des ateliers de suivi-évaluation participatif et apporter son entière collaboration aux missions de suivi-évaluation et de supervision du projet ;
  • Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les autres membres de l’Unité de coordination du projet et les parties prenantes dans la mise en œuvre des activités ;
  • Servir d’interface auprès des partenaires du projet pour la mise en œuvre (initiation, exécution et évaluation) des activités relevant de leurs mandats ;
  • Dresser périodiquement les situations des différents marchés/dossiers relatifs aux infrastructures afin d’aider aux prises de décisions de la coordination de l’UGP ;
  • Assurer la gestion de documents administratifs et bancaires spécifiques aux marchés d’infrastructures (en particuliers les cautions de soumission, de bonne exécution et de garantie);
  • S’assurer que les indicateurs du cadre logique sont bien suivi en ce qui concerne les activités dont il est responsabilisé ;
  • Veiller à la prise en compte de la dimension inclusion sociale dans tout le processus de mise en œuvre des activités liés aux aménagements hydroagricoles et infrastructures ;

 

  1. En ce qui concerne l’ingénierie civile et rurale :
    • Assurer l’identification, la sélection et la priorisation des sites destinés à l’aménagement hydroagricole et des infrastructures à construire/réhabiliter selon les études de faisabilité et les besoins identifiés;
    • Piloter la préparation des dossiers techniques (DAO, études techniques, EIES, etc.) ;
    • Veiller à la conformité des cahiers des charges et à l’intégration des aspects environnementaux et sociaux ;
    • Dresser périodiquement les situations des différents contrats relatifs aux infrastructures afin d’aider aux prises de décisions de l’UGP;
    • Assurer le cadrage des prestataires dans le démarrage des taches : études techniques, socioéconomiques et environnementales (Avant-projet sommaire, APS ; Avant-projet détaillé, APD ; Etude d’impact environnemental et social, EIES ; Dossier d’appel d’offre, DAO), exécution des travaux, contrôle de l’exécution des travaux, supervision des travaux par les services techniques, mise en œuvre des volets connexes, etc.) ;
    • Analyser et signer les attachements des travaux/prestations de contrôle faits contradictoirement avec les entreprises et cabinets ;
    • Analyser et amender les résultats des études APS, APD et DAO conduites par les prestataires ;
    • Participer aux missions terrains de vérification des résultats des études avant approbation ;
    • Coordonner et  préparer la conduite (si possible participer) des missions de remises officielles de sites aux entreprises pour le démarrage des travaux ;
    • Coordonner l’analyse et l’amendement des dossiers d’exécution (DE) et Initier les réponses aux prestataires sur les avis techniques y relatifs avant l’approbation par la coordination du projet ;
    • Garantir la mise en œuvre des missions de supervision des travaux conjointement avec les services techniques concernés ;
    • Vérifier et viser les décomptes, certifier les factures de demande de paiement dans le cadre des  études, travaux, contrôle de travaux et les prestations des services techniques; 
    • Veiller sur la qualité des outils préparés par son unité (PV de remise de sites, des réunions de supervision, de réception technique, provisoire et définitive des travaux/réalisations) ;
  2. En ce qui concerne l’ingénierie sociale :
    • Veiller au respect des processus d’analyse de la structure sociale, des organisations paysannes, ses rapports de genre et les dynamiques communautaires ;
    • Veiller au processus d’identification des acteurs clés et de leurs besoins ;
    • Organiser des campagnes d’information sur les objectifs et bénéfices du projet ;
    • Favoriser l’adhésion et la participation active des populations locales ;
    • Valider les modules destinés à la formation (gouvernance locale, gestion financière et entretien des investissements) des groupements de bénéficiaires/utilisateurs ;
    • Contribuer l’organisation et à l’évaluation des sessions de formation des groupements d’usagers de l’eau (GUE) et les organisations paysannes à la gestion des infrastructures ;
    • Organiser les sessions d’échange d’expériences entre groupements ;
    • Appuyer la création/renforcement et la légalisation des comités de gestion des investissements ;
    • Définir les règles de fonctionnement, de répartition des tâches et de résolution des conflits.
    • Veiller à la mise en place des mécanismes de suivi social pour mesurer l’impact sur les communautés et assurer le suivi de leur fonctionnement ;
    • Assurer la remontée des préoccupations des bénéficiaires et ajuster les activités ;
    • Veiller à la prévention et la résolution des différends liés à l’accès aux investissements ;
    • Promouvoir des pratiques inclusives et équitables ;
    • Veiller à l’inclusion des femmes et des jeunes dans les instances de décision ;
    • Prendre en compte les enjeux environnementaux et de durabilité sociale.
    • Veiller au respect des aspects et critères socioéconomiques dans le dimensionnement et la mise en œuvre des investissements ;
  1. Obligations du Responsable des aménagements et des infrastructures (RAI)

Sous la Supervision directe du Coordonnateur du projet, le/la Responsable des aménagements et des infrastructures (RAI) sera un(e) expert(e) en ingénierie civile/rural et assurera la coordination des activités d’ingénierie civile et d’ingénierie sociale y afférent, pour la mise en œuvre des aménagements hydroagricoles et des infrastructures du projet suivant l’approche décrite par le document de projet.

À cet effet, il(elle) assurera: (i) la planification technique et opérationnelle des activités; (ii) la préparation et le suivi des dossiers (ingénierie civile et ingénierie sociale); (iii) la supervision technique et fiduciaires de toutes les activités menées au compte des volets relevant de son mandat. Cela devra être fait dans le respect des standards de qualité, des coûts et des délais.

En effet, Il(elle), sera chargé(e) de la coordination et du suivi technique global des activités liées aux travaux et à la gestion des aménagements hydroagricoles et des infrastructures principales et connexes avec une vision axée sur la transformation du secteur agroalimentaire en un secteur agricole commercial compétitif, dans le respect des enjeux climato-environnementaux et du contexte socio-culturel.

  1. Qualifications et expériences requises  

Le(la) candidat(e) doit:

  • Être titulaire d'un diplôme d'ingénieur (niveau BAC +5/ (ou Master) en  génie civil, génie rural, travaux publics ou équivalent ;
  • Disposer d’une expérience professionnelle globale d’au moins 10 ans dans la mise en œuvre des projets et programmes de développement; (avoir une expérience de la mise en œuvre des projets et programmes avec des bailleurs de Fonds internationaux sera un atout);
  • Avoir au moins 5 ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente dans la conception et/ou la mise en œuvre et suivi des projets d’aménagement hydroagricoles et d'infrastructures (routes/pistes rurales, marchés, ports fluviaux, adduction d’eau, ou équivalent) financées par des bailleurs de Fonds internationaux comme responsable du volet aménagement hydroagricole et infrastructures ;
  • Avoir d'excellentes compétences organisationnelles, de respect des délais, d’exécution de plusieurs tâches simultanément ;
  • Être capable de travailler au sien d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire et sous pression ;
  • Être capable d'utiliser et interpréter les résultats issus des logiciels de génie civil et d’architecture ;
  • Comprendre et savoir interpréter les résultats des logicielles et applications  de génie civil, le pack office (Word, Excel, Power-Point, etc…) et autres outil d’élaboration des plans des infrastructures ;
  • Être disposé à effectuer des visites sur le terrain dans le cadre des missions de supervision
  • Être disposé à travailler en milieu rural ;
  • Ne pas avoir été défaillant dans le cadre de l’exécution des précédents contrats au niveau des projets financés par les partenaires de développement (fournir les références professionnelles antérieures).

NB : Les candidatures des femmes sont vivement encouragées.

  1. Lieu et durée de la mission

Le contrat aura une durée initiale d’un (1) an renouvelable pendant une période maximale égale à la durée du projet et sous-réserve de l’évaluation annuelle satisfaisante des performances.  Il est assorti d’une période d’essai de six (6) mois.

Le poste est basé à Conakry et au sein du Ministère de l’Agriculture avec des déplacements fréquents dans les zones d’intervention du projet en Guinée.

  1. Procédure et méthode de sélection

Un candidat sera sélectionné suivant la méthode de sélection des Consultants individuels en accord avec les procédures définies aux paragraphes 7.32 à 7.38 du Règlement de Passation des Marches de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement d’un Projet d’Investissement (FPI), édition septembre 2023.

  1. Dépôt des dossiers

Au siège de l’Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) Guinée à Dixinn, immeuble Kalinko, 1e étage, Cité ministérielle, Commune de DIxinn, au bureau du spécialiste en Passation de marchés. Les dossiers de candidature devront comprendre :

  • Un Curriculum Vitae actualisé et concis ;
  • Une lettre de motivation de la candidature (maximum 1 page) démontrant la compréhension du poste et justifiant l’expérience pertinente ou compétences pour l’assumer ;

Des copies légalisées et certifiées conformes du ou des diplôme(s) requis, des certificats et attestations de formation ;

Des copies des attestations ou certificat de travail ou documents similaires

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

 

National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB)

 

Consulting services for feasibility assessment, detailed design, procurement support, and construction supervision for the development of the VROMI Waste Diversion and Waste Management Yard

 

 

Country: Sint Maarten

Project: The Sint Maarten Emergency Debris Management Project

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Land Survey and Planning

Credit/Loan no.: TF-B9747

Reference no.: SX-NRPB-556005-CS-CQS

 

Deadline: 5:00 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time, Monday, August 10th, 2026

 

1. The Government of Sint Maarten (GoSXM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Emergency Debris Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services under this request for expression of interest.

2. The Government of Sint Maarten (GoSXM), represented by the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB) is looking to select an experienced (international or national) firm for a consultancy service to conduct the feasibility assessment, detailed design, procurement support, and construction supervision services. The objective of this consultancy is to provide multidisciplinary engineering and technical services to assess the feasibility of developing the VROMI Waste Diversion and Waste Management Yard, prepare the detailed designs and procurement documents, and supervise the implementation of the civil works.

3. The scope of services under this consultancy includes, but is not limited to, the following:

a. Conduct land assessment activities, including boundary surveys, geotechnical investigations, soil bearing capacity and groundwater analysis, utilities assessment, and environmental, social, health and safety (ESHS) screening;

b. Prepare a master site development plan, detailed engineering designs, cadastral subdivision plans, and technical documentation to support regulatory approvals;

c. Develop procurement documentation for the civil works, including technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQ), engineer's estimates, and provide technical support during the procurement and bid evaluation process;

d. Provide construction supervision services, including quality assurance, contract administration, ESHS monitoring, and reporting throughout the implementation of the works.

e. The detailed scope of services and deliverables is provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR). The assignment will be implemented in three phases:

Phase 1 – Land Assessment and Preparation;

Phase 2 – Planning, Detailed Design and Procurement Support;

Phase 3 – Construction Supervision (optional, subject to implementation of the civil works contract).

4. The detailed scope and deliverables of the assignment are available in Terms of Reference (TOR), which can be viewed and downloaded via the link: National Recovery Program Bureau of St. Maarten - Consulting Services for Land Survey and Planning. The consulting services are to be provided over an estimated 5 months; this assignment will be on a lump-sum basis (firm fixed price) for all services and expenses, including consultant travel expenses.

5. The Consultant shall ensure that all activities are implemented in accordance with the quality standards, time and budget elaborated in the contract document, in order to comply with the Project's objective.

6. The National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB) now invites eligible firms (“Consultant”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

a. General Experience

Minimum 10 years of experience in land development, infrastructure planning, engineering design, or similar multidisciplinary consultancy services.

b. Specific Experience

Demonstrated successful completion, within the last ten (10) years, of at least three (3) assignments of a similar nature involving one or more of the following:

i. land development planning and master planning;

ii. geotechnical investigations and site assessments;

iii. engineering design for infrastructure and utilities;

iv. preparation of procurement documentation for civil works;

v. construction supervision of civil engineering works.

c. Technical Capacity

Demonstrated capability to mobilize a multidisciplinary team covering, at a minimum:

Civil Engineering / Infrastructure Design;

Geotechnical Engineering;

Environmental and Social (ESHS);

Surveying / GIS / CAD;

Construction Supervision;

Procurement / Contract Administration.

CVs are not requested at the EOI stage - Key experts shall be requested only after the most qualified firm is invited to submit its technical and financial proposal.

d. Regional Experience (Desirable)

Experience in Small Island Developing States (SIDS), the Caribbean region, or projects with comparable environmental and operational conditions will be considered an

advantage.

e. Development Partner Experience (Desirable)

Experience on projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions (IFIs) will be considered an advantage.

7. The selection process will be undertaken in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fourth Edition November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”) for open competitive selection. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (November 2020) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

9. All submissions should be uploaded via the NRPB’s procurement portal which can be done via: National Recovery Program Bureau of St. Maarten - Consulting Services for Land Survey and Planning no later than Monday, August 10th, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time.

10. All queries from interested bidders must be submitted electronically to https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com through the Vendor Discussions section under the respective Project (procurement) https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com/portal/?tab=pastOpportunities Interested bidders should register in the NRPB's procurement portal at https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com/login/. Detailed instructions for registration are available at https://nrpbsxm.org/procurement/ (NRPB EUNA SOLUTIONS REGISTRATION PAGE).

11. Once registered, bidders will have access to the relevant information, may submit questions, and respond to the procurement opportunity.

Caribbean Connectivity and Logistics Regional Program – Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA)

Analytical Study to Support the Preparation of the Connectivity and Logistics Program for the Commonwealth of Dominica.

1. Background and Context

The Commonwealth of Dominica is a small island developing state (SIDS) in the Eastern Caribbean, with a population of approximately 72,000 and an economy heavily dependent on tourism, agriculture, and remittances. Like many OECS member states, Dominica faces structural connectivity challenges that constrain trade competitiveness, private sector growth, and economic resilience. Its main trade gateway — the Port of Roseau — suffers from infrastructure limitations, including a cargo pier design that restricts operational efficiency due to warehouses occupying a significant portion of the terminal, and the absence of ship-to-shore equipment. The Port of Portsmouth serves as a dedicated cargo terminal but is also constrained in capacity. Road connectivity, particularly to rural and agricultural areas, remains inadequate and highly vulnerable to natural disasters.

Dominica is also highly exposed to climate-related shocks. Hurricane Maria (2017) caused damages estimated at over 220 percent of GDP, severely disrupting transport infrastructure, supply chains, and livelihoods. This experience has underscored the urgent need to build not only more efficient but fundamentally more resilient connectivity infrastructure and logistics systems.

The Caribbean Reconnect Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA) is a joint World Bank Group initiative — involving the World Bank, IFC, and MIGA — designed to strengthen connectivity, logistics, and infrastructure across the Caribbean. The program is structured around the following three components:

  • Component 1 (Reforms), which establishes enabling regulatory foundations at national and regional levels with a focus on Private Sector Participation (PSP), trade facilitation, and supply chain security;
  • Component 2 (Enabling Infrastructure), which identifies and prepares high-impact national infrastructure investments including port modernization, resilient connectivity, digitalization, and decarbonization; and
  • Component 3 (Mobilization), which develops a regional financing scheme to aggregate projects and unlock private capital at scale.

Phase 1 of the program is expected by FY2028, with the Eastern Caribbean Corridor as the first movers.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) concerns the preparation of the Dominica country program under the Caribbean Reconnect MPA. The Consultant's primary task is to produce the analytical and strategic foundation needed to design a coherent Dominica program across all three MPA components, calibrated to Dominica's market status and grounded in the government's own priorities.

A critical and distinctive feature of this assignment is that the Government of Dominica, through DASPA, has already developed a substantive project concept — the DASPA Digitalization Project Conceptualization Proposal — covering a structured six-component digital transformation roadmap for DASPA's port operations. The Government-owned concept represents a significant investment of institutional knowledge and strategic thinking, and must be treated as the primary analytical foundation for the digitalization and infrastructure dimensions of the program. The technical review and validation of this concept will be carried out in parallel by World Bank STCs with specialized port technology expertise. The Consultant under this ToR will ensure that the findings of that review are fully integrated into the Dominica program design.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The consultancy has two (2) overarching objectives:

  • Objective 1 — Connectivity and Logistics Diagnostic: To produce a focused, evidence-based diagnostic of Dominica's connectivity and logistics landscape — covering maritime port infrastructure, road connectivity and hinterland access, inter-island maritime services, trade facilitation, private sector participation readiness, and green logistics opportunities — identifying the key constraints and opportunities that the Reconnect MPA country program should address. The diagnostic must be structured to generate findings that directly inform the design of all three MPA components (Reforms, Enabling Infrastructure, Mobilization).
  • Objective 2 — Dominica MPA Country Program Design: To produce a structured, financeable Dominica Country Program Document, aligned with the three-component architecture of the Caribbean Reconnect MPA, that integrates: (a) the findings of the World Bank STC technical review of the DASPA Digitalization Concept; (b) the broader connectivity and logistics diagnostic; and (c) an assessment of private sector participation opportunities and the joint WBG engagement strategy (World Bank, IFC, MIGA). The Country Program Document must be sufficiently developed to serve as the basis for a World Bank lending operation under the Reconnect MPA, with a target of FY2028 for Phase 1.

3. Scope of Work

3.1 Component 1: Focused Connectivity and Logistics Diagnostic

To complement the government's digitalization concept with the broader analytical framing required by the Caribbean Reconnect Program, the Consultant will conduct a targeted — not exhaustive — diagnostic of Dominica's connectivity and logistics landscape. Given the budget and duration of this assignment, the diagnostic should be focused and evidence-based, drawing heavily on existing data and studies rather than generating new primary research from scratch. The diagnostic will cover the following dimensions:

  • Port infrastructure and operations: A focused assessment of the Port of Roseau (Woodbridge Bay) and the Port of Portsmouth (Longhouse), covering physical infrastructure, equipment gaps, cargo dwell times, throughput trends, operational bottlenecks, the cruise-cargo interface challenge at Roseau, and resilience to natural hazards, with a view to identify a priority investment program, in particular for Woodbridge Bay, to improve and rationalize operations in the short-term. Where relevant, the assessment should also consider the implications of Dominica's planned new cargo port for the future configuration of port operations.  To this end, the diagnosis shall include comprehensive Terms of Reference for the drafting of a National Port Development Master Plan.

 

  • Road connectivity and hinterland access: An assessment of the road network linking ports to key productive zones (particularly agricultural areas and agro-processing facilities), population centers, and inter-island ferry terminals. The analysis should focus on: identifying the most critical road links for logistics efficiency; assessing vulnerability to natural disasters and climate events; and estimating the logistics cost implications of road quality and reliability constraints. This analysis should draw on existing road assessments and post-Maria reconstruction data rather than generating new surveys.

 

  • Inter-island maritime connectivity: A review of current maritime services connecting Dominica to its neighbors (particularly Guadeloupe, Martinique, and other OECS islands), covering frequency, reliability, cargo capacity, and freight rates. The assessment should identify specific constraints — such as port infrastructure limitations, regulatory barriers, or limited-service competition — that restrict Dominica's ability to trade efficiently within the region, and assess opportunities for improving inter-island maritime services as part of the rEconnect program.

 

  • Trade facilitation and customs: A review of existing customs procedures, border management systems, and compliance status with the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement, identifying key regulatory and procedural barriers affecting importers, exporters, and logistics service providers.

 

  • Trade flows and private sector landscape: A concise review of Dominica's import/export patterns, trade costs, and key private sector logistics actors (freight forwarders, shipping agents, trucking companies, warehouse operators), drawing on available data from Customs, DASPA, and regional sources. The analysis should assess how logistics costs and connectivity constraints affect the competitiveness of Dominica's key productive sectors, particularly agriculture and agro-processing.

 

  • Institutional and regulatory framework: An assessment of the mandates, capacity, and coordination mechanisms of DASPA, Customs and Excise Division, the Ministry of Public Works (for roads), the Ministry of Finance, and other relevant agencies. This should identify key institutional gaps, overlaps, and coordination failures that the program should address, as well as the regulatory framework governing maritime services and road transport.

Beyond the above dimensions, the diagnostic must also address two cross-cutting themes that are central to the Reconnect MPA:

  1. Private Sector Participation (PSP) Readiness: An assessment of the current state and potential for private sector participation in Dominica's port and logistics sector. This should cover: existing concession or PPP arrangements (if any); the regulatory and institutional framework governing PSP; private sector interest and capacity; and the specific barriers — legal, institutional, financial, reputational — that constrain private sector engagement. Given Dominica's classification as a less-mature market, the assessment should identify the foundational reforms and institutional strengthening measures needed to create conditions for PSP over the medium term, as well as any near-term opportunities that IFC or MIGA could support.
  2. Green Logistics and Decarbonization: A high-level baseline assessment of the carbon footprint and energy intensity of Dominica's port and logistics operations, and an identification of priority opportunities for decarbonization — such as shore power, solar energy for port facilities, fuel-efficient vessels for inter-island services, or green logistics zone design. This should inform the inclusion of decarbonization investments in the infrastructure component of the program.

The diagnostic should yield a concise, structured synthesis of findings organized around the three MPA components — Reforms, Enabling Infrastructure, and Mobilization — clearly identifying what the Dominica program should address under each component.

3.2 Component 2: Dominica MPA Country Program Document

Drawing on the Connectivity and Logistics Diagnostic (Component 1) and the World Bank STC technical review of the DASPA Digitalization Concept, the Consultant will produce a Dominica MPA Country Program Document. This is the primary output of the assignment. It must be structured explicitly around the three components of the Caribbean Reconnect MPA, and must be sufficiently detailed to serve as the basis for a World Bank lending operation targeting FY2028.

The document will cover:

  • MPA Component 1 — Reforms (National and Regional Level): Based on the institutional and regulatory diagnostic, the Consultant will design a reform agenda for Dominica covering: (a) the regulatory and governance framework for port operations and maritime services, including any changes needed to enable PSP; (b) trade facilitation and supply chain security reforms, including progress toward WTO TFA compliance and integration with regional single-window and harmonization initiatives; and (c) any regional-level regulatory commitments (e.g., OECS harmonization) that Dominica should advance as part of the MPA. For each reform area, the document should specify the reform action, the responsible agency, the expected timeline, and the technical assistance or capacity building support needed from the program.

 

  • MPA Component 2 — Enabling Infrastructure (National Level): Based on the diagnostic and the DASPA Digitalization Concept (as defined by the World Bank STC review), the Consultant will design an infrastructure investment program for Dominica covering: (a) port digitalization, structured around the government's six-component DASPA concept as technically validated by the STC review, with its own investment envelope, procurement modality, and results indicators; (b) complementary port physical infrastructure investments (where gaps are identified beyond what the digitalization program addresses), this shall include in particular priority short-term investments in Woodbridge Bay, complemented with the ToRs for a National Port Development Master Plan; (c) priority road connectivity investments linking ports to productive zones and inter-island ferry terminals; (d) inter-island maritime infrastructure (jetties, terminals, safety systems) where warranted; and (e) decarbonization investments in port and logistics operations. For each investment, the document should include an order-of-magnitude cost estimate, a proposed financing modality, and a readiness assessment.

 

  • MPA Component 3 — Mobilization: Based on the PSP readiness assessment, the Consultant will outline Dominica's positioning within the regional mobilization strategy of the Reconnect MPA. This section should: identify the foundational steps needed before private capital can be attracted at scale; propose a sequenced PSP roadmap for the medium term; identify any specific near-term opportunities for IFC engagement (e.g., advisory support for a port concession framework) or MIGA political risk coverage; and assess how Dominica's program can be aggregated with other Eastern Caribbean countries to form a viable regional investment corridor.

Cross-cutting Elements: In addition to the three component-specific sections, the document will:

  • Define the program's overall development objective, theory of change, results framework, and key performance indicators — structured to reflect outcomes across all three MPA components.
  • Propose a financing strategy that combines World Bank IDA resources, climate finance instruments (given Dominica's vulnerability and the decarbonization agenda), and potential IFC/MIGA engagement, taking into account Dominica's fiscal constraints and debt situation.
  • Provide a project preparation roadmap covering: environmental and social assessment requirements; procurement planning; institutional implementation arrangements (including the role of the CSU/PIU); and the sequencing of steps needed to reach project appraisal by the FY2028 target.
  • Incorporate lessons from comparable Caribbean and SIDS programs. Aviation-related comparators are not required.

Validation Workshop: Before finalizing the Country Program Document, the Consultant will organize and facilitate a validation workshop with relevant government decision-makers and key stakeholders. The workshop will present the proposed program scope, investment priorities, reform agenda, and implementation roadmap across all three MPA components, and will seek formal endorsement of the program direction from senior government counterparts. The workshop should be held in Dominica and timed to take place after the submission of the Draft Country Program Document (D3) and before the final version (D4), so that validation feedback can be incorporated into the final document. A brief workshop report summarizing discussions, decisions, and any agreed amendments to the program scope should be submitted alongside D4. The World Bank Task Team will co-facilitate the workshop alongside the Consultant.

5. Methodology and Approach

Given the budget and duration of this assignment, the Consultant is expected to adopt a focused, evidence-based methodology that maximizes the use of existing analytical work — particularly the DASPA Digitalization Conceptualization Proposal and the As-Is Business Process Analysis — rather than duplicating prior efforts. Key methodological requirements include:

  • Government Concept as the Anchor: The DASPA Digitalization Project Conceptualization Proposal must be the starting point and primary reference document for the entire assignment. The Consultant is expected to engage closely with DASPA from the outset to understand the government's vision and ensure the work is fully aligned with it. While the technical review of the digitalization concept is handled by World Bank STCs, the Consultant must engage with that parallel process, track its outputs, and ensure they are seamlessly integrated into the Program Framework Document.

 

  • Desk Review: Comprehensive review of the DASPA Digitalization Conceptualization Proposal, the As-Is Business Process Analysis outputs (as they become available), national development plans, World Bank analytical work on Dominica and the Caribbean, and relevant regional studies.

 

  • Stakeholder Consultations: Structured interviews with key government agencies (DASPA, Customs and Excise Division, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Trade) and selected private sector actors. The Consultant is expected to participate in at least one multi-stakeholder validation workshop in Dominica.

 

  • In-Country Mission: At least one in-country mission (minimum ten working days) covering on-site visits to the Port of Roseau and Port of Portsmouth, assessment of key road corridors linking ports to productive zones, meetings with inter-island maritime service operators, and meetings with all key government and private sector counterparts. Aviation facilities and authorities are not part of the in-country mission scope.

 

  • Climate and Disaster Resilience Lens: All design and diagnostic work must integrate climate and disaster risk considerations, consistent with World Bank climate screening requirements.

 

  • Regional Coherence: Findings and recommendations must be consistent with the Caribbean Reconnect Program framework and compatible with regional digital and logistics standards being developed across participating countries.

 

6. Required Qualifications and Experience

The assignment will be undertaken by an Individual Consultant with demonstrated expertise in transport economics, logistics, and connectivity planning. The Consultant should possess the following qualifications and experience:

Senior Transport and Logistics Economist / Connectivity Specialist

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

  • A postgraduate degree in transport economics, economics, logistics, infrastructure planning, engineering, public policy, or a related discipline.
  • At least 12 years of professional experience in transport sector development, logistics, trade facilitation, and/or connectivity, with a strong track record in analytical and program preparation assignments.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing World Bank lending operations or equivalent multilateral programs, including familiarity with results frameworks, theory of change, investment program design, financing strategies, and project preparation roadmaps.
  • Solid understanding of the broader transport and logistics sector — encompassing maritime port operations, road connectivity, inter-island shipping, and trade facilitation — sufficient to produce a credible multimodal connectivity diagnostic and to integrate the outputs of the World Bank STC review of the DASPA Digitalization Concept into a coherent program. Aviation expertise is not required.
  • Familiarity with private sector participation frameworks in the port and logistics sector, including PPP structuring, concession frameworks, and the roles of IFC and MIGA in supporting private investment in infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with green logistics and decarbonization concepts in the port and transport sector, sufficient to identify investment opportunities and integrate them into a program design.
  • Previous experience working in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or the Caribbean region is strongly preferred. Knowledge of the OECS institutional and regulatory environment is an advantage.
  • Familiarity with climate-resilient infrastructure design and disaster risk management in the transport sector.
  • Excellent written and spoken English; strong analytical writing and communication skills.

7.0 Level of Effort

The estimated level of effort of the assignment is approximately 90–100 working days over a six-month period.

The Consultant may propose to engage a local Dominica-based facilitator for in-country stakeholder consultations, within the overall budget envelope.

The Consultant will report to the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Tourism, who will serve as the primary government counterpart. The Consultant will work in close collaboration with the Dominica Air and Sea Ports Authority (DASPA). The World Bank Task Team will provide technical oversight and review all deliverables.

9.0 Budget, Timing, Duration, and Logistics

The estimated budget available for this assignment is up to USD 110,000, inclusive of all professional fees, travel, accommodation, subsistence, withholding tax in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Dominica, and any other costs required to complete the assignment. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL)

First Date of Publication: 27th August 2026

Environmental Specialist - Ref No. KVWaSIP-IC-04-083/84

1.0 Background

The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services include providing technical, procurement, financial management, environmental and social, contract management, and other professional support required for effective implementation of the Project through the Project Management Unit (PMU)

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating that they possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, and technical competence to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for each assignment are specified in the respective Terms of Reference (TOR), which may be obtained from the address or website indicated below

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Environmental Specialist and requests applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position.

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The overall objective of this assignment is to support the PMU in preparation of the environmental safeguard measures under KV WaSIP.

Specific objectives of the assignment are to:

  • Support the PMU in the preparation of environmental and social assessments and instruments commensurate with the project’s environmental and social risks and impacts, to ensure project readiness for appraisal and implementation.
  • Ensure compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards and the environmental requirements set out in the project’s Environmental and Social Management Framework.
  • Guide and support the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments, Environmental Management Plans, and other relevant instruments for future subprojects in accordance with the ESF, World Bank requirements, and applicable Government of Nepal legislation.
  • Support the PMU in ensuring that environmental mitigation measures, monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations are integrated into project design, procurement documents, contracts, and implementation arrangements.
  • Assist in the timely review, endorsement, and signing of key environmental and social documents required for project preparation and implementation.
  • Facilitate and follow up on all required environmental clearances, approvals, permits, and no-objection processes from relevant authorities.
  • Ensure that project activities comply with the Government of Nepal’s applicable laws, regulations, and policies related to environmental management, tree clearance, forest land acquisition, Occupational health  and safety (OHS), and downstream water use rights.
  • Lead and coordinate stakeholder mapping, consultations, and stakeholder engagement activities relevant to project preparation and implementation, ensuring that environmental and social risks and concerns are adequately identified and addressed.
  • Build the institutional capacity of the PMU, PIUs, and other relevant counterparts on environmental and social risk management, including the implementation of mitigation measures, monitoring, documentation, and reporting.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

The duties of the Specialist is mentioned in the Terms of Reference in detail.

4. Qualifications and Experience

All applications will be evaluated against the assignment’s required qualifications below.  

Candidates who comply with the minimum qualifications will be scored according to predefined criteria. A minimum of three candidates will be shortlisted and interviewed. The candidate with the highest score will be invited to negotiate a contract. Referees of the selected candidate may be contacted to verify prior experience, performance, and interpersonal skills. 

Qualifications and Relevant Experience

  • Education:
    • Master’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, or environmental management.
    • Training in environmental impact assessment
  • Work Experience:
  • At least 10 years of experience in the environmental safeguard sector.
  • Working experience with water or hydropower dam projects will be beneficial.
  • Experience in the preparation and review of safeguard documents under multilateral development bank safeguard policy frameworks and the ESF.
    • Experience in reviewing E&S policy documents will be an advantage..
  • Interpersonal Skills
    • Strong analytical and report writing skills in both English and Nepali.
    • Ability to coordinate effectively with concerned stakeholders at construction sites.
    • Willingness to undertake regular field visits, including to project areas that may be remote.
    • Familiarity with the Government of Nepal's legal framework on forest and environmental management.
    • Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team.

5. Evaluation and Selection Method

The Senior Dam Specialist will be hired by the PMU using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method following “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) Seventh Edition 2025. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations”.

6. Duration of the Assignment

The Environmental Specialist will be engaged on a full-time basis throughout the grant implementation period (approx. 17 months). Based on the performance and if the project is approved, the Environmental Specialist may continue in this role for the project implementation. 

7. Remuneration

A market-based salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications will be offered.

8. Reporting

The Environmental Specialist will report directly to the Project Manager, PMU. He/she will maintain close coordination with the World Bank's Environmental Specialist and other relevant Bank team members throughout the assignment.

9. Location

  • The consultant will be based at the PMU office and may be required to travel outside the valley as needed for project-related procurement activities.
  • The Project shall provide following facilities to consultant during his tenure of service:
  • Office space
  • Email and internet access
  • Required office stationery and other materials
  • Photocopying/printing facilities

10. Application Process

Interested candidates shall submit a complete application package comprising:

  1. Up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. Copies of academic and professional certificates.
  3. Contact details for at least three (03) professional references familiar with the candidate’s relevant work.

Applications shall be submitted electronically no later than 17.00 PM on 18th September 2026 to the following e-mail address: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered.

The Government of the Republic of Angola (GoA) has received financing from the International Bank of Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and co-financing from the French Development Agency (AFD) towards the cost of the Electricity Sector Improvement and Access Project (ESIAP), whose objective is to improve the operational and commercial performance of the electricity sector utilities and increase electricity access in Angola. The Project is being implemented by the Ministry of Energy and Water and consists of five complementary components: (i) Widening access to electricity and improving revenue collection; (ii) Improving electric service; (iii) Enhancing PRODEL's capacity and strengthening sustainable management of power plants; (iv) Supporting project management; and (v) Responding to Contingent Emergencies.

A Project Coordination Unit (PCU) of ESIAP intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing to procure the services of an individual consultant for the position of Contract Management Specialist.

The primary objective of the Contract Management Specialist consultancy is to support the PCU and Utilities in ensuring effective, compliant, and timely management of contracts across all components of the Angola Electricity Sector Improvement and Access Project. The specialist will play a critical role in overseeing contract administration, facilitating coordination among key stakeholders — including PRODEL, RNT, and ENDE — and providing strategic advice to enhance the operational performance of the utilities.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Project Coordination Unit (PCU) now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest in providing the services by sending a signed Cover Letter, Curriculum Vitae (CV), in a letter addressed to the Project Coordinator, along with a copy of their identification document and proof of education and skills, as indicated in the CV. Interested consultants should provide information (Statement) showing that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to carry out the work, according to the ToRs.

The selection criteria are:

Education

  • Degree in Engineering, Law, Business Administration, Project Management, or a related field, from a recognized University.
  • Relevant professional certifications in contract management or procurement (e.g., PMP, CIPS, FIDIC) are highly desirable.

Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in contract management for large-scale infrastructure projects, with at least 5 years in the energy or power sector, preferably involving transmission and distribution networks.
  • Demonstrated experience in the preparation, negotiation, administration, and monitoring of complex works and goods contracts, including FIDIC or similar international contract standards.
  • Proven experience in managing contracts: Works (at least two contracts valued USD 20,000,000.00 each), Goods and/or Non-Consulting Services (at least two contracts valued USD 2,000,000.00 each), as well as Consultancy Services (at least two contracts valued (USD 1,500,000.00 each). {Applicant to submit evidence of experience}
  • Proven track record in managing contract-related risks, claims, and dispute resolution in the context of donor-funded projects. Exposure to World Bank or other Multilateral Financing Institutions procedures will be considered an advantage.
  • Experience working in multiple countries or regions, including in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable environments, is required. Work experience in Angola will be considered an advantage
  • Prior involvement in capacity building and knowledge transfer to local counterparts is an advantage.
  • Experience in using the WB STEP system is an added advantage

Skills and Competencies

  • In-depth knowledge of the best international practices in contract management, procurement regulations, and project implementation for infrastructure investments.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to address technical, legal, and financial aspects of contract management.
  • Excellent organizational and time management abilities, with a demonstrated capacity to manage multiple contracts and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in contract management and project management software; advanced skills in Microsoft Office Suite are essential.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English; knowledge of Portuguese is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary and multicultural teams, and to interact with government officials and utility staff.
  • High ethical standards, attention to detail, and commitment to delivering results under tight deadlines.

The Contract Management Specialist will work in Angola, Luanda, in the office assigned to ESIAP . The role may also necessitate periodic travel to project implementation sites across Angola, including visits to project sites or utility offices as necessary to support project implementation and oversight.

The duration of the assignment of the Contract Management Specialist will be for a period of 18 months, on a full-time basis, with possible extension upon satisfactory performance.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, seventh edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (IC) selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Interested individual consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 16:00 hours local time.

Expressions of interest must be preferably delivered e-mail or delivered by mail or in person, to the address below, by September 14, 2026 at 16:00 hours (local time) and mention “Expression of Interest – Contract Management Specialist”.

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated in a two-stage process:

  1. Curriculum Vitae (CV) Evaluation (Mandatory);

Assignment Title: Procurement of Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway

Reference No: 926/AUDA/DITIR/RESILIENTIRRIGATIONF/QCBS/2026

Method: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)

 

  1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performance indicator values into color-coded risk flags for display in the executive dashboard. Task 3: Technical Assistance (TA) and Capacity Building: Develop and deliver a structured, tiered capacity-building programme and associated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.
