description:
GOVERNMENT OF SOMALILAND

REQUEST FOR EXPERESSION OF INTEREST FOR

CEPCU Environmental Specialist

1. Background

The Government of Somaliland has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Enhancing Public Resource Management Project (SERP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services (individual consultant). to develop a lean, portfolio-focused coordination and performance management function that strengthens oversight, reduces implementation fragmentation, and promotes institutional learning across the World Bank-financed portfolio. Therefore, the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development (MoFED) intends to hire an International Environmental Specialist. The Environmental Specialist consultant will fill this gap through portfolio-level advisory support, monitoring, and knowledge transfer.

2. Objective(s) of the Assignment

The Environmental Specialist will provide technical advisory support, portfolio-level environmental safeguards oversight, environmental risk monitoring, and systems strengthening support across World Bank-financed operations in Somaliland. The Specialist is also expected to ensure knowledge transfer to designated government counterparts, while implementation responsibility remains with the respective PIUs and implementing entities.

3. Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities

  • Provide technical advice on environmental risk management across all World Bank-financed projects in line with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) during project preparation and implementation stages, including providing oversight to PIUs Environmental Specialists to ensure compliance or projects to the Bank’s environmental standards during project implementation.
  • Support the responsible implementing agencies in developing or providing inputs to World Bank-required documents at the project preparation stage, including the, ESCP, SEP, ESMF, LMP, and ESSA/Program Action Plan, as applicable to the financing instrument and project context.
  • Provide technical guidance to implementing agencies on environmental screening and scoping processes and review outputs to ensure compliance with ESF requirements.
  • Develop and update project-level environmental risk management instruments in close coordination with the CEPCU team and implementing units and advise on implementation of environmental risk mitigation measures as outlined in the ESCP, ESMF, and LMP.
  • Ensure all advisory support is aligned with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, including applicable ESSs and Good Practice Notes.
  • Prepare and provide advisory support for the implementation of environmental framework instruments (including ESMPs) to meet the World Bank's Environmental and Social Standards for IPFs and Program Action Plans.
  • Provide advice to the PIUs Environmental and Procurement Specialists on integrating environmental risk management provisions into procurement activities, ensuring mitigation measures are factored into procurement planning and are adequately resourced.
  • Conduct regular monitoring of compliance to existing environmental mitigation measures across the portfolio and provide technical backstopping in the preparation of environmental assessment and monitoring reports and provide a portfolio wide report on environmental compliance, risks, and proposed mitigation measures to MoFED and the World Bank through the Head of CEPCU.
  • In close coordination with the Social Development Specialists, monitor the grievance redress mechanism(s) of the portfolio and provide advice to PIUs on addressing environmental and social-related grievances and incidents.
  • Develop and maintain a portfolio-level environmental risk tracking system, including consolidated ESCP compliance monitoring across all Bank-financed operations.
  • Develop and implement a structured capacity-building plan, including training modules, on-the-job mentoring, and performance assessments of the PIUs.
  • Conduct structured knowledge transfer on all the above activities to civil servants assigned to the CEPCU for environment and ensure counterparts are ready to assume the role by January 2028.
  • Consolidate lessons learned from portfolio implementation and project completion to inform future operations.  

 4. Selection Criteria

The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience, and skills should be included:

5. Consultant’s Qualifications and Experience

A. Education:

  • Master's degree in environmental sciences or a related field, including Ecology, Natural Resources Management, Geosciences, Environmental Policy, or equivalent disciplines

B. Professional Experience:

  • Minimum of ten (10) years of relevant professional experience in environmental impact assessments, environmental audits, legal and policy review, and formulation of environmental safeguard management action plans for projects financed by international donor agencies, preferably the World Bank.
  • At least 8 years of experience in donor-funded programs, with a proven track record in applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent standards.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing environmental instruments (e.g., ESMF, ESIAs, ESMPs, screening tools, guidelines, training materials) and providing quality assurance, advise or oversight functions.
  • Knowledge of relevant Somaliland and Somalia environmental laws and regulatory frameworks is an advantage.
  • Experience working in fragile and conflict-affected environments is an advantage

C. Competencies: 

  • Proven ability to advise on and support project environmental assessment and preparation.
  • Excellent interpersonal, writing, and communication skills; English proficiency is essential.
  • Knowledge of ICT-based Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Demonstrated capacity to provide on-the-job training on environmental standards and achieve successful knowledge transfer

D. Reporting and other Deliverables: The Environmental Specialist will report to the Head of CEPCU and work under the overall guidance of the Director General, MoFED

E. Duration of Assignment: The assignment is expected to take 12 months.

F. The Ministry of Finance and Economic Development with the Center of Excellence for Portfolio Coordination Unit (CEPCU) invites potential candidates for Environmental Specialist as per the Terms of Reference. Interested Individual Consultants shall provide the following: (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference persons; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; and (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

G. Submission Requirements: The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023 and March 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

H. The Individual Consultant will be hired based on the World Bank’s Guidelines for Selection and Employment of Consultants (July 1, 2016, and updated November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023) and March 2025.

I. Mode of submission of Applications: Interested applicants can access additional information, including the detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment, by visiting the following website: https://www.slmof.org or can be provided upon submission of application by e-mail or in person. The e-mail address is provided below from 8:30 to 16:00 p.m. Hargeisa time (Excluding public holidays).

J. Deadline: Expressions of interest (EOI) and CV must be delivered (by e-mail or in person) in a written form of hard copy (if not by e-mail) to the address below by 6th August 2026 at 4:00 pm (Hargeisa Time) – marked clearly as – Environmental Specialist.

Reference No.: MTHUD/F/9/IRDP/Consultancy/4/Jaffna Outer Island, MoTHUD

STEP Procurement Activity No.: LK-UDA-PMU-551519-CS-QCBS, World Bank

1.    The Government of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE) Project. The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development (MoTHUD), serving as the Executing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2.    The consulting services (“the Services”) include an integrated sustainability assessment to identify and prioritize environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, climate-resilient and financially viable tourism and related livelihood investment opportunities in the Jaffna Outer Islands. The Services include biodiversity, environmental, climate and safeguard assessment; socio-economic, cultural and community assessment; market and demand assessment; technical and infrastructure assessment; financial and economic analysis; institutional and governance capacity assessment; sustainable investment planning and prioritization; stakeholder engagement; and preparation of an evidence-based implementation roadmap for future investment planning.

3.    The total duration of the assignment is expected to be twelve (12) months from contract commencement and expected to commence in mid of December 2026.

4.    The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.transport.gov.lk/ (Urban Development  > Integrated Regional Development Programme).

5.    The Chairman of the Ministry Consultants Procurement Committee, on behalf of the REVIVE Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required firm-level qualifications, relevant experience and institutional capacity to perform the assignment.

 The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

a.     Legal status, core business and institutional experience: The Consultant shall be a legally registered consulting firm with at least ten (10) years of corporate experience in one or more of the following areas: sustainable tourism and destination development; coastal and marine resource management; biodiversity conservation; socio-economic and livelihood development; financial and economic analysis; and investment planning.

b.     Comparable assignment experience: Successful completion, during the last ten (10) years, of at least three (3) comparable consultancy assignments. A comparable assignment means a master plan, tourism or destination development plan, sustainability assessment, feasibility study, investment plan, or similar strategic planning assignment comparable in nature and multidisciplinary complexity to the present assignment. Collectively, the assignments shall demonstrate experience across several relevant dimensions, including sustainable tourism or destination development, biodiversity and environmental assessment, social and livelihood assessment, climate resilience, infrastructure planning, financial and economic analysis, institutional or governance assessment, stakeholder engagement, and investment prioritization. At least one (1) assignment shall have been undertaken in an island, coastal, remote, environmentally sensitive, or similarly complex geographic setting.

c.     Multidisciplinary institutional capability: Demonstrated institutional capacity to undertake a multidisciplinary sustainability assessment. The Consultant, including any joint venture, shall collectively demonstrate capacity in sustainable tourism and destination development, biodiversity and environmental assessment, social and livelihood assessment, climate resilience, infrastructure planning, financial and economic analysis, and institutional or governance assessment.

d.     Relevant geographic experience: Experience in Sri Lanka, South Asia, or other coastal and island environments with comparable ecological, social and implementation conditions will be considered an advantage during shortlisting.

The Consultant shall provide documentary evidence, such as signed contracts, completion certificates, client references, or equivalent records, to substantiate the firm-level experience claimed.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The Consultant shall provide information demonstrating that they have required qualification and relevant

experience to perform the services and should submit:

i)     Company profiles, qualifications of board of members, brochures, etc.

ii)    List of similar projects completed including foreign funded projects over the last ten years, along with the size of the associate consultancy contracts in man month and US Dollars equivalent terms (with contact details of the client).

iii)   Audited financial statement for last five years.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.    Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Please note that a firm / organization is allowed to participate in only one submission as a sole consultant, joint venture partner or a sub –Consultant.

7.    A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025).

8.    Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 0900 to 1600 hours, except Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.

REPÚBLICA DE MOÇAMBIQUE

MINISTÉRIO DAS COMUNICAÇÕES E TRANSFORMAÇÃO DIGITAL             

Projecto de Aceleração Digital de Moçambique (PADIM)

 

PEDIDO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

Fiscalização das obras de Reabilitação e Apetrechamento do Edifício Sede do MCTD

 

N.º do Crédito : IDA-71820-MZ

Referência n.º: 74/MDAP/MCTD/CS-CQS/26

O Governo de Moçambique recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para a implementação do Projeto de Aceleração Digital e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos na contratação de serviços de consultoria para a Fiscalização das obras de Reabilitação e Apetrechamento do Edifício Sede do MCTD.

O objetivo desta contratação é realizar a fiscalização técnica da obra de reabilitação e apetrechamento, garantindo conformidade técnica, contratual, ambiental, social e de saúde e segurança ocupacional e da comunidade durante a execução das obras, assegurando o controlo de qualidade, prazos e custos, bem como a implementação das provisões ambientais, sociais e de saúde e segurança para a mitigação de riscos durante todo o ciclo da empreitada

 

O Consultor deverá desenvolver uma abordagem de Fiscalização da obra e reporte da conformidade técnica, incluindo, aspectos ambientais, sociais, de saúde e segurança ocupacional e da comunidade, tendo como critério o MBPAS-C e outros requisitos aplicáveis; desenvolver um modelo de recolha de dados semanais/mensais ambientais, sociais e de saúde e segurança para a concepção do relatório mensal a ser submetido ao dono da obra; desenvolver ferramentas de inspeção e aprovação de equipamentos (ex.: andaimes), veículos e máquinas antes da sua utilização no local da obra. Reter copias de registos de aprovação no local da obra; desenvolver ferramentas de inspeção diária/semanal dos aspectos ambientais, sociais, de saúde e segurança no local de obra, incluindo mecanismos de registo, reporte e seguimento do tratamento das lacunas (ex.: não conformidades) identificadas, entre outros.

Os Termos de Referência (TdR) detalhados para esta contratação podem ser obtidos no endereço indicado abaixo.

O Ministério das Comunicações e Transformação Digital convida as firmas de consultoria elegíveis (“Consultores”) a manifestarem o seu interesse em realizar a consultoria acima mencionada.

Os Consultores interessados deverão apresentar informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e experiência relevante para a execução dos Serviços.

Critérios para pré-qualificação (lista curta): i) A firma deve ser de categoria II – Gestão de contratos e Fiscalização de obras, 3ª, 4ª, 5ª, 6ª ou 7ª classe e legalmente constituída em Moçambique; ii) a firma deve ter mínimo cinco (5) anos de experiência comprovada em fiscalização de obras públicas, preferencialmente em reabilitação de edifícios e financiadas pelo Banco Mundial; iii) Capacidade comprovada para emissão de relatórios técnicos.

Os Especialistas-Chave não serão avaliados na fase de pré-qualificação.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de IPF (setembro de 2023), que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflitos de interesse.

Os Consultores podem associar-se a outras firmas para reforçar as suas qualificações, devendo indicar claramente se a associação será sob a forma de consórcio (joint venture) e/ou subconsultoria. No caso de consórcio, todos os parceiros serão conjunta e solidariamente responsáveis pela totalidade do contrato, caso sejam selecionados.

O Consultor será selecionado de acordo com o método de Seleção Baseada nas Qualificações do Consultor (CQS), conforme estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

Informações adicionais podem ser obtidas no endereço abaixo durante o horário de expediente, das 08:00 às 15:30 (hora local).

As Manifestações de Interesse devem ser entregues por escrito no endereço abaixo até 4 de Agosto de 2026.

Component 2 of the “Enhancing Resilience to Natural Disasters in the Kyrgyz Republic” (ERIK) Project: Improving the safety of school and preschool educational institutions within the framework of the State Program “Safe School and Preschool Educational Organizations in the Kyrgyz Republic for 2015-2024”

Responsible government agencies: Ministry of Education and Science of the Kyrgyz Republic and the State Agency for Architecture, Construction and Housing and Communal Services under the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic.

The objective of this component is to improve the safety and functionality of the existing infrastructure of public schools by providing support to the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic within the framework of the State Program “Safe School and Preschool Educational Organizations in the Kyrgyz Republic for 2015-2024”. To achieve the set objectives, measures developed and implemented under Component 2 are aimed at retrofitting school facilities to ensure seismic safety, energy efficiency and improved functionality of schools.

The Project will modernize 40 schools, of which 10 under the Main Project and 30 under the Additional Financing. These Terms of Reference cover those schools where construction and renovation works are already underway or planned for 2026-2027.

The ERIK Project requires consulting services to provide “Outreach and awareness-raising work and media coverage for the Project ‘Enhancing Resilience to Natural Disasters in the Kyrgyz Republic ‘’.

Within the framework of the Project, the modernization of 40 schools is planned, including 10 schools under the Main Project and 30 schools under the Additional Financing. This Terms of Reference covers the schools where construction and rehabilitation works are being carried out or are planned for 2026–2027.

The ERIK Project requires consulting services to support “Information, Awareness-Raising Activities and Media Coverage of the ‘Enhancing Resilience to Natural Disasters in the Kyrgyz Republic’ Project.”

The objective of this assignment is to provide consulting support to the “Enhancing Resilience to Natural Disasters in the Kyrgyz Republic” (ERIK) Project in the development of media products (including videos, infographics, banners, and other information materials), as well as to inform the target audience and other stakeholders about the activities and achievements of the ERIK Project.

The Consultant will provide technical and advisory services to support “Information and Awareness-Raising Activities and Media Coverage of the ‘Enhancing Resilience to Natural Disasters in the Kyrgyz Republic’ Project.”

The assignment is expected to commence in September 2026. The anticipated duration of the assignment is 24 months following the signing of the contract with the successful bidder.

The estimated budget for the assignment, inclusive of all applicable taxes, shall not exceed USD 50,000.00.

Detailed terms of reference (TOR) can be found at the following links www.zakupki.gov.kg (Tenders announced by Projects), www.donors.kg, www.mchs.gov.kg  or at the address below.

The “Enhancing Resilience to Natural Disasters in the Kyrgyz Republic” (ERIK) Project invites eligible consulting firms (Consultants) to express their interest in providing services for Information and Awareness-Raising Activities and Media Coverage of the “Enhancing Resilience to Natural Disasters in the Kyrgyz Republic” (ERIK) Project.

Interested companies must provide information confirming their qualifications and relevant experience in providing services.

At the Expressions of Interest stage, the Consultant must meet the following minimum requirements:

Les critères de sélection de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

a) Activités principales ou expérience générale du consultant et nombre d’années d’expérience :

  • Expériences similaires aux prestations objet des présents TdR et fournir des références vérifiables et des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution pour chacun des projets similaires présent

C. Capacité technique et managériale du consultant

6. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

1. CONTEXTE

Le Gouvernement du Sénégal à travers le Ministère de l’Education nationale met en œuvre le Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE) financé par la Banque mondiale.

Dans le cadre du renforcement de l'équipe de l'Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP), le PAPSE recrute un(e) Assistant(e) comptable.

 

2. DESCRIPTION DU POSTE

L’Assistant (e) comptable, Placé (e) sous l'autorité du Responsable administratif et financier et du Comptable du Projet, aura notamment pour principales responsabilités de :

  • assister le Comptable dans la mise en place et le bon fonctionnement du système de suivi financier et comptable informatisé du Projet ;
  • fournir à partir du système comptable FINPRONET les informations comptables, en liens avec l’inventaire et nécessaires à la préparation des Demande de Remboursement de Fonds (DRF) et les Demande de Paiement Direct (DPD) pour le réapprovisionnement du compte désigné et les paiements directs des fournisseurs et autres prestataires ;
  • assurer la tenue de la comptabilité du Projet, en appui au Comptable du Projet conformément aux procédures d'imputation comptable (imputation suivant les codes de la comptabilité générale, analytique, financière, budgétaire et géographique);
  • assurer la saisie informatique au jour le jour de toutes les pièces comptables;
  • assurer la tenue régulière et conforme des registres comptables;
  • participer à l’élaboration des budgets et des plans de travail annuel en concertation avec les autres membres de l’équipe ;

 

 

 

 

 

  • Préparer les ordres de paiements à soumettre au contrôle du Comptable avant la validation par le RAF;
  • Assurer le paiement des indemnités des prestataires des daara ;
  • Assurer le paiement des subventions à verser aux borom daara ;
  • assurer le classement et l’archivage des pièces justificatives des opérations du Projet et tout document d’ordre financier ou comptable suivant les principes prédéfinis ;
  • produire les statistiques mensuelles sur les délais de paiement, au niveau de chaque acteur de la chaîne, pour les dépenses effectuées ;
  • Exécuter toutes autres tâches, en lien avec sa mission, qui lui seront confiées par le Comptable.

 

3. PROFIL DES CANDIDATS

Le candidat devra avoir :

  • un diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur (BAC+3 au minimum) en comptabilité, gestion financière, audit, ou équivalent. 
  • une expérience professionnelle de deux (02) ans minimum dans le domaine de la comptabilité et de la gestion financière dans une structure privée ou projet de développement.
  • une excellente compréhension des rapports financiers ;
  • une bonne aptitude dans l’organisation des tâches et du travail sous pression dans une équipe pluridisciplinaire ;
  • une bonne connaissance pratique des procédures de décaissement et système de comptabilité et de gestion financière des principaux bailleurs de fonds serait un atout
  • une bonne connaissance des logiciels comptables ;
  • une aptitude à travailler en équipe et sous pression ;
  • une maitrise des procédures de la Banque Mondiale ;
  • une bonne connaissance des logiciels usuels (Word, Excel, Power point, Email et autres outils de communication);
  • une connaissance  du logiciel TOM PRO ou FINPRONET;
  • une bonne maitrise de la langue française, et la connaissance de l’anglais est un atout.

Une expérience dans un projet financé par la Banque mondiale ou un autre partenaire technique et financier sera considérée comme un atout.

 

4. CONDITIONS D'EMPLOI

L’Assistant (e) comptable, sera recruté (e ) sur la base d'un contrat à durée déterminée CDD) d’un (01) an renouvelable en fonction des performances, des besoins du Projet et de la disponibilité des financements.

 

5. DOSSIER DE CANDIDATURE

Les candidats intéressés sont invités à transmettre un dossier comprenant :

  • une lettre de motivation précisant le poste sollicité ;
  • un curriculum vitae détaillé, daté et signé ;
  • les copies des diplômes et certificats de formation légalisées ;
  • les attestations ou certificats de travail justifiant les expériences professionnelles ;
  • les coordonnées de trois (03) références professionnelles.

 

6. MODALITES DE RECRUTEMENT

Le recrutement sera effectué à l'issue d'une présélection sur dossier, suivie d'un entretien avec les candidats présélectionnés.

Le Projet PAPSE applique les principes d'égalité des chances, de transparence et de mérite dans le processus de recrutement conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale.

7. DEPOT DES CANDIDATURES

Les dossiers de candidature devront être déposés ou transmis au plus tard le jeudi 20 août 2026 à 23h59 mm TU à l'adresse suivante : recrutement.papse@education.sn

L'objet du courrier électronique devra préciser le poste concerné :  Candidature au poste d'Assistant comptable.

 

Seuls les candidats présélectionnés seront contactés pour la suite du processus

Objavljeno: lipanj 2026.

 

1.       Republika Hrvatska je zaprimila financiranje od Svjetske banke kako bi se pokrio trošak financiranja Projekta integriranih usluga zemljišne administracije i pravosua, IBRD Zajam 9645-HR te namjerava iskoristiti dio sredstava za plaanja u okviru Ugovora za nabavu tehnike usluge digitalizacije runo voenih zemljišnih knjiga. Projekt zajedniki provode provedbene institucije Ministarstvo pravosua, uprave i digitalne transformacije i Dravna geodetska uprava.

2.    Ministarstvo pravosua, uprave i digitalne transformacije poziva prihvatljive Ponuditelje da dostave zapeaene ponude za pruanje tehnike usluge digitalizacije runo voenih zemljišnih knjiga.

3.    Nadmetanje se provodi kao domae konkurentsko nadmetanje korištenjem Poziva na dostavu ponuda (PDP), kako je to navedeno u „Propisima o nabavi za Zajmoprimce IPF-a“ Svjetske banke, izdanje rujan  2025. g. ("Propisi o nabavi") i otvoren je za sve prihvatljive Ponuditelje kako je definirano u Propisima o nabavi.

  1. Ponude e se ocjenjivati u skladu s postupkom ocjenjivanja utvrenim u dokumentima za nadmetanje. Sljedei ponderi primjenjuju se za Kriteriji za ocjenjivanje (ukljuujui tehnike i necjenovne kriterije): 40% i za cijenu ponude: 60 %.

5.    Zainteresirani prihvatljivi Ponuditelji mogu dobiti dodatne informacije od Jedinice za provedbu projekta (JPP) i pregledati dokumentaciju o nabavi tijekom radnog vremena od 10:00 do 15:00 sati na dolje navedenoj adresi.

6.    Zainteresirani prihvatljivi Ponuditelji mogu preuzeti dokumentaciju o nabavi na hrvatskom jeziku nakon podnošenja pisanog zahtjeva na e-mail adresu tender@zikprojekt.hr. Dokument se zainteresiranim ponuditeljima dostavlja iskljuivo elektronikom poštom.

7.    Ponude se moraju dostaviti na nie navedenu adresu na dan ili prije 4. kolovoza 2026. do 11 sati. Elektroniko nadmetanje nee biti dozvoljeno. Zakašnjele ponude e biti odbijene. Vanjske omotnice oznaene "IZVORNIK" i unutarnje omotnice oznaene "TEHNIKI DIO" bit e javno otvorene u nazonosti ovlaštenih predstavnika Ponuditelja i svih koji odlue prisustvovati na nie navedenoj adresi 4. kolovoza 2026. do 11 sati. Sve omotnice s oznakom "FINANCIJSKI DIO" ostat e neotvorene i uvat e se sigurno pohranjene kod Naruitelja do drugog javnog otvaranja ponuda.

8.    Uz  svaku ponudu potrebno je priloiti Jamstvo za ozbiljnost ponude u iznosu od 36.000,00 EUR.

9     Potrebno je obratiti pozornost na Propise o nabavi kojim se od Zajmoprimca zahtijeva da objavi informacije o stvarnom vlasniku uspješnog ponuditelja, u sklopu Obavijesti o dodjeli ugovora, koristei Obrazac o otkrivanju informacija stvarnog vlasnika koji je dio dokumentacije o nabavi.

NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                         Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Financial Management Specialist (FMS) 

No: MW-NLGFC-563892-CS-INDIV

                                     Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026        

 

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Financial Management Specialist (FMS) on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Financial Management Specialist (FMS) tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Financial Management Specialist (FMS) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the Financial Management Specialist position is to ensure the sound financial management of the project in compliance with the Financing Agreement, Government of Malawi public financial management regulations, including the Public Finance Management Act and related regulations, treasury instructions and IFMIS desk instructions, project operations manual, and World Bank financial management requirements. The Financial Management Specialist will be responsible for planning, budgeting, accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, funds management, audit coordination, and financial compliance to ensure that project resources are used efficiently, effectively, transparently, and for their intended purposes.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Preparation of Financial Statements in accordance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) of the Project within six months from the end of the financial year; 
  2. Coordination of the preparation of a consolidated project budget, cash flow forecasts, execution and monitoring including liaising with key ministries and departments for budget planning and execution; 
  3. Ensure that the Project resources are used in accordance with the conditions of the relevant financing agreement, Project Operation Manual with due attention to economy and efficiency, and only for the purposes for which the financing was provided;
  4. Preparation of disbursement requests and financial justifications for the project and submit to Treasury and the World Bank;
  5. Produce monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual financial reports from central and district levels, as part of the implementation of the Project;
  6. Coordinate closely with procurement and technical teams against the work plan and project objectives to ensure comprehensive mitigation measures are taken.
  7. Ensure that all necessary supporting documents, records, and accounts with physical documents have been maintained in respect of all project activities, including expenditures reported using Statement of Expenditures (SOE) or Interim Financial Reports (IFRs) methods of reporting.
  8. Periodically review the performance of control functions to ensure that internal controls are sufficient and functioning correctly and that Financial Performance of the Project is Satisfactory;
  9. Coordinate project external and internal audits and responding to management letter;
  10. Coordinate as necessary with Internal and External Audit, Government of Malawi and Bank supervision missions, including attending to follow up on findings and recommendations;
  11. Maintain accurate and traceable schedules for VAT and timely remittance of tax deductions to the Malawi Revenue Authority;
  12. Advise the Project Coordinator and Director of Finance on all financial and control considerations of the project;
  13. Supervise and strengthen the capacity of PIT and local authorities in the knowledge of the rules and procedures of the financial management of the World Bank;
  14. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics; and
  15. Undertake all other duties and responsibilities commensurate with the role and level of this position as may be requested by the Project Coordinator.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

       i.  A Bachelor’s degree in accounting and finance/ or equivalent qualification;

  1. A professional accounting qualification such as CPA (MW), ACCA, CIMA etc.;
  2. A master’s degree in accounting; auditing; finance; business administration will be an added advantage;
  3. A minimum of 8 years of experience in financial management in the public sector;
  4. Experience of financial management in donor funded projects and/or audit experience is considered an advantage; 
  5. Member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in Malawi (ICAM);  
  6. Outstanding numeracy, planning, organizing and controlling skills;
  7. Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills, communication and analytical skills;
  8. Ability to work in teams and articulation with a diverse audience;
  9. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  10. Ability and experience in training / mentoring staff in the area of financial management is an advantage;
  11. Willingness to work under pressure, tight timelines, and with minimum supervision;
  12. Knowledge of audit techniques; and
  13. Upholding of anticorruption and ant bribery ethics.

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

 

The Financial Management Specialist (FMS) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Financial Management Specialist will occasionally be required to travel to district authorities in Malawi to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation (financial management).

7.REPORTING

The Financial Management Specialist will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Finance and Fiscal Decentralization at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support the local authorities’ financial management teams.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and a Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant(INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday 11th  September  2026.

 

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

 

The Executive Director

National Local Government Finance Committee

Area 14, Red Cross Building

Presidential Way

P.O. Box 31162

Lilongwe 3

  1. Introduction Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Project Coordinator on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Project Coordinator at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Project Coordinator are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the Project Coordinator position is to provide strategic leadership and day-to-day management of the project to ensure the timely and effective delivery of project activities and achievement of project objectives. The Project Coordinator will coordinate planning, budgeting, procurement, contract administration, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, human resource management, governance arrangements, stakeholder engagement, and implementation support missions, while ensuring compliance with Government and donor requirements.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Coordination: Ensure cross-component and cross-institutional coordination and linkages through information sharing, joint implementation of project activities and provide strategic guidance and coordination to the PIT members on all project related activities in order to keep workflow on track;

 

  1. Planning: Spearhead and coordinate the preparation and implementation of Project’s Annual Procurement Plan in line with agreed timelines and budgets; spearhead the planning and implementation of project activities to each activity specific goals and project goals overall in coordination with the PIT technical specialists and relevant key stakeholders; ensure that detailed activity plans are prepared and monitored; be proactive and provide solutions to bring forward delayed/off-track activities; ensure alignment of all activities with the annual work plan and budget;  

 

  1. Budgeting: Lead the timely development of consolidated project budgets for planned activities, cash flow forecasts, executing and monitoring of budgets, and ensure that the activity budgets are aligned with the annual work plan and consistent; coordinate with the PIT Financial Management Specialist and liaise with key ministries and departments and local authorities for budget planning and execution;

 

  1. Procurement: In coordination with the PIT Procurement Specialist ensure the timely preparation, execution and updated of procurement plans at the central level and at the district level; liaise with all relevant stakeholders; ensure that all procurements for consultants, goods and works under each procurement plan are carried out in accordance with the agreed procedures, including the Financing Agreement; the World Bank Procurement Guidelines/regulations and the Government of Malawi Public Procurement and Disposal of Assets Act 2025 and World Bank policies.

 

  1. Contract Management: Lead the management of contracts for consultants and other service providers, and work with all PIT members to evaluate potential problems and technical hitches and timely develop solutions;

 

  1. Financial Management: Manage financial resources of the project in coordination with the PIT Financial Management Specialist; ensure that all project activities are executed in accordance with the Financing Agreements, and the policies and standards of all relevant implementing agencies; ensure strict adherence to project budgets by monitoring expenses and implementing cost-saving measures; and ensure the timely preparation of financial statements and audits according to the Financing Agreement; ensure that the project is timely audited by the National Audit Office and submit an annual audit report to Government of Malawi and World Bank  not later than 30th September.

 

  1. Environmental and Social Safeguards: Ensure that all environment and social safeguards are adhered in all activities financed by the GESD 2.0 project and are managed in accordance with World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP); coordinate with relevant PIT specialists, district officials and relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies to ensure eligible local authorities develop and implements environmental safeguards issues in all the sub project sites;

 

  1. Project Office Management and Staff Management: Manage the PIT on a day-to-day basis; coordinate and supervise administrative activities necessary for the successful implementation of GESD 2.0; supervise and be responsible for the specialists’ time commitment and performance on the project; ensure timely preparation and submission of all consultants reports from the Project Engineers; Financial Management Specialist; Procurement Specialist; Monitoring and Evaluation Officer; Safeguards Specialist; Occupation and Health Specialist; Environmental Safeguard Specialist and all implementing agencies; undertake staff performance appraisals with support from  NLGFC; and

 

  1. Oversight Meetings, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Supervision: Facilitate key project meetings (quarterly project progress meetings, meetings of the Project Steering Committee, meetings of the Project Technical Committee) and liaison with stakeholders regularly and submit minutes of respective meetings within 48 hours; serve as Secretary to the PTC and supervise and ensure execution of any decisions approved by the PTC; ensure that all activities at central and at district level are carried out according to the provisions of the Malawi Government legislation and as stipulated in the Project Operations Manual and Financing Agreement; prepare and submit monthly, quarterly and annual project progress reports to the Executive Director and the World Bank task team; prepare and submit bi-annual updates on project progress against the project results framework; organize World Bank implementation support missions, including follow up on mission recommendations.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. A Master's Degree in Project Management, Economics, Development Studies, Finance/Accounting, Business Administration, or Engineering from a recognized institution;
  2. At least 8 years relevant working experience in senior positions or project management positions in public sector projects with a focus on planning, budget management and execution;
  3. At least 5 years of relevant working experience with Malawi’s Public Financial Management Structures; experience in fiscal decentralization is considered an asset;
  4. Demonstrated proficiency with project and budget management software / tracking tools, project fiduciary procedures;
  5. Demonstrated problem-solving skills and managerial skills, including proactivity;
  6. Demonstrated experience to work effectively with and in multi-sectoral teams;
  7. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  8. Highly motivated with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy;
  9. Experience in working with the World Bank, multi-lateral development partners or bilateral partners is considered an asset;
  10. Willingness to work under pressure, tight timelines, and with minimum supervision;
  11. Excellent communication and report writing skills and be fluent in English; and
  12. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics.

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Project Coordinator will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Coordinator will occasionally be required to travel to district authorities in Malawi to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

7.REPORTING

The Project Coordinator will report to the Executive Director of National Local Government Finance Committee for all the project progress and implementation issues.

REPÚBLICA DE MOÇAMBIQUE

MINISTÉRIO DAS OBRAS PÚBLICAS, HABITAÇÃO E RECURSOS HDRICOS

DIRECÇÃO NACIONAL DE ABASTECIMENTO DE ÁGUA E SANEAMENTO

 

PROJECTO DE ÁGUA SEGURA PARA VILAS E ZONAS RURAIS -P173518

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

 

CONTRATAÇÃO DE SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA PARA APOIAR NA MELHORIA DE RECURSOS VISUAIS DO DASHBOARD DO PROJECTO ÁGUA SEGURA

 

GRANT. N.º D941-MZ

Ref. N.º MZ-DNAAS-85-CS-INDV

 

1. O Governo de Moçambique, recebeu do Banco Mundial o financiamento de 150 Milhões de Dólares Americanos para o Projeto Água Segura para Zonas Rurais e Vilas. O principal resultado do Projecto é aumentar os serviços de água e saneamento geridos de forma segura em pequenas cidades e áreas rurais seleccionadas das províncias de Nampula e Zambézia, na Região Norte de Moçambique.

 

2. O escopo dos serviços para a consultoria inclui diagnóstico inicial, mas não se limita à: (i) Propor ajustes técnicos nas bases de dados e ferramenta em uso pelo Projecto para o Dashboard (Kobo, Excell e Power BI) e criação de novos componentes visuais caso se justifique o seu uso e definir as responsabilidades de cada um dos Usuários do Dashboard assim como a disponibilização de dados para o mesmo; ii) Implementar regras de validação; criar uma visão da qualidade dos dados (integridade, actualização, erros); fornecer um dicionário de dados e um mapa de transformação; configurar atualizações programadas com alertas de erro e atribuir a propriedade dos dados para controle de qualidade; iii) Configurar acesso baseado em funções para utilizadores DNAAS/AIAS/provinciais/distritais; fornecer uma matriz de acesso baseado em funções e uma lista de acesso; documentar as responsabilidades dos utilizadores (entrada de dados, controlo de qualidade, verificação).; iv) Aplicar um tema consistente alinhado com o estilo utilizado pelo Projecto/Governo/Banco Mundial; redesenhar layouts para melhorar a clareza; garantir acessibilidade (contraste, tamanho da fonte); permitir a tradução português/inglês e visualização por província/distrito quando aplicável; v) Optimizar consultas, DAX e recursos visuais; definir e implementar estratégias de atualização (por exemplo, atualização incremental); Documentar as melhorias de desempenho alcançadas em relação à linha de base.

 

3. Os Termos de Referência (TdRs) detalhados para a consultoria podem ser solicitados através do seguinte endereço: procurementpas@gmail.com

 

4. A Direcção Nacional de Abastecimento de Água e Saneamento (DNAAS), convida os consultores individuais qualificados, a manifestar seu interesse em prestar os serviços. Os consultores interessados deverão apresentar informação demonstrando possuir qualificações necessárias e experiência relevante para a execução dos serviços (CV, descrição de serviços similares, experiência em condições semelhantes, disponibilidade, etc.).

5. O consultor deve possuir, pelo menos, as seguintes qualificações e experiência: (i) Apresentar o portfólio de trabalhos anteriores em visualização de dados; ii) Ao menos 5 anos de experiência em visualização de dados, BI e desenho web; iii) Experiência comprovada em Power BI (modelagem de dados, DAX, controle de acesso, ajuste de desempenho); a apresentação de certificações será considerada uma vantagem;  iv) Experiência na integração do KoboToolbox e do Excel (ou ferramentas similares) em fluxos de trabalho de BI; v)  Experiência e familiaridade com a monitoria e avaliação aplicada ao sector de WASH será considerada uma vantagem vi)  Conhecimento e habilidade sobre as boas práticas de design digital; e v)  Experiência com gestão e governança da qualidade de dados, workshops com partes interessadas e formação (necessária a proficiência em português).

 

6. A atenção dos Consultores interessados é chamada para a Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 dos "Regulamentos de Aquisição para Mutuários do IPF" do Banco Mundial, de fevereiro de 2025 ("Regulamentos de Contratação Pública"), que estabelecem a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

 

7. O Consultor será seleccionado de acordo com o método de Selecção de Consultor Individual conforme estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

8. Mais informações podem ser obtidas no endereço abaixo, no horário normal de expediente (7h30 às 15h30). As manifestações de interesse devem ser entregues por escrito a:

Endereço: Ministério das Obras Públicas, Habitação e Recursos Hídricos

Av. Karl Marx nº 606, P.O. Box 268 * Maputo, Telefone: 326081, R/C

Departamento de Aquisições,

Email: procurementpas@gmail.com

 

As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser entregues em versão física na língua portuguesa, no endereço acima e por e-mail para os endereços acima indicados até 15:30 horas do dia 04 de Setembro de 2026.

 (MOZAGRIBIZ)

 

 (Adiantamento da Preparação Programática No V5510)

                                           Manifestação de Interesse

                                                                                                                            

O Governo de Moçambique, através do Ministério da Agricultura, Ambiente e Pescas (MAAP), recebeu um Adiantamento de Fundos do Grupo Banco Mundial (BM) para financiar as actividades de preparação do Programa do Desenvolvimento das Cadeias de Valor de Agronegócio (MOZAGRIBIZ), que será implementado nos Corredores de Desenvolvimento de Nacala, Beira, Maputo e Limpopo.

 

Assim, o MAAP pretende utilizar parte destes recursos para contratar, por um período de dois (2) anos, consultores individuais para integrar a Unidade de Implementação do Projecto. Neste contexto, convida aos candidatos qualificados e experientes a manifestarem interesse para o preenchimento da vaga de Especialista em Procurement, mediante a apresentação de carta de candidatura, Curriculum Vitae actualizado, cópias de diplomas ou certificados de habilitações académicas e 3 referências de trabalhos recentes que possam ser contactadas durante o processo de avaliação.

 

  1. Qualificações Académicas

Os candidatos deverão possuir as seguintes competências e qualificações:

  • Licenciado numa das seguintes áreas: Economia, Gestão, Administração Pública, finanças públicas, Direito, Engenharia, Procurement, ou áreas afins;
  • Mínimo de 10 anos de experiência em procurement, com pelo menos 5 (cinco) anos em projectos financiados por fundos multilaterais, particularmente pelo Banco Mundial;
  • Capacidades demonstradas de organização e análise e capacidade de resolução de problemas para corresponder aos objetivos do Projeto/Programa e à elaboração e apresentação de relatórios financeiros, demonstrações e auditorias;
  • Capacidade demonstrada para assumir uma posição de liderança, motivar e promover a colaboração em um ambiente de trabalho em equipe;
  • Excelentes habilidades de comunicação escrita e verbal e capacidade de interagir e se comunicar de forma adequada e eficaz com funcionários do governo e o público;
  • Excelentes conhecimentos de informática e bom domínio do pacote MS (Word, PowerPoint, Project e Excel);
  • Capacidade de trabalhar de forma independente, prestar atenção aos detalhes e gerenciar várias tarefas em um ambiente acelerado;
  • Conhecimentos da língua inglesa, escrita e fala, como língua de trabalho.

 

Os critérios de elegibilidade, o estabelecimento da lista restrita e o procedimento de selecção devem estar de acordo com a “Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuarios de operações de IPF que está disponível no site https: World Bank Project Procurement or www.worldbank.org/procurement.

 

Os consultores serão selecionados na modalidade de Consultores Individuais(CI) e de uma forma competitiva tendo em conta as qualificações e a experiência do candidato.

 

Os consultores interessados poderão obter mais informações, incluindo os Termos de Referência, no endereço abaixo durante o horário de expediente, das 8h00 às 15h30.

 

As manifestações de interesse devem ser submetidas no endereço abaixo até às 15h30 min do dia 18 de Agosto de 2026 e mencionar “MOZAGRIBIZ Consultor individual_ a posição”.

 

As candidaturas devem ser enviadas em Português em envelope fechado ou digital único, indicando o assunto/posição a que se candidata. A não indicação do assunto/posição pode fazer com que a candidatura não seja considerada.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

 

West and Central Africa

Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES)

Project ID: P507938

Credit No.:8080-LR

 

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for RCU Public Private Partnership (PPP) Expert

 

Reference No.: LR-RCU-DARES-557723-CS-INDV

 

The Governments of Liberia, Sierra Leone, Benin, and Central Africa Republic have received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES) and intend to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consultant ("the Services") shall lead and be accountable for the development, harmonization, and implementation of PPP frameworks under Regional DARES, ensuring that procurement approaches, contractual arrangements, and regulatory frameworks are structured to maximize competition, mobilize private capital, and facilitate scalable deployment of DRE solutions across participating countries. The duration of the assignment is approximately five years, with an expected start in October 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://lecliberia.com/wp-content/uploads/R-DARES-TOR-POE-PPP-Expert-FINAL.docx 

 

The RESPITE Regional Coordination Unit (RCU) now invites eligible and selected Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should submit their Expressions of Interest (EOI), including their CV with information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the services (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills, etc.), and educational and professional qualification certificates.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s level or equivalent) in law, economics, finance, public policy, engineering, business administration, project finance, or a closely related field.
  • At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in PPP structuring, transaction advisory, infrastructure finance, concession design, competitive procurement, or related fields;
  • Demonstrated experience structuring, procuring, negotiating, or advising on PPP, concession, IPP, mini-grid, energy access, infrastructure, or utility transactions involving private sector participation;
  • Strong experience preparing or reviewing transaction documents, including RFQs, RFPs, concession agreements, grant agreements, implementation agreements, performance frameworks, and evaluation methodologies;
  • Demonstrated understanding of mini-grid, DRE, rural electrification, EaaS, or technology-neutral electricity access business models, including commercial, regulatory, and financing considerations;
  • Experience assessing bankability, risk allocation, tariff and subsidy design, blended finance structures, and financial viability of infrastructure or energy access transactions;
  • Experience working with government entities, regulators, utilities, developers, investors, lenders, legal advisers, and development finance institutions in transaction preparation or implementation;
  • Experience supporting competitive procurement, MSTs, RBF-linked tenders, or performance-based financing mechanisms is a strong advantage;
  • Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa, including fragile or lower-capacity environments, and across Anglophone and Francophone countries, is highly desirable;
  • Familiarity with World Bank or other MDB-financed operations, procurement requirements, and PPP or concession frameworks is a strong advantage.

 

The shortlisted candidates will be informed via email and invited for a virtual interview.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (Procurement Regulations”) as available on https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/c84273d1b230aeb2b0b8134de5dc8cd7-0290012025/original/Procurement-Regulations-7th-Edition-Sep-2025.pdf, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 0900 to 1700 hours GMT.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by email or by physical mail on or before Tuesday, August 18, 2026.

15th Street & Warner Avenue

Sinkor, Monrovia, Liberia

Experiencia general, la firma deberá demostrar experiencia general comprobada en al menos cinco (5) contratos sustancialmente terminados en los últimos 15 (quince) años en elaboración de proyecto y/o fiscalización de obras civiles y/o de infraestructura Urbana. (2011-2026).

Fiscalización, y/o gerenciamiento de obras que contemplen en su alcance obras de infraestructura urbana y/o obras civiles en general y/o mejoramiento de espacios públicos con una superficie mínima de 10.000 m2.

The Bidder shall demonstrate that its available liquid assets[1], lines of credit, and other financing sources are sufficient to meet the cash flow requirements for contract execution, taking into account the Bidder’s other ongoing contracts. The minimum required amount shall be no less than RMB 4 million.

The total amount of pending claims, arbitration proceedings, or other litigation shall not exceed 50% of the Bidder’s net assets.

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

SELECTION/ RECRUTEMENT D’UN LABORATOIRE POUR L’ANALYSE DE LA TOXICITE DES BOUES DES COLLECTEURS DANS LES ZONES 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7,  DANS LE CADRE DES TRAVAUX REHABILITATION DES INFRASTRUCTURES DE DRAINAGE A BANGUI

 

******************

 

NOM DU PAYS :

REPUBLIQUE CENTRAFRICAINE

NOM DU PROJET :

PROJET DES VILLES INCLUSIVES ET RESILIENTES EN RCA (PROVIR).

NO. IDENTIFICATION :

P 178774

FINANCEMENT :

BANQUE MONDIALE

NO. DU DON :

E-3700 – CF

INTITULE DE LA MISSION :

RECRUTEMENT D’UN LABORATOIRE POUR L’ANALYSE DE LA TOXICITE DES BOUES DES COLLECTEURS DANS LES ZONES 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7,  DANS LE CADRE DES TRAVAUX REHABILITATION DES INFRASTRUCTURES DE

DRAINAGE A BANGUI

N° DE REFERENCE

PROVIR - 14/SC/QC/23

I – INTRODUCTION

1. Le Gouvernement de la République Centrafricaine (RCA) prépare sur l’appui de la Banque mondiale un Projet appelé Projet des Villes Inclusives et Résilientes en RCA (PROVIR). L’objectif de développement du projet est d’améliorer l’accès à des infrastructures résilientes au climat, aux services de base dans certaines villes.

2. Ce Projet dont le montant s’élèvera à environ Soixante-dix (70) millions de dollars US sera financé par l’IDA en vue de (i) investir dans des infrastructures résilientes et des services de base pour améliorer la résilience des communautés et avec l’objectif plus large de contribuer à la reconstruction du contrat social, en particulier dans les villes secondaires et (ii) renforcer les capacités des entités gouvernementales étatiques et locales et impliquer les communautés à plusieurs niveaux (par exemple, processus de prise de décision en matière de planification urbaine et opportunités d’emploi, en particulier pour les femmes et les jeunes). 

3. Le Projet est élaboré autour de cinq composantes suivantes :

Composante 1 : Investissement dans la réduction des risques d’inondations et d’érosion ;

Composante 2 : Infrastructures de quartier et services de base ;

Composante 3 : Gestion de projet ;

Composante 4 : Intervention d’urgence

4. Le Gouvernement Centrafricain donc a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ressources du Fonds de Préparation du Projet pour financer le recrutement d’un laboratoire pour l’analyse de la toxicité des boues des collecteurs dans les zones 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7,  dans le cadre des travaux réhabilitation des infrastructures de drainage à Bangui

5. Les Services de Consultant « services » comprennent les prestations suivantes :

Le laboratoire mènera les activités suivantes dans le cadre de l’accomplissement de sa mission :

  •   Elaborer un plan d’échantillonnage
  • Préparation des kids de prélèvement des boues y compris les équipements de protection individuelle y compris moyen de transport.
  • Effectuer une descente sur les sites en vue de faire les prélèvements des échantillons par collecteurs concernés par les travaux ;
  • Le prélèvement se fera par carottage de la boue en profondeur stratifiée en fonction de l’épaisseur qui sera constaté allant de 05cm minimum jusqu’à inférieur ou égal à 50 centimètre maximum.
  • Assurer la traçabilité des échantillons
  • Procéder à la lixiviation et l’analyse des boues au Laboratoire en appliquant les normes OMS qui indiquent le degré toxicité des éléments cités ci-dessus
  • Répertorier les différents éléments toxiques retrouvés, même ceux qui ne sont pas demandés par le client mais jugés très dangereux pour la santé des populations ;
  • Interpréter les résultats et produire un rapport des analyses effectuées. 
  • Un plan Hygiène,Santé et Environnement.

 

II – EXPRESSION D’INTERET

Le Gouvernement de l’Union des Comores a obtenu un don de l’Association internationale de développement (IDA), d’un montant équivalent à 30 millions de dollars des États-Unis, pour financer le Projet de Filets Sociaux Résilients et Réactifs aux Chocs (PFSS-RRC). Le Projet répond aux besoins immédiats des populations pauvres et vulnérables tout en contribuant à la mise en place d’un système de protection sociale adaptative capable d’être renforcé en période de crise.

Afin de consolider ses objectifs et d’élargir la portée de ses interventions, le Projet bénéficie également d’un financement additionnel récemment accordé par l’IDA. Ce financement complémentaire vise à accroître les transferts monétaires aux ménages vulnérables, renforcer les capacités institutionnelles et assurer une meilleure couverture géographique et opérationnelle. Il traduit la confiance renouvelée du gouvernement et de la Banque mondiale dans la pertinence du PFSS-RRC et dans son rôle stratégique pour la résilience sociale et économique des Comores.

Placé sous la tutelle du ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale, le projet est aligné sur la Politique nationale de protection sociale, notamment sur l’amélioration des conditions de vie des ménages pauvres et vulnérables, la protection du capital humain et le renforcement de la résilience face aux chocs économiques, climatiques et sociaux.

Le Projet intervient à Ngazidja, Ndzouani et Mwali et sa mise en œuvre repose sur une Coordination nationale, des bureaux régionaux et différents partenaires opérationnels. La nature décentralisée des interventions, l’importance des transferts monétaires et la diversité des prestataires exigent une gestion administrative, financière et comptable rigoureuse, transparente et conforme aux accords de financement, aux procédures nationales applicables et aux exigences de la Banque mondiale.

Il est prévu qu’une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce Don sera utilisée pour effectuer le paiement à titre du contrat portant « Recrutement d’un Responsable Administratif et Financier (RAF) à la Coordination nationale ».

  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau Bac+5 (Master ou équivalent) en finance, comptabilité, gestion financière, audit, contrôle de gestion ou dans une discipline étroitement apparentée, délivré par un établissement reconnu.

Le Gouvernement du Sénégal à travers le Ministère de l’Education nationale met en œuvre le Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE) financé par la Banque mondiale.

Dans le cadre du renforcement de l'équipe de l'Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP), le PAPSE recrute un(e) Assistant(e) en Suivi-Évaluation.

 

2. DESCRIPTION DU POSTE

L’Assistant (e) en Suivi-Évaluation, placé (e ) sous l'autorité du Responsable Suivi-Évaluation (RSE), sera notamment chargé (e ) de :

  • Coordonner la collecte périodique des données auprès des points focaux du niveau central et des16 IA et 59 IEF, à travers les outils harmonisés (fiches papier, KoBoToolbox, bases Excel/SIGE) ;
  • Vérifier la qualité, la cohérence et la complétude des données collectées avant consolidation ;
  • Contribuer à la conception et à l’amélioration des outils de collecte et des canevas de reporting ;
  • Alimenter et mettre à jour les bases de données du projet de manière régulière.
  • Appuyer le suivi régulier des 26 indicateurs du Cadre de Mesure des Résultats, y compris les indicateurs désagrégés (genre, zone géographique) ;
  • Produire les tableaux de bord de suivi des performances pour les missions de supervision de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Préparer les notes d’analyse trimestrielles sur l’état d’avancement du projet ;
  • Alerter le RSE en cas de retard ou de déviation par rapport aux cibles fixées.
  • Contribuer à la rédaction des rapports de suivi trimestriels et annuels du projet ;
  • Préparer les éléments de reporting pour les aide-mémoires des missions conjointes Gouvernement/Banque mondiale ;
  • Documenter les progrès, les résultats atteints et les leçons apprises pour capitalisation.

 

 

 

 

  • Effectuer des missions de terrain dans les IA et IEF pour appuyer la collecte de données et vérifier les informations rapportées ;
  • Identifier les besoins en formation des points focaux S&E au niveau déconcentré et contribuer à l’élaboration du plan de renforcement des capacités ;
  • Dispenser des formations et appuis techniques ponctuels aux équipes régionales et locales ;
  • Assurer la coordination avec les partenaires techniques (INEADE, DEE, DPRE, DPTIC,  cabinets de suivi).
  • Contribuer à la documentation des bonnes pratiques et des leçons apprises issues de la mise en œuvre ;
  • Appuyer l’organisation des revues périodiques et des évaluations du projet ;
  • Participer à la supervision de la mission du cabinet de suivi des travaux ;
  • Proposer des améliorations du dispositif SERA sur la base de l’analyse des données et des retours terrain.

 

3. PROFIL DES CANDIDATS

Le candidat devra avoir :

  • un diplôme universitaire (minimum Bac+4) en statistiques, économie, sciences sociales, évaluation des politiques publiques, gestion de projets de développement ou domaine apparenté ;
  •  une formation complémentaire en communication, suivi-évaluation, gestion axée sur les résultats (GAR) ou planification serait un atout majeur ;

  • une connaissance du système éducatif sénégalais et de son architecture institutionnelle (MEN, IA, IEF) constitue un avantage significatif ;
  • une maîtrise des outils de collecte numérique : KoBoToolbox, ODK, Survey CTO ou équivalent ;

  • des qualités personnelles
  • Rigueur méthodologique et souci du détail ;
  • Capacité à travailler sous pression et à respecter les délais ;
  • Excellentes compétences rédactionnelles en français ;
  • Aptitude au travail en équipe et à la coordination multi-acteurs ;
  • Disponibilité pour des déplacements fréquents sur le terrain (régions du Sénégal).

 

Une expérience dans un projet financé par la Banque mondiale ou un autre partenaire technique et financier sera considérée comme un atout.

Les candidats intéressés sont invités à transmettre un dossier comprenant :

  • une lettre de motivation précisant le poste sollicité ;

  • les attestations ou certificats de travail justifiant les expériences professionnelles ;

6. MODALITES DE RECRUTEMENT

Le recrutement sera effectué à l'issue d'une présélection sur dossier, suivie d'un entretien avec les candidats présélectionnés.

Le Projet PAPSE applique les principes d'égalité des chances, de transparence et de mérite dans le processus de recrutement conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale.
