REPÚBLICA DE ANGOLA

MINISTÉRIO DA ADMINISTRAÇÃO DO TERRITÓRIO

PROJECTO DE FORTALECIMENTO DA GOVERNAÇÃO PARA MELHORIA DA PRESTAÇÃO DE SERVIÇOS EM ANGOLA – NJILA

Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP)

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse

 

País: Angola.

Nome do Projecto: Projecto Njila.

Projecto ID N. º P178040.

Descrição do Contrato: Parte superior do formulário

Contratação de um(a) Especialista Ambiental para a URIP3

No. do Contrato: AO-MAT-560403-CS-INDV

O Governo de Angola assinou um acordo de empréstimo com o Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação dos Serviços em Angola, cujos objectivos são: (i) Aumentar o montante e a fiabilidade das transferências fiscais para municípios seleccionados; (ii) reforçar a sua capacidade financeira e de gestão fundiária; (iii) aumentar a cobertura de identidade.

O Projecto é multissectorial, envolvendo os seguintes Departamentos Ministeriais: Ministério das Finanças, Justiça e dos Direitos Humanos, Obras Públicas, Urbanismo e Habitação, Administração Pública, Trabalho, Segurança Social e o Ministério da Administração do Território, que tem a responsabilidade de coordenar, através de uma Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP).

O Projecto terá a duração de quatro (4) anos e para assegurar a sua  implementação torna-se necessário preencher o quadro de pessoal da Unidade Regional de Implementação do Projecto (URIP), com técnicos capazes de dar suporte a execução, incluindo um(a) Especialista Ambiental, para garantir o cumprimento e conformidade ambiental ao nível das Unidades Regionais de Implementação do Projecto, apoiando a coordenação na implementação do das actividades relacionadas com as questões ambientais durante toda a fase de implementação. Esta contratação terá como principal função apoiar a Coordenação na garantia do cumprimento dos requisitos legais nacionais e os requisitos ambientais do BM, de acordo com o Quadro Ambiental e Social (QAS).

O objectivo geral desta consultoria (os serviços) é de assumir a responsabilidade pela implementação dos instrumentos preparados no âmbito do projecto, a nível regional, nomeadamente Quadro de Gestão Ambiental e Social (QGAS), Plano de Compromissos Ambientais e Sociais (PCAS), Procedimentos de Gestão de Mão-de-Obra (PGMO), entre outros.

A duração desta contratação é de 12 meses, renováveis em função do desempenho satisfatório. Os termos de referência podem ser obtidos no endereço abaixo indicado.

O Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação de Serviços em Angola, convida os candidatos “interessados” (Consultores Especialistas Ambientais) elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os serviços. Os candidatos interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem qualificações requeridas e experiência relevante para executar os serviços.

O(A) Candidato(a) deve possuir as seguintes qualificações: (I) Licenciatura em Gestão Ambientais, Engenharia Ambiental, Ciências Naturais, Biologia ou em áreas afins; (II) Mínimo 2 (dois) anos de experiência relevante para esta posição; (III) Experiência na aplicação das Políticas de Salvaguardas do Banco Mundial, com o Quadro Ambiental e Social do Banco Mundial e ainda com os Padrões de Desempenho do IFC; bem como com a legislação ambiental nacional angolana aplicável; (IV) Conhecimento dos regulamentos/directivas e operações pertinentes das organizações multilaterais de desenvolvimento e das agências de execução. Mínimo de 2 anos de experiência em organizações internacionais; (V) Experiência na elaboração e monitoria de EAS/PGAS; (VI) Formação e experiência em Saúde e Segurança Ocupacional (SSO); (VII) Capacidade comprovada em trabalhar com várias partes interessadas, incluindo entidades governamentais, organizações da sociedade civil (OSCs), comunidades locais e sector privado; (VIII) Comprovada capacidade técnica, analítica, escrita e comunicação, bem como algum conhecimento do trabalho do Banco Mundial; (IX) Domínio das ferramentas informáticas, especificamente o MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); (X) Domínio da Língua Portuguesa e inglesa.

Os candidatos deverão ter atenção ao Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Setembro de 2025, à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesse. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação:https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/products-and-services/brief/procurement-new-framework.

Os interessados deverão obter informação adicional no endereço abaixo indicado das 8H00 às 15H00. As manifestações de interesse (Currículo, cópia dos certificados de habilitações académicas e outras informações pertinentes) deverão ser entregues até o dia 26 de Agosto de 2026, apenas os Consultores qualificados na etapa de avaliação curricular serão contactados para as entrevistas.

  1. Coffee Hydropower Plant Extension. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.
  2. The Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Package 2: HEM Works for the Mt. Coffee Hydropower Plant Extension in a period of 36 months. The Mt. Coffee Hydropower Plant (MCHPP) is located about 30km from Monrovia and has an installed capacity of 88MW, accounting for about 70% of Liberia’s generation profile.  The extension endeavor will increase MCHPP capacity by 42MW through the addition of 4x 10.5 MW Z-type Kaplan Vertical turbines, and extension of the existing powerhouse and associated civil works without altering the dam or intake structures, whilst ensuring continuous operation of the existing units. The MCHPP Extension will be executed via two contracts: (i) Package 1/ Civil works; and (ii) the current contract, Package 2/ Hydro-Electrical & Mechanical (HEM) works. Generally, the scope of the HEM works contract includes the design, supply, installation, testing, and commissioning of the turbine-generator sets; penstocks; intake gates, trashracks and stoplogs; draft-tube stoplogs; the SCADA system; main power and auxiliary transformers; extension of the powerhouse overhead crane; workshop and warehouse overhead crane; and the necessary balance-of-plant systems, among others, as further defined in this Request for Bids.

Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition – September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

Réalisation des études de faisabilité, de l'Avant-Projet Sommaire (APS) et de l'Avant-Projet Détaillé (APD), couvrant l'analyse hydrologique, hydraulique et sédimentaire des bassins versants, l'évaluation des douze sites prioritaires, la collecte des données de terrain, le développement et la comparaison des options techniques, le dimensionnement hydraulique et structurel, les plans d'exécution et les estimations détaillées des coûts ;
  2. Préparation des Dossiers d'Appel d'Offres (DAO), comprenant les spécifications techniques, les plans, les bordereaux de quantités et les documents contractuels nécessaires à la passation des marchés de travaux ;
  3. Identification, évaluation et gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux, y compris les risques liés au genre et aux VBG/EAS-HS, conformément au Cadre Environnemental et Social de la Banque mondiale, ainsi que préparation des instruments requis et engagement continu des communautés et parties prenantes tout au long de la mission.

 

La mission se déroulera sur une période d’exécution de huit (8) mois.

 

 

3.Les Termes de Référence (TDRs) détaillés pour la mission peuvent être obtenus au Secrétariat de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Résilience des Transports & du Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine, Tel + 257 22 21 18 11, Adresse électronique : info@prt.bi avec copie à rmpawenayo@prt.bi et tbahori@pru.bi

 

4.L’Unité de Gestion du Projet d'Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine « UGP PRU » invite maintenant les cabinets de consultants éligibles ("Consultants") à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services.

 

5.Les critères pour l'établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

  1. Justifier d’une expérience générale d’au moins dix (10) ans dans la réalisation des missions couvrant les domaines de l’aménagement des infrastructures de lutte contre les glissements de terrain, de l’assainissement en milieu urbain, de la lutte contre les inondations ou l’élaboration de schémas directeurs de drainage pour des grandes agglomérations urbaines ;
  2. Avoir déjà réalisé, au cours des cinq (5) dernières années, au moins une (1) mission pertinente en Afrique subsaharienne ou en zone équatoriale portant sur des d’infrastructures de lutte contre les glissements de terrain, l’érosion ou des missions de nature et de complexité comparables ;
  3. Avoir réaliser au moins trois (3) missions avérées couvrant la collecte de données topographiques, bathymétriques, hydrauliques, hydrologiques ou géotechniques, d'infrastructures résilientes aux changements climatiques ;
  4. Avoir conduit au moins deux (2) Études d’Impacts Environnementaux et Sociaux (EIES) pour des projets d’infrastructures de lutte contre les inondations, les glissements de terrain ou l’érosion, etc ;

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués au stade de la présélection.

 

NB : Chaque cabinet devra présenter les preuves de ses capacités techniques et managériales accompagnées de Copies des contrats et de copies d’attestation de bonne fin des prestations, etc.

 

6.La liste restreinte sera composée d'un minimum de cinq (5) et d'un maximum de huit (8) cabinets.

 

7.L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d'Investissement FPI » 6 ème édition février 2025 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

Dans le cas d'une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront solidairement responsables de l'intégralité du contrat, s'ils sont sélectionnés.

9.Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur Qualité et le Coût (SFQC), énoncée dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

Specific Procurement Notice

                                                                                               Invitation for Prequalification

Country: Kingdom of Bhutan

Name of Project: Accelerating Transport and Trade Connectivity in Eastern South Asia (Access) – Bhutan Project

Contract Title: Construction of Gelephu-Tareythang Road and Bridges

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No: IDA 77560 (Credit)/IDAE4310 (grant)

Prequalification Reference No: ACCESS/DOST/WD-1, ACCESS/DOST/WD-2 and ACCESS/DOST/WD-3

1. The Royal Government of Bhutan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the proposed Accelerating Transport and Trade Connectivity in Eastern South Asia (ACCESS) – Bhutan Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contracts for ACCESS/DOST/WD-1, ACCESS/DOST/WD-2, and ACCESS/DOST/WD-3 for the Construction of Gelephu-Tareythang Road and Bridges.

2. The Department of Surface Transport (DoST), Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (MoIT), Royal Government of Bhutan, intends to prequalify contractors for the following work packages under the Gelephu-Tareythang Road Project involving the construction of 12,600 m of roadway and major bridge structures. The project comprises five major bridges with bridge lengths varying from 320 m to 1020 m, including PSC I-Girder and Cast-in-Situ Balanced Cantilever superstructures. The longest structure is the Mau River Bridge with a total length of 1020 m. The project corridor starts from Gelephu Town and terminates at Tareythang.

The contract packages are described below:

i. Package I:  Segment 1 to 5 (km 0.000 to km 3.868)
Construction of a 4-lane carriageway including earthworks, pavement, drainage, slope protection works, and associated ancillary works. The package also includes construction of the following two major bridges:

  • Gelephu Bridge – PSC I-Girder Bridge of span configuration (2 × 40 m); and
  • Mau River Bridge – Cast-in-Situ Balanced Cantilever Bridge of span configuration (4 × 60 m) + 2(60 + 2 × 90 + 60) + (3 × 60 m), including associated structures and ancillary works.

 

ii. Package II:  Segment 5 to 8 (km 3.868 to km 8.453)

Construction of a 2-lane carriageway including formation works, subgrade, pavement layers, cross-drainage structures, culverts, slope stabilization, and protection work. The package includes the following major bridges:

  • Taklai River Bridge – PSC I-Girder Bridge of span configuration 2(3 × 50 m) + (4 × 50 m) + 2(3 × 50 m); and
  • Langer River Bridge – Cast-in-Situ Balanced Cantilever Bridge of span configuration (60 + 3 × 90 + 60 m).

 

iii. Package III:  Segment 8 to 10 (km 8.453 to km 12.600)
Construction of a 2-lane carriageway including earthworks, pavement, drainage, and protection work. The package includes construction of the following bridge structures:

  • Singye River Bridge – Cast-in-Situ Balanced Cantilever Bridge of span configuration (60 + 3   × 90 + 60 m); and
  • Tareythang Bridge at km 10.880 – PSC Girder Bridge of span configuration (4 × 50 m) + (1 × 30 m), including all associated civil, structural, and finishing works.

It is expected that the Request for Bids (RFB) will be issued in October 2026.

3. Prequalification will be conducted in accordance with the procedures specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Applicants as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Interested eligible Applicants may obtain further information from the Department of Surface Transport, Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport, at the address provided below during office hours from 0900 to 1700 hours (Bhutan Standard Time, GMT +6:00). The Prequalification Document may be downloaded free of charge from the official website of the Department of Surface Transport, Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport, Royal Government of Bhutan. The document can be downloaded from https://moit.gov.bt/ from July 20, 2026. Applicants are encouraged to register their contact details to receive clarifications, addenda, and other updates, if any. The Employer shall not be responsible for any failure or delay in downloading the document due to internet connectivity issues, browser incompatibility, or other technical problems at the Applicant’s end.

5. Applications for prequalification should be submitted in clearly marked envelopes and delivered to the address below by 1000 hours (Bhutan Time, GMT + 0600 hours) on: September 7, 2026. Late applications may be rejected.

1.  Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a sollicité un crédit de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet de Transport Multimodal et Logistique (PTML) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du contrat sur les études d’aménagement de gares fluviales sur le canal de Pangalane, 10-APMF-C-PTML/2026.

2. Les services de consultants (« les Services ») ont pour objectif principal de porter à maturité technique, opérationnelle et économique le réseau des gares fluviales et complexes portuaires du corridor Est (Mahanoro – Farafangana), tout en définissant un niveau de service adapté aux besoins des usagers (passagers, opérateurs de transport, chargeurs, pêcheurs et populations riveraines) en matière d'accessibilité, de sécurité, de confort et de qualité d'exploitation. Les prestations seront séparées en deux tranches : Tranche ferme pour les études de faisabilité technique, socio-économique et environnementale et Tranche Conditionnelle pour les études d’avant-projet détaillé, d’impact environnemental & social, et établissement des pièces techniques du Dossier d’Appel d’Offres des travaux.

Les Termes de Référence (TDR) détaillés peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse ci-dessous.

3. L’Unité de Coordination de la Préparation du Projet PTML invite à présent les consultants (firmes) éligibles (Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt pour fournir les Services demandés. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l’expérience pertinentes pour exécuter les Services. Les principaux critères de présélection sont :

Être un bureau d'études d'ingénierie ou un consortium justifiant d'expériences solides et de références spécifiques dans les domaines suivants :

  • Ingénierie Portuaire, Fluviale et des Voies Navigables Intérieures : Expérience confirmée en études complètes (APS/APD) portant sur des ouvrages d'accostage, terminaux fluviaux ou lacustres, infrastructures portuaires intérieures, dragage de chenaux navigables et aménagements associés en milieu fluvial, lagunaire ou maritime.
  • Aménagements Logistiques, Gares Fluviales et Terminaux Multimodaux : Références dans la conception ou la réhabilitation de gares fluviales, terminaux lacustres, plateformes logistiques ou infrastructures de transport de passagers et de fret en milieu fluvial, lagunaire ou multimodal.
  • Études de Faisabilité et Modélisation Économique : Maîtrise des analyses technico-économiques (demande, rentabilité TRI/VAN) et des stratégies d'exploitation, avec une compétence spécifique dans les montages contractuels de type PPP.
  • Études d’Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) : Réalisation d'EIES conformes aux standards des bailleurs de fonds internationaux, avec une gestion rigoureuse des enjeux de désenclavement et de protection des écosystèmes aquatiques.

Les CV des experts ne seront pas évalués à ce stade.

4. L’attention des Consultants est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.15, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de Projets d’Investissement financés par la Banque mondiale », édition de septembre 2025, qui précise la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts. Veuillez également vous référer aux informations spécifiques relatives aux conflits d’intérêts conformément au paragraphe 3.13 des Règlements.

5. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes sous forme de groupement ou de soustraitance. En cas de groupement, toutes les firmes sont conjointement et solidairement responsables du contrat en cas de sélection.

6. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode Sélection Fondée sur la Qualification et le Coût (SFQC) indiquée dans le Règlement.

7. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau notamment de 8h30mn à 16h00, heures locales.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – CONSULTANCY FIRM)

ALBANIA

Project: National Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Modernization Program (P4R)

TF No.: B8448

Assignment Title: Technical Assistance to support day to day management of Regional Water Utilities on financial issues.

Reference No.: AL-AKUK – 329911-CS-CQS

Albania is implementing governance and service reforms in the WSS sector supported by the World Bank through P4R project financed by SECO (Swiss Government). In parallel, structural reform changes are being launched by the government, including the creation of the new Water Production Operator (OPU) while the details of its future role and structure are still evolving; therefore this assignment shall focus on AKUK’s current mandate and existing institutional set-up, and reflect OPU-related interfaces only where and when formally clarified or necessary as working assumptions.

This Request for Expressions of Interest aims to assist AKUK in hiring a Consultant to support the Regional Water Utility (RWU) in strengthening its financial management, financial reporting, and financial sustainability through improvements in financial planning, budgeting, revenue management, regulatory compliance, and institutional capacity.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://akuk.gov.al/

The activities described in these TORs are expected to be completed within a period of 9 months, following the signing of the consultancy contract.

The assignment requires a firm which can demonstrate a minimum of 10 years of general consulting experience.

  • The firm’s specific experience should include at least three experiences in institutional strengthening support to water supply and sanitation utilities
  • Specific experience in Albania and countries in the Western Balkans region will be considered an advantage.

No.

Key expert

Qualifications and skills

1

Team Leader

  • Master's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Management, Public Administration, Engineering, or another relevant field.
  • Fluent in English with excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong managerial and coordination skills.
  • Minimum 10 years of professional experience.
  • At least 7 years of experience leading institutional strengthening or financial management assignments in the water sector or other public utility sectors.
  • At least 5 years of experience as Team Leader or Project Manager on similar assignments.
  • Previous experience in Albania and/or the Western Balkans water sector will be considered an advantage.

2

Senior Financial Management Expert

  • Master’s degree in Management, Business Management, Engineering, Finance, Economics, or related field.  
  • At least 10 years of experience of assessing water and sanitation utilities’ organizational structure, staffing, capacity, resources, and equipment, and of recommending utility restructuring/reorganization.  
  • Strong understanding and experience with the regulatory framework governing the Albanian water supply and sanitation sector
  • Prior experience in projects within the Albanian water and sanitation sector or similar local contexts will be considered a significant advantage

3

Capacity Building and Training Specialist

  • Master's degree in Management, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, Human Resources Development, or related field.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in developing and delivering training programs.
  • Experience in institutional capacity building.
  • Experience preparing manuals, operational procedures, and training materials.
  • Previous experience with public utilities will be considered an advantage.

 

The service will be selected under the provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations), in investment project financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services November 2020, in accordance with Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS), Lump-Sum Contract. The Bank requires that firms or individuals involved in Bank IPF procurement shall not have conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 16:00, Mondays to Thursdays, and from 08:00 to 14:00 on Fridays.

UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET

---------------------------------

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊTS N°057 /HISWACA /26

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DE DIX- HUIT (18) ANALYSTES THEMATIQUES POUR APPUYER LES TRAVAUX D'ANALYSE DE L’ENQUETE DEMOGRAPHIQUE DE SANTE DU CONGO (EDSC-III)

 

1.Le Gouvernement de la République du Congo a reçu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre des activités du « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA) », et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre des contrats suivants : « recrutement de dix-huit (18) analystes thématiques pour appuyer les travaux d'analyse de l'EDSC-III».

2.Objectif principal

L’objectif principal est de recruter et mobiliser des analystes thématiques qualifiés pour produire un rapport d'analyse de l'EDSC-III de haute qualité, conforme aux standards internationaux des enquêtes EDS et répondant aux besoins d'information des décideurs.

3.Objectifs spécifiques

De façon spécifique, il s’agit de : (i) renforcer les capacités opérationnelles et méthodologiques de l'équipe d'analyse à travers un atelier de cadrage ; (ii) harmoniser la compréhension des canevas de rédaction et des outils d'analyse entre tous les analystes ; (iii) assurer la production de chapitres thématiques de qualité dans les délais impartis ; (iv) garantir la cohérence analytique et rédactionnelle de l'ensemble du rapport final.

4.Profil des analystes

Les profils requis par groupe thématique et le nombre d’analyste sont présentés dans le tableau suivant :

Nom du groupe

Chapitres traités

Profil des analystes

Nombre d’analyste

1. Méthodologie et contexte

Chapitre 1

Expert en échantillonnage et traitement DHS. Rôle de référent technique transversal, supervision qualité méthodologique.

1

2. Contexte socio-démographique

Chapitres 2–3

Démographes/statisticiens, forte maîtrise des analyses descriptives et indicateurs socio-économiques. Fournit le cadre d’interprétation du rapport.

2

3. Nuptialité et fécondité (niveau)

Chapitres 4–5

Démographe expérimenté en fécondité. Maîtrise des indicateurs EDS avancés et analyse des tendances.

2

4. Préférences et planification familiale

Chapitres 6–7

Spécialiste santé reproductive. Analyse de la demande, besoins non satisfaits, dynamique contraceptive. Forte orientation programme PF.

2

5. Mortalité

Chapitres 8 et 17

Expertise en estimation EDS de mortalité et analyse des biais. Nécessite encadrement technique étroit.

2

6. Santé maternelle et infantile

Chapitres 9–10

Spécialiste santé publique. Bonne connaissance des services de santé et du continuum de soins mèreenfant.

2

7. Nutrition et paludisme

Chapitres 11–12

Spécialistes sectoriels (nutrition, PNLP). Maîtrise des indicateurs techniques et capacité de liaison avec programmes nationaux.

2

8. VIH/Sida

Chapitres 13–14

Spécialiste VIH. Expérience en données biomarqueurs et analyse comportementale. Sensibilité dans l’interprétation.

2

9. Genre et autonomisation

Chapitre 15

Spécialiste genre/sciences sociales. Analyse des normes sociales, pouvoir de décision et dynamiques intraménage. Forte capacité analytique qualitative.

1

10. Conditions de vie et protection des enfants

Chapitres 16 et 18

Profil mixte (INS, UNICEF, ministères sociaux). Expertise WASH et protection de l’enfant.

2

Total

 

 

18

 

 5.Critères d'éligibilité

            Les candidats devront répondre aux critères suivants :

  • être titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire (Bac+4 minimum) en statistique, démographie, santé publique, épidémiologie ou domaine connexe ;
  • justifier d'une expérience d'au moins cinq (05) ans dans l'analyse de données d'enquêtes ou en recherche quantitative ;
  • avoir participé à au moins une enquête nationale de type EDS, MICS ou similaire ;
  • être spécialiste sectoriel de la thématique est un atout.

6.Composition du dossier

Le dossier de candidature doit comprendre :

  • une lettre de motivation adressée au Coordonnateur du projet HISWACA en précisant la thématique à analyser ;
  • un curriculum vitae détaillé et actualisé ;
  • les copies des diplômes et attestations de travail ;
  • la liste des publications ou rapports d'analyse réalisés (si disponible) ;
  • tout document attestant d'une expérience dans les enquêtes EDS ou similaires.

7.L’Unité de gestion du projet HISWACA invite les consultants individuels à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants individuels intéressés doivent fournir les informations sur leur qualifications et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations.

8.La sélection du consultant se fera en accord avec les procédures définies dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissements (FPI) de la Banque mondiale (version de juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, août 2018, septembre 2023 et septembre 2025).

9.Les consultants peuvent obtenir les termes de références de la mission par courriel à l’adresse : recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com / ugp@hiswaca-congo.org, de 9 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 16 heures (heures locales) du lundi au vendredi.

9.Les manifestations d’intérêts doivent être écrites en langue française et envoyées en utilisant le lien ou ou QR-CODE ci-dessous au plus tard le mardi 18 août 2026 (à minuit, heure locale) et porter clairement la mention du groupe thématique pour lequel le consultant fait acte de candidature.

 

https://ee.kobotoolbox.org/x/tLmfAj6m

Recrutement des Consultants (es) individuels (les) aux postes d'Assistants (e) Administratif et financier pour les antennes provinciales du Projet PERSE

 

NO Avis : AMI n° ZR-SPACE-262238.CS-lNDV

Source de financement : Crédit n°6692-ZR et Don n°6620-ZR

Date de publication : 28 mars 2022

Date de clôture : 13 avril 2022

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) a obtenu de l’Association Internationale du Développement ( IDA) un crédit et un don d'un montant de 800 millions de dollars américains, pour financer le Projet d’Equité pour le Renforcement du Système Educatif en sigle PERSE, et a l’intention d'utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre d’un contrat de service de consultants (e) individuels (le) aux postes  d’Assistants (e ) Administratif et financier des antennes provinciales du Projet PERSE dans les provinces de Kinshasa, Kwilu, Kongo-Central, Kasaï-Oriental, Kasaï -Central, Kasaï, Lomami, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu et Ituri.

 

  1. L’objectif de la mission du Contractuel est de : (i) Procéder par un contrôle à priori de toutes factures et autres demandes paiement ; (ii) Contrôle de toutes les pièces justificatives lui transmises au titre des avances de fonds accordées aux tiers ; (iii) S'assurer des disponibilités budgétaires de toutes les dépenses effectuées ; (iv) Assurer l'archivage et le classement des toutes les pièces comptables en perspectives des revues et audits ; (v) Appuyer le RAF dans l'établissement des notes de frais des missions ainsi que les frais complémentaires après la mission sur base des pièces probantes ; (vi) Appuyer le RAF dans la supervision des contrats signés au niveau provincial ( entretiens de véhicule, nettoyage Bureaux, maintenance du système de climatisation,… ).

 

  1. L'ECP-PERSE invite les candidats (« Consultants Individuels ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

 

  1. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

 

  1. Être détenteur au moins d’un diplôme de licence (Bac+ 5) en gestion financière ou l’équivalent délivré par une institution supérieure ou universitaire reconnue officiellement et de renommée nationale ou internationale ;
  2. Avoir une expérience professionnelle d’au moins deux (2) ans dans les fonctions liées au contrôle financier ou à la comptabilité des projets financés par les organismes internationaux, notamment la Banque mondiale, l’UE, le DFID, la BAD ;
  3. Avoir une expérience professionnelle dans un projet financé par la Banque mondiale serait un atout ;
  4. Avoir une connaissance du logiciel comptable Tompro ;
  5. Avoir la connaissance des procédures fiduciaires des projets financés par la Banque mondiale ;
  6. Avoir la maitrise de l’outils informatique (Word, Excel, …) ;
  7. Avoir une excellente capacité d’organisation, d’analyse et de rédaction ;
  8. Avoir une bonne aptitude de travailler en équipe et sous pression ;
  9. Être de notoriété et de probité morale et intellectuelle ;
  10. Ne pas être fonctionnaire de l’Etat au moment de la prise des fonctions.

 

  1. The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Clean Philippines, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include but not limited to the conduct of Pre-feasibility Study and Investment Preparation for Sustainable Material Recovery and Circular-Economy Facilities in Metro Manila. The consultant is also expected to rapidly assess 4 to 5 candidate sites for technical, financial, legal, institutional and environmental viability. Furthermore, the consultant is also expected to produce site-specific waste supply and composition data, conceptual designs, investment and O&M cost estimates, KPI/standards, business models and policy/financing recommendation to support MMDA/DEPDev approval. The projected implementation period should not exceed more than six (6) months and is projected to start within the 3rd quarter of this year. 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The MMDA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: 

1.) The firm shall have an experience with feasibility assessment and designing integrated low cost material recovery facilities in composting, refuse derived fuel/solid recovery fuel facilities, at least three (3) international and local references should be provided and at least one (1) reference in South-East Asia.

2.) The firm have at least ten (10) years of national and/or international experience and experience in undertaking geotechnical investigations for landfill/landfill remediation projects as well as carrying out environmental studies consistent with World Bank standards, at least two (2) references for landfill remediation should be provided, with on in South-East Asia/Philippines.

3.) The firm shall have an experience with Government of Philippines and World Bank regulations, standards, procedures and familiarity with FIDIC Conditions of Contract for MDB rules for this type of infrastructure and environmental management project.

- Company profile including list of relevant experience

- Business registration or equivalent documentation demonstrating company’s legal standing

- Mayor’s Permit or Business Permit (For foreign firm, please provide equivalent document)

- Tax registration or equivalent

- Audited financial statement from the past two (2) years or letter of financial capability

- Notarized Sworn Statement certifying that all information and documents submitted are true, complete and authentic to the best of its knowledge and that the submission is in compliance with applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations including 1.9 Conflict of Interest, 1.10 Unfair Competitive Advantage and 1.11 Eligibility.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE 1 ESPECIALISTA JÚNIOR PARA O CENTRO DE OPERAÇÕES DE EMERGÊNCIAS E SAÚDE PÚBLICA

País: Angola

Nome do Projecto: Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR) Título de Contracto: Contratação de Serviços de Consultoria

Empréstimo No.: 9562-AO RFP Referência No.: HEPRR-AO/C-009

O Governo de Angola recebeu uma doação no valor equivalente de USD 1.9 milhões de Dólares Norte Americanos, com o Banco Internacional de Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD) do Grupo Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR) e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos na contratação de um (1) Especialista Júnior para o Centro de Operações de Emergências e Saúde Pública -COESP.

O objectivo geral desta consultoria visa assegurar a prestação de assistência técnica à Direção Nacional de Saúde Pública (DNSP) na coordenação, implementação, expansão e operacionalização do Centro de Operações de Emergências e Saúde Pública - COESP, fortalecendo as capacidades de preparação, vigilância, coordenação e resposta às emergências de saúde pública, em conformidade com o Regulamento Sanitário Internacional (RSI 2005) e os objetivos do Projeto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência às Emergências de Saúde (HEPRR).

A consultoria terá a duração de Cinco (5) meses, renováveis em função do desempenho satisfatório, da disponibilidade financeira e das necessidades do projecto. Os termos de referência podem ser obtidos no endereço electrónico abaixo indicado.

O Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR), convida por este meio os consultores individuais ("Consultores") elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os Serviços. Os consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações requeridas e experiência relevante para executar os serviços, submetendo o seu curriculum vitae, certificados/diplomas académicos, comprovativos de experiência profissional e outros documentos de suporte que se achem necessários para a candidatura.

O(A) Consultor(a) deverá possuir as seguintes qualificações:

Formação Académica

Licenciatura em Medicina, em Enfermagem, ou áreas afins;

Mestrado ou Especialização em Saúde Pública, Gestão de Operações ou Desenvolvimento Internacional representam vantagens adicionais;

Experiência Profissional

• Mínimo de 5 anos de experiência em resposta a emergências de saúde pública, com experiência nacional ou internacional na implementação e fortalecimento de programas de resposta a emergência, incluindo COESP;

• Conhecimento e experiência de implementação do Regulamento Sanitário Internacional (RSI 2005), diretrizes internacionais de resposta a emergências, e vigilância epidemiológica;

• Conhecimento e experiência de aplicações e ferramentas de Office baseados em ICT’s (processamento de texto, planilhas e processamento de dados, PowerPoint);

• Excelente domínio da Língua Portuguesa e conhecimento da Língua Inglesa.

Os consultores serão avaliados com base nas Normas e Regulamentos de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Setembro de 2023, pelo que deverão ter em atenção à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesses. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação: https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/6c0602876d68949e80820507d90a14ed 0290012023/original/Procurement-Regulations-September-2023.pdf. O(A) Consultor(a) será selecionado com base no método de contratação de Consultores Individuais de acordo com as Normas e Regulamentos de Aquisições em vigor (Setembro 2023).

Os Consultores interessados poderão obter informação adicional, incluindo os TORs (Termos de Referência) no endereço abaixo indicado de Segunda Feira à Sexta Feira entre as 8H00 – 15H00. As manifestações de interesse (Currículo, cópia dos certificados de habilitações académicas, avaliação de desempenho e outra informação pertinente) deverão ser enviadas até ao dia 18 de Agosto de 2026 às 15H00 (Horário de Angola).

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1 – Content Expert 3 (Mathematics))


 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No. TF0C5794

 

Assignment Title: Content Expert 3 (Mathematics)

Reference No. LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1

Ukraine and World bank have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). 

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of the Consultant's assignment is to develop high-quality educational materials in the field of mathematics, aligned with NUS standards. The Content Expert will ensure the materials are mathematically accurate, pedagogically effective, and cater to the diverse needs of students and educators.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time August 19, 2026.  

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 

for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Content Expert 3 (Mathematics)

Contract No. LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

URTF Grant No. TF0C5794

 

 

  1.  BACKGROUND

 

Ukraine and the World Bank have signed the agreements for the Program "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program" (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN). The objectives of the LEARN are: to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system.

 

The total financing for the Operation is US$451 million using a combination of the World Bank's financial instruments: Program-for-Results (PforR) complemented by Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is funded by a US$235 million credit provided by Bank resources, supported by credit enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT NUMBER 7626-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN NUMBER 9721-UA). Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT NUMBER 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0C5794).

Furthermore, US$31.1 million in Additional Financing is provided through grant resources, consisting of US$30.0 million from the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund and US$1.1 million from the Global Partnership for Education Fund. This additional financing is formalized under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0D0612; GPE GRANT NUMBER TF0D0613), and supports activities related to the continued implementation of the Program.

 

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan.

LEARN will focus on supporting the Strategic Action Plan Priority 2: School education and the New Ukrainian School (NUS). The continuation of the NUS reform is a key priority of the MoES.

The objectives of the Program are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The Program is implemented in Ukraine by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) with the support of the World Bank Group. The implementation period is 2024-2027.

More detailed information is given at the link https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

 

The Operation will focus on supporting the Strategic Action Plan Priority 2: School education and the New Ukrainian School (NUS). The continuation of the NUS reform is a key priority of the MoES.

 

The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

 

For this program, "teaching and learning conditions" refer to three critical factors of education service delivery:

 

i. safety, including shelters as a pre-condition for schools to open for in-person learning and free and inclusive school bus transportation for students living further distances from schools;

 

ii. learning materials, especially updated textbooks and age-appropriate learning materials in line with the NUS model; and

 

iii. teachers trained on NUS standards, principles, and the use of the updated learning materials.

 

Meanwhile, "management capacity of the education system" refers to institutional capabilities to plan, allocate, and monitor resources based on robust data at the student and school levels.

 

The NUS Implementation Office (NIO) will be established by the Ministry as an advisory and consultative body. The NIO's primary purpose is to support and implement the New Ukrainian School (NUS) reform by providing expert guidance, strategic oversight, and coordination of reform initiatives across Ukraine.

 

  1.  OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to develop high-quality educational materials in the field of mathematics, aligned with NUS standards. The Content Expert will ensure the materials are mathematically accurate, pedagogically effective, and cater to the diverse needs of students and educators.

  1. SCOPE OF SERVICES

 

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

 

  • Develop and adapt educational materials in the field of mathematics in alignment with NUS standards.
  • Ensure the mathematical accuracy and pedagogical soundness of all developed content.
  • Review and enhance existing educational resources, making recommendations for improvements.
  • Collaborate with other content experts and the Content Experts Coordinator to ensure consistency across educational materials.
  • Provide expertise in creating content that fosters problem-solving and critical thinking skills in students.

 

  1. REPORTING

 

The Content Expert reports directly to the Content Experts Coordinator. Monthly reports detailing progress, challenges, and completed tasks must be submitted, along with time sheets.

  1. PROVIDED RESOURCES

 

MoES shall provide the Consultant with the information necessary to carry out his/her assignment in a timely manner. MoES shall provide the Consultant with a workplace, including necessary equipment to carry out his/her functions (e.g. PC, communications and office equipment).

 

  1. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum Requirements:

  • At least 3 years of professional experience in developing or reviewing educational materials in mathematics.
  • Knowledge of NUS standards and principles.
  • Experience in the education sector, preferably in school-level mathematics education.
  • Advanced proficiency in Ukrainian.

Desired Skills and Qualifications:

  • Strong understanding of mathematical concepts and pedagogy.
  • Ability to develop engaging, inclusive, and age-appropriate educational materials.
  • Attention to detail and ability to meet deadlines.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.

 

  1. PERIOD AND LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

 

The Consultant shall provide his/her services until August 31, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES) during the Project financing period.

 

The Consultant shall provide his/her services on a full-time basis.

 

The incumbent will be based in Kyiv, Ukraine. The Consultant should be required and expected to take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.

 

VIII. APPLICATION PACKAGE

 

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua, Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org and maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua  indicating the email subject: " LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1: Selection of Content Expert 3 (Mathematics): [NAME]".

 

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time August 19, 2026.

 

If the Consultant fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the Consultant's application.

Name of Project: Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People (INSON) Project

Contract Title: Procurement of Specialized Equipment for Social Service and Rehabilitation Institutions

Credit No.: 7555-UZ / Grant No.: TF C4589-UZ

RFB Reference No.: UZ-INSON-RFB-2.2.7-8

 

  1. The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People (INSON) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contracts for Procurement of Specialized Equipment for Social Service and Rehabilitation Institutions. For these contracts, the Borrower may process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing, except for those payments, which the contract provides to be made through letter of credit.

2.         The National Agency for Social Protection under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan (NASP) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Specialized Equipment for Social Service and Rehabilitation Institutions, as follows:

  • Lot 01: Pediatric/adult rehab trainers and robotics (mechanotherapy).

Lot 01 comprises pediatric and adult rehabilitation trainers and robotic mechanotherapy systems for gait, balance, and limb function restoration. It includes advanced gait and balance training systems, robotic and mechanized upper- and lower-limb trainers. The lot also contains pediatric and adult gait imitation devices, bodyweight supported walking systems, and various mechanotherapy frames and wallmounted units. Additional balance, step, ramp, and platform accessories support progressive and taskoriented training across different functional levels. There are about 50 line items (systems), the quantities per item typically vary from 20 to 55 sets but may be lower or higher, up to 110-140 sets for some items.

  • Lot 02: Pediatric/adult mobility aids and seating

Lot 2 comprises pediatric and adult mobility aids and seating systems, including wheelchairs, specialized strollers, walkers, and adaptive seating for different age and size groups. It covers indoor and outdoor mobility devices, heightadjustable and tiltinspace chairs, and rehabilitation strollers designed to support posture, pressure distribution, and safe transportation. The lot also includes supportive seating for therapy and daily activities. There are 10 line items, including the total of 550 walking devices of various sizes, 550 baby wheelchairs of various sizes, 110 chairs for children with cerebral palsy, 40 multifunctional adaptive chairs, and 55 safe adaptive chairs for children with disabilities.

  • Lot 03: Small rehab tools, hand therapy and occupational therapy accessories

Lot 03 comprises small rehabilitation tools, handtherapy devices and occupational therapy accessories, with over than 30 line items in total. It includes freeweight sets and small exercise equipment for strengthening and rangeofmotion training, portable handtherapy tools (e.g. grip and finger trainers, elastic resistance bands and bars), and compact jointmobilization and stretching devices for upper and lower limbs. The lot also covers assorted small OT accessories to support finemotor training, coordination, and basic activities of daily living. The total quantities per line item range from 55 to 550 units to equip all participating institutions.

  • Lot 04: Sensory integration, play structures, mats and flooring

Lot 04 comprises sensory integration equipment, play structures, mats and flooring, about 20 line items in total. It includes modular sensory integration frames, swings and suspension systems, tactile and balance paths, and soft play elements that support vestibular, proprioceptive and tactile stimulation. The lot also provides protective floor and wall mats, crash mats, and foam blocks for safe movement, as well as small goaloriented play sets to structure therapeutic activities in pediatric and adult sensory rooms, with total quantities per line item typically ranging from 55 to 110 units to equip all facilities.

  • Lot 05: Pediatric/adult therapy furniture, support frames and positioning aids

Lot 05 comprises pediatric and adult therapy furniture, support frames and positioning aids, there are about 15 line items in total. It includes heightadjustable therapy tables and desks, adaptive therapy chairs, and specialized seating systems that provide postural support during rehabilitation and daily activities. The lot also covers standing frames and support frames for safe upright positioning, as well as complex adjustable positioning systems (including multimodule seating/standing solutions) for children and adults with significant motor impairments, with total quantities per line item typically ranging from 35 to 55 sets to equip all facilities.

  • Lot 06: Electrophysical therapy equipment (physiotherapy).

Lot 06 comprises electrophysical therapy equipment for physiotherapy, with 06 line items in total. It includes a professional thermotherapy system (20 sets), apparatus for galvanization and medical electrophoresis (20 sets), extracorporeal shockwave therapy device (20 sets), combined multi-channel modular physiotherapy device (55 sets), lymphatic drainage therapy device (55 sets), and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS/rTMS) system (5 sets), together covering the main electrophysical modalities needed for pain management, edema reduction, and tissue healing in adult and pediatric patients.

  • Lot 07: Ophthalmological equipment.

Lot 07 comprises ophthalmic diagnostic equipment for regional MSEC offices, enabling comprehensive eye examination capabilities. The package includes seven equipment categories: slit lamps with digital imaging systems, stationary and portable autorefractor-keratometers for automated refraction measurement, portable fundus cameras for retinal imaging, trial lens sets for subjective refraction testing, LED visual acuity projectors, and specialized diagnostic lenses for posterior segment examination. The quantities vary from 14 to 15 sets per item.

  • Lot 08: Diagnostic and rehabilitation equipment.

Lot 08 covers advanced neurorehabilitation therapy equipment, including standalone interactive systems for balance assessment/training (12 sets), isokinetic muscle performance evaluation and training systems (6 sets), and hand/upperlimb rehabilitation training systems (12 sets).

            Required delivery period should not exceed 16 weeks. Following arrival to Uzbekistan the supplier shall deliver the goods to 55 Territorial Social Service Centers (TSSCs), 12 Rehabilitation Centers and 14 Medical-Social Expert Commissions (MSECs) located throughout the country, assemble, install and commission the goods, as further defined in the technical specifications, and provide training to end-user personnel on operation of the goods supplied. The margin of preference for goods manufactured in Uzbekistan shall not apply.

4.         Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016, revised September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊTS N°057 /HISWACA /26

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DE DIX- HUIT (18) ANALYSTES THEMATIQUES POUR APPUYER LES TRAVAUX D'ANALYSE DE L’ENQUETE DEMOGRAPHIQUE DE SANTE DU CONGO (EDSC-III)

 

1.Le Gouvernement de la République du Congo a reçu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre des activités du « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA) », et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre des contrats suivants : « recrutement de dix-huit (18) analystes thématiques pour appuyer les travaux d'analyse de l'EDSC-III».

2.Objectif principal

L’objectif principal est de recruter et mobiliser des analystes thématiques qualifiés pour produire un rapport d'analyse de l'EDSC-III de haute qualité, conforme aux standards internationaux des enquêtes EDS et répondant aux besoins d'information des décideurs.

3.Objectifs spécifiques

De façon spécifique, il s’agit de : (i) renforcer les capacités opérationnelles et méthodologiques de l'équipe d'analyse à travers un atelier de cadrage ; (ii) harmoniser la compréhension des canevas de rédaction et des outils d'analyse entre tous les analystes ; (iii) assurer la production de chapitres thématiques de qualité dans les délais impartis ; (iv) garantir la cohérence analytique et rédactionnelle de l'ensemble du rapport final.

4.Profil des analystes

Les profils requis par groupe thématique et le nombre d’analyste sont présentés dans le tableau suivant :

 

Nom du groupe

Chapitres traités

Profil des analystes

Nombre d’analyste

1. Méthodologie et contexte

Chapitre 1

Expert en échantillonnage et traitement DHS. Rôle de référent technique transversal, supervision qualité méthodologique.

1

2. Contexte socio-démographique

Chapitres 2–3

Démographes/statisticiens, forte maîtrise des analyses descriptives et indicateurs socio-économiques. Fournit le cadre d’interprétation du rapport.

2

3. Nuptialité et fécondité (niveau)

Chapitres 4–5

Démographe expérimenté en fécondité. Maîtrise des indicateurs EDS avancés et analyse des tendances.

2

4. Préférences et planification familiale

Chapitres 6–7

Spécialiste santé reproductive. Analyse de la demande, besoins non satisfaits, dynamique contraceptive. Forte orientation programme PF.

2

5. Mortalité

Chapitres 8 et 17

Expertise en estimation EDS de mortalité et analyse des biais. Nécessite encadrement technique étroit.

2

6. Santé maternelle et infantile

Chapitres 9–10

Spécialiste santé publique. Bonne connaissance des services de santé et du continuum de soins mèreenfant.

2

7. Nutrition et paludisme

Chapitres 11–12

Spécialistes sectoriels (nutrition, PNLP). Maîtrise des indicateurs techniques et capacité de liaison avec programmes nationaux.

2

8. VIH/Sida

Chapitres 13–14

Spécialiste VIH. Expérience en données biomarqueurs et analyse comportementale. Sensibilité dans l’interprétation.

2

9. Genre et autonomisation

Chapitre 15

Spécialiste genre/sciences sociales. Analyse des normes sociales, pouvoir de décision et dynamiques intraménage. Forte capacité analytique qualitative.

1

10. Conditions de vie et protection des enfants

Chapitres 16 et 18

Profil mixte (INS, UNICEF, ministères sociaux). Expertise WASH et protection de l’enfant.

2

Total

 

 

18

 

5. Critères d'éligibilité

            Les candidats devront répondre aux critères suivants :

  • être titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire (Bac+4 minimum) en statistique, démographie, santé publique, épidémiologie ou domaine connexe ;
  • justifier d'une expérience d'au moins cinq (05) ans dans l'analyse de données d'enquêtes ou en recherche quantitative ;
  • avoir participé à au moins une enquête nationale de type EDS, MICS ou similaire ;
  • être spécialiste sectoriel de la thématique est un atout.

6.Composition du dossier

Le dossier de candidature doit comprendre :

  • une lettre de motivation adressée au Coordonnateur du projet HISWACA en précisant la thématique à analyser ;
  • un curriculum vitae détaillé et actualisé ;
  • les copies des diplômes et attestations de travail ;
  • la liste des publications ou rapports d'analyse réalisés (si disponible) ;
  • tout document attestant d'une expérience dans les enquêtes EDS ou similaires.

7.L’Unité de gestion du projet HISWACA invite les consultants individuels à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants individuels intéressés doivent fournir les informations sur leur qualifications et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations.

8.La sélection du consultant se fera en accord avec les procédures définies dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissements (FPI) de la Banque mondiale (version de juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, août 2018, septembre 2023 et septembre 2025).

9.Les consultants peuvent obtenir les termes de références de la mission par courriel à l’adresse : recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com / ugp@hiswaca-congo.org, de 9 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 16 heures (heures locales) du lundi au vendredi.

10.Les manifestations d’intérêts doivent être écrites en langue française et envoyées en utilisant le lien ou ou QR-CODE ci-dessous au plus tard le mardi 18 août 2026 (à minuit, heure locale) et porter clairement la mention du groupe thématique pour lequel le consultant fait acte de candidature.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

Country:

Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

Name of the Project:

Somalia Productive, Resilient and Inclusive Growth Project (SPRING),

Assignment Title:

Develop Somalia’s National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2027–2031

P501662

 of EOI

5th September 2026 4:00pm

Individual/Firm:

firm Selection

Ref No.                                 SO-MOF-555945-CS-CQS  

1. Background

 In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through the Ministry of Finance, launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) Project. The project development objective is to promote private sector led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance.

The SPRING Project is organized around four main components: (i) improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) enhancing access to finance and resilience for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; and (iv) supporting project management and coordination.

Under the SPRING Project, a wide range of reform activities will be implemented to achieve the project development objective. These include improvements to regulatory and institutional frameworks, the rollout of the national digital identification system, financial sector reforms, the establishment of risk-sharing mechanisms, and the provision of business development services to MSMEs in selected economic sectors, among other priority interventions.

The Ministry of Finance has received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi Partner Fund, to implement the SPRING Project. As part of Component 2, which focuses on deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity, the Ministry of Finance intends to apply part of the proceeds to support the Central Bank of Somalia in developing Somalia’s first National Financial Inclusion Strategy for the period 2027–2031.

2. Responsibilities: The purpose of this assignment is to develop a comprehensive, evidence-based, gender-responsive NFIS (2027-2031) for Somalia that expands access to and usage of formal financial products and services, including a detailed costed action plan, institutional and governance framework, an integrated SMART targets and MEL framework, a Communication and Stakeholder Engagement Strategy, and a knowledge transfer and capacity-building programme for the CBS NFIS team. All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link: https://centralbank.gov.so/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Somalia-NFIS-ToR-2027-2031.pdf

3. Duration: The firm is expected to complete the proposed assignment within 9 Months.

4. The Ministry of Finance invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.). The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  • Core business of the firm: at least 8 years of institutional experience in financial sector development, financial inclusion policy, or closely related fields, with particular weight given to the direct NFIS/national-strategy experience.
  • The firm must demonstrate experience in developing National Financial Inclusion Strategies (NFIS) or equivalent policy frameworks, with at least three similar assignments in Africa, preferably in fragile or post-conflict states. It should also have proven expertise in digital financial services, MSME and microfinance, financial regulation, consumer protection, gender-responsive financial inclusion, financial inclusion data and M&E systems, as well as experience in knowledge transfer and capacity building for national counterparts.
  • Experience of relevant services in an environment similar to that of Somalia and
  • Technical and managerial organization of the firm (provide only the structure of the organization). Do not provide CVs of key staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5.  The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated in September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.   

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected

7.  A Consultant will be selected under the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. 

8. Interested Consultants may obtain further information (in person or by e-mail) at the address below during office hours from 8.00 a.m. - 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday except on public holidays.

9. Deadline for submission: Expressions of interest should be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 5th September 2026 4:00pm

El Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento (BIRF) - Banco Mundial, para cubrir el costo del Proyecto "Mejora del Acceso Sostenible a la Electricidad en Bolivia – IDTR III y se propone utilizar una parte de los fondos para el presente contrato de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los servicios") comprenden: la realización de un estudio de mercado para la interconexión entre los sistemas eléctricos de Bolivia y los países de Chile, Brasil y Paraguay, evaluando el potencial de intercambio binacional que permita establecer señales sobre oportunidades económicas de la interconexión y del corredor eléctrico regional.

Los Términos de Referencia (TDR) detallados para la tarea, se adjuntan a esta solicitud de manifestaciones de interés.

El Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías a través del Viceministerio de Electricidad y Energías Renovables, del Programa Electricidad para Vivir con Dignidad, y de la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto "Mejora del Acceso Sostenible a la Electricidad en Bolivia – IDTR III, invita a empresas/firmas consultoras ("Consultores") elegibles, a expresar su interés en prestar los servicios solicitados. Los "Consultores" interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para realizar los Servicios.

Los criterios de preselección para conformar la lista corta son los siguientes:

Experiencia general

  • Mínimo tres (3) estudios de interconexión y/o planificación de la expansión de sistemas eléctricos en países de la región ejecutados durante los últimos 10 años, con una duración por estudio de al menos 6 meses.
  • Haber realizado al menos tres (3) estudios técnicos - económicos de interconexión de sistemas eléctricos con penetración de energías renovables variables (eólica y solar) en países de la región.

Experiencia Específica

La firma Consultora debe acreditar como mínimo, dos (2) estudios, o servicios prestados en una de las siguientes áreas:

  • Estudios de mercado en interconexiones internacionales en países de la región.
  • Estudios de formación de precios para intercambios de energía entre países de la región.

Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en esta etapa de preselección.

Los consultores interesados deben prestar atención sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las "Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión" del Banco Mundial, quinta edición de septiembre de 2023 que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Para efectos de la decisión de manifestar interés, y de un eventual contrato, el consultor interesado deberá tener en cuenta las causales de conflicto de interés y elegibilidad establecidas en las normas señaladas en el párrafo anterior, las cuales podrán ser consultadas en la página Web: http://www.bancomundial.org/es/

Los consultores pueden asociarse con otras empresas para mejorar sus calificaciones, pero deben indicar claramente si la asociación tiene la forma de una empresa conjunta y/o una subconsultoría. En el caso de una empresa conjunta, todos los socios de la empresa conjunta serán solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si son seleccionados.

Los Consultores serán seleccionados mediante el método de Selección Basada en la Calidad y el Costo, según lo establecido en las regulaciones de adquisiciones indicada anteriormente.

Las expresiones de interés deberán entregarse (según formato adjunto) en físico o por correo electrónico, en la dirección indicada a continuación, a más tardar hasta horas 16:00 del 28 de agosto de 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

GOVERNMENT OF SIERRA LEONE

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

(Consulting Services – Individual Consultant Selection)

 

Date of Issue: 14th August 2026

Country: Republic of Sierra Leone

Name of Project:  Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project

Consulting Services: Recruitment of a Consultant for the Review for the Cybersecurity and Crime Act 2021 and Development of Governance and Regulatory Framework

Reference No: SL-MoF-565256-CS-INDV

 

    1. Introduction

The Government of Sierra Leone (GoSL) has committed to transforming its economy based on a more inclusive and human-centric digital growth and development approach. A high-level vision for the digital economy is articulated in the new National Digital Development Policy (NDDP), which was approved by the Cabinet in December 2021 setting the GoSL’s vision to transform Sierra Leone into an inclusive digital economy and society and to leverage digital technology to support the GoSL to deliver on its national development plan effectively and efficiently. The Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project (SLDTP) aims to expand access to broadband internet, increase digital skills and improve government capacity to deliver public services digitally. The project will support the development of a strong enabling environment for the nation’s digital transformation and digital development agenda as articulated in the National Digital Development Strategy.

 

    1. Objectives

The overall objective of this assignment is to undertake a comprehensive, evidence-based assessment of the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act, 2021 and the evolving national cyber landscape, and to develop a future-ready governance, legal, and regulatory framework that enables effective coordination, enforcement, collaboration, and resilience in Sierra Leone’s cyberspace.

The assignment will support the Government to ensure that its cybersecurity and cybercrime framework is coherent, adaptive, enforceable, aligned with international best practices, and responsive to emerging technologies and threats.

Specifically, the consultant will:

  • Conduct a thorough legal, regulatory, and institutional assessment of the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act, 2021 to determine its adequacy, relevance, effectiveness, and enforceability in addressing current and emerging cyber risks, cyber-enabled crimes, and digital vulnerabilities.
  • Evaluate the coherence, alignment, and interoperability of existing policies, regulations, strategies, institutional mandates, and operational arrangements governing cybersecurity, cybercrime prevention, data protection, digital governance, critical infrastructure protection, and national security.
  • Undertake a comprehensive desk review and benchmarking exercise against relevant regional and international legal instruments, frameworks, standards, and best practices, including but not limited to the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention), the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime, ITU Global Cybersecurity Index, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and ISO/IEC standards, to identify areas of convergence, divergence, and opportunity for reform.
  • Identify legal, regulatory, institutional, operational, technical, and capacity gaps, overlaps, inconsistencies, and coordination challenges that may hinder the effective implementation of cybersecurity governance and cybercrime prevention in Sierra Leone.
  • Clearly define and rationalise institutional roles, responsibilities, mandates, reporting lines, and coordination mechanisms across Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs), law enforcement bodies, regulatory institutions, national security agencies, the judiciary, private sector operators, civil society, and development partners, to ensure clarity, accountability, efficiency, and synergy in cyberspace management.
  • Design and propose a fit-for-purpose regulatory framework supported by appropriate subsidiary legislation, operational guidelines, compliance mechanisms, and enforcement protocols, ensuring a balanced, risk-based, and proportionate approach to cybersecurity regulation and cybercrime control.
  • Develop a comprehensive national cyber governance and coordination framework, including institutional architecture, multi-stakeholder collaboration mechanisms, public-private partnership models, incident response coordination protocols, information-sharing arrangements, and crisis management structures.
  • Formulate a clear, actionable, and costed implementation roadmap, including short-, medium-, and long-term actions, institutional capacity-building measures, financing strategies, and sustainability mechanisms.

The Project Coordination Unit of the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 Revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2025, Procurement Regulations setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
