1.4 Exhibition Area Materials Provision:

Production Requirements for Exhibition Booths and Floats:

28 Exhibition Booths: The booths will primarily feature a wooden frame structure, including the production of booth fascias/signboards, etc.

2 Floats: The main function of the floats is publicity and attracting visitors, providing photo opportunities for the audience and tourists. The decorations must be securely fixed using lightweight, eco-friendly materials to ensure the safety of all personnel on-site.

Production Requirements for Wayfinding Signage:

Wayfinding signage that aligns with the event's on-site theme must be produced, including floor decals, directional signs, etc. These are to effectively guide the flow of visitors to the booths for viewing and tasting, thereby ensuring the overall success of the event.

2. Science Popularization Promotional Materials and Supplies

2.1 Printing of Science Popularization Brochures:

Print 1,000 copies of clear, full-color folded brochures. The content will be provided by the Buyer. The layout, as well as the material and style of the final print, must be implemented only upon the Buyer's approval.

2.2 Quiz Materials for the Science Popularization Zone:

Technical Requirements: Prepare relevant materials to ensure the smooth execution of 4 science popularization interactive quiz sessions over the 2-day event. All materials (including prizes and promotional tote bags) must be of qualified quality and safe to use. The promotional tote bags must feature the Green High-Quality Agricultural Products logo and an information inquiry QR code.

Specific Requirements: Includes 1 spinning wheel with a stand (for the public to draw question numbers on-site), 400 prizes (aligned with the promotional theme, must be green food products, with an average unit price not exceeding RMB 10), and 1,000 promotional tote bags.

3. Event Logistics Support

3.1 Exhibition Area Supporting Facilities:
The exhibition booth design must fully consider the display characteristics of the agricultural product industry. It should rationally plan functional areas such as the product tasting zone, freezer/refrigerator storage area, and centralized storage space. Normal water and power supply must be guaranteed for all areas.

a. Storage and Mailing of Goods for Participating Green High-Quality Agricultural Product Enterprises: The supplier shall be responsible for the mailing, receiving, and storage of agricultural products from participating enterprises before, during, and after the event. The supplier must also assist participating enterprises in transporting the agricultural products to the designated exhibition area. The supplier is responsible for the safe custody of the agricultural products during the event and shall bear the corresponding insurance liability. After the event, the supplier shall safely transport the agricultural products back to the designated location of the original providing units.

b. Rental of 1 Freezer: During the event, 1 freezer shall be rented for on-site preservation of chilled/fresh agricultural products.

c. Event Drinking Water: The brand must meet the Buyer's requirements (C'estbon, Nongfu Spring, Dinghu Mountain Spring, or brands of equivalent grade). The provision includes 1 water dispenser, 12 barrels of bottled water (18.9L/barrel), and 4 cases of bottled water (210ml/24 bottles per case × 2 cases; 380ml/24 bottles per case × 2 cases).

3.2 Audience Seating:

To meet the audience seating needs at the event site, 30 seats shall be set up. At least 31 chairs must be provided on-site (including no less than 10 folding chairs with backrests).

3.3 Makeup and Styling for the Event MC:

The Event MC will be provided by the Buyer, but the supplier shall be responsible for ensuring the makeup and styling of the MC on the day of the event.

3.4 On-site Event Support:

The supplier shall purchase insurance for this event to guarantee the safety of personnel and property during the event period.

During the event, the supplier must arrange no less than 2 staff members to be stationed on-site for emergency response. Their responsibilities include conducting safety inspections for electricity usage, performing emergency equipment repairs, handling emergencies, assisting enterprises with the loading and unloading of goods, and addressing various on-site inquiries and unexpected issues.

4.Event Publicity and Media Coverage

The supplier shall utilize diversified media formats and high-quality visual content to comprehensively enhance the breadth and depth of the event's communication.

4.1 Graphic and Text Feature Publicity

During the contract period, the supplier shall plan and publish no less than 1 high-quality original publicity article. The content of the article must be approved by the Buyer before publication. Furthermore, within one working day after the conclusion of the first day of the event, the article must be published on at least 3 provincial-level or above mainstream news media platforms and 2 local mainstream news media platforms in Jiangmen (such as authoritative news websites, mobile clients, newspapers, etc.).

4.2 Short Video Production and Promotion

Content Production:

Before and after the event, the supplier shall respectively plan, shoot, and produce no less than 1 creative short video each (2 videos in total). The video content should focus on the themes of agricultural product quality and safety, as well as the Green Food Publicity Week. The pre-event promotional video should be around 60 seconds in length, and the post-event summary video should be around 150 seconds, both conforming to mobile-friendly communication patterns.

Publication and Promotion:

The short videos must be published on at least 2 provincial-level or above mainstream media platforms (or their official new media accounts) and 2 local mainstream media platforms in Jiangmen (or their official new media accounts) (e.g., Douyin, WeChat Channels, Weibo, etc.). The total follower base of the media agency undertaking the publication or its publishing account on the corresponding platform must be no less than 50,000 to ensure basic coverage. The video content must be approved by the Buyer before publication.

 

(II) Collection and Organization of Publicity Outcomes, Summary Report, and Assistance with Project Acceptance

The supplier shall be responsible for organizing materials and establishing a complete archive of publicity outputs, summary reports, and relevant supporting documents. This includes the collection of publicity outcomes from various platforms and the statistical analysis of data such as readership/view counts.

The supplier shall draft an event summary and publicity outcomes report to evaluate the effectiveness of the publicity campaign in raising public awareness of agricultural product quality and safety in the host city, etc.

(III) Other Requirements

1.The supplier shall be responsible for the venue rental and stage setup for this event (the venue shall be designated by the Buyer).

2.During the service period, the supplier must ensure the quality and safety of all materials used for the event during their utilization, and maintain cleanliness at the event site throughout the event period.

3.During both the preparation and execution phases of the event, the supplier must dynamically adjust the on-site layout according to the Buyer's requirements.

4.After the event, the supplier shall be responsible for restoring the venue to its original condition and properly disposing of solid waste generated during the event.

5.All the above-mentioned services shall be submitted to the Buyer for review and may only be executed upon the Buyer's approval.

III. Response Time

During the event service period, the supplier shall provide satisfactory on-site services and resolve any arising issues at any time. In the event of an emergency, the response time shall not exceed 10 minutes, and the issue must be resolved within 1 hour.

The service provider shall submit the publicity campaign outputs and summary report to the Provincial Project Office, including but not limited to the event summary report and relevant supporting documents.

All data, reports, converged media products, and research outcomes generated in the performance of this consulting task, along with their related intellectual property rights, shall be owned by the Buyer.

V. Support Provided by the Buyer

1.The Buyer will work closely with the service provider, designate a dedicated liaison, and provide relevant materials and other support to the service provider.

2.The service provider shall work closely with other relevant participating parties of this sub-project.

VI. Assessment and Evaluation Methods

1.Fully complete all the above-mentioned service contents;

2.Submit the deliverables on time and in full;

3.Take no less than 50 high-definition photos; publish no less than 2 short videos;

4.The total number of views for the graphic/text publicity and short videos across all online platforms shall be no less than 100,000;

5.The satisfaction rate of participants for each event shall be no less than 90%.

1.After the contract is signed, the Buyer shall pay an advance payment of 10% of the total contract price to the successful bidder within 20 working days upon receipt of the event implementation plan and a valid invoice of an equivalent amount provided by the supplier;

2.After the supplier has prepared the event acceptance report and the necessary materials for reimbursement, and upon the Buyer's acceptance and verification without any errors, the Buyer shall pay a progress payment of 90% of the total contract price to the successful bidder within 20 working days upon receipt of a valid invoice of an equivalent amount provided by the supplier.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

COUNTRY:                                                Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

NAME OF PROJECT:                              Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)  

PROJECT ID:                                             P176181   

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:                             Pricing and Interconnection Specialist

REFERENCE NO.:                                    SO-MOCT-FGS-557026-CS-INDV

PLACE OF ASSIGNMENT:                     Mogadishu, Somalia

APPLICATION DEADLINE DATE:       August 15, 2026, at (2.00pm Local Time).

Project Background:

The Federal Government of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP). The Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT) intends to apply part of the proceeds of these Grants to finance for the position of Pricing and Interconnection Specialist in support of the implementation of the National Communications Authority (NCA) in the Federal Government of Somalia.

To support the National Communications Authority's (NCA) mandate to promote fair competition, consumer protection, investment, and sustainable growth in the telecommunications sector, the  NCA seeks to engage a qualified Pricing and Interconnection Specialist to support market data collection and analysis, monitor regulatory compliance, coordinate with operators, prepare technical reports, and maintain regulatory databases.

The Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP) addresses connectivity needs for countries in the Horn of Africa region. The program aims to advance the regional integration of digital markets in Eastern Africa through supporting cross-border connectivity, harmonization of data and e-commerce regulations and policies, and removal of trade barriers, with the vision of establishing a Single Digital Market (SDM). The EA-RDIP project has four components, as briefly described below:

  • Component 1. Connectivity Market Development and Integration.
  • Component 2. Data Market Development and Integration.
  • Component 3. Online Market Development and integration.
  • Component 4. Project Management and implementation.

 

Scope of Work:

National Communications Authority's (NCA) mandate to promote fair competition, consumer protection, investment, and sustainable growth in the telecommunications sector. The NCA is implementing various initiatives related to interconnection, pricing regulation, infrastructure sharing, roaming, licensing, and universal access. To support the effective implementation of these activities, the NCA requires a dedicated Pricing and Interconnection Specialist to provide technical, analytical, administrative, and operational support to the NCA. The Pricing and Interconnection Specialist will contribute to the day-to-day implementation of regulatory activities related to interconnection, pricing, roaming, infrastructure sharing, licensing, and market analysis, while assisting in stakeholder engagement, monitoring compliance, maintaining regulatory records, and preparing technical reports. Also, the Pricing and Interconnection Specialist shall assist in collecting and analyzing market data, monitoring compliance, coordinating with operators, preparing reports, maintaining regulatory databases. For more details refer to the Terms and Reference (ToR).

Required Qualifications and Experiences:

The shortlisting criteria for the Pricing and Interconnection Specialist position are as follows:

  • A Bachelor's degree in Telecommunications Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Economics, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Business Administration.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of professional experience in telecommunications regulation, telecommunications operations, interconnection, pricing, market analysis, licensing, infrastructure sharing, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience in telecommunications market analysis, tariff monitoring, regulatory compliance, or telecommunications policy implementation.
  • Experience working with telecommunications operators, regulatory authorities, government institutions, development partners, or ICT sector projects.
  • Experience in collecting, analyzing, and interpreting telecommunications market data and industry statistics.
  • Experience supporting stakeholder consultations, industry engagements, workshops, and regulatory coordination activities.

Duration and Reporting of the Assignment: The Pricing and Interconnection Specialist will be engaged for a period of one (1) year to renewal on an annual basis based on satisfactory performance certified by NCA and availability of funds. The consultant will report to the client, the National Communications Authority (NCA), through its Director General as a supervisor; the consultant should submit written monthly and quarterly progressive reports with the review and satisfactory approval of the client.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing these services. Interested Individual Consultants must submit their Curriculum Vitae (CV) and cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: https://nca.gov.so/ or it can be forwarded to the applicant upon written request to the project generic email address indicated below.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The selection will be conducted in accordance with the procedures for selection of Individual Consultants set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers dated September 2023 (Procurement Regulations).

Interested Consultant may obtain further information in a written communication to the below project generic email address during office hours from 8:30am to 3.30pm local time (Excluding public holidays).

A Complete application of Curriculum Vitae (CV) and Cover letter should be submitted electronically (by e-mail) to the address below on, or before August 15, 2026, at 2.00pm, (Local Time) marked clearly as “Expression of Interest for Pricing & Interconnection Specialist; SO-MOCT-FGS-557026-CS-INDV)”

 

To: Procurement Office, EA-RDIP

Project Implementation Unit (PIU)

E-mail: procurement.ea-rdip@moct.gov.so

And;

Copy to: The Director General of NCA. E-mail: Dg@nca.gov.so

APPEL A MANIFESTATION

PRESTATION D’ÉTUDES TECHNIQUES, ENVIRONNEMENTALES ET SOCIALES (E&S), ET MISSION DE SUIVI ET CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX D’ALIMENTATION EN EAU POTABLE (AEP) DANS 68 CENTRES DE LA JIRAMA

Crédit IDA : 7121-MG/Don IDA EO40-MG

AMI  N°003/26 WJIR – C

Date de lancement : 29 Juillet 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du « PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES A L’EAU POTABLE, PAAEP – JIRAMA et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat pour la prestation d’études techniques, environnementales et sociales (E&S), et mission de suivi et contrôle des travaux d’alimentation en eau potable dans 68 centres de la JIRAMA.

2. Les services, au titre de ce contrat, portent sur trois missions différentes, notamment :

(i) La réalisation des Etudes d'Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES)/ Plan de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (PGES) et Plan de Réinstallation (PR) des 10 centres en vue de remplacement des conduites vétustes ;

(ii) La réalisation des études techniques et des EIES/PGES et PR des 20 centres sur 68, dont les travaux d’Alimentation en Eau Potable initialement prévus qui n’ont pas été achevés par le Ministère et ;

(iii) La mission de suivi, contrôle et supervision couvrant les aspects techniques et la gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux des travaux d’Alimentation en Eau Potable dans les 68 centres JIRAMA.

La date prévisionnelle du commencement des travaux est prévue en fin décembre 2026 et prévue pour une durée de vingt-trois (23) mois.

3. Les termes de référence détaillés (TdRs) pour la mission à manifestation d'intérêt peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

4. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PAAEP-JIRAMA invite les Consultants (Bureaux d’études, Cabinets de consultants, etc.) éligibles ("Consultants") à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations (brochures, dépliants, fiches, attestations et autres supports …) permettant d’évaluer leurs capacités, expériences, champs d’expertise et missions accomplies à assurer ladite prestation.

5. Le Consultant, ou l’un des membres dans le cas d’un groupement doit avoir au moins Dix (10) ans d’existence. Dans leur dossier de manifestation d’intérêt, les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services et joindre dans leur dossier au moins les pièces suivantes :

  • une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt ;
  • la présentation détaillée du Consultant (format libre) ;
  • les références concernant l’exécution de contrats similaires durant les Dix (10) dernières années en précisant clairement l’intitulé, le nom, l’adresse et les contacts du Client, l’année de réalisation moyennant les dates de début et de fin de la mission, le montant du contrat, la liste des profils et nombre des experts clés ayant réalisé la mission, et tout document justifiant la bonne fin de la mission.

Les critères de sélection d’une liste restreinte sont les suivants :

- Justifier d'une expérience générale d'au moins dix (10) années dans les études techniques et/ou les missions de contrôle et de surveillance de travaux d'infrastructures;

- Justifier d'au moins cinq (05) références réalisées au cours des dix (10) dernières années portant sur des missions d'études de faisabilité, d'Avant-Projets Sommaires (APS), d'Avant-Projets Détaillés (APD), de préparation de Dossiers d'Appel d'Offres (DAO) et/ou de contrôle et surveillance de travaux d'alimentation en eau potable en milieu urbain ou périurbain;

- Justifier d'au moins trois (03) références relatives à des projets de réseaux d'adduction et de distribution d'eau potable comprenant notamment des conduites, des réservoirs, des stations de pompage ou des ouvrages hydrauliques similaires;

- Disposer d'une expérience avérée dans la réalisation de prestations intégrant les aspects environnementaux et sociaux (EIES, PGES, PAR ou instruments équivalents), conformément aux exigences des bailleurs de fonds internationaux ou de la réglementation nationale;

- Démontrer une expérience de prestations financées par des institutions financières internationales (Banque mondiale, BAD, AFD, UE, etc.) ou par des organismes de financement similaires, ce critère constituant un atout;

- Présenter des références démontrant la bonne exécution des missions, attestées par des certificats de bonne fin, des procès-verbaux de réception ou tout document équivalent délivré par les maîtres d'ouvrage;

Ces références devront démontrer une expérience couvrant l'ensemble des types d'ouvrages suivants :

  • Fourniture et pose de groupes électropompes d'une capacité minimale de 50 m³/h pour des stations de pompage d’Alimentation en Eau Potable ;
  • Construction ou réhabilitation de bâtiments d'exploitation ;
  • Pose de canalisations en PEHD de diamètre DN 110 mm ou supérieur, sur un linéaire d'au moins 5 km en milieu urbain ;
  • Construction ou réhabilitation de stations de traitement d'eau brute d'une capacité minimale de 5 000 m³/j ;
  • Construction ou réhabilitation de réservoirs en béton armé d'une capacité minimale de 200 m³.

- Justifier d'au moins trois (03) références dans la réalisation d’EIES pour des projets d'infrastructures hydrauliques, dont au moins une (01) relative à un projet d’ Alimentation en Eau Potable ;

- Justifier d'au moins trois (03) références dans l'élaboration de Plan de Réinstallation (PR) pour des projets d'infrastructures hydrauliques.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à l’étape de la préparation de la liste restreinte.

6. L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI » 7ème édition - Septembre 2025 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts. En outre, veuillez-vous référer au paragraphe 3.17 du Règlement concernant les conflits d'intérêts liés à cette mission.

7. Les Consultants peuvent s'associer à d'autres firmes pour renforcer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l'association prend la forme d'une coentreprise et/ou d'une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d'une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de l'intégralité du contrat, s'ils sont sélectionnés. Les membres du groupement ne dépasseront pas Trois (03).

8. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode Sélection fondée sur la qualité et le coût (SFQC) énoncée dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

9. Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le Vendredi 04 Septembre 2026 à Dix (10) heures locales.

De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 09h00 à 14h00 (heure de Madagascar).

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Individual Consultant Services

Environmental and Social (E&S) Audit Consultant

Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC)

The Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP), through the Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC), invites qualified individual consultants to express their interest in providing consulting services for conducting an Environmental and Social (E&S) Audit of Component 1 – Labor-Intensive Infrastructure.

Background

The Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC) is financed by the World Bank and implemented under the overall oversight of the Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP). The project aims to:

  1. Increase employment opportunities for selected groups in targeted areas; and
  2. Improve the operational capacity of selected government institutions.

Under Component 1, implemented by the Municipal Development and Lending Fund (MDLF), the project finances labor-intensive public infrastructure activities across the West Bank.

In accordance with the project's Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), MoFP intends to recruit a qualified Environmental and Social Consultant to conduct an independent Environmental and Social Audit of a representative sample of sub-projects implemented under Component 1.

Scope of the Assignment

The Consultant will assess compliance of selected sub-projects with:

  • World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and relevant Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs);
  • Project Environmental and Social instruments, including the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), Land Acquisition and Livelihood Framework (LALF), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), and Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP);
  • Applicable Palestinian environmental, social, labor, and occupational health and safety regulations.

The Consultant will undertake document reviews, stakeholder consultations, field visits, compliance assessments, and prepare a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) identifying gaps and recommendations for improvement.

Key Deliverables

1. Inception Report – within three (3) weeks from contract signature.

2. Draft Environmental and Social Audit Report including Corrective Action Plan (CAP) – within eight (8) weeks from contract signature.

3. Final Environmental and Social Audit Report including CAP – within twelve (12) weeks from contract signature.

Duration of Assignment

The assignment is expected to be completed within three (3) months from contract signing.

Required Qualifications and Experience

The Consultant shall possess:

  • A Master's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Social Sciences, Planning, Development Studies, or another relevant discipline.
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in environmental and social risk assessment and management.
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting Environmental and Social Audits, with a minimum of three (3) similar assignments. Experience in donor-funded or development projects will be an advantage.
  • Proven knowledge of Palestinian environmental, social, labor, and occupational health and safety legislation.
  • Demonstrated experience with international environmental and social standards, particularly the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
  • Excellent analytical, report-writing, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Excellent command of English, both written and spoken.

Selection Method and Evaluation Criteria

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and based on the qualifications and experience of the applicant.

The evaluation will be conducted out of a total score of 100 points as follows:

Evaluation Criteria

Points

Academic Qualifications relevant to the assignment

15

General Professional Experience in Environmental and Social Risk Assessment and Management

25

Specific Experience in conducting Environmental and Social Audits, including donor-funded and infrastructure projects

35

Experience with World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and related safeguards requirements

15

Knowledge of Palestinian environmental, social and labor legislation and report-writing skills

10

Total

100

 

Only candidates obtaining a minimum technical score of 70 points may be invited for an interview, if deemed necessary by the evaluation committee.

  1. The Ministry of Health (MoH) of the Republic of Indonesia has received loan financing from the World Bank to support the implementation of the Indonesia Health System Strengthening (IHSS) Project, with total funding amounting to EUR 3.7 billion. The IHSS Project (“the Project”) is a national initiative aimed at strengthening primary healthcare, referral services, and public health laboratories through the provision of medical equipment and capacity building across health facilities nationwide. To support the timely and accountable implementation of the Project, the MoH intends to engage a qualified law firm to provide legal advisory services, ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and strengthen the Project’s documentation and record-keeping systems. The assignment is intended to promote consistent implementation of sound documentation, indexing, and legal compliance practices throughout the Project lifecycle.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise comprehensive legal and compliance support to the MoH for the implementation of the IHSS Project. The selected firm will assist the MoH in strengthening legal compliance and establishing robust documentation management, record-keeping, and indexing systems to promote sound governance and effective risk mitigation throughout the Project. The firm will conduct ongoing legal and compliance reviews across all Project implementing teams, including SOPHI, SIHREN, InPULS, and project management activities, regardless of the financing sources. In addition, the firm will provide practical recommendations and capacity-building support to MoH personnel to institutionalize a strong compliance culture and systematic documentation practices. The scope of services will include, but not be limited to, the following: i) Legal Compliance and Regulatory Review; ii) Documentation Management, Record-Keeping, and Indexing; iii) Compliance Monitoring and Reporting; iv) Legal and Regulatory Alignment; v) Governance and Risk Management Support; and vi) Training and Awareness. The assignment is expected to require approximately 162 professional staff-months over the implementation period. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://s.kemkes.go.id/LCDCIHSS
  3. The Services for Legal Compliance and Documentation Consultancy Firm is expected to commence in November 2026 and conclude by April 2028.

Interested Consultants should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (including the name and location/country of the Client, type and scope of services provided, period of contract, contract amount, role of the firm, starting and completion dates, key output delivered and experts involved in the assignment).

The consulting firm shall be a legally registered entity with a valid business license and shall provide evidence of such legal registration. The firm shall possess relevant national and/or international accreditations or certifications applicable to the scope of the assignment (e.g., ISO 37001, ISO 9001, or equivalent).

b. Core business and years in business:

Minimum seven (7) years of proven experience in legal advisory services or related services, which include, but not limited to any of the following areas: regulatory review and/or compliance, contract management, contract dispute resolutions, and governance frameworks.

c. Relevant experience:

1. Demonstrated experience in providing legal services to government agencies/SOEs, international organizations, and/or private entities in any of the following areas:

a) legal compliance review of procurement, contract or project documentation;

b) advisory services on contract drafting, negotiation, and/or dispute resolution;

c) development of legal compliance frameworks, manuals, guidance notes or documentation systems.

Similar experience in any of the above ares under projects financed by Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) such as the World Bank, ADB, AIIB, and IsDB, is an advantage.

MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (MoLGUD)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Country: Somaliland
Project ID: P508408
Project Name: Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho Project Manager
Selection Type: Individual Consultant

Reference No: SO-MOLGUD-567780-CS-INDV
Duty Station: Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project
Duration: 12 months, renewable subject to satisfactory performance
Application Deadline: September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time

1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD) of the Government of Somaliland is implementing the World Bank-financed Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408).

The Bulsho Project provides initial anchor financing to the Government’s multi-year Bulsho Program, whose main objective is to strengthen community and local institutions for improved social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. The Program places citizens and communities at the center of government action and supports decentralization, inclusive local governance, improved service delivery, community participation, and stronger citizen-government relations.

To support effective implementation of the Project, MoLGUD has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and intends to recruit a qualified and experienced PIU Bulsho Project Manager to head the PIU and oversee the overall implementation of the Bulsho Project.

2. SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The PIU Bulsho Project Manager will be responsible for the overall day-to-day management and implementation of the Bulsho Project, providing strategic leadership and supervision to the PIU and coordinating with MoLGUD departments, local governments, district authorities, communities, service providers, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders.

The Project Manager will oversee project planning and implementation; financial management and procurement; local governance and community-driven development; environmental and social safeguards; monitoring, evaluation and learning; stakeholder coordination; compliance and risk management; and sustainability and institutional capacity transfer.

The Project Manager will also oversee local governance and community-driven development processes, including participatory planning, Local Social Contract Platforms (LSCPs), Citizens’ Charters, community engagement, matching grants, community contributions, and community-level investments, ensuring that these processes are transparent, inclusive, accountable, and participatory.

The detailed scope of services, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting arrangements, and other requirements are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

3. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The successful candidate shall meet the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • A university degree in Governance, Political Science, International Relations, Public Administration, Development Studies, Project Management, or a related field. A Master’s degree in a related field is an advantage.
  • A minimum of eight (8) years of progressively responsible professional experience in project management, coordination, or implementation.
  • At least four (4) years of experience managing or coordinating large-scale government or donor-funded programs in local governance, institutional building, or service delivery, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
  • Demonstrated experience in community-driven development (CDD), participatory planning, and community-level implementation of development projects.
  • Demonstrated professional knowledge of the Government of Somaliland and Local Governments, including their structures, functions, and operational frameworks.
  • Experience working in fragility, conflict and violence (FCV) settings, with an understanding of local security dynamics and the ability to support implementation of security management plans.
  • Proven experience in decentralization, capacity building, institutional strengthening, and coordination across different levels of government.
  • Strong leadership and team management capabilities, with sound knowledge and experience in financial management, procurement, monitoring and evaluation, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Strong negotiation, organizational, communication, representation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to deliver effectively under pressure.
  • Demonstrated commitment to gender and social inclusion and engagement of marginalized groups, including women, youth, minority groups, and IDPs.
  • High standards of integrity, ethical conduct, professional accountability, and leadership.
  • In-depth knowledge of Somaliland’s governance structures, political dynamics, and local context, and familiarity with international development partners working in community development, social cohesion, and local governance.
  • Proficiency in relevant project management tools and software.
  • Excellent command of English and Somali, including reading, writing, communication, and presentation skills.

4. REPORTING AND DURATION

The PIU Bulsho Project Manager will report administratively to the Director General of the Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD).

The assignment will initially be for 12 months and may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. The duty station is Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project.

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD), Government of Somaliland, now invites eligible and qualified Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations and applicable Government of Somaliland policies.

 

 

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Interested Consultants should submit:

  1. A detailed and updated Curriculum Vitae (CV), including contact details of three (3) professional referees;
  2. Copies of relevant academic qualification certificates; and
  3. A cover letter outlining the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications in relation to the assignment.

Interested and qualified candidates should submit their applications by email with the subject line:

“Application for PIU Bulsho Project Manager – SO-MOLGUD-567780-CS-INDV”

To: bulsho.somaliland@outlook.com
Cc: dg.molgud@sldgov.org

Applications must be received no later than September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Firm Selection)

Country: Republic of Sierra Leone

Name of Project:  Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project

 

Consulting Services: Recruitment of a Consulting Firm for the Implementation and Operationalization of a License-Free National Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS). Ref: SL-MoF-565234-CS-QCBS

 

    1. Introduction

The Government of Sierra Leone (GoSL) has committed to transforming its economy based on a more inclusive and human-centric digital growth and development approach. A high-level vision for the digital economy is articulated in the new National Digital Development Policy (NDDP), which was approved by the Cabinet in December 2021 setting the GoSL’s vision to transform Sierra Leone into an inclusive digital economy and society and to leverage digital technology to support the GoSL to deliver on its national development plan effectively and efficiently. The Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project (SLDTP) aims to expand access to broadband internet, increase digital skills, and improve government capacity to deliver public services digitally. The project will support the development of a strong enabling environment for the nation’s digital transformation and digital development agenda as articulated in the National Digital Development Strategy.

 

    1. Objectives

The general objective of this assignment is to design, customize, implement, and operationalize a national, end-to-end MHEWS for Sierra Leone that enables NDMA and its partner institutions to effectively manage the full early warning value chain, from risk knowledge and hazard monitoring to warning dissemination and coordinated preparedness and response, using a license-free, sustainable, and nationally owned digital platform. The implemented system shall translate the technical recommendations, blueprint, and SRS into a fully functional, interoperable, and people-centred solution that strengthens disaster risk reduction, protects lives and livelihoods, and supports timely early action.

  1. Specific Objectives

The specific objectives of the assignment are to:

  • Configure and customize an existing, license-free EWS application (open-source or equivalent) to fully meet the functional and technical requirements defined in the approved blueprint and SRS, without developing a system from scratch.
  • Implement an integrated national EWS platform that operationalizes all four pillars of a MHEWS:
    • Risk Knowledge
    • Detection, Monitoring and Forecasting
    • Warning Dissemination and Communication
    • Preparedness and Response
  • Implement the MHEWS using a phased implementation approach, beginning with a priority hazard to validate system functionality, data-sharing workflows, and warning dissemination mechanisms before expanding the system to additional hazards, datasets, and dissemination channels.
  • Establish a centralized decision-support and early warning platform anchored at the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), with secure connectivity to District Emergency Operations Centres (DEOCs) and community-level structures.
  • Enable real-time and near-real-time data integration from multiple hazard monitoring systems, sector institutions, and external data sources, supporting automated analysis, forecasting, and impact-based decision-making.
  • Operationalize a Common Alerting Protocol (CAP)–compliant national alerting system that serves as the single authoritative source for public warnings and supports multi-channel dissemination, including digital, telecom, media, and community-based channels.
  • Ensure inclusive, people-centred warning delivery, including accessibility features for persons with disabilities, and mechanisms to reach at-risk populations in remote and low-connectivity areas.
  • Strengthen preparedness and response coordination by providing digital tools for incident management, forecast-to-action workflows, resource tracking, situation reporting, drills, and after-action review.
  • Ensure interoperability with existing national digital platforms and sector systems, using open standards and APIs, and leveraging the hosting environment provided by MoCTI.
  • Implement robust security, role-based access control, audit trails, and governance mechanisms to protect the integrity, authenticity, and reliability of life-critical warning information.
  • Design and operationalize integrated data-sharing protocols between NDMA and relevant national institutions to support effective early warning operations. This shall include the definition and implementation of data governance and access protocols; interoperability standards and application programming interfaces (APIs); secure real-time and near-real-time data exchange mechanisms; and clearly defined roles and responsibilities of participating institutions. The assignment shall also support the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to govern operational workflows for the MHEWS, including protocols for validating and acting upon field reports and community acknowledgements, alert generation and approval processes, inter-agency coordination during emergencies, and procedures for warning dissemination through telecom operators, broadcasters, and other communication channels. The data-sharing framework shall enable timely, accurate, and secure dissemination of disaster-related information to NDMA decision-makers, partner institutions, and the public, in line with national governance arrangements and security requirements.
  • Build institutional capacity and ensure sustainability through comprehensive documentation, training, knowledge transfer, and handover, enabling NDMA to fully own, manage, maintain, and expand the system without reliance on proprietary licenses or vendor lock-in.
  • Deliver a fully tested, accepted, and operational EWS that complies with national policies and international best practices for multi-hazard early warning systems and supports Sierra Leone’s commitments to disaster risk reduction and early warnings for all.

The Project Coordination Unit of the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are core business and years in business, relevant experience, and technical and managerial capability of the firm. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers July 2016 Revised September 2025 Seventh Edition, and National Public Procurement Act 2016, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Base Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information and detailed Terms of Reference can be obtained at the link below:  - https://mocti.gov.sl/tor-recruitment-of-a-consulting-firm-for-the-implementation-and-operationalization-of-a-license-free-national-multi-hazard-early-warning-system-mhews/
SLDPT - https://sldtp.gov.sl/2026/08/12/tor-recruitment-of-a-consulting-firm-for-the-implementation-and-operationalization-ofa-license-free-national-multi-hazard-early-warning-system-mhews/

Título da consultoria: Contratação de um (1) Consultor Nacional para Formação em Prevenção e controlo de infeção no laboratório associado à resistência antimicrobiana.

 

Ref. Nº: 47/C/HERR/2026

 

O Governo da República Democrática de S. Tomé e Príncipe, através do Ministério da Economia e Finanças, recebeu um finaciamento da Associação Internacional para o Desenvolvimento (IDA), para apoiar a implemantação do Projeto Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (HERR), e pretende utilizar parte deste recurso para a contratação de serviços de consultoria.

 

O serviço de consultoria consiste na contratação de um (1) Consultor Nacional para Formação em Prevenção e controlo de infeção no laboratório associado à resistência antimicrobiana.

 

 Objetivos da consultoria

Os principais objetivos da consultoria são:

  1. Selecionar um(a) especialista experiente para prestar apoio técnico especializado.
  2. Capacitar os técnicos do Laboratório Nacional de Referência (LNR), assegurando a transferência efetiva de metodologias modernas de controlo de infeção e vigilância da RAM.

O Termo de Referência (TdR) poderá ser solicitado através dos seguintes endereços eletrónicos:

 saude_regional.procurement@afap.st / dg.procurement@afap.st. 

A Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos (AFAP) convida consultores individuais elegíveis (Consultores) a manifestarem o seu interesse na prestação dos serviços, mediante a submissão de uma Carta de Intenção, documento de identificação, Curriculum Vitae atualizado e assinado, e os respetivos comprovativos de formação académica.

Os consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem possuir as qualificações e experiências necessárias para executar os serviços, em conformidade com o Termo de Referência (TdR).

O Consultor deverá possuir as seguintes qualificações mínimas:

  1. Formação Académica
  • Licenciatura em Ciências Biomédicas, Microbiologia, Análises Clínicas, Medicina, Saúde Pública ou áreas estritamente afins.
  • Pós-graduação ou Especialização (Mestrado, Doutoramento ou Curso de Especialização Avançada) em Microbiologia Clínica, Prevenção e Controlo de Infeção (PCI), Biossegurança Laboratorial ou Vigilância da Resistência Antimicrobiana (RAM) constituirá uma vantagem competitiva relevante.

 

  1. Experiência Profissional
  • Mínimo de 5 (cinco) anos de experiência profissional comprovada no domínio do diagnóstico laboratorial microbiológico.
  • Experiência prática consolidada na facilitação de ações de formação de curta ou média duração direcionadas a profissionais da área médica e de saúde.
  • Comprovada experiência de trabalho no desenvolvimento ou implementação de programas de Prevenção e Controlo de Infeção (PCI).
  • Experiência prática em recolha, transporte, processamento e análise microbiológica de amostras de matriz ambiental e hospitalar.
  • Conhecimento robusto das dinâmicas e metodologias de vigilância epidemiológica e laboratorial da Resistência Antimicrobiana (RAM).
  • Familiaridade comprovada com as diretrizes e manuais da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), bem como com os normativos e protocolos de biossegurança vigentes.

 

  1. Competência Técnica
  • Excelente capacidade pedagógica, de facilitação e de formação contínua de adultos (andragogia).
  • Elevado rigor e competência técnica em redação científica e elaboração de relatórios profissionais.
  • Excelentes capacidades de comunicação interpessoal, facilidade de articulação institucional e aptidão para trabalhar de forma colaborativa com equipas multidisciplinares.

 

  1. Competência Linguística
  • Excelente domínio da língua portuguesa, capacidade de comunicar em inglês e /ou francês.

 

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para o disposto na Seção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (FPI) do Banco Mundial, edição de setembro de 2025, que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial relativa a conflitos de interesse.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – CONSULTANCY FIRM)

ALBANIA

Project: National Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Modernization Program (P4R)

TF No.: B8448

Assignment Title: Strategic Coastal Water Supply Framework and Feasibility Studies for Priority Water Supply Investments in the South Coast of Albania

Reference No.: AL-AKUK -329330-CS-QCBS

Albania is implementing governance and service reforms in the WSS sector supported by the World Bank through P4R project financed by SECO (Swiss Government). In parallel, structural reform changes are being launched by the government, including the creation of the new Water Production Operator (OPU) while the details of its future role and structure are still evolving; therefore this assignment shall focus on AKUK’s current mandate and existing institutional set-up, and reflect OPU-related interfaces only where and when formally clarified or necessary as working assumptions.

 

This Request for Expressions of Interest aims to assist AKUK in hiring a Consultant to prepare a Feasibility Study for potable water supply within the defined Project Area with a planning horizon extending to 2050, building upon the analyses, methodologies and strategic planning principles developed under the DWD DSIP and subsequent sector planning initiatives.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://akuk.gov.al/

The activities described in these TORs are expected to be completed within a period of 10 months, following the signing of the consultancy contract.

The consulting firm shall demonstrate proven experience in assignments of similar nature, including:

  • At least one (1) completed projects in strategic water supply planning, master planning, or system development studies;
  • At least one (1) assignments involving water resources assessment and supply-demand balance analysis;
  • At least one (1) projects including water demand forecasting based on demographic, tourism, and consumption scenarios;
  • At least one (1) assignment involving strategic assessment of water supply infrastructure alternatives;
  • At least one (1) project including economic and technical evaluation of alternatives;
  • At least one (1) project carried out for a water utility, public water operator, or public authority responsible for water services;
  • Experience in GIS-based infrastructure planning and spatial analysis.
  • Experience in projects implemented in tourism-intensive areas or comparable environments will be considered an asset.
  • Preference will be given to firms with experience in projects financed by International Financial Institutions (IFI) or European Union programmes.

The assignment shall be carried out by a multidisciplinary team. The indicative total input is of approximately sixty-five (65) person-months, reflecting the feasibility, environmental and social, and field investigation components. The core team shall include, at minimum:

  • Team Leader / Senior Water Supply Engineer;
  • Water Resources / Hydrogeologist;
  • Hydraulic Modelling Engineer;
  • Financial/Economic Analyst;
  • Environmental Specialist (P-ESIA);
  • Social Development Specialist (ESS5/ESS10);
  • GIS and Data Management Specialist;
  • Institutional/Utility Specialist;
  • Climate Resilience Specialist,

The proposed experts may be national and/or international, as appropriate for the assignment, and supported by additional experts, survey teams and field investigation activities. The Consultant shall justify the proposed allocation of expert inputs in its Technical Proposal. Please see criteria for the experts within ToRs document.

The evaluation criteria to be used for selecting the successful Consultant will be the following:

•           General Qualifications, including core business and years in business, (30 points);

•           Relevant experience, including previous experience in the field of assignment, (70 points);

The service will be selected under the provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations), in investment project financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services November 2020, in accordance with Quality and Cost Based Selecton (QCBS), Lump-Sum Contract. The Bank requires that firms or individuals involved in Bank IPF procurement shall not have conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 16:00, Mondays to Thursdays, and from 08:00 to 14:00 on Fridays.

Expressions of interest (CV, Cover letter and documentary evidence for fulfilling the qualifications) must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail within September 10th, 2026.

Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité et obtenu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA)  d’un montant équivalent à US$ 250 millions de dollars en vue de financer le coût du Projet de Stabilisation et de Relèvement de l'Est de la RDC (« le projet » ou « STAR-Est » et se propose d’utiliser une partie les fonds de ce crédit pour financer les services suivants : soutenir la stabilisation et le relèvement par (i) la fourniture d'infrastructures socio-économiques communautaires de base à petite échelle ; (ii) la réinsertion socio-économique des personnes associées aux groupes armés dans leurs communautés dans les zones ciblées des provinces de Ituri, du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu et (iii) le renforcement des administrations provinciales.

Name of Project: Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR)

Grant No: P176371

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant (IC) to perform the Consultancy services to develop a Continental Statistical Database.

Reference No. TN-STATAFRIC-AUC-546831-CS-INDV.

 

  1. Background

The African Union Commission (AUC) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program for Results Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Selection of an Individual Consultant (IC) to perform the Consultancy services to develop a Continental Statistical Database.

 

Reliable and harmonized statistical data are critical for monitoring development progress, guiding resource allocation, and supporting evidence-based policy-making across Africa. The African Union Institute for Statistics (STATAFRIC), established under the African Union (AU), plays a central role in coordinating statistical development and strengthening the African statistical system at the continental level.

 

The importance of good quality data cannot be over-emphasized, and a lot of efforts and investments have been made in data production by different stakeholders. However, access to harmonized, centralized, and consistently documented statistical datasets remains largely limited due to:

  • Fragmented and siloed national and regional databases with incompatible structures.
  • Inconsistent application of data standards, indicator definitions, and classification frameworks.
  • Absence of automated or structured mechanisms for data submission to continental repositories.
  • Limited data documentation and metadata, reducing discoverability and usability.
  • Restricted public access to existing datasets, hindering research and policy uptake.

To address these structural gaps, STATAFRIC intends to establish a Continental Statistical Database (CSD), a centralized and harmonized repository and dissemination platform for key socio-economic indicators across Africa. The CSD will consolidate data from NSOs and RECs, ensure compliance with international standards, and provide open and structured access to continental statistics.

 

STATAFRIC therefore seeks to recruit a qualified individual consultant to lead the design, development, and operationalization of this continental statistical database.

 

  1. Objectives of the assignment
  1. Conduct a structured assessment of existing statistical data sources, repositories, and data quality across African countries, National Statistical Offices (NSOs) and Regional Economic Communities (RECs), as well as relevant global institutions (e.g., ILOStat, FAOStat, UNSD) in coordination with STATAFRIC.
  2. Design a conceptual and logical data model for the Continental Statistical Database, aligned with international statistical standards and with statistical harmonization standards/guidelines developed by STATAFRIC.
  3. Develop and deploy the operational database with ingestion pipelines, validation mechanisms, and scalable storage infrastructure.
  4. Establish data harmonization procedures, developed by STGs in each thematic area, to align indicators, classifications, and metadata across diverse sources.
  5. Develop a user-friendly dissemination platform with data visualization, API access, and open data capabilities.
  6. Build the institutional capacity of STATAFRIC staff through training and comprehensive documentation.

 

  1. Expected Deliverables

This consultancy service is a lump-sum and deliverables based, and submissions must be submitted in English and/or French. Deliverables are subject to review and approval by STATAFRIC before corresponding payment is made. A request by the consultant for additional time on a specific deliverable may be considered and approved by STATAFRIC, provided the overall contract duration and lump-sum budget are respected.

Reliable and harmonized statistical data are critical for monitoring development progress, guiding resource allocation, and supporting evidence-based policy-making across Africa. The African Union Institute for Statistics (STATAFRIC), established under the African Union (AU), plays a central role in coordinating statistical development and strengthening the African statistical system at the continental level.

 

The importance of good quality data cannot be over-emphasized, and a lot of efforts and investments have been made in data production by different stakeholders. However, access to harmonized, centralized, and consistently documented statistical datasets remains largely limited due to:

  • Fragmented and siloed national and regional databases with incompatible structures.
  • Inconsistent application of data standards, indicator definitions, and classification frameworks.
  • Absence of automated or structured mechanisms for data submission to continental repositories.
  • Limited data documentation and metadata, reducing discoverability and usability.
  • Restricted public access to existing datasets, hindering research and policy uptake.

 

To address these structural gaps, STATAFRIC intends to establish a Continental Statistical Database (CSD) a centralized and harmonized repository and dissemination platform for key socio-economic indicators across Africa. The CSD will consolidate data from NSOs and RECs, ensure compliance with international standards, and provide open and structured access to continental statistics.

 

STATAFRIC therefore seeks to recruit a qualified individual consultant to lead the design, development, and operationalization of this continental statistical database.

 

  1. Objectives of the Consultancy

 

  1. General Objectives:

To design and implement a comprehensive, scalable, and standards-compliant continental statistical database that consolidates and harmonizes statistical data from across Africa, and makes it accessible to policymakers, researchers, institutions, different stakeholders and the public.

 

  1. Specific Objectives
  1. Conduct a structured assessment of existing statistical data sources, repositories, and data quality across African countries, National Statistical Offices (NSOs) and Regional Economic Communities (RECs), as well as relevant global institutions (e.g., ILOStat, FAOStat, UNSD) in coordination with STATAFRIC.
  2. Design a conceptual and logical data model for the Continental Statistical Database, aligned with international statistical standards and with statistical harmonization standards/guidelines developed by STATAFRIC.
  3. Develop and deploy the operational database with ingestion pipelines, validation mechanisms, and scalable storage infrastructure.
  4. Establish data harmonization procedures, developed by STGs in each thematic area, to align indicators, classifications, and metadata across diverse sources.
  5. Develop a user-friendly dissemination platform with data visualization, API access, and open data capabilities.
  6. Build the institutional capacity of STATAFRIC staff through training and comprehensive documentation.

 

  1. Scope of Work

The consultant will carry out the following tasks, organized into six work streams:

 

  1. Assessment of Existing Data Sources.
  1. Select, in consultation with STATAFRIC and the relevant Specialized Technical Groups (STGs), a set of key priority thematic areas (such as demography, health, education, environment, agriculture), and conduct an assessment (census) of data availability and quality across all African Union member states.
  2. Assess data formats, classification standards, indicator definitions, and quality levels across identified sources.
  3. Evaluate existing databases and repositories at NSOs, RECs, and continental bodies, documenting their structure, accessibility, update frequency, and interoperability.
  4. Identify priority datasets and indicator sets for initial integration into the CSD.
  5. Produce a structured data source inventory with metadata profiles for each identified source.

 

  1. Database Design.
  1. Develop a conceptual and logical data model for the Continental Statistical Database, covering indicator dimensions, geographic levels, temporal coverage, and data provenance.
  2. Define metadata standards and data classification frameworks, aligned with SDMX, DDI, or equivalent international standards.
  3. Design the physical database architecture, including table structures, indexing strategy, partitioning approach, and storage infrastructure (on-premises, cloud, or hybrid).
  4. Specify data versioning and historization mechanisms to preserve data lineage and support trend analysis.
  5. Produce an entity-relationship diagram and a data dictionary covering all database objects.

 

  1. Database Development.
  1. Build and deploy the operational Continental Statistical Database according to the approved design specifications.
  2. Develop automated data ingestion pipelines supporting a combination of publicly available data from NSOs and RECs and, where such data is not publicly available, direct data submission by NSOs and RECs, through batch file uploads (CSV, Excel, SDMX-ML), API-based data feeds, and manual data entry for priority sources.
  3. Implement data validation rules at ingestion covering format checks, range validation, consistency checks, and duplicate detection.
  4. Ensure the database is optimized for performance with large datasets (target: support for data from all 55 AU member states across multiple time series).
  5. Implement a data versioning system enabling rollback and audit trail of all data changes.
  6. Deploy the system in a high-availability environment with a target uptime of ≥ 99.5%.

 

  1. Data Harmonization.

 

Continental data harmonization activities are carried out by the Specialized Technical Groups (STGs) of SHaSA 2 in close coordination with STATAFRIC. The consultant is expected to:

 

  1. Develop a data harmonization framework, as defined by relevant STGs, for aligning indicator definitions, units of measure, geographic classifications, and time periods across national sources.
  2. Implement automated and semi-automated harmonization rules within the ingestion pipeline, with flagging of anomalies requiring manual review.
  3. Align all integrated indicators with internationally recognized statistical standards and classifications (e.g., ISIC, COICOP, ICD, ICLS, SDG indicator framework).
  4. Define and document data quality dimensions (accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, comparability) and implement corresponding quality flags on all datasets.
  5. Establish a data quality review workflow, including roles and responsibilities for data validation and approval.

 

  1. Data Dissemination Platform.
  1. Develop a user-friendly web interface for browsing, querying, and downloading data from the Continental Statistical Database.
  2. Implement interactive dashboards and data visualization tools, including time-series charts, comparative country views, thematic maps, and exportable tables.
  3. Provide open data access for public datasets via downloadable files (CSV, Excel, JSON) and a documented public API (REST, JSON-stat or SDMX-JSON).
  4. Implement tiered access management: public access for open datasets; authenticated access for restricted or embargoed data.
  5. Ensure the platform is accessible on both desktop and mobile devices and meets basic web accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA).
  6. Implement a metadata catalogue enabling users to browse and search dataset documentation.

 

  1. Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer.
  1. Develop a structured training programme for STATAFRIC staff covering database administration, data ingestion and validation workflows, harmonization procedures, and platform management.
  2. Conduct a minimum of two (2) hands-on training sessions for STATAFRIC staff and relevant stakeholders from NSOs and RECs.
  3. Produce comprehensive documentation including database architecture documents, data dictionary, administrator manual, end-user manual, and API documentation.
  4. Develop a maintenance and sustainability plan, including recommended staffing profile, estimated annual maintenance costs, data update schedule, and an upgrade roadmap for Years 2–3.

 

  1. Expected Deliverables

This consultancy is a lump-sum and deliverables based, and submissions must be submitted in English and/or French. Deliverables are subject to review and approval by STATAFRIC before corresponding payment is made. A request by the consultant for additional time on a specific deliverable may be considered and approved by STATAFRIC, provided the overall contract duration and lump-sum budget are respected.

  2. Demonstrated experience working with large-scale statistical datasets, including data from NSOs or international statistical agencies.
  3. Practical knowledge of data harmonization methodologies and metadata standards (SDMX, DDI, or equivalent).
  4. Experience designing and implementing data ingestion pipelines, ETL processes, and automated validation mechanisms.
  5. Experience developing data dissemination platforms or open data portals accessible to non-technical users.
  6. Experience conducting data source assessments and gap analyses.

 

The following experience is an asset:

  1. Prior work with African Union institutions, regional economic communities, or national statistical offices in Africa.
  2. Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP or equivalent) for database hosting and management.
  3. Familiarity with the SDG indicator framework and international statistical classification systems (ISIC, COICOP, ICLS, ICD, etc.).
  4. Proficiency in both English and French.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Assignment Title: CONSULTANCY SERVICE FOR THE PREPARATION OF TECHNICAL-ECONOMIC-FINANCIAL FEASIBILITY STUDIES FOR THE CAÁLA INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT HUB

Reference No. 91CS2/MINPLAN/26

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the preparation of technical-economic-financial feasibility studies for the Caála Industrial Development Hub.

The consulting services (“the Services”) aim to provide a detailed analysis of the technical, economic, financial, legal, social, and environmental viability of implementing the project. The goal is to ensure the infrastructure's success, sustainability, and resilience to climate change, while maximizing economic benefits for the local and national economy.

The Consulting Firm will be responsible for:

  1. Conducting a technical feasibility assessment, including site conditions, infrastructure needs, utilities, access, logistics, and other technical requirements;
  2. Preparing an economic feasibility study, including market analysis, demand assessment, identification of priority industrial sectors, value chains, potential investors, and expected economic impact;
  3. Developing a financial feasibility study, including investment cost estimates, operating costs, revenue projections, financial modeling, funding options, and sustainability analysis;
  4. Evaluating the legal, regulatory, institutional, and environmental framework relevant to the establishment and operation of the Industrial Development Hub;
  5. Identifying infrastructure requirements, such as roads, electricity, water, sanitation, telecommunications, drainage, waste management, and other support facilities;
  6. Etc…

The expected duration of the consultancy contract will be 7 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of engineering, economics, finance, environmental and climate resilience, social issues, law, and PPPs;
  • Previous experience in projects funded by multilateral organizations (preferably the World Bank);
  • Demonstrated experience in designing strategies for Industrial Development Hubs and Special Economic Zones, such as nodes for Economic Development Corridors;
  • Demonstrated experience in preparing feasibility studies for smart and resilient industrial development hubs; 
  • Proven experience in preparing ESIA and PAR/RAP reports, preferably in Angola and sub-Saharan African countries; a consortium with a national company duly accredited by MINAMB is permitted.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” revised in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0800 to 1600 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (only by mail) until August 10, 2026.

  • Avoir une bonne maîtrise du français ;
  • Avoir une bonne capacité en analyse financière et rédactionnelle.

PEDIDO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

(SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA - SELEÇÃO DE CONSULTORES INDIVIDUAIS)

 

 

 

PAÍS: São Tomé e Príncipe

 

PROJETO: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach

 

Título da consultoria: Contratação de Consultor Nacional para Elaboração de Instrumentos Normativos de Regulamentação da Vigilância em Saúde, com foco na Institucionalização da Monitorização Contínua do Desempenho da Vigilância em Tempo Real (VIDR).

 

Ref. Nº: 49/C/HERR/2026

 

O Governo da República Democrática de S. Tomé e Príncipe, através do Ministério da Economia e Finanças, recebeu um financiamento da Associação Internacional para o Desenvolvimento (IDA), para apoiar a implementação do Projeto Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (HERR), e pretende utilizar parte deste recurso para a contratação de serviços de consultoria.

 

O serviço de consultoria consiste na contratação de um (1) Consultor Nacional para Elaboração de Instrumentos Normativos de Regulamentação da Vigilância em Saúde, com foco na Institucionalização da Monitorização Contínua do Desempenho da Vigilância em Tempo Real (VIDR).

 

Objetivos da consultoria

Os principais objetivos da consultoria são:

  1. Rever o conteúdo do Código Sanitário revogado (Decreto-lei n.º 59/80).
  2. Elaborar a minuta de um novo instrumento normativo (Regulamento da Vigilância em Saúde ou novo Código Sanitário) que institucionalize a monitorização contínua do desempenho da vigilância em tempo real (VIDR).

O Termo de Referência (TdR) poderá ser solicitado através dos seguintes endereços eletrónicos:

 saúde_regional.procurement@afap.st / dg.procurement@afap.st    

A Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos (AFAP) convida consultores individuais elegíveis (Consultores) a manifestarem o seu interesse na prestação dos serviços, mediante a submissão de uma Carta de Intenção, documento de identificação, Curriculum Vitae atualizado e assinado, e os respetivos comprovativos de formação académica.

Os consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem possuir as qualificações e experiências necessárias para executar os serviços, em conformidade com o Termos de Referência (TdR).

 

O Consultor deverá possuir as seguintes qualificações mínimas:

 

  1. Formação Académica
  • Licenciatura em Direito, com especialização ou pós-graduação em Direito Sanitário, Direito Administrativo, Políticas Públicas de Saúde ou áreas afins.

 

  1. Experiência Profissional
  • Mínimo de 6 (seis) anos de experiência profissional em assessoria jurídica, consultoria ou carreira pública na área do Direito Sanitário ou Direito Administrativo.
  • Experiência comprovada na elaboração ou revisão de códigos, regulamentos, decretos-lei ou portarias no sector da saúde, preferencialmente em São Tomé e Príncipe ou em países da CPLP.
  • Experiência em processos participativos de construção normativa com múltiplos atores (Estado, parceiros internacionais, sociedade civil).
  • Conhecimento do Código Sanitário revogado (Decreto-lei n.º 59/80) e da Lei de Bases da Saúde de 2018.

.

  1. Competência Técnica
  • Conhecimento aprofundado do Regulamento Sanitário Internacional (RSI 2005) e dos conceitos de VIDR (Vigilância Integrada de Doenças e Resposta).

 

 

 

 

  1. Competência Linguística
  • Excelente domínio da língua portuguesa, capacidade de comunicar em inglês e /ou francês.

 

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para o disposto na Seção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17, do Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (FPI) do Banco Mundial, edição de setembro de 2025, que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial relativa a conflitos de interesse.
