SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE PARA SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA INDIVIDUAL – SMI Nº 2026/006

 

Mutuário: Banco da Amazônia (BASA)

Instituição Financiadora: Banco Internacional para Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD)

País: Brasil

Projeto: Acelerando a Transição Energética na Amazônia (P177200)

Empréstimo: Loan Agreement IBRD [P181966 - TF0C8868]

 

Objeto:

Contratação de Consultor(a) Individual Especialista em Gestão Financeira para apoiar a Unidade de Gestão do Projeto (UGP) e o Banco da Amazônia na implementação do Projeto Acelerando a Transição Energética na Amazônia (AETA), mediante a realização de análises técnicas e financeiras, planejamento e monitoramento orçamentário, desenvolvimento de instrumentos e procedimentos de gestão financeira e fiduciária, apoio à execução e ao acompanhamento dos recursos do Projeto, preparação de relatórios financeiros e gerenciais, suporte aos processos de desembolso, auditoria, supervisão fiduciária e prestação de contas, bem como fortalecimento da capacidade institucional do Banco da Amazônia em gestão financeira de projetos financiados por organismos multilaterais, em conformidade com os requisitos do Banco Mundial, os acordos de financiamento, a legislação aplicável e os instrumentos de governança da operação.

 

Princípios Aplicáveis

O processo de seleção observará os princípios de Value for Money, Integridade, Eficiência, Adequação ao Propósito, Transparência, Economia e Equidade previstos no Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial.

 

Resumo:

O Projeto AETA tem por objetivo ampliar a geração de energia renovável, apoiar investimentos em infraestrutura energética sustentável e reduzir custos de energia na Amazônia Legal, por meio de financiamento do Banco Internacional para Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD) e de recursos de assistência técnica destinados ao fortalecimento institucional do Banco da Amazônia. O Banco da Amazônia atua como mutuário, instituição financeira intermediária e entidade implementadora do Projeto, sendo responsável pela gestão dos recursos financeiros, pela implementação dos componentes financiados e pelo cumprimento das obrigações assumidas perante o Banco Mundial.

No âmbito da implementação do Projeto, o Banco da Amazônia deverá assegurar a adequada gestão financeira e fiduciária dos recursos disponibilizados, incluindo atividades relacionadas ao planejamento orçamentário, monitoramento da execução financeira, gestão de desembolsos, prestação de contas, elaboração de relatórios financeiros, acompanhamento de auditorias e observância dos requisitos fiduciários estabelecidos pelo Banco Mundial e pelos acordos de financiamento da operação.

A estrutura da operação, que combina recursos de empréstimo e de doação destinados ao financiamento de investimentos em transição energética e ao fortalecimento institucional, demanda mecanismos robustos de planejamento financeiro, controle orçamentário, monitoramento da execução físico-financeira, acompanhamento da utilização dos recursos e geração de informações gerenciais e fiduciárias que apoiem a tomada de decisão da UGP e da administração do Banco da Amazônia.

Nesse contexto, a UGP necessita de apoio técnico especializado para fortalecer os mecanismos de gestão financeira e fiduciária do Projeto, apoiar a elaboração de análises financeiras, projeções de desembolso e instrumentos de planejamento orçamentário, desenvolver processos, metodologias e ferramentas de monitoramento financeiro, estruturar mecanismos de controle e conformidade, apoiar auditorias e supervisões fiduciárias e contribuir para o fortalecimento institucional do Banco da Amazônia em gestão financeira de projetos financiados por organismos multilaterais.

A presente contratação tem por finalidade selecionar Consultor(a) Individual Especialista em Gestão Financeira para apoiar a implementação do Projeto AETA, contribuindo para o fortalecimento da governança financeira e fiduciária da operação, para a adequada utilização dos recursos financeiros disponibilizados pelo Banco Mundial e para o fortalecimento da capacidade institucional do Banco da Amazônia em gestão financeira de projetos de investimento.

 

Manifestação de Interesse:

Os interessados deverão apresentar Currículo Vitae (CV) detalhado, no qual o cumprimento dos requisitos obrigatórios e desejáveis, bem como suas qualificações e experiência relevantes para o escopo dos serviços, estejam claramente demonstrados.

As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser enviadas para o e-mail [samara.farias@basa.com.br e pablo.nahmias@basa.com.br] até às [23:59 – horário de Brasília/DF] do dia [28/08/2026].

Os critérios de avaliação do perfil profissional do Consultor Individual estão descritos no Termo de Referência (TDR) da consultoria, que será disponibilizado aos interessados mediante solicitação encaminhada aos e-mails [samara.farias@basa.com.br e pablo.nahmias@basa.com.br]. Para fins de identificação, recomenda-se que a solicitação informe o número da Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse (SMI) correspondente. Os critérios incluem, minimamente: 

Qualificações Obrigatórias (Critérios Eliminatórios):

  • Formação Acadêmica Mínima:  Graduação completa em Administração, Economia, Ciências Contábeis, Finanças, Engenharia de Produção, Engenharia Econômica, Matemática, Estatística ou áreas correlatas reconhecidas pelo Ministério da Educação (MEC).
  • Experiência Profissional: Mínimo de 5 (cinco) anos de experiência profissional comprovada em atividades relacionadas à gestão financeira, planejamento financeiro, orçamento, controladoria, gestão fiduciária, finanças corporativas, auditoria, gestão de projetos, acompanhamento de investimentos ou áreas correlatas.
  • Experiência em Projetos Complexos: Mínimo de 5 (cinco) anos de experiência comprovada em projetos de elevada complexidade técnica e financeira, envolvendo investimentos, infraestrutura, energia, desenvolvimento sustentável, instituições financeiras, organismos multilaterais, programas governamentais ou iniciativas de grande porte.
  • Experiência em Gestão Financeira e Orçamentária: Experiência comprovada na elaboração, monitoramento ou gestão de orçamentos, projeções financeiras, planejamento financeiro, fluxo de caixa, acompanhamento de execução financeira ou instrumentos equivalentes de gestão financeira.
  • Experiência em Elaboração de Relatórios e Análises Financeiras: Experiência comprovada na elaboração de relatórios financeiros, análises gerenciais, pareceres técnicos, estudos financeiros, indicadores de desempenho, projeções ou instrumentos de apoio à tomada de decisão. 

Qualificações Desejáveis (Critérios de Classificação) 

Os candidatos habilitados nos critérios obrigatórios serão avaliados e classificados com base nos seguintes aspectos: 

  • Formação Acadêmica Complementar: Pós-graduação Lato Sensu (Especialização), Mestrado ou Doutorado em Finanças, Administração Financeira, Controladoria, Economia, Contabilidade, Gestão de Projetos, Gestão Pública, Planejamento, Finanças Corporativas, Avaliação Econômica, Gestão de Riscos, Governança Corporativa ou áreas correlatas.
  • Experiência com Organismos Multilaterais: Experiência profissional em projetos financiados pelo Banco Mundial, Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID), CAF, KfW, AFD, GCF, GEF ou organismos multilaterais equivalentes.
  • Experiência em Gestão Financeira e Fiduciária de Projetos: Experiência na gestão financeira, monitoramento fiduciário, planejamento orçamentário, execução financeira, prestação de contas ou acompanhamento de operações financiadas por organismos multilaterais ou instituições financeiras de desenvolvimento.
  • Experiência em Relatórios Financeiros e Prestação de Contas: Experiência na elaboração, revisão ou monitoramento de demonstrações financeiras, relatórios financeiros periódicos, relatórios fiduciários, relatórios gerenciais, indicadores financeiros ou instrumentos de prestação de contas para financiadores nacionais ou internacionais.
  • Experiência em Auditoria, Controles Internos e Conformidade: Experiência na condução, acompanhamento ou suporte a auditorias financeiras, auditorias de projetos, controles internos, gestão de riscos, compliance, controles fiduciários ou processos de supervisão financeira.
  • Experiência em Instituições Financeiras: Experiência profissional em bancos de desenvolvimento, bancos públicos, bancos multilaterais, agências de fomento, fundos de investimento, cooperativas financeiras, instituições financeiras reguladas ou organizações com processos estruturados de gestão financeira e controle fiduciário.
  • Experiência em Planejamento Orçamentário e Monitoramento Financeiro: Experiência comprovada na elaboração de orçamentos institucionais, planejamento plurianual, acompanhamento de execução financeira, projeções de desembolso, controle orçamentário e monitoramento de indicadores financeiros.
  • Experiência em Projetos de Infraestrutura, Energia ou Desenvolvimento Sustentável: Experiência profissional em projetos relacionados à infraestrutura, energia renovável, transição energética, desenvolvimento regional, sustentabilidade, mudanças climáticas ou investimentos de impacto socioeconômico.
  • Experiência na Amazônia Legal: Experiência em projetos desenvolvidos na Amazônia Legal, envolvendo investimentos, desenvolvimento sustentável, infraestrutura, energia, bioeconomia, finanças sustentáveis, financiamento ao desenvolvimento ou fortalecimento institucional.
  • Produção Técnica: Experiência comprovada na elaboração de estudos financeiros, análises econômicas, diagnósticos institucionais, modelos financeiros, matrizes de riscos, painéis gerenciais, procedimentos operacionais, manuais, metodologias de monitoramento, relatórios técnicos ou documentos de apoio à tomada de decisão.
  • Experiência em Sistemas e Ferramentas de Gestão: Experiência na utilização de sistemas corporativos de gestão financeira, sistemas orçamentários, ferramentas de Business Intelligence (BI), plataformas de monitoramento, ERPs ou sistemas de gestão de projetos.
  • Habilidades e Competências Complementares
  • Proficiência em língua inglesa, especialmente para leitura, interpretação e análise de documentos técnicos e financeiros;
  • Domínio avançado de Microsoft Excel ou ferramentas equivalentes para modelagem financeira e análise quantitativa;
  • Conhecimento de ferramentas de visualização de dados e Business Intelligence (Power BI, Tableau ou equivalentes);
  • Conhecimento sobre normas internacionais de gestão financeira aplicáveis a projetos financiados por organismos multilaterais;
  • Conhecimento sobre processos de desembolso, gestão fiduciária, monitoramento financeiro e prestação de contas em operações financiadas por organismos internacionais;
  • Capacidade de elaboração de apresentações executivas, relatórios gerenciais e documentos estratégicos para alta administração.

Os consultores individuais serão selecionados através da avaliação de qualificações e experiência, de acordo com os procedimentos do Banco Mundial para Consultores Individuais contidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos.

 

Atenção especial deve ser dada pelos consultores interessados aos requisitos de:

  • Elegibilidade e Conflito de Interesses: Conforme detalhado no Termo de Referência (TDR), Seção 14.1, que incorpora o Regulamento de Aquisições, Seção III, Parágrafos 3.16, 3.17 e 3.23.
  • Compromisso com as Diretrizes Anticorrupção do Banco Mundial: Conforme detalhado no Termo de Referência (TDR), Seção 14.2, que incorpora o Regulamento de Aquisições, Anexo IV (Fraude e Corrupção).

Avis Spécifique d’Appel d’Offres (AAO)

Appel d’Offres pour Fournitures (Processus à Une Enveloppe)

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet de Productivité et de Résilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux - Riz plus, et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre des Marchés de « Fourniture, livraison et installation de 595 kits de matériels FLID de la Région Alaotra Mangoro ».

Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, à l’exception des paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation de crédit documentaire.

2. L'Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZ PLUS sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour la fourniture, la livraison et l'installation de 595 kits de matériels FLID (kits d'irrigation solaire) destinés à la Région Alaotra Mangoro, constituant un lot unique et indivisible (595 Kits « PortaSol » (pompe solaire de surface transportable, 2 panneaux de 380 W minimum)).

Les lieux de destination finale, au sens de la version des Incoterms spécifiée dans le Dossier d'Appel d'Offres, sont constitués par les sites d'implantation des kits situés dans les trois (03) districts de Ambatondrazaka, Amparafaravola et Moramanga dans la Région Alaotra Mangoro, République de Madagascar. Les Fournitures transiteront par un magasin de transit à Antananarivo puis par les chefs-lieux de districts, conformément au calendrier de livraison figurant dans le Dossier d'Appel d’Offres.

Les prestations comprennent, outre la fourniture des équipements conformes aux Spécifications techniques de la Section VII : le transport jusqu'au magasin de transit d'Antananarivo, l'ensemble des formalités et frais d'importation et de dédouanement, le magasinage, le gardiennage et l'assurance des Fournitures au magasin de transit, l'allotissement par district et la réexpédition jusqu'aux chefs-lieux des trois districts, le transport terminal jusqu'aux sites d'implantation, l'installation et la mise en service de chaque kit avec essais de bon fonctionnement, la formation individuelle de chacun des 595 exploitants bénéficiaires sur sa parcelle, une démonstration collective par district, la fourniture de la documentation technique en langue française, la remise d'un rapport final d'exécution par district, la disponibilité des pièces de rechange et d'un point de service après-vente dans chacun des trois districts d'installation, ainsi qu'une garantie de vingt-quatre (24) mois à compter de la réception provisoire prononcée par district.

Les délais contractuels sont les suivants :

  • Fourniture et livraison de l'intégralité des 595 kits au magasin de transit d'Antananarivo : cent cinq (105) jours calendaires au plus tard, comptés à partir du lendemain de la date de notification de l'ordre de service de commencer ;
  • Allotissement par district, réexpédition et livraison de l'intégralité des kits aux chefs-lieux des trois (03) districts de la Région Alaotra Mangoro : soixante (60) jours calendaires au plus tard, comptés à partir du lendemain de la date de réception quantitative des Fournitures au magasin de transit ;
  • Services connexes comprenant le transport terminal jusqu'aux sites d'implantation, l'installation, la mise en service, les essais de bon fonctionnement et la formation des exploitants de l'ensemble des kits : cent quatre-vingts (180) jours calendaires au plus tard, comptés à partir du lendemain de la date de notification de l'ordre de service d'installation. Cet ordre de service est émis par l'Acheteur après achèvement de la livraison aux chefs-lieux de district, et au plus tôt le 1er avril 2027, la période d'installation devant coïncider avec le calendrier cultural des exploitants bénéficiaires.

Les frais de magasinage, de gardiennage, d'assurance et de réexpédition entre les délais a) et b) sont à la charge exclusive du Fournisseur et réputés inclus dans le prix de l'Offre. Les lieux de destination finale, demeurent constitués par les sites d'implantation situés dans les trois districts.

Toute offre proposant un délai supérieur à l'un ou l'autre de ces délais sera considérée comme non conforme et écartée. Aucun bonus ne sera accordé pour une exécution anticipée.

Aucune marge de préférence n'est applicable.

3. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence Nationale (AON) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, septième édition, daté de septembre 2025, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Productivité et de Résilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux - Riz plus, Bureau de la Passation des Marchés, et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres durant les heures de bureau, de 08h30 à 16h30 à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

5. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir un Dossier d’Appel d’Offres complet en Français en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous. Le document d’appel d’offres sera adressé par voie électronique ou à récupérer en main propre à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

6. Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse indiquée à la fin de cet avis au plus tard le mardi 22 septembre 2026 à 15h00, heure de Madagascar. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne choisissant d’être présente à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le mardi 22 septembre 2026 à 15h00, heure de Madagascar.

7. Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une Garantie de l’Offre, pour un montant de CENT QUARANTE CINQ MILLIONS ARIARY (145000000,00 MGA), ou son équivalent en devise librement convertible à la date limite de dépôt des offres.

8. L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

Following the devastation caused by hurricanes Irma and Maria in September 2017, the Government of Sint Maarten embarked on a large-scale recovery and reconstruction program, based on the principle of building back better.

Since January 2018, the World Bank is assisting the Government of Sint Maarten. A significant part of Sint Maarten’s ongoing recovery and reconstruction program is financed through a Trust Fund financed by the Netherlands, managed by the World Bank, and implemented by Sint Maarten.

To support the implementation of the Trust Fund, the Government of Sint Maarten established the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB), which serves as the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for the Government of Sint Maarten.

Short Description of the Project

The Wastewater Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the Project”) implements a wide range of activities, in close collaboration with government counterparts and ministries, notably Ministry of Public Housing, Spatial Planning, Environment, and Infrastructure (hereinafter referred to as “VROMI”.

The project consists of the improvement of the coverage and performance of the wastewater system in Sint Maarten. This will be done through the expansion of the existing sewerage network to enable the connection for residents and commercial enterprises, the rehabilitation of critical parts of the existing sewage system to improve its climate resilience and operational efficiency and the improvement of the wastewater treatment plant.

Role of the Engineer

NRPB is seeking the services of an Engineer [hereinafter referred to as “Consultant”] to support the NRPB with technical expertise on all construction-related activities under the Wastewater Management Project and any other project that could utilize the specific expertise of the Engineer. The Engineer will assist the NRPB in the development of terms of references, technical drawings, bills of quantities, cost estimates, bidding documents etc. (S)he will monitor works on behalf of the project Manager (PM) and represent the NRPB in technical committee meetings and evaluations upon

SWAMP PM request. The Engineer shall report regularly on the progress of project implementation to the NRPB.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

The Engineer will be a full-time professional responsible for technical aspects of project execution and supervision and will support the NRPB with all matters concerning construction under the Project. Construction activities under the project include the installation of sewerage pipes, construction of manholes, connections to buildings and upgrade works in the wastewater treatment plant.

The Engineer’s responsibilities will include:

1. Work within the NRPB on the implementation of the Project following the rules and regulations of the World Bank.

2. In coordination with NRPB Procurement, as well as line ministries/external agencies, manage and supervise the preparation of all required technical project documents including Terms of Reference (ToRs) for consultants and consulting firms, specifications, and designs for works.

3. Cooperate and coordinate with operational units of line ministries/agencies to develop technical terms of references, scope of works, bills of quantities and cost estimates.

4. Assist NRPB Procurement in the preparation of technical tender documents.

5. Identify all technical elements and documentation required to implement assigned project activities.

6. Represent the NRPB as the contracting officer’s technical representative (COTR) during project execution and serve as the principal contact with consultants and contractors during project execution.

7. Represent the NRPB in technical bid evaluations during the contracting process.

8. Track activities’ progress, specifically to ensure timely conclusion of works.

9. Regularly monitor and report on project execution progress and budget performance.

10. Regularly liaise with the Project Manager, NRPB Procurement Officers, E&S Officers, Legal Officers, and M&E Specialist to ensure achievement of the program objectives, as well as ensure compliance with World Bank procedures.

11. Work directly with project counterparts and relevant stakeholders to ensure deliverables fall within the applicable scope and budget. This will involve coordinating with other departments within the Government as well as external counterparts, to ensure all aspects of each construction activity are compatible and to clarify specific requirements of each project.

12. Report periodically to the Project Manager on progress and challenges of ongoing construction activities.

13. Make suggestions that may improve his/her own job description or implementation, the overall implementation of SWaMP or the functioning of the NRPB.

14. Assist with any other project that could utilize the specific expertise of the Engineer.

15. Conduct any other ad hoc technical or contract management work as directed by the Project Managers.

Contractual Arrangements.

A time-based contract is expected to be signed. The start date of the contract will be October 2026 or soon thereafter. The contract’s duration will be 20 months, until 30 June 2028. The successful candidate is expected to be based within Philipsburg, Sint Maarten. The Consultant is expected to perform the above-mentioned tasks on an ongoing basis during the term of his/her assignment, to the satisfaction of the Project Manager.

The consultant will report monthly to the Project Manager

The performance of the Consultant will be appraised by the Project Manager based on the timely implementation and execution of tasks described under the key responsibilities for the role.

Qualification requirements

Minimum Requirements

· Master’s degree in civil engineering, water or wastewater Engineering;

- With a Master’s Degree: A minimum of 5 years of professional experience in the field of technical design, construction management and site supervision

Or: Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering, water or wastewater Engineering;

- With a Bachelor’s Degree: A minimum of 7 years of professional experience in the field of technical design, construction management and site supervision;

· Functionally computer literate, possessing operational skills in word-processing and spreadsheet software such as MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint and project management software such as MS Project;

· Proven relevant experience in preparation of technical documentation, Terms of references, technical bidding documents and specifications.

· Proven relevant experience of wastewater installations management and site supervision;

· Proven relevant experience in managing external consultants and contractors;

· Proven experience with the preparation of technical briefings and reports.

· Fluency in English;

· Ability to work with and coordinate other professionals in engineering activities;

· Demonstrated ability to work in teams within a collaborative mode; develop and maintain effective work relationships with counterparts;

· Ability to manage priorities and workflow within deadlines and work efficiently under pressure;

· Time management and organizational skills with attention to detail;

Preferred Experience

 

· Experience in multidisciplinary, donor-funded projects.

· Familiarity with World Bank procedures would be a significant advantage.

· Proficiency in Dutch in speech and writing is an advantage.

· Understanding the challenges faced by (Caribbean), Small Island Developing States (SIDS);

 

 

Strategic Competencies – brief description

 

NRPB as an organization is committed not only to WHAT we must achieve but also on HOW we are going to reach our objectives. Therefore, for this position we are looking for a profile that displays the following competencies:

Professional Acumen - Intermediate Level

· Applies problem-solving methodologies and tools to diagnose and solve operational and interpersonal problems;

· Determines the potential causes of the problem and works on certain scenarios;

· Sees opportunities and takes the initiative to act on them;

· Understands that responsible use of resources maximizes our impact on our beneficiaries;

· Open to change and flexible in a fast-paced environment;

· Effectively adapts own approach to suit changing circumstances or requirements;

· Evaluates data and courses of action to reach logical, pragmatic decisions;

· Takes an unbiased, rational approach with calculated risks;

Looking at the bigger picture – Strategic outlook – Beginner Level

· Aligns current work and activities with the NRPB’s strategic goals;

· Acts on and implements strategies and policies in accordance with the NRPB’s strategic goals;

· Comprehends operational and organizational goals and direction;

Leading myself and the others – Intermediate Level

· Regularly provides constructive feedback and recognition to team members regarding job performance;

· Collaborates and supports the development of others;

· Shares own knowledge and best practices with others for the purpose of assisting in their ongoing development;

Respect for diversity - Intermediate level

· Treats all individuals with respect;

· Responds sensitively to differences and encourages others to do the same;

· Shows flexibility in changing the styles when faced with multiple dimensions of culture to be effective across cultural contexts;

· Understands multiple cultural frameworks, values, and norms;

Successful Communication – Intermediate level

· Explains issues clearly and succinctly;

· Writes clearly and succinctly in standard communication settings and styles;

· Can clearly identify the subject and state the purpose of the communication;

· Communicates with impact as well as with empathy;

· Remains calm when dealing with conflicts; shows empathy;

Relationship Building. Consultation and Collaboration – Intermediate level

· Shares information and readily determines to whom to go for relevant information;

· Seeks assistance and feedback in the problem-solving process;

· Fosters teamwork;

· Initiate collaboration on projects or methods of operating;

· Demonstrates understanding of the impact of own role on all partners and always puts the end beneficiary first;

Courage and Integrity –Intermediate level

· Maintains general knowledge of ethics, laws, regulations, standards that may impact the organization

· Reinforces difficult decisions that align with the organizational strategies and goals

· Enforces policies consistently

· Influences others to behave in an ethical manner

· Takes immediate action regarding reports of unethical behaviors or conflict of interest

How to Apply?

 

Interested consultants can send their CV in English by e-mail ONLY to jobopportunity@nrpbsxm.org.

Applicants should ensure that their CV is received before __________2026, at 17h00 AST. Any CVs received after this deadline may not be considered.

REPÚBLICA DA GUINÉ-BISSAU

ALFREDO SIMÃO DA SILVA (IBAP)                              PROJETO DE INVESTIMENTO NA RESILIÊNCIA DAS ZONAS COSTEIRAS DA                                                               ÁFRICA OCIDENTAL (WACA - RESIP II)

                    RECRUTAMENTO DE UM(A) ENCARREGADO(a) DE PROJETO REDD+

   I. CONTEXTO

Tal como noutros países da África Ocidental, na Guiné-Bissau a degradação dos recursos e ecossistemas costeiros está a acelerar devido à crescente pressão demográfica na costa e às alterações climáticas. A deterioração costeira está a conduzir a uma perda significativa e potencialmente irreversível de ecossistemas críticos, tais como praias, sistemas de dunas e mangais, que fornecem importantes serviços ambientais, sociais e de proteção costeira (meios de subsistência e recursos naturais, alimentos, proteção contra a erosão e inundações). Por conseguinte, o Governo da Guiné-Bissau solicitou e obteve apoio técnico e financeiro do Banco Mundial para implementar o Projeto de Investimento para a Resiliência Costeira da África Ocidental - Guiné-Bissau (WACA ResIP 2 GB). Ver mais detalhes nos termos de referência.

  II. OBJETIVO

O objetivo deste anúncio é o recrutamento de um(a) encarregado(a) de projeto REDD+ que será responsável pelo seguimento e pela coordenação das atividades relacionadas com os projetos REDD+ implementados pelo Instituto da Biodiversidade e Áreas Protegidas (IBAP) e pela Fundação BioGuiné (FBG) na Guiné-Bissau.

   III. CONVITE

A Unidade de Gestão do ResIP 2 GB da WACA (UGP do ResIP 2 GB da WACA) convida os consultores individuais elegíveis a manifestar interesse em prestar os serviços acima descritos. Os consultores interessados devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e experiência relevante. 

É levado ao conhecimento dos consultores o facto de serem aplicáveis as disposições relativas às regras do Banco Mundial em matéria de conflito de interesses, tal como descritas nos parágrafos 3.14 e seguintes dos “Regulamentos de aquisição para mutuários que procuram financiamento de projetos de investimento (FPI)”, datados de fevereiro de 2025 e revistos em setembro de 2025. 

  IV. PERFIL DO(A) CANDIDATO(A)

Os candidatos interessados em ocupar este posto, devem:

  • Formação acadêmica: Bacharelado ou mestrado em áreas como conservação da natureza, engenharia ambiental ou florestal, biologia vegetal, gestão de recursos naturais, ciências ambientais ou áreas relacionadas.
  • Experiência profissional: Pelo menos 5 anos de experiência em projetos ou instituições atuando em questões ambientais, de conservação ou de mudanças climáticas.

Conhecimento técnico:

  • Experiência na implementação de projetos relacionados a questões florestais e na redução do desmatamento ou reflorestamento.
  • Familiaridade com avaliações de impacto social, ambiental e de biodiversidade.
  • O conhecimento em sensoriamento remoto, SIG e o entendimento de como funciona o mercado de carbono é uma grande vantagem.
  • Conhecimento de projetos certificados REDD+, incluindo a aplicação de normas internacionais como Verra (VCS), ART-TREES ou Gold Standard, bem como conhecimento de metodologias de carbono azul, especialmente em ecossistemas de manguezais e áreas costeiras.
  • Experiência com monitoramento GIS e sistemas de análise espacial aplicados a florestas e áreas costeiras.
  • Habilidades linguísticas: Fluência em português e bom conhecimento de inglês. O conhecimento de crioulo ou francês é uma vantagem.Habilidades interpessoais: Habilidade de trabalhar em ambientes complexos e gerenciar múltiplos stakeholders com interesses diferentes, demonstrando habilidades de comunicação eficazes tanto com públicos técnicos quanto não técnicos. Ver mais detalhes nos termos de referência.

 

  • V. MÉTODO DE SELEÇÃO

O gabinete ou consórcio será selecionado utilizando o método de Seleção de Consultores Individuais (CI) de acordo com os procedimentos estabelecidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários que procuram Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (FPI) para Fornecimentos, Obras, Serviços e outros que Serviços de Consultoria, e Serviços de Consultoria de fevereiro de 2025, revisto em setembro de 2025.

  1. Um currículo Vitae atualizado.

  3. Uma cópia(s) autenticada(s) dos diplomas e certificados obtidos.

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS. 

SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

 

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Formulación de Instrumentos Regionales y Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial y Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres. Región Cibao Norte y Región El Valle.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPYD-475021-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") incluyen: la formulación de los Planes Regionales de Ordenamiento y Desarrollo Territorial (PRODT) de las regiones Cibao Norte y El Valle; diez (10) Planes Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial (PMOT) priorizados, de nueva formulación, actualización integral o ampliación sustantiva de alcance: ocho (8) en Cibao Norte, correspondientes a la actualización, armonización y profundización del PMOT de Santiago de los Caballeros, incluyendo sus distritos municipales Hato del Yaque, La Canela, San Francisco de Jacagua y Santiago Oeste; los PMOT de Licey al Medio, Puñal, Villa González, Tamboril, Bisonó/Navarrete y Sosúa; y el instrumento asociativo de Gaspar Hernández, incluyendo Veragua (D.M.) y Jamao al Norte; y dos (2) en El Valle, correspondientes a San Juan de la Maguana y Azua de Compostela.

Los Servicios comprenden además la revisión, actualización, complementación o armonización de cuatro (4) PMOT vigentes o en proceso: Santiago de los Caballeros, San Felipe de Puerto Plata, Moca y Villa Montellano, precisando que la referencia a Santiago no constituye un producto adicional ni un doble conteo; dos (2) Instrumentos de Delimitación de Suelo Urbano (IDSU) para Las Matas de Farfán y Comendador; nueve (9) Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático, seis (6) en Cibao Norte y tres (3) en El Valle; y dos (2) Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación, una para cada región, en un período de dieciséis (16) meses calendario, conforme al alcance establecido en los Términos de Referencia. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR).

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. Se requiere una firma con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo de proyectos, planes o políticas relacionados con el ordenamiento y desarrollo territorial en las escalas nacional, regional, municipal y/o de desarrollo urbano. Se valorará especialmente que cuente con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia específica en la formulación de instrumentos supramunicipales de ordenamiento y/o desarrollo territorial o de instrumentos de delimitación y regulación de usos del suelo a escala municipal, incluyendo el desarrollo simultáneo de múltiples instrumentos de planificación territorial en distintos niveles de gobierno.

Asimismo, deberá demostrar un mínimo de tres (3) proyectos o siete (7) años de experiencia reciente en gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, incluyendo análisis multiamenaza, modelación hidrológico-hidráulica y sísmica, integración de escenarios climáticos y articulación de resultados con instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial e inversión pública y su aplicación en procesos de planificación territorial y toma de decisiones.

Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) proyectos similares en alcance, complejidad, niveles de gobierno y extensión geográfica, ejecutados satisfactoriamente y vinculados a la formulación de instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial a escala regional y/o municipal, con integración de la gestión del riesgo de desastres y la adaptación al cambio climático. En conjunto, los proyectos presentados deberán permitir verificar, según corresponda, experiencia en planificación regional, municipal o metropolitana; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; producción y gestión de información geoespacial; formulación normativa; procesos participativos; fortalecimiento institucional; portafolios de inversión; y estrategias de implementación. Las experiencias deberán estar respaldadas mediante certificaciones, contratos, actas de recepción u otra documentación equivalente emitida por los contratantes. En caso de APCA, podrán acreditarse de manera conjunta por sus integrantes, siempre que guarden relación directa con las responsabilidades que cada uno asumirá en la consultoría.

Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para la ejecución de la consultoría, incluyendo la disponibilidad de recursos computacionales, tecnológicos y de producción digital necesarios, así como herramientas de gestión de proyectos, administración de entornos, repositorios y documentación técnica. Deberá evidenciar capacidad para gestionar contratos de magnitud y complejidad similares, cumpliendo tiempos y entregables, así como capacidad organizativa y operativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría, incluyendo la movilización del equipo.

Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas por cada postulante frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Para estos fines, se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales y municipales de ordenamiento territorial, instrumentos de gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor, gestión de información territorial y cartográfica, así como la capacidad operativa para prestar los servicios en idioma español y mantener presencia activa en las regiones objeto de la consultoría.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Cibao Norte y El Valle y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Request for Bids

Goods

Country: Georgia

Name of Project: Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor – Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (Project)

Contract Title: Procurement of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and Full Long-term Technical Maintenance

Loan No.: IBRD-99810

RFB Reference No.: GE-GR-563165-GO-RFB

 

  1. Georgia has received financing from the World Bank (Bank) toward the cost of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor – Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and Full Long-term Technical Maintenance. This contract will be jointly financed by Asian Development Bank (ADB). Bidding process will be governed by the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

2.         The JSC Georgian Railway (GR) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Procurement of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and Full Long-term Technical Maintenance to be to be delivered by a single manufacturer.

Permitted Locomotive Configuration

 

The Bidder shall offer one of the following locomotive configurations only:

 

  1. 2 × Bo-Bo integrated locomotive configuration — total quantity: 45 units; or
  2. Separate paired Bo-Bo locomotive configuration — total quantity: 90 units, forming 45 operational locomotive pairs.

 

Each proposed configuration shall meet all specified performance requirements, including traction capacity, rated power, operational efficiency, compatibility with the Purchaser’s network, and all other technical requirements.

 

No alternative quantity or mixed configuration shall be accepted. The Bid shall be based exclusively on either 45 integrated units or 90 separate Bo-Bo units forming 45 pairs (hereinafter referred to as "45 locomotives").

Delivery Requirement: The locomotives shall be delivered to the depot in city Khashuri, Georgia under the CIP conditions. The 1st locomotive shall be delivered within 27 months from the contract effectiveness date. The remaining 44 locomotives shall be delivered within the deadlines defined in Section VII – Schedule of Requirement to ensure completion of all deliveries within 55 months from the contract effectiveness date.

Scope of the contract includes design, manufacturing, delivery, testing, commissioning (supplied system fully operational, accepted, and ready for commercial service) of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and at least 2-year warranty period. The contract will be financed by 50/50 from World Bank and ADB sources.

In addition, the scope includes the provision of full technical maintenance services (excluding major overhauls) for the delivered locomotives. These services shall commence upon the Operational Acceptance of the first Locomotive and shall continue throughout the Warranty Period and the subsequent ten (10)-year post-warranty maintenance period for each Locomotive. The overall duration of the Locomotives Maintenance Agreement shall expire upon completion of the ten (10)-year post-warranty maintenance period applicable to the latest delivered Locomotive or batch of Locomotives. The maintenance services shall cover spare parts, consumables, major components, and all necessary maintenance activities. For this purpose, a separate maintenance service agreement will be entered into with the successful Bidder. The terms and conditions of this agreement and are included in the bidding documents and incorporate performance-based Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), payment mechanisms structured on measurable performance criteria, and a price adjustment formula. The maintenance service agreement will be financed from the Purchaser’s own resources and may be extended subject to satisfactory performance.

Under this arrangement, the Supplier shall, as part of its maintenance obligations and at its own cost, design, construct, equip, and commission a new fully operational service center (depot) for the maintenance of at least the forty-five (45) locomotives. Subject to the Supplier’s full compliance with the performance, availability, and maintenance obligations under the Lcomotives Maintenance Agreement, the Purchaser grants the Supplier the right to use the depot facilities for third-party rolling stock and maintenance services. Under all circumstances, the Purchaser’s operational and maintenance requirements shall take precedence. The depot shall be completed and ready for operation prior to the Operational Acceptance of the first locomotive.

For the purpose of new depot, the Borrower shall provide the Supplier with a land plot located within the existing Khashuri depot. The land shall be made available free of charge for the entire duration of the maintenance service agreement under a right of superficies arrangement, granting the Supplier the legal right to design, construct, operate, and maintain the depot on the provided land for the contract period. The Supplier shall retain ownership of the depot, its infrastructure, and all installed equipment during the period in which it is responsible for maintenance services and depot operations under the maintenance contract.

Capabilities and Qualification Requirements: To implement the scope of the contract the Bidder shall meet the following requirements:

  1. Qualification

Qualification Criteria (ITB 32.1)

The Purchaser shall assess each Bid against the following Qualification Criteria. Requirements not included in the text below shall not be used in the evaluation of the Bidder’s qualifications.

 

  1. Financial Capability:
  1. The Bidder shall submit audited financial statements or, if not required by the law of the Bidder’s country, other financial statements acceptable to the Purchaser, for the last three (3) years (2023-2024-2025) prior to bid submission deadline, demonstrating the current soundness of the Bidder’s financial position. For a joint venture, this requirement shall be met by each member.
  1. Specific Experience:

(i) The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed at least two (2) contracts in the role of prime contractor within the last ten (10) years prior to bid submission deadline, each for delivery of at least ten (10) main line electric locomotives for the maximum operating speed 120 km/h that are similar in nature and complexity to the Goods and Related Services required under this RFB. The Bidder shall submit relevant completion certificates, taking-over certificates, or equivalent documents acceptable for the Purchaser, issued by previous clients and confirming the successful completion of delivery, testing and current successful operation of locomotives.

For a joint ventures, this requirement may be met by all members combined.

(ii) The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully substantially completed[1]  at least one (1) contract in the role of prime contractor within the last ten (10) years prior to bid submission deadline, each for provision of maintenance or overhaul services of at least twenty (20) main line electric locomotives that are similar in nature and complexity to the Full Technical Maintenance service required under this RFB. The Bidder shall submit performance certificates or reference letters acceptable for the Purchaser, issued by the previous clients confirming that the contract has been or is being performed satisfactorily.

For a joint ventures, this requirement may be met by all members combined.

  1. Documentary Evidence:

The Bidder shall furnish documentary evidence to demonstrate that the offered Goods meet the following requirements:

  1. Prospective bidders must be able to show from independent data that their offered electric locomotive is of mature technology, meaning that it has operated at required contractual levels of availability and reliability in revenue-earning service for at least one year.
  2. All major components, including bogies, traction motors, control equipment and braking systems must be individually shown to be of mature technology, meaning that they have been type tested and have been in successful revenue-earning service for at least one year.

 

  1. Manufacturing experience and Technical Capacity: For the items under the Contract that the bidder is a manufacturer, the Bidder shall furnish documentary evidence to demonstrate that:

 

  1. it has manufactured goods of similar nature and complexity for at least 10 years, prior to the bid submission deadline; and

 

(ii) its annual production capacity of goods of similar nature and complexity for any of the last 10 years prior to the bid submission deadline, is at least eighteen (18) locomotives.

 

The Bidder shall provide documentary evidence to demonstrate compliance with the above requirements.

 

The Purchaser reserves the right to request additional information or clarification to verify the Bidder’s production capacity.

 

  1. Cyber security experience. The Bidder will demonstrate its cyber security experience, practice and track record, including experience in navigating compliance requirements and regulatory standards related to cyber security. The Bidder shall provide documentary evidence of relevant cyber security accreditation such as IEC 62443 or EN 50159:2010 or ISO 27000 (ISO 27001) or equivalent.

 

The Bidder shall provide a cyber security risk assessment and management plan to ensure that the product meets legal and industry-specific security standards and ensures that there are no harmful algorithms in the control systems that can negatively affect operation of the locomotive.

 

  1. Manufacturer’s authorization: A Bidder who does not manufacture an item/s where a Manufacturer Authorization is required in accordance with BDS ITB 17.2 (a), the Bidder shall provide evidence of being duly authorized by a manufacturer (Manufacturer’s Authorization Form, Section IV, Bidding Forms), meeting the criteria in (d) (i) and (ii) above, to supply the Goods;

 

A bidder who does who does not manufacture an item/s where a manufacturer authorization is not required in accordance with BDS ITB 17.2 (a), the bidder shall submit documentation on, its status as a supplier, to the satisfaction of the Purchaser (e.g. authorized dealer/ distributor of the items).

 

At the time of Contract Award, the Bidder (including each sub-contractor proposed by the Bidder) shall not be subject to disqualification by the Bank for non-compliance with SEA/ SH obligations.

3.         Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4.         Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 40% and for Bid cost: 60%.

5.         Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information on RFB document by sending e-mail at the address given below.

6.         The bidding document in English may be obtained by interested Bidders after the submission of a written request to the address: TCGATE@railway.ge. The document will be sent free of charge by e-mail.

7.         Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before October 30, 2026, time 17:00 Tbilisi time. Late Bids will be rejected. Electronic Bidding will not be permitted. The outer Bid envelopes marked “Original Bid”, and the inner envelopes marked “Technical Part” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on October 30, 2026, time 17:00 Tbilisi time. All envelopes marked “Second Envelope: Financial Part” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Purchaser until the second public opening.8.   All Bids must be accompanied by a “Bid Securing Declaration”.

9.         Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.

10.       The address(es) referred to above is (are):

 

Ms. Teona Miminoshvili,

Request for Expressions of Interest for Consulting Service

Country:        The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery (PAMP) Project  

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Support a Revenue Assessment of the National Environment Agency

Grant Number: IDA-E3820

Project ID NO:  P176924

Procurement Method: Individual Consultant Selection Method (IC)   

Reference No.   GM-CPCU-MOFEA-516921-CS-INDV

  1. Background:

The Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery Project (PAMP) supports the implementation of the Government program, the Recovery Focused National Development Plan (RF-NDP) 2023-2027. In January 2024, the GoTG approved and adopted the RF-NDP 2023-2027, i.e., program implementation is currently in its infancy. The RF-NDP aims to consolidate gains in democratic governance, accelerate green economic and social transformation, and build resilience to shocks and crises. It has three major strategic objectives: (1) building household and community resilience to address shocks and crises arising from climate change and economic volatility and to counter the effects of pandemics like COVID-19; (2) consolidating gains and addressing critical development gaps in governance and economic and social transformation; and (3) strengthening accountability, building partnerships and setting up robust and sustainable resource mobilization strategies for effective delivery of development actions and expected outcomes. The RF-NDP is organized across seven pillars.

The proposed PforR focuses on a subset of RF-NDP priority actions related to enhancing domestic resource mobilization and financial reporting, human resources management, and citizen engagement in the education sector. These include the second pillar on Governance Reforms priority actions to “enhance governance and management of civil society organizations” and “professionalize and instill meritocracy, ethical conduct, transparency and accountability in the public service and personnel management” and the third pillar on Macroeconomic Stability and Inclusive Growth priority action to “enhance Public Financial Management (PFM) for macro-fiscal stability and strengthening democracy.”

  1. Sectoral Context and Objective of The Assignment:

The National Environment Agency (NEA) established under the National Environment Management Act (NEMA), 1994 consistent with the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 as a semi-autonomous agency with an independent structure to serve as the “principal body responsible for overall management of the environment” in the Gambia.

The NEA is the advisory body to the National Management Council (NEMC) on formulation, review, revision and repealing of environmental policies, plans, standards, guidelines, criteria and regulations. The NEMC is the main policy-making body for the environmental management in the Gambia. This Council is chaired by the President of the Republic of the Gambia, with the Ministers responsible for the following Ministries as members: Natural Resources; Agriculture; Health and Social Welfare; Finance and Economic Affairs; Trade Industry and Employment; Local Government and Lands. The Executive Director of the NEA serves as Secretary to the Council. In addition to the composition of this council, the President may co-opt any person into the Council as member.

The functions of the NEA include; (a) implementing the policies of the Council on the environment; (b) liaising with the various ministries, departments, and agencies of Government on all issues relating to the environment and ensure that environmental concerns are integrated into all spheres of national planning and project implementation; (c) liaising with the private sector, inter-governmental organizations, non- governmental organizations, governmental agencies of other states on all issues relating to the environment; (d) preparing proposals for environmental policies and strategies for the Council; (e) initiating legislative proposals, standards, guidelines, and regulations in accordance with the provisions of NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 ; (f) reviewing and approving environmental impact assessments submitted in accordance with the  NEMA Amendment Bill 2025  or any other law; (g) undertaking studies and submit reports and recommendations to the Council on such matters as are likely to have an impact on the environment; (h) promoting public awareness of environmental issues through gathering, analyzing and disseminating information about the environment and publishing periodic reports on the state of the environment; attend to any complaint relating to the environment addressed to it; (j) carrying out environmental audits and monitoring; and (k) carrying out such other functions as the NEMC may assign to it or as may be incidental or conducive to the exercise by NEA of any powers provided for under the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025.

Administratively, NEA reports only to the NEMC, and is led by the Executive Director, who is assisted by a Deputy Executive Secretary and three directorates, namely, Technical Services (TSN), Inter-sectoral Services (ISN), and Administration and Finance (AFN).  Under these directorates, various programs and services are planned and carried out. 

The NEA as per the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 is overseen by the Board of Directors of the Agency which shall be the governing body of the Agency with two statutory committees namely, the Technical Advisory Committee and the Administration and Finance Committee providing day-to-day oversight and technical support to NEA management.

The overall strategic objective of the Revenue Assessment of NEA is to provide GoTG with a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative analytical assessment of the revenue framework and challenges (be they governance, administrative, regulatory, sources, thresholds and collection) of the NEA, to inform the preparation of detailed recommendations for how the NEA’s financial sustainability for the fulfillment of its mandate can be enhanced, for the consideration of the government in its quest to empower NEA with the tools it needs to be more effective

  1. Scope of Work:

 

  1. Scope of Services:
  • Review assessment of the governance (regulatory, institutional, technical, and financial) framework underpinning NEA’s revenue issues, concerns, and challenges across both the national and local government levels.
  • Preparation of a detailed and comprehensive report, including recommendations and implementation plan for the GoTG through the NEMC.
  1. Qualification and Competency
  • A relevant Master's degree (or higher) from a recognized university in Public Financial Management; Economics with a specialization in public or environmental finance; Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration; or Environmental Economics/Management with a strong finance component. A recognized professional accountancy qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CIPFA or equivalent) may substitute for the academic degree requirement.
  • Minimum 15 years of relevant professional experience in public finance, fiscal economics, or revenue management, of which at least 10 years must be post-qualification.
  • Proven track record in conducting revenue assessments, diagnostic studies, or fiscal sustainability analyses for public agencies, semi-autonomous bodies, or state-owned enterprises.
  • Experience applying financial modelling and revenue projection techniques to identify collection gaps and forecast income streams. Full econometric modelling capability is desirable but not required.
  • Ability to analyze budget execution reports, subvention systems, and mechanisms for withholding or reallocation of funds by central finance ministries.
  • Prior experience working in The Gambia is an advantage. Candidates with experience in comparable West African or small-state developing country contexts will also be considered.
  • Knowledge of The Gambia's environmental regulatory framework, including the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 and its provisions on revenue sources, earmarking, and NEA's semi-autonomous status. Candidates are expected to review the Bill prior to submission.
  • Familiarity with environmental fiscal instruments such as pollution levies, royalty regimes, and environmental impact assessment fees.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and executing stakeholder mapping and consultation processes involving government ministries, revenue authorities, private sector operators, and civil society.

Full TOR Availability Notice

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) will be made available upon request. Please send your request via email to the addresses provided below. The assignment is expected to be completed within 3 months from the date of signing the contract.

Submission of Expressions of Interest:

The National Environment Agency (NEA), through the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs (MoFEA) and the Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery (PAMP) Project, now invites eligible individual consultants to express interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information and Terms of Reference can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 09:00 to 16:00 Monday to Thursday and 09:00 to 12h30 on Friday.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

 

 

Country: Federated States of Micronesia

FSM Skills and Employability Enhancement Project

Grant No.: D-9870

Assignment Title: Tracer Study & Employer Survey Design and Pilot for FSM High Schools

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): FM-NDOE-526575-CS-INDV

 

The National Department of Education (NDOE) received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the FSM Skills and Employability Enhancement Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing technical assistance to design and pilot a high school graduate tracer study and employer survey framework and tools for the SEE Project under the National Department of Education (NDOE).   

 

The National Department of Education now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

 

Under the direct supervision of the SEE Project Manager, the Consultant will be responsible for the following areas of work:

 

  • Conduct a situational assessment of current graduate tracking, employer engagement, career guidance practices, and available labor market data.
  • Design a high school graduate tracer study framework, including survey methodology, indicators, sampling approach, and data management tools suitable for the FSM context.
  • Develop an employer survey framework, survey instruments, and sampling methodology aligned with the tracer study indicators.
  • Build the capacity of NDOE, State Departments of Education, and school focal points through training and technical support on survey implementation, data analysis, and reporting.
  • Support the pilot implementation of the tracer study in all four states, and employer survey in (a) selected state(s), analyze the findings, and recommend improvements for long-term sustainability.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is annexed to this REOI and can be found at the FSM Department of Finance and Administration (DOFA) website’s Career Opportunities page and NDOE’s website, respectively at https://dofa.gov.fm/opportunity/ and https://www.national.doe.fm.

 

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services by submitting:

  • Cover letter
  • Latest curriculum vitae/Resume with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.)

 

 Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.  The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

 

Mandatory Requirements

  • Master’s degree in business administration, labor economics, human resources development/management, social science, or related fields. A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, combined with at least 10 years of exceptional work experience related to the assignment, may be considered in lieu of a Master’s degree.
  • Minimum 7 years of experience in different types of labor market research (e.g., tracer study, employer surveys)
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in facilitation and capacity-building training workshops on data collection, analysis and interpretation

Desirable Requirements

  • Trained on data science
  • Demonstrated experience working in Pacific Island Countries or other Small Island Developing Sates (SIDS).

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: P505094

Name of Implementing Agency: Smart Zambia Institute (SZI)

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Review and Development of National Data Protection Guidelines and Compliance Frameworks.

Reference No.: ZM-SZ-554942-CS-CQS

Background

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) has received financing from the World Bank to accelerate countrywide digital transformation through the Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (DZAP) and intends to use part of the proceeds of the credit to accelerate country-wide digital transformation under the Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (DZAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for the Review and Development of National Data Protection Guidelines and Compliance Frameworks.

Objectives of the assignment

This assignment will strengthen Zambia's data protection regulatory framework by supporting the Data Protection Commission in reviewing, developing, and enhancing regulatory instruments that facilitate the effective implementation of the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021. The assignment seeks to improve regulatory certainty, promote consistent compliance, strengthen regulatory oversight and enforcement, and provide practical, legally robust, and implementation-ready guidance for the lawful processing of personal data across both the public and private sectors.

The Scope of services

The Consultant shall undertake the following activities to review, strengthen, and develop data protection regulatory instruments that support the effective implementation of the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021. In undertaking the assignment, the Consultant shall ensure that all regulatory instruments are legally sound, mutually coherent and consistent, practical to implement, aligned with recognized international best practices, and responsive to Zambia's legal, institutional, and operational context.

Invitation to eligible Consulting Firms

The SZI invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to submit Expressions of Interest (EOIs) for the provision of the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the requisite qualifications, technical capacity, and relevant experience to undertake and successfully deliver the required Services.

Firms Qualifications

The Consulting Firm shall demonstrate the institutional capacity to successfully undertake and deliver a regulatory development assignment of this nature, covering both legal and technical aspects across multiple sectors.

The Consulting Firm shall meet the following minimum requirements:

Core business of the firm(s) and years in business.

  • Be a legally registered entity with a core business in legal consultancy, regulatory advisory services, ICT governance, data protection, or a combination thereof.
  • Relevant experience which should specifically include the following:
  • Demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) assignments of a similar nature within the last seven (7) years, involving the development, review, or implementation of data protection legislation, regulatory guidelines, privacy frameworks, or related regulatory instruments.

 

  • Demonstrate the technical and managerial capacity to deliver the full scope of the assignment within the three (3) month implementation period, including the ability to mobilize and manage an appropriately qualified multidisciplinary team.

 

  • Demonstrate familiarity with the Zambian legal and regulatory environment, including the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021.

 

Technical and Managerial capability of the firm(s) (Provide only the structure of the organization and CVs of the Directors or Principals of the firm. Do not provide CVs of the Experts). Key Experts will not be evaluated at the short-listing stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, 3.17 and 3.20 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers – 7th Edition” dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The consulting firm will be selected using the Consultants' Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method through an Open International market approach, in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing, Seventh Edition, September 2025.

Country:                      Islamic Republic of Pakistan
