1.      The Borrower “Islamic Republic of Pakistan” has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Karachi Mobility Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of Package 5: LOT I: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 5, 6 &7  (From CH. 0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala pull) and LOT II: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 4 & 5  (From CH. 3+875 at Kala pull to CH. 7+571.000 at KPT interchange).

         For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

2.     The Sindh Mass Transit Authority (SMTA), Transport & Mass Transit Department, Government of Sindh, now invites sealed Bids from the eligible Bidders for Procurement of Package 5: LOT I: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 5, 6 & 7  (From CH.0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull) and LOT II: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 4 & 5  (From CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull to CH. 7+571 at KPT Interchange).

3.     The Yellow Line BRT Corridor is approximately 21 km long, starting from Dawood Chowrangi to Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection, and is part of the overall planned Karachi Mass Transit System (KMTS). Currently, Yellow Line BRT Corridor divided into five (05) packages i.e., (i) Package-1: Construction of Depots (Lot-I: Depot-I & Lot-II: Depot-II), which are (under implementation), (ii) Package-3B: Construction of Main BRT Corridor from Dawood Chowrangi to Indus Chowrangi approx. 6 km (Bid evaluation under process), (iii): Pacakge-3A: Construction of Main BRT Corridor from Brookes Chowrangi to Bilal Chowrangi approx. 6 km (Bid evaluation under process),  (iv) Pacakge-4: Construction of New Jam Sadiq Bridge (Currently Known as Taj Haider Bridge) (under implementation), and (v) Package-5: Lot I: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Line Corridor Segments 5, 6 & 7 (From CH. 0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull), and Lot II: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Line Corridor Segments 4 & 5 (From CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull to CH. 7+571 at KPT Interchange) (being tendered).

4.     This Package 5, Lot-I: covers 3.875 km from Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to Kala Pull. The scope includes construction of one underpass, one underground BRT station, three at-grade BRT stations, one pedestrian crossing bridge (V3), one vertical circulation (V5), Kala Pull Bridge, and one pump station at Tariq Road Underpass, BRT and mixed-traffic lanes, service roads, traffic signals, three electrical substations, street lighting, temporary traffic diversions, utility relocations and protection. The construction period shall be 660 days. Bidders must demonstrate financial capacity to meet the required construction cash flow of USD 6.30 million, supported by liquid and unencumbered assets, lines of credits, and other financial means, as well as sufficient funding for ongoing and future commitments. Audited financial statements for the last five years must show sound financial position and prospective profitability. Bidder must have a minimum average annual construction turnover of USD 37.60 million over the last five years, with at least seven (07) years of general construction experience. They must have satisfactorily completed either at least two (02) similar scopes contracts of more than USD 23 million each, or at least one (01) contract of more than USD 37 million, with demonstrated experience and production rates for key activities. Key activities including steel structures (>50 tons/year), urban road works (>58,000 m²/year), underpasses (>28,000 m³ concrete/year), and rigid pavements (>3,600 m²/year). All the key activities can be obtained from one contract or separate contracts, but one activity cannot be obtained from more than one contract. Additionally, bidders must demonstrate capacity and commitment to manage environmental and social (ES) risks, including SEA/SH prevention and responses.

5.     This Package 5, Lot-II: covers 3.396 km from Kala Pull to KPT Interchange. The scope includes construction of one underpass (Sunset Boulevard), six at-grade BRT stations, two pedestrian bridges, two elevated U-turn bridges, one flyover (Sunset Boulevard), one pump station, BRT and mixed-traffic lanes, service roads, traffic signals, electrical substations, street lighting, temporary traffic diversions, utility relocations and protection. The construction period shall be 780 days. Bidders must demonstrate financial capacity to meet the required construction cash flow of USD 11 million, supported by liquid and unencumbered assets, lines of credits, and other financial means, as well as sufficient funding for ongoing and future commitments. Audited financial statements for the last five years must show sound financial position and prospective profitability. Bidder must have a minimum average annual construction turnover of USD 65 million over the last five years, with at least seven (07) years of general construction experience. They must have satisfactorily completed either at least two (02) similar scopes contracts of more than USD 47 million each, or at least one (01) contract of more than USD 76 million, with demonstrated experience and production rates for key activities. Key activities including steel structures (>60 tons/year), urban road works (>68,000 m²/year), underpasses (>55,000 m³ concrete/year), and rigid pavements (>4,500 m²/year). All the key activities can be obtained from one contract or separate contracts, but one activity cannot be obtained from more than one contract.  Additionally, bidders must demonstrate capacity and commitment to manage environmental and social (ES) risks, including SEA/SH prevention and responses.

6.     The procurement of Package 5: Lot-I: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 5, 6 & 7  (From CH.0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull), Lot-II: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 4 & 5  (From CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull to CH. 7+571 at KPT Interchange), is being carried out in parallel with the procurement of Package 3A: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Line Corridor Segment 2 [From CH. 0+000 at Brookes Chowrangi To CH. 6+000 at Bilal Chowrangi], which is already in tendering. Bidders who have already submitted bids for Package 3A may bid for Package 5. However, the award of contract(s) will be subject to the most advantageous Bidder’s /Bidders’ meeting the required qualification and experience criteria on an aggregate basis for the respective packages and/or lots, as the case may be.

        The criteria for qualification are the aggregate minimum requirement for respective lots as specified under items 3.1, 3.2, 4.2(a), 4.2(b), equipment and personnel. Minimum requirements for combined contract(s) under 4.2(a) shall be the aggregate requirements of value of each contract under each package and across the two packages 3A and 5 for which the Bidder has submitted Bids as specified in 4.2(a) Specific Construction and Contract Management Experience.

7.     Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised November 2017 and August 2018 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders.

  1. The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Climate Resilience Multiphase Programmatic Approach (CResMPA) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract[1]for Procurement of Metocean Mooring Buoy. “For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing, except for those payments, which the contract provides to be made through letter of credit.”

 

2.         The Chairperson, Project Procurement Committee now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Supply, Deployment, Commissioning, Maintenance, and Operational Support of Metocean Mooring Buoy for the Department of Meteorology, Sri Lanka, shall complete at a proposed location considering various environmental, safety, and operational aspects within 03 months from the date contract singed. Margin of preference shall not apply.

3.         Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th edition September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

 

 

  1. Bidder must meet the following minimum qualification criteria
  1. General Experience: The Bidder shall have been actively engaged, in its own name, in the business of supplying, installing, and maintaining oceanographic, marine meteorological, or marine environmental monitoring equipment for at least fifteen (15) years preceding the bid submission date.

 

  1. Specific Experience: The Bidder shall have completed at least two (2) contracts in the last fifteen (15) years, each involving the supply, installation, and commissioning of metocean mooring buoys or similar marine monitoring platforms (e.g. wave-rider buoys) in WMO-member countries, and each with a minimum contract value of not less than USD 1 million /LKR 340 million (or equivalent).

 

  1. Manufacturer’s Experience: The Manufacturer of the buoy system must have at least fifteen (15) years of continuous experience in the design and manufacture of metocean mooring buoys for marine meteorological and oceanographic observational purposes.

The State of Santa Catarina is in the process of contracting a loan operation with the World Bank to finance the SC Protected and Resilient Program, with part of the resources allocated for the procurement of specialized consulting services.

Within the scope of this procurement, the services comprise the hiring of a specialized consulting firm to prepare a detailed technical assessment, strategic planning, technical specifications, and a governance model aimed at structuring an integrated system for hydrometeorological observation, forecasting, and dissemination of information for the member States of the Council for the Development and Integration of the South – CODESUL (Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná, and Mato Grosso do Sul). The initiative aims to strengthen regional capacity for monitoring, forecasting, and issuing alerts related to extreme hydrometeorological events.

The estimated period for the execution of the services is 10 (ten) months, counted from the contract signing date, with the procurement process expected to begin in December 2026, in accordance with the provisions established in the respective Terms of Reference (ToR).

The details of the services and procurement requirements are described in the Terms of Reference (ToR) attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest. The State Secretariat for Civil Protection and Defense of Santa Catarina invites qualified consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services under this procurement. Interested firms shall submit information demonstrating that they possess the technical qualifications, institutional experience, and operational capacity required for the proper execution of the Services, including the following requirements:

Experience in Similar Projects

Mandatory requirement: the firm shall have executed, within the last 10 (ten) years, at least 1 (one) project involving the following element:

  • Integration or development of hydrometeorological monitoring systems at the regional, national, or international level.

Desirable requirements: the firm shall have executed, within the last 10 (ten) years, projects involving the following elements:

  • Strategic planning or technical advisory services for national or state meteorological and/or hydrological services (National Meteorological Services, meteorological institutes, water agencies);
  • Technical specification and/or supervision of the implementation of early warning systems for natural disasters (floods, landslides, droughts, storms);
  • Consulting services for the modernization of information technology infrastructure applied to large volumes of environmental or scientific data;
  • Design of multi-institutional or multi-level governance models for shared information systems;
  • Diagnosis, assessment, or recommendations for meteorological, hydrological, or environmental observation networks
  • International experience demonstrating the capacity to operate in different institutional contexts and alignment with global best practices. Experience in projects financed by multilateral development banks, projects for international organizations, and/or initiatives conducted in multiple countries or within the framework of international technical cooperation will be considered.

Institutional Capacity

Mandatory requirement: The firm shall demonstrate institutional capacity through AT LEAST ONE of the following options:

Option A — Proven Consulting Experience and Mobilization Capacity: Certificate of at least 1 (one) relevant strategic or technical consulting project executed within the last 10 (ten) years (which may be the same project submitted under the Similar Projects Experience Requirement, if applicable).

Option B — Strategic Institutional Partnership: letter of support or formal partnership agreement with an institution of recognized national or international expertise in the fields of meteorology, hydrology, disaster risk management, or related areas, such as:

  • INPE (National Institute for Space Research);
  • INMET (National Institute of Meteorology);
  • Regional Centers of the WMO (World Meteorological Organization);
  • Leading universities with recognized programs in relevant fields;
  • National Meteorological and Hydrological Services or Institutes from other countries;
  • Research centers specialized in climate, water resources, or disaster management

Desirable requirements:

  • Meet Options A and B;
    • ISO 9001 (Quality Management System);
  • Quality Certifications – relevant and valid quality certifications, such as:
    • CMMI Level 3 or higher (Capability Maturity Model Integration);
    • Other recognized and equivalent international certifications.

The short list shall comprise a minimum of 5 (five) and a maximum of 8 (eight) selected consulting firms.

Interested Firms are hereby drawn attention to the provisions set forth in Section III, paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17, of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September 2025 edition, which address the policies applicable to conflicts of interest and unfair competitive advantage in procurement processes financed by the institution.

Firms may associate with other firms in order to complement their qualifications and technical capabilities and shall clearly indicate, in their Expression of Interest, whether such association will take the form of a joint venture and/or subcontracting arrangement. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the full performance of the contract, should the proposal be selected.

The Firm shall be selected in accordance with the applicable procurement procedures established in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September 2025 edition, and pursuant to the provisions set forth in the Request for Proposals (RFP).

Tajikistan Women’s Economic Empowerment Project (TWEEP)

Grant No.: TF-D1600 (TWEEP, P511398)

Assignment Title: Conducting a Baseline Survey for the TWEEP Project

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TWEEP-CS-CQS-01

The Government of the Republic of Tajikistan has received financing in the amount of US$4.73 million from the World Bank toward the cost of the Tajikistan Women’s Economic Empowerment Project (TWEEP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) include the engagement of a consulting firm to conduct the Baseline Survey for the TWEEP Project. The objective of the assignment is to collect and analyze baseline data to assess the subsequent progress and results of the Project in accordance with its Results Framework indicators. The selected consulting firm will develop and agree on the survey methodology and sampling plan, prepare and program the survey instruments in the CAPI system, conduct pre-testing and field piloting of the questionnaires, organize training of field staff, data collection and quality control, data cleaning and analysis, and prepare a final analytical report on the results of the Baseline Survey.

The assignment will include conducting 1,080 interviews in six target districts of the Project, including 1,000 interviews with women and 80 interviews with existing MSMEs led or managed by women. In addition, the consulting firm will organize and conduct 12 Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), two in each Project district, with approximately 8–10 participants in each group.

The firm will also be responsible for developing a detailed fieldwork plan, translating the survey instruments into the relevant languages, programming the questionnaires in the CAPI system, regularly monitoring fieldwork, conducting back-checks, spot-checks and other data quality assurance activities, preparing cleaned databases in Excel, SPSS and Stata formats, conducting quantitative and qualitative data analysis, and preparing the final report in English and Russian.

The expected duration of the consulting services is 6 (six) months from the date of contract signing.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this assignment can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gv7XTFcscnOfgOsxwWLJqxjwRv0_QRloLLE8XLiOUAY/edit?usp=sharing

The State Committee on Investments and State Property Management of the Republic of Tajikistan (SCISPM), through its Project Implementation Group (PIG), now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

(i) At least 5 years of experience in conducting comparable large-scale household surveys in Tajikistan, including at least five surveys involving no fewer than 1,000 respondents each using a Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI) system;

(ii) Availability of qualified key personnel, including field interviewers, to conduct the baseline evaluation study;

(iii) Direct experience in collecting research data in Tajikistan among entrepreneurs; knowledge or experience in interviewing women in rural areas will be considered an advantage; and

(iv) Experience in carrying out similar assignments under projects financed by international financial organizations, including the World Bank or other donors.

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

JOINT PROCUREMENT GRENADA & DOMINICA

Assignment: Outcome-Based Development of an Enhanced Lower-Secondary Curriculum and Assessment in Dominica and Grenada

Reference No.: GD-MOE-GRENADA-552260-CS-QBS
Project: WISTLE (P508559)

Grant No.: TF-C8594, TFC8596

 

Selection Method:  Selection shall follow the World Bank Procurement Regulations using the Quality-Based Selection (QBS) method.

1. Background

The Governments of the Commonwealth of Dominica and Grenada have received financing from the Global Partnership for Education through the World Bank for the Windward Islands Sector Transformation for Learning Enhancement (WISTLE) Project. The Ministries of Education intend to jointly procure a consulting firm to develop, pilot and support implementation of enhanced lower-secondary curricula and aligned assessment systems. The assignment will produce common regional solutions while contextualizing outputs for each country.

2. Objective

The consultancy will design and support implementation of an enhanced lower-secondary curriculum, strengthen national assessment systems, build institutional capacity, integrate digital delivery through an LMS, incorporate inclusive education and TVET pathways, and establish sustainable systems that remain after project completion.

3. Scope of Services

The selected consulting firm will: (i) review existing curricula and policies; (ii) develop curriculum frameworks and learning outcomes; (iii) prepare curricula, teacher guides and learning resources for Forms 1–3 in Dominica and Forms 1–2 in Grenada; (iv) develop a national assessment strategy, item bank and digital assessment library; (v) pilot and refine the curriculum; (vi) train curriculum developers, teachers and education officers; (vii) integrate resources into an existing regional LMS; and (viii) prepare sustainability and rollout plans.

4. Experience, Qualifications

The consulting firm shall demonstrate:

  • At least twelve (12) years' experience managing curriculum-reform projects, and at least twelve (12) years' experience in formative and summative assessment development, of comparable magnitude.
  • At least two (2) completed curriculum assignments and one (1) completed assessment assignment at basic/secondary level in the past five (5) years, the latter involving quality-assured items used in a large-scale assessment.
  • Graduate qualified team members in education, curriculum, or assessment, with proven research, statistical, and qualitative analysis skills.
  • Understanding of the Caribbean education context, with at least two (2) team members having demonstrated regional experience in the Caribbean or a small-island state; a local representative or partner in the Eastern Caribbean is required if the firm is not Caribbean-based.

5. Submission Requirements

Expressions of Interest shall include:

  1. Letter of interest;
  2. Company profile;
  3. Description of similar assignments;
  4. Evidence of technical and managerial capacity;
  5. Availability of key experts (Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage, CVs are not required at the EOI stage)
  6. Details of working in the region, specifically within Grenada and Dominica
  7. Contact information for client references.
  8. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

EOI’s should be a max of 10-15 pages.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered through electronic submission through the procurement system at https://in-tendhost.co.uk/gnd/aspx/Home. Candidates must register on this portal and submit all interest through this medium.

Upon receipt of the documents, a confirmation e-mail acknowledging the names of the files received will be sent.

Date for Submission: August 21st 2026, before 11:59pm Eastern Caribbean Time.

Further information can be obtained through In-Tend or via spo@procurement.gov.gd; or gilbertl@dominica.gov.dm  to seek clarification.

6. Shortlisting and Selection

Shortlisting will be based on the firm's general and specific experience, technical capability, regional experience, organizational capacity and successful completion of comparable assignments. The shortlist will comprise firms demonstrating the highest qualifications. The Request for Proposals will be issued to shortlisted firms.

7. Fraud and Corruption

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment i.e., 3.17 (c) & (d) of the Procurement Regulation.

Assignment Title: Consultancy for the Development of a Government of Saint Lucia (GOSL) Secure Wallet with Digital Payment and Integration Solutions

Reference No: LC-DPS-513171-CS-QCBS

Country: Saint Lucia

1. Background The Government of Saint Lucia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a Credit toward the cost of the Caribbean Digital Transformation Project. The Ministry of the Public Service, Transport, Information and Utilities Regulation, as the implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of the Credit to eligible payments under the contract for the Consultancy for the Development of a Government of Saint Lucia Secure Wallet with Digital Payment and Integration Solutions.

2. Objective of the Assignment The objective of the assignment is to design, develop and implement a secure Government of Saint Lucia Government Secure Wallet with an integrated Digital Payment System, secure document-management capabilities and integration with relevant Government services and platforms.

3. Scope of the assignment To deliver this objective, the Consultant will be required to undertake a comprehensive set of technical, operational, and regulatory activities, including the following:

Conduct detailed requirements gathering and analysis to inform system design and functional specifications.

Develop the overall system architecture and technical design for the Government Wallet and digital payment solution.

Build secure, scalable mobile and web applications supporting wallet functions and digital payments.

Integrate the solution with existing government platforms, including digiGov and the National Authentication Framework.

Implement secure digital payment capabilities and related documentmanagement features.

Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, and dataprotection controls aligned with international standards.

Establish business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements for the solution.

Deliver user training, operational guidance, and structured knowledgetransfer activities.

Provide warranty support to ensure stability and performance during the initial operational period.

Prepare all necessary documentation and support the Government of Saint Lucia in securing regulatory approval for the Government Wallet, including assessment of the FinTech legal and regulatory framework to ensure compliance with existing laws and policies

Deploy the solution within the hosting infrastructure provided by the Client, including servers, storage, networking, virtualization platform, and operating systems, and configure all required components to ensure full operational readiness

4. Duration of the assignment The estimated duration of the Services is 50 weeks.

5. Shortlisting Criteria Interested Consulting Firms will be shortlisted based on the following criteria:

i. At least five (5) years of proven experience in the design, development and implementation of digital payment platforms, Government Secure Wallets or comparable FinTech solutions.

ii. Demonstrated experience integrating ICT or payment systems with government platforms, databases or service portals, including the use of application programming interfaces (APIs) and authentication services.

iii. Proven experience in developing and deploying secure, scalable web and mobile applications with strong user-experience and interoperability features.

iv. Demonstrated capacity to implement secure solutions aligned with internationally recognized standards, including PCI DSS, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 20022 or equivalent standards.

v. Successful completion of at least three (3) assignments of similar scope and complexity, such as national-level payment systems, e-government platforms or enterprise-level systems-integration assignments.

vi. Demonstrated experience delivering assignments for public-sector clients in the Caribbean, the Organization of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) or comparable jurisdictions.

vii. Prior experience managing assignments financed by international development partners, such as the World Bank, Caribbean Development Bank or United Nations Development Programme, will be considered an advantage.

Interested Consulting Firms must provide sufficient information to demonstrate that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The information submitted should include:

a) a profile of the firm and a description of its core business;

b) details of relevant experience in digital payment platforms, Government Secure Wallets, FinTech solutions, secure mobile and web applications, government-system integration and cybersecurity;

c) descriptions of comparable assignments, including the name of the client, country, scope of services, contract period, completion status and contact information for verification; and

d) details of any proposed joint-venture member or sub consultant and the nature of the proposed association.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Therefore, individual experts’ CVs are not required with the Expression of Interest.

A firm may submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) individually if it considers itself fully qualified to undertake the assignment. Consultants may also form a joint venture or sub consultancy with other firms should they wish to enhance their qualifications and capacity.

The Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by Midnight, EST, Monday September 7, 2026

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                       Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:        SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT REGIONAL WORKSHOP ON SYSTEMS OF NATIONAL ACCOUNTS (SNA 2025) AS A RESOURCE PERSON TOWARDS DEVELOPMENT OF A REPORT FOR THE REGION FOR MIGRATING TO SNA 2025. BW-SADC-563175-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/459

 

DATE OF ISSUE:              25th August 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services for Conduct a Regional Workshop on Systems of National Accounts (SNA 2025) as a Resource Person Towards Development of a Report for the Region for Migrating to SNA 2025, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title             :  Individual Consultant to conduct Regional Workshop on Systems of National Accounts (SNA 2025) (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  90 calendar days

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to harmonize national accounts statistics compilation and dissemination practices in the region to ensure Member States produce and disseminate such statistics responsive to data demands performing to regional integration.

 

  1. Specific objectives

The specific objective of the assignment is to service a regional workshop on SNA 2025 as a resource person in support towards development of harmonized national accounts statistics.

  1. Expected results

 

The consultancy is expected to achieve the following results:

  • Enhanced technical capacity of National Statistics Offices (NSOs) in SNA 2025 concepts, definitions and standards;
  • Action Plan for each Member State in a report evaluating the readiness of migrating to SNA 2025 in line with specific actions and timelines for future implementation;

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant with the specific profile as provided below:

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of a master’s degree in statistics, economics or related field.

General Professional Experience

    • Demonstrated experience of 20 years of experience in national accounts statistics subject matter at national and/or international level.

Specific Professional Experience

    • Demonstrable experience in undertaking technical assistance as consultant in at least 10 assignments pertaining mainly to SNA 2008 implementation;
    • Demonstrated experience in undertaking technical assistance in rebasing of GDP in at least 3 assignments; and
    • Demonstrated experience as a resource person in at least 3 assignments in delivering regional training courses on national accounts to developing countries in Africa.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 90 calendar days.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to venue of the workshop.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Tuesday, 8th September 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            CONSULTING SERVICES TO DEVELOP FEASIBILITY STUDIES FOR MONGOLIAN CIVIL AVIATION SECTOR AND MURUN (4C AERODROME CODE) AIRPORT IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

REFERENCE NO.

(AS PER PROCUREMENT PLAN):              ZTYA/20260804058

The Government of Mongolia has received a grant financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), through the Global Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) toward the cost of the Gobi Connectivity Improvement Project under Grant No. TF0D0692 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  

The consulting services (“the Services”) include two distinct but complementary components.

Component A will establish the analytical and strategic foundations for aviation sector development in Mongolia. It will include a comprehensive aviation sector diagnostic, a proportionate first-pass review of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) safety and security compliance issues relevant to airport network planning and investment readiness, preparation of the Mongolia Airport Network Development Strategy to 2040, a companion Policy Recommendations Note, and a structured stakeholder consultation process. Together, these outputs will provide Government with a practical framework for airport classification, demand development, institutional strengthening, climate resilience, high-level investment prioritization, and identification of follow-on policy and technical assistance needs.

Component B will prepare a full feasibility study for Murun Airport. The Government has identified Murun Airport as a priority project requiring detailed assessment and project preparation. The feasibility study shall evaluate the technical, operational, environmental, social, financial, economic, fiscal, and institutional viability of the proposed investment and define an appropriate development concept for implementation.

The assignment is expected to run for approximately 6 to 7 months from the date of contract effectiveness. Component A and Component B shall proceed in parallel throughout the assignment period.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following website:

Tender.gov.mn

The Ministry of Road and Transport now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. General experience:

General experience implementing consultancy services in the field of civil aviation and transport sector strategy, planning and the feasibility studies; and preliminary/detailed engineering design of projects in cold climate regions, including economic/financial analysis and safeguard integration, during the last 10 years;

 

 

In addition, demonstrated experience in at least one assignment involving the preparation of environmental and social safeguard instruments for World Bank-financed projects or projects financed by comparable multilateral development banks, including at a minimum one of the following: Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (P-ESMP), and inputs into subsequent safeguard instruments such as a Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). Evidence should be provided in the firm`s EoI.

  1. Specific Experiences: 
  1. Proven experience in preparing civil aviation sector development strategies and/or airport feasibility studies (including associated policy, institutional, or PPP/commercial advisory) during the last 10 years. At least 2 such similar contracts should be demonstrated, each with a contract value of not less than US$300,000 (Please be sure to include the contract value in your submission).
  2. The consulting team must include Environmental and Social Specialists with demonstrated experience applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international safeguard/environmental and social risk management standards. At minimum, the team must demonstrate capacity to address environmental screening, social impact assessment, resettlement risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management.
  1. Technical and managerial organization of the firm

General description of the firm's technical and managerial organization, including the structure of the organization, general qualifications of staff, and number of permanent professional staff. Do not provide CVs of key staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The Shortlist will contain up to 6 firms. Shortlisted firms will be issued the full Request for Proposals, which will specify detailed technical and financial evaluation criteria and weightings, including key expert evaluation.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, seventh edition dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: from 09.00 to 17.00 hours (GMT+8).

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL)

First Date of Publication: 27th August 2026

Geotechnical Engineer - Ref No. KVWaSIP-IC-03-083/84

1.0 Background

The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services include providing technical, procurement, financial management, environmental and social, contract management, and other professional support required for effective implementation of the Project through the Project Management Unit (PMU)

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating that they possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, and technical competence to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for each assignment are specified in the respective Terms of Reference (TOR), which may be obtained from the address or website indicated below

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Geotechnical Engineer and requests applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position.

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

As a team member of the Project Management Unit (PMU), the overall objective of this assignment is to provide specialist geotechnical expertise, independent technical review, and quality assurance support to the PMU for the planning, feasibility confirmation, detailed engineering design, and implementation readiness of the KV WaSIP. The Geotechnical Engineer will help ensure that site investigations, geological and geotechnical interpretations, foundation assessments, construction material evaluations, slope stability analyses, and related design inputs for the proposed dam and associated bulk water supply infrastructure are technically robust, risk-informed, constructible, and consistent with applicable national requirements, World Bank requirements, and international good industry practice.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

The duties of the Specialist is mentioned in the Terms of Reference in detail.

4. Qualifications and Experience

All applications will be evaluated against the assignment’s required qualifications below.  

Candidates who comply with the qualifications will be scored according to predefined criteria. A minimum of three candidates will be shortlisted and interviewed. The candidate with the highest score will be invited to negotiate a contract. Referees of the selected candidate may be contacted to verify prior experience, performance, and interpersonal skills. 

 The Geotechnical Engineer shall possess strong academic qualifications and demonstrated professional experience relevant to geotechnical engineering, dam foundations, slope stability, seepage control, construction materials, and multidisciplinary technical review of major water infrastructure projects. The expert should have proven capability to assess the adequacy of site investigations and geotechnical analyses, review engineering assumptions and design inputs, and advise on constructability, dam safety, geotechnical risk, and long-term performance of dam and associated bulk water supply infrastructure

Qualifications and Relevant Experience

  • Education:
    • The expert shall hold at least a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, geological engineering, engineering geology, water resources engineering, or a related discipline.
    • A master’s degree in geotechnical engineering, engineering geology, dam engineering, or a closely related field is required, and a PhD will be considered an added advantage.
  • Work Experience:
    • At least 15 years of relevant geotechnical engineering experience, including site investigations, dam foundation assessment, and design review or implementation support for major water resources, dam, or bulk water infrastructure projects.
    • Demonstrated expertise in geotechnical assessment and design review for large dams and associated infrastructure, including foundations, abutments, slopes, spillways, outlet works, access roads, reservoirs, and related facilities.
    • Proven capability in interpreting geotechnical investigations and advising on dam safety, long-term performance, and construction materials, including seepage, grouting, slope stability, seismic effects, monitoring, borrow areas, and constructability.
  • Interpersonal Skills
    • The expert shall have strong analytical, report writing, and communication skills, and shall be able to communicate clearly and effectively in spoken and written English.

5. Evaluation and Selection Method

The Senior Dam Specialist will be hired by the PMU using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method following “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) Seventh Edition 2025. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations”.

6. Duration of the Assignment

The Geotechnical Engineer is expected to provide support to the PMU for an expected input of 132 person days during a 17 month project period on an intermittent basis. The Project Manager shall plan the inputs of the Engineer based on the project schedule and report deliverables of the Design Consultant. 

7. Remuneration

A market-based salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications will be offered.

8. Reporting

The Geotechnical Engineer will report directly to the Project Manager, PMU.

9. Location

  • The consultant will be based at the PMU office and may be required to travel outside the valley as needed for project-related procurement activities.
  • The Project shall provide following facilities to consultant during his tenure of service:
  • Office space
  • Email and internet access
  • Required office stationery and other materials
  • Photocopying/printing facilities

10. Application Process

Interested candidates shall submit a complete application package comprising:

  1. Up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. Copies of academic and professional certificates.
  3. Contact details for at least three (03) professional references familiar with the candidate’s relevant work.

Applications shall be submitted electronically no later than 17.00 PM on 18th September 2026 to the following e-mail address: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered.

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project – Sisneri Water Supply Project

Address: Jawlakhel, Lalitpur

Attention: Executive Director

Email: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com

Website: www.kvwsmb.org.np

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20 – Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist)

 

UKRAINE

Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project 

Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA

 

Assignment Title: Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist

 

Reference No. MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MOES) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (hereinafter referred to as Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 

The Project aims to increase efficiency and improve conditions to ensure quality and transparency in the higher education system of Ukraine.

The purpose of the Consultant's activities is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services

(Individual Consultant)

Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist

Procurement No. MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20

Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project

World Bank Loan No. 9238-UA


 

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (hereinafter referred to as "IBRD" or the "World Bank") signed Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA in the amount of US$200 million to implement the Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (hereinafter, the "Project"). The Project is implemented in Ukraine by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) with support from the World Bank Group.

Project implementation period: 2021-2027.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve the efficiency, conditions for quality, and transparency in Ukraine's higher education system.

The Project comprises six components:

  • Component 1: Sector-Wide Improvements to Governance, Financing, Quality and Transparency.
  • Component 2: Alliances and Partnerships for Improved Efficiency and Quality.
  • Component 3: Capacity Building and Education Environment Enhancement.
  • Component 4: Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation.
  • Component 5: Support to Academic and Social Scholarships for Higher Education Students.
  • Component 6: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).

The Project will finance two expenditure categories: Category (i) - investments in goods, works, and services, with disbursements made against eligible expenditures; and Category (ii) - transfers to the budget upon fulfilment of certain results-based conditions, with disbursements likewise made against eligible expenditures subject to the achievement of specified results, as set forth in the Loan Agreement and the Project Operations Manual.

Within Part 3 of the Project, specialized consultants are planned to be engaged to support the effective management of the higher education and research system, as well as higher education institutions, and to provide support for the implementation of digital, financial, human resources, and other components of higher education reform at the institutional level.

More detailed information about the Project is available at: https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P171050

These Terms of Reference set out the objective and scope of the consulting services, as well as the qualification requirements for the Consultant.

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant's scope of services shall include, but not be limited to:

  • ensure effective working interaction among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, consultants of UIHERP and other stakeholder;
  • collect and consolidate information required for UIHERP implementation;
  • organize the day-to-day work of specialists and consultants of the MoES UIHERP support team;
  • coordinate work-related matters, deadlines, and task priorities;
  • maintain working calendars and records of tasks, deadlines, status, and agreements; send reminders to responsible persons and provide timely notice of delays or the need for management decisions;
  • coordinate the preparation and conduct of working sessions, meetings, events, and visits under the Project; record agreements and monitor follow-up actions;
  • ensure the timely exchange of information among MoES management, structural units, the support consultant team, higher education institutions, partners, and UIHERP;
  • collect, verify for completeness, systematize, and technically format working materials, background information, draft letters, and meeting materials;
  • organize the clearance of documents and materials, track their routing and status, and monitor the completion of assigned tasks;
  • organize the collection of reports from engaged Support Team specialists for the preparation of monthly and other reports required under the Project, and perform other Project implementation tasks within the Consultant's competence;
  • perform other Project-related tasks within the Consultant's competence, as assigned by the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system.

The following outputs and results are expected from the services (the list is not exhaustive):

  • the day-to-day work of MoES specialists, consultants of the higher education support team, and UIHERP is organized;
  • working calendars, task lists, deadlines, status, and agreements are kept up to date; decisions and follow-up actions are recorded and tracked;
  • working meetings, sessions, events, and visits are organized in a timely manner; the necessary materials are prepared and information exchange among the parties involved is ensured;
  • working materials and evidence of task completion are systematized;
  • effective working interaction is ensured among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, the support team and UIHERP, higher education institutions, and other higher education stakeholders;
  • the day-to-day work of the team's specialists and consultants is organized.

IV. REPORTING

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator, be accountable to the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system, and work under their supervision.

The Consultant shall coordinate their activities with the Project Manager - Head of the Consultant Team and ensure the administrative coordination of specialists and consultants engaged in implementing UIHERP tasks in higher education.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports in hard copy to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator.

Each monthly report shall include a concise description of the administrative and coordination tasks performed, meetings and events organized, assignments and work processes supported, the status of interaction with engaged specialists, and the materials collected and systematized for UIHERP implementation and reporting. Where necessary, the report shall include agendas, minutes, links, task lists, or other evidence of performance.

V. RESOURCES PROVIDED

MoES shall provide the Consultant in a timely manner with the information necessary to perform the assignment.

MoES may provide the Consultant with a workspace, including the equipment necessary to perform the functions (e.g., a personal computer, communications equipment, and office equipment).

VI. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • a Master's degree or higher;
  • at least three years of professional experience in administrative coordination, project administration, or organizational support for managers or teams in the education sector;
  • experience organizing the work of a team or group of consultants while concurrently managing multiple tasks, deadlines, and clearances;
  • experience preparing working meetings and events, taking minutes or recording agreements, and monitoring their implementation;
  • experience organizing document workflows, clearance processes, and working interaction among structural units, partners, or contractors;
  • skills in collecting, systematizing, and consolidating information for working and reporting materials;
  • strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work with confidential information, manage multiple tasks, and meet tight deadlines;
  • fluency in Ukrainian;
  • English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or higher;
  • proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, videoconferencing platforms, and digital tools for task management and teamwork.

The following preferred (non-mandatory) qualifications, competencies, and experience will be considered an advantage:

  • an academic background in management, public administration, project management, international relations, political science, or a related field;
  • experience in higher education;
  • experience in the public sector;
  • experience providing administrative support to projects financed by international financial institutions or international technical assistance programs;
  • knowledge of other foreign languages will be considered an advantage.

MoES may invite the most qualified candidates for an interview to clarify information provided in their CVs.

VII. PERIOD AND PLACE OF WORK

The Consultant shall provide the services until 30 June 2027. with the possibility of extending the contract if UIHERP is extended.

The Consultant shall provide the services under this Contract on an ongoing basis throughout its term, with a level of effort equivalent to full-time engagement, to the extent necessary for the proper performance of the tasks specified in these Terms of Reference.

The Client and the Consultant may at any time agree on a different workload based on the actual volume of tasks.

Specific contractual terms and working arrangements shall be discussed and agreed separately.

VIII. APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, marina.chubenko@mon.gov.ua indicating the email subject: «MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20: [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.

(ii) Specific Experience:  The Bidder shall have successfully completed at least two (2) contracts within the last ten (10) years, each with a minimum contract value of LKR 60 million or USD 177,000.00 for the supply, installation, and commissioning of metocean stations or comparable marine monitoring platforms in WMO member countries.

1.0       Background:

The Pacific Community (www.spc.int) has received financing in the amount of USD 6.0 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific Islands Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Statistics for Development Division

The SPC Statistics for Development Division leads the implementation of the Strategic Framework for Pacific Statistics, endorsed by PICT leaders in 2023. The framework promotes a regional approach to strengthening the quality, scope, and coordination of official statistics across the Pacific.

SPC supports national statistical offices by building capacity to produce reliable demographic, economic, and social data for evidence-based policy and decision making. As a regional technical provider operating across 22 PICTs, SPC plays a key role in adapting international statistical standards to Pacific contexts, particularly for small island developing states with limited resources.

Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific (PacStat) Project

The PacStat project is an International Development Association (IDA; https://ida.worldbank.org/) funded project that is to be implemented over the period of June 2020 to February 2027 including an additional financing phase.  The overall development objective of PACSTAT is to improve the quality of welfare data collection and accessibility to comparable welfare data in the Pacific Island Countries.

The context for this project is summarized as:

  • PICs are characterised by small populations spread across vast areas.
  • Better, more timely, and more comparable data is needed to understand deprivation between countries as well as identify and monitor regional trends.
  • Data deprivation in the PICs hinders evidence-based policy design.
  • National Statistics Offices (NSOs) lack funding to meet the costs of data collection in the Pacific.
  • Low statistical capacity is a major challenge in addressing data deprivation.
  • There has been some improvement in statistical capacity over time, but results have not been sustained.
  • There is potential for improvements and innovations in both administrative and survey data to lead to one or more of substantial cost savings, new statistics, or improved quality of statistics.

The additional financing under the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific Islands project directly supports regional efforts to advance statistical innovation and capacity building, with a particular focus on operational enhancement of administrative data for official statistics. Through commissioned works endorsed by the Pacific Statistics Methods Board (PSMB), the project will assess and strengthen national administrative data systems, enabling their systematic integration into statistical production processes across Pacific Island countries.

This initiative addresses critical operational challenges including data governance, quality assurance, interoperability, and confidentiality by building institutional, legal, and technical capacity within National Statistics Offices and priority government agencies. The additional financing sustains and expands high-priority activities, such as regional workshops, technical assistance, and the development of standard operating procedures and metadata templates, ensuring readiness for regionally standardised data reporting and evidence use. By promoting the practical use of administrative data alongside traditional survey and census programmes, the project enhances the quality, timeliness, and comparability of welfare statistics, directly contributing to the achievement of project development objectives and laying the groundwork for the next phase of regional statistical innovation

2.0       Objective of the assignment:

The overall objective of the assignment is to enhance the operational readiness of national statistical offices (NSOs) and administrative data holding agencies in the Pacific region to use administrative data for the production of official statistics, building on the findings of a preliminary administrative data readiness assessment which is currently being completed by a separate assignment.

The objective will be achieved by supporting practical, implementation-oriented activities that address priority gaps identified during the readiness assessment, including:

  • Strengthening the capacity of Pacific NSOs to operationally access, manage, and use administrative data for statistical production, through the design and implementation of targeted pilots, improved workflows, and institutional collaboration;
  • Enhancing the operational usability of selected administrative data systems in the Pacific region for official statistics, including arrangements related to data access, governance, data management practices, and integration into statistical production processes, either as standalone sources or as part of a broader source mix.

The assignment is intended to move beyond diagnostic assessment and to demonstrate, through a limited number of pilots in selected Pacific countries, practical approaches and good practices for the effective use of administrative data in official statistics. It will support learning, documentation, and regional knowledge exchange, and inform the potential scalingup of successful approaches in subsequent phases.

3.0       Scope of Services:

The Scope of the assignment includes the following tasks:  

Task 1 – Selection of pilot countries and agencies: Identify and select three pilot countries, with one country selected if possible from each Pacific subregion (IDA countries) based on national contexts and involvement in the PacStat 2 project and identify relevant use cases for the production of official statistics using administrative data. Selection will be informed by previous readiness assessments, national statistical priorities, and the willingness and capacity of institutions to engage in pilot activities, and feasibility within the contract timeframe from a legal point of view. The selection process will be informed and validated by SPC, which will also be involved in initial consultations with participating countries to confirm scope, expectations, and roles. 

Task 2 – Development of agency level operational work plans: Develop agency level operational work plans for the use of administrative data in official statistics in each pilot country, in collaboration with national statistical offices (NSOs) and selected administrative agencies. Based on at least two meetings with NSOs and administrative agencies for each pilot country and building on the admin data readiness assessment project recently carried out by the World Bank, the work plans will define the intended statistical uses of administrative data, describe institutional roles and responsibilities, identify required legal, technical, and organisational arrangements, and outline a sequencing of activities and milestones. 

Task 3 – Design and documentation of administrative data flows: Design and document administrative data flows from source systems to statistical production processes for the selected pilot use cases. This will include documenting data extraction mechanisms and calendar, data structures and variables, metadata availability, data transformation and validation steps, and quality assurance procedures. The documentation will focus on clarity, consistency, and reproducibility, supporting both pilot implementation and potential future institutionalisation, with key design decisions validated by SPC. 

Task 4 – Development of data sharing protocols and arrangements: Support the development or refinement of data sharing protocols and related governance arrangements required for the regular use of administrative data for official statistics. This will include clarifying access conditions, data transfer modalities, update frequency, confidentiality and security requirements, revision policies, and roles related to data stewardship. Existing legal frameworks and institutional practices will be considered. 

Task 5 – Pilot implementation of administrative data pipelines: Support the pilot implementation of administrative data pipelines in each selected country, focusing on the operational use of administrative data for selected statistical outputs. This will include supporting the use of appropriate IT infrastructure, data ingestion, application of agreed data processing and quality checks, and the production of pilot or experimental statistical outputs. Statistical processing will be implemented using the R scripting language, with computer code hosted on a GitHub repository owned by the respective countries. The purpose of this task is to assess operational feasibility, identify practical challenges, and document lessons learned, rather than to establish full production systems. 

Task 6 – Regional workshop on administrative data for official statistics: Design and deliver a regional workshop on the use of administrative data for official statistics in the Pacific. The workshop will provide a platform for pilot countries to share experiences, challenges, and lessons learned, and to facilitate peer to peer learning and experience exchange among participating NSOs and agencies. The workshop agenda and content will be validated by SPC. 

4.0         Expected Outcomes, Deliverables, and Timeline:

The Project Development Objective is to improve the quality of welfare data collection and accessibility to comparable welfare data in the Pacific Island Countries.

5.0       Duration of the Assignment and Estimated Expert-Time Input:

The Individual Consultant will be engaged for up to 5 months. The envisaged start date for the Individual Consultant is at the earliest opportunity and no later than September 2026, and the engagement will be full time with flexible remote work and up to 3-4 country visits as needed and approved by SPC. All travelrelated costs associated with these missions shall be included in the contract price.

6.0         Reporting Requirements:

The consultant will report the PacStat Project Manager for overall assignment of coordination and project alignment, and to the SPC Data Services & Dissemination Manager or SPC Statistics Adviser (Process Modernisation) within this team for technical and methodological guidance. Reporting responsibilities include: 

The consultant will submit the following deliverables to SPC, which will form the basis for milestone payments as agreed in the Contract: 

  • Inception and pilot selection report, including methodology, detailed work plan, sequencing of activities, pilot engagement approach, justification for the selection of pilot countries and agencies, selected use cases, and confirmation of scope, roles, and expectations.
  • Agencylevel operational work plans for each pilot country, covering selected countries and agencies, priority use cases, roles and responsibilities, sequencing of activities, and implementation timelines.
  • Administrative data flow and technical documentation, including data extraction mechanisms, processing workflows, metadata, validation, and quality assurance procedures.
  • Datasharing protocols and governance arrangements, including datasharing agreements and data exchange protocols for selected country use cases.
  • Pilot implementation and outputs, including source code implementing administrative data processing pipelines, statistical outputs produced from administrative data, and implementation notes documenting operational challenges and lessons learned.
  • Regional workshop and final completion deliverables, including workshop agenda and materials, a summary of discussions, lessons learned and agreed good practices, a synthesis of results across all tasks, and recommendations for scalingup or institutionalisation.

The Finance and Administration Officer in SPC’s Statistics for Development division will be the focal point for all finance and administrative aspects of the Project. 

 All reports and deliverables should be submitted in English. Deliverables should be presented in a format suitable for SPC internal use and for sharing with relevant national and regional stakeholders. The consultant may be required to present key outputs in workshops or virtual meetings with SPC and national statistical office teams. The consultant may be asked to participate in additional briefings or ad hoc meetings as requested by SPC or the PacStat Project Manager.

7.0         Working Arrangements:

The consultant will work closely with SPC and relevant stakeholders. SPC will provide access to relevant data, resources, and personnel necessary for the successful completion of the assignment.

Throughout the assignment, the consultant is expected to operate in accordance with the mutually agreed-upon number of workdays and associated deliverables as determined in consultation with the SPC. The consultant shall demonstrate diligence and effectiveness in executing assigned duties to the highest acceptable standards.

In assessing the consultant invoices for payment, the Project Manager will review these timesheets based on guidance from SPC Statistics Adviser (Process Modernisation)

The Project’s Labour Management Procedure is to be implemented throughout the assignment. Grievances can be lodged, as follows: 

Address/post: Pacific Community (SPC), 95 Promenade Roger Laroque, BP D5 98848 Noumea, New Caledonia | Phone: +687 262000 | Fax: +687 263818 | Email: complaints@spc.int | Web: www.spc.int. https://spc.int/accountability  

8.0       Selection Criteria – Qualifications, Experience, and Skills:

The consultant should meet the following minimum requirements:

Academic qualifications 

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s level or higher) in statistics, data science, economics, information systems, public policy, or a closely related field. 
  • A Bachelor’s degree with extensive relevant professional experience may be considered in lieu of a postgraduate qualification. 

Professional experience 

  • Minimum of 8–10 years of relevant professional experience in official statistics, administrative data systems, data integration, or statistical modernisation programmes. 
  • Demonstrated experience working with national statistical offices (NSOs) and government ministries or agencies that manage administrative data. 
  • Proven experience supporting the use of administrative data for official statistics, either through readiness assessments, system design, or operational implementation. 
  • Experience working in developing country contexts, preferably Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or similar capacity constrained environments. 
  • Experience working on donor funded projects, preferably World Bank–financed or multilateral development programmes. 

Technical expertise 

  • Strong understanding of administrative data ecosystems, including data quality assessment, metadata, classifications, identifiers, and data governance. 
  • Practical experience with data integration, data flows, and statistical production processes involving administrative data. 
  • Familiarity with legal, confidentiality, privacy, and data sharing frameworks relevant to the use of administrative data for statistical purposes. 
  • Experience designing or supporting data sharing protocols, operational work plans, or pilot data pipelines. 
  • For implementation focused work: experience using statistical or data processing tools (e.g. R or similar scripting languages) for data processing and quality assurance is an advantage. 

Analytical and reporting skills 

  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to translate technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations. 
  • Proven ability to produce high-quality written outputs, including assessment reports, technical documentation, implementation plans, and synthesis reports suitable for senior management and donors. 
  • Ability to document complex technical processes in a clear, structured, and reproducible manner. 

Stakeholder engagement and communication 

  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with NSOs, line ministries, and technical counterparts across multiple institutions. 
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills, including experience supporting consultations, workshops, or knowledge exchange activities. 
  • Ability to work effectively in a multicultural and regional environment and to manage multiple stakeholders with differing capacities and priorities. 

Language and availability 

  • Excellent written and spoken English is required. 
  • Knowledge of French or another Pacific regional language is an advantage. 
  • Availability to undertake the assignment within the specified timeframe and to travel internationally, if required. 

9.0       Evaluation Criteria:

CVs of eligible candidates that meet the minimum qualification requirements will be evaluated in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, using the following criteria and scoring system.
