The Government of the Republic of Angola received a loan of US$150 million from the World Bank (WB) and a donation of US$ 49 million from the Global Partnership for Education for the implementation of the Tertiary Education, Science, and Technology Project (TEST) and intends to apply part of this financing to hire a firm to provide Supervision of the construction works of the infrastructure of ISCED Huila.

The TEST Project aims to: (i) improve the quality of student preparation to increase total enrolment and expand opportunities for more equitable access; (ii) improve the quality and alignment of curricula with the labour market and instruction in priority training areas; and (iii) improve the governance and management of the education sector.

The consultancy services (“the Services”) comprise the assessment, monitoring, and verification of the full compliance of the Executive Project and any amendments to the Contract entered between the Owner and the Contractor. They further include the supervision of execution in accordance with the contractual Specifications and the respective Work Plan, ensuring the effective coordination of the Health and Safety Plan on site, in alignment with the quality standards, environmental and social requirements established by the World Bank and the applicable national legislation.

The consulting service will have a maximum duration of thirty-six (36) months.

The estimate man-month is 39.

 The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the email address given below.

The Tertiary Education, Science and Technology Project (TEST) of the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology and Innovation, now invites eligible consulting Firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • The company must have at least 5 (five) years of proven experience in supervising civil construction works, earthmoving, and hydraulic works, preferably in large-scale educational or public infrastructure projects.
  • It should provide at least two references in projects with an intervention area of up to 20 hectares, executed in the last 5 (five) years.
  • Previous experience in projects financed by multilateral organizations (e.g., World Bank, AfDB, European Union) will be valued, demonstrating knowledge of the applicable international procedures and standards.
  • The company must demonstrate familiarity with World Bank procurement documents, FIDIC Contract Conditions, and project execution in developing countries.
  • Experience in implementing environmental and social management plans, including mechanisms for preventing and responding to gender-based violence, will be valued.

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain five (5) to eight (8) firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” published in 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest: The aforementioned document can be consulted at the following link: http://pubdocs.worldbank.org/en/813421487104372186/Procurement-Regulations-for-IPF-Borrowers-portuguese.pdf

Firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

As per the Financing Agreement between the Government of Angola and the World Bank, the Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality And Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8H00 – 15H30.

Assignment Title: Capacity Building Service Provider (CBSP) to Deliver Training and Demonstration Activities on Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA), Water-Efficient Irrigation, Climate Resilience, and Sustainable Agricultural Technologies for Farmers under the Tashiskari, Narekvavi, Shavghele Masif and Zeda Arkhi Irrigation Schemes in Kareli, Khashuri, Borjomi, Dusheti, Khobi and Bolnisi Municipalities’ Villages

Reference No: GR/CS/QCBS/05

Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land (GRAIL) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The project cost is 138.6 million EURO comprising of an equal share (50/50) by each co-financer.

The project development objectives are to: (a) improve irrigation, and drainage services, and agricultural production in project areas; and (b) strengthen national irrigation and land management institutional capacity for climate resilient planning.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Capacity Building Service Provider (CBSP) to Deliver Training and Demonstration Activities on Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA), Water-Efficient Irrigation, Climate Resilience, and Sustainable Agricultural Technologies for Farmers under the Tashiskari, Narekvavi, Shavghele Masif and Zeda Arkhi Irrigation Schemes in Kareli, Khashuri, Borjomi, Dusheti, Khobi and Bolnisi Municipalities’ Villages The main objective of this assignment is to:

The consulting services ("the Services") include the engagement of a Capacity Building Service Provider (CBSP) to design and implement an integrated farmer capacity building and technical advisory program promoting Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA), water-efficient irrigation, climate resilience, and sustainable agricultural practices within the command areas of the Tashiskari, Narekvavi, Shavghele Masif, and Zeda Arkhi Irrigation Schemes villages.

The assignment will cover 55 villages across six municipalities and support approximately 2,920 farmers through integrated capacity building, field demonstrations, technical advisory services, and dissemination of Climate-Smart Agriculture technologies and good agricultural practices. The Consultant will establish and manage approximately 55–65 demonstration plots serving as practical learning sites for technology demonstration and farmer-to-farmer knowledge exchange.

The overall objective of the assignment is to strengthen farmers' technical knowledge, practical skills, and investment readiness to improve agricultural productivity, enhance climate resilience, promote efficient water use, and accelerate the adoption of sustainable agricultural technologies and good agricultural practices in line with the objectives of the GRAIL Project.

The selected Consultant shall develop and deliver comprehensive theoretical and practical training programs, establish and manage or select relevant demonstration plots, provide field-based technical advisory services throughout the production cycle, prepare practical extension and knowledge materials, facilitate farmer-to-farmer learning and technology dissemination, support monitoring and evaluation of capacity building activities, and document lessons learned and good practices in the command target areas.

The assignment covers, among others, development of crop-specific training curricula, implementation of integrated theoretical and field-based training sessions, establishment and management of demonstration plots, farmer coaching and technical advisory services, grant application support, dissemination of knowledge products, monitoring and reporting of project activities, and strengthening the capacity of local extension services.

The Consultant shall provide also targeted capacity building and hands-on support to eligible farmers in preparing and submitting applications under the GRAIL Matching Grant Program. The Consultant shall assist farmers in understanding eligibility requirements, preparing and collecting necessary documents for the grant application, filling application forms, and complying with the requirements established by the Rural Development Agency (RDA), thereby improving the quality of applications and increasing farmers' access to investment financing.

The detailed scope of services, implementation requirements, deliverables, and reporting obligations are provided in the Terms of Reference (TOR) which can be found on the link below:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncNpf9z7gFT4c2ntNTtQfiHuUZufBenS/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=111094613369888933218&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expression of interest should cover, but not limited to: corporate profile, years in business, experience relevant to the project activities, overall key staff resources, and core business. Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • At least ten (10) years of demonstrated experience in designing and implementing agricultural development, climate-smart agriculture, irrigation, agricultural extension, farmer advisory, or rural development programs.
  • During the last eight (8) years, the Consultant shall have successfully completed at least 2 assignments of similar scope, nature, and complexity involving the design and implementation of integrated agricultural capacity building programs, including practical field demonstrations, technical advisory services, and farmer training.

Note: the MEPA reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The experience of sub-consultants will not be taken into account while evaluating the corporate experience of the consultant.

To facilitate the development of EOI and further assessment, the interested consultants are provided with a Form for References for experience in the projects relevant to the assignment. The Form for References can be found on the link below:  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hDeNiygk0vcp3qx-8uwz05_ZYcmAsjPQ/view?usp=sharing   

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection Method (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations:  Approved Selection Methods: Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers - July 2016, revised September 2025.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 10:00 a.m. to 17:00 p.m. at MEPA, Mr. Ioseb Tchonkadze, Procurement Consultant.

The hard copy of the Expression of Interest (accompanied by the electronic version of EOI) must be delivered in English in a written form to the address below (in person or by mail) by September 6, 2026, at 17:00 hrs. local time.

  3. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.

1.       Le Gouvernement Malagasy a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès en Eau Potable (PAAEP) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché pour la conception et la réalisation de la sectorisation du réseau d’eau d’Antananarivo et la réalisation d’un programme prioritaire de réduction de l’eau non facturée et de réhabilitation du réseau

  • Concevoir et réaliser des travaux d’amélioration du réseau de distribution d’eau,
  • Concevoir et exécuter un programme de réduction de l’eau non facturée,
  • Préparer un programme d’amélioration des performances commerciales.

3.       La passation de marchés sera conduite par mise en concurrence internationale par Appel d’Offres tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteur de FPI » 7ème édition mis à jour en Septembre 2025, et est ouvert à tous les Soumissionnaires éligibles comme défini dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

4.       Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. Les pondérations suivantes s'appliqueront aux Critères notés (y compris les facteurs techniques et autres que le prix) : 60 % et pour le coût de l'Offre : 40%.

5.       Les Soumissionnaires intéressés de pays éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires aux adresses ci-dessous et examiner le Document d’Appel d’Offres durant les heures de bureau de 8 00 à 16 00 heures à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous

6.       Le Document d’Appel d’Offres en langue Française peut être obtenu par tout Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles en formulant une demande écrite aux adresses ci-dessous. Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par : voie électronique

7.      Les Offres doivent être remises à aux adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 09 octobre 2026 à 10 heures (Heure locale). La remise des Offres par voie électronique ne sera pas permise. Toute Offre reçue après la date limite de remise des Offres sera écartée. Les enveloppes extérieures des Offres marquées « OFFRE ORIGINALE », et les enveloppes intérieures marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants désignés des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaitent assister à l’ouverture des Offres à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous : le 09 octobre 2026 à 10 heures. Toutes les enveloppes marquées « PARTIE FINANCIERE » devront rester fermées et seront conservées dans un lieu sûr du Maître d’Ouvrage jusqu’à la seconde ouverture publique des Offres.

8.       Toutes les Offres doivent être accompagnées d’une Garantie d’Offre, pour un montant de 150 000 USD.

9.       Veillez noter que le Règlement de Passation des Marchés exige que l’Emprunteur divulgue les informations sur les bénéficiaires effectifs du Soumissionnaire attributaire, dans le cadre de l’avis de Notification d’Attribution de Marché, en renseignant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs inclus dans le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres .]

description:
Objectives of the Assignment

 

To lead and implement the communication and public relations (PR) components of the regional One Health program, ensuring unified messaging, stakeholder engagement, and media visibility through both digital and traditional communication channels.

 

Scope of Work

 

The PR consultant will be responsible for the following:

 

  1. Strategy & Planning
     
  • Develop and implement the Regional One Health Communication Strategy, in coordination with PR manager, Project coordinator, national focal points and WB team.
  • Develop a brand identity and maintain visual consistency across all communication materials.
  • Prepare and implement a publication and content calendar, aligned with project milestones and thematic priorities.

 

  1. Media & Public Relations
     
  • Develop and implement a media outreach plan, covering traditional (TV, radio, print) and online outlets across the region.
  • Build and maintain a media contact database of relevant journalists and editorial contacts in participating countries.
  • Invite and coordinate media participation in project events, including forums, launches, consultations, and training.
  • Prepare press kits for events, including press releases, background briefs, speaker bios, visual materials, and quotes.
  • Draft and disseminate press releases, opinion articles, interviews, and news stories in collaboration with technical teams and national stakeholders.
  • Organize and moderate media briefings and press conferences as needed.
  • Liaise directly with journalists and editors to support coverage of project activities and secure interviews with project representatives.
  • Conduct ongoing media monitoring and analysis, collecting and archiving published materials and tracking media exposure on monthly basis and present this analysis to the project coordinator.
  • Prepare quarterly media monitoring reports, assessing visibility, tone, outreach scope, and communication impact.

 

  1.  Digital Communication & Social Media
     
  • Design and manage regional social media campaigns, including content planning, visual creation, and performance tracking.
  • Contribute to the Central Asian One Health Information Portal by uploading communications products and ensuring regular updates.
  • Use interactive tools (surveys, infographics, Q&A sessions) to increase engagement with the general public and stakeholder communities.
  • Coordinate with national focal points/partners to collect, verify, and package news, success stories, photos, quotes and event updates for publication.
  • Draft, design, schedule and publish posts (RU/EN) across agreed channels (e.g., Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn/Telegram), including basic community management (replying/moderation per agreed SOP).
  • Maintain a shared content pipeline (news intake form + approvals tracker) and a monthly/weekly publishing plan

 

  1. Visual Design & Content Production (In-house)

 

  • Consultant is responsible for independent development of visual materials for the project, including (but not limited to): web-banners, website sliders/covers, social media templates, story/reel covers, infographics, event visuals, roll-up/banner layouts, presentation templates, news cards, email headers, etc.
  • Consultant must provide editable source files for all designs (e.g., CDR/.PSD/.AI/.INDD + exported .PNG/.JPG/.PDF) and maintain an organized archive (cloud folder) with version control.
  • Consultant ensures brand consistency across all materials

 

  1. Coordination with Contractors and Content Production
     
  • When external production is required (photo/video/printing/large-scale creative), Consultant prepares ToRs and supervises contractors; however, routine graphic design and digital visuals are produced by the Consultant in-house.
  • Coordinate the production of visual and promotional content (banners, roll-ups, branded merchandise, video explainers, photos, educational infographics).
  • Oversee venue branding and decoration for events in accordance with project identity standards.
  • Supervise contractors to ensure quality, timeliness, and consistency in all visual communications deliverables.

 

  1. Capacity Building and Training
  • Conduct a needs assessment on communications capacity among project partners.
  • Develop and deliver training for CAREC staff, national stakeholders, and focal points on effective communication, media engagement, and public messaging.
  • Support crisis communication preparedness, including simulations and guidance development.

 

  1. Monitoring and Evaluation
  • Define KPIs for communication activities and develop simple tracking tools (e.g., dashboards).
  • Conduct quarterly assessments of campaigns and PR performance; propose adjustments.
  • Contribute to donor visibility reports, CAREC publications, and knowledge products based on communication outcomes.

 

Assignment Duration

 

The assignment will last for 12 months, beginning from contract signing. Extension may be considered based on project dynamics.

 

Reporting

 

The PR consultant reports to the CAREC OH Project Coordinator and works closely with technical teams, the M&E specialist, and national communication focal points.

 

Assignment Conditions

  • The Consultant shall use their own hardware and software and maintain valid licenses for required design tools (e.g., CorelDRAW, Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator/InDesign and/or equivalent).
  • All costs related to creation of digital visual materials (software subscriptions, fonts, plugins, stock assets) are covered by the Consultant and included in the fee, unless explicitly pre-approved in writing by CAREC.
  • Printing and physical production (e.g., printing roll-ups/banners/merch) is not covered by the Consultant unless separately agreed and budgeted; Consultant provides print-ready files and technical specs.

 

Assignment Location

 

CAREC Headquarters in Almaty, Kazakhstan or one of the Central Asian countries with the possibility of remote work, with occasional travel within Central Asia for event support and stakeholder engagement.

 

Qualifications

 

Education

  • University degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or related field.

 

Experience

  • At least 5 years of experience in PR, media relations, or strategic communications for international/regional development programs.
  • Strong background in managing social media campaigns, organizing press events, and working with multimedia contractors.
  • Previous experience in working with donors such as the World Bank, WHO, or FAO is a strong asset.

 

Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Russian.
  • Strong media writing, storytelling, and content creation abilities.
  • Proficiency in design tools (e.g., Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, CorelDRAW,Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator (plus optional Figma/After Effects) and media monitoring software.
  • Organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Cultural sensitivity and ability to work with diverse stakeholders
  • Portfolio required demonstrating banner/social/event design.

 

Detailed Terms of reference is available at the link.

Interested candidates are required to CV and cover letter to smustafin@carececo.org with copy to okravtsova@carececo.org  not later than 04 March, 2026.  

 

Please be sure to indicate PR consultant in the subject line of the email.

description:
Introduction

On June 22, 2025, the World Bank Board of Executive Directors approved an allocation of US$3.45 million from the International Development Association (IDA) to finance the first phase of the ONE HEALTH FOR PANDEMIC PREVENTION, FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE, AND ECOSYSTEM HEALTH IN CENTRAL ASIA PROJECT. This approved financing to be implemented by the Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia (CAREC) for day-to-day regional coordination and implementation.

Project Description

The objective of the Project is to establish the capacity of the Regional One Health Coordination Structure in managing priority zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and food safety issues in Central Asia through a regional One Health approach.

The Project constitutes a phase of the MPA Program, and consists of the following parts:

Part 1. Establishing One Health Governance.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for:

establishing and maintaining the Regional One Health Coordination Structure;

developing Regional One Health Action Plan(s);

establishing the Central Asia One Health Portal;

developing and implementing a regional One Health communication and stakeholder engagement strategy;

organizing regular consultations and meetings with key stakeholders;

developing a regional laboratory network strategy; and

conducting regulatory assessments and reviews relevant to regional One Health issues to suggest areas for policy improvement.

Part 2. Enhancing One Health Knowledge and Workforce Capacity.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for establishing an institutional mechanism for knowledge development and exchange, as well as technical capacity development at the regional level. Activities will include:

conducting regional risk assessments on priority regional threats from zoonoses, antimicrobial resistance and food risks;

conducting regional or cross-border outbreak response exercises;

establishing a regional training platform as part of the Central Asia One Health Portal; and

organizing targeted training and capacity building activities for key professions in the veterinary, human health and environment sectors in participating countries.

Part 3. Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Learning.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for project management activities, including:

the creation of a monitoring and evaluation framework; and

communications and supporting systems to enhance learning and tracking of effectiveness of Recipient-managed One Health activities.

In accordance with the Financing and Operating Agreements and the WB requirements, the project is subject to independent external audit to be conducted after the end of each financial year (or another period agreed with the WB) throughout the project period. The main objective of the external audit is to check whether the donor funds are used as designated and express an independent opinion on the project financial reports for the reporting financial year.

 

Objective

The objective of the audit of the Project Financial Statements (PFS) is to enable the auditor to express a professional opinion on the financial position of the Project as of the end of each fiscal year and on the Project’s sources and uses of funds for the respective reporting period, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

The audit shall cover the period from June 24, 2025 to July 31, 2027, and shall continue annually until the Disbursement Deadline Date of November 30, 2027, as applicable.

The Project’s books of account shall be maintained in accordance with sound accounting practices and shall provide the basis for the preparation of the Project Financial Statements. The accounting records shall reflect all financial transactions related to the Project.

Audit Periods

  • The first audit shall cover the period from June 24, 2025 to December 31, 2025.
  • The second audit shall cover the period from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026.
  • The final audit shall cover the period from January 1, 2027 to July 31, 2027 and include grace period.

 

 

Responsibility for preparation of financial statements

The project’s management is responsible for the preparation of financial statements, including the maintenance of adequate accounting records and internal controls, the selection and application of accounting policies, the safeguarding of the assets of the project, and adequate disclosure.  As part of the audit process, the auditor will request from management written confirmation concerning representations made to us in connection with the audit.

Scope

The audit will be conducted in accordance with International Standards on Auditing. Those Standards require that the auditor plans and performs the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatements. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.

In complying with International Standards on Auditing, the auditor is expected to pay particular attention to the following matters, including special considerations for public sector entities:

  1. In planning and performing the audit to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level, the auditor should consider the risks of material misstatements in the financial statements due to fraud, as required by International Standard on Auditing 240: The Auditor’s Responsibilities Relating to Fraud in an Audit of Financial Statements.
  2. When designing and performing audit procedures and in evaluating and reporting the results thereof, the auditor should recognize that noncompliance by the entity with laws and regulations may materially affect the financial statements, as required by International Standard on Auditing 250: Consideration of Laws and Regulations in an Audit of Financial Statements.
  3. The auditor should communicate audit matters of governance interest arising from the audit of financial statements to those charged with governance of an entity, as required by International Standard on Auditing 260: Communication with those Charged with Governance.
  4. The auditor should appropriately communicate to those charged with governance and to management any deficiencies in internal control that the auditor has identified in an audit of financial statements, as required by International Standard on Auditing 265: Communicating Deficiencies in Internal Control to Those Charged with Governance and Management.
  5. To reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level, the auditor should determine overall responses to assessed risks at the financial statement level, and should design and perform further audit procedures to respond to assessed risks at the assertion level, as required by International Standard on Auditing 330: The Auditor’s Responses to Assessed Risks.
  6. When certain aspects of an entity’s operations are performed by a third-party service provider, the auditor is expected to include an understanding and assessment of the internal control environment of the service provider during the audit process, as required by International Standard on Auditing 402: Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organization.
  7. As part of the audit process, the auditor is expected to obtain written representations from management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, as required by International Standard on Auditing 580: Written Representations. 
  8. When the external auditor decides to use the work of an entity’s internal audit function to modify the nature or timing, or reduce the extent, of audit procedures to be performed directly by the external auditor, the determination shall be in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 610: Using the Work of Internal Auditors.   In determining whether to use the work of an auditor’s expert or the extent to which the work of an auditor’s expert is adequate for audit purposes, the determination shall be made in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 620: Using the Work of an Auditor’s Expert.  

In evidencing compliance with agreed project financing arrangements, the auditor is expected to carry out tests to confirm that:

  1. All external funds have been used in accordance with the conditions of the relevant financing agreements, with due attention to economy and efficiency, and only for the purposes for which the financing was provided. Relevant financing agreements include financing agreement GRANT NUMBER TF-C7896.
  2. Goods, works, and services financed have been procured in accordance with relevant financing agreements,[1] including specific provisions of the World Bank Procurement Guidelines.[2]
  3. All necessary supporting documents, records, and accounts have been maintained in respect of all project activities, including expenditures reported using Statements of Expenditure (SOE) The auditor is expected to verify that respective reports issued during the period were in agreement with the underlying books of account.

Project financial statements

The auditor should verify that the financial statements have been prepared in accordance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)”Financial Reporting Under the Cash Basis of Accounting “cash-basis method. The financial statements should include:

 

) A statement of sources and uses of funds;

 

b) Accounting policies and explanatory notes[3] (including additional accounting policies and disclosures), which will include:

- Statement of Financial position;

- Statements of Expenditure used as the basis for submission of withdrawal applications in the notes;

- A statement on the Designated account in the notes; and

- When the entity makes publicly available its approved budget, a comparison of budget and actual amounts either as a separate additional financial statement or as a budget column in the financial statements

Review of Statements of Expenditure The auditor is required to audit all SOE submitted to the World Bank in support of requests for periodic replenishment of the project designated account(s). Expenditures should be examined for eligibility based on criteria defined in the terms of the financing agreement and detailed in the Project Appraisal Document. The auditor should report any ineligible expenditures identified as having been included in withdrawal applications and reimbursed. The auditor should pay particular attention to whether:

  1. the Summary Reports (or SOEs) have been prepared in accordance with the provisions of the relevant financing agreement;
  2. expenditures have been made wholly and necessarily for the realization of project objectives;
  3. information and explanation necessary for the purpose of the audit have been obtained;
  4. supporting records and documents necessary for the purpose of the audit have been retained, and
  5. the Summary Reports (or SOEs) can be relied upon to support the related withdrawal applications.

Review of designated accounts

During the audit of the project financial statements, the auditor is required to review the activities of the project’s designated account(s). Activities to be examined will include deposits received, payments made, interest earned, and reconciliation of period-end balances.

Audit Reports

Audit opinion

The auditor will issue an audit opinion on project financial statements. The auditor’s opinion shall be based on an evaluation of the conclusions drawn from the audit evidence obtained and shall be expressed clearly through a written report that also describes the basis for that opinion. The audit report shall be prepared in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 700: Forming an Opinion and Reporting on Financial Statements. 

A modified audit opinion shall be rendered in the financial statements when the auditor concludes, on the basis of the audit evidence obtained, that the financial statements as a whole are not free from material misstatement; or the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to conclude that the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement. Modified audit opinions shall be in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 705: Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor’s Report.

The auditor will include emphasis of matter paragraphs or other matter paragraphs in the audit opinion where the auditor, having formed an opinion on the financial statements, seeks to draw users’ attention, when in the auditor’s judgment it is necessary to do so, by way of clear additional communication in the auditor’s report. The paragraphs will refer to either a matter that, although appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements, is of such importance that it is fundamental to users’ understanding of the financial statements; or as appropriate, any other matter that is relevant to users’ understanding of the audit, the auditor’s responsibilities, or the auditor’s report. This form of opinion will be presented in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 706: Emphasis of Matter Paragraphs or Other Matter Paragraphs in the Independent Auditor’s Report.

Other audit reports

In addition to the audit opinion(s), the auditor will also, either in the audit report or in the report to management:

  1. provide comments and observations on the accounting records, systems, and controls that were examined during the course of the audit;
  2. identify specific deficiencies and areas of weakness in systems and controls and make recommendation for their improvement;
  3. report on instances of noncompliance with the terms of the financial agreement(s);
  4. quantify and report expenditures that are considered to be ineligible and either paid out of the designated account(s) or claimed from the World Bank;
  5. communicate matters that have come to attention during the audit that might have a significant impact on the implementation of the project;
  6. draw to the borrower’s attention any other matters that the auditor considers pertinent; and
  7. responses from management, including implemented and proposed remedial actions.

If, during the audit nothing has come to the attention that the auditor considers pertinent to be brought to the attention of the borrower, and a management letter is therefore not prepared, the auditor will issue a letter stating this.

The auditor’s opinion on the financial statements and management letter should be received by the Bank no later than of 30 June 2026.

Public Disclosure

In accordance with "The World Bank (the Bank) Policy on Access to Information", the Bank requires that the recipient makes project audited financial statements publicly available in a timely fashion and manner acceptable to the Bank. In addition, following the Bank’s formal receipt of these financial statements from the borrower, the Bank makes them available to the public in accordance with this policy.

Management Letters and unaudited financial statements (e.g. Interim Financial Reports) are not considered to be a part of the definition of the audited financial statements for the purposes of disclosure.

Only in exceptional cases the Bank may agree — i.e., when the audited financial statements contain proprietary or commercially sensitive information — that the borrower or designated project entity may be exempted from disclosing the full set of audited financial statements, but is still required to disclose an abridged version of them in a form acceptable to the Bank.  Exceptions are approved by World Bank management.

General

The auditor is entitled to unlimited access to all information and explanations considered necessary to facilitate the audit, including legal documents, project preparation and supervision reports, reports of reviews and investigations, correspondences, and credit account information. The auditor may also seek written confirmation of amounts disbursed and outstanding in the Bank records.

The auditor is encouraged to meet and discuss audit-related matters, including input to the audit plan, with the World Bank project task team.

It is highly desirable that the auditor reviews the Bank's financial reporting and auditing requirements contained in Operational Policies OP 10.00 Investment Project Financing;. The auditor should also be familiar with the 2017 Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing and the Loan Handbook for World Bank Borrowers (the Loan Handbook) and Financial Monitoring Reports for World Bank-Financed Projects: Guidelines for Borrowers, November 30, 2001; and World Bank Procurement Guidelines.

This term of engagement will remain effective for future fiscal years unless it is terminated, amended or superseded.

 

[1] Depending on the complexity of procurement activities, the auditor may consider involving technical experts during the audit engagement. When such experts are involved, the auditor is expected to comply with provisions of International Standard on Auditing 620: Using the Work of an Expert. Consideration of using of the work of experts should be brought to the early attention of the borrower and the World Bank for mutual agreement and appropriate guidance.

[2] See Guidelines: Procurement Under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits, Revised July 2014 and Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers, Revised July 2014.

[3] The explanations should include a reconciliation between the amounts shown by the project received from the World Bank and those paid by the World Bank, as well as the Funds Flow Statement of the Designated Account.

O Beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de n° TF0B6898. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica.

A FUNDAÇÃO GETULIO VARGAS, ou simplesmente FGV, torna público que está aberto o prazo para consultores não individuais (pessoas jurídicas) elegíveis interessados na apresentação de MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, com vistas à consultoria não individual especializada em mapeamento participativo e diagnóstico socioambiental da atividade pesqueira na Floresta Nacional de Tefé. A consultoria não individual (pessoa jurídica) interessada deverá apresentar os currículos da equipe técnica proposta, o portfólio institucional e demais documentos de acordo com os requisitos definidos no Termo de Referência.

 

Para fins desta Manifestação de Interesse, a consultoria não individual (pessoa jurídica) interessada deverá comprovar, no mínimo, a seguinte qualificação:

Experiência de pelo menos 3 (três) anos de execução de trabalhos na área socioambiental na região do Mosaico do Baixo Rio Negro e/ou em outras áreas com reconhecimento de gestão integrada na Amazônia, tais como Reserva da Biosfera da Amazônia Central, Sítio Ramsar Rio Negro, Sítio Ramsar Rio Juruá e Complexo de Conservação da Amazônia Central - Sítio do Patrimônio Mundial Natural da Amazônia.

iv. Experiência de pelo menos 3 (três) anos, na elaboração de documentos técnicos que identifiquem desafios, potencialidades e recomendações para as cadeias produtivas.

GOVERNMENT OF SOMALILAND

MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (MoLGUD)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Country: Somaliland
Project ID: P508408
Project Name: Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer
Selection Type: Individual Consultant

Reference: SO-MOLGUD-567776-CS-INDV
Duty Station: Hargeisa, Somaliland, with travel to project regions and districts
Duration: 12 months, renewable subject to satisfactory performance
Application Deadline: September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time

1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD) of the Government of Somaliland is implementing the World Bank-financed Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408).

The main objective of the Bulsho Program is to strengthen community and local institutions for improved social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. The Program places citizens and communities at the center of government action and seeks to strengthen service delivery, local governance, citizen engagement, and the social contract between communities and government.

To support implementation of the Bulsho Project, the Government of Somaliland, through MoLGUD, intends to recruit a qualified and experienced Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer as part of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU).

2. SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The PIU Bulsho MEAL Officer will lead the implementation of the Project’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning system, ensuring high-quality data collection, validation, analysis, reporting, evidence generation, accountability, and learning in accordance with the Project Appraisal Document (PAD), Project Operations Manual (POM), Results Framework (RF), Monitoring and Evaluation Plan (MEP), and World Bank requirements.

The MEAL Officer will be responsible for monitoring, evaluation and reporting; Management Information System (MIS) and data management; surveys, research and evidence generation; accountability and citizen feedback; learning and knowledge management; data quality assurance; and capacity building. The Officer will also coordinate closely with other PIU members and relevant service providers, including Third-Party Monitoring, Digital Innovation, and Knowledge Management and Research firms.

The detailed scope of services, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting arrangements, and other requirements are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

3. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The successful candidate shall meet the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • A Master’s degree from a recognized university in Statistics, Economics, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • A minimum of seven (7) years of professional experience in Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) for donor-funded projects in fragile or conflict-affected contexts, preferably in Somaliland or the East Africa region.
  • Strong skills and demonstrated experience in quantitative and qualitative data analysis, research, and data visualization.
  • Demonstrated experience with Management Information Systems (MIS), statistical software such as STATA, SPSS or R, and digital data collection tools such as KoboToolbox.
  • Experience in setting up and managing KoboToolbox projects, including form deployment, version control, submission monitoring, and administration of user roles and permissions.
  • Demonstrated experience in Knowledge Management (KM), including developing and curating knowledge products and supporting organizational learning.
  • Proven ability to use M&E and research evidence for adaptive programming, evidence-based decision-making, and continuous improvement of project implementation.
  • Experience working with government institutions, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
  • Knowledge of World Bank M&E requirements and Results Frameworks is an advantage.
  • Strong understanding of results-based management (RBM), Theory of Change, M&E frameworks, indicators, and qualitative and quantitative research methods.
  • Strong analytical, report-writing, communication, presentation, coordination, planning, and capacity-building skills.
  • Knowledge of Somaliland’s socio-political and institutional context and understanding of cross-cutting issues, including gender, inclusion, and conflict sensitivity.
  • High professional integrity and attention to detail.
  • Excellent command of English and Somali, including reading, writing, communication, and presentation skills.

4. REPORTING AND DURATION

The PIU Bulsho MEAL Officer will report to the Bulsho PIU Project Manager.

The assignment will initially be for 12 months and may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. The duty station is Hargeisa, Somaliland, with travel to project regions and districts.

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD), Government of Somaliland, now invites eligible and qualified Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services.

description:
PROJET RÉGIONAL PLUS POUR L'AUTONOMISATION DES FEMMES ET LE DIVIDENDE DÉMOGRAPHIQUE EN AFRIQUE SUBSAHARIENNE (SWEDD+)

******

AVIS À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT

Numéro de référence : BF-WAHO-BF-447082-CS-INDV

TITRE DU POSTE : Chargé de projet pour les composantes 2 et 3 du projet SWEDD+

Introduction

L'Organisation Ouest Africaine de la Santé (OOAS) est l'institution spécialisée de la Communauté Economique des Etats de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO) chargée des questions de santé.

Elle a pour mandat de fournir des soins de santé de haut niveau aux populations de la sous-région. Les maladies transmissibles et non transmissibles sont les principales causes de morbidité et de mortalité dans la région ; par conséquent, le contrôle des maladies et la prévention des épidémies font partie des priorités des 15 pays de la région de la CEDEAO et constituent un principe central des activités de l'OOAS.

La Banque mondiale a accordé des subventions à la CEDEAO pour que l'OOAS mette en œuvre le Projet d’Autonomisation des Femmes et du Dividende Démographique en Afrique Sub-Saharienne-Plus (SWEDD+) P176693.

C'est dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de ce projet que l'OOAS cherche à recruter un (e) Chargé de Projet pour les composantes 2 et 3 du projet qualifié (e) et expérimenté (e).

Description des services

Le Chargé de Projet des composante 2 et 3 apporte un soutien stratégique, technique et programmatique à la mise en œuvre du projet « Autonomisation des femmes et dividende démographique en Afrique subsaharienne » (SWEDD+) dans le cadre des interventions régionales de l'OOAS dans le domaine de l'autonomisation des jeunes filles et des femmes et du dividende démographique, en veillant à la réalisation des  objectifs des composantes 2 et 3, qui constituent un travail important visant à accroître l'utilisation de services de santé et de nutrition de qualité pour les femmes, les mères, les nouveau-nés, les enfants et les adolescents, ainsi que le recours à des agents de santé qualifiés au niveau communautaire.

Fonctions et responsabilités :

Sous la coordination de la Coordonnatrice du Projet, le Chargé de Projet assistera quotidiennement la Coordonnatrice dans la conduite efficace et efficiente des activités liées aux composantes 2 et 3 du projet SWEDD+ à l'OOAS, en collaboration avec l'équipe de gestion du projet.

Parmi ses tâches, il ou elle sera responsable de :

  • Fournir un soutien technique au projet SWEDD+ à l'OOAS sur les interventions de l'OOAS couvrant les composantes 2 et 3 ;
  • Soutenir la réalisation des objectifs des composantes 2 et 3 attribués à l'OOAS, qui sont les suivants :
  • Soutenir le renforcement des cadres juridiques – l'achèvement du guide régional et de la directive sur la santé et les droits sexuels et reproductifs (SDSR) ;
  • Soutenir l'élaboration de modules spécifiques et adaptés aux adolescents dans les programmes de formation des sage-femmes et des infirmières ;
  • Soutenir la conduite de missions de plaidoyer auprès des gouvernements et des parlements de la CEDEAO, des chefs traditionnels et religieux (CTR) en vue de l'adoption de la directive et du guide sur la santé et les droits sexuels et reproductifs dans la région de la CEDEAO, en tant que partenaires clés pour mener le changement social et comportemental et promouvoir l'égalité des sexes ;
  • Élaborer le plan de travail et le budget annuels (PTAB) du projet ;
  • Élaborer les termes de référence et les mémorandums pour les activités ;
  • Organiser les réunions et les missions sur le terrain ;
  • Préparer la correspondance et les lettres d'invitation à envoyer aux participants pour les différentes activités et réunions ;
  • Préparer les rapports d'activité et d'avancement ;
  • Préparer les réunions de suivi sur la mise en œuvre des activités avec les pays, les partenaires et les agences chargées de la mise en œuvre des projets ;
  • Collecter des informations et des données auprès des unités de coordination de projet (PCU) au niveau national, ainsi qu'auprès des partenaires du projet et des agences de mise en œuvre ;
  • Aider l'unité de suivi et d'évaluation à remplir le cadre de résultats du projet ;
  • Organiser des missions de supervision et de suivi sur le terrain ;
  • Préparer les réunions des comités techniques et du comité directeur régional du projet ;
  • Suivre la mise en œuvre des recommandations de toutes les réunions ;
  • Représenter le coordinateur du SWEDD+ à toute réunion en cas d'absence ou chaque fois que cela est nécessaire, dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet.

Accomplir toutes les autres tâches qui lui sont assignées par la direction de l'OOAS en matière d'intégration de la dimension de genre.

Documents à fournir

L’OOAS invite à présent les Consultants individuels éligibles (“Consultants”) à manifester leurs intérêts à fournir les Services. Les consultants intéressés devront fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils ont les qualifications et expériences pertinentes pour fournir les services.

Les consultants intéressés sont invités à soumettre un dossier de candidature comprenant :

 

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt adressée au Directeur Général de l’OOAS et portant en objet le titre du poste ;
  • Un Curriculum Vitae récent, daté, signé et faisant ressortir les diplômes, formations, expériences en passation des marchés y compris le nom des projets et des bailleurs, compétences et aptitudes du candidat pour la mission ;
  • Une copie du ou des diplôme (s) ;
  • Une copie des attestations/certificats de service fait ou certificat de travail attestant les expériences professionnelles du candidat telles que mentionnées dans son CV.

Seuls les diplômes et expériences prouvés seront considérés

Qualifications, expériences et compétences

  • Être titulaire d'une maîtrise en santé publique, épidémiologie, ressources humaines dans le domaine de la santé, économie, gestion, politique publique ou administration.
  • Un certificat en gestion de projet serait un atout.
  • Avoir au moins 7 ans d'expérience professionnelle.
  • Une expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de projets financés par la Banque mondiale serait un atout.
  • Excellentes compétences en matière de consolidation d'équipe et de leadership dans un environnement multiculturel.
  • Solides compétences informatiques (principales applications MS Office, y compris les outils de gestion de projet) et capacité à utiliser les technologies de l'information comme outil et ressource.
  • Très organisé et autonome, avec une attitude interpersonnelle positive.
  • Expérience avérée de la collaboration avec un large éventail de partenaires et de groupes de parties prenantes diversifiés.
  • Le candidat doit être originaire d'un des États membres de la CEDEAO.

Maîtrise de l'une des trois langues de travail/langues officielles de la CEDEAO : anglais, français, portugais. La connaissance pratique d'une deuxième langue officielle serait un atout

Título da tarefa: Consultoria para a Realização do Segundo Inquérito de Seguimento no âmbito da Avaliação de Impacto do Programa Acção Social Produtiva (PASP)

 

Data: 03 de Agosto de 2026

Identificação do Projecto: Projecto de Protecção Social e Resiliência Económica (SPERP)

Referencia do Concurso: 37/MTGAS/SPERP/CS/QCBS/2026

 

O Governo de Moçambique (GdM), representado pelo Ministério do Trabalho, Género e Acção Social (MTGAS), recebeu um donativo da Associação Internacional para o Desenvolvimento (IDA) do Banco Mundial (BM) e do Fundo Fiduciário de Multi-Doadores para a Protecção Social (MozSP MDTF), para suportar a implementação do Projecto de Protecção Social e Resiliência Económica (SPERP) e pretende aplicar parte desses fundos para a Realização do Segundo Inquérito de Seguimento de Avaliação de Impacto do Programa de Acção Social Produtiva (PASP).

 

O PASP apoia os agregados familiares economicamente activos mais pobres, oferecendo assistência financeira através da inscrição de membros adultos em obras públicas e actividades geradoras de rendimento. Desde 2012, o programa tem sido implementado em distritos seleccionados, priorizando áreas com elevados índices de pobreza e vulnerabilidade a choques climáticos. O PASP é financiado pelo Governo, com apoio do Banco Mundial através do Projecto de Protecção Social e Resiliência Económica (SPERP) e do Projecto de Investimento no Desenvolvimento de Capital Humano Inclusivo no Norte de Moçambique (HCP), visando respectivamente assistir 218.300 e 20.000 agregados familiares até ao final de 2026.

 

O objectivo da consultoria é de é avaliar em que medida a implementação do PASP contribui para a promoção da inclusão socioeconómica das populações mais vulneráveis com capacidade para o trabalho. Para isso, serão utilizados indicadores quantitativos e qualitativos que meçam as mudanças nos meios de subsistência, segurança alimentar, e capacidade de resiliência dos beneficiários e das comunidades.

 

Os Termos de Referência (TDR) detalhados para a atribuição podem ser solicitados pelo email procurement.sperp@gmail.com .

 

O MTGAS convida empresas de consultoria elegíveis (“Consultores”) nacionais e internacionais, para manifestar seu interesse em fornecer os Serviços. Os consultores interessados devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e a experiência relevante para executar os Serviços. Os critérios de pré-seleção são: (i) pelo menos cinco (5) anos no negócio com experiência  relevante; (ii) descrição de pelo menos três  (3) ) atribuições  específicas que demonstram a experiência do consultor relevante para a proposta, em contratos de $400.000 ou mais e (iii) experiencias similares comprovadas nas três regiões de Moçambique em pelo menos três (3) inquéritos domiciliários aos agregados familiares em zonas rurais de Moçambique – a empresa deve ter conhecimento das formalidades e costumes locais.

 

A informação deve ser anexada como documento de suporte a Manifestação de Interesse. As qualificações e experiência dos especialistas principais não devem ser incluídas na manifestação de interesse pois não fazem parte dos critérios de pré-seleção. Os especialistas principais não serão avaliados na fase de pré-selecção.

 

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Seção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários do IPF" do Banco Mundial, Julho de 2016, revisto em Fevereiro de 2025, que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

 

Os consultores podem se associar a outras firmas para aprimorar suas qualificações, mas devem indicar claramente se a associação é na forma de consórcio e/ou subconsultoria. No caso de consórcio, todos os sócios serão solidariamente responsáveis pela totalidade do contrato, se selecionados.

 

Os Consultores serão selecionados de acordo com o método estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições - Seleção Baseada na Qualidade e Custo (SBQC).

 

Mais informações podem ser obtidas no endereço abaixo durante as horas normais de expediente das (07:30 às 15:30 horas). As manifestações de interesse devem ter o seguinte assunto “MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE N°37/MTGAS/SPERP/CS/QCBS/2026 – Realização do Segundo Inquérito de Seguimento no âmbito da Avaliação de Impacto do Programa Acção Social Produtiva (PASP).

PROJET DE PRODUCTIVITE ET DE RESILIENCE DES MOYENS DE SUBSISTANCE RURAUX (RIZ PLUS)

APPEL A CANDIDATURES

RECRUTEMENT D'UN(E) RESPONSABLE DE LA COMPOSANTE 2 DU PROJET RIZ PLUS

Référence : CON-03-26/MG-RIZPLUS/INDV

Date de lancement : 19 août 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour financer le Projet de productivité et de résilience des moyens de subsistance ruraux (RIZ PLUS), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de consultant individuel objet du présent appel à candidatures.

Ce contrat sera financé conjointement par l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD). La passation du Marché sera conforme aux règles de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale.

2. Sous l'autorité du Coordonnateur National, le/la consultant(e) sera chargé(e) d'assurer le pilotage stratégique, la coordination et la supervision technique de la Composante 2 du Projet RIZ PLUS relative à l’intensification et à la gestion durable des infrastructures et des services d’irrigation. Il/Elle veillera notamment à la planification des activités d’irrigation et de micro-irrigation, à la coordination et à la supervision des Spécialistes Régionaux, à la qualité des études et travaux, à la préparation des dossiers de passation de marchés, à la structuration et à la pérennisation des AUE/FAUE, du FRERHA et des structures de GEPP, ainsi qu’au respect des exigences environnementales et sociales.

Le poste est basé à Antananarivo avec des déplacements fréquents dans les régions d'Alaotra Mangoro et de Sofia. Le contrat est prévu jusqu'au 29 décembre 2028, sous réserve d'évaluations satisfaisantes des performances du/de la consultant(e).

3. Les Termes de Référence détaillés peuvent être obtenus auprès de l'Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZ PLUS ou demandés à l'adresse électronique indiquée ci-dessous. Les candidats devront clairement préciser leurs coordonnées dans leur demande.

4. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZ PLUS invite les candidat(e)s à manifester leur intérêt pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels prévue dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale », 7 édition – septembre 2025. Les candidats les mieux classés à l'issue de l'évaluation des dossiers seront invités à un entretien.

5. Le/la consultant(e) recherché(e) devra répondre aux qualifications minimales suivantes :

  • Être titulaire d'un diplôme d'Ingénieur ou d'un Master II (Bac+5 minimum) en Hydraulique, Génie Rural ou Génie Civil ;
  • Avoir au moins dix (10) ans d'expérience professionnelle dans le domaine de l'hydraulique, du Génie Rural ou du Génie Civil ;
  • Avoir au moins sept (7) années d'expérience dans un poste lié à l’irrigation des périmètres de superficie de plus de 2 000 ha dans des projets de développement financés par des bailleurs de fonds internationaux ;
  • Avoir au moins cinq (5) expériences réussies dans la réalisation et la supervision d’études d’irrigation (APS/APD/DAO) et de contrôle de travaux au cours des dix dernières années ;
  • Avoir au moins trois (3) expériences en matière d'encadrement d'équipes techniques pluridisciplinaires et/ou de coordination multisites ;
  • Avoir au moins deux (2) expériences d'appui à la structuration des AUE/FAUE ou de mécanismes de financement de l'entretien des infrastructures hydro-agricoles ;
  • Maîtriser la conception, le dimensionnement et la supervision des aménagements hydro-agricoles et systèmes de micro-irrigation ;
  • Maîtriser l'informatique bureautique, internet, messagerie, les logiciels DAO (AutoCAD), les logiciels SIG (QGIS) et les applications de réunion à distance ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance de la nouvelle organisation du MiASA et de ses entités ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance des procédures de la Banque mondiale, notamment en matière de passation de marchés et de gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux, et/ou d'autres bailleurs de fonds internationaux ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance de la SNDR III et des politiques sectorielles agricoles malagasy ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance des textes réglementaires régissant les infrastructures hydro-agricoles à Madagascar, notamment le NIHYCRI, le Code de l'Eau et la Loi n°2014-042 du 9 janvier 2015 ;
  • Maîtriser le français ; la maîtrise du malagasy est indispensable et la connaissance de l'anglais est souhaitée.

Seront considérés comme des atouts :

  • Une connaissance des régions d'intervention d'Alaotra Mangoro et de Sofia ;
  • Une aptitude à réaliser des levés topographiques avec station totale ;
  • Une maîtrise de logiciels spécifiques SIG et DAO tels que QGIS et Covadis, Revit ou équivalents ;
  • Une expérience en irrigation climato-résiliente et en gestion intégrée des ressources en eau (GIRE).

6. Les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s sont invités à déposer leurs dossiers de candidature, par courrier électronique ou sous pli fermé, comprenant une lettre de motivation, un CV détaillé avec références professionnelles, les copies certifiées conformes des diplômes ainsi que les attestations de travail.

Les dossiers de candidatures doivent parvenir au plus tard le 02 Septembre 2026 à minuit pour les candidatures transmises par courrier électronique et entre 08h30 à 16h30 pour les candidatures déposées physiquement ou envoyés par courrier à l’adresse suivante :

Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZ PLUS

Lot II Y 53 Bis, Bâtiment « FIADANANTSOA », Avaratr’Antanimora (près de la Gastronomie Pizza) – 101 – Antananarivo, Madagascar.

Adresse électronique : cn.rizplus@gmail.com ; copie à : rizplus-pm@googlegroups.com

La mention suivante devra obligatoirement figurer sur l'objet de l'e-mail ou sur l'enveloppe :

« RESPONSABLE DE LA COMPOSANTE 2 DU PROJET RIZ PLUS »

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

 SAINT LUCIA

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Preparation of the Castries Urban Stormwater Management Plan

 

Reference No.: SLU-SURFIN-STMWTR-QCBS-26

 

The Saint Lucia Urban Resilient Flood Investment Project (SURF-IN) is financing flood mitigation investments in Castries and Anse La Raye. The Pre-Feasibility Study undertaken by HR Wallingford has revealed a critical data gap: the absence of stormwater drainage maps and detailed operation and maintenance plans for Castries. Responsibilities for drainage infrastructure remain unclear between the Castries City Council (CCC) and the Ministry of Infrastructure, Ports Services, Energy (MIPSE). Preliminary hazard modelling has demonstrated correlations between poor maintenance regimes and flood risk, underscoring the need for improved drain de-siltation and solid waste removal.

 

The establishment of an Urban Stormwater Management Plan will improve maintenance procedures, strengthen inter-agency coordination, enhance budgetary processes, and guide investment prioritization.  Castries has separate storm water and sanitary waste drainage systems. The proposed Plan must take adequate account of future climate scenarios as well as current conditions to ensure investments perform effectively throughout their design life. The Task and Deliverables proposed for this assignment pertain only to the storm water management system. 

 

The consulting firm will work under the direction of the Ministry of Economic Development and Youth Economy to:

  • Develop a comprehensive GIS-based drainage asset inventory and management database for the Castries urban area
  • Establish clear delineation of maintenance responsibilities between CCC and the MIPSE
  • Assess current drainage network condition and identify accumulated deferred maintenance requirements
  • Develop an optimized maintenance management plan with realistic resource requirements
  • Recommend structural improvements and equipment needs to enhance maintenance efficiency

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below and also attached with the REOI.

 

The Ministry of Economic Development and Youth Economy now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

 

 

 

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. At least five (5) years’ experience in providing consulting services in urban stormwater drainage management, flood risk management, drainage infrastructure assessment, or infrastructure planning.
  2. Demonstrated experience in at least two (2) similar assignments involving GIS-based drainage or utility asset inventory, network mapping, spatial database development, and preparation of GIS deliverables.
  3. Demonstrated experience in at least two (2) assignments involving inspection and condition assessment of open and closed drainage systems, including identification of blockages, sediment/debris accumulation, flow restrictions, and damaged drainage assets.
  4. Demonstrated experience in at least two (2) assignments involving preparation of drainage maintenance management plans, including maintenance districts, inspection schedules, resource/equipment requirements, deferred maintenance assessment, and O&M budgeting.
  5. Demonstrated experience in at least one (1) assignment involving climate-resilient drainage planning, coastal/tidal drainage influences, groundwater monitoring, or groundwater-surface water interaction.
  6. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder consultation and institutional coordination for public infrastructure assignments, including coordination between government agencies, communities, or affected property owners.

 

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. In the assessment of submissions, consideration will be given to technical competence, qualifications and experience including local and regional. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.15, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth  Edition, March 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower (paragraph 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations).

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. (0800 to 1630 hours, local time). Submissions shall include a cover page displaying the name and address of the Consultant and shall be clearly marked “SLU-SURFIN-STMWTR-QCBS-26”

REQUEST FOR EXPERESSION OF INTEREST FOR CEPCU Social Development SPECIALIST

1. Background

The Government of Somaliland has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Enhancing Public Resource Management Project (SERP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services (individual consultant). to develop a lean, portfolio-focused coordination and performance management function that strengthens oversight, reduces implementation fragmentation, and promotes institutional learning across the World Bank-financed portfolio. Therefore, the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development (MoFED) intends to hire an International Social Development Specialist. The Social Development Specialist will fill this gap through portfolio-level advisory support, monitoring, and knowledge transfer.

2. Objective(s) of the Assignment

The Social Development Specialist will provide portfolio-level advisory support on social risk management, stakeholder engagement, grievance redress, inclusion, GBV, SEA/SH risk monitoring, and social risk management systems strengthening. The role is intended to strengthen portfolio oversight and institutional capacity and shall not substitute the implementation responsibilities of PIUs and other implementing entities.

3. Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities

  • Support activities designed to manage social risks as elaborated in the ESCP, ESMF, LMP, SEP, , and all other social risk management action plans.
  • Support and advise the PIUs on how to undertake continuous and effective stakeholder and community engagements and consultations, including implementation of the Stakeholder Engagement Plan.
  • Facilitate the immediate reporting of any severe safeguard incidents per the Project Operations Manual and Environmental and Social Incidents Reporting Toolkit protocols, including input to Root Cause Analysis and support to corrective action plan implementation.
  • Develop training materials and conduct capacity development to build staff capacities for effective social risk management at the CEPCU and PIUs/implementing entities. /
  • Develop social risks management tracking system across the portfolio, Compile regular monitoring and reporting on integrated feedback and grievance management and overall project performance on social risk management, including GBV, Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (SEA/SH), as input to regular project progress narrative reports and presentations as outlined in the ESCP.
  • Ensure PIU social specialists have a structured way of monitoring and project supervision including implementation of key mission action plans; workshops, consultations, and meetings and where necessary, participate in joint implementation and supervision missions, project-related workshops, consultations, and meetings as required by the World Bank, including travel to project sites throughout Somaliland.
  • Together with the CEPFU Procurement Specialist, support PIUs/implementing entities on how to integrate E&S risk management provisions into procurement activities, ensuring mitigation measures are factored into procurement planning and adequately resourced.
  • Consolidate lessons learned from portfolio implementation and project completion to inform future operations.

4. Selection Criteria

 The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience, and skills should be included:

5. Consultant’s Qualifications and Experience

A. Education:

  • An advanced degree in Law, Social Science, Political Science, Human Rights, Development Studies, Gender Studies, or another relevant discipline
  • At least eight (8) years of experience in the social development field, with a focus on stakeholder and community engagement, inclusion, gender and GBV, complaints and grievance management, vulnerable and minority groups, disability, displaced populations, and refugee/returnee influx.
  • Familiarity with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
  • Fluency in English is required.
  • Good experience managing grievance and complaints systems within a public or private sector programme.
  • Confidence and experience managing inputs to information technology databases.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and commitment to working in teams.
  • Demonstrated capacity to provide on-the-job training on social standards/safeguards and achieve successful knowledge transfer.

B. Desirable

  • Broad understanding of Somaliland's policies, laws, and regulations on social issues.
  • Experience working on humanitarian programmes.
  • Master's degree in a relevant subject.

C. Reporting and other Deliverables: The Social Development Specialist will report to the Head of CEPCU and work under the overall guidance of the Director General, MoFED

D. Duration of Assignment: The assignment is expected to take 12 months.

addressed

· Final FSM regulatory package and recommendations - Finalized standards and licensing framework, incorporating all feedback; Proposed amendments to existing legislation and regulations; Draft legal provisions where required; Draft a roadmap for legal adoption and implementation, and the financial framework.

AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

N° 137/ ZR-CEP-O-558664-CS-QCBS/PASEA/2026

Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) d’un montant équivalent à US$ 400 000 000 en vue de financer le coût du Programme d’Accès aux Services d’Eau et d’Assainissement en RDC (PASEA) et se propose d’utiliser une partie des fonds de ce crédit pour financer les services suivants :  Audit des comptes du Programme d’Accès aux Services d’Eau et d’Assainissement (PASEA) pour les exercices 2026, 2027 et 2028

 

Le présent avis d’appel public à manifestation d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis général de Passations des Marchés publié sur UNDB le 30 novembre 2022.

 

L’objectif de l’audit financier et comptable est de permettre d’exprimer une opinion professionnelle et indépendante sur les états financiers et les relevés des dépenses à la fin de la période considérée et de s’assurer que les ressources mises à la disposition du Projet sont utilisées aux fins pour lesquelles elles ont été octroyées en vue de l’atteinte des objectifs de développement du Projet.

 

L’audit financier et comptable doit s’assurer que les états financiers, établis par l’Equipe de Coordination du Projet (ECP) sont élaborés de manière à rendre compte des transactions financières dudit projet et qu’un système de contrôle interne adéquat mis en place et en œuvre est efficace ainsi qu’un archivage approprié et acceptable des transactions.

 

De manière spécifique, la mission du consultant est de :

  • Vérifier que les ressources financières mises à la disposition du projet ont été utilisées conformément aux dispositions de l’accord de financement et exclusivement aux fins prévues dans le respect des principes d’efficience et d’efficacité ;
  • Vérifier la conformité des acquisitions de biens, travaux et services du projet avec les dispositions des accords de financement, les procédures de passation des marchés applicables ainsi que les plans de passation des marchés approuvés ;
  • Examiner la conformité du processus de passation des marchés, apprécier le respect des procédures, l’utilisation des documents et outils de gestion prévus dans le cadre du financement du projet ;
  • Vérifier la fiabilité du système comptable et financier du projet ainsi que la régularité et la tenue des comptes et pièces justificatives ;
  • Apprécier la cohérence entre les ressources mobilisées, les dépenses engagées et le niveau d’exécution des activités du projet, sur base des informations financières et opérationnelles disponibles.
  • Effectuer des vérifications physiques, des visites de terrain afin de confirmer l’existence, la réalité et la conformité des biens, travaux et services financés par le projet ;

 

Les Termes de Reference (TDR) sont joints à cette demande de manifestation d'intérêt de la mission ou peuvent être trouvés sur le site web suivant : https://www.cepordc.com/.
