description:
Request for Expressions of Interest

 

Country: The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity Project RISE

Grant Number: P1729233

Assignment Title: Consultancy to develop the National Nutrition Regulation and Guideline for NaNA

Procurement Method: Individual Consultant Selection (INDV)

Reference No.: GM-CPCU - MOFEA-556550-CS-INDV

 

Background:

The Gambia is a small country with a total area of about 10,690 square kilometers.  It is surrounded on all sides by the Republic of Senegal, except in the West by the Atlantic Ocean. The population is estimated 2.42 million with a high population growth rate of 3.1 percent per year (Census, 2024). The 2017 Human Development Index shows the country rank at 174 out of 189 countries. Efforts to fight poverty have also proven ineffective with poverty levels remaining unchanged in the past decade (the percentage of households living below the poverty line of 1.25 $/day is 48.65 per cent in 2015 (HIS 2015/2016). The average GDP growth of 3 per cent per annum has barely kept up with population growth of 3.1 per cent. Data from the 2019/20 Demographic Health Survey (DHS) showed encouraging results for U5MR having dropped to 34 per 1,000 down from  54 per 1,000 live births in 2013, Maternal Mortality Ratio estimated 189/100,000 down from at 433/100000 live births in 2013.

Micronutrient deficiencies are widespread and continue to pose serious public health risks. Anaemia affects 44.8% of children, and only 10.8% of households consume adequately iodized salt even though 77% do consume iodized salt. Vitamin A deficiency affects 18.3% of children under five (MICS 2018). These figures highlight the urgency of interventions such as supplementation, iodization, fortification, and biofortification, supported by regulatory frameworks like the Food Fortification Regulation (2020). Despite these efforts, gaps in coverage and compliance persist, particularly in rural and underserved communities. Strengthening supply chains, enforcement mechanisms, and public awareness campaigns will be essential to improving micronutrient outcomes.

Infant and young child feeding practices show mixed progress. While 98% of children are breastfed, only 36% of mothers initiate breastfeeding within one hour of birth and 53.6% of children are exclusively breastfed. Complementary feeding remains inadequate, with just 15% of children receiving a minimum acceptable diet. The prevalence of malnutrition has improved with the DHS 2019/20 estimating stunting at 17.5% from 25% in 2013, wasting 5.1% from 12% and underweight 11.6% from 16%. These indicators reflect broader food and nutrition security challenges. The country produces only 50% of its food needs and over half the population (60.2%) do not have enough to meet their food expenditure, according to the Integrated Household Survey (IHS 2022). Climate change, low agricultural productivity, and population growth exacerbate these conditions, prompting national strategies focused on climate-smart agriculture, diversified and increased local food promotion and integration of nutrition into broader development efforts.

Non-communicable Diseases (NCDs) are on the rise, driven by poor diets, sedentary lifestyles, and urbanization. Hypertension affects 47% of adults, and obesity is significantly higher among women (20.2%) compared to men (3.9%) (WHO STEPS Survey 2019). Only 6.6% of the population meets WHO physical activity guidelines, reflecting lifestyle shifts associated with urbanization, poor dietary habits and sedentary lifestyles. The Fill the Nutrient Gap analysis 2025 shows that only 29% can afford a healthy diet. National responses focus on prevention by adopting appropriate dietary guidelines and lifestyles through social and behaviour change communication, and multisectoral collaboration. However, implementation remains fragmented, and greater investment in community-based prevention and promotion of healthy behaviours is needed.

As a cross cutting issue, the improvement and implementation of nutrition interventions and programme requires a strong coordination mechanism to avoid duplication and gaps. The National Nutrition Agency (NaNA) was established in 2000 as a semi-autonomous government institution strategically placed under the Office of The Vice President through an Agency Board with the legal mandate to coordinate nutrition and nutrition-related activities and advocate for the mainstreaming of nutrition into the macroeconomic and sectoral policy frameworks, implement nutrition activities, monitor nutrition interventions and programmes, mobilize and manage resources in The Gambia.

The Agency became a legal entity in 2005 through an Act of the National Assembly (Food Act 2005) which is now repealed and replaced by the Nutrition Act 2024. This ensures effective coordination of nutrition interventions across sectors. The Agency serves as the Secretariat to the National Nutrition Council (an inter-Ministerial body chaired by the Vice President), the country Scaling Up of Nutrition (SUN) Movement and the National Alliance for Food Fortification (NAFF).

The Agency was charged with the overall coordination and implementation of the policy with the following core mandates:

  1. Coordination of policy implementation
  2. Implementation of nutrition activities
  3. Secretariat of the National Nutrition Council
  4. Nutrition policy analysis, research and indicative planning
  5. Monitoring of nutrition interventions and programmes
  6. Mobilisation, management and coordination of resources

Following the enactment of the Nutrition Act 2024, there is need to develop a regulation that is critical for establishing and  formalising the multisectoral governance structures that ensure food and nutrition security and better help to understand and implement the Nutrition Act 2024. The regulation will also translate political commitment into actionable, accountable and sustainable interventions. To work on the development of a Nutrition Regulation, The Gambia, Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity (RISE) Project  has sought the expertise of a Legal Expert for the task.

Objective of The Assignment:

The objective of exercise is to review and develop comprehensive nutrition regulation.

Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities:

The scope of the work will cover the following:

  1. Inception meeting to identify areas of focus for the development of the regulation
  2. Map out which provisions of the Nutrition Act 2024 require secondary legislation particularly focusing on:
    1. Establishment of the Nutrition Fund (modalities, management tea composition and areas of usage)
    2. Reference intake of vitamins and minerals in food sources
    3. Prescription of fortification mix
    4. Establishment of fortification coordination platform (NAFF)
  3. Draft a Nutrition Regulation
  4. Conduct consultative meetings to seek the views of the stakeholders on the new draft Nutrition Regulation
  5. Incorporate views and comments in the draft Regulation
  6. Conduct a national validation of the draft regulation
  7. Facilitate review by the Ministry of Justice
  8. Finalize the Regulation and submit for approval by the Minister responsible for Nutrition

The Draftsman will require close collaboration with the NaNA for continued guidance.

4.  Individual Consultant Qualifications and Experience

Given the high level of technical rigor required to carry out the exercise, which is a succinct and analytically sound comprehensive Nutrition Regulation, dedicated human resource capacity is required in terms of time and technical expertise in conducting such a task. National Expert will objectively review the implementation and coordination mechanisms established by the Nutrition Act 2024 and any other relevant mechanisms. Hence an appropriate experienced expert, who is familiar with the development context in The Gambia and having good working experience of drafting regulations will be preferred. The Expert should possess the following qualification and experience:

  • MSc in Law or equivalent
  • At least 5 years’ experience in legal drafting
  • Familiarity with Gambian law and with food, nutrition, or public health legislation
  • Excellent spoken and written English
  • Knowledgeable in computer

Full TOR Availability Notice

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) will be made available upon request. Please send your request via email to the address provided below. The contract duration is 3-6 months.

PLACE OF ASSIGNMENT:                     Mogadishu, Somalia

APPLICATION DEADLINE DATE:       August 22, 2026, at (2.00pm Mogadishu, Somalia Local Time).

 

Project Background:

The Federal Government of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP). The Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT) intends to apply part of the proceeds of these Grants to finance for the position of Cybersecurity Awareness and Outreach Specialist through the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP) in support of the implementation of the National Communications Authority (NCA) in the Federal Government of Somalia.

The National Communications Authority's (NCA) seeks to engage a qualified Cybersecurity Awareness and Outreach Specialist to design, coordinate, implement, and monitor a comprehensive National Cybersecurity Awareness and Outreach Programme targeting government institutions, private sector organizations, financial institutions, educational institutions, media organizations, civil society organizations, youth, women, and the general public.

The Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP) addresses connectivity needs for countries in the Horn of Africa region. The program aims to advance the regional integration of digital markets in Eastern Africa through supporting cross-border connectivity, harmonization of data and e-commerce regulations and policies, and removal of trade barriers, with the vision of establishing a Single Digital Market (SDM). The EA-RDIP project has four components, as briefly described below:

  • Component 1. Connectivity Market Development and Integration.
  • Component 2. Data Market Development and Integration.
  • Component 3. Online Market Development and integration.
  • Component 4. Project Management and implementation.

 Scope of Work:

The Cybersecurity Awareness and Outreach Specialist will design, coordinate, and implement a comprehensive National Cybersecurity Awareness and Outreach Programme aimed at promoting cybersecurity awareness, cyber hygiene, digital safety, and responsible use of digital technologies across Somalia. The Cybersecurity Awareness and Outreach Specialist will promote cybersecurity awareness, cyber hygiene, digital safety, and responsible use of digital technologies; strengthen public understanding of cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities; foster a national cybersecurity mindset; and contribute to improving Somalia’s overall cybersecurity culture in alignment with international best practices and national cybersecurity priorities. For more details refer to the Terms and Reference (ToR).

Qualifications and Experiences:

Selection Criteria

The qualifications and experience of the successful candidate are set out below.

  • Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or relevant field.
  • At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience in cybersecurity awareness, digital safety, public communication, outreach, stakeholder engagement, or related areas. 
  • Demonstrated experience in designing, coordinating, and implementing cybersecurity awareness campaigns, outreach programmes, communication strategies, and public engagement initiatives. 
  • Experience organizing and facilitating cybersecurity forums, workshops, training programmes, public awareness campaigns, stakeholder consultations, and community outreach activities.
  • Experience of relevant services in Somalia, or an environment similar to that of Somalia.

Duration and Reporting : The Cybersecurity Awareness and Outreach Specialist will be engaged for a period of one (1) year to renewal on an annual basis based on satisfactory performance certified by NCA and availability of funds. The consultant will report to the client, the National Communications Authority (NCA), through its Director General as a supervisor.

Assignment Title: Consulting Services For Sustainable Investment Facilitation Advisory (SIFA) in the Five Pilot Cities of GEF Indonesia SCIP 

Reference No.: ID-PPP BAPPENAS-508088-CS-CQS 

The Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Grant, namely Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. Directorate of Strategic and Innovative Financing will be the Executing Agency of the Project that responsible for the Component 3. 

The consulting services (“the Services”) are part of Component 3: Piloting Innovative Financing Approaches and Instruments, specifically covering the Sustainable Investment Facilitation Advisory (SIFA) in five pilot cities (Jakarta, Semarang, Palembang, Balikpapan, and Bitung).

The Services will include the preparation of investment profiles and readiness assessments for 10 (ten) sub-projects in five pilot cities, the delivery of Investor Intelligence Gathering sessions across three investor tracks, the preparation of investment packages consisting of Project Teasers and Project Briefs, the facilitation and assistance of the GEF-Indonesia SCIP Market Engagement, as well as the co-production of City Financing and Implementation Plans with the pilot city governments.

The three investor tracks are defined as follows: (i) Commercial Track covers projects with identifiable revenue streams suitable for public-private partnership (especially user charge model) and domestic banking engagement; (ii) Development Finance Track covers basic infrastructure projects suited to development finance institutions, including but not limited to PT SMI, PT PII, and BPDLH; and (iii) Ecosystem Track covers biodiversity and landscape projects requiring grant, concessional, or results-based financing, including but not limited to Green Climate Fund, carbon market mechanisms, and CSR-based funding.

The Services are expected to start in October 2026 and be performed during a period of 9 months. The further detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) describing the scope of services for this assignment can be accessed at the following link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/10s2xJ7KEXZld8J_VgrKwfIlU5puwR7rn/view?usp=sharing .

The Directorate of Strategic and Innovative Financing, Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency now inviting eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are mandatory qualifications as follows: 

  1. Legally established and operating or having a representative office in Indonesia for at least 3 (three) years (pass and fail);
  2. At least 1 (one) completed working contract in the field of consulting services within the last 2 (two) years, either with government or private sector clients (pass and fail); and
  3. Prior experience working with internationally funded projects or multilateral development organizations, including but not limited to World Bank, GEF, ADB, or comparable multilateral frameworks preferred. (pass and fail)

Shortlisted firms will be ranked according to their demonstrated capacity across the following preferential criteria, which will be assessed in aggregate rather than as individual pass-fail requirements:

  1. At least 1 (one) projects of experience in multi-stakeholder facilitation involving local governments, including prior assignments requiring substantive coordination with or capacity building for subnational government counterparts in Indonesia in the last 5 (five) years in Indonesia;
  2. At least 3 (three) projects of experience in providing consulting services related to sustainable and innovative financing, investor engagement, or investment package preparation for infrastructure sub-projects at the national or subnational level in the last 5 (five) years in Indonesia;
  3. At least 1 (one) projects of experience in at least of the following thematic areas relevant to GEF Indonesia SCIP: waste and circular economy, water and sanitation, or energy in the last 5 (five) years in Indonesia; and
  4. At least 1 (one) projects of experience in at least of the following thematic areas relevant to GEF Indonesia SCIP: urban biodiversity and/or sustainable landscapes in the last 5 (five) years in Indonesia.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers July 2016, revised November 2017, July 2018, November 2020, and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms as a joint venture or a sub-consultant to enhance their qualifications. Grant No.: IDA-E2670

Tender reference No.: RW-SAA-556292-CS-QCBS

Assignment Title: Consulting firm for the Development of a Gender Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan to Increase Women’s Participation in ICT Policy Making and Governance

 

The Smart Africa alliance has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Digital Transformation for Africa /Western Africa Regional Digital Integration Program - WARDIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services to hire consulting firm for the development of a Gender Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan to Increase Women’s Participation in ICT Policy Making and Governance.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) includes to generate empirical evidence on the current levels, barriers, drivers, and opportunities for women’s representation in ICT policymaking and governance across Africa, and to develop a comprehensive Gender Inclusion Strategy and Implementation Plan to increase women’s meaningful participation

 

Specific Objectives:

  1. Conduct comprehensive mapping and gender assessment;
  2. Develop an evidence-based Gender Inclusion Strategy and Implementation Plan for SADA-WARDIP; aligned with the SADA Capacity Building Framework, including prioritized actions to increase women’s meaningful participation

 

 

The detailed request for proposal document for this assignment can be downloaded from this link : https://smartafrica.org/job/request-for-expressions-of-interest-recruitment-of-a-consultancy-firm-for-the-development-of-a-gender-inclusion-strategy-and-action-plan-to-increase-womens-participation-in-ict-policy-making/

 

 

The Smart Africa alliance now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria will focus on specific experience of the firm in conducting relevant assignment, years of experience in core business and technical and Managerial capability of the firm.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” seventh Edition September 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Available on:

https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/c84273d1b230aeb2b0b8134de5dc8cd7-0290012025/original/Procurement-Regulations-7th-Edition-Sep-2025.pdf

 

In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment as per paragraph 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations.  

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the quality and cost best selection method set out in the world Bank Procurement Regulations.

Escopo: Seleção e contratação de consultoria individual especializada em elaboração de estudo de prospecção de novos mercados, nacional e internacional, para produtos da cadeia de óleos vegetais, no âmbito do Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil – Fase 2).

 

O Beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de n° TF0B6898. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica.

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº  0013/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETULIO VARGAS, ou simplesmente FGV, torna público que está aberto o prazo para consultores individuais elegíveis interessados na apresentação de MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, com vistas à consultoria individual especializada em elaboração de estudo de prospecção de novos mercados, nacional e internacional, para produtos da cadeia de óleos vegetais. Os consultores individuais interessados deverão demonstrar que são qualificados e que têm a experiência para desempenhar o serviço, conforme descrito no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes

 

           As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser enviadas até dia 04/09/2026, às 23:59 horas, para o e-mail  asl2.compras@fgv.br. As Manifestações deverão estar identificadas como SMI Nº 0013/2026 – Prospecção -Novos Mercados. O(a) consultor(a) individual deverá demonstrar capacidade para atuar em elaboração de estudo de prospecção de novos mercados, nacional e internacional, para produtos da cadeia de óleos vegetais, com foco nos municípios de Carauari e Itamarati (AM), garantindo que as atividades ocorram conforme o planejamento, que engloba a caracterização da cadeia produtiva de óleos vegetais, o mapeamento de mercados nacionais e internacionais, a identificação de produtos prioritários, o levantamento de exigências técnicas e regulatórias e a elaboração de um plano estratégico de mercado, conforme o cronograma de produtos e prazos estabelecido no Termo de Referência. O(a) consultor(a) individual interessado(a) deverá apresentar o seu currículo e demais documentos de acordo com os requisitos definidos no Termo de Referência.

 

Esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse não pressupõe qualquer compromisso de contratação. Os(as) consultores(as) individuais elegíveis serão avaliados(as) de acordo com as normas do “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento, edição de setembro de 2023”.

 

Informações adicionais sobre o processo seletivo poderão ser solicitadas pelo endereço eletrônico asl2.compras@fgv.br

 

A Fundação Getúlio Vargas entrará em contato somente com os(as) consultores(as) individuais elegíveis para a próxima etapa do processo.

iii. Package III:  Segment 8 to 10 (km 8.453 to km 12.600)

AVIS À MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

 

Recrutement d'un Cabinet de Consultants pour la réalisation des études techniques des Centres d'Excellence pour la Gestion Intégrée des Épidémies (CEGIE)

 

 

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Sécurité Sanitaire en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HeSP) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des ressources de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif au recrutement d’un cabinet international chargé de la réalisation des études techniques des Centres d’Excellence pour la Gestion Intégrée des Épidémies (CEGIE).

L'Unité de Coordination du Projet (UCP-HeSP) invite les cabinets de consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

1. Objet de la mission

La mission porte sur la réalisation des études techniques complètes relatives à la construction de trois (03) Centres d’Excellence pour la Gestion Intégrée des Épidémies (CEGIE), prévus respectivement à :

  • N’Djamena ;
  • Moundou ;
  • Abéché.

Les prestations comprendront notamment :

  • Les études diagnostiques, topographiques et géotechniques ;
  • L’élaboration du Programme Fonctionnel et Technique (PFT) ;
  • Les études architecturales et techniques (APS et APD) ;
  • Les études environnementales et sociales requises ;
  • L’élaboration des estimatifs détaillés ;
  • La préparation des Dossiers d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) pour les travaux ;
  • L’élaboration d’un plan de maintenance et de durabilité des infrastructures.

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est estimée à cinq (05) mois.

2. Qualifications requises

Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour exécuter la mission, notamment:

  • Une expérience avérée dans les études techniques d’infrastructures sanitaires complexes ;
  • Une expérience dans la conception d’hôpitaux, laboratoires de santé publique, centres d’isolement ou infrastructures de gestion des urgences sanitaires ;
  • Une expérience dans des projets financés par des partenaires techniques et financiers internationaux ;
  • Une connaissance des normes OMS applicables aux infrastructures sanitaires ;
  • Une expérience dans la préparation de dossiers d’appel d’offres pour des projets d’infrastructures.
  • Les cabinets devront justifier d’au moins cinq (05) missions similaires réalisées au cours des dix (10) dernières années.

NB : Le cabinet retenu devra se conformer à toutes les exigences de la réglementation de la République du Tchad applicables à l'exercice de la profession. À cet effet, il devra, avant le démarrage de la mission, produire les autorisations, agréments ou preuves d'inscription aux ordres professionnels compétents (ONIC-T et/ou ONAT), lorsqu'ils sont requis par la réglementation nationale en vigueur.

Seules les qualifications et l'expérience du cabinet seront évaluées au stade de la manifestation d'intérêt. Le consultant le mieux qualifié sera invité à soumettre une proposition technique et financière simplifiée, conformément à la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur les Qualifications des Consultants (CQS).

3. Méthode de sélection

Le consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur les Qualifications des Consultants (CQS), conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition en vigueur.

Il est porté à l'attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, relatives aux conflits d'intérêts, sont applicables à la présente mission.

Les consultants peuvent s'associer avec d'autres cabinets afin de renforcer leurs qualifications, sous la forme d'un groupement (joint-venture) et/ou d'un accord de sous-traitance. En cas de groupement, tous les membres du groupement seront solidairement responsables de l'exécution du contrat, si celui-ci leur est attribué.

4. Critères d’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt

Les manifestations d’intérêt seront évaluées sur la base des critères suivants :

  • Expérience générale du cabinet dans la réalisation d’études techniques, architecturales et d’ingénierie relatives aux infrastructures de santé ou aux infrastructures complexes ;
  • Expérience spécifique du cabinet dans la réalisation d’études de centres hospitaliers, laboratoires de santé publique, centres d’isolement, centres d’opérations d’urgence sanitaire ou infrastructures similaires ;
  • Expérience du cabinet en Afrique subsaharienne, notamment dans des contextes comparables à celui du Tchad ;
  • Expérience dans la préparation des dossiers d’appel d’offres (DAO) et des dossiers techniques de projets d’infrastructures financés par des partenaires techniques et financiers internationaux ;
  • Capacité technique et organisationnelle du cabinet à exécuter la mission, au regard de son organisation, de ses moyens techniques et de son expérience ;
  • Expérience dans l’intégration des exigences environnementales et sociales, y compris la réalisation d’études environnementales et sociales conformément aux exigences nationales et aux standards internationaux ;
  • Connaissance des normes internationales applicables aux infrastructures de santé, notamment les normes de l’OMS, les exigences de biosécurité, de prévention et contrôle des infections (PCI/IPC), ainsi que les approches de résilience climatique.

5. Dépôt des manifestations d’intérêt

Les manifestations d'intérêt, rédigées en langue française, doivent être déposées sous pli fermé ou transmises par voie électronique au plus tard le 20 août 2026 à 16 h 00 (heure de N'Djamena) à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous, avec la mention :

« Manifestation d'intérêt pour le recrutement d'un Cabinet de Consultants chargé de la réalisation des études techniques des Centres d'Excellence pour la Gestion Intégrée des Épidémies (CEGIE) »

 

Bureau de la coordination Nationale de l’UCP-HeSP sise au quartier BOLOLO en face de la SNE à l'attention de : Thierry Madjitoloum TOINA, Coordonnateur National Tél : (+235) 66 26 73 85/66 56 11 05/66 29 61 52 ou par mail à l'adresse suivante : thierrytoina@outlook.com  ou adoumtomabakar@outlook.com

 

  1. Informations complémentaires

Les consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations complémentaires et consulter gratuitement les Termes de Référence (TDR) pendant les heures ouvrables, de 08 h 00 à 15 h 30 (heure de N'Djamena), auprès de l'Unité de Coordination du Projet HeSP (UCP-HeSP), à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessus.

O Estado do Amapá, por intermédio da Agência de Desenvolvimento Econômico do Estado do Amapá – AGEAMAPÁ, convida consultores(as) individuais qualificados(as) a manifestarem interesse na prestação dos seguintes serviços:

Especialistas em Aquisições — Consultoria Individual para apoio técnico à Unidade de Gestão do Projeto (UGP) e Unidades de Implementação do Projeto (UIPs), no planejamento, execução e gestão de processos de aquisições financiados pelo Banco Mundial, assegurando a conformidade dos processos com o Acordo de Doação nº TF0C8901-BR / 8768117272/2025 e o Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos (IPF), Sétima Edição (setembro de 2025).

2. RESUMO DO PROJETO

O Programa de Sustentabilidade Fiscal, Eficiência e Eficácia do Gasto Público – PROGESTÃO AMAPÁ tem por objetivo fortalecer a gestão fiscal, financeira e patrimonial do Estado do Amapá, por meio de ações voltadas à racionalização do gasto público, à modernização da administração pública e ao fortalecimento da capacidade institucional, contribuindo para a sustentabilidade fiscal do Estado.

Para viabilizar a preparação do Projeto, foi celebrado o Acordo de Doação (Grant Facility for Project Preparation – GFPP), destinado ao financiamento de atividades preparatórias, incluindo estudos técnicos, planejamento, estruturação institucional e organização das aquisições necessárias à futura implementação do PROGESTÃO AMAPÁ.

O Projeto é financiado pelo Banco Mundial, por meio da Doação nº TF0C8901-BR / 8768117272/2025, no valor de US$ 100.000,00 (cem mil dólares), sendo coordenado pela Agência de Desenvolvimento Econômico do Estado do Amapá – AGEAMAPÁ, com vigência prevista até 31 de dezembro de 2026.

 

3. DESCRIÇÃO DOS SERVIÇOS

O(A) Especialista em Aquisições a ser contratado(a) prestará serviços de apoio técnico especializado à UGP, com atuação nas seguintes frentes principais:

  • Elaboração e atualização da Estratégia de Aquisições para o Desenvolvimento (PPSD) e do Plano de Aquisições do projeto;
  • Preparação e revisão de documentos de licitação e seleção (TDRs, SMIs, RFPs, SDOs, editais e minutas contratuais), em conformidade com os modelos e requisitos do Banco Mundial;
  • Condução e apoio aos processos de seleção de bens, obras, serviços de não consultoria e serviços de consultoria;
  • Monitoramento e gestão dos contratos firmados no âmbito do projeto, incluindo o processamento de aditivos e a identificação de riscos contratuais;
  • Operacionalização e atualização do sistema STEP do Banco Mundial e organização do arquivo dos processos de aquisição;
  • Apoio às missões de supervisão e auditorias do Banco Mundial e prestação de esclarecimentos técnicos;
  • Capacitação da equipe da UGP e UIPs sobre o Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial e as boas práticas em gestão de contratos.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

REPUBLIC OF MOLDOVA

MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES COMPETITIVENESS PROJECT

Sector: General industry and trade sector

IDA Credit No. 71740

IBRD Loan No. 94230

Reference No. MD-CEP-547270-CS-CQS

 

The Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Competitiveness Project (MSME) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include enhancement the technical competence and knowledge in the field of mass metrology of Moldovan NMI specialists through comprehensive training and structured know-how transfer, focusing on both theoretical knowledge and practical skills in the following domains: (i) Mass measurements; (ii) Length measurements; (iii) Pressure measurements and (iv) Force measurements. To achieve the assignment’s objectives, the Consultant shall develop the training materials and deliver trainings for NMI specialists at the NMI premises and ensure practical on-site trainings for specialists of NMI at Consultant’ premises according to the topics, duration and timeline suggested in ToR.

 

The assignment will be performed in the period May - July, 2026.  

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this request for expressions of interest.

 

The Project Implementation Unit of the MSME Competitiveness Project now invites eligible local consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (required qualifications and experience of the firm, but not individual experts’ bio data).

 

This assignment will require an EURAMET metrology institute or consortium of such metrology institutes with appropriate technical and metrological qualification, comparable standards and internationally recognized knowledge, which:

  • Has relevant competence in the field of length, mass pressure and force measurements including relevant Calibration and Measurement Capabilities in the Bureau International des Poids et Measures (BIPM) key comparison database.
  • Has demonstrated previous experience in providing similar internship and/or trainings in relevant subject fields.
  • Has experience in the implementation of the donors’ and/or IFI’s sponsored projects.
  • Has experience in preparation of analytical reports, training programs and training curricula.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the „Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection” method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications; but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 Terms of Reference

Consulting Services on strengthening the level of competence and know how transfer on operation of the metrology equipment (1st batch)  

 

A.           INTRODUCTION

The Government of the Republic of Moldova (GoM) is pursuing a policy agenda to support export-led economic growth. In this regard, an improved business environment is essential to foster sustainable private sector growth. Significant regulatory and institutional weaknesses in the business environment have been identified by the recently conducted Investment Climate Assessment as major obstacles to the private sector’s ability to perform efficiently and grow, and they also negatively affect investor confidence. The presence of cumbersome regulations undermines the competitiveness of private Moldovan enterprises and prevents increased investment by increasing the cost of doing business, and ultimately providing fertile ground for corruption, favoritism, and the informal economy.

GoM is currently implementing a project - the Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises (MSME) Competitiveness Project, which takes a comprehensive approach to business competitiveness with funding from the International Development Association and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

The MSME’s project development objectives (PDO) are: (i) to reduce the regulatory burden, increase access to finance, increase the export competitiveness of Moldovan enterprises, and (ii) in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to respond promptly and effectively to it.

The PDO will be achieved through a set of activities that aim to: (a) digitize government-to-business services and inspections, streamline permissive documents, and enhance national quality infrastructure to reduce the regulatory burden enterprises face; (b) support access to finance for enterprises through credit guarantees and enhance the capacity of the Credit Guarantee Fund (CGF), and (c) support the development of MSMEs and enhance their export competitiveness; d) support project management; e) support the government's response in case of an emergency.

 

B.           BACKGROUND OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The target segment of the current assignment is National Quality Infrastructure System (NQI). NQI activities under the project focuses on increasing MSME competitiveness and enabling exports. The NQI activities aim at addressing the enterprise sector’s difficulties in competing in foreign markets caused by the existing gaps in NQI and services. Improving the NQI system will be achieved through: (a) building capacity in metrology and testing area by upgrading selected laboratories and strengthening institutional capacity in order to expand the list of measurements and testing demanded by export oriented firms; (b) ensuring the traceability of the measurements performed to enterprises, as well as access to quality infrastructure services due to increased number of calibrations and accredited cross-comparisons at the European Union (EU) level and (c) strengthening accreditation and certification capacity. 

Investment and technical assistance needs are significantly higher than what the Project can support. Thus, an allocation of approximately US$7 million equivalent will address these priority needs. Special attention will be paid to building skills among specialists to perform measurements and ensure more laboratories and services are accredited meeting the EU requirements.

Within this framework, the Government of Moldova through the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization (the Client) and the National Metrology Institute (the Beneficiary) are seeking the services of an EURAMET member metrology institute (hereinafter Consultant), who has relevant expertise in the field of the assignment to provide the know-how transfer and training of the specialists of the Moldovan National Metrology Institute (hereinafter NMI).

 

C.           Objectives of the Assignment

The main objectives of the assignment are to enhance the technical competence and knowledge in the field of mass metrology of Moldovan NMI specialists through comprehensive training and structured know-how transfer, focusing on both theoretical knowledge and practical skills in the following domains: (i) Mass measurements; (ii) Length measurements; (iii) Pressure measurements and (iv) Force measurements.

D.           Task to be performed (Scope of Work)

To achieve the assignment’s objectives, the Consultant shall develop the training materials and deliver trainings for NMI specialists at the NMI premises and ensure practical on-site trainings for specialists of NMI at Consultant’ premises according to the topics, duration and timeline suggested below.

TASK I - Mass Measurements

For the topics related to mass measurements, the Consultant will have to:

  • Develop and submit to the Client training materials.
  • Design and deliver training courses (at NMI premises) and practical trainings (at Consultant’ premises) in separate courses on mass measurements as follows:
  1. Advanced Training for Calibrating Standard Weights

Further below a detailed technical composition of the expected training topics is presented.

Application of advanced calibration methods under controlled conditions including:

  • Preparation of weights for calibration;
  • Gravimetric vs. comparative calibration;
  • Choice of equipment and correct handling;
  • Determination of conventional and real mass;
  • Control of external influences (humidity, temperature, pressure).

Correct development of uncertainty budgets according to GUM including:

  • Types of uncertainty: type A and type B;
  • Applied examples of uncertainty budgets;
  • Extended calculation and expression of results;
  • Estimation of individual contributions: equipment, operator, environment.

Ensuring the quality of the calibration process and traceability of results including:

  • Metrological traceability: the traceability chain and national standards;
  • Writing calibration reports;
  • Document archiving, retention and review requirements;
  • Preparation for ISO/IEC 17025 audit.

Applying knowledge in real situations and developing analytical skills including:

  • Complete calibration of a set of weights (practical);
  • Identification and correction of possible errors;
  • Case study: internal audit simulation with technical file analysis.
  • Support of interlaboratory comparison

  1. Advanced Training for Calibrating Non-Automatic Weighing Instruments

A detailed technical composition of the expected training topics is presented further below.

Application of advanced calibration methods under controlled conditions including:

Complete understanding of the calibration method described in the EURAMET guide cg-18:

  • General test conditions: stability, environment, location;
  • Waiting time, hysteresis effects, loading-unloading;
  • Preliminary checks of the instrument;
  • Determination of indication errors at different loads;
  • Repeatability and eccentricity.

Complete application of a calibration procedure on a real NAWI:

  • Preparation of the device and selection of standard weights;
  • Multi-point calibration: increasing, decreasing loads;
  • Correction of weighing errors;
  • Evaluation of the effect of the weight position on the platform (eccentricity).

Development of the uncertainty budget associated with the calibration of a NAWI:

  • Sources of uncertainty in the calibration of scales: weights, instrument, environmental influences;
  • Structure and completion of an uncertainty budget;
  • Calculation of combined and extended uncertainty;
  • Examples of calculations in Excel.

Ensuring traceability and compliance of technical documentation:

  • Structure and content of a calibration report;
  • Metrological traceability requirements;
  • Reference equipment tracking and related records;
  • Examples of complete calibration reports.

 

Training of personnel for audits and maintaining accreditation:

  • Critical aspects assessed by auditors;
  • Process control and method validation;
  • Non-conformity management and corrective actions.

The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN), through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation (FMWRS), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds to finance the engagement of a Consulting Firm for the Construction Supervision of the Design & Build Irrigation Schemes (Modernization and Expansion) across selected irrigation schemes nationwide.

The SPIN Project is designed to strengthen dam safety and improve the management of water resources for hydropower and irrigation in selected areas of Nigeria. Under Subcomponents 2.2 and 2.3 of the Project, the FGN seeks to rehabilitate and modernize irrigation and drainage infrastructure while improving irrigation management systems to enhance water delivery efficiency, expand command areas, and strengthen climate resilience.

Purpose of the Assignment

The modernization and expansion of the irrigation schemes will be executed under a Design Build (DB) contractual arrangement governed by the FIDIC Yellow Book (2017 Edition). Due to the complexity of the DB modality, the Employer requires an independent and highly qualified Supervision Consultant (“the Consultant”) to act as the Employer’s Representative throughout the project life cycle.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for Adani and Ndieze Irrigation Scheme located in Enugu & Ebonyi States, can be accessed at the following link: https://1drv.ms/w/c/bea66a6a0847ee73/IQBvbJdu_lTLQaK7gY9BbIhQAWl_4w8Ua5FAa1Ayy2NP3PA?e=ANEyvK

The Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, through the Federal Project Management Unit (FPMU) of the SPIN Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested firms must provide sufficient information demonstrating that they meet the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

  • The firm shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of demonstrated in experience providing construction supervision services for large scale infrastructure projects, Experience with Design Build (DB) or FIDIC Yellow Book based contracts is an added advantage.

  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in supervising rehabilitation, or expansion of gravity fed and pressurized irrigation systems, including canal networks (open/closed channels), water control structures, drainage systems, and on farm distribution infrastructure.
  • The firm shall demonstrate its technical and managerial capabilities, including the capacity to mobilize a multidisciplinary team of qualified engineers and specialists for the supervision of large irrigation infrastructure projects.

Evidence of similar assignments previously undertaken (Contract Award Letters, Job Completion Letters, and other evidence that may be required to verify such experience).

The Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP) is seeking to recruit qualified Data Analysis and Reporting Officer under the Social Recovery & Job Creation Project (SRJC), financed by the World Bank for the benefit of The Ministry of Local Government.

The selected Data Analysis and Reporting Officer will be assigned to work at the Ministry of Local Government — to support the Ministry of Local Government in strengthening institutional reporting, improving data analysis, and enhancing the quality and consistency of information used for planning, monitoring, and decision-making.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Data Analysis and Reporting Officer will support the collection, validation, analysis, and reporting of institutional data and information. The Officer will coordinate with relevant departments to improve reporting processes, prepare analytical reports, and support evidence-based planning and institutional performance.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collect, organize, validate, and analyze reports and data received from relevant departments.
  • Prepare periodic reports, statistical summaries, analytical reports, briefing notes, and presentations.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments to ensure the timely submission and accuracy of reports and data.
  • Consolidate institutional reports and ensure the consistency and completeness of information.
  • Maintain and update reporting records, databases, and related documentation.
  • Develop dashboards, charts, and reporting tools to support management decision-making.
  • Review data quality and identify inconsistencies or gaps requiring follow-up.
  • Support the preparation of reports required by senior management, development partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Recommend improvements to reporting systems and data analysis practices.
  • Maintain organized electronic and hard-copy records related to reporting and data analysis.
  • Perform any other related duties as may be assigned by the Director General of the Projects Department.

Job Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in Business Administration, Statistics, Information Systems, Management Information Systems, Economics, Public Administration, or any other related field.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in reporting, data analysis, institutional reporting, or administrative coordination.
  • Demonstrated experience in preparing reports, analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, and presenting findings.
  • Experience working with government institutions or internationally financed projects is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Experience in Power BI, Excel dashboards, or other data visualization tools is considered an advantage.
  • Excellent communication and report-writing skills in both Arabic and English.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work effectively under pressure.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

O Estado de Alagoas recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear parcialmente o Programa Progestão Alagoas, e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos para serviços de consultoria.

Os recursos têm por objetivo a execução do Programa Progestão, o qual visa promover a melhoria contínua da gestão fiscal, orçamentária e patrimonial da administração pública estadual por meio de ações que findem na redução e na racionalização do gasto público com resultados perenes, de modo a contribuir para a sustentabilidade fiscal de Alagoas.

Nesse sentido, o Alagoas Previdência se propõe a utilizar parte dos recursos do programa para a seleção de Consultor Individual para desenvolvimento de solução tecnológica para apoio a administração e gestão do Assessoria Especial de Investimentos deste Alagoas Previdência, objetivando a consolidação da carteira de investimento do Alagoas Previdência, e a extração de relatórios periódicos.

Com o objetivo de contratar esse serviço, o Alagoas Previdência convida profissionais a manifestarem seu interesse na prestação dos serviços como consultor individual.

Os profissionais interessados deverão proporcionar informações que indiquem que estão qualificados para prestar os serviços, mediante a apresentação de currículo, devendo constar nome completo, CPF, endereço completo, telefone, e-mail, histórico acadêmico, experiências comprovadas nas competências abaixo.

Obs.: A presente Manifestação de Interesse deverá conter todos os documentos comprobatórios anexados juntos ao documento de Manifestação de Interesse (Currículos, Certificados, Atestados, Diplomas...), em um único arquivo com tamanho máximo de 7mb.

É necessário que o perfil do(a) profissional atendas às seguintes exigências, que são indispensáveis à presente contratação:

Formação superior em Ciência da Computação, Engenharia, Sistemas de Informação, Estatística, Economia, Matemática ou áreas correlatas;

Experiência comprovada (mínimo de 3 anos) em modelagem e desenvolvimento de dashboards com ferramentas como Power BI, Tableau, Qlik ou equivalentes;

Domínio de análise estatística e visualização de dados financeiros;

Comprovar conhecimento em modelagem de risco financeiro e compliance como desejável para o Consultor.

Para este perfil, também é desejável:

Experiência prática ou conhecimento comprovado em estruturação de carteiras de investimento de RPPS ou entidades similares;

Capacidade de interpretar extratos, rentabilidades e estruturas de ativos para auxiliar na modelagem lógica da solução.

O profissional será selecionado de acordo com os procedimentos indicados no Regulamento de aquisições para mutuários de operações de financiamento de projetos de investimento do Banco Mundial, quarta edição de novembro de 2020.

É parte integrante desta Manifestação de Interesse o e Termo de Referência (TdR) no qual consta a descrição detalhada das atividades a serem desempenhadas e dos produtos a serem elaborados, e que está disponível no website: www.sefaz.al.gov.br/licitacao

Os profissionais interessados deverão encaminhar as manifestações até o dia 02 de setembro de 2026, às 12 horas, devidamente identificadas como TR AL1.1 BR-ALPREV/AL-539014-CS-INDV, no seguinte endereço eletrônico celp@sefaz.al.gov.br.

  • Fluência na língua portuguesa e competência na comunicação oral.

A atenção dos consultores interessados deve recair sobre a Seção III, parágrafos, 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do “Regulamento de Aquisições dos Mutuários do IPF” do Banco Mundial de Setembro de 2025 (“Regulamentos de Aquisições”), estabelecendo a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

Perusahaan konsultan harus menyediakan tenaga ahli professional yang ditugaskan selama 15 bulan kalender. Kerangka Acuan Kerja (KAK) Project Supervision Consultant for Semarang River and Baru River terlampir pada REOI ini /  atau dapat diunduh pada tautan berikut: https://bit.ly/ProjectSupervisionSemarangBaru

 

Balai Besar Wilayah Sungai Pemali Juana mengundang perusahaan konsultan yang memenuhi syarat untuk memasukkan pernyataan berminat untuk memberikan layanan jasa konsultan. Perusahaan konsultan yang berminat harus memberikan informasi yang mendukung bahwa perusahaan konsultan yang bersangkutan memenuhi syarat untuk menjalankan layanan jasa tersebut diatas  (misalnya: brosur/riwayat organisasi dan pengalaman dalam menjalankan layanan jasa konsultan dengan sifat dan kondisi yang sama, dan informasi lainnya yang relevan). Kriteria untuk shortlist adalah:  

  1. Pengalaman Perusahaan

Perusahaan berpengalaman dalam jasa konsultan minimal 10 tahun dengan bisnis utamanya jasa konsultansi : Bantuan Teknis, Studi Kelayakan, Desain dan Perencanaan serta Pengawasan Teknis di dalamnya bidang Sumber Daya Air.

  1. Pengalaman serupa yang diperlukan :
  1. Perusahaan Konsultan memiliki pengalaman dalam pengawasan/supervisi pengendalian banjir di Sungai, pengawasan/supervisi perkuatan tebing Sungai, pengawasan/supervisi Pembangunan tanggul Sungai dan pengawasan/supervisi pengendalian banjir perkotaan dalam kurun waktu 10 tahun
  2. Perusahaan Konsultan diutamakan memiliki pengalaman dalam pengawasan/supervisi pembangunan kolam retensi dan/atau pengawasan/supervisi pembangunan pompa banjir dengan kapasitas ≥ 1500 l/detik dalam kurun waktu 10 tahun terakhir
  3. Perusahan Konsultan diutamakan sudah pernah menyelesaikan kontrak proyek pengelolaan dana bantuan/pinjaman luar negeri (> Rp 2.500.000.000,00) dalam kurun waktu 10 tahun terakhir

 

Setiap pengalaman perusahaan yang dicantumkan harus disertai dengan referensi dari Pengguna Jasa yang bersangkutan berupa Kontrak, Berita Acara Serah Terima, Surat Perjanjian KSO (apabila ber-KSO) serta data dukung lainnya.

 

  1. Kemampuan teknis dan Manajerial perusahaan

Perusahaan Konsultan memiliki tenaga ahli tetap (dibuktikan dengan payroll regular perusahaan atau bukti lainnya) yang relevan dengan penugasan ini. Kualifikasi dan Pengalaman Tenaga Ahli Utama (Key experts) tidak disertakan dalam kriteria pemilihan daftar pendek. Tenaga Ahli Utama (Key experts) tidak akan dievaluasi pada tahap pemilihan daftar pendek (shortlisting). Hanya pengalaman perusahaan anggota KSO yang akan dievaluasi, pengalaman sub-consultant tidak akan dievaluasi

Perusahaan konsultan yang berminat harap memperhatikan prosedur dalam paragraf 3.14, 3.16, dan 3.17 Peraturan Bank Dunia: Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, November 2020 (selanjutnya disebut: Procurement Regulations) tentang kebijakan Bank dunia mengenai konflik kepentingan. Selain itu, silakan merujuk ke informasi spesifik berikut tentang konflik kepentingan terkait dengan penugasan ini sesuai paragraph 3.17 Procurement Regulations.

 

Perusahaan konsultan diperkenankan untuk berasosiasi dengan perusahaan konsultan lain dalam bentuk KSO (Kerjasama operasi) atau sub-konsultan guna meningkatkan kualifikasinya tetapi harus menunjukkan dengan jelas apakah asosiasi tersebut berbentuk KSO dan/atau sub-konsultan. Dalam hal KSO, semua mitra dalam KSO harus secara bersama-sama bertanggung jawab atas seluruh kontrak, jika dipilih. Jumlah Perusahaan yang melakukan KSO tidak lebih banyak dari 3 (tiga) Perusahaan.

Reference no.: SX-NRPB-560450-CS-INDV

 

The Government of Sint Maarten has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Emergency Debris Management Project (EDMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The overall objective of the assignment is to engage a Senior Consultant to provide specialized technical and strategic expertise to support the implementation of activities aimed at strengthening the waste management sector. The Consultant will contribute to policy enhancement, capacity building and asset management within the Ministry of Public Housing, Spatial Planning, Environment and Infrastructure (VROMI) and other relevant government entities.

 

The assignment will support ongoing operations and the establishment of a stronger institutional and policy framework for sustainable waste management and improved sector performance.

The Supervision Consultant will deliver the following:

  • Inception Report and Work Plan
  • Develop a National Disaster Waste Policy (Activity E.1)
  • Development of Terms of Reference for dedicated policy capacity (Activity A.3)
  • Public guidance protocols for hurricane-related waste management and disaster readiness (Activity E.2)
  • Final assignment report

 

The Consultant shall ensure that all activities are implemented in accordance with the quality standards, time and budget elaborated in the contract document.

 

The National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB) now invites eligible consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The selection criteria are:

  • Advanced degree in Environmental Engineering, Waste Management, Environmental Policy, Public Administration, Civil Engineering, or related discipline.
  • At least 10 years of professional experience in disaster waste management, environmental governance, institutional strengthening, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience in coordination across multiple actors.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting standalone activities in a wide context, capacity-building initiatives, and policy advisory assignments.
  • Experience in supporting government agencies in the development of policies and operational improvement programs.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, facilitation, analytical, and report-writing skills.

 

Applicants are free to choose a format for their Expression of Interest. At this stage, Consultants are expected to provide:

  1. CVs including relevant information about qualifications and expertise, strategic competencies or achievements;
  2. Relevant references from previous similar projects/clients.

 

NRPB reserves the right to invite any or all interested candidates to an interview.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020 edition (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants as set forth in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Expressions of interest must be submitted via the NRPB’s procurement portal which can be done via: National Recovery Program Bureau of St. Maarten - Senior Waste Management Policy and Institutional Development Consultant by Monday, September 7th, 2026 at 5:00 PM (AST).

 

All queries from interested bidders must be submitted electronically to https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com through the Vendor Discussions section under the respective project. Interested bidders should register in the NRPB's procurement portal at https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com/login/. Detailed instructions for registration are available at https://nrpbsxm.org/procurement.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICES FOR NEEDS ASSESSMENT, TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS, AND SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTEGRATED BORDER INTELLIGENCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT SOLUTION

Reference No. 98CS1/MINPLAN/26

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Needs Assessment, Technical Specifications, and Support for the Development of an Integrated Border Intelligence and Risk Management Solution.

Consulting Services (“the Services”) aim to provide technical support to the Coordinated Border Management Committee (CGCF) in all phases prior to and during the development of an Integrated Border Intelligence and Risk Management Solution. The role of the consulting firm includes:

  1. Identifying the functional and operational needs at the borders, mapping and reviewing existing processes, and inventorying technological systems in use;
  2. Developing the functional and technical architecture of the solution, defining interoperability requirements, creating a data dictionary and data model, and estimating the development and implementation costs;
  3. Assisting in the preparation of the bidding documents for the selection of the technology development company and issuing a substantiated technical opinion on the recommended proposal;
  4. Technically supervising the development of the solution by the contracted company, verifying compliance with the approved technical specifications, validating deliverables and progress reports, and supporting the testing and implementation at border points;
  5. Evaluating the national legal and regulatory framework relevant to the implementation of the solution, identifying gaps, and providing advice and support to the CGCF to address them;
  6. Preparing detailed technical specifications for the core module of the solution, covering general principles, the complete risk management cycle, the risk management engine, the alert system, intelligence governance and human review, auditing, monitoring and performance, and the incorporation of artificial intelligence.

The expected duration of the consultancy contract will be twenty-four (24) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • A minimum of 7 years of proven experience in process reengineering and/or IT systems specification projects;
  • Demonstrable experience in projects related to border management, customs, immigration, or public safety;
  • Preference given to companies with MININT pre-approval to handle confidential government data;
  • PMP (Project Management Professional) certification, which validates project management skills;
  • ITIL Service Strategy Certification, which demonstrates skills in IT service strategy;
  • TOGAF® Certification Program, which demonstrates expertise in the development and implementation of enterprise architecture, essential for ensuring data integration and efficiency in the integration of complex systems;
  • Must be formally registered with the APD, ensuring compliance with current regulations regarding data protection and privacy;
  • Preference will be given to companies that hold the “Made in Angola” seal in the areas of telecommunications and/or information systems, in accordance with Presidential Decree No. 213/23, which establishes the Legal Framework for Incentives to Domestic Production;
  • Must be duly registered with the National Institute for the Promotion of the Information Society (INFOSI), ensuring that it operates in accordance with national guidelines for technological development;
  • Submit a certificate of tax compliance, proving its good standing with the tax authorities and ensuring its suitability to perform the contract.
  • Demonstrate institutional, technical, and reputational suitability consistent with national security projects and the management of sensitive information;
  • Ensure that its key employees involved in the project undergo background checks, in accordance with applicable law;
  • Comply with any additional guidelines, restrictions, or requirements established by MININT regarding the protection of national security

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” revised in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

1. This request for expressions of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for the Dar es Salaam Metropolitan Development Project - Phase 2 (DMDP 2) that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (UNDB) online Notice No. OP00277705 of March 6, 2024.

2. The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Dar es Salaam Metropolitan Development Project – Phase 2 (DMDP 2), implemented by the Prime Minister’s Office – Regional Administration and Local Government (PMO-RALG) in collaboration with the Dar es Salaam Local Authorities (DLAs). Part of the proceeds of this financing will be applied to eligible payments under the contract for the Provision of Consultancy Services for Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments and Resettlement Action Plans for Area-Based Investments in Dar es Salaam City, Kinondoni, Ubungo, Temeke and Kigamboni Municipalities, and Priority Drainage Interventions in Dar es Salaam under DMDP 2.

3. The overall objective of the assignment is to support PMO-RALG and the Dar es Salaam Local Authorities to prepare comprehensive Environmental and Social Impact Assessments, Environmental and Social Management Plans, and Resettlement Action Plans for all three (3) Sub-Assignments concurrently, ensuring that environmental, social, land acquisition, livelihood, and resettlement issues are identified, assessed, and managed in full compliance with Tanzanian requirements and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, with findings delivered in time to inform the respective parallel design processes.

Sub-Assignment A covers the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments, Environmental and Social Management Plans, and Resettlement Action Plans for selected area-based investments in Kinondoni Municipality and Ubungo Municipality under DMDP 2. Sub-Assignment B covers the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments, Environmental and Social Management Plans, and Resettlement Action Plans for selected area-based investments in Dar es Salaam City, Temeke Municipality, and Kigamboni Municipality under DMDP 2. Sub-Assignment C covers the Preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Environmental and Social Management Plan, and Resettlement Action Plan for priority drainage interventions under of DMDP 2 across all five Dar es Salaam Local Authorities.

4. The specific objectives of this assignment are to: (i) Establish environmental and social baseline conditions for each selected subproject site or drainage corridor and its wider area of influence; (ii) Assess direct, indirect, induced, cumulative, and residual environmental and social risks and impacts throughout the full project cycle; (iii) Undertake land acquisition and resettlement screening and prepare site-specific RAPs, abbreviated RAPs, or due diligence notes as required; (iv) Conduct census, socio-economic survey, asset inventory, affected-person verification, and valuation support; (v) Prepare practical, costed, and implementable ESMPs and RAPs integrating findings into design, procurement, and supervision arrangements; and (vi) Ensure compliance with applicable Tanzanian requirements and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

5. The scope of services for each of the sub-assignment will include, but not be limited to undertaking: Inception Activities, Document Review, and Work Planning; Policy, Legal, Regulatory, and Institutional Review; Site Screening and Scoping; Environmental and Social Baseline Studies; Resettlement Screening, Census, Socio-Economic Survey, and Asset Inventory; Stakeholder Engagement and Disclosure; Analysis of Alternatives; Environmental and Social Impact Assessment; Preparation of the Environmental and Social Management Plan;  Preparation of Resettlement Action Plans; Coordination with the Design Consultant; and Preparation of Final Reports and Regulatory Submission Packages. The consultant shall ensure that all deliverables/outputs are technically sound, internally consistent, and suitable for decision-making, public disclosure, and subsequent implementation.

6. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: https://www.tamisemi.go.tz. Requests for clarification should be sent through the following e-mail addresses: cities.project@yahoo.com or cities.project@tamisemi.go.tz, and the Client will send responses to clarifications through the same e-mail addresses.

7. The Permanent Secretary, PMO-RALG, now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the above services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The short-listing criteria are: (a) Type of core business and at least 10 years in relevant business; (b) Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the following: (i) Experience in similar assignments - information to be provided should include the name of the assignments, the names and full contact addresses of the clients, the contract value (in equivalent US dollars), the period (month/year) of execution of the assignments, and the role played in the assignments (Lead or JV Partner); (ii) Demonstration of experience working in similar conditions; and (c) The firm's technical and managerial capability (provide only the organizational structure, and the general qualifications, field of expertise and number of key personnel). The experience, technical & managerial capability of the sub-consultant shall not be evaluated to enhance the qualification of the Lead Firm or JV. Consultants shall not use the Affiliate Member's Managerial, Technical or Experience Capabilities to enhance their qualifications.

Note that: The Request for Expression of Interest (REOI) for this Consultancy Services for Preparation of a Combined Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for Area Based Investments in DLAs and Priority Drainage Interventions in Dar es Salaam under DMDP 2 is being advertised at the same time together with another similar Tender for Consultancy Services to Undertake an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, and Resettlement Action Plan for Flood and Erosion Control Interventions in the Middle and Upper Basin of the Msimbazi River in Dar es Salaam; and the assignments in these two Tenders will be executed simultaneously. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

 

Country:  MOZAMBIQUE

Project:  Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project

Agreement: Preparation Advance No. -V522-MZ.

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling.
