UNITE DE GESTION DU PROGRAMME DE DEVELOPPEMENT DU SYSTEME DE SANTE « UG-PDSS »

Projet de Préparation, de Réponse et de la Résilience aux urgences sanitaires de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) en utilisant l’approche programmatique en plusieurs phases

« HEPRR-MPA »

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET N° ZR-DRC-MSP-523564-CS-CQS

Recrutement d’un Bureau d’Études pour la mise en œuvre du WASH-FIT et la préparation des études techniques (APS, APD, DAO) des infrastructures WASH dans les formations sanitaires dans les provinces du Kasaï central et du Kasaï oriental.

 

SERVICE DE CONSULTANTS

Source de financement : Banque Mondiale ID Projet : 504532, Crédit IDA N°75360- ZR

Cette sollicitation des manifestations d’intérêt fait suite à l’avis général de passation des marchés de ce projet publié dans le Développent Business en date du 11 mars 2025

  1. Le Gouvernement de la RDC a obtenu auprès de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), un financement de l'ordre de 250 Millions $US de Crédit, pour la mise en œuvre du Programme HEPRR-MPA, et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ses ressources pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat des services d'un Bureau d’Études pour la mise en œuvre du WASH-FIT et la préparation des études techniques (APS, APD, DAO) des infrastructures WASH dans les formations sanitaires dans les provinces du Kasaï central et du Kasaï oriental.

L’objectif global de la mission est :

  • D’appuyer la mise en œuvre de l’outil WASH-FIT dans les infrastructures sanitaires sélectionnées et élaborer les études techniques d’avant-projet sommaire (APS), l’avant-projet détaillé (APD) et le dossier d’appel d’offre (DAO) nécessaires à la réhabilitation ou la construction d’infrastructures WASH conformes aux normes nationales et internationales ;
  • De réaliser les instruments environnementaux et sociaux conformes aux exigences de la Banque mondiale ;
  • D’assurer le contrôle-qualité et supervision des travaux, ainsi que de leur conformité aux plans, normes techniques et spécifications du DAO.

Objectifs spécifiques :

  • Compléter le diagnostic WASH-FIT dans les formations sanitaires ciblées situées dans les provinces de Kasaï-Central et de Kasaï oriental ;
  • Evaluer la conformité des infrastructures existantes aux standards OMS et nationaux ;
  • Proposer les solutions techniques réalistes et durables pour l’amélioration des installations ;
  • Elaborer les études techniques : APS, APD et DAO pour chaque site prioritaire ;
  • Appuyer l’UG-PDSS, la DHSP et les DPS dans la préparation du processus de sélection des entreprises de travaux ;
  • Assurer le contrôle et la supervision des travaux de réhabilitation ;
  • Assurer l’évaluation des travaux réalisés afin de s’assurer de leur conformité avec les plans, normes techniques et les spécifications prévues dans l’APD
  • Former le personnel local sur l’utilisation et la maintenance des nouvelles infrastructures ; 
  • Planification des mesures de control de risques et impacts sociaux, environnementaux, santé et sécurité au travail (SST).

2. Les principales tâches du Consultant sont décrites en sept (7) phases à savoir :

A. Phase 1 : Préparation et cadrage

  • Réunion de lancement et validation de la méthodologie avec l’UG-PDS et la Direction d’Hygiène et Salubrité Publique (DHSP) ;
  • Revue documentaire (plans existants, rapports techniques, normes WASH[1][2][3], guides OMS) ;
  • Elaboration du plan de travail détaillé et des outils de collecte des données validé par l’UG-PDSS ;
  • Validation de la check-list et des outils de collecte des données par la DHSP.

B. Phase 2 : Diagnostic initial et évaluation WASH-FIT

  • Actualiser l’état de lieux dans les structures sanitaires : infrastructures, sources d’eau, dispositifs d’hygiènes, assainissement, déchets médicaux, hygiène du personnel, gestion et maintenance ;
  • Appliquer la grille d’évaluation WASH-FIT pour chaque formation sanitaire ;
  • Identifier les goulots d’étranglement techniques, organisationnels et comportementaux ;
  • Classer les structures selon leur niveau de risque et de conformité WASH ;
  • Documenter les écarts entre la situation actuelle et les standards OMS/nationaux ;
  • Produire un rapport d’évaluation synthétique et cartographique.

Evaluations techniques et études préliminaires

  • Effectuer les relevés topographiques et études de terrain ;
  • Analyser la qualité et la fonctionnalité des ouvrages d’eau, d’assainissement, d’énergie et d’hygiène.
  • Identifier les besoins de réhabilitation, d’extension ou de construction.

C. Phase 3 : Etudes techniques – APS & APD

  • Réaliser les études d’Avant-Projet Sommaire (APS) :
  • Définition des besoins prioritaires en infrastructures et équipements ;
  • Proposition de solutions techniques adaptées au contexte et résilientes aux effets pervers du changement climatique (hydraulique, assainissement, gestion des déchets, énergie, etc.) ;
  • Estimation sommaire des coûts et du phasage des interventions.
  • Sur base de l’APS validé, élaborer l’Avant-Projet Détaillés (APD) :
  • Etudes topographiques et géotechniques (si nécessaire) ;
  • Dimensionnement des ouvrages et équipements ;
  • Plans d’exécution, coupes et détails techniques ;
  • Estimation détaillée des coûts ;
  • Spécifications techniques normalisées.

D. Phase 4 : Élaboration des Dossiers d’Appel d’Offres (DAO)

  • Préparer pour chaque site un DAO complet conforme aux procédures du projet et aux directives de la Banque mondiale, incluant :
  • Cahier des Clauses Techniques Particulières (CCTP) ;
  • Bordereaux de prix unitaires (BPU) ;
  • Détail quantitatif estimatif (DQE) ;
  • Plans et devis ;
  • Critères techniques de conformité.
  • Appuyer l’UG-PDSS dans la validation des dossiers techniques et dans la phase d’analyse technique des offres si requis ;
  • Développer des solutions adaptées au contexte local (matériaux, énergie, maintenance) ;
  • Intégrer les aspects de résilience climatique, efficacité énergétique et sécurité sanitaire ;
  • Proposer un plan de maintenance et de suivi durable pour les ouvrages WASH.

E.  Phase 5 : Renforcement des capacités et transfert de compétences

  • Former le personnel des DPS et des structures sanitaires sur :
  • La mise en œuvre et le suivi du WASH-FIT ;
  • La maintenance et la gestion durable des infrastructures ;
  • La prévention et de contrôle des infections avec l’appui de la DHSP ;
  • Appuyer les équipes locales (DPS, BCZ, formations sanitaires) dans le suivi post-évaluation ;
  • Fournir les manuels et outils de suivi (checklists, guides d’entretien, fiches d’indicateurs).
  • Fournir un appui à la DHSP dans l’actualisation de ses modules de formation en y intégrant les aspects d’équité, genre et changement climatique.

F. phase 6 : Contrôle, supervision et évaluation des travaux

  • Assurer le contrôle technique et la supervision permanente des travaux afin de garantir leur exécution conforme aux plans d’exécution, au calendrier contractuel et aux règles de l’art la en matière et aux exigences contractuelles ;
  • Veiller à la qualité des matériaux utilisés, au respect des méthodes d’exécution ainsi qu’à la conformité des travaux avec les prescriptions techniques ;
  • Procédera à l’évaluation continue des travaux réalisés en vue de s’assurer de leur conformité avec les plans validés, les normes techniques en vigueur et les spécifications définies dans l’Avant-Projet Détaillé (APD)
  • Identifier toute non-conformité, proposer des mesures correctives appropriées et suivre leur mise en œuvre jusqu’à leur résolution complète.

G.  Phase 7 : Rapportage et restitution

  • Produire :
  • Les rapports d’évaluation WASH-FIT pour chaque structure ;
  • Les rapports techniques APS et APD ;
  • Les DAO complets validés ;
  • Un rapport final consolidé comprenant : analyse globale, priorités d’investissement, recommandations et cartographie.
  • Organiser un atelier de restitution avec les parties prenantes ;
  • Assurer la coordination avec les partenaires impliqués, notamment le projet PASEA, pour éviter les duplications.

Dans le cadre de l’appui au processus de sélection des entreprises de travaux, le Consultant sera chargé de réaliser une évaluation technique approfondie des chantiers récents et achevés par les prestataires potentiels, en vue d’apprécier leur capacité technique, organisationnelle et opérationnelle à exécuter les travaux de réhabilitation

Les Termes de référence de la mission sont téléchargeables sur le site www.mediacongo.net.

3. L’Unité de Gestion du Programme de Développement du Système de Santé (UG-PDSS) à travers le Projet de Préparation, de Réponse et de la Résilience aux urgences sanitaires de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) en utilisant l’approche programmatique en plusieurs phases « HEPRR-MPA », invite les candidats admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants (bureaux d’études) intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l'exécution des Services notamment :

•          brochures, prospectus de présentation du consultant ;

•          qualifications pour exécuter les services ;

•          référence des clients ;

•          références techniques dans les missions similaires exécutées (années de réalisation, coûts, clients et adresse/téléphone), et les attestations de bonne exécution ou les rapports de validation, etc.

NB : Les soumissionnaires joindront obligatoirement de manière chronologique et lisible, les copies des pages de garde (mentionnant l’objet, le commanditaire, le délai d’exécution) et de signature des marchés, des attestations de bonne fin pour justifier les expériences ou sous peine de nullité de la référence. Lorsque la production de la copie du contrat est empêchée par une clause de confidentialité liant le candidat à son client, celui-ci pourra produire, à titre de preuve équivalente, une attestation du client précisant l’objet, le montant, la source de financement, la période d’exécution et le rôle exact du consultant.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à l’étape de la préparation de la liste restreinte.

4. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI), daté du 1er Juillet 2016 révisé Novembre 2017, août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février 2025 et septembre 2025 », qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

5. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés. Les candidats ne doivent pas inclure dans leurs manifestations d’intérêt, les curriculums vitae du personnel clé ainsi que la proposition technique de la mission. Le groupement désignera son chef de file et joindra à sa manifestation d’intérêt l’accord de groupement ou, à défaut, une lettre d’intention de groupement signée par l’ensemble des membres, précisant la répartition des rôles. Les qualifications et références de l’ensemble des membres du groupement sont cumulées pour l’appréciation des critères de présélection ci-après.

NB : les missions similaires s’apprécient au regard d’une complexité similaire, entendue comme : ampleur des contrats, nature de la prestation, domaine technique et contexte géographique.

6. Les bureaux intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises pour l'exécution des services ci-dessus indiqués. Les dossiers de manifestation d'intérêt comporteront notamment :

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant URFT TF0D0612

 

Assignment Title: ECPE Model Diversification Expert

Reference No. LEARN-IC-ECEDO-05

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). 

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to support hromadas during the first phase of the implementation of the “First Steps Forward” program in selecting and developing diversified service delivery models in the field of preschool education (ECE) that best respond to local needs. The Expert will ensure that the diversified service delivery models are feasible for implementation, comply with national legislation, are child-centered, and are suitable for further scaling at the national level. The Expert will provide support to hromadas in identifying appropriate options for diversification of preschool education services, as well as ensure technical guidance on service delivery models and develop recommendations for their practical application.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are available at the link https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OUwDhh3ej4tt-E1Rl9inN165bglo06wR/view?usp=drive_link

The deadline for submission of applications is 11:00 am Kyiv time September 11, 2026.

REPUBLIC OF ZAMBIA

MINISTRY OF GREEN ECONOMY AND ENVIRONMENT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Project: Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II Project

Grant/Project ID No.: P507971

Assignment Title: Feasibility Study for Establishment of the ZMD National Meteorological Calibration Facility and Automated Weather Station Workshop

Reference No.: ZM-MGEE-570804-CS-CQS

 

The Government of the Republic of Zambia, through the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE), has received financing from the World Bank, the Climate Investment Funds (CIF), the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), the Nordic Development Fund and Scaling Climate Action by Lowering Emissions (SCALE), totalling USD 137 million, to support implementation of the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II Project in Copperbelt, Luapula, Muchinga, Northern and Southern Provinces. The Government intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments under the contract for the consulting services described below.

The objective is to conduct a comprehensive, evidence-based feasibility study that produces the technical specifications, business model, operational framework, infrastructure designs and regulatory analysis required to establish and operationalise an accredited ZMD National Meteorological Calibration Facility and integrated Automated Weather Station workshop, and to provide investment-grade recommendations.

Scope of the Services

  • Map institutional mandates and the legal framework, including the operating relationship between ZMD and the Zambia Metrology Agency.
  • Define the meteorological-instrument calibration scope, equipment profile, reference standards and SI traceability arrangements.
  • Define and design the Automated Weather Station workshop and maintenance capability.
  • Prepare conceptual architectural, MEP, HVAC, environmental-control, security and other infrastructure requirements.
  • Develop financial, business and operational models, including lifecycle costs, cost-benefit analysis and sustainability options.
  • Develop an ISO/IEC 17025:2017 quality-management and accreditation roadmap aligned with SADCAS requirements.
  • Assess the pathway and feasibility for WMO Regional Instrument Centre designation.
  • Undertake stakeholder engagement and prepare the capacity-building framework.

 

The indicative period of performance is 16 weeks. The detailed scope, deliverables and requirements are provided in the Terms of Reference.

Shortlisting Criteria

The Ministry now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. At least ten (10) years of corporate experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity.
  2. Demonstrated experience in meteorological-instrument calibration and in the design and accreditation of laboratories under ISO/IEC 17025.
  3. Demonstrated experience establishing controlled-environment workshops or laboratories, including technical equipment profiling and infrastructure requirements.
  4. Experience preparing feasibility studies, investment-grade cost models, business/operational frameworks and procurement-ready technical specifications.
  5. A proven record on World Bank-financed or comparable international development assignments.
  6. Availability of appropriate multidisciplinary expertise. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The EOI should include the firm’s legal name and contact details; brief corporate profile; description of relevant assignments with client, country, dates, contract value/role and contactable references; and, where applicable, the intended form and members of any association. Firms should not submit a technical or financial proposal at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualifications Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

REPUBLIC OF ZAMBIA

MINISTRY OF GREEN ECONOMY AND ENVIRONMENT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Project: Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II Project

Grant/Project ID No.: P507971

Assignment Title: Feasibility Study for Establishment of a National Weather Radar Network for Zambia

Reference No.: ZM-MGEE-562812-CS-QCBS

 

The Government of the Republic of Zambia, through the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE), has received financing from the World Bank, the Climate Investment Funds (CIF), the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), the Nordic Development Fund and Scaling Climate Action by Lowering Emissions (SCALE), totalling USD 137 million, to support implementation of the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II Project in Copperbelt, Luapula, Muchinga, Northern and Southern Provinces. The Government intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments under the contract for the consulting services described below.

The objective is to conduct a comprehensive, evidence-based feasibility study that provides the technical, financial, institutional, environmental and operational framework for establishment of a National Weather Radar Network for Zambia, including procurement-ready specifications for radar systems, supporting infrastructure, communications and data-processing systems.

Scope of the Services

  • Situational assessment, observing-network gap analysis, user needs and sector consultations.
  • Radar-network design and site selection using terrain and coverage modelling, including site surveys and specialised aviation requirements.
  • Development of vendor-neutral, procurement-ready radar, civil-infrastructure, power, communications, processing and acceptance-test specifications.
  • Financial and economic analysis covering CAPEX, OPEX, 20-year lifecycle costs, benefits and financial sustainability.
  • Institutional, staffing, competency, training and operations-and-maintenance capacity assessment.
  • Environmental and social assessment of proposed sites and mitigation measures.
  • Phased implementation strategy, procurement approach, financing options, risk register and monitoring and evaluation framework.

The indicative period of performance is 24 weeks. The detailed scope, deliverables and requirements are provided in the Terms of Reference.

Shortlisting Criteria

The Ministry now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. At least ten (10) years of corporate experience delivering assignments of similar nature and complexity.
  2. Demonstrated experience in feasibility assessment, design, specification, implementation support or supervision of weather-radar networks or comparable national-scale remote-sensing observing networks.
  3. Demonstrated capability in radar coverage modelling and siting; radar-system and civil-infrastructure specifications; telecommunications and data integration; lifecycle costing; and environmental and social assessment.
  4. A proven record on World Bank-financed or comparable international development assignments.
  5. Relevant experience in Sub-Saharan Africa or a comparable developing-country context.
  6. Availability of appropriate multidisciplinary expertise. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The EOI should include the firm’s legal name and contact details; brief corporate profile; description of relevant assignments with client, country, dates, contract value/role and contactable references; and, where applicable, the intended form and members of any association. Firms should not submit a technical or financial proposal at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Terms of Reference: https://www.mgee.gov.zm/?page_id=6753

Submission Address

The Permanent Secretary

Ministry of Green Economy and Environment

P.O. Box 30147

Lusaka, Zambia

Electronic submission: Submit the EOI with the assignment title and reference number in the email subject line to info@npcu.org.zm, copying emmanuel.makombe@tralard.org.zm and Sibeso.Mataa@mgee.gov.zm.

Deadline: Tuesday, 15 September 2026 at 17:00 hours, Zambian local time.

BALOCHISTAN WATER SECURITY AND PRODUCTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR THE SELECTION OF SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST / INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

            The Government of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, through the Government of Balochistan (GoB), with support of the World Bank (WB), is implementing the Balochistan Water Security and Productivity Improvement Project (BWSPIP). The project development objective is to improve flood protection, increase access to water for productive use, and improve water supply service delivery in selected areas of Balochistan. It intends to apply part of the funds to cover eligible payments to hire the services of motivated, experienced, and energetic individual to work with the Project Implementation Unit as SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST / Individual Consultant.                       

S.No

Position

Qualification/Experience

1.

SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST

  • Master’s degree (minimum 16 years of education) specifically in Sociology, Social Sciences, Rural Development, Community Development, Development Studies from a recognized university.
  • Minimum seven (07) years of post-qualification professional experience in social development, social safeguards management, stakeholder engagement, community development, or social risk management, preferably in urban water supply and sanitation, municipal services, utility strengthening and infrastructure development.
  • Demonstrated experience in the development sector, preferably in projects related to urban water supply and sanitation, institutional strengthening, public service delivery, or community development.
  • Proven experience in stakeholder engagement, training and awareness raising, and community consultation processes involving project-affected communities, water consumers, residents of low-income and underserved areas, community-based organizations, vulnerable groups and conflict-sensitive engagement approaches.
  • Demonstrated experience in design, management, and monitoring of grievance redressal mechanisms (GRM) and social risk mitigation measures. (Certifications required)
  • Experience working in similar geographical and socio-cultural conditions, particularly in urban, peri-urban, underserved, and vulnerable communities. Familiarity with the institutional arrangements, local governance systems, socio-economic conditions, and community dynamics of Quetta will be an added advantage.

 1. Background: In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through its Ministry of Finance (MoF) launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) project. The project development objective is to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance.

The SPRING project is organized around four components (three mutually reinforcing and one supporting): (i) Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs; and (iv) Component 4: Project Management. A wide range of activities will be implemented as part of this project to reach its development objective, such as improvements to regulatory/institutional frameworks, the rollout of the digital ID system, financial sector reforms, the creation of a risk-sharing mechanism, and the provision of business development services for micro, small and medium enterprises in select economic sectors, among others.

The MoF received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi-Partner Fund to implement the SPRING project. As part of this initiative Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity, MoF intends to apply part of the proceeds from the World Bank to finance the Consultancy Service to conduct Strategic Plan National Payment System (NPS) – Somalia. (firm)

2. Responsibilities: The purpose of this assignment is to engage a qualified consulting firm (“Consultant”) to Develop a five-year strategic roadmap for modernizing Somalia’s NPS.: Strengthen DPI to enhance interoperability, accessibility, inclusiveness, and resilience: Align the NPS with BIS PFMIs, ISO 20022, and other global benchmarks: Support regional integration through harmonization with EAC and other frameworks: Incorporate innovations such as instant payments, open APIs, digital identity, and advanced risk management: Improve safety, efficiency, and robustness of the payment ecosystem: Provide actionable recommendations on governance, risk management, operations, and regulatory compliance. All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link:  https://centralbank.gov.so/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/TOR_NPS_Strategic_Roadmap_Consultant_Firm_Somalia-1.pdf

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.).   10. Demonstrates the ability to work both independently and within a team in an output-oriented environment. Takes initiative, works with minimal supervision, and adheres to strict timelines.
  11. Embraces learning new approaches and applies them effectively. Experience in health and social issues is an asset, along with strong analytical and cognitive skills.

N° de référence : SN-FSRP-SN-559971-CS-CQS - C_FSRP_600

AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

Le présent   avis d’appel public à manifestation d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis général de Passations des Marchés publié dans l’UNDB et dans le site officiel de la Banque Mondiale le 25 novembre 2024 et dans le journal « Le Soleil » du 05 décembre 2024, mise à jour dans le journal « Le Soleil » du 16 janvier 2026.

Le Programme de Résilience du Système Alimentaire en Afrique de l’Ouest (FSRP) approuvé par les Administrateurs de la Banque mondiale le 18 novembre 2021 est mis en œuvre dans le cadre d’une approche programmatique multi-phase. La phase 1 comprend le Burkina Faso, le Mali, le Niger et le Togo, ainsi que trois organisations régionales : la Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO), le Conseil ouest et centre africain pour la recherche et le développement agricole (CORAF) et le Centre Régional AGRHYMET (CRA) du Comité permanent interétatique de lutte contre la sécheresse au Sahel (CILSS). La phase 2 approuvée le 29 juillet 2022 concerne le Tchad, le Ghana et la Sierra Leone.

La phase 3 du FSRP concerne le Sénégal. Il est prévu sur une durée de 6 ans et pour un financement de 230 millions de dollars US dont 200 millions US$ de la Banque mondiale et 30 millions US$ du FIDA. Le FSRP Sénégal est mis en œuvre par le Ministère de l’Agriculture, de la Souveraineté Alimentaire et de l’Elevage (MASAE).

Le FSRP a l’intention d’affecter une partie du montant à des services de consultant relatifs à la réalisation d’études architecturales et techniques pour la construction du « Bulding Mbollo » du Centre Régional d’Excellence (CRE).

Les services de consultant (« les Services ») comprennent :

  • L’inventaire détaillé de l'état initial du site incluant les plans, cartes et figures utiles, de l’environnement naturel, socio-économique et humain ;
  • L’analyse des principaux enjeux du projet (enjeux économiques, enjeux sociaux et enjeux environnementaux) ;
  • L’analyse sommaire des impacts environnementaux et sociaux prévisibles, directs, indirects et cumulatifs des activités du projet et les mesures envisagées pour anticiper, prévenir, minimiser, atténuer, compenser, et si possible, supprimer les impacts négatifs ressortis du projet. Une attention particulière devra être portée à la consommation d’eau, d’énergie et le traitement des déchets de manière générale ;
  • Les plans d’implantation, d’aménagement et de voiries et réseaux divers, alliant esthétisme, fonctionnalité, sécurité, durabilité, et aboutissant à un AvantProjet Sommaire (APS) ;
  • Le dossier d’AvantProjet Détaillé (APD) incluant le devis estimatif, et appuyer l’élaboration du dossier d’appel d’offres (DAO) ;
  • Le schéma et appareillage électrique détaillé du Bulding Mbollo (câblerie, équipement de protection, coffret, …) ;
  • Le bilan de production et de consommation énergétique du Bulding Mbollo ;
  • Des sources d’énergies nécessaires pour assurer la fonctionnalité du Bulding Mbollo, y compris l’énergie solaire.

Les Termes de Reference (TDR) de la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous ; Email : cpmfsrp@fsrp.sn.

Le Programme de Résilience du Système Alimentaire en Afrique de l’Ouest (PRSA/ PSRP) invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants intéressés admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services. The Governments of the Commonwealth of Dominica have received financing from the Global Partnership for Education through the World Bank for the Windward Islands Sector Transformation for Learning Enhancement (WISTLE) Project. The Ministry of Education (MOE) intend to procure individual consulting service to provide planning and coordination support to the MOE and the Project Implementation Unit.

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS)

SÉLECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS

Recrutement d’un cabinet chargé de l’élaboration de la stratégie de renforcement des capacités et le développement des programmes de formation et leurs contenus en passation et gestion des marchés publics au Burundi.

  1. Le Gouvernement du Burundi a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour la mise en place du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique du Burundi (PAFEN). Il est prévu qu'une partie des ressources de ce projet, spécialement de ce financement additionnel dédié à la « Modernisation de la gestion des finances publiques (GEP) », soit utilisée pour financer l’introduction d’une Plateforme Électronique de Gestion des Marchés Publics (e-GP).
  2. Dans ce cadre, le projet prévoit le financement des prestations « d’un cabinet chargé de l’élaboration de la stratégie de renforcement des capacités et le développement des programmes de formation en passation des marchés publics au Burundi. »
  3. L’objectif principal de cette mission est d’élaborer une stratégie nationale de renforcement des capacités et de développer des programmes de formation adaptés, avec leurs contenus andragogique et pédagogiques, afin d’assurer une adoption réussie et durable du système de passation des marchés publics électroniques (e-GP) au Burundi.
  4. Spécifiquement, le cabinet devra :
  • Évaluer les besoins en capacités : Identifier les lacunes en compétences et les besoins en formation des différents acteurs impliqués (administrations publiques, secteur privé, société civile).
  • Formuler une stratégie nationale de renforcement des capacités : Concevoir une approche cohérente, alignée aux priorités nationales de développement et conforme aux exigences des partenaires techniques et financiers.
  • Concevoir des programmes de formation adaptés aux curricula à court et moyen terme : Développer des modules pédagogiques spécifiques à l’e-GP (débutants, intermédiaires, experts), intégrant des méthodes modernes d’apprentissage (présentiel, e-learning, blended learning).
  • Proposer un plan de mise en œuvre opérationnel : Définir le cadre pratique pour le déploiement des formations, incluant la sélection des institutions partenaires, un calendrier détaillé et des indicateurs de performance mesurables.

5. La durée de la mission du cabinet est est prévue pour une durée totale de cinq (5) mois, soit environ vingt (20) semaines à compter de la date de signature du contrat.

6. Les Termes de référence peuvent être téléchargés sur le site du PAFEN : https://pafen.gov.bi/appels-doffres/  ou obtenus aux adresses mentionnées ci-dessous.

7. L’Unité de Gestion du PAFEN invite les consultants (firmes), spécialisés dans le domaine objet desdites prestations intéressés par la présente mission à fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils disposent des qualifications requises et de l'expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

8. Critères d’établissement de la liste restreinte : 

Le cabinet ou la firme doit pouvoir démontrer :

 

  • Posséder un minimum de 10 ans d'existence légale et d'expérience générale dans le conseil ou l'enseignement supérieur ;
  • Avoir réalisé avec succès au moins trois (03) missions similaires de formulation de stratégies de renforcement des capacités ou de développement de curricula nationaux au cours des sept (7) dernières années (les références financées par les banques multilatérales de développement sont un atout).

NB : Les Experts clés ne sont pas évalués à ce stade de la présélection.

9. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de septembre 2023 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêt).

10. En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques sur les conflits d’intérêts liées à cette mission comme énoncés au paragraphe 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

11.Les consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement solidaire (joint-venture) et / ou d’un accord de sous-traitant. Dans le cas d'un groupement solidaire (joint-venture), tous les partenaires du groupement solidaire (joint-venture) seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

12. Un consultant sera sélectionné par la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

13. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau : de 8H :00 à 12H :00 et de 13H: 00 à 17H : 30 heure locale de lundi à vendredi (heure de Bujumbura : GMT+2)

14. Les manifestations d'intérêt écrites doivent être remises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous par courrier ordinaire ou par e-mail au plus tard le 02/09/2026 à 17 heures 00 (heure de Bujumbura, GMT+2) avec la mention :

« REPONSE A L’AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D'INTERET N° BI-PAFEN-PIU-2.4.5.12&2.4.5.13-CS-QCBS PORTANT RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET CHARGE DE L’ELABORATION DE LA STRATEGIE DE RENFORCEMENT DES CAPACITES ET LE DEVELOPPMENT DES PROGRAMMES DE FORMATION ET LEURS CONTENUS EN PASSATION ET GESTION DES MARCHES PUBLICS AU BURUNDI

Los Servicios comprenden además la revisión, actualización, complementación o armonización de tres (3) PMOT vigentes o en proceso, correspondientes a Santo Domingo Norte, Pedernales y Neiba, así como del POT-Capital del Distrito Nacional; dos (2) Instrumentos de Delimitación de Suelo Urbano (IDSU) para San Antonio de Guerra y Jimaní; catorce (14) Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático, ocho (8) en Ozama y seis (6) en Enriquillo; y dos (2) Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación, una para cada región, en un período de dieciséis (16) meses calendario, conforme al alcance establecido en los Términos de Referencia. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR).

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. Se requiere una firma con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo de proyectos, planes o políticas relacionados con el ordenamiento y desarrollo territorial en las escalas nacional, regional, municipal y/o de desarrollo urbano. Se valorará especialmente que cuente con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia específica en la formulación de instrumentos supramunicipales de ordenamiento y/o desarrollo territorial o de instrumentos de delimitación y regulación de usos del suelo a escala municipal, incluyendo el desarrollo simultáneo de múltiples instrumentos de planificación territorial en distintos niveles de gobierno.

Asimismo, deberá demostrar un mínimo de tres (3) proyectos o siete (7) años de experiencia reciente en gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, incluyendo análisis multiamenaza, modelación hidrológico-hidráulica y sísmica, integración de escenarios climáticos y articulación de resultados con instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial e inversión pública y su aplicación en procesos de planificación territorial y toma de decisiones.

Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) proyectos similares en alcance, complejidad, niveles de gobierno y extensión geográfica, ejecutados satisfactoriamente y vinculados a la formulación de instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial a escala regional y/o municipal, con integración de la gestión del riesgo de desastres y la adaptación al cambio climático. En conjunto, los proyectos presentados deberán permitir verificar, según corresponda, experiencia en planificación regional, municipal o metropolitana; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; producción y gestión de información geoespacial; formulación normativa; procesos participativos; fortalecimiento institucional; portafolios de inversión; y estrategias de implementación. Las experiencias deberán estar respaldadas mediante certificaciones, contratos, actas de recepción u otra documentación equivalente emitida por los contratantes. En caso de APCA, podrán acreditarse de manera conjunta por sus integrantes, siempre que guarden relación directa con las responsabilidades que cada uno asumirá en la consultoría.

Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para la ejecución de la consultoría, incluyendo la disponibilidad de recursos computacionales, tecnológicos y de producción digital necesarios, así como herramientas de gestión de proyectos, administración de entornos, repositorios y documentación técnica. Deberá evidenciar capacidad para gestionar contratos de magnitud y complejidad similares, cumpliendo tiempos y entregables, así como capacidad organizativa y operativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría, incluyendo la movilización del equipo.

Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas por cada postulante frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Para estos fines, se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales y municipales de ordenamiento territorial, instrumentos de gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor, gestión de información territorial y cartográfica, así como la capacidad operativa para prestar los servicios en idioma español y mantener presencia activa en las regiones objeto de la consultoría.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Ozama y Enriquillo y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse de manera organizada, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados por la firma o integrante de la APCA, escala territorial, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.

  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

The Government of the People's Republic of China has received a loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to improve food safety management at the national and sub-national levels and to reduce food safety risks in selected value chains. The project is being implemented by the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, Guangdong Province, and Shandong Province (Yantai City).

As part of this project, this study proposes to conduct research on the AI-Based Digital Standardized Aquaculture Technology Model. Building upon existing development advantages and targeting the modernization of aquaculture, the study will dynamically monitor the growth status of aquatic products and implement timely interventions. This will continuously enhance quality and safety throughout the production process, ultimately establishing a standardized aquaculture system.

Under this Contract, World Bank loan funds shall be utilized to procure the services of a consulting advisor (hereinafter referred to as the "Consultant") for the sub-project on Research on AI-Based Digital Standardized Aquaculture Technology Model. The Consultant shall research and develop a standardized aquaculture system based on big data, integrate multi-source data, and comprehensively analyze aquaculture growth processes, feeding records, and early warnings for growth status, thereby achieving the digitalization of the aquaculture process. Meanwhile, based on time-series analysis and observation, the system will monitor aquaculture quality in real-time and implement timely interventions, continuously enhancing product quality and safety throughout the production process, and ultimately establishing a standardized aquaculture system.

The implementation period of this Contract is 12 months, with an estimated total input of 36 person-months. The anticipated start date for the assignment is September 2026. Please refer to the Attachment for the detailed Terms of Reference.

TOR for the Consulting Advisor's Work on Research of AI-Based Digital Standardized Aquaculture Technology Model (Contract No.: GDCS-020) under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

To facilitate the organization and implementation of the agricultural product quality and safety research under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project (hereinafter referred to as the "World Bank Loan Project"), and to ensure the successful completion of the project in accordance with its objectives and schedule, the Guangdong Center for Agricultural Product Quality and Safety (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) intends to hire a consulting advisor to conduct research on the AI-based digital standardized aquaculture technology model.

I.Background

As a vital component of China's agricultural economy, the aquaculture industry is a key sector for ensuring food security and optimizing dietary structures. With the continuous upgrading of consumer demands for aquatic product quality and increasingly stringent ecological and environmental protection policies, the traditional extensive aquaculture model can no longer meet the requirements of high-quality development. Particularly in terms of quality and safety supervision, aquaculture still faces prominent challenges, such as opaque production processes, delayed risk early warnings, and difficulties in tracing key indicators.

Due to its unique industrial characteristics, aquaculture still exhibits significant shortcomings in digital supervision practices. On the one hand, the dynamic and ever-changing aquatic environment involves multi-dimensional spatial interactions across the upper atmosphere, surface water bodies, and underwater ecosystems, making it difficult for traditional single monitoring methods to achieve full-scenario coverage. On the other hand, aquatic activities are characterized by concealment and suddenness. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from limited scope, untimely information acquisition, difficulty in identifying hidden behaviors, insufficient data accuracy, and high labor costs. These issues make the establishment of a standardized aquaculture system an urgent priority.

The core of this research lies in utilizing modern information technologies to achieve intelligent management of agricultural product quality and safety. Traditional production monitoring methods still face issues such as incomplete information collection and delayed responses to risk early warnings. To better address these challenges and further promote the digitalization of agricultural product quality and safety supervision, there is an urgent need to rely on modern information technologies—including AI, big data, IoT sensors, and cloud computing—to continuously improve the regulatory system. This is particularly crucial for process supervision and quality traceability in aquaculture, aiming to achieve full-chain safety management from production to distribution. This will not only help enhance the market competitiveness of agricultural products but also lay a solid foundation for the sustainable development of agricultural product quality and safety.

 

II.Objectives and Tasks

(I) Objectives

To address the current issues in aquaculture, including restricted information collection, delayed acquisition of key indicators, and the difficulty of tracing growth processes that lead to insufficient quality and safety, this project proposes to carry out the Development of an AI-Based Standardized Aquaculture System. Building upon existing development advantages and targeting the modernization of aquaculture, the project will dynamically monitor the growth status of aquatic products and implement timely interventions. This will continuously enhance product quality and safety throughout the production process, ultimately establishing a standardized aquaculture system.

(II) Specific Tasks

This research utilizes integrated space-air-ground intelligent technology, combined with remote sensing meteorological inversion, to accurately forecast key meteorological factors for the next 7 to 15 days, providing data support for large-scale cowpea planting management. By leveraging deep visual technology and crop growth prediction models, the study forecasts cowpea growth trends and establishes a pest and disease risk early-warning system. This enables precise fertilizer and pesticide application, promoting green and precision pest control. Furthermore, demonstration sites will be set up to host technical observation and training sessions, ultimately driving the safe, green, and sustainable development of cowpea production.

1.SWOT Analysis 

Summarize the current application status and existing challenges of new technologies, including satellite remote sensing, UAV remote sensing, ground sensors, and AI, in aquaculture production. Taking into account the actual conditions of the aquaculture production areas in the project pilot city, and considering multiple factors such as policy, economy, society, and technology, identify specific areas for investigation and evaluation. Examples include cost-benefit analysis, user acceptance surveys, and technical reliability testing. Meanwhile, ensure that the analysis provides a solid basis for subsequent strategy formulation.

2.Development of Intelligent Recognition Algorithms for Aquaculture Status Based on Low-Altitude Sensing Technology

Utilize drones to capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with deep learning technology, accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics. The study will precisely extract the intrinsic correlations between image features and aquaculture status, effectively addressing the issues of untimely and imprecise perception in traditional monitoring methods. This will significantly enhance the timeliness and accuracy of aquaculture status monitoring, providing robust algorithmic support for the intelligent management of aquaculture.

3. Development of a Big Data-Driven Standardized Digital Aquaculture Management System

Integrate multi-source data to comprehensively analyze aquaculture growth processes, feeding records, and growth status early warnings, thereby achieving the digitalization of the aquaculture process. Meanwhile, based on time-series analysis and observation, monitor aquatic product quality in real-time and implement timely interventions to continuously provide quality and safety recommendations throughout the production process. Comprehensively map the complex relationships among the water environment, meteorological conditions, biological status, and aquaculture farming operations to establish a standardized digital aquaculture system. This will realize full-process digital and information-based management of aquaculture, thoroughly resolving industry pain points such as unsmooth information flow and untimely farming operations. Ultimately, it will ensure the quality and safety of aquatic products across the entire chain from source to terminal, driving the high-quality development of the aquaculture industry.

4.Exploration and Screening of New Technologies

Develop aquaculture status recognition algorithms that integrate remote sensing with low-altitude sensing. The remote sensing analysis will utilize drones to dynamically and automatically capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with remote sensing technologies for aquaculture environment analysis, the system will accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics, thereby achieving refined aquaculture status recognition.

Screening Criteria: Focusing on core indicators such as technological maturity, cost-effectiveness, and environmental adaptability, the optimal technology portfolio will be determined through laboratory simulations and pilot validations.

5.Development of an Integrated "Space-Air-Ground-Water" Technical System

Hardware Layer: Deploy a satellite remote sensing monitoring network, UAV inspection systems, and IoT water quality sensors to achieve full-dimensional dynamic tracking and identification of aquatic product status and the environment in the production areas.

Platform Layer: Utilize an aquaculture big data cloud platform to integrate a multi-source data fusion engine, AI analysis modules (such as density recognition and disease prediction), and a visual decision-making dashboard, supporting synchronized access via both PC and mobile clients.

Application Layer: Implement an intelligent decision-making system. Based on inversion models and growth prediction algorithms, it will automatically generate agronomic recommendations such as feeding amounts and water replacement cycles, and push them to farmers via mobile apps or mini-programs.

6. Effectiveness Evaluation and Promotion & Application

Multi-dimensional Evaluation: Quantify evaluation indicators such as the water quality compliance rate and disease incidence rate. Select two typical aquaculture demonstration sites in the Pearl River Delta to conduct application demonstrations. Verify the technological effectiveness through comparative trials, thereby providing a complete technical solution for the Guangdong Aquatic Product Quality and Safety Enhancement initiative. This will strongly drive the digital transformation and high-quality development of the aquaculture industry, demonstrating robust competitiveness and development potential in the era of the digital economy.

Basic Requirements for Aquaculture Demonstration Bases: The pond aquaculture area must be no less than 200 mu. Bases must establish an agricultural product quality and safety management system in accordance with the law, produce in compliance with relevant agricultural product quality and safety standards, and maintain digitalized production records for agricultural products.

III.Qualification Requirements for the Consultant

1.Capability to independently bear civil liability (Must provide a copy of the Business License or the Certificate of Legal Person for Public Institutions);

2.Sound financial accounting system (Must provide audited financial reports for the past 3 years);

3.Possess the equipment and professional technical capabilities necessary for the performance of the contract (A commitment letter providing the supporting inspection drones and essential testing equipment [as specified in ] must be submitted);

4.Good record of tax and social security payment in accordance with the law (Must provide proof of tax payment and social security contribution for the past 3 months);

5.Good business credit and sound business performance (Must provide a statement certifying no major illegal or irregular business activities in the past 3 years, and that the applicant is not listed on the "Credit China" website as a "person subject to enforcement for dishonesty," "major tax violation entity," or "entity with serious illegal acts in government procurement").

6.Track Record: Within the past five years (from January 1, 2021, up to the deadline for submitting the Letter of Intent for this project, subject to the contract signing date), the Consultant shall have signed no less than one similar performance contract. A similar performance contract refers to a technical consulting service contract involving the application of drones, remote sensing imagery, or AI intelligent recognition in agricultural research, or a service contract for research on intelligent and standardized aquatic product production technology. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES– INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

COUNTRY:

Ethiopia

NAME OF PROJECT:

Grant No.:

IDA-E1110

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:

HIRING OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS TO DEVELOP A NATIONAL INTEROPERABILITY FRAMEWORK FOR HEALTH INFORMATION EXCHANGE IN TWO MEMBER STATES (Tunisia and Seychelles)

REFERENCE NO.:

ET-AUC-568094-CS-INDV

ISSUE DATE:

3 SEPTEMBER 2026                              

The African Union has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Africa Centres for Disease Control Support Program to Combat Current and Future Public Health Threats Project. The Project Development Objective is to enhance the capacity of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) to support AU Member States in preventing, detecting, and responding to current and future public health threats and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

1. BACKGROUND

Health Information Systems interoperability is a foundational requirement for implementing national Health Information Exchange (HIE). A robust, standards-based interoperability framework is essential to enable secure data exchange, support system integration, and establish the technical and governance foundation for sustainable HIE implementation. Findings from the HIE maturity assessments conducted across AU Member States have identified interoperability as a high-impact priority, critical to enabling subsequent phases such as governance strengthening and phased digital health system implementation.

As part of the support by Africa CDC in implementing HIE across Member States, digital maturity assessments were conducted in 12 AU Member States, alongside the development of HIE roadmaps. Following this, Africa CDC will support two of countries, Tunisia and Seychelles, through the engagement of two individual consultants to support each of the countries to design and develop comprehensive interoperability frameworks aligned with international best practices and tailored to their national contexts.

2. OBJECTIVES

The purpose of this assignment is to design two country-specific, standards-based national interoperability frameworks that provide:

  • A structured architecture for health data exchange
  • Governance and institutional coordination mechanisms
  • Standards alignment and implementation guidance
  • A phased, actionable roadmap for national HIE implementation

3. SCOPE OF WORK

The consultants will provide technical leadership and advisory support to develop national interoperability framework as a foundational component of its Health Information Exchange (HIE). The consultants will conduct a structured review of the current digital health ecosystem, identify interoperability needs and gaps, and design a comprehensive framework aligned with internationally recognised best practices.

The scope of work includes:

  • Defining a layered interoperability model addressing technical, semantic, organisational, and legal dimensions,
  • Proposing standards-based data exchange approaches aligned with recognised international frameworks,
  • Developing high-level architecture principles to guide secure system integration,
  • Providing governance guidance to support institutional coordination and oversight,
  • Identifying security, privacy, and sustainability considerations,
  • Developing a phased implementation roadmap suitable for national adoption,
  • Developing an M&E framework.

The consultants will conduct consultations, technical discussions, document reviews, and validation sessions with designated counterparts. The assignment focuses on framework development and strategic planning; it does not include system procurement, software development, or direct implementation activities.

Specific institutional stakeholders and documentation to be reviewed will be provided by the Ministry of Health

4. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE

Deliverable

Description

Purpose

Format

Indicative Timeline

Detailed workplan, methodology, stakeholder engagement plan, and information requirements

To establish a clear implementation approach and confirm expectations with Africa CDC and national counterparts

Situational Analysis and Interoperability Landscape Review

Assessment of current digital health systems, standards usage, data exchange practices, and interoperability gaps

To provide an evidence-based baseline for framework design

By end of Month 2

Draft National Interoperability Framework

To present proposed national framework for technical and stakeholder review

Validation Workshop Materials and Revised Framework

Presentation materials and updated framework incorporating stakeholder input

To ensure national ownership and technical validation

Month 5

Final Interoperability Framework and Implementation Roadmap

Finalized framework and phased implementation roadmap with recommendations and executive summary

To provide an actionable, endorsed national interoperability framework

Final report with roadmap and executive summary

End of Month 6

5. METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH EXPECTATIONS

The consultants are expected to apply internationally recognized best practices in digital health interoperability, drawing on established guidance and frameworks such as those promoted by global public health and standards organizations (for example WHO digital health guidance, HL7 interoperability standards, ISO principles for information systems, Open HIE architectural approaches, etc). The methodology should be consultative, evidence-based, and iterative, ensuring alignment with national priorities and feasibility within institutional capacities.

The approach should demonstrate clear consideration of security, privacy, scalability, governance alignment, and long-term sustainability. The consultants should ensure that recommendations are practical, actionable, and structured for phased implementation.

Consultants may exchange information among themselves to explore approaches, tools, strategies that may make their efforts more effective.

6. DURATION AND LEVEL OF EFFORT 

The assignment will be conducted over a maximum period of six months. The level of effort is expected to be full-time or near full-time engagement as required to complete deliverables within agreed timelines.

Specific start and end dates: Upon signing contract.

7. DUTY STATIONS

Duty station and modality: In country at the Ministry of Health of the respective countries (Tunisia and Seychelles)

8. REPORTING AND INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

The consultants will report technically to Director of Surveillance and Disease Intelligence at Africa CDC and the Ministry of Health-designated national counterparts. The consultants will work closely with relevant technical teams and stakeholders identified by the Ministry to ensure that the interoperability framework reflects national priorities and institutional realities.

The Consultants should have a strong understanding of the national digital health ecosystem. They will be based in-country and will regularly engage with key stakeholders through meetings and consultations. In addition, regular coordination meetings, technical discussions, and document review sessions will be held with Africa CDC and relevant national stakeholders to ensure alignment and steady progress.

Oversight and review mechanisms, including designated focal points, validation procedures, and formal approval processes, will be established at the start of the assignment. These arrangements will define communication channels, feedback timelines, and deliverable endorsement procedures to ensure accountability and quality assurance throughout the consultancy period.

Administrative coordination and contractual management will be handled by Africa CDC.

9. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The consultants must possess advanced expertise in digital health interoperability, health information systems architecture, or a closely related field. The consultants should demonstrate substantial experience designing interoperability frameworks, enterprise architectures, or national digital health strategies, preferably at national or multi-country level.

The consultant must meet the following requirements:

  • Advanced university degree in health informatics, information systems, computer science, public health, or related discipline,
  • Demonstrated experience developing interoperability frameworks or national health information system architectures,
  • Proven knowledge of global interoperability standards and frameworks,
  • Proven experience working with ministries, public agencies, or international organizations on comparable assignments.
  • Strong analytical and technical writing skills,
  • Fluency in English and French is mandatory for candidates applying to be selected to support Seychelles. Furthermore, fluency in Arabic is required for candidates applying to be selected to support Tunisia,
  • A minimum of ten (10) years of relevant experience is required in areas such as digital health interoperability, health information systems architecture, or national digital health strategy development.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the preferred country’s health and digital health context, relevant institutions, governance arrangements, and stakeholder landscape, together with proficiency in the country’s applicable working language(s), sufficient to conduct consultations, review relevant documentation, and deliver the assignment effectively.

10. CORE COMPETENCIES

The consultant should demonstrate strong professional competencies including strategic thinking, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, communication skills, and the ability to translate complex technical concepts into practical guidance. The consultant must also show strong organizational skills, ability to meet deadlines, and capacity to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.

11. CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION, AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

The consultants shall adhere to the highest standards of professional integrity and confidentiality. All information, documents, data, and materials accessed during the assignment shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party without prior written authorisation.

The consultants shall comply with applicable data protection principles and institutional policies concerning the handling of sensitive or restricted information.

All reports, frameworks, tools, and materials developed under this assignment shall become the property of Africa CDC and the Ministry of Health. The consultants shall not use, reproduce, or distribute any deliverables or underlying materials for purposes unrelated to this assignment without prior written approval.

12. PAYMENT TERMS AND SCHEDULE

Consultancy fees are capped at $50,000 per consultant, totalling $100,000 for two consultants, with each consultant assigned to support one country. Payments will be made upon satisfactory completion and formal acceptance of agreed deliverables, based on a milestone schedule linked to the submission and approval of key outputs. Payments will be made based on satisfactory completion and formal acceptance of agreed deliverables. 13. CLARIFICATIONS, AMENDMENTS, AND COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL

All communications regarding this assignment shall be conducted through officially designated focal points identified at the start of the consultancy. Communication channels, reporting frequency, and feedback timelines will be formally agreed upon during the inception phase.

Any substantive modifications to the scope of work, deliverables, timeline, or level of effort must be agreed in writing by Africa CDC and the respective Ministry of Health. Amendments shall be formalised through written addenda to the contract, in accordance with applicable procurement procedures.

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing objective assurance to the World Bank Group through the African Union Commission Office of Internal Oversight that: the governance processes, financial management and procurement processes comply with requirements; and that project procedures and internal controls are adequate and effective to mitigate current and emerging risks and fraud. Specific tasks include:

  • Conduct audits and investigate possible fraudulent behavior and communicate findings and recommend appropriate action to the Office of Internal Oversight Directorate and World Bank Group.

  • Evaluate internal control efficiency and effectiveness and provide management assurance that the controls in place are adequate to respond to the risks that threaten the projects. Also examine operations to determine whether they are efficient and effective
