The Consultant shall also provide adequate administrative staff (secretaries, translators, etc.) needed to support the expert team.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, items 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers[1], dated September 2023 with amendments of September 2025[2] (hereinafter referred to as the "Procurement Regulations"), which contains the World Bank's policy regarding conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

Selection of a Consultant will be performed in accordance with Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS) method following World Bank’s Consultants Guidelines.

Further information may be obtained at the address below.

Expressions of interest must be submitted in Ukrainian or English via email to the address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org; uiherp@mon.gov.ua by 2:00 PM Kyiv time on September 30, 2026.[3]

Expressions of interest to be clearly marked: "LEARN-1.1-CIRRICULA: Expression of Interest".

Consultants should provide not only information demonstrating their compliance with the Mandatory Minimum Qualification Requirements, but also information that meets the specific requirements of the assignment and will be considered an advantage. The Consultant rating will be based on compliance with these latter requirements. The Consultant with the highest rating, determined according to the established criteria for evaluating the Consultant’s qualifications, will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal.

Information on the Consultant’s experience provided by the Consultants must be documented (copies of contracts or parts thereof, and acceptance certificates for services provided; additionally, client references may be submitted, describing the specifics of the completed assignment).

Interested Consultants are additionally advised to pay attention to the following aspects when preparing their information:

  • Files submitted by the Consultant should be in PDF (Portable Document Format) and/or JPG formats and should be as consolidated as possible;
  • When preparing information describing your qualifications and experience, provide as much detail as possible to demonstrate compliance with the established qualification criteria and relevance to the assignment;
  • Include copies of documents confirming the stated experience and competencies, and provide contact information of third parties who can confirm your experience and provide relevant references.

Consultants who have submitted an EOI should not submit any documents or information after the deadline for EOI submission, except for providing documents and/or information requested by the Employer for clarification or explanation of the submitted EOI. Any exchange of information between the Employer and Consultants must be in writing via the official email addresses specified in this announcement.

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$451 million provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at aligning the education system with labour market needs, supporting economic recovery, and advancing Ukraine’s European integration agenda.

A key component of this reform is the introduction of professionally oriented upper secondary education, which integrates general education with early professional orientation and creates structured pathways between general secondary education, vocational education, and professional pre-higher education.

The regulatory and methodological framework required for this transformation has already been established, including:

  • adoption of the Law of Ukraine “On professional (vocational) education” (August 2025);
  • development of secondary legislation and regulatory acts;
  • approval of competency-based professional education standards;
  • entry into force of the State Standard of Specialised Secondary Education (Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated July 25, 2024 No. 851);
  • Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 08.06.2026 no. 898);
  • Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine No. 675 dated 05.06.2023

 

Initial experience in developing model programs has demonstrated strong demand, high institutional interest, and significant scalability potential. At the same time, the system currently lacks a sufficient number of professionally oriented model programs across priority economic sectors, as well as adapted academic content aligned with professional pathways.

Given that the regulatory framework has only recently been finalised, this Assignment represents the first opportunity to implement curriculum transformation at scale within a fully operational legal and methodological environment.

Under the GPE-financed institutional capacity activities, MoES intends to engage a qualified Consultant to develop a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education. The Assignment shall be implemented over a period of six (6) months from the Effective Date of the Contract. The Assignment will enable rapid, scalable transformation of curriculum content, directly impacting over 37,000 learners in priority economic sectors and creating a foundation for nationwide implementation of professionally oriented upper secondary education.

 

The Assignment is expected to be implemented in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable Ukrainian legislation.

 

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of the Assignment is to support MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

Specifically, the Assignment is to develop forty-one (41) model programs of mandatory educational components by educational domains for four (4) specializations of professionally oriented specialised secondary education, namely, Construction, Engineering and Technology, Information Technology, and Medical specialization (aligned with priority economic sectors) under the State standard of profile secondary education.

The model programs should be aligned with professional standards, labour market needs and sectoral requirements, as well as provide a unified national approach to curriculum development and adaptation.

The Consultant shall achieve the above objective in full compliance with applicable regulatory and legal framework of Ukraine, including relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, and procurement and implementation requirements of the World Bank.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

3.1 Overall Approach

The Consultant shall provide comprehensive technical, methodological and organisational support to MoES for the development of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The Assignment shall build upon the existing regulatory framework developed by MoES.

The implementation logic shall follow a structured sequence:

  1. Mobilisation of the expert pool.
  2. Development of specialised model programs.
  3. Quality assurance and validation.

All activities shall ensure consistency, scalability, and alignment across programs.

3.2 Components

Component 1. Expert Mobilisation and Coordination

The Consultant shall mobilise and manage a structured expert pool and ensure effective coordination throughout all stages of the Assignment.

The Consultant shall:

  • mobilise and manage a structured expert pool including:
    • VE and PPHE educators;
    • scientific and research-pedagogical staff (academics involved in relevant fields of study); 
    • sectoral experts from industry;
    • methodological specialists from NMCs;
  • ensure balanced representation across sectors;
  • establish coordination mechanisms and workflows;
  • assign clear roles and responsibilities;
  • develop Quality Assurance Plan;
  • ensure timely delivery of outputs.

It is recommended that each Model Program draft be developed by a compact drafting team comprising at least two (2) Subject Experts (Non-Key Experts) responsible for its development.

Each Sectoral Expert shall coordinate all drafts of Model Programs  within the assigned specialization and responsible for:

  • methodological supervision;
  • coordination of drafting teams;
  • ensuring consistency across all Model Programs within the specialization;
  • ensuring compliance with the State Standard of Specialized Secondary Education, the Typical Educational Program and methodological guidance approved by MoES;
  • internal quality control before submission for independent review.

Subject Experts may contribute to the development of more than one Model Program draft depending on their qualifications and the implementation methodology proposed by the Consultant.

All experts shall be engaged on a contractual basis, with clearly defined deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations.

Component 2. Development of Specialised Model Programs

The Consultant shall develop forty-one (41) specialised model programs across four (4) specializations defined according to priority economic sectors in accordance with State standard of specialised secondary education, Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation and Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums.The four priority sectors are:

    • Construction;
    • Engineering and technology;
    • Information technology;
    • Medical

Each program shall:

  • integrate general education subjects into applied, sector-specific contexts;
  • align with professional standards and occupational requirements;
  • reflect labour market needs;
  • follow State standard of specialised secondary education and Typical educational program of specialised secondary education;
  • be developed in accordance with the academic integrity values.

The development of every model program draft shall be based on the Typical educational programme for professionally oriented specialised secondary education approved under Order 898 and on the corresponding Typical curriculum plan for each of the four profiles listed above. The list of mandatory educational components for which MPs shall be developed for each profile, together with the corresponding number of teaching hours, hours of independent work, ECTS credits and their distribution between the profile-adaptation cycle (year 1) and the profile cycle (years 2-3), is set out in Annex 1 to this ToR.

 

Each MP shall comply with the structure and content requirements established in the Typical Educational Programme and shall consist, at minimum, of the following four parts:

  • Title page – name of the ministry/institution; type of programme (model programme / programme based on a model programme / programme not based on a model programme); type of mandatory educational component (subject, discipline, integrated/crosssectoral/special course, module, etc.); programme title; education level; profile of study; educational domain(s); assessment benchmarks (basic or advanced); author(s); year of development;
  • Introductory part – author's concept and the role and significance of the component; relevance for the selected profile; aim and objectives aligned with the assessment benchmarks of the State Standard and with the chosen profile; references to the relevant educational domain(s) and to professional standards, occupational qualification characteristics or professional prehigher education standards used as a basis; crossreferences to other MPs jointly covering the same mandatory learning outcomes, where applicable; workload in hours and ECTS credits; structural elements; recommended forms of organising the educational process;
  • Main part – titles and workload in hours of structural elements (content lines, sections, topics); expected learning outcomes linked to, and retaining the indexation of, the mandatory learning outcomes of the State Standard; proposed content reflecting professionally oriented, sectorspecific contexts relevant to the profile; recommended learning activities and active/interactive forms of organising learning; recommended methodological support bearing the "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" grif;
  • Concluding part – strategy and methodological recommendations for achieving the expected learning outcomes; description of assessment tools and instruments; reference to possible alternative assessment systems.

 

Each MP shall be submitted in the following format: paper size A4 (210×297 mm); font Times New Roman; main text – 14 pt; tables, footnotes and supplementary text – 10–12 pt; line spacing – 1.0; continuous page numbering starting from the second page.

The total workload of each MP, expressed in hours and ECTS credits, shall correspond exactly to the figures established for the relevant educational component for the respective profile, as set out in Annex 1. Any deviation shall be justified in writing by the Consultant and shall require prior written approval by MoES.

Although the educational domains of the components listed in Annexes 1 are common to all profiles, the content of each MP shall be professionally oriented to the specific profile for which it is developed, in accordance with Section 4 of the Typical Educational Programme. In particular, each MP shall:

  • integrate the competency potential and core knowledge of the relevant educational domain(s), as defined by the State Standard, with applied, occupation specific contexts relevant to the profile;
  • be consistent with the values, cross cutting skills and recommended forms of learning activity described in the Typical educational rogramme.

The development cycle shall be completed within 90 working days.

Considering the large number of tasks included under this component, it may be practical to divide it into two implementation stages.

In accordance with the Quality Assurance Plan and MoES regulations the Consultant shall ensure the quality of all specialised model programs developed under this Assignment through a two-tier quality assurance system: (i) the Consultant's own internal quality assurance process, and (ii) the official State expertise and grif procedure administered by MoES and  in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes (MoES Order No. 675 of 5 June 2023).

Tier 1 - Consultant's internal quality assurance

The Consultant shall:

  • conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle;
  • ensure consistency of outputs across all profiles through centralised coordination by the Quality Assurance Expert;
  • develop all the outputs following the academic integrity values

The Consultant may conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle and/or organise independent blind peer review as part of the Consultant’s internal quality assurance processes.

Tier 2 - Submission for the official MoES grif procedure

Each MP shall be submitted by the Consultant, through MoES to Ukrainian Institute of Education Development for expertise and the grant of the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine," in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes.

The Consultant shall note that, pursuant to paragraph 6 of Section IV of the Procedure, expertise of model programmes (as objects falling under subparagraph 3 of paragraph 5 of Section I of the Procedure) is exempt from the standard fee-based expertise mechanism. The Consultant's budget shall accordingly cover only its own internal quality assurance activity.

 Expertise process and timelines to be reflected in the Work Schedule

The Consultant's Work Schedule shall account for the following parameters of the official procedure:

  • expertise is conducted by at least two members of the relevant Commission and/or expert group, selected by a method of random selection with regard to their professional background, specialisation and place of work;
  • the Commission's reasoned expert opinion is to be expected within two months of submission, unless a different period is agreed;
  • where the Commission requires revision, the Consultant shall resubmit the revised MP together with a reasoned response to each comment within 30 calendar days of receipt of the extract from the Commission's protocol;
  • the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" is granted by MoES order and is valid for five years, expiring on 1 July of the relevant year;
  • upon granting of the grif, the MP is entered in the public Catalogue of Granted Grifs maintained by MoES and the Institution.

The Assignment shall be deemed complete in respect of Component 2 only once the full package of drafts of model programs has obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue, once each tranche of programs has obtained such confirmation. Evidence of the grant of the grif and of the Catalogue entry shall be annexed to the relevant Interim or Final Completion Report.

IV. DELIVERABLES

The Consultant shall deliver the following key deliverables during the implementation of the Assignment.

Deliverable 1. Inception Report

Within 20 calendar days from the Effective Date of the Contract, the Consultant shall submit a Draft Inception Report, including:

  • work plan and timeline;
  • expert mobilisation plan;
  • risk assessment and mitigation measures;
  • Quality Assurance Plan.

Deliverable 2. Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs

The following outputs shall be produced under Deliverable 2:

  • 20 drafts of specialised model programs developed and obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities.

 

Deliverable 3. Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs

The following outputs shall be produced under Deliverable 2:

  • 21 drafts of specialised model programs developed and obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities.

Deliverable 4. Final Completion Report

The following outputs shall be delivered under this deliverable and documented in the Final Completion Report:

  • full package with forty-one (41) final approved programs;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities;
  • lessons learned and next steps for further implementation.

The Consultant shall submit a Draft Final Completion Report no later than one month before the completion of the Assignment, summarising overall implementation results, achievement of objectives and targets, key lessons learned, and recommendations for further institutionalisation and sustainability.

Reports Submission and Acceptance Procedure

The following procedure shall apply to all reports submitted under this Assignment: the Inception Report (Deliverable 1), Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 2), and Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 3) and the Final Completion Report (Deliverable 4).

The exact format of the reports will be discussed and agreed upon with MoES and, where applicable, with the World Bank, upon contract signing and before the commencement of the Assignment. All reports and deliverables will be submitted in a minimum of two (2) hard copies in English and two (2) hard copies in Ukrainian. The products developed (model programs as well as methodological materials for development for Ukrainian-speaking users) shall be submitted in Ukrainian only, without translation, and included as annexes to the relevant reports. All materials developed under this Assignment shall become the property of MoES.

The Consultant shall submit:

  • the draft version of the Inception Report – within 20 calendar days from the Effective Date;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs  – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of the Final Report – at latest 30 calendar days before the completion of the services.

The draft of each report shall be submitted in electronic (Word/Excel and PDF) format to the Client’s email address specified in the Contract. The Client will review the draft within 14 calendar days from the date of receipt and provide comments, or confirm the quality and correspondence of the Assignment with the requirements of these Terms of Reference. The Consultant, within 7 calendar days from receipt of comments, shall process them and submit the revised report in electronic and paper format, together with a table indicating, for each comment, the method of its consideration or justification for any deviation.

If the Client has no comments on the revised report, the report shall be deemed approved, which shall be confirmed by a signed Acceptance Certificate for Services. If the Client does not respond with comments within the above-mentioned period, the draft report shall be deemed accepted.

If required by MoES, the Consultant shall provide ad-hoc reports within 3–7 calendar days, depending on the complexity of the request.

V. REQUIREMENTS

5.1 Consultant

The Consultant must be a legally registered firm or a Joint Venture / Consortium of firms.

Minimum Qualification Requirements (Pass/Fail Basis)

Failure to meet any of the requirements below shall result in disqualification.

Core Business and Experience

  • At least 3 (three) years of experience in education, curriculum development, institutional development, or related fields;
  • At least 3 (three) successfully completed assignments during the last 6 years in one or more of the following areas:

–       curriculum development or educational program design;

–       vocational education or education sector projects;

–       capacity building programs for education institutions.

In case of a Joint Venture / Consortium (JVCA), the Lead Member shall demonstrate substantial compliance with the above requirements, including at least 3 (three) years of relevant experience and participation in at least 2 (two) relevant assignments. The JVCA as a whole must meet all qualification requirements.

Financial Capacity

  • Average annual turnover for the last 3 completed financial years shall be at least USD 150,000 or equivalent.

 In case of a JVCA: Lead Member: minimum 50% of the annual turnover requirement; Other members: minimum 25% of the annual turnover requirement; Combined: must fully meet the annual turnover requirement. Audited financial statements or verified financial documents shall be provided.

Experience with Donor-Funded Projects

  • At least one assignment financed by international financial institutions or bilateral donors (e.g., World Bank, EBRD, EU, GIZ, UNICEF, etc.) within the last 5 years is an advantage.

Avis d’Appel d’offres, Services physiques

Pays : République de Madagascar

Nom du Projet : Projet de Productivité et de Résilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux – Riz Plus (P175269)

No Prêt/Crédit/Don : IDA 7280-MG, COFN-C2530

Nom du Marché: _____-2026/MiASA/SG/RIZPLUS/NCS

AO No: _____-2026/MiASA/SG/RIZPLUS/RFB

Emis le : 25 juillet 2026

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de Banque Mondiale pour financer le Projet de productivité et de résilience des moyens de subsistance ruraux (RIZ PLUS), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché Prestation de service de Gestion de Bons Electroniques. Ce contrat sera financé conjointement par l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD). La passation du Marché sera conforme aux règles de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale. Pour ce Marché, l’Emprunteur effectuera les paiements en recourant à la méthode de décaissement par « Paiement direct », comme définie dans les Directives de la Banque Mondiale applicables aux Décaissements dans le cadre de Financements de Projets d’Investissement.
  2. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Productivité et de Resilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux - Riz plus, sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour assurer la prestation de service d'une Agence de Gestion de Bons Électroniques (e-Voucher), comprenant la conception, le développement, le déploiement et l'exploitation d'un système numérique de gestion des subventions agricoles reposant sur des cartes NFC, l'authentification multi facteur, le traitement hors ligne avec synchronisation différée, la traçabilité par blockchain et l'interopérabilité avec le paiement par Mobile Money, en vue d'enregistrer 80 000 bénéficiaires et d'émettre 130 000 bons sur quatre campagnes agricoles, dans les régions d'Alaotra-Mangoro et de Sofia, jusqu'à la clôture du projet fin 2028.
  3. La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en recourant à un Appel d’Offres (AO) telle que définie dans le « Règlement applicable aux Emprunteurs – Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement, édition de novembre 2020, de la Banque Mondiale (« le Règlement de passation des marchés »), » et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans le Règlement de passation des marchés.
  4. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Productivité et de Resilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux - Riz plus, Bureau de la Passation des Marchés et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous (dernier paragraphe) de 08h30 à 16h30.
  5. Le Dossier d’Appel d’offres en Français peut être obtenu par tout Soumissionnaire intéressé en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous. Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par voie électronique ou à récupérer en main propre à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.
  6. Les offres devront être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 17 août 2026 à 11:00, heure de Madagascar. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Toute offre arrivée après l’expiration du délai limite de remise des offres sera rejetée. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le 17 août 2026 à 11:00, heure de Madagascar.
  7. Les offres doivent être accompagnées d’une Déclaration de garantie de l’offre.
  8. Veuillez noter que le Règlement de Passation des Marchés exige que l’Emprunteur divulgue les informations sur les propriétaires effectifs du Soumissionnaire attributaire, dans le cadre de l’avis de Notification d’Attribution de Marché, en renseignant le Formulaire de divulgation des bénéficiaires effectifs inclus dans le dossier d’appel d’offres.
  9. Les adresses auxquelles il est fait référence ci-dessus sont :
    • Nom de l’Agence d’exécution : Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZ PLUS
    • Nom et titre du responsable : Monsieur RAKOTOMAHEFA Bruno
    • Bureau : Passation des Marchés de l’UGP Riz Plus, 2ème étage
    • Adresse : Bâtiment « FIADANANTSOA », lot II Y 53 Bis, Avaratr’Antanimora (près de la Gastronomie Pizza) – 101 – Antananarivo, Madagascar.
    • Adresse électronique : cn.rizplus@gmail.com ;
    • copie : rizplus-pm@googlegroups.com

Monsieur RAKOTOMAHEFA Bruno

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(SELECTION OF IT CONSULTANT FIRM)

Country: Bangladesh

Name of Project: ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host Community and FDMN                                    through Capacity Enhancement Project, Credit No: IDA-7546-BD & E326-BD

Assignment Title: Selection of consulting firm for Design, Development & Implementation of RSS Digital Financial System (RSS-DFS) with Integrated Beneficiary Survey, Poverty Reduction Tracking & Behavioral Change Identification Module for Rural Social Services (RSS) programs of DSS.

Reference No.: SD-13

The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Inclusive Services and Opportunities (ISO) for the Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Populations project”. The Bangladesh Rural Social Service (RSS) Program, administered by DSS since the 1970s, manages an annual disbursement portfolio of approximately USD 3.8 billion, serves 8.5 million active borrowers across all 64 districts through a network of Union Social Woker (USWs), Upazila Social Service Officers (USSOs), and District Social Service Offices. Despite its remarkable scale and geographic reach, the Program continues to operate entirely on manual, paper-based processes generating severe systemic inefficiencies and fiduciary risks.

Governments across developing economies continue to rely on manual, paper-based financial management systems to administer social protection programs, public expenditure tracking, and beneficiary payment processes. These legacy systems are characterized by significant operational inefficiencies, including delayed payment processing, limited audit trails, high administrative overhead, susceptibility to fraud and data loss, and an inability to generate real-time financial intelligence for evidence-based decision-making.

The rapid proliferation of mobile technology across low- and middle-income countries has created an unprecedented opportunity to leapfrog traditional financial infrastructure. Mobile/Digital Financial Systems (DFS) offer a transformative pathway to digitize government financial operations, enabling secure, transparent, and cost-effective delivery of payments and services - particularly to vulnerable and hard-to-reach populations.

Beyond the digitization of financial transactions, there is a growing recognition among governments and development partners that social protection programs must move beyond simple cash transfer delivery toward a more holistic model of human capital development. This requires robust tools to track whether beneficiaries are graduating out of poverty, achieving economic self-sufficiency, and demonstrating measurable behavioral changes in areas such as health-seeking behavior, children's school attendance, savings culture, and productive asset accumulation.

In this context, the Government [hereinafter referred to as "the Client"] seeks to engage a qualified consulting firm to:

  • Design and implement a fully functional Digital Financial System (DFS) to replace the existing RSS manual financial management processes; and
  • Develop an integrated Beneficiary Graduation Tracking and Behavioral Change Survey Module to monitor program outcomes and inform adaptive management decisions.
  1. This assignment is aligned with the Government's broader digital transformation agenda and its commitment to strengthening social protection delivery systems in accordance with international best practices. The World Bank, as a development partner, will provide technical oversight and quality assurance throughout the implementation process.
  2. Implementation period will be approximately 18 months, and expected start date of assignment may be July 1, 2027, to ensure full consistency with the TOR.
  3. Department of Social Services under Ministry of Social Welfare represented by the Project Director, The ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host Community and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project, now invites eligible FIRMs (“FIRMs”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested FIRMs should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.
  4. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a) General experience of the FIRM(s);

(b) Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required area;

(c) Financial soundness, staffing and logistics of the FIRM;

        Specific Considerations

General Experience in Relevant Assignments

    • Minimum of 10 years of experience in the design and implementation of Microcredit/Digital Financial Systems.

Technical and Regional Capacity

    • Demonstrated experience in at least three comparable assignments involving in the development and implementation of Mobile Financial Systems or the development of Microcredit/Digital Financial Systems, preferably in South Asia.

Specific Experience in Relevant Assignments

    • Proven experience in transforming manual/semi-manual financial system to digital financial system.
    • Experience in designing and developing Survey and Data collection tools for social protection /  livelihoods support / economic inclusion programs, including beneficiary tracking, graduation monitoring, or behavioral change measurement.
    • Demonstrated knowledge of mobile money ecosystem integration, including experience working with mobile network operators and mobile money APIs.
    • Mandatory certification of CMMI Level 3 and PCI-DSS.
    • Demonstrated commitment to Data privacy and Cybersecurity, with relevant certifications of ISO 27001, ISO 9001 and TL 9000.

Firms are requested to submit the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

  1. Up To Date Relevant Registration papers of the FIRM(s);
  2. JV agreement/letter of intent (if applicable) along with the proposed JV agreement;
  3. Brochure including staffing;
  4. Audited financial reports for last three years (including mentioning turnover, current asset & liability and fixed asset & liability);
  5. Work experience record of Last ten (10) years (including nature, total cost of Contract, total input in terms of man month, employer, location of work etc.)

Assignment Title: Consultant to Develop Regional IGAD Soil Information System (SIS)

Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567401-CS-INDV

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from International Development Agency (IDA) towards the cost of the Food systems resilience program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Grant to payments under this contract to payments under this contract: Consultant to develop regional IGAD Soil Information System (SIS)

  1. The objective of the assignment:

To develop Data Governance Framework and Data-Sharing Protocols for a Regional SIS in IGAD.

  1. Specific Objectives
  • Assess existing soil information systems, databases, standards, and institutional arrangements within IGAD Member States.
  • Develop a data sharing framework and mechanism for Soil and Fertilizer related data from MS to the regional Soil Information System to be developed

 

  1. Minimum Consultant’s qualifications and experience requirements

The consultant should be a senior expert with extensive experience in soil information systems, geospatial data management, digital agriculture, data governance, and regional data-sharing frameworks. The expert should have demonstrated experience in assessing national information systems, developing data governance frameworks, establishing interoperability standards, and facilitating multi-country data exchange initiatives.

Required Qualifications

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s or higher) in one of the following fields: Soil Science, Agronomy, Agricultural Information Systems; Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing; Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science; Environmental Science, Land Management, or related disciplines.
  • Additional qualifications or certifications in data governance, geospatial information systems, database management, or digital transformation will be an advantage.

Professional Experience

The consultant should have:

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in soil information management, geospatial systems, agricultural data platforms, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing, assessing, or implementing Soil Information Systems (SIS), Land Information Systems, or other environmental/agricultural information systems.
  • Proven experience conducting stakeholder assessments, institutional mapping, and data availability assessments involving government institutions, research organizations, universities, laboratories, and development partners.
  • Experience developing data governance frameworks, data-sharing policies, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs), and institutional arrangements for multi-stakeholder or multi-country platforms.
  • Strong knowledge of soil and fertilizer data systems, including soil fertility databases, soil health indicators, laboratory datasets, nutrient mapping, fertilizer recommendations, and digital soil mapping.
  • Experience in developing data standards, metadata frameworks, classification systems, and interoperability guidelines for geospatial and scientific datasets.
  • Practical experience with GIS databases, database management systems, cloud-based data platforms, and web-based geospatial portals.
  • Experience in assessing and applying open data standards, APIs, data exchange protocols, and system interoperability approaches.
  • Experience working with regional organizations, governments, research institutions, or international development organizations on agricultural data initiatives.
  1. The Consulting Services Contract is expected to be for a period of 120 calendar days from the date of contract commencement.
  2. The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites individuals to express their interest in providing the services. Interested individuals must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of Academic qualifications, and Professional Qualifications.
  3. An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (Regulations).
  4. Interested individuals may obtain further information at the address below from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday EAT).

The Government of Vanuatu (Gov) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program (PROP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include supporting the GoV in the pre-design, preparation, procurement and contract management, and supervision of infrastructure packages to be financed under the Project, in compliance with relevant national legislation and World Bank requirements.

.          

The Ministry of Fisheries, Ocean and Maritime Affairs (MFOMA) now invite eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process. The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Essential requirements and desirable criteria

The Infrastructure Engineer (Advisor) is expected to have the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, coastal/marine engineering, or other relevant engineering discipline (Master’s degree desirable).
  • At least 15 years of relevant professional experience in planning, design, and/or supervision of infrastructure projects, including experience with procurement and contract management, including at least five infrastructures costed above US$2 million.
  • Experience with coastal and marine infrastructure (e.g., jetties, reclamation/sheet pile quays) and/or public building projects (including seismic/cyclone-resistant design).
  • Demonstrated experience preparing or reviewing ToR, technical specifications, BoQs/cost estimates, and procurement documents for works and consultancy services.
  • Demonstrated experience in construction supervision and quality assurance, including reviewing contractor work programs, method statements, progress reports, and payment certification.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating climate and natural hazard resilience considerations into infrastructure design (e.g., cyclone and seismic design, coastal hazards and drainage).
  • Strong understanding of occupational health and safety and community health and safety requirements for construction projects
  • Ability to work effectively with E&S specialists to integrate E&S measures into designs and contracts.
  • Strong analytical, communication and report-writing skills in English.
  • Experience in small island / Pacific Island Country contexts, including working with public sector counterparts and operating in capacity-constrained environments.

Desirable skills, knowledge and competencies

  • Experience working on World Bank- or other development partner-financed infrastructure projects, including familiarity with procurement and contract management requirements.
  • Oral and written skills in Bislama and/or French.
  • Experience working in Vanuatu.
  • Experience with energy efficient infrastructure, solar energy plants, low-cost infrastructure designs, and climate resilience infrastructure considerations.

Assignment Title: Consultancy for The Development of an Interactive Dashboard for The IGAD Region Food Systems Resilience Analysis

Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567385-CS-INDV

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from International Development Agency (IDA) towards the cost of the Food systems resilience program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Grant to payments under this contract: Consultancy for The Development of an Interactive Dashboard for The IGAD Region Food Systems Resilience Analysis

1.The objective of the assignment:

The objective is to enhance evidence based decision-making on food systems resilience across the IGAD region by transforming the IGAD Food Systems Resilience Analysis Framework and its 2024 evidence base into an accessible, interactive and sustainable analytical tool.

2. Specific objectives

  1. Consolidate, harmonize and quality assure the food systems resilience data covering fourteen (14) years across the seven (7) IGAD Member States addressed in the 2024 report.
  2. Design and develop an interactive, user friendly dashboard that operationalizes the IGAD Food Systems Resilience Analysis Framework and visualizes resilience indicators, trends and cross country comparisons.
  3. Deploy the dashboard on IGAD infrastructure and ensure its interoperability with existing IGAD data systems and platforms.
  4. Build the capacity of IGAD staff to operate, update, maintain and further develop the dashboard beyond the assignment.

3. Minimum Consultant’s qualifications and experience requirements

  • The Consultant should have a Master Degree in Computer Science or ICT with demonstrated experience in building interactive dashboards and data visualizations; proficiency in modern visualization and web technologies; GIS/geospatial visualization capability an advantage.
  • The consultant should have at least 7 years demonstrated experience designing and developing interactive data dashboards or analytical web platforms, ideally in food security, climate, agriculture or resilience domains.
  • Proven experience consolidating and harmonizing multi country, multi-year datasets.
  • Prior work in Africa and, preferably, the IGAD/Horn of Africa region.
  • Demonstrated capacity building and knowledge transfer experience.
  • Have general experience relevant to the assignment (data platforms / dashboards; food security, climate or resilience analytics)
  • Specific experience developing interactive data dashboards and consolidating multi-country, multi-year datasets

 

4. The Consulting Services Contract is expected to be for a period of 150 Calendar Days from the date of contract signature.

5. The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites individuals to express their interest in providing the services. Interested individuals must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of Academic qualifications, and Professional Qualifications.

Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)-Djibouti

Request for Expression of Interest

 

(Consulting Services – Individual Consultant Selection)

 

Name of project: FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE PROGRAM FOR EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA)

 

Project No.: (P178566)

 

 Grant No: IDA-E 0820

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy for compiling baseline information on soil/fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region

Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567394-CS-INDV

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from International Development Agency (IDA) towards the cost of the Food systems resilience program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Grant to payments under this contract: Consultancy for compiling baseline information on soil/fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region

  1. Objectives of the Assignment

The main objectives of the assignment are:

  1. To Assess existing policy, institutional, financial and technical opportunities and gaps affecting fertilizer access and sustainable soil management.
  2. To map out the current status of soil health management initiatives, including: Soil fertility management, Soil conservation; Integrated Soil Fertility Management (ISFM), Climate-smart soil management, Regenerative agriculture, Organic nutrient management, Precision agriculture.
  3. Document available soil information systems including, Soil laboratories; Soil testing services
  4. To document best practices, innovations and success stories on sustainable soil and fertilizer management.
  5. Recommend directions for strengthening regional collaboration, policy harmonization and investment.
  1. Scope of the consulting services and specific tasks

The study will focus on the IGAD Region and Member states including Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Uganda.

The specific tasks will include: 

  1. Map out the existing soil and fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region
  2. Literature review and data collection from governments, research institutions, development partners and regional organizations
  3. Preparation of Data collection tool and Key informant interviews with relevant stakeholders;
  4. Conduct a Review of existing Regional and national policies including gap analysis and recommendations for harmonization and investment, strategies or guidelines, including cross border agreements between countries. Regional inventory of soil and fertilizer policies, fertilizer use and consumption and recommendation systems, Soil health status profile for each Member State; database of soil laboratories and information systems, regional best practices.
  5. Validation of compiled information with Member States

3. Minimum Consultant’s qualifications and experience requirements

  • The consultant should possess 5 years of experience in Agriculture, Soil Science, Agronomy, Plant Nutrition, Natural Resource Management and communication skills.
  • Clear understanding of Regional Policy processes and experience policy analyses.
  • Clear understanding of Good Agricultural Practices related to soil Health and Fertilizer use efficiency.
  • Experience in Integrated Soil Fertility Management, ISFM Practices.
  • Experience in IGAD Region Agro-ecology and Integrated Sustainable Land and Management
  • Good knowledge of African agricultural policy frameworks, including CAADP, the Africa Fertilizer and Soil Health Action Plan, and sustainable land management initiatives.
  • Good Communication, analytical and Reporting Skills.

4. The Consulting Services Contract is expected to be for a period of Six (6) calendar months from the contract commencement date.

5.The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites individuals to express their interest in providing the services. Interested individuals must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of Academic qualifications, and Professional Qualifications.

6. An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (Regulations).

7. Interested individuals may obtain further information at the address below from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday EAT).

Expression of interest shall be sent by e-mail by 20th of September, 2026 at 1700hours EAT to:procurement@igad.int copy: hassan.salah@igad.int , with subject line ‘‘FSRP- Consultancy for compiling baseline information on soil/fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region, CONTRACT NO-.: DJ-IGAD-567394-CS-INDV ’’.

Le pays est frappé depuis 2019 par trois chocs exogènes successifs celui lié au cyclone Kenneth en avril 2019, de la pandémie de la COVID-19 dès avril 2020 et la crise de l’énergie et alimentaire mondiale consécutive à la guerre en Ukraine.

Ces chocs ont impacté négativement le pouvoir d’achat des ménages Comoriens. L’augmentation des prix des hydrocarbures en début du mois de juin 2022, à savoir une hausse de 25% pour l’essence, 44% le Gasoil et 40% pour le pétrole (Kérozène), la hausse du transport à hauteur de 25%, la hausse de l’électricité et tant d’autres bien et service a créé un effet sur la hausse de prix de biens et services de consommation

Le Gouvernement des Comores a exprimé son souhait de pouvoir apporter une assistance financière aux ménages directement affectés par cette crise.

La proposition de réponse vise en particulier à protéger la population pauvre et vulnérable contre l’insécurité alimentaire induite par la flambée des prix en mobilisant entre autres les filets sociaux de sécurité.

A la demande du Gouvernement de l’Union des Comores, la Banque mondiale a accordé un Don de 30 millions USD pour financer le PROJET DE FILETS SOCIAUX DE SECURITE RESILIENTS ET REACTIFS AUX CHOCS (PFSS-RRC)

        PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES

Financement Groupe de la Banque mondiale : Crédits IDA n° 65750 & 78840-CI

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET N° CI-INS COTE D'IVOIRE-565978-CS-INDV

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET D’AUDIT POUR L’AUDIT COMPTABLE ET FINANCIER DU PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES AU TITRE DE L’EXERCICE 2026 ET DE L’AUDIT DE CLOTURE DU PROJET

 

           I. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

La République de Côte d’Ivoire bénéficie d’un crédit de 45 millions USD dans le cadre d’un financement global de 379 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour contribuer à l’harmonisation et au renforcement des systèmes statistiques dans sept pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest (Burkina Faso, Cap Vert, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Libéria, Sierra Leone et Togo).

Le projet vise à contribuer à une amélioration et une harmonisation des statistiques économiques et sociales dans la sous-région ouest-africaine.

Les activités du projet sont structurées sous trois composantes que sont :

1)       une composante régionale pour produire des outils harmonisés, collecter un ensemble de statistiques sociales, économiques et administratives de base tout en améliorant leur qualité, diffuser et faciliter l'utilisation des données, ainsi qu’améliorer l’environnement institutionnel au niveau de la gestion et de la capacité des ressources humaines ;

2)       une composante propre à chaque pays pour remédier aux lacunes qui ne sont pas nécessairement communes à tous les pays mais qui permettront aux Systèmes Statistiques Nationaux de tirer parti des activités régionales, par exemple en répondant aux besoins en matière d’infrastructures et de logiciels ; et

3)       une composante de gestion de projet pour surveiller et superviser les activités 1 et 2.

Le cadre institutionnel et organisationnel du Projet prévoit les organes suivants :

-         (i) un Comité de pilotage du Projet (CPP) ;

-         (ii) un Comité Technique ;

-         (iii) une Unité de Coordination du Projet (UCP) ayant en charge la gestion des ressources du projet et qui assurera la coordination globale des aspects administratifs et fiduciaires du projet à travers ses différentes composantes.

-         (iv) une Cellule de points focaux qui sont les responsables des activités représentant les structures du Projet

Le présent avis à manifestation d’intérêt est élaboré en vue de la sélection d’un cabinet d’audit pour la réalisation de l’audit comptable et financier au titre de l’exercice 2026 et de l’audit de clôture du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques (PHAS).

            II. OBJECTIFS DE LA MISSION

L’objectif de l’audit comptable et financier est de :

  • permettre d’exprimer une opinion professionnelle et indépendante sur la situation financière du Projet au titre du prêt à la fin de chaque exercice comptable y compris sur le compte désigné et les relevés de dépenses ;
  • s’assurer que les ressources mises à la disposition du Projet sont utilisées aux fins pour lesquelles elles ont été octroyées en vue de l’atteinte de l’Objectif de Développement du Projet ;
  • s’assurer que les états financiers, qui sont établis par le Projet sont élaborés de manière à rendre compte de manière sincère des transactions financières du Projet ;
  • procéder à l’examen et à l’évaluation du dispositif de contrôle interne adéquat ainsi qu’une documentation acceptable des transactions.

L’audit sera réalisé conformément aux Normes Internationales d’Audit (International Standard of Auditing) définies par l’International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) et comprendra tous les tests et les contrôles jugés nécessaires par l’Auditeur eu égard aux circonstances.

         III. RESULTATS ATTENDUS

  • Les résultats attendus de la mission sont :
  • réalisation de l’audit comptable et financier au titre de l’exercice 2026 ;
  • réalisation de l’audit de clôture du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques

            IV. DUREE DE LA MISSION

La mission d’audit sera exécutée sur une durée maximum de quarante-cinq (45) jours calendaires (y compris la remise du rapport final d’audit) à compter de la date de démarrage indiquée dans l’Ordre de Service qui sera notifié au consultant pour l’exercice concerné.

            V. TACHES ET RESPONSABILITES DU CABINET

L’auditeur s’assurera que :

  • toutes les ressources de la Banque Mondiale ont été employées conformément aux dispositions de l’Accord de financement dans un souci d’économie et d’efficience, et uniquement aux fins pour lesquelles elles ont été fournies ;
  • les fonds de contrepartie nationale (budget de l’Etat) ont été obtenus et employés conformément aux dispositions des accords de financement applicables, dans un souci d’économie et d’efficience, et uniquement aux fins pour lesquelles ils ont été fournis ;
  • les acquisitions des biens et services financés ont fait l’objet de marchés passés conformément aux dispositions des accords de financement applicables fondés sur les procédures de passation de marché de la Banque Mondiale et ont été proprement enregistrés dans les livres comptables ;
  • tous les dossiers, comptes et écritures nécessaires ont été tenus au titre des différentes opérations relatives au Projet (y compris les dépenses couvertes par des relevés de dépenses ou des rapports de suivi financier) ;
  • les Comptes Désignés sont gérés eu égard aux dispositions de l’accord de financement du Projet ;
  • traitement fiscal applicable aux rémunérations versées au personnel contractuel et aux consultants de l’Unité de Gestion du projet et autres consultants individuels ;
  • la gestion des fonds de contrepartie ou tout autre fonds de l’Etat décaissé dans le cadre de ce projet est conforme aux dispositions applicables au projet notamment le Décret 475 (Instruction 192 révisée) relatif aux modalités de gestion des projets financés par les PTFs et l’accord de financement.
  • Etc.

Les termes de référence peuvent être retirés en faisant une demande écrite à l’adresse : t.ourega@stat.plan.gouv.ci avec en copie phas@stat.plan.gouv.ci

          VI. PROFIL DU CABINET

Le Consultant doit être un Cabinet d’Audit et d’Expertise Comptable indépendant, faisant profession habituelle de réviser les comptes, régulièrement inscrit au Tableau d’un Ordre des Experts-Comptables reconnu au plan international par l’IFAC ou la FIDEF.

Il doit :

  • justifier d’au moins 5 ans d’expériences dans le domaine de l’audit comptable et financier des projets de développement ;
  • avoir audité les états financiers annuels d’au moins dix (10) projets financés par les Partenaires Techniques et Financiers (PTFs) ;
  • avoir réalisé l’audit des comptes d’au moins cinq (05) projets financés par la Banque mondiale ;
  • avoir une connaissance suffisante des dispositions administratives et réglementaires en Côte d’Ivoire ;
  • avoir une connaissance suffisante des normes internationales en matière d’audit financier et comptable.

N.B : L’expérience du cabinet est évaluée à partir des Attestations de Bonne Exécution (ABE) accompagnées des fiches projets.

 VII. CONSTITUTION ET DEPOT DES MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS

Les manifestations d’intérêt élaborées exclusivement en français, devront comprendre :

  1. une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt précisant l’objet de la manifestation d’intérêt adressée au Coordonnateur National du PHAS ;
  2. une fiche fournissant des informations sur la dénomination de la firme, sa nature juridique, sa création, etc. ;
  3. la preuve d’inscription du cabinet au tableau d’un Ordre des Experts-Comptables reconnu au plan international par l’IFAC ou la FIDEF ;
  4. la garantie de l’application des Normes International d’Audit ;
  5. des fiches de projet décrivant toutes les références relatives aux missions d’audit comptables et financiers (montant, date, durée, lieu, description des tâches réalisées, nature du client).

Les manifestations d’intérêts en français seront transmises physiquement ou électroniquement aux adresses ci-dessous indiquées au plus tard le jeudi 24/09/2026, à 10 heures GMT en cinq (05) exemplaires (01 original et 04 copies) sous plis fermés avec la mention : « Recrutement d’un cabinet d’audit pour l’audit comptable et financier du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques (PHAS) au titre de l’exercice 2026 et de l’audit de clôture du projet » ou par voie électronique : t.ourega@stat.plan.gouv.ci avec en copie phas@stat.plan.gouv.ci

Unité de Coordination du PHAS sise à Abidjan, Cocody Angré 7ème Tranche en face du projet filets sociaux productifs. Téléphone : (+225) 07 11 11 11 23

 

             VIII. PROCEDURE DE SELECTION

La procédure de recrutement de la firme sera conduite conformément à la méthode de Sélection au Moindre Coût (SMC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale de juillet 2016, révisé en septembre 2025.

Les services de consultant (“les Services”) comprennent pour les groupes de femmes : le ciblage, la structuration, le renforcement de capacité et Coaching ; le développement économique, l’appui aux business plans et l’accès au financement; la structuration organisationnelle, la gouvernance et la pérennisation; le suivi-évaluation, le reporting et la capitalisation. Ces services se dérouleront sur 30 mois. Les Termes de Référence peuvent être retirés auprès de l’Unité de Coordination du PACRI-MDK à Maroua à Pitoaré à côté du club KALIAO et à Yaoundé au bâtiment annexe du MINEPAT entre le carrefour Lissouck et le camp YEYAP.
  3.  Le Coordonnateur du Programme Spécial de Reconstruction et de Développement de la Région de l’Extrême Nord invite dès à présent les firmes/ONG/OSC admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant:
  • de l’existence égale: copie de l’acte de création (registre de commerce, attestation d’immatriculation, …), document justifiant que le soumissionnaire n’a pas de dette fiscale ;
  • qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services. Les critères de sélection d’une liste restreinte sont les suivants : expérience générale au cours des dix dernières années et expériences similaires (l'entrepreneuriat féminin, l'autonomisation économique des femmes ou l'accompagnement de femmes et de groupements féminins) au cours des dix dernières années. NB : Le Consultant devra obligatoirement fournir dans son offre pour chaque référence, les justificatifs de ses références en termes de contrat déjà réalisés avec succès (1ere page, 2e page ou toute page du contrat permettant d’avoir une meilleure compréhension de l’activité, page de signature des contrats, PV de recette technique ou attestation de bonne fin). Les références réalisées en zone rurale du septentrion du Cameroun constitueront des atouts.
  1. La liste restreinte comprendra cinq consultants au moins et huit consultants au plus.
  2. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.13, 3.15 et 3.16 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, révisé en septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés»), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.
  3. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.
  4. Les Consultants seront sélectionnés conformément aux dispositions de la Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement sous-décrite, sur la base du nombre total de projets pertinents et d’expérience présentés et justifiés pour les critères sus référencés.
  5. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau 07h30 à 15h30.
  6. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être fournies par écrit ou par mail à l’adresse ci-dessous aux heures ouvrables ou par email (fanch2010@yahoo.fr). Les termes de référence de cette mission sont disponibles et peuvent être retirés à L’Unité de Coordination du Programme Spécial de Reconstruction et du Développement de la Région de l’Extrême Nord ou envoyés par e-mail aux consultants intéressés, à leur demande; au plus tard quatorze (14) jours après publication à 15h30.

5Potential Bidders should note the provisions of Clause 4 of the Instructions to Bidders concerning eligibility and conflicts of interest. Any Bidder with a conflict of interest shall be deemed ineligible.

6The qualification requirements for Bidders include:

Business Scale

The Bidder’s average annual turnover for the most recent three years (2023–2025) shall be not less than RMB 10 million.

Contract Experience

Within the past ten years (from January 1, 2016 to the present), the Bidder, acting as a supplier, shall have successfully completed at least 15 contracts for the supply of laboratory instruments or equipment similar in nature and complexity to the products to be procured under this project, with the value of each individual contract being not less than RMB 3 million.

Not Applicable.

The Bidder’s audited annual financial statements for the most recent three years (2023, 2024, and 2025), including the balance sheets and income statements, shall demonstrate the Bidder’s sustained financial capacity and profitability. As a minimum requirement, the Bidder’s net assets, calculated as total assets less total liabilities, shall be positive in each of the three most recent financial years.

The Bidder shall have sufficient readily available liquid assets, lines of credit, and other financing resources to meet the cash flow requirements for contract performance, taking into account the Bidder’s other ongoing contractual commitments. The minimum requirement shall be RMB 4 million.

Litigation History

The total amount of any pending claims, arbitration proceedings, or other litigation shall not exceed 50% of the Bidder’s net assets.

Country: Eastern and Southern Africa (ESA)

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.: TF0C5097-3E

Assignment Title: Recruitment of Seychelles Country Focal Point

Reference No.: MZ-REPAIR-495524-CS-INDV-2

African Risk Capacity Limited (ARC Ltd.) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery (REPAIR) Programme and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services include the recruitment of a Country Focal Point for Seychelles to support the implementation of the REPAIR Programme at country level. The Country Focal Point will serve as the principal in-country liaison officer between ARC Ltd. and national stakeholders, including the Ministry of Finance and representatives of various distribution channels, support project execution and stakeholder communication, ensure alignment of in-country activities with World Bank Environmental and Social Safeguards, support monitoring, evaluation and reporting, and contribute to the achievement of the Programme Development Objective of strengthening financial and operational preparedness to respond rapidly to climate and other shocks. The assignment is full-time for an initial period of one (1) year, renewable annually subject to satisfactory performance.

ARC Ltd. now invites eligible individual consultants ("Consultants") who are nationals of Seychelles and/or hold a valid work permit authorising employment in Seychelles to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should submit documentation demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://arcltd.org/opportunities/

The Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025, and will be evaluated based on the criteria indicated below.

The shortlisting criteria are:

· At least a Master's degree (or equivalent) in Project Management, Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Risk Management, Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change, Development Studies, Public Administration, or a related field.

· A minimum of ten (10) years of relevant professional experience in project or programme management, development programmes, disaster risk management, climate resilience, humanitarian response, insurance, disaster risk financing, public sector programmes, or related fields.

· At least five (5) years of experience coordinating and collaborating with government institutions, development partners, donors, financial institutions, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), United Nations agencies, or other relevant stakeholders.

· Demonstrated knowledge and practical experience in one or more of the following areas: disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, disaster risk financing, resilience programmes, humanitarian response, insurance, sovereign disaster risk financing, or related fields.

· Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with government counterparts, development partners, donors, financial institutions, and other key stakeholders.

· Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, coordinate multiple activities and stakeholders, identify implementation challenges, and propose practical solutions in a dynamic working environment.

· Fluency in English and French, both written and spoken, is mandatory.

· The Consultant must be a national of Seychelles.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, first published in July 2016 and revised in September 2025, Seventh Edition ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. All inquiries should be sent to the following email address: procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int Expressions of Interest must be submitted by email to procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int no later than the 22nd of September 2026 at 17:00 hours (South Africa time). The email subject line should clearly state: “MZ-REPAIR-495524-CS-INDV-2 – Seychelles Country Focal Point".

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153)

Loan No/Credit No/Grant Number

GFPP Grant No. TF0D0728

Assignment Title

Gap analysis for National Control Center (NCC) with higher level of Variable Renewable Energy (VRE) systems, and propose initial design of the new NCC for EFL

Procurement Plan Ref Number

FJ-EFL-567211-CS-CQS

Reference No.

EOI-02/2026

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the costs of the Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

 

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise a comprehensive gap analysis of EFL's National Control Centre (NCC) at Vuda Back Road, Nadi, and the definition of an initial design and modernisation roadmap for a future NCC capable of securely operating the Fiji grid at high levels of variable renewable energy penetration. EFL is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, serving Vitilevu, Vanualevu, Ovalau and Taveuni. Demand on the main VLIS grid currently exceeds 213 MW and is expected to exceed 300 MW within ten years, while EFL's Renewable Energy Roadmap targets the installation of 165 MW of solar capacity and over 40 MW of battery energy storage within five years. The NCC's current infrastructure, systems and operating procedures must be assessed against this future state.

 

The Services will cover:

  • assessment of the current SCADA/EMS infrastructure, data acquisition and analytics capability, and communications infrastructure (telemetry, fibre/OPGW, microwave, backup systems), including latency, signal loss and failover readiness;
  • evaluation of operational processes and readiness, including SOPs for normal and emergency conditions, demand and generation forecasting, grid security studies (contingency analysis, load flow, voltage stability), AVR and load frequency control performance, management of distributed energy resources and low-inertia conditions, disaster recovery and black-start coordination;
  • review of grid code and regulatory compliance against international standards and good practice, and delivery of a reviewed grid code document;
  • assessment of cybersecurity for operational technology and IT, and of physical security at the main and backup control centres, against Critical Infrastructure Protection standards;
  • assessment of staffing levels, competencies, training, control room ergonomics and human factors;
  • assessment of environmental and social aspects, including energy efficiency, waste management, sustainable procurement, disability inclusion and gender-appropriate facilities;
  • preparation of a Gap Analysis Report (inception, draft and final) mapping current versus desired "to-be" states, categorised by risk level, with a prioritised modernisation roadmap, action plan, timelines and cost estimates; and
  • support to EFL to define a fit-for-purpose procurement strategy — including packaging and contract type — and to prepare the corresponding draft bidding documents.

 

The assignment requires desktop review, stakeholder consultations, site visits and physical inspection of the control room and backup facilities, and benchmarking against international best practice (e.g. IEEE, IEC, ENTSO-E).

 

Implementation period: the assignment is expected to be completed within a maximum of seven (7) months from contract signature. Expected start date: October 2026.

 

Terms of Reference:  The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window) and is also attached to this REOI as Appendix 1.

 

Energy Fiji Limited now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, latest’s edition, ("the Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.
