REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Title of Assignment: Owner’s Engineer

Name of Project: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Transformation (ASCENT)

Project ID: P513939

Implementing Agency: Ministry of Energy and Mining

Country: Kingdom of Lesotho

Contract Type: Time-based Contract

 

The Government of Lesotho has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation (ASCENT) Project. The ASCENT is being implemented by the Ministry of Energy and Mining (MoEM). One of the components of ASCENT is Component 1, titled “Increasing Access to On-Grid Electrification”. This component is the primary focus of this assignment. It finances expansion of the national distribution network and last-mile connections in targeted peri-urban and highland rural areas identified as least-cost grid electrification zones under the Lesotho's National Electrification Strategy (NES). Activities to be undertaken under Component 1 include construction of new Medium Voltage (MV) lines and Low Voltage (LV) distribution networks; installation of transformers, service drops, and prepaid meters; provision of ready boards for households unable to afford internal wiring costs; and reinforcement and upgrading of existing transformers to improve reliability and climate resilience. The component targets the connection of approximately 24,842 non-electrified households, businesses, and public facilities.

The Project Implementation Unit (PIU) is established within the MoEM and is supported by two Technical Units: the On-Grid Technical Unit and the Off-Grid Technical Unit, respectively tasked with implementing the off-grid and on-grid project activities. Working closely with the Lesotho Electricity Company (LEC), which is the state-owned utility responsible for the transmission and distribution of electricity nationwide, the On-Grid Technical Unit is specifically mandated to bear the primary responsibility for technical due diligence, land acquisition, and oversight of electrical works contractors under Component 1. Under the On-grid Technical Unit, the PIU intends to hire an individual consultant to provide support to the Project in managing and implementing of Component 1 of ASCENT project. This assignment is central to the successful achievement of the project.

 

 

 

Objectives and Scope of the Assignment

The objective of this assignment is to support the ASCENT PIU in the effective and efficient implementation of Component 1. The individual consultant will provide integrated support across three key areas: contracts management and coordination, review of designs prepared by LEC for the Project, and ad hoc supervision of civil and electrical works including quality assurance and control.

The consultant under the supervision of On-grid project engineers will work in close collaboration with the PIU team, LEC, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that project activities are delivered on time, with required quality, within budget, and in compliance with World Bank fiduciary, technical, and the applicable environmental and social (E&S) standards.

 

The Summary Scope of the Assignment

The assignment is structured around three core areas of support, covering both the design/procurement phase and the construction supervision phase of the project.

  • Project Management and Coordination Support
  • Support to Design Review
  • Support to Procurement Process
  • Support to Supervision of Works and Acceptance (Quality Assurance and Control)

   

Qualifications and Experience Requirements

 

  •  A university degree (minimum bachelor’s level) in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, or a closely related field. A master’s degree would be considered plus point in evaluation
  • A minimum of 10 years of professional experience in the power distribution projects, with demonstrated expertise in MV/LV network design, construction supervision, and project/contract management.
  • Proven experience in at least two similar assignments involving grid extension or rural electrification projects, preferably in Sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Strong familiarity with World Bank procurement procedures, experience in preparing tendering documents and managing works contracts.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and coordinate effectively with government counterparts, utilities, contractors, and development partners.
  • Proficiency in written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of Sesotho is an advantage.
  • Experience in the application of electrification design softwares such as Microstation, Reticmaster, or PowerOffice shall be an added advantage.

           

Recruitment Process and Contract Type

The selection method shall follow the World Bank’s Individual Consultant Selection method, and the procurement process shall be governed by the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers February 2025 (Sixth Edition). The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower. 

This is a time-based assignment. The consultant will be based in Maseru, Lesotho, with regular travel to project sites in the field as required. The Employer will provide the consultant with access to relevant project documents, data, and office space as needed. The initial contract will be signed for 1 year with 3 months’ probational period. The contract may be extended depending on the need and performance during the first year.

The incumbent shall be selected on the basis of their relevant experience, qualifications, and capability to carry out the assignment. Candidates shall be considered if they meet minimum relevant requirements which shall be determined by the Client on the basis of the nature and complexity of the assignment and assessed on the basis of academic background and relevant specific experience and, as appropriate, knowledge of local conditions such as national language, culture, administrative systems, and government organization.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 0800 to 1700 hours, local time.

 

Submission

Interested candidates must submit their expressions of interest with certified copies of their educational certificates in a single PDF format to the email addresses mentioned below on or before 25th September 2026 at 17H00. The subject of the email must be “Expression of Interest – Owner’s Engineer”. Hand delivered expressions of interest shall not be accepted.

 

Email addresses for submission and clarification requests:

120 Lancers Street, Maseru West

Assignment Title: FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT(S) FOR THE DESIGN & SUPERVISION FOR WATER INFRASTRUCTURE REPAIR.

The Lebanese Republic (hereinafter called “Borrower”) has received financing in the amount of 250 million US Dollars from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) (the “Bank”) toward the cost of the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP). The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), acting as the executing agency for and on behalf of the Government of Lebanon, intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of this loan to eligible payments under contracts for consulting services under Framework Agreements.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve engaging Design & Supervision Consultants under Framework Agreements for several contracts to repair, rehabilitate, and reconstruct damaged water infrastructure across Beirut & Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and South Lebanon. The Framework Agreements will be conducted under a Two-Stage Selection Process and the consulting services shall be across three core tasks:

  • Task 1: Engineering Studies, Data Validation, Topographic Surveys, Detailed Engineering Designs, and Preparation of Tender Documents (covering pumping stations, reservoirs, water networks/transmission lines repairs, and solar PV systems for water facilities).
  • Task 2: Assistance in Bid Evaluation and Award of Contracts.
  • Task 3: Supervision of Construction Works and Contract Administration (including environmental and social safeguards monitoring and defects liability period services).

The Framework Agreement will be signed for a duration of Thirty-Six (36) months with multiple qualified engineering consultancy firms. Specific assignments will be awarded as Call-Off contracts across distinct Call-Off Modules (ranging from slight to severe/full damage levels) on an as-needed basis.

The full version of the Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found on the CDR website at: https://www.cdr.gov.lb/Procurement.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultant Brochures may also be included in the submission.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Firm Legal Standing, Core Buiesness and Years of Experience:
  • Legal registration and authorization to operate in its country of incorporation, demonstrating financial soundness.
  • Legally established consulting firm (or lead partner in a Joint Venture of maximum 2 members) with a minimum of ten (10) years of experience in design and supervision services for water infrastructure projects.

 

 

       2. Specific Technical Experience:

  • Design: Completion of at least three (3) projects of similar nature and complexity within the last ten (10) years, involving detailed engineering design of water distribution networks, high-pressure transmission pipelines, and water facilities (e.g., reservoirs, pumping stations).
  • Supervision: Experience as Lead Engineer/Supervision Consultant of at least two (2) projects within the last ten (10) years involving construction supervision and contract management of water infrastructure.
  • Experience under international financing institutions (preferably World Bank standards and Guidelines) and familiarity with Lebanese technical/regulatory frameworks are considered as advantage.

 

      3. Technical and Managerial Capacity and a general Quality Management:

  • Submission of an accessible Key Experts pool available to the consulting firm.

Page Limit: The EOI submission shall be limited to twenty (20) pages maximum.

Please note that at this shortlisting stage: Technical and financial proposals are not requested. While the pool of available key experts will be considered, however specific Key Experts, if proposed for the assignment, will not be evaluated at shortlisting stage.  Request for clarifications on the REOI or TOR may not be replied to at this time, as the allocated time for submission of EOI does not permit for such exchanges.

The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting services” dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. 

Shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit their proposals, upon which a Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Least Cost Selection described in the “World Bank “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting services” dated February 2025 and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) project and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve serving as the primary focal point for site-level traffic safety management while directly assisting the PIU Coordinator in project administration, contract compliance, and tracking progress. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Country: Republic of Mozambique

Name of Project:  Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) PROGRAM

Grant number:    IDA-E0780

Job title: SRSEI Project Coordinator

Reference Number: MZ-PMU-561409-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve accountability for day-to-day implementation oversight of assigned PIU activities in the designated province(s), serving as the primary operational interface between field execution and the PCU. The PIU Coordinator will ensure that all components are effectively executed, and in a timely manner in accordance with the implementation plan.

The Project Coordinator will be required to work in close liaison with the PCU, ANE, INATRO and other stakeholders and in accordance with the Legal Agreements, and various approved project implementation manuals. A high degree of initiative and a pro-active and consultative approach will be required from the Project Coordinator in order to achieve the outcomes of this assignment. The expected duration of the assignment is 24 months. There will be a probationary period of 3 months from the date of signing the contract. The contract will be renewed upon satisfactory performance. The Project Coordinator is required to report to the Portfolio Coordinator at the CPU of the MTL

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work; (ii) a cover letter, no more than two pages long, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

The Project Coordinator should have the following minimum qualifications and skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field. 
  • At least Fifteen (15) years general working experience, of which least 10 years of progressive experience in civil works project management specifically for roads of at least 50 km or other infrastructure of similar complexity to the program
  • Experience in contract administration and management of consultants/contractors, including tracking deliverables, reviewing outputs, facilitating acceptance, and supporting invoice certification processes.
  • Experience  in contract management based on FIDIC, including prevention and/or mitigation of claims that involve financial losses to the Employer.
  • Knowledge of the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), in particular ESS1, ESS2, ESS4, and ESS5..
  • Demonstrated ability to lead or coordinate teams and to work effectively with government counterparts at central and provincial levels, private sector, communities and other stakeholders.
  • Working experience in Mozambique.
  • Fluency in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken)

Desirable requirements

  • Master degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field.
  • Familiarity with OPBRC and/or Design Build contract structures.
  • Familiarity with the latest project management techniques and tools is essential. Having professional accreditation for Project Management from a recognized body.
  • Proven experience coordinating procurement processes and supporting preparation of TORs/specifications/bidding documents, and following procurement steps through contract award.
  • Demonstrated experience in GBV/SEA/SH-sensitive programme environments.
  • Good knowledge of BOQ interpretation, Detailing, Specifications, Public Procurement, Project/Contract management, Quality Control and dispute resolution.
  • Experience in the road safety standards.
  • Familiarity with national policies, procedures, and government processes.
  • Experience coordinating field implementation and undertaking regular site visits, including documenting progress, risks, quality and safeguards issues.
  • Familiarity with STEP (World Bank's procurement tracking platform) and experience with e-SISTAFE or equivalent government financial management systems.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Country: The People's Republic of China
Project Name: IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

Loan No.: 9213-CN

Assignment Name: Project Publicity

Contract No.: GDCS-030

Bidding No.: 0733-26083817

The Government of the People's Republic of China has received a loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to improve food safety management at the national and sub-national levels and to reduce food safety risks in selected value chains. The project is being implemented by the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, Guangdong Province, and Shandong Province (Yantai City).

As part of the China Food Safety Project, Guangdong Province is responsible for the implementation of the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project. The project comprises four sub-components: Food Safety Supervision Process, Institution Building and Regulatory Performance, Whole Value Chain Food Safety Control, and Project Implementation Support.

This Contract, namely the Project Publicity Contract (Contract No.: GDCS-030), utilizes World Bank loan funds to procure a Project Publicity Consulting Advisor (hereinafter referred to as the 'Consulting Advisor') to carry out promotional activities for the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project. Through a matrix-based publicity strategy across short video platforms, newspapers, official social media accounts, and news media, the project will showcase and promote its implementation outcomes and achievements from multiple perspectives and through diverse channels.

Terms of Reference (TOR) for the Consulting Services on the Project Publicity under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

 

To promote the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project and showcase its implementation outcomes, the Guangdong Center for Agricultural Product Quality and Safety (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) intends to engage a Project Publicity Consulting Advisor to provide professional publicity services for the project

 

I.Project Background

Agricultural product quality and safety are critical issues of national importance that directly affect people's livelihoods. In recent years, national authorities have successively introduced policy documents such as the Regulations for the Implementation of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and the 14th Five-Year Plan for National Agricultural Green Development, explicitly proposing the establishment of a comprehensive quality and safety management system spanning the entire supply chain 'from farm to table'.

As part of the China Food Safety Project, Guangdong Province is responsible for the implementation of the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project. The project comprises four sub-components: Food Safety Supervision Process, Institution Building and Regulatory Performance, Whole Value Chain Food Safety Control, and Project Implementation Support.

II.Objectives of the Consulting Services

By engaging a Consulting Advisor, this project aims to carry out comprehensive publicity activities for the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, showcase its implementation outcomes, and enhance the project's visibility and public awareness.

III.Scope of Services

The Consulting Advisor shall provide end-to-end services for this project. The main scope of services includes:

(I) Formulate the Publicity Plan

Develop a comprehensive publicity plan for the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project.

(II) Convergent Media Publicity

1.Provincial-level Media Coverage: Conduct regular publicity on provincial-level media platforms covering specific project activities, events, and outcomes. A minimum of ten (10) news reports shall be published.

2.New Media Campaigns: Launch a series of promotional campaigns on new media platforms. Produce and publish a minimum of fifty (50) short videos on platforms such as Douyin and WeChat Channels (Shipinhao). Content Requirement: At least five (5) of these videos must focus on food safety risk communication. Duration Requirement: Each video must be no less than forty (40) seconds in length. Performance KPIs: Each published video must achieve a minimum of two thousand (2,000) views and five hundred (500) likes.

3.Promotional Videos: Shoot, produce, and edit high-definition (HD) promotional videos for the project to introduce its activities and showcase its outcomes. A minimum of five (5) videos shall be produced, with each video being no less than two (2) minutes in duration.

4.Graphic and Text Promotional Articles: Write a minimum of twenty (20) graphic and text articles related to project activities. At least five (5) of these articles must focus on food safety risk communication. The articles shall be reposted on a minimum of three (3) official social media accounts (WeChat Official Accounts), and each published article must achieve a minimum of one thousand (1,000) views.

(III) Live-streaming Promotion: Conduct live-streaming coverage of project trainings and events (including both photo live-streaming and video live-streaming). Video Live-streaming: A minimum of three (3) sessions shall be conducted, with each lasting no less than one (1) hour. At least one (1) of these sessions must be dedicated to an event focusing on food safety risk communication. Photo Live-streaming: A minimum of two (2) sessions shall be conducted, providing no less than one hundred (100) high-definition (HD) photos per session.

(IV) Posters, Brochures, and Other Promotional Materials: Design, produce, print, and distribute promotional materials such as posters and brochures related to project activities. Posters: A minimum of thirty (30) promotional posters shall be designed. Brochures: Brochures may be revised based on existing project brochures, newly designed, or printed according to specific requirements.

(V) Conceptual Promotion: Conduct conceptual promotion at designated venues of the Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Center (Guangdong Green Food Development Center). Regularly update the content of visual and text display boards at these venues.

(VI) Event Photography and Videography: Provide photography, videography, and photo collection and processing services for at least five (5) important events, including visits and supervision missions by World Bank experts, as well as project field research.

(VII) Publicity Outcomes Collection, Summary Report Drafting, and Project Acceptance Assistance: Be responsible for organizing and compiling data, including collecting publicity outcomes across various platforms and compiling statistical data such as views and watch counts. Draft activity summaries and publicity outcome reports, and assist the Client with project acceptance and verification.

Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a reçu un don de 92 millions de dollar USD de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique dont l’objectif de développement est d’accroitre l’accès à l’internet haut débit en particulier pour les communautés mal desservies et d’améliorer la capacité du gouvernement à gérer les ressources plus efficacement et fournir les services publics par voie numérique.

Il a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du contrat pour « recrutement d’un cabinet pour l’assistance technique à la mise en place d’un système de management de la qualité conforme à la norme ISO 9001 :2015 au sein du SETIC ».

L’objectif global est d’accompagner le Secrétariat Exécutif des Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication (SETIC) dans la conception, la mise en œuvre, le déploiement, l'appropriation, l'évaluation et l'amélioration continue d'un Système de Management de la Qualité (SMQ) conforme aux exigences de la norme ISO 9001:2015, afin de renforcer durablement la qualité, l'efficacité, la fiabilité, la traçabilité et la performance de ses services, d'améliorer la satisfaction des parties intéressées et de préparer l'institution à l'obtention de la certification ISO 9001:2015.

Plus spécifiquement, il s’agit de :

  1. Réaliser un diagnostic organisationnel du SETIC et une analyse des écarts (Gap Analysis) entre les pratiques existantes et les exigences de la norme ISO 9001: 2015.
  2. Déterminer et faire valider le contexte de l'organisation, le périmètre du SMQ, les enjeux internes et externes ainsi que les parties intéressées pertinentes et leurs besoins et attentes.
  3. Identifier et analyser les exigences légales, réglementaires, contractuelles, normatives et techniques applicables aux activités du SETIC.
  4. Élaborer, en concertation avec la Direction, la politique qualité, les objectifs qualité, les indicateurs de performance et le cadre de gouvernance du SMQ, en cohérence avec les missions du SETIC et les objectifs du Projet d'Appui aux Fondations de l'Économie Numérique (PAFEN).
  5. Identifier, cartographier, documenter, standardiser, optimiser et déployer l'ensemble des processus de pilotage, des processus métiers et des processus supports, ainsi que leurs interactions.
  6. Définir les responsabilités, autorités, mécanismes de coordination et modalités de pilotage nécessaires au fonctionnement efficace du SMQ.
  7. Élaborer le système documentaire du SMQ comprenant notamment les procédures, les fiches processus, les instructions de travail, les formulaires, les modèles d'enregistrements et toute autre information documentée requise par la norme.
  8. Concevoir et mettre en œuvre une approche fondée sur les risques et les opportunités, incluant leur identification, leur évaluation, leur traitement et leur suivi.
  9. Mettre en place un dispositif de mesure et de suivi de la performance des processus reposant sur des indicateurs pertinents, des tableaux de bord et des mécanismes réguliers d'analyse.
  10. Mettre en place un système de gestion des non-conformités, des réclamations, des actions correctives, des actions d'amélioration et des retours d'expérience.
  11. Développer les compétences du personnel à travers des actions de sensibilisation, de formation et de transfert de compétences, notamment au profit des pilotes de processus, des responsables qualité et des auditeurs internes.
  12. Accompagner le SETIC dans la planification et la réalisation d'un cycle complet d'audits internes conformément aux lignes directrices de la norme ISO 19011.
  13. Assister la Direction dans la préparation et la tenue de la revue de direction, ainsi que dans le suivi des décisions et actions qui en découlent.
  14. Accompagner la conduite du changement afin de favoriser l'appropriation du SMQ par l'ensemble du personnel et d'assurer sa pérennisation.
  15. Réaliser un pré-audit (audit à blanc), élaborer un plan d'actions de levée des écarts éventuels et préparer le SETIC à l'audit de certification ISO 9001: 2015, sans créer de conflit d'intérêts avec l'organisme certificateur.

La durée indicative de la mission est de huit (8) mois, soit trente-deux (32) semaines, à compter de la notification de l’ordre de service. Le cabinet proposera une charge en jours-experts cohérente avec sa méthodologie et garantira une présence suffisante sur site durant le diagnostic, les ateliers, le déploiement, les audits internes et la revue de direction.

La mission se déroulera principalement à Bujumbura, dans les locaux du SETIC et du PAFEN, ainsi que sur les sites techniques concernés. Certaines tâches de préparation pourront être menées à distance après accord préalable, sans réduire les obligations de transfert de compétences ni la disponibilité des experts clés.

Les Termes de référence peuvent être téléchargés sur le site du PAFEN : https://pafen.gov.bi/appels-doffres/  ou obtenus aux adresses mentionnées ci-dessous.

L’Unité de Gestion du PAFEN invite les consultants (firmes)/institutions spécialisés, ayant une expérience et expertise dans le déploiement et le suivi des projets de déploiements de réseaux de télécommunications/TIC intéressés par la présente mission à fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils disposent des qualifications requises et de l'expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

Critères d’établissement de la liste restreinte :  

  • Etre légalement constitué et justifier d’au moins dix (10) années d’expérience générale en conseil organisationnel, management de la qualité ou domaines connexes ;
  • Justifier d’au moins cinq (3) missions achevées de mise en place ou d’amélioration d’un SMQ ISO 9001, dont au moins deux (2) ayant conduit à une certification ;
  • Avoir réalisé au moins une (1) mission similaire dans une administration publique, une agence gouvernementale, un opérateur d’infrastructure ou une organisation fournissant des services numériques critiques ;

Pour être acceptables, les références doivent indiquer le projet, bailleur de fonds, l’année de réalisation, et le montant du contrat. Les références seront soutenues par des copies des contrats et des certificats de bonne fin de mission.

Les Experts clé ne sont pas évalués au stade de la présélection stade.

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.15, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de novembre 2020 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêt).

En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques sur les conflits d’intérêts liées à cette mission comme énoncés au paragraphe 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

Les consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement solidaire (joint-venture) et / ou d’un accord de sous-traitant. Dans le cas d'un groupement solidaire (joint-venture), tous les partenaires du groupement solidaire (joint-venture) seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

Un consultant sera sélectionné par la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

Name of Project:  Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2)

Grant number:    IDA-E4810

Job title: Senior Economist

Reference Number: MZ-MTL-564463-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) project and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve provision of high-level economic and financial advisory services to the PMU and the Ministry of Transport and Logistics. The core objective of the assignment is to strengthen the Government's capacity to assess, negotiate, and manage the economic performance of transport and logistics corridor concessions in a manner that maximises sovereign value capture, ensures macro-fiscal sustainability, and aligns with international standards of regulatory best practice.

The Senior Economist will engage the National Institute of Statistics (INE) to prepare the future transport and logistic satellite account to capture regularly the contribution of the sector in the gross domestic product (GDP). There will be a probationary period of 3 months from the date of signing the contract. The contract will be renewed upon satisfactory performance. The SE will report directly to the Project Coordinator.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address provided below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work and (ii) a cover letter, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

The criteria for selecting the consultant are:

a) A Master's degree or higher in Economics, Finance, Business Administration, International Banking, or a related discipline from a recognised university.

b) A minimum of 15 years of progressive professional experience in economics, finance, investment banking, or financial advisory roles, with demonstrated exposure to capital markets, regulatory environments, and financial governance at a senior level.

c) Demonstrated expertise in macroeconomic and financial modelling, with ability to develop quantitative analyses of corridor economics, concession financial structures, and fiscal risk.

d) Strong understanding of regulatory frameworks governing infrastructure concessions and public-private partnerships, as well as familiarity with prudential and fiscal governance frameworks applicable to government-held infrastructure assets.

e) Familiarity with World Bank operational procedures, including guidelines applicable to advisory and analytical assignments under Investment Project Financing.

f) Knowledge of the economic and institutional context of Mozambique, including the transport sector, public finance framework, and macroeconomic environment

g) Fluency in English is required, as the majority of analytical outputs and development partner communications will be produced in English.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For more information, please visit the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Submissions of Interest in Portuguese and English must be sent in writing to the address below (by e-mail only) by 15:00 hours on September 30, 2026, local time, CAT/UTC +2.

 

Ministry of Transport and Logistics,

Attention:Portfolio Coordinator

The Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Flood System Resilience Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds Consulting service for Supervision and Contract administration of compressive National laboratory construction

Objective:

This service is required to provide necessary service/support to the implementing agency, i.e., MoA in contract administration and construction supervision aspects for Establishing Comprehensive (Plant Protection, Seed Quality, Pesticide and Health Regulatory) Laboratory, so that the following major objectives shall be achieved:

  • Consultant shall provide engineering expert service in supervision of pre-construction, construction and post-construction phase of the project implementation activities carried out by the Contractors ensuring complete compliance with the drawings, technical specifications and various stipulations contained in the Contract Documents.
  • The service shall ensure the suitability/accuracy of quality construction and transparent project execution.
  • The service shall mitigate/resolve probable technical problems associated with the project and hence accelerate project execution.
  • The service shall ensure technically sound project implementation and contract administration.
  • To ensure safety during construction and adherence to all requirements under the Contract..

The scope of this assignment is to provide contract administration and construction works supervision services with the duties and responsibilities stipulated in the General Conditions of Contract for Construction Works. During the performance of the contract, the service provider is accountable to the employer/MoA and will report to MoA as per the contract with MoA. Prior to the start of activities, the service provider will prepare and submit for approval a detailed methodology and work plan for the implementation of the assignment .The  detail will be included in the Term of Reference.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                       Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:        REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO DEVELOP THE NATIONAL STRATEGY FOR DEVELOPMENT OF STATISTICS (NSDS) OF SOUTH AFRICA- BW-SADC-563161-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/460

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 9 September 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to coordinate and compile a National Strategy for the Development of Statistics (NSDS) for South Africa, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title             :  Individual Consultancy to Develop the National Strategy for Development of Statistics (NSDS) of South Africa (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  180 Calendar Days

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this consultancy is to support National Statistical offices (NSOs) on strategic and policy aspects pertaining to Official Statistics to strengthen governance and provide strategic direction ensuring fulfillment of its mandate in the development process at national and international level.

 

  1. Specific objectives

 

The specific objective of this consultancy is to develop a draft NSDS for South Africa as a guiding policy framework for coordination and implementation of statistics in support of national priorities and responsive to regional, continental and global agendas. The NSDS also need to cater for specific issues such as advocacy, communication, gender mainstreaming, cybersecurity, results-based framework, innovative data sources and others relevant.

 

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following results in the following as part of drafting the NSDS:

 

  1. Assessment and review of the existing policy and strategic frameworks identifying gaps and challenges amongst others with a defined and well-structured stakeholders engagement plan;

ii.       Identification of specific and impactful recommendations with justification for implementation towards drafting of the NSDS and its strategic focus areas and discussion within the governance structure for consideration; and

iii.      Detailed explanation of the strategic focus areas with a results-based monitoring & evaluation framework aligned to national and international priorities/commitments.

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant expert and should be an expert in strategic and policy formulation in Official Statistics.  The specific profile is provided below:

 

Qualifications and Skills

 

    • A minimum of a Degree in Statistics, Economics or related field. A Master’s Degree those having a PhD in the same field shall be an added advantage.

 

General Professional Experience

 

    • The Expert Must have at least ten (10) years of experience in statistical coordination of statistical systems at the highest level.

 

Specific Professional Experience

 

    • At least 5 years of experience of leading a statistics department at national, regional, continental or global level;
    • Demonstrated experience in at least 2 exercises of coordinating the development and implementation, of policy frameworks guiding statistical functions in statistics such as NSDS and related;
    • Demonstrated Experience on undertaking high-level activities pertaining to advocacy, gender mainstreaming, communication, innovative data sources, cybersecurity and applying results-based monitoring & evaluation within the national statistical system.
  2. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 180 Calander Days.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate for visa entry in South Africa, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment may involve traveling to Pretoria, South Africa.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Wednesday, 23rd September 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank and other Development Partners toward the cost of ETOL and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting service intended duration is for Two (2) months.

  1. Objectives of the assignment

The objectives of the IPA will be to:

  1. Review the procurement, contracting, and implementation processes and timeliness and appropriateness of awards for a sample of contracts under ETOL, to confirm their consistency with the agreed procedures. And also review the implementation status of agreed Procurement Program Action Plans.
  2. Seek a professional opinion on compliance by the procurement processes with the general principle of economy and efficiency, equal opportunities, transparency and verify technical compliance, physical completion and price competitiveness of each contract in the selected representative sample of contracts;
  3. Review the capacity of implementing agencies (MoE and Regional Education Bureaus) in handling procurement efficiently, comment on the quality of procurement and contracting, and identify reasons for delays, if any, and overall how procurement management facilitates program implementation; 
  4. Identify any indicators of questionable standards of ethics in the procurement management and oversight environment that make the processes vulnerable to fraud and corruption or collusive and obstructive practices, and report any suspicious cases; and
  5. Recommend actions needed to improve programme procurement performance in light of deficiencies.
  1. Scope of the Procurement Audit

The Independent Procurement Audit will cover all implementing agencies (IAs) and sample contracts under the ETOL Program (from all implementing agencies). The number of IAs in which the IPA will be conducted shall be as follows:

  • MoE:                                                                      One Office
  • EAES:                                                                    One Office
  • MOF:                                                                      One Office
  • Regional Education Bureaus:                                12 Offices
  • City Administration Education Bureaus: Two Offices
  • Total    17 Implementing Agencies (IAs)

To attain the specific objectives, the consultant will carry out the review in four stages as outlined below, under the supervision of the ETOL National Programme Coordination Office at the Ministry of Education (MoE) which is responsible for coordinating this assignment.

       SELECTION D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) INDIVIDUEL(LE) NATIONAL(E), BIBLIOTHÉCAIRE DE FORMATION, CHARGÉ(E) DE LA CRÉATION D’UN FONDS DE LECTURE DÉDIÉ À LA SANTÉ SEXUELLE ET REPRODUCTIVE DANS LES BIBLIOTHÈQUES SCOLAIRES

I.    CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

Le Gouvernement de Côte d’Ivoire a reçu un financement conjoint de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA-Banque mondiale) et du Partenariat Mondial pour l’Éducation (GPE) pour la mise en œuvre du Programme de Renforcement du Système Éducatif de Base (PRSEB). Ledit financement s’élève à 425,35 millions de dollars (US$). Ce programme utilise un mécanisme de financement axé sur les résultats concrets, tout en intégrant les réformes des États Généraux de l’Éducation Nationale et de l’Alphabétisation (EGENA) pour créer une école plus juste et inclusive.

Cependant, la santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR) freine le maintien des filles à l’école, comme en témoignent les 4 266 grossesses scolaires enregistrées en 2024-2025, les mariages précoces et le manque d’informations fiables. Ce déficit est renforcé par les tabous socioculturels et l’absence totale d’ouvrages dédiés dans les bibliothèques scolaires, ce qui pousse les jeunes vers des canaux informels à risque.

Pour y remédier, la Direction de l’Égalité et de l’Équité du Genre (DEEG) du Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de l’Enseignement Technique (MENAET) souhaite transformer les bibliothèques scolaires existantes en espaces d’information fiables et discrets sur la SSR.

C’est pourquoi, les présents Termes de Référence (TDR) sont produits en vue de sélectionner un(e) consultant(e) individuel(e) national(e), bibliothécaire de formation, pour conduire cette mission dans les établissements secondaires bénéficiaires du Paquet d’Appui Minimum Favorable pour la Rétention des Filles au Collège.

II. OBJECTIF GÉNÉRAL DE LA MISSION

L’objet général de la mission est de fournir au MENAET un catalogue de ressources documentaire, un fonds de lecture fonctionnel consacré à la santé sexuelle et reproductive dans le respect des normes de bibliothéconomie et des orientations nationales en matière d’éducation et de santé.

III. OBJECTIFS SPÉCIFIQUES DE LA MISSION

De manière plus spécifique, le ou la consultant(e) individuel(le) aura pour mission de :

  • établir un diagnostic de la disponibilité des ressources documentaires sur la SSR dans les bibliothèques scolaires ciblées ;
  • recenser et cataloguer les ressources documentaires existantes sur la SSR, en leur appliquant un système de classification exploitable par les gestionnaires de bibliothèque ;
  • sélectionner, sur la base de critères scientifiques, pédagogiques, culturels et financiers, les ouvrages et supports à intégrer au fonds de lecture ;
  • élaborer à l’attention du personnel chargé de l’animation de la bibliothèque dans les établissements ciblées, un guide très simplifié de gestion du fonds (classement, prêt, conservation) ;
  • élaborer des messages pour sensibiliser la communauté éducative pour garantir l’utilisation effective et durable du fonds documentaire.

IV. RÉSULTATS ATTENDUS DE LA MISSION

Au terme de la mission, les résultats suivants sont attendus :

  • un diagnostic de la disponibilité des ressources documentaires sur la SSR dans les bibliothèques scolaires des établissements bénéficiaires est réalisé ;
  • un répertoire catalogué des ressources documentaires existantes sur la SSR (ouvrages, guides, bandes dessinées, supports numériques) est élaboré, classé selon un système de classification adapté ;
  • une liste nationale des ouvrages et supports prioritaires à acquérir est validée, avec spécifications techniques et quantités par établissement ;
  • un guide simplifié pratique de gestion du fonds documentaire est disponible ;
  • une banque de messages pour sensibiliser les communautés éducatives est sensibilisés et outillés pour assurer l’appropriation et la pérennité du dispositif.

V.    LIVRABLES

Le (la) consultant(e), choisi(e), produira les livrables suivants :

  • Livrable(s) 01 : rapport de démarrage présentant la méthodologie, les outils de diagnostic et le chronogramme.
  • Livrable(s) 02 : rapport de diagnostic technique des bibliothèques scolaires, établissement par établissement, validé par la DEEG.
  • Livrable(s) 03 : répertoire catalogué et classé des ressources documentaires existantes ; grille et rapport d’évaluation.
  • Livrable(s) 04 : liste nationale validée des ouvrages et supports à acquérir, par établissement.
  • Livrable(s) 05 : guide pratique de gestion et de pérennisation du fonds documentaire ; note de sensibilisation des communautés éducatives.
  • Livrable(s) 06 : compte rendu de l’atelier ; versions validées du répertoire catalogué, de la liste nationale et du guide de gestion.
  • Livrable(s) 07 : rapport final de la consultance.

VI.   PROFIL DU/DE LA CONSULTANT(E) INDIVIDUEL(LE) 

Le profil recherché est celui d’un(e) bibliothécaire confirmé(e). Le ou la consultant(e) doit respecter les critères ci-dessous :

  • être titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau Bac+3 minimum (Master ou équivalent) en bibliothéconomie, sciences de l’information et de la documentation critère éliminatoire) ;
  • justifier d’une expérience générale d’au moins dix (10) années ;
  • justifier d’au moins sept (07) années d’expérience professionnelle en gestion de bibliothèque, centre de documentation ou service d’archives, décomptées à partir de l’obtention du diplôme requis ;
  • avoir conduit ou participé, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, à au moins trois (03) missions de diagnostic, de catalogage ou de constitution de fonds documentaires, dont le nombre exact doit être précisé et justifié dans le CV ;
  • justifier d’au moins deux (02) années d’expérience dans le système éducatif ivoirien ou dans un contexte de bibliothèque scolaire comparable en Afrique de l’Ouest.
  • avoir réalisé au moins une (01) mission portant sur des ressources documentaires en santé, éducation à la vie familiale ou santé sexuelle et reproductive.

VII. DURÉE DE LA MISSION ET CALENDRIER

La mission est prévue pour une durée de trente (30) jours étalés sur soixante-dix (70) jours.

VIII. PROCÉDURE POUR LA SOUMISSION DES MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊTS

Le ou la consultant(e) sera choisi(e) conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), édition de septembre 2025 et relatif à l’acquisition de Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants.

La Sélection du Consultant Individuel sera fondée sur les qualifications et l’expérience du Consultant en rapport avec la mission. Le Consultant individuel sera sélectionné parmi ceux ayant répondu à l’AMI.

Le dossier de soumission devra être composé de :

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêts dûment signée ;
  • Un Curriculum Vitae détaillé indiquant clairement les qualifications et expériences similaires ou pertinentes ;
  • Une copie des diplômes mentionnés dans le Curriculum Vitae (CV) ;
  • Une copie de(s) certificat(s) ou attestation(s) de travail ou une attestation d’exécution d’études ou missions similaires qui justifient des expériences et qualifications figurant dans le Curriculum Vitae (CV).

Les manifestations d’intérêt comportant des informations de nature financière seront rejetées.

La date limite pour le dépôt des manifestations d’intérêts est prévue pour le 23 septembre 2026 à 11 heures précises. L’enveloppe du Consultant Individuel devra porter la mention « AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊTS N° 023CI/PRSEB-PROJET/IDA-2026 – SELECTION D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) INDIVIDUEL(LE) NATIONAL(E), BIBLIOTHÉCAIRE DE FORMATION, CHARGÉ(E) DE LA CRÉATION D’UN FONDS DE LECTURE DÉDIÉ À LA SANTÉ SEXUELLE ET REPRODUCTIVE DANS LES BIBLIOTHÈQUES SCOLAIRES »

Les manifestations d’intérêts devront être soumises en français et en cinq (05) exemplaires don’t un (1) original et quatre (04) copies (le tout dans une grande et même enveloppe) et déposées sous plis fermé à l’adresse ci-dessous ou transmis par DHL, CHRONOPOSTE, FEDEX, etc.

Les soumissions par voie électronique ne seront pas acceptées.

Les manifestations d’intérêts seront ouvertes en présence du Comité d’évaluation et des représentants des soumissionnaires présents, à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le même jour le 23 septembre 2026 à 11 heures 30 minutes.

AVIS D’APPEL A CANDIDATURE POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DE DEUX (02) STAGIAIRES EN COMPTABILITE DU PROJET EDUCATION A LA COORDINATION NATIONALE

Date de l’avis : 09 Septembre 2026

Financement Projet N° P507220

Don N°E4100-KM

D’une manière générale, l'Union des Comores à travers le Ministère de l’Education Nationale, de l’Enseignement, de la Recherche Scientifique, de la Formation et de l’Insertion Professionnelle s’associe et participe à l’Approche programmatique multiphase (APM) pour promouvoir des méthodes innovantes pour favoriser l’apprentissage en Afrique de l’est et australe. L’APM proposée, intitulée « Advancing Innovative Methods to Promote Learning » (AIM4Learning) ou Favoriser des méthodes innovantes pour promouvoir l’apprentissage, intègre des approches résolument nouvelles pour offrir une meilleure éducation aux élèves.

Cependant, l’Union des Comores a subi ces dernières années des chocs et des perturbations qui ont fortement impacté le système éducatif du pays, accentué les pertes d’apprentissages, les profondes inégalités scolaires et les risques d’exclusion scolaire des groupes les plus vulnérables. Il est nécessaire de rétablir et sauvegarder l’éducation en tant que droit fondamental, vecteur de développement, facteur de réduction de la pauvreté et levier puissant pour la paix, la résilience aux changements climatiques et au développement durable.

C’est ainsi que le Gouvernement comorien a obtenu un Don de l’Association International de Développement (IDA) et du Fonds du Partenariat mondial pour l’éducation équivalent à 23,7 millions de dollars pour répondre aux besoins du pays en matière d’amélioration et du renforcement de l’éducation pour l’amélioration des Résultats en Matière de Capital Humain aux Comores.

Il est prévu qu’une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce Don sera utilisée pour effectuer le paiement à titre du contrat portant « Recrutement de deux (02) stagiaires en Comptabilité du Projet Education à la Coordination Nationale ».

Les Stagiaires seront recrutés Conformément au « Règlement de Passation des Marchés dans le Cadre du Financement de Projets d’investissements (FPI) Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants », 7ème Edition- Septembre 2026.

La méthode de sélection est la « Sélection de Consultants Individuels (SCI) ».

Tous les consultants intéressés sont priés de retirer les Termes de Référence (TDR) au site du projet : pfss-comores.org

Conditions de candidature pour le stage

Les conditions requises sont les suivantes :

  • Nationalité comorienne,
  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de grandes écoles au minimum de Bac+3 en gestion ou diplôme équivalent ;
  • Avoir une maîtrise du français (écrit, oral)
  • Expérience professionnelle non requise,
  • Connaître les outils informatiques de base (Word et Excel),
  • Avoir de bonnes compétences en communication orale et écrite. La maîtrise de l'anglais sera un avantage.

Composition des dossiers de candidature :

Le dossier à soumettre sont les suivants :

  • Lettre de motivation adressée au Coordinateur du projet REHEMA ;
  • Curriculum vitae détaillé et actualisé ;
  • Copie du ou des diplômes et attestations de formation pertinents ;
  • Attestations ou certificats de stage ou d’expérience, le cas échéant ;
  • Toute autre pièce jugée nécessaire dans le cadre de l’avis de recrutement...

Les dossiers de candidatures peuvent être déposées au Secrétariat de la Coordination nationale ou dans les Bureaux Régionaux du PFSS à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous au plus tard le Mardi 22 Septembre 2026 à 11 heures 30 (heure locale) avec la mention suivante :

« Recrutement de deux (02) stagiaires en Comptabilité du Projet Education à la Coordination Nationale »

Pour toutes informations complémentaires, veuillez consulter les Termes de Références (TDR) dans le site Web : pfss-comores.org/ www.pfss-comores.org

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D'INTERETS (SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS : SELECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS)

Pays

: République du Burundi

Nom du Projet 

: Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine (PRU) 

Numéro de Don

: IDA Nº E3520

N° du projet               

: P177146 

Titre de la mission

Termes de référence pour le recrutement d’un cabinet/firme pour l’élaboration des études d’impact environnemental et social ( EIES) des infrastructures à faible regret et audit environnemental et social du mur en gabion et   des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation de la station de pompage d’eau de la Regideso

 

 

N° de référence (selon le Plan de Passation de Marchés dans STEP)

: BI-MIELS-PIU-571282-CS-QCBS

 

Le Gouvernement du Burundi a obtenu un don de 113 millions de dollars de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine (PRU, P177146), qui vise à renforcer la résilience face aux inondations et à améliorer la gestion urbaine résiliente au climat à Bujumbura sur cinq ans.

Il est prévu qu’une partie des ressources de cette avance soit utiliser pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de services suivant : « termes de référence pour le recrutement d’un cabinet/firme pour l’élaboration des études d’impact environnemental et social (EIES) des infrastructures à faible regret et audit environnemental et social du mur en gabion et   des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation de la station de pompage d’eau de la REGIDESO

La mission a pour objectif global l’élaboration des Etudes d’Impacts Environnementaux et Sociaux détaillées des infrastructures à faible regret dans les six (6) bassins versants du Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine à savoir Kanyosha-Kizingwe, Mugere, Mutimbuzi, Muha, Ntahangwa et Rusizi. Les objectifs spécifiques de la mission sont les suivants :

  • Évaluer les risques environnementaux et sociaux liés aux infrastructures à faibles regret ;
  • Proposer les mesures d’adaptation pour les infrastructures à faible regret ;
  • Déterminer les coûts des mesures nécessaires pour prévenir, minimiser, atténuer ou compenser les nuisances et optimiser les impacts positifs.

 Pour le volet l’Audit La présente évaluation poursuit un double objectif. D'une part, elle vise à examiner de manière rétrospective la mise en œuvre des activités déjà réalisées dans le cadre du sous-projet, afin de vérifier leur conformité avec le Code de l'Environnement du Burundi ainsi qu'avec les Normes Environnementales et Sociales (NES) de la Banque mondiale applicables (voir Section V infra). D'autre part, elle a pour objet d'évaluer de manière prospective les impacts environnementaux et sociaux des nouveaux travaux prévus sur le site, et de proposer les mesures d'atténuation et de suivi nécessaires pour en assurer la durabilité.

Les compétences recherchées et qui constituent les critères de présélection sont les suivantes :

  • Avoir huit (8) ans d’expérience avérée dans les prestations analogues à la mission actuelle
  • Avoir mené, en tant que firme, au moins trois (03) consultances d'importance similaire et élaboré des documents similaires approuvés préférentiellement par la Banque mondiale

N.B : Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à ce stade.

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’une coentreprise et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

Le bureau d'études sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection fondée qualité le coût (SFQC) conformément au Règlement applicable aux Emprunteurs-Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement de la Banque Mondiale et conformément aux critères exigés au regard des termes de référence.

De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau : Lundi à jeudi de 08h00 à 12h00 et de 13h00 à 17h00 et vendredi de 8h à 12h.

Les manifestations d'intérêt rédigées en français portant la mention « Termes de référence pour le recrutement d’un cabinet/firme pour l’élaboration des études d’impact environnemental et social ( EIES) des infrastructures à faible regret et audit environnemental et social du mur en gabion et   des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation de la station de pompage d’eau de la Reguides doivent être transmises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par la poste ou par courriel) au plus tard le 28/09/2026 à 10 heures, heure de Bujumbura (GMT+2)

6. Qualifications requirements include:

(1) Average annual turnover over the last three years (2023-2025) shall not be less than CNY 4.3 million.

(2) At least 3 contracts successfully completed as supplier within the last three years. Value, nature, and complexity of these contracts should be comparable to the contract to be let.

(3) Goods offered have been in production for at least 3 years (from January 1, 2023) and a minimum of 5 units of similar capacity (Steel Grade: J55, Length: R3, Specification: 177.8mm×9.19mm heatexchanger technical casing (oil casing)) have been sold and have been in operation satisfactorily for at least 2 years.

(4) Minimum supply and/or production capacity required to assure that the Bidder is capable of supplying the type, size, and quantity of the Goods required, the annual production capacity of heatexchanger technical casing (oil casing) shall be no less than 4000m.

(5) Soundness of the Bidder’s financial position showing long-term profitability demonstrated through audited annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement) for the last three years (2023-2025). As a minimum, a Bidder’s net worth calculated as the difference between total assets and total liabilities for each of the three years should be positive.

(6) Availability of or access to liquid assets , lines of credit, and other finances sufficient to meet any possible cash flow requirement which may arise during the execution of the contract (This should in appropriate cases also take into account the Bidder’s commitments for other contracts) shall not be less than: CNY 800,000.00.

(7) All pending claims, arbitration, or other litigation shall represent in total not more than 50% of the Bidder’s net worth.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA

ADELE PROJECT (P171742)

 

Credit No.: IDA 68570

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Design and Establishment of a Wholesale (Apex) Development Finance Framework

Reference No. ET-DBE-571276-CS-QCBS

  1. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received World Bank financing for the Access to Distributed Electricity and Lighting in Ethiopia (ADELE) Project. It intends to apply part of the proceeds to consulting services.

The Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) is one of the state-owned financial institutions providing project finance and lease financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to support the country's overall economic development. In addition to financing projects, the bank serves as a financial intermediary that administers funds and appraises and monitors participating financial institutions through its wholesale financing program, ensuring successful project implementation.

2. DBE invites expressions of interest (EOIs) from legally formed consulting firms to provide consultancy services for the Design and Establishment of a Wholesale (Apex) Development Finance Framework.

3. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise technical assistance to the Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) to design, document, and prepare for implementation a wholesale (apex) development finance capability as an institutional pillar of the Bank. The services include the design of a wholesale banking framework covering the lending model and the intermediary engagement model; an assessment of the institutional, legal, and delivery structure options for housing the wholesale function; the development of a Wholesale Lending Policy and Operational Manual and of a credit guarantee and de-risking framework grounded in an explicit additionality framework; the design of a technical advisory and capacity-building program for participating financial institutions, including a dedicated module on expanding outreach to women entrepreneurs and women consumers; the integration of environmental and social risk management into intermediary accreditation and supervision; and support to DBE in preparing pilot wholesale arrangements and the associated portfolio segregation and ring-fencing arrangements. The assignment is financed under Sub-component 5.3 of the project. The implementation period is approximately twenty (20) weeks from contract signature, with the consultant based primarily in Addis Ababa for the core design and approval phases.

4. The Development Bank of Ethiopia now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

       4.1. Relevant experience of the firm

Assignments count only if completed within the last ten (10) years and only where the consultant acted as lead firm or joint venture member – sub-consultancy roles do not count. A single assignment may satisfy more than one of the requirements listed below.

  • At least three (3) completed assignments involving the design of wholesale or apex lending frameworks, on-lending or refinancing facilities, blended-finance or credit-guarantee structures, or DFI institutional design.
  • Of these, at least one (1) was carried out for a development finance institution, state-owned development bank or apex financial institution.
  • At least one (1) assignment involving the design or operationalization of a credit guarantee, first-loss, risk-sharing or partial credit guarantee instrument, including its pricing, eligibility and claims arrangements.
  • At least one (1) assignment on a World Bank or other multilateral-financed line of credit, apex facility or financial intermediary lending operation.
  • At least two (2) assignments delivered in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable frontier and emerging markets. For this purpose, a country is a comparable frontier or emerging market if, as at the date of the EOI submission deadline, it is (a) eligible for IDA financing (including blend countries), (b) classified by the World Bank as a low-income or lower-middle-income economy, or (c) a constituent of the MSCI Frontier Markets Index. Consultants must state, for each assignment relied upon, the country and the limb (a), (b) or (c) relied upon.

 

Assignments consisting solely of the following do not count under this sub-section 4.1: general management or organizational consulting; audit, tax or accounting services; IT or core-banking system implementation; training delivery without design content; market or feasibility studies without design of a lending framework or instrument; retail or corporate lending work with no financial-intermediary component.

       4.2. Technical and Managerial Capability of the Firm

  • The consultant demonstrates in-house coverage of the following disciplines through named permanent professional staff: development finance/apex lending; credit risk; financial modeling; institutional or organizational design; inclusive/gender-responsive finance. An organogram and headcount by discipline are required. There is no minimum total headcount; the in-country mobilization requirement set out below tests capacity to deliver at the scale of this assignment.
  • The Consultant has a documented quality assurance and project management system (ISO 9001 certification or an equivalent internal QA manual, described in no more than one page).
  • The Consultant has completed at least one (1) assignment in the last seven (7) years in which it mobilized and sustained a team of five (5) or more international and national experts in-country for a period of four (4) months or more, demonstrating capacity to deploy in Addis Ababa for an engagement of approximately 20 weeks. Evidence: client name and contact, assignment dates, team size and composition, and country of deployment.

      4.3. Core Business and Organizational Experience

  • The Consultant is a legally registered firm and has at least ten (10) years of organizational experience in development finance, financial sector development or financial institution advisory. Evidence: certificate of incorporation or registration, together with the experience record submitted under the following bullet.
  • Development finance, financial sector development, or financial institution advisory is a core business line of the Consultant, evidenced by at least five (5) completed consulting assignments in this field in the last ten (10) years.

5. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, the following specific information on conflict of interest applies to this assignment: a firm that DBE has engaged to prepare or implement activities that would place it in conflict with the obligations of this assignment, or that would confer an unfair advantage, is not eligible. Consultants shall disclose any current or prior advisory or contractual relationship with DBE within the last five (5) years.

6. The selection process will be conducted using Quality and Cost Based Method of Selection (QCBS) as laid out in the World Bank Procurement Regulation.

7. The consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Where the consultant is a joint venture, the core business requirement in sub-section 4.3 and at least two (2) of the three (3) assignments required under the first bullet of sub-section 4.1 shall be met by the lead member alone; the remaining requirements may be met by the members combined; and each member individually shall be eligible under Section III of the Procurement Regulations and shall not be subject to World Bank suspension or debarment. A joint venture shall submit a joint venture agreement or a letter of intent signed by all members, identifying the lead member. The qualifications, experience, and resources of sub-consultants are not taken into account in shortlisting.

8. Consultants/Applicants shall submit the required documents for the EOI consideration, including the business registration certificate, renewed trade license, VAT registration certificate (for local consulting firm only), and tax clearance certificate (for local consulting firm only). The EOI must not exceed twenty (20) pages, excluding the cover letter, registration certificate, and financial statements.

9. Interested applicants may obtain further information and clarification from DBE Head Office, Procurement Directorate, in front of DBE head office (Kiyamed Building, 1st floor), Tel. +251 11 5578088, ext. 364; Fax +251 11 553 7982 or via email attention to Mr. Kirubel Girma, Procurement Director, kirubelg@dbe.com.et and copy to tesfahunge@dbe.com.et

10. The Expression of Interest/ EoIs shall be submitted in English, one original and one copy, EoIs shall be submitted into the tender box prepared for the purpose on or before September 22, 2026 at 4:00 P.M (in the afternoon) at the Development Bank of Ethiopia, in front of DBE head office (Kiyamed Building 1st floor) or via email to Mr. Kirubel Girma, Procurement Director, kirubelg@dbe.com.et

DBE reserves the right to accept or reject a part/all of the entire bid.

REPUBLIQUE DE CÔTE D’IVOIRE

 

PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT DES CHAINES DE VALEURS VIVRIERS

 

Numéro de Crédit : 69080

 

Intitulé de la Mission : Recrutement d’un consultant/firme pour la réalisation d’une mission de suivi et contrôle des travaux de réhabilitation des stations d'alevinage de Abengourou et Mopoyem.

 

N° de référence STEP : CI-PDC2V-558241-CS-CQS

 

1. La République de Côte d’Ivoire a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Développement des Chaînes de Valeurs Vivrières (PDC2V) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de consultant.

 

2. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») consisteront à assister l’unité de coordination du projet dans le suivi et contrôle des travaux de réhabilitation des stations d'alevinage de Abengourou et Mopoyem.

 

3. La mission se déroulera sur une durée maximale de huit (08) mois calendaires à compter de la réception de l’ordre de service de démarrage.

 

4. Les Termes De Référence (TDR) détaillés de la mission peuvent être téléchargés gratuitement via le lien suivant : www.pdc2v.ci ou à la demande à l’adresse : edwige.solou@pdc2v.ci avec copie à maurel.zede@pdc2v.ci.  Les adresses électroniques fournies seront utilisées pour toute communication ultérieures (clarification etc.).

 

5. Le Projet de Développement des Chaînes de Valeurs Vivrières invite dès à présent les consultants Firmes admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Firmes intéressées doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

 

6. Compétences et qualifications du consultant firme :

 

Le Consultant recherché est une firme ou un groupement de Cabinets exerçant dans le domaine du génie civil et ayant réalisé en maitrise d’œuvre de suivi et contrôle au cours des dix (10) dernières années, au moins un ou plusieurs projets de réhabilitation ou construction de bâtiments ERP (Etablissement Recevant des Travailleurs) et aménagement hydro piscicole/ agricole d’un montant de travaux minimum de 25 000 000 FCFA par mission.

Les expériences similaires doivent être respectivement justifiées par des attestations de bonne exécution (ABE) délivrées par les Maitres d’Ouvrage.

 

La firme devra disposer des experts suivants :

Désignation

Formation

Expérience générale

Expérience spécifique

•              Deux (02) Ingénieurs en Bâtiment, Chef de mission

Ingénieur de Conception en Bâtiment ou Génie Civil de niveau minimum (BAC +5) ou tout autre diplôme équivalent

Au moins sept (7) ans d’expérience en étude, exécution ou contrôle de travaux bâtiments ou de génie civil

Avoir réalisé au moins trois (03) missions de maitrise d’œuvre de travaux de bâtiment recevant du public ERP

Deux (02) Ingénieurs en Génie Rural ou Aménagement Hydro-piscicole
