TERM OF REFERENCE

To ensure the implementation of the World Bank China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project Information Technology Third-Party Service Package I (Supervision Services)of the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulationand to achieve the informatization construction goals of the project, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to engage a third-party service agency to carry out the implementation of this project.

I. Background and Description

The World Bank Loan China Food Safety Demonstration Project officially entered into force on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period until March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance the modern governance capacity for food safety at both national and local levels. As a key implementer of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation plans to apply for a World Bank loan of 10 million US dollars and will precisely support the achievement of the project goals through the construction of six core sub-projects:

i. Develop a full-chain traceability platform for "coding, tracing, and recalling" food in key areas, enabling whole-process traceability and risk early warning with 15 functional modules and 359 functional points;

ii. Build the "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" system under the Guangdong Food Safety initiative, covering intelligent video supervision of scenarios such as elderly care and campus canteens;

iii. Upgrade and transform the emergency real-time dispatching and command system, and improve the accident emergency response mechanism;

iv. Carry out a capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of 75 course videos, and the organization of skill competitions;

v. Establish a high-quality food standard system and conduct promotion activities, developing no less than 30 standards and carrying out quality monitoring within two years;

vi. Provide professional consulting services throughout the entire project implementation process.

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the above-mentioned construction content, we plan to refer to advanced practices from other World Bank projects to further optimize procurement management and improve service coordination efficiency; in the next phase of actual procurement operations, while keeping the total project budget unchanged, we intend to integrate the supervision services of the four projects—the "Coding, Tracing, and Recalling" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Areas (or Key Varieties), the Guangdong Food Safety "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" System Construction Project, the Emergency Real-Time Dispatching and Command System Upgrade, Transformation, and Operation Project, and the Capacity Improvement Project for Food-Related Personnel in the Market Supervision Field—into a single package for unified procurement and management, so as to ensure the smooth achievement of the project's construction goals.

II. Objectives

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the informatization sub-projects under the World Bank Loan Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, third-party supervision services will be provided throughout the entire process for four informatization sub-projects: the "Coding, Tracing, and Recalling" full-chain traceability platform, the "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" intelligent supervision system, the emergency real-time dispatching and command system, and the learning and assessment system for capacity improvement of food-related personnel. Through full-cycle, closed-loop management and control covering quality, progress, investment, changes, contract compliance, safety, intellectual property, multi-party collaboration, and documentation during project construction, we will ensure that project construction activities are legal, compliant, economical, and scientific; strictly control risks such as project overspending, delays, and quality defects; and guarantee the project is completed with high quality within the agreed schedule and budget. With the core goal of comprehensively enhancing modern governance capacity for food safety, we will build a full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early warning response, and closed-loop disposal through the system construction and coordinated advancement of the informatization sub-projects. This will provide a solid data foundation and institutional guarantee for the scientific calculation of the "proportion of early warnings for which mitigation measures have been initiated," realize systematic training for food safety inspectors and supervisors while quantifying the participation ratio of female supervisors, comprehensively improve the quality and management level of project implementation, ensure that the collection, accounting, and reporting of all indicator data comply with World Bank standards, and help promote the efficient implementation of the World Bank project.

III. Service Overview

The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 1.6003 million.

(I) Scope of Services

The service scope of this project covers the full-process supervision services for four informatization sub-projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Content

The supervision service agency shall provide full-process supervision services for the implementation of the aforementioned four informatization sub-projects, assisting the project undertaking company and the user party in carrying out their work to ensure the achievement of the predetermined project goals. In accordance with supervision work specifications, the agency shall implement full-process control over project quality, schedule, investment, contracts, and information security. This is to ensure that the construction activities are legal, compliant, reasonable, scientific, and economical, thereby reducing project construction risks and achieving both the overall project goals and the current phase goals.For details:

 

  1. Quality Control

Adopt a full-process control mechanism of pre-prevention, in-process management and control, and post rectification. Control the quality of system development in accordance with regulatory standards, project contracts and design documents; regularly review project documents, issue supervision briefs and conduct quantitative evaluation; assist in reviewing design schemes and software selection, and supervise software testing, installation and commissioning links; formulate project acceptance standards and disposal plans, urge the implementation unit to rectify quality defects and follow up the operation and maintenance services during the warranty period. Simultaneously control the training quality, review the training plan, supervise the implementation of training and recheck the training summary.
 

  1. Schedule Control
    Review the development schedule plans at all levels of the implementation unit and verify their feasibility; track the progress of requirements, coding, testing and online stages in real time, and urge dynamic adjustment of the construction period; put forward optimization schemes in a timely manner and urge implementation of rectification when there is a serious deviation in the construction period; realize visual control of development progress relying on standardized project management tools.
     
  2. Investment Control
    Optimize the software development implementation plan, reasonably control the costs of customized development, third-party component procurement, etc., to ensure the cost-effectiveness of capital investment; track the use of funds in real time, give early warning and adjustment suggestions in time if there is a large deviation in the budget, and strictly control the risk of overspending.
     
  3. Change Control
    Unify the management of various changes such as software requirements, functions, interfaces and architecture, and standardize the whole process of change application, impact assessment, multi-party review, approval and implementation, and regression testing; evaluate the impact of changes on quality, schedule, investment and safety, eliminate disorderly demand spread, completely retain the change ledger and complete the change filing of local government projects.
     
  4. contract management
    Assist the construction unit in drafting, reviewing and signing software development and supporting procurement contracts; track the performance of the contract throughout the process; coordinate the handling of construction period extension, change, breach of contract, claim, subcontracting and project dispute mediation; review the payment application of the implementation unit according to the contract terms and issue supervision review opinions.
     
  5. Document Information Management
    Unify the collection and management of a full set of software project materials such as requirements, design, testing, operation and maintenance, and training; regularly submit project dynamic materials to the construction unit; urge the implementation unit to sort out and file technical materials in accordance with specifications; transmit notices and contact sheets issued by the construction unit; report software quality problems to the superior immediately and supervise the closed-loop rectification.
     
  6. Safety and Intellectual Property Management
    Supervise the hierarchical protection of government business data and internal materials throughout the process to strictly prevent unauthorized access and leakage of data; control the operation safety of development, testing and online links, implement code security and relevant requirements of classified protection, and eliminate safety accidents. At the same time, protect the intellectual property rights of project development achievements, software source codes and customized functions, and strictly prohibit illegal reuse or private external transmission of achievements.
     
  7. Organization and Coordination

Establish a standardized project meeting mechanism, organize weekly meetings, demand coordination meetings, technical special meetings, problem notification meetings and phased acceptance meetings, and completely retain meeting minutes; coordinate the work relations among the construction unit, business departments, development and implementation units and software and hardware suppliers, and build a normalized communication channel; coordinate to solve various problems such as demand differences, development (stuck points), testing disputes, etc., and simultaneously implement the project safety supervision objectives.
(III) Service Period

The supervision service period for this project shall commence from the date of contract signing and continue until the project closing date (March 31, 2029).

Country: Zambia

Name of Project: Irrigated and Sustainable Agriculture for Transformation (ISAT) Project (P182068)

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: E5970

Assignment Title: Consultancy services for Designing and Piloting of a Farmer-Led Irrigation Development (FLID) intervention in Zambia

Reference No. ZM-MOFNP-570604-CS-QCBS

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Irrigated and Sustainable Agriculture for Transformation (ISAT) Project Preparation and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  The Project Preparation Grant financing is intended to support the identification, technical assessment, and preparation of priority irrigation schemes that can be taken forward under the full ISAT operation.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Designing and Piloting of a Farmer-Led Irrigation Development (FLID) intervention in Zambia.

Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the design of a FLID component for the ISAT project, including the design and piloting of a Results-Based Financing framework tailored to FLID.

Scope of Work

The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks:

a) Fast diagnostic (data collection, analysis): Understand the bottlenecks to scaling up FLID in Zambia and scoping for a Result Based Financing (RBF) framework around the identified irrigation schemes.

  • Characterize FLID potential at farm level (farm size, assets, affordability gaps)
  • Survey the current private sector landscape that is providing goods (supply of irrigation equipment) and services (irrigation services) to assess equipment capital and operational costs for the range of farmer types and farm sizes, understand private sector challenges and draw on private sector insights into opportunities for rapid irrigation technology uptake and expansion.
  • Understand the existing public financing structures and mechanisms for financing smallholder irrigation.
  • Explore the policy and legal barriers in the enabling environment constraining smallholder farmers in autonomously carrying out small-scale irrigation development.

b) FLID intervention and RBF Design: Translate the diagnostic into a set of feasible, scalable FLID intervention models.

  • Develop the design of potential FLID interventions within the ISAT project, providing different options and potential scenarios based on the diagnostic of farmers’ assets, willingness to pay, providers’ capacity, among others.
  • Design an RBF framework and its parameters: Key Result Indicators (KRIs), payment triggers/schedules, eligibility, verification, financial flows, subsidy/rebate, risk-sharing.

c) Piloting the Methodology: The pilot phase serves as a controlled environment to test the feasibility, scalability, and sustainability of the proposed FLID intervention. Particularly irrigation modernization, financing mechanisms, and private sector partnerships. The four sequential stages of the methodology include:

  • Elaborate a piloting methodology of the proposed interventions in Zambia accounting for the time constraint of the project preparation, outlining the process for selecting testing sites, testing financing mechanisms, partnering with irrigation equipment providers and any other intervention design aspects that might be piloted.
  • Identify 10 appropriate sites for piloting based on a set of pre-defined characteristics.
  • Onboard participants of the pilots such as providers, financial institutions, districts, farmers.
  • Define the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework to assess the pilot’s performance.

d) Pilot implementation and evaluation: Implement FLID interventions with continuous technical support, collect baseline, midline and end-line data, identify challenges along the implementation process to refine the model and document lessons for national scale-up. Specifically:

  • Deploy the FLID interventions and RBF mechanisms in the selected zones.
  • Execute the MEL framework.
  • Conduct a structured assessment of pilot outcomes and rank the best-performing options

Duration of the Assignment

The assignment is expected to be completed within seven (7) calendar months after signing of contract between November 2026 and May 2027.

Invitation

The National Authorising Office now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Must be a legally registered firm with a minimum of 5 years of continuous operations in providing consultancy services.
  2. Experience in similar assignments, evidence of at least three similar assignments completed in Sub-Saharan Africa within the past ten years. Experience must include:
  • At least one assignment related to Farmer-Led Irrigation Development or smallholder irrigation systems
  • At least one assignment involving performance-based or results-based contracting.

      3. Proven track record working with government agencies, private sector actors, and                          development partners (Consultant to provide copies of contracts for past assignments or                completion certificates as evidence).

      4. The firm must demonstrate strong technical multidisciplinary expertise in Irrigation and                Water Resources Engineering, Agricultural Economics, Market Systems Development and            Private Sector Engagement and Environmental and Social Risk Management

      5.  Managerial capabilities indicating the general qualifications and experience of Principals               (key staff of the firm) and the structure of the organization.

The above required relevant qualifications and experience relate to the qualifications and experience of the firm and should not be based on individual experts as this is not required at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on Conflict of Interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or a sub- consultancy. In the case of a Joint Venture, all the partners in the Joint Venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Therefore, each member of JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria. The experience, technical & managerial capability of the Sub-Consultant shall not be evaluated to enhance the qualification of the Lead Firm or JV.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested Consultants firms may obtain detailed terms of reference (ToRs) at the address below during office hours from 08.00 to 17.00 hours Local time Monday to Friday except public holidays or visit https://nao.gov.zm/

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by 1st October 2026, at 10:00 Hours Central African Time (+2hours GMT), clearly marked “EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DESIGNING AND PILOTING OF A FARMER-LED IRRIGATION DEVELOPMENT (FLID) INTERVENTION IN ZAMBIA

The firms that will submit their EOI via e-mail must get confirmation of the receipt of their documents. In case the firm does not receive acknowledgement within two working days after sending the documents via email, they should call the numbers provided below for follow-up.

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(SELECTION DE CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL)

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) ASSUMANT LA FONCTION DE SPECIALISTE EN ENGAGEMENT/DEVELOPPEMENT COMMUNAUTAIRE AU SEIN DU PROGRAMME DE DEVELOPPEMENT INGA 3 (PDI3)

 

N° de crédit / N° de don : 7816-ZR (A) & 7815-ZR (B)

N° de référence de l’Avis : ZR-ADEPI-520109-CS-INDV

Date de Publication : le 10 septembre 2026

Date de clôture : le 24 septembre 2026

 

1. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie de réduction du déficit énergétique au niveau national, le Gouvernement de la RDC a demandé et obtenu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) deux lignes de crédit (A et B) pour financer le « Programme de Développement du Projet INGA 3 (PDI 3) », et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit en vue d’effectuer des paiements au titre d’un contrat pour les prestations des services d’un(e) « Consultant(e) individuel(le) assumant la fonction de Spécialiste en Engagement/Développement communautaire au sein du Programme de Développement du Projet Inga 3 (PDI3)».

 

2. Au titre des services, sous l’autorité du Directeur du PDI3, l’objectif principal de la mission est d’assurer la planification, la coordination, la supervision, le contrôle qualité, la veille sociale, le suivi, le reporting et l’appui méthodologique aux activités de développement communautaire, de mobilisation des parties prenantes, de gouvernance locale et de redevabilité du Pilier 2a, afin que les interventions du PDI3 soient socialement acceptées, inclusives, traçables, conformes aux exigences E&S et orientées vers la durabilité.

 

De manière spécifique, le (la) Consultant(e) aura comme responsabilité, entre autres de :

  • organiser et suivre un dispositif structuré de mobilisation communautaire, fondé sur le Plan de Mobilisation des Parties Prenantes (PMPP) et adapté aux réalités sociales des territoires ciblés ;
  • appuyer l’Équipe de Coordination du Projet (ECP-PDI3) et l’Unité Provinciale d’Appui (UPA) dans la planification des consultations, la mobilisation communautaire, l’identification des risques sociaux et le suivi des engagements pris envers les communautés ;
  • appuyer les structures locales et les communautés dans l’identification, la priorisation et le suivi des besoins, sans se substituer aux prestataires de facilitation ;
  • superviser les prestataires chargés des activités de facilitation, d’enquêtes, de mobilisation ou d’appui communautaire, en contrôlant la qualité, la conformité et la traçabilité de leurs livrables ;
  • préparer, actualiser et suivre le plan opérationnel de mobilisation communautaire, en cohérence avec le PTBA, le PMPP, les calendriers des sous-projets et les priorités validées par le Directeur de Projet ;
  • cartographier les parties prenantes locales, les relais communautaires, les autorités coutumières et administratives, les CLD/CCP, les organisations de femmes et de jeunes, les associations locales, les groupes vulnérables et les autres acteurs concernés ;
  • appuyer la mise en place, le renforcement ou l’animation des CLD et autres structures locales pertinentes, en veillant à leur inclusivité et à la clarification de leurs rôles ;
  • assurer l’interface avec les CLD, le CCP, les autorités locales, les organisations communautaires, les femmes, les jeunes et les groupes vulnérables, en articulation avec les spécialistes environnementaux et sociaux, VBG/EAS-HS et communication ;
  • veiller à ce que les priorités communautaires relatives notamment à l’eau, à l’électrification, aux routes rurales, aux travaux à haute intensité de main-d’œuvre (THIMO), à la gouvernance locale et aux services sociaux soient enregistrées, analysées et transmises aux équipes compétentes de l’ECP ;
  • contribuer au suivi des plaintes communautaires et des mécanismes de redevabilité, tout en laissant aux spécialistes E&S et VBG les procédures spécialisées relevant de leurs mandats ;
  • mettre en place et tenir à jour un registre de veille sociale permettant de suivre les tensions, rumeurs, griefs récurrents, blocages de terrain, conflits de leadership, enjeux fonciers, perceptions d’exclusion et risques de contestation ;
  • organiser, en lien avec l’UPA et les spécialistes E&S, une procédure graduée de traitement des alertes comprenant notamment l’identification, l’analyse, la médiation locale lorsque appropriée, la documentation, l’escalade au Directeur de Projet et le suivi des mesures correctives ;
  • contribuer à l’inclusion effective des femmes, des jeunes, des personnes handicapées, des ménages pauvres, des personnes déplacées, des groupes marginalisés et des autres catégories vulnérables dans les processus de consultation et de suivi ;
  • contribuer à l’analyse de genre contextualisée et veiller à la prise en compte des obstacles à la participation et à l’accès aux bénéfices du Projet ;
  • contribuer à la préparation ou à la revue des TDR, critères d’évaluation, clauses pertinentes, plans de travail, rapports et livrables des prestataires de facilitation communautaire, d’enquêtes, de diagnostics participatifs ou de mobilisation sociale ;
  • examiner les plans de travail, rapports, supports de consultation et livrables des prestataires, formuler des observations écrites, suivre la levée des commentaires et recommander leur validation ou leur révision au Directeur de Projet ;
  • produire des notes d’alerte et d’aide à la décision lorsque des risques sociaux, communautaires ou institutionnels sont susceptibles d’affecter les délais, l’acceptabilité sociale ou la conformité des activités ;
  • produire des rapports analytiques périodiques permettant notamment de suivre les consultations, les préoccupations communautaires, les plaintes, les risques sociaux, la cohésion sociale, l’inclusion et les mesures correctives ;
  • contribuer à la pérennisation des acquis communautaires, au renforcement des capacités des structures locales et au transfert progressif des outils et mécanismes de redevabilité aux acteurs compétents.

 

Le/la Consultant(e) devra exercer une fonction de maîtrise d’ouvrage communautaire au sein de l’ECP-PDI3. Il/elle ne se substituera notamment pas aux prestataires, bureaux d’études, entreprises, spécialistes E&S/VBG, autorités locales ou organes de décision du Projet et ne traitera pas directement les cas sensibles d’EAS/HS en dehors des procédures spécialisées.

 

3. La durée de la mission est de douze (12) mois dont trois (3) de période probatoire.  Le contrat est renouvelable annuellement, sous réserve d’une évaluation satisfaisante des performances du (de la) Consultant(e).

 

Le poste sera basé à Matadi (ou à Kinshasa, selon le niveau d’opérationnalisation de l’Unité Provinciale d’Appui (UPA), avec des missions régulières à Inga et dans les territoires ciblés du Kongo Central, dont des zones rurales à contraintes logistiques.

 

4. L’Agence pour le Développement et la Promotion du Projet Grand Inga (ADPI-RDC) invite les candidats (Consultants Individuels) admissibles à manifester leur intérêt pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter de cette mission.

 

5. Le/la Consultant(e) à recruter devra disposer des qualifications et expériences requises ci-après :

  • être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 ou équivalent en sciences sociales, développement communautaire, sociologie, anthropologie, développement rural, gestion de projet, géographie humaine ou dans une discipline connexe pertinente ;
  • justifier d’au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente en développement communautaire, mobilisation sociale, gouvernance locale, redevabilité sociale, médiation communautaire ou développement local ;
  • justifier d’au moins cinq (5) ans d’expérience spécifique dans des programmes multisites, interventions communautaires ou de mobilisation sociale, projets d’infrastructures à impact social, programmes financés par des bailleurs ou dans la coordination de prestataires communautaires ;
  • disposer d’une bonne maîtrise des approches participatives, de la consultation communautaire, de la médiation, de l’inclusion sociale, du suivi communautaire, de la sensibilité aux conflits, du suivi qualitatif, des mécanismes de plaintes, du genre et du renforcement des capacités locales ;
  • disposer d’une capacité démontrée en rédaction professionnelle, analyse, coordination multi-acteurs, reporting orienté vers la prise de décision et travail en équipe pluridisciplinaire ;
  • justifier d’une expérience pertinente de travail en République Démocratique du Congo, au Kongo Central ou dans des contextes ruraux comparables, laquelle constituera un atout important ;
  • avoir une connaissance des exigences environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale, du PMPP/MGP et des projets financés par l’IDA, laquelle constituera un atout sans être une exigence éliminatoire ;
  • avoir une excellente maîtrise du français écrit et oral ; la connaissance de l’anglais à un niveau intermédiaire est souhaitable ;
  • la connaissance des langues locales utiles dans la zone d’intervention constitue un atout significatif.

 

Les candidats devront également démontrer leur capacité à travailler avec les autorités locales, les structures communautaires, les prestataires et les différentes composantes de l’ECP-PDI3

 

Le dossier de candidature devra inclure :

  • Une lettre de motivation signée et datée
  • Un curriculum vitae signé et daté renseignant entre autres les expériences passées et les informations sur les personnes de référence
  • Les copies des diplômes académiques
  • Les attestations de travail antérieur.

 

6. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) », édition révisée de septembre 2025 ci-après désigné « Règlement de Passation des Marchés », qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables.

 

7. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultant Individuel, telle que décrite dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », édition révisée de septembre 2025.

 

8. Les Consultants (Individuels) intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires, notamment sur les termes de référence, à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau suivantes : de 9 à 16 heures (heure locale, TU+1) ou sur le site web « www.adpi-rdc.com ».

 

9. Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées, en langue française, doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous, par courrier physique ou électronique (e-mail), au plus tard le 24 septembre 2026 à 16 heures (heure locale, TU +1) et porter clairement la mention ci-après : AMI N°ZR-ADEPI-520109-CS-INDV « Recrutement d’un(e) Consultant(e) assumant la fonction de Spécialiste en Engagement/Développement communautaire au sein du Programme de Développement Inga 3 (PDI3)».

2. Os objectivos dos Serviços são:

O objectivo da consultoria é actuar como Entidade de Monitoria Independente, responsável por realizar auditorias regulares de prevenção e mitigação de riscos de:

  • Exploração e Abuso sexual
  • Assédio sexual e
  • Violência Baseada no  Género

As Manifestações de Interesse deverão incluir o nome, endereço e dados de contacto da empresa, bem como informações sobre a sua estrutura de propriedade. 

5. A avaliação das Manifestações de Interesse será realizada com base na qualidade, e os critérios para a elaboração da lista curta são os seguintes:

  • A empresa de consultoria deve ter 5 anos experiência em avaliação e monitoramento da implementação de políticas de VBG/EAS/AS e ESMPs em Moçambique e em outros países com condições sociais, geográficas e económicas semelhantes;
  • Mínimo de 3 anos de experiência comprovada na execução de tarefas semelhantes em projectos financiados por parceiros de desenvolvimento, como IDA/ADB/JICA/BID em Moçambique.
  • A empresa de consultoria deve possuir um código de conduta e uma política interna clara voltada para a prevenção e o combate ao assédio, à exploração e ao abuso sexual.

As empresas deverão anexar o(s) certificado(s) de conclusão para cada referência de projecto concluído.

Os especialistas-chave não serão avaliados na fase da lista curta.

6. Chama-se a atenção aos consultores interessados para a Seção III, parágrafos 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 dos Regulamentos de Licitação do Banco Mundial “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial no concernente a conflitos de interesse

SOLICITAÇÃO DEMANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE CAR/BPA Nº 004/2026 COMPANHIA DE DESENVOLVIMENTO E AÇÃO REGIONAL – CAR

PROJETO BAHIA QUE PRODUZ E ALIMENTA

 

A Companhia de Desenvolvimento e Ação Regional – CAR, vinculada à Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Rural do Estado da Bahia – SDR, executora do Projeto Bahia que Produz e Alimenta, torna público que convida empresas de consultoria a apresentarem manifestações de interesse para a prestação dos seguintes serviços:

 

Objeto: Contratação de Entidade de Apoio para a Implementação do Projeto Bahia que Produz e Alimenta, compreendendo, entre outras atividades, o suporte técnico à gestão e à comercialização; a elaboração de estudos temáticos e estudos de viabilidade de subprojetos; a realização de análises de cadeias e arranjos produtivos; a organização de capacitações e eventos; o monitoramento e a avaliação das ações; e a disponibilização e gestão de equipes destinadas ao apoio à execução do Projeto, com atuação na sede da CAR e nos 27 Territórios de Identidade do Estado da Bahia, conforme detalhado no Termo de Referência disponível em https://www.ba.gov.br/car/editais.

 

Método de Seleção: Seleção com Orçamento Fixo (SOF), conforme Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial (julho/2016, revisado em novembro/2020). A presente Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse destina-se à identificação de entidades qualificadas para formação da Lista Curta de consultores. A Solicitação de Propostas – SDP será posteriormente encaminhada às entidades que integrarem a lista curta. As entidades interessadas deverão apresentar informações que demonstrem sua qualificação e experiência institucional para a execução de serviços de natureza e complexidade semelhantes aos previstos no Termo de Referência, mediante apresentação de portfólio, atestados de capacidade técnica, relação e descrição de contratos ou trabalhos similares e demais documentos que evidenciem sua experiência pertinente ao objeto.

 

Para fins de formação da Lista Curta, serão consideradas a qualificação institucional e a experiência comprovada da entidade em serviços de natureza, porte e complexidade semelhantes ao objeto da contratação, especialmente:

 

a) apoio à implementação ou à gestão de projetos de desenvolvimento rural e agricultura familiar;

b) prestação, coordenação ou gerenciamento de serviços de assistência técnica e extensão rural;

c) apoio à comercialização, estruturação de cadeias produtivas, empreendimentos rurais ou acesso a mercados;

d) mobilização e gestão de equipes multidisciplinares, inclusive com atuação territorial descentralizada;

e) monitoramento físico e financeiro, gestão de contratos, organização de eventos, capacitações, viagens e despesas operacionais; e

f) execução de projetos financiados por organismos nacionais ou internacionais, especialmente aqueles submetidos a regras específicas de aquisições, gestão financeira, integridade e prestação de contas.

 

Nesta etapa não deverão ser apresentadas Proposta Técnica, Proposta Financeira, metodologia detalhada, composição da equipe-chave ou currículos dos profissionais. As informações solicitadas destinam-se exclusivamente à verificação da qualificação institucional e à formação da lista curta. A inclusão na lista curta não implica adjudicação ou contratação.

 

As manifestações de interesse deverão ser entregues no endereço abaixo ou enviadas para o e-mail indicado, até o dia de 14 de setembro de 2026 às 23h59min.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Republic of Tajikistan

Sustainable Financing for Rogun Hydropower Project (P181029)

Projects Management Group for Energy Facilities Construction under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan (PMG)

Grant No.: IDA-E3800

Assignment Title: Lenders Technical Advisor of the ROGUN HPP (LTA).

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TJ-PMG-EFC-CS-QCBS-02

The Republic of Tajikistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Financing for Rogun Hydropower Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Lenders Technical Advisor of the ROGUN HPP (LTA). ). The cost of the LTA contract will be covered by joint financing of the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB).

The objective of the assignment is to provide the participating Financiers with independent, high-level technical, environmental, social, occupational health and safety, cost, schedule, and operational assurance throughout construction, commissioning, and the initial operations-monitoring phase of the Rogun Hydropower Project. The Consultant will act independently of the Employer, PMG, the Project Management Consultant (PMC), the HSE Supervisor, the Panels of Experts, contractors, and other project participants, and will report directly to the participating Financiers.

The scope of services includes, among others, the following:

  1. independently monitoring project implementation, construction quality, design progress, schedule, costs, budget, technical integrity, and compliance with the Financing Documents;
  2. reviewing the adequacy and effectiveness of the PMC’s construction supervision, quality management, dam-safety activities, project controls, contract administration, and document management;
  3. conducting regular site visits and maintaining permanent resident site presence during construction and commissioning, including independent verification of progress and quality;
  4. independently reviewing environmental, social, labor, resettlement, occupational health and safety performance and the outputs of the HSE Supervisor, in accordance with applicable IFI standards and project instruments;
  5. reviewing and advising the Financiers on change orders, claims, variations, schedule and cost deviations, and related technical, contractual, environmental and social implications;
  6. reviewing milestone-payment requests and issuing independent disbursement certificates;
  7. reviewing punch lists, completion lists, factory and site acceptance tests, commissioning plans, performance tests, as-built drawings, and operation and maintenance manuals;
  8. issuing independent opinions and certificates for mechanical completion, provisional acceptance, final acceptance, and impoundment readiness; and
  9. monitoring initial operations, plant performance and technical integrity, and reviewing annual operation and maintenance budgets and operational performance reports.

Anticipated date for commencement of the Services is April 2027 and the tentative duration of the assignment for the Services is five (5) years (60 months) .

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the link 

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hCcRXBIZnJs3lKgKMdJKTHG6qHuLkvjO/view?usp=sharing

or can be obtained at the address given at the end of this REoI.

The Project Management Group for Energy Facilities Construction under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan (PMG) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Legal status: The Consultant shall be a legally registered entity, established and in operation for at least the last 10 years. A copy of the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the relevant authority in the country of establishment shall be provided. In the case of a joint venture (JV), this shall be demonstrated for each member.
  2. General experience: The Consultant shall have at least ten (10) years of experience providing lenders’ technical advisory, independent engineer, owner’s engineer, project-management, construction-supervision, technical due-diligence, or monitoring services for large and complex infrastructure projects..
  3. Specific experience.
    The Consultant shall have successfully completed, within the last 10 years:
  1. at least two (2) assignments as lenders’ technical advisor, independent engineer, or equivalent independent technical-monitoring advisor for projects financed by the World Bank, AIIB, ADB, EIB, EBRD, IsDB, or another multilateral or bilateral development financier, of which at least one (1) assignment shall relate to a large hydropower plant or dam project; and
  2. experience monitoring environmental, social, labor, resettlement, and OHS compliance on at least one large infrastructure project financed by an international financial institution.
  3. experience with FIDIC-based contracts and multi-contract project interfaces, including review of variations/change orders, claims, schedules, costs, milestone payments, testing, commissioning, and completion certification.
  4. the combined construction/works value of the projects presented to demonstrate the above experience shall be at least US$1 billion.

4. Capacity to deliver. Demonstrated managerial and organizational capacity to mobilize and maintain a multidisciplinary international team, permanent site presence, specialist home-office support, and responsive inputs over a long-duration assignment. The Consultant shall submit an organogram and evidence of a quality management system (ISO 9001 or equivalent).

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (Seventh Edition, September 2025) (Procurement Regulations) setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly in the Expression of Interest whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 17:00.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form in English to the address below (in person, by mail, or by e-mail) by October 12, 2026, 15:00 Dushanbe time.

GOVERNMENT OF GRENADA

MINISTRY OF FINANCE
CENTRAL PROCUREMENT UNIT

OECS DATA FOR DECISION-MAKING PROJECT (DDM)

Loan/Credit No.: IDA-71110

SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS

Country: Grenada
Project: OECS Data for Decision Making Project (DDM)
Contract Title: Non-Consultant Services for the Household Budget Survey / Survey of Living Conditions (Enumerators)
Reference No.: GD-PCU-Grenada-562454-NC-RFQ

1. Background

The Government of Grenada, through the Central Statistical Office (CSO), will conduct the Household Budget Survey (HBS) and Survey of Living Conditions (SLC) from September 2026 to March 2027.

The surveys will generate critical information on household expenditure, education, health, nutrition, housing, demographics and other socio-economic conditions to support evidence-based national planning and policymaking.

2. Invitation

The Government of Grenada, through the Central Procurement Unit, now invites applications from suitably qualified individuals to provide enumerator services for the Household Budget Survey / Survey of Living Conditions.

The selected Enumerators will be responsible for conducting household interviews and collecting accurate and complete survey information within assigned districts.

3. Scope of Services

The selected Enumerators will be required to:

  • Conduct face-to-face interviews with household members using electronic devices, including tablets.
  • Administer survey questionnaires and accurately record responses.
  • Visit and interview all households within assigned districts.
  • Maintain detailed records of daily food expenditures reported by households.
  • Navigate assigned district boundaries using maps and visit every building, dwelling unit and household.
  • Conduct follow-up visits to verify or correct information where required.
  • Maintain regular communication with supervisors and submit completed work and reports in accordance with established schedules.
  • Maintain the confidentiality and security of all information collected and comply with the Oath of Secrecy.
  • Attend and successfully complete all required training prior to field deployment.
  • Maintain all equipment issued for the assignment, including tablets, chargers and identification cards, in good condition and return all issued equipment at the end of the assignment.

4. Minimum Qualification Requirements

Interested applicants should possess the following:

  • At least four (4) CXC passes, including English Language and Mathematics.
  • Previous experience in data collection, particularly household surveys, will be considered an asset.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to establish rapport with households.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy in recording information.
  • Ability to work independently, manage time effectively and meet established deadlines.
  • Familiarity with survey software, including Survey Solutions, will be considered an advantage.
  • Fluency in the local language is required.

5. Duration of Services

The assignment is expected to commence on September 1, 2026 and conclude on March 31, 2027.

6. Submission of Quotations

Interested and suitably qualified applicants are invited to submit:

  1. Curriculum Vitae (CV); and
  2. Cover letter demonstrating relevant experience and suitability for the assignment.

Applications and supporting documents should be submitted electronically to:

Central Procurement Unit
Attn: Ms. Erisa Bleasdille, Procurement Officer
Ministry of Finance
The Galleria Mall
Grand Anse, St. George’s, Grenada

REPUBLIC OF SOUTH SUDAN

MINISTRY OF INFORMATION, COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY AND POSTAL SERVICES (MICT&PS)

PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION  UNIT (PIU)

Specific Procurement Notice

Request for Bids

Non-Consulting Services

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

Employer: Ministry of Information Communication Technology and Postal Services (MICT&PS)

Project: Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EARDIP) – SOP-1

Contract title: Capex for Fibre Deployment for Route A-B

Country: South Sudan

Grant No.: E1780

RFB No: SS-MICT&PS-544330-NC-RFB

Issued on: September 14 2026

1. The Government of South Sudan (GOSS) has received financing from the World Bank to participate in the first series of projects for the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EARDIP-SOP-1). The project development objective is to increase access to broadband and digital services through the development and integration of digital markets in the Eastern Africa Region.

2. Government of South Sudan (GOSS) intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the Fiber Optic Network Backbone. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s “Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing”.

3. The Ministry of Information Communication Technology and Postal Services (MICT&PS) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for matching investments from EARDIP for the design, supply and owner operation of the approximately 397 km backbone terrestrial fibre optic cable (FOC) along the Juba–Nadapal road corridor (to the border with Kenya), with a minimum 17 Points of Presence (POPs) and aggregation points along the route that are designed to support the interconnection of commercial traffic from several major cities and communities served by Mobile network operators (MNOs) and to facilitate last-mile connectivity by MNOs and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to a number of named public institutions (schools, health centres and governmental locations) within a 10 km radius on both sides of the corridor. The total contract duration between the commencement date and contract completion date is 12 months.

4. Key Qualification Criteria include:

Specific Experience

The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed, or substantially completed, during the last three years, at least one of the following:

  • One contract for fiber optic or similar telecommunications/connectivity infrastructure with a value of not less than US$6,000,000; or
  • Two similar contracts, each with a value of not less than US$3,000,000.

The contracts shall be of a nature, scale, and complexity comparable to the works required under this procurement. For each contract submitted, the Bidder shall provide documentary evidence, such as a client-issued completion or performance certificate, indicating the contract value, scope of works, completion status, and dates of execution

Average Annual Turnover

The Bidder shall demonstrate an average annual turnover from contracts of fiber-optic, telecommunications, or similar connectivity infrastructure works of at least US$3,000,000, calculated over any three of the last five financial years. The Bidder shall submit certified financial statements, audited accounts, or other acceptable documentary evidence to substantiate the reported turnover.

Liquid Assets and/or Credit Facilities

The Bidder shall demonstrate access to liquid assets and/or confirmed lines of credit, net of other contractual commitments, of not less than US$1,500,000. Acceptable evidence may include recent bank statements, bank certificates, or a letter from a regulated financial institution confirming the availability of the required funds or credit facilities. The evidence shall be issued no earlier than the period specified in the Bidding Documents.

5. Bidding will be conducted through an international competitive tender using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, July 2016” as amended from time to time and is open to all bidders with public telecommunications services experience who are the licensed in South Sudan, as well as potential new entrants who must qualify and eligible for this competition. All bidders may collaborate with any licensed subcontractors, so long as full responsibility for meeting the requirements of this Procurement Document rests fully with the eligible prime contractor. Bidders may also form joint ventures in accordance with the rules of this Procurement Document.

6. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the procurement document. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 30% and for Bid cost: 70%.

7. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Senior Procurement Specialist, Ministry of Information Communication Technology and Postal Services, Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and inspect the bidding document during office hours from 10.00 hrs to 16:00 hrs at the address given below.  The bidding document in English may be purchased by interested Bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a non-refundable fee of United States Dollars three Hundred ($300) or its equivalent in South Sudanese Pounds at prevailing rate. The method of payment will be by cash. The document will be sent by email to those who have paid. Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 2:00pm South Sudan local time on October 26, 2026. Electronic Bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. The outer Bid envelopes marked “ORIGINAL BID”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below at 2:15pm or immediately after the deadline time for bid submission on October 26, 2026. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Employer until the second public Bid opening.

8. All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid-Securing Declaration

9. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.

The overall objective of this consultant service (“the Service”) is to provide support in managing social risks directly or indirectly attributable or identified as a consequence of the Project, materially compliant to the ESF. The Social Development Specialist will assist MAFWM in ensuring that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs) and this Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), in a manner acceptable to the World Bank.

 

The Social Development Specialist shall be engaged to deliver all the needed support on a full-time daily basis (8 hours per day, working days, from Monday to Friday). The consultancy is expected to start in September 2026 and continue up to the project's implementation (end of March 2031), including a probation period of three months.

 

The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, through Technical Service Unit, now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Service. Interested consultants must provide Cover Letter and CV representing description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions and availability of appropriate skills (scanned diplomas to be sent with CV). Individual consultants may be offered through firms or other organizations, but the qualifications of the individual consultant will be the basis of selection. Contract will be signed with proposed individuals.

 

The criteria for selection are following:

  • Graduate/Advanced Degree (Master’s Degree) in the environment & social safeguard area, Social Sciences, Law, or related discipline.
  • Minimum 5 (five) years of relevant professional experience in social safeguards, community engagement, stakeholder processes, and risk management in investment projects (international and local).
  • Experience in at least 2 internationally funded projects in the field of social risk management under ESF or other IFI standards.
  • Direct involvement in preparation and implementation of ESMF, ESMP, ESMP checklists, RAPs.
  • Knowledge of international good practice for management of E&S risks, including World Bank ESF/Safeguard’s policies and International Finance Corporation (IFC) Sustainability Framework and supporting documents such as Guidance Notes.
  • Previous experience with World Bank-funded projects as a social reviewer and an understanding of their requirements would be an advantage.
  • Knowledge of domestic social and labor legislation would be an advantage.
  • Good analytical skills, ability to think strategically, analyze and synthesize diverse qualitative and quantitative socially related data and information.
  • Excellent spoken and written Montenegrin and English.
  • Computer skills, including word processing and spreadsheets.
  • Driving license, no obstacles for traveling within Montenegro for various field trips.

 

The evaluation criteria will be the following:

(i)         General Qualifications, including education, trainings and qualifications (40 points).

REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO

Agence pour le Développement et la Promotion du Projet Grand Inga
(ADPI-RDC)

Programme de Développement du Projet Inga 3 « PDI3 »

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(SELECTION DE CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL)

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) ASSUMANT LA FONCTION DE SPECIALISTE DE L'ENVIRONNEMENT AU SEIN DU PROGRAMME DE DEVELOPPEMENT INGA 3 (PDI3)

 

N° de crédit / N° de don : 7816-ZR (A) & 7815-ZR (B)

N° de référence de l’Avis : ZR-ADEPI-520117-CS-INDV

Date de Publication : le 10 septembre 2026

Date de clôture : le 24 septembre 2026

 

1. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie de réduction du déficit énergétique au niveau national, le Gouvernement de la RDC a demandé et obtenu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) deux lignes de crédit (A et B) pour financer le « Programme de Développement du Projet INGA 3 (PDI 3) », et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit en vue d’effectuer des paiements au titre d’un contrat pour les prestations des services d’un(e) « Consultant assumant la fonction de Spécialiste de l'environnement au sein du Programme de Développement Inga 3 (PDI3)».

 

2. Au titre des services, sous l’autorité du Directeur de Projet, le/la Spécialiste Senior en Environnement aura pour mission d’assurer, pour le compte de l’ADPI-RDC au sein de l’ECP-PDI3, la prise en charge adéquate, efficace et traçable des aspects environnementaux de toutes les activités du Projet, conformément à la législation nationale applicable, au Cadre environnemental et social de la Banque mondiale, à l’Accord de financement, au Manuel d’Exécution du Projet (MEP), au Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social (PEES) et aux instruments environnementaux et sociaux du PDI3.

 

De manière spécifique, le (la) Consultant(e) aura comme responsabilité, entre autres de :

  • conseiller le Directeur de Projet, les équipes de l’ECP-PDI3 et de l’ADPI-RDC sur les questions sectorielles ainsi que sur la gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux liés au Projet ;
  • intégrer les exigences environnementales dans le Plan de Travail et Budget Annuel (PTBA), le Plan de Passation des Marchés (PPM), les Termes de Référence (TDR), les Dossiers d’Appel d’Offres (DAO), les contrats, les plans de travail, les livrables et les rapports des consultants et prestataires recrutés par le Projet ;
  • organiser ou appuyer le screening environnemental des activités et sous-projets et déterminer les instruments environnementaux requis ;
  • assurer la revue qualité et le suivi de la mise en œuvre des instruments environnementaux préparés par les consultants ;
  • contribuer à la préparation et au suivi des TDR des études environnementales et sociales, notamment les études environnementales et sociales stratégiques, les études d’impact cumulatif, les études d’impact environnemental et social (EIES), les Plans de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (PGES), les plans de gestion spécifiques et les TDR d’assistance technique ;
  • vérifier l’intégration des clauses environnementales, sociales, d’hygiène et de sécurité (ESHS), des codes de conduite, des exigences de santé et sécurité au travail (SST) et des mesures de gestion environnementale dans les marchés ;
  • contribuer, lorsque sollicité par l’ECP-PDI3, à l’évaluation technique des offres sur les aspects environnementaux, sans se substituer aux commissions compétentes ;
  • suivre l’exécution des mesures environnementales prévues dans le PEES, le Cadre de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (CGES), les PGES et les autres instruments spécifiques ;
  • réaliser ou appuyer les missions de surveillance et de suivi environnemental sur les sites d’études, de travaux, de réhabilitations, de routes rurales, de zones d’emprunt, de corridors ou d’installations temporaires ;
  • examiner les rapports environnementaux des consultants, entreprises et missions de contrôle et assurer le suivi de la clôture des commentaires, réserves et non-conformités ;
  • suivre les non-conformités, incidents, accidents, plaintes environnementales, mesures correctives et rapports des prestataires ;
  • notifier immédiatement au Directeur de Projet tout incident ou accident environnemental, de SST ou communautaire significatif et contribuer à la préparation des rapports requis ;
  • appuyer la formation des équipes du Projet, des prestataires et des parties prenantes sur les exigences environnementales, la SST, la gestion de la pollution et des déchets, la biodiversité et les clauses ESHS ;
  • veiller à l’appropriation des instruments environnementaux et sociaux par les équipes de l’ADPI-RDC et de l’ECP-PDI3, l’Unité Provinciale d’Appui (UPA), les prestataires et les bénéficiaires institutionnels ;
  • tenir et mettre à jour une base documentaire environnementale comprenant notamment les screenings, avis, rapports, incidents, non-conformités, preuves de clôture, formations, consultations techniques et différentes versions des instruments ;
  • préparer les rapports mensuels, trimestriels, annuels et circonstanciés, les rapports de mission, les contributions aux aide-mémoire et les rapports de clôture ;
  • capitaliser les leçons apprises et assurer le transfert des outils de gestion environnementale aux équipes du Projet.

 

3. La durée de la mission est de douze (12) mois, assortie d’une période probatoire de quatre (4) mois. Le contrat est renouvelable sur la base des besoins du Projet, de la disponibilité budgétaire, d’une évaluation de performance jugée satisfaisante et de toute non-objection requise.

 

Le poste sera basé à Kinshasa, au sein de l’ECP-PDI3, avec des missions régulières à Matadi, dans les territoires ciblés du Kongo Central, sur le site d’Inga et dans toute autre zone pertinente pour les activités du PDI3. Background

 

The SADC Secretariat through the SADC Regional Statistics Project has received a grant. The aim of this grant is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC and participating countries to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonization and collaboration.

 

The main guiding frameworks are SADC Vision 20250 and the SADC Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan 2020-2030 (RISDP 2020-2030). The Regional Infrastructure Development Master Plan (RIDMP), the SADC Regional Agricultural Policy (RAP), the Industrialisation Strategy and the Roadmap, among others, are complementary guiding frameworks for achieving the regional integration agenda. SADC has also developed various Protocols for domestication and implementation by Member States including the most recent one, the Protocol on Statistics, to enhance harmonization of statistics. The operating framework for implementing statistical activities as priorities for the region is the Regional Strategy for Development of Statistics (RSDS) and is aligned to SADC Vision 2050 and RISDP 2020-30.

 

Demand for quality and harmonized statistics has been on the rise to monitor progress in developmental agendas at national, regional, continental, and global level. The scope of data demand cuts across economic, social, and on emerging issues such as climate change, disaster-risk, environment and others related.

  1. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
    1. Partner country

The Southern African Development Community (SADC).

 

    1. Contract authority

The Contracting Authority is SADC Secretariat, represented by its Executive Secretary.

 

    1. Background

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) is a Regional Economic Community comprising 16 Member States, namely; Angola, Botswana, Comoros, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe. Established in 1992, SADC is committed to Regional Integration and poverty eradication within Southern Africa through economic development and ensuring peace and security.

 

Article 14 of the SADC Treaty establishes the SADC Secretariat as the principal executive institution of SADC. The Secretariat performs its mandate and functions within the policy, strategic and programme provisions outlined in the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan (RISDP) and the Vision 2050. The SADC Vision 2050 earmarks Statistics a priority cross-cutting sector whereby by 2050, the region strategic objective in statistics is to realize a robust and responsive regional statistical system to underpin regional integration processes, including measurement of progress and impact.

 

    1. Current situation in the sector

In the discipline of Official Statistics there is an absolute necessity of evolving towards programming languages oriented to modern data science to face new challenges such as fast prototyping innovative ideas, standardizing production processes and automatizing manual tasks. The implementation of statistical techniques, methods and methodologies can be done with Python functions and scripts in a more efficient way.


The Secretariat is prioritizing statistical capacity building as part of its implementation plan guided by the Regional Strategy for Development of Statistics (RSDS) 2020-30. With the Regional Statistics Project funded by the World Bank, capacity building shall basically come in the form of development of practical guidelines in specific domains; rolling out national and regional training programmes and; assisting Member States through technical assistance. Data management and processing is within the sub-component 1.1 on improving capacity for data production, management and dissemination of the World Bank project.

 

With the growing need of analysing voluminous and complex survey data on a timely basis, open-source statistical softwares play a significant role. Thus, Secretariat is recruiting a consultancy firm which may include but not limited to research centres or universities to train SADC Member States statisticians on Python for beginners and intermediate level.

 

    1. Needs assessment

Member States were also requesting training on Python for official statisticians involved or not in Big Data and Data Science activities having no specific knowledge on the subject.

 

 

  1. OBJECTIVES, PURPOSE AND EXPECTED RESULTS
    1. Overall objective

The overall objective of this exercise is to train Member States on the use of statistical software for management of large database and analysis of complex surveys.

    1. Specific objectives (Purpose)

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake a national training on Python  for processing of data for official statistics, especially:

  1. to introduce participants to the Python language and ecosystem and to make them able to write basic Python programs for data processing, analysis and visualization; and

 

  1. to provide participants with intermediate level knowledge on Python language and ecosystem and to make them able to write Python programs for official statistics.

 

    1. Results to be achieved by the Consultancy Firm

The Consultancy Firm is expected to achieve the following result:

  1. Python component: Strengthened technical capacity of Statisticians from National Statistics Offices to have a good understanding of Python language and its ecosystem for use for Official Statistics purposes and to be familiar with syntax of Python for reading of a file, processing of data, modelling, aggregation and visualization.

 

  1. SCOPE OF WORK FOR TRAINING ON PYTHON
    1. Scope of work

The selected service provider is expected to deliver in-person technical training workshop on Python to process and analyze official statistics for data producers of official statistics at national level for respective Member State for 10 working days (5 working days for Beginners and 5 working days for intermediate levels)

The training includes theoretical and practical sessions to help participants understand Python syntax and its ecosystem for data management, statistical analysis, tabulations, graphics, and maps from complex census, survey data, and big data. The training report should contain summary of topics covered during training week. Training materials should also be shared to all participants and annexed to be training report

It is expected that the training to be done with real anonymized data obtained from censuses, survey and administrative data undertaken by National Statistics Offices.

 

    1. Geographical area to be covered

The assignment will be carried out in 10 selected Member States of SADC Region, namely (Botswana, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, Zimbabwe).

    1. Target groups

This consultancy is expected to target the National Statistics Office and other stakeholders, in particular, statisticians involved in processing and analysis of official statistics, large data and complex surveys.

    1. Specific work

The assignment will be carried out primarily through a national training in five selected Member States of SADC Region.

In particular, the consultant will be required to:

  1. Inception report detailing approach, methods, assumptions, risks, timelines and content of topics covered and training programme
  2. Develop a generic training materials to cater for practical training on Python.
  3. To tailor the programme to the needs of each Member State for intermediate level.
  4. To deliver the training at mutually agreed dates
  5. To give training on application of Python in data processing, management and analysis in survey data and census and other complex data, big data, satellite image data and to cover at least the following topics for beginners’ level:
  • Essentials of Python environment and knowledge about the individual aspects of data processing pipeline (reading file, processing data, saving results, modelling, aggregation, visualization and saving results)
  • Essential syntax of Python; functions, main data structures (tuples, lists, dictionaries)
  • Importing data in Python
  • Creating, manipulating and converting common data structures
  • Merging data from different data sources or different questionnaires
  • Writing functions and using pre-existing functions
  • Introduction to the NumPy library
  • Creation and handling of arrays
  • Packages like Pandas, Matpotlib, Seaborn, Scikit-learn, Geopandas,

 

  1. To give training on application of Python in data processing, management and analysis in survey data and census and other complex data, big data, satellite image data and to cover at least the following topics for intermediate level:

 

  • Performance and differences with respect to Python lists
  • Object-oriented programming
  • Mathematical operations and broadcasting
  • Use of Encapsulation with Python for official statistics and big data
  • Use of Inheritance with Python for official statistics and big data
  • Usage of universal functions (ufuncs)
  • Polymorphism applied to official statistics
  • Python and production of official statistics
  • Sampling and weighting with Python
  • Statistical models with Python
  • Python and processing of big data
  • Python and satellite image/GIS
  • Python and automation/machine learning

 

 

  1. Produce well documented Training Materials to be shared with participants with step-by-step indication for all the topics covered
  2. Produce a Training Report for each Member State with a summary of topics covered during the training and recommendations for implementation
  3. To do a pre- and Post-Training Surveys assessment of participants knowledge and identifying areas of improvement

The experts from the Firm shall assist participants in first handling of Python on the first day of the training for them to use it correctly.

 

    1. Reserve for continuation of contract

The assignment is for training in 10 SADC Member States. The Firm shall be subject to evaluation after each training in a Member State. Continuation of contract is upon satisfactory completion and quality of the previous assignment.

 

    1. Eligible entities

Eligible entities for the current assignment are consultancy firm which may include but not limited to research centres or universities.
