description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

Country: Moldova

Name of Project: Moldova Rural Connectivity Project

Project ID: P180153

 

Assignment Title: Technical assistance for the further development of Road Asset Management System in Moldova

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MRCP/CS/08

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank (the “Bank” or the “WB”) in the form of a loan/credit toward the cost of the Moldova Rural Connectivity Project. The S.A. ”Administraia Naional a Drumurilor” (“NRA” or JSC “National Road Administration”), an implementing agency (the “Client”), intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan/credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is issued.

NRA has developed and operates a Road Asset Management System (RAMS). However, there are still many unresolved issues that prevent the proper use of the RAMS as a key pillar for the further effective road investment and maintenance planning processes, such as: lack of integration/interoperability of sub systems; manual intensive data collection; fragmentation of roles in RAMS related data collection and utilization; non-clear future alignment with the road register; lack of the sufficient legal regulation.

NRA intends to retain a consultant to lay the strategic, technical, institutional, and legal groundwork for the modernization of NRA's Road Asset Management System, so that Moldova's national road network can be managed efficiently, cost-effectively, and in line with European standards. Specifically, consultant will be required to review business processes and recommend improvements; review of existing IT based tools, software, databases, etc. architecture and integration and recommendations for further improvement preparation; develop a future RAMS Roadmap; define the asset inventory scope and data governance framework required for the future RAMS; Policy Framework Development; develop a training program and conduct a number of in-person workshops covering mentioned above topics.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained following a formal request to the Client to procurement.wb@andsa.md.

 

The NRA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Consulting Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Consultant will be a firm or a group of firms (JVCA[1]) with previous project experience related to Construction Supervision Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria:

The following shortlisting criteria will be applied to all consulting firms (individual company or joint venture overall) that have submitted EoI:

1. Criterion: General Firm Experience

Proven general experience and verifiable track record in providing consultancy/technical assistance related to Road Asset Management Systems (RAMSs), completed within the past ten (10) years. RAMS-related consultancy/technical assistance may cover studies; strategies; policy frameworks; institutional support; or preparation of methodologies, guidelines, and standards.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 20 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

2. Criterion: Development or implementation of RAMS solutions

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to development or implementation of the existing RAMS solutions, deployed on local and/or national road networks with paved and unpaved roads, completed within the past ten (10) years. For the purpose of this criterion, an assignment shall be considered completed if the RAMS solution has been fully developed and/or deployed and formally accepted by the client, regardless of subsequent maintenance or update activities.

Preference will be given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 40 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

3. Criterion: Road network data

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to road network data survey, collection, and verification to be incorporated in a developed road database, completed within the past ten (10) years.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 30 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

4. Criterion: Training

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in delivering training related to RAMS completed within the last ten (10) years, with preference given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 10 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

As a proof, the Consultant shall prepare a table listing following information: name of the relevant assignments, year of contract’s implementation (start year, end year), information on contract value, length of road network covered, percentage carried out by Consultant in case of association of firms and short description of main activities, contracting entity/client, country/region, contact reference (name, e-mail, phone number).

The maximum score that can be awarded to the Consultant is 100 points based on the cumulative evaluation of all criteria.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The submitted EOI shall not exceed 40 pages.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection method (QCBS) set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.15 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the abovementioned World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 09:00 to 16:00 local time.

 

Expressions of Interest, in English, must be delivered to the Client to the address below, marked “Expression of Interest” for Technical assistance for the further development of Road Asset Management System in Moldova (RAMS), by e-mail or in person - one hard copy (placed in an envelope - one original and one copy and one electronic copy on memory stick), to the address mentioned below, by October 27th , 2026, at 10:00 AM, local time.

Expressions of Interest received after this time and date will not be considered. 

Consultants should be aware that distance and customs formalities may require longer than expected delivery time.

 

 

Executing Agency (Client)

National Road Administration

Attn: Mrs. Natalia Capatina

Office 336, Bucuriei str. 12A, MD 2004

Chisinau, Republic of Moldova

E-mail: procurement.wb@andsa.md

Website: www.andsa.md

 

[1] JVCA – Joint Venture, Consortium or Association

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

APPEL A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET N° CI 17-26/CN

RECRUTEMENT D'UN(E) RESPONSABLE SOCIAL(E) AU NIVEAU DE L’UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET DE RESILIENCE DES SYSTEMES ALIMENTAIRES A MADAGASCAR (FSRP)

  1. La République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour couvrir le coût du PROJET DE RESILIENCE DES SYSTEMES ALIMENTAIRES DE MADAGASCAR (FSRP) sous tutelle du Ministère de L’Agriculture et de la Souveraineté Alimentaire et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit/don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Recrutement d'un(e) Responsable Social(e) au niveau de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Résilience des Systèmes alimentaires à Madagascar ».
  2. Les services de consultant individuel (« les services ») auront pour objectif principal l’amélioration continue de la performance sociale du projet tout en veillant à l’écoute permanente des différentes parties prenantes. De manière spécifique, le consultant individuel sera appelé(e) à intégrer la gestion des risques et effets sociaux à toutes les phases de préparation et d’exécution des différentes activités ou sous-projets liés aux différentes composantes, et à respecter et mettre en œuvre les principes et les activités liées à l’engagement citoyen dans le cadre du projet. 
  3. La durée du contrat s’étendra jusqu’au 30 Juin 2029, sous réserve d’une période d’essai de six (06) mois concluants, et des évaluations annuelles performantes et satisfaisantes par le projet. Le poste est basé à Antananarivo avec des déplacements probables dans les zones d’interventions du projet. Les termes de référence détaillés (TdR) pour la mission et le modèle de CV peuvent être obtenus aux adresses indiquées ci-dessous (point 10).
  4. L’Unité de Gestion du PROJET DE RESILIENCE DES SYSTEMES ALIMENTAIRES DE MADAGASCAR (FSRP) invite maintenant les consultants individuels éligibles ("Consultants individuels") à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants individuels intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services, et constituer un dossier de manifestation d’intérêt incluant :
  • Une lettre de motivation rédigée en français ;
  • CV détaillé ;
  • Copie certifiée des diplômes, certificats et attestations de travail ;
  • Les attestations / certificats de travail ;
  • Une adresse email et numéro de téléphone pour contact rapide.

      5. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

  • Un diplôme académique (Bac +4 minimum) en sciences sociales ou humaines (sociologie, anthropologie, géographie, droit, développement rural, sciences politiques ou disciplines connexes) ;
  • Ayant au moins cinq (05) années d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion des risques et impacts sociaux de projets de développement financés par des partenaires techniques et financiers nationaux ou internationaux ;
  • Au moins trois (03) expériences avérées dans la préparation, la revue ou le suivi de la mise en œuvre de Plans de Réinstallation (PR), Cadres de Réinstallation (CR) ou autres instruments liés à l’acquisition foncière et à la réinstallation involontaire ;
  • Une bonne connaissance pratique des Normes Environnementales et Sociales (NES) de la Banque mondiale démontrée par une expérience professionnelle pertinente dans leur application ;
  • Expérience dans l’identification, l’évaluation et le suivi des risques sociaux liés aux activités de travaux, y compris les risques relatifs aux travailleurs, aux conflits communautaires, aux restrictions d’accès aux ressources, aux déplacements économiques et physiques, ainsi qu’aux violences basées sur le genre/EAS-HS ;
  • La maîtrise du cadre juridique et institutionnel national en matière d’évaluation environnementale et sociale ;
  • Une parfaite maîtrise du cadre juridique et institutionnel national en matière d’expropriation pour cause d’utilité publique à l’acquisition à l’amiable de propriétés immobilières par l’Etat ou les collectivités publiques secondaires et aux plus-values foncières ;  
  • La maîtrise des textes juridiques applicables en matière de droit des travailleurs, et violences basées sur le genre ;
  • Expérience dans la conduite de consultations publiques, la mobilisation des parties prenantes et le suivi de Plans de Mobilisation des Parties Prenantes (PMPP) ;
  • Bonne compréhension des enjeux liés à l’inclusion sociale, au genre, à l’accès équitable aux bénéfices du projet et à la prise en compte des groupes vulnérables ;
  • Ayant une capacité justifiée en rédaction de rapport en langue Française, et Malagasy, la connaissance pratique de l’anglais constitue un atout ;
  • Capacité démontrée à travailler avec des équipes multidisciplinaires et à intégrer les recommandations des partenaires techniques et financiers dans les instruments de gestion des risques sociaux.

       6. L'attention des Consultants individuels intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI », 7ème édition, Septembre 2025, énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

       7. Un consultant individuel sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection agréée pour les Consultants Individuels énoncée dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

       8. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 09h00 à 17h00.

       9. Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être remises en version physique et/ou en version électronique à l'adresse ci-dessous, sous enveloppe fermée mentionnant clairement sur l’enveloppe extérieure le nom du poste au plus tard le 28 septembre 2026 à 17 heures 00 minute.

1. The Government of Suriname has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the project Suriname Competitiveness and Sector Diversification project (SCSD) loan IBRD 8985 SR and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract[1] for Machines online

All goods shall be new and unused.

 

Please note: This Invitation consists of a total of 6 items. Bids will only be accepted for evaluation if the 2 mandatory items (Item 1. Big CNC  and Item 2, 1 Fiber Laser  are fully priced. Failure to provide pricing for these 2 mandatory items shall result in the immediate rejection of the bid as non-responsive."

 

Bidding will be conducted through national competitive procurement through the procurement method RFQ as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

  1. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Project Implementing Unit, Suriname Competitiveness and Sector Diversification project (SCSD) at the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation, the procurement specialist at the email addresses:  procurement.ez@gov.srcc: cus@surinamecompete.org
  2. The bidding document can be requested through email.
  3. Bids must be delivered by email by June 18, 2026, at 2.00 PM. Late Bids will be rejected.
  4. All Bids must be accompanied by a signed Bid-Securing Declaration.
  5. The addresses referred to above are:

Attn: PIU SCSD Project

Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation

CUS Department 2nd floor unit 2.2

Frederik Derbystraat 68a

Email: procurement.ez@gov.sr and cc; cus@surinamecompete.org

 

 

 

Mandatory RFQ Conditions and Submission Requirements

Equipment FabLab – SCSD Project

 

1. Quotation Addressed To

Mr.Jean van Eenaeme, Procurement Specialist SCSD Project

jean.van.eenaeme1@gmail.com

The quotation must be prepared for the delivery, installation, commissioning, and training of the requested equipment for the SCSD project/FabLab.

 

2. Scope of Supply

The quotation must include, at a minimum:

•  Supply of the offered equipment in accordance with the requested specifications.

•  Delivery to the FabLab location in Suriname.

•  Installation and setup of the equipment.

•  Functional testing and commissioning.

•  Operator training and basic maintenance instruction.

•  Warranty and aftersales support during the warranty period.

•  All required standard accessories for normal operation.

•  Technical documentation, datasheets, manuals and warranty documentation.

Supply-only quotations, or quotations limited to shipment/delivery of boxed equipment without installation, commissioning and training, may be considered non-responsive.

 

3. Technical Compliance

The bidder shall quote in accordance with the requested specifications. Any deviation from the requested specifications must be clearly stated and explained. A technical compliance matrix must be submitted with the quotation, showing for each requirement: requested specification; offered specification; compliance status; deviation, if any; and reference to datasheet/brochure page. Offers that do not clearly identify deviations may be considered non-responsive.

 

4. Mandatory Product Information

For each offered item, the bidder must provide:

•  Brand, exact model, and manufacturer.

•  Product installed dimensions and net weight.

•  Country of origin.

•  Full technical datasheet of the exact offered model/configuration.

•  Configuration list and included accessories.

•  List of exclusions, if any.

•  Recommended spare parts and consumables list, including pricing.

Generic catalogues without clear identification of the exact offered model/configuration may be rejected.

 

5. Supplier Qualification

The bidder must provide evidence of capability to supply, install and support the offered equipment. The bidder shall submit:

•  Company registration details (KKF).

•  Confirmation whether the bidder is the manufacturer, authorized distributor, authorized reseller, or system integrator.

•  If not the manufacturer, a manufacturer authorization letter or proof of authorized supply/support relationship may be requested.

•  Details of the technical support team and local support provider.

 

6. Electrical, Utility and Site Requirements

For each machine, the bidder must provide a site preparation sheet including: required voltage; phase and frequency; maximum current; recommended breaker size; plug or connection type; grounding requirements; compressed air or gas requirements (if applicable); water cooling/chiller requirements (if applicable); ventilation/fume extraction requirements; floor space and working clearance; floor loading requirements; environmental requirements (temperature and humidity); and unloading/forklift/crane requirements. The FabLab will arrange the required facilities based on the information provided by the bidder.

 

7. Installation, Commissioning and Training

The quotation must include installation, commissioning and training. Commissioning shall include: physical installation/setup; power-up and functional testing; test run or sample output; verification of main machine functions; basic operator and maintenance instruction; handover of manuals and warranty documents; and a signed commissioning/acceptance report. Training shall cover safe operation, basic machine use, routine maintenance, and basic troubleshooting.

 

8. Warranty and Aftersales Support

The warranty period shall be a minimum of one year from the date of successful commissioning and signed acceptance. The quotation must state the warranty period, scope, exclusions, local support arrangement, and procedure for warranty claims. The bidder shall provide local support and aftersales service throughout the warranty period.

 

9. Safety Requirements

Where applicable, offered machines must include relevant safety provisions such as: emergency stop; safety interlocks; protective covers or enclosures; laser safety protection/PPE; fume extraction or ventilation provisions; safety labels and operating instructions; and user manuals with safety instructions. Laser equipment must include appropriate safety documentation and recommended PPE.

 

10. Pricing Requirements

The quotation must be priced in USD and must clearly show: equipment price; required accessories; delivery to FabLab; installation; commissioning; training; warranty/aftersales support; and optional spare parts and consumables (listed separately). Prices must be quoted inclusive of import duties and delivery to the FabLab. VAT shall be quoted at 0%. Any exemption from import duties will be determined after award.

 

11. Payment Terms

•  85% of the contract sum upon delivery of the equipment to the FabLab.

•  15% of the contract sum after successful installation, commissioning, training and signed acceptance.

 

12. Delivery Time

The bidder must state the delivery time to the FabLab, including production time, shipping time, import/customs clearance, and local delivery.

 

13. Quotation Validity

The quotation and pricing must be valid for four weeks from the date of issue.

 

14. Clarifications and Right to Reject

The purchaser may request clarifications, additional technical documentation, manufacturer confirmation, or proof of supplier capability. The purchaser reserves the right to reject incomplete quotations, non-compliant offers, offers with unclear deviations, or offers that do not demonstrate sufficient capability for delivery, installation, commissioning and aftersales support.

 

15. Evaluation Criteria

Quotations will be evaluated based on: technical compliance with the requested specifications; completeness of submitted documentation; supplier qualification and experience; delivery and installation capability; warranty and aftersales support; delivery time; and price. The purchaser is not obligated to select the lowest-priced quotation if the offer does not sufficiently meet the technical, support, documentation, or delivery requirements.

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE Nº 06/2026

(SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA INDIVIDUAL)

País: Brasil

Mutuário: Estado de Sergipe

Nome do Projeto: Projeto para Aceleração Digital Eficiente de Sergipe – Conecta-SE

Título do Contrato: Serviços de Consultoria Individual especialista em Data Center.

Empréstimo no 9793-BR

Referência nº : BR-SEPLAN-472988-CS-INDV

 

O Estado de Sergipe recebeu um financiamento do Banco Mundial para o custo Projeto para Aceleração Digital Eficiente de Sergipe – Conecta-SE, Acordo de Empréstimo nº 9793-BR, e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos para Contratação de Consultor individual especializado para: (i) planejar e executar diagnóstico técnico baseado em evidências da infraestrutura de data centers e dos ambientes computacionais definidos no Anexo de Escopo; (ii) projetar cenários de arquitetura-alvo e recomendar solução para horizonte de 10 (dez) anos, com análise de riscos, TCO/LCC, continuidade, segurança e sustentabilidade; (iii) auxiliar na elaboração dos artefatos técnicos da contratação subsequente; (iv) realizar transferência de conhecimento; e (v) prestar apoio técnico consultivo e independente ao processo de seleção, nos limites e produtos P1 a P6 abrangendo o site principal do Estado de Sergipe (localizado nas atuais dependências da EMGETIS e seu site-backup (antigo prédio da SEFAZ).

 

Os serviços de consultoria incluem: diagnóstico técnico e auditoria da infraestrutura atual e legada de Data Centers e ambientes computacionais; levantamento e inventário de ativos, análise de capacidade, resiliência, conformidade, segurança e governança; planejamento estratégico e modelagem de cenários de arquitetura futura, incluindo análise comparativa de TCO/LCC, continuidade operacional, riscos e sustentabilidade; apoio à elaboração de especificações técnicas e Termo de Referência para a contratação da nova infraestrutura; transferência de conhecimento às equipes do Estado; e apoio técnico especializado e independente na avaliação das propostas do processo de seleção subsequente. O escopo completo encontra-se descrito no Termo de Referência, no seguinte link: https://www.se.gov.br/seplan/conecta_se

Diante do exposto, a Secretaria Especial de Planejamento, Orçamento e Inovação – SEPLAN, por meio de sua Unidade de Gerenciamento do Programa (UGP), torna público que está aberto o prazo para Consultores Individuais manifestarem seu interesse em prestar os serviços de consultoria descritos. Os interessados deverão demonstrar, por meio de seu currículo, que possuem as qualificações e experiência relevante para desempenhar os serviços.

Manifestação de Interesse: Os interessados deverão apresentar Currículo Profissional, no qual o cumprimento dos requisitos obrigatórios e desejáveis, bem como suas qualificações e experiência relevantes para o escopo dos serviços, estejam claramente demonstrados.

Os critérios de avaliação do perfil profissional do(a) Consultor(a) Individual estão descritos no item 6 do Termo Referência (TDR) da consultoria – disponível no seguinte link: https://www.se.gov.br/seplan/conecta_se

 

O(a) consultor(a) individual será selecionado(a) através da avaliação de suas qualificações e experiências, de acordo com os procedimentos do Banco Mundial para Consultores Individuais contidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos, Quinta Edição – setembro de 2023, Seção VII, Parágrafos 7.34 a 7.39 (Métodos aprovados para seleção de consultores individuais).

Caso haja mais de um processo de seleção de consultores individuais em andamento no âmbito do CONECTA-SE, o profissional poderá se candidatar a todos aqueles para os quais entenda possuir as qualificações necessárias. Contudo, apenas poderá ser contratado em um deles. Assim, caso seja selecionado em mais de um processo, deverá optar por apenas um.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para os parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 da  Seção III do Regulamento que define a política do BIRD em matéria de Conflito de Interesses, bem como, as cláusulas de Fraude e Corrupção contidas no Anexo IV do Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento, edição setembro/2023.

 

Mais informações podem ser obtidas por meio do e-mail:

aquisicoes.conecta@seplan.se.gov.br

As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser entregues vi correio eletrônico/e-mail aquisicoes.conecta@seplan.se.gov.br  até às 23:45 horas do dia 02 de outubro de 2026, de acordo com os dados a seguir:

 

Manifestação de Interesse nº 06/2026

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(FRAMEWORK AGREEMENTS FOR CONSULTING SERVICES )

 

Lebanese Republic

Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR)

Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP)

Reference No.: FA-CS-BLDG (PARTIAL DAMAGE)

 

Assignment Title: Framework Agreemtns for the Design, structural assessment, rehabilitation and construction supervision of public buildings affected by varying levels of damage (slightly, partially damaged)

 

The Lebanese Republic (hereinafter called the “Borrower”) has received financing in the amount of US$250 million from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) (the “Bank”) toward the cost of the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP). The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), acting as the executing agency on behalf of the Government of Lebanon, intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under contracts for consulting services under Framework Agreements.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve engaging Design & Supervision Consultants under Framework Agreements for several contracts to Design, structural assessment, rehabilitation and construction supervision of public buildings affected by varying levels of damage (slightly, partially damaged  across Beirut & Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and South Lebanon

The Framework Agreements will be concluded through a Two-Stage Selection Process and the consulting services shall include the preparation of:

  • Task 1: Structural Validation and Damage Assessment
  • Task 2: Supporting the Environmental and Social Framework
  • Task 3 a - Design of Slightly Damage

            b - Detailed Design for Moderate and partially damage

  • Task 4  Support to Procurement and Contracting Process
  • Task 5   Construction Supervision

The Framework Agreement will be signed for a duration of Thirty-Six (36) months with multiple qualified engineering consultancy firms. Specific assignments will be awarded as Call-Off contracts across distinct Call-Off Modules (ranging from slight to moderate  damage levels) on an as-needed basis.

The full version of the Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found on the CDR website at: https://www.cdr.gov.lb/en-US/Procurment.aspx

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultant Brochures may also be included in the submission.

The shortlisting criteria for Stage 1 evaluation are:

1. Firm Legal Standing & Core Buisness and Years of Experience

  • Legal registration and authorization to operate in its country of incorporation, demonstrating financial soundness.
  • Legally established consulting firm (or lead member of a Joint Venture of maximum two (2) members) with a minimum of Fifteen  (15 ) years of demonstrated experience   in design and supervision services for  buildings projects. (preferably Public Building)

 

2. Specific Technical Experience :

  • Design: Experience with at least three (3) projects of building designs within the last ten (10) years, with one involving detailed assessment and structural evaluation of damaged buildings (slightly, partially), including designs, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities Of buildings.  Building Rehabilitation Design experiences have added advantage.
  • Supervision: Experience as Lead Engineer/Supervision Consultant on at least two (2) projects within the last ten (10) years involving construction supervision and contract management of Buildings
  • Proven experience with Lebanese technical/regulatory frameworks. Experience under international financing institutions (including World Bank standards and Guidelines) is considered as an advantage.

3. Key Staff Pool & Quality Management (Stage 1 Requirements):

  • Submission of an accessible Key Experts pool available on an "on-call" basis.
  • A standard Quality Management Approach and preliminary methodology

 

4. Organizational & Managerial Capacity:

  • Demonstrated organizational and managerial capacity, including adequate in-house technical resources and project management systems to deliver assessment, technical verification, rehabilitation, repair, strengthening, and design services for slightly to partially damaged public buildings, including multiple sites concurrently.
  • Submission of a Quality Management Approach (maximum ten (10) pages) describing the Firm’s standard procedures, organizational arrangements, and quality assurance and quality control mechanisms for condition assessment and technical verification; feasibility and rehabilitation studies; architectural, structural and seismic assessment and design; MEP assessment and design; preparation of technical specifications, BOQs, cost estimates, tender documents; and construction-related technical services for slightly to partially damaged public buildings.

Interested consultants are requested to keep their EOIs to a maximum of twenty-five pages.

Please note that at this shortlisting stage:

  • Technical and financial proposals are not requested.
  • Key Experts, if proposed for the assignment, will not be evaluated.
  • Requests for clarification on the REOI or TOR may not be replied to at this time, as the allocated time for submission of EOI does not permit such exchanges.

The shortlist shall comprise five (5) to eight (8) consulting firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting Services and Consulting Services, dated February 2025, setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a Joint Venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.

Shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit their proposals, upon which a Consultant will be selected in accordance with the (LCS) described in the “World Bank “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting services” dated February 2025 and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Shortlisted Consultants will subsequently be invited to submit proposals under the Framework Agreement selection process in accordance with lcs  the Quality Based Selectionmethod described in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (February 2025).

The deadline for receiving Expressions of Interest shall be by Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026 at 12:00 noon Beirut local time.

                                           MINISTERE DE L’EDUCATION NATIONALE, DE L’ALPHABETISATION ET DE L’ENSEIGNEMENT TECHNIQUE

                                                                                                                                     --------------------

                                                                   PROJET DU PROGRAMME DE RENFORCEMENT DU SYSTEME EDUCATIF DE BASE

                                                                                                   Volet Financement de Projet d’Investissement (IPF)

 

                                                                     AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS N° 020C/PRSEB-PROJET/IDA-2026-

             SELECTION D'UN CABINET DE COMMUNICATION CHARGE DE LA CONCEPTION ET DE LA MISE EN ŒUVRE D'UNE CAMPAGNE NATIONALE D'INFORMATION ET DE SENSIBILISATION SUR LE PROGRAMME NATIONAL D'AMELIORATION DES PREMIERS APPRENTISSAGES SCOLAIRES (PNAPAS)

 

I.    CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

La Côte d'Ivoire a instauré l'école obligatoire de 6 à 16 ans (loi n°2015-635 du 17 septembre 2015). Si l'accès a progressé (taux brut de scolarisation de 101% en 2022), les évaluations PASEC 2014-2019 révèlent une crise des apprentissages fondamentaux : 67% des élèves en début de scolarité et 60% en fin de primaire sous le seuil suffisant en lecture ; 83% en mathématiques en fin de primaire.

Pour y répondre, le MENAET a élaboré la SNAPAS, opérationnalisée via le PNAPAS, qui fédère plusieurs initiatives antérieures (PAPSE, PEC, PNAAF, AVSI, PALEC, ELAN-CI) et introduit : nouveaux manuels, méthode structurée de lecture par décodage, pédagogie différenciée et remédiation, encadrement de proximité renforcé, et enseignement bilingue progressif dans les écoles pilotes.

Un risque majeur pèse sur l'appropriation du programme : scepticisme de la communauté éducative (perception de « laboratoire permanent »), résistances pédagogiques de certains enseignants et encadreurs, méconnaissance du programme par les parents et les maîtres de maison/répétiteurs.

Le pilier 7 de la SNAPAS prévoit donc une mobilisation de tous les acteurs via un plan de communication de masse (SCRP et DAPS-COGES). Le MENAET/DPFC recrute ainsi un cabinet de communication pour concevoir et déployer une campagne nationale d'information et de sensibilisation sur le PNAPAS, en capitalisant sur les canaux numériques existants (page Facebook DPFC, site dpfc-ci.net, plateforme pnapas.dpfc.ci) tout en s'appuyant prioritairement sur les canaux à forte pénétration populaire : radio (68% des ménages), télévision (93%), et téléphone mobile (WhatsApp, Facebook, TikTok), ainsi que les espaces de parole informels (marchés, grins, prêches, réunions APE/COGES).

Les présents termes de référence ont pour objet de définir le cadre de sélection d'un cabinet de communication national justifiant d'une expertise avérée dans la conduite de campagnes de changement social et comportemental (CCSC) dans le secteur social, en particulier en éducation, en Côte d'Ivoire.

II.   OBJECTIF GENERAL DE LA MISSION

L‘objectif général de la mission est de susciter l'adhésion, la confiance et l'engagement actif de l'ensemble de la communauté éducative ivoirienne, acteurs institutionnels de mise en œuvre, enseignants, parents d'élèves et maîtres de maison/répétiteurs, autour du PNAPAS, afin de favoriser une application effective et durable de ses innovations pédagogiques dans les salles de classe et un accompagnement cohérent des enfants à la maison.

III.  OBJECTIFS SPECIFIQUES DE LA MISSION

  • Faire connaître le PNAPAS (justification, vision, finalité 2030, articulation avec la SNAPAS) auprès des parties prenantes ;
  • Lever les éventuelles réticences au changement chez les acteurs de mise en œuvre (chaîne de supervision et d'encadrement pédagogique, directeurs d'école, enseignants, formateurs de CAFOP) en valorisant les résultats probants déjà obtenus à mi-parcours du PRSEB et par les projets pilotes dont le PNAPAS est issu, et en démontrant la pérennité de la démarche par rapport aux initiatives antérieures ;
  • Faire comprendre et accepter les innovations pédagogiques du PNAPAS : nouveaux manuels et intrants (décodables, déchiffrables, cahiers d'exercices, planches, guides-maîtres), méthode structurée d'apprentissage de la lecture-écriture fondée sur le décodage explicite, pédagogie différenciée et remédiation, de même que les innovations dans l’enseignements des mathématiques et les évaluations régulières des apprentissages ;
  • Clarifier le rôle attendu de chaque acteur (enseignants, encadreurs pédagogiques, directeurs d'école, parents d’élèves) dans la réussite du programme, et le rôle spécifique des maîtres de maison et répétiteurs scolaires à domicile ;
  • Sensibiliser les parents d'élèves à l'importance de l'assiduité, du suivi scolaire à la maison et de l'harmonisation entre l'accompagnement à domicile et les méthodes enseignées en classe ;
  • Sensibiliser spécifiquement les maîtres de maison et répétiteurs scolaires, acteurs non institutionnels mais très présents dans l'accompagnement scolaire à domicile en Côte d'Ivoire, notamment en milieu urbain, à l'utilisation des méthodes et outils du PNAPAS, afin d'éviter que des pratiques concurrentes (par exemple une méthode de lecture différente de celle enseignée en classe) ne brouillent les apprentissages et ne perturbent les enfants ;
  • Renforcer la visibilité institutionnelle du PNAPAS et l’engagement du MENAET auprès de l'opinion publique, des médias et des partenaires techniques et financiers.

IV.  PROFIL ET QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES DU CABINET

Critères d'éligibilité du cabinet

  • Être une agence ou un cabinet de communication légalement constitué en Côte d'Ivoire (ou un groupement incluant un partenaire local), en règle vis-à-vis de ses obligations fiscales et sociales ;
  • Justifier d'au moins cinq (5) années d'expérience dans la conduite de campagnes de communication institutionnelle, de sensibilisation ou de changement social et comportemental (CCSC)
  • Avoir conduit au moins deux (2) missions similaires dans le secteur social (éducation, santé, protection de l'enfance) en Côte d'Ivoire ou en Afrique de l'Ouest francophone au cours des cinq dernières années, avec preuves à l'appui (attestations de bonne exécution) ;
  • Démontrer une expérience de travail avec des institutions publiques ivoiriennes et/ou des partenaires techniques et financiers de l'éducation, avec preuves à l'appui (attestations de bonne exécution) ;
  • Disposer de capacités de production multicanale (imprimé, audiovisuel, digital, radio communautaire) et d'un réseau de diffusion couvrant les 31 régions et 14 districts autonomes du pays (images des équipements, tout document justifiant la propriété du matériel et l’attestation de Bonne Exécution en sont une preuve) ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience au minimum de communication en langues nationales ivoiriennes (attestation de bonne exécution, spot vidéo…).

Composition de l'équipe clé

Poste

Qualifications minimales requises

Chef de mission / Directeur de la stratégie de communication

Bac+4 en communication, sciences sociales ou marketing social ; 10 ans d'expérience dont 5 dans la conduite de campagnes CCSC, Justifier au moins 3 missions de production de spots et capsules pour le grand public, y compris en langues nationales ; expérience dans le secteur éducatif souhaitée.

Expert(e) en communication pour le changement social et comportemental

Bac+3 ; Justifier d’une expérience au minimum confirmée en conception de stratégies CCSC dans un contexte de réforme sectorielle, Justifier d’au minimum deux expériences d’organisation de communication sur terrain dans les espaces publics et/ou de travail avec les relais locaux (chefferies, leaders religieux, leaders communautaires, COGES).

Spécialiste en conception graphique / directeur artistique

Bac+2 dans une filière de Formation en design graphique ; portfolio de campagnes institutionnelles.

Expert(e) en gestion des réseaux sociaux et community management

Bac+2 en communication/en sciences sociales ou informatiques. Justifier de 3 créations Expérience dans l'animation de pages institutionnelles à forte audience, avec une pratique confirmée de WhatsApp (groupes/diffusion) en plus de Facebook et TikTok.

Spécialiste en suivi-évaluation / enquêtes de perception

Bac+5 en statistique, sociologie ou sciences de l'éducation ; expérience en enquêtes CAP (Connaissances, Attitudes, Pratiques).

NB : Les CV détaillés, diplômes et certificats de travail ou Attestation de Bonne Exécution (ABE) des Experts mobilisés doivent être joints aux dossiers de soumission des cabinets/groupements de cabinets.

Evaluation des cabinets / Groupements de cabinets

Le pourcentage de la note technique minimum (NT) requis pour être admis est de 70/100.

L’expertise du cabinet comptera pour 80% et le personnel clé pour 20%.

V.    DUREE DE LA MISSION ET CALENDRIER

La mission est prévue pour une durée globale de 12 mois à compter de la notification de l'ordre de service de démarrage.

VI.  PROCEDURE POUR LA SOUMISSION DES MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERETS

La Sélection de la radio se fera selon la méthode de la Sélection fondée sur la Qualification du Consultant (SQC) et ce, conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), édition de septembre 2025 et relatif à l’acquisition de Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants.

Le dossier de soumission devra être composé de :

  • Pour la conformité administrative le cabinet devra fournir :
  • Une lettre de manifestation d'intérêt/soumission adressée à l’UGP PRSEB ;
  • Les statuts et documents attestant de l'existence légale du cabinet (RCCM, Attestation de non-faillite,…) ;
  • Les attestations de régularité fiscale et sociale (ARF, Attestation de mise à jour CNPS, Quitus de non-redevabilité de l’ARCOP pour les cabinets ivoiriens……);
  • Références professionnelles et attestations de bonne exécution pour les missions similaires citées.
  • Pour la conformité techniques le cabinet devra :
  • Démontrer sa compréhension des termes de référence et des enjeux du PNAPAS ;
  • Produire une note méthodologique détaillée par phase, incluant l'approche de diagnostic, la démarche créative et le dispositif de déploiement et de suivi-évaluation ;
  • Proposer un calendrier éventuel détaillant de la mise en œuvre ;
  • L'équipe proposée, avec curriculum vitae et diplômes des experts clés ;
  • Portfolio de réalisations similaires (visuels, liens vers des campagnes antérieures).

La date limite pour le dépôt des manifestations d’intérêts est prévu pour le 30 septembre 2026 à 10 heures. L’enveloppe du cabinet devra porter la mention « AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS N° 20C/PRSEB-PROJET/IDA-2026 - Sélection d'un Cabinet de Communication chargé de la conception et de la mise en œuvre d'une Campagne Nationale D'information Et De Sensibilisation Sur Le Programme National D'amélioration Des Premiers Apprentissages Scolaires (PNAPAS) ».

Les manifestations d’intérêts devront être soumis en français et en cinq (05) exemplaires dont un (1) original et quatre (04) copies (le tout dans une grande et même enveloppe) et déposées sous plis fermé à l’adresse ci-dessous ou transmis par DHL, CHRONOPOSTE, FEDEX, etc.

Les soumissions par voie électronique ne seront pas acceptées.

Les manifestations d’intérêts seront ouvertes en présence du Comité d’évaluation et des représentants des soumissionnaires présents, à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le même jour le 30 septembre 2026 à 10 heures 30 minutes à l’adresse suivante :  Unité Projet PRSEB, sise à Cocody 2 Plateaux, 7ème tranche - Ilot 252 - Lot 3039 - Téléphone : (225) 27 22 55 94 40 Adresse électronique : atmbra@yahoo.com     Cc      yeo_pefougne@yahoo.fr

NB : Le retrait des termes de référence est obligatoire pour tout cabinet qui désire soumissionner. Ils sont disponibles sur demande ou à retirer au siège de l’Unité Projet.

Assignment Title: Consulting Firm Services for Strengthening Synergized Low-Carbon & Climate Resilience Development, Circular Economy, and Biodiversity Policy and Planning in Bitung City

Reference No.: ID-LH-567731-CS-CQS

 

The Government of Indonesia had received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Global Environment Facility Indonesia Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: (a) inventory data, profiling and scenario analysis, (b) developing strategies and action plans and (c) formulating practical guidelines to integrate low-carbon, climate-resilient, circular economy, and biodiversity. The Services are expected to start in November 2026 and be performed during a period of 8 months. The total estimated level of effort is approximately 67 technical/professional staff months. Further detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website: https://bit.ly/4inBnfx

 

The Directorate of Environmental Affairs, Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

Necessary:

  1. Preparing an action plan document related to environment indicators, city-wide masterplan development, spatial planning, and/or urban design in the last five years;
  2. Having experience working with Indonesian Government Officials at national and/or sub-national level in the last three years; and
  3. Experience working on the preparation and/or implementation of environmental and social policies of World Bank and/or other multilateral development banks.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms as a joint venture or a sub-consultant to enhance their qualifications. In the case of an association, the EOI must explicitly specify whether it is a Joint Venture (all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment) or Sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, the member firm appointed to represent it must be clearly identified. All the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Only the qualifications and experience of members of the joint venture, but not of sub-consultants, shall be considered in the EOI evaluation process.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09.00 AM to 03.00 P.M. Jakarta time (GMT+7) email: ulp@bappenas.go.id

Expressions of interest must be submitted electronically through the SPSE ICB system of Bappenas at https://spseicb.lkpp.go.id/ by September 21st, 2026, 10.00 A.M Jakarta time (GMT+7).

 

Jakarta, September 11st, 2026

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY CYBERSECURITY LEVEL PROTECTION ASSESSMENT SERVICE AND COMMERCIAL CRYPTOGRAPHY APPLICATION SECURITY EVALUATION SERVICE

for 

China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

Country: People's Republic of China

Name of Project: China Food Safety Improvement Project

Loan No.: IBRD-92130

Assignment Title: Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project Information Technology Third-Party Service Package II (Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Service and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Evaluation Service)

Reference No.:  GD-FSS-GAMR-CS13

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 0.56 million.

(I) Scope of Service

The service scope of this project covers the Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment services required for four informatization projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Contents

1. Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Services

Based on the assessment results of security technology and security management controls, as well as the overall system assessment, the service agency shall conduct a comprehensive assessment of the information system in accordance with the corresponding level standards and provide relevant security review opinions. This specifically includes two aspects: First, security control assessment, which primarily evaluates the implementation and configuration of basic security controls required by the cybersecurity level protection standards within the information system. Second, overall system assessment, which primarily analyzes the overall security of the information system. The security control assessment serves as the foundation for the overall security assessment of the information system.

2. Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment Services

The service agency shall provide security assessment services for systems upgraded with domestic cryptography. For the upgraded national cryptographic systems, the agency shall formulate an assessment plan, conduct the assessment, propose rectification opinions, and track the rectification progress in accordance with national specifications, thereby providing a basis for project acceptance. Through this assessment service, the agency will comprehensively understand the current status of cryptography application in the relevant information systems and evaluate the gap between the current status and the corresponding levels stipulated in the Information Security Technology—Basic Requirements for Cryptographic Application of Information Systems (GB/T 39786-2021). This aims to achieve the goals of promoting construction, rectification, and application through assessment. On-site assessments and technical verifications will be conducted covering physical and environmental security, network and communication security, equipment and computing security, application and data security, key management, and security management. The agency will identify weak links and potential risk hazards in cryptographic applications, propose targeted rectification recommendations, and ensure the compliance, correctness, and effectiveness of cryptographic applications. Furthermore, cryptographic security protection measures will be precisely implemented to guarantee the authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation of the information systems.

(III) Service Period

The service period for this project shall commence from the date of contract signing and continue until the project closing date (March 31, 2029). The specific service timeline will be implemented in phases based on the system launch schedule of the four informatization projects.

(IV) Deliverables

The deliverables required for this project are as follows:

No.

Report

Submission Date/Phase

1

Mobilization Report

Within 10 working days after contract signing and system launch (subject to the actual system launch date).

2

Information System Rectification List

Within 10 working days after the completion of the gap assessment.

3

Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Report

For Level 3 systems: Within 15 working days after the acceptance assessment is conducted upon the user's completion of rectification to meet the acceptance requirements. For the annual re-assessment report: The annual re-assessment must be initiated 3 months before the expiration of the previous year's assessment report, and the annual assessment report must be issued before the expiration of the previous year's report.
For Level 2 systems: Within 15 working days after the acceptance assessment is conducted upon the user's completion of rectification to meet the acceptance requirements.

4

Filing Materials and Filing Receipt

Issued within 10 working days after the assessment report is stamped by both parties and submitted online to the cyber police department.

5

Commercial Cryptography Application Rectification List

Within 10 working days after the completion of the gap assessment.

6

Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment Report

For Level 3 systems: Within 15 working days after the acceptance assessment is conducted upon the user's completion of rectification to meet the cryptographic assessment acceptance requirements. For the annual re-assessment report: The annual re-assessment must be initiated 3 months before the expiration of the previous year's assessment report, and the annual assessment report must be issued before the expiration of the previous year's report.
For Level 2 systems: Within 15 working days after the acceptance assessment is conducted upon the user's completion of rectification to meet the cryptographic assessment acceptance requirements.

7

Filing Materials and Filing Receipt

Issued within 10 working days after the assessment report is stamped by both parties and submitted to the Cryptography Administration.

Upon receiving the deliverable reports submitted by the assessment service agency, the Project Management Office (PMO) shall review them. TERM OF REFERENCE

To ensure the implementation of the World Bank China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project Information Technology Third-Party Service Package II (Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Service and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Evaluation Service) of the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulationand to guarantee the achievement of the project's objectives, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select a service agency through procurement to be responsible for the implementation of this project.

 

I. Background and Description

The World Bank Loan China Food Safety Demonstration Project officially entered into force on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period until March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance the modern governance capacity for food safety at both national and local levels. As a key implementer of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation plans to apply for a World Bank loan of 10 million US dollars and will precisely support the achievement of the project goals through the construction of six core sub-projects:

i. Develop a full-chain traceability platform for "coding, tracing, and recalling" food in key areas, enabling whole-process traceability and risk early warning with 15 functional modules and 359 functional points;

ii. Build the "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" system under the Guangdong Food Safety initiative, covering intelligent video supervision of scenarios such as elderly care and campus canteens;

iii. Upgrade and transform the emergency real-time dispatching and command system, and improve the accident emergency response mechanism;

iv. Carry out a capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of 75 course videos, and the organization of skill competitions;

v. Establish a high-quality food standard system and conduct promotion activities, developing no less than 30 standards and carrying out quality monitoring within two years;

vi. Provide professional consulting services throughout the entire project implementation process.

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the above-mentioned construction content, we plan to refer to advanced practices from other World Bank projects to further optimize procurement management and improve service coordination efficiency; in the next phase of actual procurement operations, while keeping the total project budget unchanged, we intend to integrate the network security level protection assessment services and commercial cryptography application security assessment services for these 4 projects—the "Coding, Tracing, and Recalling" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Areas (or Key Varieties), the Guangdong Food Safety "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" System Construction Project, the Emergency Real-Time Dispatching and Command System Upgrade, Transformation, and Operation Project, and the Capacity Improvement Project for Food-Related Personnel in the Market Supervision Field—into a single package for unified procurement and management, so as to ensure the smooth achievement of the project's construction goals.

 

II. Objectives

The core objective of this project is to comprehensively enhance the modern governance capacity for food safety. Through the in-depth integration and linkage of the "Code Tracing" full-chain traceability platform, the "Internet + Smart Kitchen & Bright Stove" intelligent supervision system, and the emergency real-time dispatch and command system, a full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early warning response, and closed-loop disposal will be established, providing a data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating result indicators such as the "proportion of early warnings for which mitigation measures have been initiated." Additionally, the food-related personnel capacity improvement learning and assessment system will enable systematic training for regulatory personnel and quantify the participation proportion of female regulatory personnel.

The core purpose is to conduct a comprehensive and objective security assessment of the above-mentioned information systems in accordance with relevant national standards and norms, accurately identify and locate risks and weaknesses in the systems' network security and cryptographic applications, and propose targeted rectification suggestions accordingly. Through the approach of "promoting construction through assessment, promoting reform through assessment, and promoting application through assessment," it will ultimately ensure that all information systems meet the requirements of compliance, correctness, and effectiveness in terms of network security protection and cryptographic applications. This will provide a solid guarantee for the smooth acceptance and safe operation of the project, ensure that the collection, accounting, and reporting of all indicator data comply with World Bank norms, and help promote the efficient implementation of the World Bank project.

 

III. Service Overview

The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 0.56 million.

(I) Scope of Services

The service scope of this project covers the Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment services required for four informatization projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Content

a. Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Services
Based on the assessment results of security technology and security management controls, as well as the overall system assessment, the service agency shall conduct a comprehensive assessment of the information system in accordance with the corresponding level standards and provide relevant security review opinions. This specifically includes two aspects: First, security control assessment, which primarily evaluates the implementation and configuration of basic security controls required by the cybersecurity level protection standards within the information system. Second, overall system assessment, which primarily analyzes the overall security of the information system. The security control assessment serves as the foundation for the overall security assessment of the information system.

 

b. Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment Services

The service agency shall provide security assessment services for systems upgraded with domestic cryptography. For the upgraded national cryptographic systems, the agency shall formulate an assessment plan, conduct the assessment, propose rectification opinions, and track the rectification progress in accordance with national specifications, thereby providing a basis for project acceptance. Through this assessment service, the agency will comprehensively understand the current status of cryptography application in the relevant information systems and evaluate the gap between the current status and the corresponding levels stipulated in the Information Security Technology—Basic Requirements for Cryptographic Application of Information Systems (GB/T 39786-2021). This aims to achieve the goals of promoting construction, rectification, and application through assessment. On-site assessments and technical verifications will be conducted covering physical and environmental security, network and communication security, equipment and computing security, application and data security, key management, and security management. The agency will identify weak links and potential risk hazards in cryptographic applications, propose targeted rectification recommendations, and ensure the compliance, correctness, and effectiveness of cryptographic applications. Furthermore, cryptographic security protection measures will be precisely implemented to guarantee the authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation of the information systems.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

In order to ensure the effective implementation of PackageThird-Party Informatization Services (‌Special Security Evaluation and Acceptance Evaluation Services) under the above-mentioned project, and to achieve the targeted objectives of project information technology development, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select and engage qualified service institutions through public procurement to carry out the implementation of this project.

1. Project Background and Overview

The World Bank-financed China Food Safety Improvement Project took effect on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period ending on March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance national and local modern food safety governance capacity. As a key implementing entity of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to apply for a World Bank loan of USD10,000,000. It will provide targeted support for the achievement of project objectives through the implementation of six core sub-projects, as detailed below:

First, develop a full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su" for food in key sectors, which consists of 15 functional modules and 359 functional points to realize whole-process traceability and risk early warning.

Second, build the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen" of Guangdong Food Safety to realize intelligent video supervision covering canteens of elderly care institutions, campuses and other scenarios.

Third, upgrade and renovate the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and improve the emergency response mechanism for food safety incidents.

Fourth, launch a capacity improvement program for food-related personnel in the market supervision field, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of 75 course videos, and the organization of professional skills competitions.

Fifth, establish and promote a high-quality food standard system, develop no fewer than 30 standards within two years, and carry out corresponding quality monitoring work.

Sixth, provide full-process professional consulting services for project implementation.

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the above contents, relevant practices of other World Bank projects will be referenced to optimize procurement management and enhance the overall efficiency of service coordination. In the subsequent actual procurement process and without changing the total project budget, the special security evaluation and acceptance evaluation services of four sub-projects - namely, the full-chain food traceability platform project with“ShangMa Su”for key food sectors (categories), the Guangdong Food Safety “Internet-based Visualization Kitchen” system construction project, the upgrading, renovation and operation project of the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and the capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field - will be integrated into one single packaged project, so as to guarantee the smooth achievement of project objectives.

2.Project Objectives

Centered on the core objective of comprehensively improving the modern governance capacity of food safety, this project integrates the full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su", the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen", the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and capacity improvement for food-related personnel in the market supervision field. It aims to establish a closed-loop full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early-warning response and disposal, so as to provide data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating outcome indicators such as“proportion of early-warnings for which mitigation measures have been activated". Meanwhile, the learning and assessment system for capacity improvement program for food-related personnel enables systematic training for supervisors and quantifies the participation rate of female supervisor.

The core objectives are to carry out the non-destructive security evaluation by adopting methods such as simulated hacker attacks before system launch to comprehensively assess the protection capabilities of network, host, application and other layers, so as to ensure compliance with industrial safety management and control requirements and protect the security of sensitive information and public privacy; conduct multi-dimensional evaluation and compliance inspection covering functionality, performance, information security and compatibility before final project acceptance to strictly control project quality, so as to ensure that all indicators fully comply with the contract, requirement specification and construction specifications. This provides a solid guarantee for the smooth acceptance and safe operation of the project, ensures the collection, accounting and reporting of all indicator data conform to World Bank standards, and facilitates the efficient implementation of the World Bank project.

The Electricité du Cambodge (EDC) has obtained a grant from the World Bank’s Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) under the Cambodia Sustainable Energy Transition Project (CSET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

  • The Project is designed to support the government’s priorities of strengthening the power grid and energy efficiency, while promoting cost-effective demand-side energy management to ensure energy stability, system resilience, and affordability.

 

  • To achieve these outcomes, the proposed Project aims to significantly: (i) strengthen power transmission and distribution infrastructure to increase capacity, enhance reliability; (ii) expand access to modern electricity services in remaining unelectrified rural areas; and (iii) implement energy efficiency and demand-side management measures across industrial and residential sectors. By strengthening power infrastructure for VRE integration while improving energy productivity, the proposed Project will reduce system costs, increase new or improved access to energy, and strengthen industrial competitiveness.   • The selected Consultant will support Project Preparation Unit of EDC to roll out preparation activities needed for EDC towards project approval by Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC). description:
Background:  In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through its Ministry of Finance (MoF) launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) project. The project development objective is to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance. 

The SPRING project is organized around four components (three mutually-reinforcing and one supporting): (i) Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs; and (iv) Component 4: Project Management. A wide range of activities will be implemented as part of this project to reach its development objective, such as improvements to regulatory/institutional frameworks, the rollout of the digital ID system, financial sector reforms, the creation of a risk-sharing mechanism, and the provision of business development services for micro, small and medium enterprises in select economic sectors, among others.  MoF received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi-Partner Fund to implement the SPRING project. As part of this initiative, under Component 1, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoCI) is strengthening its role in Advancing regional trade integration through Somalia’s accession to the East African Community (EAC) and the World Trade Organization (WTO).

 MoF intends to apply for part of the proceeds from the World Bank to finance the position of Industrial Development Advisor for the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The Industrial Development Advisor will support MoCI in implementing industrial policies, formalizing businesses, improving export readiness, developing Special Economic Zones, strengthening intellectual property administration, coordinating stakeholders, drafting regulatory instruments, delivering staff training, facilitating public–private dialogue, and preparing implementation plans and progress reports.

 

 

 

Responsibilities: an The Industrial Development Advisor will support the implementation of Somalia’s industrial policies by developing work plans, regulatory instruments, standards, incentive frameworks, and procedures. The Advisor will promote business formalization, export readiness, and access to EAC, AfCFTA, and WTO markets. The Advisor will provide technical support for Special Economic Zones, intellectual property administration, investment facilitation, value-chain development, and environmental compliance. The role will also strengthen coordination between MoCI, government institutions, and the private sector, with attention to micro, small, and women-owned industries. The Advisor will train MoCI and SEZ staff and support public–private consultations on industrial and trade barriers. The Advisor will also prepare regulatory frameworks, implementation plans, training materials, progress reports, and strategic advisory documents.

All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link: https://moci.gov.so/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ToR-Industrial-Development-Advisor-2.pdf 

2.   Skills and qualifications

Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

•   Master’s degree in industrial economics, Development Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.

•    Minimum of 8 years of demonstrated experience in industrial development, investment facilitation, value chain development, or related regulatory reform work within government or international development contexts and supportive of business formalization and external trade.

•    Demonstrated knowledge of industrial policy design, business formalization and licensing systems, special economic zone governance, or productive sector development in sub-Saharan Africa or comparable fragile and conflict-affected settings.

•    Experience with intellectual property administration or quality and standards systems is an advantage.

•    Demonstrated ability to manage inter-ministerial coordination and facilitate multi-stakeholder consultation processes.

•    Experience with World Bank or international development projects is highly preferred.

•    Proficiency in English and excellent written and verbal communication skills are required. Fluency in Somali is an advantage.

3.   Duration: The proposed duration for the assignment is one year (12) calendar months from starts date.

4.   The Ministry of Ministry of Finance now invites eligible consulting (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services and furnish the Curriculum Vitae (CV).

5.   Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14, 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services dated in September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.   A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

7.   Interested Consultant may obtain further information (in person or by e-mail) at the address below during office hours from 8.00 a.m. – 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday except on public holidays.

8.   Deadline for submission: Expressions of interest should be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 30th September 2026 4:00PM. Local Time.

The Government of the Republic of Zambia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing technical advisory support and developing the Terms of Reference (ToRs) for both the design consultant and a Technical Advisor firm for the SMART Corridor project. The SMART Corridor aims to enhance transport efficiency, road safety, and trade facilitation along key regional corridors, particularly the Lusaka–Nakonde section of the Dar es Salaam corridor. This consultancy is expected to be undertaken within a period of 4 weeks.
The individual consultant will work closely with the Road Transport and Safety Agency (RTSA) and other key stakeholders to ensure that the ToRs align with project objectives. The scope of work includes reviewing relevant project documentation, engaging with stakeholders, drafting the ToRs for the design consultant and the Technical Advisor, incorporating feedback, and finalizing the ToRs for use in procurement. The consultancy will also include providing technical advisory support to RTSA during the ToR preparation process.
The Road Transport and Safety Agency (RTSA) now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

1.    Educational Background:
•    Advanced degree in Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Transport Planning, Project Management, Digital Planning, or a related field.
2.    Relevant Experience:
•    At least 10 years of experience in developing and managing transport infrastructure projects.
•    Demonstrated experience working on projects related to Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS), traffic management, road safety, tolling systems, and/or trade facilitation.
•    Experience working with multilateral development banks (e.g., World Bank) and familiarity with their procurement guidelines is an added advantage.
•    Experience working with government agencies and coordinating with multiple stakeholders on infrastructure projects.
3.    Technical Skills:
•    Strong understanding of transport infrastructure design and project implementation, particularly digitization of transport systems.
•    Expertise in drafting comprehensive Terms of Reference, technical documents, and consultancy reports.
•    Proven ability to facilitate stakeholder consultations and incorporate diverse perspectives into technical documents.
4.    Communication and Coordination Skills:
•    Excellent communication and presentation skills.
•    Ability to coordinate effectively with multiple stakeholders, including government agencies and international organizations.
•    Proven ability to deliver high-quality work within tight deadlines.
5.    Language Requirements:
•    Proficiency in both written and spoken English.

REPUBLIC OF MOLDOVA

The Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Competitiveness Project (MSME) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
