The Government of Indonesia had received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Global Environmental Facility Indonesia Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: (a) Knowledge Product Development, and (b) Concept Development of the National Urban Summit Series of Activities. The Services are expected to start in November 2026 and be performed during a period of 7 months. The total estimated level of effort is approximately at 46 technical/professional staff months. Further detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found in the following website: https://bit.ly/4Ab90rz

 

The Directorate of Spatial Planning, Urban Affairs, Land Affairs and Disaster Management at the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency (BAPPENAS) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide comprehensive information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Interested Consultants must provide sufficient description of similar assignments (including location/ country, name of the Employer/ Client, type of services provided, period of contract, contract amount, starting and completion dates), and availability of appropriate skills among permanent staff, and so forth. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • At least 1 (one) project within the last 5 (five) years of experience in providing consulting services related to capacity building/knowledge product development related to urban planning/ urban development at the national or subnational level.
  • At least 1 (one) project within the last 5 (five) years of experience in providing consulting services related to sustainable urban development at the national or subnational level.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms as a joint venture or a sub-consultant to enhance their qualifications. In the case of an association, the EOI must explicitly specify whether it is a Joint Venture (all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment) or Sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, the member firm appointed to represent it must be clearly identified. All the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Only the qualifications and experience of members of the joint venture, but not of sub-consultants, shall be considered in the EOI evaluation process.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09.00 AM to 03.00 P.M. Jakarta time (GMT+7) email: ulp@bappenas.go.id.

 

Expressions of interest must be submitted electronically through the SPSE ICB system at https://spseicb.lkpp.go.id/  by September 30th, 2026, 10.00 A.M Jakarta time (GMT+7).

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de 225 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) au profit du Projet de Développement Urbain Integré et Résilient pour l’Emploi (PRODUIRE) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer le contrat de services d’un Responsable des infrastructures de l’Unité de Gestion de Projet à Antananarivo.

  L’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) est de renforcer la résilience climatique des communautés urbaines, d'améliorer l'administration foncière et de soutenir l'emploi dans certaines villes.

2. Les services du consultant (« les services ») consistent à fournir une expertise au projet sur la mise en oeuvre des infrastructures de drainage urbain et de protection contre les inondations ainsi que la mise en place des infrastructures urbaines dans les quartiers d’intervention dans le Grand Antananarivo .

3. Le mandat fera l’objet d’un contrat de 60 mois assorti d’une tranche ferme de douze mois et de 04 tranches conditionnelles de 12 mois dont la condition d’affermissement sera l’évaluation positive de la perfomance du consultant. Un période d’essai de 6 mois est prévue dans la tranche ferme. Le lieu de travail est au siège du projet à Antananarivo.

4. Le Responsable des infrastructures doit répondre au profil suivant :

- Titulaire d’un diplôme Bacc+5 ou d’ingénieur en BTP ou en Génie Civil ou en hydraulique ;

- Au moins dix (10) ans d’expériences générales dans l’ingénierie de construction dont cinq ans en bureau d’études techniques ou projet de développement construisant des infrastructures,

- Au moins cinq (5) années d’expériences professionnelles dans la conduite, le suivi et l’exécution des travaux d’infrastructures urbaines financés par les Bailleurs de fonds internationaux,

- Au moins cinq (5) années d'expérience dans la conception, le suivi ou la supervision d'ouvrages hydrauliques urbains, de drainage ou de protection contre les inondations,

- Connaissance opérationnelle d'au moins un logiciel de modélisation hydraulique et hydrologique (HEC-RAS, MIKE FLOOD, SWMM ou équivalent) permettant la lecture critique et la validation des études hydrauliques produites par les bureaux d'études ;

- Connaissance des normes techniques dans le domaine des infrastructures urbaines,

- Bonne connaissance du Cadre Environnemental et Social (ESF) de la Banque mondiale et expérience dans la supervision d’infrastructures intégrant les exigences environnementales, sociales, de santé-sécurité et de résilience climatique,

- Aptitude à effectuer des fréquents déplacements sur terrain ;

- Aptitude à travailler en équipe et ayant une bonne capacité de synthèse et d’analyse ;

- Aptitude à identifier les problèmes et à les résoudre rapidement et de façon pragmatique et technique ;

- Aptitude à communiquer de façon claire et concise tant oralement que par écrit, en malgache et en français, et une bonne compréhension de l’Anglais serait un atout ;

- Maîtrise des logiciels de dessin assisté par ordinateur (AutoCAD ou équivalent) et bonne connaissance des logiciels de calcul de structures (GRAITEC Advance Design, Robot Structural Analysis ou équivalent). La connaissance de logiciels de modélisation hydraulique constitue un atout.

- Maîtrise des outils informatiques de base.

AVIS DE SOLLICITATIONS DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN SPECIALISTE EN SAUVEGARDES ENVIRONNEMENTALES

 

 

  1. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATIONS 

 

Le Gouvernement du Niger a sollicité l’appui de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) en vue de la mise en œuvre du Projet d'Harmonisation et d'Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l'Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) Niger (HISWACA SOP 1).

Le projet est un projet régional qui vise à soutenir les pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest et du Centre conjointement pour améliorer les performances statistiques des systèmes statistiques nationaux et régionaux, en particulier les sources de données et l'infrastructure de données, tout en veillant à ce que les statistiques produites soient harmonisées et rendues plus comparables. La phase 1 du projet régional se concentrera sur le soutien aux pays ouest-africains suivants : Bénin, Guinée, Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Mauritanie, Niger, Sénégal et Gambie.

Le SOP 1 de HISWACA soutiendra également le département statistique de la Communauté Economique des États d'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO), l'Institut de Statistique de l'UA (STATAFRIC) et la Commission de l'Union Economique et Monétaire Ouest-Africaine (UEMOA) dans leur rôle de coordination et de plaidoyer pour améliorer la comparabilité et l'harmonisation des statistiques.

L’objectif de ce projet est d'améliorer la performance statistique, l'harmonisation régionale, l’accès aux données et leur utilisation et de renforcer la modernisation de leurs systèmes statistiques.

 

 

  1. Objectif de la mission

L’objectif général de cette consultation est de renforcer le projet PHASAOC par le recrutement, d’un Spécialiste en Sauvegardes Environnementales qui accompagnera le projet tout au long de la mise en œuvre.

  1. MANDAT ET TACHES DU SPECIALISTE EN SAUVEGARDES ENVIRONNEMENTALES

Sous la supervision du Coordonnateur et en étroite collaboration avec le consultant en charge des sauvegardes sociales, le/la Consultant(e) a pour missions de conduire et coordonner l’ensemble des activités et mesures de sauvegardes environnementales du projet en relation avec les autres spécialistes de l’UGP et les Structures Focales Nationales. Il/Elle contribuera à l’amélioration des missions d’intérêt général en matière de connaissance et de gestion de l’environnement y compris des bonnes pratiques internationales, notamment l’identification des impacts environnementaux potentiels pouvant découler des activités du projet et la mise en œuvre des mesures d’atténuation pertinentes proposées. Il/Elle veillera à l’application des mesures environnementales et le suivi des mesures d’atténuation proposées.

Plus spécifiquement, le (la) Spécialiste en Sauvegardes Environnementales et Sociales est chargé(e) de :

(a) En matière de planification et de gestion des aspects environnementaux

  • Participer à l’élaboration des Plans de Travail et Budget annuels (PTBA) en veillant à y intégrer tous les aspects concernant  les sauvegardes environnementales et identifiant les cohérences en termes de besoins en études, formations et tout autre activité en matière de sauvegardes environnementales, conformément aux objectifs des Normes Environnementales et Sociales (NES) de la Banque mondiale, en général, et des mesures et actions prévues dans le Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social (PEES), en particulier ;
  • Veiller au respect du cadre législatif et règlementaire national relatif aux questions environnementales applicables au projet ;
  • Définir la démarche, au plan environnemental, qui répondra aux normes et pratiques de sauvegarde de la Banque mondiale en matière d’évaluation d’impact ;
  • Veiller dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités, à la conformité par rapport aux dispositions des lois et règlementations nationales en vigueur au Niger et aux normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale pertinentes dans le cas du projet ;
  • Réaliser le screening environnemental des activités inscrites dans le plan de travail annuel, en collaboration avec le Ministère en charge de l’Environnement à travers le Bureau National des Evaluations Environnementales (BNEE), avant leur démarrage, les catégoriser et assumer les mesures de conformité environnementale y relatives ;
  • Assurer la revue, la mise à jour et la diffusion du Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social (PEES) et du Plan de Mobilisation des Parties Prenantes du projet en conformité avec les exigences du Cadre Environnemental et Social (CES) de la Banque mondiale et des politiques de gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux et sociaux du Niger ;
  • Superviser la préparation, la mise en œuvre et l’évaluation du Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social ;
  • Participer à la conception et à la programmation physique et financière des activités à mettre en œuvre en matière de sauvegarde environnementale et à la préparation des Plans de Travail et Budget Annuels (PTBA) dans le cadre du Projet pour s’assurer de la prise en compte des aspects de sauvegarde environnementale pendant la planification ;
  • Participer à la planification opérationnelle et la mise en œuvre des activités du projet afin de s’assurer de, l’insertion des Clauses Environnementales et Sociales dans les Dossiers d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) et des devis quantitatifs estimatifs et leur prise en compte dans les contrats des entreprises chargées des travaux et dans les Dossiers d’Exécution et de leur conformité pendant la mise en œuvre des activités inhérentes au projet ;
  • Assurer l’intégration des clauses environnementales dans les DAO, en veillant à leur prise en compte dans les tableaux de devis quantitatif (DQE) ;
  • Analyser les dossiers techniques (termes de référence, rapports d’études, dossiers d’appels d’offres) en vue de la prise en compte des aspects environnementaux ;

(b) En matière de communication, sensibilisation, renforcement des capacités et échanges

  • Participer à la diffusion auprès de toutes les parties prenantes des instruments de sauvegarde environnementale du Projet et la communication / sensibilisation au sujet des différentes procédures (au démarrage du projet et pendant toute sa durée) ;
  • Participer à la coordination et la supervision de toutes les initiatives de sensibilisation des parties prenantes au sujet des défis et de enjeux environnementaux du Projet ;
  • Participer à la formation des acteurs par rapport aux objectifs et aux procédures des normes environnementale et sociales (NES) de la Banque mondiale (y compris par rapport à la préparation du matériel pédagogique) et ce, tout au long du cycle des activités ;
  • Contribuer à développer un système de coordination et d'échanges d’expériences avec les spécialistes en sauvegarde environnementale d'autres projets (appuyées par la Banque mondiale et d'autres partenaires techniques et financiers) intervenant dans la même zone géographique et/ou dans des domaines similaires
  • Veiller à l'appropriation des documents de sauvegardes environnementales par l’équipe du projet PHASAOC, les parties prenantes au projet et les bénéficiaires des activités du projet au Niger.

(c) En matière d’études, de suivi, de surveillance et de rapportage

  • Participer au processus de sélection et au recrutement de consultants individuels ou bureaux d’études impliqués dans toute étude, audit ou évaluation des aspects relatifs aux sauvegardes environnementales (y compris la préparation des TdRs, le recrutement, le suivi, la revue et la validation, le suivi et la diffusion des documents produits) ;
  • Contribuer à l’identification et la mise en œuvre des mesures clés sélectionnées dans le cadre de l’Evaluation Environnementale Stratégique du Secteur des bâtiments ;
  • Veiller à la mise en œuvre des mesures de sauvegardes environnementales du projet, à travers la surveillance, le suivi et l’évaluation et prendre toutes les dispositions pour alerter par anticipation, de tout problème de non-conformité et proposer des mesures correctives immédiates sur les non-conformités ;
  • Participer à l’élaboration et à la mise en œuvre du Mécanisme de Gestion des Plaintes (MGP), en particulier par rapport aux aspects environnementaux ;
  • Assurer le suivi des mesures d’atténuation des impacts du Projet sur le milieu biophysique et le milieu humain par rapport à tous les aspects de sauvegarde environnementale, en conformité avec les prescriptions des outils de sauvegardes (EIES, PAR, PGES, CGES), la législation nationale dans les domaines de l’environnement et du social ainsi et le Cadre Environnemental et Social de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Elaborer et définir les indicateurs d’impacts environnementaux prenant en compte les coûts associés et s’assurer de leur renseignement par le Spécialiste du Suivi & Evaluation ;
  • Effectuer des missions de terrain et de suivi dans les zones d’intervention du projet pour s’assurer de la bonne exécution des activités de sauvegarde environnementale ;
  • Accompagner l’élaboration de directives (ou de guides) environnementales et sociales pertinentes, y compris les procédures de gestion du travail ;
  • Préparer et mettre en place des sessions de sensibilisation sur la santé, la sécurité et l'environnement (HSE) ;
  • Participer à la réception provisoire et définitive des travaux pour s’assurer de la conformité des mesures environnementales et sociales ;
  • Superviser et assurer le contrôle qualité de l’Evaluation Environnementale et Sociale Stratégique, des Etudes d’Impacts Environnementaux et Sociaux (EIES), des Plans de Gestion Environnementale, Notices d’Impacts Environnementaux et Sociaux (NIES), des Audits Environnementaux et Sociaux et tous autres instruments de gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux et sociaux ;
  • Produire régulièrement des rapports sur l’état de la mise en œuvre des mesures de sauvegardes environnementales et sociales en collaboration avec les parties prenantes (trimestriels et annuels) ;
  • Élaborer les outils de collecte des données pour la réalisation des rapports périodiques de suivi des mesures de gestion de risques et impacts environnementaux et sociaux et assurer la documentation et l'archivage de l'ensemble des activités liées à ces mesures, ainsi que le reporting pour l'UGP et pour la Banque mondiale ;
  • S’assurer de la conduite du suivi externe de conformité par le Bureau National des Evaluations Environnementales (BNEE) et autres entités impliquées dans le suivi externe ;
  • Exécuter toutes tâches à lui/elle confiées par le Coordonnateur du projet et qui sont en relation avec les tâches définies dans les présents TdRs.
  1. PROFIL DU SPECIALISTE EN SAUVEGARDES ENVIRONNEMENTALES :

  Le (la) spécialiste en sauvegardes environnementales doit avoir le profil suivant :

  • Être titulaire d'un diplôme de Spécialiste en Sciences de l’Environnement et/ou Spécialiste dans le domaine du développement durable (au moins BAC+5) ou équivalent ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience d’au moins cinq (5) années dans le domaine de la protection de l’environnement de l’évaluation et du suivi environnemental, dont au moins trois (3) années dans la mise en œuvre ou le suivi des mesures d’atténuation des impacts environnementaux dans le domaine des infrastructures ;
  • Maitriser la législation nigérienne et les conventions internationales relatives à la protection de l’environnement ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance des politiques et normes de sauvegardes environnementales et du nouveau cadre environnemental et social de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Disposer d’une bonne capacité d’analyse de documents techniques ;
  • Être capable d’identifier les besoins en renforcement de capacités en évaluation environnementale d’autres experts nationaux et animer des sessions de formation ;
  • Avoir une maîtrise orale et écrite du français, une connaissance professionnelle de l’anglais et une bonne connaissance des langues locales seraient un atout ;
  • Avoir une bonne capacité de synthèse et de rédaction de rapports ;
  • Avoir des aptitudes à travailler en équipe ;
  • Avoir une connaissance informatique des logiciels courants (Word, Excel, Power Point, Email et autres outils de communication).
  1. Procédures de sélection :

Le (la) candidat(e) retenu(e) aura un statut de consultant.

Le Candidat sera sélectionné en accord avec les procédures définies dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) » Révision de Septembre 2023 puis en février 2025.

Il reste entendu que le recrutement d’un candidat fonctionnaire doit satisfaire aux dispositions de la clause 3.23 d) du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) » Révision de Septembre 2023, puis en février 2025.

Seul(e)s les candidat(e)s présélectionné(e)s seront contacté(e)s pour la suite du processus.

  1. LIEU D’AFFECTATION ET DUREE DU CONTRAT :

Le (la) candidat(e) retenu(e) sera invité(e) à signer un contrat de prestation de services d’un (01) an, renouvelable après évaluation satisfaisante de ses performances. Il/Elle travaillera à temps plein, conformément à la réglementation en vigueur. La première année est assortie d’une période d’essai de trois (3) mois.

Le lieu d’affectation est Niamey, au siège de l’UGP/PHASAOC, à la Direction Générale de l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS).

  1. Budget

Le Financement sera assuré par le projet PHASAOC/BM.

  1.  Méthode de sélection et dépôt des plis :

 

Le dossier devra être composé des pièces suivantes :

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêts ;
  • Un curriculum vitae à jour en adéquation avec la mission ;
  • Les copies légalisées des contrats similaires ou certificats et attestations de travail attestant l'expérience professionnelle du candidat ;
  • Les copies légalisées des diplômes et attestations de formation ;

 

Les dossiers de candidature doivent être déposés au plus tard le 06 octobre 2026 à 16 H00, heure locale de Niamey (TU+1) :

  • Soit sous plis fermés à l’INSTITUT NATIONAL DE LA STATISTIQUE (INS) Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) BP : 13 416 Niamey – Niger Téléphone : (227) 20 72 35 60, 2 -ème étage porte 212 ;
  • Soit envoyés par email (format PDF) à l’adresse suivante : Email : aribrahim@ins.ne ; avec copie à : kiamoulasani@gmail.com; ari2006_toubo@yahoo.fr;

Dans le cas où les candidatures sont communiquées sous plis fermés, les dossiers doivent être envoyés dans une enveloppe format A4 portant l’intitulé du poste.

Le Candidat sera sélectionné en accord avec les procédures définies dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) » Révision de Septembre 2023 puis en février 2025.

To: The World Bank (WB) Task Team,

The ODA Project Management Unit (PMU) - The University of Da Nang respectfully presents this report and requests the World Bank’s review and comments on its proposal regarding the processing plan for Package DN-CS--03: Supervision of packages for Supply and installation of specialized equipment and furniture. This package is selected using the Consultants’ Qualifications Selection (CQS) method in accordance with the Project’s Procurement Plan.

The Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI) for Package DN-CS--03 was published on the National Procurement Network System on August 25, 2026, under REOI No. IB2600484579, with the initial submission deadline set for 2:00 PM on September 11, 2026. At the closing time, only one (01) consultant submitted an Expression of Interest (EOI). To provide further opportunities for other firms to participate, thereby enhancing competition, fairness, transparency, and economic efficiency in the procurement process, the ODA PMU issued Document No. 276/QLDAODA-T dated September 11, 2026, extending the submission deadline to 2:00 PM on September 21, 2026 (a 10-day extension). This extension has been updated on the National Procurement Network System.

Package DN-CS--03 is a supervisory consulting service with a broad scope of work that spans multiple specialized fields simultaneously. Consequently, the qualification requirements are comprehensive and specialized, covering various sectors. As a result, the number of interested consultants with relevant experience matching the package's required scope may be limited. This is an objective characteristic of the consulting market for multi-disciplinary supervision assignments.

The selection of the supervisory consultant for Packages DN-GO--01, DN-GO--02 and DN-GO--03 is crucial to meeting the schedule for equipment supply, installation, acceptance, disbursement, and the overall progress of the Project. Therefore, we respectfully request the World Bank to review and provide its no-objection to the following proposal: In the event that only one (01) consultant has submitted an EOI by 2:00 PM on September 21, 2026, the ODA Project Management Unit will close the receipt of EOIs, prepare the closing minutes, and proceed to open the submitted EOI at 2:30 PM on the same day.

We look forward to receiving the World Bank’s comments to serve as a basis for implementing the next steps, ensuring the progress of the consulting selection and the overall timeline of the Project.

We highly appreciate the World Bank’s continued cooperation and support.

Sincerely,

 

Nguyen Duc Phong
        Director of ODA PMU

description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - CONSULTANT’S QUALIFICATIONS BASED SELECTION (CQS)

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153)

Loan No/Credit No/Grant Number

GFPP Grant No. TF0D0728

Assignment Title

Consultancy Services for Replacement of Ageing Assets (Generation and Power Network)

Procurement Plan Ref Number

FJ-EFL-567212-CS-CQS

Reference No.

EOI-03/2026

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

Selection Method

Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS)

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), intends to engage a qualified consulting firm to support the preparation and implementation of an Aged Asset Replacement Program covering selected hydropower generation and power network assets.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise the development of an Aged Asset Replacement Policy and Plan, identification and prioritisation of replacement projects, environmental and social screening and assessment, preparation of an implementation and procurement framework, and development of procurement documentation for the first batch of priority investments.

The Services will cover:

•    Review of EFL’s existing aged asset replacement policies and procedures, including risk evaluation and recommended improvements.

•    Stakeholder consultations and preparation of a stakeholder engagement plan aligned with applicable environmental and social requirements.

•    Development of a new Aged Asset Replacement Policy consistent with Good International Industry Practice and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework.

•    Assessment of the Wainiqeu and Nagado hydropower stations and the identified network substations, switchboards, transformers and related assets.

•    Project identification, prioritisation, cost estimates, economic analysis, environmental and social screening, risk classification and preparation of proportionate management instruments.

•    Development of a procurement strategy, technical specifications, bills of quantity and draft bidding documents, including relevant environmental and social provisions.

•    Knowledge transfer and training for relevant EFL personnel, together with a final implementation roadmap and recommendations.

Consultancy Services for Replacement of Ageing Assets

 

  1. Background and Context

Fiji's energy sector plays a central role in the economic development, investment in climate resilience renewable energy projects, and ensure long-term sustainability of the Fijian Economy. The country's electricity supply is dominated by Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), a majority owned government utility responsible for the generation, transmission, distribution, and retail of electricity. EFL currently produces approximately 93 percent of electricity, with Independent Power Producers (IPPs) contributing the remaining balance.

EFL is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, responsible for the generation, transmission, and retail of electricity across the four (4) main islands of Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Ovalau and Taveuni. Formerly known as the Fiji Electricity Authority (FEA) which was established under the Electricity Act in 1966, it was corporatized in 2018 to operate as a public company limited by shares.

 

Some of EFL’s major power generation assets (Renewable/thermal) have gone past their useful or replacement life due to their old age. The age of these generation assets is over 20 years or more. Some generators have long been out of production with spare parts no longer available or have become obsolete.

EFL has over the years worked on a number of projects to replace its ageing assets in both the Generation and Network Areas. Some were funded through debt funding and the remaining through EFL’s internal cashflow with progress subject to availability of funds.

The Government of Fiji (GoF), supported by the World Bank under the proposed Fiji Energy Transformation Project, is committed to assisting Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) in the implementation of EFL’s Aged Asset Replacement program, and the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) is used to support this ageing assets screening and preparation.

 

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The primary objectives of this consultancy are to:

  1. Develop an Aged Asset Replacement policy for EFL, aligned with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards (ESS);
  2. Establish an Aged Asset Replacement Plan; and
  3. Develop a framework for the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement Plan in an efficient, cost-effective and transparent manner, aligned with the World Bank’s ESS.

The Aged Asset Replacement Policy should address the following:

  1. Facilitate broad interest in the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement plan;
  2. Establish clear, transparent, and competitive procurement processes for the implementation of the Aged Asset Replacement Plan;
  3. Promote energy security and affordability for all Fijian consumers.
  4. Promote Good International Industry Practices (GIIP) in terms of environmental sustainability and social safeguards.

Specifically, the Consultancy should address the following:

  1. Identify ageing assets to be replaced or rehabilitated. A list is provided, with detailed information below.
  2. Promote energy-efficient replacement technologies
  3. Conduct a comprehensive E & S risk screening and assessment, including the corresponding mitigation measures / management plans, for all identified generation and substation upgrade, covering hazardous material handling, recovery (likelihood ACM in the switchboards, PCB and SF6 in the transformers etc.), waste disposal, emissions, and community impacts.
  4. Investment needs, and cost benefits analysis
  5. Facilitate broad interest in the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement plan;
  6. Proposed implementation plan, including procurement packaging
  7. Draft bidding documents, BoQ and Technical Specifications, or other procurement documents.
  8. Promote energy security and affordability for all Fijian consumers including community safety awareness, emergency preparedness, and communication strategies to inform residents of planned outages or risks.

Annex. E&S Screening, Risk Classification, and E&S Assessment and Management

 

E&S Screening and Risk Classification

As part of the project identification and prioritization process, the Consultant shall conduct an Environmental and Social (E&S) screening of all assets and sub-projects identified for potential inclusion under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. The purpose of this screening is to identify, at an early stage, the nature and significance of potential environmental and social risks and impacts associated with each sub-project, and to classify them accordingly to inform prioritization and downstream assessment requirements under Task 5.

The E&S screening shall be carried out in accordance with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and shall include the following activities:

(a) Screening Checklist Development. The Consultant shall develop a standardized E&S screening checklist, to be reviewed and approved by EFL and the World Bank, covering the following parameters for each sub-project or asset replacement activity:

  • Nature, scale, and location of the proposed asset replacement works (e.g., generation assets, transmission and distribution infrastructure, substations, switchboards, transformers, and hydropower plant components);
  • Proximity to environmentally sensitive areas, including watercourses, riparian zones, protected areas, forests, and ecologically significant habitats;
  • Proximity to communities, settlements, sacred sites, and areas of cultural heritage significance;
  • Land access requirements, including temporary or permanent land acquisition, easements, or restrictions on land use;
  • Potential for generation of hazardous waste, including oils, asbestos-containing materials (ACM), SF6 gas, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), and other legacy contaminants associated with aging electrical infrastructure;
  • Potential for impacts on labor and working conditions, occupational health and safety, and community health and safety during works; and
  • Potential for disproportionate impacts on vulnerable or marginalized groups, including women, youth, and indigenous communities.

(b) Application of the Screening Checklist. The Consultant shall apply the approved screening checklist to each sub-project or asset cluster identified in Task 4, drawing on available data, site reconnaissance findings, and stakeholder inputs gathered under Task 2. For hydropower-related asset replacements, the screening shall additionally assess:

  • The potential for works to alter water release regimes, turbine operations, or intake structures in ways that may affect downstream river flows, including environmental flows (eflows);
  • Potential impacts on aquatic ecosystems, freshwater biodiversity, and ecosystem services dependent on river flows; and
  • Any associated civil works within or adjacent to river corridors, including intake structures, penstocks, tailraces, and powerhouses.

(c) E&S Risk Classification. Based on the screening outcomes, the Consultant shall assign each sub-project or asset replacement activity a preliminary E&S risk classification consistent with the World Bank ESF risk categories (High, Substantial, Moderate, or Low). The classification shall consider both the type and scale of potential impacts and the sensitivity of the receiving environment and social context.

(d) Screening Report. The Consultant shall prepare an E&S Screening Report summarizing the results of the screening exercise for all sub-projects. The report shall include, for each sub-project: the completed screening checklist, the preliminary E&S risk classification, the rationale for the classification, and recommended E&S assessment and management measures required under Task 5. The Screening Report shall form an input to the Project Identification deliverable and shall be shared with EFL, the Ministry of Finance, and the World Bank for review and clearance prior to finalization.

The outcomes of the E&S screening shall directly inform the selection and sequencing of sub-projects for the first batch of implementation, ensuring that sub-projects with manageable E&S risks are prioritized, and that appropriate assessment and management measures are in place before procurement commences.

 

 

Environmental and Social Assessment and Management

Building on the E&S screening conducted under Task 4, the Consultant shall undertake Environmental and Social (E&S) assessments and prepare the corresponding management instruments for the sub-projects identified for the implementation under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. All assessments and instruments shall comply with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable national environmental legislation of Fiji (including the Environment Management Act 2005 and associated regulations), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP).

    1. Scope and Approach

The E&S assessment shall cover all sub-projects in the first batch, as identified and screened under Task 4, including but not limited to:

  • Replacement of aged switchboards, transformers, and associated substation equipment across EFL's network;
  • Rehabilitation or replacement of generation assets at EFL's hydropower stations as identified under in the main text; and
  • Any associated civil, structural, or access works.

The scale and depth of assessment shall be proportionate to the E&S risk classification assigned to each sub-project under Task 4.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Assessment — Hydropower Asset Replacement

For asset replacement activities at hydropower stations, the Consultant shall prepare a standalone E&S assessment addressing the specific environmental and social sensitivities associated with hydropower infrastructure. The ESIA shall be prepared by qualified environmental and social specialists and shall include, at minimum, the following components:

 

(a) Description of the Existing Environment and Baseline Conditions

The Consultant shall compile and, where necessary, supplement existing baseline data to characterize the environmental and social baseline for each hydropower site and its area of influence, including:

  • Hydrology and water resources: river flow regimes, seasonal variability, historical discharge data, and existing water abstractions or diversions;
  • Aquatic ecology: species composition, abundance, and distribution of freshwater fish, macroinvertebrates, and other aquatic biota in rivers upstream and downstream of each facility;
  • Riparian and terrestrial ecology: vegetation communities, wildlife habitats, and any protected or endemic species in the project area;
  • Water quality: existing water quality conditions in receiving waterbodies;
  • Ecosystem services: identification and characterization of ecosystem services provided by river systems and dependent on flow regimes, including provisioning services (fisheries, water supply for downstream communities and agriculture), regulating services (flood attenuation, water purification), and cultural services (recreational, spiritual, and cultural values associated with rivers); and
  • Social baseline: communities and livelihoods dependent on river resources downstream of each facility, including subsistence fishing, smallholder irrigation, and cultural or ceremonial uses of water.

 

(b) Environmental Flow (E-Flow) Assessment

Given the small scale of the hydropower facility, the Consultant shall conduct a proportionate desktop E-flow review rather than a full E-flow assessment study. The review shall be commensurate with the nature of the asset replacement works and the associated level of hydrological risk.

The desktop review shall:

  • Document the existing operational flow regime at the facility, including any minimum flow release requirements specified in the facility's existing operating licence, consent conditions, or EFL operational procedures;
  • Confirm whether the proposed asset replacement works involve any physical changes to the intake structure, diversion weir, penstock, or tailrace that could alter the volume, timing, or continuity of water diverted or released — and if no such changes are proposed, note this explicitly as a basis for scoping out a detailed E-flow assessment;
  • Apply a simple hydrological desktop method — such as the Tennant (Montana) Method using available mean annual flow data — to provide a reference check on whether existing minimum flow releases at the facility are broadly consistent with accepted thresholds for maintaining basic ecological functions in the downstream river reach; and
  • Based on the above, conclude either that: (i) existing minimum flow provisions are adequate and no additional E-flow measures are required; or (ii) a gap exists that warrants a specific operational protocol or condition to be incorporated into the ESMP.

 

(c) Impact Assessment

The Consultant shall identify, predict, and evaluate the significance of potential environmental and social impacts associated with hydropower asset replacement works, covering both the construction and operational phases. Key impact pathways to be assessed shall include:

  • Changes to downstream flow regimes during works (e.g., dewatering, cofferdam installation, temporary flow diversion) and their effects on aquatic habitats, species, and ecosystem services;
  • Alteration of sediment transport and geomorphic processes resulting from changes to turbine operation or intake structures;
  • Impacts on aquatic biodiversity, particularly fish passage and migration, arising from works at intake or tailrace structures;
  • Risks of water quality degradation from construction activities, including turbidity, sedimentation, and potential release of oils, lubricants, or hazardous materials;
  • Hazardous waste generation and management, including oils, asbestos-containing materials, PCBs, SF6 gas, and other materials associated with aged electrical and mechanical equipment;
  • Community health and safety risks
  • Impacts on downstream communities dependent on river-based livelihoods and ecosystem services.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs)

The Consultant shall prepare ESMPs for each sub-project in the first batch, integrating findings from the E&S assessment (for hydropower facilities) and the E&S screening assessments. The ESMPs shall:

  • Describe, for each identified impact, the proposed hierarchy of mitigation measures (avoidance, minimization, mitigation, and compensation or offset where residual impacts remain);
  • Include specific management measures for: hazardous waste handling and disposal (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6); erosion and sediment control during civil works; hydropower operational protocols to maintain E-flows during construction phases; worker health and safety; community health and safety;
  • Specify monitoring requirements, including parameters to be monitored, monitoring locations, frequency, responsible parties, and reporting arrangements, with particular attention to downstream aquatic ecology and water quality monitoring at hydropower sites;
  • Define institutional responsibilities for ESMP implementation, supervision, and reporting within EFL;
  • Include a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) consistent with World Bank ESF requirements, covering all project-affected communities; and
  • Include an estimated budget for ESMP implementation.

 

    1. Stakeholder Engagement and Disclosure

In coordination with Task 2, the Consultant shall support EFL in conducting targeted stakeholder consultations on the E&S assessment and ESMP findings for each sub-project. Consultations shall be conducted in accordance with the Stakeholder Engagement Plan developed under Task 2, and shall be culturally appropriate and accessible to women, indigenous communities, and other vulnerable groups. Consultation records, including attendance, issues raised, and responses, shall be documented and appended to the ESIA and ESMP.

 

    1. Integration of E&S Requirements into Bidding Documents

The Consultant shall work closely with the procurement specialist engaged for Task 6 to ensure that all relevant E&S requirements are systematically integrated into the bidding documents for the asset replacement sub-projects. This shall include:

(a) E&S Specifications and Requirements. The Consultant shall prepare an Environmental and Social Requirements (ESR) section to be included within the bidding documents for each contract package, covering: Contractor obligations with respect to ESMP implementation, including preparation and submission of a Contractor Environmental and Social Management Plan (C-ESMP) prior to commencement of works; specific technical requirements for hazardous waste management (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6, and other hazardous materials from aged equipment), including approved disposal or recycling methods, handling procedures, and documentation requirements;

(b) E&S Performance Standards in Contract Conditions. The Consultant shall recommend appropriate contract conditions and performance standards to ensure contractor compliance with E&S requirements, including provisions for: submission and approval of the C-ESMP as a condition precedent to commencement of works; regular E&S reporting by the contractor;  and consequences for non-compliance, including stop-work orders and financial remedies.

(c) E&S Rated Criteria. The Consultant shall recommend criteria for evaluating contractor E&S capacity and performance as part of the qualification and evaluation criteria for each bidding package, covering contractor experience with E&S management on similar infrastructure projects, availability of qualified E&S personnel, and approach to hazardous materials management.

REPÚBLICA DEL ECUADOR

MINISTERIO DE INFRAESTRUCTURA Y TECNOLOGÍA - MIT

“PROYECTO DE VIVIENDA Y DESARROLLO URBANO INCLUSIVOS Y

RESILIENTES EN ECUADOR”

CONTRATO DE PRÉSTAMO BIRF 9598-EC

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS PARA LA “ELABORACIÓN DEL

DISEÑO URBANO-ARQUITECTÓNICO DEFINITIVO DE LA PRIMERA INICIATIVA BARRIAL (OBRA DE CONFIANZA), LA ELABORACIÓN DE LA AGENDA BARRIAL Y LA ELABORACIÓN DEL DISEÑO URBANO-ARQUITECTÓNICO DEFINITIVO DE LA OBRA PRIORIZADA, BARRIO LAS ACACIAS (GADM MANTA)”.

CÓDIGO DE REFERENCIA: EC-MIT-555609-CS-QCBS

 

La República de Ecuador ha recibido un Préstamo del Banco Mundial para el financiamiento del “PROYECTO DE VIVIENDA Y DESARROLLO URBANO INCLUSIVOS Y RESILIENTES EN ECUADOR”, y parte de los recursos de ese préstamo serán destinados a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

 

La presente consultoría se enmarca en el objetivo general del Componente 2 y se ejecuta dentro del Subcomponente 2.2, como parte del Programa de Mejoramiento Integral de Barrios (MIB), el cual tiene como finalidad mejorar la calidad de vida de la población residente en los barrios priorizados, mediante la implementación, ampliación y mejora del espacio público y la infraestructura urbana, la reducción de la vulnerabilidad frente a amenazas naturales y climáticas, y la promoción de procesos de participación comunitaria que fortalezcan la cohesión social y la apropiación del entorno urbano.

Como resultado de la implementación del Programa de Mejoramiento Integral de Barrios (MIB), se generan productos técnicos y operativos que estructuran la intervención integral a escala barrial, entre los cuales se incluyen:

 

  1. Primera Iniciativa Barrial (Obra de Confianza): Obra definida por el barrio en un proceso participativo, es una construcción de rápida y fácil ejecución, de alto impacto social que demuestra compromiso entre residentes, actores locales, GAD y ahora el Ministerio de Infraestructura y Tecnología (MIT), cuyo propósito es generar confianza y entusiasmo, mientras avanza la Agenda Barrial.
  2. Agenda Barrial: La Agenda Barrial es un instrumento técnico-social estratégico de planificación territorial a escala barrial, elaborado de manera participativa con la población, el Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado, el ahora Ministerio de Infraestructura y Tecnología (MIT) y otros actores locales.

 

Este instrumento define la hoja de ruta para el desarrollo integral del barrio en el corto, mediano y largo plazo, mediante la identificación y priorización de las necesidades del territorio, e incorpora mecanismos de gobernanza local a través de procesos metodológicos adaptados a contextos de vulnerabilidad climática, riesgos naturales y exclusión social.

 

Asimismo, la Agenda Barrial permite la elaboración de diagnósticos urbano- arquitectónico y social, la identificación de riesgos, oportunidades y necesidades, y la priorización participativa de soluciones de hábitat que orientan una hoja de ruta técnica, para la inversión pública, constituyéndose en un insumo para la ejecución posterior de estudios, diseños y obras físicas que determinará un portafolio de proyectos conforme el Hito de Implementación – Paso 8, Elaboración de la Agenda Barrial del Manual Operativo del Proyecto (MOP).

  • Portafolio de proyectos: es un listado de proyectos dentro del polígono barrial específico y su entorno inmediato que han sido identificados, analizados y priorizados participativamente en el desarrollo de la Agenda Barrial. Es una herramienta que contiene fichas técnicas de cada proyecto en las cuales indica información pertinente como ubicación, presupuesto estimado, justificación, importancia, viabilidad y el impacto que genera, así como, el diseño del proyecto a nivel de idea, incluyendo el contenido mínimo establecido en la ficha técnica adjunta (Anexo 10).
  1. Obra Priorizada: Obra definida por el barrio en un proceso participativo, es una obra de mayor escala, que materializa la visión definida por la comunidad e identificada en el proceso de la Agenda Barrial, busca cumplir todos los objetivos del Programa de Mejoramiento Integral de Barrios (MIB).

El alcance, la metodología e hitos del presente proceso se encuentran determinados en el término de referencia y sus anexos.

Los términos de referencia detallados para la presente consultoría podrán consultarse en el siguiente enlace: https://www.mit.gob.ec/postulaciones/

El MIT, invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles (“Consultores”) a manifestar sus expresiones de interés en la prestación de los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deberán proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para realizar los Servicios.

La presente contratación está dirigida a firmas consultoras o asociaciones de firmas legalmente constituidas, con experiencia demostrable en estudios urbanos, diseño urbano–arquitectónico, gestión y participación social y formulación de instrumentos de planificación participativa a escala barrial o urbana.

La firma consultora deberá:

  1. Estar legalmente constituida y habilitada para prestar servicios de consultoría en el país, de conformidad con la normativa vigente.
  2. Acreditar experiencia general en la ejecución de estudios o consultorías vinculadas a planificación urbana, mejoramiento barrial, diseño urbano–arquitectónico, gestión y participación social y/o proyectos de inversión en hábitat y vivienda.
  3. Acreditar experiencia específica en al menos uno de los siguientes ámbitos:
  • Proyectos de mejoramiento integral de barrios u operaciones similares.
  • Formulación participativa de agendas barriales, planes o programas a escala barrial o urbana.
  • Estudios y diseños definitivos de espacio público, equipamientos comunitarios o intervenciones urbanas en contextos similares al barrio.
  1. Preferentemente, acreditar experiencia previa en proyectos financiados por organismos multilaterales (Banco Mundial u otros), o en proyectos con requerimientos de salvaguardas socioambientales y enfoques transversales similares.

Los criterios para la selección de la lista corta son los siguientes:

Experiencia mínima exigida para la firma consultora

Tipo

Descripción

Monito mínimo por proyecto

Experiencia general

 

Experiencia general. La firma consultora deberá acreditar un mínimo de tres (3) contratos en: ejecución de proyectos financiados por entidades públicas, gobiernos locales, cooperación internacional o multilaterales (BID, Banco Mundial, GIZ, PNUD, instituciones públicas, etc.); programas de urbanismo social o mejoramiento de barrios; Planes de Desarrollo y Ordenamiento Territorial (PDOT) o Planes de Uso y Gestión de Suelos (PUGS).

 

El monto acumulado de los contratos acreditados deberá ser superior a USD 100.000

Experiencia específica

 

Experiencia específica. La firma consultora deberá acreditar un mínimo de dos (2) contratos en: elaboración de agendas barriales o planes de desarrollo comunitario participativos; proyectos

de diseño participativo; proyectos de mejoramiento integral de barrios con componentes sociales y urbanos; proyectos urbanos temporales o planificados con las comunidades; planes de ordenamiento barrial o esquemas urbanos comunitarios; modelos de gestión.

Cada contrato deberá acreditar un monto mínimo de USD 40.000.

 

El personal técnico clave no será evaluado en la etapa de conformación de la lista corta.

Las Expresiones de Interés (SEI) de los Consultores interesados es requerida conforme al párrafo 7.3 de la Sección VII de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, vigente. De igual forma, se llama la atención de los consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.16 y 3.17 de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones, que establecen la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflicto de interés.

Los Consultores pueden asociarse con otras empresas para mejorar sus calificaciones, pero deben indicar claramente si la asociación adopta la forma de una empresa conjunta y/o una subconsultoría. En caso de asociación bajo la modalidad de empresa conjunta (Joint Venture), todos los integrantes responderán solidariamente por la totalidad del contrato, si son seleccionados.

Se seleccionará un Consultor de acuerdo con el método de Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo (SBCC), descrito en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones.

Los Consultores podrán obtener más información en la dirección que figura en los datos de la Contratante durante el horario de oficina 08h30 a 16h30

Juan León Mera N26-220 y Av. Orellana, piso 14, en el horario de 08h30 a.m. a 16h00 p.m.

Documentación de respaldo de la experiencia: Para acreditar la experiencia general y específica, los consultores deberán presentar contratos, convenios, órdenes de servicio, certificados de experiencia, actas de entrega-recepción definitivas o documentos equivalentes, emitidos por la entidad contratante o fuente independiente, que permitan verificar el objeto, alcance, período de ejecución y demás condiciones requeridas en los Términos de Referencia.

No serán aceptables documentos de respaldo emitidos por la propia firma consultora.

Country: Mongolia

Project Title: Fifth Energy Sector Project (ESP-5)

Grant No.: GFPP Grant No. TF0C8834

Assignment Title: Detailed Engineering Design and Preparation of Bidding Documents for the Expansion and Modernization of the Power Transmission and Distribution Grid in Ulaanbaatar and Surrounding Areas – Lot 2

Reference No.: MN-MOE-ESP5-CS-QCBS-LOT2

The Government of Mongolia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Fifth Energy Sector Project (ESP5) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) include preparing the Detailed Engineering Design for the Expansion of the Electricity Transmission and Distribution System for Lot 2. The assignment will last sixteen (16) months. During this period, the Consultant shall prepare comprehensive detailed engineering designs and draft bidding documents for ten (10) identified sub-projects under Lot 2. The Services shall be carried out in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations of Mongolia, relevant international and national technical standards, and the World Bank’s Environmental, Social, Health, and Safety (ESHS) requirements.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are available at:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1k_Y0V5s0IlTTuYfPKud8JvhzGIkEYaA_dYyVcRwOXlo/edit?usp=sharing

The Ministry of Energy now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the Services, including:

  • Relevant experience in assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity, particularly in detailed design of power transmission lines and substations.
  • Firm’s core business, years in operation, and technical and managerial capabilities relevant to the assignment;
  • Organizational capacity, availability of qualified personnel, quality assurance and monitoring approaches, and resources available to undertake the Services; and
  • Other supporting documentation demonstrating the firm’s qualifications and experience, as appropriate.

Shortlisting criteria are as follows:

Interested firms must provide evidence demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services, including:

  1. General Experience: Minimum seven (7) years of continuous experience in the energy sector, with focus on the detailed engineering design of power transmission lines and substations.
  2. Specific Experience: Successful completion of at least two (2) contracts within the last ten (10) years involving the preparation of Detailed Engineering Designs for substations, overhead transmission lines, and cable lines rated at 110 kV or above, which shall have been approved by the relevant State Expert Review authority. Experience in projects financed by international financial institutions (IFIs) will be considered an advantage.
  3. Licensing Requirement: The firm shall hold valid licenses specified in Articles 8.1.3.1 and 8.1.14.7 of the Law of Mongolia on Permits (for high-complexity facility construction and engineering design).
  4. Organizational and Technical Capability: Information demonstrating the firm’s organizational structure, quality management systems, technical resources, professional capabilities and managerial capacity relevant to the assignment.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Only shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below by e-mail at munkhbadral@energy.gov.mn no later than 17:00 hours (local time) on 16 October 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

National Project Manager/M&E

(Ref. No. C3-IC-01.1, Project ID No. P178883, IDA Credit No. 7431-LA)

The Government of Lao PDR (GOL) is implementing the Reducing Rural Poverty and Malnutrition Project II (RRPMP II) (P178883) from 2024 to 2029 with financing from the World Bank (WB).  The RRPMP II will implement a nutrition-sensitive social protection program or a Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) Program to address issues of poverty and malnutrition and develop and implement mechanism to ensure multi-sectoral coordination, planning, monitoring, and evaluation of the nutrition convergence approach: the Reducing Rural Poverty and Malnutrition Project. The Project Management Unit (PMU) for the RRPMP II is the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRP) within the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE ) in Vientiane Capital, which has overall responsibility for operational aspects of the project at the national and sub-national level including contract administration, financial management, procurement, and monitoring and evaluation, as well as overseeing implementation. 

 

Rural Resilience and Poverty Reduction Project (RRPMP II) intends to engage a full-time Project Manager/M&E will provide overarching support to the implementation of the RRPMP II and the various activities that it comprises. The manager will work with DRP, MAE and IFCD, MOF and will report to the Project Director and the Project Coordinator.

 

RRPMP II now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested candidate should provide information (CV, Expression of Interest, other supporting information, if any) demonstrating that she/he has the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. In order to qualify for this position, the candidates shall meet the following experience and competence requirements:

 

  • A Bachelor’s degree in public or business administration, management or relevant field;
  • At least 05 years’ experience in project management, preferably of large-scale development projects financed by IFIs; experience with large-scale data collection and/or cash or asset transfer programs a plus;
  • Good up to date knowledge of World Bank procedures, policies and financial rules, and regulations preferred.
  • Excellent organizational, planning, time and personnel management, and problem-solving skills;
  • Excellent leadership and interpersonal skills and ability to work with multiple teams in different geographic locations;
  • Computer literacy: word processing, spreadsheets, PowerPoint, and database programs;
  • Excellent English and Lao communication skills, written and spoken (two samples of written work or pass a written test); 
  • Availability and willingness to undertake extensive visits to remote and hard to reach project locations.

 

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 4th edition of November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by           30 September 2026, 16:00 o’clock Lao time (submissions via email are also acceptable). Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499) - Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP)

Loan No/Credit No/Grant Number

GFPP Grant No. TF0D0728

Assignment Title

International Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist

Procurement Plan Ref Number

FJ-EFL-567224-CS-INDV

EOI-04/2026

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of preparing the Fiji Energy Transformation Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise specialist environmental and social support to EFL's Project Preparation Unit. The Consultant will lead preparation of appraisal-stage environmental and social instruments, integrate requirements of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework into technical and procurement outputs, support policy and regulatory reviews, and prepare a procurement-ready terms of reference for a separate assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional Environmental and Social Management System.

 

The Services will cover:

• general environmental and social support to the Project Preparation Unit, including screening, risk-register management, ESCP inputs, coordination and practical capacity building;

• preparation of E&S scoping studies with critical-habitat screening, a site-specific ESMP for aging asset replacement, an RPF, negotiated land agreement due diligence, an integrated SEP, and LMP;

• preparation of a procurement-ready TOR for development and operationalization of EFL's institutional ESMS;

• environmental and social review of Electricity Act amendments, Rooftop Solar PV Policy, and private-sector renewable-energy participation;

• E&S inputs to the National control-centre upgrade, , aging power-infrastructure, grid-interconnection, hydropower and solar PV/BESS studies and concept designs; and

• monthly and quarterly reporting, disclosure support and an appraisal-stage E&S readiness summary.

 

Implementation period: The assignment is expected to be part-time for the full GFPP implementation period, estimated at [24 months], subject to satisfactory performance and availability of GFPP financing.

 

Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference are attached to this REOI as Appendix 1.

 

Energy Fiji Limited now invites eligible individual consultants ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers concerning conflict of interest.

 

EOI Evaluation Criteria

2. Demonstrated application of the World Bank ESF or IFC Performance Standards and preparation of ESMP, land/resettlement, SEP/GRM and LMP instruments

3. Experience in biodiversity and critical-habitat screening, ESS5 land due diligence, and ESS7 engagement and FPIC

4. Relevant renewable-energy, grid infrastructure, hazardous-materials, Pacific or Fiji experience, including familiarity with iTaukei land tenure and governance

Form and content of the Expression of Interest:
