Submission

Further information may be obtained by emailing tenders@efl.com.fj during office hours, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM Fiji Time, Monday to Friday, no later than three clear days before the closing date.

Expressions of interest must be uploaded to the EFL e-Tender Portal (TenderLink) at https://www.tenderlink.com/efl by registering your company, by 4:00 PM (1600 hrs) Fiji Time on Wednesday, 30th September 2026.

EOI documents may be viewed and downloaded from www.efl.com.fj(opens in new window) or https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window).

Submissions by email or facsimile will not be accepted. Hard-copy submissions to the tender box at EFL Head Office, Suva, will not be accepted.

 

 

Appendix 1 - Terms of Reference

TERMS OF REFERENCE

INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL (E&S) SPECIALIST

Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499)

Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) - Energy Fiji Limited (EFL)

1. Introduction and Background

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) is preparing the Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499), a World Bank-supported initiative estimated at USD 230 million. The project aims to accelerate renewable-energy development, modernize the power grid, rehabilitate aging infrastructure, and reform the power sector to attract private investment in solar energy. Key interventions span Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni, including solar PV/BESS parks of more than 50 MW each, grid-evacuation infrastructure, transmission-line upgrades and modernization of existing power stations.

The Initial Environmental and Social Review Summary has classified the project's environmental and social risks as Substantial, reflecting biodiversity impacts, customary iTaukei land tenure, community health and safety, labor influx, SEA/SH risks, and supply-chain concerns associated with PV modules and battery energy storage systems.

EFL is establishing a Project Preparation Unit (PPU) to prepare the project for appraisal and Board approval. The E&S Specialist will lead preparation of required E&S instruments, integrate E&S requirements into technical and procurement outputs, and prepare the TOR for a separate capacity-building assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional ESMS.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The objective is to ensure that GFPP-financed preparation activities and the investments they support comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, the project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, applicable Fiji law, and Good International Industry Practice.

3. Scope of Work

The Consultant will perform the following tasks, organized into five functional areas:

3.1 General E&S Support to the PPU

• Serve as the PPU's E&S focal point and advise the Project Manager and technical teams on application of the ESF.

• Screen preparation activities and concept designs, identify applicable standards and instruments, and maintain an E&S Risk Register with actions, responsibilities and status.

• Prepare ESCP inputs, TORs for specialized studies, and E&S requirements for technical specifications and bidding documents; oversee related consultant outputs.

• Provide practical ESF training and on-the-job support to the PPU and relevant EFL staff.

• Coordinate with the World Bank, relevant Fiji agencies, TLTB, technical consultants and EFL departments, and maintain records of key decisions and actions.

3.2 Preparation of E&S Instruments Required by Appraisal

This is the most critical function of the assignment. The E&S Specialist will prepare the following appraisal-stage instruments and related outputs:

a. E&S Scoping Studies with Critical Habitat Screening

• Lead scoping studies for solar PV/BESS parks on Vanua Levu and Taveuni, grid-evacuation infrastructure, and new or upgraded transmission lines.

• Conduct structured Critical Habitat screening under ESS6 using available biodiversity data, including IUCN Red List species, Fiji endemic avifauna information, and protected-area registries.

• Where critical habitat is identified or cannot be ruled out, prepare detailed assessments and, where necessary, a Biodiversity Management Plan with offset strategies, no-go zones and seasonal restrictions.

• Include baseline social surveys, land-tenure mapping, community presence, vulnerable-group identification, and climate-resilience considerations such as cyclone, flooding and sea-level-rise risks.

b. Environmental and Social Management Plan - Aging Asset Replacement

• Prepare a site-specific ESMP for rehabilitation and replacement of aging power infrastructure under Component 3, covering baseline conditions, construction and operational risks, hazardous materials including PCBs, asbestos and e-waste, mitigation, monitoring, emergency response, contractor requirements, responsibilities, schedules and costs.

c. Resettlement Policy Framework

• Prepare an RPF consistent with ESS5 covering legal and institutional arrangements and gap analysis; eligibility and cut-off dates; entitlements and replacement-cost valuation; livelihood restoration; procedures for site-specific plans; consultation and grievance arrangements; monitoring, responsibilities and budget provisions.

d. Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report

• Identify and document all project sites or corridors where land or access rights have been or may be secured through negotiated settlement or other voluntary arrangement, and verify consistency with ESS5 and Fiji law.

• Prepare an inventory of leases, easements, access and land-use agreements, donations, transfers and other consensual arrangements, recording parcels, rights-holders, status, duration, consideration, benefits and supporting evidence.

• Assess whether each arrangement is voluntary, transparent, informed and free from coercion; whether formal, informal, customary, secondary and shared rights-holders were identified and represented; and whether participants had sufficient information, time, advice and a genuine right to refuse.

• For customary land and resources, screen whether ESS7 and FPIC apply. Where required, document a culturally appropriate collective process through institutions selected by affected iTaukei communities, with participation of women, youth and potentially excluded rights-holders. Do not infer FPIC solely from approvals by TLTB, agencies or individual owners.

• Where applicable, confirm and document eligibility cut-off dates, culturally appropriate public notice, valuation and compensation or benefit methodology, replacement-cost consistency, implementation status, grievances and corrective actions.

• Conclude for each arrangement whether ESS5 criteria are demonstrated and identify any additional instrument, remedial action, responsible party and completion deadline required before access or civil works.

e. Integrated Stakeholder Engagement Plan

• Prepare a project-level SEP consistent with ESS10, including stakeholder analysis, differentiated engagement for disadvantaged or vulnerable groups, disclosure, responsibilities, schedule, monitoring and reporting.

• Include a culturally appropriate consultation plan for communities potentially affected by solar PV/BESS and associated infrastructure, covering languages, timing, representation, feedback, land arrangements, benefit sharing and any ESS7 FPIC process.

• Establish an accessible project grievance mechanism and a confidential, survivor-centered SEA/SH reporting and referral pathway.

f. Labor Management Procedures

• Prepare LMP consistent with ESS2 for direct, contracted, community and primary supply workers, including applicable law and gaps, terms and conditions, OHS, emergency preparedness, accommodation, labor influx, child and forced labor, PV/BESS supply-chain due diligence, codes of conduct, worker grievances, contractor obligations and training.

g. TOR for Development and Operationalization of EFL's ESMS

• Prepare a procurement-ready TOR and supporting inputs for a separate assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional ESMS including potential staffing and structure to ensure the ESMS is properly resourced, strategically aligned, and embedded within EFL for lasting effectiveness.

• Define objectives, scope, methodology, deliverables, schedule, expertise, coordination, knowledge transfer and acceptance criteria. Cover policy and governance; screening; stakeholder, labor, land, biodiversity, pollution, community-safety, cultural-heritage, contractor and supply-chain management; incident response; monitoring; reporting; tools; templates; training; and a time-bound implementation plan.

• Consult relevant EFL departments. This assignment does not include development or implementation of the ESMS.

3.3 Policy and Regulatory Support

• Review proposed amendments to Fiji's Electricity Act from an E&S perspective, identify gaps with the World Bank ESF and international good practice, and recommend measures for the revised policy.

• Review the proposed Rooftop Solar PV Policy from an E&S perspective, including potential effects on consumers, community uptake and grid workers.

• Advise on E&S requirements for private-sector renewable-energy participation, including application of IFC Performance Standards and World Bank ESF requirements to PPP or private-investment components.

• Assess EFL's potential for an Environmental and Social Policy and support EFL's E&S team to derive and implement a practical policy.

3.4 E&S Inputs to Technical Studies and Infrastructure Components

• National Control Center Upgrade: identify E&S risks associated with civil works, OHS, asbestos and PCBs, and recommend mitigation for technical specifications.

• Modernization of Nabouwalu Government Station: conduct site-specific screening, identify community-proximity, worker-community and hazardous-material risks, and prepare an ESMP if required.

• Aging Infrastructure Rehabilitation: supplement the Component 3 ESMP with screening and, where feasible, inspection of all proposed sub-sites for hazardous materials, cultural heritage and social risks.

• Power Grid Interconnection, Vanua Levu-Taveuni: support feasibility and engineering studies with environmental and social routing-alternatives analysis and identification of a preferred route based on E&S criteria.

• Hydropower: prepare assessment TOR requirements covering direct, indirect, induced and cumulative life-cycle impacts across the relevant catchment, including flows, sediment, biodiversity, ecosystem services, water use, livelihoods, land, safety, cultural heritage, associated facilities, alternatives, mitigation, monitoring and adaptive management.

• Solar PV/BESS Parks: provide E&S inputs to concept designs for two parks of more than 50 MW each, including environmentally and socially informed site-selection criteria and ESF compliance review.

3.5 Monitoring, Reporting and Disclosure

• Submit monthly E&S progress reports covering instrument preparation, risk-register actions, engagement, grievances, emerging issues and preparation-phase ESCP commitments.

• Prepare quarterly stakeholder-engagement summaries.

• Coordinate disclosure through EFL and other required channels and make accessible copies available to affected communities.

• Prepare an appraisal-stage E&S readiness summary recording instrument status, review, disclosure, outstanding actions and post-appraisal timelines.

4. Methodology

• Desktop review of project, legal, technical and E&S documentation and available baseline data.

• Structured screening, site visits and physical inspections where feasible.

• Stakeholder consultations with EFL, government agencies, TLTB, affected communities, technical consultants and the World Bank.

• Application of the World Bank ESF, ESCP, applicable Fiji law, GIIP and the mitigation hierarchy.

• Iterative preparation, review and revision of instruments, with clear evidence trails, action tracking and quality assurance.

• Practical knowledge transfer and on-the-job support to EFL and PPU personnel.

5. Key Deliverables

Deliverable

Timeline

E&S screening notes for all GFPP-financed activities (rolling)

Within 1 week of initiation of each activity

E&S Risk Register, initial and updated quarterly

Within 1 month of mobilization, then quarterly

Inputs to ESCP

As directed by World Bank task team

E&S Scoping Studies with Critical Habitat Screening

By 15 December

ESMP for Component 3, Aging Asset Replacement

By 15 December

Resettlement Policy Framework

By 15 December

Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report(s)

By 15 December

Stakeholder Engagement Plan, including consultation plan, project GRM and SEA/SH pathway

By 15 December

Labor Management Procedures

By 15 December

Procurement-ready TOR and supporting inputs for EFL ESMS assignment

Within 3 months of mobilization and in time for procurement

Advisory notes on Electricity Act amendments and Rooftop Solar PV Policy

As requested

E&S inputs to bidding documents and technical specifications

As required by procurement schedule

E&S technical input notes for infrastructure studies and components

According to relevant technical-study schedule

Monthly E&S progress reports

Monthly

Quarterly stakeholder-engagement summaries

Quarterly

ESF capacity-building and on-the-job training program, materials and attendance records

Within 2 months of mobilization, then as required

Disclosure record and consolidated Appraisal-Stage E&S Readiness Summary

Before appraisal, updated as required

All deliverables shall be submitted in English, professionally edited, and formatted in accordance with any World Bank templates provided.

6. Reporting and Coordination

The E&S Specialist will report to the PPU Project Manager on a day-to-day basis. For technical E&S matters, the Specialist will coordinate closely with World Bank E&S Specialists and participate in World Bank supervision missions and project-preparation meetings.

The Specialist will also coordinate with:

• EFL's full-time Environmental Officer and Social Officer, once recruited;

• GFPP technical consultants in engineering, energy and finance;

• iTaukei Land Trust Board on land-tenure and customary-engagement matters;

• Department of Environment and other relevant Fiji government agencies; and

• external E&S consultants engaged for specialized studies.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

7.1 Education

• University degree, at minimum Bachelor's level, in environmental science, social science, natural-resource management, engineering or a closely related field. A postgraduate qualification in environmental or social assessment is strongly preferred.

7.2 Professional Experience

• At least seven years of relevant experience in E&S assessment and management for infrastructure or energy projects.

• Demonstrated application of the World Bank ESF or IFC Performance Standards and preparation of ESMPs, land or resettlement instruments, SEPs/GRMs and LMPs.

• Experience in biodiversity and critical-habitat screening, ESS5 land and resettlement due diligence, and ESS7 engagement and FPIC.

• Experience with hazardous materials, renewable energy, grid infrastructure or power generation is desirable.

• Pacific or Fiji experience, including familiarity with iTaukei land tenure and governance, is strongly preferred.

• Strong writing, coordination, consultation and capacity-building skills in multicultural settings.

8. Duration and Location

• Duration: Part-time for the full GFPP implementation period, estimated at [24 months], subject to satisfactory performance and GFPP availability.

• Location: Remote-based, with regular travel to project sites on Vanua Levu, Taveuni and other islands as required for scoping, consultation and supervision.

    Crédit IDA 78730

    AC N° C-534-PIC3-INV

    Date de lancement :  16 septembre 2026

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a obtenu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour financer la mise en œuvre du Projet de Transformation économique pour la croissance inclusive (PIC3). Une partie du crédit sera utilisée pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de consultance cité en objet.

2. La mission principale de l’Assistant technique chargé d’accompagner le Ministère de l’Industrialisation et du Développement du Secteur Privé (MIDSP) dans l’identification, la structuration et la mise en œuvre de ses projets prioritaires et structurants, est d’accompagner le MIDSP dans la préparation d’un cadre stratégique et de réforme intégré fondé sur cinq étapes clairement articulées : diagnostiquer les réalités institutionnelles et sectorielles, prioriser les filières et chaînes de valeur à fort potentiel, formuler les orientations stratégiques, réformes et projets structurants, élaborer le cadre stratégique intégré, puis définir les modalités opérationnelles de mise en œuvre, de coordination et de suivi-évaluation.

3. Les termes de référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être consultés sur le site www.pic.mg

4. La Coordination Nationale du Projet PIC3 invite les candidats à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services cidessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Un consultant sera sélectionné en accord avec les procédures de recrutement de Consultant Individuel de la Banque Mondiale définies dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) pour les Fournitures, Travaux, Services autres que les Services de Consultants », 6ème édition – Février 2025. Les trois (03) candidats jugés pertinents, après évaluation des dossiers, seront invités pour un entretien.

5. L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI », énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

6. Le consultant recherché doit répondre aux qualifications suivantes :

  • Diplôme universitaire de niveau Master au minimum en économie, planification, politiques publiques, développement industriel, gestion de projets, administration publique, entrepreneuriat, finance, droit des affaires ou tout autre domaine pertinent.
  • Expérience professionnelle d’au moins 7 à 10 ans dans l’élaboration de politiques publiques, de stratégies sectorielles, de réformes économiques, de plans d’actions ou de programmes de développement.
  • Expérience confirmée dans les domaines couverts par la mission, notamment le développement industriel, le secteur privé, les PME/PMI, l’entrepreneuriat, l’investissement, l’environnement des affaires ou le développement des chaînes de valeur.
  • Expérience de collaboration avec les administrations publiques et les parties prenantes économiques, notamment les ministères, structures publiques, partenaires techniques et financiers, organisations professionnelles, institutions financières, secteur privé et acteurs régionaux.
  • Maîtrise des outils de planification stratégique, de gestion axée sur les résultats et de suivi-évaluation, ainsi que des méthodes de diagnostic, de formulation de plans d’actions et de conduite de consultations.
  • Excellentes capacités d’analyse, de rédaction, de synthèse et de facilitation, avec une aptitude démontrée à produire des documents stratégiques de qualité, animer des ateliers et travailler avec des équipes multidisciplinaires.
  • Parfaite maîtrise du français écrit et oral.

7. Les candidats intéressés doivent envoyer exclusivement par mail leur dossier de candidature, sous format PDF, composé d’une lettre de motivation, d’un CV détaillé avec les références professionnelles, d’une copie certifiée du diplôme le plus élevé ainsi que les attestations de travail au plus tard le 30 septembre 2026 à minuit à l’adresse : procurement@pic.mg

8. L’objet du mail d’envoi doit porter obligatoirement la mention suivante : AC N° C-534-PIC3-INV « AT ACCOMPAGNEMENT MIDSP »

Le Projet décline la responsabilité de la nonconsidération des candidatures ne respectant pas cette disposition obligatoire.

PROJET D’APPUI AU DEVELOPPEMENT DES CULTURES IRRIGUEES ET A L’INTENSISIFICATION DE LA PRODUCTION ANIMALE (PACIPA)

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET OU GROUPEMENT DE CABINETS POUR LA MISE EN OEUVRE DE SIX (6) PLANS D’ACTION DE REINSTALLATION DE SOUS PROJETS DE REHABILITATION ET D’AMENAGEMENT HYDRO AGRICOLE DANS LES REGIONS DE ZINDER ET DIFFA

 

Crédit IDA N° 76070-NE

 

N° de référence : NE-LAMP-565743-CS-CQS

 

Cet Avis à Manifestations d’intérêt fait suite à la publication de l’Avis Général de Passation des Marchés (AGPM) publié sur le site de la Banque Mondiale le 05 Août 2025 et sur le Sahel Dimanche du 08 Août 2025.

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger a sollicité un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant du financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET OU GROUPEMENT DE CABINETS POUR LA MISE EN OEUVRE DE SIX (6) PLANS D’ACTION DE REINSTALLATION DE SOUS PROJETS DE REHABILITATION ET D’AMENAGEMENT HYDRO AGRICOLE DANS LES REGIONS DE ZINDER ET DIFFA.

2. Les services du Consultant (« Services ») comprennent : lire plus bas les Termes de référence.

Objet et objectifs de la prestation

Objet

La mission a pour objet d’appuyer le PACIPA dans la mise en œuvre complète, transparente, inclusive et traçable des six PAR, jusqu’à la production des rapports d’achèvement et à la documentation de la libération des emprises, sans se substituer aux décisions et responsabilités régaliennes de l’État ni à l’obligation de paiement du Projet.

Objectifs spécifiques

Il s’agit plus spécifiquement de :

  • préparer et opérationnaliser le dispositif de mise en œuvre sur chaque site ;
  • informer et consulter les PAP et les autres parties prenantes dans des formats et langues accessibles ;
  • Préparer les dossiers individuels des PAP ;
  • vérifier, mettre à jour et sécuriser les bases de données et dossiers individuels des PAP, sans rouvrir arbitrairement l’éligibilité ;
  • accompagner la formalisation des ententes, la gestion des cas particuliers et la constitution des pièces administratives ;
  • appuyer le PACIPA et les structures compétentes pendant les opérations de compensation et assurer leur traçabilité ;
  • rendre opérationnels les comités locaux de réinstallation et le mécanisme de gestion des plaintes ;
  • assurer un accompagnement spécifique des personnes vulnérables et la prise en compte du genre, de l’EAS/HS et de la sécurité ;

  1. Contexte et justification

Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger, avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale, met en œuvre le Projet d’Appui au Développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA). Le Projet vise à accroître la productivité, la commercialisation et la résilience climatique des productions agricoles et pastorales. Il intervient notamment à travers la réhabilitation et l’aménagement de périmètres hydro-agricoles.

Ces investissements peuvent entraîner des pertes de terres, d’actifs ou de moyens de subsistance. Six Plans d’Action de Réinstallation (PAR) ont ainsi été préparés pour les sites de Harpa, Kakibaré, Kidikidiram, N’Guel Djaobol, Karmakawa et N’Gor Guidiyé. Leur mise en œuvre doit respecter la législation nationale, les instruments environnementaux et sociaux du PACIPA et la Norme environnementale et sociale n°5 (NES 5) de la Banque mondiale.

Compte tenu du nombre de personnes affectées, de la dispersion géographique des sites et de la sensibilité des opérations de compensation, le PACIPA souhaite mobiliser un cabinet ou un groupement de cabinets disposant d’une expérience démontrée dans la mise en œuvre opérationnelle de PAR complexes, particulièrement en contexte rural et hydro-agricole.

  1. Présentation du PACIPA

Le PACIPA est financé à hauteur de 350 millions de dollars pour sa première phase. Il couvre les régions de Diffa, Dosso, Maradi, Tahoua, Tillabéri et Zinder et s’articule autour des composantes suivantes :

Composante 1 : renforcement de la production agricole et pastorale résiliente ;

Composante 2 : amélioration des marchés agricoles et du bétail ;

Composante 3 : facilitation de l’accès au financement ;

Composante 4 : coordination, gestion et renforcement institutionnel ;

Composante 5 : intervention d’urgence (CERC).

  1. Objet et objectifs de la prestation
    1. Objet

La mission a pour objet d’appuyer le PACIPA dans la mise en œuvre complète, transparente, inclusive et traçable des six PAR, jusqu’à la production des rapports d’achèvement et à la documentation de la libération des emprises, sans se substituer aux décisions et responsabilités régaliennes de l’État ni à l’obligation de paiement du Projet.

    1. Objectifs spécifiques de la prestation

Il s’agit plus spécifiquement de :

  • Préparer et opérationnaliser le dispositif de mise en œuvre sur chaque site ;
  • Informer et consulter les PAP et les autres parties prenantes dans des formats et langues accessibles ;
  • Préparer les dossiers individuels des PAP ;
  • Vérifier, mettre à jour et sécuriser les bases de données et dossiers individuels des PAP, sans rouvrir arbitrairement l’éligibilité ;
  • Accompagner la formalisation des ententes, la gestion des cas particuliers et la constitution des pièces administratives ;
  • Appuyer le PACIPA et les structures compétentes pendant les opérations de compensation et assurer leur traçabilité ;
  • Rendre opérationnels les comités locaux de réinstallation et le mécanisme de gestion des plaintes ;
  • Assurer un accompagnement spécifique des personnes vulnérables et la prise en compte du genre, de l’EAS/HS et de la sécurité ;
  • Documenter la restauration des moyens de subsistance prévue par les PAR et produire les rapports d’achèvement par site.

 

  1. Étendus de la prestation et tâches

5.1 Phase de démarrage et appropriation

  • Analyser les six PAR, leurs bases de données, les instruments du PACIPA, les observations de validation et la documentation foncière disponible ;
  • Réaliser une revue de cohérence des listes de PAP, biens affectés, montants, vulnérabilités et pièces justificatives ;
  • Préparer une méthodologie, un plan de déploiement multi-sites, une matrice des risques, un protocole de protection des données et un chronogramme détaillé ;
  • Établir les modalités de coordination avec l’UGP, les UCR, les autorités, le Code rural, l’ONAHA, le BNEE et les autres services concernés.

5.2 Information, consultation et mobilisation

  • Élaborer et mettre en œuvre un plan de communication adapté aux langues et réalités locales ;
  • Divulguer les informations essentielles des PAR : droits, critères, barèmes, calendrier, voies de recours et contacts du mécanisme de gestion de plaintes ;
  • Organiser les consultations, réunions publiques et séances ciblées avec les femmes, jeunes, personnes handicapées et autres groupes vulnérables ;
  • Tenir des registres de participation désagrégés et documenter les préoccupations et réponses apportées.

5.3 Actualisation et sécurisation des dossiers des PAP

  • Contrôler l’identité, les coordonnées, les actifs, les montants et le statut de chaque PAP ;
  • Mettre à jour les changements survenus depuis la date butoir (décès, succession, procuration, incapacité, erreur matérielle), selon une procédure validée par le PACIPA ;
  • Accompagner, lorsque nécessaire, les audiences foraines pour l’établissement des CIN et la délivrance des pièces administratives ;
  • Constituer un dossier individuel complet, une fiche d’entente et une piste d’audit pour chaque PAP ;
  • Mettre en place une base sécurisée, interopérable et assortie d’un registre des modifications.

5.4 Structures locales, conciliation et gestion des plaintes

  • Mettre en place ou redynamiser les CLR ou CAC, CGP et autres instances prévues, puis former leurs membres ;
  • Enregistrer, catégoriser, traiter et suivre les plaintes dans les délais du MGP ;
  • Orienter immédiatement et de manière confidentielle les plaintes sensibles, notamment EAS/HS, vers les mécanismes appropriés ;
  • Appuyer les sessions de conciliation et, le cas échéant, les travaux des commissions administratives compétentes, sans exercer leurs prérogatives ;
  • Produire un tableau de bord des plaintes, décisions, délais et taux de clôture.

5.5 Compensation, accompagnement et libération des emprises

  • Préparer les listes de paiement contrôlées et les dossiers nécessaires à l’opérateur de paiement ;
  • Informer individuellement les PAP et organiser leur mobilisation dans des conditions sûres et dignes ;
  • Observer et documenter les paiements, les échecs de transaction, les absences et les cas litigieux ;
  • S’assurer que les compensations et mesures d’assistance sont réalisées avant la prise de possession des terres et le démarrage des travaux concernés ;
  • Appuyer le suivi des mesures de restauration des moyens de subsistance et l’assistance aux personnes vulnérables ;
  • Documenter la libération volontaire et régulière des emprises, sans coercition.

5.6 Clôture et capitalisation

  • Réconcilier les données des PAR, dossiers individuels, paiements et plaintes ;
  • Identifier les écarts résiduels et proposer un plan d’actions correctives assorti de responsables et délais ;
  • Produire les rapports d’achèvement par site et un rapport consolidé de mission ;
  • Transférer au PACIPA l’intégralité des bases, pièces, supports et outils dans des formats ouverts et exploitables.

6. Résultats attendus

  • R1. Le dispositif de mise en œuvre, de coordination, de communication et de gestion des risques est opérationnel sur les six sites.
  • R2. Toutes les PAP sont informées de leurs droits, des montants, du calendrier et des voies de recours dans un format accessible.
  • R3. Les bases de données et dossiers individuels sont contrôlés, actualisés, sécurisés et traçables.
  • R4. Les structures locales de réinstallation et le mécanisme de plaintes sont fonctionnels et documentés.
  • R5. Les compensations et mesures d’assistance sont suivies, rapprochées et documentées avant libération des emprises.
  • R6. Les personnes vulnérables et les cas particuliers reçoivent un accompagnement adapté.
  • R7. Les écarts résiduels sont identifiés et traités à travers un plan d’actions correctives validé.
  • R8. Les rapports d’achèvement par site et le rapport consolidé sont validés par le PACIPA et, lorsque requis, par la Banque mondiale.

La durée prévisionnelle de la prestation est de quatre (0 3) mois à compter de la notification de l’ordre de service. Le Consultant proposera une organisation permettant des interventions parallèles dans les régions de Zinder et Diffa, tout en garantissant une coordination centrale, l’harmonisation des outils et le contrôle qualité.

Obligation de résultat organisationnel : La connaissance préalable d’un site ou du PACIPA n’est pas exigée. Le Consultant doit toutefois démontrer sa capacité à être opérationnel rapidement, à reprendre des bases existantes et à assurer un transfert complet et sécurisé des données.

 

9. Responsabilités des parties

9.1 Responsabilités du Consultant

Les responsabilités dévolues au consultant sont :

  • Mobiliser à temps le personnel, les équipements et la logistique prévus dans son offre ;
  • Assurer la qualité, la cohérence et la confidentialité des données ;
  • Faciliter l’identification des huissiers de justice par département afin de superviser les opérations de paiement ;
  • Respecter la NES 5, les autres NES pertinentes, la législation nationale, le code de conduite et les exigences EAS/HS du Projet ;
  • Ne prendre aucun engagement financier ou juridique au nom du PACIPA sans mandat écrit ;
  • Signaler sans délai tout risque de coercition, conflit, fraude, double paiement, atteinte à la sécurité ou violation de données ;
  • Remettre tous les livrables, justificatifs et fichiers sources au PACIPA.

9.2 Responsabilités du PACIPA

Les responsabilités du PACIPA sont :

  • Mettre à disposition les PAR validés, bases disponibles, instruments applicables et contacts institutionnels ;
  • Faciliter les introductions officielles et la coordination avec les autorités et services compétents ;
  • Examiner et valider les outils, listes et livrables dans les délais convenus ;
  • Prendre les décisions institutionnelles et assurer la disponibilité des ressources de compensation ;
  • Contractualiser l’opérateur de paiement, le cas échéant, et autoriser les paiements ;
  • Superviser la prestation par l’UGP et les UCR.

Le Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection fondée sur les Qualifications du Consultant (QC), conformément au Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement de la Banque mondiale, édition de juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023 et mars 2025, ainsi qu’aux dispositions de l’Accord de financement, du Plan de passation des marchés approuvé et de la sollicitation de manifestations d’intérêt.

La procédure sera conduite dans le respect des principes de libre concurrence, d’économie, d’intégrité, de transparence, d’équité et d’égalité de traitement. Toute situation de conflit d’intérêts sera traitée conformément au Règlement applicable.

15. Confidentialité, propriété des données et éthique

  • Toutes les données nominatives et pièces des PAP sont confidentielles et ne peuvent être utilisées à d’autres fins que la mission.
  • Les fichiers, outils, rapports et bases produits dans le cadre du contrat sont remis au PACIPA ; le Consultant en conserve uniquement les copies autorisées par écrit.
  • Le Consultant applique des contrôles d’accès, des sauvegardes, un registre des modifications et une procédure de notification des incidents de données.
  • Le personnel signe un code de conduite couvrant notamment la fraude, la corruption, la coercition, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, le harcèlement sexuel et la confidentialité.

Assignment Title: Detailed Engineering Design and Preparation of Bidding Documents for the Expansion and Modernization of the Power Transmission and Distribution Grid in Ulaanbaatar and Surrounding Areas – Lot 1

Reference No.: MN-MOE-ESP5-CS-QCBS-LOT1

The Government of Mongolia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Fifth Energy Sector Project (ESP5) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) include preparing the Detailed Engineering Design for the Expansion of the Electricity Transmission and Distribution System for Lot 1. The assignment will last sixteen (16) months. During this period, the Consultant shall prepare comprehensive detailed engineering designs and draft bidding documents for eleven (11) identified sub-projects under Lot 1. The Services shall be carried out in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations of Mongolia, relevant international and national technical standards, and the World Bank’s Environmental, Social, Health, and Safety (ESHS) requirements.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are available at:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1k_Y0V5s0IlTTuYfPKud8JvhzGIkEYaA_dYyVcRwOXlo/edit?usp=sharing

The Ministry of Energy now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the Services, including:

  • Relevant experience in assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity, particularly in detailed design of power transmission lines and substations;
  • Firm’s core business, years in operation, and technical and managerial capabilities relevant to the assignment;
  • Organizational capacity, availability of qualified personnel, quality assurance and monitoring approaches, and resources available to undertake the Services; and
  • Other supporting documentation demonstrating the firm’s qualifications and experience, as appropriate.

Shortlisting criteria are as follows:

Interested firms must provide evidence demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services, including:

  1. General Experience: Minimum seven (7) years of continuous experience in the energy sector, with focus on the detailed engineering design of power transmission lines and substations.
  2. Specific Experience: Successful completion of at least two (2) contracts within the last ten (10) years involving the preparation of Detailed Engineering Designs for substations, overhead transmission lines, and cable lines rated at 110 kV or above, which shall have been approved by the relevant State Expert Review authority. Experience in projects financed by international financial institutions (IFIs) will be considered an advantage.
  3. Licensing Requirement: The firm shall hold valid licenses specified in Articles 8.1.3.1 and 8.1.14.7 of the Law of Mongolia on Permits (for high-complexity facility construction and engineering design).
  4. Organizational and Technical Capability: Information demonstrating the firm’s organizational structure, quality management systems, technical resources, professional capabilities and managerial capacity relevant to the assignment.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Only shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal.

Assignment Title:

Consulting Service for Development of a detailed Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) with Strategic Environment Management Plan (SEMP)

Reference No.: S-9

Project ID No: P501274

The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Development of a detailed Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) for the existing and proposed Policies, Plans, Programs, and Projects in the region of Cox’sBazar District with adjoining Marine and Marine Coastal areas  as well as other impacted areas and prepare a Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP) with future intervension to manage and restore the environment and ecosystem in the impacted area.

 

  1. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes but not limited to:
  • Inception
  • Screening
  • Scoping
  • A report on Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) along with the detailed analysis of the PPPPs
  • Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP)
  • Draft Final SEA Report including SEMP
  1. The objectives of the consultancy services are to come-up with the cumulative environmental impacts of the existing and proposed Policies, Plans, Programs, and Projects (PPPPs) in Cox’s Bazar district including Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs-impacted areas so that the GoB can address them at the earliest phase of decision making alongside economic and social considerations. The specific objectives are:
  • Consideration of environmental and socio-economic consequences of existing and proposed PPPs (national and Cox’s Bazar district including Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas) that cover the target area of this assignment and promoting that these issues be addressed when formulating and implementing future, as well as existing and proposed PPPs to promote sustainable development in the target area and conservation of their environmental and ecological value;
  • Identification of key stakeholders relevant to selected sectors and organizing consultation meetings to obtain knowledge on existing bio-physical settings and socio-economic conditions, impacts of current and proposed developments, and potential strategies for future development of the Cox’s Bazar district-Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas;
  • Development of alternative strategies to minimize the direct/indirect, domestic/transboundary and cumulative impacts of development on the study area of the Chattogram division;
  • Prepare a SEMP with potential recommendations to improve environmental performance management in both the public and private sectors with regard to current and future development activities as well as to manage and restore the environment and ecosystem in the impacted area.
  • Formulation of a comprehensive monitoring framework as part of the Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP) for the study area of the Chattogram division including Cox’s Bazar district-Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas to support decision making and monitoring of the implementation of PPPs that are likely to affect the environment and socio-economic conditions of the target area.
  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: www.doe.gov.bd The ToR or any further information can be obtained at the address of the undersigned given below, during office hours from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm Bangladesh Standard Time (BST).
  2. The Department of Environment (DoE) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The shortlisting criteria are:

a)   General Experience of the Firm in providing similar services (core business and years in business);

b)   Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required areas;

c)   Experience in development partners funded similar Projects.

  1. Consultants are requested to submit, but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

(i)  The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/registration documents from the country of the firm (ii) Firm’s brochures; (iii) description of similar consultancy contracts, including the scope, contract amount, name of Client, period of the contract (date of contract signing to date of completion), location/ country of the services, etc.

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the Section III, Para 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  2. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or a sub-consultancy (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultant must explain in the EoI submission (a) the rationale/ justification for the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide the above explanation in the EoI may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. However, the qualifications/ experience of sub-consultants will not be considered by the Client in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for Shortlisting purposes.
  3. A Consulting Firm will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method as set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.
  4. Expected date for commencement of the services is March 2027 and the tentative duration of the entire assignment is 9 months.

Lot 1: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kyiv HPP / PSP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (46 MW BESS capacity).

Lot 2: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kaniv HPP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (66 MW BESS capacity).

Lot 3: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kremenchuk HPP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (60 MW BESS capacity).

Lot 4: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Seredniodniprovska HPP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (25 MW BESS capacity).

Source of financing:

IBRD Loan No.: 9284-UA;

CTF Loan No.: TF0B5994;

CTF Loan No.: TF0C5903-UA; and

CTF Grant No.: TF-0B5724.

Project ID: P176114

RFB reference No.: UHE-IPSR-DSI-1

1. Private Joint Stock Company “Ukrhydroenergo” (PJSC “Ukrhydroenergo” or UHE) has received financing from the World Bank (hereinafter referred to as the “Bank”) toward the cost of the Project “Ukraine – Improving Power System Resilience for European Power Grid Integration (Installation of Hybrid Systems for Electricity Production in Ukrhydroenergo)” and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the Contract. Under this Contract, UHE intends to make payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

2. PJSC “Ukrhydroenergo” now invites eligible Bidders to submit Bids for the Contract. Bidders can bid for any one lot, more than one lot or all the four lots. The Time for Completion shall be between 420 and 510 calendar days from the Effective Date of the Contract. No credit will be given for early completion, and Bids offering a Time for Completion exceeding 510 days shall be rejected.

3. Prospective Bidders shall meet the following minimum qualification requirements:

(a) General Experience: Experience in activities related to the design, supply and installation of equipment for energy infrastructure facilities, including generating facilities, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and MV and HV grids, under contracts in the role of contractor, subcontractor, or management contractor since at least January 2020. Design and construction experience may be from different contracts.

(b) Financial Capabilities: The Bidder shall submit audited balance sheets or, if not required by the law of the Bidder’s country, other financial statements acceptable to UHE for the last five (5) fiscal years to demonstrate the current soundness of the Bidder’s financial position and its prospective long-term profitability.

(c) Average Annual Turnover:

The Bidder shall demonstrate a minimum average annual turnover for the last three (3) fiscal years as follows:

Lot 1 – USD 36 million;

Lot 2 – USD 51 million;

Lot 3 – USD 46 million;

Lot 4 – USD 20 million.

Bidders submitting Bids for multiple Lots shall meet the cumulative average annual turnover requirements applicable to those Lots.

The Bidder must demonstrate access to, or availability of, financial resources such as liquid assets, unencumbered real assets, lines of credit, and other financial means, other than any contractual advance payments, to meet the following minimum cash-flow requirements:

Lot 1 – USD 9 million;

Lot 2 – USD 13 million;

Lot 3 – USD 12 million;

Lot 4 – USD 5 million.

Bidders submitting Bids for multiple Lots shall meet the combined financial resources requirements applicable to those Lots.

(d) Specific Experience:

(i) The Bidder shall demonstrate participation as contractor, joint venture member, subcontractor, or management contractor in at least two (2) contracts since 01.01.2020, each of which has been successfully and fully completed and has a minimum power and energy capacity of at least:

Lot 1 – 35 MW / 35 MWh;

Lot 2 – 50 MW / 50 MWh;

Lot 3 – 48 MW / 48 MWh;

Lot 4 – 20 MW / 20 MWh.

Completion shall be based on obtaining of the Operational Acceptance Certificate, Commissioning Certificate, Taking Over Certificate, Commercial Operation Certificate, Facility Readiness Certificate, or equivalent documents demonstrating successful completion.

The similarity of the contracts shall be based on experience in the design, supply and installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems, either as a stand-alone facility or as part of a larger power project, including but not limited to a hybrid renewable energy project.

The referenced contracts shall demonstrate experience covering design, supply and installation of the relevant facility under the Bidder’s overall contractual responsibility.

A Bidder submitting Bids for more than one Lot shall meet the specific experience requirement for the largest individual Lot for which it is bidding. The experience related to design could have been met even through a specialized subcontractor.

(ii) For the contracts specified above and/or other relevant contracts, the Bidder shall demonstrate experience in, inter alia, the following activities:

A. For any Lot: at least one (1) successfully and fully completed contract involving the performance of/participation in an IEC 62443 Security Risk Assessment and implementation of Cyber Security concepts in accordance with IEC 62443-3-3, SL-2/3 level.

B. For Lots 1, 2 and 4: design, construction and commissioning of at least one (1) HV substation of at least 110 (150) kV class. New-build, refurbishment, rehabilitation, extension, reconstruction and modernization projects shall be acceptable.

C. For any Lot: design and construction of at least one (1) successfully and fully completed BESS project with a total installed capacity of at least 10 MW, with confirmed integration of the BESS into a power system operating in accordance with ENTSO-E requirements.

D. Design, with proof of positive state expertise, of at least one (1) project of the applicable consequences class in the field of industry or energy (production facilities; generation, distribution, transmission):

for Lots 2 and 3 – CC3;

for Lots 1 and 4 – CC2.

E. For any Lot: design in accordance with the requirements of Order No. 45 of the Ministry of Regional Development and Construction dated November 16, 2011, in the field of industry or energy (production facilities; generation, distribution, transmission) – at least one (1) project.

F. For Lot 4: design of projects involving connection to the Transmission System Operator (TSO) and/or Distribution System Operator networks – at least one (1) project.

These experience requirements listed under item (ii) may also be met through proposed specialized subcontractor(s).

Full and detailed qualification requirements, as well as additional information on the scope of the Contract and the technical, commercial and other requirements, are provided in the Bidding Document.

 

4. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (November 2020 edition) (Procurement Regulations) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

The procurement process will be conducted through the national electronic procurement system Prozorro, available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/, including authorized electronic marketplaces through which UHE and Bidders shall interact with the system. The RFB documents, amendments and clarifications will be published on the Prozorro website and on all authorized electronic marketplaces with free access at the following link: https://prozorro.gov.ua/uk/tender/UA-2026-09-15-013943-a

In order to submit the Bid and/or request clarifications, the Bidder shall register at one of the authorized electronic marketplaces of the Bidder’s choice in accordance with the terms and conditions of the selected marketplace.

5. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the Bidding Document. The weight assigned to the Rated Criteria (technical and non-price factors) is: 50% (fifty percent); the weight assigned to the Cost factors is: 50% (fifty percent). 

[NOTE: Due to Prozorro system limitations the weight assigned to the Cost factors is shown as 100% (hundred percent), which should be ignored. For details, refer to the Bidding Documents.]

The Rated Criteria include:

()  Cyber security and supply chain risks management approach;

() Availability of a technical support center to provide technical support related to the maintenance and repair of the key equipment;

() Organization of Construction and Installation Works Under Wartime Conditions; and

(iv) Implementation of sustainable development and environmental responsibility policies.

6. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain additional information from the Bidding Document published at the link provided above. Requests for clarification shall be submitted by the Bidder no later than 14 days before the deadline for submission of Bids specified in the electronic procurement system. Prospective Bidders are invited to attend the pre-Bid meeting, which will be organized by UHE in the format of a video conference. Detailed information about the date, time and registration is provided in the Bidding Document.

7. Bids shall be submitted by uploading the complete Bid through the electronic procurement system before the Bid submission deadline, which is 16:00 (Kyiv time) on November 12, 2026. After the deadline, Bidders will not be able to submit Bids and this option will be automatically closed by the system. Further details on the electronic Bid submission process are provided in the Bidding Document.

8. A Bid Security shall not be required. Each Bid shall be accompanied by a Bid-Securing Declaration using the form provided in the Bidding Document.

9. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring UHE to disclose information on the successful Bidder’s beneficial ownership in the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form included in the Bidding Document.

MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND SOCIAL PROTECTION

STATE DEPARTMENT FOR SOCIAL PROTECTION & SENIOR CITIZEN AFFAIRS

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES-INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION-IC)

 

Country                            : Kenya

Name of Project              : Second Kenya Social and Economic Inclusion Project (KSEIP-

   2)

Credit No                         : IDA-78450-KE

Project ID No                  : P504218

Assignment Title            : Individual Technical Consultant for Enhanced Single Registry and Community Development MISs 

Reference No                  : KE-SDSP-555513-CS-INDV

  1. The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received funding from the World Bank towards the cost of Second Kenya Social and Economic Inclusion Project (KSEIP -2), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for consulting services. The Program has three key result areas;
    1. Building human capital of children and adolescents  aiming to expand social protection to vulnerable Kenyans during childhood and adolescence through scaling up the existing Nutrition Improvement through Cash and Health Education (NICHE) program, which targets malnutrition among poor households with pregnant or lactating women or children under age three, as well as increasing educational attainment and preventing teenage pregnancy among poor and vulnerable adolescents;
    2.   Building Climate and Economic Resilience of Adults   by supporting working-age adults from poor households to emerge from poverty, save for the future, and gradually become self-sufficient by scaling up the existing Economic Inclusion Program (EIP) from five up to twenty- counties, and providing additional support to a subset of EIP beneficiaries to adopt climate resilient livelihoods and linking EIP graduates to contributory social insurance schemes; and
    3.  Advancing Systems and Strengthening Adaptive Social Protection  by supporting enhancements to systemwide reforms to increase the overall efficiency, impact, and climate-shock responsiveness of SP programs and delivery platforms
  2. The objective of this assignment is to provide specialized full-stack software development support to the National Social Protection Secretariat (NSPS) under the State Department for Social Protection and Senior Citizen Affairs (SDSP&SCA), Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MLSP), in enhancing and modernizing the Enhanced Single Registry (ESR AND CDMIS) system. The consultant will be responsible for improving both the front-end and back-end components of the ESR AND CDMIS platform, strengthening its integration with other national databases and systems (including CCTP MIS, CDMIS, NICHE MIS, AdoP MIS,  IPRS, NRB, CRS, CPF, NSSF, SHA among others), and enabling dynamic, secure, and efficient data exchange among stakeholders.
  3. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs,3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Procurement Regulations of September 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  4.  The State Department For Social Protection & Senior Citizen Affairs now invites eligible individual consultants to submit Expressions of interest for consideration. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to provide the services. The short listing criteria will be as indicated in the TORs.
  5. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers.
  6. Interested Individual Consultants may obtain further information at the address below from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours EAT) and public holidays.
  7. The terms of reference are available on The Public Procurement Information Portal https://tenders.go.ke, and the State Department For Social Protection & Senior Citizen Affairs Website https://www.socialprotection.go.ke/
  8. Interested Individual Consultants should submit their expression of interest, which must be delivered in a written form and must be accompanied with copies of CVs and copies of relevant documents and testimonials/recommendations (copies of Academic and Professional Qualifications and Registration/Licensing Certificates) in plain sealed envelope clearly marked: Individual Technical Consultant for Enhanced Single Registry And Community Development MISs  Reference No.  KE-SDSP-555513-CS-INDV and addressed (in person, or by e-mail) to;
    • The Principal Secretary,
    • State Department For Social Protection & Senior Citizen Affairs
    • P.O. Box 30478-00100 Nairobi.
    • Attention: HEAD SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT SERVICES
    •  E-mail: Scm@socialprotection.go.ke
  9. The Expression of Interest shall be delivered using one of the following modalities;
    • Deposit in the Tender Box located on   14th floor, NSSF Building, Block A, Eastern Wing, Kenya.
    • Send via email to; Scm@socialprotection.go.ke
  10. Deadline for submission of Expression of Interest is 7th  October,2026  at 1100 hours East African time. Note: Late submissions will not be accepted.

UNITÉ DE GESTION DU PROJET

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

N°0124/E/2/AMI/MINHDU/SG/PVGFD/REAF/RPM/RPMJC2/2026 DU 11 SEPTEMBRE 2026

Pays :                      Cameroun

Projet :                     Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durable (PVGFD)

Financement :          Crédit IDA A-7793 et B-7794-CM

Titre de la mission :  Recrutement d’une maîtrise d’œuvre privée pour la digitalisation des services, procédures et produits domaniaux, cadastraux, fonciers et patrimoniaux.

N° de référence :      CM-MINHDU-561022-CS-QCBS du Plan de Passation de Marchés approuvé du 23 juillet 2026

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Cameroun a obtenu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), pour couvrir le coût du Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durable (PVGFD) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de Consultants pour le recrutement d’une maîtrise d’œuvre privée pour la digitalisation des services, procédures et produits domaniaux, cadastraux, fonciers et patrimoniaux.

 

  1. Les services de consultants comprennent entre autres le contrôle et surveillance du déroulement de toutes les étapes et la qualité des prestations et livrables produits par le prestataire chargé de la digitalisation des services, procédures et produits domaniaux, cadastraux, fonciers et patrimoniaux pour le compte du Ministère des Domaines, du Cadastre et des Affaires Foncières. Ces services comprennent les missions suivantes :
  • Appuyer / conseiller le MINDCAF dans les stratégies et préconisations en vue de la bonne exécution des activités ;
  • Proposer un plan de contrôle de la qualité basé sur les spécifications techniques et prescriptions du contrat ;
  • Examiner la méthodologie globale au début dudit projet ;
  • Contrôler les travaux de terrain ;
  • Valider chaque étape du projet et faire le contrôle qualité des différents livrables produits par le prestataire ;
  • Examiner les rapports d’étapes et livrables produits par le prestataire ;
  • Contrôler toutes les étapes de la réalisation de chacune des composantes ci-dessous citées pour qu’elles correspondent aux exigences du cahier de charges soumis au prestataire.

 

Les prestations techniques attendues par ces services de maîtrise d’œuvre privée sont regroupées en trois (03) principales composantes qui interagissent entre elles ; à savoir :

 

  • Composante 1 : Conception, fourniture et installation d’un système d’information foncière (SIF) à Yaoundé et à Douala ;
  • Audit technique : examen des infrastructures, logiciels, hébergement, cybersécurité ;
  • Audit fonctionnel : revue des processus de collecte, traitement et mise à jour des données, ainsi que les flux d’information ;
  • Vérification sur site : inspection de guichets fonciers, entrevues avec les agents ;
  • Analyse juridique : conformité aux lois foncières, gestion des droits et conflits ;
  • Analyse de la gouvernance et des responsabilités des acteurs du secteur foncier et domanial ;
  • Evaluation de l’interopérabilité avec les autres systèmes indiqués dans le cahier de charges du prestataire ;
  • Appui aux réformes : propositions de mise à jour du cadre législatif et réglementaire, organisationnel et opérationnel.

 

  • Composante 2 : Numérisation des archives cadastrales et foncières de Yaoundé et Douala
  1. Audit du processus de numérisation
  2. Contrôle de la qualité des données converties
  3. Audit de la sécurité et de la traçabilité
  4. Revue documentaire et organisationnelle
  • Composante 3 : Mise en place de deux (02) stations GNSS permanentes ou stations CORS.
  1. Audit technique de la station GNSS
  1. Audit du centre de diffusion et contrôle
  1. Examen des protocoles et procédures
  1. Revue documentaire et organisationnelle
  2. Essais de performance

Les Termes de Référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

  1. La durée de cette prestation est de trente-sept (37) mois à compter de la date indiquée sur l’ordre de service de commencer les prestations.

 

  1. Le Ministre de l’Habitat et du Développement Urbain, invite les firmes de consultants (ci-après désignés Consultants) à manifester leur intérêt pour la réalisation des présentes prestations. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdites prestations (brochures, description de missions semblables, expérience dans des conditions similaires, disponibilité des compétences parmi le personnel, …).

N.B. : Bien vouloir justifier par les pages de garde et de signature du contrat, ainsi que les attestations de bonne fin ou tout autre document attestant que le contrat a été exécuté dans de bonnes conditions. La liste détaillée des références, faisant ressortir pour chacune, l'intitulé de la mission, l'année de réalisation, les dates de début et de fin de mission, le montant des travaux supervisés et le commanditaire.

Les critères de présélection sont les suivants :

 

  • Justifier d'une expérience dans le domaine de la mise en œuvre et/ou suivi de l’implémentation des systèmes d’information foncière (SIF) ou géographique (SIG), de conversion des données et numérisation des documents, ainsi que des stations GNSS permanentes d’au moins cinq (05) ans ;
  • - Avoir réalisé, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, au moins trois (03) projets similaires, couvrant collectivement les composantes suivantes : (i) SIF/SIG, (ii) numérisation/gestion électronique de document (GED), (iii) stations permanentes/CORS. Une expérience intégrant plusieurs de ces composantes au sein d'un même projet, ainsi qu'une expérience en Afrique, seront considérées comme des atouts ;
  • Avoir une expérience antérieure sur des projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d'autres institutions financières internationales constituera un atout.

 

  1. Il est porté à l'attention des consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.15, 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d'intérêt ») sont applicables et disponibles sur le site web de la Banque à l’adresse : www.worldbank.org.

 

  1. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement solidaire ou d’un accord de sous-traitant.
  2. De plus, le Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement sus-décrit.

 

  1. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires aux heures ouvrables entre 08 heures à 17 heure, heure locale et à l’adresse ci-dessous :

 

Unité de Gestion du Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durables,

3ème étage sis Immeuble OKTOPUS, à la Rue Frédéric Foe, quartier hippodrome, Montée Anne Rouge à Yaoundé, E-mail : pvgfd.minhdu@gmail.com, ou envoyés par e-mail aux consultants intéressés, à leur demande.

 

  1. Les dossiers de candidature, rédigés en français doivent parvenir / être déposés soit en version numérique en formats PDF & Word par courrier électronique, soit en version physique accompagnée de la version numérique sur clé USB en format PDF & Word en six (06) exemplaires dont un (01) original et cinq (05) copies, à l’adresse ci-dessus, au plus tard 06 OCTOBRE 2026, à quinze (15) heures, heure locale. Elles doivent être transmises avec la mention :

 

« APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UNE MAITRISE D’ŒUVRE PRIVEE POUR LA DIGITALISATION DES SERVICES, PROCEDURES ET PRODUITS DOMANIAUX, CADASTRAUX, FONCIERS ET PATRIMONIAUX ».

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – FIRMS SELECTION)

Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery (REPAIR) Program Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA)

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.: TF0C5097-3E

Assignment Title: Third-Party Monitoring Agent (TPMA) for the REPAIR Program - Framework Agreement

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MZ-REPAIR-549332-CS-QBS

ARC Ltd, acting on behalf of the participating countries, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery (REPAIR) Program, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") consist of engaging one or more Third-Party Monitoring Agent(s) (TPMA) to: (i) verify that funds disbursed under REPAIR's Regional Climate Risk Fund (RCRF) financial instruments, following an eligible shock activation, are used by Delivery Channels for their intended purposes and reach targeted beneficiaries, in compliance with the REPAIR Governance Framework; (ii) confirm compliance of the activities implemented by Delivery Channels with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework and applicable national regulations; (iii) evaluate the impact of the response on selected beneficiaries; and (iv) document lessons learned and recommendations to strengthen future REPAIR activations. Services will be delivered across up to eight participating countries (Mozambique, Madagascar, Comoros, Burundi, Angola, Malawi, Zambia, and Seychelles) under a Framework Agreement with an initial term of two years and renewable based on performance. During the framework term, the selected Firm(s) will submit technical and financial proposals in response to country-specific call-off orders issued following individual REPAIR activations.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

ARC Ltd now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

1. Internationally recognized expertise in financial auditing of public institutions and in environmental and social (E&S) monitoring and auditing, evidenced by recognized professional certifications in auditing and financial management and demonstrated fluency in applicable international or national auditing standards.

2. At least 10 years of proven experience in financial management, E&S monitoring, and operational auditing in Sub-Saharan Africa, including in contexts of fragility and crisis response, with a minimum of two completed Third-Party Monitoring Agent (or equivalent third-party monitoring) assignments. Experience in disaster response will be considered a competitive advantage.

3. Demonstrated organizational capacity to deliver assignments across all eight REPAIR countries (Mozambique, Madagascar, Comoros, Burundi, Angola, Malawi, Zambia, and Seychelles); consortia of firms are encouraged to apply to achieve the required geographic coverage.

4. Demonstrated ability to mobilize experts fluent in English, French, and Portuguese across all REPAIR countries. This is a mandatory requirement; single firms or consortia that cannot collectively demonstrate full trilingual operational capacity will not be considered for the Framework Agreement.

5. Demonstrated knowledge of the World Bank's fiduciary and environmental and social frameworks, evidenced by at least one completed assignment under a World Bank- or donor-financed project within the last seven years.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, first published in July 2016 and revised in September 2025, Seventh Edition ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For the purposes of this assignment, a conflict of interest exists where a firm, consortium member, or any of their proposed key personnel has a financial, contractual, institutional, or other relationship - whether current or recent - that could affect, or be reasonably perceived to affect, their ability to carry out this assignment with full independence, objectivity, and impartiality. This includes any ongoing or recent engagement with the Ministries of Finance and Planning, delivery channel operators, project contractors, or other entities directly involved in the implementation of the REPAIR Program in any of the eight participating countries.

Interested firms are requested to identify and disclose, as part of their Expression of Interest submission, any actual or potential conflict of interest relevant to this assignment and to indicate how such conflict has been or could be mitigated.

Any undisclosed conflict of interest identified at any stage may result in disqualification

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained by sending an inquiry to the following e-mail address: procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int.

Expressions of interest must be submitted by e-mail to procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int no later than the 05th of October 2026 at17h00 hours (South Africa time). The e-mail subject line should clearly state: "MZ-REPAIR-549332-CS-QBS – Third-Party Monitoring Agent (TPMA) for the REPAIR Program – Framework Agreement".
