República de Moçambique 

Ministério da Saúde

Direcção de Planificação e Cooperação

Programa de Revitalização dos Serviços Distritais e Comunitários de Saúde (PREDICOS) – P179913

ANÚNCIO DE VAGA: Assistente de Procurement

1. Introcução
O Governo de Moçambique, através do Ministério da Saúde (MISAU), recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para a implementação do Programa de Revitalização dos Serviços Distritais e Comunitários de Saúde em Moçambique (PREDICOS). No âmbito da implementação deste programa, o MISAU pretende contratar um Assistente de Procurement para reforçar a equipa de aquisições da Unidade de Gestão e Execução das Aquisições (UGEA) central.


2. Objectivo
O Assistente de Procurement terá como principal responsabilidade apoiar a equipa de especialistas em aquisições em todo o ciclo do processo de contratação desde o início até à
 onclusão, assegurando a observância dos princípios de relação custo-benefício, adequação ao propósito, economia, eficiência, transparência, igualdade e legalidade. A função exige o estrito cumprimento do Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (IPF), 5.ª Edição de Setembro de 2023.


3. Tarefas

  • Realizar actividades de procurement de bens, serviços, obras públicas e consultorias do MISAU, com especial enfoque nos projectos financiados pelo Banco Mundial;
  •  Apoiar na preparação e actualização dos Planos de Procurement a nível central e provincial;
  • Inserir e actualizar as actividades no sistema STEP do Banco Mundial;
  • Rever toda a documentação de procurement sujeita a revisão prévia do Banco Mundial antes do envio para Não Objecção;
  • Prestar apoio técnico aos técnicos de aquisições a nível central e nas Direcções Provinciais de Saúde (DPS);
  • Trabalhar em estreita colaboração com todas as partes envolvidas no projecto, incluindo os distritos abrangidos;
  • Apoiar na gestão e consolidação da base de dados de fornecedores;
  • Elaborar relatórios trimestrais de progresso e planos de acção;
  • Apoiar na gestão dos bens e equipamentos adquiridos, promovendo o uso racional de recursos;
  • Participar nas auditorias dos projectos do Banco Mundial;
  • Participar nas reuniões regulares da Unidade de Coordenação do Projecto.

4. Qualificações e Experiência Exigidas

  • Licenciatura em Procurement, Engenharia, Logística, Gestão, Administração ou áreas afins.
  • Mínimo de três (3) anos de experiência profissional relevante na área de aquisições;
  • Pelo menos um (1) ano de experiência em projectos financiados pelo Banco Mundial ou outras instituições multilaterais;
  • Experiência de trabalho em instituições do Estado, preferencialmente no sector da saúde é uma vantagem;
  • Experiência em contratação baseada na legislação nacional é uma vantagem.
  • Português: fluente (obrigatório); Inglês: capacidade de comunicação (vantagem).

5. Duração do Contrato
O contrato inicial terá a duração de um (01) ano e poderá ser renovado anualmente por igual período. A renovação dependerá de uma avaliação anual positiva de desempenho.


6. Conflicto de Interesse
A atenção dos Consultores interessados é chamada para a Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do Regulamento de Contratação para Mutuários do IPF do Banco Mundial, de julho de 2016 estabelecendo a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.


7. Submissão
As expressões de interesse devem ser entregues, por escrito e em envelope fechado,  nas instalações do Ministério da Saúde, no Departamento de Aquisições (DA), sito na Av. Eduardo Mondlane, n.º 1008, R/C, até o dia 02 de Outubro de 2026 as 15h00.

THE REVOLUTIONARY GOVERNMENT OF ZANZIBAR

MINISTRY OF BLUE ECONONMY AND FISHERIES

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Country: United Republic of Tanzania.

Name of project: Tanzania scaling up sustainable marine fisheries and aquaculture management (TASFAM) project (p.179969).

Assignment tittle: Consultancy services for Development of temporarily reallocation plans (TRP) for construction of Kizimkazi and Wete fish landing sites.

REF. NO: TZ-MBEF-561760-CS-CDS

This request for expression of interests follows the General Procurement Notice for the Tanzania scaling up sustainable marine fisheries and aquaculture management (TASFAM) project which appeared in the UN Development Business Online on 5th June 2025.

The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar through the United Republic of Tanzania has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Tanzania Scaling up Sustainable Marine Fisheries and Aquaculture Management (TASFAM) Project and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing to cover eligible payments under the contract for consultancy services for Development of temporarily reallocation plans (TRP) for construction of Kizimkazi and Wete fish landing sites.

The objective of the assignment is prepare a comprehensive, ESS5-compliant Temporary Relocation Plan for both Kizimkazi Mkunguni and Wete Selemu that provides a clear, time-bound, and adequately resourced framework for managing the temporary displacement of all affected persons during the construction period.

The consultant shall conduct several activities as stated in the TOR’s.

The assignment shall be carried out for a period of three (3) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be obtained through a project website https://tasfam.blueeconomysmz.go.tz.  

The Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries Zanzibar now invites eligible consulting firms to submit their expression of interest in providing these services.  Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications, relevant experience and key experts to perform the services. The qualification and shortlisting criteria shall include: -

  1. General experience of the firm, at least 15 years’ experience in consultancy
  2. Specific experience:                                   
  •  Minimum of three assignments over the last five years in costing and pricing models, financial feasibility analysis, cost-benefit analysis, participatory market assessment, benefit-sharing models, governance practices, need assessments, and market operations.                                  
  • The firm should have conducted at least two feasibilities relating to the establishment of fisheries facilities or operations. (Information to be provided should include name of assignment, name and full contact address of the client, contract value and period (dates) of execution of assignment.

PROJETO PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA - ASL

Acordo de Doação Nº TF - B6898 / Projeto Nº P158000

 

Aviso Específico de Licitação (AEL)

 

CONTRATAÇÃO DE SERVIÇO ESPECIALIZADO EM ELABORAÇÃO DE RELATÓRIO DE GESTÃO INSTITUCIONAL PARA O PROJETO ASL BRASIL

PROJETO PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZONIA – FASE 2

(DE-ASL2-POA3-MMA-2026-0017)

 

AEL0024/2026 - BR-FGV- 572837 -NC-RFQ

 

 

  1. DESCRIÇÃO DO OBJETO

Contratação de serviço técnico especializado em organização, sistematização, consolidação, revisão editorial, tratamento gráfico, editoração, diagramação, acessibilidade e preparação para publicação do Relatório intitulado Comunicado de Gestão Institucional da SBIO/MMA (Unidade de Coordenação do Projeto UCP), período 2023-2026.

 

 

  1. CONTEXTO

O Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil), que tem como objetivos ampliar e aperfeiçoar o gerenciamento de Unidades de Conservação estaduais e federais, aumentar a área sob recuperação da vegetação e incentivar o uso sustentável da floresta, e fortalecer as cadeias produtivas dos produtos da biodiversidade na Amazônia.

 

O projeto é gerido pelo Global Environment Facility (GEF), o ASL Brasil é parte do Programa Regional Amazon Sustainable Landscapes, que envolve oito países na fase 1, 2 e 3 Brasil, Colômbia, Peru, Bolívia, Equador, Guiana, Suriname e Venezuela. O Banco Mundial é a agência implementadora do programa, tendo como diretriz principal a visão integrada do bioma.

 

No Brasil, o Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA), por meio da Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBio), é a instituição coordenadora do projeto, responsável pela supervisão, articulação institucional e monitoramento da implementação. Assim como, Unidade Operativa do projeto responsável pela implementação de ações do projeto.

 

A Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO), do Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA), desempenha papel estratégico na formulação, coordenação e implementação de políticas públicas voltadas à conservação da biodiversidade, à gestão sustentável das florestas, à proteção da fauna e ao fortalecimento da governança ambiental no Brasil. Suas ações estão alinhadas aos instrumentos de planejamento governamental, aos compromissos nacionais e internacionais assumidos pelo País e às prioridades estabelecidas no âmbito do Ministério.

 

No período de 2023 a 2026, a SBIO vem conduzindo um conjunto de iniciativas voltadas à implementação de políticas, programas, projetos e instrumentos normativos que contribuem para a conservação da biodiversidade, a recuperação de ecossistemas, o fortalecimento da bioeconomia, a gestão territorial, a valorização dos povos e comunidades tradicionais e o cumprimento dos compromissos internacionais relacionados à Convenção sobre Diversidade Biológica (CDB), à Convenção-Quadro das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (UNFCCC), à Agenda 2030 para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável e à Convenção sobre a Conservação das Espécies Migratórias de Animais Silvestres (CMS).

 

Nesse contexto, torna-se necessária a elaboração de um Relatório intitulado Comunicado de Gestão Institucional da SBIO (2023–2026), com o objetivo de consolidar, sistematizar e apresentar, de forma integrada e acessível, os principais resultados alcançados pela Secretaria no período. O documento deverá constituir-se em um instrumento de comunicação institucional voltado à transparência, à prestação de contas e à divulgação das ações e dos impactos das políticas públicas implementadas pela SBIO, traduzindo informações técnicas em linguagem clara e acessível aos diferentes públicos.

 

A elaboração do comunicado deverá considerar a integração entre os principais instrumentos de planejamento, monitoramento e gestão governamental, incluindo o Plano Plurianual (PPA), os Acordos de Gestão Anuais, o Planejamento Estratégico do MMA, o Planejamento Estratégico da SBIO, os compromissos decorrentes das Conferências das Partes (COPs) e demais referenciais institucionais pertinentes. Como fontes de informação deverão ser utilizados os instrumentos normativos e estratégicos da Secretaria, relatórios técnicos dos departamentos, relatórios de execução de projetos e demais documentos institucionais relevantes.

 

Além da consolidação de indicadores e evidências quantitativas, o comunicado deverá apresentar, de forma clara e acessível, os resultados e informações institucionais definidos e validados pela SBIO/MMA. Para favorecer a comunicação com os diferentes públicos, deverão ser empregados recursos editoriais e gráficos, como infográficos, mapas, quadros, tabelas, linhas do tempo, fotografias e demais elementos visuais, elaborados a partir dos dados e conteúdos disponibilizados pela Secretaria.

 

Considerando o volume de informações a serem organizadas e a necessidade de tratamento editorial e gráfico, revisão, tradução, diagramação, acessibilidade e preparação do material para publicação, faz-se necessária a contratação de empresa especializada para executar esses serviços. A definição do conteúdo técnico, das fontes, das mensagens institucionais, dos resultados a destacar e a validação das informações permanecerão sob responsabilidade da SBIO/MMA.

 

  1. UNIDADE DEMANDANTE

A unidade de execução do projeto demandante desta contratação é a Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV). Esta aquisição está vinculada à estratégia de fortalecimento da comunicação institucional do Projeto ASL Brasil e enquadra-se nas atividades de divulgação e sensibilização.

A unidade operativa demandante desta aquisição é a Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO), do Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA).

 

  1. ESPECIFICAÇÕES

 

OBJETO DO SERVIÇO:

O serviço especializado tem por objetivo organizar, sistematizar, consolidar e apresentar as informações referentes à gestão da Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO/MMA), no período de 2023 a 2026, com base nos dados, documentos, conteúdos, fontes e orientações disponibilizados ou indicados pela SBIO/MMA. O trabalho compreenderá a organização e estruturação das informações conforme modelo e diretrizes definidos pela Secretaria; transposição e consolidação de dados; elaboração de gráficos, tabelas, mapas, infográficos, linhas do tempo e demais recursos visuais; adequação e revisão editorial dos textos fornecidos; tradução; editoração; diagramação; acessibilidade; incorporação dos ajustes solicitados; e preparação dos arquivos finais para publicação. O conteúdo técnico e a validação das informações serão de responsabilidade da SBIO/MMA. Como resultado, deverá ser entregue o “Comunicado de Gestão Institucional da SBIO/MMA (2023–2026)”, revisado, diagramado e finalizado para divulgação institucional em meio digital.

 

ATIVIDADES A SEREM DESENVOLVIDAS

O fornecedor deverá desenvolver as atividades descritas a seguir, de forma integrada e em articulação com a equipe técnica da Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO/MMA):

Reuniões

  • Participar de reuniões de alinhamento com a equipe da SBIO/MMA para recebimento de orientações, acompanhamento do cronograma e dos fluxos de trabalho, apresentação das versões produzidas e registro dos ajustes solicitados;

Organização e sistematização de informações

  • Receber, organizar, classificar e sistematizar as informações secundárias necessárias à elaboração do relatório, a partir de fontes oficiais, bases de dados e documentos institucionais, incluindo, entre outros, a Estratégia e Plano de Ação Nacionais para a Biodiversidade (EPANB), o Plano Nacional de Recuperação da Vegetação Nativa (PLANAVEG), as listas nacionais de espécies ameaçadas, relatórios técnicos dos departamentos da SBIO, relatórios de execução de projetos, instrumentos normativos, documentos estratégicos, bases de dados oficiais e demais materiais pertinentes ao período de referência;

Sistematização das informações

  • Sistematizar e consolidar os dados e as informações secundárias, organizando-os de acordo com a estrutura e as correlações com os instrumentos de planejamento e gestão institucional previamente indicadas pela SBIO/MMA, incluindo o Plano Plurianual (PPA), os Acordos de Gestão, o Planejamento Estratégico do MMA e da SBIO, bem como os compromissos, metas e agendas nacionais e internacionais pertinentes às áreas de atuação da Secretarial;

Adequação e formatação do conteúdo

  • Organizar e adequar editorialmente os conteúdos fornecidos pela SBIO/MMA, promovendo padronização, clareza e uniformidade de linguagem, sem alteração de seu conteúdo técnico;
  • Elaborar, a partir dos dados e conteúdos fornecidos ou validados pela SBIO/MMA, quadros, gráficos, mapas, infográficos, linhas do tempo e demais elementos visuais, incorporando os ajustes solicitados pela Secretaria;

Tradução

  • Traduzir para o português documentos ou informações em língua inglesa ou espanhola indicados pela SBIO/MMA para inserção no relatório;

Revisão textual

  • Realizar revisão ortográfica, gramatical, textual e de padronização editorial de todo o documento, promovendo os ajustes necessários de linguagem, coerência, referências, notas de rodapé, links, legendas e elementos gráficos, bem como incorporar as contribuições apresentadas pela equipe da SBIO;

Adequação para publicação

  • Preparar a versão final do relatório para publicação, observando os requisitos técnicos e editoriais estabelecidos pelo MMA, incluindo editoração, diagramação, adequação para publicação digital, acessibilidade, resolução de imagens, fechamento dos arquivos e entrega das versões editáveis em formato .docx ou compatível e versões finais em formato PDF para publicação institucional.

  1. Qualification of Consulting Firm

To effectively carry out the tasks for the consulting services, the consultancy firm should have gained experience at least five (5) years in the conduct of Feasibility Study on Aquaculture and Fisheries Infrastructure or related projects in the Philippines.

 

Further, the firm is preferably ISO 9001-2015 certified and should be able to field key professional personnel with adequate educational and technical background, experience and capability in the fields of port planning, engineering[1] [2] , economics, finance and management. Any changes or replacements of assigned personnel shall be subject to BFAR NPMO review and approval.

 

 

  1. Qualification of Key Staff

 

All the structures to be designed are located in a highly corrosive marine environment and the key staff are required to be knowledgeable of the impacts of marine corrosion on structures and equipment. The following are the minimum qualifications of key staff:

 

  1. Team Leader must be a licensed Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer or Civil Engineer with at least five (5) years as Team Leader in similar projects.
  2. Economists/Financial Specialist must be a degree holder in Economics/Business related courses with at least five (5) years as Economist/Financial Specialist in projects of similar nature.
  3. Planner/ Engineer must be a licensed Engineer/Architect with at least ten (5) years as Planner Engineer in projects of similar nature.
  4. Project Development Specialist must be a  degree holder in Management/Business with at least five (5) years as Project Development Specialist in projects of similar nature.
  5. Environmental Specialist must be a degree holder in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering and other related courses with at least  five (5) years in the position in projects of similar nature.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 as revised last February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

AUDIT DES CONVENTIONS PLURIANNUELLES DE MAITRISE D’OUVRAGE DELEGUEE (MOD) DE L’AGEROUTE AU COMPTE DU PROJET MALI NAFA SORO SIRAW (Mali-NSS-P507921/Crédit A 78130 -ML /Crédit B 78140 - ML).

 

Le Gouvernement du Mali a obtenu de la Banque mondiale deux crédits destinés au financement des activités du Projet Mali Nafa Soro Siraw (Mali-NSS). L’Unité Nationale de Coordination du Projet Mali Nafa Soro Siraw (Mali-NSS) a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des fonds pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif à l’audit des conventions pluriannuelles de maîtrise d’ouvrage déléguée (MOD) exécutées par l’AGEROUTE. Ces conventions concernent notamment les opérations pluriannuelles d’entretien routier et leur mise en œuvre avec les structures publiques concernées.

 

 

OBJECTIF GÉNÉRAL

 

L’objectif général de la mission est de réaliser un audit indépendant des conventions pluriannuelles de maîtrise d’ouvrage déléguée exécutées par l’AGEROUTE, afin d’évaluer leur gestion, leur conformité, leur performance et leur efficacité, et de formuler des recommandations visant à améliorer leur mise en œuvre.

 

 

OBJECTIFS SPÉCIFIQUES 

 

Les objectifs spécifiques de l’audit sont :

 

  1. examiner le cadre juridique et institutionnel des conventions et apprécier la conformité de leur mise en œuvre ;

 

  1. apprécier le respect des engagements contractuels des différentes parties et analyser les conditions d’exécution des conventions ;

 

  1. évaluer les performances techniques, financières et opérationnelles, ainsi que les dispositifs de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques ;

 

  1. identifier les insuffisances, risques et dysfonctionnements et proposer des mesures correctives ainsi qu’un plan d’amélioration.

 

L’Unité Nationale de Coordination du Projet invite les consultants (cabinets) à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les cabinets intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

 

 

LES CRITÈRES POUR L’ÉTABLISSEMENT DE LA LISTE RESTREINTE

 

  • être un Cabinet ou groupement de cabinets régulièrement constitué, disposant des capacités professionnelles et techniques nécessaires et justifiant d’au moins cinq (5) ans d’expérience générale dans l’audit de projets, programmes, conventions ou opérations du secteur des transports ;
  • disposer d’une (1) expérience avérée en audit technique, financier, institutionnel et de performance, notamment dans le domaine de l’entretien routier et des infrastructures de transport ;
  • avoir réalisé au moins cinq (5) missions similaires, dont des missions d’audit de conventions, contrats, projets ou programmes routiers ou d’infrastructures financés sur ressources publiques ou extérieures.

 

À ce titre, le consultant (cabinet) devra fournir les pièces à conviction y afférentes (attestation de service fait ou bonne fin d’exécution ; les pages de garde et de signature des contrats, ou tout document équivalent permettant de vérifier les références présentées).

 

 

DUREE ET LIEU DE CONSULTATION :

 

            La mission couvrira les travaux de préparation, de collecte et d’analyse documentaire, les travaux de terrain auprès de l’AGEROUTE et des parties prenantes concernées, les vérifications techniques, financières et institutionnelles, les restitutions et la production du rapport final.

 

 

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est estimée entre huit (08) et douze (12) semaines, incluant les travaux de terrain, les analyses, les restitutions et la finalisation du rapport définitif.

 

Les consultants seront classés par la justification et par ordre du plus grand nombre de marchés similaires réalisés.

 

La méthode de sélection est la sélection fondée sur les qualifications du consultant (SQC) conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale et aux dispositions du dossier de consultation.

Description du projet
L’Institut National de la Statistique des Études Économiques et Démographique (INSEED)
est le chef de file de la production, du traitement et de la diffusion de l’information
statistiques au niveau national. Cette activité est stipulée par l’article 24 de la Loi n°11-
003/AU du 26 mars 2011 portant organisation et règlementation des activités statistiques
aux Comores. L’INSEED a bénéficié des Fonds fiduciaire pour le renforcement des
capacités statistiques (TFSCB) de la Banque Mondiale en 2014-2015 et du projet « statistique
de Comores » financé par la Banque Mondiale pendant la période de 2017 à
2020. Ces projets ont apporté une multitude de résultats concrets répondant aux besoins
de Comores en matière de statistiques à l’instar de l’institutionnalisation de l’INSEED
(crée en 2014), de la quatrième édition du Recensement Général de la
Population et de l’Habitat (RGPH4), de l’Enquête Harmonisée des Conditions de Vies
de Ménages (EHCVM20), des nouveaux statisticiens agricoles et des cadres de l’INSEED
renforcés en formations ponctuelle. Afin de maintenir les acquis de ces projets
et d’améliorer davantage la capacité en statistique en Union de Comores, l’INSEED,
avec l’appui de la Banque Mondiale entame le projet d’investissement de soutien aux
capacités statistiques de la communauté de développement de l’Afrique australe.
Ainsi, l’INSEED souhaite recruter les membres de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet aux
postes suivantes : Responsable de Suivi et Évaluation; Responsable en Passation de
Marché; Responsable Administratif et Financier et Comptable

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET – AMI N°35/2026

 

PAYS : SENEGAL

PROJET : PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES A L’ELECTRICITE AU SENEGAL (PADAES)

Coût Financement Crédit/Prêt du Projet : 150 000 000 USD$

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT POUR LA REALISATION DES ETUDES APS, APD, POUR L’ELECTRIFICATION A MOINDRE COÛT DES LOCALITES DANS LE PERIMETRE DE SENELEC

 

N° Projet : P176620             

N° de Crédits IDA : 70470-SN et 8066-SN

N° de Référence PPM Banque Mondiale : 34-CONS-PADAES-2026

N° de Référence PPM SENELEC 2022 : C_PADAES_338

1. Cette sollicitation de manifestations d’intérêt (MI) fait suite à l’Avis Général de Passation des Marchés publié dans le système STEP de la Banque mondiale, puis dans United Nations Development Business (UNDB) Online, sous la référence publiée le 29 mars 2022, ainsi qu’à la publication nationale parue dans le quotidien Le Soleil N° 16668 des mercredi 24 et jeudi 25 décembre 2025.

2. L’État du Sénégal a reçu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des ressources de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat portant sur le :

« Recrutement d’un consultant pour la réalisation des études d’Avant-Projet Sommaire (APS), d’Avant-Projet Détaillé (APD), pour l’électrification à moindre coût des Localités situées dans le périmètre de SENELEC. »

3. OBJECTIF DE LA MISSION :

L’objectif global de la mission est de recruter un consultant chargé de réaliser l’étude de faisabilité de l’électrification des localités situées dans le périmètre de Senelec et éligibles à une électrification par extension du réseau moyenne tension.

 A cet effet, le consultant sera chargé de réaliser les prestations suivantes :

  • La réalisation des études techniques d’Avant-Projet Sommaire (APS) et d’Avant-Projet Détaillé (APD) ;
  • L’analyse économique et financière du projet ;
  • La réalisation des études environnementales et sociales (EIES/AEI), y compris l’élaboration des Plans de Réinstallation (PR), le cas échéant ;
  • L’élaboration du dossier d’appel d’offres (DAO) en vue de la réalisation des travaux.

De manière spécifique, il est attendu du consultant qu’il propose une méthodologie claire, cohérente et optimisée permettant la réalisation, à moindre coût, des études de faisabilité relatives à l’électrification des localités concernées, ainsi que l’élaboration du dossier d’appel d’offres.

Les objectifs spécifiques de la mission sont les suivants :

  • Déterminer, pour chaque localité, le tracé de raccordement optimal au réseau moyenne tension afin de minimiser les pertes techniques et d’optimiser les coûts d’investissement ;
  • Évaluer les investissements nécessaires à l’électrification de l’ensemble des clients potentiels situés dans la zone d’étude ;
  • Proposer un calendrier réaliste de mise en œuvre des travaux ;
  • Élaborer les instruments de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale (EIES, AEI et Plans de Réinstallation), sur la base des résultats du screening environnemental et social ;
  • Analyser les impacts environnementaux et sociaux potentiels du projet et proposer des mesures d’atténuation conformes à la réglementation nationale ainsi qu’aux exigences applicables de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Élaborer le dossier d’appel d’offres (DAO) destiné à la passation des marchés de travaux.

Le consultant devra mobiliser toutes les compétences, ressources humaines et moyens matériels nécessaires à la bonne exécution de la mission et à l’atteinte des objectifs fixés.

4. DESCRIPTION DU PROJET :

 

Pour soutenir l’ambition nationale d’atteindre l’accès universel à l’électricité d’ici 2029, la SENELEC, avec l’appui de ses partenaires au développement, a engagé des investissements stratégiques visant à moderniser et à étendre le réseau électrique national.

5. Qualification et Compétences du Consultant

                                                     

Le Consultant doit être un Cabinet ou Firme ou un Groupement et doit respecter les critères de préqualification ci-après :

                                      

  • Être un Consultant d’Etudes Techniques et Environnementales, intervenant dans le Secteur de l’Energie Electrique et de l’Environnement, avec une expérience avérée en électrification rurale, et détenir un agrément délivré par le Ministère de l’Environnement et de la Transition Ecologique du Sénégal pour la Réalisation d’Etudes Environnementales (en cas de Groupement au moins un des membres doit détenir cet agrément) ;
  • Disposer d’expérience d’au moins dix (10) ans dans le domaine de l’Electricité, et des Etudes Techniques des Réseaux de Distribution d’Electricité HTA et BT ;
  • Disposer d’une Expérience avérée dans la Conduite d’Etudes Environnementales et Sociales ;
  • Justifier avec des attestations de Bonne Exécution, la réalisation au cours des Quinze (15) dernières années (2010-2025) :
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Etude d’Avant-Projet Détaillée (APD) de taille similaire pour des Projets de Distribution d’Electricité HTA et BT;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Elaboration de Dossier d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) pour des Travaux de Réseaux de Distribution HTA et BT ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Evaluation Economique et Financière de Projet d’Electrification Rurale ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Evaluation Environnementale et Sociale de Projet(s) d’Electrification Rurale financé par un Partenaire Technique Financier (PTF) comme la Banque Mondiale, l’AFD, la BEI, l’UE, la KfW, la BAD, etc. ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins en matière d’Elaboration de PR suivant la Réglementation Nationale en vigueur et la NES 5 de la Banque Mondiale ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins dans les Pays de la Sous-Région, Francophone.

 

  • Le Consultant doit aussi : 

                                                                                              

  • Détenir une Licence et justifier de la capacité d’utilisation d’un Logiciel spécialisé SIG ;
  • Détenir une Licence et justifier de la capacité d’utilisation d’un Logiciel de Planification.

NB : Le Consultant doit fournir des Attestations de Bonne Exécution ou de Services Faits pour chaque expérience annoncée. Les Contrats signés ne remplacent pas les Attestations de Bonne Exécution ou de Services Faits.

 

6. DUREE DE LA MISSION :

 

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission du Consultant est de Quinze (15) mois à partir de son Entrée en Vigueur marquée par la Notification du Contrat immatriculé au Consultant par Senelec et un (01) mois pour l’Elaboration du Rapport de Consolidation.

 

7. Les Consultants (Cabinet ou Firme ou Groupement), seront sélectionnés selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Cout (SFQC). Les Critères d’Eligibilité, l’établissement de la liste restreinte et la procédure de sélection seront conformes aux Règlements de la Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) des éditions référenciées au-dessus (Juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Août 2018, Novembre 2020 et en Février 2025) », applicable au Projet et les dispositions de la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement, relatives aux Règles de la Banque Mondiale en matière de Conflit d’Intérêts sont applicables.

Les Consultants (Cabinet ou Firme ou un Groupement) intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations en transmettant une demande à l’adresse ci-dessous, tous les jours ouvrables de 07 H 30 mn à 16 H 30 mn : Direction Passation des Marchés Senelec, sise, au 19 rue Abdou Karim Bourgi x Wagane Diouf au 2ème étage de la Résidence Khoudia - Dakar, Sénégal. Adresse électronique : notificationcpm@senelec.sn.

The Government of Liberia has signed financing agreements with the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group for the implementation of the Excellence in Learning in Liberia (EXCEL) Project. The project is co-financed through a Grant from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and a concessional loan/credit from IDA.

 

The project will support the Government in implementing a defined strategy to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system in Liberia. To do this, the project will use a combination of investment project financing and results-based financing.

 

The project’s development objective (PDO) is to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system.

 

The EXCEL Project is a five-year initiative that aims to drastically reduce learning poverty by improving foundational literacy and numeracy for students in kindergarten 2 (KG-2) through Grade 6. This assignment will contribute to addressing these challenges by developing English Language Arts (ELA) Teaching and Learning Materials (TLMs) that align with the recently updated curriculum standards and the Global Proficiency Framework (GPF), ensuring that all outputs are pedagogically sound, culturally relevant, and foster mastery of core literacy skills.

  1. Project Origin

 

The Department of Agriculture (DA) is the government agency responsible for the promotion of agricultural development by providing the policy framework, public investments, and support services needed for domestic and export-oriented business enterprises. With support from the World Bank, the DA is implementing the Philippines Sustainable Agricultural Transformation (PSAT) Program. PSAT is a five-year program (July 2026 to December 2030) that aims to improve productivity, diversification, climate resilience, and public resource use efficiency in the agrifood systems in the Philippines.

 

The DA will implement the PSAT program that will support achievement of the agriculture and fisheries sectors’ development objectives by providing budgetary assistance for five (5) years to existing and new department programs. It will incentivize DA performance by linking funding support to the accomplishment of the set of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) and its corresponding Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs). The promised additional funding will compel and enable the agency to accelerate its programs to meet established targets and deliver on its commitments. 

 

The PSAT program is funded by the World Bank through a Program-for-Results Financing (PforR) Loan in the amount of One Billion US Dollars (1,000,000,000.00 USD). The PforR instrument is linked to the achievement of targets for a set of ten (10) DLIs and associated DLRs. There are a total of twenty (20) DLRs spread over five years. The disbursement will be contingent upon the 

DA endorsing to DOF an acceptable Results Verification Report (RVR) and the DOF subsequently furnishing the RVR to the World Bank as satisfactory evidence that the relevant Disbursement-Linked Results (DLRs) have been achieved and independently verified by the Independent Verification Agency (IVA). Therefore, verification of these results is an integral part of the Program given the nature of the instrument.

 

The purpose of this Terms of Reference (ToR) is to appoint an administratively, technically, and financially autonomous Independent Verification Agency (IVA) to undertake verification of the achievements of the DLRs. The appointed agency will verify the achievement of the DLRs as per the methods outlined in the ToR and submit the verification reports to the Project Management Office (PMO) and the World Bank.

 

The PSAT Loan Agreement signed with the World Bank on April 2026, and Project Appraisal Document (PAD) establishes a monitorable and verifiable Disbursement-Linked Indicator System, where the completion status of the pre-identified DLIs through verified DLRs is directly linked to loan disbursement. 

 

Therefore, the Project Management Office (PMO) intends to procure an Independent Verification Agency (IVA) to facilitate this aforementioned Disbursement-Linked Indicator System

 

  1. Program Result Areas

 

The PSAT activities are organized around three result areas that contribute to the achievement of the Program Development Objective of improving productivity, diversification, climate resilience and public resource use efficiency in the agrifood systems in the Philippines:

 

  • Result Area 1: Enhanced production and incomes in rice-based farming, supports climate-resilient and diverse rice-based farming by (a) improving the rice seed program by ensuring distribution of approved and registered rice varieties suited to local agro-climatic conditions; (b) increasing diversification of rice-based farming by integrating the government’s rice program with other commodity programs; (c) promoting mechanical direct seeding to lower labor costs, optimize seed use, and reduce GHG emissions; (d) implementing the use of IMC to improve the efficiency of fertilizer support; (e) fostering climate-smart agriculture through training and adoption of resilient technologies; and (f) increasing the intensity of available mechanization for rice-based farming; 

 

  • Result Area 2: Enhanced efficiency and resilience of food value chains, supporting climate-resilient, high-value crop production and enhancing post-harvest infrastructure to minimize food losses and improve marketable output through, among others: (a) increasing vegetable production using modern technologies such as tissue culture, climate-resilient screen-houses, and rain shelters; (b) expanding cold storage and promoting green technology adoption, including modular storage designs for broader private sector uptake; and (c) facilitating agricultural exports by upgrading food safety and plant quarantine laboratories and providing certification for agricultural exports; and

 

  • Result Area 3: Enhanced institutional delivery and performance, strengthening institutional frameworks and systems to support a competitive agri-food economy by, among others: (a) improving budgetary processes to enhance programmatic and results-based public expenditure; (b) establishing and operationalizing a data Command Center for integrating, storing, and analyzing datasets across DA agencies, enabling data-driven decision-making and climate disaster response; and (c) optimizing DA procurement systems to improve efficiency, shorten bid evaluation and award timelines, and promote environmentally sustainable “green procurement” practices.


 

  1. Objective of the Assignment 

 

The objectives of this consultancy assignment are to:

 

  1. Conduct an independent verification of the achievement of DLRs  under the PSAT Program, based on the Verification Protocol agreed between the Government of the Philippines and the World Bank; and 

 

  1. Prepare and submit to DA comprehensive Results Verification Reports (RVRs), in form and substance acceptable to the DA and the World Bank, documenting the achievement of the DLRs and providing the evidence required to support withdrawal applications. Upon acceptance by the DA, the RVRs shall be endorsed by the DA to the Department of Finance (DOF) for submission to the World Bank as part of the requirements for loan disbursement. 

 

These reports will be reviewed by the DA. Subsequently, the DA will submit to the DOF an acceptable RVR for the World Bank’s review as part of the requirements for processing PSAT Loan disbursements.

 

  1. Scope of Work

 

The Procurement of the Independent Verification Agent will follow the World Bank Procurement Guidelines harmonized with the Philippines’ domestic consulting service procurement guidelines and approach through a Quality Based Selection (QBS). 

 

The World Bank's Project Appraisal Document (PAD) and Loan Agreement (LA) for PSAT outlines the following DLIs and DLRs with its relevant Loan Disbursement schedule (See Annex A).

 

The independent verification agency must use the PAD and LA as the primary references to ensure the method of verification of the DLIs and DLRs as well as ensuring that the conduct of monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of the project are in line with the Project Design and the Verification Protocols. 

 

The verification agency shall verify the accomplishment of the above-mentioned DLR Items. Verification will take place against a verification framework and frequency, described in detail in the Verification Protocol (See Annex B).

 

The detailed scope of work of the Independent Verification Agency (IVA) will cover the following:

 

  1. Submission of an Inception Report for the PSAT and TASAT PMO’s review and approval. This report shall include a DLI and DLR verification plan, which shall be approved by the PSAT and TASAT PMO and shall accomplish the following: 

 

  1. Establish the evaluation framework and detailed methodology for assessing the baselines and results against DLRs, which includes the sampling design, data collection instruments, primary and secondary information sources, and verification methods;

 

  1. Prepare DLI/DLR Verification Procedures and On-site Verification Plans, field operations and processing manuals, interview or survey plan,  questionnaires and other analogous methods or instruments for Verification; and

 

  1. Conduct a workshop on the proposed Verification Procedures, On-site Verification Plans and related documents of the Verification Agent which must be in line with that provided by the World Bank. Such protocols must consider all inputs from all relevant offices for each DLI/DLR.

 

  1. Carry out the Independent Verification of DLIs and DLRs, which involves but is not limited to the following tasks: 

 

  1. Implement the approved Disbursement-Linked Indicator Verification Plan and conduct verification in a timely manner. Any additions or changes to the verification plan will require prior approval in writing by the DA and the World Bank;

 

  1. Generate and provide  empirical, statistically robust and qualitative/ anecdotal evidence to the DA as Verified Accomplishment of the pre-identified DLIs and DLRs for PSAT;

 

  1. Pre-test data collection instruments especially those requiring large-scale data collection conducted over multiple time periods;  

 

  1. Implement the Verification Procedures and On-site Verification Plans. This includes conducting field data collection visits to farms, farming households, offices of relevant government institutions and the private sector as well as any stakeholder deemed appropriate and necessary. The visits will be conducted in coordination with the PSAT-TASAT PMO to complement desk reviews and will include spot checks and interviews with government officials, beneficiaries and end-users;

 

  1. Hire the needed dedicated personnel, consultants, Contract of Service (COS) Workers, Statistical Researchers, and Processors to be available during the entire period of the verification process and analysis/ reporting;

 

  1. Coordinate closely with the PSAT-TASAT PMO and conduct regular consultation meetings based on agreed outputs and timetable of activities, or as needed. The timetable of activities as provided in a latter section of this TOR;

 

  1. Strictly follow the timetable of activities in the delivery of outputs and revisions thereto;

 

  1. Comply with any changes provided by the DA in relation to the timeline of activities;

 

  1. Report to the DA the occurrence of any event or condition that might delay or prevent the completion of the survey or the services following the schedule, indicating the steps that are being undertaken to rectify the situation; and

 

  1. Comply with any comments of the DA in relation to the outputs provided in this Section of the TOR.


 

  1. Data Management and Analysis Systems. The IVA shall design and set up the back-end data processing systems (simple and robust) to host field data. A secure database system storing primary data collected for analysis and reporting will be shared with the PSAT PMO. This system must be in line and in compatible with the PMO’s Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework and system

 

  1. Process Documentation. Prepare detailed documentation of all evaluation processes to ensure transparency and accountability to be shared with the DA and other stakeholders.

 

  1. Submit Verification Reports documenting the DA’s implementation of program interventions resulting in the achievement of DLIs and DLRs. The report must be written in English and should include: summaries of verification activities undertaken to check the accuracy of results data, supporting documents, verified baselines and results of all DLIs and DLRs, recommended disbursement levels for each DLI, summaries of major discrepancies accompanied by short explanations, and recommendations and analysis of progress for each DLI. 

 

These reports must include the work conducted, data sources and analysis, verification process and methods, assessment criteria, indicator achievement status, and conclusions.  

 

  1. Develop standardized verification mission templates for each DLR to be applied in every semi-annual verification cycle, detailing (i) the DLR description and measurement criteria (qualitative and/or quantitative), (ii) applicable verification targets for the relevant period, and (iii) the scope of activities covering pre-verification, verification, and post-verification stages; and

 

  1. Assist the DA, PSAT-TASAT PMO and project stakeholders in understanding project progress and implementation effectiveness, identifying issues arising during execution, and providing a basis for adjustments to DLIs and DLRs.

DLIs are the framework/ indicators and DLRs are the specific targets/achievements within that framework.

Background

The Government of Liberia has signed financing agreements with the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group for the implementation of the Excellence in Learning in Liberia (EXCEL) Project. The project is co-financed through a Grant from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and a concessional loan/credit from IDA.

 

The Project will support the Government in implementing a defined strategy to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system in Liberia. To do this, the project will use a combination of investment project financing (IPF) and results-based financing (RBF).

 

The project’s development objective (PDO) is to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system.

 

The EXCEL Project is a five-year project, supported by the World Bank and GPE, which aims to drastically reduce learning poverty by improving foundational literacy and numeracy for students in Kindergarten 2 (KG-2) through Grade 6. Current gaps include a severe shortage of high-quality textbooks and a lack of structured, evidence-based pedagogical tools, resulting in low proficiency levels. This assignment will contribute to addressing these challenges by developing English Language Arts (ELA) Teaching and Learning Materials (TLMs) that align with the recently updated curriculum standards and the Global Proficiency Framework (GPF), ensuring that all outputs are pedagogically sound, culturally relevant, and foster mastery of core literacy skills.

Prêt/Crédit : IDA 72690

Numéro de référence STEP : N° SN-MCTN-567507-CS-QCBS

 

1. La République du Sénégal a sollicité un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) d’un montant équivalent à cent cinquante millions (150 000 000) de US dollars en vue de financer le coût du Projet d’Accélération de l’Economie Numérique au Sénégal (PAENS) et se propose d’utiliser une partie les fonds de ce crédit pour financer les services suivants : « Etude des besoins en infrastructure technique de la Plateforme d’Interopérabilité Nationale du Sénégal (PINS) basée sur X-Road».

2. Les services (« Services ») consistent en la définition, sur des bases techniques, organisationnelles et budgétaires robustes des éléments suivants : l’architecture cible d’hébergement de la PINS, les environnements requis, les composants critiques à mettre en place, les exigences opérationnelles associées, ainsi que les prérequis d’interfaçage avec l’infrastructure nationale de confiance numérique, notamment la PKI-SN.

Plus spécifiquement le cabinet devra :

  • analyser l’environnement existant susceptible d’accueillir ou de supporter la PINS, en matière d’hébergement, de réseau, de sécurité, de supervision, de sauvegarde, de reprise d’activité et d’exploitation;
  • identifier les exigences fonctionnelles et non fonctionnelles induites par les cas d’usage prioritaires. Ces cas d’usage seront fournis par le MTN/SENUM ou, à défaut, identifiés et priorisés par le cabinet au démarrage de la mission ;
  • concevoir une architecture de référence selon une approche progressive de type « Start small & scale », en déployant un socle technique initial opérationnel, sécurisé, extensible et compatible avec les exigences de haute disponibilité, de supervision, de sauvegarde, de reprise d’activité et d’amélioration continue ;
  • préparer l’évolution vers une architecture nationale multisites, intégrant progressivement les data centers nationaux et sectoriels, tout en évitant une architecture surdimensionnée dès la phase initiale.

Les besoins spécifiques de mise en œuvre de la PKI sont traités dans l’activité y relative. La présente mission devra donc uniquement identifier les prérequis, dépendances, interfaces et exigences de confiance numérique nécessaires au bon fonctionnement de la PINS, sans financer ni dupliquer les activités propres au projet PKI national.

À ce titre, elle devra préciser les exigences d’intégration avec la PKI-SN, notamment la chaîne de confiance applicable, les certificats requis par X-Road, les mécanismes de validation de statut, les impacts éventuels sur la disponibilité de la plateforme et les mesures de mitigation associées, sans prescrire ni financer une PKI dédiée à la PINS.

3. Les termes de référence peuvent être consultés sur le site Web du MTN dans le lien suivant : https://www.mctn.sn/appels-d-offres-et-appels-a-candidatures. et dans le site du PAENS au lien https://paens.sn/manifestation-dinteret/;

4. Le MTN/PAENS invite les candidats intéressés à présenter leur candidature en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations : (i) l’expérience générale du cabinet ; (ii) l’expérience spécifique ; (iii) la réalisation de missions similaires (avec des attestations de service lisibles) ; (iv) les capacités techniques et managériales de la firme. Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à ce stade de la présélection mais appréciés.

Objet : RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET D’AUDIT EXTERNE INDEPENDANT-AUDIT DU PPA ET DES EXERCICES 2027,2028 ET 2029

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Gabonaise met en œuvre, avec l’appui financier de la Banque mondiale, le Projet d’Accès aux Services de Base et d’Amélioration des Performances (PASBAP). Ce projet vise à étendre et améliorer l’accès à l’eau potable, à l’assainissement et à l’électricité, en cohérence avec les priorités nationales de développement et dans la continuité du PASBMIR clôturé en 2023. Il comprend quatre composantes majeures : (i) l’amélioration de l’accès à l’eau et à l’assainissement, (ii) le renforcement de l’accès aux services énergétiques, (iii) l’amélioration de la gouvernance sectorielle, et (iv) la gestion du projet et le suivi-évaluation. La mise en œuvre opérationnelle est assurée par le Ministère de l’Accès Universel à l’Eau et à l’Énergie (MAUEE), en coordination avec les entités techniques concernées, sous la supervision d’une Unité de Gestion du Projet établie au sein de la CNTIPPEE.

Les services de consultant (« les Services ») comprennent le « RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET D’AUDIT EXTERNE INDEPENDANT-AUDIT DU PPA ET DES EXERCICES 2027,2028 ET 2029 ».

Les Termes de Référence (TdRs) sont disponibles à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.  

La Commission Nationale des Travaux d’Intérêt Public pour la Promotion de l’Entreprenariat et de l’Emploi (CN-TIPPEE) invite dès à présent les consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessous. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdits services (à travers une lettre de motivation adressée au Secrétaire Permanent).

Les critères de sélection sont les suivants :

Profil et qualifications de l’auditeur externe

Le consultant devra être un cabinet d’audit et d’expertise comptable indépendant, faisant profession habituelle de réviser les comptes, régulièrement inscrit au tableau d’un Ordre des Experts-Comptables reconnu sur le plan international par l’IFAC ou la FIDEF, ayant une expérience confirmée en audit financier de projets de développement et acceptable par la Banque mondiale.

À l’issue de la manifestation d’intérêt, un cabinet /une firme sera retenu (e) et consulté (e) à partir de la méthode de Sélection au Moindre Coût (SMC) et ce, conformément aux procédures définies dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI »

Background

The Government of Liberia has signed financing agreements with the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group for the implementation of the Excellence in Learning in Liberia (EXCEL) Project. The project is co-financed through a Grant from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and a concessional loan/credit from IDA.

 

The project will support the Government in implementing a defined strategy to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system in Liberia. To do this, the project will use a combination of investment project financing and results-based financing.

 

The project’s development objective (PDO) is to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system.

 

The EXCEL Project is a five-year initiative that aims to drastically reduce learning poverty by improving foundational literacy and numeracy for students in kindergarten 2 (KG-2) through Grade 6. Current gaps include a severe shortage of high-quality textbooks and a lack of structured, evidence-based pedagogical tools, resulting in low proficiency levels. This assignment will contribute to addressing these challenges by developing English Language Arts (ELA) Teaching and Learning Materials (TLMs) that align with the recently updated curriculum standards and the Global Proficiency Framework (GPF), ensuring that all outputs are pedagogically sound, culturally relevant, and foster mastery of core literacy skills.

Reporting Line

1. Introduction and Background

The Fiji Energy Transformation Project is proposed as a USD 230 million World Bank-supported initiative aimed at accelerating renewable energy, modernizing the power grid, and reforming the energy sector to attract private investment. Key interventions include large-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) parks of 50 MW or more each, grid evacuation infrastructure, transmission line upgrades, and modernization of existing power stations across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. The project’s environmental and social risks have been classified as Substantial under the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

A significant portion of land in the project area is held under customary iTaukei tenure and managed through the iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB). Many affected communities are iTaukei Fijians who qualify as Indigenous Peoples under ESS7. The project may also involve economic and physical displacement linked to land acquisition for solar parks, transmission lines, and associated infrastructure, triggering ESS5 on Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement.

The Social Officer will be embedded within the PPU and will work under the day-to-day supervision of the Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist, who has overall leadership of the project’s E&S function. The Social Officer will work in close coordination with the Environment Officer. Together, these positions constitute the project’s E&S team and are jointly responsible for delivering the suite of ESF instruments required for project appraisal and for supporting implementation thereafter.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the timely preparation of all social-related ESF instruments required for appraisal, ensure ongoing and meaningful stakeholder engagement throughout project preparation and implementation, and serve as the PPU’s primary liaison with government line ministries and agencies responsible for land, indigenous affairs, and social protection.

3. Scope of Work

3.1 Stakeholder Engagement and Community Liaison

a. Lead the preparation, implementation, and updating of the project’s Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), in close coordination with the E&S Specialist, who will review and finalize the instrument. The SEP must include:

  • A project-wide grievance redress mechanism (GRM), including a reporting structure for complaint escalation and resolution within specified timeframes.
  • A dedicated pathway for Sexual Exploitation and Abuse / Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) complaints, including resolution or escalation timeframes.
  • Differentiated engagement approaches for iTaukei communities, women, and other vulnerable groups.
  • A disclosure schedule compliant with ESF requirements.

b. Serve as the PPU’s primary point of contact for community-level consultations across project sites on Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. Coordinate field consultation logistics with the Environment Officer so that environmental and social consultations are sequenced and, where possible, combined to minimize the burden on communities.

c. Maintain a consultation log recording meetings, attendees disaggregated by gender and community role, issues raised, and follow-up actions. Share the log with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer on a fortnightly basis.

d. Ensure that Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes are properly documented for all iTaukei communities in the project’s area of influence, in accordance with ESS7 and applicable Fijian law.

3.2 Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF)

a. Lead the preparation of the Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF) in accordance with ESS7. The IPPF must:

  • Liaise with the EFL Lands Team to identify all iTaukei communities and landowning units (mataqali) in the project’s area of influence.
  • Set out a methodology for social assessment and FPIC at the site-specific level.
  • Define entitlements and culturally appropriate benefit-sharing mechanisms.
  • Establish culturally sensitive grievance and feedback channels.
  • Address gender dynamics and vulnerabilities within iTaukei communities.

b. Coordinate with the E&S Specialist to ensure consistency between the IPPF, the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and the SEP, so that the instruments present a coherent and non-contradictory framework for community engagement and entitlements.

c. Where site-specific Indigenous Peoples Plans (IPPs) are required, support their preparation in parallel with, or as a follow-on to, the IPPF.

3.3 Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF)

a. Support the E&S Specialist in preparing the RPF in accordance with ESS5. The Social Officer will be responsible for:

  • Conducting or supervising social baseline surveys required to inform the RPF.
  • Documenting existing land use, livelihoods, and community assets in project-affected areas.
  • Drafting the entitlement matrix in coordination with the E&S Specialist.
  • Ensuring that the RPF reflects the specificities of iTaukei land tenure and customary rights.

b. Coordinate with the Environment Officer to ensure that environmental footprint assessments underpinning the RPF, including site boundaries, buffer zones, and access routes, are accurate and consistently applied across instruments.

3.4 Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence

a. Support the E&S Specialist in preparing the Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report. The Social Officer will:

  • Coordinate with the EFL Lands Team and liaise with the TLTB and relevant landowning units (mataqali) to understand existing or proposed negotiated land agreements for solar park and transmission line sites.
  • Verify the voluntariness of negotiations and document indicators of undue pressure or inadequate community representation.
  • Identify gaps between existing agreements and ESF requirements and propose remediation measures.

3.5 Gender and Vulnerability

a. Integrate gender analysis into all social instruments, ensuring that the project identifies and responds to differential impacts on women, girls, and other vulnerable or marginalized groups.

b. Support the preparation of a Gender Action Plan or equivalent measures, in coordination with the E&S Specialist.

c. Identify and document vulnerable households in the project area, including elderly people, persons with disabilities, female-headed households, and households with insecure tenure, and ensure they are reflected in the RPF entitlement matrix and the IPPF.

3.6 Labor and Working Conditions - Social Dimensions

a. Contribute to the Labor Management Procedures (LMP) by preparing the social dimensions, including community hiring provisions, management of labor influx risks, SEA/SH and communicable disease risks in host communities, supply chain social due diligence requirements, and conflict resolution between workers and community members. The E&S Specialist retains overall responsibility for the LMP.

b. Coordinate with the Environment Officer on environmental health dimensions of labor influx, including waste, water, and camp management, to ensure that the LMP presents unified and internally consistent measures.

3.7 Coordination with Government Line Ministries and Agencies

The Social Officer will serve as the PPU’s primary liaison with the following entities on social matters:

  • Ministry of Lands and Mineral Resources: land acquisition procedures, state land matters, and coordination of required land surveys or valuations.
  • iTaukei Affairs Board / Ministry of iTaukei Affairs: customary governance, community protocols, and support for FPIC processes.
  • iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB): management of iTaukei land, negotiated agreements, lease arrangements, and consent from landowning units.
  • Department of Social Welfare / Ministry of Women, Children and Poverty Alleviation: identification of vulnerable households and gender considerations.
  • Any other relevant agency identified during preparation as having a mandate over affected communities or social protection matters.

The Social Officer will establish and maintain regular contact with focal points in each agency, keep records of correspondence and meetings, and report on ministry engagement to the E&S Specialist as part of the fortnightly joint E&S team update.

3.8 Capacity Building

a. Together with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer, contribute to the preparation of the TOR for EFL’s institutional Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS), specifically the social management components.

b. Provide on-the-job guidance to EFL staff engaged in community liaison activities during project preparation.

3.9 Reporting and Coordination

a. Prepare monthly progress reports on social preparation activities and submit them to the E&S Specialist for integration into the consolidated E&S team report to the PPU Project Manager.

b. Maintain a live Social Risk Register tracking identified social risks and mitigation measures, updated fortnightly and shared with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer.

c. Participate in the mandatory weekly joint E&S team meeting and the fortnightly joint risk register review.

d. Coordinate all field visits jointly with the Environment Officer and E&S Specialist. Where a visit has environmental and social dimensions, the Social Officer and Environment Officer will attend together wherever possible to minimize multiple visits and support integrated data collection.

e. Before submitting an instrument draft to the E&S Specialist, circulate it to the Environment Officer for a peer consistency check covering site boundaries, affected population figures, and mitigation commitments.

f. Support the E&S Specialist during World Bank supervision missions and technical reviews, including preparation of briefing materials and attendance at relevant meetings.

4. Methodology and Approach

The Social Officer will apply an integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approach throughout the assignment. The approach will include:

  • Desktop review of available project documents, land information, consultation records, and relevant social baseline information.
  • Field-based social assessment and community consultation across relevant project locations.
  • Culturally appropriate engagement with iTaukei communities and landowning units, including documentation of FPIC where required.
  • Coordination with the E&S Specialist, Environment Officer, EFL Lands Team, government agencies, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Preparation, review, updating, and consistency checking of social instruments and associated records.
  • Routine monitoring through consultation logs, the Social Risk Register, progress reports, and agreed coordination meetings.

5. Key Deliverables and Indicative Timing

All deliverables are subject to World Bank review and clearance. The primary target is project appraisal. Specific submission dates will be agreed with the E&S Specialist and PPU Project Manager upon commencement.

6. Assignment Duration and Work Programme

The position is expected to commence as soon as possible and will cover the full project preparation period through appraisal, with the possibility of extension into implementation. Upon commencement, the Social Officer will agree detailed submission dates, priorities, and an activity schedule with the E&S Specialist and PPU Project Manager. Regular field travel will be required.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

7.1 Education

  • A university degree in social sciences, anthropology, development studies, law, or a related field. A postgraduate degree is an advantage.

7.2 Professional Experience

  • A minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in social safeguards or social risk management on infrastructure or energy projects.
  • Demonstrated experience with World Bank ESF instruments, including ESS1, ESS2, ESS5, ESS7 and ESS10, or equivalent IFC Performance Standards.
  • Demonstrated experience working with Indigenous Peoples and customary land tenure systems in the Pacific or comparable contexts.
  • Experience liaising with government land administration agencies. Familiarity with Fiji’s iTaukei land tenure system and the role of the TLTB is a strong advantage.

7.3 Skills and Competencies

  • Strong facilitation and consultation skills, including experience conducting consultations with rural and indigenous communities.
  • Strong coordination, record-keeping, analytical, and report-writing skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary E&S and project preparation team.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of iTaukei Fijian or Fiji Hindi is an advantage.

8. Reporting and Working Arrangements

The Social Officer is a full-time position based at the PPU office, with regular field visits to project sites across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. The Social Officer reports to the E&S Specialist on a day-to-day basis and to the PPU Project Manager on overall project matters. The Social Officer will participate in the weekly joint E&S team meeting and the broader PPU team meeting.

9. Application Requirements

Interested candidates should submit a curriculum vitae and a cover letter describing their relevant experience in relation to the scope of work set out in this TOR. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

 

Submission

Further information can be obtained by emailing to tenders@efl.com.fj during office hours 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM (Fiji Time), Monday to Friday clear 3 days from the closing date of this EOI.

Expressions of interest must be uploaded to the EFL e-Tender Portal (TenderLink) at https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window), by registering your company, by 4:00 PM (1600 hrs) Fiji Time on Wednesday 5th October 2026.

Request for Quotations

Country: Ukraine

Name of Project: Center for Advancement in Restoration and Modernization Capacity Project

Contract Title:  Organization and Delivery of I_CAN Training Program Sessions No. 1–2 in Ivano-Frankivsk

Grant No.: TF0C4831

RFB Reference No.: NCS-RFQ-2.5-11

1.         The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association (the World Bank) and Kyiv School of Economics Institute (KSEI) have signed the Grant Agreement No. TF0C4831 dated May 7, 2024, in an amount not to exceed three million two hundred twelve thousand United States Dollars (USD 3,212,000) for the Project ‘Center for Advancement in Restoration and Modernization Capacity (CARMC)’ (hereinafter referred to as the I_CAN Project). The KSEI is the implementing entity for the Project. A portion of these funds is intended to cover expenditures under the contract for the financing of logistical support for event organization.

2.         The KSEI now invites Quotations from eligible Service providers for:

Organization and Delivery of I_CAN Training Program Sessions No. 1–2 in Ivano-Frankivsk:

The procurement is organized into a single lot, resulting in the award of one contract upon completion of the tender process.

Services shall be rendered during  November, 2026.

Planned events dates:

  • 05.10.2026 - 08.10.2026 - training No. 1 (Ivano-Frankivsk);
  • 06.10.2026 - 09.10.2026- training No. 2 (Ivano-Frankivsk);

The prospective Service providers shall meet the following Qualification Criteria:

Experience:

            - the Service provider must have experience in the execution of at least 1 (one) contract for the provision of comprehensive logistical support services for conferences, training sessions, or similar events within the last 3 (three) years, specifically since January 1, 2023;

- the Service provider must not be subject to ongoing bankruptcy proceedings and/or be in a state of insolvency as of the date of the price quotation submission, in accordance with the provisions of the legislation of Ukraine.

Evaluation will be conducted based on comparing price quotations received from Service providers.

Detailed information is described in the Request for Quotations (the Tender Documents).

3.         The tender will be conducted through national competitive procurement using a Request for Quotations (RFQ) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September, 2023) (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Service providers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

The KSE shall use the following electronic-procurement system to manage this Tender process:

“Electronic procurement system” or “e-procurement system” means national electronic procurement system “Prozorro” available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/, including authorized electronic procurement marketplaces.

The full list of authorized electronic marketplaces is available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/en/majdanchiki-prozorro.

In order to submit the Quotations and/or request clarifications, the Participants shall register at one of the authorized electronic marketplaces of Participant’s choice in accordance with terms and conditions of selected marketplace.

4.         The full set of Tender documents in Ukrainian, including addenda and clarifications thereof, if any, is published by the KSE at the website of electronic procurement system and will be available for free for downloading at the following link:

https://prozorro.gov.ua/tender/UA-2026-09-21-012442-a  

5.         Quotations must be submitted by uploading the complete tender documents through the electronic-procurement system before the quotations submission deadline which is 17:00 (Kyiv time) on September 30, 2026. After the deadline the participants will not be able to submit the quotations and this option will be closed by the system automatically.

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

***************

 

Nom du pays :

REPUBLIQUE CENTRAFRICAINE

Nom du projet :

Projet REGIONAL d’amélioration des corridors des transports routier et fluvial en afrique centrale

N° identification :

P 175235

Financement :

BANQUE MONDIALE

N° du Don IDA :

Don IDA E215-CF

Intitulé de la mission :

Recrutement d’un Cabinet pour la réalisation d’une étude de faisabilité technique, économique, environnementale et sociale de la mise en place d’une zone économique spéciale pilote à Boali en République Centrafricaine.

 

N° DE REFERENCE :

PRACAC – 68/SC/QC/26.

 

1. La République Centrafricaine a obtenu un Don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour couvrir le coût du Projet Régional d’Amélioration des Corridors des Transports Routier et Fluvial en Afrique Centrale (PRACAC) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des ressources pour financer les services d’un consultant firme pour « l’Etude de faisabilité technique, Economique, Environnementale et Sociale pour la mise en place d’une Zone Economique (ZES) Spéciale Pilote à Boali en République Centrafricaine ».

2.    Le Consultant aura pour mission de réaliser l’étude de faisabilité économique, environnementale et sociale pour la mise en place d’une Zone Economique Spéciale Pilote à Boali en République Centrafricaine. L’objectif de la mission vise à créer les conditions à la viabilisation de la zone économique spéciale de Boali en fournissant une analyse complète permettant de décider ou non de la mise en œuvre d’une ZES pilote.

3. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services. Les dossiers de candidature (20 à 30 pages maximum) comprendront les éléments essentiels suivants :

 

  1. Une brève description de l’entreprise expliquant l’activité principale et le nombre d’années d’existence du Cabinet en adéquation avec la mission proposée ;
  2. Qualifications professionnelles du Cabinet en matière d’audit externe ;
  3. Organisation technique et administrative de la firme (Organigramme) ;
  4. Compétences générales du Cabinet ainsi que le nombre de membres clés de son personnel.

 

4. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

 

  1. Démontré une expérience générale de 10 ans dans le domaine des études économiques, échanges commerciaux, développement des zones commerciales et de l ’aménagement du territoire,

 

  1.  Avoir réalisé au moins une (1) étude de faisabilité technique et économique pour la création d’une zone économique spéciale,

 

  1. Disposer du personnel requis pour la mission.

 

  1. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

a) Être un bureau d’études ayant au moins une expérience dans la conduite d’études similaires dans les cinq (05) dernières années en tant que bureau principal,

b) Être capable de mobiliser une équipe de professionnels disposant de qualifications appropriées et d’une solide expérience dans les domaines pertinents du transport urbain et de l’économie. 

  1. Il est porté à l’attention du consultant que les dispositions du paragraphe 3.23 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque Mondiale relatives aux règles de la Banque Mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêt sont applicables.

 

  1. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de qualification des consultants (SQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de « Passation des Marchés dans le cadre du financement des projets de développement « Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants ». La version courante du règlement susmentionné, 7ème édition de septembre 2025 est accessible au site Web de la Banque Mondiale sur http : //www.worldbank.org/procurement en cliquant sur « New Policy and Regulations ».

  Les cabinets intéressés peuvent s’associer avec d’autres pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement solidaire.  

  1.  Les cabinets intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures des bureaux de 9 heures à 15 heures et cliquez sur le lien suivant pour obtenir les Termes de Référence de la mission : www.puric-pracac.com  
  2.  Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées sous pli cacheté en trois (3) exemplaires physiques en personne ou par courrier express, au plus tard le 20 Octobre 2026 à 13 heures, heure locale à l’adresse suivante :

« Manifestation d’Intérêt – Recrutement d’un cabinet pour réaliser l’Etude de faisabilité technique, Economique, Environnementale et Sociale pour la mise en place d’une Zone Economique (ZES) Spéciale Pilote à Boali en République Centrafricaine »
