Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) en vue de financer le coût du financement additionnel de la deuxième phase du Projet d’Amélioration des Résultats Nutritionnels (PARN2) et se propose d’utiliser une partie du financement pour effectuer des paiements autorisés au titre du contrat d'un consultant individuel Responsable de la comptabilité qui est en charge de la mise en œuvre du projet.

 

  1. D’une manière générale, la mission du consultant a pour mission principale d’assurer le traitement des dossiers comptables, des opérations financières et la tenue à jour de la comptabilité générale et analytique du projet conformément aux procédures en vigueur et le réapprovisionnement régulier des comptes et de la disponibilité des données de reporting financiers sous la supervision du Responsable Financier. Il pilote l'ensemble du mécanisme comptable, de la trésorerie et de la gestion des immobilisations du projet PARN2-FA.

 

         Spécifiquement, il s’agit de :

  •   Assurer la tenue de la comptabilité informatisée et la production des états financiers et tableaux de bord du Projet.
  • Contrôler la conformité, l'éligibilité et le règlement rapide des dépenses après vérification des pièces justificatives.
  • Gérer la trésorerie (suivi des décaissements, demandes de paiement/retrait et réapprovisionnement des comptes auprès des banques primaires et de la Banque mondiale).
  • Assister et suivre l'exécution budgétaire au niveau de la Direction Nationale, des Offices Régionaux de Nutrition (ORN) et des ONG partenaires.
  • Assurer la gestion, l'inventaire semestriel et la mise à jour du fichier des immobilisations du projet.

Qualification académique :

 

  • Master en Gestion et Comptabilité.

 

 

 

 

 

Expériences :

 

Le consultant devra répondre au profil suivant :

 

  • Expériences réussies d’au moins 3 ans à un poste similaire sur les 5 dernières années.
  • Connaissance approfondie du PCG 2005, du PCOP 2006 et de la réglementation comptable et fiscale à Madagascar
  • Maîtrise des outils informatiques (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) et des logiciels de comptabilité de projet (la connaissance de TOMPRO est un atout).

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DEUX (2) SUPERVISEURS REGIONAUX DU FINANCEMENT ADDITIONNEL DU PROJET PARN II

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) en vue de financer le coût du financement additionnel de la deuxième phase du Projet d’Amélioration des Résultats Nutritionnels (PARN2) et se propose d’utiliser une partie du financement pour effectuer des paiements autorisés au titre du contrat de deux consultants individuels superviseurs régionaux qui sont en charge de la mise en œuvre du projet.

 

  1. D’une manière générale, la mission des consultants consiste à assurer le contrôle de conformité financière, le suivi budgétaire et la gestion du patrimoine du projet au niveau décentralisé. Il sert de garant pour l'utilisation efficace des fonds de la Banque mondiale en faisant le lien entre la Direction Nationale et les Offices Régionaux de Nutrition.

 

         Spécifiquement, il s’agit de :

  • Vérifier l’exactitude, l’existence, l’exhaustivité et le classement des dépenses documentées dans les Demandes de Réapprovisionnement de Fonds (DRF) envoyées par les ORN à la Direction Nationale.
  • Identifier les retards, anomalies et goulots d’étranglement budgétaires, comptables et financiers au niveau régional et proposer des mesures correctrices.
  • Veiller à l’existence, à la traçabilité et à la protection des immobilisations et matériels affectés aux ORN, ONG partenaires et sites communautaires.
  • Suivre la gestion et l’exécution administrative et financière des contrats des ONG partenaires, techniciens superviseurs (TS) et animateurs encadreurs (AE).
  • Contrôler la fiabilité des données servant à la souscription et au paiement régulier des motivations des agents communautaires via MVola.
  • Assurer le suivi documenté de la mise en œuvre des recommandations de la Direction nationale, des missions de supervision et des audits.

 

  1. Les termes de référence détaillées du poste peuvent être envoyés aux Consultants intéressés qui en font la demande à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous. Le nom et l’adresse du Consultant devront être clairement spécifiées dans la requête.

 

  1. L’Unité du Programme National de Nutrition Communautaire invite maintenant les Consultants individuels admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications et l'expérience appropriées pour cette fonction. Le dossier de candidature devra inclure une lettre de manifestation d'intérêt, un curriculum vitae détaillé présentant notamment les références du Consultant dans l'exécution de contrats similaires, ainsi que les copies des diplômes, le(s) numéro(s) de téléphone et l'adresse électronique.

 

  1. Le consultant devra répondre au profil ci-après :

 

Qualification académique :

    • Minimum Bac +4 en gestion ou économie ou dans un domaine apparenté

 

Expériences :

  • Une expérience pertinente d’au moins dix (10) ans dans le domaine de la finance et comptabilité ;
  • Expériences relevant de l’audit des projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds internationaux ;
  • Expériences relevant de la nutrition communautaire ;

      Qualités et atouts :

  • Expériences en audit des projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds internationaux ou dans les programmes de nutrition communautaire.
  • Bonne maîtrise des directives des bailleurs de fonds dans les procédures de décaissement.
  • Capacité à mener des formations d’adultes et esprit d'analyse/synthèse poussé.
  • Aisance relationnelle, aptitude au travail en équipe multidisciplinaire et capacité à effectuer des déplacements fréquents sur le terrain.

Projet : Projet d’appui au renforcement des filets sociaux pour le développement humain au Maroc

Numéro du Projet : P507373

Financement : Banque mondiale

Référence STEP : MA-ANSS-564536-CS-QCBS

Approche de marché : Ouverte internationale

  1. Objet et aperçu de la mission

Le Royaume du Maroc a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour le Projet d'appui au renforcement des filets sociaux pour le développement humain au Maroc, dont l’objectif est de renforcer l’efficacité du système de protection sociale.

Dans le cadre de sa composante 3, consacrée au soutien de l’évolution de l’Aide Sociale Directe (ASD) par le biais d’innovations et d’une approche fondée sur des données probantes, l’Agence Nationale du Soutien Social (ANSS) souhaite réaliser une évaluation des premiers effets observés des nouvelles mesures d’accompagnement prévues par la loi n° 41.26 modifiant et complétant la loi n° 58-23 relative au régime des ASD.

Les prestations consistent à accompagner l’ANSS dans la conception et la mise en œuvre d’une évaluation des premiers effets observés des mesures d’accompagnement prévues par la loi susmentionnée n° 41.26. Elles comprennent notamment l’élaboration du cadre méthodologique de l’évaluation, la conception et la réalisation d’une enquête quantitative auprès des bénéficiaires du programme ASD, l’analyse des effets déclarés de ces mesures sur les comportements des bénéficiaires vis-à-vis de l’emploi formel, ainsi que la formulation de recommandations opérationnelles visant à améliorer leur mise en œuvre.

Les termes de référence détaillés de la mission sont disponibles sur le site internet de l’ANSS à l’adresse suivante : https://anss.gov.ma/fr/appels-offres.

  1. Méthode de sélection

Le cabinet ou le groupement de cabinets sera sélectionné selon la méthode de sélection fondée sur la qualité et le coût, conformément au Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI).

  1. Obtention des termes de référence et demandes d’éclaircissements

Les termes de référence (TDR) complets ainsi que leurs annexes sont téléchargeables sur le site internet de l’ANSS à l’adresse suivante : https://anss.gov.ma/fr/appels-offres.

Les demandes d’éclaircissements doivent être adressées par écrit à marches@anss.ma, au plus tard le 05 octobre 2026 en indiquant en objet la référence MA-ANSS-564536-CS-QCBS.

Les réponses aux demandes d’éclaircissements ainsi que les éventuels additifs seront publiés sur le même lien de téléchargement du dossier de consultation, conformément aux dispositions applicables.

  1. Composition du dossier de manifestation d’intérêt

Le dossier de manifestation d’intérêt comprend :

(i)  La lettre de manifestation d’intérêt, signée par une personne dûment habilitée, établie selon le modèle annexé à la présente demande ;

  6.  La convention constitutive du groupement ou, lorsque celui-ci n’est pas encore constitué, une lettre d’intention de constituer le groupement, signée par les représentants habilités de tous les membres. Ce document doit préciser :

Projet d'Amélioration de l'Accès à l'Eau Potable et à l'Assainissement à Kinshasa

« PAAEPA » P513301

Recrutement d’un consultant (firme) chargé du contrôle et de la surveillance des travaux de construction d’un nouveau système de captage d’eau brute sur le fleuve Congo pour l’usine de N’djili de capacité 440 000 m³/jour, d’achèvement et réhabilitation de trois (03) modules de traitement d’eau potable de l’usine de N’djili de capacité globale de 330 000 m³/jour et de construction du module 4 de traitement d’eau potable de l’usine de N’djili à Kinshasa de capacité de 110 000 m³/jour.

AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

N° 01/ZR-CEP-O-572233-CS-QCBS/PAAEPA/2026

Date de publication : 23 septembre 2026

Date limite de réception des candidatures : 23 octobre 2026

Le Gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo, avec l’appui de l’Association internationale de développement (IDA) du Groupe de la Banque mondiale et d’autres partenaires techniques et financiers, a sollicité un financement pour la mise en œuvre du Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès à l’Eau Potable et à l’Assainissement à Kinshasa (PAAEPA) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement afin d’effectuer des paiements au titre du marché de recrutement d’un consultant (firme) chargé du contrôle et de la surveillance des travaux de construction d’un nouveau système de captage d’eau brute sur le fleuve Congo pour l’usine de N’djili de capacité 440 000 m³/jour, d’achèvement et réhabilitation de trois (3) modules de traitement d’eau potable de l’usine de N’djili de capacité globale de 330 000 m³/jour et de construction du module 4 de traitement d’eau potable de l’usine de N’djili à Kinshasa de capacité de 110 000 m³/jour.

Au titre des services, objet de ce marché, le consultant devra réaliser les prestations suivantes :

Mission 1 – Vérification et approbation des documents de conception et d’exécution

Mission 2 – Suivi et contrôle des Travaux

Mission 3 – Assistance aux opérations de réception et de mise en service

Mission 4 – Coordination et suivi des plannings

Mission 5 – Assistance à la mise en œuvre du Plan de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale du chantier (PGES-E) et du Plan d’Hygiène et sécurité du chantier (PHS)

Les Termes de Reference (TDR) sont joints à cette demande de manifestation d'intérêt de la mission ou peuvent être trouvés sur le site Web suivant : https://www.cepordc.cd/.

La Cellule d’Exécution des Projets-Eau (CEP-O) invite les Consultants (Firmes) admissibles à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les prestations énoncées ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations.

Les prestations attendues seront assurées par un Consultant (Firme) ayant de l’expérience pertinente dans la surveillance et le contrôle des travaux de construction des systèmes complets d’alimentation en eau potable en milieu urbain. Cette expérience sera justifiée par au moins deux (02) références similaires durant les dix dernières années comme indiqué ci-dessous :

  1. Deux références des systèmes complets d’AEP partant de la prise d’eau de surfaces jusqu’au niveau du refoulement eau traitée :

La description de la référence devra porter sur les travaux de réhabilitation et/ou de construction :

  • D’ouvrages de prise d’eau brute de surface, implantés en milieu fluvial, lacustre ou maritime, d’une capacité minimale de 110 000 m³/jour ;
  • De stations de pompage d’eau brute d’une capacité minimale de 110 000 m³/jour ;
  • De conduites d’adduction d’eau brute d’un diamètre supérieur ou égal à 1 000 mm ;
  • De ponts spéciaux avec piles fixées sous eaux et des routes-digues présentant une hauteur de remblai supérieure ou égale à 6,00 m ;
  • D’usines de traitement d’eau potable d’une capacité minimale de 110 000 m³/jour ;
  • De réservoirs d’eau potable en béton armé d’une capacité minimale de 5 000 m³.

Ou encore

  1. Deux références pour chaque partie du système d’AEP dont toutes les parties regroupées devront former des systèmes complets d’AEP comme repris au point (i) ci-dessus. Les parties du système peuvent se présenter de deux ou trois manières ou autres selon les cas et devront comprendre :
  • 1ère partie : Travaux de réhabilitation et/ou construction :
  • D’ouvrages de prise d’eau brute de surface, implantés en milieu fluvial, lacustre ou maritime, d’une capacité minimale de 110 000 m³/jour ;
  • De stations de pompage d’eau brute d’une capacité minimale de 110 000 m³/jour ;
  • De conduites d’adduction d’eau brute d’un diamètre supérieur ou égal à 1 000 mm.
  • 2ème partie : Travaux de réhabilitation et/ou construction :
  • D’usines de traitement d’eau potable d’une capacité minimale de 110 000 m³/jour ;
  • De réservoirs d’eau potable en béton armé d’une capacité minimale de 5 000 m³.
  • 3ème partie : Travaux de réhabilitation et/ou construction :
  • De ponts spéciaux avec piles fixées sous eaux et des routes-digues présentant une hauteur de remblai supérieure ou égale à 6,00 m.

NB :

  • Une expérience similaire en Afrique subsaharienne serait un atout.
  • L’expérience du consultant dans la supervision des travaux de construction de barrage hydroélectrique de grande puissance serait un atout.

Les candidats peuvent s'associer avec d'autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d'un groupement solidaire ou d'un accord de sous-traitant. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’il est sélectionné.

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions de la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) (juillet 2016, révisée septembre 2025) « Règlements de Passation des marchés »), relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables.

Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de sélection basée sur la qualité et le coût (SFQC). Les critères d’éligibilité, l’établissement de la liste restreinte et la procédure de sélection seront conformes aux « Règlements de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) ((juillet 2016, révisée en septembre 2025) « Règlements de Passation des marchés » et les « Lignes Directrices »  de la Banque mondiale sur la Prévention et la Lutte contre la Fraude et la Corruption dans les projets financés sur les Prêts de la BIRD, et les crédits et les subventions de l’IDA (datant du 1er juillet 2016), ainsi que les dispositions stipulées dans l’Accord de financement applicables au projet

Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être envoyées par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par courrier ou par e-mail) au plus tard le vendredi 23 octobre 2026.

GOMBE STATE GOVERNMENT

SUSTAINABLE POWER AND IRRIGATION FOR NIGERIA (SPIN) PROJECT

Gombe State Project Implementation Unit (SPIU)

IDA Credit No: IDA76370

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE PREPARATION OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT (ESIA) AND A RESETTLEMENT ACTION PLAN (RAP) FOR THE REHABILITATION OF BALANGA DAM IRRIGATION SCHEME AND ASSOCIATED DAM INFRASTRUCTURE, BALANGA LGA, GOMBE STATE

Reference No.: NG-GOMBE SPIN-556295-CS-CQS        Method: CQS

Date of Issue: 25th September, 2026        Closing Date: 9th October, 2026

The Federal Government of Nigeria has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project. The Gombe State Government, through the Gombe State SPIN Project Implementation Unit (SPIU), is implementing the Project in the State and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and a Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for the rehabilitation of the Balanga Dam Irrigation Scheme and associated dam infrastructure in Balanga Local Government Area, Gombe State.

1. Background

Balanga Dam (9°54′22″N, 11°32′09″E) is an earthfill dam (72.6 × 10 m³ storage; 40 m high; 180 m crest) built in 1982–1985 on the River Balanga, a tributary of the Gongola River. The scheme has a design command area of 4,000 ha (about 2,200 ha developed under Phase I and 1,800 ha planned under Phase II) within an irrigation potential of about 11,000 ha. The proposed Design and Build works include rehabilitation of the dam embankment, spillway, intake and outlet works; about 22 km of main canal, 35 km of secondary and 96 km of feeder canals; about 220 km of drains; two night storage reservoirs; about 56 km of inspection roads; land development, infield drainage, flood control and ancillary works.

2. Objectives and Scope of the Assignment

The consultancy comprises two (2) assignments:

S/N

Assignment

1

Preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for the Rehabilitation of Balanga Dam Irrigation Scheme and Associated Dam Infrastructure, Balanga LGA, Gombe State

2

EAST AFRICAN COMMUNITY

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

Project Name: Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR)

Project ID: P176371

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Development of Animated Video Content with Infographics, Data Visualizations and Voice-over Narration for EAC Online Statistics Learning Materials

Reference No.: TZ-EAC-564358-CS-CQS

1. BACKGROUND

The East African Community (EAC) Secretariat is implementing the EAC component of the Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR), with financing from the World Bank. The Program seeks to strengthen the production, harmonization, dissemination, and use of quality economic and social statistics in Eastern Africa.

Under EARSPforR, the EAC Secretariat has developed online learning materials in fourteen priority statistical domains for use by Partner State institutions and other data users. Although technically sound, many of the materials are text-heavy and rely on static presentations and manuals, which can limit learner engagement, accessibility, and understanding, particularly among non-specialist audiences.

The Secretariat intends to engage a qualified consulting firm to develop new multimedia content where explanation gaps exist and to transform selected approved learning materials into concise animated videos. The videos will incorporate infographics, accurate data visualizations, professional voice-over narration, captions, and transcripts, and will be suitable for the EAC Learning Management System, websites, and mobile access.

The assignment will be completed within a maximum of ten weeks from contract commencement. The principal deliverables will include an inception report and production plan; scripts, storyboards, and visual style; a pilot video; a complete draft video package; and final master, LMS/mobile, caption, transcript, thumbnail, editable-source-file, asset/licence, and completion-report packages.

The detailed Terms of Reference for the assignment can be accessed at www.eac.int under Procurement/Consultancies.

2. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

The EAC Secretariat now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the assignment.

Interested firms should demonstrate:

  • at least five years of experience in animation, motion graphics, audiovisual production, instructional design, or digital learning content development;
  • successful completion of at least three comparable assignments involving conversion of technical, policy, research, statistical, or learning content into multimedia products;
  • demonstrated capacity in animation, data visualization, professional voice-over production, captions and transcripts, accessibility, quality assurance, copyright and licensing compliance, and delivery of multi-video assignments;
  • adequate technical and managerial capacity, including appropriate production workflows, software/equipment access, review controls, and capacity to complete the assignment within ten weeks; and
  • experience with regional organizations, governments, National Statistical Offices, development partners, or training institutions. East African or comparable multi-country experience will be an advantage.

3. SHORTLISTING CRITERIA

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis against the following criteria:

  • Legal status and eligibility: The Consultant must be a legally constituted entity and provide evidence of registration and eligibility.
  • Core business and general experience: At least five years of demonstrated experience in animation, motion graphics, audiovisual production, instructional design, or digital learning content development.
  • Relevant comparable assignments: Evidence of at least three successfully completed assignments of similar nature and complexity involving technical, policy, research, statistical, or learning content transformed into multimedia products.
  • Specialized technical capability: Team Composition and Expertise- Do not provide the CVs of the staff. Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The firm must demonstrate access to qualified key experts. Demonstrated capability in animation, instructional design, infographics, data visualization, professional voice-over, captions/transcripts, accessibility, audiovisual quality assurance, editable-source-file handover, and copyright/licensing management.
  • Regional or institutional experience: Experience with regional organizations, governments, National Statistical Offices, development partners, or training institutions. Experience in East Africa or a comparable multi-country environment will be an advantage.
  • Technical and managerial capacity: Evidence of an adequate organizational structure, production workflow, internal quality controls, software and equipment access, and capacity to deliver a multi-video assignment within the required period.

Consultants should submit a company profile and supporting evidence for the above criteria, including descriptions of relevant assignments, client names and contact details, contract dates, assignment values where available, the Consultant’s role, and links to or samples of comparable work.

4. CONFLICT OF INTEREST

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

5. ASSOCIATIONS

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected. Therefore, each member of the JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria. The experience, technical capability, and managerial capability of the sub-consultant shall not be evaluated to enhance the qualification of the lead firm or JV. Consultants shall not use the Affiliate Member's managerial, technical, or experience capabilities to enhance their qualifications.

6. SELECTION METHOD

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

7. SUBMISSION OF EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Expressions of Interest must be prepared in English and clearly marked:

“Expression of Interest for Consultancy Services for Development of Animated Video Content and Voice-over Narration for EAC Online Statistics Learning Materials - Reference No. [insert reference]”

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTANCY SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Assignment Title: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR UNDERTAKING ROAD SAFETY AUDIT OF THE PROPOSED MAPUTO METROPOLITAN AREA URBAN MOBILITY PROJECT (MMAUMP)

 

Reference No.: 105/CONS/MMAUMP/26

  1.  INTRODUCTION

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) is inviting Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified and experienced Consultancy Firms to provide “Consultancy Services Undertaking Road Safety Audit of the Proposed Maputo Metropolitan Area Urban Mobility Project (MMAUMP)”. The EOI will lead to a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the below-mentioned Consultancy Services package from the short-listed Consultants.

 

  1.  BACKGROUND

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Maputo Metropolitan Area Urban Mobility Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake independent Road Safety Audits of the proposed BRT system at key stages of project development, implementation, and operation to identify existing and potential road safety risks and recommend practical measures to eliminate or mitigate those risks, with particular emphasis on preventing fatal and serious injuries.

The consulting services (the Services) include, but not limited to assess, identify and evaluate road safety risks associated with: station access and egress, pedestrian crossing facilities, sidewalks along BRT corridors, grade-separated pedestrian facilities, speed management, depot and terminal operations, operational safety, traffic signal operation, safe System performance.

 

  1. SCOPE OF SERVICES 

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics now invites eligible consulting firms (Consultants) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 The consulting firm that is to be selected shall have its core business and experience as consultancy in design and supervision in the urban highway-roads, supervision of mass transit transport infrastructure being an advantage. Must be an officially registered consulting firm on its country of origin. The short-listing criteria will be as follows:

(i)Core Business: experience as consultancy in road safety audits, over the last 10 years; (ii)experience in project supervision consulting in the field of mass urban transport (Metro, Tramway, BRT, bus, etc.) in PPP or not, over the last 10 years; (iii) provide information necessary for the execution of the services, providing the conditions for the Audit Consultant to fulfill the contract; (iv) experience over the last 10 years in technical consulting missions relating to projects in the field of road safety and urban mass transport (Metro, Tramway, BRT, bus, etc.); (v) provide information necessary for compliance with environmental and social standards, over the last 10 years;

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The Consultancy will have a duration of 30 months, from the effectiveness day of the assignment.

 Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. Any party to the association, either joint venture member’s or sub-contractor’s experience will count on the qualifications criteria. In the case of a Joint Venture (JV), the Consultant shall specify the lead partner and all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14 to 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on Conflict of Interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Only shortlisted Consultants will be approached directly by Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) to submit proposals for the services required in the RFP phase.

AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

N° 140/ZR-CEP-O-545773-CS-CQS/PASEA/2026

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a reçu un appui de l'Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) du Groupe de la Banque mondiale, pour mettre en œuvre le Programme d’Accès aux Services d’Eau et d’Assainissement en RDC, « PASEA » en sigle, et le Projet d’Accès, de Gouvernance et de Réforme des secteurs de l’Electricité et de l’Eau, « AGREE » en sigle, et se propose d’utiliser une partie des fonds du PASEA pour financer les services suivants :  Conduite de deux enquêtes de référence (Baselines) sur l’Accès à l’Eau Potable dans les Provinces du Kasaï, Kasaï Central, Kasaï Oriental et Kwilu dans le Cadre des Projets PASEA et AGREE

 

Le présent avis d’appel public à manifestation d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis général de Passations des Marchés publié sur UNDB le 30 novembre 2022.

 

L’objectif général de ces deux études de référence est d’établir la situation initiale de l’accès à l’eau potable dans les villes, localités et ETD des provinces du Kasaï, Kasaï-Central, Kasaï-Oriental et Kwilu pour le Projet PASEA et dans la ville de Kananga pour le Projet AGREE afin d’évaluer les services existants et mesurer les écarts par rapport aux objectifs de l’ODD 6 relatifs à un accès universel et équitable à l’eau potable.

 

De manière spécifique, les études visent notamment à :

 

  • Mesurer le niveau actuel d’accès à l’eau potable dans les zones susmentionnées;
  • Apprécier les paramètres de la qualité de l’eau (paramètres microbiologiques et physico-chimiques) dans les zones concernées uniquement au niveau des infrastructures existantes (ASUREP, REGIDESO, PRISE et autres.);
  • Analyser la disponibilité (heures de service par jour) et la proximité (distance entre les ménages et les points d’eau principaux et secondaires);
  • Procéder à la cartographie des points d’eau existants (y compris des puits traditionnels, forages, etc.) ;
  • Mesurer le niveau de satisfaction actuel des répondants par rapport aux services existants ;
  • Identifier les zones les plus vulnérables pour prioriser les investissements ;
  • Procéder à l’analyse démographique et socio-économique des ménages (niveau de revenu, rôle des femmes et filles dans l’approvisionnement etc.);
  • Estimer les dotations moyennes journalières des ménages approvisionnés en toute sécurité (branchement particulier) ou bénéficiant d’un service de base (bornes fontaines).
  •  

Les Termes de Reference (TDR) sont joints à cette demande de manifestation d'intérêt de la mission ou peuvent être trouvés sur le site web suivant : https://www.cepordc.cd/.

Le Consultant (Firme) doit avoir un statut juridique reconnu par le Gouvernement de la RDC lui permettant de mener des enquêtes au niveau des villages et des ménages, des interventions en matière de développement. Une expérience dans la collecte de données sur la santé et le WASH en RDC est un atout majeur.

Plus spécifiquement, il s’agira de : 

  • Conseiller le Gouvernement du Bénin (GdB) pour que globalement les objectifs environnementaux, économiques et de sécurité visée par le projet en général et les autres instruments de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale (Evaluation environnementale et sociale Stratégique, Etude d’Impact Environnemental et Social, Plan d’Action de Réinstallation, Plan d’Urgence, Plan gestion de la biodiversité, Plan de gestion de la biomasse, etc.) en particulier soient atteints ;

  • Donner un avis sur le Dossier de Consultation des Entreprises (DCE) ainsi que sur les marchés des ouvrages y compris les questions relatives à la gestion des risques environnementaux;
  • Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le Panel Technique des barrages pour que les avis et recommandations donnés au Coordonnateur du projet par les experts soient en cohérence avec les exigences environnementales et transmis dans les délais.
  • Appuyer l’équipe du projet dans ses activités relatives aux aspects environnementaux dont entre autres :
  • donner au Coordonnateur du projet un avis d’expert indépendant sur les aspects environnementaux du projet, y compris la sécurité, et des recommandations pour que des synergies soient établies entre les aspects techniques, économiques et environnementaux du projet ;
  • donner des avis sur tous les documents environnementaux à produire dans le cadre de la préparation du projet et ce pour tous ouvrages et infrastructures retenues ;
  •  recommander des études complémentaires ;
  • donner un avis sur tous les termes de référence et les rapports de toutes les études (l’étude d’impact environnemental et social, l’étude d’impact cumulatif, l’étude de la gestion des forêts hors retenue, la gestion de la biomasse, la gestion des gaz à effet de serre, l’étude archéologique, l’étude faune aquatique, etc.) ;
  • donner un avis sur les coûts estimatifs et le planning de mise en œuvre des PGES ;
  • s’assurer que les clauses environnementales répondant aux standards nationaux et internationaux sont bien intégrées dans les dossiers d’appel d’offre des ouvrages ;
  • fournir l’appui nécessaire au Coordonnateur du projet pour que les recommandations environnementales soient correctement incorporées dans la documentation juridique et financière du projet ;
  • faire des recommandations pour garantir la bonne gestion des impacts environnementaux du projet pendant toutes ses phase, incluant notamment  la phase travaux ;
  • assister le Coordonnateur du projet lors des réunions avec les bailleurs de fonds ;
  • organiser des échanges avec les parties prenantes et des visites de terrain ;
  • préparer des rapports périodiques suivis des recommandations et des plans d’actions.

  • Mission d’élaboration de Plan de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale au cours des dix (10) dernières années (2016 à 2025) ou de l’année en cours sur un projet sur financement de la Banque mondiale : 10 points par mission pour un maximum de 20 points ;

Targeted Assessment and Amendment of Fiji's Electricity Act 2017 to Enable Private Sector Participation in Renewable Electricity Generation

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through the relevant implementing agency for the Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of project preparation and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise a targeted assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments to identify priority legal and regulatory barriers to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation, and to develop targeted, evidence-based amendments and complementary reform measures. The assignment will distinguish matters requiring amendment to the Act from those that may be addressed through subsidiary regulations, license conditions, regulatory decisions, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines, or improved implementation and enforcement.

 

The Services will cover:

  • An inception report setting out methodology, workplan, stakeholder consultation plan, information requirements, and delivery schedule.
  • A targeted legal, policy and regulatory assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments affecting Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, self-generators, energy storage providers, mini-grid operators, and other private renewable electricity participants.
  • A Legal Issues and Barriers Matrix identifying relevant provisions, barriers, practical effects, affected participants, and the appropriate legislative, regulatory, contractual, institutional, or administrative response.
  • Targeted consultations with Government, FCCC, EFL, relevant ministries and agencies, existing and prospective IPPs, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Assessment of proportionate reform and renewable electricity procurement options, including improved implementation, targeted legislative amendments, subsidiary instruments, regulatory guidance, strengthened negotiated PPAs, competitive procurement, and other approaches appropriate to Fiji.
  • Preparation of targeted amendments to the Electricity Act 2017, explanatory notes, consequential changes to associated instruments, a validation record, and a concise implementation roadmap.

 

Implementation period: The assignment is expected to be completed over twenty (20) weeks, with the final targeted legislative amendment package and implementation roadmap due in Week 20.

 

 

 

Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference are attached to this REOI as Appendix 1.

The implementing agency now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers concerning conflict of interest.

submissions to the tender box at EFL Head Office, Suva, will not be accepted.

At the current stage, consultants are only required to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) demonstrating their qualifications, relevant experience, and capability to undertake the assignment. A financial proposal is not required at the EOI stage.

 

 

 

Appendix 1 - Terms of Reference

Terms of Reference

Targeted Assessment and Amendment of Fiji’s Electricity Act 2017 to Enable Private Sector Participation in Renewable Electricity Generation

1.0 Background

Energy is a key driver of economic growth and social development in Fiji. Ensuring energy security and reliable access is increasingly important given external shocks such as pandemics, global geopolitical disruptions, and climate-driven natural disasters. Fiji’s energy transition requires strengthened sector planning led by Government in coordination with sector stakeholders (including Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC), and private investors) to ensure that enabling legislation, regulations, and policies support investment, accelerate renewable energy (RE) deployment, and strengthen climate resilience and energy efficiency in electricity infrastructure.

Fiji has committed to a low-carbon development pathway and aims to transition its electricity sector toward renewable energy. Fiji’s updated Nationally Determined Contributions (2020) and the SDG 7 Roadmap (2022) reflect the national ambition to increase renewable generation capacity and progress toward a predominantly renewable electricity system by 2036. Fiji’s electricity access rate in 2024 was approximately 97%, and renewable energy contributed an estimated 51% of generation excluding bioenergy.

While renewable technology costs have declined significantly over the past decade and private sector interest in investment is growing, private participation remains constrained by gaps in policy implementation and by legal and regulatory barriers affecting market access and the bankability of Independent Power Producer (IPP) projects.

The Electricity Act 2017 was enacted to modernize the sector, corporatize the former Fiji Electricity Authority into EFL, and confirm FCCC as the independent economic regulator. However, private investment in renewable energy has remained limited, and the legal and regulatory framework continues to present barriers to achieving Fiji’s energy transition goals.

2.0 Rationale

To strengthen the enabling environment for Fiji’s energy transition, the Government of Fiji (GoF), in partnership with the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) through the Small Island Developing States (SIDS) Lighthouses Initiative (LHI), undertook a gap analysis study titled “Assessment of Legislative and Regulatory Frameworks for a Just and Inclusive Energy Transition.”

The Gap Analysis examined Fiji’s legal, regulatory and institutional framework for electricity generation, transmission and supply. It identified barriers and uncertainties that may constrain the deployment of renewable energy and private sector participation in electricity generation. The study found that, while the Electricity Act 2017 allows IPPs to participate in electricity generation, the existing framework does not provide sufficient clarity, predictability and certainty regarding how private renewable energy participants can enter, operate and invest in Fiji’s electricity sector.

The Gap Analysis identified several areas requiring further assessment and possible legislative or regulatory reform, including:

  • unclear or limited recognition of renewable energy, Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, energy storage and other emerging forms of private renewable electricity generation;
  • dependence on negotiated Power Purchase Agreements between EFL and Independent Power Producers, without a sufficiently clear and predictable framework for pricing, risk allocation, negotiation timelines, approval and dispute resolution;
  • the need for clearer arrangements for procuring new renewable electricity generation, including assessment of competitive and other procurement approaches suitable for Fiji;

This assignment will build upon the relevant findings of the Gap Analysis and undertake a targeted assessment of the provisions of the Act and associated instruments that affect private sector participation in renewable electricity generation. The assessment will examine the legal and regulatory arrangements affecting IPPs, distributed generation, self-generation, storage and mini grids. It will also identify whether the barriers to private participation should be addressed through amendments to the Act, subsidiary regulations, license conditions, standard agreements, procurement arrangements or improved implementation.

The assignment is not intended to constitute a comprehensive review, redrafting or replacement of the Electricity Act 2017. The assessment shall focus on priority provisions and arrangements that materially affect private sector participation in renewable electricity generation and the enabling environment required for such participation.

In this context, the Government of Fiji, supported by the World Bank Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) for the Fiji Energy Transformation Project, seeks to identify and develop targeted, evidence-based amendments to the Electricity Act 2017 and any related reforms required to establish a transparent, predictable and workable legislative environment for private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.

The proposed reforms shall support renewable energy development while safeguarding affordability, system reliability, security of supply, consumer interests and the financial and operational sustainability of Fiji’s electricity system.

3.0 Objective of the Assignment

Building upon the findings of the Gap Analysis Study, the primary objective of this assignment is to undertake a targeted assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments to identify priority legal and regulatory barriers to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation, and to develop targeted, evidence-based amendments and complementary reform measures to address those barriers.

The assignment shall identify the appropriate legal, regulatory, contractual, institutional or administrative mechanism for addressing each priority barrier and shall distinguish matters requiring amendment to the Electricity Act 2017 from those that may be addressed through subsidiary regulations, licence conditions, regulatory decisions, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines or improved implementation and enforcement.

The assignment shall support a clear, transparent and predictable framework for participation by Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, self-generators, energy storage providers, mini-grid operators and other relevant renewable energy participants, while safeguarding electricity affordability, system reliability, security of supply, consumer interests, and the financial and operational sustainability of Fiji’s electricity system.

The specific objectives of the consultancy are to:

  • Build upon the relevant findings of the Gap Analysis Study to identify priority legal and regulatory barriers to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.
  • Undertake a targeted assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments affecting Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, self-generators, storage providers and mini-grid operators.
  • Identify priority barriers to private renewable electricity generation, including those relating to but not limited to licensing and exemptions, self-supply, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, Power Purchase Agreements, pricing arrangements, risk allocation and dispute resolution.
  • Assess proportionate reform options for addressing the identified barriers, including improved implementation of existing regulatory powers, negotiated PPAs, competitive procurement and other arrangements appropriate to Fiji’s market size, institutional capacity, affordability requirements, grid conditions and security-of-supply needs.
  • Determine which priority barriers require amendments to the Electricity Act 2017, and which may be addressed through subsidiary regulations, license conditions, regulatory decisions, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines or improved implementation and enforcement.
  • Prepare targeted legislative amendments and a concise implementation roadmap setting out the actions, sequencing, responsible institutions, indicative timeframes, transitional arrangements, and consequential changes required to implement the proposed amendments.

4.0 Scope of Works

The consultant shall undertake a thorough and targeted assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments to identify provisions that may constrain, discourage, or create uncertainty for private sector participation in renewable electricity generation. The assignment shall be informed by the findings of the Assessment of Legislative and Regulatory Frameworks for a Just and Inclusive Energy Transition in Fiji. However, the consultant shall independently scrutinise the Electricity Act 2017 and shall not be limited to the barriers identified in the Gap Analysis.

The consultant shall distinguish between matters requiring amendments to the Electricity Act 2017 and matters that may be addressed through subsidiary regulations, licence conditions, regulatory decisions, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines, or improved implementation and enforcement.

Task 1: Inception and Targeted Legal, Policy and Regulatory Assessment

The consultant shall:

  • Prepare an Inception Report setting out the proposed methodology, workplan, stakeholder consultation plan, information requirements, and schedule for completing the assignment.
  • Undertake a thorough assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 to identify provisions that may constrain, discourage, or create uncertainty for private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.
  • Examine the Electricity Regulations 2019, relevant electricity licences, and applicable regulatory instruments only to the extent necessary to understand how the relevant provisions of the Act operate in practice.
  • Assess the legal, policy and regulatory treatment of Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, self-generators, energy storage providers, mini-grid operators, and other relevant private renewable electricity participants.
  • Examine priority matters relating to definitions, licensing and exemptions, self-supply, distributed generation, EFL’s exclusive rights, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, Power Purchase Agreements, electricity purchase-price arrangements, institutional responsibilities, dispute resolution, compliance, and enforcement.
  • Identify whether each barrier arises from the Electricity Act itself or from subsidiary instruments, licence conditions, regulatory practices, commercial arrangements, institutional responsibilities, or implementation and enforcement.
  • Prepare a Legal Issues and Barriers Matrix identifying the relevant provision, the barrier identified, its practical effect on private sector participation, and the appropriate mechanism for addressing it.

Task 2: Targeted Stakeholder Consultations

The consultant shall:

  • Conduct targeted consultations with DOE, FCCC, EFL, relevant Government ministries and agencies (the Ministry of Finance, Office of the Attorney-General, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, relevant land and planning authorities), existing and prospective IPPs, and other relevant stakeholders, e.g. consumer and community representatives.
  • Obtain practical evidence on barriers affecting licensing, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, PPA negotiations, pricing certainty, project financing, regulatory approvals, and dispute resolution.
  • Determine whether the identified barriers arise from the legislation itself or from its administration, interpretation, implementation, or enforcement.
  • Seek stakeholder views on possible legislative and regulatory responses and their likely implications for private investment, EFL, consumers, electricity affordability, system reliability, and security of supply.
  • Prepare a concise Stakeholder Consultation Report and Consultation Matrix setting out the principal issues raised, areas of agreement and disagreement, and how stakeholder input informed the proposed reforms.

The consultations shall build upon the wider stakeholder consultation process previously undertaken under the Gap Analysis and shall focus on obtaining updated information and evidence relevant to this targeted assignment.

Task 3: Assessment of Reform and Procurement Options

Based on the legal, policy and regulatory assessment and stakeholder consultations, the consultant shall:

  1. Identify and compare proportionate options for addressing the priority barriers to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation. Depending on the nature of each barrier, the measures may include, but are not limited to:

a. improved administration, interpretation, and enforcement of existing powers.

b. targeted amendments to the Electricity Act 2017.

c. amendments to subsidiary regulations or licence conditions.

d. clearer regulatory guidance, technical codes, or standard agreements.

e. strengthened arrangements for negotiated Power Purchase Agreements.

f. competitive procurement for suitable categories of renewable electricity generation; or

g. an appropriate combination of these measures.

 

  1. Recommend other measures where supported by the assessment and identify the most appropriate legislative, regulatory, contractual, institutional, or administrative mechanism for addressing each priority barrier.
  2. Assess options for establishing a transparent and fit-for-purpose renewable energy procurement framework, including competitive and other appropriate procurement approaches, taking into account Fiji’s market size, institutional capacity, consumer affordability, investor confidence and project bankability, system reliability and security of supply, and the appropriate allocation of risks among Government, EFL and private-sector developers.
  3. Where a renewable energy procurement framework is recommended, identify the necessary legal and regulatory arrangements, institutional roles, core procurement principles, standard documentation requirements, and appropriate legal instruments for implementation.
  4. Provide drafting instructions for any supporting procurement instruments requiring subsequent development. The consultant shall not be required to prepare complete procurement regulations, bidding documents, a model PPA, or a detailed auction design under this assignment.
  5. Assess whether different arrangements may be appropriate for utility-scale IPPs, distributed energy resources, commercial and industrial self-generation, energy storage, mini-grids, and other categories of renewable electricity generation. The structure options include but not limited to PPPs, SPV and JV financial model concessions, and other private-investment structures, and compare these with conventional IPP arrangements.
  6. Consider the likely implications of the principal reform options for private sector participation, EFL’s financial and operational sustainability, consumer affordability, whole-of-system costs, grid integration, system reliability, and security of supply.
  7. Recommend the most appropriate and proportionate reform approach, or combination of approaches, for Fiji, supported by clear evidence and reasoning. Competitive procurement, including auctions, shall be assessed as one possible approach and shall not be presumed to be appropriate for every technology, project type, or project scale.
  8. The assessment of renewable energy procurement options shall be undertaken at a strategic, legal, regulatory and institutional level. It shall identify and compare procurement approaches appropriate to Fiji and recommend the preferred framework and associated legal and institutional arrangements. The assignment shall not require detailed electricity system modelling, detailed financial or tariff modelling, detailed auction design, preparation of bidding documents, preparation of a model Power Purchase Agreement, or development of complete procurement regulations.

Task 4: Targeted Legislative Amendments and Implementation Roadmap

Based on the preferred reform approach, the consultant shall:

  1. Prepare targeted amendments to the Electricity Act 2017, in the form of a draft Electricity (Amendment) Bill or equivalent legislative drafting document, clearly identifying the specific provisions to be inserted, amended or repealed, together with concise explanatory notes setting out the rationale and legal effect of each amendment. The amendments shall be limited to priority barriers identified through the assignment and shall not constitute a comprehensive redraft or replacement of the Act.
  2. Ensure that the proposed amendments provide clear and proportionate arrangements for relevant categories and scales of private renewable electricity generation.
  3. Address, where required, barriers relating to licensing, exemptions, self-generation, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, PPAs, purchase-price arrangements from private generators, dispute resolution, compliance, and enforcement.
  4. Clarify any institutional powers, functions and responsibilities necessary to implement the proposed amendments relating to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.
  5. Include any enabling powers necessary for subsequent regulations, licence conditions, procurement rules, technical codes, standard agreements or regulatory guidelines required to implement the proposed amendments.
  6. Ensure that the proposed amendments retain sufficient flexibility to accommodate future developments in renewable energy technologies, energy storage, project structures, and business models.
  7. Ensure that the proposed amendments safeguard electricity affordability, consumer interests, system reliability, security of supply, and the financial and operational sustainability of Fiji’s electricity system.
  8. Identify consequential changes required to the Electricity Regulations 2019, electricity licences, regulatory instruments, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines, or other associated instruments.
  9. Present the proposed amendments and recommendations to DOE and selected stakeholders through a validation session and incorporate comments where appropriate.
  10. Prepare a matrix recording significant comments received and explaining how they were addressed.
  11. Finalise the targeted amendments and explanatory notes following the validation process.
  12. Prepare a concise implementation roadmap identifying the required actions, sequencing, responsible institutions, indicative timeframes, approval requirements, transitional arrangements, consequential changes to associated instruments, and priority follow-on activities.

5.0 Environmental and Social Considerations

Although this assignment does not involve construction or civil works, the consultant shall consider whether the Electricity Act provides an adequate legal basis for managing environmental and social issues that may arise from future electricity sector investments, including land access, community impacts, vulnerable consumers, climate resilience, and environmental protection.

Collectively, the consultancy team shall have:

  2. At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in electricity sector legal and regulatory reform, renewable energy development, utility regulation, or private sector participation in electricity generation.
  3. Demonstrated experience in reviewing and drafting primary legislation, including amendments to electricity, energy, utilities, infrastructure, or other regulated sector legislation
  4. Practical knowledge of the legal, regulatory, commercial, and institutional arrangements governing Independent Power Producers, electricity licensing, Power Purchase Agreements, grid access and interconnection, self-generation, distributed energy resources, energy storage, mini-grids, and renewable energy procurement

  7. Knowledge of electricity pricing and cost-recovery principles, utility financial and operational sustainability, consumer affordability, system reliability, and security of supply.
  8. Experience assessing the implications of legislative and regulatory reforms for private investment, investor certainty, consumers, utilities, regulators, and Government.

                                      develop guidelines and architectural drawings for

                                      climate resilient and energy efficient health care

                                      infrastructure in various sites around Malawi

Reference No.                  : MW-MOH-565052-CS-QCBS

Date of Issue                     : 28th September, 2026

 

 

 

 

  1. BACKGROUND

 

The Government of Malawi through the Ministry of Health and Sanitation is implementing the Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (MHEPRR) project.  The project is financed through the International Development Association (IDA) and Global Financing Facility (GFF) at an estimated budget of US$60 Million.  The project aims at consolidating efforts from the World Bank and development partners to provide relief and strengthen health systems against economic shocks, climate disasters, and public health emergencies, aligning with the Government's focus on Pandemic Preparedness and Response after COVID-19.  The expected duration for implementation of the Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (MHEPRR) project is 5 years with a close date of December 2029. This five-year initiative is aimed at strengthening the country’s ability to respond to health crises, including those intensified by climate change.

 

Alignment with HSSP III and the Resilience Framework

In direct response to these vulnerabilities and in alignment with the Health Sector Strategic Plan III (HSSP III), the Ministry of Health and Sanitation is prioritizing the construction of specialized climate resilient health care infrastructure as a fundamental pillar of national resilience. This initiative represents a strategic shift from centralized care to a decentralized “Surge Ready” model. By establishing high standard climate resilient health care infrastructure in geographically vulnerable areas, the Ministry aims to bridge the critical gap between primary care and overstretched central facilities.

 

Project Scope

 

Under the first phase of the MHEPRR project, the Ministry is utilizing funding from the World Bank to conduct comprehensive technical assessments for the construction of these facilities in selected disaster-prone sites. This includes the development of standardized architectural designs and technical specifications that can be adapted to the specific climate change related risks of each location and conducting Environmental and Social Assessments for the proposed sites.

 

 

  1. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

 

The purpose of this assignment is to engage a qualified multidisciplinary consulting firm to undertake the planning and design of standardized, cost effective, modular, climate resilient and energy efficient functional community hospitals to be constructed across various sites in Malawi.

 

The consulting firm will provide comprehensive architectural and engineering design services, including site specific adaptation for multistory and modular structures to be used by the Ministry of Health and Sanitation.

 

 

2.1. Specific objectives

The specific objectives of the assignment will include the following:

 

  1. To conduct a comprehensive pre-design assessment and feasibility study for each proposed site to inform the planning and design of the community hospitals. The findings of this assessment shall guide the functional brief, space requirements, service scope, phasing strategy and overall design approach to ensure the proposed facilities are responsive to local health service needs and site conditions.
  2. To prepare coordinated architectural and engineering designs for community hospitals to be constructed across multiple districts while remaining adaptable to site specific conditions. This will result in complete and integrated construction drawings, technical specifications and bill of quantities that are sufficient.
  3. To prepare blank Bills of quantities and costed bills of quantities that will lead to cost estimates
  4. To prepare complete tender documentation per site which will be used to procure a contractor to execute the works on the sites.

 

  1. Conduct Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) and prepare a report

 

  1. Prepare comprehensive Bidding Documents for tendering in accordance with World Bank requirements and Government of Malawi procurement regulations, ensuring the inclusion of an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) from the approved ESIA report to be added to the Bills of Quantities for the entire proposed hospital

 

 

  1. DETAILS OF THE ASSIGNMENT

 

The consulting firm will come up with designs for various sites and associated Bills of Quantities that will be packaged according to the needs of each site. Geotechnical and topographical surveys will have to be carried out to ascertain specific site conditions and disaster-prone areas. Social and environmental assessments will be carried out and the key findings or parameters to be considered in the structural designs and the development of bills of quantities.

 

 

  1. SCOPE OF CONSULTANCY WORK

 

The consultancy will conduct the following actions:

 

(a) Site Surveys

 Making an initial visit to the site and carrying out an appraisal of the site and existing buildings

 

  • Conduct detailed site surveys to assess existing physical conditions, topography, geotechnical surveys, utilities, environmental and social considerations, access routes, and any site constraints.
  • Carry out geotechnical investigations, including soil testing and analysis and provide recommendations for foundation systems and structural considerations based on ground conditions.
  • Prepare a site assessment report outlining findings and implications for design.
  • Environmental and social assessment: identify existing natural features such as water and air quality,  wildlife habitats, forests, pre-existing hazardous waste, soil stability and natural disaster risks etc. to be affected and any other natural resources and habitats to be preserved.

 

(c) Design development and cost estimations

 

  • Prepare conceptual, schematic, and detailed architectural and engineering designs.
  • Develop spatial layouts in accordance with Community hospital infrastructure standards.
  • Provide detailed cost estimates at each design stage to ensure alignment.
  • Revise designs as necessary based on stakeholder feedback and regulatory requirements.

 

(d) Regulatory and Standards compliance:

  • Ensure full compliance with guidelines issued by the World Health Organization (WHO), particularly in relation to spatial planning and healthcare facility requirements under the Safe Hospitals Initiative Guidelines (SHIG).
  • Obtain or support the acquisition of necessary approvals and clearances from relevant authorities.

(e) Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA):

  • Prepare a project brief to be submitted to the MEPA upon client review
  • Undertake ESIA in accordance with the provisions of international policies and laws such as the World Bank Environmental and Social standards, policies as well as national policies, legislations and regulations. Provide a concise description of the biophysical characteristics and the social-economic environment status of each site. The assessment will also include Occupational, Health and Safety considerations, high-level assessment of waste,noise and dust impacts,air quality, climate change and risk assessment.
  •  
  • Prepare ESIA report for each site and a consolidated assessment report which will feed into the main report.
  1. DESIGN PRINCIPLES

 

•         Patient-centred and clinically functional planning.

•         Universal accessibility and inclusive design.

•         Infection prevention and control.

•         Fire and life safety.

•         Climate resilience and disaster risk reduction.

•         Energy and water efficiency.

•         Low-maintenance and locally supportable systems.

•         Appropriate security and controlled circulation.

•         Provision for future expansion.

•         Whole-life cost/value-for-money considerations.

 

6.       DELIVERABLES

 

The output from the consultancy will include an inception report, architectural designs, engineering drawings, bills of quantities, cost estimates based on bills of quantities, tender documents, a masterplan for each site, an environmental and social assessment report for each site, consolidated ESIA report based on terms of reference issued by MEPA  and a comprehensive final design report. 1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Finance has received financing from the World Bank and a grant from the European Union toward the cost of the Construction of a New Runway and Other facilities for Plaine Corail Airport, Rodrigues and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards recruitment of Individual Consultancy for Procurement Assistant.

2. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT 

The Procurement Assistant is to support all activities and procedures related to the procurement of goods, works, consulting services and non-consulting services under the specified threshold and act as an understudy to the Procurement Specialists and Sr. Procurement Specialist, providing support in procurement operations, ensuring compliance with policies and timely delivery of procurement activities. The Assistant will progressively assume more responsibility under supervision to support the project’s procurement needs

3.0       BRIEF SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

  • The Procurement Assistant will handle procurement activities under supervision, of the Procurement Specialist.
  • The Assistant will support and assist the Procurement Specialist with procurement activities and procedures as described in the Project Operations Manual (POM) and the World Bank Procurement Regulations.
  • Assist in the preparation and publication of procurement notices, bidding documents, evaluation reports, and contract documentation under supervision.
  • Prepare and update the Project’s Annual Procurement Plan using STEP.
  • Assist with organizing bid opening sessions, evaluation meetings, and negotiation documentation.
  • Prepare the minutes of the Evaluation Committee meetings.
  • Maintain updated procurement records, databases, and filing systems according to project and donor requirements.
  • Assist in updating the STEP system with procurement activities and contract management information.
  • Maintain and organize procurement documentation and ensure records are complete and audit ready.
  • Help ensure procurement activities comply with World Bank, Airports of Mauritius Co. Ltd and Government of Mauritius policies and regulations.

4. INVITATION FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

The Airports of Mauritius Co. Ltd now invites eligible candidates (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

5.0       QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE                                 

The consultant should have the following minimum qualifications and experience:

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Procurement, supply chain management, Project Management, Engineering, Economics, Law, or a related field would be considered an asset.
  • A diploma or certificate in Procurement or Contract Management is an asset.

Experience

  • At least 2 (two) years of experience in procurement as a Procurement Assistant.
  • Familiarity with World Bank or other international financial institution procurement policies and procedures is preferred.
  • Experience with e-procurement systems, such as the World Bank’s STEP platform, will be an advantage.
  • Work experience in similar projects financed by international multilateral institutions in a similar position, will be a definite advantage.
  • Experience in the procurement for building/civil projects, including bid documents, opening and evaluating bidders' proposals, negotiating and managing contracts

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the following link: https://aml.mru.aero/index.php/business/rap

The attention of interested individual Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November, 2020, and September, 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.0 CONFLICT OF INTEREST

Please refer to paragraph 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations on conflict of interest related to this assignment which is available on the Bank’s website athttp://projects-beta.worldbank.org/en/projects- operations/products-and-services/brief/procurement-new-framework.    

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8:00 am to 5:00 pm on Mondays to Fridays.
