PROJET D’ACCÉLÉRATION DIGITALE EN CÔTE D’IVOIRE (PADCI)

AVIS DE PUBLICATION DE LA DEMANDE DE COTATION N° CI-PADCI-571924-NC-RFQ POUR LA SÉLECTION D’UN PRESTATAIRE POUR LA MISE EN ŒUVRE D’UN PROJET PILOTE DE SAUVEGARDE DE DONNÉES DANS UN DATACENTER EXISTANT

Le Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), mis en œuvre par le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation, invite les entreprises spécialisées intéressées à soumettre leurs offres dans le cadre de la Demande de Cotation relative à la :

« Sélection d’un prestataire pour mettre en œuvre un projet pilote de sauvegarde de données dans un datacenter existant ».

1. Objet de la consultation

La mission a pour objet de sélectionner un prestataire qualifié chargé de concevoir et de mettre en œuvre un projet pilote de sauvegarde et de restauration des données dans un datacenter existant, à travers l’analyse de l’environnement technique, la conception d’une architecture de sauvegarde sécurisée et redondante, le déploiement et la configuration de la solution, la réalisation des tests de sauvegarde et de restauration, ainsi que la formation et le transfert de compétences aux équipes internes et la production de la documentation technique et opérationnelle.

2. Financement

La présente consultation est financée dans le cadre du Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale. Le PADCI est financé selon le mécanisme de Financement des Projets d’Investissement (IPF).

3. Conditions de participation

La participation est ouverte aux entreprises légalement constituées, disposant des capacités techniques, professionnelles, administratives et financières nécessaires à l’exécution des prestations, objet de la présente consultation.
Le prestataire devra également être en mesure de mobiliser une équipe comprenant au minimum un Chef de projet, un Ingénieur informaticien, un Ingénieur systèmes et un Ingénieur Administrateur de bases de données (DBA), conformément aux exigences du cahier des charges.

4. Retrait du dossier

Le dossier de Demande de Cotation peut être retiré gratuitement auprès de :

Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Accélération Digital en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI)
Abidjan Angré 8ème Tranche, Cité les Elites II, non-loin du Fast Food Chicken Nation

Voir la Cellule Passation des Marchés

Tél : (+225) 07 08 32 89 34/ 07 09 46 99 70.

Email : ju.koffi@telecom.gouv.ci  avec copie obligatoire à gn.kouame@telecom.gouv.ci padci@telecom.gouv.ci
à compter de la date de publication du dossier, aux jours et heures ouvrables notamment du lundi au vendredi de 8 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 17 heures, Temps Universel.

Le retrait du dossier ne sera plus autorisé à compter du troisième (3ème) jour précédant la date limite de remise des offres.

La présente publication est faite à l’attention de toute agence de communication intéressée et répondant aux conditions de participation définies dans le dossier de consultation.

5. Constitution du dossier de candidature

Le soumissionnaire devra soumettre un dossier de candidature complet comprenant notamment les pièces suivantes :

-  une copie du Registre de Commerce et du Crédit Mobilier (RCCM) de l’entreprise ;
-  une attestation de situation fiscale délivrée par les services compétents ;
-  une attestation de mise à jour CNPS ;
- une présentation de l’entreprise et de ses principales activités ;
-  les références de l’entreprise en matière de prestations similaires, accompagnées des Attestations de Bonne Exécution (ABE) ;
- la liste et les CV des experts proposés pour l’exécution de la mission ;
- les diplômes et certifications des membres de l’équipe, conformément aux exigences du cahier des charges ;
- tout document permettant d’apprécier les capacités techniques et professionnelles du soumissionnaire.

6. Date et heure limites de dépôt des plis

Les offres doivent être déposées au plus tard le vendredi 02 octobre 2026 à 9 heures 30 minutes, sous pli fermé, avec la mention :« Consultation de Prestataire N° CI-PADCI-571924-NC-RFQ pour la sélection d’un prestataire pour mettre en œuvre un projet pilote de sauvegarde de données dans un datacenter existant »

Le dépôt des offres devra faire l’objet d’un enregistrement sur la fiche de réception des offres tenue à cet effet au service Passation des marchés du PADCI.

7. Ouverture des plis

L’ouverture des offres aura lieu en séance publique le vendredi 02 octobre 2026 à 10H30 dans les locaux du PADCI sis à la 8ème Tranche, non-loin du Fast-Food Chicken Nation Cité les Elites II, Email : ju.koffi@telecom.gouv.ci  avec copie obligatoire à gn.kouame@telecom.gouv.ci; padci@telecom.gouv.ci,  Tel : (+225) 07 08 32 89 34 / 07 09 46 99 70.

Les services de consultant (« Services ») consistent à recruter un Consultant individuel chargé de renforcer les capacités institutionnelles de l’UCP et de mettre en place un processus d’amélioration systématique de ses performances. Dans ce cadre, le Consultant contribuera à la structuration organisationnelle de l’Unité et à l’amélioration de ses procédures, à la mise en place d’un système de supervision et de suivi de la performance des financements en cours, ainsi qu’à la structuration de nouvelles opportunités de financement et à la mobilisation de ressources nécessaires au fonctionnement de l’UCP.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES -FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

ZAMBIA

ACCELERATING SUSTAINABLE AND CLEAN ENERGY ACCESS TRANSFORMATION (ASCENT) PROJECT.

 

Grant No.: P180547

 

Assignment Title: Framework Agreement for Geospatial Electrification Planning and Analytical Services.

 

Reference No. ZM-COMESA-565158-CS-QBS

 

  1. The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation (ASCENT) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services

 

2. The objective of the consulting services (“the Services”) is to support the development and application of geospatial least-cost electrification planning approaches, including the identification of optimal combinations of grid extension, mini-grid, and standalone systems to achieve universal access objectives, and to be grounded in internationally recognized methodologies that ensure transparency, consistency, and reproducibility of analytical approaches, as well as the development or strengthening of related geospatial data systems, data governance arrangements, interoperability mechanisms, and digital decision-support tools

 

3. Scope of service”; The services to be provided under the Framework Agreement are organized into indicative service components, which describe the range of technical support that may be required

 

Individual assignments issued under the Framework Agreement may involve one or several service components, depending on the needs of the requesting Project Implementation Unit (PIU).

 

The combination and scope of services to be provided under each assignment will depend on the specific needs of the requesting PIU and the nature of the Service Request submitted to COMESA.

Service component 1:

 Development of National Electrification Analyses (NEAs).

 

Consulting firms may support participating PIUs in preparing or updating National Electrification Analyses using geospatial least-cost electrification modelling methodologies. Activities may include the collection and validation of spatial datasets, development or updating of geospatial least-cost electrification models, analysis of grid extension, mini-grid and standalone electrification options, and preparation of electrification investment planning scenarios.

 

Service component 2:

Updating Existing Electrification Plans and Models.

 

Consulting firms may assist PIUs in reviewing and updating existing electrification plans and modelling tools. Activities may include updating modelling assumptions and datasets, recalibrating electrification planning models, incorporating updated demand forecasts or policy targets, and producing revised electrification planning outputs.

Service component 3:

Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI), Data Governance and Interoperability.

 

Consulting firms may assist PIUs in establishing or strengthening national spatial data infrastructure (SDI) systems, data governance arrangements and interoperable geospatial data platforms to support energy access planning. Activities may include assessing SDI readiness, identifying data architecture and interoperability gaps, developing data governance frameworks and standards, and establishing or enhancing geospatial data platforms, metadata catalogues and data-sharing mechanisms, including, where relevant, open-source or interoperable platforms such as GeoNode, CKAN, or equivalent tools.

 

Service component 4:

Development of Visualization and Decision-Support Platforms.

 

Consulting firms may support the development of digital platforms and tools that facilitate the analysis and dissemination of electrification planning outputs. Activities may include development of geospatial dashboards, creation of data portals for electrification planning outputs, and integration with national energy information systems.

Service component 5:

Capacity Building and Institutional Support.

 

Consulting firms may provide technical assistance and training to strengthen national capacities in geospatial electrification planning. Activities may include training on modelling methodologies and planning tools, support for data management processes, and preparation of technical guidelines and operational manuals.

 

The consulting services “Framework Agreement for Geospatial Electrification Planning and Analytical Services” include establishment for an initial period of three (3) years and may, subject to satisfactory performance, continued need, availability of financing, and any applicable approvals, be extended for up to two (2) additional one-year periods.

 

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment

can be found at the following website: https://www.comesa.int/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/TOR_FA_GeoSP_Primary_Proc-_-30.09.2026.docx

 

 

4. The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. At least ten (10) years of relevant experience;
  2. Successful completion of at least three assignments of similar nature and complexity;
  3. Experience with government institutions, utilities, regional organizations, or development partners;
  4. Experience in Sub-Saharan Africa, preferably in the energy sector;
  5. Capacity to deploy multidisciplinary teams for multi-country assignments.

 

Submission requirements:

 

  • Company profile and legal registration documents.
  • Description of the firm's relevant experience.
  • List of up similar assignments completed within the last ten years.
  • Information on contract value, client, implementation period, and firm's role.
  • Description of organizational and technical capacity.
  • Contact details for client references.

 

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“[Procurement in Investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on Conflict of Interest”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

 

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality-Based Selection (QBS) method set out in the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’ July 2016 and revised Seven Edition, September 2025.

 

     Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 09:00 to 16:00 hours Monday to Thursday, on Fridays from 09:00 to 12:30 hours Zambian time except for weekends and Public Holidays. Address:  Head of Procurement, COMESA Secretariat, Ben Bella Road, Lusaka, Zambia. Email address:  procurement@comesa.int].

TERMS OF REFERENCE

CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION

TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

PART I: 

Position

Operations Manager

Category of Consultancy

Local (Level 5)

Contract Type

Time-based Individual Consultant

Hiring Entity

TRHDP Project Office

Location

Honiara, Solomon Islands

Duration

2 years

Start date

As soon as possible upon agreement

 

 

Tina River Hydropower Development Project              

Project Details

Strategic Context

The Tina River Hydropower Project is the first large-scale infrastructure to be developed under a public-private partnership arrangement and the first utility-scale renewable energy project for the Solomon Islands expected to deliver benefits such as more affordable electricity and improved accessibility to cleaner, more reliable energy sources for community now and in the future.

 

The Tina River Hydropower Project consists of (i) 15-megawatt hydropower facility located on the Tina River southeast of Honiara, comprising: a dam, headrace tunnel and a powerhouse about 3km downstream of the dam; (ii) access road to facilitate the construction and operation of the hydropower facility; and (iii) transmission lines - two parallel (on separate poles) single circuit transmission lines connecting the powerhouse to the existing Lungga Power Station. Further project details are included in Annex A.

 

The Tina Hydro Project Office under the Ministry of Mines, Energy and Rural Electrification is responsible for the coordination of the project activities to ensure Tina Hydropower Limited as implementing entity responsible for the hydropower facility and access road and Solomon Power as Offtaker under the Power Purchase Agreement fulfil their obligations under the project agreements. The Project Office has a fundamental advisory role to Solomon Islands Government, ensuring that the interests of the government are protected in line with the project agreements. The Project Office is responsible for monitoring and supporting the implementation of the social and environmental safeguard arrangements, the Gender Action Plan and Community Development Plan, and maintaining the Dam Safety Advisory Panel (DSAP) and the Lender’s Technical Advisor (LTA) including the independent social and environmental monitoring agent. The Project Office also supports entities participating in the implementation arrangements agreed under the land acquisition process, the communities in utilizing their share of project benefits for community development, and the tribes which would be interested and committed to the establishment of a protected area in the upper catchment.

 

The Operations Manager of the Project Office is expected to enhance leadership within the Project Office to efficiently support project implementation in the best interests of the Solomon Islands Government.

Contract Details

Details

Objective

The Operations Manager shall be based in Honiara, Solomon Islands, providing support to the Project Manager (PM) in managing the Tina River Hydropower Project Office.

Duration 

The position is for a period of 2 years with expected opportunity to renew subject to satisfactory performance evaluation rating by the PM annually.

Reporting

The Operations Manager will report to the PM. The Operations Manager will shadow the PM to learn the various aspects of the Project including the following:

  • All the 4 components of the Project
  • The Stakeholders
  • Implementation
  • Flow of funds
  • Agreements including EPC contract
  • The Financial Model
  • Additional financing
  • Technical aspects of the dam, tunnel and powerhouse
  • Pending work at the site
  • Up to date Disbursements
  • Future disbursements
  • Pending design issues
  • Role of LTA and DSAP
  • Meetings
  • SharePoint structure
  • Procurement through STEP
  • Status of contracts of the Consultants
  • Performance Management
  • World Bank and other CFP Missions, aide memoir

The Operations Manager will hold briefing meetings with the PM monthly or as otherwise agreed in writing with the PM.

 

The Operations Manager, under the guidance of the PM and Deputy Project Manager, will provide project implementation progress updates to the Project Steering Committee (PSC) at the quarterly PSC meetings or as required by the Chairperson of the PSC.

The Operations Manager will liaise and work very closely with the CBSP 2 Project Manager, the Deputy Project Manager and the Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager such that he/she develops a very good understanding of the finances, procurement, administrative, communications & media, grievance redress mechanism, gender action plan, biodiversity management plan, safeguards, health and safety, Tina Core Land Company (TCLC), Cooperatives, Land, Influx,  all 4 components of the Community Benefits Sharing Project 2 (CBSP2)

The Operations Manager will shadow the Project Manager; however, it is expected that he/she to learn about the project he/she will actively be involved in the deliverables listed on page 6. The Operations Manager will conduct and chair meetings, preparing the agenda and minutes of the meetings.

 

The Operations Manager will act in the role of the Project Manager during periods of absence of the PM from Honiara. During this period the Operations Manager will be solely responsible for the running of the Project Office. The delegations include: authority to endorse and sign purchase vouchers, review and approve timesheets for the ESSM, the Financial & Commercial Advisor (FCA), review and approve invoices from LTA, DSAP members, Ashurst, the FCA, the ESSM; review and approve agenda for the Project Steering Committee meetings, CFP missions, review and approve imprest requests, review/endorse memos from DSAP, correspond with THL on pending matters, conduct and chair progress meetings, chair meetings with ADB, WB, MMERE, MOFT and respond to emails.

 

The Project Office organization chart is included in Annex B.

 

 

DETAILED POSITION DESCRIPTION

           

The Operations Manager will support the PM, the Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager, the Deputy Project Manager and the CBSP 2 Project Manager for ensuring the effective and efficient management of the Project Office by:

 

  1. Implementing the project activities under the Project Office’s responsibility, including monitoring and supporting the implementation of the social and environmental safeguard arrangements, the Gender Action Plan and Community Development Plan.

 

  1. Supporting the entities participating in the implementation arrangements agreed under the land acquisition process (Tina Core Land Company and the five core landowning tribes’ co-operatives), the communities in utilizing their share of project benefits for community development through the CBSP project, and the tribes which would be interested and committed to the establishment of a protected area in the upper catchment.

 

  1. Monitoring the project activities of Tina Hydropower Limited as implementing entity responsible for the hydropower facility and access road and Solomon Power as Offtaker under the Power Purchase Agreement to ensure they fulfil their obligations under the project agreements.

 

  1. Monitoring Solomon Islands Government commitments to ensure it is meeting and maintaining its obligations as required by the project agreements.

 

The Operations Manager’s detailed project description is set out as follows.

 

General Responsibilities & Objectives

 

  • Overall in-depth understanding of the relevant documents/agreements including:
    • Project Documents including Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), Implementation Agreement (IA). Government Guarantee Agreement (GGA), the Land Lease Agreement and the Side Letter Agreement.

 

    • Financing agreements and project agreements of all Concessional Financing Partners (CFPs), the Facilities Agreement, and various security agreements and documents.

 

    • Safeguards documents including Environmental Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Land Acquisition and Livelihood Restoration Plan (LALRP), Gender Action Plan (GAP), Community Development Plan (CDP); and implementation of the Construction Environment and Social Management Plans (CESMP).

 

    • Project Operations Manuals (POMs) and any other relevant documents.

 

  • Implement the project management system including suitable office administration for the Project Office, including appropriate document and records storage systems (SharePoint), communication, procurement, risk, meeting and administration management, ensure project management procedures and systems are accessible to all staff and consultants as relevant, and in consultation with the Deputy Project Manager, ESSM , train staff and consultants as relevant on the use of project management procedures and systems.

 

  • Assist the PM in the implementation of effective internal and external communication protocols as part of the overall project management procedures and systems.

 

  • Assist the PM in leading the coordination and collaboration of the key project stakeholders to ensure timely project implementation to resolve any major implementation hindrances efficiently and effectively.

 

  • Assist the PM to maintain an overview of the TCLC, and associated tribal cooperatives, and benefit share arrangements with a view to ensure that they are functioning according to the Land Lease Agreement and the Implementation Agreement.

 

Project Office Staff and Consultants

 

  • Assist the PM to oversee and manage the Project Office staff plan to ensure the Project Office is appropriately resourced to fulfil its mandate and implementation of the key project activities under its responsibility effectively and efficiently in accordance with the project agreements.

 

  • Work very closely with the Deputy Project Manager, Environmental and Social Safeguards manager to deliver in accordance with their terms of reference.

 

  • Review of Project Office staff and consultant performance in accordance with their contract terms and deliverables. Performance review will be coordinated in consultation with the Deputy Project Manager and Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager. Performance review will be on a six-monthly basis or as otherwise agreed in writing with the PM. 

 

  • Ensure capacity development of all national staff including identification of opportunities to participate in training and workshops for professional development and skills development.

 

  • Assist the PM in the management of the Dam Safety and Advisory Panel member’s contracts to ensure that Concessional Financers’ requirements are adhered to during project implementation. Assist the PM in convening Dam Safety and Advisory Panel meetings, visits and progress meetings in accordance with the project agreements.

 

  • Assist the PM in the management of the Lender’s Technical Advisor (LTA) contract to ensure that Concessional Financers’ requirements are adhered to during project implementation. In accordance with the terms of contract, assist the PM to manage the LTA’s  input, review and advice, quaterly and six-monthly site visits, and facilitate discussions with relevant project stakeholders and CFPs.

 

  • Assist the PM in the management and support the interface between LTA and Tina Hydropower Limited to complete submission of the utilization requests and supporting documents to ensure timely provision of the Technical Advisor’s Certificate in accordance with the Facilities Agreement.

 

Project Reporting

 

  • Assist the PM to ensure the reporting obligations of the Project Office are fulfilled, on time and of the required standard, including establishing an appropriate communications protocol, reporting format and processes for timely delivery. The project reports include overall quarterly progress reports, mid-term review, completion report, and other reports as required by the project agreements. The Project Office is responsible for collecting all relevant reporting inputs to complete the overall quarterly progress report, including those from Tina Hydropower Limited and Solomon Power. 

 

  • Assist the PM to update and implement the Project Operations Manual for the Project Office and coordinate the update and implementation of the Project Operations Manual for Tina Hydropower Limited, as necessary by obtaining consents of the relevant stakeholders and no objection from the relevant CFPs.

 

  • Assist the PM to lead the Project Office and coordinate key project stakeholders’ participation in CFPs periodic implementation support missions.

 

Resource Management

 

  • Assist the PM to ensure transparent, accurate and organized financial management of Project Office.

 

  • Assist the PM in his role to oversee the Project Office budget and be accountable for the funds provided to the Project Office by the CFPs, Solomon Islands Government, and other development partners as relevant.

 

  • Assist the PM to lead preparation of the Annual Work Plan and Budget for the Project Office by closely aligning with the scheduled activities of Tina Hydropower Limited for the Hydropower facility and access road and Solomon Power for the transmission line. Liaise with the Deputy Project Manager, the Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager and the Financial and Commercial advisor and assist the PM to prepare the Annual Work Plan and Budget with all relevant inputs from Project Office staff and consultants. The Annual Work Plan and Budget is due to the relevant parties not later than 30th September of each calendar year.

 

  • Assist the PM in the coordination activities with the Financial and Commercial Advisor to ensure timely preparation of Tina Hydropower Limited Annual Work Plan and Budget for the Hydropower facility and access road.

 

  • Assist the PM to lead the Project Office’s input to Ministry of Mines, Energy and Rural Electrification for its national annual development budget bid for the counterpart financing required to cover the Project Office’s operational costs. The input is to be managed in close coordination with the Deputy Project Manager. The budget bid to reach MMERE by 31st July each year. 

 

  • Assist the PM to ensure that the Project Office funds are audited on an annual basis in accordance with the project agreements.

Specific Deliverables of contract and Key Dates

These deliverables are the responsibility of the Operations Manager with support from Deputy PM and the PM.

Key Deliverables

Timing

Quarterly Project Reports and quarterly Interim Financial Reports (IFRs) by the dates stipulated in the POM.

Quarterly

Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) for the Project Office by the dates stipulated in the POM

Annually

Consolidated AWPB with inputs from THL and Solomon Power, by the dates stipulated in the POM.

Annually

Solomon Islands budget request as per requirement of the Ministry of Mines, Energy and Rural Electrification.

Annually

Financial Statements (FS) for FY2026, FY 2027 and FY 2028 and Completed Audit reports plus opinions from the Office of the Auditor General, well before the deadline in accordance with POM.

Annually

Project Implementation Completion Report by not later than 6 months after the Project Closing Date (PCD), with input from Tina Hydropower Limited and Solomon Power.

6 months post PCD

DSAP meeting minutes.

As required

Steering Committee meeting minutes (quarterly and/or ad-hoc basis). Updated POMs on a six-monthly basis or as may be agreed with the World Bank

Quarterly

Selection Criteria

This section details the basis upon which selection of the successful candidate will be made.

 

Mandatory Criteria – These criteria must be met in order to be considered for this role. The candidate will possess high levels of personal and working integrity including sense of urgency and attention to detail.

 

Mandatory Criteria

Description

Education/Qualification

A Masters’ qualification in any of the following fields is required: engineering or project management. Project management certification such as PMP would be a plus.

Work Experience

A minimum of five (5) year professional engineering experience and or project management experience in an electricity utility gained on capital project and /or planning for generation, transmission or distribution infrastructure

Leadership Experience

Proven leadership experience in multistakeholder environments, at managerial level. Previous work experience in managing or working at a managerial level in a power facility/electricity utility.

Project Management and or Planning Experience

Experience in establishing well-functioning management units and to manage community expectations and other project risks using various communications platforms and strategies. Proven communication skills as spokesperson for project or company.

Communication Skills

Good communication skills in English and in Pidgin.

Driver’s license/clean police record

15

Resources Provided

Provide an outline of items/resources the Project Office will provide to enable delivery of the contract outcomes.

Resources

Equipment (IT/Comms etc) 

The project will provide access to IT equipment, stationery, internet, communications, and related utilities.  The Operations Manager will be fully responsible for the cost of local transportation (to/from the office).

Office Space 

The project will provide the office space, including office furniture.

Documents

MMERE will provide to the Operations Manager all the existing reports and materials related to the Project Funding and administration needs.

 

Selection Process

 

The position will be advertised following the open competitive method prescribed by the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers 2023 noting that at least 3 qualified CVs would be compared and documented. Applicants will be assessed on (their) Resume as submitted and any supporting documentation.

Applicants who do not pass Mandatory criteria requirement will not be evaluated further.

Applicants passing mandatory criteria requirements will be assigned points on presented Desirable Criteria. 

The Project Management Unit and stakeholders will then interview highest ranked individuals. Interviews will assess the strengths and weaknesses of candidates.

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Consultoría para aplicar control de calidad de vuelos fotogramétricos, MDS y MDT y ortoimágenes.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPyD-470659-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden la supervisión, verificación progresiva, control de calidad externo y validación técnica de los productos cartográficos básicos generados por el contrato de producción cartográfica del Proyecto. La firma consultora deberá revisar la correcta aplicación del aseguramiento de calidad del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y realizar las comprobaciones independientes adicionales que resulten necesarias, en gabinete y, cuando corresponda, en campo, para verificar la conformidad de los insumos, procesos, productos intermedios y productos finales con las especificaciones técnicas, estándares y criterios de aceptación aplicables.

El alcance comprende, principalmente, los vuelos fotogramétricos con captura de imágenes aéreas y datos LiDAR; puntos de fotocontrol y comprobación; orientación de imágenes y aerotriangulación; ajuste, filtrado y clasificación de nubes de puntos LiDAR; Modelos Digitales de Superficie (MDS) y Modelos Digitales del Terreno (MDT); y mosaicos de ortoimágenes digitales verdaderas (true-orthos), así como la documentación técnica, metadatos, formatos, certificados de calidad y demás respaldos asociados. La producción objeto de supervisión cubre aproximadamente 48,196.00 km² del territorio nacional, diferenciados en zona urbana (2,896.70 km²) y zona rural (45,299.30 km²). Los Servicios tendrán una duración de doce (12) meses calendario, conforme al alcance y condiciones establecidos en los Términos de Referencia (TDR). Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los TDR.

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. La firma consultora deberá acreditar trayectoria institucional en servicios relacionados con información geoespacial, cartografía, geodesia, fotogrametría aérea, teledetección, LiDAR, modelos digitales de elevaciones, ortoimágenes, control de calidad cartográfica, supervisión técnica o validación de productos geoespaciales. Deberá demostrar una experiencia general mínima de ocho (8) años y haber ejecutado satisfactoriamente al menos cinco (5) contratos relacionados con estos servicios durante los últimos ocho (8) años.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) contratos de naturaleza comparable ejecutados satisfactoriamente durante los últimos ocho (8) años. En conjunto, dichas experiencias deberán incluir: (i) al menos dos (2) contratos con actividades de supervisión, auditoría técnica, QA/QC, validación o aceptación de productos fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR; (ii) al menos un (1) proyecto de cobertura nacional, subnacional extensa, regional o territorialmente continua; y (iii) al menos un (1) proyecto que haya comprendido productos LiDAR y modelos digitales de elevaciones, además de ortoimágenes u ortofotos. Un mismo contrato podrá acreditar más de una condición cuando su alcance lo demuestre de manera verificable. La experiencia en producción cartográfica será considerada únicamente cuando evidencie funciones sustantivas de aseguramiento o control de calidad sobre los productos generados.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad para ejecutar revisiones concurrentes y especializadas por bloques, productos o frentes de trabajo; aplicar procedimientos de QA/QC; gestionar grandes volúmenes de imágenes aéreas, nubes de puntos LiDAR, MDS, MDT y ortoimágenes; y mantener trazabilidad documental, control de versiones y seguimiento de observaciones y subsanaciones. Deberá acreditar disponibilidad de recursos computacionales, software, licencias, infraestructura de procesamiento y almacenamiento, herramientas especializadas y mecanismos seguros de intercambio y respaldo de información, así como capacidad organizativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría y cumplir los tiempos de revisión previstos.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la escala y complejidad de los Servicios. Se considerará especialmente la experiencia en revisión y validación de planes de vuelo, cobertura y GSD, GNSS/IMU, control terrestre, aerotriangulación, ajuste y clasificación LiDAR, MDS/MDT, ortorrectificación, ortoimágenes verdaderas, exactitud posicional, completitud, consistencia radiométrica, formatos, metadatos y trazabilidad documental, así como la capacidad para coordinar técnicamente con el Contratante y el Proveedor del Servicio de producción preservando la independencia del control de calidad externo.

La firma consultora deberá actuar con independencia técnica respecto del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y declarar cualquier vínculo contractual, societario, comercial, técnico o profesional que pueda comprometer la objetividad de la supervisión. Los Servicios se prestarán en idioma español, en modalidad combinada de gabinete y, cuando corresponda, actividades presenciales o verificaciones de campo. La firma adjudicataria deberá disponer o establecer una oficina local en Santo Domingo durante la ejecución de la consultoría.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección y no deberán presentarse CV en esta etapa.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia general y específica, capacidad técnica y de gestión de acuerdo con los criterios indicados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, superficie o cobertura territorial, componentes fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR comprendidos, funciones de QA/QC, supervisión o validación realizadas, criterios o estándares de calidad aplicados, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado. Para acreditar las experiencias no será necesario presentar el contrato completo; podrán aportarse únicamente las páginas pertinentes del contrato, certificaciones, actas de recepción, constancias de conformidad, informes finales aprobados u otra documentación equivalente emitida o validada por el cliente o contratante que permita verificar la experiencia declarada.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales, recursos permanentes, infraestructura computacional, software y mecanismos de gestión y control de calidad relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Declaración de independencia técnica y ausencia de conflictos de interés que puedan afectar la objetividad de la consultoría, con el compromiso de informar al Contratante cualquier posible conflicto que se identifique durante el proceso de selección o la ejecución del contrato.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial”, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), en las que se establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

El Consultor será seleccionado conforme al método de Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo (SBCC/QCBS), de acuerdo con las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

Los TDR podrán solicitarse, sin costo, mediante comunicación dirigida al correo electrónico antes indicado, haciendo constar en el asunto la referencia del proceso, o descargarse desde el enlace correspondiente a este proceso, publicado en el Portal de Transparencia del Ministerio de la Presidencia: https://minpre.gob.do/transparencia/compras-y-contrataciones/contratacion-de-consultoria-para-aplicar-control-de-calidad-de-vuelos-fotogrametricos-mds-y-mdt-y-ortoimagenes-ref-do-mepyd-470659-cs-qcbs/.

Las expresiones de interés deben enviarse por escrito a la siguiente dirección (en persona, por correo o por correo electrónico) hasta el 26 de octubre de 2026, a las 4:00 p. m. (hora de la República Dominicana).

Financement :

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET (AMI) N° SN-MEN-560754-CS-QCBS/C_PAPSE_240

RECRUTEMENT D'UN CABINET DE VERIFICATEUR INDEPENDANT CHARGE DE L'EVALUATION DES CONTRATS DE PERFORMANCE (CDP) DES DAARA

Pays

République du Sénégal

Emprunteur

République du Sénégal

Secteur

Ministère de l’Education nationale (MEN)

Nom du Projet

Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du système Educatif (PAPSE)

Numéro du Projet

P169916

Mode de Financement

Crédit IDA 70440-SN 

Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP)

Coordination PAPSE

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

  1. Le Sénégal a obtenu dans le secteur de l’Education un financement de la Banque mondiale d'un montant équivalant à cent millions (100 000 000) $ USD pour financer le Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant « Cabinet de vérificateur indépendant chargé de l'évaluation des Contrats de Performance (CDP) des daara. »
  2. Les services de consultant (« Services ») permettront de recruter un cabinet indépendant chargé de vérifier, de manière fiable, traçable et documentée, les résultats déclarés par les daara et leurs IEF au titre des Contrats de Performance, au regard des indicateurs de performance définis dans ces contrats, et de produire un avis de vérification servant de base aux décisions de financement fondées sur les résultats.

De façon spécifique le cabinet sera chargé de:

  • vérifier l’exactitude des valeurs déclarées pour chacun des indicateurs de performance inscrits dans les CDP, par rapport aux valeurs réellement constatées ;
  • vérifier l’existence, la disponibilité, la complétude et la fiabilité des sources de vérification prévues par les CDP : registres d’inscription et de présence, cahiers journaux, résultats d’évaluations pédagogiques, registres sanitaires, registres et rapports de cantine, arrêté et procès-verbaux du CGD, rapports d’activités ;
  • contre-vérifier sur le terrain la réalité des résultats déclarés, par observation directe, recomptage, entretiens et contre-évaluation d’un échantillon de ndongo daara ;
  • déterminer, pour chaque structure vérifiée, le taux d’atteinte de chaque indicateur et le taux global d’atteinte du CDP, selon une méthode de calcul documentée, uniforme et reproductible ;
  • documenter les écarts entre résultats déclarés et résultats vérifiés, en analyser les causes et en apprécier l’incidence sur la validation des résultats ;
  • apprécier la fiabilité de la chaîne de production, de consolidation et de remontée des données de performance, et identifier les maillons faibles du dispositif ;
  • formuler des recommandations opérationnelles, hiérarchisées et assorties de responsables et de délais, en vue d’améliorer la qualité des données déclarées et l’atteinte des résultats ;
  • émettre, pour chaque cycle de vérification, un avis de vérification sur les résultats déclarés, exploitable par l’UGP pour la validation des décaissements fondés sur les résultats.

 

3. Le Coordonnateur du Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE) invite les firmes (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils disposent des qualifications requises et de l’expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdits services. À ce titre, les dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt devront comporter au moins: (i) une présentation générale de la firme (brochures, statut juridique, etc.) ; (ii) des références pertinentes concernant l’exécution de missions similaires, dûment justifiées ; (iii) une description de l’expérience générale et spécifique de la firme, incluant le nombre d’années d’expérience ; (iv) une présentation de l’organisation managériale et technique, y compris l’organigramme, les ressources humaines clés, ainsi que les moyens logistiques et techniques disponibles.

4. Les firmes intéressées peuvent obtenir les termes de référence (TDR) en envoyant leur demande à l’adresse électronique suivante : bm.papse@education.sn .

5. La liste restreinte comprendra un minimum de trois (3) et un maximum de six (6) cabinets.

6. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants intéressés que les dispositions relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts telles que décrites dans les paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 et suivants, du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », daté du 1er Juillet 2016 révisé en septembre 2025, sont applicables.

7. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés. 

8. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode « Sélection de Consultants Fondée sur la Qualité et sur le Coût (SFQC) » conformément aux dispositions décrites dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés et qui sera expressément énoncé dans la Demande de Propositions (DP).

9. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations complémentaires à l’adresse suivante : PAPSE, 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor-Téléphone : (+221) 33 820 74 71-email : bm.papse@education.sn, tous les jours ouvrables de 9h30mn à 16h30mn TU.

10. Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées à l’adresse suivante : PAPSE au 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor-Téléphone : (+221) 33 820 74 71–ou par email : bm.papse@education.sn, adressé au Coordonnateur du PAPSE, avec la mention « AMI N° SN-MEN-560754-CS-QCBS/C_PAPSE_240 - Cabinet de vérificateur indépendant chargé de l'évaluation des Contrats de Performance (CDP) des daara», au plus tard  le lundi 19 octobre 2026 à 11 h00mn TU.

description:
AVIS DE PUBLICATION DE LA DEMANDE DE COTATION N° CI-PADCI-571937-NC-RFQ-26 POUR LA SELECTION D’UNE AGENCE DE COMMUNICATION POUR LE DEVELOPPEMENT DE CONTENUS DE COMMUNICATION SPECIFIQUEMENT ADAPTE POUR EDUQUER ET SENSIBILISER A L'UTILISATION DES SERVICES PUBLICS NUMERIQUES.

Le Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), mis en œuvre par le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation, invite les entreprises et agences de communication intéressées à soumettre leurs offres dans le cadre de la Demande de Cotation relative à la :

« Sélection d’une agence de communication pour le développement de contenus de communication spécifiquement adaptés pour éduquer et sensibiliser à l’utilisation des services publics numériques ».

1. Objet de la consultation

La présente consultation porte sur la sélection d’une agence de communication chargée de concevoir, produire, mettre en œuvre, piloter et évaluer une stratégie intégrée de communication et de sensibilisation visant à favoriser l’appropriation et l’utilisation durable des services publics numériques.

 

2. Financement

La présente consultation est financée dans le cadre du Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale. Le PADCI est financé selon le mécanisme de Financement des Projets d’Investissement (IPF).

 

3. Conditions de participation

La participation est ouverte aux agences de communication légalement constituées, disposant des capacités techniques, professionnelles, administratives et financières nécessaires à l’exécution des prestations, objet de la présente consultation.

Le soumissionnaire devra notamment être en mesure de mobiliser une équipe comprenant au minimum un Chef de Projet/Directeur de mission, un Expert en communication institutionnelle et digitale, un Directeur artistique/Graphiste, un Chef de contenu/Rédacteur et un Community Manager. Les CV des experts clés devront être joints à l’offre technique.

4. Retrait du dossier

Le dossier de Demande de Cotation peut être retiré gratuitement auprès de :

Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Accélération Digital en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI)
Abidjan Angré 8ème Tranche, Cité les Elites II, non loin du Fast Food Chicken Nation

Voir la Cellule Passation des Marchés

Tél : (+225) 07 08 32 89 34/ 07 09 46 99 70

Email : ju.koffi@telecom.gouv.ci  avec copie obligatoire à gn.kouame@telecom.gouv.ci padci@telecom.gouv.ci
à compter de la date de publication du dossier, aux jours et heures ouvrables notamment du lundi au vendredi de 8 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 17 heures, Temps Universel.

Le retrait du dossier ne sera plus autorisé à compter du troisième (3ème) jour précédant la date limite de remise des offres.

La présente publication est faite à l’attention de toute agence de communication intéressée et répondant aux conditions de participation définies dans le dossier de consultation.

5. Constitution du dossier de candidature

 

Veuillez soumettre un dossier de candidature complet comprenant les pièces suivantes :

  • une copie du Registre de Commerce et du Crédit Mobilier (RCCM) de l’entreprise ;
  • une attestation de situation fiscale délivrée par les services fiscaux compétents ;
  • une attestation de mise à jour délivrée par la Caisse Nationale de Prévoyance Sociale (CNPS) ;
  • une fiche signalétique détaillée de l’entreprise comprenant :
  • une description de l’entreprise, de ses activités, de ses produits et services.
  • Le profil du dirigeant et des membres clés de l’équipe ;
  • Les moyens humains et matériels dont dispose l’entreprise ;
  • Les références de l’entreprise en matière de réalisation de prestations similaires (Attestation de Bonne Exécution) ;
  • L’agrément délivré par le Conseil Supérieur la Publicité (CSP).

 

6. Date et heure limites de dépôt des plis

Les offres doivent être déposées au plus tard leVendredi 02 octobre 2026 à 09H30, sous pli fermé, avec la mention : « Consultation de Prestataire N°CI-PADCI-571937-NC-RFQ-26 pour la sélection d’une agence de communication pour le développement de contenus de communication spécifiquement adaptés pour éduquer et sensibiliser à l’utilisation des services publics numériques ».

Le dépôt des offres devra faire l’objet d’un enregistrement sur la fiche de réception des offres tenue à cet effet au service Passation des marchés du PADCI.

7. Ouverture des plis

L’ouverture des offres aura lieu en séance publique le Vendredi 02 octobre 2026 à 09H30 dans les locaux du PADCI sis à la 8ème Tranche, non loin du Fast Food Chicken Nation Cité les Elites II, Email : ju.koffi@telecom.gouv.ci  avec copie obligatoire à gn.kouame@telecom.gouv.ci; padci@telecom.gouv.ci,  Tel : (+225) 07 08 32 89 34 / 07 09 46 99 70.

Non-Consulting Services
 

Project Title

Southeast Asia Regional Program on Combating Marine Plastics (SEA-MaP)

Grant Number

E 051/P175659

Reference Number

ID-ASEAN-573181-NC-RFQ

Activity Title

Event Organizer (EO) to Support the 8th SEA-MaP Project Steering Committee (PSC) Meeting

Date

1 October 2026

 

Dear Supplier,

1.   The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Southeast Asia Regional Program on Combating Marine Plastics (SEA-MaP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to procure an event organizer (EO) to support the 8th SEA-MaP Project Steering Committee (PSC) Meeting.

 

2.    The objective of this Request for Quotation (RFQ) is to seek a highly qualified EO to plan and support the delivery of the 1-day event of 8th PSC Meeting of SEA-MaP on 2 December 2026. The selected EO shall provide coordination and logistical support to deliver the 1-day event in coordination with the SEA-MaP Project Management Unit (PMU).

 

3.    You are invited to submit your price quotation for the provision of the following services:

Item Name/Services Required

Qty

Location of Delivery

Timing of Delivery

Deliver event organizing services for the 8th PSC Meeting of SEA-MaP (1-day meeting). The scope of services broadly refers to:
(i) Event management for the meeting and site visits. This includes venue, accommodation, token of appreciation, and other logistical matters;
(ii) Documentation and reporting

 

The event will approximately be attended by 40 participants.

This is a one-off service

Manila, Philippines

December 2026

           

Additional note: the 8th PSC Meeting is scheduled to be held back-to-back with the SEA-MaP 3rd High-Level Policy Dialogue (HLPD-3) and Project Closing Event, which is a 2-day event planned in late November/early December 2026. The participants joining the 8th PSC Meeting are eligible to participate in the Regional Event. Accordingly, the selected EO will coordinate with the Hotel, appointed vendors, and the contractor managing the Regional Event on the relevant logistical arrangements.

 

4.    The estimated duration of the assignment is from November 2026 to January 2027 (may be subject to adjustments, if necessary). Further details of the services required and other relevant documents, are available via the following link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bM9icDxOr5JYWJMBQsm2SWKdNPXVIz5B/view?usp=sharing

 

5.    This RFQ invites suppliers to submit a quote that is inclusive of all the items/services required under this RFQ and specified in the Terms of Reference (TOR) attached to this RFQ. Price quotations will be evaluated for all the items together and contract awarded to the supplier offering the lowest evaluated total price for the complete package, if substantially responsive to the requirements.

 

6.    The price quotation may be submitted by post or electronically to the address below:

Attention/Name: Procurement of the SEA-MaP PMU

Southeast Asia Program on Marine Plastics (SEA-MaP) Project Management Unit

1st Floor, The ASEAN Secretariat Heritage Building

70A Jalan Sisingamangaraja, Jakarta 12110

Email: seamap.admin@asean.org

 

7.    The deadline for submission of your quotation at the address indicated in above Paragraph 6 is 12 October 2026 at 17.00 Jakarta time (GMT+7). Late submissions will not be accepted.

 

8.    Your quotation must be submitted in the English language and should be accompanied by adequate technical documentation and other pertinent information in English.

 

9.    Your quotation should be submitted as per the instructions contained in this RFQ and in accordance with the Contract.

 

10.    PRICES: Suppliers must submit all-inclusive fees in USD, including lump sum travel and subsistence costs, as applicable. Suppliers are requested to give their best and final prices as negotiations are not allowed.

 

11.    EVALUATION OF QUOTATIONS: In evaluating the quotations, the Purchaser will determine for each quotation the evaluated price by adjusting the price quotation by making any correction for any arithmetical errors as follows:

a.     where there is a discrepancy between amounts in figures and in words, the amount in words will govern;

description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

No.055/REOI/MINDDEVEL/PROLOG/PIU/PSM/ESN 2026 OF 01st  OCTOBER 2026  FOR THE RECRUITMENT OF A LOCAL SUPPORT ORGANISATION (LSO) FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT, DISSEMINATION AND MONITORING OF A GRIEVANCE REDRESS MECHANISM (GRM), INCLUDING GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE (GBV), IN THE NORTH-WEST REGION UNDER THE LOCAL GOVERNANCE AND RESILIENT COMMUNITIES PROJECT (PROLOG) 

  1. The Republic of Cameroon has secured financing from the International Development Association (IDA) to cover the cost of the Local Governance and Resilient Communities Project (PROLOG), and intends to use part of the proceeds to finance consultancy services for the establishment, dissemination and monitoring of a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), including Gender-Based Violence (GBV), in the North-West Region under the Local Governance and Resilient Communities Project (PROLOG).
  2. The mission is intended to continue a process that has already been initiated, with the objective of providing holistic coverage of all areas hosting infrastructure at the regional, municipal and community levels, across all ongoing financing windows.
  3. The consultancy services covered by this Request for Expressions of Interest concern Local Support Organisations (LSOs) which, in accordance with the applicable regulations, will be responsible for establishing, operationalising and disseminating the GRM, including GBV-related mechanisms, at the regional, local and community levels in twenty-three (23) councils in the North-West Region.
  4. The Consultant/Firm will be responsible for: 
  • Identifying and training community focal points in villages and neighbourhoods hosting sub-projects. These focal points shall be locally resident individuals of good standing, capable of learning and communicating accurate information in French and the local language on the GRM, and able to maintain confidentiality. As indicated above, they will work in collaboration with the resource persons selected by the communities in each village, as well as with the contractors’ QHSE officers, in carrying out awareness-raising activities and collecting grievances;
  • Raising awareness among and training communities living around construction sites on the use of the mapping of potential referral services available in the work areas, particularly on appropriate entry points for different groups of women, including girls and adolescents;
  • Training and raising awareness among site personnel of contractors responsible for carrying out the works on the Code of Conduct and the procedures for handling complaints relating to GBV/SEA/SH and VAC;
  • Informing and raising awareness among communities, using all appropriate communication channels, including leaflets, suggestion boxes, posters, picture boxes, community radio stations and local languages, as well as the project toll-free number, on the GRM (including the procedure, complaint submission points and processing timelines) and the content of the Code of Conduct;
  • Training GRM focal points and members of local and regional grievance committees in the effective management of ordinary grievances and grievances relating to Gender-Based Violence, while ensuring strict compliance with the survivor’s right to confidentiality;
  • Supporting communities, where necessary, in submitting grievances, including providing assistance with their formulation and drafting; informing village chiefs of the schedule of community awareness-raising activities on grievance management in the project areas and participating in those activities;
  • Organising, through the focal points, awareness-raising, advocacy and behaviour change communication activities on GBV and VAC, with a focus on the risks associated with infrastructure construction works and the influx of labour;
  • Ensuring the production, provision and dissemination, to members of local and regional grievance committees and community focal points, of communication and awareness-raising materials on the GRM and GBV.  The designs/templates for these materials will be provided by the Project;
  • Updating the GBV referral pathways for the various councils, based on data available from PROLOG or other World Bank-financed projects;
  • Ensuring the ethical and safe management of potential survivors, in accordance with the provisions set out in the PROLOG survivor assistance protocol.
  1. The duration of the mission shall be nine (9) months, commencing on the date of signature of the Service Order authorising commencement of the services.
  2. The Terms of Reference (ToR) for the mission are available at the address indicated below.
  3. The National Coordinator of the Local Governance and Resilient Communities Project (PROLOG) hereby invites Local Support Organisations (LSOs) (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services.
  4. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services, including references relating to the execution of similar contracts.
  5. The main selection criteria are as follows:
  • General criteria;     
  • Technical criteria;
  • Qualifications and competence of the Team Leader.
  1. Interested Consultants’ attention is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, revised in September 2025, which set out the World Bank’s policy on conflicts of interest.
  2. A Consultant will be selected using the “Consultant Qualifications Selection (CQS)” method, as described in paragraph 7.11 of the “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, revised in September 2025.

Further information may be obtained at the address indicated below during working hours, from 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (local time).

  1. Expressions of interest must be submitted exclusively by email in a single submission to the address indicated below, no later than fourteen (14) days from the date of publication of this notice in the Cameroon Tribune daily newspaper, i.e. 16th october 2026, at 3:30 p.m. (local time), and shall comprise the following documents:
  • A detailed submission letter highlighting the Consultant’s specific capabilities that will contribute to the successful performance of the mission, as well as its collaboration with key stakeholders; documentary evidence of legal existence and capacity to enter into contracts;
  • A presentation and organisation of the Firm;
  • The Consultant’s general references in implementing community development support activities, and evidence of qualified, experienced and adequately staffed human resources;
  • References demonstrating the successful support provided to one or more councils in establishing and operating a GRM, including the prevention and mitigation of GBV risks;
  • References demonstrating experience in carrying out at least two similar missions, and a thorough knowledge of the North-West Region and the councils in which the mission will be implemented;
  • Technical references demonstrating a geographical presence in the North-West Region and credibility among beneficiaries, as evidenced by certificates of satisfactory performance for similar services.
  • Evidence of sufficient cash resources to pre-finance the activities pending payment for the Services;
  • An understanding of the sociological characteristics of the various communities and personnel capable of communicating in the local language;
  • The Curriculum Vitae (CV) of the proposed Team Leader, highlighting similar experience, dated less than three (3) months prior to submission, signed and indicating his/her full contact details (postal address, telephone number, email address, etc.), together with certified copies of diplomas, certificates and/or employment certificates, as well as copies of similar contracts (first and signature pages). 

NB: For validation, each reference must be justified by the following elements:

  • A copy of the first page and last page signed. These references must be clear and legible;
  • Copies of acceptance reports, or certificates of satisfactory completion issued by the Contracting Authority or its services, or certificates confirming the release of performance security.

The submission shall bear the following wording:

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

No.055/REOI/MINDDEVEL/PROLOG/PIU/PSM/ESN 2026 OF 01st OCTOBER 2026 FOR THE RECRUITMENT OF A LOCAL SUPPORT ORGANISATION (LSO) FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT, DISSEMINATION AND MONITORING OF A GRIEVANCE REDRESS MECHANISM (GRM), INCLUDING GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE (GBV), IN THE NORTH-WEST REGION UNDER THE LOCAL GOVERNANCE AND RESILIENT COMMUNITIES PROJECT (PROLOG)

                                                                                                                    TERMS OF REFERENCE

Provision of Consulting Services for the Planning and Design Development of the Dvin and Dashtadem Museum and Cultural Sites under the Implementation of TRIP-DP-01 and TRIP-DP-02 Subprojects in the Republic of Armenia

  1. BACKGROUND

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Program (TRIP) aims to promote Armenia’s tourism potential through targeted infrastructure and non-infrastructure investments in a number of regions. The Program will support seven out of the twenty identified tourism clusters, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, cultural, educational, and ecotourism in the regions of Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Tavush, and Syunik. Within the framework of the Program, access to the identified clusters will be improved, and infrastructure at tourism destinations will be developed. The Program also seeks to leverage Armenia’s natural resources and human potential by developing the entrepreneurial and professional skills of residents of neighboring communities, with the aim of maximizing employment opportunities. In addition, the TRIP Program is aligned with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment to these tourism clusters.

The infrastructure investment component of the TRIP Program includes the construction of new public buildings, including museum buildings; the restoration and preservation of historical and cultural monuments; the revitalization of the urban environment of historic towns and villages, including the restoration of building façades, public spaces, museums, and roads; as well as the improvement of cultural and natural heritage sites, including ensuring their accessibility and appropriate presentation.

Under the World Bank’s Local Economy and Infrastructure Development (LEID) Project, which preceded the Tourism and Regional Infrastructure (TRIP) Program, designs for the museum buildings at the Dvin archaeological site and Dashtadem Fortress were developed and approved in 2024. Based on these designs, construction works will be implemented under the TRIP Program.

Under the TRIP Program, in parallel with the work of the museum specialist, the design documentation will be updated, the cost estimate will be recalculated based on current prices, and the accompanying documentation will be updated, including the Architectural Planning Assignment (APA), technical specifications, expert examination conclusions, approvals, and other relevant documents. The revision of the design will be carried out through the conclusion of a direct contract with the original design author.

At present, within the framework of the TRIP Program, it is necessary to develop conceptual approaches for the organization of the museum environment and exhibitions for the museums at the Dvin and Dashtadem archaeological sites, including exhibition design, taking into consideration their respective missions, visions, and objectives.

 

  1. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to:

  • Dvin: Present the archaeological museum of Dvin and the preserved monuments of the archaeological site of the “Capital of Dvin” to tourists by creating a culturally rich and, at the same time, scientific and educational environment that is historically grounded while incorporating modern amenities and design, archaeological exhibits, and historical reconstructions.
    Proposed museum type: Archaeological Museum.
  • Dashtadem: Determine the type and content of the Dashtadem Museum; develop and collect exhibits; plan interactive activities and festivals; recreate historical events using the entire area of the large fortress; and incorporate all structures of the restored fortress into programs featuring reenactments of historical episodes and military-sport games.
    Proposed museum type: Military-Historical Museum, though a broader historical scope could also be suggested (subject to further discussion).

Expected Results of the Assignment

The expected result of the assignment is the establishment of operational archaeological and military-historical museums at Dvin and Dashtadem, respectively, featuring:

  • Exhibitions developed on a sound scientific basis;
  • Modern lighting and design;
  • Information delivered through multimedia tools;
  • A management system compliant with modern museum standards, including digitized databases and appropriate conditions for the preservation, conservation/restoration, and display of exhibits;
  • Increased tourist visitation and increased tourism-generated revenues.

 

  1. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The scope of consulting services is divided into three phases:

Phase 1. Preliminary Study, Collection Assessment and Documentation, and Development of the Exhibition Concept and Layout Plans

This phase shall include a preliminary study of the sites and museums, assessment and documentation of the existing collections, and development of the conceptual approach to the organization of the exhibitions and the relevant layout plans.

Phase 2. Development of Museum Content, Exhibition Planning, and Development of Exhibition Design and Lighting Schemes

This phase shall include the development of the museums’ content, exhibition planning, and the development of exhibition design and lighting schemes for both interior and exterior spaces, in accordance with the requirements applicable to the “Design Developement” stage.

Phase 3. Integration of the Approved Solutions into the Museum Design Documentation, Capacity Building, Support for the Development of Management Policies, and Final Reporting

This phase shall include:

  • Integration of the solutions approved under Phase 2 into the design documentation of the museums;
  • Capacity building for museum staff;
  • Support for the development of museum management policies; and
  • Preparation and submission of the final report.

The interim and final deliverables shall be submitted to the Armenian Territorial Development Fund (ATDF) (the Client) for review and comments.

Key Stakeholders

The key stakeholders of the assignment are:

  • The Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Armenia, Tourism Committee (MoE Tourism Committee);
  • The Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports of the Republic of Armenia (MoESCS);
  • The World Bank;
  • The “Service for the Protection of Historical Environment and Cultural Museum-Reservations” State Non-Commercial Organization; and
  • Relevant local self-government and state administration bodies.

 

PHASE 1. PRELIMINARY STUDY, COLLECTION ASSESSMENT AND DOCUMENTATION, AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE EXHIBITION CONCEPT AND LAYOUT PLANS

Task 1. Preliminary Study

  • Study the key objectives and priorities of the Program, as well as the principles governing the organization and development of similar museums.
  • Review the existing collections and exhibits; review and update the collection inventory; and assess the physical condition of the collections, the level of documentation, the potential for expanding the exhibitions, and opportunities for the application of modern technologies and best practices.
  • Update or create object records/passports for the collection items in the Collection Management System (CMS) or other appropriate information platforms.
  • Review the design documentation for the Dvin and Dashtadem museums and assess all spaces suitable for exhibition purposes.
  • Conduct inception meetings with the museum (and archaeological site) management and relevant departments to discuss existing challenges and perspectives, with the participation of all relevant stakeholders. The Client (ATDF) shall be notified in advance of the scheduled meetings.
  • Prepare and submit to the Client a brief report summarizing the work carried out, meetings held, and recommendations and proposals received from stakeholders.

 

Task 2. Collection Assessment and Documentation

For Dvin:

  • Classify the exhibits and archaeological finds into two lists: items intended for display and items to be placed in storage for further study and/or conservation/restoration.
  • For the items intended for display, identify their proposed display locations, such as exhibition halls, entrance/lobby areas, outdoor platforms, excavated pits protected by glass covers or shelters, and other appropriate locations.
  • Assess the informational signage and other small-scale architectural elements included in the design, and provide recommendations on whether they should be retained or modified.
  • Prepare preliminary classified lists of exhibits and archaeological finds according to their proposed display locations (e.g., exhibition hall, entrance/lobby, outdoor areas, archaeological site recreation/rest area, etc.).

 

For Dashtadem:

  • Identify, collect information on, and inventory all potential exhibits and archaeological finds, including their current locations and the organizations holding them. Classify them into two lists: items intended for display and items to be placed in storage for further study and/or conservation/restoration, indicating the current location of each exhibit and the arrangements made for obtaining/accessing it.
  • Propose a list of exhibits to be reconstructed and/or reproduced, together with sketches or photographs of relevant examples.
  • Assess the informational signage and other small-scale architectural elements included in the design, and provide recommendations on whether they should be retained or modified.
  • Prepare preliminary classified lists of exhibits and archaeological finds according to their proposed display locations (e.g., exhibition hall, entrance/lobby, outdoor areas, archaeological site recreation/rest area, etc.).

Task 3. Development of the Exhibition Concept and Layout Plans

For Dvin and Dashtadem:

  • Develop the exhibition concept, including proposed display locations, visitor circulation routes, descriptions, justification of the selected exhibition schemes, principles for organizing the interior spaces, the proposed design and lighting style, the placement of information panels and exhibit labels, and other relevant elements.
  • Develop exhibition layout plans and/or wall elevations, assigning identification numbers to the displayed items. Prepare a numbered list of exhibits, indicating for each exhibit its name, historical information, and photograph.
  • Develop preliminary interior and exterior lighting schemes.
  • Propose design options for furnishing the exhibition halls, including the appearance, materials, and mounting/installation methods of display pedestals, tables, shelving, lighting fixtures, and other furnishings.

Consolidated Deliverables for Tasks 1–3

The findings and outputs of Tasks 1–3 shall be consolidated into two comprehensive reports, one for Dvin and one for Dashtadem, with the following structure:

  • Summary description of the work carried out;
  • Museum organization concept, exhibition and lighting schemes, and classified list of exhibits;
  • Visitor routes for viewing the key monuments and displayed exhibits:
    • For Dvin: An integrated visitor route covering the archaeological site and the museum, indicating the entrance, exit, all visitor stops, and the visitor-use scheme for supporting facilities, including the ticket office, restrooms, café, library, recreation area, viewing platform, etc.
    • For Dashtadem: An integrated visitor route covering the Great Wall, fortress, other historical structures, and the museum, indicating the entrance, exit, all visitor stops, and the visitor-use scheme for supporting facilities, including the ticket office, restrooms, pavilions, etc.
