Duration and Timeline of Phase 1

Duration: 60 calendar days

Implementation period: 60 calendar days from the day following the date of signing of the Contract, including the process of review, comments, and approval of the reports.

Deliverables for Phase 1

  • Summary Report No. 1 (Dvin), with annexes;
  • Summary Report No. 2 (Dashtadem), with annexes.

Indicators of Achievement for Phase 1

  • Approval of the Summary Reports by the Client.

 

PHASE 2. DEVELOPMENT OF MUSEUM CONTENT, EXHIBITION PLANNING, AND DEVELOPMENT OF EXHIBITION DESIGN AND LIGHTING SCHEMES FOR INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR SPACES

 

!!! The activities under Phase 2 shall be developed in accordance with the solutions approved under Phase 1.

!!! Any new concept, idea, or solution shall be agreed with the Client in advance.

!!! The outputs shall be developed as separate packages for Dvin and Dashtadem.

Task 1. Development of Museum Content and Exhibition Planning

  • Define the overall exhibition concept, the key interpretation themes, and the expected learning outcomes for visitors, ensuring their alignment with the cultural and historical significance of the archaeological site.
  • Prepare curatorial notes and research dossiers for significant exhibits. At the same time, define the key interpretation themes and sub-themes that will connect the exhibits to meaningful narratives and visitor experiences.
  • Develop the exhibition narrative structure, storylines, and educational content.
  • Develop the textual content of the exhibition, including labels, information panels, guides, and catalogues.
  • Develop all informational materials, exhibit labels, and other textual materials in Armenian and English, with the Armenian and English texts presented together on the same exhibit labels, posters, and other information panels.
  • Integrate the descriptive content of the exhibition into audio and video systems in order to enhance visitors’ understanding of and overall experience of the exhibition.

Task 2. Development of Exhibition Design and Lighting Schemes for Interior and Exterior Spaces

  • Develop a master plan incorporating the archaeological site, historical structures, and the museum, including:
    • The visitor routes approved under Phase 1, indicating the entrance, exit, and visitor stops, including historical structures and cultural sites; selected outdoor exhibits; posters and information signage; viewing platforms; pavilions; the museum’s main exhibition halls; temporary exhibition spaces; outdoor pavilions and recreation areas; cafés; restrooms; excavated areas; parking areas; and other relevant facilities;
    • A tourist route map developed on the basis of the master plan, with the potential for subsequent publication and use as a tourist map.
  • Develop layout plans and/or wall elevations for the placement of exhibits in the main exhibition hall and other areas, including entrance/lobby areas, passageways, corridors, and outdoor platforms, covering:
    • The location of each exhibit, exhibit identification number, exhibit name, photograph, and accompanying label text in Armenian and English;
    • Pedestals, supports, tables, display cases, shelving, and exhibit mounting/installation schemes;
    • Modular solutions enabling exhibits to be periodically replaced, temporary exhibitions to be organized, and the museum exhibition to be updated in the future.
  • Develop the detailed design of furniture and display equipment for all spaces included in the visitor routes, including exhibit pedestals, supports, display cases, shelves, etc., in accordance with the requirements of the “Design develoment” stage and with sufficient detail to enable a furniture manufacturer to prepare detailed shop drawings and manufacture the items based on the design.
  • Develop the exhibition lighting scheme and lighting scenarios, including specifications for lighting fixtures.
  • Develop audio-visual system schemes and equipment specifications.
  • Provide recommendations regarding other engineering systems, where applicable.
  • Provide a list of potential companies capable of manufacturing the proposed furniture and display equipment, together with their submitted price quotations, from at least three companies.

 

!!! Ensure that all exhibition supports, display cases, information panels, lighting systems, and digital/interactive elements comply with current international best practices in museology, accessibility, and preventive conservation of exhibits.

Additional Requirements for Dashtadem

  • Develop sketches and detailed descriptions of exhibits to be reproduced and/or reconstructed, including weapons, military equipment and clothing, tools, means of transportation, and other relevant items, based on the analysis of historical sources and/or archaeological finds.
  • Develop sketches of mannequins representing military personnel from different historical periods, including detailed designs and specifications of the respective uniforms /if a broader historical scope is accepted for Dashtadem, the sketches may also include examples from secular life/.
  • For the three outdoor pavilions representing the workshops of a medieval blacksmith, leatherworker, and carpenter, provide descriptions of the furnishings and equipment, illustrative sketches, dimensions, materials of manufacture, and other details sufficient to enable the procurement or fabrication of the required furnishings and equipment.

 

Duration and Timeline of Phase 2

Duration: 120 calendar days.

Implementation period: 180 calendar days from the day following the date of signing of the Contract, including the process of review, comments, and approval of the reports.

Deliverables for Phase 2

Package 1 – Dvin

The package shall include:

  • Master plan, visitor route, and design and content of information panels;
  • Tourist route map, ready for printing;
  • Exhibition layout plan, list of exhibits, and descriptions;
  • Lighting scheme, lighting scenarios, and specifications;
  • Audio-visual system schemes and equipment specifications;
  • Other recommendations.

Package 2 – Dashtadem

The package shall include:

  • Master plan, visitor route, and design and content of information panels;
  • Tourist route map, ready for printing;
  • Exhibition layout plan, list of exhibits, and descriptions;
  • Sketches of exhibits to be reproduced and reconstructed, descriptions of materials and methods of production, historical clothing and equipment patterns/templates, and mannequin sketches;
  • Sketches of the furnishings and equipment for the medieval blacksmith, leatherworker, and carpenter workshops, including fabrication instructions and other relevant details;
  • Lighting scheme, lighting scenarios, and specifications;
  • Audio-visual system schemes and equipment specifications;
  • Other recommendations.

Indicators of Achievement for Phase 2

  • Approval by the Client of both packages:
    • Package 1 – Dvin; and
    • Package 2 – Dashtadem.

 

PHASE 3. INTEGRATION OF APPROVED SOLUTIONS INTO THE MUSEUM DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, MUSEUM STAFF CAPACITY BUILDING AND SUPPORT FOR POLICY DEVELOPMENT, AND SUBMISSION OF THE FINAL REPORT

Task 1. Integration of the Solutions Approved under Phase 2 into the Museum Design Documentation

  • Develop Design Assignment No. 1, containing clear instructions regarding the changes, additions, and further developments to be incorporated into the design and cost-estimate documentation of the Dvin and Dashtadem museums. The assignment shall be substantiated by the schemes, specifications, and instructions approved under Phase 2.
  • Develop Design Assignment No. 2, containing clear requirements to be included in procurement requests for the acquisition and/or fabrication of furniture and reconstructed/reproduced exhibits. The assignment shall be substantiated by the design developed and approved under Phase 2, including sketches, schemes, specifications, quantities, and other relevant instructions.

Task 2. Museum Staff Capacity Building and Support for Policy Development

  • Organize training sessions and/or workshops for museum staff (at this stage, the staff of the “Service for the Protection of Historical Environment and Cultural Museum-Reservations” SNCO) on the following topics:
    • Best practices in exhibition curatorial work;
    • Collection registration and documentation;
    • Exhibition development and organization;
    • Improvement of institutional activities and processes, as applicable, including:
      • Collection Management Policy;
      • Collection Acquisition and Deaccession Policy;
      • Conservation and Preventive Care Policy;
      • Exhibition and Interpretation Policy;
      • Object Loan and Reproduction Policy;
      • Digitization and Information Access Policy.

Task 3. Submission of the Final Report

  • Prepare and submit the Final Report on the Consulting Services, which shall include:
    • A summary description of the work carried out;
    • The final, revised and proofread packages of all deliverables specified for all phases, submitted in electronic format and four (4) hard copies;
    • Minutes/proceedings of meetings, consultations, discussions, and training sessions conducted, including lists of participants;
    • Strategic recommendations aimed at ensuring the sustainability of the museum’s operations and supporting the further development of its institutional capacities.

 

Duration and Timeline of Phase 3

Duration: 40 calendar days.

Implementation period: 220 calendar days from the day following the date of signing of the Contract, including the process of review, comments, and approval of the reports.

Deliverables for Phase 3

  • Design Assignment No. 1 and Design Assignment No. 2 – Dvin;
  • Design Assignment No. 1 and Design Assignment No. 2 – Dashtadem;
  • Report on the training sessions conducted and support provided, signed by the head of the organization that received the training and/or support.

Indicators of Achievement for Phase 3

  • Approval by the Client of the submitted Design Assignments and the Report.

 

  1. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS, IMPLEMENTATION MECHANISMS AND ALLOCATION OF RESPONSIBILITIES
    1.  Language of Development
  • The deliverables envisaged under Phases 1–3 shall be prepared and submitted in Armenian.
  • Museum exhibit labels, texts for information panels, information delivered through audio-visual media, and other visitor guidance and interpretive textual materials shall be developed bilingually, in Armenian and English.
  • Training sessions and support shall be provided in Armenian, or with Armenian interpretation provided.
    1. Submission Formats and Supporting Materials

Each deliverable shall be submitted in both editable and non-editable formats and shall include:

  • Textual materials: MS Word and PDF;
  • Graphic materials: AutoCAD (or other appropriate graphic design software) and PDF;
  • Calculations, lists, specifications, and other tables: Excel, Word, and PDF formats.
    1. Criteria for Review and Acceptance of Submitted Work

Each deliverable shall be considered acceptable if it:

  • Fully complies with the scope of the assignment;
  • Consistently meets the required content, structure, and level of detail;
  • Is consistent with previously approved deliverables; and
  • Incorporates revisions made based on comments received from the Client and relevant stakeholders.
    1. Review and Approval Sequence

All deliverables shall be submitted and reviewed according to the following sequence:

  1. Initial submission by the Consultant to the Client (ATDF);
  2. Coordination with the MoE Tourism Committee and relevant stakeholders, including the MoESCS, World Bank, and other relevant authorities;
  3. Consolidated comments communicated to the Consultant through the ATDF;
  4. Submission by the Consultant of a revised version incorporating all comments, including the relevant revisions and/or clarifications;
  5. Obtaining “no objection” confirmation from the MoE Tourism Committee, MoESCS, World Bank, and other relevant authorities regarding the revised materials;
  6. Final approval by the Tourism Committee and acceptance by the ATDF.
    1. Review Periods
  • Each review stage shall not exceed three (3) weeks from the date of submission.
  • The Consultant shall be provided with one to two (1–2) weeks to incorporate comments and submit the revised version.
  • The duration of the review process, number of review iterations, and approval procedure shall be agreed upon during the inception stage.
    1. Scope of the Consultant’s Activities and Responsibilities

The Consultant shall be responsible for:

  • Collecting and studying historical data related to the two cultural sites; conducting site visits and field assessments; and collecting, studying, classifying, and supplementing information on exhibits related to the sites;
  • Cooperating with specialists in the cultural, museum, and archaeological fields; determining the types of the Dvin and Dashtadem museums (archaeological, historical, thematic, etc.) and agreeing the proposed museum types with the Client;
  • Studying and analyzing baseline data, existing materials, and approved design documentation;
  • Preparing conceptual/sketch proposals for the content, organization, and design of the exhibitions and agreeing them with the Client;
  • Developing and agreeing with the Client the design of the furnishing of the museum buildings, including exhibit pedestals, niches, supports, exhibition hall partitions, exhibits displayed in entrance/lobby areas, posters, signage, and other related elements;
  • Developing the lighting system and lighting scenarios for exhibition halls and other public spaces, and providing specifications for lighting fixtures;
  • Designing audio-visual systems for the museums and preparing audio and video guides;
  • Within the scope of its assignment, the museum specialist may propose changes to the functional designation of certain rooms, subject to agreement with the Client (e.g., auditorium/lecture hall, temporary exhibition hall, café, workshop/studio for children, etc.);
  • Organizing training sessions and providing support to museum staff;
  • Cooperating with the design organization under the coordination of the Client.

The Consultant shall be responsible for the timely delivery of high-quality outputs, as well as for effective communication and coordination of activities with the Client and the Program stakeholders.

The Consultant shall not be responsible for the physical collection or acquisition of archaeological objects and other exhibits. However, the Consultant shall provide recommendations regarding their selection, acquisition, scholarly interpretation, and display.

The Consultant shall prepare an Exhibit Identification and Acquisition Plan, specifying:

  • Proposed exhibits and collections;
  • Locations of the exhibits, potential acquisition opportunities, and preliminary arrangements;
  • Exhibits to be provided by archaeological expeditions, museums, state institutions, or private collections;
  • Exhibits requiring reproduction, reconstruction, illustration, modeling, or creation of a digital version;
  • Recommendations regarding the development of replicas, scale models, audiovisual materials, and interactive interpretation tools.

The Consultant’s recommendations shall not require changes to the architectural and/or structural solutions included in the Museum designs. Where recommendations concerning finishes or interior treatments are made, they shall be coordinated with the design author and the Client.

At the Client’s request, the Consultant shall prepare reports/presentations on visitor routes, exhibition schemes, and furniture/display design. The Consultant shall be prepared, under the coordination of the Client, to discuss the proposed solutions with the Design Team, stakeholders, and community representatives.

The Consultant shall participate in working meetings organized by the Client to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integration of the exhibition content and the interconnection of its various components.

The Consultant shall independently bear all costs associated with the provision of the consulting services, including:

  • Transportation costs;
  • Office and administrative expenses;
  • Costs related to organizing meetings;
  • Costs of interpretation and translation services;
  • Costs of printing and reproduction of documents.
    1.   Client Responsibilities and Scope of Activities

The Client shall ensure coordination among the Museum Specialist, the Designer, and all relevant stakeholders.

The Client shall coordinate the deliverables submitted for each phase with the MoESCS, MoE Tourism Committee, World Bank, and, as necessary, other relevant stakeholders. Upon obtaining the required coordination and approval from the MoE Tourism Committee, the Client shall accept the respective deliverable.

The deliverables of each phase shall be approved before proceeding to the activities of the subsequent phase. The approval timelines shall be agreed upon among the relevant stakeholders; however, as a general principle, they shall not exceed ten (10) working days.

Following the Client’s acceptance of proposals submitted by the Museum Specialist’s team that involve modifications to the lighting, audio-visual, and/or other engineering systems, such proposals shall be forwarded to the design authoring organization with instructions to incorporate them into the working design documentation and cost estimate.

The production of furniture, exhibit pedestals, and other soft elements shall be procured by the Client through a separate procurement process. The design proposals, sketches, and three-dimensional visualizations developed by the Museum Specialist shall contain sufficient information to enable the furniture manufacturer to prepare detailed shop drawings and manufacture the furniture and related elements.

    1. Intellectual Property Requirements

The Consultant shall be the author of the work prepared under this Terms of Reference, and the work shall constitute the Consultant’s intellectual property.

The Client shall be the owner of the accepted work and may use it at its discretion, in whole or in part. In the event that substantial modifications become necessary during the implementation period, the Client shall discuss such modifications with the Consultant.

The Client undertakes not to use the outputs of the work for other museums and/or buildings or structures of a different nature.

The Consultant shall not have the right to disseminate, publish, include in lectures, or present on other public platforms any interim outputs of the work until the work has been fully completed and formally accepted by the Client.

Any disputes not regulated under this section shall be resolved in accordance with the procedure established by the legislation of the Republic of Armenia.

 

  1. DATA, DOCUMENTS AND SUPPORT TO BE PROVIDED BY THE CLIENT

The Client shall provide the Consultant with the design documentation for the two museums, the lists of exhibits intended for display and storage at the Dvin Museum, and reports on archaeological excavations carried out at the Dashtadem Fortress site at different times.

The documents to be provided by the Client include:

  • Design and cost-estimate documentation package for the “Improvement of the Dvin Archaeological Site and Adjacent Area and Provision of Tourism Infrastructure” project
    Link to Google Drive
  • Design and cost-estimate documentation package for the “Partial Rehabilitation of Dashtadem Fortress, Establishment of a Museum, and Improvement of the Area Adjacent to the Monument” project
    Link to Google Drive
  • List of exhibits intended for display and storage at the Dvin Museum
    Link to Google Drive
  • Reports on archaeological excavations carried out at the Dashtadem Fortress site at different times
    Link to Google Drive

The Client shall support the Consultant in organizing necessary meetings and consultations, participate, as necessary, in meetings and discussions with stakeholders, and facilitate cooperation with the local community.

O Governo do Estado de Pernambuco firmou Contrato de Empréstimo nº 9678-BR com o Banco Internacional para Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD) para execução do PROJETO DE SANEAMENTO RURAL DE PERNAMBUCO – PROSAR/PE, e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos desse financiamento para contratação do seguinte serviço de consultoria:

“Contratação de empresa de consultoria para elaboração dos projetos básico e executivo para construção do novo edifício sede da Agência Pernambucana de Águas e Clima (APAC).”

Os serviços de consultoria (doravante "os Serviços") incluem: execução dos serviços técnicos especializados de:

 

1. ESTUDO DE ALTERNATIVAS CONSTRUTIVAS;

2. ELABORAÇÃO DE PROJETO BÁSICO DE ARQUITETURA, DE ENGENHARIA E PROJETOS COMPLEMENTARES;

3. ELABORAÇÃO DO PROJETO EXECUTIVO DE ARQUITETURA, ENGENHARIA, PROJETOS COMPLEMENTARES E ORÇAMENTO;

4. ELABORAÇÃO DO PLANO DE EXECUÇÃO DA OBRA, PROJETO DO CANTEIRO DE OBRAS E PROJETO LEGAL;

 

para construção do edifício sede da APAC, devendo ser incorporadas as exigências contidas no PGMO (Procedimento de Gestão de Mão de Obra). Os trabalhos serão realizados pela contratada no prazo de 07 (sete) meses.

 

A Secretaria de Recursos Hídricos e de Saneamento (SRHS), por meio de sua Secretaria Executiva de Saneamento (SESAN) e da Unidade de Gerenciamento do Projeto (UGP), convida Empresas ou Consórcios de Empresas elegíveis a manifestar seu interesse em executar o referido serviço. Os critérios para escolha de Consultores levarão em consideração as descrições de serviços semelhantes executados e as experiências em condições similares, considerando campo central de atuação, quantidade de anos em projetos e/ou contratos de natureza semelhante, experiências relevantes, capacidade gerencial e técnica da empresa.

Os especialistas principais não serão avaliados na fase Manifestação de Interesse.

As empresas interessadas deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem qualificações e experiências relevantes para prestar os serviços, incluindo pelo menos as seguintes informações:

• Portfólio ou prospecto apresentando a empresa.

• Lista de contratantes para os quais tenha prestado serviços semelhantes. A lista deve incluir, para cada contrato:

1.1. Descrição dos serviços prestados e data de conclusão do contrato,

AVIS À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT

Recrutement d’un consultant individuel national chargé d’appuyer l’élaboration d’une loi spécifique sur l’Accès et le Partage juste et équitable des Avantages (APA) découlant de l’utilisation des ressources génétiques au Tchad

  1. Contexte

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un financement de l’Association internationale de développement (IDA), au titre du Don n° E5230-TD, pour la mise en œuvre du Projet de Sécurité Sanitaire en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HeSP), dont l’objectif est d’améliorer la capacité du pays à prévenir, détecter et répondre aux urgences sanitaires. Une partie de ce financement est destinée au recrutement d’un consultant individuel national pour appuyer l’élaboration d’une loi spécifique relative à l’accès aux ressources génétiques et au partage juste et équitable des avantages découlant de leur utilisation.

L’activité relève de la sous-composante 1.1 « Gouvernance, planification et gestion de la sécurité sanitaire ». Elle est conduite au bénéfice de la Direction de la Faune et des Aires Protégées (DFAP), selon une approche participative, inclusive et multisectorielle intégrant les principes « Une Seule Santé » (One Health).

  1. Objet et principales tâches de la mission

Le consultant national appuiera le consultant international dans l’élaboration de l’avant-projet de loi APA et de son exposé des motifs. Il contribuera à leur conformité avec la Convention sur la Diversité Biologique (CDB), le Protocole de Nagoya et les orientations du Cadre mondial de la biodiversité de Kunming-Montréal, ainsi qu’à leur ancrage dans le contexte juridique, institutionnel et social tchadien.

La mission couvre les ressources génétiques végétales, animales et microbiennes ainsi que les connaissances traditionnelles associées sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Le consultant sera notamment chargé de :

• appuyer l’analyse des instruments internationaux, de leur transposition dans le droit tchadien et des expériences comparables en matière d’APA ;

• appuyer l’analyse du cadre juridique et institutionnel national, documenter ses lacunes et établir la cartographie des parties prenantes ;

• collecter et analyser la documentation nationale pertinente, recenser les textes applicables et documenter les réalités institutionnelles, sociales et économiques liées à l’utilisation des ressources génétiques au Tchad ;

• coordonner et conduire les consultations nationales, notamment avec les institutions publiques, les chercheurs, les universités, la société civile, les opérateurs privés, les peuples autochtones et les communautés locales (PACL) ;

• contribuer aux procédures d’accès, au consentement préalable donné en connaissance de cause (CPCC), aux conditions convenues d’un commun accord (CCCA), au partage des avantages et aux mécanismes de suivi, de contrôle et de sanctions ;

• fournir les données techniques nécessaires à la rédaction et contribuer aux dispositions protégeant les droits des communautés, en intégrant le genre, l’équité sociale, la participation inclusive et l’approche One Health ;

• appuyer l’élaboration de l’avant-projet de loi et de son exposé des motifs, organiser l’atelier national de validation, en préparer le rapport, consolider les observations et contribuer à la finalisation des livrables.

Les livrables propres au consultant national sont le rapport de démarrage, le rapport des consultations, la contribution technique au projet de loi, le rapport de l’atelier et le rapport final. Ses contributions appuieront la production de l’avant-projet de loi APA accompagné de son exposé des motifs et de la version finale intégrant les observations de l’atelier de validation.

  1. Durée et supervision

La mission nécessitera un niveau d’effort estimé à quarante-cinq (45) jours-personne, répartis sur une période maximale de trois (3) mois calendaires. Elle sera réalisée sous la supervision technique directe de la DFAP, en collaboration avec le consultant international et l’UCP-HeSP. Les modalités détaillées d’exécution et de validation figurent dans les TDR.

  1. Profil et qualifications recherchés

L’UCP invite les consultants individuels nationaux intéressés à présenter leur candidature. Les qualifications et expériences recherchées sont les suivantes :

• Master (BAC+5) au minimum en biodiversité, gestion des ressources naturelles, écologie, droit de l’environnement, santé environnementale, développement rural ou discipline équivalente ;

• au moins dix (10) années d’expérience en conservation de la biodiversité, gestion durable des ressources naturelles, gouvernance environnementale ou mise en œuvre de politiques et stratégies relatives à la biodiversité ;

• expérience confirmée dans l’élaboration de documents stratégiques, politiques publiques, cadres réglementaires ou études techniques liés à la CDB, à ses protocoles, notamment celui de Nagoya, ou aux autres instruments internationaux relatifs à la biodiversité ;

• expertise avérée en APA concernant les ressources génétiques et les connaissances traditionnelles associées ; expérience pratique des consultations et travaux de terrain avec les PACL, les populations riveraines des aires protégées et les autres parties prenantes ;

• bonne maîtrise des approches relatives au genre, aux droits humains, à la participation inclusive et à One Health ; excellente connaissance des savoirs traditionnels associés à la biodiversité, du cadre juridique et institutionnel tchadien et des enjeux nationaux de conservation et d’utilisation durable des ressources génétiques ; maîtrise du français.

Les expériences dans des projets financés par des partenaires internationaux constituent un atout, ainsi que l’élaboration de documents stratégiques relatifs à la biodiversité et à la CDB au Tchad ou en Afrique subsaharienne. Les références de documents de portée nationale ou internationale doivent être clairement mentionnées dans le CV.

  1. Dossier de manifestation d’intérêt

Les consultants intéressés devront fournir :

Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée ;

Un curriculum vitae détaillé, daté et signé mettant en évidence les qualifications et expériences pertinentes ;

Les copies des diplômes et certificats pertinents ;

Les références de missions similaires réalisées, accompagnées dans la mesure du possible des attestations de bonne exécution ou tout document justificatif ;

Une proposition technique présentant la compréhension de la mission, la méthodologie et le calendrier de travail proposés ;

Tout document permettant d’apprécier la capacité du consultant à réaliser la mission.

  1. Méthode de sélection et critères d’évaluation

Le consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de sélection de consultants individuels, conformément au Règlement de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant un financement de projets d’investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, dans sa version applicable au projet. The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), and the Ministry of Communications and Technology intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) is required to be undertaken as an external consultant firm supporting the client, Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS to carry out the implementation of “Government Data Governance, Interoperability Standards and Digital Service Risk Framework”. The assignment aims to establish a coherent, standardized and implementable government-wide foundation for data governance, interoperability, data exchange, reference and master data management, and digital service risk management across the Federal Government of Somalia. This includes developing government-wide standards for open data, metadata, APIs, registry data and digital service design; a Master Data Management Governance Framework and Register of Authoritative Sources; a Government Common Data Model; data quality, data-sharing and data classification frameworks; a Digital Service Risk-Profile Framework; and a sequenced implementation roadmap.   1. Le Gouvernement de la République du BENIN a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet d’identification unique pour l’intégration et l’inclusion en Afrique de l’Ouest (WURI) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de consultant. 
  2. La mission du consultant (cabinet) consistera à produire un documentaire de référence internationale retraçant la construction du système béninois d’état civil, d’identification et d’identité numérique, en mettant en évidence les réalisations, les difficultés, les choix stratégiques, les erreurs, les innovations et les leçons apprises pouvant inspirer d’autres pays.

De façon spécifique, le documentaire devra permettre de :

  1. Retracer l’histoire de l’état civil et de l’identification au Bénin ;
  2. Présenter les enjeux ayant conduit aux réformes ;
  3. Analyser l’évolution du cadre juridique et institutionnel ;
  4. Documenter les choix organisationnels et technologiques réalisés ;
  5. Mettre en évidence les impacts sur les citoyens et l’action publique ;
  6. Identifier les contraintes rencontrées tout au long du processus ;
  7. Analyser les échecs, limites et difficultés ;
  8. Capitaliser les bonnes pratiques et les leçons apprises ;
  9. Présenter les perspectives d’évolution vers l’identité numérique et la gouvernance numérique ;
  10. Constituer une ressource pédagogique et stratégique destinée aux gouvernements, institutions internationales, chercheurs et praticiens.

  • Les conditions préalables à une réforme réussie ;
  • Les erreurs à éviter ;
  • Les facteurs critiques de succès ;
  • Les choix technologiques et institutionnels possibles ;
  • Les mécanismes de gouvernance à mettre en place ;
  • Les défis liés à la qualité des données ;
  • Les enjeux de financement ;
  • Les défis liés à l’identité numérique.

  2. La mission consiste à poursuivre un processus déjà amorcé avec pour objectif de couvrir de manière holistique toutes les zones qui accueillent les infrastructures aussi bien au niveau régional, communal que communautaire, et ceci dans tous les guichets de financements en cours.
  3. Le Consultant-firme objet du présent avis à sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt concerne les Organisations d’Appui Locales (OAL) qui conformément à la règlementation en vigueur, pourront assurer au niveau régional, local et communautaire la mise en place, l’opérationnalisation et la vulgarisation du MGP, y compris les VBG dans vingt-cinq (25) Communes de la Région de l’Est
  4. Il s’agira pour la Consultant/Firme de : 
  • D’Identifier et former les points focaux communautaires dans les villages et quartiers abritant les sous projets. Ces points focaux doivent être des personnes avec résidence locale, de bonne moralité, capables d’apprendre et de transmettre des messages précis en français et en langue locale sur le MGP, et pouvant garder des informations confidentielles. Ils travailleront comme précisé ci-dessus, en collaboration avec les personnes ressources qui seront choisies dans chaque village par les populations, ainsi qu’avec le responsable QHSE des entreprises, dans leurs activités de sensibilisation et de collecte des plaintes ;
  • De sensibiliser et former les populations environnantes des sites des travaux sur l’utilisation de la cartographie des services de référencement potentiels existant dans les zones de chantier, notamment sur les points d’entrée appropriés pour les différents groupes des femmes y compris les filles et les adolescents; 
  • De former et sensibiliser les personnels des chantiers des entreprises chargées d’exécuter les travaux sur le code de bonne conduite et les modalités de traitement des plaintes relatives aux VBG/EAS/HS et VCE ;
  • D’informer et sensibiliser les populations, sur l’utilisation de tous les canaux appropriés de communication, à l’instar des dépliants, des boites à suggestions, des affiches, des boîtes à images, des radios communautaires et en langues locales, le numéro vert sur le projet et le mécanisme de gestion des plaintes (procédure, point de dépôt et délai de traitement des plaintes) et le contenu du code de bonne conduite ;
  • De former les points focaux et les membres des comités locaux, et régionaux de gestion des plaintes à la gestion efficiente des plaintes ordinaires et de celles relevant des questions de Violences basées sur le genre, en s’assurant du respect strict du principe de confidentialité de la survivante ;
  • D’accompagner les populations dans la formulation des plaintes (appui dans la formulation/rédaction), le cas échéant ; informer les chefs de village du calendrier de la tenue des activités de sensibilisation communautaire liées à la gestion de plaintes dans les zones de projet et y prendre part ;
  • D’organiser à travers les points focaux, des activités de sensibilisation, de plaidoyer et de communication pour le changement de comportement à l'égard des VBG et VCE, avec un focus sur les risques associés aux travaux de construction des infrastructures et à l’afflux de la main d’œuvre ;
  • D’assurer la production, la mise à disposition et la vulgarisation auprès des membres des comités locaux et régionaux de gestion des plaintes ; et des points focaux communautaires des outils de communication et de sensibilisation sur le MGP et les VBG. Les maquettes de ces outils seront fournies par le Projet ;
  • De mettre à jour le circuit de référencement VBG des différentes communes en s’appuyant sur les données disponibles au niveau du PROLOG ou d’autres projets financés par la Banque mondiale ;
  • D’assurer la prise en charge éthique et sûre des survivant(e)s éventuelles conformément aux dispositions énoncées dans le protocole de prise en charge du PROLOG.

Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être soumises exclusivement par courrier électronique en un seul dossier à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous, au plus tard quatorze (14) jours à compter de la date de publication du présent avis dans le quotidien Cameroun Tribune, soit le16 octobre 2026, à 15 heures 30 minutes (heure locale) et devront comprendre les documents suivants :

  • Les références dans la conduite d’au moins deux missions similaires, et d’une parfaite connaissance de la Région de l’Est et des communes d’exécution de la mission ;

description:
Specific Procurement Notice

 

Request for Bids

Goods

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

 

Country: Republic of Moldova

Name of Project: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Competitiveness

Contract Title: Procurement of a Dedicated Hosting Infrastructure (Equipment to enhance governmental digital infrastructure)

Loan No. 9423-MD

Credit No. 7174-MD

RFB Reference No.: MD-CEP-547274-GO-RFB

 

  1. The Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Competitiveness Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of a Dedicated Hosting Infrastructure (Equipment to enhance governmental digital infrastructure).

2.         The Project Implementation Unit of the World Bank MSME Competitiveness Project now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for the delivery and installation of a dedicated, high-availability hosting infrastructure - comprising compute, storage, network, and cybersecurity components (including Privileged Access Management, Security Information and Event Management, and vulnerability management systems) to support the Qualified Trust Services of the Government Certification Authority (PKI) of the Republic of Moldova, together with associated implementation, training, warranty, and technical support services, to be delivered and implemented across two geographically distinct data centers (a Primary Data Center and a Disaster Recovery Data Center) operated by the Information Technology and Cyber Security Service (STISC) in Chisinau, Republic of Moldova. No margin of domestic preference applies to this procurement.

3.         Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB)  as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations that meet the following minimum qualification criteria:

  1. Financial Capability: The Bidder shall submit audited financial statements or, if not required by the law of the Bidder's country, other financial statements acceptable to the Purchaser, for the last three (3) years prior to the Bid submission deadline (i.e., 2023, 2024, and 2025), demonstrating the current soundness of the Bidder's financial position. For a joint venture, this requirement shall be met by each member.

Minimum average annual turnover: The Bidder shall demonstrate a minimum average annual turnover, calculated as the total certified payments received for contracts in progress or completed, within the last three (3) years (2023, 2024, and 2025), of at least EUR 3,000,000.00 or equivalent.

For a joint venture, the sum of all Partners' average turnover amounts may be used to meet this requirement. In such case, the Partner in charge (leader) must have had an average annual turnover equivalent to at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the amount required for the most recent three (3) years, whereas the other Partner(s) shall have not less than twenty-five percent (25%) of the total requirement.

  1. Specific Experience: The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed at least two (2) contracts within the last five (5) years prior to the Bid submission deadline, each with a value of at least EUR 800,000.00 or equivalent, that have been successfully and substantially completed and that are similar in nature and complexity to the Goods and Related Services under the Contract (i.e., supply and installation of hyper-converged/virtualized infrastructure with integrated cybersecurity components such as PAM and/or SIEM, SOAR).

For a joint venture, this requirement may be met by all members combined.

  1. Staff experience: qualification requirements for the personnel proposed by the Bidder, including education, certifications and professional experience for each position, are fully specified in Section VII, Schedule of Requirements, Technical Specifications and are assessed as mandatory minimum requirements.

For each proposed position the Bidder shall submit (i) a CV signed by the individual, stating the role performed, the responsibilities, and the start and the completion dates of the assignment; (ii) copies of the university diplomas of the proposed project team (iii) copies of the certifications relied upon; and (iv) a written declaration by the Bidder confirming that information.

  • Project Manager: higher-education graduate holding a bachelor's degree; project-management competencies as specified in the Bidding document; at least 5 years' professional experience.
  • Architect: bachelor's degree in computer science or IT engineering; the active certifications specified in the Bidding document, including CISSP and an internationally recognized trainer diploma, the active certifications specified in the Bidding document; at least 10 years' professional experience.
  • Infrastructure and Automation Engineer: bachelor's degree in computer science or IT engineering; the active certifications specified in the Bidding document; at least 5 years' professional experience.
  • Security Testing Expert: bachelor's degree in computer science or IT engineering; CEH, CISSP or CompTIA Security+ certification; at least 5 years' professional experience.
  • Auditor: bachelor's degree in IT engineering, a technical field or economics; the active certifications specified in the Bidding document, including CISA, CISM, CRISC and CISSP; at least 5 years' professional experience and at least 5 system-audit projects.
  • Cybersecurity Trainer (Instructor): bachelor's degree; active cybersecurity and trainer certifications (equivalent to or higher than CISSP, CISM, or GIAC GSLC, NSE7); at least 5 years' professional experience in cybersecurity and at least two references confirming delivery of similar courses; able to deliver the training in Romanian.

 

  1. Manufacturing Experience and Technical Capacity: if the Bidder itself manufactures any of the items offered under the Contract (e.g., the HCI compute servers, network/security appliances), the Bidder shall furnish documentary evidence to demonstrate that:
  1. it has manufactured goods of similar nature and complexity for at least three years, prior to the bid submission deadline; and
  2. its annual production capacity of goods of similar nature and complexity for each of the last three years prior to the bid submission deadline, is at least 2 times the quantities specified under the contract.

Where the Bidder is not the manufacturer of an item, sub-paragraph (f) below apply instead.

  1. Cyber Security Experience: Given the cybersecurity-sensitive nature of this Contract (PKI/trust services infrastructure, PAM, SIEM, and vulnerability management components), the Bidder shall demonstrate:
  1. successful completion of at least two (2) projects within the last five (5) years involving the design, supply, and/or implementation of Privileged Access Management (PAM), Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), or comparable cybersecurity infrastructure (SOAR, etc.), of similar scope and complexity to the Related Services under this Contract; and
  2. that the Bidder (or the subcontractor/partner responsible for the cybersecurity components, if applicable) holds a valid ISO/IEC 27001 certification (Information Security Management System), or equivalent, current as of the Bid submission deadline.
  1. Manufacturer's Authorization: A Bidder who does not manufacture an item/s where manufacturer authorization is required in accordance with BDS ITB 17.2(a), shall provide evidence of being duly authorized by a manufacturer (Manufacturer's Authorization Form, Section IV, Bidding Forms), meeting the criteria in (d) above, to supply the Goods.
  2. State Security Investment Screening: The Goods and Related Services under this Contract fall within the domains referred to in Article 4, letters (a), (b), and (j) of Law No. 174/2021 of the Republic of Moldova on the mechanism for examining investments of importance for State security, namely the operation of data processing or storage infrastructure, the operation of information technologies within cyber security infrastructure, and the security of public networks and information systems.

Accordingly, the Bidder shall obtain the prior approval of CEIISS for its planned investment/participation in this Contract, in accordance with Law No. 174/2021, before signature of the Contract (https://www.asp.gov.md/ro/informatii-utile/consiliul-pentru-examinarea-investitiilor-de-importanta-pentru-securitatea).

Where the Bidder is a joint venture, this approval shall be obtained by, and shall be required for, each member of the joint venture.

The Bidder (and, where applicable, each member of the joint venture) shall state whether it already holds such approval, attaching a copy if so, or shall submit confirmation that it has requested prior approval of the investment from CEIISS.

 

At the time of Contract Award, the Bidder (including each subcontractor proposed by the Bidder) shall not be subject to disqualification by the Bank for non-compliance with SEA/SH obligations.

VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT

Recruitment of Individual Consultant

                                                                                                            Job Position: PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST

 

WBTTFP–8929-MKD-411L-1

General Information: The Ministry of Transport (the CLIENT) intends to engage a highly qualified Consultant to provide services as a Procurement Specialist of the Project Implementation Unit (the PIU) in the Ministry of Transport in North Macedonia. The Project Implementation Unit is staffed with different expert profiles in order to carry out complete project management for the projects financed by the World Bank, the Trade and Transport Facilitation Project (TTFP), the Local Roads Connectivity Project (LRCP), and the Project Preparation for the Railway Sector Reform Project (GFPP for the RSRP).

The assignment is full-time until November 15, 2027, and in any event for no less than the duration of the Projects.

Project Background:  The TTFP is implemented in its first phase in Serbia, North Macedonia and Albania, the Local Roads Connectivity Project (LRCP) is in final phase of implementation and the Project Preparation for the Railway Sector Reform Project (GFPP for the RSRP) is in preparation phase and shall be implemented in North Macedonia.

The Project Implementation Unit in North Macedonia is staffed with different expert profiles to support implementation, monitoring and coordination of these activities.

 

The Trade and Transport Facilitation Project Phase 1 includes a combination of investments, technical assistance, and regulatory and institutional reforms. Its focus is on the adoption and implementation of a National Single Window (NSW) solution, improvements at the border crossing points at Deve Bair and Kjafasan, deployment of an Intelligent Transport System (ITS) on the A1 motorway, which is part of Corridor X, and related technical assistance.

 

The Local Roads Connectivity Project (LRCP) supports selected municipalities through investments in the reconstruction, rehabilitation and upgrading of local roads and streets to improve mobility, connectivity and road safety. Investments may also include sidewalks, bicycle paths, street lighting, slope and landslide stabilization, junction improvements, pedestrian crossings, drainage, and capacity building of municipal staff.

 

The Preparation Grant for the Railway Sector Reform Project (RSRP), financed through the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), Grant No. TF0D2237, is envisaged to facilitate the preparation of a proposed project designed to support the Recipient's railway operator, Railways of the Republic of North Macedonia Transport, to advance its organizational restructuring and achieve financial stability. The activities financed under this Grant include procurement readiness activities, such as early market engagement and market analysis, drafting of terms of reference, preparation of technical documentation and bidding documents, as well as capacity building and training activities to enhance the Recipient's procurement capacity.

.

Position Objective: To plan, coordinate, monitor and control procurement activities under the Projects and to ensure that procurement of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services is carried out in accordance with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations, the approved Procurement Plans and the relevant Legal/Financing Agreements and legislation in force in North Macedonia.

The Procurement Specialist shall work in close cooperation with the Ministry of Transport, the PIU and other stakeholder agencies to ensure timely and compliant planning and implementation of procurement activities under the Projects.

 

Tasks and Responsibilities: The Procurement Specialist of the PIU will be responsible for the following duties:

  •      Manage day-to-day procurement activities under the Projects;

           Prepare and provide procurement inputs for periodic project progress reports required by the Ministry of Transport, the Government of the Republic of North Macedonia, the World Bank and other relevant stakeholders;

           Coordinate any amendments and changes relevant to procurement to the Project Operational Manuals and submit them to the relevant Committees for approval;

           Support the Project Director, with regard to procurement, to represent the project vis-à-vis Government institutions, local government units, international finance institutions and other multi-lateral and bilateral donors;

           Based on approved work plans, prepare and update the Projects’ Procurement Plans and coordinate their submission to the World Bank, as required;

           Monitor overall project implementation from the procurement perspective;

           Consolidate requests for procurement of goods, works, consulting and non-consulting services and reflect them as relevant in the projects’ procurement plans;

           Prepare, in cooperation with project focal points and technical teams, procurement documents, clarifications, amendments, evaluation reports and other required procurement documentation, and coordinate the required approvals;

           Coordinate timely submission of procurement documents and actions for World Bank review and no-objection, where required;

           Coordinate publication and advertising of procurement notices through the channels required by the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations and project arrangements;

           Coordinate each procurement/selection process, including preparation of procurement documents, clarifications, amendments and communications with bidders/consultants, as applicable; Participate in and coordinate all relevant stages of procurement and selection processes for assigned contracts;

           Organize and coordinate evaluation processes, provide guidance to evaluation committees and prepare evaluation reports using the applicable World Bank forms;

           Use the World Bank’s online procurement planning and tracking tools to record procurement actions, prepare and update procurement notices and Procurement Plans, submit relevant documents and record Bank review/no-objection actions, as required;

           Act as the PIU’s key procurement contact in STEP and manage procurement exchanges between the implementing agency and the World Bank;

           Track procurement progress against approved plans, identify delays and remedial actions, and report material issues regularly to the Project Director and Project Coordinator;

           Prepare and submit for Bank review periodic procurement progress reports, keep list of completed, on-going and planned contracts and keep updated list of contracts subject to the WB post review;

           Revise the procurement plans in coordination with the PIU experts, as needed, and submit to WB for no-objection;

           Provide assistance during project implementation activities with regard to procurement issues;

           Prepare draft contracts and procurement-related contract amendments/addenda, as required;

           Liaise with the World Bank Procurement Specialist(s) assigned to the Projects;

           Interact with other PIU Experts in order to support overall Projects activities;

           Perform any other activities related to implementation of the Projects as assigned by the Project Director, Project Coordinator and/or Minister of Transport.

Knowledge, experience, skills, and competences:

Educational qualifications: University Degree requiring at least three years of study (180 ECTS credits), or equivalent.

Area of professional expertise: Procurement;

Years of experience: Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in procurement of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services;

Additional qualifications or training: Relevant procurement training and/or professional certification is desirable;

Required skills and competencies: Experience in procurement of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services;Experience in procurement under projects financed by international donors; Strong MS Word and Excel skills.

Desired: Knowledge of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers; Relevant procurement training and/or professional certification;
Experience using STEP or similar electronic procurement tracking systems.

Required: Excellent Knowledge of English language (reading, speaking, and writing) and Fluency in Macedonian language;

Computer skills: Strong MS Word and Excel skills.;

Managerial skills: Self-planning & organizing, problem-solving, communication, teamwork, initiative, ability to take initiative and work independently when needed, and good organizational and time-management skills.

Applications: The candidates should submit their Letters of Application, CVs, and Letters of Motivation (all documents in the English language) only electronically to the following e-mail: konkursi@mtc.gov.mk. The deadline for submitting the applications is October 14, 2026, at the latest. The candidates can find the ToR for the announced job position in the following link http://mtc.gov.mk and https://e-nabavki.gov.mk/PublicAccess/home.aspx#/international-donor-announcements.

  • Preparar o estudo de viabilidade e elaborar modelos de gestão;
  • Elaboração de instrumentos ambientais e sociais, projecto executivo das infraestruturas e um conjunto de edifícios de diferentes funções que compreendem o Centro de Formação e Incubação de Jovens;
  • Mapa de quantidades e estimativa de custos baseada em preços unitários;

  • Monitoria da correcção de defeitos durante o período da garantia da obra.

3. O Ministério da Economia e Finanças (MEF) convida as empresas de consultoria (“Consultores”) elegíveis para indicar seu interesse em fornecer os Serviços. Os consultores interessados devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e a experiência relevante para prestar os serviços (brochuras, descrição de contratos semelhantes, experiência em condições semelhantes, etc).  

 

Os critérios de avaliação para a lista curta são os seguintes:

  • No geral, a empresa de consultoria deverá ter no mínimo de 10 anos de experiência em   arquitectura e engenharia civil , estudos ambientais e sociais, para edificação, reabilitação de edifícios, centros de formação profissional, escolas, internatos.
  • No específico a consultoria deverá ter pelo menos, 3 (três) trabalhos de edifícios semelhantes ao objecto destes ToR, que demonstrem a experiência do consultor com contratos em condições semelhantes (como por exemplo, escolas, centros internatos, centros de formaçãoo) ou serviços semelhantes;
  • Experiência na elaboração de estudos de viabilidade e modelos de gestão para centros de formação (ou outras infraestruturas públicas semelhantes), planos de manutenção de infrarestruturas diversas; 
  • Experiência de trabalho demonstrada com projetos em Moçambique, em particular os executados em ambientes rurais remotos;
  •  O Consultor deve ser plenamente experiente em trabalhos com documentos e padrões de salvaguardas ambientais e sociais da República de Moçambique e do Banco Mundial;
  • São igualmente vantagens:
    • A experiência de trabalho na região do Vale do Zambeze.
    • Capacidade da empresa para prestar apoio à equipa do projecto;
    • Localização do(s) escritório(s), a estrutura organizacional da empresa, disponibilidade de profissionais permanentes e pessoal de apoio, etc. 
    • Certificação em gestão da qualidade (ISO ou similar).

Os consultores podem incluir no máximo, 15 referências (dos últimos 10 anos, de janeiro 2016 até a data  de submissão da proposta), para mostrar a sua experiência relevante para os critérios acima mencionados. Cada referência deverá ser breve, no máximo 1 página seguindo o modelo fornecido.

 

Nesta fase a Equipa Chave não será objecto de avaliação para a Lista Curta.

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden la formulación de los Planes Regionales de Ordenamiento y Desarrollo Territorial (PRODT) de las regiones Valdesia y Higuamo; siete (7) Planes Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial (PMOT) de nueva formulación: tres (3) en Valdesia, correspondientes a Bajos de Haina, Baní y San Gregorio de Nigua; y cuatro (4) en Higuamo, correspondientes a Guayacanes, Hato Mayor, Sabana de la Mar y Monte Plata.

Además, comprenden la revisión, actualización, complementación, apoyo o armonización de cuatro (4) instrumentos municipales existentes o en formulación: dos (2) en Valdesia, correspondientes a San Cristóbal y San José de Ocoa, y dos (2) en Higuamo, correspondientes a San Pedro de Macorís y Yamasá; la formulación de cinco (5) Instrumentos de Delimitación de Suelo Urbano (IDSU), tres (3) en Valdesia, para Villa Altagracia, Yaguate y Nizao, y dos (2) en Higuamo, para Bayaguana y Sabana Grande de Boyá; nueve (9) Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático, cinco (5) en Valdesia y cuatro (4) en Higuamo; y dos (2) Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación, una para cada región, con determinaciones territorializadas para doce (12) municipios, en un período de catorce (14) meses calendario, conforme al alcance establecido en los Términos de Referencia. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR).

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. Se requiere una firma con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo de proyectos, planes o políticas relacionados con el ordenamiento y desarrollo territorial en las escalas nacional, regional, municipal y/o de desarrollo urbano. Asimismo, deberá acreditar experiencia específica en la formulación de instrumentos regionales o supramunicipales y de instrumentos municipales de ordenamiento territorial que incorporen zonificación, regulación del uso del suelo, cartografía, normativa y mecanismos de implementación, incluyendo experiencia en la ejecución simultánea de instrumentos correspondientes a distintos niveles de gobierno. Asimismo, deberá demostrar experiencia reciente, adquirida durante los últimos diez (10) años, en gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, acreditada mediante al menos tres (3) contratos o proyectos relevantes o siete (7) años de experiencia institucional acumulada, incluyendo análisis multiamenaza, modelación hidrológico-hidráulica y sísmica, integración de escenarios climáticos y articulación de resultados con instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial e inversión pública.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) proyectos similares en alcance, complejidad, niveles de gobierno y extensión geográfica, ejecutados satisfactoriamente. En conjunto, los proyectos deberán incluir: (i) al menos una experiencia en planificación regional, supramunicipal o de escala territorial equivalente; (ii) al menos una experiencia en formulación o actualización de instrumentos municipales con zonificación, cartografía y normativa de uso del suelo; y (iii) al menos una experiencia que integre gestión del riesgo de desastres, adaptación al cambio climático o Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica. Un mismo contrato podrá ser utilizado para acreditar simultáneamente más de uno de los requisitos de experiencia específica descritos anteriormente, siempre que la documentación presentada permita verificar claramente cada aspecto requerido. Las experiencias deberán permitir verificar, según corresponda, planificación regional y municipal, instrumentos normativos de uso del suelo, información geoespacial, participación territorial, fortalecimiento institucional, portafolios de inversión y estrategias de implementación.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para trabajar de forma simultánea en dos regiones con dinámicas territoriales diferenciadas, manteniendo coordinación técnica, control de calidad, presencia en territorio, gestión documental, producción cartográfica, participación y revisión de productos en paralelo, detallando las capacidades institucionales y herramientas utilizadas por la firma para la gestión de proyectos, producción cartográfica y administración de información.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales, supramunicipales y municipales de naturaleza y alcance equivalentes a los PRODT, PMOT, IDSU y Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación previstos en esta consultoría, así como Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático; procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor; formulación normativa; gestión de información territorial y cartográfica; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; fortalecimiento institucional; y productos de implementación.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Valdesia e Higuamo y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse de manera organizada, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, escala territorial, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales y recursos permanentes relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

AVIS D’APPEL D’OFFRES OUVERT INTERNATIONAL

Appel d’Offres No : N° PAAEP-WJIR-AOI-040-F-26

Projet : PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES A L’EAU POTABLE A MADAGASCAR (PAAEP)

Pays : MADAGASCAR

Intitulé du Marché : FOURNITUTRE DE COMPTEURS D’EAU DE DN 15

Prêt/Crédit/don No : IDA 7121-MG : Don IDA E040-MG

Emis le : 02 octobre 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le « PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES A L’EAU POTABLE A MADAGASCAR », et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché pour la Fourniture des compteurs d’eau DN 15.

2. L’UNITE DE GESTION DE PROJET PAAEP-JIRAMA (UGP PAAEP-JIRAMA) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir des compteurs d’eau DN 15.

La fourniture concernent l'acquisition de 113 000 compteurs d'eau de diamètre nominal DN 15.

La fourniture constitue un lot unique indivisible.

3. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence internationale (AOI) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale, 7ème édition, Septembre 2025 », et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’UGP PAAEP JIRAMA et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres durant les heures de bureau de 08h00 à 16h00 à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

5.Les soumissionnaires devront satisfaire aux principaux critères de qualification ci-après :

- Capacité financière : disposer d’une capacité financière suffisante pour l’exécution du marché, évaluée à environ trois millions (3 000 000) USD, conformément aux exigences détaillées du Dossier d’Appel d’Offres;

- Expérience spécifique : avoir réalisé avec succès, au cours de la période spécifiée dans le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres, des contrats similaires portant sur la fourniture de compteurs d’eau ou de fournitures de nature comparable, pour une valeur minimale d’environ quatre millions cinq cent mille (4 500 000) USD, selon les modalités et conditions précisées dans le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres ;

- Autorisation du fabricant : lorsque le soumissionnaire n’est pas le fabricant des fournitures proposées, disposer d’une autorisation du fabricant conforme aux exigences du Dossier d’Appel d’Offres ;

- Autres exigences : satisfaire aux autres critères de qualification, d’éligibilité et aux exigences techniques spécifiés dans le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres.

6. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir le dossier d’appel d’offres complet en Français en formulant une demande par lettre ou par mail mentionnant leurs coordonnées complètes à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

7. Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 17 novembre 2026 à Dix (10) heures. La soumission des offres par voie électronique «ne sera pas autorisée. Toute offre arrivée après l’expiration du délai limite des offres sera rejetée et ne sera pas acceptée.

8. Les enveloppes extérieures de l’offre marquées « ORIGINAL DE L’OFFRE » et les enveloppes intérieures marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes publiquement à l’adresse ci-dessous le 17 novembre 2026 à dix (10) heures (heures de Madagascar).

9. Les deuxièmes enveloppes marquées « PARTIE FINANCIERE » devront rester non ouvertes et seront conservées en un lieu sûr par l’Acheteur jusqu’à la deuxième ouverture publique.

10. Les offres doivent être accompagnées d’une Garantie à mettre dans les enveloppes marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE »., d’un montant de soixante-dix mille (70 000 USD) ou son équivalent en monnaie librement convertible ;

11. L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

12. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :

Antananarivo – 101 - MADAGASCAR

Specific Procurement Notice – Request for Proposals without Prequalification

Request for Proposal

Information Systems

(Design, Supply and Installation)

(Without Prequalification)

 

Purchaser: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA)

Project: Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land Project (GRAIL)

Contract title: Design, Development, Integration, Migration, Testing, Deployment, and Support of the Preferential Agro-Credit Project System (PACPS)

Country: Georgia

Loan No: 9504-GE

RFP No.: GRAIL/G/RFP/03

Issued on: October 02, 2026

1.        Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land Project (GRAIL), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the Design, Development, Integration, Migration, Testing, Deployment, and Support of the Preferential Agro-Credit Project System (PACPS).

2.        The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA) now invites sealed Proposals from eligible Proposers for the design, development, integration, migration, testing, deployment, and support of the Rural Development Agency's Preferential Agro-Credit Project System (RDA-PACPS). The Rural Development Agency (RDA) is a state agency under the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA), which is responsible for the administration of the “Preferential Agro-Credit Project.” The Project provides access to loans and leasing products by subsidizing the interest rates. The proposed PACPS will support RDA and MEPA in administering the Preferential Agro-Credit Project on a fully digital, centrally governed, and auditable basis. The system will comprise a Core Case Management System, a Transactional and Financial Reconciliation Module, an API and Integration Layer, and a Financial Institutions Portal, and will enable structured, API-based and portal-based interoperability with participating financial institutions (banks and leasing companies) and relevant state registers.

The installation, configuration, and full operational acceptance of the system shall be completed within twelve (12) months from the Effective Date of Contract, followed by an eleven (11)- month warranty.

The Project implementation will take place in Tbilisi, Georgia, primarily at MEPA’s and RDA’s central offices, with remote access and integration points across participating agencies.

3.        The procurement process will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September  2025, (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4.        Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 75 % and for Bid cost: 25%.
