REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

Country: Ethiopia

Name of Project: The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project

Grant No: P180117

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant to Design and Institutionalize a Comprehensive Multi-Year Planning and Budgeting (MYB) Framework Across AU Organs and Institutions

 

Reference No. ET-AUC-564013-CS-INDV

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include to institutionalize a comprehensive Multi-Year Planning and Budgeting Framework that enhances fiscal discipline, budget predictability, strategic resource allocation and alignment with African Union priorities. Specific tasks include:

Phase 1: Inception, Diagnostic Assessment and Framework Design

 

The Consultant shall:

  • Conduct a comprehensive review of existing AU planning, budgeting and reporting practices and tools.
  • Develop a structured Multi-Year Budgeting Framework.
  • Define methodologies for rolling budgets and medium-term budget projections.
  • Establish linkages between the MYB Framework and Results-Based Management (RBM).

 

Phase 2: Systems Development, Policy Alignment and Tools Design

 

The Consultant shall:

  • Design standardized templates and tools to support Multi-Year Budgeting.
  • Recommend system enhancements and integration mechanisms for embedding MYB within existing planning and budgeting systems.
  • Update the AU Budget Manual to incorporate MYB and RBM principles.
  • Develop policy notes and implementation guidance.

 

Phase 3: Capacity Building and Implementation

 

The Consultant shall:

 

  • Design and implement a comprehensive capacity-building programme.
  • Provide hands-on technical assistance to Departments, Offices and Organs.
  • Develop user manuals, operational procedures and guidance notes.
  • Capture lessons learned and refine methodologies, templates and implementation guidelines.

 

Phase 4: Institutionalization, Governance and Stakeholder Engagement

 

The Consultant shall:

 

  • Develop a detailed institutionalization roadmap.
  • Establish governance mechanisms for sustained implementation and oversight.
  • Strengthen institutional ownership and ensure long-term integration of MYB into AU planning and budgeting processes.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The African Union Commission now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • An advanced university degree in Public Finance, Economics, Public Administration or a related discipline.
  • At least fifteen (15) years of demonstrated experience in Public Financial Management, Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks (MTEF), strategic planning and budgeting reforms.
  • Proven experience supporting international organizations, regional institutions or multilateral development organizations.
  • Experience in institutionalizing Results-Based Budgeting and Medium-Term Budget Frameworks.
  • Familiarity with international organizational budgeting systems will be an added advantage.
  • Strong analytical, facilitation, communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO DESIGN AND INSTITUTIONALIZE A COMPREHENSIVE MULTI-YEAR PLANNING AND BUDGETING (MYB) FRAMEWORK ACROSS AU ORGANS AND INSTITUTIONS

 

  1. Background

 

The African Union Commission (AUC) is committed to strengthening strategic planning, results-based management, and sound financial governance in support of the aspirations of Agenda 2063: Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan (STYIP) 2024–2033 and the AUC Strategic Plan 2024–2028. Achieving these continental priorities requires planning and budgeting systems that are strategic, integrated, predictable and focused on delivering measurable results.

 

In accordance with Article 13(4) of the African Union Financial Rules, every AU Organ and Institution is required to contribute to a consolidated budget proposal comprising an annual budget together with projections for the following two years. This provision establishes the foundation for a Medium-Term Planning and Budgeting Framework that aligns strategic priorities with sustainable resource allocation and institutional performance.

 

To support this transformation, the African Union Commission intends to engage a consultant to design and institutionalize a comprehensive Multi-Year Planning and Budgeting (MYB) Framework across AU Organs and Institutions. The assignment will facilitate the integration of strategic planning, medium-term expenditure planning, annual budgeting and performance management.

 

The Consultant will work closely with the Finance Directorate and the Office of Strategic Planning and Delivery (OSPD) to develop practical implementation arrangements, strengthen institutional coordination and support organizational change management.

 

  1. Objective of the Assignment

 

Overall Objective

 

To institutionalize a comprehensive Multi-Year Planning and Budgeting Framework that enhances fiscal discipline, budget predictability, strategic resource allocation and alignment with African Union priorities.

 

Specific Objectives

 

The Consultant shall:

 

  • Establish an operational Multi-Year Planning and Budgeting Framework with a rolling three-year planning horizon.
  • Strengthen Results-Based Budgeting (RBB) practices and improve the linkage between strategic planning and budgeting.
  • Enhance the credibility, transparency and realism of AU budgets.
  • Build institutional and technical capacity across AU Organs and Institutions.
  • Standardize methodologies, templates and implementation tools for MYB.

 

  1. Scope of Work

 

The Consultant shall undertake the following activities.

 

Phase 1: Inception, Diagnostic Assessment and Framework Design

 

The Consultant shall:

  • Conduct a comprehensive review of existing AU planning, budgeting and reporting practices and tools.
  • Develop a structured Multi-Year Budgeting Framework.
  • Define methodologies for rolling budgets and medium-term budget projections.
  • Establish linkages between the MYB Framework and Results-Based Management (RBM).

 

Phase 2: Systems Development, Policy Alignment and Tools Design

 

The Consultant shall:

  • Design standardized templates and tools to support Multi-Year Budgeting.
  • Recommend system enhancements and integration mechanisms for embedding MYB within existing planning and budgeting systems.
  • Update the AU Budget Manual to incorporate MYB and RBM principles.
  • Develop policy notes and implementation guidance.

 

Phase 3: Capacity Building and Implementation

 

The Consultant shall:

 

  • Design and implement a comprehensive capacity-building programme.
  • Provide hands-on technical assistance to Departments, Offices and Organs.
  • Develop user manuals, operational procedures and guidance notes.
  • Capture lessons learned and refine methodologies, templates and implementation guidelines.

 

Phase 4: Institutionalization, Governance and Stakeholder Engagement

 

The Consultant shall:

 

  • Develop a detailed institutionalization roadmap.
  • Establish governance mechanisms for sustained implementation and oversight.
  • Strengthen institutional ownership and ensure long-term integration of MYB into AU planning and budgeting processes.

The African Union Commission shall provide:

  • Coordination with AUC Departments, Offices and Organs.
  • Meeting facilities and logistical support for workshops and stakeholder consultations, where applicable.

  1. Consultant's Qualifications, Experience and Competencies

 

The Consultant shall possess:

 

  • An advanced university degree in Public Finance, Economics, Public Administration or a related discipline.
  • At least fifteen (15) years of demonstrated experience in Public Financial Management, Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks (MTEF), strategic planning and budgeting reforms.
  • Proven experience supporting international organizations, regional institutions or multilateral development organizations.
  • Experience in institutionalizing Results-Based Budgeting and Medium-Term Budget Frameworks.
  • Familiarity with international organizational budgeting systems will be an added advantage.
  • Strong analytical, facilitation, communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

 

  1. Client's Assignment Management Arrangements

 

The Consultant shall report to the Head of Budget Division, Finance Directorate, and work closely with the Office of Strategic Planning and Delivery (OSPD).

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING FIRM)

 PREPARATION OF A NATIONAL LAND USE PLAN

FOR BELIZE

Institution:    Ministry of Finance

Country:        Belize, Central America

Project:          Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project (P181064)

Process ID:     BZ-CEU-460793-CS-QCBS

Duration:       18 months

Deadline:       October 21, 2026; 9:00 AM. (Local Belize Time)

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Prepare a National Land Use Plan for Belize.

The Government of Belize has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project and intends to apply part of the Project’s proceeds to contract a firm to prepare a National Land Use Plan for Belize.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve the preparation of a comprehensive and legally sound National Land Use Plan (NLU Plan) for Belize. The assignment will operationalize the National Land Use Policy (NLUP) by establishing a national spatial and technical framework to guide sustainable land use, zoning, and development across sectors and administrative levels. The consultancy will include situational analysis, preparation of strategic and zoning frameworks, stakeholder consultations, development of digital and GIS-enabled planning tools, institutional strengthening, capacity building, and establishment of a monitoring and evaluation framework.

The assignment will be implemented under the Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project, managed by the Central Executing Unit (CEU) within the Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the Ministry of Natural Resources, Petroleum and Mining, through the Lands and Surveys Department.

Implementation Period:

The duration of the consultancy is eighteen (18) months.

Expected Start Date:

The consultancy is expected to commence following completion of the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) process and contract signing. Based on the application submission deadline of October 21, 2026, at 9:00 AM, the anticipated start date is the beginning of 2027.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest and can be found at the following website: https://procurement.gov.bz/mof-ceu-consultancy-services-to-prepare-a-national-land-use-plan-for-belize-ceu-firm-bz-ceu-460793-cs-qcbs-mof-ceu-2026/.

The Central Executing Unit, Ministry of Finance, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:  

  1. General Experience: Demonstrated experience in national or regional land use planning, spatial planning, or sustainable land management assignments for public sector institutions, including the preparation of policy, regulatory, or strategic planning instruments. Firms should have completed at least two (2) similar assignments of comparable scope and complexity.
  2. Specific Experience: The Firm must demonstrate experience in at least two (2) similar assignments within the last ten (10) years involving the preparation of national or regional land use plans, spatial development frameworks, or zoning instruments. Experience in integrating spatial analysis, stakeholder consultations, and institutional capacity support will be considered an asset.
  3. Adequacy of Assignment: At least two (2) references must be submitted and should demonstrate assignments of comparable scope and institutional context, involving coordination with government entities, preparation of comprehensive planning instruments, and support to implementation or institutional strengthening processes.

To be considered for shortlisting, Consultants must meet the required criteria above. Key Experts will not be evaluated at this stage.

The shortlist will contain not fewer than five (5) and not more than eight (8) eligible firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" (September 2025), which sets out the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The GOB reserves the right to cancel this invitation, in whole or in part, without assigning any reason. It is under no obligation to select any consultant and will not be liable for any costs incurred by applicants in the preparation and submission of their Expressions of Interest.

description:
DEMANDE DE MANIFESTATIONS D'INTÉRÊT

(SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS)

SÉLECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS

Pays : République du Burundi

N° du Projet : P176396

DON IDA N° E0930-BI

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET CHARGE D’ASSURER LES FORMATIONS DES CADRES DE LA BRB SUR EMV

 Réf. STEP: BI-PAFEN-PIU-2.2.3.18_7-CS-CQS 

Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a obtenu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) un Don d’un montant équivalant à 92 000 000 USD pour le financement du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique (PAFEN) dont l’Objectif de Développement (ODP) est d’accroître l’accès à l’internet haut débit, en particulier pour les communautés mal desservies, et améliorer la capacité du Gouvernement à gérer les ressources plus efficacement et fournir des services publics par voie numérique.

Il a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements prévus au titre du contrat des services d’un « CABINET CHARGE D’ASSURER LES FORMATIONS DES CADRES DE LA BRB SUR : EMV »

  1. Objectif de principale

Dans un environnement de paiement en constante évolution, il est essentiel que les gestionnaires et surveillants des systèmes et moyens de paiement soient formés aux normes de sécurité et aux certifications pertinentes. Chacune de ces formations vise à approfondir les connaissances et les compétences dans des domaines spécifiques de la gestion des paiements, de la sécurité des informations, et de l'audit, offrant ainsi aux professionnels des compétences pratiques et théoriques ainsi que des outils nécessaires pour exceller dans leur domaine.

  1. Objectifs spécifiques

La formation EMV a pour objectif de fournir aux participants une compréhension approfondie des spécifications techniques et fonctionnelles liées aux cartes à puce et aux paiements sans contact. Elle prépare les professionnels à gérer la migration, l’implémentation et la sécurisation des systèmes de paiement EMV, tout en garantissant la conformité avec les standards internationaux et les exigences de certification.

Plus spécifiquement, elle vise à :

  • Comprendre les spécifications EMV et leur rôle dans les transactions par carte à puce et sans contact, incluant les architectures, les flux transactionnels et les mécanismes de sécurité intégrés.
  • Acquérir les compétences nécessaires pour gérer et implémenter des transactions EMV, depuis la personnalisation des cartes jusqu’à l’intégration avec les terminaux et systèmes bancaires.
  • Maîtriser les aspects de sécurité liés aux paiements EMV, notamment la cryptographie, l’authentification dynamique et la protection contre la fraude.
  • Préparer et accompagner la migration vers les standards EMV, en assurant la compatibilité avec les infrastructures existantes et les nouvelles technologies (NFC, paiements mobiles).
  • Renforcer la capacité à conduire et réussir les processus de certification EMV, en respectant les procédures, tests et exigences des organismes internationaux.
  • Développer une vision prospective des évolutions de l’écosystème EMV, incluant l’EMV 3-D Secure, l’acceptation mobile et l’impact des paiements instantanés.

Durée de la mission

  • Durée de la mission : La mission s’étendra sur dix (10) jours calendaires.
  • Durée de la formation : La formation elle-même se déroulera sur cinq (05) jours consécutifs.
  • Lieu : La formation sera dispensée au Burundi.
  • Calendrier indicatif :
    • Jours 1 à 5 : Animation des sessions de formation, incluant les exercices pratiques, études de cas et évaluations intermédiaires.
    • Jours 6 à 10 : Consolidation des acquis, évaluation finale des participants, rédaction et finalisation du rapport de formation.
  • Livrables :
    • Rapport final de formation, incluant :
      • Contenu détaillé des sessions dispensées
      • Résultats des évaluations des participants
      • Recommandations pour le suivi et la mise en pratique des acquis
  • Modalité de paiement : Le paiement unique sera effectué à la livraison du rapport final de formation.

Les Termes de référence peuvent être téléchargés sur le site du PAFEN : https://pafen.gov.bi/appels-doffres/  ou obtenus aux adresses mentionnées ci-dessous.

Le PAFEN invite pour le moment les Cabinets éligibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services (brève présentation de leurs cabinets, références concernant l’exécution de contrats analogues, expérience dans des conditions semblables, copies des contrats déjà réalisés, etc.).

Les missions similaires réalisées doivent être accompagnées des preuves de réalisation.

PROFIL DU CABINET 

Le Cabinet devra remplir au minimum les conditions suivantes :

  • Etre un cabinet international de formation et de conseil spécialisé dans les systèmes de paiement, la sécurité des données et les normes internationales associées.
  • Disposer d’une expérience d’au moins 20 ans dans l'accompagnement des professionnels des secteurs bancaire, fintech et technologique dans la maîtrise des normes de paiement et de sécurité.
  • Disposer de capacités à combiner expertise technique pointue, pédagogie interactive et conformité stricte aux exigences réglementaires.

La formation devra être assurée par un consultant hautement qualifié et disposant d'une expérience significative dans le domaine de la sécurité des systèmes de paiement et de la formation. Le formateur/consultant devra avoir le profil suivant :

  • Être titulaire d’un Diplôme de Master (minimum) en informatique, sécurité de l'information, finance ou domaine connexe.
  • Avoir les certifications suivantes :
  1. Certification EMVCo : Pour la compréhension et l'implémentation des standards EMV.
  2. PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) : Pour la sécurité des transactions.
  3. CISSP ou équivalent : Pour une connaissance globale en sécurité de l'information.
  • Avoir au moins 5 ans dans le secteur des paiements, avec une expérience directe dans :
  1. L'implémentation de systèmes de paiement EMV.
  2. La gestion de projets de migration vers EMV.
  3. La gestion ou la consultation en sécurité des paiements.
  • Avoir déjà formé des équipes techniques ou commerciales sur les systèmes de paiement ou la sécurité des informations.
  • Avoir des connaissances approfondies :
  1. Des protocoles et standards EMV.
  2. De la cryptographie, en particulier pour les transactions sécurisées.
  3. Des systèmes de gestion des transactions.
  • Avoir une parfaite maîtrise des outils de test et de certification EMV, et des logiciels de gestion des transactions.
  • Expérience démontrée dans la formation, idéalement dans un cadre financier ou bancaire.
  • Capacité à adapter le contenu éducatif aux différents niveaux de compréhension et besoins des apprenants.
  • Une bonne maîtrise du français est exigée

L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur la section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) datant de septembre 2023 ». En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques sur les conflits d'intérêts liés à cette mission.

Les consultants peuvent s'associer à d'autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l'association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d'un sous-traitant. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de l'intégralité du contrat, s'ils sont sélectionnés.

Le bureau de consultants sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur les Qualifications du consultant (SQC), conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI), édition de Septembre 2023 et conformément aux critères exigés au regard des termes de référence.

Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être livrées par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, ou par courrier, ou par e-mail) avant le 27/10/2026 au plus tard à 16 heures avec mention :

Assignment Title: Independent Verification Agent

1. BACKGROUND

 

The World Bank, through the International Development Association, has extended a credit of EUR 49.3 million (USD 52 million) to the Government of Kosovo, under a financing agreement for the Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project. The main objective of the Project is to strengthen financial stability and promote financial inclusion in Kosovo by enhancing the capacity of the Deposit Insurance Fund, supporting access to finance for underserved firms, and catalyzing faster payment systems.

The Project is structured as an Investment Project Financing incorporating elements of results-based financing through Performance-Based Conditions as well as Financial Intermediary Financing. Accordingly, the Project is organized into several components and subcomponents which reflect different implementation areas.

 

2. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

 

The objective of this assignment is to engage a qualified consulting firm to conduct the independent verification of the achievement of PBCs 1-7 as defined under the Project. The disbursement of the funds for the project is contingent upon the successful fulfillment of PBCs associated with each component and subcomponent for the project. In this context, the Borrower, represented by the MF, must submit satisfactory evidence to the World Bank in the form of a Verification Report.

3. SELECTION METHOD

The consulting firm will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. The firm with the best qualifications and relevant experience will be invited to submit combined technical and financial proposals and negotiate the contract.

4. SHORTLISTING CRITERIA

The Consultant shall meet the competence related criteria as follows:

  • A minimum of ten (10) years of institutional experience providing advisory, audit, or verification services in the financial sector. Within this period, at least five (5) of those years must be evidenced by completed audit engagements for financial sector institutions specifically. The firm's year of establishment and date of first qualifying financial sector engagement shall be confirmed through its company registration documents and the complete list of relevant assignments.
    • To demonstrate a verifiable track record, the firm shall submit a portfolio of at least ten (10) completed engagements in the financial sector conducted within the last ten (10) years, where the firm's scope explicitly included advisory, audit, monitoring and evaluation, or verification services. Of the ten engagements, at least five (5) must be audit engagements for financial sector institutions specifically. For each engagement, the firm shall provide the client's name and contact details, contract value and duration, a brief description of the scope, and key deliverable produced. The MoF reserves the right to contact listed clients to verify the scope and quality of delivery.
    • At least one (1) of the five qualifying engagements must have been conducted in Kosovo, and at least one (1) additional engagement must have been conducted in a comparable country context, defined for this assignment as a country in the Western Balkans, Eastern Europe, or Central Asia.
  • Proven institutional banking and financial sector expertise, demonstrated through the relevance of the scope of firm assignments, to adequately review and evaluate information furnished to confirm the authenticity and completeness of achievement of the Project’s PBCs, including through the preparation of the respective verification reports. The firm must demonstrate, through its submitted assignment list, experience in two (2) of the following focus areas:
    • i) financial sector legal and regulatory frameworks, and
    • ii) governance and operations of financial institutions.

At least two (2) of the submitted assignments must explicitly demonstrate experience in each focus area. The relevance of each assignment to a focus area must be evident from the scope description field in the assignment list; no separate narrative will be assessed.

 

Other specific tasks, deliverables, professional and qualified key staff requirements, etc. are indicated under ToR for this assignment.

 

The evaluation criteria are: 

  • General qualifications and institutional capacity (30%) (Core business and years of experience, Corporate and organizational capacity to undertake the assignment).
  • Relevant experience in similar assignments (60%) (Experience in audit, verification, assessment, or monitoring assignments; Experience in the financial sector and related institutions).
  • Overall capacity to deliver the assignment (10%) (Availability of qualified personnel within the firm-not the key experts needed for the assignment but in general-and ability to mobilize resources and deliver the assignment within the required timeframe)

5. CONFLICT OF INTEREST PROVISIONS

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

  1. Introduction

The African Union (AU) was established as a unique Pan African continental body, charged with spearheading Africa’s rapid integration and sustainable development by promoting unity, solidarity, cohesion and cooperation among the peoples of Africa and African States as well as developing a New Partnership worldwide. Its Headquarters is located in Addis Ababa, capital city of Ethiopia.

The African Union Commission (AUC) is the secretariat of the AU, which is the key organ playing a central role in the day-to-day management of the AU.  Amongst other mandates, the AUC represents the Union and defends its interests; elaborates draft common positions of the Union; prepares strategic plans and studies for the consideration of the Executive Council; elaborates, promotes, coordinates and harmonizes the programmes and policies of the Union with those of the Regional Economic Commissions (RECs) and ensures the mainstreaming of gender in all programmes and activities of the Union.

  1. Project Background

In 2008, AUC embarked on automation project and selected the SAP software to bring efficiency, transparency and accountability in business processes and information management. The project went live at the AUC in 2009, and with addition of several modules over the years, the system has since been rolled out to over 45 ROs/LOs and 8 Organs.

Currently, AUC runs SAP ERP ECC 6, Enhancement Package Level 7 (EHP7) system having implemented the following key modules;

  • Financial and Controlling (FI/CO) including Fund Management, Treasury Management, Bank Communication Management.
  • Human Resource (Payroll, Time Management, Personnel Administration, Organization Management, & Personnel Development)
  • Material Management (Purchasing and Inventory Management)
  • Travel Management
  • Employee and Manager Self Service
  • Electronic Document Workflow (SAP Document Access solution)
  • Integration with OpenText 10 for Document Archival
  • Integration to SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting system
  • Integration with SAP Governance, Risk & Compliance system (GRC) for user management
  • Interface with other in-house applications e.g. Medical System, AMERT,

The diagram below depicts the current SAP landscape alongside AUC’s vision by 2026/2027.

 

 

 

Despite the numerous strides made with the implementation of the modules above, the current system has some gaps and challenges in terms of system utility, process integration, data issues, reporting and inflexibility to some needs of the organization.  In cognizance of these gaps and in seeking to fully leverage the use of SAP within the Commission, there is therefore need to enhance/upgrade the ERP to a more robust system that will better meet the current and future needs.

 To date, the approach to automation at the AUC has focused on the implementation of point solutions that do not adequately address the present needs of AU Business Units, ROs and Policy Organs as a whole. The solutions provided have essentially automated the existing manual processes rather than follow best practices.  Lack of funds to adopt new SAP technologies has led to heavy customization of processes such as travel, financial management and reporting thus restricting the value that SAP can provide. Further, inadequate capacity building has rendered the ERP unit as a fire-fighter on day-to-day business support rather than the unit focusing on innovation to provide new solutions. There is great potential to maximize utility of SAP through varied and targeted training of both business users and the ERP team members.

  1. AU CURRENT PAINS AND GAPS

The AU has deployed the SAP Travel Management Module without the DSA calculation component resulting in DSA being manually calculated by excel by the respective payment processing Division of the Directorate of Finance.  The same also affects the imprest retirement process.  SAP users are not able to generate financial statements from SAP system.  SAP users want the budget execution report to be reviewed and enhanced. SAP users are creating manual reports in excel.  Fund availability is being done manually by all Departments.

 

  1. MERITS OF IMPLEMENTING REQUIRED FUNCTIONALITY
  • Efficient DSA calculation process thereby reducing the risks resulting from human errors
  • Timely retirements of imprests.
  • Accurate Financial statements generated from SAP without any manual intervention by users.
  • Efficient fund availability approval process.

The objective of the assignment is to implement the functionality (Section 4) mentioned above.  To achieve the stated objective, AUC wishes to engage the services of a consultant to work with the Commission to develop and implement the required functionality.

description:
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS

Project: West Africa Coastal Areas Resilience Investment Project 2

Grant No.: E1400-GM

Procurement Category: National & International FIRMS

Assignment Title: Group training on Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM), Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), and Environmental Management

Procurement Reference:  GM-CPCU-557470-CS-CQS

The Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the West Africa Coastal Areas Resilience Investment Project 2 (WACAResIP 2) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for non-consulting services (“the Services”) for capacity building training on Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM), Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), and Environmental Management for National Environment Agency (NEA)  for approximately twenty-five (25) NEA staff.

  1. Objectives of the Consultancy

The primary objective of this consultancy is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the NEA staff to effectively implement Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM), Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), and evidence-based environmental management systems in The Gambia.

Specific Objectives and Scope of Work

The Training Service provider is expected to design and deliver a comprehensive, in-house training program for approximately twenty-five (25) NEA staff. The training should be practical, participatory, and tailored to the specific context of The Gambia's coastal environment. The scope of work covers the following key areas:

  1. Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) and Environmental Governance
  • Build a clear and practical understanding of the ICZM concepts, principles and approaches
  • Provide training on coastal planning, zoning, permitting systems, and integration of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA)
  • Enhance understanding of institutional arrangements, inter-agency coordination mechanisms, and stakeholder management for effective ICZM implementation
  • Strengthen understanding of coastal hazards, climate change, coastal erosion, flooding, ecosystem degradation and competing coastal land uses
  • Introduce practical approaches for addressing coastal development pressures and cumulative impacts

 

  1. Monitoring, Evaluation and Environmental Data Management

 

  • Improve understanding of M&E concepts, principles and frameworks
  • strengthen participants’ ability to develop appropriate environmental indicators
  • Develop capacity to establish baselines, targets, milestones and means of verification
  • Improve systems for environmental data collection, management, analysis, and results-based reporting
  • Equip participants with skills for compliance monitoring and enforcement procedures

 

  1. GIS, Remote Sensing and Spatial Planning
  • Provide practical training on the use of GIS, remote sensing, and other digital monitoring tools for coastal management
  • Demonstrate remote sensing applications for environmental monitoring
  • Demonstrate mapping of coastal risks, land-use change and ecosystem conditions

 

  1. Action Planning
  • Facilitate the development of practical implementation strategies and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to translate training into actionable institutional improvements.

 Training Methodology

The training must adopt a highly interactive, participatory and adult-learning oriented methodology, recognizing that participants are experienced professionals who require practical application of concepts to their institutional responsibilities. The methodology should combine the following approaches:

  • Expert-led presentations and lectures
  • Interactive group discussions and case studies based on the Gambian context
  • Hands-on practical exercises and scenario-based simulations
  • GIS and mapping exercises
  • Field demonstrations
  • Experience sharing from national and regional experts

 

  1. Firm Experience and Key Experts

 

Qualifications and Experience of the Consulting Firm

4.1. General Experience

The consulting firm must demonstrate the following minimum general experience

 

No.

Requirement

Minimum experience

1

Proven experience in designing and delivering successful capacity-building programs in ICZM, M&E, environmental management, and related fields

At least 3 comparable assignments 

2

Demonstrated experience working with government institutions, particularly environmental agencies

At least 2 assignments with government/environmental agencies 

3

A team of experts with complementary skills in the required thematic areas (ICZM, M&E, GIS/Remote Sensing, Environmental Law/Governance)

Minimum 4 key experts covering all thematic areas

4

Experience in West Africa or similar developing-country contexts

At least 1 assignment in West Africa or comparable coastal developing-country context

5

Experience in developing training materials, case studies, and practical exercises tailored to local contexts

At least 2 assignments involving development of training materials

 

  1. Key Expert Team – Flexible and Multidisciplinary Structure

The consulting firm should propose a lean or multidisciplinary team appropriate to the short-term training assignment. The proposed team should collectively demonstrate the following competences:

  • Integrated Coastal Zone Management, coastal planning, coastal resilience, environmental governance and sustainable coastal development
  • Monitoring and Evaluation, environmental indicators, baselines, targets, results-based management, compliance monitoring and environmental data management
  • GIS, remote sensing, spatial analysis and practical applications for coastal and environmental monitoring
  • Environmental law, regulatory frameworks, permitting, EIA/ESIA integration, compliance and institutional governance
  • Capacity building, professional training and adult-learning methodologies, including facilitation, experiential learning, problem-based learning, practical exercises, peer learning, coaching and assessment of learning outcomes

 

6.1. Minimum Qualifications and Experience of Key Experts

For the key experts proposed, the following minimum requirements should apply. The requirements are intended to recognize the specialized nature of ICZM while allowing relevant professionals from closely related coastal, marine, environmental, natural-resource, spatial-planning, governance and climate-resilience disciplines to contribute where they demonstrate practical relevance to the assignment.

 

Team Leader / Senior ICZM and Coastal Management Specialist

  • Master’s degree or higher in Coastal Zone Management, Environmental Management, Marine Science, Natural Resources Management, Geography, Climate Change, or a closely related discipline
  • Minimum 10 years of professional experience in coastal, marine, environmental, natural resources, climate-resilience or related management fields
  • Minimum 5 years of demonstrated experience in ICZM, coastal planning, coastal governance, coastal resilience, marine spatial planning or closely related integrated coastal management work
  • Demonstrated experience in at least two relevant areas such as coastal planning/zoning, policy and institutional development, stakeholder coordination, coastal hazards and resilience, permitting, ecosystem-based management, environmental governance or related areas
  • Demonstrated experience designing and/or delivering professional training or capacity-building for government officials, technical institutions or other adult professional audiences
  • Strong practical experience in adult-learning approaches, facilitation, case-based learning, group work, coaching, practical exercises and assessment of learning outcomes is highly desirable
  • Experience in West Africa or comparable coastal developing-country contexts is desirable.

 

Other Key Experts / Specialists

The remaining experts may be drawn from the following competency areas, with one expert allowed to cover more than one area where appropriately qualified:

  • Environmental Management, M&E and Compliance – minimum 8 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 5 years in M&E, environmental indicators/frameworks, compliance monitoring, environmental data or results-based management
  • GIS, Remote Sensing and Spatial Planning – minimum 7 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 5 years applying GIS/remote sensing to environmental, coastal, marine or land-use planning and demonstrated experience delivering hands-on training
  • Environmental/ICZM Legal and Institutional Governance – minimum 8 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 5 years in environmental law, policy, regulation, permitting, EIA/ESIA, compliance or institutional governance
  • Training and Adult Learning – where this competency is not adequately covered by the Team Leader or another proposed expert, the team should include an expert with demonstrated experience in adult education, competency-based training, instructional design, facilitation and evaluation of professional capacity-building programmes.

Firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (JV) and/or a sub-contracting. In the case of a JV, all the partners in the JV shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. JV Agreement should be included in the submission.

Further information (including the TOR) can be obtained electronically by email or at the address below during office hours from Monday-Thursday 09:00am to 1600 pm, Friday 09:00 to 12:00pm Gambian time.

Your technical proposal should clearly outline the methodology, work plan, qualifications and experience of the proposed experts and strategies you intend to implement in carrying out the assignment, with a strong focus on the terms of reference to ensure the successful execution of the project.

Additionally, your financial proposal should provide a comprehensive breakdown of all fees and remunerations required for the assignment.

TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL PROPOSALS can be delivered in a written form or electronically to the address below (in person, by mail, or by e-mail) marked “capacity building training on Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM), Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), and Environmental Management” on or before Wednesday 21st October, 2026.

DEMANDE DE MANIFESTATIONS D'INTÉRÊT

N° du Projet : P176396

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET CHARGE D’ASSURER LES FORMATIONS DES CADRES DE LA BRB SUR ISO 8583

 Réf. STEP: BI-PAFEN-PIU-2.2.3.18_9-CS-CQS 

 

Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a obtenu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) un Don d’un montant équivalant à 92 000 000 USD pour le financement du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique (PAFEN) dont l’Objectif de Développement (ODP) est d’accroître l’accès à l’internet haut débit, en particulier pour les communautés mal desservies, et améliorer la capacité du Gouvernement à gérer les ressources plus efficacement et fournir des services publics par voie numérique.

Il a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements prévus au titre du contrat des services d’un « CABINET CHARGE D’ASSURER LES FORMATIONS DES CADRES DE LA BRB SUR : ISO 8583 »

  1. Objectif de principale

Dans un environnement de paiement en constante évolution, il est essentiel que les gestionnaires et surveillants des systèmes et moyens de paiement soient formés aux normes de sécurité et aux certifications pertinentes. Chacune de ces formations vise à approfondir les connaissances et les compétences dans des domaines spécifiques de la gestion des paiements, de la sécurité des informations, et de l'audit, offrant ainsi aux professionnels des compétences pratiques et théoriques ainsi que des outils nécessaires pour exceller dans leur domaine.

  1. Objectifs spécifiques

La formation ISO 8583 vise à fournir aux participants les compétences nécessaires pour comprendre, analyser et mettre en œuvre les standards de messagerie financière. Elle s’articule autour des objectifs spécifiques suivants :

  • Comprendre et maîtriser la norme ISO 8583 et son rôle central dans l’échange de messages financiers.
  • Développer des compétences pratiques pour analyser, concevoir, développer et assurer le support des systèmes basés sur ISO 8583.
  • Garantir l’interopérabilité et la sécurité des transactions financières à travers l’application correcte des formats et protocoles de messagerie.

Durée de la mission

  • Durée de la mission : La mission s’étendra sur dix (10) jours calendaires.
  • Durée de la formation : La formation elle-même se déroulera sur cinq (05) jours consécutifs.
  • Lieu : La formation sera dispensée au Burundi.
  • Calendrier indicatif :
    • Jours 1 à 5 : Animation des sessions de formation, incluant les exercices pratiques, études de cas et évaluations intermédiaires.
    • Jours 6 à 10 : Consolidation des acquis, évaluation finale des participants, rédaction et finalisation du rapport de formation.
  • Livrables :
    • Rapport final de formation, incluant :
      • Contenu détaillé des sessions dispensées
      • Résultats des évaluations des participants
      • Recommandations pour le suivi et la mise en pratique des acquis
  • Modalité de paiement : Le paiement unique sera effectué à la livraison du rapport final de formation.

Les Termes de référence peuvent être téléchargés sur le site du PAFEN : https://pafen.gov.bi/appels-doffres/  ou obtenus aux adresses mentionnées ci-dessous.

Le PAFEN invite pour le moment les Cabinets éligibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services (brève présentation de leurs cabinets, références concernant l’exécution de contrats analogues, expérience dans des conditions semblables, copies des contrats déjà réalisés, etc.).

Les missions similaires réalisées doivent être accompagnées des preuves de réalisation.

PROFIL DU CABINET 

Le Cabinet devra remplir au minimum les conditions suivantes :

  • Etre un cabinet international de formation et de conseil spécialisé dans les systèmes de paiement, la sécurité des données et les normes internationales associées.
  • Disposer d’une expérience d’au moins 20 ans dans l'accompagnement des professionnels des secteurs bancaire, fintech et technologique dans la maîtrise des normes de paiement et de sécurité.
  • Disposer de capacités à combiner expertise technique pointue, pédagogie interactive et conformité stricte aux exigences réglementaires.

La formation devra être assurée par un consultant hautement qualifié et disposant d'une expérience significative dans le domaine de la sécurité des systèmes de paiement et de la formation. Le formateur/consultant devra avoir le profil suivant :

  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de master (minimum) en gestion des systèmes d'information, en sécurité des données, ou en informatique bancaire serait particulièrement valorisé.
  • Avoir les certifications suivantes :
  1. Certifications spécifiques à ISO 8583
  2. Certifications en sécurité des informations : CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional
  3. Certifications en technologies financières
  • Au moins 10 ans dans le secteur bancaire ou des paiements, avec une expérience directe dans :
    • La conception, l'implémentation, ou la maintenance de systèmes utilisant ISO 8583.
    • La gestion de projets ou l'ingénierie logicielle liée aux transactions financières.
    • La sécurisation des transactions financières et la gestion des messages interbancaires.
  • Connaissance approfondie :
    • Des spécifications ISO 8583, y compris les différents types de messages, les champs, et les codes de transaction.
    • Des protocoles de communication pour les transactions financières, comme TCP/IP, SSL/TLS.
    • Du traitement des données dans les systèmes de paiement, y compris la validation, la transformation, et la transmission des messages.
  • Connaissance de plusieurs langages de programmation, en particulier ceux utilisés dans les systèmes de paiement comme C, Java, ou Python.
  • Familiarité avec les outils de test de messages ISO 8583, les logiciels de simulation de transactions, et les systèmes de gestion de base de données.
  • Expérience démontrée dans la formation, idéalement dans un cadre financier ou bancaire.
  • Capacité à adapter le contenu éducatif aux différents niveaux de compréhension et besoins des apprenants.
  • Une bonne maîtrise du français est exigée

L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur la section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) datant de septembre 2023 ». (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

Country: Ethiopia

Grant No: P180117

Assignment Title: Principal Data Analyst for the African Programme on Aviation Data (APAD)

 

Reference No. ET-AUC-568151-CS-INDV

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the day-to-day management, quality assurance and analytical use of aviation data across APAD. The Principal Data Analyst leads the APAD reporting architecture, data-quality framework, analytics and dissemination products, and the functional coordination of the APAD data platform, and provides technical recommendations to the Director of Air Transport. Specific tasks include:

Leadership of APAD aviation statistics and reporting architecture

  • Lead the design and maintenance of the APAD reporting architecture, including data flows, indicator frameworks, definitions, standard templates and reporting cycles, aligned where relevant with ICAO, AU and international standards.
  • Oversee the regular collection and consolidation of aviation data from States, RECs and partner institutions, and set priorities and standards for completeness, timeliness and comparability.
  • Strengthen reporting through ICAO statistical forms and other agreed instruments, and oversee the APAD submission workflow, evidence tracking, scorecards, annual reporting calendar and escalation process.

Data quality, governance and standards

  • Lead the APAD data-quality framework, including validation rules, quality checks, metadata, definitions and quality-assurance procedures.
  • Identify anomalies, gaps and inconsistencies, decide on corrective actions, and oversee their implementation with data providers and the Assistant Data Analyst.
  • Contribute to APAD data governance arrangements, including roles, responsibilities, submission protocols, confidentiality and information-security practices.

Analytics, reporting and dissemination

  • Lead the production of statistical tables, analytical briefs, dashboards, snapshots and State reporting performance summaries at State, group-of-States, REC and continental levels.
  • Lead AFCAC statistical bulletins, annual aviation statistical reviews, thematic briefs and evidence notes, and quality-assure outputs prepared with support from the Assistant Data Analyst.
  • Define and track corporate and programme key performance indicators, including BIASHARA / SAATM results indicators.

APAD platform functional coordination

  • Lead the functional coordination of the APAD aviation data platform, database and portal, translating APAD requirements into functional specifications in coordination with AFCAC IT, the consultancy firm and data providers.
  • Coordinate platform requirements, validation workflow, user roles, access rights, hosting and security arrangements from a functional and data-governance perspective.
  • Oversee the integration of datasets, metadata, dashboards and dissemination tools, and confirm that platform outputs meet APAD reporting and quality requirements.

 

Support to Member States and RECs

  • Lead capacity-building activities (workshops, clinics, on-the-job guidance) to strengthen Member State and REC reporting practices and the use of AFCAC / APAD tools.
  • Represent APAD in technical missions, meetings and technical assistance activities as delegated by the Director of Air Transport.
  •  

Supervision and guidance of the Assistant Data Analyst         

  • Plan, assign, guide and quality-assure the work of the Assistant Data Analyst, including data collection follow-up, data cleaning, submission tracking and documentation.
  • Set priorities and standards, review outputs, and support the professional development and effective performance of the Assistant Data Analyst.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The African Union Commission now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Transport Economics, Information Systems, Mathematics, Computer Science or a related field.
  • A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible professional experience in data management, statistics, analytics, monitoring and evaluation, or related work, including experience in a lead or senior technical role; experience in aviation or transport is a strong asset.
  • Relevant experience in aviation, transport, public policy or economic regulation, and in working with international, regional or intergovernmental organizations, will be a strong advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience working with multi-country datasets, reporting systems or institutional statistics programmes, and in supervising technical staff or service providers, is highly desirable.
  • Strong knowledge of statistics, data management, quantitative analysis and data governance, preferably applied to transport, aviation, regulation or public-sector programmes.
  • Experience with aviation statistical reporting, including ICAO statistical forms and State reporting systems, is a strong advantage.
  • Proven ability to design and lead data-quality frameworks, reporting architectures and analytics products.
  • Functional understanding of data platforms, databases, interoperability and information security sufficient to coordinate platform requirements with IT teams and service providers.
  • Proficiency with spreadsheets and at least one statistical or BI / visualization tool (e.g. R, Python, Power BI, Tableau or similar).
  • Demonstrated experience in coordinating or supervising staff, consultants or technical service providers, including deliverables tracking and quality review.
  • Excellent drafting skills for technical notes, procedures, briefs and reports.
  • Strong leadership, coordination and stakeholder-engagement skills; ability to work with senior management, Member State focal points, RECs and partner organizations.
  • Ability to work effectively in a multicultural and multilingual environment.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 

Individual Consultant as Principal Data Analyst for the African Programme on Aviation Data (APAD)

Ref: ET-AUC-568151-CS-INDV

1. Organizational Setting

 

AFCAC is the Executing Agency for the Yamoussoukro Decision and supports the realization of the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM), contributing to the African Union Agenda 2063. Within this mandate, AFCAC must provide credible, timely and comparable aviation statistics to underpin regulatory oversight, market liberalization, safety and security initiatives, infrastructure planning, and evidence-based policy dialogue at continental and global levels.

The African Programme on Aviation Data (APAD) was established to assist AFCAC in providing comprehensive and reliable data for States and aviation stakeholders.

To operationalize APAD, AFCAC requires a Principal Data Analyst to serve as the lead technical expert for APAD aviation statistics, reporting, data quality, analytics and platform coordination, and to lead the monitoring and technical support of the APAD consultancy under the BIASHARA project. The Principal Data Analyst is supported by an Assistant Data Analyst, whose work the Principal Data Analyst guides and supervises.

2. Purpose of the Position

 

The Principal Data Analyst is the lead expert responsible for the day-to-day management, quality assurance and analytical use of aviation data across APAD. The Principal Data Analyst leads the APAD reporting architecture, data-quality framework, analytics and dissemination products, and the functional coordination of the APAD data platform, and provides technical recommendations to the Director of Air Transport. The Principal Data Analyst also leads the monitoring and technical support of the APAD consultancy firm under the BIASHARA project and supervises and guides the Assistant Data Analyst.

3. Major Duties and Responsibilities

 

3.1 Leadership of APAD aviation statistics and reporting architecture

 

  • Lead the design and maintenance of the APAD reporting architecture, including data flows, indicator frameworks, definitions, standard templates and reporting cycles, aligned where relevant with ICAO, AU and international standards.
  • Oversee the regular collection and consolidation of aviation data from States, RECs and partner institutions, and set priorities and standards for completeness, timeliness and comparability.
  • Strengthen reporting through ICAO statistical forms and other agreed instruments, and oversee the APAD submission workflow, evidence tracking, scorecards, annual reporting calendar and escalation process.

3.2 Data quality, governance and standards

 

  • Lead the APAD data-quality framework, including validation rules, quality checks, metadata, definitions and quality-assurance procedures.
  • Identify anomalies, gaps and inconsistencies, decide on corrective actions, and oversee their implementation with data providers and the Assistant Data Analyst.
  • Contribute to APAD data governance arrangements, including roles, responsibilities, submission protocols, confidentiality and information-security practices.

3.3 Analytics, reporting and dissemination

 

  • Lead the production of statistical tables, analytical briefs, dashboards, snapshots and State reporting performance summaries at State, group-of-States, REC and continental levels.
  • Lead AFCAC statistical bulletins, annual aviation statistical reviews, thematic briefs and evidence notes, and quality-assure outputs prepared with support from the Assistant Data Analyst.
  • Define and track corporate and programme key performance indicators, including BIASHARA / SAATM results indicators.

3.4 APAD platform functional coordination

 

  • Lead the functional coordination of the APAD aviation data platform, database and portal, translating APAD requirements into functional specifications in coordination with AFCAC IT, the consultancy firm and data providers.
  • Coordinate platform requirements, validation workflow, user roles, access rights, hosting and security arrangements from a functional and data-governance perspective.
  • Oversee the integration of datasets, metadata, dashboards and dissemination tools, and confirm that platform outputs meet APAD reporting and quality requirements.

 

3.5 Support to Member States and RECs

 

  • Lead capacity-building activities (workshops, clinics, on-the-job guidance) to strengthen Member State and REC reporting practices and the use of AFCAC / APAD tools.
  • Represent APAD in technical missions, meetings and technical assistance activities as delegated by the Director of Air Transport.
  •  

3.6 Supervision and guidance of the Assistant Data Analyst   

 

  • Plan, assign, guide and quality-assure the work of the Assistant Data Analyst, including data collection follow-up, data cleaning, submission tracking and documentation.
  • Set priorities and standards, review outputs, and support the professional development and effective performance of the Assistant Data Analyst.

 

4. Required Expertise and Skills

 

  • Strong knowledge of statistics, data management, quantitative analysis and data governance, preferably applied to transport, aviation, regulation or public-sector programmes.
  • Experience with aviation statistical reporting, including ICAO statistical forms and State reporting systems, is a strong advantage.
  • Proven ability to design and lead data-quality frameworks, reporting architectures and analytics products.
  • Functional understanding of data platforms, databases, interoperability and information security sufficient to coordinate platform requirements with IT teams and service providers.
  • Proficiency with spreadsheets and at least one statistical or BI / visualization tool (e.g. R, Python, Power BI, Tableau or similar).
  • Demonstrated experience in coordinating or supervising staff, consultants or technical service providers, including deliverables tracking and quality review.
  • Excellent drafting skills for technical notes, procedures, briefs and reports.
  • Strong leadership, coordination and stakeholder-engagement skills; ability to work with senior management, Member State focal points, RECs and partner organizations.
  • Ability to work effectively in a multicultural and multilingual environment.

 

5. Qualifications and Experience

 

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Transport Economics, Information Systems, Mathematics, Computer Science or a related field.
  • A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible professional experience in data management, statistics, analytics, monitoring and evaluation, or related work, including experience in a lead or senior technical role; experience in aviation or transport is a strong asset.
  • Relevant experience in aviation, transport, public policy or economic regulation, and in working with international, regional or intergovernmental organizations, will be a strong advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience working with multi-country datasets, reporting systems or institutional statistics programmes, and in supervising technical staff or service providers, is highly desirable.

 

6. Core Competencies

 

  • Leadership and strategic thinking sets direction and standards, understands how aviation data supports AFCAC’s mandate, and generates practical evidence for management and policy decisions.
  • Professionalism and accountability: reliability, sound judgment, accuracy, and a strong commitment to delivering high-quality outputs on time.
  • Communication skills: communicates clearly and persuasively in writing and orally with senior management, technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Planning, coordination and supervision: plans and manages complex workstreams, tracks deliverables and risks, and supervises and develops staff and service providers.
  • Client orientation and teamwork: supports internal and external users constructively and leads collaborative work across technical, administrative and partner institutions.
  • Integrity and confidentiality: upholds high standards of ethical conduct, discretion and confidentiality in handling institutional and potentially sensitive datasets.

 

7. Reporting and Working Relationships

Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI)

Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT)

Southeast Asia Regional Economic Corridor and Connectivity Project – Additional Financing (SEARECC - AF)

Consulting Services for Implementation Support and Works Supervision (ISWS)

for OPBR Contract (OPBRC) for Rehabilitation of National Road No.2 West, Section 4

(Pak Beng to Muang Ngeun, Thai Border) and Local Road in Samphanh District, Phongsaly Province

(Consulting Service - Firms Selection, Reference No. SEARECC-QCBS-001- FS001-AF)

The Government of Lao People’s Democratic Republic (GoL) has applied financing support from the International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Lao PDR Southeast Asia Regional Economic Corridor and Connectivity Project – Additional Financing (SEARECC-AF) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services are required to support the Employer in the detailed design review, implementation and supervision of the rehabilitation and improvement works to be financed under the SEARECC Additional Financing (AF), including NR2W Section 4 under the Output- and Performance-Based Road Contract (OPBRC) and the Khua–Samphan Local Road in Phongsaly Province under the Hybrid Performance-Based Contract (HPBC).

The services include but are not limited to: (i) reviewing the detailed designs prepared by the Contractors for NR2W Section 4 under the OPBRC and the Khua–Samphan Local Road under the HPBC, and providing recommendations to the Employer; (ii) supervising the rehabilitation and improvement works and monitoring compliance with the applicable technical specifications, performance requirements and contractual obligations; (iii) reviewing the Contractors’ site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans and associated plans, including the Traffic Management Plan, Community Health and Safety Plan, Labor Management Plan and Occupational Health and Safety Plan; (iv) supporting the Employer in monitoring compliance with the Project’s environmental and social requirements and approved instruments; (v) advising and supporting the Employer on relevant aspects of Project implementation; and (vi) engaging a certified laboratory, where required, to undertake environmental monitoring, including air-quality, noise and water-quality monitoring. All environmental and social activities shall be consistent with the applicable Site-Specific Environmental and Social Management Plans, ARAP/RAP, EGEP, SEP and other approved Project environmental and social instruments, and shall comply with the applicable Environmental and Social Standards and Government of Lao PDR requirements. The Services shall be carried out in accordance with applicable Project requirements and Good International Industry Practice.

The ISWS Consultant is expected to commence the assignment in parallel with the OPBRC and HPBC Contractors, whose contracts are expected to be awarded by May 2027. The assignment comprises two parts: (i) supervision of the rehabilitation of NR2W Section 4 under the OPBRC; and (ii) supervision of the improvement of the Khua–Samphan Local Road under the HPBC. The services are expected to cover the 36-month rehabilitation and improvement works period, commencing in the second quarter of 2027. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be request from the address given below or download from link: https://1drv.ms/w/c/4b4fca78445f7e3e/IQD6xUUXRNy0T5JCNSzoBGezASfwFa3cY6MZitkSEtlBW1E?e=ztqWJd.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport, through the Department of Roads now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

Criterion 1 - Supervision of road works:  At least ten (10) years of experience in Works Supervision of national road improvement or rehabilitation contracts of equivalent or comparable value, scope of nature in the capacity of prime contractor (i.e. individually or as lead member of JV); such experience in South/ Southeast Asia is a strong asset;

Criterion 2 - Type of road works and services:  At least 3 supervision contracts or equivalent or comparable value, scope and nature under OPBRC, OPRC, DBMOT or similar arrangement, successfully completed in the capacity of prime contractor (i.e. individually or as lead member of JV) within the past 10 years; such experience under WB or other multilateral development banks is an asset;

Criterion 3 - Monitoring of ESF in road works and services: Minimum 3 contracts of similar scope and nature performed in the past 10 years in the capacity of prime contractor (i.e. individually or as lead member of JV), including implementation and/or monitoring of RAP, ESIA, ESMP for road construction, improvement or rehabilitation.

Expressions of Interest (EOIs) shall be submitted in English. Consultants shall include maximum 15 contracts per criterion listed above and will arrange the “past contract information forms” separately for each criterion. Failure to provide the required detail in the past contract information forms shall be under full Consultant’s responsibility – there will be no clarifications carried out during evaluation. In case the Consultant shall provide more than 15 contracts for each criterion, only the first 15 references shall be considered for evaluation. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Regulations - Procurement in Investment Project Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (September 2025 edition), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A consulting firm will be selected under the method of quality and cost-based selection (QCBS) in accordance with the said WB Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 8:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday.

Expression of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by email by 17:00 hours (Local time of Vientiane Capital, Lao PDR, GMT+7) of 23 October 2026.

Department of Planning and Finance, Ministry of Public Works and Transport

Lanexang Avenue, Phonxai Village, Saysettha District, Vientiane Capital, Lao PDR.

Attention : Mr.Phitsphol Philavong, Deputy Director General, Department of Roads

Email : proc.dpf.mpwt@gmail.com with Cc : pphonh.plv@gmail.com, sk.venvongsoth@gmail.com and maxmahaxay11@hotmail.com

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Mr. Sysouphanh Chansavat

Director General, DOR, MPWT

  2. El Ministerio de la Presidencia (MINPRE) invita a los Licitantes elegibles a presentar Ofertas en sobres cerrados para la modernización del marco geodésico de referencia vertical y el establecimiento de la Red de Nivelación de Alta Precisión de República Dominicana (RNAPRD), incluyendo el análisis y propuesta del marco geodésico de referencia vertical, diseño detallado, reconocimiento de campo y monumentación de bancos de nivel (BM), mediciones de nivelación geométrica de alta precisión y GNSS, procesamiento y ajuste, catálogo final de coordenadas y alturas, capacitación y transferencia de conocimientos, conforme a los requisitos técnicos, productos, entregables, estándares de calidad, plazos, condiciones de ejecución y demás disposiciones establecidas en el documento de licitación.

La licitación se llevará a cabo por medio de adquisiciones competitivas internacionales, utilizando el método de Solicitud de Ofertas (SDO), conforme a las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, de noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), y se encuentra abierta a todos los Licitantes elegibles, según se define en dichas Regulaciones de Adquisiciones.
  5. Las ofertas se evaluarán de acuerdo con el procedimiento de evaluación establecido en los documentos de licitación. Se aplicarán las siguientes ponderaciones para los Criterios con Puntaje (incluidos los factores técnicos y no relacionados con el precio): 65% y para el costo de la oferta: 35%.
  6. Los Licitantes elegibles interesados podrán solicitar más información al Ministerio de la Presidencia, a la atención del Sr. Domingo Matías, Viceministro de Ordenamiento Territorial y Desarrollo Regional, al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do, y consultar el documento de licitación en el horario de atención 09:00 a 16:00, en la dirección que figura más abajo.
  7. Los Licitantes elegibles interesados podrán adquirir el documento de licitación en español previa presentación de una solicitud por escrito dirigida a la dirección que figura más abajo. El documento de licitación estará disponible sin costo. No aplica pago por la adquisición del documento, podrá ser descargado en la página web indicada debajo, o solicitado a través del correo electrónico indicado.
  8. Las Ofertas deberán dirigirse a la dirección que se indica más abajo, a más tardar el día 24 de noviembre de 2026, a las 10:00 a.m. hora de República Dominicana. No está permitida la presentación electrónica de Ofertas. Las Ofertas recibidas fuera del plazo establecido serán rechazadas. Los sobres exteriores de la Oferta marcados como “OFERTA ORIGINAL” y los sobres interiores marcados como “PARTE TÉCNICA” se abrirán públicamente en presencia de los representantes designados de los Licitantes y de cualquier persona que decida asistir, en la dirección que figura a continuación el día 24 de noviembre de 2026, a las 10:10 a.m. hora de República Dominicana. Todos los sobres marcados como “PARTE FINANCIERA” permanecerán sin abrir y se mantendrán bajo custodia segura del Contratante hasta la apertura pública de las Partes Financieras.
  9. Todas las Ofertas deberán ir acompañadas de una Declaración de Mantenimiento de la Oferta. Esta debe estar incluida en el Sobre Técnico.
  10. Se llama la atención sobre las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones del Banco Mundial, que requieren que el Prestatario divulgue información sobre la propiedad efectiva del adjudicatario, como parte de la Notificación de Adjudicación de Contrato, utilizando el Formulario de Divulgación de la Propiedad Efectiva incluido en el documento de licitación.
