KINGDOM OF CAMBODIA

Ministry of Interior (MOI)

Cambodia Solid Waste and Plastic Management Improvement Project

IDA Grant No. 7292-KH

Request for Expression of Interest

For Individual Consultants

  1. Introduction
  1. The objective of the solid waste and plastic management improvement project (the Project) is to improve solid waste and plastic management in selected areas. The project will be implemented over a period of 6 years (2023-2029), and budget of US$67.3 million will be allocated for the following four components: Component 1 – Institutional Strengthening for Solid Waste and Plastic Management (US$ 4.32 million, implemented by Ministry of Environment), Component 2 – Integrated Solid Waste and Plastic Management, Planning, Monitoring, and Capacity Building for Participating Provinces, Municipalities and Districts (US$8.42 million, implemented by Ministry of Interior). Component 3 – Solid Waste and Plastic Management Infrastructure (US$54.56, implemented by Ministry of Public Works and Transport) and Component 4 –emergency response with zero allocation has been provisioned for the Bank to provide emergency support in the event of a natural disaster, emergency and/or catastrophic event.
  1. The Project Development Objective (PDO) and Key Results Indicators
  1. The PDO is to improve solid waste and plastic management in selected areas, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it. There are three PDO level indicators that will be measured through the following indicators: (i) Proportion of population in selected areas with regular household waste collection, to be measured by the percentage of population that will have regular waste collection; (ii) the landfill disposal capacity operational per defined criteria, to be measured by the amount of landfill disposal capacity that will be realized under the project in Cubic Meter (m3); (iii) plastics policies, guidelines, or standards developed, to be measured by the number of policies, guidelines or standards developed; and (iv) the percentage of municipal solid waste recovered, recycled, composted and/or treated with other techniques.
  1. The Project now invites expressions of interest from qualified and experienced individual consultants to undertake with the assignment listed below:
  1. National Procurement Consultant (Intermittent), Ref. No: MOI-INV-16
  2. Administrative and Contract Management Assistant, Ref. No: MOI-INV-17
  1. The interested consultants will be evaluated based on the qualification and relevant experience in regards to the minimum criteria listed below:
  1. National Procurement Consultant (Intermittent)
  • At least Bachelor degree in Business Administration, Commerce or other relevant field;
  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in carrying out procurement of goods, works and consultant services under bilateral/multilateral funded projects/programes including WB, ADB, EU and other development donors;
  • Experience of procurement with the Royal Government of Cambodia’s Standard Procurement Manual, Bidding Documents and Proposals for Externally financed Projects will be an advantage;
  • Have ability to work independently and provide trainings to other staffs when needed;
  • Demonstrated ability to consult and work cooperatively with others as a team; and
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Khmer and good report writing skill.
  1. Administrative and Contract Management Assistant
  • At least Bachelor degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Law, Engineering, or other relevant field;
  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in carrying out administrative services under bilateral/multilateral funded projects/programes including WB, ADB, EU and other development donors;
  • Experience in office management, project operation and procurement will be an advantage;
  • Ability to work independently, provide trainings and work as  a team, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines under pressure;
  • Demonstrated ability to consult and work cooperatively with others as a team; and
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Khmer and good report writing skill.
  1. The consultants will be based at the Project Management Unit.
  1. The selection process will be carried out in accordance with provisions set forth in the Government Procurement Manual for Externally Financed Projects/Programs in Cambodia and Approved Selection Method for Individual Consultants - Section VII. Approved Selection Methods: Consulting Services of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Fourth Edition (November 2020).
  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found with the link: https://www.owso.gov.kh/wp-content/uploads
  1. Interested candidates are requested to obtain detailed terms of reference (TOR) and send your expression of interest (EOI) by submitting the updated curriculum vitae with current photo and cover letter with at least three referees by email and attention to: Mr. Ung Keorattanak, Deputy Project Manager, Email: rattanak.ukr@gmail.com and Copy to and Mr. Soun Samreth, Procurement Officer, Email: dst.samreth@gmail.com.
  1. Expression of Interest must be submitted no later than October 21, 2026 before 5:00 pm (Local Time). Only Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interview.
  1. Contact Address: Ministry of Interior, Rom No.356, 3rd Floor, Preah Norodom Boulevard, Tonle Bassac, Chamkamon, Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D'INTERET N° CI-PADCI-568100--CS-INDV-26

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D'UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) INDIVIDUEL(LE) POUR ACCOMPAGNER LE MINISTERE DE LA TRANSITION NUMERIQUE ET DE L’INNOVATION TECHNOLOGIQUE DANS L’ELABORATION DES REFORMES LEGALES

CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), financé par la Banque mondiale, le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de l’Innovation Technologique (MTNIT) lance un Avis à manifestation d’Intérêt en vue du recrutement d’un consultant (e) individuel (le).

La mission porte sur l’accompagnement dans l’élaboration des reformes juridiques en vue de l’opérationnalisation de la loi sur les communications électroniques.

L’objectif général de l’étude est (i) d’accompagner juridiquement le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de l’Innovation Technologique (MTNIT) afin d’accélérer l’élaboration des reformes légales, (ii) de rédiger des textes pour l’opérationnalisation de la loi n° 2024-352 du 06 juin 2024 relative aux communications électroniques selon les bonnes pratiques internationales et les recommandations communications, (iii) identifier les dispositions règlementaires supplémentaires à mettre en place pour encadrer des sujets innovants tels que l’usage de l’intelligence artificielle, le développement du Big data , (iv) de renforcer les capacités et transfert  de connaissances en droit du numérique et les nouvelles pratiques internationales ; (v) donner des conseils juridiques divers (avis et conseils juridiques sur toute question en rapport avec le droit du numérique).

1. Missions du/de la consultant(e)

  • Rédiger une note de cadrage de la mission : Lors du démarrage de la mission, une réunion de cadrage sera organisée avec le Consultant afin d’harmoniser la compréhension des termes de référence, ainsi que la démarche à suivre pour une bonne exécution de la mission. Par la suite, le Consultant fournira au Coordonnateur du projet PADCI, la méthodologie et le calendrier détaillé d’exécution de la mission ;
  • Collecter les données à travers une revue documentaire de l’existant ;
  • Consulter les acteurs concernés à travers des rencontres ;
  • Procéder au traitement des données collectées.
  • Examiner les lois, règlements et jurisprudences existants pertinents au sujet traité. Cette analyse permettra de s'assurer que les textes rédigés sont conformes aux normes légales et réglementaires en vigueur.
  • Rédiger une première version des textes juridiques en tenant compte des données collectées et des consultations effectuées. Cette version servira de base pour les discussions et les révisions ultérieures.
  • Animer des consultations pour recueillir les avis et commentaires des parties prenantes, et du public si nécessaire. Cela peut inclure des ateliers, des réunions publiques ou des consultations en ligne.
  • Intégrer les commentaires reçus lors des consultations et réviser les textes en conséquence.
  • Préparer des documents de formation à l’attention de la DAJCI.

1. Profil du consultant individuel

Les consultants intéressés devront justifier :

  • Avoir au moins un diplôme de BAC+5 en droit ;
  • Avoir une expérience d’au moins dix (10) années dans le domaine du numérique ;
  • Avoir conduit au moins deux (02) missions en tant qu’expert dans l’accompagnement des Etats dans le domaine du numérique ;
  • Avoir mené au moins deux (02) missions des réformes du secteur en matière de transition numérique et de digitalisation ou dans l’analyse ou la révision de cadre réglementaires TIC au cours des dix (10) dernières années ;
  • Avoir une bonne maîtrise des textes régissant l’écosystème numérique ivoirien ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience de travail d’au moins trois (03) ans dans une autorité de régulation des télécommunications ;
  • Avoir participé à l’élaboration de la Loi sur les Communications Electroniques en Côte d’Ivoire serait un atout majeur ;
  • Avoir une bonne expérience de l’administration publique ivoirienne serait un atout ;
  1. CONSTITUTION ET DEPOT DES MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

Les manifestations d'intérêt soumises par les consultants individuels devront comprendre les pièces suivantes :

  • Une lettre de manifestation d'intérêt datée, signée et cachetée ;
  • Un curriculum vitae détaillé, daté et signé, accompagné d'une copie des diplômes requis ;
  • Les justificatifs attestant de l'exécution des missions similaires déclarées, notamment des attestations de bonne exécution, des certificats de service fait, des fiches de projet ou tout autre document probant équivalent.                             

 Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être déposées sous pli fermé comprenant cinq (05) exemplaires dont un original, et une version électronique (sur clé USB ou tout autre support électronique) portant clairement la mention « Manifestation d’intérêt N° CI-PADCI-568100-CS-INDV pour le recrutement d’un(e) consultant(e) individuel(le) pour accompagner le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de l’Innovation Technologique (MTINT) dans l’élaboration des reformes légales » au plus tard le mardi 06 octobre 2026 à 10 heures GMT à l’adresse géographique ci-dessous :

 Siège du PADCI, sis à Angré 8ème Tranche, Cité les Elites II, non loin du Fast Food Chicken Nation, Tél. : (225) 07 08 32 89 34 / (225) 07 09 46 99 70.

 

L’ouverture publique des plis ayant lieu le même mardi 06 octobre 2026 à 10 heures 00 minute GMT.

La durée de la mission est estimée à quatre (04) mois.

 

Le/la consultant(e) intéressé(e) devront solliciter l’intégralité des Termes de Références aux courriels suivants : ju.koffi@telecom.gouv.ci, avec en copie obligatoire à gn.kouame@telecom.gouv.ci et à padci@telecom.gouv.ci.

MINISTERE DE L’ENTREPRENEURIAT ET DEVELOPPEMENT DES PETITES ET MOYENNES ENTREPRISES

UNITE DE COORDINATION DU PROJET TRANSFORME/RDC

PROJET D’AUTONOMISATION DES FEMMES ENTREPRENEURES ET MISE A NIVEAU DES PME POUR LA TRANSFORMATION ECONOMIQUE ET L’EMPLOI

« TRANSFORME-RDC »

 

N° de crédit / N° de don : Banque mondiale, Crédit n°7101-ZR / Don E0280-ZR

Titre de la mission : Recrutement d’un consultant/cabinet chargé de l’actualisation de la stratégie nationale de développement des PME.

N° de référence : ZR-TRANSFORME- 566554-CS-CQS

Date de publication : 07 octobre 2026

Date de clôture :  21 octobre 2026.

 

AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité et reçu un crédit et un don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) d’un montant total équivalent à 300 000 000,00 USD en vue de financer le coût du « Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et une mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi (TRANSFORME-RDC)» et se propose d’utiliser une partie des fonds de ce crédit et don pour financer les services suivants : « Recrutement d’un consultant/cabinet chargé de l’actualisation de la stratégie nationale de développement des PME »

         Pour ce faire, le Consultant procédera à l’évaluation de la Stratégie nationale de développement des PME de 2016.

         Les services consistent à : 

  • Réaliser le diagnostic de l’écosystème entrepreneurial sectoriel ;
  • Réaliser un diagnostic documentaire sur les principaux cadres nationaux, régionaux et internationaux de référence ;
  • Identifier les contraintes structurelles, institutionnelles, juridiques, fiscales, financières et techniques ainsi que les points d’amélioration pour son adaptation aux réalités du moment ;
  • Évaluer la mise en œuvre du draft de stratégie de 2021 ;
  • Identifier les autres travaux stratégiques en cours d’élaboration (notamment la plan stratégique climat des affaires, feuille de route climat des affaires, l’initiative formalisation de masse, etc.) afin d’assurer une cohérence d’ensemble des orientations et maximiser les complémentarités ;
  • Conduire des consultations inclusives avec les parties prenantes publiques et privées ;
  • Définir les orientations stratégiques, les axes prioritaires et programmes d’actions ;
  • Structurer un cadre logique assorti d’indicateurs de performance ;
  • Développer une théorie de changement établissant les liens de causalité entre les interventions proposées, les résultats attendus et les impacts recherchés ;
  • Concevoir une stratégie de financement assortie d’un plan de mobilisation des ressources ;

description:
AVIS DE PUBLICATION DE LA DEMANDE DE COTATION N° CI-PADCI-568102-NC-RFQ-26 POUR LA SÉLECTION D’UN PRESTATAIRE POUR CONCEVOIR, DÉPLOYER ET METTRE EN EXPLOITATION UNE PLATEFORME DE CENTRE DE CONTACT OMNICANAL ET UNE BASE DE CONNAISSANCES INTELLIGENTE, PLEINEMENT INTÉGRÉES À L’ÉCOSYSTÈME E-JUSTICE

Le Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), mis en œuvre par le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation, invite les entreprises spécialisées intéressées à soumettre leurs offres dans le cadre de la Demande de Cotation relative à la :

« Sélection d’un prestataire pour concevoir, déployer et mettre en exploitation une plateforme de centre de contact omnicanal et une Base de Connaissances intelligente, pleinement intégrées à l’écosystème e-Justice ».

1. Objet de la consultation

La présente consultation porte sur la sélection d’un prestataire qualifié chargé de concevoir, déployer et mettre en exploitation une plateforme de centre de contact omnicanal et une Base de Connaissances intelligente intégrées à l’écosystème e-Justice. La mission comprend notamment la mise en place d’une solution Helpdesk/ITSM multicanale, la création et l’alimentation d’une Base de Connaissances, l’intégration avec les plateformes et systèmes existants du Ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, ainsi que la formation des équipes et l’assistance au démarrage. La solution devra être sécurisée, évolutive et conforme aux exigences applicables en matière de protection des données et de cybersécurité.

2. Financement

La présente consultation est financée dans le cadre du Projet d’Accélération Digitale en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI), avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale. Le PADCI est financé selon le mécanisme de Financement des Projets d’Investissement (IPF).

3. Conditions de participation

La participation est ouverte aux entreprises légalement constituées, disposant des capacités techniques, professionnelles, administratives et financières nécessaires à l’exécution des prestations objet de la présente consultation.

Le soumissionnaire devra notamment être en mesure de mobiliser une équipe comprenant au minimum un Chef de projet IT senior, un Expert Helpdesk / ITSM, un Architecte sécurité et un Spécialiste en formation et conduite du changement.

4. Retrait du dossier

Le dossier de Demande de Cotation peut être retiré gratuitement auprès de :

Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Accélération Digital en Côte d’Ivoire (PADCI)
Abidjan Angré 8ème Tranche, Cité les Elites II, non loin du Fast Food Chicken Nation

Voir la Cellule Passation des Marchés ; Tél : (+225) 07 08 32 89 34/ 07 09 46 99 70

Email : ju.koffi@telecom.gouv.ci  avec copie obligatoire à gn.kouame@telecom.gouv.ci padci@telecom.gouv.ci
à compter de la date de publication du dossier, aux jours et heures ouvrables notamment du lundi au vendredi de 8 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 17 heures, Temps Universel.

Le retrait du dossier ne sera plus autorisé à compter du troisième (3ème) jour précédant la date limite de remise des offres.

La présente publication est faite à l’attention de toute agence de communication intéressée et répondant aux conditions de participation définies dans le dossier de consultation.

5. Constitution du dossier de candidature

Veuillez soumettre un dossier de candidature complet comprenant notamment :

- une copie du Registre de Commerce et du Crédit Mobilier (RCCM) de l’entreprise ;

- une attestation de situation fiscale délivrée par les services fiscaux compétents ;
- une attestation de mise à jour délivrée par la Caisse Nationale de Prévoyance Sociale (CNPS) ;

- une fiche signalétiques de l’entreprise et une presentation de ses activités ;

- le profil du dirigeant et des membres clés de l’équipe (les CV, diplômes et certifications des experts clés);

- Les références de l’entreprise en matière de réalisation de prestations similaires (Attestation de Bonne Exécution).

6. Date et heure limites de dépôt des plis

Les offres doivent être déposées au plus tard le mardi 06 octobre 2026 à 10 heures 00 minute, sous pli fermé, avec la mention :  « Consultation de Prestataire N° CI-PADCI-568102-NC-RFQ-26 pour Sélection d'un prestataire pour l'acquisition et la mise en place de la plateforme technologique y compris la base de connaissances ».

Le dépôt des offres devra faire l’objet d’un enregistrement sur la fiche de réception des offres tenue à cet effet au service Passation des marchés du PADCI.

7. Ouverture des plis

L’ouverture des offres aura lieu en séance publique le mardi 06 octobre 2026 à 14H00 dans les locaux du PADCI sis à la 8ème Tranche, non-loin du Fast Food Chicken Nation Cité les Elites II, Email : ju.koffi@telecom.gouv.ci  avec copie obligatoire à gn.kouame@telecom.gouv.ci; padci@telecom.gouv.ci,  Tel : (+225) 07 08 32 89 34 / 07 09 46 99 70.

REPUBLIQUE DU BENIN

PRESIDENCE DE LA REPUBLIQUE

PROJET DE CONSTRUCTION DU BARRAGE MULTI-FONCTIONS DE DOGO-BIS : PHASE 1 : P513979

FINANCEMENT : CREDIT IDA

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET : BJ-DOGO BIS-534378-CS-INDV

Expert Social auprès du Panel d’Experts-Environnements Sociaux Barrage

Cet avis à manifestation d’intérêt annule et remplace celui paru le mercredi 23 septembre 2026 dans le journal La Nation N° 9079

Date : 07 octobre 2026

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Bénin a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet de Construction du Barrage Multi-fonctions de Dogo-Bis Phase 1, et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif au recrutement d’un Expert Social auprès du Panel d’Experts-Environnements Sociaux Barrage, qui sera conclu à la suite de la présente sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt.
  2. Les services à fournir par le consultant dans le cadre de cette mission consisteront à conseiller et assister à temps plein l’équipe de préparation du Projet Dogo Bis sur les problématiques sociales relatives à la réalisation dudit projet.

Plus spécifiquement, il s’agira de : 

  • Conseiller le Gouvernement du Bénin (GdB) pour que globalement les objectifs sociaux visés par le projet en général et les autres instruments de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale (Evaluation environnementale et sociale Stratégique, EIES, Plan d’Urgence, Plan de gestion de la biomasse, etc.) en particulier soient atteints ;
  • Conseiller le GdB pour que la préparation du projet soit d’une part cohérente avec la politique environnementale et sociale nationale, les textes législatifs et réglementaires liés à la gestion des aspects sociaux ou ayant un rapport direct/indirect avec le projet, et d’autre part, soit en mesure de satisfaire les exigences de la Banque mondiale en matière de gestion des diligences sociales ;
  • Donner un avis sur le Dossier de Consultation des Entreprises (DCE) ainsi que sur les marchés des ouvrages y compris les questions relatives à la gestion des risques sociaux ;
  • Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le Panel Technique des barrages pour que les avis et recommandations donnés au gestionnaire du projet par les experts soient cohérents et transmis dans les délais.
  • fournir au Gouvernement du Bénin, à l’Unité de gestion du projet (UGP) et aux partenaires financiers des avis indépendants sur toutes les questions relatives aux domaines suivants :
    • Évaluation et gestion des risques et effets sociaux ;
    • Mobilisation des parties prenantes, consultations approfondies et diffusion des informations ;
    • Emploi et conditions de travail ;
    • Afflux de main-d’œuvre et relations entre les travailleurs et les communautés ;
    • Questions de santé et de sécurité des populations comportant d’importantes dimensions sociales ;
    • Prévention et atténuation des risques d’EAS/HS et prise en charge centrée sur les survivant(e)s ;
    • Mécanismes de gestion des plaintes des communautés et des travailleurs ;
    • Inclusion sociale et prise en compte des individus et groupes défavorisés ou vulnérables, ainsi que cohésion communautaire ; et
    • Suivi des risques sociaux émergents pendant la préparation et la mise en œuvre du Projet.
  • donner des avis sur tous les documents sociaux à produire dans le cadre de la préparation du projet et ce pour tous les ouvrages et infrastructures retenues :
  • recommander des études complémentaires ;
  • donner un avis sur tous les termes de référence et les rapports de toutes les études (l’Etude d’Impact Environnemental et Social, l’étude d’impact cumulatif, l’étude de la gestion des forêts hors retenue, la gestion de la biomasse, l’étude archéologique, etc.) ;
  • donner un avis sur les coûts estimatifs et le planning de mise en œuvre des PGES;
  • s’assurer que les clauses sociales répondant aux standards nationaux et internationaux sont bien intégrées dans les dossiers d’appel d’offre des ouvrages ;
  • fournir l’appui nécessaire au Coordonnateur du projet pour que les recommandations sociales soient correctement incorporées dans la documentation juridique et financière du projet ;
  • faire des recommandations pour garantir la bonne gestion des impacts sociaux du projet pendant toute phase du projet, incluant notamment la phase travaux ;
  • assister le Coordonnateur du projet lors des réunions avec les bailleurs de fonds ;
  • organiser des échanges avec les parties prenantes et des visites de terrain ;
  • préparer des rapports périodiques avec recommandations et des plans d’actions.

3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Construction du Barrage Multi-fonctions de Dogo-Bis Phase 1 par la présente sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt, invite les consultants individuels intéressés à exprimer leur intérêt à fournir les services ci-dessus décrits. Ils doivent être des experts en développement social ayant au moins quinze (15) ans d’expériences confirmées dans l’élaboration des instruments de sauvegarde, la mise en œuvre d’activités sociales telles les consultations publiques et la mobilisation des parties prenantes, et d’expérience en gestion des risques en matière de travail, de santé et sécurité des communautés, d’EAS/HS des plaintes. Les consultants doivent fournir les informations indiquant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour exécuter ces services (CVs signés avec les références concernant l’exécution de contrats analogues, expérience dans des conditions semblables, capacité technique). Les informations doivent être fournies en deux exemplaires dont un original. En cas de différence entre les exemplaires, l’original fera foi.

Les critères d’évaluation des CVs sont les suivants :

  1. Qualification d'ordre général : Vingt-cinq (25) points

   Niveau d’étude : 05 points

  • BAC+5 minimum en sciences sociales: 05 points
  • BAC+5 minimum dans un domaine équivalent : 03 points
  • Autres: 0 point

Expérience : 20 points

  • Expérience professionnelle d’au moins quinze (15) ans dans les études sociales

< 15 ans d’expérience : 2,50 points par période de 5 ans

> = 15 ans d’expérience : 10 points (A justifier par des attestations de travail ou tout autre document pertinent)

  • Avoir été membre d’un panel d’experts indépendant d’un grand projet d’aménagement hydroélectrique en zone tropicale : 10 points.

b) Adéquation pour la mission : Soixante-quinze (75) points

  • Mission d’élaboration d’instruments de sauvegarde sociale de grands projets d’infrastructures y compris hydraulique et hydroélectrique au cours des dix (10) dernières années (2016 à 2025) ou de l’année en cours en Afrique subsaharienne : 5 points par mission pour un maximum de 20 points ;
  • Mission en matière de mobilisation de parties prenantes, de gestion des risques en matière de travail, de santé et sécurité des communautés, d’EAS/HS et de plaintes de grands projets d’infrastructures y compris hydraulique et hydroélectrique au cours des dix (10) dernières années (2016 à 2025) ou de l’année en cours en Afrique subsaharienne : 5 points par mission pour un maximum de 20 points 
  • Mission en matière de mobilisation de parties prenantes, de gestion des risques en matière de travail, de santé et sécurité des communautés, d’EAS/HS et de plaintes de grands projets d’infrastructures y compris hydraulique et hydroélectrique au cours des dix (10) dernières années (2016 à 2025) ou de l’année en cours en Afrique de l’ouest : 12,50 points par mission pour un maximum de 25 points ;
  • Mission en matière de mobilisation des parties prenantes et de gestion des risques en matière de travail, de santé et sécurité des communautés, d’EAS/HS et des plaintes de grands projets d’infrastructures y compris hydraulique et hydroélectrique au cours des dix (10) dernières années (2016 à 2025) ou de l’année en cours sur un projet sur financement de la Banque mondiale : 5 points par mission pour un maximum de 10 points ;

En cas d’égalité du nombre total de points obtenus, les consultants seront départagés par le nombre de mission en matière de mobilisation de parties prenantes, de gestion des risques en matière de travail, de santé et sécurité des communautés, d’EAS/HS et de plaintes de grands projets d’infrastructures y compris hydraulique et hydroélectrique au cours des dix (10) dernières années (2016 à 2025) ou de l’année en cours en Afrique subsaharienne.

Les prestations similaires doivent être prouvées par les attestations de bonne fin d’exécution assorties de contrat (page de garde, page de signature et pages portant la durée effective de la mission et le montant en copie simple). Toute mission indiquée non soutenue par les preuves ci-dessus indiquées ne sera pas prise en compte. Les missions en cours ne seront pas prises en compte. Le Consultant devra fournir également la copie légalisée de son diplôme.

description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Identification of Sectoral Opportunities in Regions of Georgia – Least Cost Selection)

Country: Georgia

Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Project No: P173975

Loan No. 9239-GE

Assignment Title:  Identification of Sectoral Opportunities in Regions of Georgia

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): GE-GEDC-CS-LCS-03

Implementing Agency: JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation

Date: 07.10.2026

The Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia (MoESD), within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank, intends to apply part of the loan proceeds to support the identification and assessment of sectoral and business opportunities across the regions of Georgia, with a focus on regional and municipal competitive advantages, value-chain potential, and actionable investment and business opportunities.

The Project, Relief and Recovery for MSMEs, will be implemented nationwide and will consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. Component 1 is implemented by JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation (GEDC) (hereinafter – Client). It comprises of the following sub-components:

  • Sub-component 1.1 provide micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 provide partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 provide technical assistance to MSMEs in COVID-proofing, strengthening managerial skills, and digitalization through establishing Consulting Centers in the regions of Georgia (Growth Hubs - hereinafter GHs) to deliver specific services to MSMEs locally.

This Assignment:

The assignment consists of conducting a study to identify and prioritize sectoral opportunities across the municipalities and regions of Georgia.

The study shall:

  • Analyze Georgia’s existing and potential sectoral strengths at the national level, including established and emerging sectors, infrastructure, market trends, and other factors relevant to identifying economic and investment opportunities in the regions of Georgia;
  • Assess competitive advantages and sectoral opportunities at the municipal level across the regions of Georgia, identifying existing specializations, underutilized assets and capabilities, and opportunities for expansion, upgrading, diversification, and new sector development;
  • Map existing and potential value-chain linkages across municipalities and regions, identifying how production, processing, services, logistics, distribution, export, and other value-chain functions are currently distributed or could be developed across different locations;
  • Validate and refine the analytical findings through consultations with relevant institutions, businesses, and other stakeholders at the national, regional, and municipal levels;
  • Identify specific investment and business opportunities within the shortlisted priority sectors and locations, and prepare preliminary investment-readiness assessments for a prioritized shortlist of opportunities, covering the principal market, location, infrastructure, workforce, financing, regulatory and other enabling conditions and constraints;
  • Develop conclusions, recommendations, and a prioritized action plan for advancing the identified opportunities, including recommended next steps, required institutional and policy actions, potential business-support measures, further studies where required, and indicative short-, medium-, and longer-term priorities.

The outcome of the assignment shall enable the relevant stakeholders to direct investment promotion, regional development, and business support efforts toward the municipalities, regions, and sectors where competitive advantage and readiness are strongest.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xfvaZ4O82S6uumDtD2wDbG5aBNd0jEVb/edit usp=sharing&ouid=114433811295150382465&rtpof=true&sd=true

GEDC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The minimum selection criteria are:

  • Be a legal entity registered under the law of Georgia on Entrepreneurs, with no outstanding tax liabilities (unless deferred or exempt by law);
  • General Experience – The Consultant shall have at least six (6) years of demonstrated professional experience in economic research and advisory services, regional or local economic development, sectoral analysis, competitiveness assessment, investment-related advisory services, or other fields directly relevant to the Assignment.
  • Specific Experience - The Consultant shall have successfully completed, within the last six (6) years, at least three (3) regional economic development studies, sectoral opportunity assessments, and/or economic assessments, at least one (1) of which involved municipal- or regional-level analysis in Georgia or a comparable country.

To be considered for the selection, the interested consulting firm must submit the following documents:

  1. A brief description of the company’s background and organizational structure, including the year of legal registration/incorporation and an extract from the Registry of Entrepreneurial and Non-entrepreneurial (Non-commercial) Legal Entities. In the case of a Joint Venture (JV), this information shall be provided for each JV member.
  2. To demonstrate compliance with the experience requirement above, the Consultant shall provide a list of completed assignments under the contracts which shall include: 
  • Assignment name,
  • Scope (brief description of the deliverables/outputs),
  • name of clients and country of assignment,
  • duration (start and end dates), 
  • Contract Value (if was done in a form of a Joint Venture (JV) or sub-consultancy, the amount paid to the consultant), if was done in a form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy, the Consultant’s role/involvement.

Note: To support the preparation of Expressions of Interest (EOIs) and facilitate the assessment process, interested Consultants are provided with an experience form. Consultants are requested to complete this form in line with the requirements outlined above.

The Form is available at the link below:

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1efb3T6xdt7EvotIWpGeFBN7tPpXU0-Cb/view?usp=drive_link

        3. Proof of completion of similar contracts (contracts and respective delivery and acceptance certificates); Where confidentiality obligations apply, the firm may provide other information or documents that enable the relevant experience to be confirmed without breaching such obligations.

When evaluating jointly performed projects, only the experience and scope of work actually performed by the relevant firm and capable of being confirmed by the information submitted shall be taken into account.

Joint Venture (JV) Requirements – Consultants may form a Joint Venture consisting of a maximum of two (2) member firms. The JV members shall jointly demonstrate compliance with the General and Specific Experience requirements specified above.

The JV shall demonstrate at least six (6) years of relevant professional experience and at least three (3) successfully completed regional economic development studies, sectoral opportunity assessments, and/or economic assessments within the last six (6) years. At least one (1) of these studies shall have involved municipal- or regional-level analysis in Georgia or in a comparable country.

The Lead Member of the JV shall have successfully completed at least one (1) of the three (3) required studies.

The experience and qualifications of sub-consultants shall not be taken into consideration for the purpose of meeting the above qualification requirements.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Least-Cost Based Selection (LCS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit technical and financial proposals. Only the Consultants whose technical proposals achieve at least the minimum technical score specified in the RFP will have their financial proposals opened, and the Consultant offering the lowest evaluated price will be selected and invited for negotiations.

The attention of interested consulting firm is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, revised August 2018 and revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Interested consulting firm may obtain further information by email: gmaisuradze@gedc.ge.

Expressions of Interest in English language must be submitted electronically to the address below not later than October 22, 2026, at 17:00 (Tbilisi Time). The required documents (attached to the EOI) may be submitted in Georgian.

To: JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation

Attn: Guranda Maisuradze, Procurement Specialist

E-mail To: gmaisuradze@gedc.ge

Please include the title of the announced selection in subject line of the email.

The Government of the Republic of Angola (GoA) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), along with co-financing from the French Development Agency (AFD), to support the Electricity Sector Improvement and Access Project (ESIAP). Part of these funds is intended to finance the services of an Individual Consultant for the position of Senior Procurement Specialist, to strengthen the Project’s capacity in the implementation of procurement activities related to ESIAP.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The Senior Procurement Specialist will be responsible for carrying out procurement activities under the ESIAP Project. The main responsibilities include:

(i) Designing and implementing the procurement function within the PCU, including defining staffing structure, functional assignments, coordination with other departments/areas and electricity sector companies (PRODEL, RNT, ENDE, and IRSEA), providing training and mentoring in procurement, preparing procedures, and supporting the development of procurement manuals, in close cooperation with the procurement team and the aforementioned institutions; (ii) Establishing procurement instruments in strict compliance with World Bank procedures (Operational Manual, Procurement Regulations, and procurement management documents in line with the Project Implementation Manual); (iii) Executing procurement activities, including the development of procurement management tools tailored to project needs: preparation, consolidation, and updating of procurement plans in coordination with other areas and electricity sector entities; preparation of bidding documents in compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations; support during the authorization process, preparation of notices, responding to bidders’ requests for clarification, participation in proposal evaluation processes, and contract management; (iv) Developing mechanisms to monitor contract implementation, as well as procedures and practices necessary to ensure the integrity of the procurement system, including the filing system; (v) Coordinating and supervising training for stakeholders on procurement procedures.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for this assignment can be obtained at the address provided below.

The Project Coordination Unit (PCU) of the Ministry of Energy and Water (MINEA) hereby invites eligible Individual Consultants to express their interest in providing these services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the services (description of similar assignments, experience under similar conditions, etc.).

The Consultant should have the following qualifications:

  • Degree in Engineering, Economics, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law or equivalent, from a recognized University;
  •  Ten (10) years’ specific experience in procurement and contract management activities, from which at least eight (8) years’ experience in projects financed by the World Bank or other multilateral or bilateral institutions;
  • Documented previous experience in Larger Works contracts and experience in using World Bank or other multilateral and bilateral institutions documents;
  • Experience in using the WB STEP system;
  • Working experience in energy sector is an asset;
  • Computer skills (Word, Excel, and Power Point) as a user;
  • Working knowledge in Portuguese language. Fluency is an asset;
  • Working knowledge in English language;
  • Proven experience in contracting Works (at least two contracts valued USD 10,000,000.00 each), Goods and Non-Consulting Services (at least two contracts valued USD 2,000,000.00 each), as well as Consultancy Services (at least two contracts valued (USD 1,000,000.00 each), including elaboration of the associated ToRs, bidding documents, opening and evaluating bids/proposals, negotiating and managing contracts. {Applicant to submit evidence of experience}

Additional qualifications considered an advantage:

  • Master’s degree or Postgraduate Diploma in Engineering, Economics, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law from a recognized University or attendance of WB specific procurement related courses/seminars in addition to other relevant courses/technical seminars;
  • Three (3) years' experience in Angola in administrative processes of public institutions;
  • Knowledge of the Angola’s Government procurement procedures.

The Senior Procurement Specialist will be based in Luanda, Angola, at the ESIAP Office, and will report to the PCU Coordinator.

The Senior Procurement Specialist’s contract will have a duration of 12 months, on a full-time basis, renewable subject to satisfactory performance. While awaiting the issuance of an entry visa (if applicable), the consultant may work remotely, except when physical presence is required.

Arab Republic of Egypt

Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change Project

Loan No.: P172548

Assignment Title: “Updating guidelines for Healthcare Waste Management in Egypt”

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): EG-EEAA-559382-CS-QCBS

The Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change Project (herein “the Project”) aims at reducing air emissions from critical sectors and increasing resilience to air pollution in Greater Cairo. The Project aims more specifically at reducing air emissions which is a key step toward the reduction of pollution concentrations and improvement of air quality. The Project will focus on two of the primary sources of air pollution in the Greater Cairo (GC) region (i.e., Cairo, Giza and Qalyoubia Governorates): open burning of solid waste and vehicle emissions; and will include six main components aiming at: (i) enhancing the air quality management framework and decision support system in Egypt; (ii) improving Solid Waste Management services; (iii) reducing air and climate pollutants from vehicle emissions; (iv) furthering stakeholder engagement, awareness and communication; (v) project management and monitoring & evaluation (M&E); (vi) addressing the important issue of unintended emissions of POPs.

Brief description about the  Enhanced E-Waste and HCW management for Reduction of uPOPs:                 

 It is an additional finance (AF) to the parent project; this new activity focuses on reduction of unintended persistent organic pollutants (uPOPs) aligns with the “GEF Project Design and Review Considerations in Response to the COVID-19 Crisis and the Mitigation of Future Pandemics”. This new component will comprise 3 sub-components.

Sub-component 6.2: Supporting Effective Healthcare Waste Management, Models, and Solutions has been designed under the proposed Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change project (P172548).

This sub-component aims to strengthen the enabling environment for sustainable healthcare waste (HCW) management. It seeks to develop and pilot innovative solutions to reduce unintentional Persistent Organic Pollutants (uPOPs) emissions and promote long-term systemic changes in HCW practices across Egypt.

Key activities under this sub-component include:

(i)         developing and modeling public/private financing and investment models for collection and treatment of HCW.

(ii)        providing technical assistance to select healthcare institutions on utilization of possible financial mechanisms, procurement of environmentally-sound equipment, training of staff, and integration with the new protocols and facilities.

(iii)       supporting the preparation of a plan to roll out proper HCW management throughout the country in collaboration with key agencies and stakeholders (including women and other vulnerable communities).

(iv)       pilot appropriate recycling and re-sale of safely segregated HCW.

The requested services covered by these terms of reference are to support the Project Coordination Unit (PCU) and the Technical Implementation Units (TIUs) of “Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change (GGAP&CC) Project” in the implementation of the service of Developing Guidelines for the Healthcare Waste Management in Egypt

The Project now invites eligible consultancy firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested suppliers should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the scope.

The expected duration of the assignment is 12 months

Scope of Work:

The selected Consultant will be required to:

1. Review Existing Institutional Framework

  • Assess the roles and responsibilities of existing committees (for example, the Hazardous Waste Materials Committee in MOH, Committee 53 on Hazardous Materials and Waste in WMRA, Technology Accreditation Committee in MOH, and Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA)) within each relevant entity to ensure integration and effective coordination among stakeholders.

2. Review Existing Legal Guidelines

  • Review and update the existing HCWM guidelines developed under the GEF Medical and E-waste Project (2018), incorporating legislative and institutional updates, including the roles and responsibilities of all relevant authorities and stakeholders (WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, MOHE, EDA) involved in healthcare waste management. Identify gaps and areas requiring updates based on current regulations and practices.

3. Stakeholder Engagement

  • Collect and consolidate requirements, standards, and procedures from key entities such as WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, EDA, Ministry of higher education (MOHE), and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Organize consultations and workshops with stakeholders to gather feedback and ensure alignment.

4. Review HCW audit report conducted for the Ain Shams Specialized and French Kasr elany hospitals conducted within project.

  • The consultant should review and take into consideration the findings of the healthcare waste audit report conducted in this project at the two hospitals under study.

5. Update Existing Guidelines

  • Draft comprehensive HCWM guidelines incorporating:
    • National regulations and policies.
    • Input from stakeholders.
  • Address all stages of HCWM, including generation, identification, segregation, storage, transportation, treatment, and disposal.

6. Validation and Finalization

  • Circulate the draft guidelines to stakeholders (WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, MOHE, EDA) for validation and feedback.
  • Revise and finalize the guidelines based on received input.
  • Organize a workshop with all stakeholders to present the final version.

Deliverables:

  • A detailed work plan outlining the timeline for the proposed tasks.
  • Report on the review of existing guidelines and identified gaps.
  • Stakeholder consultation report summarizing collected inputs and feedback.
  • Draft  healthcare waste management guideline for adoption by the Ministry of Local development and Environment in coordination with the relevant competent authorities. Submit a concise "Key Issues and Resolution Report" outlining:

 (i) the main gaps and inconsistencies identified in the existing HCWM guidelines and how they have been addressed in the updated draft; and

 (ii) the key improvements and strengthened provisions introduced, together with a brief rationale for each revision.

  • Final updated guidelines, incorporating all feedback and aligning with national and international standards.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at https://www.eeaa.gov.eg/Uploads/Notification/Files/2026082412552499.pdf

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) a adressé à la Banque Mondiale une requête relative au financement de deux nouveaux projets, le Projet de Facilitation des Investissements (PFI) et le Projet de Développement de la Capacité Statistique pour Améliorer la Prise de Décision (DECIDE) et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie du financement du projet PFI pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché de recrutement d’un(e) Spécialiste en Passation des Marchés (SPM).

Sous l'autorité directe du Coordonnateur de l'UGP-PFI/DECIDE (et sous la supervision du RPM de la CEP-O pendant la phase transitoire de préparation), le/la Spécialiste en Passation des Marchés (SPM) est chargé(e) d'assurer le bon déroulement de toutes les activités de passation des marchés du projet. A ce titre, il/elle réalise toutes les activités relatives à la planification, la conduite et la gestion du processus de passation des marchés des biens, travaux, services non-consultants et services de consultants dans le cadre des projets PFI et DECIDE.

Le/la SPM aura notamment pour mission de :

  • Élaborer et assurer la mise à jour régulière du Plan de Passation des Marchés (PPM) ;
  • Assurer le suivi des activités de passation des marchés et identifier les sources de retard ;
  • Conseiller le RPM et/ou le Coordonnateur ainsi que les membres de l’équipe sur les procédures de passation des marchés.
  • Apporter un appui lors de l’ouverture des plis, de l’évaluation des offres et de la proposition d’attribution des marchés.
  • Préparer les dossiers de passation des marchés, notamment les AMI, AAO, AAP, DAO, DC et DP.
  • Assurer la revue qualité des rapports d’évaluation des offres, propositions, candidatures et manifestations d’intérêt, ainsi que des TDR et prescriptions techniques.
  • Assurer l’archivage physique et électronique des dossiers de passation des marchés, notamment dans STEP.
  • Participer à la gestion et au suivi des contrats, notamment des garanties, délais, ordres de service et avenants.
  • Coordonner et superviser les activités des Assistants en passation des marchés placés sous sa responsabilité.
  • Contribuer à l’évaluation des besoins en renforcement des capacités et au transfert de compétences.
  • Assurer la conformité des procédures de passation des marchés avec le Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale.

Les Termes de Reference (TDR) et le modèle de CV sont joints à cette demande de manifestation d'intérêt de la mission ou peuvent être trouvés sur le site web suivant : https://www.cepo.cd/.

La CEP-O invite les candidats intéressés à présenter leur candidature en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience (lettre de motivation datée et signée, curriculum vitae suivant le modèle à télécharger, attestations de service rendu ou tout autre document faisant foi de l’expérience acquise, copies légalisées du ou des diplômes par les autorités compétentes et autres supports) démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations.

1.  Background

The Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project is funded by the Japan Social Development Fund (JSDF) and administered by the World Bank. The Project is implemented by Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA) in close collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS) of Cambodia.

The Project aims to enhance access to and quality of Early Childhood Education (ECE) through the promotion of learning through play and the integration of digital technology in target districts in Cambodia. The Project supports teacher professional development, establishment of an ECE digital resource platform, parental and community engagement, improvement of preschool learning environments through construction and renovation, and implementation of pilot school meal programs.

The Project is implemented in selected districts in Battambang, Banteay Meanchey, and Pailin provinces, targeting public preschools with the objective of strengthening equitable access to quality ECE services for young children aged 3–5 years.

Under Component 2 of the Project, SVA will implement phase 1 of civil works activities, comprising: (i) construction of 8 new preschool buildings, toilets, water tanks and 6 kitchen facilities.; (ii) renovation of 17 existing preschool buildings; and (iii) outdoor environment improvements at  25 targeted preschools. These works are spread across three districts in Battambang province and one district in Banteay Meanchey Province., and procured through Request for Bids (RFB) and Request for Quotations (RFQ) methods

To strengthen day-to-day site supervision during the main construction period, SVA seeks to recruit two (2) National Individual Consultants – Site Engineers, one (1) based in Battambang Province and one (1) based in Banteay Meanchey Province. The Site Engineers will provide full-time, on-site supervision over the prime contractor(s) at project sites in their assigned provinces, under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

2.  Objectives

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that the prime contractor’s civil works at project sites are executed in accordance with the approved drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQ), and contract requirements, through on-site supervision by the Site Engineer.

Specifically, the Site Engineer will:

  • Provide full-time, day-to-day on-site supervision of the prime contractor’s works at project sites in the assigned province.
  • Ensure quality of materials and workmanship are complied with specification, approved drawing, method statement and schedules.
  • Ensure that the prime contractor executed all work in compliance with approved Environmental and Social(E&S) document
  • Maintain accurate and complete site records, including site diaries, inspection checklists, measurement records, and photo documentation.
  • Provide verified site-level information (progress, quantities, defects) to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer to support progress monitoring, payment certification, and completion.

3.  Scope of Work

Under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer, the Consultant shall undertake the following tasks at project sites in the assigned province:

a.  Site Mobilization and Pre-Construction

  • Become familiar with the approved drawings, technical specifications, BoQs, contract documents, and contractors’ work programs for each assigned site, and report any discrepancies to the Civil Engineer and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in site handover to contractors and in pre-mobilization meetings with contractors, school representatives, and the SVA project team.
  • Sites readiness: coordinate with contractor’s supervisor and relevant stakeholders at target schools during contractor mobilization.
  • Prepare and submit updated sites plan including photos
  • Confirm that contractors have mobilized the required personnel, equipment, materials, site signage, and safety arrangements before works begin.

b.  Day-to-Day Site Supervision and Quality Control

  • Conduct full-time, day-to-day supervision of civil works at assigned sites, prioritizing site visits according to construction schedules and critical activities.
  • Inspect and verify key construction stages before contractors proceed (e.g., reinforcement and formwork inspection prior to concreting), using standard inspection checklists.
  • Verify that materials delivered to site comply with approved samples and technical specifications, and reject and record non-compliant materials.
  • Witness and record field and material tests (e.g., concrete slump tests, sampling of concrete test cubes, compaction checks), and follow up on test results.
  • Issue site instructions to contractors on quality and workmanship issues within delegated authority, and refer matters beyond this authority, including design changes and variations, to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

c.  Site Records, Progress Monitoring and Reporting

  • Maintain a site diary for each site, recording daily activities, workforce and equipment, weather conditions, materials delivered, inspections, instructions issued, visitors, and issues.
  • Maintain photo documentation (before, during, and after works) and inspection records for each site.
  • Monitor actual progress against contractors’ approved work programs, and report delays together with proposed corrective measures.
  • Prepare weekly site progress reports and monthly reports, and submit them to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in regular site meetings and record minutes and agreed actions, as required.

d.  Measurement and Payment Support

  • Verify at sites the actual completed works in Activity Schedule submitted by contractors
  • Prepare measurement sheets and supporting documentation for contractors’ payment applications, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Record and report site conditions or instructions that may give rise to variations or claims, with supporting evidence, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

e.  Environmental, Social, and Safety Compliance

  • Monitor contractors’ daily implementation of occupational health and safety (OHS) measures, including use of personal protective equipment (PPE), site fencing and barricading, safety signage, safe working at height, and first aid, with particular attention to the safety of children, teachers, and community members at operating preschools.
  • Monitor implementation of E&S mitigation measures at construction sites, including dust and noise control, waste management, drainage, and agreed working hours, in coordination with the E&S Specialist.
  • Monitor contractor compliance with labor management requirements, including workers’ code of conduct and prevention of child labor.
  • Report E&S incidents, accidents, and non-compliance to the E&S Specialist and SVA Project Manager immediately, and in any case within 24 hours, and follow up on corrective actions.
  • Liaise with school directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), and local authorities on site-level matters, and refer community concerns and grievances to the Project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

f.  Completion and Handover

  • Participate in pre-completion and final inspections, and prepare defect (snagging) lists for each site.
  • Monitor rectification of defects by contractors and confirm completion of rectification works.
  • Compile site-level completion documentation, including as-built mark-ups, photo records, test records, and site diaries.
  • Support the handover of completed facilities to schools, School Management Committees (SMCs), and relevant government counterparts.

4.  Expected Outputs and Deliverables

The following deliverables are expected over the course of the assignment. Timelines are indicative and subject to adjustment based on project implementation progress and construction schedules.

5.  Work Supervision

The Consultant will work under the overall supervision of the SVA Project Manager and will receive day-to-day technical guidance from the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

The Consultant will coordinate and liaise with:

  • The Civil Engineer, the SVA Engineer, and the other Site Engineer, to ensure a consistent supervision approach across provinces;
  • PMU members and field staff;
  • The E&S Specialist and other technical consultants engaged under the Project;
  • Contractors, site supervisors, and construction personnel at project sites;
  • School directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), community representatives, and sub-national authorities at project sites.

The Consultant shall submit site records and weekly reports to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer, and monthly reports to the SVA Project Manager through the SVA Engineer, for review and approval. The Consultant shall participate in regular coordination meetings, site meetings, and World Bank supervision missions, as required.

6.  Contract Term and Location of Assignment

The contract period is eight (8) months, from November 2026 to July 2027, with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding.

The Consultant will be engaged as a full-time Individual Consultant (IC) under the NEST Project and is expected to be present at project sites on a daily basis throughout the assignment period.

Key arrangements are as follows:

  • Duty Station: Position 1 – Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts) Position 2 – Banteay Meanchey Province (covering project sites in Phnom Srok District)
  • Contract Modality: The contract will be time-based, with remuneration at a fixed monthly rate for the duration of the assignment.
  • Working Arrangements: Full-time, in accordance with SVA working hours. Work outside regular working hours may be required in line with construction activities, subject to SVA policy.
  • The Consultant is expected to work primarily at project sites and to make their own arrangements for workspace. No office space will be provided by SVA; however, the Consultant may use the SVA Battambang Office for meetings or as required. The Consultant is expected to provide their own computer, smartphone for photo documentation, and personal working equipment.
  • Payment Modality: Payment shall be made on a monthly basis upon submission and approval of monthly reports and agreed deliverables.
  • Travel costs directly related to project implementation and approved by SVA, including daily travel to project sites, will be covered in accordance with SVA travel policy.

7.  Consultant Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or other relevant technical field. A technical diploma with additional relevant site experience may be considered.

Experience

  • Minimum two (2) years of relevant professional experience in site supervision of building construction and/or renovation works.
  • Hands-on experience in site-level quality control, including stage inspections, material checks, and quantity measurement.
  • Experience in maintaining site diaries, inspection records, and progress reports.
  • Experience in construction of schools or other public or community buildings is an advantage.
  • Experience working on World Bank-financed or other internationally funded projects is an advantage.

Technical Competencies

  • Sound practical knowledge of building construction methods, materials, and quality control at site.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, technical specifications, and Bills of Quantities.
  • Ability to carry out site measurements and quantity verification.
  • Familiarity with occupational health and safety (OHS) requirements and environmental and social compliance in construction settings.
  • Ability to keep accurate records and prepare clear and timely reports.
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word and Excel); knowledge of AutoCAD is an advantage.
  • Fluency in Khmer is required; working knowledge of English, both written and spoken, is required.

Other Considerations

  • Willingness to reside in or near the assigned province and to travel daily to project sites, including remote rural areas.
  • A valid driving license is required.
  • The Consultant must not hold a government position during the contract period.
  • The Consultant must not have any conflict of interest with contractors engaged under the Project.

GOVERNMENT OF THE REPUBLIC OF MALAWI

 

 

 

Ministry of Health and Sanitation

 

 

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION

 

 

Country                          : Malawi

Name of Project              : Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and

                                            Resilience Program

Project ID No                   : P505187

Assignment Title              Consultancy services to develop a written document for

                                         integration strategies of tier-specific diagnostic testing for

                                         the animal, environment, and human health sector

Reference No.                  : MW-MOH-573848-CS-INDV

Date of Issue                     : 7th October, 2026

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

  1. Background

The Government of Malawi through the Ministry of Health is implementing the Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience project (MHEPRR). The project is financed by the International Development Association (IDA) and Global Financing Facility (GFF). The five-year project seeks to strengthen the capacity and resilience of Malawi’s health system to prevent, prepare for, detect and respond effectively to public health emergencies. It places particular emphasis on strengthening multisectoral coordination, surveillance, laboratory systems and other core capacities required for health emergency preparedness and response.

Laboratories across human, animal and environmental sectors are essential for surveillance, diagnostics, research and response, but often function in silos, leading to fragmented data sharing, inconsistent protocols and inefficient resource utilization. Harmonizing these laboratories strengthens collaboration, improves early detection systems, and supports evidence-based policies at national, regional and global levels.

The MHEPRR Project therefore seeks to engage a consultant to undertake a comprehensive assessment of the existing laboratory landscape and develop a strategic framework for strengthening inter-sectoral laboratory collaboration in Malawi.

  1. Objectives of the consultancy

Main objective: To develop and provide clear, actionable strategies and a framework for strengthening inter-sectoral laboratory collaboration to achieve more effective, efficient, and sustainable health outcomes in Malawi.

Specific objectives:

    • Conduct a comprehensive analysis of the current state of inter-sectoral laboratory collaboration, identifying existing mechanisms, gaps, challenges, and opportunities.
    • Engage with key stakeholders to understand their perspectives, roles, and potential contributions to collaborative One Health initiatives.
    • Develop a strategic framework that outlines different levels of collaboration in areas of communication, partnership, integration, and potential mechanisms like joint committees, policy agreements, and others.
    • Provide concrete, evidence-based recommendations and action plans for implementing a strategic framework that includes specific activities such as

 

achieving SLIPTA 3-star accreditation,               strengthening point             of entry laboratories, establishing national proficiency testing programs, etc.

  1. Scope of work
    • Conducting a situational analysis of existing diagnostic and laboratory services.
    • Identifying opportunities for test integration, economies of scale, and cost savings.
    • Proposing recommendations for policy harmonization and coordination.
    • Providing technical advice and supporting stakeholder interaction.
    • Developing strategies to integrate tier-specific testing for human, animal, and environmental health.

Specifically, the consultant will perform the following tasks:

    • Analyze existing policy documents, reports, and strategic plans related to health and development.
    • Identify and analyze the roles, interests, and potential influence of key

stakeholders from different sectors: human, environment, veterinary, plant and wild-life health.

    • Conduct in-depth interviews with senior officials and experts from relevant sectors.
    • Facilitate participatory workshops with stakeholders to build consensus and gather insights.
    • Develop a detailed report outlining the collaboration framework, strategies, and implementation plan.
    • Present the draft findings and recommendations to stakeholders for feedback and validation.
    • Deliver a final, comprehensive report incorporating all feedback and detailed action plans.
  2. Deliverables

The consultant is expected to produce the following:

    • Inception report: A document detailing the consultant's understanding of the TOR, proposed methodology, work plan, and timeline.
    • Data collection and analysis report: A report summarizing data collection findings and the stakeholder mapping of roles, interests, and influence.
    • Draft collaboration strategy: The main report presenting the harmonized strategic framework, recommendations, and action plans.

 

    • Final collaboration strategy: The final validated report, including all annexes such as interview and workshop summaries.
  2. Deliverables and Timelines

 

Deliverables

Timelines

Acceptance Criteria

Responsible

Inception report

7 days after signing contract

Report demonstrates a clear understanding of the TOR and objectives; includes a sound methodology and analytical framework; identifies key stakeholders across human, animal, environmental, plant and wildlife health sectors; includes appropriate data collection tools; provides a realistic work plan and timeline

PHIM/PIU

Data Collection and Analysis Report

30 days after approved inception report

Report provides a comprehensive assessment of existing diagnostic and laboratory services and inter-sectoral collaboration mechanisms; identifies gaps, challenges, opportunities and duplication; presents stakeholder mapping covering roles, interests and influence; identifies opportunities for test integration, documents consultation findings; and provides evidence to inform development of the collaboration strategy.

PHIM/PIU

Draft Collaboration Strategy

10 days after approved analysis report

Strategy provides a clear and practical framework for collaboration across human, animal, environmental, plant and wildlife health sectors; defines roles and responsibilities; proposes appropriate coordination mechanisms; identifies opportunities for integrated testing and shared services; includes evidence-based recommendations and prioritized action plans; and includes timelines and proposed resource requirements.

PHIM/PIU

Final Validated Collaboration Strategy

10 days after the approved draft collaboration strategy

Final strategy that will incorporate feedback from stakeholders and from the validation process.

 PHIM/PIU

 

 

 

 

  1. Consultant qualifications and experience

The consultant should possess the following:

  • An advanced degree (Master's or higher) in Laboratory Sciences, One Health, Public health, Health System Management or other health related fields.
  • Minimum of 5 years proven experience in health systems strengthening, strategic planning, and fostering multi-sectoral collaboration, preferably in a developing country context.
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting research, stakeholder engagement, and developing actionable strategies.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and report-writing skills.
  • A strong understanding of the dynamics and challenges of inter-sectoral laboratory work.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing national or regional laboratory networks.
  • Proven ability to work with One Health approaches and integrated disease surveillance.
  • Experience in areas like disease outbreak investigation, antimicrobial resistance, or specific diagnostics is highly desirable.

 

  • Excellent technical knowledge in diagnostics, laboratory systems, biosafety and Biosecurity.
  1. Duration of the assignment

The assignment shall be completed within 120 calendar days.

 

  1. Management and supervision

The consultant will be hired under the terms of the MHEPRR Project and will be supervised by the Public Health Institute of Malawi, in collaboration with the Project implementing Unit, solely for the purpose of delivering the agreed outputs. The Ministry, as the client, shall provide the necessary support to the consultant to facilitate the execution of the assignment throughout the consultancy period. This support will include:

  • Access to relevant project documents necessary for the execution of duties under this consultancy.
  • Contact details of relevant stakeholders.

 

Regular progress updates will be required to ensure alignment with the project objectives and timelines.

 

9. SELECTION METHOD

 

The Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section I, paragraphs 1.9 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations” Selection and Employment of Consultant under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants by World Bank Borrowers, July 2016 Revised November 2017 and August 2018 (“Procurement Regulations”- Consultant Guidelines), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

KINGDOM OF CAMBODIA

Ministry of Interior (MOI)

Cambodia Solid Waste and Plastic Management Improvement Project

IDA Grant No. 7292-KH

Request for Expression of Interest

For Individual Consultants

  1. Introduction
  1. The objective of the solid waste and plastic management improvement project (the Project) is to improve solid waste and plastic management in selected areas. The project will be implemented over a period of 6 years (2023-2029), and budget of US$67.3 million will be allocated for the following four components: Component 1 – Institutional Strengthening for Solid Waste and Plastic Management (US$ 4.32 million, implemented by Ministry of Environment), Component 2 – Integrated Solid Waste and Plastic Management, Planning, Monitoring, and Capacity Building for Participating Provinces, Municipalities and Districts (US$8.42 million, implemented by Ministry of Interior). Component 3 – Solid Waste and Plastic Management Infrastructure (US$54.56, implemented by Ministry of Public Works and Transport) and Component 4 –emergency response with zero allocation has been provisioned for the Bank to provide emergency support in the event of a natural disaster, emergency and/or catastrophic event.
  1. The Project Development Objective (PDO) and Key Results Indicators
  1. The PDO is to improve solid waste and plastic management in selected areas, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it. There are three PDO level indicators that will be measured through the following indicators: (i) Proportion of population in selected areas with regular household waste collection, to be measured by the percentage of population that will have regular waste collection; (ii) the landfill disposal capacity operational per defined criteria, to be measured by the amount of landfill disposal capacity that will be realized under the project in Cubic Meter (m3); (iii) plastics policies, guidelines, or standards developed, to be measured by the number of policies, guidelines or standards developed; and (iv) the percentage of municipal solid waste recovered, recycled, composted and/or treated with other techniques.
  1. The Project now invites expressions of interest from qualified and experienced individual consultants to undertake with the assignment listed below:
  1. National Procurement Consultant (Intermittent), Ref. No: MOI-INV-16
  2. Administrative and Contract Management Assistant, Ref. No: MOI-INV-17

  • Have ability to work independently and provide trainings to other staffs when needed;

  1. Administrative and Contract Management Assistant

  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in carrying out administrative services under bilateral/multilateral funded projects/programes including WB, ADB, EU and other development donors;
  • Experience in office management, project operation and procurement will be an advantage;
  • Ability to work independently, provide trainings and work as  a team, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines under pressure;
  • Demonstrated ability to consult and work cooperatively with others as a team; and
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Khmer and good report writing skill.
  1. The consultants will be based at the Project Management Unit.
  1. The selection process will be carried out in accordance with provisions set forth in the Government Procurement Manual for Externally Financed Projects/Programs in Cambodia and Approved Selection Method for Individual Consultants - Section VII. Approved Selection Methods: Consulting Services of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Fourth Edition (November 2020).
