Contract title: Reconstruction of Abbosey Okai Bridge

Country: Ghana

Credit No.: IDA-64100

RFB No: GH-MWH-219663-CW-RFB

Issued on: October 14, 2026

  1. The Government of Ghana has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Reconstruction of Abbosey Okai bridge. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.
  2. The Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources invites sealed bids from eligible contractors for the Reconstruction of the Abbosey Okai Bridge. The project involves the demolition of the existing concrete arch bridge, approximately 47.5m long and 15.0m wide, which currently spans over the Odaw River. The existing structure is in a deteriorated condition, with visible concrete cover detachment, oxidized reinforcing steel bars, and vertical misalignment of the paving surface.

 

The new bridge structure to be constructed consists of a 47.5m single-span deck, made of COR-TEN steel beams and reinforced concrete slabs, supported by reinforced concrete abutments with pile foundations. The bridge will have sixteen HL 1100 M (S460) steel beams, spaced at 0.95m, with a reinforced concrete slab (C40/50) placed on top. The abutments will be 6.50m high, 16.20m long, and 2.20m thick, with 24 reinforced concrete piles (diameter 1.20m, depth 25m) ensuring structural stability.

 

The project also includes the elevation and reinstatement of the approach roads and surrounding areas affected by the bridge replacement. The existing vertical clearance of the bridge will be increased, preventing frequent submergence during floods. The bridge deck width will be maintained at 15m to guarantee continuity with the existing roadway.

 

Additional works involve jet grouting consolidation at the abutments, with 130 jet grouting columns per abutment, extending 15m below the foundation slab, to mitigate soil liquefaction risks. Drainage modifications include DIA150mm pipes discharging rainwater directly into the river and covered side drains connecting to the existing drainage system. Traffic management and road diversions during construction will be a very critical aspect of works, considering the highly congested area where the new bridge has to be located.

The contract shall be executed within 9 months.

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÕES DE INTERESSE

(SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA)

Concurso: SERVIÇO DE CONSULTORIA PARA EXTENSÃO DO SISTEMA DE LICENCIAMENTO NOS POSTOS FRONTEIRIÇOS, INCLUINDO MEIOS TECNOLÓGICO E CAPACITAÇÃO TÉCNICA

REF: 80CS1/MINPLAN/25

 

O Governo de Angola recebeu um financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear o Projecto de Aceleração da Diversificação Económica e Criação de Emprego (Diversifica Mais), e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para contratação dos Serviços de Consultoria para Serviço de Consultoria para Extensão do sistema de licenciamento nos postos fronteiriços, incluindo meios tecnológico e capacitação técnica.

Os serviços de consultoria ("os Serviços") têm como objectivo avaliar o estado de implementação das medidas de simplificação do licenciamento comercial no Corredor do Lobito e prestar assistência técnica à execução de reformas prioritárias que contribuam para a harmonização, racionalização e modernização dos procedimentos de licenciamento a nível provincial e municipal.

Os serviços de consultoria serão executados em duas fases articuladas:

  • Fase 1 — Diagnóstico Situacional e Roteiro de Reformas
  • Fase 2 — Assistência Técnica à Implementação

 

O prazo previsto do contrato de consultoria será de 15 (Quinze) meses.

Os Termos de Referência (TdR) detalhados para a tarefa podem ser obtidos no endereço abaixo.

O Projecto de Aceleração da Diversificação Económica e Criação de Emprego (Diversifica Mais) convida as empresas de consultoria elegíveis (“Consultores”) a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os Serviços. Os Consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e experiência relevante para executar os Serviços. Os critérios de selecção são:

  • Experiência comprovada na concepção, implementação e acompanhamento de reformas de processos administrativos;
  • Experiência relevante em licenciamento, simplificação de procedimentos, modernização administrativa e prestação de serviços públicos;
  • Experiência sólida em mapeamento, padronização, racionalização e harmonização de processos administrativos;
  • Experiência em reformas institucionais e operacionais no sector público, preferencialmente em contextos de desconcentração, descentralização ou coordenação interinstitucional;
  • Experiência de trabalho com entidades nacionais, provinciais e municipais;
  • Capacidade comprovada de facilitar processos de mudança organizacional e reforço de capacidades;
  • Experiência em transformação digital, governação electrónica, informatização de processos e interoperabilidade de sistemas;
  • Experiência prévia de trabalho em pelo menos um país de língua oficial portuguesa, com elaboração de relatórios e documentos técnicos em língua portuguesa; e
  • Conhecimento do enquadramento legal, institucional e operacional de Angola, incluindo as práticas de licenciamento comercial e o funcionamento da Administração Pública (constitui vantagem).

Os especialistas chaves não serão avaliados nesta fase de selecção.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de IPF” do Banco Mundial, revisado em Setembro de 2025 (“Regulamentos de Aquisições”), estabelecendo a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

Os consultores podem associar-se a outras empresas para melhorar as suas qualificações, mas devem indicar claramente se a associação assume a forma de uma joint venture e/ou de uma subconsultoria. No caso de uma joint venture, todos os parceiros da joint venture serão solidariamente responsáveis pela totalidade do contrato, se selecionados.

Um Consultor será selecionado de acordo com o método de Selecção Baseada nas Qualificações do Consultor (CQS) estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

Maiores informações poderão ser obtidas no endereço abaixo, no horário comercial das 08h00 às 16h00.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: KENYA

Name of Project: NATIONAL YOUTH OPPORTUNITIES TOWARDS ADVANCEMENT (NYOTA)

Credit No. IDA-7355-KE/ Grant No: E210-KE

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Provision of Monitoring and Verification Firm for NYOTA Project

 

The Government of Kenya, with financing from the World Bank, invites eligible consulting firms to submit Expressions of Interest (EOI) for the assignment indicated above under the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) Project.

The NYOTA Project aims to increase employment and earnings and promote savings for targeted youth at national scale. The Project is expected to reach 820,000 vulnerable youth across all 47 counties of Kenya, including refugees in Garissa and Turkana counties. The Project beneficiaries are youth aged 18-29 years, and up to 35 years for persons with disabilities, with little or no education, who are unemployed or in vulnerable employment.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include independent monitoring and verification of results reported by Employer Organizations and other Service Providers under the NYOTA On-the-Job Experience (OJE) results-based financing arrangement. The assignment will cover verification of placement into apprenticeship, retention during apprenticeship, and retention in paid employment after apprenticeship, including review of Project system records, administrative data, remote verification, field verification, spot checks, evidence logs, and payment eligibility summaries. For clarity, the results-based financing milestones to be verified are: Milestone 1: placement into apprenticeship; Milestone 2: retention in apprenticeship for five months; and Milestone 3: retention in paid employment for six months after apprenticeship. These are referred to in the TOR as M1, M2 and M3 verification cycles, respectively. The estimated beneficiary population from which verification claims may arise is 90,000, with geographic coverage across the 47 counties.

The initial contract period shall be twelve (12) months. The contract may be renewed in twelve-month periods, subject to satisfactory performance against agreed deliverables, continued need for the services, availability of funds, and compliance with quality and timeliness requirements. The contract shall not extend beyond the Project closing date of 31st December 2028, unless that date is formally extended and the Contract is amended in accordance with the applicable procurement and contract provisions.

Interested firms should provide information and proof demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

a) Demonstrated seven (7) years' experience in independent verification, results-based financing, performance audit, monitoring and evaluation, social protection, labour market, skills development, youth employment, or other large-scale beneficiary programmes, preferably including experience in sub-Saharan Africa;

b) Proven track record of having undertaken at least two (2) assignments of a similar nature and complexity in the last five (5) years, including verification of results, payment-linked outputs, or large beneficiary datasets;

c) A consultancy profile that includes the organizational structure, clearly stating the duties assigned to each of the personnel identified to support the delivery of verification, measurement and reporting;

d) Demonstrated technical and managerial capability to deliver the assignment.

Note: Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated July 2016 and revised in September 2025 (6th Edition) ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. In addition, consulting firms shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower.

Consultants may submit their REOI as an individual firm or in association in the form of a joint venture or sub-consultancy. All the members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment. However, the experience of sub-consultant will not be considered while short-listing.

A Consultant/firm will be selected in accordance with Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Regulations.

Interested firms may obtain further information from the Project Supply Chain Management Office at NYOTA offices, Bruce House, Standard Street, 3rd Floor Northern Wing Room No. 321 during official working hours (8.00 a.m-5.00 p.m.) and days. Complete REOI document (paginated and stamped/signed on each page) and enclosed in plain sealed envelope marked with the tender reference number and addressed to the Principal Secretary, State Department of Youth Affairs and Creative Economy, P. O. Box 34303 –00100, Nairobi, Kenya and should be deposited in the Tender Box at Bruce House 3rd Floor to be received on or before 29th October, 2026, at 10.00 hours

The REOIs will be closed/opened immediately thereafter at the NYOTA Boardroom, Bruce House, 3rd Floor Standard Street Nairobi.

The Consultant’s primary responsibility is to be the focal point for communications and outreach work across Rogun PMG, JSC Rogun HPP, DFZ and other key stakeholders involved in Rogun HPP Project to support communications for effective reflection of Project activities.

The Terms of Reference for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/160SSXMvyZISsZWQgzSIXlHI7ovnoQ0JP/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106350143139932323844&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Consultant should have the following qualifications:

  • University degree (bachelor’s or a master’s degree) in Communications, Political Science, International Relations, Journalism, Public Affairs;
  • Five (5) or more years’ experience working with International Organizations, Donors’ funded projects, communications, international relations, public affairs, political science, or other related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. In addition, working experience in Investment Operations will be valued;
  • State-of-the art knowledge in the field of strategic communications, and ability to address a range of issues related to a business group, including taking the lead on highly visible and sensitive assignments;
  • Highly developed verbal and written communications skills in English, Tajik and Russian languages, ability to convey complex messages succinctly and diplomatically;
  • Demonstrates an in-depth understanding of target audiences, highly effective writing style, and expertise in high-impact messaging to global audiences;
  • Has excellent working knowledge of digital and social media, including Facebook and Twitter, with experience in creating and sharing digital content;
  • Shows sensitivity when delivering politically sensitive communication to large group/public forums and/or strategic parties;
  • Effectively counsels /coaches team members, senior management in their delivery of messages to a variety of constituents, even on challenging topics;
  • Anticipates problems and opportunities; with potential problems, surfaces contributing factors and resolves them before there is negative impact;
  • Coaches others in selecting and using appropriate problem-solving methods;
  • Experience in working closely with senior leaders on communications and in dealing with media;
  • Proven ability to operate effectively in a multicultural environment;
  • Understanding of multilateral development banks, including the WB/AIIB, its policies and operations a plus.

An individual Consultant shall be selected following Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants in accordance with Section VI, paragraphs, 7.36 and 7.37 of “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

  1.   1. Les services sollicités consistent à appuyer le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo et la Banque Centrale du Congo dans la finalisation du mécanisme de Ligne de Crédit en préparation et dans l’évaluation du cadre institutionnel, fiduciaire et opérationnel applicable aux mécanismes d’intermédiation financière financés par les partenaires techniques et financiers.

 

  1. L’UCP-TRANSFORME invite les Candidats (Consultants Individuels) admissibles à manifester leurs intérêts pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants (Individuels) intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.  

 

  1. Le Consultant devra disposer du profil minimum suivant :

 

  • Être titulaire au minimum d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau Master en finance, banque, économie, administration publique ou domaine équivalent ;
  • Justifier d’au moins quinze (15) années d’expérience professionnelle dans les domaines du développement financier et intermédiation financière, inclus des lignes de crédit, des fonds de garantie et des institutions financières de développement ;
  • Démontrer une expérience significative dans la réalisation d’évaluations OP10/FIF ou d’autres évaluations similaires pour des institutions financières intermédiaires ;
  • Posséder une expérience avérée dans la conception, la restructuration ou l’évaluation de mécanismes de lignes de crédit financés par des bailleurs de fonds ;
  • Avoir travaillé avec des institutions telles que la Banque mondiale, l’IFC, la Banque Africaine de Développement, la Banque Européenne d’Investissement, la Banque Asiatique de Développement ou des institutions financières et développements similaires (régionaux ou bilatéraux) ;
  • Disposer d’une solide expertise en gouvernance financière, gestion des risques, supervision des intermédiaires financiers et institutions Apex ;
  • Posséder une excellente capacité de rédaction et d’analyse ;
  • Maîtriser parfaitement le français écrit et oral.

 

 

  1. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 7.34, 7.36 et 7.37 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) », édition de septembre 2025 ci-après désigné « Règlement de Passation des Marchés », qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts.

 

  1. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels, telle que décrite dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », édition de septembre 2025 en vertu du Nouveau Cadre de Passation des Marchés Publics (NCPM), et des « Lignes Directrices »  de la Banque mondiale sur la Prévention et la Lutte contre la Fraude et la Corruption dans les projets financés sur les Prêts de la BIRD, et les crédits et les subventions de l’IDA (datant du 1er juillet 2016), ainsi que les dispositions stipulées dans l’Accord de financement applicables au projet.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Consultancy Services for the Feasibility Study and Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for the Proposed Underwater Museum

Reference No.: SVGUBEC-C-QCBS-13

Date of Issue: 7 October 2026

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise the preparation of a Feasibility Study and an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for the proposed Underwater Museum, together with an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), a site-specific Stakeholder Consultation Plan and the related consultations, subproject grievance mechanism arrangements, and the associated environmental and social management instruments. The Services will determine whether the Client’s 2025 preliminary concept, “The Submerged Museum: A Museum of Slavery & Resistance”, including its proposed repurposed-vessel configuration, is technically, environmentally, socially, economically, financially, legally and institutionally feasible, and will compare it with lower-impact or non-vessel alternatives.

The assignment is expected to be completed within approximately twenty-six (26) weeks from contract signing. The expected start date is February 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment may be downloaded at the following website: https://procurement.gov.vc/eprocure/index.php/current-bids.

The Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation and Sustainable Development, through the UBEC Project Implementation Unit, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services

The shortlisting criteria are:

1. At least ten (10) years of corporate experience in feasibility studies and/or environmental and social impact assessments for marine, coastal, tourism, blue economy or biodiversity-sensitive projects.

2. Completion, within the last ten (10) years, of at least three (3) comparable assignments involving coastal or marine infrastructure, marine tourism, underwater attractions, artificial reefs or vessel-related marine installations, or biodiversity-sensitive coastal and marine sites, of which at least one (1) shall have been an ESIA (or equivalent environmental and social assessment) for a marine or coastal investment.

3. Demonstrated experience in coastal and marine assignments in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or comparable developing coastal nations; experience in the Caribbean will be an advantage.

4. Demonstrated experience in applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (in particular ESS1, ESS6, ESS8 and ESS10), or comparable environmental and social requirements of another multilateral development bank, including marine habitat assessment and stakeholder engagement with coastal communities, fisherfolk and marine users.

5. Technical and managerial capability of the firm to deliver an integrated multidisciplinary assignment, covering marine ecology and biodiversity, coastal engineering and vessel suitability, tourism and financial analysis, social development and livelihoods, cultural heritage, occupational health and diving safety, and GIS/mapping, including capacity to plan and supervise marine field surveys and to apply quality control across deliverables.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

To facilitate the assessment, Expressions of Interest should include, at a minimum:

(a) a covering letter signed by an authorized representative of the firm;

(b) evidence of the firm’s legal registration or incorporation;

(c) a firm profile describing its core business, years in business, organization and permanent technical staff;

(d) a list of comparable assignments, indicating for each the client and contact details, country and location, contract value, start and completion dates, the firm’s role (lead firm, joint venture partner or sub-consultant) and a brief description of the services provided; and

(e) where applicable, details of any proposed association, identifying the lead firm and the role of each member, and stating whether the association is a joint venture or a sub-consultancy.

Consultants should submit their Expressions of Interest in English and are requested to limit their submission to a maximum of twenty-five (25) pages excluding covering letter and certificates. Submissions will be assessed only against the criteria listed above; additional material will not be evaluated.

 Shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit technical and financial proposals.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 [revised November 2017, August 2018 and November 2020, September 2023, February 2025] (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Given that the Feasibility Study and ESIA must provide impartial advice on site selection and on the vessel-based concept, Consultants should disclose in their Expression of Interest any prior or current involvement in the preparation of the Underwater Museum concept, and any commercial interest in dive, tourism, salvage or marine operations at or near the candidate sites, so that any potential conflict of interest can be assessed.

Firms or individuals that have been declared ineligible or sanctioned by the World Bank Group in accordance with its Anti-Corruption Guidelines and Sanctions Framework are not eligible to participate. The Bank’s Anti-Corruption Guidelines, including its right to sanction and its inspection and audit rights, apply to this selection and to the resulting contract.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. For the purposes of shortlisting, the experience and qualifications of the lead firm and of the joint venture partners will be considered; the experience of sub-consultants will not be taken into account.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations, using the World Bank’s Standard Procurement Document, Request for Proposals: Selection of Consultants.

Further information may be obtained at the address below during office hours, 09:00 to 16:00 hours (local time).

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, by mail, or by e-mail) no later than 16;00 hours (local time) on Monday, 23 October 2026. E-mail submissions should be sent as a single PDF file with the subject line “EOI – SVGUBEC-C-QCBS-13 – Feasibility Study and ESIA for the Proposed Underwater Museum”. Submissions received after this time will not be considered. Only shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit proposals.

  • Expérience professionnelle générale d’au moins cinq (5) ans dans le secteur du numérique, des télécommunications, des systèmes d’information ou de la transformation digitale, acquise notamment au sein d’administrations publiques, entreprises du secteur numérique ou des télécommunications, cabinets de conseil, institutions internationales, projets de développement ou organisations comparables ;
  • Expérience spécifique d’au moins trois (3) ans dans la conduite de projets de transformation digitale, de gouvernance numérique ou de services publics digitaux ;
  • Bonne compréhension des principes et enjeux liés à l’identité numérique, à l’interopérabilité, à la gouvernance des données, à la cybersécurité et à la protection des données personnelles ;
  • Maîtrise de la chaîne de valeur des projets de transformation digitale, de la conception des solutions au contrôle qualité des applications, plateformes et infrastructures ;
  • Connaissance avérée du contexte et des enjeux du secteur du développement numérique et/ou de l’énergie à Madagascar ;
  • Expérience dans au moins un projet financé par la Banque mondiale ou par un autre partenaire technique et financier ;
  • Connaissance des processus de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Solides capacités de rédaction de documents techniques et de rapports, avec une aptitude à analyser et à synthétiser des informations complexes ;
  • Excellente maîtrise du français à l’écrit et à l’oral ; bonne maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais permettant notamment de comprendre, analyser et produire des documents techniques ;
  • Disponibilité et aptitude à effectuer de fréquents déplacements.

Atouts

  • Certification reconnue en gestion de projet (PRINCE2, PMP) ou en méthodes agiles ;
  • Bonne connaissance du contexte institutionnel de l’administration malgache ;
  • Expérience dans la mise en place de services publics digitaux ou dans l’élaboration de documents-cadres relatifs à la gouvernance numérique ;
  • Expérience dans un projet combinant à la fois le secteur numérique et celui de l’énergie en zones rurales

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, édition septembre 2023, qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts liés à cette mission. SUE Directorate of Flooding Zone of Rogun HPP(DFZ)

Project Background

The Government of the Republic of Tajikistan has received financing from the World Bank in the amount of US$15,000,000 toward the cost of the Technical Assistance (TA) for Financing Framework for the Rogun Hydropower Project This project is jointly financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) (US$ 5.0 million).

The TA Project will help to: (a) strengthen technical, environmental, and social aspects of the Rogun hydropower plant construction project (Rogun HPP Project); (b) develop the commercial framework of the Rogun HPP Project; and (c) strengthen the institutional capacity of the Project Management Group for Energy Facilities Construction under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan Rogun (Rogun PMG), which is the implementing entity for Rogun HPP Project.

Main objectives of the assignment

The Consultant will be responsible for the following tasks: together with other E&S staff, they will prepare Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) for all selected resettlement sites and DFZ’s infrastructure facilities (construction and/or renovation works). The ESMP will be prepared in Tajik and Russian and will be translated into English to ensure full understanding by stakeholders.

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1u6E7HJw65P7Pm_KFLbyjGoDeigdp0F0z/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106350143139932323844&rtpof=true&sd=true

  • At least three (3) years of proven experience in monitoring social development, including gender issues in development projects;
  • Understanding of the World Bank’s environmental and social standards and social development approaches, knowledge of the relevant rules and procedures of the Republic of Tajikistan;
  • Experience of interaction with social institutions in Tajikistan and awareness of their activities, especially in the areas of stakeholder/citizen engagement, social protection, social inclusion and gender issues, as well as their role in governance issues at the central, regional, district and local levels;

  • Expérience d'au moins un (01) an dans un projet financé par un bailleur de fonds dans les cinq (05) dernières années ;
  • Expertise en matière de règlementation des contrats ;
  • Ayant suivi une formation en passation des marchés ;
  • Connaissances pratiques des règles de passation de marchés des bailleurs ;
  • Maîtrise de l’outil informatique comme Word, Excel, PowerPoint,
  • Maîtrise le Français à l’écrit et à l’oral, avec capacité de rédaction
  • Être méthodique et organisé(e), rigoureux(se), et intègre ;
  • Avoir une excellente capacité d’analyse, de synthèse, de communication et de rédaction ;
  • Apte à effectuer des déplacements dans des localités éloignées et dans des conditions difficiles.

Atouts :

  • Connaissance du System Tracking Exchange Procurement (STEP) de la Banque Mondiale
  • Formation en Passation de marchés

REPÚBLICA DA GUINÉ-BISSAU

                                                                                   Ministério do Ambiente, Biodiversidade e Ação Climática

                                                              Instituto da Biodiversidade e das Áreas Protegidas - Dr. Alfredo Simão da Silva (IBAP)

                                                        Projeto de Investimento na Resiliência das Zonas Costeiras da África Ocidental (WACA - ResIP 2 GB)

                                                        ANÚNCIO DE CONCURSO – Refª AN/004/outubro/WACA-ResIP 2 GB/CI/2026

 

     RECRUTAMENTO DE UM(A) CONSULTOR(a) PARA REALIZAR O Inquérito de Satisfação de Beneficiários do WACA ResIP 2 Guiné-Bissau.

  I. CONTEXTO

Tal como noutros países da África Ocidental, na Guiné-Bissau a degradação dos recursos e ecossistemas costeiros está a acelerar devido à crescente pressão demográfica na costa e às alterações climáticas. A deterioração costeira está a conduzir a uma perda significativa e potencialmente irreversível de ecossistemas críticos, tais como praias, sistemas de dunas e mangais, que fornecem importantes serviços ambientais, sociais e de proteção costeira (meios de subsistência e recursos naturais, alimentos, proteção contra a erosão e inundações). Por conseguinte, o Governo da Guiné-Bissau solicitou e obteve apoio técnico e financeiro do Banco Mundial para implementar o Projeto de Investimento para a Resiliência Costeira da África Ocidental - Guiné-Bissau (WACA ResIP 2 GB). Ver mais detalhes nos termos de referência.

  II. OBJECTIVO

O objetivo deste anúncio é o recrutamento de um(a) consultor(a) para realizar um Inquérito de Satisfação de Beneficiários do WACA ResIP 2 Guiné-Bissau.

  III. CONVITE

A Unidade de Gestão do ResIP 2 GB da WACA (UGP do ResIP 2 GB da WACA) convida os consultores individuais elegíveis a manifestar interesse em prestar os serviços acima descritos. Os consultores interessados devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e experiência relevante. 

É levado ao conhecimento dos consultores o facto de serem aplicáveis as disposições relativas às regras do Banco Mundial em matéria de conflito de interesses, tal como descritas nos parágrafos 3.14 e seguintes dos “Regulamentos de aquisição para mutuários que procuram financiamento de projetos de investimento (FPI)”, datados de fevereiro de 2025 e revistos em setembro de 2025. 

  IV. PERFIL DO(A) CONSULTOR(A)

Os candidatos interessados devem possuir as seguintes qualificações:

  • Pelo menos um mestrado em ciências sociais, economia, estatística, gestão ambiental ou áreas relacionadas;
  • Pelo menos sete (7) anos de experiência demonstrada no desenho e implementação de inquéritos de perceção de beneficiários, inquéritos socioeconómicos, trabalhos de monitorização e avaliação, ou avaliações de projetos;
  • Experiência demonstrada no desenho e implementação de inquéritos quantitativos e qualitativos, incluindo metodologias de amostragem, desenho de questionários, garantia de qualidade dos dados e análise estatística;
  • Experiência comprovada no desenho de quadros de monitorização e avaliação e na medição de indicadores de resultados de projetos, preferencialmente para projetos de desenvolvimento financiados internacionalmente;
  • Forte capacidade em análise estatística quantitativa e análise qualitativa de dados utilizando pacotes de software adequados;
  • Experiência comprovada em trabalho de campo e consultas participativas com comunidades locais, incluindo grupos vulneráveis e mulheres;
  • A experiência prévia em projetos financiados pelo Banco Mundial ou outros parceiros internacionais, incluindo familiaridade com quadros de resultados e inquéritos de satisfação dos beneficiários, será considerada uma grande vantagem;
  • A experiência prévia de trabalho na Guiné-Bissau ou em contextos costeiros semelhantes na África Ocidental é altamente desejável;
  • É obrigatório português escrito e falado. O conhecimento das línguas locais ou os arranjos para recolha de dados em línguas locais é altamente desejável. Ver mais detalhes nos termos de referência.

   V. MÉTODO DE SELEÇÃO

O/A consultor(a) será selecionado(a) utilizando o método de Seleção de Consultores Individuais (CI) de acordo com os procedimentos estabelecidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários que procuram Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (FPI) para Fornecimentos, Obras, Serviços e outros que Serviços de Consultoria, e Serviços de Consultoria de fevereiro de 2025, revisto em setembro de 2025.

O dossiê de manifestação de interesse deve incluir e não só os documentos a seguir:

  1. Carta de manifestação de interesse
  2. Um curriculum vitae atualizado incluindo as missões similares realizadas
  3. cópia(s) autenticada(s) dos diplomas e certificados obtidos.
  4. Indicação do mínimo do nome e dos contatos (número de telemóvel e email) de duas pessoas de referência.

O projeto reservase o direito de solicitar aos consultores que justifiquem as suas experiências similares através de atestados de boa execução.

VI. APRESENTAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÕES DE INTERESSE

Os candidatos interessados devem entregar ou enviar as suas candidaturas à Unidade de Coordenação do WACA ResIP 2 GB, Avenida Dom Settimio Arturo Ferrazzetta, Caixa Postal Nº 70, Guiné-Bissau, Bissau, à atenção do seu Coordenador Nacional, Sr. Leonildo Alves Cardoso ou por correio eletrónico: samuelfernandesspmwaca@gmail.com  com cópia para: leonildocardoso@hotmail.com  até o dia 22 de outubro  de 2026 às 16 horas em ponto, hora de Bissau.

VII.       INFORMAÇÕES COMPLEMENTARES

Os candidatos interessados podem obter mais informações sobre os documentos de referência no endereço abaixo: samuelfernandesspmwaca@gmail.com  ou visitando o departamento administrativo do projeto WACA ResIP 2 GB na sua sede, localizada na Avenida Dom Settimio Arturo Ferrazzetta, Caixa Postal Nº 70, Guiné-Bissau, Bissau, entre as 10 horas em ponto e as 15 horas em ponto de segunda a sexta-feira.

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IDA Credit No. 77910 (IDA Credit) 

Assignment Title: Procurement of consulting services for end-to-end business development services (BDS) Providers to Support Youth Employment under the Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP)

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SZ-EWADE-549413-CS-QCBS 

1. The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini, has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the implementation of the Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project is a five-year, national, multi-sectoral initiative that seeks to expand income-earning opportunities for Eswatini youth by strengthening employability, promoting entrepreneurship and supporting inclusive, resilient livelihoods. The Project delivers an economic inclusion package comprising market-relevant skills training, business development support, access to finance and integration into value chains, and is implemented through three components, including Component 1: Youth Income-Earning Opportunities, under which Sub-component 1.1 (Income-Earning Opportunities for Youth in Agriculture), led by the Eswatini Water and Agricultural Development Enterprise (EWADE), targets 20,000 youth (at least 50% female, 5% disabled) in agriculture and related value chains.

The consulting services comprise of the provision of end-to-end Business Development Service Providers to support youth participation in priority agricultural and agribusiness value chains under Sub-component 1.1 (Youth Income-Earning Opportunities) of EYEOP. The Services will support eligible youth through an integrated pathway covering value chain intelligence and market analysis; beneficiary profiling and pathway allocation; socio-emotional, entrepreneurship, technical and business skills development; business planning and enterprise establishment; finance readiness and access productive finance; market linkages and value chain facilitation; mentorship, coaching and aftercare support; and monitoring, quality assurance and performance monitoring.

The services will focus on prioritized value chain including selected commodities across vegetables, field crops, small ruminants, poultry and aquaculture sub-sectors.

The assignment is expected to commence upon contract signature and will be implemented throughout the EYEOP implementation period, in accordance with approved Annual Work Plan and Budgets (AWPB). The engagement will initially be for one (1) year, with the possibility of annual renewal, subject to satisfactory performance, achievement of agreed deliverables and performance targets, availability of funding and continue need for the services.

2. The Terms of Reference for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest in Annex 1.

3. The Eswatini Water and agricultural development Enterprise invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core business and institutional experience: Demonstrated core business in business development services, enterprise development, business advisory services, entrepreneurship development, skills development, training, mentorship, market linkage facilitation or related areas relevant to the assignment.
  • Relevant assignment experience: Successful completion of at least one (1) assignment of similar nature, scope and complexity within the last five (5) years, demonstrating experience in the delivery of BDS, enterprise development, youth entrepreneurship, business advisory services, training, mentorship, market linkages or related services.
  • Experience in youth and enterprise development: Demonstrated experience in implementing youth entrepreneurship, employment, skills development or economic inclusion programmes, including support to emerging and/or existing enterprises.
  • Agriculture, agribusiness and value-chain experience: Demonstrated experience in agriculture, agribusiness or related value-chain development, including facilitating linkages between smallholder farmers or enterprises and buyers, aggregators, processors, financial institutions, input suppliers or other private-sector actors.
  • Financial and business development experience: Demonstrated institutional experience in financial literacy, finance readiness, business planning, enterprise financing and/or agriculture and value-chain financing.
  • Geographic and contextual experience: Demonstrated experience working in Eswatini and/or Southern Africa, with an understanding of the regional agricultural, youth employment, entrepreneurship and enterprise-development context.
  • Technical and operational capacity: Demonstrated institutional capacity, systems and operational reach to deliver integrated BDS at the scale envisaged under EYEOP, including the ability to mobilize and manage appropriate technical resources, delivery personnel, logistics, data-management systems and quality-assurance arrangements.
  • Experience in inclusive and sustainable development approaches: Demonstrated experience integrating gender, youth inclusion, disability inclusion, climate resilience, climate-smart agriculture, environmental sustainability or related cross-cutting considerations into programme delivery.
  • Development programme experience: Experience implementing donor-funded, government-funded or multi-stakeholder development programmes will be considered an advantage.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Their qualifications and experience will be assessed at the Request for Proposals (RfP) stage in accordance with the applicable evaluation criteria.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

 

Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower. Without limitation on the generality of the foregoing, Consultants shall not be hired under the circumstances set forth below:

a) a firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Goods, Works, or Non-Consulting Services for a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that firm), shall be disqualified from providing Consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to, those Goods, Works, or Non-Consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

b) a firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Consulting Services for the preparation or implementation of a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consulting firm), shall be disqualified from subsequently providing Goods, Works, or Non-Consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to those Consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

c) neither a Consultant (including personnel and sub-consultants), nor an affiliate (that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consultant), shall be hired for any assignment that, by its nature, creates a conflict of interest with another assignment of the Consultant;

d) Consultants (including their experts and other personnel, and sub-consultants), that have a close business or family relationship with a professional staff of the Borrower, or of the project implementing agency, or of a recipient of a part of the Bank’s financing, or any other party representing or acting on behalf of the Borrower, that is directly or indirectly involved in any part of:

i. the preparation of the ToR for the assignment;

ii. the selection process for the contract; or

iii. the supervision of the contract;

may not be awarded a contract, unless the conflict stemming from this relationship has been resolved in a manner acceptable to the Bank throughout the selection process and the execution of the contract.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Provision of End-to-End Business Development Services

(Business Development Management Support TA)

Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP)

1. Background

The Kingdom of Eswatini faces persistent challenges of high youth unemployment, limited formal-sector job creation and widespread poverty, particularly in rural areas. Women, youth with disabilities, youth who are not in education, employment or training, and youth engaged in low-productivity activities face additional barriers to productive opportunities.

The Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP) is a five-year national, multisectoral initiative supported by the World Bank to expand income-earning opportunities for youth. The Project combines market-relevant skills, entrepreneurship and business development support, productive start-up support, access to finance, mentorship, and integration into agricultural and related value chains.

Under Subcomponent 1.1, EWADE will support 20,000 youth in agriculture and related value chains, with at least 50 percent women. The beneficiary pathway covers socio-emotional and mindset-change support, technical and business skills, business planning, productive grants where applicable, enterprise development, market or employment linkages, mentorship and post-support monitoring.

The assignment will focus on Government-prioritized value chains: vegetables (onions, potatoes, tomatoes and baby vegetables), dry beans, small ruminants, poultry and aquaculture. Youth opportunities may cover on-farm production and off-farm activities such as input supply, nurseries and hatcheries, aggregation, logistics, processing, mechanization, e-extension, e-commerce and related business services.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective is to engage a qualified BDS Provider to deliver a comprehensive, demand-driven and results-oriented package that enables eligible youth to establish, improve, sustain and grow viable enterprises or access wage-employment opportunities, while contributing to measurable improvements in employment, income, productivity, market participation and resilience.

The specific objectives are to:

  • Profile beneficiaries and allocate them to suitable employment, enterprise, on-farm or off-farm pathways.
  • Strengthen technical, socio-emotional, entrepreneurship, business-management, financial and digital capabilities.
  • Support viable business planning, enterprise establishment, operational improvement and growth.
  • Improve finance readiness and facilitate appropriate access to productive grants or other finance.
  • Facilitate sustainable market, value-chain and employment linkages.
  • Provide structured mentorship and generate reliable beneficiary-level performance evidence.

3. Scope of Services

Under Subcomponent 1.1, the BDS Provider shall provide training, capacity building and mentoring services to support EWADE in the design and implementation of economic inclusion interventions. The Consulting Firm shall undertake the following major tasks:

3.1 BDS Package Design, Curriculum Review and Pilot Testing

The Provider shall establish an EYEOP-approved BDS package that is practical, interactive, youth-centred and tailored to beneficiary needs and priority value chains. Existing local and international good-practice content shall be used as the starting point for customization rather than developing all content from first principles.

  • Review existing BDS, entrepreneurship, business-management, socio-emotional, financial-literacy, digital-skills, technical-training and mentorship materials.
  • Assess suitability for NEET youth, vulnerable informal workers, women and youth with disabilities, and identify gaps requiring adaptation or additional modules.
  • Customize content to EYEOP pathways, priority value chains, the Eswatini market context, beneficiary literacy levels and language needs.
  • Develop clear learning objectives, session plans, practical exercises, participant outputs, assessment methods, facilitator manuals, participant materials and a structured mentorship guide.
  • Pilot the package with an agreed beneficiary group; assess content, language, timing, accessibility and practicality; document findings and revise the package before EWADE approval.

3.2 Youth Mobilization, Communication, Profiling and Pathway Allocation

  • Support awareness, beneficiary communication, registration and screening in accordance with Project eligibility and targeting requirements.
  • Assess skills, interests, aspirations, productive assets, constraints, readiness, entrepreneurial potential and relevant labour-market or value-chain characteristics.
  • Match beneficiaries to wage-employment, self-employment, on-farm or off-farm pathways and identify required technical training, enterprise support and reasonable accommodations.
  • Communicate schedules, participation requirements and logistics through appropriate approved channels.
  • Maintain accurate profiles, selection records and pathway-allocation data in formats compatible with the EYEOP MIS.

3.3 Socio-Emotional, Mindset, Life and Business Skills Training

  • Deliver practical training in initiative, confidence, resilience, goal-setting, problem-solving, communication, adaptability and decision-making.
  • Address gender-related, household, cultural, disability-related or other barriers affecting participation and enterprise performance.
  • Deliver business-model development, customer identification, marketing, costing, pricing, record keeping, cash-flow management and financial literacy.
  • Use experiential methods, including demonstrations, case studies, role play, group work and application to a beneficiary’s own business or employment pathway.
  • Ensure training is accessible and adapted to education, literacy, language and disability needs.

3.4 Technical and Competency-Based Training

  • Deliver technical training relevant to the selected priority value chain and pathway, aligned with applicable DIVT or other competent standards.
  • Provide practical and experiential learning suited to the selected commodity, occupation or business opportunity.
  • Integrate climate-smart agriculture, green business practices, food safety, quality standards and appropriate digital agriculture solutions.
  • Support competency assessment and certification in coordination with relevant institutions.
  • Align delivery with production calendars, market cycles and employment demand where applicable.

3.5 Enterprise Development and Business Start-Up Support

  • Validate enterprise opportunities against market demand, competition, costs, risks and beneficiary capabilities.
  • Support business models, enterprise profiles, business plans, production and marketing plans, budgets, cash-flow forecasts and growth plans.
  • Provide incubation, business advisory, coaching and technical support during establishment and early operations.
  • Support formalization, governance, compliance, record keeping, productivity, innovation, digital adoption and climate resilience where relevant.
  • Assess enterprise-specific technical, operational, financial and market constraints and coordinate referrals to suitable specialist services.
  • Support enterprises to improve operational continuity, sales, customer retention, market access, income and employment creation.

3.6 Finance Readiness and Productive Resource Management

  • Conduct finance-readiness assessments and support grant applications, budgets, cash-flow projections, investment cases and financing plans.
  • Explain eligibility and application requirements for Project grants and other relevant financing.
  • Facilitate linkages with financial institutions, investors and financing providers without influencing third-party decisions or representing finance as guaranteed.
  • Strengthen responsible use of grants and other finance through budgeting, basic financial management and record keeping.
  • Track referrals, applications, approvals, financing accessed, reasons for rejection and use of finance where required.

3.7 Market, Value-Chain and Employment Linkages

  • Identify viable commercial and employment opportunities based on market demand, value-chain requirements and beneficiary capabilities.
  • Maintain an engagement pipeline of buyers, employers, processors, aggregators, exporters, retailers, lead firms and other relevant market actors.
  • Facilitate supplier relationships, off-take arrangements, aggregation, contract farming, buyer-seller engagement, trade events and employment placement.
  • Support beneficiaries to meet quality, volume, reliability, packaging, certification, pricing and delivery requirements.
  • Facilitate access to inputs, equipment, logistics, extension, mechanization, digital market access and other services needed for sustainable participation.

3.8 Mentorship, Coaching and Post-Support Follow-Up

  • Establish a structured mentorship and coaching system appropriate to beneficiary pathways and enterprise stages.
  • Recruit, assess and train mentors under EWADE-approved requirements and maintain a qualified mentor roster.
  • Match beneficiaries with suitable entrepreneurs, business owners, technical specialists, extension officers, employers or private-sector mentors.
  • Provide individual and group coaching during critical production, operational, marketing and business-growth stages.
  • Use a structured guide, session plans, action plans, attendance records and follow-up logs; monitor mentor performance and replace underperforming personnel.
  • Conduct agreed tracer and follow-up activities to assess enterprise operation, employment, income, sales, productivity and sustainability.

3.9 Monitoring, Quality Assurance, Learning and Adaptive Management

  • Maintain complete beneficiary and service-delivery records interoperable with the EYEOP MIS and submit data in prescribed formats and frequencies.
  • Track agreed output and outcome indicators, including completion, enterprise establishment and survival, market participation, finance, employment, income, sales, productivity and jobs.
  • Undertake quality assurance of curricula, trainers, mentors, venues, materials, attendance, accessibility and beneficiary experience.
  • Collect beneficiary feedback and satisfaction data; maintain supporting evidence; perform data-quality checks; and implement corrective actions.
  • Document implementation lessons, innovations, constraints and emerging risks for each cohort or service cycle and submit evidence-based recommendations.
  • Record and refer complaints through the Project grievance mechanism and comply with environmental and social, safeguarding, anticorruption, confidentiality and data-protection requirements.

4. Methodology & Workplan

The TOR defines the mandatory service requirements, minimum standards, outputs and intended results. The Provider shall propose the detailed methodology, staffing deployment, sequencing, tools, logistics and quality-assurance arrangements in its technical proposal. The approach shall demonstrate how all service areas will be integrated into a coherent beneficiary journey rather than delivered as disconnected activities.

Delivery shall be organized around defined beneficiary cohorts or service cycles. The contract will specify the number and profile of beneficiaries, geographic coverage, value chains, pathway mix, delivery period, required modules, mentorship frequency, service standards, deliverables, indicators and verification requirements. Training, enterprise support and mentoring shall be aligned with agricultural production calendars, market cycles and relevant employment demand.

The detailed methodology shall be finalized during inception with EWADE. Adjustments may be proposed during implementation in response to beneficiary needs and evidence, but shall require written approval and shall not reduce agreed coverage, service quality, outputs, results, safeguards or contractual accountability.

4.1. Delivery and Contracting Model

An applicant may participate as:

  • A single firm possessing the required end-to-end capabilities; or
  • A joint venture or consortium with complementary capabilities, with a clearly defined Lead Firm supported by formally identified specialist subcontractors or technical partners.

The Lead Firm shall enter into the contract with EWADE and assume full responsibility for end-to-end delivery, coordination, quality assurance, reporting, fiduciary compliance, risk management, safeguarding, data quality and achievement of all contracted outputs and results. The proposal shall identify each participating entity, its legal relationship to the Lead Firm, its role, the services it will provide, key personnel, coordination arrangements and the mechanism for managing performance and risks across the delivery chain.

EWADE will hold the Lead Firm accountable and will not separately manage consortium members, subcontractors or specialist partners. The Lead Firm shall consolidate all work plans, reports, invoices, evidence and communications; monitor the performance of participating entities; address delivery failures; and ensure consistent service standards. Any material change in consortium membership, specialist arrangements, key responsibilities or proposed personnel shall require prior written approval by EWADE.

4.2 Performance Review and Adaptive Management

Performance shall be reviewed for each cohort or service cycle against agreed service standards, output quality, beneficiary satisfaction, data quality, safeguarding compliance, market or employment linkage performance and outcome indicators measurable within the review period.

A broader implementation review shall be undertaken after the initial six months, or at another point specified in the contract, to assess the effectiveness of the integrated delivery model, coordination arrangements, beneficiary progression and the Lead Firm’s management of participating entities. EWADE may require a corrective action plan, enhanced supervision, replacement of personnel, revised sequencing or other reasonable adjustments within the contract. Any adjustment shall preserve the agreed objectives and the Lead Firm’s unified accountability.

5. Expected Outputs and Performance Framework

The assignment shall use results-based performance management. Performance will be assessed on delivery of contracted outputs and measurable contributions to agreed employment, enterprise, income and market outcomes. The Provider shall not be evaluated solely on the number of activities conducted. The contract shall distinguish between outputs within the Provider’s direct control and outcome indicators to which the Provider contributes.

7. Schedule and Duration

The services will commence upon contract signature and will be delivered throughout the implementation period of the Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project (EYEOP), in accordance with approved Annual Work Plans and Budgets, applicable project implementation arrangements and the performance requirements specified in the contract.

The engagement will be structured as a performance-based contract, initially covering one year and renewable annually, subject to satisfactory performance, achievement of agreed deliverables and performance targets, availability of funding and the continued need for the services. Subject to these conditions, the contract may be renewed on an annual basis for the duration of the EYEOP implementation period

The BDS Provider will be expected to provide services on a demand-driven and continuous basis, responding to the evolving needs of participating youth and the implementation schedule of the project. Key areas of service delivery will include:

  1. Mobilization and onboarding: Support the profiling, assessment and onboarding of participating youth into the relevant EYEOP economic inclusion and entrepreneurship interventions.
  2. Business assessment and planning: Conduct business diagnostics, develop or strengthen business plans and profiles, and support beneficiaries to develop viable and market-oriented enterprises.
  3. Capacity building and incubation: Deliver tailored business development training, coaching, mentorship, incubation and other technical assistance required to strengthen youth-owned enterprises.
  4. Enterprise development and growth support: Provide ongoing technical assistance to supported enterprises, including support for implementation, business formalization, financial management, productivity improvement and enterprise growth.
  5. Market and value-chain linkages: Facilitate linkages with buyers, lead firms, financial institutions, input suppliers, service providers and other relevant market actors to enhance access to markets and sustainable business opportunities.
  6. Performance monitoring and reporting: Monitor beneficiary and enterprise performance against agreed indicators and targets, and submit periodic reports demonstrating progress, results, challenges, corrective actions and lessons learned.
  7. Continuous improvement and adaptive support: Adjust the nature and intensity of BDS support based on beneficiary performance, emerging needs, project priorities, market conditions and lessons from implementation.

The specific annual deliverables, targets, timelines and performance indicators will be agreed with the EYEOP implementing agency at the commencement of each contract year and may be reviewed periodically to reflect the project's implementation priorities.

Continuation or renewal of the services will be subject to satisfactory performance against the agreed performance indicators and deliverables, compliance with contractual and project requirements, availability of funds, and approval in accordance with applicable procurement and project procedures. The sequence and timing of individual BDS activities may therefore vary during the project period depending on beneficiary needs, project implementation progress and approved annual work plans.

8. Team Composition

The Consultant shall propose suitably qualified key experts, including a Task Team Leader/BDS Team Leader; Agriculture Production, Agribusiness and Value Chain Expert, Training, Skills and Youth Development Expert; Market Systems and Private Sector Linkages Expert; Finance and Investment Readiness Expert, MEL/Data Management Expert, Digital Agriculture and Innovation Expert as well as Gender, Social Inclusion and Environment Safeguards Expert. For each proposed expert, the Consultant shall provide the key responsibilities, academic and professional qualifications, relevant professional experience, experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, proposed level of effort expressed in person-months and/or percentage of time, and availability for the assignment.

9. Firm Qualifications and Experience

The applicant shall demonstrate relevant institutional experience, technical expertise, operational capacity and systems relevant to deliver EYEOP Business Development Services. As a minimum mandatory requirement, the applicant shall have successfully completed at least one (1) assignment of similar nature, scope and complexity within the last five (5) years. The assignment shall demonstrate relevant experience in the delivery of BDS, enterprise development, youth entrepreneurship, business advisory services, training, mentorship, market linkages or related services.  In addition to the mandatory minimum requirement above, the applicant shall demonstrate the following relevant institutional experience, technical expertise and operational capacity:

  • Proven experience in delivering BDS, enterprise development, business advisory services, mentoring and coaching, including supporting emerging and existing entrepreneurs to establish, grow and sustain viable businesses across multiple sectors
  • Demonstrated experience implementing youth entrepreneurship, employment or skills development programmes.
  • Demonstrated experience in facilitating partnerships and establishing market linkages between smallholder farmers and buyers, aggregators and other private sector actors.
  • Demonstrated Experience in financial literacy, financial readiness and agriculture/value chain financing.
  • Proven experience implementing donor-funded, government-funded, or multi-stakeholder development programmes will be considered an advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience working in Eswatini and/or Southern Africa, with a sound understanding of the local agricultural, youth and enterprise development context.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating gender, youth, disability inclusion, climate-smart agriculture and green business practices.
  • Demonstrated adequate technical, financial and operational capacity to deliver BDS at the scale envisaged under EYEOP.

10. Environmental, Social Framework (ESF) Requirements

The assignment shall comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable national requirements as referenced in the Project Appraisal Document (PAD), with responsibilities proportionate to the Training, Capacity Building, and Mentoring category for delivery of business development services supporting income earning opportunities for youth under the EYEOP.

  • Comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, applicable national requirements and relevant Project instruments.
  • Apply gender-responsive and disability-inclusive approaches and provide agreed reasonable accommodations.
  • Integrate climate resilience, occupational health and safety, stakeholder engagement and beneficiary feedback into service delivery.
  • Record, refer and report grievances through the Project grievance mechanism and ensure personnel comply with safeguarding requirements and codes of conduct.
  • Protect beneficiary information, maintain required disaggregation and ensure confidentiality and data-protection obligations extend to consortium members and subcontractors.

11. Reporting Lines

The Lead Firm shall enter into the contract with EWADE and report to EWADE for all activities under this assignment, assuming full responsibility for end-to-end delivery, coordination, reporting and achievement of contracted outputs and results.

  • Accountability: EWADE will hold the Lead Firm accountable and will not separately manage consortium members, subcontractors or specialist partners. The Lead Firm shall consolidate all work plans, reports, invoices, evidence and communications; monitor the performance of participating entities; address delivery failures; and ensure consistent service standards.
  • EWADE responsibilities: EWADE will confirm beneficiary cohorts and targets; provide or facilitate access to applicable Project documents, beneficiary information and systems; designate technical and contract-management focal points; coordinate relevant Government stakeholders; review deliverables; monitor service quality; and verify performance.
  • Provider responsibilities: The Lead Firm shall provide all personnel, specialist inputs, logistics, equipment, materials, communication and management systems required for delivery unless otherwise stated in the contract. It shall maintain complete technical, financial and beneficiary records and make them available for supervision, audit and verification. It shall promptly report material delays, safeguarding issues, fiduciary concerns or other risks requiring management attention.
  • Escalation and corrective action: Where a broader implementation review identifies performance concerns, EWADE may require a corrective action plan, enhanced supervision, replacement of personnel, revised sequencing or other reasonable adjustments within the contract, preserving the agreed objectives and the Lead Firm's unified accountability.

11. Proposal and Evaluation Requirements

The technical proposal shall explain the applicant’s understanding of the assignment; integrated methodology; beneficiary profiling and pathway allocation; training, enterprise, finance, market, mentorship and M&E approaches; staffing and deployment; consortium governance; geographic capacity; quality assurance; risks and safeguards; output verification; and relevant past performance.

Evaluation shall consider capacity to manage the full beneficiary journey, the credibility and complementarity of any consortium arrangement, methodology, qualifications of key personnel, delivery and monitoring systems, relevant experience, financial and operational capacity, and value for money.

12. Payment Terms 

Payments shall be output-based and linked, as appropriate, to accepted deliverables, verified service delivery and verified performance results. The payment structure shall clearly distinguish inputs, outputs and outcomes and shall not reimburse consultant time without a corresponding accepted deliverable or contracted service result unless expressly provided in the contract.

The RfP and contract shall define each payment milestone, indicator definition, target, acceptance criterion, evidence requirement, verification method, payment trigger and treatment of incomplete or non-conforming outputs. Where payment is calculated per beneficiary, it shall be based on the verified number receiving the contracted package and satisfying applicable service-verification requirements. Submission of a report alone will not constitute acceptance where the underlying service or beneficiary-level evidence cannot be verified.

EWADE may verify reported outputs and results through document review, MIS checks, site visits, beneficiary confirmation, attendance validation, data-quality assessments, financial review or independent verification. All payments will be subject to written acceptance by the authorized EWADE representative and applicable contractual and fiduciary requirements.

13. Items to be Finalized in the RfP and Contract

  • Final beneficiary volumes, geographic coverage, cohorts, value chains, duration and delivery calendar.
  • Detailed outputs, targets, indicators, acceptance criteria, verification arrangements and reporting schedule.
  • Final payment milestones and any performance-linked share.
  • Key experts, minimum inputs, service standards, logistics and implementation milestones.
  • MIS protocols, applicable environmental and social instruments, data requirements and client inputs.
  • Provisions governing the Lead Firm, consortium members, specialist subcontractors, substitutions, remedies and termination.

  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the provision of overall management and technical oversight of civil and building works under the project (Components 2 and 3). Working under MWTI’s direction, the IAC will lead planning and implementation of engineering activities, deliver expert guidance across design, procurement, and construction, conduct technical studies and feasibility assessments, and monitor progress, risks, and compliance with safeguards. The role also includes coordinating stakeholders, building capacity through training and mentorship, strengthening institutional systems for project management, and ensuring accountability through regular reporting and transparent advisory outputs.
  3. The assignment will be undertaken by an Individual Consultant (IC) on a full-time basis in Samoa for an initial period of 24 months, with a possible extension subject to performance appraisal and MWTI-PMD’s project needs. It is anticipated to commence by December 2026.
  4. The Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure now invites all eligible Individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications, relevant experience and skills to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms' staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process. The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Minimum experience and capability:

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil and/or structural engineering (or relevant discipline) with a minimum 15 years of progressively responsible professional experience in leading and managing complex engineering projects as a government or private sector employee, consultant, or contractor.
  • Holder of a Chartered Engineering Membership and registration with IPES or similar (e.g.CPEng) in Civil or Structural Engineering.
  • Demonstrated experience in design, contract administration and construction supervision of at least 5 major civil or structural infrastructure projects.
  • Proven work experience with Government or development partner-funded projects and other relevant institutions.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience integrating climate resilient, disaster risk reduction and hazard risk reduction development.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing or working in countries with cyclonic, volcanic, and seismic activity with involvement in at least three (3) relevant projects.
  • Proven track record in reviewing and approving complex civil and structural engineering detailed designs, including compliance with applicable international and national standards and codes.
  • Experience in delivering workshops and training particularly the module list detailed in the Terms of Reference.
  • Served as Engineer or Superintendent to the Contract or equivalent role on at least five (5) infrastructure projects valued at US$1 million or more, covering design-build, design and supervise, and build only contract arrangements.
  • Demonstrated experience in project risk management, including identification, assessment mitigation, and monitoring of technical, financial, environmental and social risks.
  • Proven knowledge and practical experience in applying Environmental and Social Safeguards, environmental management, social risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and compliance monitoring processes.
  • Fluent in written and spoken English; and
  • Minimum five (5) years of professional experience working in developing countries.

Skills and competencies:

  • Demonstrated proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Suite (e.g., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), with a minimum of five (5) years of professional application for technical reporting, project management, communication, and data analysis.
  • Proficient in AutoCad, or another professional drawing applications software, demonstrated through application on a minimum of five (5) civil or structural engineering projects.
  • Minimum five (5) years of hands-on experience with using structural assessment software such as ETABS, SAP2000, or STAAD or similar, for structural assessment, modelling, design verification, and seismic or wind loading analysis.
  • Demonstrated knowledge in occupational health and safety in construction projects.
  • Analytical skills:  understanding of building works construction difficulties and situational analysis, and providing the most accurate and cost-effective technical solutions to ensure achievement of project objectives.
  • Excellent professional oral and written communication skills in English, including via email, audio/video conference, and face-to-face with World Bank and Government officials.
  • Demonstrated experience in managing, supervising, or coordinating the work of consulting firms, multidisciplinary engineering teams, or contractors on at least three (3) infrastructure projects.
  • Proven organizational and project management skills, including the ability to work independently and proactively to manage own workload. and
  • Willingness and ability to undertake regular travel within Samoa for visiting sites and inspection of project works.

Desirable qualifications, experience, and skills:

  • Prior experience working in the Pacific islands or on Small Island Developing States (Samoa experience highly regarded) with participation in at least three (3) infrastructure, urban development, climate resilience or community development projects. Prior experience in Samoa will be considered a distinct advantage.
  • Minimum five (5) years of professional experience working within an international organization, multilateral bank, or any other donor-financed projects, related to urban, infrastructure, community development and/or climate change adaptation and resilience.
